```

`.gitattributes`:

```
# Text is LF in the working tree on every platform. Git for Windows (core.autocrlf=true) otherwise
# turns it into CRLF, which breaks things quietly: a shell script with CRs ("bash\r: No such file"),
# and files of boot-arguments (devices/*/soc.args) whose lines are joined into the kernel's command
# line with a CR left inside every value. Git tells text from binary by content, so nothing here has
# to list the binaries.
* text=auto eol=lf

# A patch is not converted at all: the Mu-Silicium files it patches have CRLF line endings upstream, and
# the context lines of its hunks carry them (BootManager.c, BootManagerLib.inf). Turning them into LF
# would make the patch fail to apply.
*.patch -text

```

`CHANGELOG.md`:

```md
# Changelog

What changed, newest first. One line a change: the part of the system, then what is different for whoever runs it.
The commits say how; `docs/` says why.

## Sources

What a build is made of, and where each part is fetched from. Nothing of these is kept in the repositories but the
changes to it; the scripts named fetch the release and put the changes on.

- the kernel: Apple's [XNU](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu), tag `xnu-8796.121.2` (the release the Darwin 16.5 user space was built from) -- `xnu/apply.sh`, the changes in `xnu/hakios.patch` and `xnu/files/`, the drivers in `drivers/`
- the data volume: Apple's [HFS Plus](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/hfs), tag `hfs-627.100.6` -- `xnu/hfs/hfs.sh`, the changes in `xnu/hfs/hfs.patch`
- the boot: [U-Boot](https://source.denx.de/u-boot/u-boot) `v2026.07` -- `hakios-uefi/u-boot/apply.sh`, the changes in `hakios-uefi/u-boot/hakios.patch` and `files/`; the device's part in `hakios-sm7325/u-boot/`
- the UEFI (the other way to start): [Project Silicium's Mu-Silicium](https://github.com/Project-Silicium/Mu-Silicium) at `e51cd877e31c` -- `hakios-uefi/apply.sh`
- the GPU's OpenGL ES: [Mesa](https://archive.mesa3d.org/) 25.0.7, the freedreno driver for the Adreno -- `tools/mk-mesa.sh`, the changes in `tools/mesa/`
- the GPU's Vulkan: the same Mesa's Turnip -- `tools/mk-turnip.sh`, the changes in `tools/mesa/turnip-darwin.patch` and `tools/mesa/hakios-drm/`
- Metal, the direct path: `hakios-metal/` in this tree -- `userland/build.sh METAL_PLUGIN=ca`, with `userland/src/HakiosMetalCA.m`
- Metal, on Vulkan: [UniXNU/AdrenoMetal](https://github.com/UniXNU/AdrenoMetal) at `243d63c` and [steelbrain/metal2vulkan](https://github.com/steelbrain/metal2vulkan) at `624bab3` with AdrenoMetal's 30 patches -- `tools/mk-m2v.sh`, the changes in `tools/m2v/`
- the build tools: Apple's [libdispatch](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/libdispatch), [libpthread](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/libpthread) and [AvailabilityVersions](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/AvailabilityVersions), [bootstrap_cmds](https://github.com/markmentovai/bootstrap_cmds), [unifdef](https://github.com/fanf2/unifdef), the [macOS 13.3 SDK](https://github.com/joseluisq/macosx-sdks) and the [iPhoneOS 16.5 SDK](https://github.com/theos/sdks) -- `xnu-deps/setup.sh`
- not fetched by anything here: the Darwin 16.5 user space, which you lay out from your own IPSW (`sysimage/`), and the phone's own firmware, pulled from its Android (`fw-*`)

## 2026-11-05: 2.3.4

- metal: a pipeline CoreAnimation makes at run time, which its library does not hold, gets the nearest variant of the same kind and not one that draws something else. That was the red at the top of the default wallpaper (its head was not drawn), the white band behind the status bar (`darkenSourceOver`), and materials like the Weather widget's
- touch: a finger's lift 5 ms after its last move at most 6, on the phone under real fingers; 88 to 169 before. `touch: N strokes` in the log says so without `touch_lat=1`'s lines
- metal: at the default screen with the right shaders, on the phone: 109.6 frames a second over the bench's gestures, 1.3% of them over 16.7 ms. 120 is not reached: what is left is SpringBoard's main thread at the start of a gesture (up to 100 ms on the bench, up to 300 under fingers), and the GPU at the home button and opening an app
- windows: `tools/metal-run.sh` renders at the iPhone X's layout at 2 pixels a point by default, 750x1624 stretched to the panel, in place of the iPhone XR's screen: at that class a swipe from the bottom edge opened a sheet under real fingers. Not yet seen under real fingers at this one
- ports: `devices/<name>/metal.args` holds a phone's own arguments for `tools/metal-run.sh`, and a phone other than redwood no longer gets redwood's
- docs: the READMEs, the index and the Windows guide name `hakios-metal/` of this tree; the repository beside it says it has moved

## 2026-11-05: 2.3.3

- metal: `hakios-metal/` is in this tree with its history, and `userland/build.sh` links it: one checkout builds everything
- framebuffer: `fb_beam` and `fb_measure` read the display interface's registers only on `sc7280` or with `fb_intf=`: they read SM7325's address on any SoC before
- hakios-metal: a GPU of another chip ID is refused by name, and the window server stays on OpenGL ES
- tools: `tools/metal-run.sh` takes the phone's own arguments from `DEVICE_ARGS=`; [Port a device](docs/porting/index.md) says what Metal needs from a port
- touch: with a finger down every look reads a report; a finger's lift no longer waits up to 169 ms for the look of every 80 ms
- framebuffer: slow frames are filtered at once, so a still screen no longer moves back and forth 10 times a second; nothing is drawn again from a surface the GPU has taken back

- metal: `metal_fps=passes` prints every pass of a slow frame; the full-screen pass of the home screen is 6 to 13 ms of the GPU's ~10 a frame

- springboard: vibrant views keep their filters when the window server draws through Metal; `ui_lite=1` turns on Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion, `ui_lite=0` turns them off
- windows: `tools/metal-run.sh` runs on eight cores at 120 Hz with six scaling threads and without `-v` (VERBOSE=1 brings it back), and its summary shows the frames on the panel; `tools/frames.py` counts the Metal road's frames and the share over 8.3 ms

## 2026-10-29

- u-boot: HakiOS's own U-Boot, started by the phone's bootloader from RAM; it starts the loader and the kernel from memory, nothing of the vendor's firmware in between
- u-boot: the loader's fastboot works under U-Boot (USB 2.0 without the link power states that dropped the cable after 3 s, endpoints and packet sizes as the loader asks, DWC3 transfers started when queued)
- u-boot: every download and every step says what it does on the screen, tagged `[oosexgang]`

- install: `tools/userdata-carve.py --wipe` makes `darwin` at the end of userdata; `tools/sparse-split.py` cuts an 8 GB image into pieces Windows fastboot can send
- storage: the data volume is HFS Plus in `darwin` after the system, about 12 GB, journaled, kept between starts; before, `/private/var` was a memory volume shown as 1 GB and empty at every start
- storage: HFS Plus built into the kernel; Apple's sources are fetched at `xnu/apply.sh`, only this port's changes are kept
- storage: the data volume's writes go straight to the flash and the cache is flushed when the journal asks (a flush and a read back after every write made the system crawl)
- storage: the loader takes any phone's `darwin` (name, type, unit, at least 20 GiB), not only the first phone's place and identifier
- storage: `tools/mkdatavol.py` makes the empty volume as a 50 KB image that leaves the system volume alone

- loader: nothing printed over the system's screen while it runs; the log still takes every line
- loader: its log written under U-Boot too; a download the computer gave up on no longer hangs it
- wifi: the Wi-Fi controller is found where the system looks for its address, so registering applications no longer waits 5 s for each (found by the ios-sapphire port)
- tree: Darwin, not iOS, in the sources, the scripts, the file names and the documentation; no file of Apple's in the repositories
- docs: installing beside Android, step by step (`docs/dual-boot.md`, in Russian too), and the U-Boot page with everything as it was done and checked

`COMMUNITY.md`:

```md
# Community

HakiOS is built by whoever turns up and does the work: people who own a phone and a debugger, people who read
Apple's open source, people who write drivers, tests and documents. This file says how to take part, and keeps the
code and the money apart.

## Taking part

- **You need nothing but a patch.** No account with anybody, no membership, no token. Open an issue, send a pull
  request, or put a result in `docs/` ([CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)).
- **What a contribution is licensed under** is what the file it touches is under: the kernel patch and the files
  that sit in Apple's tree under APSL 2.0, everything else MIT ([LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md), [NOTICE](NOTICE)).
- **A contribution brings nothing of Apple's or a vendor's.** No Darwin file, no firmware, no key, no screenshot of
  either. CI runs `tools/provenance-check.py` and fails a change that does. If you are not sure what counts, ask first.
- **Results are reported as seen.** A test says what ran, on which phone, with which arguments, and what did not.
  "Does not work" and "I did not try" are both useful, and are not the same.

## Ways to help that need no phone

The open configuration (`make qemu-open`) boots in QEMU with nothing of Apple's and nothing of any phone's. Most of
the project is reachable from there: the loader, the configuration tools ([configs.md](docs/configs.md)), the boot
argument catalogue ([boot-args.md](docs/boot-args.md)), the driver reviews ([driver-review/](docs/driver-review)), the
translations, and a port to another SoC starting from its device tree ([devices/](devices)).

## The token

There is a community token, `$HackiOS`. This is what the repository says about it, and it is deliberately short:

- **It is not part of this project's code, licence or governance.** Holding it, buying it or selling it gives no
  right in this repository: no licence, no commit access, no vote on what is merged, no access to a file or a feature.
  Nothing here is gated behind it, and nothing will be.
- **The repository is not a place to promote it.** Issues, pull requests and discussions are for the code. A price,
  a "when", a promise of a return does not belong in them, and will be removed.
- **Nothing in this repository is investment advice or an offer of anything.** What a token is in law depends on what
  it promises and where you are; whoever runs a token is responsible for that, not this repository. If you are thinking
  of buying one, the code is not a reason, and a lawyer who knows your country is a better one.
- **Contributors are judged by their contribution**, not by what they hold.
- **Payments for work** (if the community decides to make any) are for specified work, agreed in advance, by whoever
  agreed to pay. They are not a share of anything and not a reward for holding.

The people who run the token are expected to say, in their own channel and in their own name, who they are, what the
token is meant to do, and what it does not. This file does not speak for them, and they do not speak for the code.

## Conduct

Be exact, be kind about people and hard on claims. No harassment; no doxxing; no pressure to run something
you do not understand. Maintainers may remove what breaks this, and say why.

## Reporting

A security problem, or a file that infringes somebody's rights: open an issue marked as such, or write to the
maintainers listed in the repository, and it will be looked at and, where warranted, removed.

```

`COMPLIANCE.md`:

```md
# License compliance

How HakiOS meets the terms of the licenses that apply to it. This is a working checklist, not a
legal opinion, and it does not assert that the project is free of all risk. See `LEGAL.md` and
`THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`.

## Apple Public Source License 2.0 (the kernel)

`xnu/hakios.patch` and everything under `xnu/files/` and `drivers/` are modifications of Apple's XNU, which Apple
publishes under the APSL 2.0. The full text is in `LICENSE.APSL`. The obligations we track:

- **Source availability (APSL 2.3).** Our modifications are published here as source. The exact
  Apple base they apply to is the tag `xnu-8796.121.2` at
  `github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu`, fetched by `xnu/apply.sh`. CI checks that the patch
  still applies to that tag.
- **Retention of notices (APSL 2.1).** Apple's original copyright and license notices are kept in
  the files they belong to. Our added files carry their own notices and do not remove Apple's.
- **Marking modifications (APSL 2.2).** Changes are described in the patch and in the commit
  history; the project's own files are named `hakios.<thing>.c` so that what is ours is
  distinguishable from Apple's original code.
- **Executable distribution (APSL 2.3(c)).** Where a built kernel is distributed (`prebuilt/`),
  the corresponding source is in the same repository, and this file points at it.
- **No re-licensing.** The XNU-derived code stays under the APSL; it is **not** relabeled MIT. The
  MIT License in `LICENSE` applies only to our own non-XNU code.

What is NOT covered and must not be assumed covered by the APSL: Darwin user space, Apple firmware,
trademarks, and any Apple binary. None of those are in this repository.

## MIT (our own code)

The loader, user-space sources, tools, scripts, docs and the device layer are under the MIT
License (`LICENSE`). Contributions are accepted under the same terms (`CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Third-party components

Each third-party component is listed in `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` with its origin, license, and
whether it is redistributed in the tree or fetched at build time. Components fetched at build time
(the Darwin SDK, Mesa and its Turnip, AdrenoMetal, metal2vulkan and its Rust crates, Procursus/Sileo, lzfse, ath11k, LinuxKPI headers) are
never committed; they are obtained from their own upstreams under their own licenses.

## Items still to verify

These are flagged for review and are **not** asserted to be settled:

- **UEFI driver binaries** under `devices/redwood/uefi/files/Binaries/` are the phone
  vendor's (Qualcomm/Xiaomi), extracted from the device's own `xbl.img`. They are needed only to
  rebuild the UEFI image and can be removed and re-extracted by each user from their own phone
  with UEFIReader. Whether redistributing them is permitted has not been confirmed with the
  vendor; a user who is unsure should delete them and extract their own. Tracked in
  `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`.
- **The FocalTech touch-controller firmware header** (`drivers/input/hakios.focaltech_fw.h`)
  is generated from a firmware blob on the device. Its redistribution terms are the touch
  vendor's and have not been confirmed; it is a candidate for moving to the pull-from-device
  model the rest of the firmware already uses.
- **Mu-Silicium / Project Mu** derived files under `devices/redwood/uefi/` carry upstream
  BSD-2-Clause-Patent and GPL-2.0-or-MIT headers; the derived parts keep those licenses.

- **Metal on Vulkan (`M2V=1`).** metal2vulkan is `GPL-2.0-or-later OR LGPL-3.0-or-later`, and `userland/build.sh` links it statically into the
  Metal plug-in and `m2v_test`. A binary so built has obligations; what they are here, and whether they can be met together with the other
  parts of that binary, has not been settled. **No such binary is distributed**: nothing of it is in `prebuilt/`, and each user fetches and
  builds it. Before anyone distributes one, this must be answered ([third-party licenses](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md#a-binary-built-with-m2v1-to-verify)).
- **`tools/m2v/metal2vulkan-hakios.patch`** is in the tree and changes GPL/LGPL code, so it is under those terms and not the MIT License
  that `LICENSE` gives the rest of `tools/`. It carries no notice of its own.
- **`userland/src/HakiosMetalCA.m`** began as vcvkk's plug-in (github.com/vcvkk/darwin-redwood). Its header names the origin; that
  repository states no license (read 2026-11-04), so the permission to carry and change this file is not established.
- **The Rust crates of `M2V=1`** not read from a local registry (`THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`).

If any of these cannot be confirmed as redistributable, the fallback is the same as for all
device firmware: remove the file from the tree and have each user obtain it from their own
hardware.

```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing

- One phone, one directory: anything that only one device needs goes to `devices/<name>/`; the
  kernel, loader and user space stay device-neutral and take their numbers from the device tree
  and the phone's own Android.
- Nothing of Apple's in the tree: no Darwin files, images, caches, screenshots or headers derived
  from the firmware. The build takes what it needs from the IPSW the user got
  themselves (`sysimage/unpack.sh`, `xnuloader/mkidentity.sh`); no script downloads Apple's files. CI refuses pictures and Darwin files.
- Nothing of the vendor's either: firmware is pulled from the user's phone (`make firmware`).
- Kernel changes are made in `xnu-src/` and exported with `xnu/export.sh` before committing;
  the patch must apply to Apple's `xnu-8796.121.2` tag (CI checks).
- Say in the commit message what the phone did, not only what the code does: a run's log line
  is worth more than an adjective.
- Names: files are `hakios.<thing>.c`, identifiers `hakios_<thing>`, sysctls `kern.hakios.*`,
  devices `/dev/hakios-<thing>`.
- Licenses: the kernel patch and files are APSL 2.0 (derived from XNU); everything else is MIT, but for
  a patch to third-party code, which keeps that code's license (`THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`).
  Third-party code goes into `NOTICE`.

## Legal and licensing

- HakiOS is an independent research project and is not affiliated with Apple. See `LEGAL.md`.
- The kernel patch and files are APSL 2.0 (derived from XNU); everything else is MIT, but for a
  patch to third-party code, which keeps that code's license. Do not relabel XNU-derived code as MIT. New third-party code goes into `NOTICE` and
  `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` with its origin and license.
- Nothing of Apple's in the tree: no Darwin files, images, caches, screenshots or headers derived
  from the firmware. Nothing of the vendor's firmware either. If you add a file whose origin or
  license you are not certain of, mark it "to verify" in `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` rather than
  asserting it is cleared.
- You can build and test the whole open path with nothing of Apple's:

  ```sh
  make qemu-open      # kernel + placeholder loader + the hello RAM disk, under QEMU
  ```

  The full Darwin user space (`make qemu`, `make phone`) additionally needs software and firmware you
  supply yourself.

## CI

`ci/github-check.yml` is a GitHub Actions workflow (Python compiles, scripts parse, no Apple
files or pictures in the tree, the kernel patch applies to Apple's tag). Enable it by copying it
to `.github/workflows/check.yml`; a push that adds it needs a token with the `workflow` scope,
or do it in the web editor.

```

`LEGAL.md`:

```md
# Legal

HakiOS is an independent open-source research project that ports the open-source XNU kernel to
ARM64 Qualcomm hardware. It is **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Apple Inc.**
"Darwin", "iPhone", "XNU", "Apple" and other marks belong to their owners and are used here only to
describe what the code works with.

This file explains, in plain terms, what is and is not distributed by this repository. It is a
description of the project's intent and current state, **not legal advice**, and it does **not**
claim that any use of the project is lawful in your jurisdiction. Running the full system image
requires software and firmware you must obtain and are licensed to use yourself; whether you may
do so is your responsibility. If in doubt, consult a lawyer.

## Three layers, and who decides what

HakiOS is an adaptation of the Darwin kernel to hardware that is not Apple's, in the way Android is an adaptation of
Linux to phones. It has three layers, and the project says plainly which one it stands behind.

1. **The open core.** The kernel port (a patch to Apple's open-source XNU, APSL 2.0), the boot loader, the drivers,
   the tools, the configurations. All of it is source in this repository, builds and runs with nothing of Apple's and
   nothing of any phone's (`make qemu-open`), and is what this project develops, documents and supports.
2. **What you put on top of it.** The kernel can start an operating-system user space that you supply. The project
   ships none, distributes none, and does not decrypt, circumvent or patch anything to obtain one: the tools only lay
   out, on your own machine, files that you have downloaded yourself from the vendor. **Whether you may use such
   software on this hardware is your decision and your responsibility.** Be aware of what you are deciding: Apple's
   software licence for Darwin ties it to Apple-branded hardware and restricts copying and modification, courts have
   treated that differently (see `docs/legal-review.md`), and the answer depends on your country and on what you do.
   The project does not tell you that it is permitted, and does not tell you that it is not; it tells you that it is
   not the project's to decide.
3. **Apple's services.** Activation, Apple ID, iCloud, iMessage, the App Store: not supported and not a goal. Nothing
   here makes a device pass as an iPhone to Apple's servers, and a change that tries to is refused.

## What the project writes to your phone

By default the boot loader runs from RAM (`fastboot boot`) and a reboot restores Android. It does write one thing: its
own log, a few KB, to the phone's `logdump` partition at the end of a run. Only if you turn on `ufs_write=1` does the
kernel write, and then only to a partition called `darwin` that you created yourself (`tools/userdata-carve.py` prints
the commands and changes nothing). Every other write is refused by the loader. `tools/provenance.allow` lists each
program that can write to flash, and CI fails if one appears that is not listed.

## What this repository contains

- **The kernel changes**: a patch to Apple's open-source XNU (`xnu/hakios.patch`) and added
  source files (`xnu/files/`, `drivers/`). These are a derivative work of XNU and are licensed under the
  Apple Public Source License 2.0 (`LICENSE.APSL`). See `COMPLIANCE.md` for how the APSL terms
  are met.
- **Our own original code**: the boot loader (`xnuloader/`), user-space programs
  (`userland/src/`), the tools (`tools/`), the build and run scripts, the documentation, and the
  device layer under `devices/`. These are licensed under the MIT License (`LICENSE`).
- **Third-party open-source components** that are redistributed or fetched at build time, each
  under its own license. They are listed with origin and license in `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`.
- **Pre-built artifacts** in `prebuilt/`: the kernel, user-space programs and libraries built
  from this repository's own source. They carry the same licenses as the source they are built
  from. Metal on Vulkan (`M2V=1`) and the window server's Metal plug-in are not among them: you fetch and
  build those yourself, and whether a binary of them may be distributed is to verify (`COMPLIANCE.md`).

## What this repository does NOT contain and never distributes

- **No part of Darwin**: no Darwin binary, image, cache, font, picture or screenshot. The user-space
  half of the system image is built on your machine from the Darwin userland 16.5 IPSW, which you
  get yourself, under Apple's license, and hand to `sysimage/unpack.sh` on your machine; no script
  here downloads it. Nothing of it is committed here.
- **No device firmware**: the GPU, Wi-Fi, audio DSP, modem, haptics and camera firmware is the
  vendor's (Qualcomm/Xiaomi). It is pulled from your own phone (`make firmware`) and is git-ignored.
- **No keys, certificates, activation data, or anything to impersonate a genuine Apple device to
  Apple's services.** Signing in to an Apple account is not possible here and is not a goal.

## The Apple-free configuration

The core kernel, the boot loader and the open tools build and run with **nothing of Apple's**:

    make qemu-open

builds the kernel and a placeholder loader (no IPSW needed, see `xnuloader/mkidentity.sh
--placeholder`) and boots a small raw-syscall user space (`userland/src/hello.c`) under QEMU.
This is the configuration a contributor can build and test without downloading any closed Apple
software. The full Darwin user space is an optional target that depends on software you supply.

## Reporting

If you believe a file in this repository infringes anyone's rights, open an issue (or email the
maintainer listed in the repository) and it will be reviewed and, where warranted, removed.

`Makefile`:

```
# HakiOS: one Makefile at the top, the way an Android tree has one. Every target is a script
# below it; run the script itself for its options.
#
#   make                 help
#   make unpack IPSW=F   the OS files out of your own Darwin userland 16.5 IPSW into sysimage/ (sysimage/unpack.sh)
#   make images          userland/root.apfs and userland/system.apfs (userland/build.sh)
#   make kernel          the kernel from source (xnu/apply.sh, xnu-deps/setup.sh, xnu-build.sh)
#   make loader          the boot loader, with identity.h made from your IPSW (xnuloader/build.sh)
#   make firmware        the phone's firmware off the phone over adb (devices/$(DEVICE)/pull-firmware.sh)
#   make qemu            a 20-minute session in QEMU (needs the Darwin images)
#   make qemu-open       boot the open kernel in QEMU with NO Apple software
#                        (kernel + the hello RAM disk + a placeholder loader)
#   make phone           a session on the phone, then back to Android (tools/modem-cycle.sh)
#   make prebuilt        refresh prebuilt/ from what was built (tools/update-prebuilt.sh)
#   make clean           build output of the kernel, loader and images
#   make doctor          check this machine and a phone on adb for what HakiOS needs (tools/doctor.sh)
#   make esp             an EFI system partition tree in build/esp: the loader and a payload it reads itself,
#                        to copy to a FAT32 volume (UEFI-native boot, no fastboot; docs/uefi-boot.md)
#   make u-boot          HakiOS's U-Boot for $(DEVICE) (uefi/u-boot/apply.sh, uefi/u-boot/build.sh; docs/u-boot.md)
#   make u-boot-img      hakios-u-boot.img: U-Boot as a boot image for fastboot boot, starting the loader from RAM
#   make qemu-u-boot     make qemu-open's payload booted the phone's way: U-Boot, the hakios command, bootefi
#
# Configuration, the way Linux's make does it (configs/, tools/hakios-config.py; docs/configs.md):
#   make redwood_defconfig   .config from configs/defconfig + redwood_defconfig (devices/redwood/configs/), which is
#                            common_defconfig + sc7280.config (devices/redwood/soc/) + redwood.config
#                            (any NAME_defconfig; make common_defconfig is the common kernel alone; docs/configs.md)
#   make devices             the device and SoC repositories (tools/hakios-device.py list; docs/porting/repositories.md)
#   make virt.config         lay a fragment (configs/virt.config) over the .config there is
#   make config              show the .config: its symbols, the kernel's arguments, the firmware it wants
#   make savedefconfig       the .config as a minimal defconfig
#   make phone               with a .config, its arguments are the kernel's; without, the phone line below
#   FRAGMENTS="open trace"   fragments for a NAME_defconfig: make redwood_defconfig FRAGMENTS=open
#
#   DEVICE=redwood   the device directory under devices/ (default redwood)
#   ARGS="..."           kernel arguments for make phone (default: the .config's, else everything the phone has)
#   SECS=600             the session's length for make phone / make qemu
#   JOBS=8               parallel jobs for the kernel build

DEVICE ?= redwood
JOBS ?= 8
SECS ?= 600
# qemu-open runs the open configuration: configs/defconfig (nothing of a phone's own, one core)
ARGS_OPEN ?= $(shell tools/hakios-config.py args --defconfig defconfig)
ifneq ($(wildcard .config),)
# a .config is the kernel's arguments; the runner then does not add its own four (cores, clock, storage): they are in it
ARGS ?= $(shell tools/hakios-config.py args)
RUNNER_BASE = BASE_ARGS=
else
ARGS ?= touchscreen=1 gpu=1 adsp=1 sound=4 wifi=1 haptic=5 modem=1 modem_again=1 modem_buffer=0xa8000000
RUNNER_BASE =
endif
IMAGE_OPTS ?= REST=1
ESP_DIR ?= build/esp
PAYLOAD ?= qemu/payload.bin
# make u-boot-img: the payload put in the image's ramdisk with the loader (none: U-Boot waits for them over fastboot)
UBOOT_PAYLOAD ?=

.PHONY: devices help unpack images kernel loader loader-open hello qemu qemu-open qemu-u-boot u-boot u-boot-img phone prebuilt clean all doctor defconfig config savedefconfig esp

help:
	@awk '{ if (!/^#/) exit; sub(/^# ?/, ""); print }' Makefile

doctor:
	tools/doctor.sh

all: kernel loader images

unpack:
	sysimage/unpack.sh $(IPSW)

images:
	$(IMAGE_OPTS) userland/build.sh

kernel:
	[ -d xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2 ] || xnu/apply.sh
	[ -e xnu-deps/host/bin/ld64 ] || xnu-deps/setup.sh
	tools/make-kernel.sh -j$(JOBS)

loader:
	xnuloader/build.sh

firmware:
	devices/$(DEVICE)/pull-firmware.sh

qemu:
	mkdir -p logs
	qemu/run-darwin.sh $(SECS) -display gtk | tee logs/qemu.log

# The Apple-free path: no IPSW, no Darwin user space. The loader is built with a placeholder identity
# (xnuloader/mkidentity.sh --placeholder), and the kernel boots the raw-syscall `hello` RAM disk.
# This is the configuration an outside contributor can build and run with nothing of Apple's.
loader-open:
	PLACEHOLDER=1 xnuloader/mkidentity.sh
	xnuloader/build.sh

# `hello` on its own: a static, raw-syscall program (no Darwin SDK, no Apple libraries).
hello:
	. ./xnu-env.sh && xnu-clang -arch arm64 -Os -static -nostdlib -ffreestanding \
		-fno-stack-protector -fno-builtin -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-pagezero_size,0x100000000 \
		-o userland/hello userland/src/hello.c

qemu-open: kernel loader-open hello
	mkdir -p logs
	xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o qemu/payload.bin \
		kernel=hakios-kernel \
		ramdisk=userland/hello --cmdline "$(ARGS_OPEN)"
	qemu/run.sh $(SECS) | tee logs/qemu-open.log

# HakiOS's U-Boot (docs/u-boot.md): the phone's ABL starts it from RAM (fastboot boot), and it starts the loader from
# memory; nothing is flashed. u-boot/ is made once by uefi/u-boot/apply.sh, with every device's U-Boot files.
u-boot:
	[ -d u-boot ] || uefi/u-boot/apply.sh
	uefi/u-boot/build.sh $(DEVICE)

u-boot-img:
	tools/mkubootimg.py -d $(DEVICE) $(if $(wildcard $(UBOOT_PAYLOAD)),-p $(UBOOT_PAYLOAD))

qemu-u-boot: kernel loader-open hello
	[ -f u-boot/build-qemu/u-boot.bin ] || { [ -d u-boot ] || uefi/u-boot/apply.sh; uefi/u-boot/build.sh qemu; }
	mkdir -p logs
	xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o qemu/payload.bin \
		kernel=hakios-kernel \
		ramdisk=userland/hello --cmdline "$(ARGS_OPEN)"
	qemu/run-u-boot.sh $(SECS) | tee logs/qemu-u-boot.log

phone:
	[ ! -f .config ] || tools/hakios-config.py check
	XL_SB_DELAY=8 $(RUNNER_BASE) tools/modem-cycle.sh "$(ARGS)" $(SECS)

# The loader and a payload (make qemu-open makes qemu/payload.bin; xnuloader/mkpayload.py makes any other) as the files an
# EFI system partition holds, which the loader reads itself: UEFI-native boot. The default tree is made again each time.
esp:
	[ "$(ESP_DIR)" != build/esp ] || rm -rf build/esp
	tools/mkesp.py $(ESP_DIR) $(PAYLOAD)

# ---- configuration (configs/, tools/hakios-config.py) ---------------------------------------------------------
defconfig:
	tools/hakios-config.py defconfig defconfig $(FRAGMENTS)

devices:
	@tools/hakios-device.py list

%_defconfig:
	tools/hakios-config.py defconfig $* $(FRAGMENTS)

%.config:
	tools/hakios-config.py merge $*

config:
	tools/hakios-config.py show

savedefconfig:
	tools/hakios-config.py savedefconfig

prebuilt:
	tools/update-prebuilt.sh

clean:
	rm -rf xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2/BUILD xnuloader/loader.obj xnuloader/loader.efi userland/root.apfs userland/system.apfs userland/obj

```

`README.md`:

```md
# HakiOS

English · [中文](README.zh.md) · [Українська](README.uk.md)

**Apple's open-source Darwin kernel (XNU, xnu-8796.121.2) on Android phones**, the way Android is Linux on phones: a boot loader of its
own, drivers of its own, a configuration system and a version of its own. The same kernel runs in QEMU with nothing of Apple's and
nothing of any phone's (`make qemu-open`). A research bench, not a ROM: by default it runs from RAM, and a reboot gives the phone back to
Android.

**Documentation:** [docs/](docs/index.md), and the site, [hackios-web.vercel.app](https://hackios-web.vercel.app).

**News, 4 November 2026:** on the POCO X5 Pro 5G the window server draws through Metal on the Adreno 642L, two ways. hakios-metal: page
swipes 110 to 115 frames a second, Settings' scroll 118, the home button 106, rendering at 828x1792 stretched to the panel; 101, about 90 and about 90 at the full 1125x2436. UniXNU's Metal on Vulkan: swipes 50 to 57, scroll 41. The panel is 120 Hz,
and **120 frames a second has not been reached**. [Metal on the Adreno](docs/reference/metal.md),
[the measurements](docs/reference/metal-measurements.md).

Start with [Getting started](docs/getting-started/index.md), [On the phone](docs/getting-started/phone.md) or
[Port a device](docs/porting/index.md). What works, part by part: [the documentation's front page](docs/index.md#what-works).

## Repositories

| Repository | Contents |
|---|---|
| [hakios-xnu-kernel](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-xnu-kernel) | **common**: the kernel port, every common driver, the loader, user space, the tools, this documentation, and `devices/qemu` |
| [`hakios-metal/`](hakios-metal) | Metal's command model on the Adreno, through the kernel's GPU driver |
| [hakios-sm7325](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-sm7325) | POCO X5 Pro 5G: its defconfig, status, UEFI platform, firmware script, and its SoC's layer (Qualcomm SC7280 family) |
| [hakios-mt6768](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-mt6768) | Infinix Hot 20 (MediaTek Helio G85): an experimental port with its own loader. Not in this repository's manifest |
| [hakios-uefi](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-uefi) | the firmware that starts the loader: Mu-Silicium with HakiOS's boot path, banner and name, and HakiOS's U-Boot |
| [hackios-web](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-web) | the website |
| [hackios-xnu-userland](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-userland) | old: a pointer kept for its links. User space is `userland/` here |

How they fit: [the repositories](docs/porting/repositories.md).

## What you bring, and what is never here

Nothing of Apple's and no vendor's firmware is in these repositories. The Darwin user space, if you want it, you lay out yourself from an
IPSW you get yourself, and the firmware comes off your own phone; nothing is downloaded for you, decrypted or circumvented. Apple's
services (activation, Apple ID, iCloud, the App Store) are not supported and not a goal.
[What is in the repository, and what never is](docs/index.md#what-is-in-the-repository-and-what-never-is).

# HakiOS

[English](README.md) · [中文](README.zh.md) · Українська

**Відкрите ядро Darwin від Apple (XNU, xnu-8796.121.2) на Android-телефонах**, так само як Android — це Linux на телефонах: власний
завантажувач, власні драйвери, власна система конфігурацій і власна версія. Те саме ядро працює в QEMU без нічого від Apple і без нічого
з будь-якого телефона (`make qemu-open`). Це дослідницький стенд, а не прошивка: за замовчуванням усе працює з ОЗП, а перезавантаження
повертає телефон в Android.

**Документація:** [docs/](docs/index.md) (англійською) і сайт [hackios-web.vercel.app](https://hackios-web.vercel.app).

сторінок 110–115 кадрів на секунду, прокручування в Settings 118, кнопка «додому» 106, рендер 828x1792, розтягнутий на панель; 101, близько 90 і близько 90 на повних 1125x2436. Metal поверх Vulkan від UniXNU: гортання 50–57, прокручування 41.

[вимірювання](docs/reference/metal-measurements.md).

## Що приносите ви, і чого тут ніколи немає

У цих репозиторіях немає нічого від Apple і жодних прошивок вендора. Користувацький простір Darwin, якщо він вам потрібен, ви збираєте самі
з IPSW, який берете самі, а прошивки знімаються з вашого власного телефона; за вас нічого не завантажується, не розшифровується й не
обходиться. Сервіси Apple (активація, Apple ID, iCloud, App Store) не підтримуються і не є метою.
[Що є в репозиторії, а чого ніколи немає](docs/index.md#what-is-in-the-repository-and-what-never-is).

# HakiOS

[English](README.md) · 中文 · [Українська](README.uk.md)

**运行在 Android 手机上的 Apple 开源 Darwin 内核（XNU，xnu-8796.121.2）**，就像 Android 是手机上的 Linux 一样：有自己的引导加载器、自己的驱动、自己的配置系统和自己的版本。同一个内核可以在 QEMU 中运行，不需要任何 Apple 的东西，也不需要任何手机的东西（`make qemu-open`）。这是一个研究平台，不是 ROM：默认从内存运行，重启后手机回到 Android。

**文档：** [docs/](docs/index.md)（英文），以及网站 [hackios-web.vercel.app](https://hackios-web.vercel.app)。

**动态，2026 年 11 月 4 日：** 在 POCO X5 Pro 5G 上，窗口服务器通过 Metal 在 Adreno 642L 上绘制，有两条路径。hakios-metal：翻页每秒 110 至 115 帧，Settings 滚动 118 帧，主屏幕按钮 106 帧（以 828x1792 渲染并拉伸到面板；完整 1125x2436 时为 101、约 90、约 90）。UniXNU 的 Metal on Vulkan：翻页 50 至 57 帧，滚动 41 帧。屏幕是 120 Hz，**尚未达到每秒 120 帧**。[Adreno 上的 Metal](docs/reference/metal.md)，[测量结果](docs/reference/metal-measurements.md)。

从 [Getting started](docs/getting-started/index.md)、[On the phone](docs/getting-started/phone.md) 或 [Port a device](docs/porting/index.md) 开始。各部分的工作情况：[文档首页](docs/index.md#what-works)。

## 仓库

| 仓库 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| [hakios-xnu-kernel](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-xnu-kernel) | **公共部分**：内核移植、所有公共驱动、引导加载器、用户空间、工具、本文档以及 `devices/qemu` |
| [`hakios-metal/`](hakios-metal) | 通过内核的 GPU 驱动，在 Adreno 上实现 Metal 的命令模型 |
| [hakios-sm7325](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-sm7325) | POCO X5 Pro 5G：defconfig、状态、UEFI 平台、固件脚本及其 SoC 层（Qualcomm SC7280 系列） |
| [hakios-mt6768](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-mt6768) | Infinix Hot 20（MediaTek Helio G85）：实验性移植，有自己的引导加载器。不在本仓库的清单中 |
| [hakios-uefi](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-uefi) | 启动引导加载器的固件：带有 HakiOS 启动路径、横幅和名称的 Mu-Silicium，以及 HakiOS 的 U-Boot |
| [hackios-web](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-web) | 网站 |
| [hackios-xnu-userland](https://github.com/oosexgang/hackios-xnu-userland) | 旧仓库：只为保留链接而存在的指向。用户空间现在在这里的 `userland/` |

它们如何组合：[仓库说明](docs/porting/repositories.md)。

## 你需要自带什么，以及这里永远没有什么

这些仓库中没有任何 Apple 的东西，也没有厂商固件。如果需要 Darwin 用户空间，你要用自己获取的 IPSW 自行布置；固件取自你自己的手机；没有任何东西会替你下载、解密或绕过。Apple 的服务（激活、Apple ID、iCloud、App Store）不受支持，也不是目标。[仓库里有什么，永远没有什么](docs/index.md#what-is-in-the-repository-and-what-never-is)。

## 参与贡献

见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) 和 [COMMUNITY.md](COMMUNITY.md)。

## 许可与法律

XNU 补丁及其派生文件采用 Apple Public Source License 2.0（[LICENSE.APSL](LICENSE.APSL)），其余采用 MIT（[LICENSE](LICENSE)），以文件头为准。第三方组件：[NOTICE](NOTICE)、[THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md)、[COMPLIANCE.md](COMPLIANCE.md)。分发什么、不分发什么：[LEGAL.md](LEGAL.md)。以上都不构成法律意见。

HakiOS 是一个独立的研究项目，**与 Apple 没有关联，也未获其认可**；提及 “Darwin”、“iPhone”、“XNU” 和 “Apple” 只是为了说明代码面向什么。如果你认为这里的某个文件侵犯了任何人的权利，请提交 issue，它会被移除。

## 团队

hakios 是一个实验性项目，致力于把 darwin 带到 android 硬件上。我们的目标是让 hakios 免费并人人可用。

## A binary built with `M2V=1`: to verify

`userland/build.sh TURNIP=1 M2V=1` links `libadreno_metal_bridge.a`, which holds the metal2vulkan runtime (`GPL-2.0-or-later OR
LGPL-3.0-or-later`), statically into the Metal plug-in (`HakiosMetal`) and into `m2v_test`, beside AdrenoMetal's frontend (MIT), the plug-in's
own code and hakios-metal. Whoever distributes such a binary takes on that license's obligations for it, whichever of the two is chosen: under
the LGPL, among others, a recipient's ability to relink against a changed library; under the GPL, the whole binary's source under compatible
terms. What exactly that requires here, and whether the parts in the row above marked **to verify** allow it, is **to verify**, and has not
been settled. Until it is, no such binary is distributed: nothing of it is in `prebuilt/` (`prebuilt/userland` has no `HakiosMetal`), and you
fetch and build it yourself, on your machine. `libvulkan_freedreno.dylib` (Turnip) is a separate library, loaded at run time, under Mesa's terms.

## How to rebuild the inventory

- Tracked non-text/binary files: `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 file --mime-type | grep -v text/`
- License mentions in tracked files: `git grep -li "SPDX-License-Identifier\|GPL\|BSD\|MIT\|APSL\|copyright"`

If a component's origin is uncertain, it is marked **to verify** above and must be treated as not
yet cleared for redistribution until confirmed with its owner.

`VERSION`:

```
# The version of the HakiOS kernel, given the way the Makefile of Linux and an Android kernel give theirs:
#
#   VERSION.PATCHLEVEL.SUBLEVEL EXTRAVERSION
#
# tools/kernel-version.py makes the whole string from this file, the active configuration (.config) and
# git: 2.3.4-hakios-darwin22.5-sc7280-g1a2b3c4d  (the version, EXTRAVERSION, the Darwin it is built on, the
# SoC family the configuration is for, and the commit; "-dirty" when the tracked files have changed).
# The loader prints it as kernel.ver= under its banner, passes it to the kernel as the boot-arg hakios_kver,
# and the kernel keeps it as sysctl kern.hakios.version. docs/versioning.md says when each number moves.
#
# VERSION    major: a change that breaks what a user, a port or a boot image relies on (the payload format, the
#            boot-arguments, the layout of the partition `darwin`)
# PATCHLEVEL a feature: a driver, a device, a tool
# SUBLEVEL   a fix
# EXTRAVERSION is what the tree is called; a vendor's branch says so here (Android's "-android12-9")
VERSION = 2
PATCHLEVEL = 3
SUBLEVEL = 4
EXTRAVERSION = -hakios
NAME = Hello Darwin

# the Darwin this kernel is built on: Apple's open xnu tag (xnu/apply.sh fetches it)
DARWIN = 22.5.0
XNU = xnu-8796.121.2

```

`ci/github-check.yml`:

```yml
name: check
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: The SoC, device and UEFI repositories devices/manifest.conf names
        # they are private repositories of their own: a token that can read them, in the secret HAKIOS_SYNC_TOKEN; without it the
        # checks of the reference phone's configuration and the made device pages are skipped, and say so
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HAKIOS_SYNC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
            git config --global url."https://x-access-token:${TOKEN}@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"
            python3 tools/hakios-device.py sync
          else
            echo "no HAKIOS_SYNC_TOKEN: only the common repository is checked"
          fi
      - name: Python compiles
        run: |
          git ls-files '*.py' | xargs -r python3 -m py_compile
      - name: Shell scripts parse
        run: |
          git ls-files '*.sh' xl | xargs -r -n1 bash -n
      - name: Scripts that start with #! are executable in git (a Windows commit with a pathspec records 644)
        run: |
          bad=$(git ls-files -s | awk '$1=="100644"{print $4}' | while read -r f; do
            case "$f" in *.sh|*.py|xl) head -c2 "$f" | grep -q '^#!' && echo "$f";; esac; done)
          if [ -n "$bad" ]; then echo "not executable in git (git update-index --chmod=+x):"; echo "$bad"; exit 1; fi
      - name: Makefile help
        run: make help
      - name: Provenance - every binary and blob explained, nothing proprietary, nothing writes to the phone
        run: |
          # The rule of the repository: nothing of Darwin, no pictures of it, no vendor firmware, and a
          # promise that the project boots from RAM and does not write to the phone's storage. Every
          # binary must have a line in tools/provenance.allow saying where it came from.
          # (This replaces two lines of the form `! git ls-files | grep ...`: bash -e does not stop on
          # a negated pipeline, so the first of them could never fail, and a committed screenshot passed.)
          python3 tools/provenance-check.py
      - name: The provenance check itself: what it lets through and what it stops
        run: python3 tools/provenance-test.py
      - name: A run sends only the soc_* values that differ from the kernel's defaults
        run: bash tools/soc-only-changes-test.sh
      - name: Configurations - defconfigs, fragments, the arguments made from them
        run: python3 tools/hakios-config-test.py
      - name: The EFI system partition tree is laid out as the loader looks for it
        run: python3 tools/mkesp-test.py
      - name: The kernel's version string is made as it should be
        run: python3 tools/kernel-version-test.py
      - name: The backup tool only reads, copies exactly, and proves every copy
        run: python3 tools/backup-partitions-test.py
      - name: The boot-argument catalogue is read from the source, and is current
        run: |
          python3 tools/boot-args-test.py
          python3 tools/boot-args.py --check
      - name: The drivers are kept by subsystem, every one is in drivers/map, and drivers/*/conf builds each exactly once
        run: python3 tools/drivers-check.py
      - name: The device and SoC repositories hold together, and a device's own drivers reach the kernel
        run: |
          python3 tools/hakios-device.py check
          python3 tools/hakios-device-test.py
      - name: The documentation pages made from the source are current
        run: |
          [ ! -d devices/redwood ] || python3 tools/docs-gen.py --check
          python3 tools/docs-check.py
      - name: The Metal plug-in's reading of a .metallib refuses every file cut short or bent (sanitizers)
        run: sh tools/metallib-test.sh
      - name: The kernel patch applies to Apple's tree
        run: |
          git clone -q --depth 1 --branch xnu-8796.121.2 https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu.git /tmp/xnu
          git -C /tmp/xnu apply --check "$PWD/xnu/hakios.patch"
      - name: APFS tools self-test
        run: |
          [ -x tools/apfs/run-tests.sh ] && tools/apfs/run-tests.sh || echo "no self-test on this runner"
      - name: SoC args generator reproduces the POCO X5 Pro values
        run: |
          sh tools/soc-args-test.sh
          # ... and finds the AOSS mailbox however a phone's own device tree describes it
          python3 tools/soc-args-test-aoss.py
          # ... and tools/new-device.py makes a port's directory from a phone's tree, and refuses what it should
          python3 tools/new-device-test.py

```

`configs/persist.config`:

```config
# Fragment: keep /private/var across reboots. THIS WRITES TO THE PHONE'S STORAGE, to the partition `darwin` only.
# The kernel and the loader refuse any other write. The partition has to exist: it is cut off the end of Android's
# userdata once, by hand (tools/userdata-carve.py prints the commands and says what they do to Android's data).
# Without that partition, leave this fragment out.
CONFIG_UFS=2
CONFIG_UFS_WRITE=y
CONFIG_VAR_STORE=y

```

`devices/README.md`:

```md
# Device repositories

`devices/manifest.conf` names every device; `tools/hakios-device.py sync` clones each into `devices/<name>/`. `devices/qemu/` is
kept here: QEMU's machine, with none of a phone's drivers, the device every checkout of the common repository can build and run.
A device of your own: `tools/hakios-device.py new` ([Port a device](../docs/porting/index.md)).

```

`devices/manifest.conf`:

```conf
# devices/manifest.conf: every SoC and device repository HakiOS knows of (Android's repo manifest, UniXNU's devices.toml).
#
#   device|uefi <name>                                  (a device carries its SoC's layer in soc/; the UEFI is one, in uefi/)
#   soc <name>                                          (a SoC layer of its own, in socs/<name>: for one many devices share)
#       path        <directory in this tree>                kept here, for now: tools/hakios-device.py split makes it a repository
#       repository  <git URL>                               a repository of its own, cloned into socs/<name> or devices/<name>
#       revision    <commit>                                ... at this commit (tools/hakios-device.py lock writes it)
#
# `tools/hakios-device.py sync` clones and updates the ones with a repository; `list` shows them all; docs/porting/repositories.md
# is the guide. A device of yours: open a pull request that adds its block here, with its repository and revision.

device redwood
	repository  https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-sm7325.git
	revision    af52dfba33f91340bde68dbbe238ae583f9fd472

device qemu
	path        devices/qemu

uefi hakios-uefi
	repository  https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-uefi.git
	revision    1c6522893266157506c767e2ca427053ed3634a8

```

`devices/qemu/device.conf`:

```conf
# devices/qemu/device.conf: QEMU's virt machine as a device: what a port looks like with none of a phone's drivers built in.

device qemu
	title       QEMU virt (aarch64)
	vendor      QEMU
	soc         none
	defconfig   qemu_defconfig
	maintainer  the HakiOS developers (README.md)
	status      display     works     ramfb, through the loader
	status      touch       works     virtio tablet as the touch screen (CONFIG_HAKIOS_VIRTIO_INPUT)
	status      buttons     works     virtio keyboard: H is Home, L the power button, arrows the volume
	status      storage     works     virtio-blk images (CONFIG_HAKIOS_VIRTIO_BLK)
	status      audio       works     virtio sound (CONFIG_HAKIOS_VIRTIO_SOUND)
	status      network     works     virtio-net as en0 (CONFIG_HAKIOS_VIRTIO_NET)
	status      gpu         missing   no GPU: the screen is drawn in software

```

`devices/qemu/u-boot/files/configs/hakios_qemu_defconfig`:

```
# HakiOS's U-Boot on QEMU's virt machine: the phone's way of starting (the hakios command: the loader and its payload
# from memory, bootefi) on a machine anyone has. qemu/run-u-boot.sh puts the HKUB container in memory at 0x50000000,
# where a phone's ABL would have put its ramdisk.
#include "qemu_arm64_defconfig"

CONFIG_CMD_HAKIOS=y
CONFIG_BOOTDELAY=0
CONFIG_BOOTCOMMAND="hakios load 0x50000000 && run hakios_start"
# (a host tool that needs GnuTLS, and capsules are not used here)
# CONFIG_TOOLS_MKEFICAPSULE is not set
# the menu of an installed HakiOS (tools/mkubootimg.py --install), tried here before a phone
CONFIG_CMD_BOOTMENU=y

```

`docs/air.md`:

```md
# AIR → NIR: a Metal shader frontend for Mesa

This is the compiler third of running Metal on the Adreno of this port: a translator from Apple's
shader bitcode (AIR, the contents of a `.metallib`) to Mesa's NIR, so that ir3 — the same compiler
that already runs the port's OpenGL ES through freedreno — turns Metal shaders into Adreno code.

The other two thirds are **not** here and are not started: the `_MTLDevice`/`IOGPUMetalDevice`
object graph (AGXMetalA11 alone is 53 classes and 1158 methods, IOGPU.framework 711 more), and the
kernel ABI that submits work. Where a decision below constrains them it says so, and section 7
collects those constraints in one list.

Why this is worth doing at all, and what it costs, is argued in `docs/metal.md` section 9. This
document assumes those measurements and records the decisions taken on top of them.

## Where it stands, and what that does not mean

Of the 456 modules of the device's system `.metallib` files (`tools/air/check.sh`, and
`docs/air-report.md` for the breakdown):

| | of 456 |
| --- | --- |
| read by our own bitcode reader, byte for byte as `llvm-dis` reads them | 456 |
| translated to NIR, passing `nir_validate` | 321 |
| compiled by ir3 into Adreno machine code | 321 |
| numerically identical to LLVM's own execution, and drawn | 255 |
| **run on the phone's GPU** — 7 drawn, 47 dispatched | **54** |

And of the 119 distinct `air.*` operations those modules call (`tools/air/intrincheck.py`):

| | of 119 |
| --- | --- |
| checked numerically, one operation at a time, against a reference outside this tree | 78 |
| of those, exactly defined and agreeing on every case (45 697 cases) | 71 |
| of those, approximate, so measured against libm and nothing concluded | 7 |
| of those, also *run* by a Gallium driver rather than folded (softpipe, 2 586 cases) | 47 |
| of those, run **on the phone's own Adreno** (714 cases) and agreeing there | 61 |
| of those, disagreeing before the `ir3` rounding fix this port now carries (0 after) | 5 |
| of those, set aside: they return `half`, which `air_run` cannot read back | 10 |
| the atomics and the barrier, against kernels written for them (`atomiccheck.py`) | 10 |
| texture operations verified exactly, on several texels each (`texopcheck.py`) | 13 |
| texture operations with a case softpipe cannot run: a 16-bit result | 7 |
| texture operations with no case: multisample, depth, write | 11 |

321 of 456 is **every entry point** of the corpus: 271 fragment shaders, 47 compute kernels and 3
vertex shaders. The other 135 modules are `air.visible` library functions, not entry points at
all, and they have a measurement of their own:

| the 135 library functions | |
| --- | --- |
| wrapped in a generated entry point and translated (`--library`) | 124 |
| refused: a texture, sampler or matrix argument the wrapper cannot pass | 11 |
| dispatched by a Gallium driver and read back | 124 |
| of those, agreeing with our own constant folding of the same shader | 104 |
| of those, run but disagreeing | 0 |
| ran, but the folder did not reduce the result to a constant | 20 |
| **agreeing with LLVM on this machine, bit for bit** | **21 of 21** |

`tools/air/libcheck.py` prints that table and refuses to print it when the rows do not add up.
The last row is the one that counts, and it is small for a stated reason: LLVM can be the
reference only for a function that calls no `air.*` at all, because an `air.*` call is an
undefined symbol on the host and defining one would put our own reading of that operation on
both sides of the comparison. 57 more call only exactly defined `air.*` operations and could be
compared that way if those definitions were written; 46 call an approximate one
(`air.fast_pow` and the like), which nothing compares bit-exactly anywhere.

**What a library function's measurement is not: evidence about Metal's stitching.** Metal links
these into a caller at pipeline time through the ABI their own metadata describes
(`air.stitching_info`, with the four functions that do it and each argument's size and
alignment). That ABI is the runtime's, not the compiler's, and it is not implemented. The wrapper
is this project's own calling convention, invented to make the bodies runnable.

**And what the 456 itself is not: the number of shaders on the device.** It is the number of
modules in the `.metallib` *files* under `sysimage/rootfs`. A library can also be a blob inside a
dylib — `GPUCompiler`'s own `GNR.videoprocessor` carries one in `__DATA`, found while looking for
something else — so every statement here of the form "the corpus contains no X" is bounded by how
the corpus was collected, not by what the system contains. Where that distinction matters, this
document says so; extending the corpus to embedded libraries would move this denominator and
every percentage computed from it, so it is a change to make in one commit and recount, not a
figure to adjust.

**What those numbers are not**, because they will be quoted without this paragraph otherwise:

- **The arithmetic operations are checked; two of them have now been checked against the
  Adreno, and the other 76 have not.** 71 of the corpus's declarations agree with C's own
  functions on every one of 45 697 cases, and 47 of them agree again when *executed* by softpipe
  instead of folded — which is a real answer to what used to be the largest hole here (section 4,
  item 4), and found three bugs getting there. But those two engines are both on an x86 host. An
  opcode whose Adreno instruction differs from what `nir_opt_constant_folding` and TGSI compute is
  invisible to all 48 283 of those cases, and the 24 narrow-type declarations softpipe cannot run
  at all are exactly the ones where ir3 differs most from it.

  On 20 October that stopped being true. All 78 declarations ran on the phone's own Adreno, and
  twice: once as the port stood, and once with the one-line `ir3` rounding fix this tree now
  carries (`tools/mesa/ir3-round-default.patch`).

  | | agree | differ | set aside | cases |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | as the port stood (`logs/090218-run.log`) | 56 | **5** | 10 | 714 |
  | with the rounding fix (`logs/090918-run.log`) | **61** | **0** | 10 | 714 |

  The 5 were the whole point of having gone there, because every engine on this machine agrees
  with C about them. All five are integer-to-float conversions:
  `air.convert.f.{f32,v2f32,v3f32}.u.*` and, once the pool was sharpened to ask,
  `air.convert.f.{f32,v2f32}.s.*` as well — `i2f` truncates exactly as `u2f` does, which the
  earlier pool had no value to notice. With the fix all five agree and nothing else moved, which is
  the useful shape of an after-measurement: the thing that was wrong is right, and nothing that was
  right has changed.

  **An earlier version of this paragraph said 66 agree on 808 cases, and that was 10 declarations
  too many.** It also said the 24 narrow-type declarations softpipe cannot run had all run on the
  Adreno and agreed, which was the part that mattered and the part that was wrong. Ten of them
  return `half`, `air_run` reads back through a 32-bit float target and has none that is 16 bits
  wide, so the half is widened at once and NIR folds the conversion into a 32-bit one: the
  reference describes an operation the shader does not perform. They are now set aside by name —
  `air.convert.f.f16.{s.i32,u.i16,u.i32,u.i8}`, `air.fmax.{f16,v4f16}`, `air.fmin.{f16,v4f16}`,
  `air.mix.f16`, `air.saturate.f16` — and 56 + 5 + 10 = 71 closes the account. What is true of the
  narrow types is narrower than before: the `i1`, `i8` and `i16` ones ran and agree; the `f16` ones
  were never asked. Nothing refused to run, though: no assertion, no fallback, no module missing.

  The row "run on the phone's GPU" in the first table above does not count these: it counts
  modules of the 456-module corpus, and these are generated modules that are not in it. The two
  measurements are deliberately not added together. That row now reads **51** for a different
  reason — 7 fragment shaders drawn and 44 compute kernels dispatched, which are disjoint sets
  because a kernel is not a fragment shader. It read 7 until the kernels ran, and it stayed 7 for
  a while after they did, which is the third time this one figure has been left behind by the work
  that moved it.
- **Two traps this frontend's own checks fell into, kept here for the instances; the general forms
  are in README's "Как врут собственные проверки", which collects all six and belongs there because
  the others came from the camera, the services and the build rather than from AIR.** Comparing one
  file of Mesa's `main` against ours had to start from a fresh tarball extract, because ours carries
  our own patch — 202 487 bytes against 202 144 clean — so a comparison from this tree would have
  differed by exactly our own change. And `patch -s --dry-run` exiting 0 against that file was
  written down as "applies cleanly" when without `-s` it says "succeeded at 410 (offset 2 lines)":
  the context matched and the line number had moved, which is the more useful statement and the one
  the patch header now carries.

- **A `continue` that adds nothing to a total is where this check has gone wrong three times.**
  Not a maxim but a thing to grep for, and the general form is in README beside the other five.
  Three times on 20 October an absent check was dressed as a passing one, and each time the shape
  was identical: a loop skipped a case and incremented no counter, so "not examined" was reported
  as "examined and agreed".

  - `if idx >= len(flat): continue` dropped every case whose value was missing from the log, and
    the total fell by exactly as much as nobody was watching;
  - `read_whole`'s predecessors read a configuration file with one `read()` into a fixed buffer, so
    a file past its buffer silently lost its tail and the jobs in it never ran;
  - `check_log` skipped every infinite expectation, which is how ten `half`-returning declarations
    came to be reported as agreeing on every case when three of every four cases were not compared
    at all.

  So the rule is not "skip less". It is that every case set aside must reach the summary with its
  own number and its own reason, and that a verdict resting on very few cases must say how few —
  `air.all.v2i1` agrees on two cases, and that is worth knowing before quoting it. Green has to
  mean "looked at and agreed", never "did not look".

- **The Adreno truncates `u32 → f32` where C, NIR and softpipe round.** This is the first thing
  found here that no engine on this machine could have found, and it is why the suite was carried
  to the phone at all. `air.convert.f.f32.u.i32` and its 2- and 3-component forms, given
  `0xFFFFFFFF` (4 294 967 295 unsigned), return **4 294 967 040** where C returns
  **4 294 967 296**.

  The arithmetic is worth writing out, because the two numbers look like a printing difference and
  are not. In `binary32` the spacing between representable values in [2³¹, 2³²) is 2⁸ = 256, so the
  neighbours of 2³² − 1 are 2³² − 256 and 2³². Their distances from it are 255 and 1, so
  round-to-nearest gives 2³² = `0x4f800000`, which is what `(float)4294967295u` is in C, checked
  by compiling it. The Adreno's answer, 2³² − 256, is exactly `0xFFFFFFFF & 0xFFFFFF00`: the low
  eight bits dropped. That is truncation toward zero, not rounding. Metal's conversions are
  OpenCL's, which require round-to-nearest-even, so this is a real divergence and not a matter of
  taste. Only the cases where rounding decides anything differ — 1 of 4, 2 of 8 and 3 of 12 — and
  every value that is exactly representable agrees.

  **Where it comes from is settled as far as inspection can settle it, and no further.** Two of the
  three possible culprits are eliminated by reading code rather than by guessing:

  - the frontend emits `nir_u2fN`, the correct opcode (`air_intrinsics.c`, the `convert` branch);
  - ir3 turns that into a *single* `cov.u32f32` with no compensation. For a 32-bit source
    `create_cov` has no special case at all — the special cases there are for 8-bit sources and
    for `f32 → u8`. The generated Adreno code for the module is five instructions, four of them
    `cov.u32f32` reading straight out of the constant buffer, with nothing between the load and the
    conversion.

  So the truncation is the behaviour of the a6xx `cov.u32f32` instruction itself. **Whose job it is
  to compensate is not established**, and needs the a6xx ISA documentation, which is not to hand:
  if `cov` is specified to round, this is a hardware erratum ir3 should work around; if it is
  specified to truncate, then every API that requires round-to-nearest — OpenCL, Metal, and Vulkan's
  `ConvertUToF` — has to compensate, and ir3 does not. Not worked around in the frontend, because
  the frontend is emitting the right opcode and a workaround there would hide a fault that belongs
  to everything ir3 compiles.

  **The prediction that followed has been tested and holds, by a peer session rather than here.**
  The port's OpenGL ES goes through the same ir3 and the same instruction, so a GLES shader should
  truncate identically — and `userland/src/u2f_test.c` (`RC=rc.u2f`) asks GLSL ES 3.0 the same
  question through the same Mesa, with no AIR anywhere in it. Four of its six inputs disagree with
  C on `freedreno; Adreno 7c+ Gen 3; OpenGL ES 3.2 Mesa 25.0.7`, and the two that agree are exactly
  the two where truncation and rounding give the same answer — so agreement there is the absence of
  a question, not a confirmation. **Everything ir3 compiles on this phone converts unsigned to
  float by truncating, the window server's drawing included**, and this frontend is not party to
  it: it is physically absent from that test.

  **The cause is ir3 and not the a6xx instruction, and an earlier draft of this section had that
  wrong.** It said inspection had eliminated two of three culprits and the remaining one was the
  hardware. The steps were right and the conclusion was not: `create_cov` ends with a rounding
  field that the reading stopped short of. `cov` *has* a rounding mode — `ROUND_ZERO = 0`,
  `ROUND_EVEN = 1` in `instr-a3xx.h` — and `ir3_compiler_nir.c` sets it for a destination of
  `TYPE_F16` or `TYPE_F32` from `float_controls_execution_mode`, which is a SPIR-V declaration.
  `nir_get_rounding_mode_from_float_controls` returns `nir_rounding_mode_undef` when nothing is
  declared, so neither branch fires and the field keeps its zero, which is truncation. GLSL ES
  declares nothing and this frontend declares nothing, which is exactly why two independent paths
  returned the same wrong number. **The hardware can round; ir3 only asks when someone else has
  asked first, and supplies no default where IEEE-754 and GLSL both require round-to-nearest.**
  **How much this reaches is a number and not an adjective.** Of the 456 modules of the corpus, 20
  contain a conversion the patch can change — a `u2f`, an `i2f` or an `f2f16`, the three that
  round; none contains only the exact kinds (`f2f32`, `b2f`), where setting the mode cannot alter a
  value. So on the Metal side the blast radius is 20 modules, not all 313 that translate, and
  whether each of those 20 actually changes depends on the values it meets at run time.

  That bounds this frontend's half. **The other half has now been measured too, by a peer session,
  and the answer has a shape worth keeping.** The port's OpenGL ES reaches ir3 through Mesa's own
  GLSL compiler, which the count above does not look at, so what the patch does to the screen could
  only be answered by looking at the screen: one image, one command line, an ordinary boot to the
  home screen, patched against unpatched.

  | | differ by 1–8 | differ by more than 8 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | patched against unpatched (4 min 33 s apart) | 10 835 | 2 508 |
  | unpatched against unpatched (8 min 36 s apart) | **13 738** | 2 286 |

  Both large patches in the pair were cut out and looked at rather than guessed from their
  coordinates: the Clock icon, whose hands had moved, and the status bar's clock. **No geometry
  moved and no colour changed.** The small residue sat in the bottom bands — search, dock, page
  dots, the transparent things with a blur behind them — exactly where a rounding change would show
  and at exactly the magnitude predicted, which is why the control mattered: two runs of the *same*
  binary, with a larger gap, differ by **more**. So the residue belongs to the run and not to the
  patch, and the honest statement is not "nothing changed" but **"any change is smaller than what
  the screen does to itself between launches"**.

  That is the useful form here, because the pair alone would have supported a confident wrong
  answer. The pixels were in the right place, of the right size, and told a coherent story about
  blur arithmetic; a measurement without a control answers a question nobody asked, and it cost one
  extra run to find out.

  The fix is one line, and unlike the `ir3_cmdline` bug this one is in a file upstream still
  carries, with reproduction down two independent paths — so it is the first thing in this work
  that can actually be reported. The change is now carried here as `tools/mesa/ir3-round-default.patch`, measured on the
  phone before and after down both paths.

  **The same branch covers `TYPE_F16`, and that half of it is still unanswered — this suite cannot
  ask it.** Ten declarations of the corpus return `half`, and every one of them was reported as
  agreeing on the Adreno while being tested on almost nothing: the pool gave them only values that
  overflow `f16`, so their expectations read `[0, inf, inf, inf]`, and the comparison skipped every
  infinity without counting it, leaving the zero to carry the verdict. They are set aside by name
  now (the table at the top of this document has their row), and the reason is the harness and not
  the hardware: `air_run` reads back through a 32-bit float target, so a half result is widened at
  once and NIR folds the conversion into a 32-bit one. The generated Adreno code for
  `air.convert.f.f16.u.i32` is four `cov.u32f32` and not one `cov.u32f16`.

  The pool has the value that would decide it. In `f16` integers are exact to 2048 and spaced by 2
  above, so **2051** is the discriminator — between 2050 and 2052 with an odd lower neighbour,
  where round-to-nearest-even gives 2052 and truncation gives 2050 — and 2049 is carried beside it
  as a midpoint where both rules agree, to show that a midpoint is not automatically a test.

  **`air_run` now has the 16-bit render target, and it is not enough.** Picking
  `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` for a `half` output was necessary and was only one of two causes; the other
  is in the generator, which packs every float-ish result into a `float4` with an explicit
  `fpext half ... to float` (`intrincheck.py`, `emit_buffered`). The widening therefore happens
  inside the shader and no choice of target can undo it.

  **Going further would mean guessing, so it stops here.** A half-returning fragment shader needs
  `!"air.render_target"` metadata naming the type, and the corpus is the authority on that
  vocabulary — the whole `air.*` meaning was read out of `AGXCompilerCore` rather than invented. Of
  the 456 modules, the render-target type names used are `float4` (275), `int4` (268), `uint4` (268)
  and `ushort` (2). **There is no `half4` among them.** The token does occur once somewhere in the
  shared cache, which makes the spelling plausible and attests nothing about this use of it.

  **And there is a second half to the f16 question that no harness can settle, because nothing is
  required.** One F16 path through that `create_cov` branch is `pack_half_2x16`, and
  `nir_lower_mediump.c` says of it, in Mesa's own words, "pack_half rounding is undefined". Where
  the specification requires nothing, a truncating `packHalf2x16` is a permitted choice and not a
  fault, so a measurement of it would be an observation about an implementation rather than an
  argument about conformance — and the patch's header now scopes its case to the destinations where
  a mode *is* required, integer to float, naming the `pack_half` path as a reviewer's question
  instead of leaving it to be found. A peer session had planned to reach the F16 branch through
  `packHalf2x16` for exactly that reason and dropped it on this, which is the better call: the
  experiment would have answered our internal question and been useless for the report.

  So the f16 question is two questions. For integer-to-half, round-to-nearest-even is required and
  this instrument cannot ask. For `pack_half`, nothing is required and there is nothing to ask.

  And the spelling is the smaller problem. A `half` render target appears in **no** module of the
  corpus, so a shader built around one would exercise a path through this frontend that Apple's own
  shaders never take and that nothing else here tests. A disagreement would then sit between two
  explanations — the GPU rounds wrong, or this frontend mishandles a construct it has never seen —
  and an ambiguous measurement is worth less than a stated gap. So the ten declarations stay set
  aside, and **the rounding fix is measured for 32-bit destinations only**, which is what the
  patch's header claims and no more.

  **Which rule it is, as against merely "not round-to-nearest", is settled by one value.**
  `0x01000003` is 2²⁴+3, half way between the representable 2²⁴+2 and 2²⁴+4; round-half-to-even and
  round-half-away-from-zero both give 2²⁴+4, and the GPU gives 2²⁴+2. That is truncation and nothing
  else. `0xFFFFFFFF` alone could never have shown this, and neither could `0x01000001`, the other
  midpoint, where truncation and round-to-even happen to agree — which is why the pool carries both
  and why one midpoint is not a test of a rounding rule. What remains unestablished is only whose
  job the compensation is, and that still needs the a6xx ISA documentation.

- **`air.fast_pow` returns NaN on the Adreno for a negative base, where softpipe returns the exact
  value.** `fast_pow(-0.5, 1)` is `-0.5` in C and on softpipe, and NaN on the phone. This is
  recorded rather than reported as a bug: Metal's `fast::` functions, like OpenCL's `native_`
  ones, are explicitly undefined outside a restricted domain, and a negative base is outside it.
  It is worth naming because it sits inside the "approximate, nothing concluded" bucket, which is
  exactly where a real difference can hide behind a reasonable-looking ulp figure — the line says
  "worst inf ulp", and an inf ulp is not a rounding difference. Any corpus shader that calls
  `fast_pow` with a base that can go negative will behave differently on this phone than in any
  test on this machine.
- **The atomics compute the right thing and the barrier waits; whether the atomics are *atomic*
  is still open.** `tools/air/atomiccheck.py` dispatches two kernels written for the purpose
  (section 4, item 5) and all eight operations the corpus uses agree — five on device memory
  (`add.s`, `load`, `max.s`, `min.s`, `store`), three on threadgroup memory (`add.u`, `load`,
  `store`) across two `air.wg.barrier`s. Among them a signed minimum taken across negative
  values, which is where an unsigned one passes unnoticed. The barrier is genuinely under test:
  softpipe advances its invocations in groups of four, so making the barrier a no-op leaves every
  thread seeing 4 of 16 increments, and the check says exactly that. **Atomicity is not under
  test**, because softpipe applies a group's atomic lane by lane and so cannot lose an update
  however the lowering is written. That needs the phone. Two things are settled without running
  anything: every atomic in the corpus asks for `memory_order_relaxed`, and a stronger order is
  now refused by name instead of ignored, which is what the lowering used to do.
- **All 119 declarations are now accounted for**, which is new as of tonight and is a weaker
  claim than "all checked" — the distinction matters and an earlier draft of this paragraph, and
  the commit message of `bbf6c3c`, ran the two together:

  | | of 119 |
  | --- | --- |
  | verified: the answer was compared with one computed elsewhere and agreed | 94 |
  | measured, no verdict: approximate arithmetic, against this machine's libm | 7 |
  | has a case, which softpipe cannot run: a 16-bit result or operand | 7 |
  | has no case, for a reason given in section 4 item 6: multisample, depth, write | 11 |

  The 94 are 71 arithmetic operations, 10 atomics and the barrier, and 13 texture operations. The
  derivatives and the simd reductions are in none of these rows because **no module of the corpus
  calls them**: unexercised code, not untested behaviour, and saying "unverified" of them would
  overstate what is at stake.
- **The weakest of the three groups is the textures**, and the gap is not in the fetch — which is
  now checked at the corners as well as the middle, and for integer and unsigned textures too —
  but in everything Metal's sampler state decides. The 64-bit `constexpr sampler` word is still
  not decoded (section 3.3) and every coordinate checked is a texel centre or a clean footprint
  corner, where nearest filtering has no weights to round and clamping has no arithmetic.
  The six texture shaders that drew on the Adreno took their sampler from the API too, so what
  they are evidence about is binding, descriptors and ir3's texture instructions — exactly what
  they were built to be — and silence about everything Metal's sampler state decides. **Ten**
  modules of the corpus declare a `constexpr sampler`, carrying three distinct state words, all
  ten in `PortraitFilters.cifilter/default.metallib`; everywhere else the API supplies it. This
  paragraph said "two" for a while, while the mapping table in section 7 said ten: two numbers for
  one fact in one file, and the disagreement was enough to settle it without any new evidence.
  Where the "two" came from is not established. What is worth recording is how the ten were
  counted, because the obvious way does not work: a plain `grep` for `__air_sampler_state` over
  the 456 modules finds **none**, since bitcode is bit-packed and a name matches only when it
  happens to land on byte boundaries. The count above is from `llvm-dis` output, module by
  module.
- **A function of the module that takes a texture: done, and the diagnosis was the work.** All
  four such entry points translate — three with this fix, the fourth once the shuffle mask it also
  stopped on was decoded. The fix is a split of `translate_globals`, and arriving at it took two
  reverts and three failed guesses, which is the part worth keeping.

  A texture is not a value in this frontend: it is resolved at translation time into a binding,
  and `tex_handle` wants an `AIR_VAL_PTR` rather than an SSA def. So a pointer-class argument is
  bound from the caller's own resolution and takes no NIR parameter, which specialises the callee
  to its call site — free here, since each of the four has exactly one. That much worked at once.

  What did not was everything after. The callee needs the module's globals, and copying the entry
  point's values into it crashed three of the four in `nir_lower_goto_ifs` → `nir_repair_ssa` →
  `nir_block_is_unreachable`. **Two hypotheses died with evidence before the right one arrived**:
  the callee has no unreachable block at all, and `nir_validate_shader` — the test a peer session
  proposed for it — fails identically on `fbs_slice_trilinear`, which translates perfectly, so
  its complaint about block indices in an unstructured impl was true and about something else.
  The peer's reading of the assertion was right and their route was not: it asks *the block's own*
  impl for dominance metadata, so a use in another function's block asks the wrong function — but
  the cross-function value arrived through the globals, not through an argument. A guard refusing
  a pointer argument with a byte offset was evaluated 26 times over the corpus and never fired, so
  arguments are not the carrier; the count is the evidence, because a silent guard and an
  unreachable guard look the same.

  So `translate_globals` is now two. `plan_globals` decides what each global is and runs **once**,
  because it appends inline samplers to `info->resources` and lays out shared and scratch memory.
  `materialise_globals` builds the values and runs **per function**, because a byte offset is an
  `nir_def` and a def belongs to the impl that made it. Module-level constants needed neither:
  `air_get` already materialises one in whichever builder asks, which was checked rather than
  assumed.

- **Of Apple's own 47 kernels, all 47 are dispatched on the Adreno and none crash.**
  `tools/air/kernelcheck.py` prints where each one stops, as a table whose rows are checked
  against the total before it is printed:

  | | on softpipe | **on the Adreno** |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | dispatched and read back | 6 | **47** |
  | softpipe's `nir_to_tgsi`: scratch and intrinsics it lacks | 41 | — |
  | a shuffle mask our reader would not decode (ours, now fixed) | 0 | 0 |
