the tarball and the patch applies — but it is not a route that survives a Mesa upgrade, and it
could never have been upstreamed. `air_run` does not share the problem: it uses the ordinary
Gallium interface (`screen->context_create`, `create_fs_state`, `draw_vbo`), which is what the
drivers and the port's own Mesa are built on. The durable way to get the `ir3` number after an
upgrade is `air_run` against a freedreno screen, which means on the phone, because freedreno
needs a real `msm` device and this machine has none.

A working copy also needs the phone's own firmware for the GPU to start at all: `fw-gpu/`
(`a660_gmu.bin`, `a660_sqe.fw`, the `a660_zap.*` pieces), which is not in the repository and which
`tools/new-workspace.sh` does not copy. Without it the kernel says so plainly and the system falls
back to software, so a run that looks fine can be a run on no GPU.

Needed on this machine: meson, ninja, bison, flex, python3 with venv, and LLVM's `llvm-as` /
`llvm-dis` for the reader check (22.1.8 here). The host build also patches Mesa 25.0's
`src/c11/threads.h`, because glibc 2.43 and later declare C11's `once_flag` and `call_once` in
`<stdlib.h>` and Mesa defines them again; the Darwin cross build has its own libc and does not.

## 7. What this decides for the runtime (2) and the kernel ABI (3)

**Read this as intent, not as design.** The runtime and the kernel ABI do not exist; nothing below
has been built against, and none of it is a measurement. What each item *is* is the consequence
that this frontend's choices force on whoever writes those parts — so an item can be wrong in two
ways: the consequence may be mis-stated, or the frontend may have changed since. Where the
frontend already does its half, the item says so; where it does not, the item is a promise nobody
has kept yet. The one thing here that has been exercised at all is item 2's buffer binding, and
only through `air_run`, which is not a Metal runtime and binds by the same indices the frontend
reports.


1. **Compilation happens at pipeline creation, not at `newLibraryWithData:`.** Function constants
   (`newFunctionWithName:constantValues:`), vertex/fragment varying linking and visible-function
   linking are only known then. The library step can translate eagerly and cache NIR; the ir3
   step cannot run before the pipeline. (On real Darwin the compile also leaves the process, for
   `MTLCompilerService`; whether this runtime does the same is a decision for (2), and NIR
   serialization — `nir_serialize` — makes either possible.)
2. **Buffers are bound per stage by index, as UBOs (constant) and SSBOs (device).**
   *(The frontend's half is done: it emits `load_ubo`/`load_ssbo` at Metal's own index and reports
   the kind per index in `air_shader_info`. `air_run` binds by those indices and the results come
   back right, which is the only thing that has tested this.)*
   `setVertexBuffer:offset:atIndex:` maps to the UBO or SSBO slot `index` of that stage; the
   frontend reports which kind each index is. Adreno's UBO and SSBO base addresses have alignment
   rules Metal's offsets do not (Metal allows 4-byte offsets for constant buffers); the runtime
   must bind an aligned base and the frontend will take the remainder from a driver uniform when
   that becomes necessary. Argument buffers (pointers in memory) will need GPU virtual addresses
   of buffers stable across submissions — a requirement on (3) — and 64-bit global access.
3. **One Metal texture index may be a sampler view or an image** depending on the shader's access
   qualifier; the frontend reports which, the runtime binds accordingly.
4. **Threadgroup memory passed as an argument is sized at dispatch**
   (`setThreadgroupMemoryLength:atIndex:`): the translator addresses it from base offsets in a
   driver uniform and Gallium's `variable_shared_mem` carries the total (as rusticl does for
   OpenCL `__local` arguments). The threadgroup size is a dispatch argument too
   (`dispatchThreadgroups:threadsPerThreadgroup:`), so `workgroup_size` is not fixed in NIR.
5. **Vertex outputs and fragment inputs match by name** (`"generated(8texcoordDv2_f)"`, `user(...)`),
   not by location: a pipeline-time link step assigns the same `VARYING_SLOT_VAR*` to the same
   name on both sides. Visible functions (CoreImage's 135 stitchable kernels are all of this
   kind) are linked into the calling shader by name with `nir_link_shader_functions`.
6. *(Half done: the frontend sets `origin_upper_left` on the fragment shader. `clip_halfz` is
   rasterizer state and nothing sets it — `air_run` never needed it, because its quad is already
   in clip space.)* **Clip space and the framebuffer are Metal's:** NDC depth is [0, 1] (`clip_halfz`), the
   framebuffer origin is the top-left; the frontend emits no flips, the runtime's viewport and
   rasterizer state must say this.
7. **Inline samplers** (`constexpr sampler` in the source, `!air.sampler_states`) are created by
   the runtime and bound after the API's samplers. *(Half done, and the half that is missing is
   the important one: the frontend assigns the index and passes the state word through, but it
   does **not** decode it — section 3.3. The earlier wording here said "from the state the
   frontend decodes", which was never true.)*

```

`docs/boot-args.md`:

```md
# Boot-arguments

Made by `tools/boot-args.py --markdown`; CI fails if it is out of date with the source (`tools/boot-args.py --check`).

Every argument that the kernel, the loader or user space of this port reads, and which file reads it. **350 arguments**: 279 read by the kernel, 14 by the loader, 68 by user space (one is read in more than one place).

This is a catalogue of what exists and who reads it, not a manual. What an argument means is in the head of the file that reads it. The stable switches have a symbol in the configuration (`tools/hakios-config.py help SYMBOL`, `docs/configs.md`); the rest are the knobs of bring-up (a driver's steps, pauses, traces, test modes) and can change with the driver. Any of them can be given in a configuration with `CONFIG_BOOTARGS="name=value ..."`, which checks that each name is in this list. What the arguments of the two Metal paths do: [Metal on the Adreno](reference/metal.md#boot-arguments).

Layers: **K** the kernel, **L** the loader, **U** user space (through `sysctl kern.bootargs`).

`docs/cellular.md`:

```md
# Cellular

Where the modem stands (October 2026). The detailed, step-by-step diary in Russian is
`docs/ru/cellular.md`.

## What works

- The modem (the Hexagon MPSS) boots from XNU: its firmware goes through TrustZone, the shared
  memory, SMP2P, GLINK and QRTR come up, and it announces about 88 QMI services.
- Its file systems (modemst1, modemst2, fsc, fsg) are served from the UFS partitions over RMTFS,
  read-only: writes stay in kernel memory for the session, the phone's flash is never touched.
- TFTP over QRTR and the service registry (what Android's tqftpserv and pd-mapper do) are ours.
- The IPA packet engine runs: firmware through TrustZone, its clock through RPMh, both of its SMMU
  streams through a translation context of ours (the hypervisor takes one match register per
  stream), the registers Android programs, the modem's filter-table item in shared memory, and the
  SMP2P entry `ipa` the modem's driver waits for. The INIT_DRIVER handshake goes through.
- The modem goes online and stays up. The SIM is found (physical slot 2 on the first phone),
  logical slot 1 is pointed at it, the provisioning session is bound to its USIM, and NAS reads
  the signal (-70 to -87 dBm on UMTS).
- SpringBoard's status bar: the signal item is hooked (`userland/src/inject_sb.c`) and shows the
  kernel's bars (`sysctl kern.hakios.cellular_bars`) once the modem is registered.

- The data session: once NAS reports registration, the kernel binds its QMI WDS client to QMAP
  mux 1 of the embedded port (the IPA), sets the port's data format (WDA: raw IP in QMAP, no
  checksum offload), starts an IPv4 session on the SIM's default profile and reads its settings
  (address, gateway, DNS, MTU: `sysctl kern.hakios.cellular_ip`, `_gateway`, `_dns`, `_mtu`,
  `_data`).

## The data path (2.0)

Packets go through the IPA, the SoC's packet engine, the way Linux's `drivers/net/ipa` does it
for IPA 4.11; everything is in `drivers/modem/hakios.ipa.c` and `hakios.cell.c`.

- Before the modem starts, the kernel sets up this processor's side of the IPA: four GSI
  channels with their event rings (the command channel 5, the LAN receive channel 14, the modem
  transmit channel 2 and the modem receive channel 7), the matching endpoints (7, 9, 2, 16:
  QMAP headers, deaggregation on the way out, aggregation up to 12 KB or 500 us on the way in),
  and the IPA's filter, route and header tables through immediate commands, so that the modem
  finds valid tables and adds its own rules to them.
- The rings are polled by the interface's thread; no interrupt is taken from the GSI.
- The modem's packets are an Ethernet-looking interface, `en1`, with a made-up router behind it.
  The kernel answers ARP for every address and DHCP with the session's address, a /24 around it,
  the router and the DNS servers, so Darwin's configd configures `en1` as it would a USB Ethernet
  adapter and routes through it. IPv6 is not carried.
- The modem is told about this side the way ModemManager does for a phone behind the IPA
  (`net_driver == "ipa"`): **DPM Open Port** (Data Port Mapper) names the embedded port's IPA
  endpoints (the modem receives on our TX endpoint 2 and sends on our RX endpoint 16), then **WDA
  Set Data Format** sets raw IP in QMAP on it. Only then do the WDS steps run: **Bind Mux Data
  Port** (mux 1), **Set IP Family** (IPv4), **Start Network Interface** (with the APN) once NAS is
  registered, retried while the packet domain is still attaching. Skipping the DPM step was why
  WDA and the session answered InvalidOperation and the bind Internal (cycles 38-41): the modem
  had no embedded port to bind to.
- The rings are polled by the interface's thread; no interrupt is taken from the GSI.
- The modem's packets are an Ethernet-looking interface, `en1`, with a made-up router behind it.
  The kernel answers ARP for every address and DHCP with the session's address, a /24 around it,
  the router and the DNS servers, so Darwin's configd configures `en1` as it would a USB Ethernet
  adapter and routes through it. IPv6 is not carried.
- `modem_ipa_data_off=1` leaves all of this out; `modem_dpm_off=1` / `modem_wda_off=1` skip those
  steps; `modem_ipa_data_trace=1` logs every packet.

## Another phone: the SoC addresses

The modem and IPA drivers carry the POCO X5 Pro's register and memory addresses as defaults and
take any that differ from boot-args `soc_*` (`hakios.mpss.c` `soc_override()`, `hakios.ipa.c`).
`tools/soc-args.py` reads a phone's own device tree (`devices/<name>/pull-soc.sh` pulls
`/sys/firmware/fdt` over adb) and prints the `soc_*` it needs; the run scripts append
`devices/<name>/soc.args`. For the first phone every generated value equals the default, so it
needs no arguments.

## Not yet

- Registration reaches full LTE service, but the data session is still refused until the packet
  domain attaches; the DPM/WDA/bind order above is the current attempt, untested on hardware since
  the phone went off USB.
- Calls, SMS, IPv6.

## How to run it

```sh
XL_SB_DELAY=8 tools/modem-cycle.sh "modem=1 modem_again=1 modem_buffer=0xa8000000" 600
```

`modem_step=N` runs the bring-up step by step and returns to the loader with the log;
`modem=1` brings the modem up beside the system. Everything is in
`drivers/modem/hakios.mpss.c` (the modem), `hakios.nas.c` (NAS), `hakios.qmi.c` (QMI).

## Kernel arguments

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `modem=1` | the modem beside the system, on a thread of its own |
| `modem_step=N` | steps 1..N, then back to the loader (`modem_return=1`) |
| `modem_again=1` | start it although a kernel before this one left it shut down |
| `modem_buffer=0xa8000000` | the RMTFS buffer (below 4 GB) |
| `modem_nas_wait=S` | how long step 11 waits for registration |
| `modem_online=0` | do not put the modem online |
| `modem_ipa=3` (default) | the SMP2P entry `ipa`: valid, clock on |
| `modem_sim_switch_off=1` | do not point logical slot 1 at the slot with the ready card |
| `modem_sim_probe_off=1` | no SIM and network-selection queries |
| `modem_data_off=1` | no data session at all |
| `modem_dpm_off=1` / `modem_wda_off=1` | skip the DPM / WDA step |
| `modem_data_nobind=1` | the session without binding the client to the mux |
| `modem_apn=NAME` | the session to that APN instead of the SIM's default profile |
| `modem_ipa_data_off=1` | no IPA data path for this processor, no `en1` |
| `modem_ipa_data_trace=1` | a log line per packet, command and DHCP/ARP answer |

```

# HakiOS next to the other XNU-on-a-phone projects

There are other projects that put Apple's open-source XNU on hardware that is not Apple's. This page says, as plainly
as it can, where this one is different. It is written from their public pages as read on 2026-11-04 (for UniXNU also its
documentation, at its commit `c1ecc5b`); they change, so read theirs, and tell us if a line here is out of date or wrong
(an issue is enough). Where the table says something about **our** runtime state, it is what
[the documentation's front page](index.md#what-works) claims; the things this repository has *tested* are marked.

| | [ios-sweet](https://github.com/dipa-studio/ios-sweet) | [UniXNU](https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU) | [Bergamota](https://github.com/ry-diffusion/bergamota) | HakiOS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | one phone, bring-up of Darwin userland 16 | a general UEFI environment for Darwin/macOS on ARM64, in the manner of OpenCore: shared build tools, OS profiles, a component catalog, SoC and device repositories | one phone, bring-up of Darwin userland 18 (a fork of ios-sweet) | a Darwin kernel port with its own loader and driver set, and a Linux-style configuration system |
| Hardware | Redmi Note 10 Pro (SM7150) | Xiaomi Pad 6S Pro (SM8550) as the reference; 234 device entries in its `devices.toml`, many of them other people's ports (how far each goes: its own pages) | Poco F1 (SDM845) | POCO X5 Pro 5G (SM7325), the Infinix Hot 20 (MT6768, [a port of its own](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-mt6768)), and a generator for a new device from its own device tree |
| Kernel | Apple's open xnu-8796 | by OS profile: xnu-10063.141.1 for an arm64 profile; an arm64e series for newer ones | xnu-11215 ("Heartwood") | Apple's open xnu-8796.121.2 |
| Boot | `fastboot boot` of a shim; HFS+ root in `userdata` | UEFI | its own bootloader from `boot` | `fastboot boot` (RAM only); U-Boot in `boot_a` beside Android ([installing](dual-boot.md)); or a UEFI loader that reads its payload from the volume it was started from (tested in QEMU; not yet on a phone) |
| GPU | none: drawn by the CPU, 20 to 30 frames a second by its page | Metal on Vulkan on the Adreno 740: [AdrenoMetal](https://github.com/UniXNU/AdrenoMetal), metal2vulkan, Turnip, its own kernel driver | none yet: drawn by the CPU; the Adreno 630 is in progress | Adreno 642L: OpenGL ES through Mesa by default; Metal for the window server, by a direct path and by a port of UniXNU's ([numbers](reference/metal-measurements.md): 100 to 104 frames a second at best in page swipes, not 120) |
| Licence of its code | MIT | BSD-2-Clause-Patent | none stated on the page | MIT; kernel changes APSL 2.0 |
| Says it ships Apple binaries | no | not stated | no | no, and CI fails if a binary of a kind that cannot be ours is added |

## What this project does that the others' pages do not describe

These are things that exist in this repository and that a reader can check:

- **A configuration system, like Linux's.** `configs/defconfig`, `configs/<device>_defconfig`, fragments, a `.config`,
  `savedefconfig`, and dependency and length checks ([configs.md](configs.md)). A kernel that is configured by its
  command line gets a file format for it, with the typo caught before the boot rather than after.
- **A version string that says what it is built from**, shown by the loader and by `sysctl kern.hakios.version`
  ([versioning.md](versioning.md)).
- **A catalogue of every boot-argument**, made from the source by a scanner, checked in CI, so the list cannot go
  stale ([boot-args.md](boot-args.md), 300+ arguments).
- **An open configuration that needs nothing of Apple's and nothing of the phone's**: `make qemu-open` boots the kernel
  with its own userland and prints the banner, `kern.hakios.version` and a hello. This is the part anybody can
  contribute to without touching an IPSW or a firmware file. (Tested.)
- **A provenance guard** (`tools/provenance-check.py`, in CI): it refuses a binary that is not explained, a file of
  a kind the project promises never to carry, and a writer to the phone's flash that is not declared. The answer to
  "what exactly does this write to my phone?" is a file you can read ([legal-review.md](legal-review.md),
  [LEGAL.md](../LEGAL.md)).
- **Its own loader, its own drivers**: GPU (Mesa and Metal over a Darwin driver), Wi-Fi, audio, haptics, cameras, touch, storage,
  modem bring-up. [driver-review/](driver-review/README.md) says what each is, and what has and has not been verified.

## What the others have that this one does not

- ios-sweet and Bergamota are small enough to read in an afternoon, and Bergamota targets a newer Darwin (18) with its
  own tool for the arm64e/pointer-authentication gap. HakiOS targets the Darwin userland 16.5 generation, whose userland the
  open xnu-8796 matches.
- UniXNU is a shared UEFI layer that many devices use, with a catalog of components and a page per driver. HakiOS's loader is one
  device family's, so far.
- UniXNU had Metal on Vulkan first, and it is theirs: HakiOS's second Metal path is AdrenoMetal's frontend and metal2vulkan, built by
  `tools/mk-m2v.sh` with patches for an older system. Their kernel driver for the Adreno 740 does ring scheduling and preemption by its
  documentation, which HakiOS's does not. Their Adreno 740 is another GPU and their system a newer one, so our numbers say nothing
  about how theirs runs.
- UniXNU has OS profiles for several systems, arm64e among them. HakiOS targets the Darwin 16.5 generation alone.
- Bergamota ships a macOS control app. HakiOS has `xl` and `make`, which are command lines.

## What nobody here can do

Run an Apple account, activation, iMessage or the other Apple services: no project here can, and ours does not try
(see [LEGAL.md](../LEGAL.md)). None of the four is an iPhone to Apple's servers, and none should pretend to be.

## What "different" does not mean

It does not mean better on a given day. The things in the first section are about how the project is built and checked,
not about how many apps open. If you want to see which of these the phone has actually passed, read
[the status table](index.md#what-works) and `docs/port-pkg110.md`, and run it yourself.

`docs/concepts/architecture.md`:

```md
# Architecture

HakiOS is three programs of its own between a phone's firmware and a user space: a UEFI application that loads the kernel, the
kernel (Apple's XNU with this port), and the drivers inside it. Everything else is either the phone's (its UEFI, its firmware) or
yours (the user space you lay out).

## A boot, from the button to the home screen

```
 Android's fastboot        HakiOS UEFI              xnuloader              XNU + HakiOS             launchd       user space
 (the phone's own)   -->   (Mu-Silicium with   -->  (loader.efi,     -->   (xnu/, drivers/)   -->            -->   (yours: Darwin userland 16.5,
  fastboot boot             HakiOS's changes,        xnuloader/)            drivers started                       or userland/hello)
                            uefi/ + the device's)    reads the payload      by boot-arguments
```

| Step | What happens | Where it is |
|---|---|---|
| 1. into RAM | Android's fastboot receives a boot image and runs it; nothing is flashed | `./xl enter` |
| 2. UEFI | HakiOS's UEFI (Mu-Silicium with HakiOS's changes and banner, and the phone's platform) starts on the SoC, shows the HakiOS logo, offers the framebuffer and storage, and starts the loader from the image | `uefi/`, `devices/<name>/uefi/` |
| 3. the loader | `xnuloader` reads the payload (the kernel, the command line, `kernel.ver`), lays out memory and the device tree the kernel expects, keeps a service for the storage, starts the kernel; at the end of a run it takes control back | `xnuloader/` |
| 4. the kernel | XNU with this port: Apple's patched files (`xnu/hakios.patch`), new ones (`xnu/files/`), the drivers (`drivers/`) | [Building](../getting-started/building.md) |
| 5. the drivers | each one does nothing until its boot-argument asks; those the configuration left out are not in the kernel at all | [Drivers in the configuration](../drivers-config.md) |
| 6. user space | launchd starts what the system image holds: Darwin 16.5's (layer 2, yours), or `userland/hello` for the open kernel | `userland/` |

## How a configuration becomes a kernel and a command line

```
 configs/common_defconfig                 (common)
 devices/redwood/soc/configs/sc7280.config  (SoC)      make redwood_defconfig
 devices/redwood/configs/redwood.config      (device)   ------------------------->  .config
                                                                                    |
               CONFIG_HAKIOS_*  ->  tools/hakios-config.py kernel  ->  XNU's options (config/MASTER.hakios, conf/files)  ->  make kernel
               every other CONFIG_*  ->  tools/hakios-config.py args  ->  the kernel's boot-arguments  ->  make phone, ./xl run
```

Two kinds of symbol: `CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>` decides whether a driver is compiled in, through XNU's own option mechanism; every other
`CONFIG_` symbol is a boot-argument, because XNU takes its knobs from the command line. One `.config` gives both.
[Configuration](../configs.md) and [Drivers in the configuration](../drivers-config.md) have the detail.

## Common, SoC, device

What is true of every device is the common repository's; what is true of a SoC family, the SoC's; what is true of one device, that
device's. A device's defconfig is three lines: the common kernel, its SoC's fragment, its own.
[How the repositories fit](../porting/repositories.md).

| Layer | Has | Example |
|---|---|---|
| common | the kernel port, every driver, the loader, user space, the tools, the documentation | this repository |
| SoC | the SoC's facts (cores, addresses that are the family's), its drivers; carried by each device that has the SoC | `devices/redwood/soc` |
| device | its defconfig, its status, its UEFI platform, its firmware script, drivers of its own | `devices/redwood` |
| UEFI | Mu-Silicium with HakiOS's boot path, banner and name | `uefi` ([its README](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-uefi/blob/main/README.md)) |

## What is written to the phone

| What | When | Where |
|---|---|---|
| the loader's log, a few KB | at the end of every run | the `logdump` partition |
| `/private/var` | only with `ufs_write=1 var_store=1` | the partition `darwin`, which you create yourself (`tools/userdata-carve.py` prints the commands; it changes nothing) |
| anything else | never | the loader refuses every other write; `tools/provenance.allow` lists each piece of code that can write, and why |

[LEGAL.md](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-xnu-kernel/blob/main/LEGAL.md) has the same, with what is and is not distributed.

## Where the code is

| Directory | What |
|---|---|
| `xnu/` | the kernel: `hakios.patch` (Apple's files, changed), `files/` (new files), `apply.sh`, `export.sh` |
| `drivers/<subsystem>/` | the drivers, by subsystem, each with its `conf` ([reference](../reference/drivers.md)) |
| `xnuloader/` | the boot loader (a UEFI application, no EDK2) |
| `userland/` | programs and libraries of our own (`src/`), the Metal plug-in, the image build, launchd jobs |
| `configs/` | the common kernel's configuration and the generic fragments |
| `devices/` | the device repositories (each with its SoC's layer in `soc/`), and `devices/manifest.conf` |
| `sysimage/` | scripts that fetch and unpack the OS files from the IPSW (none of the files) |
| `tools/` | configuration, devices, checks, APFS, firmware, QMI, the run scripts |
| `qemu/` | running in QEMU |
| `prebuilt/` | the kernel, loader and libraries built from this source |

`docs/configs.md`:

```md
# Configurations: the common kernel, a SoC, a phone

A Linux kernel is configured with a `.config` made from a defconfig, and an Android kernel is put together from layers: the
common kernel's `gki_defconfig`, the SoC vendor's fragment, the device's. This kernel does the same, with one difference that
is most of the design: **most of its options are not compiled in.** XNU takes them from the boot-arguments, so most of a
configuration here is `CONFIG_*` symbols that `tools/hakios-config.py` turns into the kernel's command line. The exception is
the drivers themselves: `CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>` decides whether a driver is compiled into the kernel at all, through XNU's own
`options` and `conf/files` ([drivers-config.md](drivers-config.md)), so that a device's defconfig builds the drivers that phone has.

```
configs/defconfig             what every configuration starts from: the OPEN one (nothing of a phone's own, one core)
configs/common_defconfig      THE COMMON KERNEL: every setting there is, each with what it does (about 1000 lines)
configs/sc7280.config         the Qualcomm SC7280 family (SM7325, QCM6490): eight cores, the sensors, the chip's identity
configs/redwood.config        the POCO X5 Pro 5G: its vibration motor, where its modem's buffer is
configs/redwood_defconfig     a phone: #include common_defconfig, sc7280.config, redwood.config (three lines)
configs/qemu_defconfig        QEMU's virt machine: the phone's drivers left out of the kernel (CONFIG_HAKIOS_*)
configs/open.config           fragment: the open profile (CONFIG_FIRMWARE="none")
configs/virt.config           fragment: QEMU's virt machine (virtio network)
configs/trace.config          fragment: log a line for each of the first frames on the network interfaces
configs/persist.config        fragment: keep /private/var across reboots (THIS WRITES TO THE PHONE, partition `darwin`)
configs/symbols.tsv           the symbols that are made from the source (see below); do not edit
```

The common kernel does not say which phone it is for. A phone is the common kernel plus the facts of its SoC plus its own, which
is how Android builds a device's kernel; a new device adds a fragment and a three-line defconfig, not a new copy of everything.

## Use

```bash
make redwood_defconfig                  # .config = defconfig + common_defconfig + sc7280.config + redwood.config
make redwood_defconfig FRAGMENTS=trace  # ... and a fragment on top
make common_defconfig                   # the common kernel alone, for a phone that has no fragments yet
make virt.config                        # lay a fragment over the .config there is
make config                             # show it: symbols, the kernel's arguments, the firmware it wants
make savedefconfig                      # the .config as a minimal defconfig (what differs from configs/defconfig)
make phone                              # with a .config, ITS arguments are the kernel's
```

The same without make: `tools/hakios-config.py defconfig|merge|args|check|show|needs|savedefconfig|list|listing|complete|help`.
`tools/hakios-config.py help GPU` says what a symbol means, what it needs and what it requires. `make doctor` checks the host.

## What a symbol is

`CONFIG_HAKIOS_GOODIX=y` is not an argument: it builds the touch driver into the kernel ([drivers-config.md](drivers-config.md)).
Every other symbol is one: `CONFIG_GPU=y` is the argument `gpu=1`; `CONFIG_CPUS=8` is `cpus=8`; `CONFIG_MODEM_BUFFER=0xa8000000` is
`modem_buffer=0xa8000000`. A symbol that is `# CONFIG_X is not set` is left out, and the kernel's own default applies.
Three symbols are facts about the build, not arguments: `CONFIG_DEVICE`, `CONFIG_SOC` (it goes into the kernel's version
string, see [versioning.md](versioning.md)) and `CONFIG_FIRMWARE`.

There are two kinds of symbol, and the difference is honest:

- **The stable switches** are written by hand in the `SYMBOLS` table at the top of `tools/hakios-config.py`: they have a
  meaning, a type, a range, a firmware they need, a symbol they require (`CONFIG_SOUND` requires `CONFIG_ADSP`). About thirty.
- **The rest** are made from the source. Every argument that the kernel, the loader or user space reads
  ([boot-args.md](boot-args.md)) gets a symbol, except the few that the loader and the runner set themselves (`epoch`, the time
  of the run ...). They are typed as "a switch (`y` is 1), a number as written, or a quoted text", and the one-line meaning is
  taken from the source where the file that reads the argument has a documentation line for it; where it has none, the line
  says which file reads it and nothing more. They are `configs/symbols.tsv`, made by `tools/boot-args.py --symbols`, and CI fails
  when a driver adds an argument and the file is not made again. Most of these are the knobs of bring-up (a driver's steps and
  pauses, traces, test modes); they are here so that a run is written down in one file with typos refused, not because each one
  is a feature.

## `common_defconfig`: every setting, documented

Linux's defconfigs list only what differs from the defaults. This one lists **every** symbol, set or `# CONFIG_X is not set`,
each under a comment that says what it does, in groups (GPU and display, Wi-Fi, Cellular, Storage ...). That is why it is a
thousand lines long, and why a reader of one file can see every setting the kernel has. It is made, not written:

```bash
tools/hakios-config.py listing common -o configs/common_defconfig    # after changing a value or adding a driver
tools/hakios-config.py complete common                               # it must name every symbol (CI runs this, in the tests)
```

Change a value by editing the line and running `listing common -o configs/common_defconfig` again: the file reads back the
same. Not `listing common > configs/common_defconfig`: the shell empties the file before the tool reads it, and what is written is
then `configs/defconfig` alone. That is how `common_defconfig` once lost the values of the phone line (the GPU, Wi-Fi, audio and
modem switches, `CONFIG_FIRMWARE="device"`), and why `-o` exists.

## `#include`: putting a device together

A line `#include NAME` in a defconfig or fragment (a comment to any other reader) stands for `configs/NAME`, `NAME_defconfig` or
`NAME.config`, laid first; the including file wins over what it includes; a loop is an error. This is the whole of
`redwood_defconfig`. The order for `make redwood_defconfig` is `defconfig` (open, one core), then the common kernel, then the
SoC, then the phone, then the fragments you named.

## What is checked, and why

- **Types and ranges.** A bool is `y` or not set, a hex number starts with `0x`, `CONFIG_CPUS` is 1 to 8, `CONFIG_THERMAL_STOP`
  is 0 to 160. A typo in a name gets a suggestion (`no symbol CONFIG_GPUU (did you mean CONFIG_GPU?)`).
- **Dependencies.** `CONFIG_VAR_STORE` requires `CONFIG_UFS_WRITE`, which requires `CONFIG_UFS=2`; `CONFIG_SOUND` requires
  `CONFIG_ADSP`; `CONFIG_THERMAL_STOP` requires `CONFIG_THERMAL`; the modem requires the storage service.
- **Firmware.** `CONFIG_FIRMWARE="none"` is the open profile: *nothing of the phone's own is loaded.* The check refuses
  a configuration that says `none` and still asks for the GPU, Wi-Fi, audio, haptics, cameras or the modem, because each
  of those uses firmware pulled from the owner's own phone (`fw-*/`, never in this repository).
- **The command line fits.** The kernel's boot line holds 607 characters, and a longer one loses its tail without an
  error. The check counts the arguments, adds what a run adds itself (about 260) and refuses what cannot fit.

## `CONFIG_BOOTARGS`: Linux's `CONFIG_CMDLINE`

For an argument that has no symbol of its own, or a value the symbols cannot say: `CONFIG_BOOTARGS="fb_beat=2 loader_return_after=5"`. It is not an
escape from the checks. Every name must be one the source reads ([boot-args.md](boot-args.md)), so `fb_beet=2` is an error with a
suggestion rather than a silent no-op; an argument that a symbol already sets (`cpus=8`) is refused with the name of the symbol; a
word is `name=value` with no space, quote or backslash in it; and the words count towards the 607 characters.

## What is the same as Linux, and what is not

| | Linux / Android | here |
|---|---|---|
| the common kernel | `gki_defconfig` | `common_defconfig` |
| a SoC, a device | vendor and device fragments, `build.config` | `sc7280.config`, `redwood.config`, `#include` |
| a fragment | `kernel/configs/*.config`, `merge_config.sh` | `configs/*.config`, `make NAME.config` |
| the result | `.config`, compiled in | `.config`: the drivers compiled in (`CONFIG_HAKIOS_*`), the rest becomes the boot-arguments |
| a driver's options | `Kconfig` + `obj-$(CONFIG_X) += x.o` | `drivers/<subsystem>/conf`, XNU's `options` and `optional` in `conf/files` |
| a minimal config | `make savedefconfig` | `make savedefconfig` |
| a command line baked in | `CONFIG_CMDLINE` | `CONFIG_BOOTARGS` (names checked) |
| an option that needs a blob | `CONFIG_EXTRA_FIRMWARE` | `CONFIG_FIRMWARE="device"` / `"none"`, and `needs` |
| the version | `uname -r` | `kern.hakios.version`, `kernel.ver=` |
| how many options | thousands, in Kconfig | about 310, one for each argument the source reads |

The last row is the honest one. This is not Kconfig and has no thousand options: apart from which drivers it has, the kernel is not
built from its options. The number of symbols is the number of arguments the code reads, plus one for each driver.

## A new device

`tools/new-device.py` makes `devices/<name>/` from a phone's own device tree. Its configuration is a fragment and a defconfig of a few
lines: `configs/<name>.config` with what is true of that phone only, and `configs/<name>_defconfig` that includes the common kernel, the
SoC's fragment and that one, and nothing more until the phone has been shown to do it. The fragment is also where the phone leaves out
the drivers of hardware it does not have or that has not been ported to it (`# CONFIG_HAKIOS_GOODIX is not set`: see
[drivers-config.md](drivers-config.md)).

## What a configuration does not do

It does not make a driver exist, and it does not make a driver work on a phone it was not written for. A symbol builds
in, or turns on, a part of the kernel that is already there; whether it works on a given phone is what [the device's page](../devices)
and the tests say, and the project does not claim a result it has not seen.

```

`docs/devices/index.md`:

```md
<!-- Made by tools/docs-gen.py from devices/*/device.conf and socs/*/soc.conf. Do not edit: change that, then run tools/docs-gen.py. -->


# Devices

Every device with a repository, and how far each part of it works. A device of yours: [Port a device](../porting/index.md).

| Device | SoC | display | touch | buttons | cpu | gpu | storage | audio | battery | haptic | camera | torch | wifi | bluetooth | cellular | network | thermal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [QEMU virt (aarch64)](qemu.md) | `none` | yes | yes | yes |  | no | yes | yes |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | yes |  |
| [POCO X5 Pro 5G](redwood.md) | `sc7280` | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | partly | yes | yes | partly | yes | no | partly |  | partly |

`docs/driver-review/README.md`:

```md
# Driver review

Ten read-only audits of the kernel's drivers and of the boot loader, then one pass of fixes. The audits were done by
reading the code (nothing was run against hardware); each finding has a file and line, a failure scenario and a
confidence. A fix pass re-read every finding, called some of them not worth fixing, and changed the code only where a
fix was mechanical and safe (a bound, a wider integer, a lock, an error path). **Nothing here was tested on a phone.**
What was run: the kernel and the loader build from `drivers/` (via `xnu/apply.sh`), boot in QEMU both from the payload
device and from the volume (`QEMU_ESP=1`), and the host-side test suites pass (`tools/wpa-test` passes for the
Wi-Fi supplicant change). The phone-only paths (UFS, GPU, DSP, camera, Wi-Fi bring-up) compile, which is all that was
checked about them.

| Report | Covers | Findings | After the fix pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| [input.md](input.md) | touch, input queue, buttons | 10 | most fixed; firmware verification and the 0666 node left (below) |
| [gpu-display.md](gpu-display.md) | Adreno, IOSurface, framebuffer | 17 | surface and fence checks fixed; **G1 (no GPU command validation) left** |
| [camera-haptic-torch.md](camera-haptic-torch.md) | camera, flashlight, vibration | 12 | use-after-free read, torch latch, haptic start fixed |
| [adsp-battery-cpufreq.md](adsp-battery-cpufreq.md) | audio DSP loader, battery, cpufreq | 18 | DSP-supplied lengths and offsets bounded |
| [sound.md](sound.md) | speakers, microphone, `/dev/hakios-audio` | 16 | volume clamp, table bounds, guard arithmetic fixed |
| [wifi-bringup.md](wifi-bringup.md) | Wi-Fi subsystem start | 13 | remote lengths and offsets bounded |
| [wifi-stack.md](wifi-stack.md) | WPA2 supplicant, 802.11, WLFW | 12 | forged message 1 and last-writer-wins fixed; crypto was found correct |
| [storage.md](storage.md) | UFS, images, **the write guard** | 12 | guard held against every route tried; timeouts and bounds fixed |
| [loader.md](loader.md) | USB command parser, payload, volume read | 12 | bounds, busy state and half-read payload fixed |
| [policy-glue.md](policy-glue.md) | AMFI/MAC stand-ins, device nodes, sysctls, patch hunks | 7 | **nothing changed: decisions for the owners** |

Each report ends with a "Fix status" section: what was fixed and where, and what was left and why.

## Decisions that are not mechanical (open)

These are in the reports; they are listed here because a fix is a choice, not a repair.

1. **Persona entitlement removed from `posix_spawn`** (policy-glue P1, in `xnu/hakios.patch`). Any process can spawn
   a root child. The reason in the patch comment (nobody carries the entitlement) is out of date, because the
   code-signing stand-in now reads entitlements from signatures. Restore the check, or document the whole system as
   single-user.
2. **`PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_SOCKET_DELEGATE` granted to every credential** (P4, patch). Same kind of choice.
3. **Six device nodes are mode 0666** (P3: touch, audio, microphone, camera, haptic, flashlight): any process can
   read the microphone and the camera and read or forge the touch stream. They are open because every Darwin daemon,
   whatever its user, has to reach them today; tightening them means choosing which user gets which node, and
   that needs the Darwin user space running to check. The volume ioctl that made the audio node dangerous is fixed;
   the modes are not changed. Until this is decided, a process on this system is trusted with the sensors.
4. **GPU command streams are not validated and no `CP_PROTECT` table is written** (gpu-display G1). A client can
   make the GPU write anywhere its SMMU context reaches. Needs hardware knowledge of the Adreno's protection
   registers; until then, GPU access is as trusted as root.
5. **Touch controller firmware is downloaded without a checksum or read-back** (input F6), and its header is the
   open licensing item `hakios.focaltech_fw.h` (`tools/provenance.allow`, `COMPLIANCE.md`).
6. **Camera: a user-chosen mode can ask for a very large allocation** (CAM-2) needs an ABI decision (a maximum frame
   size).
7. **Wi-Fi: a forged message 1 before message 3 can still fail a join** (wifi-stack W1, rest of it): the proper fix
   keeps a candidate key set and needs a change to the header the supplicant shares with the 802.11 layer.
8. **The vsync notification is now sent with the framebuffer's lock held** (input/gpu fix G8). It closes a
   use-after-release of the notification port; it was not run with the Darwin user space. If a deadlock shows up in
   `IOMobileFramebufferUserClient::vsync`, that is the place to look.

## What the audits did not cover

The modem drivers (left out on purpose), XNU itself, `tools/darwin-write.py`, `var_store.c`, parts of `apfs_lib.c`,
anything that needs a device on the desk (register values, timings, safe limits).

```

`docs/driver-review/adsp-battery-cpufreq.md`:

```md
# Driver review: audio DSP loader, battery, CPU frequency

## Scope and method

Files read in full (paths under `xnu/files/`):

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `drivers/audio/hakios.adsp.c` | 3244 |
| `drivers/power/hakios.battery.c` | 198 |
| `drivers/power/hakios.battery.cpp` | 230 |
| `drivers/power/hakios.cpufreq.c` | 597 |

Context also read: the callers `drivers/input/hakios.input.c:217-226`, `osfmk/arm64/loader_return.c:377-379,445,492`, the consumer `drivers/camera/hakios.torch.c:454`, and the lock declarations in `hakios.wifi.c:190-192`. Nothing from the modem files was analysed.

Method: read-only, line-by-line. For every value that the DSP, the always-on processor (AOP) or the firmware files supply (SMEM entry headers, SMP2P words, GLINK queue messages, QRTR and APR payloads, battmgr answers, MDT/ELF segment headers, the AOP mailbox descriptor, the command database) I traced how it becomes a size, an offset, a loop bound or an index. For every wait loop I noted the bound and the timeout action. Nothing was built or run, and no hardware facts were assumed. Where severity depends on silicon behaviour the finding says NEEDS-HARDWARE.

Threat model used: the DSP (and AOP) can write arbitrary bytes into the shared memory it shares with us, and so can stale state left by an earlier kernel or Android.

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Confidence | Where | One line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | High | CONFIRMED | adsp.c:2012-2023, 2058, 2099, 2150 | GLINK message length wraps to 0: the listener livelocks holding `glink_lock`; the stop path then hangs |
| F2 | High | CONFIRMED | adsp.c:408, 424, 1861-1867, 1907, 1940 | SMEM item size underflows and offsets are unchecked: GLINK queues are accessed outside the SMEM window |
| F3 | Medium | CONFIRMED | adsp.c:2488, 2495, 2515 | APR payload length underflows: 256-byte out-of-bounds read, leaked to handlers and the log |
| F4 | Medium | CONFIRMED | adsp.c:2400, 2420 | QRTR `at + size > length` wraps: out-of-bounds read |
| F5 | Medium | CONFIRMED (severity NEEDS-HARDWARE) | battery.c:98-110, 139; adsp.c:2752-2808; torch.c:454 | Battery temperature has no freshness or range check, and the flashlight thermal guard consumes it |
| F6 | Medium | CONFIRMED | adsp.c:686 | `box + size > aoss.size` can overflow: mailbox writes outside the mapped block |
| F7 | Low-Med | CONFIRMED (a), PLAUSIBLE (b) | adsp.c:1145-1159, 1096-1099, 1123 | Firmware-file cleanup frees with the wrong size; mixed-source free; tiny `.mdt` read |
| F8 | Low | CONFIRMED | adsp.c:1257, 1594-1596 | Our SMP2P item is zeroed (340 bytes) at an unvalidated SMEM offset |
| F9 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | adsp.c:1371-1374, 900 | Panic way-back path calls `rails(0)`, which takes a mutex |
| F10 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | adsp.c:1893-1909, 2004-2010 | No read barrier between loading the DSP's queue head and its payload |
| F11 | Low | CONFIRMED | adsp.c:1407-1430, 1982-1983, 2916-2925 | Leaks: header page every start, GLINK intent buffers never freed |
| F12 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | adsp.c:2514-2519, 2575-2582 | `apr_answer` is published with no ordering |
| F13 | Low | CONFIRMED | cpufreq.c:573, 588-590 | `cpufreq=2` (any value) also starts `membench=2` |
| F14 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | cpufreq.c:557-587 | `cpufreq=1` / `ddr=1` have no platform check, unlike `adsp=1` |
| F15 | Low | CONFIRMED | cpufreq.c:358, 366 | Command-DB bounds checks are dead or off by 0x50 (diagnostic mode) |
| F16 | Low | CONFIRMED | battery.c:134, 139; battery.cpp:118, 130 | DSP-supplied values: signed overflow in `+50` rounding, negative to unsigned casts |
| F17 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | battery.c:188-189 | Shared struct can straddle the single mapped 16 KB page |
| F18 | Low | NEEDS-HARDWARE | adsp.c:1654 vs 1367 | IPCC GLINK enable bit set at start, never cleared at shutdown |

## Details

### F1 - GLINK length arithmetic wraps; zero-length message livelocks `glink_pump` (High, CONFIRMED)

`glink_pump()` computes the message length from DSP-written fields in 32-bit arithmetic:

- `adsp.c:2012`: `length += message.param2;` (OPEN)
- `adsp.c:2014`: `length += 8 * message.param2;` (INTENT)
- `adsp.c:2020`: `length = 16 + words[0];` (DATA, DATA_MORE)
- `adsp.c:2022-2023`: `length = (length + 7) & ~7u;` then `if (length > glink.theirs_size - 8)`

Failure scenarios (the DSP writes one 8-byte or 16-byte message into its own queue):

1. OPEN with `param2 = 0xFFFFFFF8`, or DATA with `words[0] = 0xFFFFFFF0`, or INTENT with `param2 = 0x1FFFFFFF`: `length` wraps to exactly 0. The size check passes and `waiting < length` is false. The handler then calls `glink_advance(length)` (2058, 2150, 2111) which moves the tail by 0. The `while (glink.up && !glink.broken)` loop at 2004 sees the same message again, forever. For DATA the drop path at 2148 also prints a line every iteration. For OPEN each pass sends another OPEN_ACK until our queue is full.
2. INTENT with `param2 = 0x20000001`: `8*param2` wraps to 8, so `length = 16` and the check passes. The loop at 2099 then runs 536,870,913 iterations of `glink_peek` (8 byte-wise SMEM reads each) plus a 64-entry scan.

`glink_pump()` runs with `glink_lock` held (`link_thread` at 2870-2871, `glink_send` at 2225-2231). Consequences:

- The link thread spins at 100% on one core.
- Every `glink_send` caller (QRTR, APR, battmgr, sound, mic) blocks in `lck_mtx_lock` with no timeout.
- `link_stop()` (called from `dsp_shutdown`, reached from `hakios_adsp_stop`, `loader_return.c:445`) waits 2 s, then does `lck_mtx_lock(&glink_lock)` at 2914 and blocks forever. The orderly return to the loader never completes.

Fix (compute in 64 bits and reject non-progress):

```diff
-	uint32_t waiting = glink_waiting(), length = sizeof(message);
+	uint32_t waiting = glink_waiting();
+	uint64_t length = sizeof(message);
 ...
-		length += message.param2;
+		length += message.param2;            /* now 64-bit: cannot wrap */
 ...
-		length += 8 * message.param2;
+		length += 8ull * message.param2;
 ...
-		length = 16 + words[0];
+		length = 16ull + words[0];
 	}
-	length = (length + 7) & ~7u;
-	if (length > glink.theirs_size - 8) {
+	length = (length + 7) & ~7ull;
+	if (length < sizeof(message) || length > glink.theirs_size - 8) {
```

Also make the INTENT loop `for (i = 0; i < message.param2 && 8 + 8*(uint64_t)(i+1) <= length; i++)`.

### F2 - SMEM entry size underflows and offset is never bounded; GLINK queues are accessed without bounds checks (High, CONFIRMED)

`smem_items()` builds each item's extent from DSP-writable entry headers:

- `adsp.c:408` and `adsp.c:424`: `found[count].size = entry.size - entry.padding_data;` (`padding_data` is a uint16 and `entry.size` a uint32, with no `padding_data <= size` check; an underflow yields about 4 GB).
- `adsp.c:407`, `adsp.c:423`: `found[count].offset = partition + at + sizeof(entry) + entry.padding_header` (up to 64 KB past the entry; never compared with `SMEM_SIZE` or the partition end).

`glink_find()` (1861-1867) accepts item 480 (created by the DSP itself, see the comment at step_survey 959) if `size >= 1024 && !(size & 7)`. It then uses the values raw, with no `smem_peek`-style window check:

- `adsp.c:1907`: `smem[glink.theirs + (at + i) % glink.theirs_size]`
- `adsp.c:1932`, `1940`: `queue[(head + i) % glink.ours_size] = ...` (a write)
- `smem_word(glink.descriptor + ...)` and `smem_poke(...)` are likewise unbounded.

Scenario: the DSP writes entry header item=480, `size=0x400`, `padding_data=0x408`. The size becomes 0xFFFFFFF8, which passes `glink_find`. The head/tail checks (`< theirs_size`, 1895 and 1922) now accept any 32-bit value. The first `glink_peek` reads `smem + theirs + up to 4 GB` and the link thread takes a data abort, which is a kernel panic. Even without the wrap, `offset + size` can exceed the mapped 2 MB window (padding_header adds up to 64 KB) and writes from `glink_put` land outside it. Items 478/479 have the same problem, because the DSP can edit their headers too.

Fix:

```diff
 /* in smem_items(), both loops */
-	found[count].size = entry.size - entry.padding_data;
+	if (entry.padding_data > entry.size || entry.padding_header > header.size ||
+	    (uint64_t)off + entry.size > partition + header.size) break;   /* off = computed offset */
+	found[count].size = entry.size - entry.padding_data;
```

And in `glink_find()` add `(uint64_t)x + size <= SMEM_SIZE` for each of the three items.

### F3 - APR payload length underflows (Medium, CONFIRMED)

`adsp.c:2488`: `payload = (header.size < length ? header.size : length) - header_length;`. `header_length` is 20..60 (validated against `length`); `header.size` is a DSP-written uint16 and is not validated against `header_length`. If `header.size < header_length` (for example `size = 0`) the subtraction wraps to about 4 billion.

The wrapped `payload` is then used at:

- `adsp.c:2495-2497`: `memcpy(words, data + header_length, payload < sizeof(words) ? payload : sizeof(words))` copies 256 bytes from a packet that may be only 20 bytes long, which is a heap over-read of up to 236 bytes. It is passed to the sound and mic event handlers with length 256.
- `adsp.c:2509`: the same for the first 16 bytes, which are printed.
- `adsp.c:2515-2516`: the over-read bytes go into `apr_answer.words`, with `apr_answer.length = payload` (about 4 G). `hakios_adsp_apr` copies those words to its caller (2581), and `step_apr` prints `apr_answer.words[i]` (3082-3083).

Result: kernel heap contents leak to the log and the handlers, and the read can fault if the packet sits at the end of a mapping.

Fix:

```diff
-	payload = (header.size < length ? header.size : length) - header_length;
+	{
+		uint32_t total = header.size < length ? header.size : length;
+		if (total < header_length) { printf("adsp: apr: size %u below header %u: dropped\n", total, header_length); return; }
+		payload = total - header_length;
+	}
```

### F4 - QRTR datagram size check wraps (Medium, CONFIRMED)

`adsp.c:2400`: `if (header.size == 0 || at + header.size > length)`. `at` (32 or `16 + data[3]`) and `header.size` (a DSP-supplied uint32, read at 2382 or 2388) are both uint32, so `header.size = 0xFFFFFFF0` wraps the sum to a small number and the datagram is accepted. At 2420, `memcpy(&control, data + at, header.size < sizeof(control) ? header.size : sizeof(control))` then copies 20 bytes from `data + at`. With a v1 header in a 32-byte packet that reads 20 bytes past the `kalloc_data(sizeof(*packet) + length)` element. For the v3 header `at` can be up to 271 bytes past `length`. The over-read bytes become `control->words`, which are stored in `qrtr_servers[]` (2343-2346) and printed.

Fix:

```diff
-	if (header.size == 0 || at + header.size > length) {
+	if (header.size == 0 || at > length || header.size > length - at) {
```

### F5 - Battery temperature: no freshness or range handling, consumed by the flashlight thermal guard (Medium, CONFIRMED; real-world severity NEEDS-HARDWARE)

- `battery.c:139`: `battery_temperature_c = (b->temperature_hundredths + 50) / 100;` (DSP path). `battery.c:104`: `battery_temperature_c = sample.temperature_c;` (loader path). Neither has a timestamp or a range check.
- `hakios_battery_temperature()` (47-51) returns the last value forever.
- `torch.c:454`: `if (hakios_battery_temperature() >= HOTTEST_BATTERY_C)` is the only check of the battery temperature.

Staleness paths, all traced:

1. `battmgr_thread` leaves its loop for good when the DSP closes PMIC_RTR_ADSP_APPS (`adsp.c:2752`, `channel->open=false` at 2184) or `glink.up` clears, and is never restarted (2807-2808). The last temperature stays.
2. If any of the seven `battmgr_get` calls fails, `good` is false and nothing is reported (2765): the old value stays, with only a log line.
3. `battery_poll` failure (`battery.c:95-99`) only increments `battery_failures`.

The unknown value is -273, which is below 45, so the guard treats "unknown" and "stale" as safe.

Range: `temperature_hundredths` comes straight from a DSP uint32 cast to int32 (2781). For `0x7FFFFFFF` the `+ 50` is signed overflow (undefined behaviour; in practice it wraps negative), so a garbage or lying DSP reads as cold, not hot.

Fix:

```diff
 /* battery.c */
+static uint64_t battery_temp_at;   /* mach_absolute_time of last good report */
 int hakios_battery_temperature(void) {
-	return battery_temperature_c;
+	return (mach_absolute_time() - battery_temp_at < FRESH_TICKS) ? battery_temperature_c : -273;
 }
-	battery_temperature_c = (b->temperature_hundredths + 50) / 100;
+	battery_temperature_c = (int)(((int64_t)b->temperature_hundredths + 50) / 100);
+	battery_temp_at = mach_absolute_time();
```

and make the torch guard fail closed on -273 if the board is known to have a battery. Whether fail-closed is right depends on policy, so I only flag it.

### F6 - AOP mailbox bounds check overflows (Medium, CONFIRMED)

`adsp.c:686`: `if (size < QMP_MESSAGE + 4 || box < 0x3c || box + size > aoss.size || (box & 3))`. `box` and `size` are uint32 read from the AOP's message RAM (684-685), and `aoss.size` is 0x400. With `box = 0x3fc` and `size = 0xFFFFFF00` the sum is 0x2FC and the check passes. `mailbox_send` then writes `aoss.base + our_box + 4 + 4*i` for 16 words (749-752), which goes from 0x400 to 0x43f, outside the mapped block, into whatever the neighbouring AOSS registers are (NEEDS-HARDWARE for the effect). The AOP is a remote processor, so this value is untrusted input. (The same pattern exists in `hakios.wifi.c`; not reviewed here.)

Fix: `|| size > aoss.size - box` after `box < 0x3c || box >= aoss.size`.

### F7 - Firmware image bookkeeping (Low-Medium)

(a) CONFIRMED. `adsp.c:1145` stores the header's `file_size` in `image.segment[n].file_size`. The file was allocated with `attributes.va_data_size` (`root_file`, 1003). On a size mismatch (1156-1159) the code does `image.segments++` so the file is released, but `image_forget()` (1098) calls `kfree_data(data, image.segment[s].file_size)`, which is the header's value, not the allocation size. With a wrong `adsp.bNN` on the root file system, the clean "has N bytes, the header says M" failure becomes a `kfree_data` size mismatch (a zone panic or heap corruption). Fix: store the real `file_size` (`image.segment[n].file_size = file_size;`) before `goto fail`, or keep a separate allocation size.

(b) PLAUSIBLE. `from_root` (1053) is set when any one file came from `/fw` on the root. `image_forget()` then frees all files, including `image.header` and segments that came from the small image (`hakios_image_file`, 1043), which are not `kalloc` memory. This needs a partly populated small image (header there, a segment missing, taken from root). Fix: track the source per file (a flag per segment and for the header).

(c) CONFIRMED but trivial. `adsp.c:1123`: `memcmp(header, "\177ELF\1", 5)` is evaluated before any size check, so a 1..4 byte `adsp.mdt` over-reads up to 4 bytes (and the print at 1124 reads `header[0..3]`).

Checked fine in the same function: segment window checks (1138-1139) correctly bound `paddr`, `file_size` and `memory_size` in 64 bits against `[0x86700000, +64 MB)`, and `count <= MAX_SEGMENTS` bounds `image.segment[]`.

### F8 - Our SMP2P item is written at an unvalidated offset (Low, CONFIRMED)

`our_item_find()` (1252-1258) accepts item 429 if `size >= sizeof(struct smp2p)`, where `size` is the F2-underflowable value, and returns the raw offset. `step_our_item()` then does `for (at < 340) smem_poke(our_item + at, 0)` (1594-1596) and several more pokes, with no `smem_peek` bounds check first (unlike `dsp_listen` and `dsp_ask_to_stop`, which peek first). A stale or corrupt entry for item 429 (padding_header up to 64 KB, or size underflowed) makes the kernel write 340 bytes outside the item. That is either a data abort past the 2 MB window or corruption of other processors' SMEM items. At this step the DSP has been shut down, so the source is stale state from an earlier run. Fix: reuse the F2 validation and `if (!smem_peek(our_item, &ours, sizeof ours)) return false;` before the zeroing loop.

### F9 - Panic way-back path takes a mutex (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

`hakios_adsp_quiesce()` (3141-3150) sets `leaving` and calls `dsp_shutdown()`. `mailbox_send` honours `leaving` (no lock), but `rails(0)` (1371-1374) unconditionally does `lck_mtx_lock(&hakios_rsc_lock)` at line 900, with interrupts off and the other CPUs stopped. If a stopped CPU held `hakios_rsc_lock` (the modem driver `hakios.mpss.c:899,959` takes the same lock), the panic return hangs and the loader never gets control back. The window is small: `rails_asked` is only true until the DSP says "handover" (about 40 ms after start) or after a failed give-back. Fix: `if (!leaving) lck_mtx_lock(...)` as `mailbox_send` does, and skip `hold()` (it is already skipped when `leaving`).

Related note: `ddr_rpmh_write` in cpufreq.c (465-507) drives the same TCS 0 with no `hakios_rsc_lock`. That is safe today because `ddr_raise` runs at the start of `hakios_input_init` before any DSP driver exists, and `hakios_ddr_quiesce` runs with the other CPUs stopped. A CPU stopped mid-`rails()` leaves the TCS busy and the vote is skipped after a 200 ms wait. This is latent only.

### F10 - No read barrier between queue head and payload (Low, PLAUSIBLE, NEEDS-HARDWARE)

`glink_waiting()` (1893) loads the DSP's head with `rd()`. This is a plain `ldr` with only a compiler barrier. `glink_pump` then reads the payload with byte loads from the same Normal-NC (VM_WIMG_WCOMB) mapping (1907). There is no `dmb ld` between them (a control dependency does not order loads), so on a weakly ordered core the payload loads can be satisfied before the head load and show stale bytes (zeros or an old message). The result is a mis-parsed message, and an unknown command sets `glink.broken` (2192-2196), which permanently stops the link. The producer side is correct (`settle()` before the head update in `glink_put`, 1943). Whether the core reorders here is NEEDS-HARDWARE. Fix: `__asm__ volatile("dmb ishld" ::: "memory");` after reading the head in `glink_waiting`. `battery_snapshot()` already does this correctly (`battery.c:81,83`).

### F11 - Leaks (Low, CONFIRMED)

- `step_header` (1407) allocates a page with `kmem_alloc` and never frees it, on any return path. The comment does not say why. Linux keeps the metadata buffer until after `auth_and_reset`, so it may be deliberate until that point, but nothing releases it afterwards. This is 16 KB per start; the code runs once per boot with `adsp=1`, but `adsp_step` and `adsp_again` re-runs repeat it.
- `glink_offer` (1982-1983) allocates intent buffers (up to about 115 KB at the default sizes, up to 24 x 64 KB per channel when the DSP requests sizes). `link_stop` frees queued packets (2920-2923) but never `our_intents[].data`. When the size at a slot differs from the previous one, the old pointer is overwritten (1982-1983) and leaked.
- `step_image` returns false on a misaligned segment (1464-1467) without `image_forget()`; it is freed on the next `step_firmware` only.

### F12 - `apr_answer` is published without ordering (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

The link thread fills `apr_answer.words/length/opcode/token` and then sets `there = true` (2514-2519). `hakios_adsp_apr` polls `there` and `token`, then `memcpy`s the words (2575-2581). Only `there` is `volatile`, and volatile gives no ordering with the other (non-volatile) fields. There is no `dmb`, no atomic release or acquire. On arm64 the reader can see `there` and `token` before `words`, and so copy a stale or half-written answer. The one-answer-at-a-time design (`apr_lock`) limits exposure. Compare `battmgr`, which does this correctly with `os_atomic_inc(..., release)` / `os_atomic_load(..., acquire)` (2692, 2700-2706). Fix: use `os_atomic_store(&apr_answer.there, true, release)` and `os_atomic_load(&apr_answer.there, acquire)`.

### F13 - `cpufreq=2` also starts the all-core memory benchmark (Low, CONFIRMED)

`cpufreq.c:572-573` reads `cpufreq` into `enabled`. At 588: `if (PE_parse_boot_argn("membench", &enabled, ...) && enabled == 1) {...} else if (enabled == 2)`. When `membench` is absent the parse leaves `enabled` unchanged, so the `else if` tests the `cpufreq` value. With `cpufreq=2` (accepted as "on" by `cpufreq_wanted`), 8 threads each allocate 2 x 16 MB and run a spin-wait rendezvous. Fix: use a separate variable for `membench`.

### F14 - cpufreq/ddr have no platform check (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

`hakios_cpufreq_init` runs unconditionally from `hakios_input_init` (`hakios.input.c:217`). `adsp=1` refuses to run unless `pe_arm_get_soc_base_phys() == HAKIOS_SOC_BASE` (`adsp.c:3209`). The cpufreq code instead relies only on the boot-arg: `cpufreq=1` maps and reads EPSS at 0x18591000 and the RSC at 0x18220000 (95-106, 390-400); `ddr=1` does the same without needing `cpufreq`. The file header says the addresses are the phone's. On QEMU or any other board those addresses are unrelated MMIO or RAM, so the first access is likely an external abort (panic). The effect is not traced, since QEMU's memory map is outside this repository. Fix: the same `pe_arm_get_soc_base_phys()` gate at the top of `hakios_cpufreq_init`.

### F15 - Command-database bounds checks are dead or off by 0x50 (Low, CONFIRMED; diagnostic code)

`cpufreq.c:358` and `452`: `slave->header_offset >= CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000` is never true, because `header_offset` is a uint16 (max 0xFFFF < 0x1F000). The entry array is still inside the window (max 0xFFFF + 0x90 + 512 x 24 < 0x20000), so that one is only a dead check. At `cpufreq.c:366` the check is `slave->data_offset + entry[i].offset + sizeof(aux) < CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x40`, but the read is `db->data + that`, and `data` starts at +0x90. The read can end at 0x20050, which is 0x50 bytes past the mapped 0x20000. Compare the correct check in `adsp.c:852` (`> CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000`, ending before 0x1F090). The command database is written by the boot firmware, so the practical risk is low, and the code only runs with `ddr=1`. Fix: use the check of `adsp.c:852`.

### F16 - Arithmetic on DSP-supplied battery values (Low, CONFIRMED)

DSP words become `int32_t` at `adsp.c:2778-2791` with no range check. Then:

- `battery.c:134`: `(b->percent_hundredths + 50) / 100` is signed overflow for values above INT32_MAX-50 (undefined behaviour; it wraps negative in practice and the clamp turns 100% into 0%). The same is at `battery.c:139` and `battery.cpp:118, 225`.
- `battery.cpp:130`: `setVoltage((unsigned)(b->voltage_uv / 1000))`, a negative value becomes about 4 million mV.
- `battery.cpp:133`: `number("Temperature", ...)` stores negative values in a 32-bit unsigned OSNumber. Whether powerd reads it as signed is unverified.

No crash path: the divisors are constants, so there is no division by zero. Fix: do the rounding in `int64_t`, and clamp voltage, current and temperature to plausible ranges and reject the sample otherwise.

### F17 - Shared battery struct can straddle the mapped page (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

`battery.c:188-189` maps one 16 KB page, `ml_io_map(shared_pa & ~0x3fff, 0x4000)`, and points `shared_battery` at `page + (shared_pa & 0x3fff)`. Nothing checks that the offset plus `sizeof(struct loader_battery)` (56 bytes) stays inside the page, and `sample.size` is only checked as a minimum (96). The boot-arg comes from the loader, so this is a robustness issue. Fix: reject `(shared_pa & 0x3fff) + sizeof(*shared_battery) > LOADER_PAGE_SIZE`.

### F18 - IPCC GLINK enable bit is never cleared (Low, NEEDS-HARDWARE)

`step_start` enables the LPASS doorbell for both SMP2P and GLINK (`adsp.c:1653-1654`). `dsp_shutdown` disables only SMP2P (`1367`). Nothing disables GLINK, including on the failed-start paths (1657-1679). The effect of leaving a stale enable in the IPCC, after the DSP is off and rails are given back, is a hardware matter.

## Checked and found fine

Every wait loop has a bound, and a stated action at the bound:

- `mailbox_wait` (655-664): 1000 ms each. On timeout `mailbox_open` takes our link and channel down again (700-722). `mailbox_send` takes the message back (755-758).
- `rails()` completion wait (925-931): 100 ms. The TCS is cleaned up and `false` is returned. The busy-TCS pre-check (902-907) is under `hakios_rsc_lock`.
- `step_start` watch (1685-1729): `adsp_wait` seconds (default 10), shortened to 3 s after "up". `adsp_wait` times 1000000ull cannot overflow. On timeout or `DSP_FATAL` the step fails, and `steps_over()` shuts the DSP down (3108-3109), because `dsp_started` is already true. The DSP is not left running on this path.
- `dsp_ask_to_stop` (1328-1334): 5 s (2 s when leaving). On timeout it takes our stop bit back (1339) and `dsp_shutdown` still goes on to the TrustZone shutdown.
- `scm()` (1229): at most 100 retries on `SCM_INTERRUPTED`. Both the return value and the answer are checked by all four callers. `answer` is initialised to `~0` so a failure cannot read as success.
- `our_item_make` hardware spinlock (1513-1520): about 1 s, released on every exit (1556).
- `glink_send` (2230-2263): 5000 x 1 ms with the mutex dropped around the sleep. `battmgr_get`: 1000 ms. `hakios_adsp_apr`: `ms`. `step_link`: 5 s. `battmgr_stop` and `link_stop`: 2 s each.
- `doorbells()` and the pre-start doorbell drain: 8 iterations.
- cpufreq `ddr_rpmh_write`: 2000 x 100 us at both waits. `load_thread` and `bench_all` waits are diagnostic and by design.

Start and stop sequencing:

- The stop sequence order (ask the DSP, TrustZone shutdown, tell the AOP "off", give back rails) is what the file header says (`dsp_shutdown`, 1348-1376). `link_stop` runs first, so the link thread is no longer a second reader of SMEM when `dsp_ask_to_stop` runs.
- Error mid-start: failed `rails()` and failed `mailbox_send` and failed AUTH_AND_RESET each release the rails and the `dsp_lock` (1657-1679). A failed `mailbox_open` leaves the mailbox in its previous state.
- A `hakios_adsp_stop` that arrives while `step_start` is mid-flight cannot miss a started DSP: `dsp_started` is set under `dsp_lock`, and the panic path re-checks `dsp_started` (3144).
- `dsp_words`' static `at` and `smem_item`'s static `found[256]` are only used concurrently if `dsp_words` has never found item 443. Once the DSP is up, `at` is cached and `link_thread` does not call `smem_item`.

Memory-safety items traced and fine:

- `smem_peek` bounds the read in 64-bit (`offset + size`). `smem_partition` checks `table.count <= 64`, `entry.offset + entry.size` in 64-bit, and the `$TOC`/`$PRT` magics. `smem_items` loops always progress (at least 16 bytes) and are bounded by the 2 MB window; the cached-side loop guards `step_back` with `cacheline` being a power of two and `entry.size > at`. SMP2P entries are used only with `i < min(valid, 16)`. SMP2P `smem_poke` offsets are at most 336 + 4 inside the 340 bytes that `smem_peek` validated first. Crash-reason text is clamped to 80 bytes and zeroed first.
- `rail_position` (825-877): the command-DB entry array and data reads are inside the 0x20000 window (`CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000` check at 852). `levels[160]` cannot overflow (at most about 124 bytes).
- GLINK: head and tail are validated against the queue sizes at each use (`glink_waiting` 1895, `glink_room` 1922); `glink_peek` and `glink_advance` take the modulus. OPEN names are clamped to 32 bytes plus a terminating zero. DATA copies are bounded by `our_intents[].size - fill`, `intent < our_intent_count <= 24`, and the received packet is allocated at `fill` bytes. `glink_offer` is capped at 0x10000 bytes x 24 intents. `their_intents` insertion is bounded to 64.
- battmgr: `battmgr_input` copies at most `sizeof(m)` into a zeroed struct; `battmgr_get` requires `length >= sizeof(m)`; the answer is published with release/acquire atomics. Only `get` opcodes are sent, so there are no SCM, setting or limit writes to the charger. With `battery=1` battmgr refuses to start (2822), so the two writers of the `battery_*` globals are never both active.
- Firmware loading: the MDT header is bounded to `PAGE_SIZE`, `count <= 48`, `52 + 32*count <= size`, the hashes size is cross-checked, every segment is checked in 64-bit against the reserved window, and the 8-byte alignment is checked before writing (1464). Writes and read-back stay inside `[0x86700000, +64 MB)`. `memcpy` of the header into the SCM page is bounded by the header's `PAGE_SIZE` check. The cache is cleaned (`dc civac`) and `dsb`'d before the SCM call. SCM `MEM_SETUP` is passed the exact window and the computed image size (at most 64 MB).
- Barriers: `settle()` (dsb sy) before every IPCC doorbell and before every queue head update; `(void)rd()` after the mailbox message; `battery_snapshot` seqlock uses `dmb ishld` correctly and retries a bounded 4 times.
- Locks: `glink_lock`, `dsp_lock`, `apr_lock`, `say_lock` are all mutexes; the only sleeps under a lock are `sleep_*` inside mutex sections (legal). Nested orders found: `dsp_lock` then `hakios_rsc_lock` or `hakios_aop_mailbox_lock`, and `dsp_lock` then `glink_lock` (via `link_stop`). The reverse orders do not occur in this file, and `hakios.wifi.c` does not take `hakios_rsc_lock`. `qrtr_input` and `apr_input` are called without `glink_lock` held, so their `glink_send` calls do not self-deadlock.
- cpufreq: the value written to hardware is a table row index chosen from rows 0..39 only (`EPSS_TABLE_ROWS`); the table read stays below 0x1A0, inside the 0x1000 domain window. The selection rule (strictly increasing frequency) cannot pick an out-of-table row. No boot-arg or user-space interface selects a row: `cpufreq=` is on/off only, and there is no sysctl or ioctl in these files that writes frequency. `domain_of` returns 0..2, matching `cores[EPSS_DOMAINS]`. `ddr_vote` is range-checked to 1..0x3fff (`ddr_raise`, 527), `ddr_rest` is clamped to 0x3fff, and `ddr_rest=0` means "no request" (documented: slow loader USB, nothing unsafe is traced). `load_thread`'s buffer logic is safe, and `100 * busy / (now - then)` cannot divide by zero after a >= 1 ms delay.
- battery: every sysctl is `CTLFLAG_RD` over plain `int`, so user space can read but not write (the `kern.hakios` node itself is `CTLFLAG_RW`, with no handler). No division by a variable exists anywhere in these files. `HakiosBatteryReport` validates both `size` and `b->size`, and all OSObject allocations (the adapter dictionary, the numbers) are released on every path read; `attach` and `start` failure paths release or detach.
- Boot-args in the audio DSP file (`adsp`, `adsp_step`, `adsp_wait`, `adsp_listen`, `adsp_pause`, `adsp_new`, `adsp_keep`, `adsp_again`, `adsp_return`, `battmgr`): all parsed into uint32 with defaults. Only `adsp=1` or `adsp_step` start anything, and the platform check is at 3209. `adsp_listen * 1000` can wrap only for values above 4,294,967 (a harmless short wait).

## Not checked

- The Wi-Fi, modem and shared helper implementations in `hakios.wifi.c`, `hakios.mpss.c` (the same QMP mailbox, SMEM and RPMh pattern appears there; F6 applies to `hakios.wifi.c` at the same lines, unverified).
- The consumers of `hakios_adsp_apr` and the APR event handlers (`hakios.sound.c`, `hakios.mic.c`), including whether a handler called from the link thread can wait for an answer that only that thread can deliver.
- `hakios_image_file` (`hakios.image.c`), i.e. what memory the small-image pointers refer to, which F7(b) depends on.
- IOKit internals: `IOPMPowerSource::updateStatus()` being called before `attach`/`start` (`battery.cpp:212`), and `OSNumber` signedness as read by powerd.
- Hardware facts, all NEEDS-HARDWARE: that EPSS has 40 rows, its register layout, and thermal limiting of the top row (I found no software thermal path for the CPUs in these files); RPMh command timing and what clearing a TCS while a request is in flight does; whether `ml_io_map` returns NULL on failure (none of `smem`, `cmd_db`, `dsp_memory`, `ipcc.base` is checked for NULL); cache and WC-mapping coherence of the reserved DSP memory against the kernel's own linear map; TrustZone behaviour on a failed AUTH_AND_RESET (whether a PAS shutdown is needed).
- The loader side of the battery cache (`xnuloader`) and the QEMU build.
- Not built or run; all findings are from reading the code.

## Fix status

- F1: FIXED. adsp.c `glink_pump()`: the message length is worked out in 64 bits (`wide`) and checked against the queue before it is narrowed, so it cannot wrap to 0 and the loop always makes progress; an oversize message sets `glink.broken` as before.
- F2: FIXED. adsp.c `smem_items()` (both loops): stop at an entry with `padding_data > size` or whose item ends beyond its partition; `glink_find()` and `glink_reset()`: descriptor and both queues must lie inside the SMEM window (64-bit sums).
- F3: FIXED. adsp.c `apr_input()`: a packet whose size is below its header length is dropped before `payload` is computed.
- F4: FIXED. adsp.c `qrtr_input()`: the check is now `at > length || header.size > length - at`.
- F5: SKIPPED. A freshness limit or a "stale means unknown" value needs a policy decision, and the guard (`torch.c`, not one of my files) treats -273 as safe, so only a fail-closed change there would help. The signed overflow in the temperature rounding is fixed under F16.
- F6: FIXED. adsp.c `mailbox_open()`: `box >= aoss.size || size > aoss.size - box` instead of `box + size > aoss.size`.
- F7: (a) FIXED: on a file size mismatch the real allocation size is stored before the cleanup (`step_firmware()`); (c) FIXED: `size < 5` is tested before the `memcmp` and the log line prints from a bounded copy; (b) SKIPPED: PLAUSIBLE only, needs a per-file "came from the root" flag and knowledge of what `hakios_image_file()` returns.
- F8: FIXED. adsp.c `our_item_find()` requires the item to end inside the SMEM window; the F2 fix also bounds the offset.
- F9: FIXED. adsp.c `rails()` takes and drops `hakios_rsc_lock` only when `!leaving`, as `mailbox_send()` does.
- F10: SKIPPED. Needs hardware knowledge (whether and where a `dmb ld` is needed on this Normal-NC mapping); report says NEEDS-HARDWARE.
- F11: PARTLY FIXED. The intent buffers are given back in `link_stop()` and a buffer of another size is freed before it is replaced in `glink_offer()`. SKIPPED: the `step_header` page (when TrustZone is done with it is unknown). `step_image` is not a leak: the image is freed at the next `step_firmware()`.
- F12: FIXED. adsp.c `apr_input()` publishes `apr_answer.there` with `os_atomic_store(..., release)` and `hakios_adsp_apr()` reads it with `os_atomic_load(..., acquire)`.
- F13: FIXED. cpufreq.c `hakios_cpufreq_init()`: `membench` has its own variable, so `cpufreq=2` no longer starts the all-core benchmark.
- F14: SKIPPED. PLAUSIBLE only (the effect on other boards is not shown), and a platform gate would silently turn cpufreq off if the SoC base value differed; the owner should decide.
- F15: FIXED. cpufreq.c `ddr_look()`: the data read check now counts the header (`sizeof(*db) + ... <= CMD_DB_SIZE`). The dead `header_offset` checks (`ddr_look()`, `cmd_db_address()`) are harmless and left as they are.
- F16: FIXED in part. The `+50` roundings are done in 64 bits (battery.c `hakios_battery_report()`, battery.cpp `report()` and the log line), and a negative voltage becomes 0 before the unsigned `setVoltage()`. SKIPPED: clamping current, voltage and temperature to plausible ranges (hardware knowledge) and the negative temperature in the unsigned OSNumber (whether powerd reads it as signed is unverified).
- F17: FIXED. battery.c `hakios_battery_init()` rejects a `battery_shared_pa` whose struct would cross the end of the mapped page.
- F18: SKIPPED. NEEDS-HARDWARE (effect of a stale IPCC enable bit).
- S-13: FIXED. Same fix as F3 (adsp.c `apr_input()`): the packet is dropped when `header.size` is below the header length, and the copies are bounded by `min(header.size, length) - header_length`.

```

`docs/driver-review/camera-haptic-torch.md`:

# Driver review: camera, haptics, torch

## Scope and method

Read-only audit. Files read in full unless noted.

| File | Lines | Read |
|---|---|---|
| drivers/camera/hakios.torch.c | 763 | all |
| drivers/haptic/hakios.haptic.c | 1005 | all |
| drivers/camera/hakios.camera.c | 4264 | all except 1568-1750 only skimmed (read-only RPMh/SMMU/PLL printers) |
| xnu/files/bsd/sys/hakios.camera.h | - | all (user ABI) |
| userland/src/camera_device.c (1280-1420), camera_isp.c (840-1033) | - | the parts that talk to the kernel node and parse the `.isp` file |
| tools/camsensor.py, tools/camtuning.py | - | header comments and pack lines only (to learn the on-disk format) |
| hakios.buttons.c (spmi lock), loader_return.c (quiesce call site), hakios.wifi.c (`hakios_wifi_file`) | - | the few lines needed |

Method: traced every user-reachable entry (torch `write`/`read`, haptic `write`, camera `open`/`close`/`read`/`write`; none of the three nodes has an ioctl, all use `eno_ioctl`/`eno_mmap`) end to end; followed every table-derived length and count; checked every polling loop for a bound; checked lock use between the service thread and the file operations; checked each boot-arg. Nothing was built or run. No hardware facts are asserted: where an outcome depends on how the chip behaves it is marked NEEDS-HARDWARE.

## Findings

| id | severity | confidence | file:line | one line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CAM-1 | high | CONFIRMED | hakios.camera.c:3873-3884 vs 3363-3376, 3401-3425 | `camdev_read` copies from `ring` with no reference held; the capture thread frees `ring` under it (use-after-free read, or panic in `dc civac`) |
| CAM-2 | medium | CONFIRMED | hakios.camera.c:3969-3978, 4019-4035, 3379-3384, 3500-3503, 4000 | any process (node is 0666) picks sensor and any table mode, so can force a huge kernel allocation or a permanent camera shutdown |
| TORCH-1 | medium | CONFIRMED (code path); effect NEEDS-HARDWARE | hakios.torch.c:330, 506-511, 605-633 | the "light off" path is blocked by the sticky `broken` flag, so after one failed write the LED stays on with no monitoring and no timer |
| TORCH-2 | medium | CONFIRMED (code path); effect NEEDS-HARDWARE | hakios.torch.c:487-499, 697-717, 632, 750 | `lit` is set only after all enabling writes succeed; a write that lands but fails read-back leaves the LED possibly on with `lit == false`, so nothing turns it off |
| HAPTIC-1 | medium | CONFIRMED (code path); effect NEEDS-HARDWARE | hakios.haptic.c:961-971, 570-580 | haptic=5 starts serving the motor even when the waveform file did not load |
| CAM-3 | low | PLAUSIBLE / NEEDS-HARDWARE | hakios.camera.c:2989 vs 1830, 3003, 3066 | lens-motor supply is not given back if RPMh did not report "done" in time, unlike the CX/MX rails |
| CAM-4 | low | CONFIRMED | hakios.camera.c:1218-1225, 1269 vs 2708-2710 | power-sequence delays from the table are not clamped (sensor-register delays are): up to ~71 min with rails on, or in the panic path |
| CAM-5 | low | CONFIRMED (arithmetic), PLAUSIBLE (reach) | hakios.camera.c:3316, 3347, 4053, 4036, 3436, 2197 | mode fields from the table only partly range-checked: `frame_length < 40` underflows, width/height unbounded |
