```md
| CAM-6 | low | CONFIRMED | hakios.camera.c:3906-3938 | `keep_picture` has no lock: two writers interleave into the same `keep` buffer and header |
| HAPTIC-2 | low | PLAUSIBLE | hakios.haptic.c:847-866 | the 1 s cap applies per vibration; back-to-back taps from user writes have no rest or duty limit, only the chip's fault flags |
| TORCH-3 | low | CONFIRMED | hakios.torch.c:585-590, 608-618 | the 30 s cap is "ask anew": an unprivileged writer that writes 0 then a level again keeps the light on indefinitely |
| DEV-1 | info | CONFIRMED | torch.c:575, haptic.c:828, camera.c:4000 | all three nodes are mode 0666: any process can use the camera, torch and motor, so user-space permission prompts are the only gate |

## Details

### CAM-1 camera read vs. session end: use-after-free of the frame ring

`camdev_read` marks a place READING under `darwin_lock`, drops the lock at 3869, then reads the globals `ring`, `ring_place_bytes` and `ring_frame_bytes` with no lock and copies the frame:

```
3873  vm_offset_t at = ring + (uint64_t)b * ring_place_bytes;
3879  for (vm_offset_t line = at & ~63ul; line < at + n; line += 64) dc civac
3884  error = uiomove((caddr_t)at, (int)n, uio);
```

The capture thread ends a session in `darwin_stop()` (3401): it sets every place FREE under the lock (3405-3407, which also overwrites READING), then, without waiting for any reader, runs `titan_down(); power_down(); ring_free();` and `ring_free()` does `kmem_free(kernel_map, ring, ring_bytes)` and `ring = 0` (3370-3374). Nothing counts readers, so a reader mid-copy keeps a pointer into freed memory.

Ways the session ends while a reader is copying (a 12 MB frame is copied in milliseconds, and the code itself logs the time at 3891):
- another process writes `HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR` (3969-3978): `darwin_switch_to` is seen by the loop at 3512, `darwin_stop` runs within about 1 ms;
- no read activity for `IDLE_MS` (1000 ms, 3526): `darwin_last_read` is only refreshed at the start of a read (3810, 3843) and at its end (3899), not during the copy, so a reader that is descheduled or stuck in page faults on a big user buffer for 1 s is declared idle;
- any fault (`healthy()`, SMMU fault, 1.5 s without a frame, an exposure write NACK) -> `give_up` -> `darwin_stop`.

Result: `dc civac` on the unmapped VA (a cache-maintenance fault from kernel code with no recovery handler) -> kernel panic; if the range was reused (the next `ring_alloc`, or any other kmem allocation) `uiomove` copies unrelated kernel memory out to user space; if `ring` was already zeroed, `at` is a near-NULL address. Reachable by any process that can open the 0666 node.

Fix (sketch):
```
+ static unsigned darwin_readers;                 /* under darwin_lock */
  camdev_read: under darwin_lock, after choosing b:
-   place[b].state = PLACE_READING;
+   place[b].state = PLACE_READING; darwin_readers++;
+   snapshot at/n/ring_frame_bytes into locals here, still under the lock
  ... at the end (the existing lock at 3895):
+   darwin_readers--; wakeup(&darwin_readers);
  darwin_stop(), before ring_free():
+   lck_mtx_lock(&darwin_lock);
+   while (darwin_readers != 0) msleep(&darwin_readers, &darwin_lock, PZERO, "hakios-camera-drain", NULL);
+   lck_mtx_unlock(&darwin_lock);
```
Also refresh `darwin_last_read` while `darwin_readers != 0` in the idle test.

### CAM-2 unprivileged control of sensor and mode; permanent shutdown

`HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR` accepts any sensor index (< 4) and any mode number `c.b` (3969-3978). `darwin_select()` honours an explicit mode directly: the 4:3 / 31 fps / 13 MP filter at 4019-4032 only runs when `mode_n >= ctab->modes`; an explicit mode is accepted if it passes the checks at 4035 (lanes, data type 0x2b, `width % 4`, fps and frame length non-zero). `darwin_start()` then calls `ring_alloc(RAW10_STRIDE(width) * height)` (3436) for `RING = 3` places (3254, 3383) of kernel memory. If a table has a full-resolution mode (the S5KHM2SD is a 108 MP sensor; the tables are not in the repository, so NEEDS-HARDWARE/IMAGE for the actual sizes) this is hundreds of MB per session from an unprivileged process, and each session start repeats it.

Consequences of failure are permanent: a failed `ring_alloc` or any other step in `darwin_start` returns false -> `give_up("the camera did not start")` (3500-3503); `darwin_select` failing for a sensor with no `.tab` in `fw/` (the build only installs tabs for module files present in `fw-camera/`, userland/build.sh:392-400) -> `give_up("a sensor that cannot be used")` (4091-4093). `broken` is never cleared (except in quiesce), every later open/read returns EIO (3785, 3816). The same holds for one transient NACK: `exposure_write` -> `give_up` (3356-3358, 3593-3595), `sensor_table` has no retry (2703), whereas the PMIC and chip-ID reads retry (697, 1432).

Fix (sketch):
```
 camdev_write, HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR:
-   darwin_switch_mode = c.b;
+   darwin_switch_mode = c.b;               /* and in darwin_select(): */
 darwin_select(), for an explicit mode_n also require
+   pixels <= 13000000 && fps_milli <= 31000
 darwin_select failure / darwin_start failure for a switch requested from user space:
-   give_up(...)
+   fall back to the previous sensor/mode; only give_up on hardware faults
 devfs_make_node(..., 0666, ...) -> 0660 with a group the media daemon is in
```

### TORCH-1 the off path is gated by the sticky `broken` flag

`put()` begins with `if (broken || !allowed || ...) { give_up(...); return false; }` (330-333) and every failure inside `put()` calls `give_up()`, which sets `broken` (308-314). `dark()` is a chain of four `put*` calls (506-507) joined by `&&`. So:

1. light is lit (`lit == true`), user asks a different level, `light()` -> `put_bits(FLASH_ITARGET0)` writes but the read-back differs (or the read fails) -> `broken = true`, `light()` returns false.
2. `serve()` breaks out (605) and runs the last-ditch `if (lit) (void)dark();` (632-634). `dark()` -> `put_bits(FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, 1, 0)` -> `get()` works (reads are not gated) -> value differs -> `put()` sees `broken` -> false. The channel stays enabled.
3. The thread says "the light is given up on" and terminates (636, 723). From here nothing checks fault flags, battery temperature or the time limit; the LED stays on at the last current until `hakios_torch_quiesce()` at the run's end (which does reset `broken = false`, 751).

The same happens when `dark()` itself loses a write mid-chain (cut path 612-614, trouble path 625: dark runs first, so a failed first step blocks the remaining steps). The retry at 632 is dead code in exactly the situations it is there for. Contrast with camera.c, whose off path uses a `force` argument (`pm8008_put(..., true)` at 813, `pgpio_put(..., true)`) for the same reason.

Cheap trigger: none needed beyond one dropped/failed SPMI transfer; user space only has to change the level while lit (any process, 0666).

NEEDS-HARDWARE: whether a LED stays lit after a failed read-back, and what it dissipates, is not derivable here (the file's own comment says Android's torch has no safety timer, 125 mA channel 0).

Fix (sketch):
```
-static bool put(uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
+static bool put(uint8_t reg, uint8_t value, bool force)
-	if (broken || !allowed || ...
+	if ((broken && !force) || !allowed || ...
 dark(): use force=true for every write, and do not stop at the first failure (try all four, retry each up to 3 times)
 serve() end: if (lit) { dark(); } with the forced path; also keep calling dark() every 100 ms until it succeeds or the run ends
```

### TORCH-2 `lit` is set after the enabling writes

`light()` sets `lit = true` only at line 498, after `put(FLASH_MODULE_EN, 0x80)` and `put_bits(FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, 1, 1)` (495-497). If the module-enable write lands and the channel write lands but fails its read-back (or the read fails), `put()` returns false, `lit` stays false, `broken` is set. Then:
- level 2 (697): `light(1000)` false -> the whole `if` is skipped, no `dark()` at all (713);
- level 3: `serve()` end `if (lit)` skipped (632);
- `hakios_torch_quiesce()` `if (lit)` skipped (750); it only prints "(NOT DARK)" (762) and does not act on it.

The module/channel may therefore stay enabled and unmonitored. NEEDS-HARDWARE for whether the chip actually lights in that state.

Fix: set `lit = true` before the first enabling write (before `put(FLASH_MODULE_EN, ...)`), and let `dark()` clear it only on success; make quiesce call `dark()` when the read-back says not dark.

### HAPTIC-1 haptic=5 serves without waveforms after a load failure

```
961  if (level >= 3 && configure() && load_waveforms() && level == 4) { ... play_effect }
969  } else if (level == 5 && !broken) { serve(); }
```
`load_waveforms()` returns false without `give_up()` when the file is missing, shorter than 8 bytes, or its checksum does not add up (570-580). For level 5 the `else if` is then taken and `serve()` starts the motor service (waveform 1 for taps, 11 looped) although Android's waveforms were never written to the chip's RAM (the header comment promises "configured and loaded as for 3"). Effects played from RAM that holds whatever the chip had after reset/Android: NEEDS-HARDWARE (strength and length of such a waveform are unknown; the gain and the 1 s cap still apply).

Fix:
```
-	} else if (level == 5 && !broken) {
+	} else if (level == 5 && !broken && loaded) {
```
with `loaded` set by `configure() && load_waveforms()` evaluated separately from `level == 4`, and `give_up("the waveforms are not loaded")` on that path.

### CAM-3 lens-motor supply vote not tracked on timeout

`rails()` records the vote before asking (`rails_voted |= on;`, 1830) so a request that RPMh finishes after our 100 ms poll is still given back. `vaf()` records it only on success: `vaf_voted = on && done;` (2989). In `af_up()`, `if (!vaf(true)) return;` (3003) leaves `vaf_voted == false`, so `af_down()` (3066) never sends the off request, and quiesce does not know about it either. If the WRITE_WAITED commands were accepted but completion was not seen in 100 ms (rpmh_write 1796-1806), the DW9800's supply stays on. NEEDS-HARDWARE (whether a late completion happens).

Fix: `vaf_voted |= on; ... if (!on) vaf_voted = !done;`, i.e. set it before the write like `rails()`.

### CAM-4 power-sequence delays are not clamped

`power_step()` ends with `sensor_delay(e->delay_us)` (1269). `delay_us` is a 32-bit field of the table (camsensor.py:131 packs `d * 1000` into a `<I`), `sensor_delay()` sleeps `us / 1000` ms (up to 4,294,967 ms) and the sensor-register path is clamped at 100 ms (2708-2710) but this one is not. A corrupt or odd table keeps the rails/MCLK up for the whole delay during power-up; in `power_down()` under `leaving` (panic path) `wait_ms` becomes `spin_us` (141-147) and spins with interrupts as they are. The table comes from the system image built by this repo's tool, so this is robustness, not an attack.

Fix: `sensor_delay(us > 100000 ? 100000 : us)`.

### CAM-5 mode fields only partly validated

`darwin_select()` checks lanes, data type, `width % 4`, fps and frame_length != 0 (4035-4036) but:
- `frame_length < EXPOSURE_MARGIN (40)` makes `darwin_ask.lines = frame_length - EXPOSURE_MARGIN` (4053) wrap to ~4G (clamped later at 3311) and `*frame_lines - EXPOSURE_MARGIN` (3316) wrap so the final clamp of `lines` is skipped; `exposure_write` default branch computes `extra = frame_lines - darwin_mode->frame_length` (3347), which wraps if `shortest > FRAME_LINES_MAX`.
- width/height have no upper bound: `RAW10_STRIDE(width) * darwin_mode->height` is 32-bit (3436; also `frames_alloc` 2084 and 3161) and wraps; the SMMU mapping (sized from the ring) and the IFE's real write size then disagree, the SMMU refuses the overflow (so this is a fault, not corruption). In `smmu_up()` a mapping above 1 GiB gives `thirds > 512` and `second[... + t]` (2197) writes past the second-level page into the third-level pages of the same allocation (SMMU table corruption, not a heap overflow).

Reachable only through the table (or CAM-2's mode selection). Fix: reject modes with `frame_length <= EXPOSURE_MARGIN`, `width > 16384`, `height > 16384` in `darwin_select()` and `capture_sensor()`.

### CAM-6 `keep_picture` unserialised

`HAKIOS_CAMERA_KEEP` (3959-3960 -> 3906) does `bzero(keep header)`, fills the header, `uiomove`s into `keep + 4096` and updates `loader_recording[]` with no lock. Two writers (any process) interleave: header of one picture over the data of the other, `frames = 1`. Memory-safe (same bounds, `want <= keep_bytes` is checked at 3914). Fix: take `darwin_lock` (or a dedicated mutex) around the body.

### HAPTIC-2 no duty-cycle limit across taps

`HAPTIC_MAX_MS` (349) limits one LOOP state, followed by an equal rest (906-910). A TAP (waveform 1, 856-859) has no rest: Darwin (or any process writing to the 0666 node) writing a burst, 30 ms of silence, another burst ... starts a new tap each time `onset_us` changes (847). Only the chip's fault flags (checked every 50 ms, 925-929) stop it. PLAUSIBLE; whether this can overheat the motor is NEEDS-HARDWARE.

### TORCH-3 30 s cap restarts on request

`waiting_for_off` is cleared when `wanted == 0` is sampled (585-587) and `since` restarts when `applied` goes from 0 to nonzero (593-596). Any writer that writes `0`, waits more than the 20 ms poll, then writes a level re-arms the light for another `max_secs`. The cap is therefore a per-request cap, not a limit; the fault/temperature checks (100 ms) stay active. Informational unless the intent was a hard on-time limit.

### DEV-1 device node permissions

`devfs_make_node(..., 0666, ...)` for hakios-torch (575), hakios-haptic (828) and hakios-camera (4000). Anything that can open a device node gets frames, light and vibration. This is the precondition for CAM-1, CAM-2, CAM-6, HAPTIC-2 and TORCH-3 being reachable by unprivileged code.

## Checked and found fine

Torch
- `torch_write` (520-533): loop reads exactly 4 bytes per `uiomove`, value clamped to 1000 (529), the current is then computed in `light()` as `125000 * permille / 1000` (no 32-bit overflow: max 1.25e8) and clamped twice (`code > ANDROID_ITARGET` 484). Nothing user-set reaches the ITARGET register unclamped. A trailing 1-3 bytes are left unconsumed (write returns short), no memory issue.
- `torch_read` (539-544): `uiomove` of `MIN(4, resid)` from a local; no leak.
- Register allow-list in `put()` (303-305, 327-333), read-back of every write (349-358), arbiter channel re-check before each write (335-338), `flash.id` check, mapping sizes: `ARB_CHANNEL(n)` and `ARB_OWNER(n)` at n <= 511 are inside the 0x1100/0x1000 mappings, observer `0x80 * 511 + 0x1c` is inside 0x10000, write channel mapped 0x1000.
- `spmi_read_once`/`show_registers`/`trouble` buffers (`r[8]`, `more[8]`, `latched[2]`, `data[2]`) sized for the counts used; `count - 1` with count 1-8 only.
- Every polling loop has a bound: `wait_done` 2 ms, retries 3, serve loop 20 ms steps, level-2 loop `secs`.
- Boot-args: `torch` (clamped 1-3, 731-734), `torch_max_s` (1..120, 687), `torch_secs` (1..max, 694); `now - since >= max_secs * 1000ull` (608) is 64-bit.
- `hakios_spmi_lock` is a spin lock held for at most one transfer (<= 2 ms); not held across `say`/sleep.
- Light is switched off in the cut path (612) and the trouble path (625) in the right order (dark before give_up), and on quiesce (750-752).

Haptic
- `haptic_write` (689-727): 512-byte stack buffer, `bytes` capped to that and made even (698-701), `uiomove` size matches; `-(int32_t)samples[i]` cannot overflow in 32 bits; shared state is `volatile` 64/32-bit, a lost update of `heard_peak` is benign. No path blocks.
- `load_waveforms` (563-621): size >= 8 checked before any index; checksum over the file; writes `file + 4 + at` in chunks of at most 32 with `n = min(32, length - at)` so never past `size`; read-back compared chunk-wise with a 64-byte local; `length = size - 4` cannot underflow. The chip's RAM capacity is NEEDS-HARDWARE, but a too-large file fails the compare and gives up.
- I2C by hand: clock stretch bound 100 x 5 us (216), bus_take restores the pins when the bus is not at rest, no unbounded loop; register read buffers sized to counts (1, 2); `regs_read` leaves caller buffers initialised (callers zero them).
- LOOP vibration stop path: cut at `HAPTIC_MAX_MS` (902-908); a stop that fails -> `give_up` -> reset pin low (352-359), which does not depend on I2C; a failed gain write or health check also gives up. Exits from `serve()` all go through `broken`. `gain_for` cannot exceed Android's 0x80 (814-816).
- Boot-args: `haptic` (clamped 5, 985), `haptic_effect` (1..10, 965).
- Quiesce puts the chip in reset (997-1003).

Camera, kernel side
- Sensor table parse (`ctab_load` 1106-1143, `ctab_block` 1146-1161, `ctab_find`): magic, `size >= sizeof(head)`, `modes` 1..16, `at + 12 > end` before each power block header, `ctab_tables + 4 > end`; every block is re-checked `at + 12 + n * 12 <= end` before use (`n * sizeof` is 64-bit so it does not wrap; the pointer arithmetic can only exceed `end` by < 51 GB, no wrap at kernel VAs); the mode array is covered by the `ctab_power` check. `sizeof(struct ctab_entry)` is 12 and `ctab_mode` 48, matching camsensor.py's packing.
- `sensor_table` (2676-2714): operation/address/data widths validated per entry (2689), `out[4]` always enough, per-entry delay clamped to 100 ms. `read_chip_id`: `in` forced to 1-4 so `id[4]` is safe, `out` is 1 or 2.
- All table-driven power kinds are validated (`power_step` 1233-1268): MCLK only 0/19200/24000, supply kinds only 1-3, others -> give up; the voltage written to an LDO can only be the one in `sensors[]` (`sensor_ldo`/`pm8008_put` allow-lists 645-653, 688-691; arrays indexed with `n <= 7`).
- Register write allow-lists: camcc (875-879), PM8008i, PMIC GPIO 3 (555-559); read-backs on all of them; off paths for camera use `force` and always run to the end (`power_down`, `ldo_off`).
- Every polling loop is bounded: `wait_done`, `wait_bits`, `wait_reg`, SMMU TLB sync (2222), clock branches (1986), `rpmh_write` (100 ms), `darwin_session` (frame timeout 1.5 s, 3521), `wait_standby`, `bus_unwedge`, `capture_tpg` (2 s), `capture_sensor` (5 s).
- User commands (`camdev_write` 3942-3981): fixed 24-byte struct, size checked first; `HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR` index bounds-checked (3970); EXPOSURE values are unclamped when stored but clamped before use in all three consumers (3480, 3591, 3705, 3728); FOCUS clamped to 1023 in `af_move` (3039). `keep_picture` bounds: `bytes != 0`, `d` 1-3, `stride * height <= 2 * bytes` in 64-bit, `want <= keep_bytes`, copy size `min(bytes, resid)`.
- `camdev_read` header: `bzero(&f)` before filling, `MIN(sizeof(f), resid)`, so no uninitialised bytes leave; place indexes `b < RING`; state reads/writes under `darwin_lock`, the lock is not held across `uiomove`/`msleep` misuse (msleep releases it).
- Locking between ioctl-side and capture thread: shared `place[]`, `darwin_ask`, `darwin_given` are under `darwin_lock`; `darwin_switch_to`/`darwin_open` etc are volatile flags; lock order is always (darwin_lock) or (hakios_smmu_lock) or (spmi spin), never nested with each other. The one gap is CAM-1.
- Single reader: a reader cannot be handed the place that is being programmed for the next frame (the next place is the lowest-sequence non-READING place, the reader takes the highest unread), so I found no tearing with one reader; with two simultaneous readers I did not prove either way.
- IFE DMA is confined by an SMMU context that maps only the ring (or `frames_bytes`); the order in `darwin_stop` stops the write master (`paths_down`), tears the SMMU context down and only then frees memory. Cache maintenance (`dc civac` before reads, `dsb sy`) is present where the CPU reads DMA memory.
- Idle timeout and frame timeout: a stalled sensor ends the session in 1.5 s (3521-3525).
- Boot-args: `cam` (clamped 0-5), `cam_sensor` (string compared against the fixed names, cannot index out of range), `cam_mode` (checked against `modes` in both paths), `cam_frames` (1..300), `cam_fake_fps` (1..30), `cam_keep_mb` (<= 64), `cam_settle` (masked to a byte), `cam_vblank` (<= 0x3fff), `cam_gain`/`cam_shutter` clamped before the registers are written (3091-3103, `exposure_limits`). `cam_after` is unclamped, `secs * 1000` wraps for absurd values: trusted boot-arg.
- `RPMh` command DB parse (`rpmh_resource`): `slave->count > 512` skipped, data offsets checked against the mapping, `levels[]` filled up to `max` only.

Camera, user-space side
- `isp_load_tuning` / `tune_set` (camera_isp.c:880-960): size window 8 B..16 MB, every count (`n <= 6`, `ccts <= 6`, `refs <= 16`) is checked before it is used as a loop bound or array index, every read is preceded by an `end - p` check, `memcpy(t->ref, p, refs * 12)` fits `ref[16][3]`. Gamma lookup is clamped to 0..4095 (line 411), so a NaN or huge gain from a bad file cannot index out of range. File and descriptor are released on every error path.
- `camera_device.c` worker: header size handshake and read sizes match the kernel's `ring_frame_bytes`; EIO stops the worker.

## Not checked

- The cellular modem, QMI, IPA (out of scope).
- Hardware facts: register layouts, timings, safe LED current and motor limits, whether reset stops the motor, whether RAM survives a soft reset, RPMh completion timing, SMMU attribute encodings (`CAM_PTE`, `SMMU_MAIR0`): not derivable from the repository.
- The sensor tables and the `.isp` files themselves (`fw-camera/` is not in the tree): mode sizes, delays, lane assignments are assumed from tools/camsensor.py's description. `camsensor.py` and `camtuning.py` parsing of the vendor files (host-side tools) was not reviewed, only their output format.
- The 1568-1750 stretch of hakios.camera.c (read-only `show_*` printers) and `userland/src/camera_isp.c` outside the tuning loader (demosaic, AE, AWB) and `camera_test.c`, `camera_avtest.m`: not read for safety.
- `hakios_wifi_file()`/`image_file()` (hakios.wifi.c): assumed to return a stable read-only pointer into the image; ownership and alignment not verified.
- `ml_io_map_unmappable` failure mode in `rpmh_resource` (cmd_db NULL dereference if the mapping fails): not verified.
- Behaviour with two simultaneous camera readers beyond what is said above; behaviour when `psci_smp_stop_others()` leaves a stopped CPU holding `darwin_lock` or `hakios_smmu_lock` (the quiesce paths skip those locks when `leaving`, torch/haptic/camera all do).
- Interplay with the audio DSP driver's use of the RPMh TCS 0 and with hakios.speaker.c / buttons for shared pins and the SPMI arbiter beyond the spin lock.
- userland/src/inject_media.c (writes the torch node) and the camera ISP's float handling.

## Fix status

Nothing was built or run; each edit was re-read for syntax and types only.

- CAM-1: FIXED (hakios.camera.c). New `darwin_readers` count (under `darwin_lock`); `camdev_read` counts itself in the same lock hold that marks the place READING and takes `at` and the frame size from `ring`, `ring_place_bytes` and `ring_frame_bytes` there; it leaves the count (and `wakeup`s) in its final lock section. New `darwin_drain_readers()` (waits under `darwin_lock` with `msleep` until the count is 0) is called before `ring_free()` in `darwin_stop()` and in `fake_session()`. Lock order: the drain holds only `darwin_lock` (power is already down); nothing else nests with it. The optional "refresh `darwin_last_read` while a read is in progress" was not done: the drain already makes an idle stop safe.
- CAM-2: SKIPPED. Capping the mode's pixels or fps for user-chosen modes changes the documented ABI (`HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR` takes any mode), and the real mode sizes live in tables that are not in the tree. Replacing `give_up` with a fall back to the previous sensor and mode is a design change. Node mode is policy (see DEV-1).
- TORCH-1: FIXED (hakios.torch.c). `dark()` sets a `forcing` flag while it runs and `put()` ignores the `broken` latch only then (all other checks, the allow-list, the arbiter check and the read-back stay). `dark()` also tries all four steps instead of stopping at the first failure; a clean run does the same writes in the same order. Not done: the repeated dark() retry every 100 ms in `serve()` (a design change).
- TORCH-2: FIXED (hakios.torch.c). `light()` sets `lit = true` before the module-enable write; `dark()` still clears it only on success. In the torch=2 path, a failed `light(1000)` now calls `dark()` if `lit` is set. Quiesce is unchanged: it already calls `dark()` when `lit` is set, which is now true in the failing case.
- HAPTIC-1: FIXED (hakios.haptic.c). `loaded = level >= 3 && configure() && load_waveforms()` is evaluated apart from `level == 4`; level 5 calls `serve()` only when `loaded`, otherwise `give_up("the waveforms are not loaded")` (chip into reset).
- CAM-3: FIXED (hakios.camera.c). `vaf()` records `vaf_voted = on` before the RPMh request, as `rails()` does, so `af_down()` sends the "off" even if RPMh did not report done in time. Worst case is one extra harmless "off" request. Whether a late completion really happens is hardware behaviour.
- CAM-4: FIXED (hakios.camera.c). `power_step()` passes `delay_us` capped at 100000 to `sensor_delay()`, the same cap the sensor-register path uses.
- CAM-5: FIXED (hakios.camera.c). `darwin_select()` rejects modes with `frame_length <= EXPOSURE_MARGIN`, `frame_length > FRAME_LINES_MAX`, width or height over 16384; `capture_sensor()` rejects width/height over 16384 and `frame_length <= 40` (EXPOSURE_MARGIN is defined later in the file, so the literal 40 as in `exposure()`). 16384 x 16384 keeps the 32-bit sizes and the SMMU third-level count in range.
- CAM-6: FIXED (hakios.camera.c). New `keep_lock` mutex (own mutex, not `darwin_lock`, so the capture thread never waits on a user copy) held across the header and data writes in `keep_picture()`; never nested with `darwin_lock`.
- HAPTIC-2: SKIPPED. A duty-cycle limit needs the motor's thermal limits (hardware) and is a policy change.
- TORCH-3: SKIPPED. The cap is per request by design; a hard on-time limit is a policy change.
- DEV-1: SKIPPED. Node mode 0666 is policy and was not to be changed.

```

`docs/driver-review/gpu-display.md`:

```md
# GPU and display driver review

## Scope and method

(This review came before HakiosGPU's request `0x7d`, the client's own pages as a buffer, added 3 November: [Metal on the Adreno](../reference/metal.md#hakiosgpu-driversgpuhakiosgpucpp). That request has not been reviewed, and it adds to G6's wired memory without a cap of its own.)

Read-only review of the user-reachable surface of the GPU and display code. Nothing was built or run; the XNU source tree itself is not in this repository (only `xnu/files` overlays), so XNU API behaviour is not verified here.

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `drivers/gpu/hakios.adreno.c` | 3843 |
| `drivers/gpu/hakios.gpu.cpp` | 1192 |
| `xnu/files/iokit/Kernel/MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp` | 1531 |
| `xnu/files/iokit/Kernel/MiniIOSurface.cpp` | 1814 |
| `xnu/files/iokit/Kernel/MiniIOSurface.h` | 174 |

Method: read all of `hakios.gpu.cpp`, `MiniIOSurface.cpp/.h` and `MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp` end to end; in `hakios.adreno.c` read the register helpers, SMMU/page-table code, ring and submit code, the "GPU kept on" API (lines 3157-3520), firmware parsing, boot-arg parsing and the init path. The bring-up steps (clocks, RPMh, TrustZone) were skimmed only. Each finding below was traced from an entry point (IOKit external method) to the faulty line. Hardware effects are labelled NEEDS-HARDWARE.

## Findings

| id | severity | confidence | location | summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | High | CONFIRMED | adreno.c:2399-2404,2569-2571; gpu.cpp:928-944 | User command buffers go to the GPU unvalidated, in the same SMMU context as the kernel's ring and fence page, mapped writable; no register protection |
| G2 | High | CONFIRMED | MiniIOSurface.cpp:574-613; MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:738,786-787 | Surface geometry (row stride, element height, wrapped size) is not checked against the allocation; the display reads past the surface |
| G3 | Medium | CONFIRMED | gpu.cpp:1139-1149,189-215 | Any client can latch the "GPU stopped answering" flag forever by waiting on a fence that was never issued |
| G4 | Medium | PLAUSIBLE | gpu.cpp:463-508,189-209 | freeBuffer() drops the lock inside gpuWait() while the buffer is still live: concurrent close of the same handle can free it twice |
| G5 | Medium | CONFIRMED | MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:733-745,608-613 | Destination rectangle from the swap request is not clipped; int32 arithmetic and a multi-billion-iteration row loop |
| G6 | Medium | CONFIRMED | gpu.cpp:698,1037-1045; MiniIOSurface.cpp:598-615 | No per-client or global memory caps on wired buffers/surfaces; kHakiosShow allocates rowBytes*height unbounded |
| G7 | Low | CONFIRMED | MiniIOSurface.cpp:1203-1211 | Read of a freed MiniIOSurface in methodCreate() when the reply buffer is too small |
| G8 | Medium | PLAUSIBLE | MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:1256-1274 vs 1213-1219 | vsync thread sends to a notification port that registerNotificationPort() can release concurrently |
| G9 | Low-Medium | CONFIRMED (absence of check) | MiniIOSurface.cpp:1255,731; gpu.cpp:782; all initWithTask | Surfaces are looked up (and mapped, and handed to the GPU) by small sequential ID with no ownership or privilege check |
| G10 | Low | CONFIRMED | MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:750-770 | Allocation-failure path leaves fBlendRowSize=0 while helper arrays exist; a later free uses the wrong size |
| G11 | Low | CONFIRMED | gpu.cpp:871-872,986-987 | Submit with only non-CMD_BUF commands logs uninitialised stack words |
| G12 | Low | CONFIRMED | adreno.c:1836-1837,1810 | GMU firmware block address+size is 32-bit and can wrap in range checks (image is trusted, so hardening only) |
| G13 | Low | CONFIRMED | adreno.c:3314-3336,3352-3364 | GPU address free list has no double-free check; TLB sync result ignored |
| G14 | Low | CONFIRMED | gpu.cpp:253-265 | Signed overflow in millisecondsUntil() on user-supplied seconds (effect bounded by the 5 s cap) |
| G15 | Low | CONFIRMED | adreno.c:3460-3466 | hakios_gpu_submit() busy-waits up to ~2 s with the global GPU lock held when the ring is full |
| G16 | Low | NEEDS-HARDWARE | adreno.c:2399; MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp (drawLayer) | CPU caches are cleaned before the GPU runs but never invalidated before the CPU reads what the GPU wrote |
| G17 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | gpu.cpp:538-575 | A request racing clientClose() can create a buffer after the cleanup loop; free() does not release it |

## Details

### G1 No command-stream validation; kernel GPU memory shares the user address space (High, CONFIRMED)

- `hakios.gpu.cpp:928-944` accepts any buffer/offset/size for a command buffer and passes the GPU address to `hakios_gpu_submit()` (`hakios.adreno.c:3479-3484`) as an indirect-buffer packet. The only checks are alignment and `offset+size <= b->size`. Contents are never inspected.
- `hakios.adreno.c:2395-2396` states that the register-protection setup of Linux's hw_init was deliberately left out ("less ... the protection of registers against user programs' commands"). A search of the file finds only `CP_PROTECT_STATUS` (a read); no protect table is ever written.
- The kernel's own ring (`CORE_RING_ADDRESS 0x01000000`), the fence/timing scratch page (`CORE_SCRATCH_ADDRESS 0x01200000`) and, during bring-up, the target page are created by `block_new(..., PTE_CORE)` (lines 2569, 2571, 2895) in `core_space`, the same context that user buffers are mapped into (`hakios_gpu_map`, line 3342). `PTE_CORE` has the "unprivileged" bit and is not read-only. User buffers start at `GPU_ADDRESSES_START 0x20000000` in the same tables.
- Failure scenario: a client builds a command buffer whose packets write to the fixed ring or fence addresses, or to another client's buffers (all clients share one address space; the file header admits this). Effects: forged fence completion (so `freeBuffer()`/`reap()` release memory the GPU still uses), a corrupted ring (the kernel's next commands are replaced), cross-client reads and writes of pixel buffers, and a command stream that never completes (no hang recovery exists; `gGPUReported` then stays set). Which GPU registers a user packet can reach with no protect table is NEEDS-HARDWARE.
- Suggested fix (outline): map ring, scratch and microcode with the privileged attribute so unprivileged GPU accesses to them fault; write a CP_PROTECT table as Linux does; give each client its own SMMU context or at least IOVA ranges, as the header already lists as future work; add a hang timeout and reset.

```
-#define PTE_CORE (PTE_GMU | PTE_UNPRIVILEGED)
+#define PTE_CORE_USER (PTE_GMU | PTE_UNPRIVILEGED)   /* user buffers */
+#define PTE_CORE_KERNEL PTE_GMU                       /* ring, scratch, sqe */
```
(and use `PTE_CORE_KERNEL` in `step_core_space`/`step_frame`; privilege semantics are NEEDS-HARDWARE).

### G2 Surface geometry not validated against the allocation (High, CONFIRMED)

Path: `IOSurfaceRootUserClient::methodCreate` (user dictionary) -> `surfaceCreate()` -> later `IOMobileFramebufferUserClient` SwapEnd -> `present()` -> `show()` -> `drawLayer()`/`record()`. The framebuffer trusts `s->info.bytesPerRow`, `info.width/height` and `pixels()`.

What is checked at creation (`MiniIOSurface.cpp`):
- width/height <= 16384, element sizes <= 255, `needed = bpr * ceil(height / eh)` (line 580) must fit in `alloc` and <= 512 MB.

What is not:
1. No minimum for `IOSurfaceBytesPerRow` (line 574): a stride smaller than `width * bytesPerElement` is accepted. `drawLayer` (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:738) only checks the source rectangle against `info.width/height`, then reads `sy*stride + sx*4 .. + sw*4` per row, so the last row ends beyond `allocSize`.
2. The row count used for the size is `ceil(height/eh)` but the display reads `height` rows. With `IOSurfaceElementHeight` > 1 the allocation is smaller than `height * bytesPerRow`, by up to a factor of 255.
3. Wrapped client memory (lines 608-613): after `alloc` was raised to `needed`, it is overwritten by `IOSurfaceAllocSize` as given (possibly smaller than needed, or zero) with no re-check and no 512 MB limit. `kpixels` then points into a kernel mapping of exactly `alloc` bytes while `info` still claims the larger geometry.
4. Multi-plane case: `p->size = p->bytesPerRow * rows` (line 539) is 32-bit and can wrap; plane width/height are not capped (only the top-level ones are); `p->offset` is taken from the caller.

Failure: the presenter thread reads kernel memory past the surface (kernel panic if the range is unmapped; otherwise adjacent kernel data is rendered to the panel and, with `rec_secs`, into the recording). Needs any process that can open the surface and framebuffer user clients; neither does a privilege check (G9).

Suggested fix:
```
 bpr = dictNumber(props, "IOSurfaceBytesPerRow", 0);
+minRow = alignUp((uint64_t)((width + ew - 1) / ew) * bpe, 1);
+if (bpr != 0 && bpr < minRow) return NULL;
...
-needed = (uint64_t) bpr * ((height + eh - 1) / eh);
+needed = (uint64_t) bpr * height;            /* the display reads `height` rows */
...
 } else {
-    alloc = dictNumber(props, "IOSurfaceAllocSize", (uint32_t) needed);
+    if (alloc > MINISURF_MAX_ALLOC) { ...release; return NULL; }
 }
```
and in `drawLayer()` refuse any surface where `info.offset + (uint64_t)(info.height-1)*bytesPerRow + (uint64_t)info.width*4 > info.allocSize`; compute plane sizes in 64-bit and cap them.

### G3 Any client can latch the GPU-stopped flag (Medium, CONFIRMED)

`externalMethod` case `kMsmWaitFence` (gpu.cpp:1139-1149) passes the fence number from the request straight to `gpuWait()`; `hakios_gpu_done()` (adreno.c:3375-3381) compares with a signed difference, so a fence number ahead of the last issued one is never "done". The wait time comes from the caller's timeout, capped at 5000 ms (`millisecondsUntil`). In `gpuWait` (lines 210-213), a wait of >= 1000 ms that fails sets `gGPUReported = true` and calls `hakios_gpu_report()`. The flag is never cleared (searched), and `gpuWait()` returns false immediately while it is set (line 203).

Effect for all clients afterwards: every wait fails at once, the display presents half-drawn surfaces (`MiniIOSurfaceDrawn` false), and `freeBuffer()` treats any buffer the GPU is still busy with as stuck and keeps its memory and GPU address permanently (lines 480-490).

Suggested fix: reject fences greater than `hakios_gpu_last()` in `kMsmWaitFence`, and set the latch only for a fence that has really been issued:
```
 case kMsmWaitFence:
+    if ((int32_t)(r.waitFence.fence - hakios_gpu_last()) > 0) { ret = kIOReturnBadArgument; break; }
```

### G4 Lock dropped inside freeBuffer() while the buffer is still live (Medium, PLAUSIBLE)

`freeBuffer()` (gpu.cpp:467-468) calls `gpuWait(b->fence, 1000)` when all 64 `fLeft` slots are taken; `gpuWait` unlocks `gGPULock` (lines 206-208) around `delay_for_interval`. During that window `b->memory` is still non-NULL and the handle is valid, so a second thread issuing `kDrmGemClose` (line 1163) for the same handle (or `clientClose`) enters `freeBuffer()` for the same buffer. Both then do the same `hakios_gpu_unmap`/`hakios_gpu_address_free`/`memory->release()`/`MiniIOSurfaceDrop`, and `fBufferCount--`/`fBufferBytes` are decremented twice. `hakios_gpu_address_free` has no overlap check (G13), so a double free corrupts the address free list. Needs 64 submissions' worth of busy buffers closed early plus two racing threads, hence PLAUSIBLE.

Suggested fix: mark the buffer as being freed before any unlock:
```
+struct gpu_buffer * b ... ; save = *b; b->memory = NULL; b->surface = NULL; /* handle gone */
+/* operate on `save` from here on */
```
(or set a `closing` flag that `buffer()` honours).

### G5 Destination rectangle from the swap request is unclipped (Medium, CONFIRMED)

`drawLayer()` takes `dst[]` (x, y, w, h as int32) straight from the swap structure (`swap + SWAP_DEST(layer)`). Only `dw <= 0 || dh <= 0` selects defaults (line 733). `py0 = dy*panelH/H`, `py1 = (dy+dh)*panelH/H` (lines 743-745) where `dy+dh` is computed in 32 bits first (signed overflow). Only `py1 <= py0` is rejected, and `drawRows()` iterates `for (y = y0; y < y1; y++)` with a `continue` for rows outside the panel (lines 608-613), so a rectangle spanning about 2 billion rows costs seconds of CPU per frame in the presenter thread; the helper threads split the same range. Panel memory writes themselves are bounded by the `y` and `cx0/cx1` clipping.

Suggested fix: clamp `py0/py1` to `[0, fPanelHeight]` (and `px0/px1` to the panel width) immediately after computing them, and compute `dx+dw`, `dy+dh` in int64.

### G6 No resource limits on wired memory (Medium, CONFIRMED)

- `gemNew` (gpu.cpp:698): each buffer is limited to 256 MB and each client to 8192 handles, but `fBufferBytes` is only used for logging; there is no byte cap per client or in total. The GPU address pool (3.5 GB) is shared by all clients, so one client can also exhaust it.
- `surfaceCreate` (MiniIOSurface.cpp:598-615): up to 512 MB each, 16384 table slots, `gSurfaceBytes` tracked but not limited. Memory is wired kernel memory.
- `HakiosGPUUserClient::show` (gpu.cpp:1037-1045): `size = rowBytes * height` with `rowBytes` a free 32-bit value (only `>= 4*width` is checked) and height up to 4096, passed to `IOMallocData()` and then `copyin()`. Size can reach tens of terabytes; large-but-satisfiable values wire memory. This selector also works when the GPU is not ready (line 1103).

Suggested fix: cap `rowBytes` (e.g. `<= 4 * 4096`... use `rowBytes <= 64 * width` or an absolute 1 MB), add per-client and global byte budgets enforced in `newBuffer()` and `surfaceCreate()`.

### G7 Use of a freed surface in methodCreate() (Low, CONFIRMED)

At MiniIOSurface.cpp:1201-1207: `addRef(s)` takes a hold; if `returnSurface()` fails (the caller's output buffer is smaller than the result, a caller-controlled condition: line 1059), `dropRef(ref)` runs, then `surfaceUnhold(s)` drops the creator's hold, `holders` reaches zero and `s->release()` frees the object. Line 1211 then reads `s->info.allocSize` after the unlock. Only a stale read that selects the logging block, but it is a use-after-free on a heap object whose state the caller influences indirectly.
Fix: copy `allocSize` into a local before `surfaceUnhold(s)`.

### G8 Notification port released while the vsync thread may still send to it (Medium, PLAUSIBLE)

`vsync()` (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:1256-1274) copies `fPorts[kFBNotifyVSync]` into an async reference under `fLock`, unlocks, then calls `sendAsyncResult64WithOptions`. `registerNotificationPort()` (1213-1219) swaps the port under the lock but releases the old one outside it. A client that re-registers the port while the timer fires can leave the thread sending to a released port. Whether `sendAsyncResult64WithOptions` takes its own reference is XNU behaviour not verifiable here.
Fix: hold the lock across the send, or take a port reference in `vsync()` and drop it afterwards.

### G9 No privilege or ownership checks (Low-Medium, CONFIRMED absence)

`initWithTask` of all three user clients (gpu.cpp:438, MiniIOSurface.cpp:921, MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:1145) accept any task. `methodLookup` (MiniIOSurface.cpp:1255) maps any existing surface by its integer ID (IDs are sequential from 1 up to 16383 and reused; `gSurfaceNext`), `kHakiosSurface` (gpu.cpp:782) hands any surface's pixels to the GPU, and `SwapEnd` accepts any surface ID. Any process that can open these services can therefore read or overwrite other processes' pixel buffers and drive the panel. If the intended design is that the sandbox gates these services, this is by design; it should be documented.
Related, needs verification against XNU: freed big-surface memory is kept and re-issued to later surfaces (`surfaceMemoryBack`, lines 228-231) on the strength of `getRetainCount() == 1`, which counts IOKit references only, not duplicate VM mappings that a process may have made of the shared memory.

### G10 fBlendRow allocation-failure path (Low, CONFIRMED)

MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp:750-770: on a failed `IONew` the code frees `fBlendRow` and sets `fBlendRowSize = 0`, but the helper arrays that did get allocated (with the new, larger size) remain; the next growth runs `IODelete(fHelperBlend[i], uint32_t, fBlendRowSize)` with size 0. Keep a separate size per allocation or free all arrays on failure.

### G11 Uninitialised words logged (Low, CONFIRMED)

gpu.cpp:871-872: `addresses[]`/`words[]` are uninitialised; if every command has `type != MSM_SUBMIT_CMD_BUF`, `count` is 0 and the first four submissions log `addresses[0]`, `words[0]` (lines 985-988), exposing stack bytes to the kernel log. Also a zero-command submission is passed to the ring. Fix: `memset` the arrays and reject `count == 0`.

### G12 GMU firmware block arithmetic (Low, CONFIRMED)

adreno.c:1836-1837: `block.address + block.size <= gmu_blocks[i].address + gmu_blocks[i].size` is evaluated in 32 bits; a wrapping block passes the check and `memcpy` (line 1838) writes `block.size` bytes into a block that is smaller. Same pattern at line 1810 (`in_tcm(block.address + block.size - 1)`). The file is part of the signed-by-nobody boot image, so this is hardening against a corrupt or malicious image. Compute in `uint64_t`, and also check `block.size <= remaining file size` before copying (the loop at 1756 does check the end of the file).

### G13 Address allocator and TLB invalidate (Low, CONFIRMED)

`hakios_gpu_address_free()` (adreno.c:3314-3336) merges by position only; freeing a range that is already free (see G4) or overlapping silently corrupts the list, and when the 1024-entry table is full the range is dropped. `hakios_gpu_unmap()` (3362) polls `TLBSTATUS` at most 1000 times and ignores the result; the memory is released by the caller immediately afterwards, so a context whose invalidate did not complete could still translate to freed pages (NEEDS-HARDWARE).

### G14 Signed overflow (Low, CONFIRMED)

gpu.cpp:260: `when->seconds * (int64_t) NSEC_PER_SEC` overflows for caller-supplied seconds. The wait is still capped at `GPU_PATIENCE_MS`, so the effect is a wrong timeout, not unbounded.

### G15 Long poll with the global lock held (Low, CONFIRMED)

adreno.c:3460-3466: up to 20000 iterations of `sleep_us(100)` with `gGPULock` held (caller `submit()`), blocking every other GPU request for about two seconds when the ring is full (which a client can cause, see G1).

### G16 Cache maintenance direction (Low, NEEDS-HARDWARE)

Before each submission buffers are cleaned and invalidated (`dc civac`, adreno.c:1219-1222 via gpu.cpp:922). After the GPU finishes, CPU readers (display `drawLayer`, `record`) do not invalidate the surface memory. Page-table attributes for GPU accesses are non-cacheable (`PTE_CACHED` is never set in `PTE_CORE`, adreno.c:1177,2399). Whether stale CPU cache lines for surface pages can reappear between submit and completion depends on prefetching and on the bus's coherency, which cannot be established from the repository.

### G17 Close racing a request (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

`clientClose()` (gpu.cpp:538-565) walks `fBuffers` once with the lock dropped inside `gpuWait`; `free()` (567-575) frees the table without releasing any buffer still present. A request that creates a buffer in the gap leaks its memory descriptor and GPU address. IOKit's own serialisation of close against in-flight calls was not verified.

## Checked and found fine

- `externalMethod` input handling in `hakios.gpu.cpp` (1095-1107): the structure size is bounded by `sizeof(r)`, the union is zeroed before the copy, output is clamped to the input size and copied from the zeroed union, so no uninitialised data goes back.
- `submit()` array bounds: `nr_cmds <= 128` and `nr_bos <= 8192` are checked before the `IONew`/`copyin` size multiplication (no overflow possible), `submit_idx < nr_bos` is checked, `submit_offset + size <= b->size` is computed in 64-bit, size and offset are 4-byte aligned, `nr_relocs != 0` is rejected, `addresses[]/words[]` are bounded by 128, the error path unlocks and frees both allocations.
- Ring arithmetic in `hakios_gpu_submit()`/`ring()`/`ring_send()` (adreno.c:2486-2519,3456-3497): fixed packet words (20) plus 4 per IB is below the `26 + 4*count` reservation; wrap-around flushes both halves; free space formula is correct for an empty and a full ring; fence slots (`GPU_TIMES_AT + 16*slot + 8*end`) stay inside the scratch page; the fence compare is wrap-safe for issued fences.
- `gemNew`: size rounding via `round_page_64` cannot wrap to a nonzero value (a wrap gives 0 and is rejected); the kept-buffer path matches size and flags, rewrites the handle slot completely (`bzero`) and keeps counters balanced; `keep()` cannot dereference a NULL victim while the byte accounting is balanced.
- Buffer lifetime across create/free: `freeBuffer`/`reap` release the descriptor and the surface hold exactly once on every branch except the G4 race; the "stuck" branches deliberately leak one reference, and the IOSurface variant retains the parent memory before releasing the sub-range, which keeps the pages alive.
- `newBuffer`: address and handle are returned on failure, the partial mapping is unmapped, and the allocation size is page-granular; `IOSubMemoryDescriptor` range creation is done on `[PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_SIZE + round_page(allocSize))`, which fits inside the memory allocated for non-wrapped surfaces (`PAGE_SIZE + alloc` with `alloc` page-aligned); wrapped surfaces are refused by `surfaceBuffer`.
- `clientMemoryForType`: the descriptor is retained under the lock and only the buffer's own range is exposed (surface buffers expose the pixel range, not the shared-state page).
- Lock order: `gGPULock` is taken before `gSurfaceLock` (via `MiniIOSurfaceDrop`) and nothing takes them the other way round; `gSurfaceKeptLock` is a leaf.
- `MiniIOSurface` per-client operations: `findRef` requires the caller's own reference; `copyValue`/`removeValue` require a NUL-terminated key; `setBulkAttachments` copies at most 0x65 bytes into the 0x70-byte area with the input length checked to 0x88; `returnSurface` checks the output size against `planeCount` (maximum 4, fits the planes array); use counts cannot go negative.
- Page-table code (`space_map`, `space_next`, `space_commit`): the 39-bit check, 1024-table limit, table flush before the SMMU sees entries and use of `dsb` after `dc civac` look correct; the `static` spare-page allocator is always called under `gGPULock` after bring-up.
- `drawLayer`/`drawRows` for in-rectangle reads: the source rectangle is bounded by `info.width/height` (int32 sum overflow cannot yield an accepted value), column indices are bounded by the panel width, blended reads of column `c+1` only happen when `c+1 < sw`; panel writes are clipped to the panel rows and `cx0..cx1`.
- `MiniIOMobileFramebufferShow` (display driver side of `kHakiosShow`): row/column clipping against `vinfo` is correct given `rowBytes >= 4*width` (the allocation size is the problem, see G6).
- Swap queue (`present`/`presenter`/`show`): slots are indexed modulo `SWAP_QUEUE`, surface holds are taken in `present` and dropped once by the presenter, the timeout path returns without leaking a hold.
- Boot-arg parsing in `hakios_adreno_init()`: `adreno_only` is range-checked, `last_step` is clamped to `STEPS`, shift counts are at most 22, the `what[]` index is in range; `gpu_cached`, `gpu_keep`, `touch_lat`, `surftrace*`, `surf_clear` and the framebuffer tunables only select behaviour (`fb_threads`, `fb_queue`, `fb_hz`, `rec_step` are range-checked before use). `rec_mb` is not range-checked (a boot-arg only, outside the user attack surface).
- Firmware loading in `step_gmu_space`/`zap_header`/`step_core_space`/`step_zap_load`: sizes from the file are bounded (`<= PAGE_SIZE` for the mdt header, `<= 0x40000` for the SQE image, `<= 0x1000` for the zap segment, `block.value <= 0x100000` and block count limited to 12 for the GMU) except the 32-bit arithmetic in G12; ELF header fields are checked against the file size before use.
- Unbounded polling loops: all register polls in the files read are counted loops (`wait_for`, the GMU start poll, `ring_run`, `hakios_gpu_stop`); the user-facing waits are bounded by `GPU_PATIENCE_MS`.

## Not checked

- The bring-up steps' register sequences (clocks, RPMh, TrustZone/SCM calls, GMU message queue code `hfi_*`, steps 1-12 and 16-17 beyond skimming), and the quiesce/stop path (`gpu_block_stop`, 2960-3150) other than its interaction with `gpu_kept`.
- Whether XNU zero-fills `IOBufferMemoryDescriptor` memory (the code relies on it), what `IOSubMemoryDescriptor::withSubRange` does with out-of-range arguments, how `OSUnserializeXML` treats size and NUL termination, whether the user mapping of a client's input descriptor is a copy or the live user memory (a double-fetch question for `methodCreate`/`setValue`), and cache attributes of user mappings requested through `IOConnectMapMemory`.
- Whether IOKit serialises `clientClose()` against calls in flight (G17), and whether a user mapping of kernel-shared memory can outlive the `IOMemoryMap` (G9, second part).
- Hardware behaviour: which GPU registers user packets can reach without a protect table, what the SMMU/GBIF coherency model is, and the SMMU TLB timing (G1, G13, G16).
- `hakios.image.c` (`hakios_image_file`) and the callers outside this group (`HakiosGPUStart/Stop` call sites, `loader_return.c`).
- Userland (`userland/src/eagl.c`, `tools/mesa/hakios-drm`) and the display_probe code (`adreno.c:3568-3703`; it only reads and writes two clock-enable bits).
- Cellular modem code (out of scope).

## Fix status

Edited: drivers/gpu/hakios.gpu.cpp, drivers/gpu/hakios.adreno.c, xnu/files/iokit/Kernel/MiniIOSurface.cpp, MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp (MiniIOSurface.h unchanged). Nothing was compiled or run; every edit was re-read for syntax and types.

- G1 SKIPPED. Command-stream validation, CP_PROTECT and kernel-only mappings are a design and hardware matter (register semantics, privilege bit meaning); not invented here.
- G2 FIXED. MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp: new `surfaceHolds()` (64-bit arithmetic) is checked in `drawLayer()` for the rows and columns it reads (offset + (rows-1)*stride + columns*4 must be within allocSize) and in `record()` for the whole display; a surface that does not hold them is not read. This covers a small stride, element height above 1 and a wrapped client size, whatever they were created with. MiniIOSurface.cpp `surfaceCreate()`: wrapped surfaces' owner-given IOSurfaceAllocSize must be non-zero and at most 512 MB (same limit as other surfaces); plane width/height are capped at 16384 and a computed plane size is done in 64 bits and refused above 512 MB. NOT changed: creation still accepts a stride below width*bytes-per-element and the element-height row count, because a client with an unusual element definition would be refused; the read-side check makes both memory-safe.
- G3 FIXED. gpu.cpp `kMsmWaitFence`: a fence ahead of `hakios_gpu_last()` returns kIOReturnBadArgument before `gpuWait()`, so a bad argument can no longer latch `gGPUReported`.
- G4 FIXED. gpu.cpp `freeBuffer()`: the buffer is taken out of its handle (memory/surface NULL, counters decremented) and the rest works on a local copy, before `gpuWait()` can drop the lock; a second close of the handle now gets BadArgument.
- G5 FIXED. MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp `drawLayer()`: destination rectangle computed in 64 bits; one beyond +-16M panel pixels, or wholly off the panel, is not drawn (a layer wholly left of the panel previously computed columns far outside the source row); the row loop and the helper threads' split use the on-panel rows (`ry0/ry1` in `RowJob`), while the scaling still uses the original py0/py1 so partly off-panel layers draw exactly as before.
- G6 FIXED in part. gpu.cpp `show()`: `rowBytes * height` above 256 MB (the buffer maximum) is refused. SKIPPED: per-client and global byte budgets for buffers and surfaces (a policy choice of limits), and the surface table.
- G7 FIXED. MiniIOSurface.cpp `methodCreate()`: `allocSize` copied to a local before the creator's hold is dropped.
- G8 FIXED. MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp `vsync()`: the async send is done with `fLock` held (as the report suggests); `registerNotificationPort()` swaps under the same lock, so the old port is only released after the send. The send uses kIOUserNotifyOptionCanDrop; owner to confirm it cannot block.
- G9 SKIPPED. Ownership and privilege checks on surface IDs are policy, not to be changed here.
- G10 FIXED. MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp `drawLayer()`: on any failed blend-row allocation every array that was made is freed with the size it was made with and set to NULL before the size is reset to 0.
- G11 FIXED in part. gpu.cpp `submit()`: the log no longer prints `addresses[0]`/`words[0]` when `count == 0`. NOT done: rejecting a submission with no command buffer; what the ring does with an empty submission (fence only) was not established, so behaviour is unchanged.
- G12 FIXED. adreno.c `step_gmu_firmware()`: block address + size is computed in 64 bits in both checks (TCM write is refused if the block wraps past 4 GB; memory copy only if the block lies inside a block that was made).
- G13 FIXED in part. adreno.c `hakios_gpu_address_free()`: a range overlapping a free one is refused with a message, so a double free cannot corrupt the list. SKIPPED: the TLB sync result (timing and a recovery action need hardware knowledge).
- G14 FIXED. gpu.cpp `millisecondsUntil()`: seconds*1e9 and the nanosecond add use overflow-checked builtins; an overflowing positive time is the 5 s cap, a negative one is "now".
- G15 SKIPPED. Releasing the global GPU lock while waiting for ring space is a locking-design change.
- G16 SKIPPED. Cache invalidation after GPU writes depends on the SMMU/bus coherency model; NEEDS-HARDWARE.
- G17 SKIPPED. Needs to know whether IOKit serialises `clientClose()` against calls in flight; not established.

```

`docs/driver-review/input.md`:

```md
# Driver review: input and touch

## Scope and method

Read-only audit; this is the only file written.

| File (under xnu/files/bsd/) | Lines | Read |
|---|---|---|
| dev/hakios.input.c | 228 | all |
| dev/hakios.goodix.c | 1515 | all, except the array in hakios.focaltech_fw.h (only its header: `FOCALTECH_FW_LENGTH 116448`, declared as `focaltech_fw[FOCALTECH_FW_LENGTH]`) |
| dev/hakios.buttons.c | 583 | all |
| dev/hakios.virtio_input.c | 365 | all |
| sys/hakios.input.h | 125 | all |

Method: traced the producer path (goodix/focaltech/buttons/virtio thread -> `hakios_touch_post` -> `touch_queue` -> `touch_read` -> `uiomove`), every length that comes from a chip, the SPI engine, the command database or the firmware blob, every polling loop, every boot-arg. Cross-checked the shared hardware (RPMh TCS 0, GCC vote register, SPMI arbiter) against the other drivers in `dev/` by grep. The XNU kernel source itself is not in this tree, so behaviour of kernel primitives (`ml_io_map`, `delay_for_interval`, `uiomove`, `PE_parse_boot_argn`) is assumed to be standard. Nothing was built or run. No hardware facts are asserted beyond what the repository's own comments say.

Confidence: CONFIRMED = path traced end to end in the source; PLAUSIBLE = mechanism is in the source but depends on timing or an input I cannot show occurs; NEEDS-HARDWARE = the code is as described but the effect depends on chip behaviour.

## Findings

| Id | Severity | Confidence | Where | One line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Medium | PLAUSIBLE | goodix.c:203-239 | `rpmh_write` uses RPMh TCS 0 without `hakios_rsc_lock`, which adsp.c and mpss.c take for the same TCS |
| F2 | Medium | CONFIRMED (effect NEEDS-HARDWARE) | goodix.c:1353 | `io_supply_on()` result ignored; analog supply and pins are driven anyway, and a failed bring-up leaves everything powered |
| F3 | Medium | CONFIRMED | input.c:213 | `/dev/hakios-touch` is mode 0666: any process can forge touches and buttons (including Lock) and read everyone's touches |
| F4 | Low | CONFIRMED | input.c:170-176 | A record is dequeued before `uiomove`; a failed copy-out loses it |
| F5 | Low | CONFIRMED | input.c:162-181 | `read()` with fewer than 24 bytes blocks for data, then returns 0 (EOF) without consuming anything |
| F6 | Medium | CONFIRMED (absence); effect NEEDS-HARDWARE | goodix.c:1155-1161 | FocalTech firmware download is bounded but never verified before the application is started |
| F7 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | goodix.c:1222-1227 | FocalTech coordinates are not clamped before mirroring: x above max-1 underflows |
| F8 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | virtio_input.c:260-263 | No load barrier between reading `used->idx` and reading the ring entry and event |
| F9 | Low | CONFIRMED | virtio_input.c:286-312 | Page from `kmem_alloc` leaked, device left half-initialised, on the two failure returns |
| F10 | Low | NEEDS-HARDWARE | goodix.c:1410-1419 | Bit-bang fallback's second attempt drives the pin that the first attempt used as input |

Counts: 6 CONFIRMED (F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F9), 3 PLAUSIBLE (F1, F7, F8), 1 NEEDS-HARDWARE (F10). No memory-safety bug (out-of-bounds, overflow, info leak) was found in the queue or in the SPI buffers; see "Checked and found fine".

## Details

### F1. RPMh TCS 0 used without the shared lock (goodix.c:203-239)

`rpmh_write()` programs command slots in TCS 0 of the application processor's DRV2 (`TCS(reg)` is `rsc + 0xd00 + reg`, goodix.c:122), with no lock. hakios.adsp.c programs the same TCS 0 (`RPMH_TCS 0`, adsp.c:821, 912-937) and mpss.c does too (mpss.c:899-937, 959-991), and both take `hakios_rsc_lock` (defined at wifi.c:192) for exactly this reason (the comment at wifi.c:192 and adsp.c:112 says the sequencer is shared). goodix.c does not reference `hakios_rsc_lock` anywhere.

Scenario: `hakios_input_init()` starts the goodix thread (input.c:219) before adsp/modem init (input.c:226-227). The goodix thread calls `io_supply_on()` -> `rpmh_write()` at the start of `bring_up()`. If the audio-DSP or modem thread reaches its own `rails()` request while that is in flight, the two threads interleave writes of MSGID/ADDR/DATA, ENABLE and TRIGGER on one TCS. The worst outcome is a request mixing one driver's address with the other's data on a power rail (lcx/lmx level, or ldoc2 voltage). The window is short (the goodix request happens within milliseconds of the thread's start), so the likelihood depends on how soon the other threads get that far: PLAUSIBLE.

Fix:
```
+extern lck_mtx_t hakios_rsc_lock;
 static bool rpmh_write(...) {
+	lck_mtx_lock(&hakios_rsc_lock);
 	...
-	return done;
+	lck_mtx_unlock(&hakios_rsc_lock);   /* and on the early "stay busy" return */
+	return done;
```
(`<kern/locks.h>` is needed; goodix.c does not include it today.)

### F2. I/O supply failure ignored; failed bring-up leaves hardware on (goodix.c:1348-1357, 1454-1458)

`power_on()` calls `io_supply_on();` and discards the bool (line 1353). That function returns false when the command database has no `ldoc2` (goodix.c:250-253) or when the TCS stays busy or the request times out (rpmh_write). The code then switches the analog supply on (`gpio_output(PIN_AVDD, true...)`, line 1355), configures the reset and interrupt pins as driven outputs/pull-ups (1351-1352), and goes on to drive SPI pins towards a chip whose I/O rail may be off. Whether back-powering or damage can occur is NEEDS-HARDWARE; the ignored error is CONFIRMED.

Related error path: when `bring_up()` fails the thread prints and calls `thread_terminate` (1454-1458) with AVDD still high, the GCC clock votes still set, and the five `ml_io_map` mappings (1448-1452) never released. Small and one-time, but the chip is left powered with no driver.

Fix:
```
-	io_supply_on();
-	sleep_ms(3);
+	if (!io_supply_on()) { return false; }   /* make power_on() return bool; bring_up() then reports and returns false before touching AVDD */
```
and, in the failure path, drive `PIN_AVDD` low and clear the votes.

### F3. Device node is world read/write (input.c:213)

`devfs_make_node(..., UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "hakios-touch")`; `touch_open` (143-147) does no check. Any process that can open the node (subject to whatever sandbox the Darwin userland applies; not examined here) can:
- `write()` records: forged DOWN/MOVE/UP samples and `HAKIOS_BUTTON_DOWN/UP` with `finger = HAKIOS_BUTTON_LOCK`, which backboardd turns into the power key (inject.c:871-879). Only the five-finger exit is protected (it counts driver fingers only, input.c:130).
- `read()`: steal the real touch stream (any reader takes records away from backboardd, since there is one shared queue with no exclusive open).

Whether this matters depends on the Darwin sandbox profile for third-party apps; in the kernel there is no restriction.

Fix: `0600` (or `0660` with a dedicated group) and, if backboardd runs as another user, set that uid/gid in `devfs_make_node`; optionally make `touch_open` return `EBUSY` for a second opener.

### F4. Record lost when copy-out fails (input.c:170-176)

```
t = touch_queue[touch_head++ % TOUCH_QUEUE];
lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
error = uiomove((caddr_t)&t, sizeof(t), uio);
```
`touch_head` is advanced before the copy. If `uiomove` fails (a user buffer that is partly unmapped, or one the process unmaps concurrently), the sample is gone; if `moved > 0` the function returns 0 and the failure is invisible. A lost UP or DOWN leaves the consumer's finger state stale (inject.c:818-821 ignores non-DOWN events for fingers it believes are up, and keeps a finger down until an UP). Same effect, from the producer side, when the 512-record ring overflows: `touch_head++` at input.c:115-117 drops the oldest record whatever its type. That second case is by design ("nobody reads") and only noted.

Fix: peek first, advance after success (single-reader assumption) or push the record back:
```
-	t = touch_queue[touch_head++ % TOUCH_QUEUE];
+	t = touch_queue[touch_head % TOUCH_QUEUE];
 	unlock; error = uiomove(...); lock;
-	if (error) break;
+	if (error) break;
+	touch_head++;     /* only if it is still the same record: with two readers, re-check head */
```

### F5. Short read returns EOF (input.c:162-181)

The first loop waits until the queue is non-empty regardless of the buffer size. The second loop requires `uio_resid(uio) >= sizeof(t)` (24). With a buffer of 1..23 bytes, `read()` blocks until a sample exists, then returns 0 with nothing consumed, which a caller reads as end of file; callers that retry spin at 100% CPU because the queue stays non-empty. The shipping consumer reads exactly 24 bytes (inject.c:950), so there is no current victim.

Fix: at entry `if (uio_resid(uio) < (user_ssize_t)sizeof(struct hakios_touch)) return EINVAL;`.

### F6. Touch-controller firmware download is bounded but not verified (goodix.c:1101-1124, 1155-1161)

What is bounded: `focaltech_write_pram()` loops `offset < len` in 32-byte chunks, with the last chunk shortened (1106-1110); `len` is `FOCALTECH_FW_LENGTH` (116448, a multiple of 32), the array is declared with exactly that size, and the transfer buffer (71 bytes) holds the largest frame (7 + 32). The 24-bit PRAM address in `addr_bytes` cannot wrap (116448 < 2^24). The sequence is only entered after `focaltech_enter_boot_rom()` has read back the boot ID 0x56 0x62 with a valid CRC (1076-1094).

What is missing: nothing checks the blob or what the chip received before `focaltech_start_app()` makes the boot ROM jump to it (1161). There is no checksum/length/magic check of `focaltech_fw` against a value fixed at build time, no read-back or on-chip check of the written PRAM, and the only per-chunk check is the status byte `rx[3] & 0xa0` (focaltech_write 1000-1001), which is the busy/CRC-error bit of the transfer, not of the content. A corrupted source blob or a dropped/duplicated chunk (retried up to 3 times by `focaltech_write`) is started as is. This download also runs automatically on every cold start where the runtime ID is not yet valid (1144-1167), and again up to three times in total if bring-up falls back to the pin-driven bus (chip_probe is re-run, 1402-1420).

Whether this PRAM download can leave a persistent bad state in the chip's flash is not answerable from the sources here: NEEDS-HARDWARE. The comments (1096-1100) describe it as a RAM upload only.

Fix: generate a CRC-32 (or SHA-256) of the blob next to `FOCALTECH_FW_LENGTH` in hakios.focaltech_fw.h and compare before the first write:
```
+	if (crc32(0, focaltech_fw, FOCALTECH_FW_LENGTH) != FOCALTECH_FW_CRC) { printf(...); return false; }
```
and, if the boot ROM offers a checksum command (the vendor flow does, per its own source; I did not verify here), run it before `focaltech_start_app()`.

### F7. FocalTech coordinates not clamped before mirroring (goodix.c:1222-1227)

`x` is built from a 15-bit field (up to 32767, goodix.c:1265-1268) and the panel size is 10800 (1246). The code's own comment (1191-1192) calls the values 15-bit sub-pixel values. In `focaltech_contact_update` there is no clamp: with `touch_flip` 1 or 3, `x = max_report_x - 1 - x` wraps to about 4.29e9 when `x > 10799`, and `(uint64_t)x * 65535 / 10799` truncated to `uint32_t` is an unrelated number; `touch_post` only clamps values above 65535, so the touch can land anywhere. Without flip, the result exceeds 65535 and is clamped, so only the flip case is wrong. The Goodix path does clamp (`x >= max_x ? 65535 : ...`, line 819). Whether the chip ever reports above the panel size is NEEDS-HARDWARE, hence PLAUSIBLE.

Fix: `if (x > max_report_x - 1) x = max_report_x - 1;` (same for y) before the `switch (flip)`.

### F8. Missing load barrier on the virtio used ring (virtio_input.c:260-263)

```
while (d->seen != *(volatile uint16_t *)&d->used->idx) {
	uint32_t id = d->used->ring[d->seen++ % QUEUE_SIZE].id % QUEUE_SIZE;
	input_event(d, &d->events[id]);
```
The loads of `ring[]` and of `events[id]` are not ordered after the load of `idx` (the ring address depends on `d->seen`, not on the idx load; a control dependency does not order loads on arm64). The return path does have `dmb ish` before `avail->idx++` (265-267). Effect: on a host where the device model runs on another core with weak ordering (QEMU under KVM/HVF), a stale ring entry or event can be read, giving a repeated or wrong sample. Not reproduced; PLAUSIBLE. QEMU-only code (boot-arg `virtio_input=1`).

Fix: `__builtin_arm_dmb(0x9);  /* ISHLD */` after the `idx` read inside the loop, before touching `ring`/`events`. (The ring's `id` is already reduced `% QUEUE_SIZE`, so a bad value cannot index out of `events`.)

### F9. Page leak and half-initialised device on attach failure (virtio_input.c:286-312)

`input_attach` takes a page (286), then returns false at 305 ("features refused") and 312 (queue too small) without `kmem_free` and without resetting the device status (it stays at `FEATURES_OK` or lower, never `FAILED`). The caller just skips the slot (354). Cost: one 4 KiB page per failing slot, at boot, under QEMU only. Fix: `kmem_free(kernel_map, page, PAGE_SIZE); reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, 0x80);` before each `return false`.

### F10. Bit-bang fallback may drive a chip output (goodix.c:1410-1419)

If the serial engine path gets no answer, the driver tries twice by hand: first MOSI=gpio53 out / MISO=gpio52 in, then the reverse, because "which of the two data pins is the input is not written down anywhere" (its own comment). On the second attempt `bitbang_init()` configures gpio52 as a driven output (1413-1415, 565-568). If gpio52 is the chip's MISO output, two drivers fight on one line; the comment at lines 80-83 names 52 as MISO. Duration is short (one probe) but nothing limits the current beyond pin drive strength set at 6 mA. NEEDS-HARDWARE. Fix: probe the second orientation only with the former output pin as a pulled input and read-only for one cycle, or drop the swap now that the pin roles are documented in the same file.

## Checked and found fine

Queue and user space (hakios.input.c, hakios.input.h):
- `struct hakios_touch` is 8+4+4+4+4 = 24 bytes, natural alignment, no padding. Every queue slot is fully written in `touch_post` (time, type, finger, x, y) before it is published under `touch_lock`; the static array is zero-initialised. `touch_read` copies a stack copy of one whole record: nothing uninitialised reaches user space.
- Ring arithmetic: `TOUCH_QUEUE` is 512, `head`/`tail` are `uint32_t` free-running counters, indexed `% 512`; 2^32 is a multiple of 512, so wrap-around is exact. `tail - head == 512` is the full test and is correct across wrap; overflow drops the oldest, never writes past the array.
- Locking: all `head`/`tail`/`fingers_down` accesses are under `touch_lock` (mutex); `msleep` releases it atomically so there is no lost wakeup; `wakeup` after unlock is fine. `touch_post` takes a mutex and calls thread_call APIs: it must not be called from interrupt context, which the header says, and none of the producers (goodix thread, buttons thread, virtio thread_call) does.
- `touch_write` validates `type` in 1..5 before posting and clamps x, y to 65535 in `touch_post`; `finger` is unbounded in the queue but `count_fingers` ignores `finger >= 32` and driver-only posting is required for the exit combo; the consumer bounds `f >= MAX_FINGERS` (inject.c:818).
- `count_fingers`: shifts guarded by `finger >= 32`; `thread_call_enter_delayed`/`cancel` under the lock are safe; `exit_call` is allocated before any driver starts (input.c:216-219).
- `latency_lines()` is only called with the lock held; `hakios_tl` uses a 192-byte buffer with `vsnprintf`.

Goodix chip path:
- `goodix_read`/`goodix_write` reject lengths above 1024; `spi_tx`/`spi_rx` are 8+1024 bytes and the largest frame is 8+1024 / 5+1024. All callers pass constants or values bounded before the call.
- `goodix_probe`: the chip-supplied description length is checked (`40 <= length < 1024`) before the second read; the five-list walk checks `offset >= length` before each `info[offset]`; the following reads at `offset+44..47`, `offset+122+16..19` are guarded by `offset + 48 + 2 <= length` and `offset + 122 + 20 + 2 <= length`; the version string prints use precision (`%.6s`, `%.8s`) on a non-terminated 28-byte buffer, and the offsets stay inside it. The 16-bit-sum check is weak, but the addresses taken from it (`touch_address`, `command_address`) are only used as SPI register addresses of the chip itself.
- `goodix_poll`: `report` is 90 bytes; the first read is 26, the second `8 + 8*count + 2` with `count <= 10` (guard at line 862), maximum 90; `count` 11..15 is refused at line 885 after the header checksum. The ack write is a single zero byte.
- `goodix_report`: finger id >= 10 skipped; `x * 65535 / max_x` cannot overflow `uint32_t` because `x < max_x <= 65535` is tested first; `max_x`/`max_y` come from `le16` and are only adopted if non-zero.
- `goodix_command`: fixed 16-byte buffers, 6x6 bounded attempts, and `command_address == 0` is rejected.
- `geni_transfer`: 200 ms deadline; busy-wait before start bounded (2000 x 100 us, then cancel/abort in `geni_recover`, itself bounded to 2 x 2000 x 100 us); `geni_drain` never writes beyond `length` (guarded by `*received < length`), and the unsigned underflow of `bytes` when `words == 0` is not used because the loop runs zero times; transfer lengths (<= 1032) fit the 24-bit TRANS_LEN registers; `fifo_depth >= 4` is checked before `fifo_depth - 3`, `- 2`.
- Other polling loops all have counters: `rpmh_wait` (2000 x 100 us), the TCS-idle wait (2000), GCC clock wait (1000 x 10 us), SE clock configuration wait (500 x 10 us), `focaltech_wait_valid` (5 x 200 ms), `focaltech_enter_boot_rom` (3 attempts), `focaltech_read` (3 attempts), `goodix_command` (36 looks). The main loop is intentionally endless and sleeps `poll_us` per tick.
- `rpmh_address`: the check `header_offset >= CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000` is vacuous for a `uint16_t`, but the largest possible access is 0x90 + 0xffff + 512 x 24 = 0x13090, inside the 0x20000 mapping, so there is no out-of-range read from a corrupt database. `count > 512` is skipped.
- `rpmh_write` is only called with `count == 3` and 3-element arrays; `(1u << count) - 1` is in range.
- `rcg_rate`: 64-bit intermediate, `cfg >> 8 & 7` indexes an 8-entry table, division guarded by `if (n)`.
- Global `GCC_VOTE` (gcc + 0x52008) is only touched by this driver in the tree (grep over `dev/hakios.*.c`), so the read-modify-write at 310/340 has no other writer. The TLMM per-pin registers used here are not used by other drivers for these pins (not exhaustively checked for every pin number).
- Boot-args: `touchscreen` (1508), `touch_flip` (1511, a mask or a switch value with no out-of-range effect), `touch_poll_us` (range-checked 250..100000 else 8000; `1000000 / poll_us` and `80000 / poll_us` cannot divide by zero; `idle_looks` becomes 0 above 80000 us, which means "look every tick", harmless), `touch_spi_hz` (100 kHz..10 MHz else 1 MHz; the 12-bit divider cannot overflow for the sources this code can pick, <= 600 MHz / 100 kHz = 6000 would, but the chosen source is the lowest preset >= 4 MHz or the crystal, so in practice <= 192), `touch_rate` (only the value 480 acts), `touch_lat`, `touch_flip`. All use `PE_parse_boot_argn` with a 4-byte target.
- FocalTech: `focaltech_read` length bounded by `transfer_length > sizeof(focaltech_tx)` (callers pass 1, 2 or 62; the check could wrap for `length` near 2^32, but no caller can pass that); `focaltech_report` reads at most `report[2+6*9+4] = report[60]` of the 62-byte buffer; the read is CRC-checked before use; `focaltech_write_pram` frames never exceed 7+32. The boot-ROM entry is gated on reading back the boot ID, so the firmware blob is not sent to a chip that does not answer as the FT3680 boot ROM (this is also what protects a Goodix phone if the strap detection is wrong).

Buttons (hakios.buttons.c):
- `spmi_read` takes `count` 1..8 from constant callers (1, 2, 8) and writes `bytes[i]` for `i < count` into buffers of matching size (`is[2]`, `r[8]`, `c[8]`, `&status`); `data[1]` is read only for `count > 4`.
- Channel numbers come from the arbiter's table (`n < channels <= 512`); `ARB_CHANNEL(n)` max 0x10fc < `ARB_CORE_SIZE` 0x1100, `ARB_OWNER(n)` max 0xefc < 0x1000, observer offset `0x80 * 511 + 0x1c` < 0x10000. The version is checked (`>= 5`, `< 7`) before anything else is read.
- The SPMI spin lock is held for at most the 2 ms read timeout, with only MMIO and `mach_absolute_time` inside; nothing sleeps under it. Lock order: `spmi_lock` is a leaf; `touch_lock` is taken after it is dropped.
- Only register reads go to the PMICs (as the file comment says); the single write is the arbiter's command word.
- State (`power`, `volume_*`, `bus`) is touched by the one buttons thread only. `status & PON_KPDPWR` converts to `bool` by non-zero test, so 0x80 is true.
- The "held at start is not believed until seen released" logic matches the comments; the thread ends with `thread_terminate` on all paths.

virtio_input.c:
- `used->ring[...].id % QUEUE_SIZE` bounds the event index; `seen`, `avail->idx` are `uint16_t` and 65536 is a multiple of 64, so wrap-around is exact; the `avail` update has a `dmb ish` before the index bump and one before the notify.
- `command_key`: `name[32]`, `length < 31` guard, NUL written at `name[length]` with `length <= 31`; the key table index is checked against `sizeof(plain) - 1`; the keyboard-typed name is only passed to `ustacks_now` through `%s`/a string argument.
- Static state (`name`, `shift`, ...) is shared by the up-to-four devices but only touched from `input_poll`, which re-arms itself after finishing, so it never runs concurrently with itself.

## Not checked

- Anything outside the five files: the consumer side (userland/src/inject.c) beyond the finger bounds check; `loader_log_line`/`loader_log_putc` (whether they are safe to call while holding `touch_lock`, input.c:124); `loader_return()` and what happens to the endless polling thread when the run ends (the touch thread has no stop flag and keeps polling hardware: goodix.c:1472-1499).
- The kernel's behaviour for `ml_io_map` failure: all `ml_io_map` results are used unchecked (goodix.c:1448-1452, buttons.c:458-460, virtio_input.c:342). Whether it can return 0 here needs the XNU source.
- Any register layout, timing or strap meaning (TLMM, GCC, GENI, RPMh, SPMI arbiter, Goodix Berlin command format, FocalTech boot ROM protocol, PIN_GOODIX_ID/PIN_FOCALTECH_ID being valid for this board) beyond internal consistency with the repository's comments.
- Whether a Goodix finger lift is always reported as a status with the touch bit and zero count: if the chip instead reports status 0, `goodix_poll` returns at line 857 without posting UP and the finger stays down. NEEDS-HARDWARE; a hand test is noted in the buttons comment but not for this.
- The content of `focaltech_fw` (706 KB array) and its provenance.
- Whether the PRAM download can touch persistent flash, and whether the vendor flow's own integrity step exists in the boot ROM.
- The Darwin sandbox profile for `/dev/hakios-touch` (F3 impact).
- Build correctness (flags of `kmem_alloc`, `__builtin_arm_dmb` use) and the other drivers in the tree, other than reading the lines named above for `hakios_rsc_lock`.

## Fix status

Edited: drivers/input/hakios.goodix.c, hakios.input.c, hakios.virtio_input.c. Nothing was compiled or run; every edit was re-read for syntax and types.

- F1 FIXED. goodix.c: `rpmh_write()` now takes `hakios_rsc_lock` (extern declared next to the other externs, `<kern/locks.h>` included) before the first TCS 0 access and releases it on the busy return and at the end.
```
