Same lock the audio DSP and modem drivers take; the lock is a leaf here (nothing else is taken while it is held), so no ordering problem. The mutex is held across `sleep_us`, exactly as adsp.c does.
- F2 FIXED (the ignored error). goodix.c: `power_on()` returns bool and `bring_up()` stops with a message before AVDD or any bus work if `io_supply_on()` fails. NOT done: driving AVDD low and clearing the GCC clock votes when a later bring-up step fails. Power-down order and clock-vote semantics are hardware knowledge; SKIPPED for that part.
- F3 SKIPPED. Mode 0666 of /dev/hakios-touch is policy and was explicitly not to be changed.
- F4 FIXED. input.c `touch_read()`: if `uiomove` fails, the dequeued record is put back at the head (only if the ring still has room, so it can never overwrite a live slot).
- F5 FIXED. input.c `touch_read()`: a zero-length read returns 0, a read of 1..23 bytes returns EINVAL instead of blocking and then returning EOF. Reads of 24 bytes or more behave as before.
- F6 SKIPPED. A checksum of the FocalTech firmware needs a value generated at build time for hakios.focaltech_fw.h (not a file I may edit) and, for an on-chip check, knowledge of the boot ROM protocol that cannot be established from the repository.
- F7 FIXED. goodix.c `focaltech_contact_update()`: x and y are clamped to `max_report - 1` before the flip, so the mirroring cannot underflow. In range values and the unflipped case are unchanged (an out-of-range value was already ending at 65535).
- F8 FIXED. virtio_input.c `input_poll()`: `__builtin_arm_dmb(0x9)` (ISHLD) after the `used->idx` check, before the ring entry and the event are read.
- F9 FIXED. virtio_input.c `input_attach()`: both failure returns now write STATUS_FAILED (0x80, new define) to the device and `kmem_free` the page. The device was never given the queue on those paths.
- F10 SKIPPED. Which of gpio52/gpio53 is the chip's output is hardware knowledge, and dropping or changing the probe order is a behaviour decision for the owner.

```

`docs/driver-review/loader.md`:

```md
# Review: boot loader (xnuloader/loader.c)

## Scope and method

Files read (read-only; nothing built, nothing run, no git state touched):

| file | lines |
|---|---|
| xnuloader/loader.c | 4135 (read in full for the parts below; the UFS survey/GPT diagnostics 1100-1440 and the battery/charger code only skimmed) |
| xnuloader/efi.h | 298 (struct layouts, EFI_FILE_INFO offset, allocate_pages/free_pages signatures) |
| xnuloader/mkpayload.py | 59 (payload producer: are text entries NUL-terminated, what does `size` mean) |
| tools/mkesp.py | 96 (payload validator on the host side) |
| docs/uefi-boot.md | read for what the doc claims about the payload region |

Method: traced the USB command path (usb_command_loop / usb_poll_command -> fb_command), then every user of host-controlled
bytes (command text, `download:` size and data, the payload header/entries, the payload's cmdline), then
load_payload_from_volume(), block_poll()/block_start(), the memory-map code, the device-tree writer and the kernel
command-line assembly. Each finding below was traced from input to effect in the source; where an effect depends on
hardware or firmware behaviour that this repository does not state, the confidence is NEEDS-HARDWARE.

Threat-model note that affects every severity below. The USB host chooses the payload, and the payload contains the
kernel that the loader then jumps to (and the cmdline, including `ufs_write=1`, `ufs_native=`, `physbase`). A hostile host
therefore already has code execution at EL1 with the MMU off and direct UFS controller access through `ufs_native=`. Memory-safety
flaws in payload parsing are consequently robustness/brick-avoidance problems (a malformed or truncated payload corrupting
the loader, the kernel window or boot_args; a wedged loader), not privilege escalations over a trusted loader. The same holds
for block_write's guard: it protects darwin's first 2042368 blocks and the other partitions against a buggy kernel, not against a
malicious one. I rate with that in mind. Findings that matter even for a benign host (wrong state, truncated file,
stale data) are rated higher than ones that need a deliberately lying payload.

## Findings

| id | severity | confidence | where | one line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | medium | CONFIRMED | loader.c:2255, 3627, 3630, 3548 | "busy" is `running_live != NULL`, but running_live is NULL for any kernel without a kernel_live block; then download/oem run/oem ramdisk are accepted while the kernel runs |
| L2 | medium | CONFIRMED | loader.c:4005-4016, 4123 | failed volume read frees the pages but leaves a valid XNUP header there; efi_main then boots the torn payload |
| L3 | medium | NEEDS-HARDWARE | loader.c:3997-4001, 3679, 3188 | volume load claims only `pages` of the file, but `download:` and the panic-log memset use the whole 63/64 MiB |
| L4 | low-medium | CONFIRMED | loader.c:2523-2551, 2832-2833, 3993 | payload header size and entry sizes are never checked against the file/region; ramdisk memcpy can read up to 4 GiB past the payload |
| L5 | low-medium | CONFIRMED | loader.c:2751-2827 | Mach-O segment extents unchecked (vmaddr+vmsize wrap, filesize>vmsize, cmdsize 0, fileoff): arbitrary physical writes before the kernel starts |
| L6 | low | CONFIRMED | loader.c:2787-2812 | `rdres` (resident_rd_size) has no upper bound; rounding and `dt_pa` arithmetic can wrap |
| L7 | low | CONFIRMED | loader.c:398-408, 2809, 3049, 3287 | device-tree writer has no bound; dt_len never compared with the 64 KiB reserved; boot_args sits right after it and is written first |
| L8 | low | CONFIRMED / NEEDS-HARDWARE | loader.c:3600-3606, 3647, 3685, 3696-3701 | `download:` to the resident area accepts >= 4 GiB but replies with 32 bits; received count `r` is not clamped to `want` |
| L9 | low | CONFIRMED | loader.c:3664-3667, 3694-3710 | `oem ramdisk none` leaves the ramdisk download armed; a failed `download:` leaves a half-overwritten payload with a valid header |
| L10 | low | CONFIRMED | loader.c:2868-2871, 1984, 2988 | flags that are not reset per run: hc_requested, block_probe_requested, block_enabled (stale page and ufs_shared_pa offered to a run that did not ask) |
| L11 | low | CONFIRMED | loader.c:266, 1391, 1406, 1877, 1894 | every locate_handle_buffer() result is leaked (no free_pool anywhere); find_log_partition() runs on every log write |
| L12 | low | PLAUSIBLE | loader.c:2090-2094 | block_poll takes bounds (parts, blocks, block_size, read twice) from the kernel-writable shared page; the write guard itself uses loader-private state and is sound |

No finding lets the USB host write outside the documented regions through the command parser itself: `download:` is bounded to
PAYLOAD_BASE..+63 MiB or to the resident area (L8 covers the one assumption it makes).

## Details

### L1 (medium, CONFIRMED) busy state is lost when the kernel has no kernel_live block

- Code: `running_live = live;` (loader.c:2255, in run_on_other_cpu) and `int busy = running_live != NULL;` (3627).
  `live` is `kernel_live`, which run_kernel sets only if it finds KERNEL_LIVE_MAGIC while scanning the loaded kernel
  (2891-2898); otherwise it stays NULL and is passed on at 3329.
- Scenario: payload with `usb`, cmdline `bootcpu=N` (kernel on another core) and a kernel image that does not contain the
  magic (older kernel, the QEMU hello kernel). run_on_other_cpu still polls the host every pass (`usb_poll_command()` at
  2348, which only checks `USB == NULL`). fb_command is entered with busy == 0, so:
  - `download:` writes to PAYLOAD_BASE or, after `oem ramdisk`, over the resident root image at win_base+0x08000000 while that
    kernel is running and using it as its root device;
  - `oem run` re-enters run_kernel: it memsets and rewrites the kernel segments under the running kernel and overwrites
    loader_ctx (the saved return context of the first run), so the first kernel's return lands in the wrong frame;
  - `oem stop` does nothing (3636 requires busy), so the run cannot be ended from the host;
  - usb_wait's 3 s give-up (3548) is also keyed to running_live != NULL, so a nested `download:` whose host goes quiet blocks the
    watcher forever (it only pets the watchdog), and the kernel's return is never noticed.
- Fix (text diff):
  ```
  -static const struct kernel_live *running_live;
  +static const struct kernel_live *running_live;
  +static int run_active;                  /* set for the whole of run_on_other_cpu(), live block or not */
   ...run_on_other_cpu():
  -	running_live = live;
  +	running_live = live; run_active = 1;
   ...
  -	running_live = NULL;
  +	running_live = NULL; run_active = 0;
   ...fb_command():
  -	int busy = running_live != NULL;
  +	int busy = run_active;
   ...  "oem stop": if (busy && running_live) ...
   ...  "oem log":  if (busy && running_live) compose_live_log(...); else compose_logs(NULL, 0);
   ...usb_wait(): if (run_active && ...) return -1;
  ```

### L2 (medium, CONFIRMED) a failed or short volume read leaves a valid payload header behind

- Code: loader.c:4002-4009. The first 1 MiB chunk is read to PAYLOAD_BASE (so `magic == XNUP` is already in memory); if a later
  `file->read` fails or returns 0, the code sets the note, calls `BS->free_pages(PAYLOAD_BASE, pages)` and returns 0. Nothing clears
  the header and free_pages does not scrub. efi_main then calls `parse_payload(&pi, 0)` (4123), which only tests
  `ph->magic == PAYLOAD_MAGIC` at PAYLOAD_BASE (2519) and returns 1.
- Scenario: a payload.bin larger than 1 MiB on a flaky card/USB stick, or a volume that returns an error on the second read.
  Screen says "payload: none in memory, and ... could not be read to its end" (4096), yet the loader goes on to run_kernel with the
  truncated payload (the kernel Mach-O or ramdisk is cut off, the rest of it is whatever the freed pages held) or enters the USB
  loop. The same applies to the `magic != XNUP` path only if the header was valid, which it is not, so that path is fine.
- Fix:
  ```
  	if (EFI_ERROR(file->read(...)) || chunk == 0) {
  		volume_payload_note = "...could not be read to its end";
  +		((struct payload_header *)PAYLOAD_BASE)->magic = 0;
  		BS->free_pages(PAYLOAD_BASE, pages);
  		goto close;
  ```
  Also validate `ph->size` there (see L4).
- Handle handling in this function is otherwise right: every path after a successful `open` reaches `close:` exactly once; `root` is
  closed on the open-failure return; no double close; pages are freed on every failure after allocation.

### L3 (medium, NEEDS-HARDWARE) volume load claims only the file's pages, the rest of the region is used anyway

- Code: `pages = (size + 0xfff) / 0x1000; allocate_pages(AllocateAddress, ..., pages, &address)` (3997-3998), i.e. only the bytes
  of the file. But `download:` writes up to `PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE - 0x100000` (3679-3680) at PAYLOAD_BASE, run_kernel zeroes the
  panic log at PANIC_LOG_BASE = PAYLOAD_BASE+63 MiB, 512 KiB (3187-3188), and choose_window() assumes the whole 64 MiB is outside any
  allocation (2669, 2685-2691). docs/uefi-boot.md:47-51 says "the loader's payload region is 64 MiB"; with the shim or QEMU the
  region is placed and (per the comment at 42) reserved in the memory map; in the volume case the success of AllocateAddress
  implies the region was NOT reserved.
- Scenario: payload.bin (say 15 MiB) from a volume, with a `usb` entry. usb_start() then allocates two 1 MiB transfer buffers
  (3516-3517), and other drivers allocate; any of them may land in the unclaimed 48 MiB. A following `download:` of a larger
  payload overwrites them mid-transfer (corrupt data or wedged USB), and the panic-log memset zeroes whatever lives at
  0xF3F00000. Whether the firmware's allocator hands out those pages is firmware behaviour: not stated in this repository.
- Fix: claim the whole region when the loader will use it, e.g. allocate `PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE >> 12` pages (fall back to the file's
  pages and refuse `usb` mode / panic log if the full claim fails), or at least claim PANIC_LOG_BASE separately.

### L4 (low-medium, CONFIRMED) payload sizes are never validated against the payload

- parse_payload (2523-2551) and payload_kernel_version (4037-4048): `pend = p + ph->size` is only used to stop the walk;
  `ph->size` is not compared with the file size (volume: 3993 checks only `size >= 8` and `<= 63 MiB`), nor with
  PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE, and no entry is checked for `p + sizeof(entry) + e->size <= pend`.
- Arithmetic itself (what you asked for): `e->size` is uint32_t and `15` is int, so `(e->size + 15) & ~15u` is evaluated in 32 bits.
  For `e->size` in 0xFFFFFFF1..0xFFFFFFFF it wraps to 0 and `p` advances 24 bytes (no loop, no hang; the next "entry" is parsed out of
  the current entry's data). For 0x...F0 or below `p += 24 + up to 4 GiB` in 64-bit pointer arithmetic: cannot wrap, the loop condition
  `p + 24 <= pend` then ends the walk. Both are safe from loops; neither rejects the entry. (tools/mkesp.py:49-50 uses Python
  integers, so for those sizes it parses differently from the loader.)
- Effects: (a) `pi->ramdisk = p + 24; pi->ramdisk_size = e->size` (2534-2535) is used as `memcpy((void *)rd_pa, pi.ramdisk, pi.ramdisk_size)` (2833).
  The destination is bounded (2813 checks the window), the source is not: a ramdisk entry claiming up to 4 GiB reads beyond the payload
  into whatever follows (stale RAM, the loader's own image, possibly unmapped or device memory -> exception -> reset). The
  kernel-version walk and the banner read the same stale memory. (b) With `ph->size` larger than the file, an entry walk without a
  terminator continues through unclaimed memory (fresh AllocatePages memory is not zeroed).
- Names that are not NUL-terminated within 16 bytes: str_eq stops at the literal's NUL, so lookups never read past the 24-byte header;
  only the verbose `print("%s", e->name)` (2531) runs on into the size field and data until a NUL (bounded by log_buf's check in put_char).
- Text values (`cmdline`, `kernel.ver`, `physbase`, `rdres`, `checkpoint`): mkpayload.py always appends a NUL inside the entry and pads, but the
  loader does not check it. Reads of an unterminated value run to the next NUL anywhere in memory. All writes derived from them are
  bounded: the cmdline copy by `n < BOOT_LINE_LENGTH - 1`, hakios_kver by `n + need < BOOT_LINE_LENGTH - 1` with `need` from the same str_len.
  `parse_number` wraps silently on long digit strings (no overflow trap) and returns 0 when there are no digits; no memory effect.
- Fix: in load_payload_from_volume, `if (ph->size > size - 8) fail`; in parse_payload and payload_kernel_version bound `pend` by a
  caller-supplied limit (volume size, or the download size recorded at `download:` time; fall back to PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE - 1 MiB) and add
  `if ((uint64_t)e->size > (uint64_t)(pend - (p + sizeof(*e)))) break;` with the 64-bit rounding
  `(((uint64_t)e->size + 15) & ~15ULL)`; for `ramdisk`/`kernel` require the whole entry inside; for text entries require a NUL within `e->size`.

### L5 (low-medium, CONFIRMED) Mach-O segments are loaded without bounds

- Code: first pass 2751-2767, load pass 2820-2827. `vm_hi = sg->vmaddr + sg->vmsize` can wrap; `vm_lo` is only compared with the low
  limit; the load does `memset(vmaddr + slide, 0, vmsize); memcpy(vmaddr + slide, kernel + fileoff, filesize)` with no check that
  `vmaddr+vmsize` is inside `[kern_lo, kern_hi)` (it is not if it wrapped), that `filesize <= vmsize` (a larger file size writes past
  kern_hi into the resident image, device tree or boot_args), or that `fileoff + filesize` is inside the payload. `lc->cmdsize == 0`
  keeps `lc` in place for `ncmds` (up to 2^32) iterations; `ncmds`/`cmdsize` are not checked against `sizeofcmds` or the payload. LC_UNIXTHREAD
  reads 17 words without checking cmdsize.
- Scenario: a payload whose kernel is truncated, corrupt or made for another link layout; or a second segment with a high vmaddr. The
  loader writes into physical memory outside the window it claimed (its own image, UEFI, the payload being read), and the failure is a reset
  or a silent corruption, not a diagnostic.
- Fix: after the extent pass `if (vm_hi < vm_lo || kern_hi > win_base + win_size) fail;` and per segment require
  `filesize <= vmsize`, `vmaddr >= vm_lo`, `vmaddr + vmsize <= vm_hi` (no wrap), `fileoff + filesize <= kernel_len` (needs L4's
  entry bound), and `cmdsize >= sizeof(struct load_command)` and `cmdsize <= sizeofcmds - consumed`.

### L6 (low, CONFIRMED) resident image size from `rdres` is unbounded

- Code: `if (pi.resident_rd != 0) resident_rd_size = pi.resident_rd;` (2787-2789), then `res_size = (resident_rd_size + 0x3fff) & ~0x3fff` (2792),
  `dt_pa = rd1_pa + rd1_size` (2808), `top`, and the check `win_size < top - phys_base + 0x4000000` (2813). The `download:` path caps the size at
  `win_size - OFFSET - RESERVE` (3685), the `rdres` path does not. For `rdres` >= 2^64 - 0x3fff the rounding wraps to 0
  (resident entry with size 0, kernel starts without a root). For `rdres` near 2^64 - 0x108000000, `rd1_pa + rd1_size` wraps, `top - phys_base`
  becomes small, the 2813 check passes and the device tree and boot_args are written at a wrapped `dt_pa` inside the kernel's own segments.
  The value also persists in `resident_rd_size` for later runs (it is a static), even when the next payload has no `rdres`.
- The overlap check itself is right for what it covers: `kern_hi + rd_size > res_pa` (2794) uses 64-bit values from sizes that are bounded by 2813
  except for the wrap above.
- Fix: `if (resident_rd_size > win_size - RESIDENT_RD_OFFSET - RESIDENT_RD_RESERVE) fail;` right after the assignment (and check
  `win_size > OFFSET + RESERVE` first).

### L7 (low, CONFIRMED) device-tree writer has no bound

- Code: dt_prop (399-408) writes `36 + ((len+3)&~3)` bytes at `w->cur` without comparing with an end; `dt_len` is computed at 3287 and never compared with
  `dt_max = 0x10000` (2809), the space reserved before boot_args (`ba_pa = dt_pa + dt_max`). boot_args is memset and fully filled
  (2921-3045) BEFORE the tree is written (3049...), so an oversized tree silently overwrites commandLine, bootFlags etc. Names of 32 or more
  characters would run into the length field (memcpy of `str_len(name)` bytes into a 32-byte field).
- Bound on actual content: everything except identity.h is constant (8 KiB NVRAM image + a few KB, at most 8 cpu nodes). identity.h is generated
  from the builder's own IPSW (not in the repository, see build.sh/mkidentity.py), so its size cannot be established here; `mkidentity.py` copies
  property values without a size limit, names are Apple's (31 chars). Probability low, consequence a corrupt boot with no message.
- Depth: counts[16], deepest nesting used is 3: fine. `dt_prop_padded`'s 64-byte `field` takes at most 17 characters + the 32-byte size: fine.
- Fix: give dt_writer an `end` pointer, make dt_prop refuse (set an `overflow` flag) when `cur + 36 + padded > end`, and
  `if (w.overflow || dt_len > dt_max) { print("device tree too big\n"); return 0; }` before using it.

### L8 (low, CONFIRMED / NEEDS-HARDWARE) `download:` size reply and chunk accounting

- 32-bit reply: fb_reply_data (3600-3606) prints only the low 32 bits. The resident-area limit (3685) is `win_size - 0x08000000 - 0x30000000`, up to
  0x148000000 (win_size max 6 GiB, 2704). A host asking for `download:100000000` .. limit is accepted and answered `DATA00000000`; the loader waits for
  the full count while the host sends none, then the next command is swallowed as data (into the resident area) and the transfer ends "short download".
  `getvar:max-download-size` says 0xffffffff in this mode (3647) even though the real limit can be lower or higher. Fix: `if (limit > 0xffffffffULL) limit = 0xffffffffULL;`
  and advertise `limit`.
- r not clamped (NEEDS-HARDWARE): `r = usb_rx(usb_rx_buf, want)` then `memcpy(dest + got, usb_rx_buf, r)` (3696-3701) and `got += r`. If the controller ever
  reports more than `want` (a USB 3 burst delivering more than the request; not stated anywhere in this repository), the memcpy runs past `total`,
  and past `limit` at the end of the region, and reads past the 1 MiB receive buffer. Fix: `if (r > (int64_t)want) r = (int64_t)want;`.
- `parse_number` on `download:`: overflow wraps (17+ hex digits), "no digits" gives 0 -> "bad size". Wrapped values are small and are used consistently as
  `total`, so there is no memory effect, only a surprising size.

### L9 (low, CONFIRMED) command-state slips

- `oem ramdisk none` (3664-3667) returns after clearing resident_rd_size but does not clear `download_to_ramdisk`. Sequence `oem ramdisk`, `oem ramdisk none`,
  `download:<payload>`: the payload goes over the resident area (and `resident_rd_size = total`, the next kernel gets the payload file as md0) instead of
  to PAYLOAD_BASE. Fix: `download_to_ramdisk = 0;` in that branch.
- A `download:` to PAYLOAD_BASE writes straight over the live payload (3700). If it fails ("short download", cable event, 3703-3710) the old header may still be
  valid but its entries/tail are a mix of new and old data; `oem run` then parses that. Fix: zero `ph->magic` at the start of the download and write it
  back only when `got == total`.
- Parser/command state otherwise: `oem stop` when idle is a no-op; `oem run` when not busy runs; `reboot`, `oem hang`, `upload`, `oem log` while busy are by design.
  After OTHER_CPU_HUNG (3336-3342) run_on_other_cpu has cleared running_live, so the loader reports idle and accepts `download:`/`oem run` while a hung kernel
  may still be alive on its core; the only warning for a core left running (3373-3380) is on the came-back path. PLAUSIBLE: add a "kernel_may_be_alive" flag, set on
  HUNG, that makes fb_command refuse download/run/ramdisk until `reboot`.

### L10 (low, CONFIRMED) flags that outlive the run that set them

- run_kernel resets gamut_p3, block_write_requested and block_write_part per run (2849-2853) with the comment that the loader stays resident. Three
  similar states are not reset: `hc_requested |= ...` (2871; only |= exists, never `= 0`), `block_probe_requested |=` (2868), and `block_enabled` (set at 1984, never
  cleared). Effect: a run that asks for `ufs=2` after one that had `ufs_native=1` gets the kernel-owned transfer list offered (1966, 1768) without asking; a run
  that does NOT ask for ufs=2 after one that did still gets `ufs_shared_pa=0x...` appended to its command line (2988) and is still served by block_poll
  (2345-2349) from the stale page (read-only: block_write_part is -1 so writes are refused; `write_part_plus_one` in the stale page still says otherwise, so a
  kernel would try and be refused).
- Fix: `hc_requested = 0; block_probe_requested = 0; block_enabled = 0;` next to 2849-2853.

### L11 (low, CONFIRMED) pool leak

- `BS->locate_handle_buffer` allocates the handle array from the pool; `free_pool` is not called anywhere in loader.c (it is only declared in efi.h:50). Sites: 266
  (find_log_partition, called from every write_logs; flush_log runs every 2 s for 24 s of each other-core run, 2285-2294), 1391/1406 (ufs_survey), 1877/1894 (block_start).
  A phone with ~100 GPT partitions leaks ~0.8 KB per call, order of 10 KB per run, with the loader resident across many runs. Fix: `BS->free_pool(handles)` after use.

### L12 (low, PLAUSIBLE) block_poll relies on kernel-writable fields for bounds

- Code: 2090-2094 reads `block_shared.parts`, `block_shared.part[part].block_size` (twice: once in the `count <=` test, once for `bytes`) and `.blocks` from the page the kernel can
  write (it is the kernel's mailbox, same page, 8 KB aligned). The write guard is not among them and is sound: `block_write_part` and `BLOCK_WRITE_FIRST` are loader statics, `lba + count`
  is checked by subtraction (no overflow: `count <= 4 MiB / block_size`), there is exactly one `write_blocks` for the kernel (2123), the other is the logdump write (361), and
  block_start sets block_write_part only for the entry that passes block_is_darwin (1927-1929). What a kernel that corrupts the page (a stray store, or a data race against the
  re-read of block_size between 2090 and 2094) can do: pass `bytes > BLOCK_BUFFER_SIZE` to read_blocks/write_blocks (write beyond or read from beyond block_buffer) or an `lba`
  past the end of darwin (then only UEFI's own partition bound stops it, as the comment at 1454 says).
- Fix: keep a loader-private copy (`static uint32_t priv_block_size[]; static uint64_t priv_blocks[]`) or read them from `block_bios[part]->media` (block_size, last_block + 1), and read each once into locals.

## Checked and found fine

Command parser
- usb_command_loop (3835-3857) and usb_poll_command (3802-3832): the receive is 511 bytes into a 1 MiB buffer (3516), the copy into `cmd[128]` is clamped to 127 and NUL-terminated both places
  (3828-3830, 3850-3854); a longer command is truncated, not overflowed. No command takes an argument longer than 127 bytes (the longest is a number).
- starts_with (3610-3618) never reads past the NUL of `s`; prefix matching is loose ("oem runX" runs, "rebootfoo" reboots) but harmless. `cmd + 9`, `cmd + 7`, `cmd + 11`, `c[8]`, `c[9]`, `c[11]` accesses happen only after
  the prefix matched, so they read at most the NUL.
- `getvar:` replies: fb_reply copies at most 63 text characters into usb_tx_buf (1 MiB); the `screen` reply goes through print and restores log_len; log_buf[log_len] is in range
  because put_char keeps log_len <= sizeof-1 (177).
- `download:` bounds: PAYLOAD_BASE target limited to 0x03f00000 = PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE - 1 MiB (never touches the panic-log MiB) and equal to the advertised max-download-size; ramdisk target limited
  to `win_size - 0x08000000 - 0x30000000` with `win_size > OFFSET + RESERVE` verified at `oem ramdisk` time (3671) and win_size never shrinking (choose_window returns early once set);
  `total == 0` and `total > limit` rejected before any write; `to_ramdisk` consumed once (3681-3683); resident_rd_size zeroed before a ramdisk transfer and set only on full success (3687, 3704-3706).
- `oem ramdisk`, `oem run`, `oem selftest`, `oem hang`, `oem recording`, `oem sound`, `oem clearscreen`, `oem memmap` are refused while busy (3630-3633) when `busy` is true (see L1 for when it is not).
  `oem ramdisk none` while busy is also refused because it begins with "oem ramdisk".
- parse_number (2498-2510): no digits -> 0; invalid character stops; arithmetic wraps without UB (unsigned); callers: download size (checked afterwards), checkpoint (only compared with 999 and stored), physbase, rdres.
- `oem run [N]`: `arg = cmd + 7` is within the command; checkpoint 999 maps to the self-test path as `oem selftest` does.
- upload: `staged_len` chunks of at most 1 MiB copied into usb_tx_buf (3714-3720); out_buf is 2 MiB and staged_len is clamped by compose_logs (312-314) and compose_live_log's PUT (1011-1018)
  with `n <= room` invariant (n starts at log_len <= 32767); the log text written to logdump is at most about 2 MiB - 8 KiB + 4 KiB rounding, below sizeof(out_buf).

Payload parsing
- Termination: every iteration advances `p` by at least 24 bytes (size wrap gives 0 padding, not negative); no infinite loop; no 64-bit pointer wrap. Entry header is fully inside `[p, pend)`
  before it is read (`p + 24 <= pend`).
- str_eq against literals never reads beyond the literal's length + 1, so a name without a NUL in 16 bytes is not over-read by matching.
- The cmdline scans in run_kernel (2854-2873, 2899-2906, 2937-2939, 2959-2960, 2975-2977) test `c[-1]` only for `c > pi.cmdline` (via `c == pi.cmdline ||`), and never read past a NUL.
  `loader_return_after=` digit loop stops at NUL; `kernel_budget` can wrap with 20+ digits (only effect: stops petting the watchdog sooner).
- mkpayload.py NUL-terminates every text entry inside the entry's size and pads to 16; its header size covers the 24-byte terminator; mkesp.py's PAYLOAD_LIMIT equals the loader's
  `PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE - 0x100000`.

Volume loader (load_payload_from_volume, 3962-4022)
- Size: read from get_info at offset 8 (efi.h:207 documents it), `size >= 8` and `<= 63 MiB` enforced before allocation; `pages` rounded up correctly; `info` is 512 bytes (only a short file name is returned; a
  BUFFER_TOO_SMALL would just fail into the "cannot be read" note).
- The read loop reads at most 1 MiB at a time at `PAYLOAD_BASE + done`, handles short reads, stops on `chunk == 0`, and never exceeds `size`.
- Close paths: `root->close` on open failure; `file`/`root` closed exactly once at `close:` on all later paths (including success); no handle leaked and none closed twice; the pages are freed on both
  read failure and bad magic; success keeps them on purpose. (The one defect on these paths is the stale header, L2.)

Block service
- Only one kernel-reachable `write_blocks` (2123) and it is behind `block_write_part >= 0 && part == block_write_part && lba >= BLOCK_WRITE_FIRST`; `lba + count` overflow is excluded by `count <= blocks - lba`;
  `bytes = count * block_size` cannot exceed 4 MiB given the same block_size; unknown `op` touches nothing (2144-2146); division by a zero block_size yields 0 on AArch64 and the request is refused.
- block_write_part is the index of the entry in `block_shared.part[]` at the time block_is_darwin passed (1927-1928, before `parts++`); units are appended after the partitions so indices do not shift; limits:
  `parts + nunits < 160`, `nunits <= 16`. block_is_darwin requires exact name "darwin" (7 bytes compared, ufs_name maps non-ASCII to '?'), both GUIDs, start/end LBA, unit 0, block size 4096, block count, not read-only.
  A second partition cannot pass it (unique GUID).
- Per-run reset of block_write_requested/block_write_part (2852-2853) holds; a run without `ufs_write=1` has writes refused even if the page is stale (L10 notes the page contents).
- The tally reset (1973) and the answer/mailbox handshake (request volatile, dmb before `answered`) are consistent.

Memory map / window
- choose_window's exclusion of PAYLOAD_BASE..+64 MiB (2685-2691) is correct for all four overlap shapes; the unsigned `pay_lo - lo` only matters where `pay_lo > lo` is also tested. A descriptor that
  ends inside the payload region is dropped rather than trimmed (loses memory, never overlaps). `claim` goes through AllocateAddress, so the firmware refuses overlap; `best_size >> 12 == 0` fails cleanly.
- `win_size < top - phys_base + 64 MiB` (2813) is the single check that makes the DT, boot_args, kernel and payload ramdisk copies land inside the window, given kern_hi is sane (L5) and the resident size
  is bounded (L6).
- print_memory_map: `totals[d->type]` guarded by `type < 16`; `get_memory_map` failure is handled; a 64 KiB static buffer is used.

Command line (BOOT_LINE_LENGTH 608)
- All base pieces (2964-2987) and the two `*_shared_pa=0x%016x` pieces (2993-3013) check `n < BOOT_LINE_LENGTH - 1` per character, so none can write past index 606; ba was memset to 0, so index 607 stays NUL.
- hakios_kver (3015-3031): `need = 12 + strlen + 1`, tested with `n + need < 607` before any byte is written; the copy writes at most `need` bytes (the loop stops at a space, so possibly fewer); the else branch
  prints the warning and writes nothing. No overflow, no uninitialised read. The cmdline tail (3037-3044) is bounded by the same limit; the truncation warning prints `str_len(rest)` correctly and the
  `print` arguments are cast to uint64_t as print's `%d`/`%x` require. A value with a tab or other whitespace in kernel.ver is passed through (only ' ' ends it); whether the kernel's boot-arg parser treats
  those as separators is not in this repository (no isargsep found), so not decided here.
- The loader's own `ufs_write=1` / `ufs_native=` detection requires a preceding space or start of line; the kernel could accept other separators, which can only make the loader stricter (writes refused), not looser.

Device tree
- Depth never exceeds 3; `dt_prop_padded` field is 64 bytes for strings of at most 17 characters; per-property copy uses the same padded length as the memset; names written by the loader itself are all < 32 characters.

## Not checked

- Hardware behaviour: whether PAYLOAD_BASE..+64 MiB is free or reserved on the phone, whether the USB controller can return `bytes_completed > requested`, how Qualcomm's block I/O bounds a partition, cache state of the
  panic-log region that run_kernel zeroes (3188) with the data cache on while the cache-clean loop (3309-3320) only covers some memory-map types (NEEDS-HARDWARE; not traced).
- identity.h is not in the tree (generated from the builder's IPSW), so the device tree's real size and the property names/lengths could not be measured (L7).
- The kernel-supplied fields: kernel_live (log/log_len/log_head/log_ring pointers and offsets, recording and sound pointers and lengths up to 1 GiB used by `upload` and write_logs, loader_ctx log pointer/length printed
  unclamped when there is no log partition). They come from the kernel the host chose, so I treated them as trusted (see the threat-model note).
- USB device protocol details of the Qualcomm stack (usb_start, descriptors, handle_event semantics), the UFS host-controller take-back code (hc_*), the charger/battery code, the Block I/O 2 probe, ramfb/fw_cfg code (QEMU only),
  the assembly (loader_save_ctx, return stubs, other_cpu_entry), the watchdog SMC code and the exception hook. Only skimmed or not read.
- The ufs_survey/ufs_check_gpt/ufs_dump_super diagnostics read flash-controlled GPT/liblp data; I looked at their size arithmetic (all reads stay inside the 1 MiB ufs_buffer) but did not audit them line by line.
- docs/ and Makefile/qemu scripts beyond what is quoted above; tools/darwin-write.py (the build side of the darwin identity constants).

## Fix status

Each finding was re-read in the current tree first. Nothing was built or run; edits were re-read for syntax only. All edits are in `xnuloader/loader.c`. The write guard (`block_is_darwin`, the write branch of `block_poll`, the `ufs_write=` parse) was not touched.

- L1: FIXED. New `run_active` flag, set for the whole of `run_on_other_cpu()`. `fb_command` (`busy`) and `usb_wait` (the 3 s give-up) use it; `oem stop` and `oem log` still need `running_live != NULL` for the live block itself.
- L2: ALREADY FIXED (the header's magic is zeroed before the pages are freed in `load_payload_from_volume`).
- L3: ALREADY FIXED (the volume load now claims the whole 64 MiB region).
- L4: FIXED, in part. `payload_walk_size()` caps the header's size at what the region holds; `parse_payload` refuses a payload (returns 0, one message) whose entry claims more than is left, and `payload_kernel_version` stops the walk there; so the 32-bit rounding cannot wrap and the ramdisk copy cannot read past the payload. SKIPPED: the check that text entries hold a NUL (mkpayload.py always writes one, and the entry-size bound limits the over-read).
- L5: FIXED. `parse_payload` records `kernel_size`; `run_kernel` now refuses a kernel whose `sizeofcmds` exceeds it, a load command shorter than its header or past `sizeofcmds` (also stops a `cmdsize` of 0), a segment whose `vmaddr + vmsize` wraps, whose `filesize > vmsize` or whose file range leaves the kernel entry, a `vm_hi` more than `MAX_MEM_SIZE` past the virtual base, and an LC_UNIXTHREAD too short to hold pc.
- L6: FIXED. An `rdres` larger than the window above `RESIDENT_RD_OFFSET` is refused before it is stored (not the 768 MiB `RESIDENT_RD_RESERVE` of the `download:` path: that would reject setups the room check accepts today).
- L7: FIXED. `dt_writer` has an `end` (`dt_pa + dt_max`) and an `overflow` flag: `dt_prop` and `dt_begin` write nothing that does not fit (and refuse a name over 32 bytes), `run_kernel` prints "device tree does not fit" and returns 0 instead of handing the kernel a tree that overwrote boot_args.
- L8: FIXED, in part. The `download:` limit in ramdisk mode is capped at 0xffffffff (the reply carries 32 bits), and the received count `r` is clamped to `want`. SKIPPED: advertising the real limit in `getvar:max-download-size`.
- L9: FIXED, two of three. `oem ramdisk none` clears `download_to_ramdisk`; a `download:` over the payload takes the XNUP magic out as soon as it arrives and puts it back only when the whole file is in, so a failed transfer leaves no payload instead of a mix. SKIPPED: the `kernel_may_be_alive` flag after OTHER_CPU_HUNG (a design change in what the loader accepts after a hang).
- L10: FIXED. `hc_requested`, `block_probe_requested` and `block_enabled` are reset at the start of each run, next to the existing `block_write_requested` reset.
- L11: FIXED. `BS->free_pool(handles)` after every `locate_handle_buffer` use: `find_log_partition` (both exits), `ufs_survey` (both calls), `block_start` (both calls).
- L12: SKIPPED. The fix changes the bound check that gates both the read and the write branch of `block_poll`, which is the write guard's function; the report finds the guard itself sound, so it is left as it is.

```

## Findings

|---|---|---|---|---|

Once P1 holds, every "root required" statement below (sysctls, raw storage nodes) stops being a boundary for a
process that can call `posix_spawn`; I note that where it matters.

## P1. Any process can become root: persona check removed (High, CONFIRMED)

Where. patch:518-606, which changes `spawn_validate_persona()` and `spawn_persona_adopt()` in bsd/kern/kern_exec.c.

What Apple's code did (Apple kern_exec.c:3092-3166, called from 3591 and 3985):

- `spawn_validate_persona()` returned EPERM unless the caller held `PERSONA_MGMT_ENTITLEMENT`
  (3097-3099), and ESRCH if the persona did not exist (3107-3111).
- `spawn_persona_adopt()` then applied `pspi_uid`, `pspi_gid` and the groups from the caller's `posix_spawn` argument
  to the child's credential (3139-3159).
- The sibling argument `posix_cred_info` is guarded differently: `kauth_cred_issuser()` or EPERM (Apple
  kern_exec.c:3604-3607).

What the patch does. Both guards are deleted (patch:522-524, 543-547, 556-558). When the persona does not exist
(which is always the case here) the new branch at patch:566-606 sets the uid, gid and groups from the caller's request
on the child with `proc_update_label()` and returns 0.

Failure scenario. Any process, at any uid, with no entitlement and no signature, calls `posix_spawn` with a persona
attribute (`posix_spawnattr_set_persona_np`, flags OVERRIDE, `posix_spawnattr_set_persona_uid_np(attr, 0)`) for any
path. The child is created with uid 0, gid and groups of the caller's choosing. Nothing in the spawn path checks the
caller. The patch's own comment says this is what Sileo relies on to become root ("Sileo asks posix_spawn for persona
99 with OVERRIDE and uid 0 ... that is how it runs apt and dpkg"). The comment justifies the removal with "the
entitlement is one nobody carries here (nothing is signed, AMFI is a stub)".

Why that justification is out of date. miniamfi_entitlements.cpp now answers entitlement queries from the entitlements
in the program's own signature, `IOCurrentTaskHasEntitlement()` reaches it (iokit/Kernel/IOUserClient.cpp:1507,
iokit/bsddev/IOKitBSDInit.cpp:1495-1559), and the sibling hunk in the same file keeps the check for bindfs
(patch:964-973). So the entitlement route works now; the unconditional removal is not needed for Sileo, whose binary
can carry `com.apple.private.persona-mgmt` in an ldid signature.

Consequences. A root child can open /dev/rufs_* and /dev/rvblk0 (see the table below), set `kern.exec_inject`, call
`reboot(2)` (which now returns to the loader, see halt_all_cpus in patch:2199-2211), and so on.

Fix (text only):

```
 spawn_validate_persona(struct _posix_spawn_persona_info *px_persona)
 {
 	int error = 0;
 	struct persona *persona = NULL;
 
+	if (!IOCurrentTaskHasEntitlement(PERSONA_MGMT_ENTITLEMENT)) {
+		return EPERM;
+	}
 	if (px_persona->pspi_flags & POSIX_SPAWN_PERSONA_GROUPS) {
```

and sign Sileo (and anything else that must do this) with that entitlement. Keep the `persona == NULL` branch in
`spawn_persona_adopt()`, which is only reachable after the check.

## P2. Unprivileged volume ioctl wraps uint32: loudest level, guard blinded, thread stuck (CONFIRMED trace, NEEDS-HARDWARE effect)

Same defect as sound.md S-01/S-02; traced again here because the node is part of the user-reachable surface.

Trace. `HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME` (hakios.audio.c:259-275, node mode 0666 at :343) stores any `uint32` `below`
(`volume_below = volume->below`, :268) with no range test. The sound watcher (hakios.sound.c:1253-1279) computes
`below + extra` in `uint32_t` (default `below` is 240) and passes it to `hakios_speaker_volume()` and `guard_level()`.
In `hakios_speaker_volume()` (hakios.speaker.c:897 and :914) `target = a->volume_at + below` wraps again.

With `extra = 0xFFFFFF0F` the sum is `0xFFFFFFFF`:

- `guard_level(0xFFFFFFFF)` is `HAKIOS_GUARD_SILENT` (hakios.sound.c:1214-1216, `guard_as` defaults to UINT32_MAX), so
  in hakios.guard.c:160 `to_speaker = 0`: no power limit, only the full-scale clip at :225.
- `target = volume_at - 1`. `set_volume()` clamps up to `volume_at` (hakios.speaker.c:707-709) and stores the
  clamped value in `a->volume`, so `a->volume == target` never holds (:919). The `for (;;)` at :909 never ends (with
  `step_ms == 1` the fault check at :928 is skipped), and the watcher thread never reaches `hakios_speaker_stop()`.

Failure scenario (sound=4 boot-arg, phone): any process does the ioctl `{below = 0xFFFFFF0F, muted = 0}` and writes
non-silent frames. The amplifiers go to Android's loudest level, the guard computes zero speaker power, and the
amplifiers are never powered down. Whether Android's level without the guard damages the speakers is NEEDS-HARDWARE.

Fix: see sound.md S-01 (clamp `below` at the ioctl, saturating add in sound.c and speaker.c); and fix P3 for this node.

## P3. Six device nodes are world read/write (Medium, CONFIRMED for the mode)

Every node the port creates, with mode and owner:

| Node | Created at | Mode, owner | What an unprivileged opener can do |
|---|---|---|---|
| /dev/hakios-touch | hakios.input.c:213 | 0666 root:wheel | read every touch sample (and consume them: one shared queue, `touch_read` pops); write forged DOWN/MOVE/UP and button events, including Lock/Home/Volume (`touch_write`, :184-200; only real-driver fingers count towards the five-finger exit, :87-107) |
| /dev/hakios-audio | hakios.audio.c:343 | 0666 root:wheel | inject audio into the speaker path; set or reset volume and mute (P2) |
| /dev/hakios-mic | hakios.mic.c:1732 | 0666 root:wheel | `mic_dev_open` (:1522) switches the DSP microphone path on; `mic_dev_read` returns live samples to any reader; two readers split the stream (no lock on `ring_read`, memory-safe) |
| /dev/hakios-camera | hakios.camera.c:4000 | 0666 root:wheel | `camdev_read` (:3803) starts the sensor and returns frames; `camdev_write` sets exposure, focus, sensor, and fills the "picture for the host" buffer that the loader hands out (`keep_picture`, :3906-3940, bounded by `want <= keep_bytes`) |
| /dev/hakios-haptic | hakios.haptic.c:828 | 0666 root:wheel | drive the vibration motor (`haptic_write`) |
| /dev/hakios-torch | hakios.torch.c:575 | 0666 root:wheel | light the flashlight (`torch_write`; level clamped to 1000, the driver has a 30 s limit) |
| /dev/ufs_* , /dev/rufs_* | hakios.ufs.c:1517, 1522 | 0640 root:operator | raw phone storage, read only (see below) |
| /dev/rvblk0, /dev/rrvblk0 | hakios.virtio_blk.c:516-518 | 0600 root:operator | QEMU disk image |
| /dev/rsp0 | hakios.sparse.c:270 | 0600 root:operator | part of an image, block device |
| /dev/md*, /dev/rmd* | Apple bsd/dev/memdev.c:686-697 (unchanged) | 0600 root:operator | RAM disks, including the second image added at patch:1713-1723 |

Can an unprivileged process read the phone's raw storage? Not directly: /dev/ufs_* and /dev/rufs_* are 0640
root:operator (owner root, group operator read-only; on Darwin the group has only root in it), /dev/rvblk0 and /dev/rsp0
are 0600. With P1, any process can reach root and therefore all of them. The write path to /dev/rufs_darwin is bounded
(see "Checked and found fine").

The code does no check of its own in any `d_open` (`touch_open`, `audio_open`, `mic_dev_open`, `camdev_open`,
`haptic_open`, `torch_open`); file mode is the only gate. Whether the Darwin sandbox adds one is out of reach here (the
Sandbox is a stub that allows everything, kern_minimac.c:230-242).

Fix: create these nodes 0600 root:wheel, or 0660 with the group of the one daemon that uses each (backboardd for touch,
mediaserverd for audio, mic, camera, haptic, torch), or test an entitlement in `d_open`, for example in touch_open:

```
 static int
 touch_open(...)
 {
-	return 0;
+	return IOCurrentTaskHasEntitlement("com.apple.hakios.touch") || suser(kauth_cred_get(), NULL) == 0 ? 0 : EPERM;
 }
```

## P4. A privilege that was refused is now granted to everyone, before the deny policies (Medium)

Where. patch:828-839, `priv_check_cred()` in bsd/kern/kern_priv.c:

```
if (priv == PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_SOCKET_DELEGATE) { return 0; }
```

placed before `mac_priv_check()` (Apple kern_priv.c:89-94), so no MAC policy can deny it, and for every credential, not
just mobile.

What it enables. The privilege is the gate for socket delegation: `so_set_effective_pid()`/`so_set_effective_uuid()`
when the target is not the caller (Apple uipc_socket.c:8111-8117, :8235), `socket_delegate()` (Apple
uipc_syscalls.c:270-276), NECP client delegation (necp_client.c:6917, necp.c:6847), and the Skywalk delegate checks
(fsw.c:973, nx_netif.c:1575). With the hunk any process can attribute its sockets to any other pid and executable UUID,
so per-process network policy, statistics and accounting see the victim instead of the caller.

The stated reason is stale. The comment says no process carries an entitlement. Today miniamfi_entitlements.cpp reads the
entitlements from each program's signature, and kern_minimac.c:290 already maps this very privilege to
`com.apple.private.network.socket-delegate`; trustd, nsurlsessiond and mediaserverd carry it in their Apple signatures.
So the hunk is redundant and makes the stub's entry dead code. (kern_minimac.c:253-258 says the NECP refusal "costs
nothing"; with this hunk the macro is never refused, so that comment and this hunk cannot both describe the current
tree.)

Reach is PLAUSIBLE only because I did not run it: whether anything in this port enforces NECP policy per app was not
examined.

Fix: delete the hunk. The entitlement path in `minisandbox_priv_grant()` grants the privilege to the daemons that hold
the entitlement.

## P5. An unconditional kernel printf on a user-controlled path (Low, CONFIRMED)

patch:853-859 adds, in `__pthread_kill()`:

```
if (signum == SIGABRT) { user_abort_trace(); }
```

`user_abort_trace()` (user_exception_trace.c:112-145) has no gate. Its sibling `user_exception_trace()` returns at once
unless the boot-arg `systrace` is set (:48); `ustacks` is boot-arg driven. The file's header says the facility is on
"with boot-arg systrace set".

Failure scenario. A process ignores SIGABRT (`signal(SIGABRT, SIG_IGN)`) and calls `pthread_kill(pthread_self(),
SIGABRT)` in a loop. Each call does one `printf` of up to 24 return addresses, plus the process name (which the process
chooses: its executable's last path component, so it can embed newlines). That goes to the console (video console and
UART, which the loader comments call very slow), to the kernel message buffer, and from there into the loader's log
(which keeps the first 256 KB and the last 1 MB, loader_return.c:30-38): the log's evidence is pushed out and the CPUs
that printf are slowed. Not a memory-safety problem: the frame walk is bounded (24 frames, monotonic, `copyin`).

Fix:

```
 void
 user_abort_trace(void)
 {
 	thread_t thread = current_thread();
+	if (!user_exception_trace_enabled) {
+		return;
+	}
```

## P6. Pid-version bump skipped by process name only (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

patch:726-742 skips `proc_setpidversion()` in `exec_handle_sugid()` (Apple kern_exec.c:6639) when
`strncmp(p->p_comm, "xpcproxy", ...) == 0`. At that point `p_comm` is still the name of the image that is exec'ing
(`set_proc_name()` runs later, Apple kern_exec.c:1924, after `exec_handle_sugid` at 1581). So the exception applies to
any process whose comm is `xpcproxy`, for any exec it does, not only the exec into the service xpcproxy was spawned
for. A process inherits the comm through fork, and a user can name a program `xpcproxy`.

The pid version in the audit token is what makes a daemon that holds an audit token notice an exec; without the bump a
process called xpcproxy can send an XPC message as itself, exec an entitled system binary, and the daemon's later
entitlement check on the unchanged token resolves to the new image (the classic exec race). On this port the same
effect is already cheaper through a self-written signature (the AMFI stub reads entitlements without validation), so
the practical gain is small; but the hunk regresses a property the kernel otherwise keeps. Reach depends on daemon
behaviour I did not examine, hence PLAUSIBLE.

Fix: also require the spawn that created the process to be launchd's, for example only skip when `p->p_ppid == 1` and
the target is not xpcproxy itself, or mark xpcproxy's spawn with a posix_spawn flag that the kernel records in the
`proc`, and test that instead of the name.

## P7. Sandbox request 4: container of any pid, read from memory the process owns (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

kern_minimac.c:147-225 answers `sandbox_container_path_for_pid()` for any `args.pid` the caller names (:173-176): no
check of the caller's credential, of its relation to the target, or of an entitlement. The answer is taken by scanning
the target's exec strings for `CFFIXED_USER_HOME=` in its live user stack (:196-222). That memory is writable by the
target after exec, and at exec time it is whatever environment the parent passed.

Failure scenario. Process A rewrites the `CFFIXED_USER_HOME=` string in its own stack (or execs itself with the
variable set). A daemon that asks the kernel "what is A's container" (the call exists for exactly that) gets the path A
chose, for example another application's data container, and may then read or write there on A's behalf. A different
process learns the container path of any other process. The kernel side is memory-safe: `strnlen` and `s + len < end`
bound the scan, `len < args.size` bounds the copyout, the map is referenced, and the page-rounded copy covers `argslen`.

The comment (kern_minimac.c:137-142) says the environment is where the container comes from, so this is by design; what
the comment does not say is that the answer is exposed for other pids and that the source is mutable. Which user-space
daemons use the answer for an access decision was not examined.

Fix, if it matters: cache the string in `struct proc` at exec time (the kernel already walks the strings in
`exec_extract_strings`) instead of re-reading the stack, and require `kauth_cred_getuid` equality or
`PRIV_...` for pid != caller.

## Checked and found fine

Policy stand-ins

- AMFI (miniamfi.c): `vnode_check_signature` sets CS_SIGNED and, for ad hoc signatures, CS_PLATFORM_BINARY, and returns 0
  (:45-62). That is stated at kern_minimac.c:11-17. The consequences I traced: `task_conversion_eval_internal` (Apple
  ipc_tt.c:2489) lets a platform binary resolve other platform binaries' task ports, and `F_ASSERT_BG_ACCESS` (Apple
  kern_descrip.c:5048) is platform-only; both are therefore open to any ad hoc signed program, which anyone can make.
  By design; noted so that nobody reads "platform" as a trust statement.
- The trust-cache and OSEntitlements tables answer "not found" or "unsupported" everywhere except the three
  `...WithProc` queries, which read the program's signature (miniamfi.c:93-124); only the `WithProc` variants are called
  by the kernel (IOKitBSDInit.cpp:1495/1526/1559, IOUserClient.cpp:1507). No stub answers "yes" for an entitlement the
  signature lacks; an absent signature has none (`cs_entitlements_blob_get` returns NULL when CS_SIGNED is unset, Apple
  kern_cs.c:1725-1727).
- `copy_entitlements` (miniamfi_entitlements.cpp:32-64): rejects `length <= sizeof(CS_GenericBlob)`, copies
  `length - 8` into a buffer of `+1` and terminates it. Notes, not findings: the plist is re-parsed on every query
  (no cache), and its size is bounded only by the code-signature blob limit.
- dyld policy request 0x5a and boot-arg query 0x60 (miniamfi.c:89-111): fixed 8-byte copyout to the address the caller
  gives; `copyin` of exactly 16 bytes; everything else is ENOPOLICY. It answers "allow everything" to every process,
  including DYLD_* variables and interposing for restricted programs; that is the purpose (kern_minimac.c:64-69).
- Sandbox (kern_minimac.c:230-242): every request except 4 returns 0 and writes nothing. A caller of an "issue
  extension" style request then reads an unwritten out buffer in user space; stated in the file's header.
- `minisandbox_priv_grant` (:318-349): consulted only after the root test (Apple kern_priv.c:104-119); the entitlement
  is read from the current process and only when `cred == kauth_cred_get()`; PRIV_WORK_INTERVAL is granted to all
  (:325, needed by UIKit; it gates `WORK_INTERVAL_OPERATION_CREATE2`, Apple sys_work_interval.c:71, and the effect of the
  work-interval classes needs a workload id, which I did not trace). The table maps privileges to entitlements that a
  user can write into their own signature (no validation: stated at miniamfi_entitlements.cpp:4-9), so for non-root
  these privileges are as strong as the signature a user chooses. Log lines are bounded (32 privileges).
- AppleKeyStore (MiniAppleKeyStore.cpp): answers "no passcode, unlocked" for state; lock, unlock and `UnlockBag`
  return success for any input, which is the right answer for a device with no passcode and, since no
  change-passcode selector exists (`kIOReturnUnsupported`, :314), no caller can set one. Wrap/unwrap are a reversible XOR
  (:173-181) and the file says so. Bounds: wrap needs `1..64` bytes into `wrapped[72]` (:261-277); unwrap
  `9..72` into `key[64]` (:285-290); DER buffers `der[128]` hold 91 and 30 bytes; `scalarOutputCount` and
  `structureOutputSize` are checked before writes. The user client has no task check, but nothing it returns or does is
  secret or persistent.
- Data protection: the APFS port implements no protection class and `apfs_vnop_ioctl` returns ENOTTY
  (apfs_vnops.c:1190-1197), so `F_SETPROTECTIONCLASS`-style callers get "unsupported", not success.
- MiniIONetworkStack: a service, an openable user client, `setProperties` refuses (:85-94); the open logs the registry
  state; no state is shared.
- GenericARMPE: CPU nubs are indexed only after `number >= MAX_CPUS` is excluded (:234); `reg` length checked (:77);
  `cpus[]` is static; the thread-call lambda touches only `cpus[]` and the topology. The device tree is the loader's.

Surface

- Every sysctl the port adds (grep over xnu/files; the modem files were not read):
  - writable: `kern.exec_inject` (root; see below), `kern.hakios_switch_root` (pid 1 and root, once, input
    `< 512` bytes, hakios.apfs_check.c:1753-1766), `kern.apfs_synthetic` (explicit `suser`, `newlen < MAXPATHLEN`,
    NUL-terminated, apfs_vfsops.c:660-671), `kern.apfs_stats` (write zeroes the counters, root through the sysctl
    layer), `kern.hakios.var_save`, `kern.hakios.var_busy`, `kern.hakios.ufs_native` (`sysctl_io_number`, a small state
    machine, root).
  - read-only: `kern.hakios.version`, `kern.hakios.battery_*`, `kern.hakios.ufs_*` counters, `kern.hakios_memory`
    (apfs_vfsops.c:474-478).
  - none uses CTLFLAG_ANYBODY (grep), and Apple's `sysctl_root` demands `proc_suser` for any write to an OID without it
    (Apple kern_newsysctl.c:1737-1745). So all writes need uid 0, which P1 makes available to any process.
- `kern.exec_inject` (patch:625-677): `SYSCTL_STRING(... exec_inject_conf, 512)`; Apple's `sysctl_io_string` refuses
  `newlen >= 512` and terminates at `newlen` (kern_newsysctl.c:530-536), so the buffer always has a NUL. The parser
  advances at least one byte per iteration or exits at NUL; the append test `used + 1 + liblen < size` leaves room for
  the `:` and the NUL; `inject_env` is 512 bytes, the same size as the buffer; matching is on the file's basename with an
  exact length compare. An unprivileged user can only get the library into a process they run themselves by naming it;
  that gives them nothing they lack. The variable is added after the caller's own environment, so a caller-supplied
  `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` comes first.
- bindfs exemption (patch:964-973): the entitlement test remains (and can now be satisfied from a signature); the extra
  `pid == 1` clause only matters to a process that is pid 1, which stays launchd after init execs it. Mounting still
  needs root.
- Raw-storage write path (hakios.ufs.c:566-625, 823-857): block aligned, only the one partition selected by the
  `ufs_write=1` boot-arg, from `UFS_WRITE_FIRST` on, `offset` and `len` checked against the partition size in uint64,
  the character open of that partition clears FWRITE before the open check but the node mode (0640, owner root) still
  decides who may open it for writing, and one writer at a time through the `var_busy` claim.
- Camera, mic, audio, haptic, torch handlers: every `uiomove` length is bounded by the destination size (`audio_write`
  chunks to the stack buffer; `mic_dev_read` `n <= RING_FRAMES`; `camdev_read` `n <= ring_frame_bytes`; `haptic_write`
  256 samples; `torch_write` clamps to 1000); exposure and focus values are clamped before they reach registers
  (`exposure_limits` :3306, `af_move` :3039).
- User-visible patch hunks, regression check: `mdevrw` (patch:311-321) keeps the original treatment of a negative offset
  (root-only, Apple's behaviour); `km.c` TIOCSCTTY refusal only affects the console; work-interval cases 6-8
  (patch:924-939) return 0 only for CoreAudio threads, otherwise the old ENOTSUP; vm_unix.c shared-region hunk
  (patch:1442-1462) adds an accept branch for a volume mounted directly inside Preboot's Cryptexes (root-only mount; the
  `va_uid == 0` owner check at Apple vm_unix.c:2475 still applies earlier) and keeps `vnode_put` balanced in all three
  arms; `percpu_foreach_secondary` rewrite is integer arithmetic with the same bounds; `halt_all_cpus` and
  `kdp_machine_reboot_type` call `loader_return()` first, which returns at once if no loader stub exists; the
  `systrace`, `applog`, `regtrace`, `exec_trace` hooks are boot-arg gated and bounded (`copyinstr` into 160- and 32-byte
  buffers, at most 6 mib words); `startup.c` declares `minimac_policy_init` inside `#if CONFIG_VNGUARD` while the call is
  outside it (a RELEASE configuration without vnguard would not compile; DEVELOPMENT builds are unaffected).
- Loader return (loader_return.c, start.s hunk patch:2392-2631): the stub address and the PA-VA offset are read from
  `loader_stub_slot`, which the loader patches in the kernel image and nothing user-reachable writes;
  `loader_jump` rejects `t0sz` outside 25..33 or a stub that does not fit under it, so `loader_l1[stub >> 30]` is
  below 512; the ring arithmetic keeps every index below `LOADER_LOG_SIZE`; the early exception vectors branch to the
  loader only while VBAR holds a physical address and spin as before when no stub was patched. The kernel does not check
  the slot's magic or that the stub lies outside the kernel, and it acts on `loader_live.stop` as soon as it is
  non-zero; both are writable only by the loader or by whoever has kernel memory. The loader in turn trusts the
  `loader_recording`/`loader_sound` physical addresses and lengths (at most 1 GB) that the kernel writes; the
  only user-influenced writer is the camera's `keep_picture`, which stores the address of its own buffer.
  Minor: `loader_return_entered` is tested and set without an atomic, so two processors reaching `loader_jump`
  together (a panic and the five-finger exit) could both pass it; `psci_smp_stop_others()` runs first and I did not trace
  its handling of that.

## Not checked

- IOKit user clients of MiniIOSurface.cpp, MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp, hakios.gpu.cpp, hakios.wlan.cpp,
  hakios.battery.cpp (external methods, shared memory): outside the file list given to me.
- bsd/miscfs/ramfs and apfs vnode operations: how ownership, setuid bits and `access` are enforced there (ramfs stores
  `va_mode & ALLPERMS`, ramfs.c:152, 1032).
- What Darwin user space does with the stub answers: whether cfprefsd, lsd or containermanagerd use P7's container path
  for an access decision; whether dyld honours DYLD_* for setuid programs given the allow-all AMFI answer; whether this
  port ships any setuid-root program; whether `task_for_pid` is otherwise gated for ad hoc signed callers.
- Behaviour on hardware: P2's effect on the speakers, whether the Sandbox stub's `0` for unknown requests produces
  usable values in `libsystem_sandbox`.
- gic_v3_irq.c, psci_smp.c, generic_arm64_support.c, minicrypto, the cellular files, xnuloader's USB side.
- The scheduler hunks for slower cores (sched_prim.c, machine_routines.c): read, not analysed for correctness; they
  are policy, not privilege.

```

`docs/driver-review/sound.md`:

```md
# Driver review: sound path (speakers, microphone, /dev/hakios-audio)

Read-only audit; nothing was built, run or changed except this file.

## Scope and method

Files (all under `xnu/files/bsd/dev/` unless noted):

| file | lines |
|---|---|
| hakios.audio.c | 354 |
| hakios.sound.c | 1518 |
| hakios.speaker.c | 1211 |
| hakios.mic.c | 1847 |
| hakios.virtio_sound.c | 406 |
| `userland/src/audio_plugin.c` (writer/reader side, volume control) | 1041 |

Also read because the sound path depends on them (not in the group, so only the parts the sound path uses):
`xnu/files/bsd/sys/hakios.audio.h`, `hakios.guard.c` (the guard that limits what the amplifiers get), and in `hakios.adsp.c`
only `root_file()`/`hakios_adsp_fw_file()` (loader of aw882xx_acf.bin) and `apr_input()`/`hakios_adsp_apr()`.

Method: whole-file reading of the five kernel files and the I/O and volume parts of the plug-in; each finding traced from
the input (user write/ioctl/read, file contents, DSP event, boot-arg) to the faulty operation. Tracing of arithmetic was
done by hand (uint32 wrap points worked out with concrete numbers). Nothing was executed, and the real
aw882xx_acf.bin is not in the repository, so file-driven findings are traced against the parser only.
Hardware facts (register layouts, what level is safe for the amplifier) are not asserted; where a consequence
depends on them the finding says NEEDS-HARDWARE.

Severity is about the effect if the trigger happens; confidence is as defined in the task (CONFIRMED = path traced end to end).

## Findings

| id | severity | confidence | file:line | one line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-01 | High | CONFIRMED (effect on hardware: NEEDS-HARDWARE) | audio.c:268, sound.c:1267/1272/1279, speaker.c:897-941, guard.c:160 | unclamped user `below` can make the volume fade loop spin forever at Android's loudest level while the guard is told "amplifiers off" |
| S-02 | Medium | CONFIRMED | audio.c:268, sound.c:1267/1279 | `below + extra` wraps: any local user can lift the level to Android's maximum, past `sound_below` |
| S-03 | Medium | CONFIRMED | speaker.c:478-479, 484, 495 | monitor-table bounds check done in uint32: crafted ACF makes the row pointer go up to 3.5 GB out of the file buffer |
| S-04 | Medium | PLAUSIBLE | speaker.c:688-696, 1033-1065, sound.c:1346 | `hakios_speaker_stop()` gives up on the first failed I2C read, leaves both amplifiers up, and its caller then stops the TDM clock |
| S-05 | Medium | PLAUSIBLE | speaker.c:623-646, 1068-1080 | `power_down_now()` clears `started` even when its power-down write was not acknowledged; the panic quiesce then skips the amplifier that is still on |
| S-06 | Medium | CONFIRMED | mic.c:1737-1778 | mic=4: a bring-up that fails without setting `broken` is retried forever (no failure count), re-toggling the codec reset and the DSP votes |
| S-07 | Low | CONFIRMED | sound.c:635, 693-706 | page tables for the DSP's SMMU context are allocated at every `space_on()` and never freed (12 KB per recording in mic=4) |
| S-08 | Medium | PLAUSIBLE (mode CONFIRMED; reach depends on Darwin sandbox) | audio.c:343, mic.c:1732, 1524-1534 | both device nodes are 0666; any process can start the microphone, steal/split its samples, set the volume or mute; open state is a flag, not a count |
| S-09 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | mic.c:719, 727 | SoundWire read id cycles through 0; an empty (zero) FIFO word matches id 0 and is returned as a successful read of 0 |
| S-10 | Low | NEEDS-HARDWARE | mic.c:704-710 | `swr_write()` waits for FIFO room at most 10 ms and then writes anyway; the result is always `true` |
| S-11 | Low | NEEDS-HARDWARE | sound.c:719, mic.c:1614-1617 | DSP-written mic buffer is only invalidated after the DSP has used it; dirty zero-fill lines are never cleaned first |
| S-12 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | virtio_sound.c:249-251 | used-ring entry read without a load barrier, and its `id` trusted as an index into `tx_free[]`/the shared area |
| S-13 | Low | CONFIRMED (file outside this group) | hakios.adsp.c:2488-2495 | `payload` underflows when the DSP's `header.size` < header length; 256 bytes are then copied from beyond the packet |
| S-14 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | audio_plugin.c:282, 788-793 | a NaN volume passes the clamp, `lround(NaN)` gives `below` 0 and `muted` 0: loudest |
| S-15 | Low | CONFIRMED | sound.c:1195-1199, mic.c:1644 | a period whose submission to the DSP fails is never re-submitted: the stream starves one period at a time |
| S-16 | Low | CONFIRMED | mic.c:1597 | mic=1..3 `listen(false)` ignores `stopping`: `hakios_mic_dsp_down()` can block for `mic_secs` (up to 600 s) |

## Details

### S-01  High  CONFIRMED (hardware effect NEEDS-HARDWARE)

Unclamped `below` from user space reaches `hakios_speaker_volume()`, whose fade loop can never finish, and it also makes the guard think the amplifiers are off.

Chain:

1. `audio.c:268` `volume_below = volume->below;` ioctl `HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME` stores any uint32; the node is mode 0666 (`audio.c:343`), no privilege test, no range test.
2. `sound.c:1253-1272` (watch thread) takes it as `extra` and does `guard_level(below + extra)` (1272) and `hakios_speaker_volume(below + extra, 1)` (1267, 1279). `below` is `sound_below`, default 240. The sum is uint32 and wraps.
3. `speaker.c:897` and `:914`: `uint32_t target = a->volume_at + below;` wraps again. Take `extra = 0xFFFFFF0F` (so `below + extra = 0xFFFFFFFF`): `target = volume_at - 1`, which is *below* `volume_at`. With the profile's level (the header comment says Android's is -2.1 dB, so `volume_at` is about 17, never 0) the clamp `if (target > VOLUME_LOWEST)` does not trigger.
4. `speaker.c:919` `if (a->volume == target) continue;` can never be true: `set_volume()` (707-709) raises every request to `volume_at`, so `a->volume` bottoms out at `volume_at` and `target` stays under it. The `for (;;)` at 909 sees `moved = true` forever: one I2C write plus read-back and a 1 ms wait per round, two log lines each. There is no `stopping` check and, with `step_ms = 1`, not even the status check (928 needs `step_ms >= 10`). The watcher thread is stuck, so no silence timeout, no fault polling and no `hakios_speaker_stop()` happens. Only `take_down()` at the run's end breaks it, because it calls `hakios_speaker_stop()` after 3 s and a failed/`broken` write makes the loop return.
5. At the same time step 2's `guard_level(0xFFFFFFFF)` equals `HAKIOS_GUARD_SILENT` (`guard_level()` takes `min(level, guard_as)` and `guard_as` defaults to UINT32_MAX). In `hakios.guard.c:160` that means `to_speaker = 0` (no power limit) and at `:225` the peak ceiling stays at full scale: the guard only clips. Any `s` in `[2^32 - volume_at, 2^32 - 1]` is blind in the same way, because `amplitude(2 * attenuation)` wraps to a huge index and returns 0.

Failure scenario: `ioctl(fd, HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME, {below = 0xFFFFFF0F, muted = 0})` from any process, then any non-silent write to the same node (or Darwin playing anything). The amplifiers are faded to Android's loudest level, the speaker guard is off, and the thread that should turn them off after three seconds of silence is in an endless I2C loop. Whether that level without the guard can hurt the speakers is NEEDS-HARDWARE (the guard exists "for want of the DSP's speaker protection", per `hakios.audio.h`).

Fix (three independent layers; do all):

```diff
--- hakios.audio.c  audio_ioctl
+#define HAKIOS_AUDIO_BELOW_MAX  (90 * 8)        /* the amplifiers' own floor: speaker.c VOLUME_LOWEST */
 	lck_mtx_lock(&audio_lock);
-	volume_below = volume->below;
+	volume_below = volume->below > HAKIOS_AUDIO_BELOW_MAX ? HAKIOS_AUDIO_BELOW_MAX : volume->below;
--- hakios.sound.c  watch()
-	hakios_speaker_volume(below + extra, 1)
+	hakios_speaker_volume(below_total, 1)        /* uint32 below_total = below > 720 ? 720 : below; below_total += extra (extra already <= 720) */
--- hakios.speaker.c  hakios_speaker_volume
-	uint32_t target = a->volume_at + below;
+	uint32_t target = a->volume_at + (below > VOLUME_LOWEST ? VOLUME_LOWEST : below);   /* (both loops) */
 	/* and make the loop finish: */
-	if (a->volume == target) continue;
+	if (a->volume == target || target < a->volume_at) continue;     /* (target is already clamped, belt and braces) */
```
Also give the guard a value that cannot collide with the sentinel (`guard_level()` should clamp to `HAKIOS_GUARD_SILENT - 1`), and add an iteration limit (about 2 * VOLUME_LOWEST / 1 steps) to the fade loop.

### S-02  Medium  CONFIRMED

Same cause as S-01: `sound.c:1267, 1279` computes `below + extra` in uint32 with `extra` from user space. `extra = 2^32 - 240` (with `below = 240`) gives 0, so `hakios_speaker_volume(0, 1)` fades to `volume_at`, Android's level, 30 dB louder than the cap (the code's default `below = 240` eighths; the header comment says 160) that `sound_below` is documented to be ("sound_below, which stays the loudest", `sound.c:31-32`; `hakios.audio.h:34-36`). Here the guard still sees the true level (`guard_level(0)`), so its power and peak limits apply; the cap that the operator set at boot does not. Whether Android's level is safe for this phone is NEEDS-HARDWARE; the cap bypass itself is certain. The fix of S-01 (clamp `extra`, saturating add) closes it.

### S-03  Medium  CONFIRMED

`acf_monitor()` bounds check in 32-bit arithmetic, `speaker.c:478-479`:

```c
temp_at + temp_count * temp_size > length || vbat_at + vbat_count * vbat_size > length
```
`temp_count` is checked `<= 8` but `temp_size` has only a lower bound (`>= 12`). All three are uint32, so `temp_count = 8, temp_size = 0x20000000, temp_at = 0x48` gives `8 * 0x20000000 = 0` (mod 2^32), the check passes, and the loop at 483-493 reads `row = block + temp_at + i * temp_size` for i up to 7: reads from `block + 0xE0000048`, 3.5 GB past a buffer of at most 1 MB (`acf_profiles()` limits the file to 0x100000). Also `temp_at = 0xFFFFFFFC, count 1, size 12` wraps to 8 and passes (row at `block + 4 GB`). The same holds for `vbat_*` at 494-504. The byte-sum checksum (469-471, 478) is trivial to satisfy for whoever crafts the file. Effect: synchronous data abort (kernel panic) in `hakios_speaker_prepare()` at the first sound=3/4 start, or, if the address happens to be mapped, garbage reductions in `temp_rows/vbat_rows`. The file comes from the system image, so the realistic trigger is a corrupted or hostile image rather than a remote attacker; but this is the loader the task asked about and the only parser step whose bounds are not sound (the others are fine, see below).

Fix:
```diff
-	    temp_at + temp_count * temp_size > length || vbat_at + vbat_count * vbat_size > length) {
+	    (uint64_t)temp_at + (uint64_t)temp_count * temp_size > length ||
+	    (uint64_t)vbat_at + (uint64_t)vbat_count * vbat_size > length) {
```
and loop with `(uint64_t)i * temp_size`. Also saturate the `less` additions at 502 (`uint16_t` wrap, a file with a large `vmax` turns a big reduction into a small one).

### S-04  Medium  PLAUSIBLE

`hakios_speaker_stop()` abandons the sequence on the first failure and does not power anything down:

- `speaker.c:688-696` `sysctrl()`: if `get()` (an I2C read) fails it returns false and does *not* call `power_down_now()` (only `put()` does).
- `speaker.c:1045-1061` `hakios_speaker_stop()`: `return;` on every failed step (1046, 1051, 1055, 1059). The `return` is inside the loop over the two amplifiers, so a failure at amplifier 0 leaves amplifier 1 untouched (still started, unmuted, volume as it was) and amplifier 0 half-way (e.g. ULS-muted, volume stepped but not powered down).
- Callers: `sound.c:1299` (watcher, after silence; `on = false` is set regardless) and `sound.c:1346` (`take_down()`), which ignores the failure and goes on to `stream_off()` and `afe_off()` (`sound.c:1347-1348`), i.e. stops the TDM clock the amplifiers are locked to.

Scenario: one NACK or "bus not at rest" (`bus_take()` returning false: SDA or SCL read low, `speaker.c:272`) during the final stop. Result: amplifier(s) left with power-down off, no bit clock, nothing retrying. In the watcher case the next `hakios_speaker_start()` restarts the sequence, so only the run-end case is permanent. How an Awinic amplifier behaves without a clock is NEEDS-HARDWARE.

Fix: make `hakios_speaker_stop()` finish every amplifier regardless of earlier ones and fall back to the unconditional power-down:
```diff
-		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE, true)) { return; }
+		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE, true)) { power_down_now("stop: could not mute"); return; }
 		...  (same for the other `return;` lines)
```
and let `take_down()` check a returned bool / `hakios_speaker_quiesce()` after a failed stop.

### S-05  Medium  PLAUSIBLE

`power_down_now()` (`speaker.c:623-646`) sets `broken = true` first and `a->started = false` at 644 after the write, whether or not the write and read-back at 639 were acknowledged (the failure only logs "NOT ACKNOWLEDGED", 640). After that:

- `put()`, `sysctrl()`, `hakios_speaker_stop()` all return at once on `broken` (654, 692, 1035): nothing retries.
- `hakios_speaker_quiesce()` (1068-1080) returns early when no amplifier has `started` set (`any` false), so the panic path of `hakios_sound_quiesce()` does not even try.

Scenario: an I2C fault (bus not at rest, NACK) in the very moment a fault is handled leaves an amplifier powered with the code believing it is off. Also in a panic: other CPUs are halted wherever they were, possibly with SCL or SDA held low by an interrupted bit-bang transfer; `bus_take()` then refuses to touch the bus (272-278) and `quiesce` gets no power-down through, and there is no bus-recovery (clocking out up to nine pulses) anywhere. Hardware behaviour of the frozen bus is NEEDS-HARDWARE, the bookkeeping error is not.

Fix: keep `started` true when the power-down write failed (`if (ok) a->started = false;`), let `quiesce` run when `broken && any prepared amplifier is not known off`, and add a bus-recovery step (SCL pulses with SDA released, then STOP) before giving up in `bus_take()`.

### S-06  Medium  CONFIRMED

mic=4 retry loop, `mic.c:1737-1778`. `failed = broken;` (1761) is the only failure signal counted (`++failures >= 3`, 1770). But `path_up()` fails *without* setting `broken` in several places: `clocks_on()` false (1696-1699), `codec_wait() == 0` (1704-1706), `bolero_look()` unknown version (1118), `dsp_path_on()`/`dsp_port_on()` (APR refusal), `datapath_on()` returning false after a failed `swr_read()` (1001-1003), and `listen()` returning early on a refused RUN (1565-1569). In all of those `failed` is false, the code prints "ended", runs `undo()` and loops: `darwin_wants` is still 1 while Darwin keeps the device open, so it immediately starts another attempt. Each attempt is `clocks_on` (DSP votes and clock commands, up to 1 s per unanswered command), the codec reset pulse on GPIO 83, pins, SoundWire master bring-up, `codec_wait()` (200 ms) and the undo of all of it, indefinitely, with lines suppressed by `quiet` after the first. `recordings` grows without limit.

Scenario: codec or DSP not answering (the case the retry cap was written for) while the audio server holds the input open: the cap never fires.

Fix:
```diff
-			if (path_up()) {
-				listen(true);
-			}
-			failed = broken;
+			bool up = path_up();
+			if (up) { listen(true); }
+			failed = broken || !up || (listen produced no samples, e.g. reads_done == 0);
```
(then the existing `failures >= 3` and the "wait until Darwin closes" logic apply).

### S-07  Low  CONFIRMED

`sound.c:635` `kmem_alloc(... &space.tables, 3 * 4096 ...)` in `space_on()`; `space_off()` (693-706) and the rest of the file never free it (`grep kmem_free`: no hits in the five files). `shared_get()` calls `space_on()` whenever `space_users == 0` and `!space.on` (725-730). With mic=4 and no sound=N every Darwin recording takes and gives back the last user (`hakios_audio_dsp_memory()` / `_put()`), so each recording leaks 12 KB of wired kernel memory and overwrites the pointer. The same happens after the TLB-wait timeout return at 672-675 (tables allocated, `space.on` false, next call allocates again). Not freeing while the context could still be walked is safe (the pointer is simply lost); fix: keep one allocation (`if (space.tables == 0) kmem_alloc(...)`) and re-zero it, or free it in `space_off()` after the context is switched off and the TLB invalidated.

### S-08  Medium  PLAUSIBLE (mode CONFIRMED, effect depends on sandboxing, which I did not examine)

`audio.c:343` and `mic.c:1732` create the nodes with mode 0666. In XNU file permissions are the only gate in the kernel for `open()` (a sandbox profile may add more).

- Microphone: opening `/dev/hakios-mic` sets `darwin_wants = 1` (mic.c:1524-1526), which makes the for_darwin thread power the codec path up and fill `ring`; any reader gets the audio (`mic_dev_read`, 1484-1519). Two readers split the stream. The ring is not cleared between sessions (only reset in the thread, 1752-1754, which races with a reader that starts at open).
- `darwin_wants` is a single flag: `mic_dev_close` sets it to 0 (1532). If any other process opens and closes the node (or XNU calls `d_close` for a close that is not the last: I could not confirm from this tree which, the XNU `spec_close` source is not in the repository), the audio server's recording path is taken down while it still reads.
- `/dev/hakios-audio`: any process can inject audio and call `HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME` (mute, unmute, S-01/S-02). Each ioctl also logs through `printf` (audio.c:272) and, in sound.c, `say()` to the loader log (1258), so a loop of ioctls floods a log that "keeps its beginning and its end".

Memory safety of the concurrent readers was checked and is fine (all indices are taken modulo the ring size and every copy length is clamped; at worst a reader gets torn or repeated audio).

Fix: create both nodes `0600`/root:wheel (or a dedicated group of the audio server), refcount opens (`darwin_wants` as a counter or open-exclusive with `EBUSY`), rate-limit the ioctl logging.

### S-09  Low  PLAUSIBLE

`mic.c:719` `read_id = read_id < 14 ? read_id + 1 : 0;` so ids 0..14 are used, and 727 accepts `((answer >> 8) & 0xf) == read_id`.
