`docs/driver-review/wifi-bringup.md`:

```md
# Wi-Fi bring-up review: hakios.wifi.c

## Scope and method

- File: `drivers/wifi/hakios.wifi.c`, 4394 lines, read in full, line by line.
- A few lines of context were read in other files to size the impact of a finding. They were not audited:
  `xnu/files/bsd/sys/hakios.qrtr.h`, `drivers/modem/hakios.qmi.c` (the receive path only), `userland/build.sh` (how `fw/network` is installed), and a grep for users of `hakios_wifi_say`, `hakios_wifi_tell` and `passphrase`.
- Modem code was not examined.
- Method: manual tracing of every value that comes from a remote processor or the firmware (SMEM partition and item headers, SMP2P, the QMP descriptor, GLINK queue words, QRTR headers, MDT/ELF header, QMI-reported register window) to its first use as a size, offset or index. Wait loops, error paths, locks, the shutdown path, the log functions and boot-arg parsing were traced the same way.
- Nothing was built or run. Findings carry CONFIRMED (traced end to end in the source), PLAUSIBLE, or NEEDS-HARDWARE. "Remote" below means the DSP, the AOP or the radio firmware, and the shared memory is writable by them by design.

## Findings

| id | severity | confidence | where | one line |
|----|----------|------------|-------|----------|
| W1 | HIGH | CONFIRMED | 2470-2488, 2519-2523, 2586-2599 | GLINK message length overflows uint32 to 0; the message is never consumed and `glink_pump()` loops forever with `glink_lock` held, which also wedges shutdown |
| W2 | HIGH | CONFIRMED | 571-572, 587-589, 2312-2318, 2358-2363, 2388-2396 | SMEM item offset and size are not checked against the partition or the 2 MB mapping; the GLINK queues index the mapping with remote-chosen extents |
| W3 | MEDIUM | CONFIRMED | 866, 1480, 1562-1566 | the AOP's mailbox `box + size <= 0x400` check wraps in uint32, so `our_box` can lie outside the mapped block |
| W4 | LOW | CONFIRMED | 2915, 2935, 3251 | QRTR `at + header.size > length` wraps; the receiver is handed a huge length and a pointer that is not inside the packet |
| W5 | MEDIUM | PLAUSIBLE / NEEDS-HARDWARE | 3086-3091, 3974-3977 | a DSP that says "err-fatal" is only logged; the driver is not stopped and `hakios_wifi_dsp_is_up()` still says yes |
| W6 | LOW | PLAUSIBLE | 604-620, 657-661, 3035, 3217 | state shared by the link thread and the main thread without a lock: static `found[256]`, static `at`, `link_thread_is` |
| W7 | LOW | CONFIRMED | 3437-3466 | step 16 maps `size` bytes at a firmware-given address with no upper bound, and does not check the map result |
| W8 | LOW | CONFIRMED | 1894-1897, 1832-1836, 2440-2442, 399, 502, 1889 | error-path leaks (25 MB mapping, a page per start, intent buffers) and unchecked `ml_io_map*` results |
| W9 | LOW | NEEDS-HARDWARE | 2146-2156, 1810-1856, 4149-4163 | errors between step 8 and `dsp_started = true` never ask TrustZone to shut the image down; a panic in a small window is not cleaned up |
| W10 | LOW | PLAUSIBLE | 4104-4113 | the end-of-run stop waits at most 40 s for the start thread, then shuts the DSP down under it |
| W11 | LOW | PLAUSIBLE | 2602-2614 | the list of received packets and the intents' DONE_REUSE have no bound; a flooding DSP can use unbounded memory while the link thread is slow |
| W12 | LOW | NEEDS-HARDWARE | 2469-2475, 2358-2363 | no load barrier between reading the DSP's queue head and reading the payload |
| W13 | LOW | CONFIRMED | 4016, 4048-4052, 4080 | `wifi_mac` is a boot-arg although the file's own text says boot-args are echoed and printed with a panic; the passphrase length is logged |

Counts: 7 CONFIRMED (W1, W2, W3, W4, W7, W8, W13), 4 PLAUSIBLE (W5, W6, W10, W11; W5 also depends on hardware), 2 NEEDS-HARDWARE (W9, W12). Severity: 2 HIGH (W1, W2), 2 MEDIUM (W3, W5), 9 LOW.

## Details

### W1 GLINK length overflow: an endless loop under `glink_lock` (HIGH, CONFIRMED)

`glink_pump()` (line 2470) works out the message length in a `uint32_t` from fields of the DSP's own message.
- Line 2470: `uint32_t ... length = sizeof(message)`.
- Line 2477: OPEN, `length += message.param2`.
- Line 2479: INTENT, `length += 8 * message.param2`.
- Line 2485: DATA/DATA_MORE, `length = 16 + words[0]`.
- Line 2487: `length = (length + 7) & ~7u`.
- Line 2488: the only check is `length > glink.theirs_size - 8`.

All three sums wrap. With OPEN `param2 = 0xfffffff8`, `length = 8 + 0xfffffff8 = 0`, and `(0 + 7) & ~7 = 0`, so both of these pass:
- `0 > theirs_size - 8` is false;
- `waiting < 0` is false.

The `GLINK_OPEN` case then runs `glink_advance(0)` (line 2522), which stores the tail it just read, and breaks. The queue has not moved, `waiting` is still at least 8, and the `while (glink.up && !glink.broken)` loop (line 2469) reads the same message again, forever. The same happens with DATA and `words[0] = 0xfffffff0`. The intent is invalid, so the message is dropped with `glink_advance(0)` at line 2594, and again nothing is consumed.

A third variant is INTENT with `param2 = 0x20000000`. Then `8 * param2` is 0 and `length` is 8, but the loop at line 2546 runs 536 million times with `glink_peek` inside it, reading past the message. It runs only if `param1 == glink.their_channel`.

Consequences, all traced:
- The link thread spins at 100% CPU holding `glink_lock`. The OPEN path prints one log line per turn (line 2524), which floods the log and the loader log.
- `glink_send()` takes `glink_lock` (line 2671), so every QRTR sender (the driver, step 14 and step 15) blocks for good.
- Shutdown cannot finish. `dsp_shutdown()` calls `hakios_lx_stop()`, which sends through `glink_send` and blocks. Even without that, `link_stop()` waits 2 s (line 3125) and then does `lck_mtx_lock(&glink_lock)` (line 3132), which never returns. TrustZone is never asked to shut the DSP down, and the next kernel finds it running.

A crashed or hostile DSP can produce this by writing one 8-byte message into its queue.

Fix (sketch):
```
-	uint32_t waiting = glink_waiting(), length = sizeof(message);
+	uint32_t waiting = glink_waiting();
+	uint64_t length = sizeof(message);
 ...
-		length += 8 * message.param2;
+		length += 8ull * message.param2;
 ...
-		length = 16 + words[0];
+		length = 16ull + words[0];
 	}
-	length = (length + 7) & ~7u;
-	if (length > glink.theirs_size - 8) {
+	length = (length + 7) & ~7ull;
+	if (length < sizeof(message) || length > glink.theirs_size - 8) {
 		... glink.broken = true; return;
 	}
```
Also bound the INTENT loop by `length / 8 - 1` rather than `param2`, and consider a per-call iteration cap in the pump so that a DSP that never stops writing cannot hold the lock indefinitely.

### W2 SMEM item extents unchecked: remote-chosen offsets and sizes index the mapping (HIGH, CONFIRMED)

`smem_items()` builds `found[].offset` and `.size` from the entries in the partition. The partition is in shared memory, and the DSP makes item 480 itself when it starts (see the comment at line 2230).
- Bottom entries (lines 571-572): `offset = partition + at + sizeof(entry) + entry.padding_header`, `size = entry.size - entry.padding_data`.
  - Both paddings are `uint16_t` fields from memory.
  - `padding_data > entry.size` makes `size` wrap to about 4 GB.
  - The only bound is `entry.size > header.size` (line 566). Nothing checks that `at + 16 + padding_header + size` stays inside `header.size`, or inside `SMEM_SIZE`.
- Top entries (lines 587-589) have the same `entry.size - entry.padding_data` wrap. Their offset is bounded (`entry.size <= at`).

Consumers trust the result:
- `glink_find()` (line 2312) accepts any `ours_size` or `theirs_size` that is a multiple of 8 and at least 1024. A wrapped `0xfffffff8` passes.
- `glink_waiting()` (line 2349) only compares head and tail with `theirs_size`. Both words are in the DSP-writable descriptor.
- `glink_peek()` (line 2361) reads `smem[glink.theirs + (at + i) % theirs_size]` and `glink_put()` (line 2396) writes `queue[(head + i) % ours_size]`. Neither has any bound against the 2 MB mapping.
- A DSP that publishes item 480 with `size = 0x400, padding_data = 0x408` gets `theirs_size = 0xfffffff8`, then a head word of 0x7ffffff8 is "valid". The next `glink_peek` reads far outside the mapping, which is a kernel data abort (panic). For item 479 (`ours`), `glink_put` writes the kernel's message bytes at the same kind of unchecked offset.
- `smem_poke()` (line 515) has no bound check at all. `step_our_item()` pokes `our_item + 0..340` (line 2059) and `dsp_listen()` and `dsp_ask_to_stop()` poke into `our_item`. `our_item_find()` (line 1603) only checks `size >= sizeof(struct smp2p)`, and for a bottom entry that wrapped, this passes with an offset that can lie past the mapping.

`smem_peek()` itself is safe (it checks `offset + size > SMEM_SIZE`). The unsafe parts are `smem_word()`, `smem_poke()`, `glink_peek()` and `glink_put()`.

Fix (sketch), in `smem_items()` before using `entry`:
```
+	if ((uint32_t)entry.padding_data + entry.padding_header > entry.size ||
+	    at + sizeof(entry) + entry.padding_header + entry.size > header.free_uncached) { break; }
```
For top entries require `entry.padding_data <= entry.size`. Then, in `smem_item()` and `glink_find()`, reject any item with `offset + size > SMEM_SIZE`. Make `smem_poke()` and `smem_word()` check `offset + 4 <= SMEM_SIZE` and return false (or ignore) otherwise.

### W3 QMP mailbox bounds wrap (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED)

- `step_mailbox_open_locked()` line 1480: `if (size < QMP_MESSAGE + 4 || box < 0x3c || box + size > aoss.size || (box & 3))`.
- `step_mailbox()` line 866 has the same check.

`box` and `size` are read from the AOP's message memory (`get()` at 1478-1479). Both are `uint32_t`. `box = 0x100000` and `size = 0xffff0000` sum to 0 and pass. `our_box = 0x100000` is accepted (line 1488 or 1523). `mailbox_send_locked()` then does `rd(aoss.base + our_box)` and 16 `wr(aoss.base + our_box + 4 + 4*i, ...)` (lines 1557-1564). The mapping is 0x400 bytes (line 804). This is a read and write outside the mapping, at an offset chosen by the AOP. In `step_mailbox` it is a read only. The AOP is more trusted than the DSP, but its message memory is remote input all the same.

Fix:
```
-	if (size < QMP_MESSAGE + 4 || box < 0x3c || box + size > aoss.size || (box & 3)) {
+	if (size < QMP_MESSAGE + 4 || box < 0x3c || box > aoss.size || size > aoss.size - box || (box & 3)) {
```
(the same in `step_mailbox`).

### W4 QRTR size check wraps (LOW, CONFIRMED)

Line 2915: `if (header.size == 0 || at + header.size > length)`. Both `at` and `header.size` are `uint32_t`. With a v1 header (`at = 32`) a `header.size >= 0xffffffe0` makes the sum wrap to a small value and the datagram is accepted. For a v2 header `at` is 16..271 and the same holds for `size >= 0x100000000 - at`.
- `receive(context, ..., data + at, header.size)` (line 2948) is called with a length of about 4 GB and a pointer that may run past the packet allocation (the packet is `sizeof(*packet) + fill` bytes).
- The QMI path is protected: `qmi_receive` at `hakios.qmi.c:686` rejects `length > largest + QMI_HEADER_SIZE`.
- `wlfw_receive()` (line 3248) clamps to 64 bytes, so it over-reads at most 64 bytes of adjacent heap into `wlfw_answer_bytes`. Only step 14 with `wifi_ask=1` prints it (line 3520).
- For control messages, line 2935 copies `min(header.size, 20)` bytes from `data + at` (up to 20 bytes beyond the packet).

Impact is a small heap over-read from remote-chosen sizes. Fix: `if (header.size == 0 || header.size > length || at > length - header.size)`.

### W5 A crashed DSP is not reported to the driver (MEDIUM, PLAUSIBLE / NEEDS-HARDWARE)

`link_thread()` (lines 3086-3091) prints once when the DSP's "slave-kernel" word has bit 0 ("err-fatal") and keeps pumping. `hakios_wifi_dsp_is_up()` (line 3974) returns `dsp_started && glink.open`, with no fatal state. Nothing stops the driver, or marks the link broken, so `glink_send()` waits 5 s per call and the driver's own threads keep running.

The file's own comment (lines 3332-3339) records that a phone reset without a word when the driver's thread "was then still writing ring pointers into registers that had stopped answering". After an err-fatal the radio's registers are in the same state. Whether that is the same fault could not be settled from the repository: NEEDS-HARDWARE.

Fix (sketch): add a `static volatile bool dsp_dead`, set it in `link_thread` (and in `dsp_listen`) when `DSP_FATAL` is seen, make `hakios_wifi_dsp_is_up()` return false, make `glink_send()` return `ENOTCONN` at once, and ask the driver to stop (`hakios_lx_stop()` from the shutdown path is already in place).

### W6 State shared across threads without a lock (LOW, PLAUSIBLE)

- `smem_item()` (line 604) uses one `static struct smem_item found[256]`, filled and then searched with no lock. It is called from the link thread (`show_crash_reason()` at 3089, and `dsp_words()` while `at == 0`) and from the main thread (`our_item_find()` in `dsp_ask_to_stop()` during shutdown, `glink_reset()`). If two scans overlap, a match in one can return the offset of an entry that the other has overwritten, and `smem_poke()` then writes at the wrong place. Window: a DSP crash message at the same moment as a shutdown, which is narrow. Fix: make `found` a stack or per-caller array, or take `hakios_smem_alloc_lock` around the scan.
- `dsp_words()` caches `at` in a function static (line 657) written by both threads (harmless today because the value is idempotent).
- `link_thread_is` (lines 3035 and 3217) holds a `thread_t` that has been deallocated once the thread has ended. `qrtr_close()` compares `current_thread()` against it to decide whether to wait on `qrtr_calling`. If the address is reused by a new thread, that thread skips the wait and a callback that is running can use a closed port. It is set after `kernel_thread_start` returns, so the first moments are also unprotected. Fix: clear it when `link_runs` goes false.

### W7 Step 16 trusts the firmware's register window (LOW, CONFIRMED)

Lines 3437-3454: `address` (from `hakios_wlfw_registers`, i.e. what the Wi-Fi firmware told over QMI) is bounded only by `<= 0xffffffff`, and `size` only by `>= 3 * RADIO_WINDOW`. The step maps `ml_io_map_unmappable(radio.phys, radio.size, VM_WIMG_IO)` (line 3454), checks nothing about the result, and reads seven words at fixed offsets below `3 * RADIO_WINDOW`. A firmware that reports another physical address makes the kernel read there (a protected region ends the kernel, as the comment at 3384-3395 says). It only runs with `wifi_radio_read=1`. Fix: require `size == 0x200000` (or `<= 0x200000`), `address + size <= 0x100000000`, and a non-zero map result.

### W8 Error-path leaks and unchecked map results (LOW, CONFIRMED)

- `step_image()` lines 1894-1897 return false on a misaligned segment without `ml_io_unmap()` of the 25 MB mapping made at 1889. A step that fails here and is retried leaks address space. Fix: break out and fall through to the unmap.
- `step_header()` allocates one page per start with `kmem_alloc` (line 1832) that is "never freed" (the comment says so), including on every failure path after it. One page per start attempt.
- `glink_offer()` lines 2440-2442: when `our_intents[i].data != NULL` and `size != size`, a new buffer replaces the pointer and the old one is leaked. The size comes from the DSP's INTENT_REQUEST (line 2576), and `our_intent_count` is reset by every `step_link`. Bounded at 24 buffers of 64 KB per link restart.
- `need()` (line 399), `smem_peek()` (line 502), `step_image()` (line 1889) and `step_registers()` (line 3454) use the result of `ml_io_map*` without a check. If the call returns 0 on failure (not verified, see Not checked), the next access is a load from a low address.

### W9 Half-started TrustZone state (LOW, NEEDS-HARDWARE)

- Step 8 ends with TrustZone holding the image header and the memory window (`INIT_IMAGE`, `MEM_SETUP`). If step 9, 10 or 11 then fails before `AUTH_AND_RESET` succeeds, `steps_over()` only shuts down when `dsp_started` (line 4152-4157), so `PAS_SHUTDOWN` is never called for that peripheral. The AUTH failure path (line 2150-2154) tells the AOP "off" but does not call `PAS_SHUTDOWN` either. The file's own history (lines 69-77) says a wrong TrustZone shutdown state stopped the DSP from starting again. Whether TrustZone needs the shutdown after a failed start, as Linux's remoteproc error path does, cannot be told from the sources here.
- `dsp_started` is set only at line 2156, after the SMC returns, a `printf` inside `scm()` (which takes `say_lock` and prints to the console) and the code after it. A panic on another processor inside that window makes `hakios_wifi_quiesce()` return at line 4135 with the DSP running and not stopped. The window is a few milliseconds at most.

Fix (sketch): set a `dsp_starting` flag before the SMC and let `quiesce` and `steps_over` treat it as started; call `PAS_SHUTDOWN` on every failure after step 8 succeeded.

### W10 The end-of-run stop does not wait for the start thread for long enough (LOW, PLAUSIBLE)

`hakios_wifi_stop()` (lines 4107-4109) waits `whole_runs` for 40 s and then goes on regardless. With `wifi=1` the thread can still be inside step 15 (the driver start, calibration alone is 7 s, and the file's own comment documents a 12 s join). Shutting the DSP down under a driver that is still starting is the "registers stop answering" case at lines 3332-3339. Fix: either wait without a bound (the thread's own steps all have bounds) or set a "stop wanted" flag that `whole_thread` checks between steps and `link_stop`/`glink_send` honour.

### W11 Unbounded queue of received packets (LOW, PLAUSIBLE)

In `glink_pump()` lines 2600-2616, a complete DATA message is copied into a `kalloc_data` packet and appended to `glink.first/last`, and the DSP is told DONE_REUSE at once, so it can send again at once. The consumer is the link thread, which can be held in a callback or in `glink_send()` for up to 5 s (line 2701) while the main thread's `glink_send()` also pumps and enqueues. A DSP that streams packets of up to 64 KB (`size > 0x10000` is rejected in `glink_offer`) grows the list without bound during that time. Fix: cap the list (count or bytes) and delay DONE_REUSE until the packet has been consumed.

### W12 Missing load barrier on the DSP's queue (LOW, NEEDS-HARDWARE)

`glink_waiting()` reads the DSP's head with `rd()` (line 2347), and `glink_peek()` then reads the payload with plain byte loads from the same mapping (line 2361). The producer side is ordered (`settle()` between payload and head in `glink_put`, lines 2399-2400), but the consumer has no `dmb ishld` or `dsb ld` between reading the head and the payload. Whether the mapping (`VM_WIMG_WCOMB`) allows the loads to be reordered is not stated in this repository: NEEDS-HARDWARE. Fix: `__asm__ volatile ("dmb ld" ::: "memory")` in `glink_waiting()` after the head read.

### W13 Credentials and identifiers in the log and in boot-args (LOW, CONFIRMED)

- `hakios_wifi_radio_address()` (line 4016) reads the radio's MAC from the boot-arg `wifi_mac`. The comment above `hakios_wifi_network()` (4048-4052) says boot-args "are echoed by the loader and printed with a panic", which is why the passphrase is not one; the same reasoning applies to the MAC (a device identifier). No code in this file reads `fw-wifi/mac`; if the reviewer's brief expects it, it is not here (lines 4001-4007 say the value is "nowhere in these sources"). The log prints only the length of the MAC (line 4039), which is fine.
- `hakios_wifi_network()` prints the lengths of the name and the passphrase (line 4080) and nothing else; `join_given()` zeroes its copy after the join is asked for (4196). The passphrase itself never reaches the log from this file. `userland/build.sh:384` installs `fw/network` with mode 0600.
- A failed join flushes the whole kept log (`say_kept()`, line 4210) into the real log and into the loader's log. That log holds what the driver and the steps said; this file's own lines contain no secrets, and the driver files were not audited for them (`lx_80211.c:24` says only lengths are said).

## Checked and found fine

- `smem_peek()` bound (line 504): `offset` is `uint64_t`, so `offset + size` cannot wrap; every `smem_peek` caller is safe from out-of-range reads. The unsafe parts are listed in W2.
- `smem_partition()` (521-549): the TOC `count` is capped at 64 (3104 bytes of table, within the 4 KB), partition `offset + size` is checked against the TOC, `header.size == entry.size` is required.
- `smem_items()` loop termination: each bottom iteration advances `at` by at least 16 and the loop ends at `free_uncached`, which is bounded by `header.size`; the top loop ends on `at <= free_cached` and on the `entry.size + step_back > at` guard (line 592), so a corrupt partition cannot make it loop. The scan cost is bounded (at most 131072 entries).
- `smp2p_entry()` and every use of `words->valid`: capped at 16. `show_words()` uses `%.16s` and a bounded `snprintf` with a size guard. `dsp_ask_to_stop()`, `dsp_listen()` and `step_our_item()` index `entry[]` only with the capped value, and the poke offsets (at most 336 of 340 bytes) fit the item.
- `show_crash_reason()` (710-726): `text[81]` is zeroed, the copy is `min(size, 80)`, printed with `%s` as an argument (not a format).
- Torn reads of the 340-byte SMP2P item: `smem_peek` copies bytewise, so a snapshot can mix old and new bytes, but no state bit can appear that was not set in the old or the new value, and `memcmp` change detection is only an optimisation.
- Every `say()`, `hakios_wifi_say()`, `hakios_wifi_tell()` and `printf` (macro for `say`) call in this file has a literal format; remote data (DSP names, crash text, SMP2P names, QRTR sizes) is only passed as `%s`, `%u` or `%.16s` arguments. Buffers are 400 bytes with `vsnprintf`, `say_kept()`'s `piece[201]` and its modulo indexing are right, the `kept[]` ring writes are under `say_lock`. The one effect left is that remote text can contain control characters or a fake log line (cosmetic).
- `rd()`, `wr()` and `need()`: every `rd` or `wr` on a block (`ipcc`, `aoss`, `rsc`, `arb_*`, `tlmm`, `apps_smmu*`, `smem_lock`) is preceded by a `get`/`put`/`need` in the same step, and the steps run in order: `wifi_step=N` always runs 1..N, and `needed[]` for `wifi=1` includes step 2 (which maps `ipcc` and `aoss`) before any step that uses them. Offsets checked against block sizes: `RSC_TCS(7) + TCS_COMMAND(15)` fits 0x10000; `ARB_CHANNEL(511)` and `ARB_OWNER(511)` fit 0x1100 and 0x1000; the observer window for channel 511 ends at 0x10000; `GPIO_*` for pins 84-86 fit 0x3000; SMMU `SMR`/`S2CR` for 255 entries fit 0x2000.
- `cmd_db`/RPMh readers: slave counts are capped at 512, offsets stay inside the 128 KB map for the sizes involved, `data_offset + entry->offset + length` is checked against `CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000`, `levels[160]` is guarded. (The command database is the boot loader's, not remote-writable at run time.)
- MDT/ELF loading (1312-1385): the size is capped at one page, segment count is 3..16 and `52 + 32 * count <= size`; each loaded segment is checked against the reserved window in 64 bits (`paddr >= WPSS_MEMORY`, `file_size <= memory_size`, `paddr + memory_size <= window end`), so the uint32 `highest` cannot wrap; `image.segment[]` cannot overflow because `count <= MAX_SEGMENTS`; the segment file sizes are compared to the header; `52 + 32 * count + hashes == size` is required; `name[16]` fits `wpss.bNN`. `step_image()` requires 8-byte alignment of start and length, writes only inside the window, reads everything back, and `segment_word()` cannot read beyond `file_size`. Only the first few bytes of `header[0..4]` are read before the size is known to be at least 5 (the file is in the RAM disk; at most a few bytes past a tiny file).
- SCM calls (1724-1755): all arguments are compile-time constants or validated values (`image.size`, `WPSS_MEMORY`, `kvtophys` of a page-aligned single page from `kmem_alloc(KMA_KOBJECT)`), the metadata page is cache-cleaned before the call, a preempted call is retried at most 100 times, errors are checked by every caller.
- Wait and poll loops, with what happens at the timeout: `mailbox_wait` (1 s, link and channel taken down again on each failure), `mailbox_send_locked` (1 s, message taken back), `our_item_make_locked` (1 s, lock not owned so nothing written; the hardware lock is released on every other path), `spmi_read` (2 ms), `radio_space_on` TLB sync (100 ms, returns false before the context is switched on), `step_start` (`wifi_wait`, always bounded by `limit` or `!dsp_started`), `dsp_ask_to_stop` (`bound_ms`), `glink_send` (5000 ms), `step_link` (5 s), `link_stop` (2 s), `doorbells()` (8 iterations), the IPCC drain in `step_start` (8). The only unbounded loop reachable from remote data is W1.
- Shutdown path (`dsp_shutdown`, `hakios_wifi_stop`, `steps_over`, `hakios_wifi_quiesce`): order is driver, wlfw, link, ask-to-stop, TrustZone shutdown, doorbell disable, AOP "off", SMMU context back (only for a DSP started by this kernel, and only after TrustZone has agreed: if the shutdown fails the SMMU is left on, which is the safe choice). The panic path takes no lock and does not rely on a thread (the `leaving` flag), and its waits are loops. A failed `PAS_SHUTDOWN` leaves `dsp_started` true.
- Lock order: `dsp_lock` -> `hakios_aop_mailbox_lock`/`glink_lock` -> `say_lock`; `qrtr_calling` -> `qrtr_lock`/`glink_lock`; no path takes them the other way round. No spinlock is held across a sleep (there are none in this file; sleeps are `delay_for_interval` with mutexes held, which is allowed). `qrtr_close()` waits for a running callback with `qrtr_calling` unless called from the link thread.
- Use after free: `link_thread()` reads `packet->length` while building the `kfree_data` argument, before the free; `link_stop()` frees queued packets under `glink_lock`; QRTR callbacks run under `qrtr_calling`; `our_intents[].data` buffers are never freed (so never dangling); `qrtr_out_packet()` frees after `glink_send` returns (which copies into the queue).
- Uninitialised data: `struct smp2p` copies are fully written by `smem_peek` before use; `qrtr_control` is zeroed before the copy; `mailbox_send_locked` zero-fills its 64 bytes; `show_words`'s `line` is zeroed; `dsp_ask_to_stop()`'s `theirs.flags` printout follows a successful `dsp_words`.
- `glink_pump()`'s other cases: the name copy is bounded (`min(param2, 32)`) and zero-terminated; DATA copies at most the intent's free space (`words[0] <= size - fill` is checked before the copy and `fill <= size` is an invariant); the intent index is checked against `our_intent_count`; `their_intents[]` insertion is bounded to 64; `glink_offer()` caps at 24 intents of at most 64 KB and rejects zero.
- `glink_send()` and `glink_put()` sizes: the message size is bounded against the queue (`EMSGSIZE`), `glink_room()` checks the head and tail from shared memory against `ours_size` (apart from W2), the head is reduced modulo `ours_size`, and a head that is changed between the room check and the use is still reduced.
- `qrtr_out_packet()`: length 1..8192, allocation `sizeof(header) + padded`, and `memcpy` of `length`. Tables (`qrtr_servers[64]`, `qrtr_ports[16]`, lookups[4]) are bounded; a full table drops silently. A DSP cannot make us answer HELLO more than once.
- Boot-arg parsing: `wifi_mac` (lines 4008-4046): at most 32 characters, at most 2 digits per byte, at most 6 bytes, a multicast or all-zero address is refused, `bytes[]` is only copied when valid. `wifi_step` is clamped to `STEPS`; the other numeric args (`wifi_wait`, `wifi_listen`, `wifi_watch`, `wifi_pause`, `wifi_new`) only affect how long a step waits and use 64-bit arithmetic for the time (the one 32-bit product, `seconds * 1000` in `step_qrtr`, wraps only for a boot-arg above about 4 million seconds). `hakios_wifi_option()` returns 0 for anything unknown.
- `hakios_wifi_network()` parsing: bounds are by `end`, an empty line gives 0, CR is trimmed only when present, lengths over the destination size are not copied, a missing second line leaves `lengths[1] = 0`, which fails the 8..63 check. The result is rejected unless the name is 1..32 and the passphrase 8..63.
- SMMU code: `radio_space_find()` bounds `used[256]` and the context against `contexts`; `radio_enter()` indexes page tables by shifted bits, stops at `RADIO_TABLES` (32) and returns false; `radio_map()` bounds the address pool; every `put` into the SMMU is undone by `radio_space_off()` once `radio_space.on` is true.
- DMA coherence: the header page and the radio's page tables are cleaned with `dc civac` and followed by `dsb sy`; the image is written through a write-combining map with a `dsb sy` before TrustZone starts the DSP.

## Not checked

- Everything outside this file: `hakios.lx.c`, `hakios.wlfw.c`, `hakios.qmi.c` (beyond the one bound read), `hakios.sta.c`, `hakios.apple80211.c`, `hakios.adsp.c` (which shares the mailbox lock and the SMEM allocation lock), `hakios_image_file()`, `loader_log_putc()` and the Wi-Fi driver under `wifi/lx/`. Whether any of them logs a key or the passphrase, takes `hakios_wifi_say` in interrupt context (it takes a mutex), or calls `qrtr_close()` from a context that deadlocks with `qrtr_calling`, is open.
- Whether `ml_io_map`, `ml_io_map_unmappable` or `ml_io_map_wcomb` return 0 on failure or panic (W8); how `PE_parse_boot_argn` treats a non-numeric value for a 4-byte buffer (a value like `wifi_file=off` could be read as non-zero); how `thread_terminate(current_thread())` behaves on a kernel thread that is finishing itself.
- Hardware facts: the mapping attribute behind `VM_WIMG_WCOMB` (so the alignment and ordering rules for W12 and unaligned `ldr` on item offsets), register layouts of IPCC, QMP, the PMIC arbiter, the RSC, the SMMU and TZ calling conventions, and whether a stale `STATUS_DONE` in the arbiter's observer can answer a new read early (`spmi_read`, line 1104). Timings stated in comments were not verified.
- Whether TrustZone expects `PAS_SHUTDOWN` after a failed start (W9) and whether the DSP's SMP2P "restart" handshake in `dsp_listen()` matches Linux in every case.
- Modem code (out of scope) and the audio loader beyond the shared-lock declarations.
- No build, run, or runtime test was done.

## Fix status

All edits are in `drivers/wifi/hakios.wifi.c`; nothing was compiled or run. Line numbers are from the file after the edits.

- W1 FIXED: `glink_pump()` (about 2505-2535) sums the message length in a `uint64_t` (`wide`), so OPEN, INTENT and DATA lengths can no longer wrap to 0; the existing `> theirs_size - 8` check now rejects them (queue marked broken), and `length` is narrowed only after that check. This also bounds the INTENT loop. Not done: a per-call iteration cap in the pump (design change).
- W2 FIXED: `smem_items()` ends the walk for an entry with `padding_data > size` or one that reaches past `free_uncached` (bottom), or `padding_data > size` (top); `glink_find()` requires the descriptor and both queues to lie inside the 2 MB mapping; `smem_poke()` and `smem_word()` ignore/return 0 for an offset outside the mapping or while it is not mapped.
- W3 FIXED: the mailbox check is now `box > aoss.size || size > aoss.size - box` in both `step_mailbox()` and `step_mailbox_open_locked()`.
- W4 FIXED: `qrtr_input()` checks `header.size > length || at > length - header.size` instead of the wrapping sum.
- W5 SKIPPED: the fix is a new "dead" state that stops the driver and changes what `glink_send()` and `hakios_wifi_dsp_is_up()` return; it is a design change, and what the radio does after err-fatal needs hardware.
- W6 PARTLY FIXED: `link_thread_is` is cleared when the link thread ends. SKIPPED: the shared `static found[256]` in `smem_item()` (a mutex cannot be used, because the panic path calls it with no lock taken; a 3 KB stack array needs a decision on stack use), and the `dsp_words()` static `at` (idempotent).
- W7 FIXED: step 16 requires `size <= 4 * RADIO_WINDOW` (2 MB) and `address + size <= 4 GB`, and returns false if the map result is 0.
- W8 PARTLY FIXED: `step_image()` unmaps the 25 MB window on the misaligned-segment return and returns false if the map is 0; `glink_offer()` frees a kept intent buffer of another size before replacing it; `smem_peek()` and `step_registers()` check the map result. SKIPPED: the page of `step_header()` that is "never freed" on purpose (TrustZone may still use it; whether it can be freed needs hardware knowledge), and `need()` (it returns void and its callers cannot handle a failure; whether `ml_io_map` can return 0 is not known).
- W9 SKIPPED: needs knowledge of what TrustZone expects after a failed start, and a new "starting" state (design change).
- W10 SKIPPED: waiting without a bound or a "stop wanted" flag changes the shutdown flow (design change).
- W11 SKIPPED: capping the list and delaying DONE_REUSE changes the protocol flow (design change); a plain cap would drop packets.
- W12 SKIPPED: whether the WCOMB mapping reorders the loads is hardware behaviour, and a barrier there is a memory-ordering decision.
- W13 SKIPPED: reading the MAC from somewhere other than a boot-arg is a new feature, and the logged lengths of the name and passphrase are deliberate and documented in the comments (they help to diagnose a bad `fw/network`); no secret reaches the log.

```

`docs/driver-review/wifi-stack.md`:

```md
# Wi-Fi stack above the bring-up: security and robustness review

Read-only audit. Nothing was built, run or modified except this file.

## Scope

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `wifi/lx/src/lx_wpa.c` (WPA2-PSK arithmetic, 4-way and group handshake) | 523 |
| `wifi/lx/src/lx_wpa.h` | 49 |
| `wifi/lx/src/lx_80211.c` (frames, scan, join, 802.11 <-> Ethernet) | 2097 |
| `wifi/lx/src/lx_base.c` (LinuxKPI stand-ins: threads, work, memory, DMA pool) | 1235 |
| `wifi/lx/src/lx_bus.c` (bus, ring service thread, IRQ glue, driver start/stop) | 863 |
| `wifi/lx/src/lx.h` | 20 |
| `drivers/wifi/hakios.lx.c` (kernel side of the driver object) | 582 |
| `drivers/wifi/hakios.wlfw.c` (WLFW client; also read the codec in `hakios.qmi.c` 197-575 and the rx/txn code 617-963, only as far as WLFW uses it) | 545 |
| `drivers/wifi/hakios.sta.c` | 371 |
| `drivers/wifi/hakios.apple80211.c` | 739 |

Also read for evidence: `tools/wpa-test/test_wpa.c`, `xnu/files/bsd/sys/hakios.sta.h`, `hakios_wifi_network()` in `hakios.wifi.c`, the boot seed in `xnuloader/loader.c` 3050-3080, `xnu/files/osfmk/minicrypto/mc_provider.c` (PRNG part).

Method: full read of every file above, tracing every length that comes from the air, firmware or userland to its use, checking `lx_wpa.c` line by line against IEEE 802.11-2020 clause 12.7 (key hierarchy, EAPOL-Key layout, supplicant rules), RFC 8018 (PBKDF2), RFC 2104 and RFC 3394. The ath11k driver sources are not in this tree (`xnu-deps/build/ath11k` is absent), so driver and firmware behaviour is inferred from comments only. The test program in `tools/wpa-test` was read but not run (no C compiler on this host).

Notes on the previous review (`docs/net-review.md`): beacon parsing in `heard()` and the SSID/element copies in `apple80211.c` were not redone; I only re-confirmed in passing that `element()` and the copies are bounded.

## Findings

| Id | Severity | Confidence | Where | One line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Medium | CONFIRMED | lx_wpa.c:472-477, 369-384; lx_80211.c:1809-1812 | An unauthenticated message 1 re-derives and overwrites the live KCK/KEK/TK, at any time, from any spoofed sender |
| W2 | Medium | CONFIRMED | lx_80211.c:807-813, 1795-1808 | Handshake result is last-writer-wins: one forged EAPOL frame aborts the join or hides a good message 3 |
| W3 | High if reachable | NEEDS-HARDWARE (code gap CONFIRMED) | lx_80211.c:752-777, 817-826, 913 | 802.11-format data frames reach the IP stack without any "protected / decrypted" check (mac80211's drop-unencrypted rule is missing) |
| W4 | Medium | CONFIRMED (absence in this layer) | lx_80211.c:16-18; lx_wpa.c:429; lx_wpa.h:31 | No packet-number (replay) check for group-addressed frames; the RSC from message 3 is stored and never used |
| W5 | Medium | PLAUSIBLE | lx_base.c:794-834, 759 | DMA ring pool is never freed; every peer or BA session consumes it for good, and the pool is a fixed 12 MB |
| W6 | Low-Medium | PLAUSIBLE | xnuloader/loader.c:3053-3057 -> lx_80211.c:1660 | The supplicant nonce comes from a CSPRNG whose boot seed is a function of the timer counter |
| W7 | Low | CONFIRMED | lx_wpa.c:415-434, 480-515 | Message 3 is not checked for RSNE match, Install/Secure bits, or GTK length/index |
| W8 | Low | CONFIRMED | lx_80211.c:1603, 1626-1628, 565-576 | A requested BSSID is ignored on the scan path, and the chosen target can be replaced by a stronger same-SSID beacon during the join |
| W9 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | lx_80211.c:1474-1503, 850, 872, 804-806 | Teardown races: rx path can queue work or use `radio->sta`/`radio->wpa` while `station_leave()` frees or wipes them |
| W10 | Low | CONFIRMED | lx_80211.c:1417-1428, 1380-1401 | Group rekey: a failed `set_key` is only logged and the old key is dropped anyway |
| W11 | Low | PLAUSIBLE | lx_base.c:342-357, 278-279; lx_bus.c:410-414 | `timer_delete_sync` does not wait for a running callback; `irq_group` can loop without bound under load |
| W12 | Info | CONFIRMED | lx_80211.c:669-672; lx_wpa.c:259-288 | The user's own AP BSSID is logged although the name is hidden; AES intermediates and failed-unwrap plaintext are not wiped |

Counts: 7 CONFIRMED (W1, W2, W4, W7, W8, W10, W12), 4 PLAUSIBLE (W5, W6, W9, W11), 1 NEEDS-HARDWARE (W3). The WPA2 arithmetic itself (PBKDF2, PRF, MIC, key unwrap, replay rule, nonce check) found no defect; see the section "Checked and found fine".

## Details

### W1 - an unsigned message 1 overwrites the live keys (Medium, CONFIRMED)

`lx_wpa.c:472-477`:

```c
if ((info & (INFO_PAIRWISE | INFO_ACK | INFO_MIC)) == (INFO_PAIRWISE | INFO_ACK)) {
	memcpy(wpa->peer_nonce, message + AT_NONCE, 32);
	derive(wpa);
```

`derive()` (369-384) writes `wpa->kck`, `wpa->kek`, `wpa->pairwise` and sets `have_keys`. There is no state check: the branch runs in any state, including after message 3 was accepted and after `joined`. The only filter is in `handshake_message()` (lx_80211.c:789): `radio->sta != NULL` and Ethernet source == the AP's BSSID, both of which an attacker in range can satisfy with a plaintext frame (EAPOL frames are plaintext by design; no MIC protects message 1).

Failure scenarios:

1. Window during join. After message 3 is accepted, `station_join()` waits (handshake loop) and then `lx_pause_ms(30)` (line 1809) before `key_set(radio, radio->wpa.pairwise, ...)` (1810). A forged message 1 arriving in that window replaces `wpa.pairwise` with a key derived from the attacker's ANonce. The firmware gets a wrong TK; the AP's frames cannot be deciphered and ours are rejected; the join reports success ("THE NETWORK IS JOINED"), the link is dead.
2. After join. A forged message 1 replaces KCK/KEK. Every later genuine group-key message (message 1 of the group handshake) then fails the MIC (`lx_wpa_message` returns `LX_WPA_BAD`), so the group key is never updated; once the AP rotates its GTK, broadcast and multicast traffic (ARP requests for our address, IPv6 RA/NS) stops reaching us. A retransmitted genuine message 3 also fails ("nonce is not message 1's").
3. Amplification: each forged message 1 costs one PRF (3 HMAC-SHA1) plus a transmitted 121-byte message 2, and one unconditional `printf` (lx_80211.c:800).

Standard: IEEE 802.11-2020 12.7.6 treats message 1 as unauthenticated; the supplicant is expected to tolerate extra or forged message 1 frames without changing the keys in use until a message 3 passes MIC verification (the usual solution is a candidate PTK). I could not quote the exact sentence offline, so the rule is marked as my reading of 12.7.6.2-12.7.6.4.

Suggested fix (candidate keys, promoted by a valid message 3):

```diff
 struct lx_wpa {
+	unsigned char cand_kck[16], cand_kek[16], cand_tk[16];  /* from the latest message 1, not yet proven */
 	unsigned char kck[16], kek[16];
@@ derive():
-	memcpy(wpa->kck, keys, 16);
-	memcpy(wpa->kek, keys + 16, 16);
-	memcpy(wpa->pairwise, keys + 32, 16);
-	wpa->have_keys = 1;
+	memcpy(wpa->cand_kck, keys, 16);  memcpy(wpa->cand_kek, keys + 16, 16);  memcpy(wpa->cand_tk, keys + 32, 16);
+	wpa->have_cand = 1;
@@ lx_wpa_message(), signed path:
+	/* message 3 (pairwise bit): verify with cand_kck; every other signed message with kck */
+	kck = (info & INFO_PAIRWISE) ? wpa->cand_kck : wpa->kck;   /* mic_of takes the key as a parameter */
+	... after MIC, nonce, replay, unwrap and GTK all pass, for a pairwise message:
+	memcpy(wpa->kck, wpa->cand_kck, 16); memcpy(wpa->kek, wpa->cand_kek, 16); memcpy(wpa->pairwise, wpa->cand_tk, 16);
+	wpa->have_keys = 1;
```

The unwrap in a pairwise message also has to use `cand_kek`. Message 2 is answered with `cand_kck` as it is now.

### W2 - the handshake outcome is overwritten by whatever came last (Medium, CONFIRMED)

`handshake_message()` stores every non-`NOTHING` result: lines 807-813 (`radio->handshake = said;`). `station_join()` waits with `while (radio->handshake != LX_WPA_KEYS && radio->handshake != LX_WPA_BAD && ...)` (1795-1797), then requires `radio->handshake == LX_WPA_KEYS` (1800).

Two failures, both from a spoofed plaintext EAPOL frame:

1. Any forged signed-looking key frame with `MIC|ACK` set and a bad MIC (or no message 1 seen yet) makes `lx_wpa_message` return `LX_WPA_BAD` (lx_wpa.c:484, 493). The loop exits at once and the join fails with `EAUTH`, which Darwin shows as "wrong password" (`apple80211.c:639` maps `EAUTH` to result 21, "invalid PMK").
2. A genuine message 3 sets `handshake = KEYS`; a forged message 1 right behind it sets `ANSWER` before the join thread has run. The loop then keeps waiting and times out after 8 s, although the handshake succeeded and message 4 was sent.

Fix: make KEYS sticky, and do not end the wait on BAD (the standard says to silently discard bad frames):

```diff
-	if (said != LX_WPA_NOTHING) {
+	if (said == LX_WPA_KEYS || (said != LX_WPA_NOTHING && said != LX_WPA_BAD && radio->handshake != LX_WPA_KEYS)) {
 		...radio->handshake = said;
@@ station_join():
-	while (radio->handshake != LX_WPA_KEYS && radio->handshake != LX_WPA_BAD && radio->answer != ANSWER_GONE && ...
+	while (radio->handshake != LX_WPA_KEYS && radio->answer != ANSWER_GONE && ...
```

Keep a separate `radio->handshake_bad` counter and `handshake_why` for the log line.

### W3 - no "was it protected" check on the 802.11 data path (NEEDS-HARDWARE; code gap CONFIRMED)

`linuxkpi_ieee80211_rx()` (lx_80211.c:913) sends any 802.11 data frame through `to_ethernet()` and `ethernet_received()`. `to_ethernet()` reads the Protected bit (0x4000) only to size the header (line 767); it never requires it. `ethernet_received()` (817-826) hands every non-EAPOL frame to `lx_os_net_input()` when `radio->joined`. `RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED` is not looked at anywhere in the tree (grep), and the module header lists the missing group-frame PN check (see W4) but not this.

Under Linux, mac80211 supplies the rule (drop unencrypted data frames once a key is installed, except EAPOL). This layer replaces mac80211, so the rule has to be here. Failure scenario if the firmware passes a frame up in 802.11 form without having deciphered it: an attacker in range sends a From-DS data frame (TA = BSSID, RA = our MAC, Protected = 0, LLC/SNAP + ARP or IP) after the join; it is accepted and enters the IP stack (ARP poisoning, forged DNS or TCP). The RX_FLAG_8023 path (firmware decapsulates and deciphers) is not affected. Whether the ath11k firmware drops such frames itself I cannot tell from this tree; hence NEEDS-HARDWARE. A test: with a second radio, inject the frame after the join and watch `received` in the `lx_station_say()` line.

Suggested fix:

```diff
-static bool to_ethernet(struct sk_buff *skb, bool cipher_header_gone)
+static bool to_ethernet(struct sk_buff *skb, bool cipher_header_gone, bool *protected)
 ...
+	*protected = (control & 0x4000) != 0;
@@ linuxkpi_ieee80211_rx():
-	} else if (to_ethernet(skb, (status->flag & RX_FLAG_IV_STRIPPED) != 0)) {
-		ethernet_received(radio, skb);
+	} else if (to_ethernet(skb, (status->flag & RX_FLAG_IV_STRIPPED) != 0, &prot)) {
+		ethernet_received(radio, skb, prot && (status->flag & (RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED | RX_FLAG_IV_STRIPPED)));
@@ ethernet_received(radio, skb, bool ciphered):
-	} else if (radio->joined && skb->len >= 14) {
+	} else if (radio->joined && (ciphered || hardware_decap) && skb->len >= 14) {
```

(`hardware_decap` is true on the RX_FLAG_8023 call.)

### W4 - no replay check for group-addressed frames (Medium, CONFIRMED absence)

The module header (lx_80211.c:16-18) says "the check of the packet numbers of the group's frames that the driver leaves to this layer" is not done. `lx_wpa.c:429` stores the RSC from message 3 / group messages into `wpa->group_counter`; nothing reads it (grep: only lx_wpa.c:429 and lx_wpa.h:31). Unicast PN checking is in the firmware; for broadcast and multicast, ath11k's own comment says mac80211 does it.

Failure: an attacker records a genuine broadcast or multicast frame (ARP request, DHCP, mDNS, IPv6 router advertisement) and replays it later; it is accepted. A replayed RA with a short lifetime or an old prefix, or a replayed ARP, is enough to disturb the host. Standard: IEEE 802.11-2020 12.5.3.4.4 (CCMP decapsulation: discard an MPDU whose PN is not greater than the replay counter of the key/TID); the initial counter comes from the RSC in the key message (12.7.6.4). The clause number is from memory, hence the rule is PLAUSIBLE; the absence of any check is CONFIRMED. Whether the firmware performs a group PN check on its own is NEEDS-HARDWARE.

Fix: in the RX_FLAG_8023 path the PN is not visible, so either enable the firmware's group replay detection (driver option) or have the driver pass `status->extiv` for group frames and compare it with a per-key counter seeded from `wpa.group_counter` (reset on every group-key install):

```diff
+	if (is_multicast_ether_addr(da) && !pn_greater(status->extiv, radio->group_pn)) drop();
+	memcpy(radio->group_pn, status->extiv, 6) ... (little-endian PN, 6 bytes)
```

### W5 - the ring pool is never given back (Medium, PLAUSIBLE)

`linux_dma_alloc_coherent()` (lx_base.c:794-812) advances `pool.rings_used`; `kmem_free()` (814-818) and `dma_free_noncoherent()` (831-834) are empty. The pool is `POOL_RINGS` = 12 MB, of which the author notes the data path uses "about 6 MB" (759). The comment at 820-824 states that the data path takes a few KB per traffic class of every station and that "here they stay taken". `station_join()` creates a new station each attempt (lx_80211.c:1702-1708; a failed attempt included), `ba_handle()` restarts an RX BA session on every ADDBA from the AP.

Failure: each (re)join, each failed join, and each ADDBA (with `wifi_ba=1`) permanently consumes pool space. A phone that re-joins often (spoofed deauth frames are accepted because PMF is not implemented, so an attacker can force a re-join as often as wifid retries) eventually reaches "no room for N more bytes of rings" (line 804): the driver cannot create peers and Wi-Fi stays down until reboot. The leak is certain from the code; the per-join size (about 17 TIDs x 1 KB if ath11k sets up every TID) and thus the number of joins to exhaustion (a few hundred) is my estimate, and which ath11k allocations go through these two functions I cannot see.

Fix: replace the bump allocator with a free list of 64-byte-aligned extents (or a bitmap of 4 KB pages) and implement `kmem_free()` / `dma_free_noncoherent()`; also rate-limit RX_START per TID in `ba_handle()`.

### W6 - the supplicant nonce depends on a weak boot seed (Low-Medium, PLAUSIBLE)

Source of the SNonce: `get_random_bytes(radio->wpa.own_nonce, 32)` (lx_80211.c:1660) -> `arc4random_buf()` (lx_base.c:1206) -> `read_random()` (hakios.lx.c:205) -> the minicrypto HMAC-DRBG (`mc_provider.c`, seeded from the device-tree `random-seed`). That seed is built in the loader (`xnuloader/loader.c:3053-3057`):

```c
seed[i] = (uint8_t)(READ_SYSREG(CNTVCT_EL0) >> (i & 7)) ^ (uint8_t)(i * 37);
```

All 64 bytes are a function of a few consecutive reads of the virtual counter, so the entropy is that of the counter value at that moment, roughly 25-30 bits if the boot time is known to a few seconds (19.2 MHz counter assumed). Unless the kernel's entropy collector reseeds the DRBG with real entropy before the first join (`mc_prng_refresh`, not verifiable from here), the nonce, and everything else the kernel draws from `read_random`, is predictable by enumeration.

Impact on WPA2 itself is limited: the SNonce is sent in the clear in message 2, and the standard needs it to be unique, not secret (IEEE 802.11-2020 12.7.5: nonces to be random with negligible chance of repeating; the section number is from memory). A repeated SNonce combined with a repeated ANonce would repeat the PTK; the AP's ANonce is random. The finding is therefore mainly about the shared kernel PRNG; it is listed here because the task asked where the nonce comes from.

Fix: seed from several independent sources (CNTVCT jitter over many samples, the SoC's TRNG/PRNG registers, the DT `rng-seed` from the previous boot, UFS/timing jitter) and block the first `read_random` consumer until a reseed has happened.

### W7 - message 3 is not fully validated (Low, CONFIRMED)

`lx_wpa.c:480-515` accepts a message 3 on MIC, replay counter, ANonce match, Encrypted bit and a parseable GTK KDE. Not checked: (a) the RSNE in the key data against the RSNE the AP announced (the standard asks for this and for a deauthentication with reason 17 on mismatch; IEEE 802.11-2020 12.7.6.4, clause number PLAUSIBLE), so there is no downgrade protection for anybody holding the PSK; (b) Install and Secure bits; (c) GTK KDE: `e[1] - 6` may be anything from 5 to 32 (line 425-427) and the key id `e[6] & 3` may be 0, while `key_set()` always copies 16 bytes (lx_80211.c:1396) and installs with that index. `protection()` only accepts CCMP, so the right length is 16 and the right index 1-3.

Failure: an AP (or a PSK holder) can make the station install a GTK that is shorter than 16 bytes (the rest is stale `wpa->group` content, zero at join) or with index 0; this breaks group traffic rather than leaking anything.

Fix:

```diff
-	e[1] - 6u <= sizeof(wpa->group)) {
+	e[1] - 6u == 16 && (e[6] & 3) != 0) {
```

and in `lx_wpa_message()` for a pairwise message: `if (!(info & INFO_INSTALL) || !(info & INFO_SECURE)) -> BAD`, plus compare the RSNE found in `data` with the RSNE of the beacon (pass the target's element 48 to `lx_wpa_message`).

### W8 - requested BSSID ignored on the scan path; target replaced during join (Low, CONFIRMED)

`station_join()` honours `what->bssid` only when choosing from the already-heard list (lx_80211.c:1612-1613). If nothing matches, `station_scan()` is called up to three times (1626-1628) and `heard()` (565-576) fills `radio->target` with the strongest beacon of that name, with no BSSID filter. So an ASSOCIATE for a given access point (Apple80211 `bssid`, copied at apple80211.c:540) joins a different one.

`heard()` keeps overwriting `radio->target` as long as `radio->sta == NULL` (567), i.e. through the whole of the join up to line 1702, including the PMK derivation (1651-1665) and the channel set-up. A stronger beacon with the same SSID replaces address, capability and elements; `vif->bss_conf.bssid` is a pointer to `radio->target.address` (1668), so it changes under the driver. Also `bzero(target, ...)` at 1603 is done without `lx_os_lock()` while `heard()` writes it under the lock.

Fix: store `what->bssid` in `radio->want_bssid` and have `heard()` test it; stop `heard()` from updating `target` once `joining` is set (do the selection once, under the lock); copy the address into `vif->cfg.ap_addr`-backed storage instead of pointing at `target`.

### W9 - teardown races (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

`station_leave()` cancels `group_work` and `ba_work` (1474-1475) and later frees `radio->sta_memory` (1502) and wipes `radio->wpa` (1480), but rx runs on another thread. In between, `management_received()` still passes its guards (`radio->sta != NULL`, `radio->reached >= ASSOC`, line 850; `reached` is reset only at 1504) and calls `queue_work(radio->work, &radio->ba_work)` (872); `ba_handle()` captures `params.sta = radio->sta` (1107) before testing it (1122) and calls `ampdu_action` on a station that the driver has already removed or that is freed. Likewise `handshake_message()` can call `ethernet_send()` (798) which passes `radio->sta` to the driver while it is freed, and queue `group_work` after `joined` was cleared by someone else, in which case `group_rekey()` (1425) installs `radio->wpa.group` after it was zeroed (an all-zero GTK). The window is the duration of the `station_state` steps (tens of ms); `wifi_ba=1` is needed for the first case.

Fix: take `lx_os_lock()` around `radio->sta`/`reached` tests in the rx path and set a `radio->leaving` flag first in `station_leave()`; cancel the works after the flag is set; make `ba_handle()` read `radio->sta` once under the lock.

### W10 - a failed group-key install is only logged (Low, CONFIRMED)

`group_rekey()` (1417-1428): `radio->group_key = key_set(..., &error)`, then `key_drop(radio, &old, false)` whatever `error` is. `key_set()` returns the config even when `set_key` failed, or NULL on ENOMEM. After a failure the old key is removed from the firmware and the new one is not installed: group traffic is lost, `rekeys` is still incremented, only a `lx_tell` line says so. Also the replay counter was already advanced for this message, so the AP's retransmission is rejected.

Fix: drop the old key only if `error == 0`; on failure free the new config, keep the old key, and return the failure to the handshake so that the group message 2 is not sent (the AP will retransmit).

### W11 - timers and the IRQ thread (Low, PLAUSIBLE)

- `timer_delete_sync()` (lx_base.c:343-357) returns without waiting for a callback that the ticker thread is running (`due->function_415(due)` is called after unlocking, lines 278-279); the comment at 342 says so. If the driver frees the structure that contains the timer right after, the callback runs on freed memory. Fix: record `running` under the lock and wait for it in `timer_delete_sync()`.
- `irq_group()` (lx_bus.c:410-414) loops `do { ... } while (done >= DATA_BUDGET)` while holding `bus.service`, on the one thread that serves every vector. Sustained receive load keeps copy-engine interrupts (WMI, handshake) and the ring thread waiting. Fix: bound the loop (for example 4 rounds) and re-arm the vector so the thread yields.

### W12 - minor (Info, CONFIRMED)

- `say_heard()` (lx_80211.c:669-672) hides the name of "the network that is wanted" but prints its BSSID, channel and signal; the file header (24) and the code comment at 666 promise only that the name and passphrase are not said. A BSSID is a location identifier.
- Not wiped: `t[16]` in `aes_decrypt()` (lx_wpa.c:260-286, holds the last decrypted block, that is part of the GTK) and `a[8]` in `aes_unwrap()`; in `lx_wpa_message()` the `data[]` buffer is wiped on success and on "no group key" but not when `aes_unwrap()` fails (line 503-505). Kernel stack residue only.

## Checked and found fine

Cryptography in `lx_wpa.c`:

- PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 (RFC 8018 5.2 with SHA-1, 4096 iterations, 32-byte output = block 1 whole plus 12 bytes of block 2): salt is SSID || INT(block) with a big-endian 32-bit block number (149-154), `U_1 = HMAC(P, S || INT(i))`, `U_j = HMAC(P, U_{j-1})`, XOR-accumulated, 4095 further rounds (156-164). HMAC handles keys over 64 bytes by hashing. Matches the structure used by IEEE 802.11-2020 Annex J.4. `tools/wpa-test` checks the J.4.2 vectors and RFC 2202 (read, not run).
- PRF (171-185): label || 0x00 || data || counter byte, counter from 0, 20 bytes per round, 48 bytes for CCMP (KCK 16, KEK 16, TK 16); matches 12.7.1.2 / 12.7.1.3. PTK data (369-378): min(AA,SPA) || max(AA,SPA) || min(ANonce,SNonce) || max(...), 76 bytes with exact offsets. Roles: `own` is `vif->addr`, `peer` is the BSSID (lx_80211.c:1658-1659); correct for infrastructure (AA = BSSID).
- EAPOL-Key layout (`AT_*` offsets): 4+1+2+2+8+32+16+8+8 = 81 for the MIC, 97 for the data length, 99 for the data; matches figure 12-35.
- MIC (355-365): HMAC-SHA1 over the EAPOL frame from the version byte through the end of the declared body, with the 16 MIC bytes replaced by zeros, truncated to 16 bytes, key = 16-byte KCK; this is the rule for key descriptor version 2 (HMAC-SHA1-128). Computed over `4 + body` (the declared length), not the received length. Comparison is constant time (488-490). Descriptor version is required to be 2 (462) and descriptor type 2 (458).
- AES key unwrap (RFC 3394 2.2.2): six rounds j = 5..0, i = n..1, `t = n*j + i` XORed big-endian into A (307-320), integrity value A6A6A6A6A6A6A6A6 checked over all 8 bytes with an OR accumulator (321-323, 326); length must be a multiple of 8 and at least 24 (301); output buffer `data[640]` vs plaintext at most 4+body-99-8 <= 533. The `n = length/8 - 1` before the length test wraps for length 0 but is not used before the test. The `ENCRYPTED` bit is required (503). Test vectors in `tools/wpa-test` cover RFC 3394 4.1, a spoiled input and a wrong length.
- Key data length from the air: `4 + body` is bounded by the received length and by 640 (451); `AT_DATA + data_length > length` is rejected (466); reads of fixed offsets up to 98 only after `length >= 99`. Truncated or short frames return NOTHING or BAD without reading past the buffer (also covered by the test "a key message cut short").
- Replay counter: 8-byte big-endian comparison, strictly greater (495); updated only after MIC, nonce, unwrap and GTK parse all passed (513). Message 3 must carry message 1's ANonce (499). A retransmitted message 3 (higher counter) is answered again and does not reinstall keys: `handshake_message()` only queues work for `LX_WPA_GROUP`, and `station_join()` installs the PTK once, so there is no key-reinstallation (KRACK) exposure through message 3 retransmission. A replayed message 3 or group message 1 is rejected.
- GTK KDE walk (415-434): both `at + 2 <= length` and `at + 2 + len <= length`; `memcpy` size at most 32 into `group[32]`; the copy ends at the element end. Group message 1 requires MIC and ACK, the same MIC and replay path.
- Reply buffer: `handshake_message()` gives 14+256 bytes; replies are 99+22 = 121 (rsn_length is the constant 22, lx_80211.c:1662) or 99.
- Nonce source: see W6 (CSPRNG, fresh per join; one per join, reused for message 1 retransmissions, which is allowed).
- Wiping: PBKDF2 temporaries (166-167), HMAC pad and inner (137-138), PRF digest (184), derived `keys[48]` (382), unwrap round keys and block (324-325), `data[]` on success; `explicit_bzero(&radio->wpa)` at leave (lx_80211.c:1480); `key_drop()` wipes the key config; `what` zeroed after the join (1858); `apple80211.c:560-565` uses `memset_s`; `hakios.sta.c` zeroes the queued join request after copying it. `explicit_bzero` in `lx_base.c:1187` is a separate-TU `bzero` and is not elided.
- Logs: no printf or `lx_tell` in `lx_80211.c`, `lx_wpa.c`, `apple80211.c` or `hakios.sta.c` prints a passphrase, PMK, PTK, GTK or nonce; the join prints lengths only; `apple80211.c` logs types, lengths and kinds only. The Apple80211 `set_join` validates passphrase length 8..63 and PMK length 32 (543-549); `hakios_wifi_network()` validates 1..32 and 8..63 (4087-4090). `station_join()` itself does not re-check `passphrase_length <= 64` (it is a `uint8_t`; `lx_wpa_pmk` would over-read the `what` struct for larger values), but every in-tree caller validates.

Frame paths in `lx_80211.c`:

- Management: every fixed-offset read is behind a length test (`length < 26`, `>= 30` for authentication and association response, `>= 28`/`>= 33` for the ADDBA/DELBA action frames); `answer_length` is clamped to `ELEMENTS_MOST` (847); `aid` masked to 14 bits; deauthentication/disassociation handling reads only f[24..25]. The `tid` index is masked to 0..7. The sender (TA) and receiver (RA) addresses are compared against the AP and our own address.
- `to_ethernet()`: header size at most 24+6+2+4+8 = 44, `skb->len >= header + 8` checked before the LLC test, `skb_pull(header + 8 - 14)` is at least 18 and at most `len`; address and ethertype are copied out before the pull. (Minor: `f[0]`, `f[1]` are read before the first `skb->len` test; two bytes inside the same buffer, not exploitable.)
- A-MSDU and fragments: the A-MSDU bit is never interpreted, so flipping it (FragAttacks CVE-2020-24588) has no effect; there is no fragment reassembly, so the mixed-key and fragment-cache attacks do not apply here; fragments are not reassembled (a first fragment would be passed as a frame, but only decrypted data reaches this path, see W3 for the caveat).
- Association response parsing: `element()` walkers are bounded; WMM parse requires `e[1] >= 24` and reads at most `e+25`; HT (>= 26), VHT (>= 12), HT operation (>= 22) and TIM (>= 2) lengths are tested before use. A concurrent overwrite of `answer_elements` by a forged association response can change content under `station_abilities()`, but all reads stay in the 1024-byte array or at worst the next field of the same struct.
- `request_elements()` output is at most about 131 bytes into a 300-byte buffer.
- Rx serialization: when `wifi_irq=1`, copy-engine and data-path service run under `bus.service` (lx_bus.c:318, 397, 410), otherwise only the ring thread runs them; so `lx_wpa_message()` and `management_received()` are never run concurrently with themselves.
- Scan: `station_scan()` request is sized from the channel counts; channel list bounded by `frequency_count <= 64` (set in `apple80211.c:484`); SSID copy bounded (32).

`lx_base.c`, `lx_bus.c`, `hakios.lx.c`:

- DMA: `lkpi_dma_map_phys()` refuses anything outside the pool; `pmap_kextract` answers only for pool memory; ring allocations are rounded, overflow-safe (`size_t` arithmetic) and zeroed; skb data slots are bounds-checked against `POOL_SLOT` before allocation (879). The pool is one physically contiguous allocation behind the SMMU window; nothing is sized from a hardware register except the register window offsets in `window()`/`refused()`, which are range-checked against the three windows.
- Thread/IRQ model: the hard handler only masks the vector, ORs the pending bit and wakes; handlers run on one thread; `lx_os_irq_disable()` and `detach_all` wait for a running handler; there is no lost wakeup (`assert_wait` before the `xchg`). Sleeping lock words panic on self-recursion by design. `idr_*` and `rhashtable_*` are under the layer's lock. The transmit queue (`lx_queue`) keeps its slot reserved until `lx_queue_out++`; full-queue test is `in - out == LX_QUEUE`.
- `hakios.sta.c`: one worker thread, one lock; `hakios_sta_attach(NULL)` waits for calls and readers; request structs are copied under the lock and zeroed after use. `standing` (the passphrase of the file network) is kept for the life of the system by design (to re-join when the radio is switched on).
- `apple80211.c`: `give()` clamps `copyout` to the caller's `req_len`; `give_network()` clamps elements to the room the caller declared and to 1024; scan request lengths are checked against `sizeof`.

QMI codec as used by `hakios.wlfw.c` (WLFW service only):

- `decode_counted()` rejects a count above `elem_len` before storing it (499); arrays (numbers or structures, nested) therefore stay inside the C structure; static arrays use `elem_len`; strings need `length < elem_len` and are NUL-terminated (476-480), so the `%s` prints of `fw_build_id` and `fw_build_timestamp` (wlfw.c:449-454) are safe; each TLV's length is checked against the message and the message against the datagram (`qmi_receive`, 686-693); unknown TLVs are skipped; a TLV that does not describe a known element is ignored; the destination of a reply is decoded under the lock and the transaction is removed under the lock on timeout, so a late reply cannot write into a dead stack frame. Every `ask()` caller zeroes its reply structure first, and `send_file()` bounds the file (256 KiB) and each piece (`QMI_WLANFW_MAX_DATA_SIZE_V01`). A reply without the result TLV reads as "success" (the zeroed `result` is 0), as it does in Linux's qmi helpers.

Concurrency and lock order: no cycle found among `lx_lock`, `bus.service`, `wiphy->mtx`, `sta_lock`, `apple80211_lock`; `station_leave()` cancels work items without holding `wiphy->mtx`, so `ba_handle()`/`group_rekey()` cannot deadlock against it; the deauth path in the rx thread calls the station events after dropping `lx_os_lock`.

## Not checked

- The ath11k driver itself and the firmware (not in the tree): whether it drops unprotected data frames (W3), checks multicast PN (W4), and how much of its DMA goes through `dma_alloc_coherent`/`dma_alloc_noncoherent` (W5, its rate).
- `tools/wpa-test` was not run (no compiler available on the Windows host), and `reference.py` was not read line by line; the AES, PBKDF2 and unwrap checks above are by reading the code against the standards' vectors that the test cites.
- `hakios.wifi.c` (bring-up, firmware loading, DSP), `hakios.net.c` (what `hakios_net_input` does with a frame), the QRTR transport under `hakios.qmi.c`, and the generated `hakios.wlfw_ath11k.h` tables.
- The minicrypto DRBG internals and whether the kernel entropy collector reseeds it before the first join (W6).
- Side channels: the AES code is table-driven and `times()` has a data-dependent ternary; it runs only for the key unwrap, so only a local cache-timing attacker would matter.
- 40/80 MHz width selection and rate/HT/VHT handling were read for bounds only, not for correctness against the standard; power save, roaming, regulatory domain logic and the `wifi_lx=1` register-trace path were skimmed.
- Behaviour on hardware (everything marked PLAUSIBLE or NEEDS-HARDWARE).

## Fix status

- W1: FIXED (partly). `lx_wpa.c` `lx_wpa_message()`: an unsigned message 1 is accepted only while no signed message has been accepted yet (`!replay_known`); afterwards it is ignored (`LX_WPA_NOTHING`, no reply, keys untouched). This closes the 30 ms window before `key_set()` and the after-join KCK/KEK overwrite. SKIPPED: the candidate-key scheme for a forged message 1 *before* message 3 (needs new fields in `struct lx_wpa`, i.e. `lx_wpa.h`, which was not in the editable set; the forged frame still makes that join fail, as W2 case 1 describes).
- W2: FIXED. `lx_80211.c` `handshake_message()`: `radio->handshake` is no longer overwritten once it is `LX_WPA_KEYS`; `station_join()`: the wait no longer ends on `LX_WPA_BAD` (only KEYS, the AP's deauthentication or the 8 s timeout), the reason is still logged on timeout. A genuinely wrong passphrase still ends through deauthentication or the timeout.
- W3: SKIPPED. NEEDS-HARDWARE: whether the driver sets `RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED`/`IV_STRIPPED` on every legitimate 802.11-form frame is not known; requiring it could drop real group traffic.
- W4: SKIPPED. Protocol/design change (per-key PN state, and whether `status->extiv` carries the PN depends on the firmware/driver).
- W5: SKIPPED. Replacing the bump allocator with a freeing allocator is a design change and needs knowledge of which ath11k allocations go through it.
- W6: SKIPPED. The seed is in `xnuloader/loader.c`, outside the editable files.
- W7: FIXED (partly). `lx_wpa.c` `group_key()`: the GTK KDE must be 16 bytes and have key number 1 to 3. SKIPPED: the Install/Secure bit checks (supplicants such as wpa_supplicant do not require them; rejecting could break real APs) and the RSNE comparison with the beacon (needs a changed `lx_wpa_message()` signature / `lx_wpa.h`).
- W8: FIXED. `lx_80211.c`: the requested BSSID is stored in `radio->want_bssid` and tested in `heard()`; a new `radio->target_fixed` stops `heard()` from replacing `target` once the join has chosen; the `bzero(target)` is now under `lx_os_lock()`. SKIPPED: `vif->bss_conf.bssid` still points at `target.address` (now stable after the choice).
- W9: SKIPPED. Locking/teardown redesign (PLAUSIBLE, needs a `leaving` protocol across rx, work items and the driver).
- W10: FIXED (partly). `lx_80211.c` `group_rekey()`: on a failed `set_key` the old key is kept and the new configuration is wiped and freed. SKIPPED: not sending group message 2 and not consuming the replay counter on failure (needs a handshake design change).
- W11: SKIPPED. `timer_delete_sync()` waiting risks self-deadlock when called from the ticker's own callback, and bounding `irq_group()` needs knowledge of the vector's (edge/level) re-arm behaviour.
- W12: FIXED. `lx_80211.c` `say_heard()`: the BSSID of the wanted network is not printed. `lx_wpa.c`: the last AES block `t[16]` in `aes_decrypt()`, `a[8]` in `aes_unwrap()` and `data[]` after a failed unwrap are wiped.

Test: `tools/wpa-test` (copied to WSL, built with the sanitizers, no output left in the tree) passes, 195 checks 0 failed (seed 1); with seed 7 and one extra ad-hoc check (a forged message 1 after message 3 changes no key and gets no reply) 207 checks, 0 failed. `lx_80211.c` was only re-read, not compiled.

`docs/drivers-config.md`:

```md
# Drivers in the configuration: what the kernel is built with

A Linux kernel builds a driver when its `Kconfig` symbol is on: `drivers/input/touchscreen/Kconfig` declares
`TOUCHSCREEN_GOODIX`, the directory's `Makefile` says `obj-$(CONFIG_TOUCHSCREEN_GOODIX) += goodix.o`, and a device's defconfig
(`arch/arm64/configs/vendor/<device>_defconfig` in an Android kernel) turns on what that phone has. Every phone vendor's tree is
that, with its own drivers added the same way.

This kernel is Apple's XNU, which has the same idea under other names, much older than Kconfig: `config/MASTER` declares the
**options** (`options APFS # <apfs>`), a component's `conf/files` lists its files as `standard` or `optional <option>`, and a
configuration (`DEVELOPMENT = [ ... ]` in `MASTER.<arch>.<platform>`) is the list of what is on; `SETUP/config/doconf` and
`config(8)` turn that into the list of objects and `-D<OPTION>` for the compiler. The drivers of this port are XNU options of
that kind. Nothing here imitates Kconfig's files; what a driver is, is written once per subsystem, in `drivers/<subsystem>/conf`.

```
drivers/<subsystem>/conf      the drivers of a subsystem: their files, what they require, what they are
configs/*_defconfig           CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y or `# CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME> is not set`, beside the boot-argument symbols
tools/hakios-config.py kernel the choice of the .config put into the kernel tree (make kernel runs it)
```

## `drivers/<subsystem>/conf`

```
standard bsd/dev/hakios.input.c
	help    /dev/hakios-touch, the queue of touches and buttons, and where the phone's drivers are started from

driver GOODIX
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.goodix.c
	help    the touch screen: a Goodix GT9916 or a FocalTech FT3680 on SPI (touchscreen=1) ...

driver SOUND
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.sound.c
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.guard.c
	requires ADSP SPEAKER
	help    the speakers playing (sound=N) ...
```

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| `standard PATH [OPTION...]` | a file every kernel has (with XNU options of its own, if given: `hakios.apfs_check.c apfs`) |
| `driver NAME` | the symbol `CONFIG_HAKIOS_NAME`, the XNU option `HAKIOS_NAME`, the attribute `hakios_name` |
| `file PATH [OPTION...]` | one of its files, as its path in Apple's tree; a `.cpp` of `iokit/Kernel` also wants `iokitcpp` |
| `requires NAME...` | drivers it cannot be built without (it calls them, and nothing could stand in for them) |
| `default y\|n` | what a configuration that does not name it gets; `y` if not said |
| `help TEXT` | what it is, and which boot-argument starts it; more `help` lines go on |

Every `.c` and `.cpp` of `drivers/map` is built by exactly one `standard` line or `driver`, of the conf of its own subsystem;
`tools/drivers-check.py` (CI) checks that, and a file that none builds would be in the tree and never compiled.

The 25 drivers there are now, by subsystem:

| Subsystem | Drivers (`CONFIG_HAKIOS_*`) | Always built |
|---|---|---|
| core | `SOCINFO` | `hakios.version.c`, `hakios.platform.c`, `hakios.stubs.c` |
| input | `VIRTIO_INPUT`, `GOODIX`, `BUTTONS` | `hakios.input.c` |
| storage | `UFS`, `VIRTIO_BLK` | `hakios.image.c`, `hakios.sparse.c`, `hakios.apfs_check.c` |
| gpu | `ADRENO` | |
| camera | `CAMERA`, `TORCH` | |
| haptic | `HAPTIC` | |
| audio | `ADSP`, `SPEAKER`, `SOUND` (requires ADSP, SPEAKER), `MIC` (requires ADSP, SOUND), `VIRTIO_SOUND` | `hakios.audio.c` |
| power | `BATTERY`, `CPUFREQ`, `THERMAL`, `PMIC`, `BATTGUARD` | |
| wifi | `WIFI` (requires QMI) | |
| bluetooth | `BT` | |
| modem | `QMI`, `MODEM` (requires QMI, UFS) | |
| net | `VIRTIO_NET` | `hakios.net.c` |

`tools/hakios-config.py help HAKIOS_SOUND` says the same of one of them, and what requires it.

## A device's defconfig chooses its drivers

A driver nobody names is built (`default y`): every driver was built before there were these symbols, and a `.config` made
then still gives the same kernel. A device leaves out what it does not have:

```
# configs/qemu_defconfig (in the tree): QEMU's virt machine, the phone's drivers left out of the kernel
#include common_defconfig
#include open.config
#include virt.config
CONFIG_DEVICE="qemu"
# CONFIG_HAKIOS_GOODIX is not set
# CONFIG_HAKIOS_ADRENO is not set
...
```

```bash
make qemu_defconfig        # .config: 4 drivers built in (the virtio ones), 21 left out
make config                # says which are built and which are not
make kernel                # builds that kernel
```

A port to another phone starts the same way: its `configs/<name>.config` leaves out each driver whose hardware it has not
ported yet (the addresses and pins in a driver are the POCO X5 Pro's, and its head says where each came from), and turns one
on when it has been made to work there. A phone with another touch controller adds a driver, not a branch: its file in
`drivers/input/`, a line in `drivers/map`, a `driver` block in `drivers/input/conf`, and `CONFIG_HAKIOS_<IT>=y` in its defconfig.

### What is checked

- `# CONFIG_HAKIOS_X is not set` means **left out**, not "the default": a fragment can take a driver out of a configuration
  that an earlier file put it in, as in Linux.
- A driver built without one it `requires` is refused: `CONFIG_HAKIOS_SOUND requires CONFIG_HAKIOS_ADSP (drivers/audio/conf:13)`.
- A boot-argument that only left-out drivers read is refused, with the driver named:
  `CONFIG_TOUCHSCREEN gives touchscreen=, which only hakios.buttons.c, hakios.goodix.c read, and they are not built
  (CONFIG_HAKIOS_BUTTONS, CONFIG_HAKIOS_GOODIX)`. The kernel would not complain: the argument would just never be looked at.
  (The readers are found the way `tools/boot-args.py` finds them, in the source.)

## How the choice reaches XNU's build

`tools/hakios-config.py kernel` (run by `make kernel` through `tools/make-kernel.sh`, and by `xnu/apply.sh`) writes, into the
kernel tree, only what has changed:

| File in the tree | What | In `xnu/hakios.patch`? |
|---|---|---|
| `bsd/conf/files`, `iokit/conf/files` | one block between `# HakiOS drivers: ...` and `# end of the HakiOS drivers`: each file `standard` or `optional hakios_<name>` | yes: it does not depend on the configuration |
| `config/MASTER.hakios` | `#  HAKIOS_DRIVERS = [ hakios_goodix ... ]` (the attributes that are on) and an `options HAKIOS_<NAME> # <hakios_<name>>` line for every driver | no: made for each build, kept out by `xnu/export.sh` |
| `bsd/dev/hakios.drivers.h` | the list, for `sysctl kern.hakios.drivers` and the boot log line `hakios-kernel: N drivers built in` | no |

and what the patch carries once: `SETUP/config/doconf` reads `MASTER.hakios` after `MASTER` and `MASTER.arm64.bcm2837`; the
kernel configurations of `MASTER.arm64.bcm2837` (`RELEASE`, `DEVELOPMENT`, `DEBUG`, `KASAN`) include `HAKIOS_DRIVERS`; each
component's `conf/Makefile` makes its configuration again when `MASTER.hakios` changes. XNU's build passes the options as
`-DHAKIOS_<NAME>` in the compiler's command line rather than as a file an object depends on, so when the choice changes,
`kernel` also removes the objects of the files that ask about it (`#ifdef HAKIOS_*`): they are built again.

Linux's `ath11k` object (`tools/mk-ath11k.sh`) is linked in only with `CONFIG_HAKIOS_WIFI` (`xnu-build.sh`): its calls are
answered by `hakios.lx.c`.

## Leaving a driver out without breaking the others

The rest of the kernel calls the drivers in a few places: where they are started (`hakios.input.c`, `hakios.audio.c`,
`bsd_init.c`), where a run ends or a panic leaves (`loader_return.c`, the thermal and battery guards, `machine_routines.c`),
and a few questions on the way ("is this device one of the storage's?", "how warm is the battery?"). Those calls stay as they
are. For a driver that is left out, `drivers/core/hakios.stubs.c` (XNU keeps `bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c` for the same purpose) has
what each such call then does: nothing, and the answer "no", "not known" or "not there". With every driver built it compiles to
nothing, so the phone's kernel is the one it was.

What several drivers share was moved where none of them owns it, `drivers/core/hakios.platform.c`: the PMIC arbiter's lock
(from `hakios.buttons.c`), the locks of the always-on processor's mailbox, the shared memory's allocation, RPMh and the SMMU
(from `hakios.wifi.c`), and the `kern.hakios` sysctl node (from `hakios.battery.c`). Before, the camera could not be linked
without the Wi-Fi driver, and every driver's sysctls without the battery's. The camera's and the motor's firmware is read with
`hakios_image_file()` directly instead of through the Wi-Fi driver.

## What was checked

On a Mac (Apple clang, the toolchain of `xnu-deps/`), 27 October 2026: the kernel built and linked with every driver
(`make kernel` without a `.config`), and with `make qemu_defconfig`, four drivers of 25. The QEMU kernel was not booted yet,
and nothing here was run on the phone. `tools/hakios-config-test.py` and `tools/drivers-check.py` pass.
