`docs/port-pkg110.md`:

```md
# Bring-up on the connected device (branded PKG110)

Status of getting HakiOS — and the cellular path — running and debuggable on the phone attached to
this machine. Everything below was verified on the actual device or the actual files; nothing is
assumed.

## The decisive finding: it's `redwood` / SM7325, the reference platform

The connected phone reports itself as OnePlus **PKG110**, but that branding is spoofed (KernelSU +
`rezygisk` + `tricky_store`). The device tree — which the bootloader fills and which is not spoofed
— tells the truth:

```
/proc/device-tree/model = "redwood based Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. SM7325"
compatible              = qcom,yupik-idp qcom,yupik qcom,idp
ro.soc.model            = SM7325
ro.product.board        = redwood
```

**Same SoC (SM7325) and same board codename (`redwood`) HakiOS already targets as the POCO X5 Pro 5G.**
This is not a new port; it is bring-up of the existing `redwood` support on this unit. No new
`devices/<name>/` with its own SoC map, UEFI port or driver addresses is required.

### SoC args verified against the hardware

Pulled the phone's own `/sys/firmware/fdt` (via root) and ran `tools/soc-args.py` on it. Every
address it produced matches the reference `devices/redwood/soc.args`:

```
soc_ipa_base=0x1e40000   soc_gsi_base=0x1e04000   soc_ipcc=0x408000
soc_rsc=0x18220000       soc_apps_smmu=0x15000000 soc_cmd_db=0x80860000
soc_mpss_mem=0x8b800000  modem_ipa_fw_at=0x8b710000 soc_smem=0x80900000
soc_imem=0x14600000      soc_ipa_stream=0x480     soc_ipa_stream_uc=0x482
soc_pas_mpss=0x4         soc_pas_ipa=0xf          soc_ipa_fw=yupik_ipa_fws
```

Only `soc_aoss` was not emitted (its node is named differently in this unit's DT); that register is
fixed by the SoC, not the board, so the kernel's built-in SM7325 default (`0xc300000`) applies.
**No boot-arg overrides are needed on this device.**

## Firmware: pulled — after a real porting fix

The stock `devices/redwood/pull-firmware.sh` got **0 files** on this ROM. Not because anything
is missing: `/vendor/firmware_mnt` is a vfat mount owned by `system` with `fmask=0337`, and
`/vendor/firmware` is not readable by the adb shell user either, so a plain `adb pull` is refused
for every file. Under root all of it is there.

Fix: `devices/redwood/pull-firmware-root.sh` — the same pull by way of `su`, through a
world-readable staging directory in `/data/local/tmp` that is removed afterwards. Nothing on the
phone is changed. Result, verified:

| dir | contents | size |
|---|---|---|
| `fw-modem/` | `modem.mdt` + 28 segments, and `image/` (370 files: the modem's own files for TFTP) | 273 MB |
| `fw-audio/` | `adsp.mdt` + b00–b36 (38) | 21 MB |
| `fw-wifi/` | `wpss.mdt` + b00–b07 (9) | 7.3 MB |
| `fw-gpu/` | `a660_gmu.bin`, `a660_sqe.fw`, `a660_zap.*` (7) | 137 KB |
| `fw-haptic/` | `aw8697_haptic.bin` | 7.5 KB |

(837 files, 313 MB, 10.7 s. Camera firmware is not pulled: its files carry the first phone's renamed
names and are not needed for the modem or the network.)

## Bootloader

`ro.boot.flash.locked=1`, `verifiedbootstate=green`, `ro.secureboot.lockstate=locked` — but
`tricky_store` is installed, whose whole job is to report a locked/green state while the device is
unlocked. KernelSU cannot be installed on a genuinely locked bootloader of this class, so the
bootloader is almost certainly **unlocked, with its lock state spoofed**. The definitive check is
the boot test itself: `./xl enter` does a `fastboot boot`, which a truly locked device refuses.

## Running from Windows (Git Bash) — what had to be solved

- **No theos needed for a first boot.** `xl` falls back to `prebuilt/hakios-kernel` and
  `prebuilt/loader.efi` when nothing is built (`xl:50-53,120`): those are the `redwood` kernel and
  loader, i.e. for this SoC. The toolchain is only needed to build a *changed* kernel (which the
  cellular fix eventually is).
- **The Darwin system image IS needed for a modem run** (a correction: the first run proved the
  earlier assumption wrong). With no ramdisk at all (`XL_RAMDISK=none`) the kernel panics before
  the modem thread starts -- `Failed to mount root device @IOKitBSDInit.cpp:926` -- because the
  modem steps run "once the root is there" (`hakios.mpss.c:6256`). And the modem's firmware is read
  from `/fw` of the system image, which `MODEM=1 userland/build.sh` fills from `fw-modem/`
  (`hakios.mpss.c:1045-1110`). The modem's own file systems (modemst1/2, fsc, fsg) do come from the
  phone's UFS (`ufs=2`), but in addition to the image, not instead of it. So the project's standard
  path applies: `sysimage/unpack.sh YOUR.ipsw` (Darwin userland 16.5, which you supply; ~7.4 GB unpacked) and
  `PREBUILT=1 REST=1 MODEM=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh`.
- **Build in WSL's own ext4, not on `/mnt/d`.** `unpack.sh` relies on 7z leaving files named
  `NAME:com.apple.decmpfs` (finished by `unzbm`); `:` is not a legal NTFS file-name character, and
  drvfs is slow on tens of thousands of small files. A local clone in `~/hakios` plus a copy of
  `fw-*` is used; the finished `root.apfs`/`system.apfs` are copied back to the D: checkout for `xl`.
  Verified beforehand: 7-Zip 26 (>= 23 reads APFS), `cc` (builds `unzbm`), `numpy` present and
  guarded anyway; `lzfse` is not on the build path (`mkapfs.py` is stdlib-only) -- note the PyPI
  package `pyliblzfse` provides the module `liblzfse`, not `lzfse`; what the scripts import is the
  PyPI package `lzfse`. `modem_firmware.py` validated this unit's 28 modem segments against the DTB
  window to the byte (the last segment ends exactly at `0x9ae00000`).
- **`flock` is absent in Git Bash**, and `xl` wraps every `fastboot` call in it (`xl:60`) and takes a
  run lock on a file descriptor (`xl:109`). `tools/win-bin/flock` is a shim that drops the lock
  arguments and runs the command as it is (one `xl` at a time here, so the lock buys nothing).
  Verified for both forms. WSL2 would have the real `flock` but cannot see USB without usbipd.
- **`python3` is real** (3.14.7, not the Store stub); `mkpayload.py` and `mkxnuimg.py` are stdlib only.
- **The modem run payload builds locally** with the exact invocation `xl run` uses:
  16 809 392 bytes (the kernel is 16 809 112), the command line embedded. This is what gets staged.

## The build (done, verified)

In WSL's ext4 (`~/hakios`, a local clone plus `fw-*`):

- `sysimage/unpack.sh`: ~9 min. `done: 2.9G rootfs, 26M cryptex, 11M App cryptex, 2.6G dyld shared
  cache` (5.7 GB in `sysimage/`); `unzbm` built by `cc`, the LZBITMAP files finished, PingFang
  trimmed 74 -> 26 MB.
- `PREBUILT=1 REST=1 MODEM=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh`: ~4 min, exit 0. The small image got
  `fw/` from `fw-gpu fw-wifi fw-haptic fw-audio` (15 files; camera absent, not needed); the modem's
  firmware went into `system.apfs` `/fw` (`MODEM=1`, validated first).
- `root.apfs`: 2371 blocks x 4096 = 9 711 616 bytes. `system.apfs`: 641 948 blocks x 4096 =
  2 629 419 008 bytes (2.5 GB). Copied to the D: checkout's `userland/` for `xl`: sizes identical
  byte for byte, both carry the APFS container magic `NXSB` in block 0.

## The run (the project's own cellular runner)

With `userland/system.apfs` and `root.apfs` in the D: checkout, from the repository root in Git Bash:

```sh
XL_SB_DELAY=8 XL_END=android \
tools/modem-cycle-win.sh "modem=1 modem_again=1 modem_buffer=0xa8000000 modem_ipa_data_trace=1 net_trace=20" 600
```

`modem-cycle-win.sh` is `tools/modem-cycle.sh` with only its PATH lines changed. The original
prepends `tools/macos-bin`, whose `stat` and `timeout` exec `/opt/local/bin/gstat`/`gtimeout`
(MacPorts) and whose `flock` is a Python script on `fcntl` -- none of which exist under Git Bash, so
the original fails there on its first `fastboot` call (`xl:60`). The variant uses Git Bash's own
GNU `stat` and `timeout` and the `tools/win-bin/flock` shim. It does `./xl enter`, `./xl ramdisk userland/system.apfs` (~80 s), then `./xl run`
with `debug=0x8 rd=md0 hv_wdt_pet=1 bootcpu=7 cpus=8 cpufreq=1 ufs=2` plus those args, follows the
log live, prints a modem-only summary of it, and (`XL_END=android`) returns the phone to Android.
This is the full bring-up through registration and the data session; `modem_ipa_data_trace=1` and
`net_trace=20` make the QMI exchange and the first frames visible -- the evidence the fix is made from.

### What the first run showed

Booted with no ramdisk at all, the prebuilt kernel came up, then panicked at 56 s on
`Failed to mount root device` -- before any `mpss:` line. Not a modem failure: a missing root. That
run did prove the bootloader unlock, the Windows fastboot driver and the whole local pipeline.

## What this does to the phone — read before saying go

`./xl enter` **reboots the phone out of Android** into fastboot and RAM-boots the loader; `./xl run`
RAM-boots an experimental kernel for the session. **Nothing is flashed**: `./xl reboot` (or a
power-cycle) brings the phone's own Android back. If the bootloader turns out to be genuinely
locked, `fastboot boot` is refused and the phone sits in fastboot until `fastboot reboot`. It is
your daily phone, so this step runs only on your explicit go-ahead.

## After the log

Read `logs/*-run.log` → find where registration / the data session stops (QMI error codes, timing)
→ make the targeted fix in `hakios.mpss.c` / `hakios.qmi.c` → set up theos to rebuild → re-run →
iterate. The fix is made and verified only against the real on-device log; nothing here fabricates
a result.

```

`docs/porting/drivers.md`:

```md
# Writing a driver

A driver here is one or more C or C++ files of the kernel, a block in a `conf` file that makes it a configuration symbol, and a
boot-argument that starts it. This page goes through adding one; [Drivers in the configuration](../drivers-config.md) is the
reference for the mechanism.

## Where it goes

| The driver is | Put it in |
|---|---|
| for hardware many devices share, or a SoC family's | the common repository: `drivers/<subsystem>/` |
| one device's own (a touch controller only it has) | that device's repository: `devices/<name>/drivers/<subsystem>/` |
| a SoC family's own | the SoC's layer: `devices/<name>/soc/drivers/<subsystem>/` |

Subsystems: input, storage, gpu, camera, haptic, audio, power, wifi, bluetooth, modem, net, core.

## 1. The file

`hakios.<name>.c` (or `.cpp` for an IOKit service). The head says what it is, where every address and number came from (the
device tree, the vendor's Linux driver, a measurement), and what has been seen working:

```c
/*
 * The touch screen of the My Phone (mydevice): a Novatek NT36672 on I2C 2, as a source of touches for /dev/hakios-touch
 * (sys/hakios.input.h). Only with boot-arg touchscreen=1.
 *
 * Where the numbers come from: the phone's device tree (i2c@988000, novatek,nt36xxx), Novatek's Linux driver ...
 *
 * Status: written, not yet run.
 */
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>

void
hakios_nt36672_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("touchscreen", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;                 /* nothing is touched unless a boot-argument asks */
	}
	/* ... hakios_touch_post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN, finger, x, y) for each sample ... */
}
```

Rules every driver here follows:

- **nothing happens without its boot-argument**; a driver that is built in and not asked for touches no register;
- every value read from the phone is checked before it is used: a length, an offset, an index;
- a step that fails says which, in one log line, and the driver stops rather than guessing;
- writes to a PMIC or to storage are the exception, and are listed in `tools/provenance.allow` with why.

## 2. Make it a symbol

In the `conf` of its subsystem (common: `drivers/input/conf`; a device's: `devices/<name>/drivers/input/conf`):

```
driver NT36672
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.nt36672.c
	help    the touch screen of the My Phone: a Novatek NT36672 on I2C (touchscreen=1)
```

`file` is the file's place in Apple's tree: `bsd/dev/` for C, `iokit/Kernel/` for C++ (with `iokitcpp`). `requires` names
drivers it cannot be built without.

A common driver is also a line of `drivers/map` (`input    bsd/dev/hakios.nt36672.c`); a device's is not, it is found by its conf.

## 3. Start it

Drivers are started in one of two ways:

- by XNU's own initcall, `STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, my_init);` at the end of the file. Nothing else to change; this
  is how `socinfo`, `thermal`, `pmic`, `battguard` and `bt` start. **Prefer this for a new driver.**
- from a hub's list (`hakios_input_init()` in `hakios.input.c`, `hakios_audio_init()` in `hakios.audio.c`), when the order
  matters. Then the hub calls it whether or not it is built: give it a stand-in in `drivers/core/hakios.stubs.c`
  (`#ifndef HAKIOS_NT36672 void hakios_nt36672_init(void) {} #endif`), or the kernel will not link without it.

## 4. Build it, check it

```sh
echo CONFIG_HAKIOS_NT36672=y >> devices/mydevice/configs/mydevice.config
make mydevice_defconfig && make kernel
python3 tools/drivers-check.py          # (common drivers) the map and the conf files agree
tools/hakios-device.py check mydevice   # (a device's) its files are there
python3 tools/boot-args.py --check      # a new boot-argument is in the catalogue: run without --check to add it
python3 tools/docs-gen.py               # the reference page
```

The boot log says `hakios-kernel: N drivers built in (... nt36672 ...)`, and `sysctl kern.hakios.drivers` the same.

## 5. Write down what it does

The driver's head says what has been seen (on the phone, in QEMU, compiled only). The device's `device.conf` has a `status` line
for the part it makes work. [docs/driver-review](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-xnu-kernel/tree/main/docs/driver-review)
holds the audits of the common drivers: a new common driver gets one before it is relied on.

```

`docs/porting/index.md`:

```md
# Port a device

What it takes to bring HakiOS to a phone that does not have it yet, in the order that works: first a repository and a
configuration, then a boot with nothing of the phone's, then the drivers one at a time. Each step says how you know it is done.

> **Before you start.** A port runs from RAM and writes nothing by default, but you are working on a phone's hardware. Read
> [What is written to the phone](../concepts/architecture.md#what-is-written-to-the-phone), keep a way back to Android
> (`fastboot` and the stock images), and pull the phone's firmware before anything else.

## What you need

- a phone with an ARM64 Qualcomm SoC, its boot loader unlocked; a UEFI port for it (a Mu-Silicium port, as `devices/redwood/uefi` is, or your own);
- the phone's own device tree (`adb shell` with root, or from its boot image) and its Android running, for the firmware;
- a machine that builds the kernel ([Building from source](../getting-started/building.md)).

## 1. The repository, from the phone's own device tree

```sh
adb pull /sys/firmware/fdt device-tree.dtb          # the tree of the phone's own Android (or --adb below, which pulls it)
tools/hakios-device.py new mydevice --soc sc7280 --title "My Phone" --vendor Someone --maintainer "you" --fdt device-tree.dtb
make mydevice_defconfig
make config
```

That makes `devices/mydevice/` with:

- `soc.args`, `pull-soc.sh` and a README from `tools/new-device.py`: what the kernel needs to know about the SoC (`soc_*`: the
  modem's blocks, the IPA, the mailboxes) read out of your phone's tree and compared with the reference phone. The same values
  as the reference: the SoC code already fits. Differences go to the kernel through `soc.args`;
- `device.conf`, a defconfig of three `#include` lines and a fragment in which **every phone driver of the common repository is
  left out**: their addresses, pins and rails are the phone they were written for, and a driver of another phone touching yours
  is the last thing you want. The drivers of your SoC (from its fragment) and QEMU's stay in.

The SoC's layer comes with the device, in `devices/mydevice/soc/`: a copy of the one another device carries when the SoC is one
HakiOS knows (`--soc sc7280` copies redwood's), or a new one to fill in for a SoC nobody has ported yet (`--soc sm8250
--soc-title "Snapdragon 865"`). `--repo` makes the directory a git repository, ready to push as `hakios-mydevice`.

**Done when** `tools/hakios-device.py check mydevice` says it holds together, and the README says which SoC values differ and you
know why.

## 2. The first boot, with nothing of the phone's

```sh
make kernel                         # the kernel with only what the fragment kept
make loader
make phone SECS=120                 # or ./xl enter, ./xl ramdisk, ./xl run, one at a time
```

What to look for in `logs/`: the loader's banner, `kernel.ver=`, the kernel's first lines, `hakios-kernel: N drivers built in (...)`
with only the drivers you meant, and launchd. The display shows UEFI's framebuffer.

**Done when** a run reaches launchd and ends by itself, and the phone comes back.

## 3. The drivers, one at a time

Bring them back in the order each needs the ones before it:

| Order | Driver | Why then |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CPUFREQ`, `THERMAL`, `SOCINFO` | the SoC's: they read what the chip is and how warm, and touch nothing that is the phone's |
| 2 | `BUTTONS`, then the touch screen (`GOODIX` or one of your own) | input, so that the system can be used |
| 3 | `UFS` | the phone's storage, read only; the modem needs it |
| 4 | `ADRENO` | the GPU; needs `fw-gpu/` |
| 5 | `ADSP`, `BATTERY`, `SPEAKER`, `SOUND`, `MIC` | audio and the battery's level come through the audio DSP |
| 6 | `WIFI` (and `QMI`) | needs `fw-wifi/` |
| 7 | `HAPTIC`, `CAMERA`, `TORCH`, `MODEM`, `BT` | the rest |

For each: read the head of the driver (`drivers/<subsystem>/hakios.<name>.c` says where every address and number came from), find
the same in your phone's device tree, and change what differs. A value that is a SoC fact goes to the SoC's fragment or the
kernel's defaults; a value that is the phone's goes into a boot-argument of the device's fragment where the driver reads one, or
into a driver of the device's own when the hardware is another chip altogether ([Writing a driver](drivers.md)). Then
`CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y` in `configs/mydevice.config`, and the driver's boot-argument.

**Done when** the part works on the phone: write it down as a `status` line in `device.conf`, with how it is turned on.

## 4. Write it down

```sh
python3 tools/docs-gen.py           # the device's page, from device.conf
tools/hakios-device.py check mydevice
```

`device.conf` is the record of what works. Only what you have seen on the phone is `works`; what is written and not yet seen is
`partial` with a note; what is not there is `missing`.

## 5. Publish it

[Publishing a device](repositories.md#publishing-a-device): split it into a repository of its own and add it to
`devices/manifest.conf` in a pull request.

## Metal and the panel

The window server's Metal path is built for one GPU and one display controller so far, and it says so instead of guessing:

- **The GPU.** `hakios-metal/` has the tables of the Adreno of chip ID `0x06030500` (`include/hakios-metal/a6xx.hpp`). Another's is
  refused by `hakios_metal_open()`, the reason goes to the log and the window server stays on OpenGL ES. A port of another
  Adreno starts there, with Mesa's `freedreno_devices.py`.
- **The scan.** `fb_beam` (frames written behind the panel's scan) and `fb_measure` read the display interface's registers.
  They are known for `sc7280`; on another SoC nothing is read and frames go on their beat. `fb_intf=PHYSICAL` names them,
  from Linux's catalogue for your SoC. `fb_beam` checks that they count like a line counter before it trusts them.
- **The run.** `tools/metal-run.sh` reads `devices/<your phone>/metal.args`, which `tools/hakios-device.py new` makes: its big core,
  its cores, its panel's rate and its touch poll, for instance `bootcpu=7 cpus=8 fb_hz=60 fb_threads=4 touch_poll_us=8000`.
  `DEVICE_ARGS=` overrides it for one run. Without either, a phone other than redwood gets `fb_hz=60 fb_threads=3`.
- **The picture.** Any panel is stretched to from the screen class chosen: `fbscale=`, or `fbwidth=`, `fbheight=`, `fbsubtype=`.

## When a step does not work

| Symptom | Look at |
|---|---|
| nothing after the loader's banner | the UEFI port: the loader needs the framebuffer and its file from UEFI |
| the kernel stops early | the SoC's addresses (step 1); `soc.args` |
| a driver's step fails | its log lines name the step and the register; the head of the driver says what each step needs |
| `make config` reports a problem | it names the symbol and why: a driver left out that an argument needs, firmware the open profile does not load |

```

`docs/porting/repositories.md`:

```md
# How the repositories fit

HakiOS is put together from layers, the way an Android device's source is (`device/<vendor>/<name>`, a `<soc>-common`, a manifest
that names them):

```
hakios/                          common: the kernel port, every common driver, the loader, user space, the tools, the docs
├── devices/<name>/              a device, one repository: device.conf, configs/, drivers/, its UEFI platform, scripts
│   └── soc/                     ... and its SoC family's layer: soc.conf, configs/<soc>.config, the SoC's drivers
├── uefi/                        HakiOS's UEFI (Mu-Silicium with HakiOS's changes), one for every device
└── devices/manifest.conf        every device and the UEFI: kept in this tree, or a repository of its own at a revision
```

A SoC or device directory is the same whether it is kept in the common tree (`devices/qemu` is) or is a git repository of its own
that `tools/hakios-device.py sync` cloned into place (the others are): the tools look for `socs/*/soc.conf` and
`devices/*/device.conf`, whatever put them there. The common repository ignores what `sync` clones.

## A device repository

| File | What | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `device.conf` | what the device is, and how far each part works | yes |
| `configs/<name>_defconfig` | `#include common_defconfig`, `#include <soc>.config`, `#include <name>.config` | yes |
| `configs/<name>.config` | what is this device's own: drivers left out or in, arguments, `CONFIG_DEVICE="<name>"` | yes |
| `drivers/<subsystem>/conf` and the files it names | drivers of its own ([Writing a driver](drivers.md)) | no |
| `soc/` | its SoC family's layer: `soc.conf`, `configs/<soc>.config`, the SoC's drivers ([below](#the-socs-layer)) | yes, unless `soc none` |
| `pull-firmware.sh` | the device's firmware, from your own device, into `fw-*/` | for a phone |
| `uefi/`, `prebuilt/` | the device's UEFI port and the images made of it | for a phone |
| `README.md` | anything else a person needs to know | yes |

### `device.conf`

```
device redwood
	title       POCO X5 Pro 5G
	vendor      Xiaomi
	soc         sc7280
	defconfig   redwood_defconfig
	firmware    pull-firmware.sh
	maintainer  the HakiOS developers (README.md)
	status      touch       works     Goodix GT9916 / FocalTech FT3680 on SPI, multitouch (touchscreen=1)
	status      cellular    partial   the modem boots, sees the network; no registration yet
	status      bluetooth   missing   step one only
```

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| `title`, `vendor` | what it is called |
| `soc` | the SoC family: `socs/<soc>/` must be there; `none` for a machine without one (QEMU) |
| `defconfig` | its defconfig, in its `configs/` |
| `firmware` | the script that pulls its firmware |
| `maintainer` | who answers for it |
| `status <area> works\|partial\|missing <note>` | how far a part works, **as seen on this device**; the note says how it is turned on and what is not done. Areas: display, touch, buttons, cpu, gpu, storage, audio, battery, haptic, camera, torch, wifi, bluetooth, cellular, network, thermal, usb, sensors |

The device's page in this documentation ([redwood](../devices/redwood.md)) and the table of [all devices](../devices/index.md)
are made from it by `tools/docs-gen.py`: the status is written once, next to the code it describes.

## The SoC's layer

A device carries its SoC family's layer with it, in `soc/`, so that one repository is all a device needs:

```
soc sc7280
	title       Qualcomm SC7280 family (SM7325 "Snapdragon 778G", QCM6490; "yupik", "kodiak")
	vendor      Qualcomm
	cores       8, the biggest is core 7
	gpu         Adreno 642L
	maintainer  the HakiOS developers (README.md)
```

and `soc/configs/<soc>.config`, the SoC's facts: `CONFIG_SOC`, its cores, and **the drivers of the SoC family**
(`CONFIG_HAKIOS_CPUFREQ=y`, `CONFIG_HAKIOS_THERMAL=y`, ...), so that the device has them whatever it leaves out of its own.

Two devices with the same SoC each carry a copy. The copies must be the same: the tools take the SoC once, and refuse two copies that
differ, naming both, because a build would otherwise depend on which device was checked out. `tools/hakios-device.py new --soc sc7280`
copies the layer from a device that has it; a SoC nobody has yet gets a new layer to fill in. A SoC many devices share can also be a
repository of its own in `socs/<soc>/` (a `soc` block in the manifest); the tools read both.

## The manifest

`devices/manifest.conf` names every SoC and device:

```
device redwood
	repository  https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-sm7325.git
	revision    

device qemu
	path        devices/qemu                       kept in the common tree

device sheng
	repository  https://github.com/<you>/hakios-device-sheng.git
	revision    0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `tools/hakios-device.py list` (`make devices`) | every device and SoC, where it is, how much of it works |
| `tools/hakios-device.py check [NAME...]` | a repository holds together: its conf reads, its defconfig includes the common kernel and its SoC's fragment and passes `hakios-config.py check`, its drivers' files are there, no two repositories have a configuration of the same name |
| `tools/hakios-device.py new NAME --soc SOC --title ... [--fdt FILE] [--repo]` | a whole new device repository, its SoC layer with it; `--repo` makes it a git repository ready to push ([Port a device](index.md)) |
| `tools/hakios-device.py sync [NAME...]` | clone or update the repositories that live elsewhere, at their revisions |
| `tools/hakios-device.py lock NAME` | write the revision checked out into the manifest |
| `tools/hakios-device.py split NAME DIR` | a device kept in this tree, as a git repository of its own with its history, ready to push |

## How a device's own driver reaches the kernel

A driver in `devices/<name>/drivers/<subsystem>/conf` is a `CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>` symbol like the common ones. `make kernel` copies
its files into the kernel tree (`xnu/sync-drivers.sh`, through `tools/hakios-config.py external-files`) and writes it into XNU's
`conf/files` as `optional`; `xnu/export.sh` leaves it out of the common patch, because it is the device's. A device repository
cannot declare `standard` files: what every kernel has is the common repository's to decide.

## Publishing a device

1. `tools/hakios-device.py check NAME` passes.
2. `tools/hakios-device.py split NAME ../hakios-device-NAME` makes it a repository of its own.
3. Push it to a repository named `hakios-device-NAME` (or `hakios-soc-SOC` for a SoC).
4. In a pull request to the common repository: its block in `devices/manifest.conf` with `repository` and `revision`
   (`tools/hakios-device.py lock NAME` writes it), and nothing else.

## Compared with others

| | Android | UniXNU | HakiOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| the shared part | AOSP, the GKI kernel | `UniXNU` (tools, components, ARM64 support) | `hakios` (the kernel port, drivers, loader, tools) |
| a SoC | `<soc>-common` | `UniXNU-<soc>-common` (`soc.toml`) | `soc/` inside each device repository (`soc.conf`); `socs/<soc>` for a shared one |
| a device | `device/<vendor>/<name>` | `UniXNU-<name>` (`board.toml`) | `devices/<name>` (`device.conf`) |
| what names them | `repo` manifest | `devices.toml` | `devices/manifest.conf` |
| a driver | kernel module, `Kconfig` | a component repository | `drivers/<sub>/conf`, an XNU `option` |
| the status of a device | nothing of the kind | a page per device | `status` lines in `device.conf`, the page made from them, checked in CI |

```

`docs/reference/drivers.md`:

```md
<!-- Made by tools/docs-gen.py from drivers/*/conf and the SoC and device repositories' drivers. Do not edit: change that, then run tools/docs-gen.py. -->


# Drivers

Every driver the kernel can be built with. `CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y` in a defconfig builds it in; [Drivers in the configuration](../drivers-config.md) says how, and [Writing a driver](../porting/drivers.md) how to add one.

## Always built

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `hakios.audio.c` | /dev/hakios-audio, the sound Darwin plays, to whatever plays it; and where the camera, flashlight, motor and speaker drivers are started from |
| `hakios.version.c` | kern.hakios.version, and the version in the boot log |
| `hakios.platform.c` | what the drivers share (the locks of the PMIC arbiter, the always-on processor, RPMh and the SMMU), and kern.hakios.drivers, the list of the drivers built in |
| `hakios.stubs.c` | what the rest of the kernel calls in a driver that is left out: nothing, and "not there" |
| `hakios.stubs.cpp` | the same, for the calls that are C++ (the display asking whether the GPU is done with a surface) (with XNU's `iokitcpp`) |
| `hakios.input.c` | /dev/hakios-touch, the queue of touches and buttons, and where the phone's drivers are started from |
| `hakios.net.c` | en0, an interface that is Ethernet to the rest of the kernel, for whatever link carries its frames |
| `hakios.image.c` | a file of one of the RAM disks by path, for the drivers that load firmware before there is a root |
| `hakios.sparse.c` | /dev/rsp0, a block device over an image that holds only some of its blocks (apfs_sparse=) |
| `hakios.apfs_check.c` | a walk of the APFS volume on /dev/rvblk0 through VFS, to compare with tools/apfs/apfs.py (with XNU's `apfs`) |

## audio

| Driver | Files | Requires | Boot arguments | qemu | redwood | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`HAKIOS_ADSP`**<br>the audio DSP started and linked (adsp=1, adsp_step=N); the battery's state comes through it too. Needs the DSP's firmware from the phone (fw-audio/) | `hakios.adsp.c` |  | `adsp=`, `adsp_again=`, `adsp_apr_wait=`, `adsp_keep=`, `adsp_listen=`, `adsp_new=`, `adsp_pause=`, `adsp_return=` and 3 more |  | built | |
| **`HAKIOS_SPEAKER`**<br>the two speaker amplifiers on I2C, and their watch of temperature and battery | `hakios.speaker.c` |  | `speaker_probe=` |  | built | |
| **`HAKIOS_SOUND`**<br>the speakers playing (sound=N): what the DSP's services are told, the feeder, and the speakers' guard that limits what the amplifiers get | `hakios.sound.c`<br>`hakios.guard.c` | `HAKIOS_ADSP`, `HAKIOS_SPEAKER` | `sound=`, `sound_below=`, `sound_gain=`, `sound_guard_as=`, `sound_pause=`, `sound_secs=` |  | built | |
| **`HAKIOS_MIC`**<br>the microphones, through the audio DSP (mic=N) | `hakios.mic.c` | `HAKIOS_ADSP`, `HAKIOS_SOUND` | `mic=`, `mic_adc=`, `mic_input=`, `mic_main=`, `mic_secs=`, `mic_tap=`, `mic_test=` |  | built | |
| **`HAKIOS_VIRTIO_SOUND`**<br>QEMU's virtio sound device as the player of /dev/hakios-audio (virtio_sound=1). QEMU only | `hakios.virtio_sound.c` |  | `virtio_sound=` | built | built | |

## gpu

```md
# Metal measurements

What the phone did, in numbers. How to get the same numbers: [Metal on the Adreno](metal.md#measure). **120 frames a second has not
been reached**: not on hakios-metal, not on metal2vulkan, and not on OpenGL ES.

## The setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Phone | POCO X5 Pro 5G (`redwood`), SM7325 |
| GPU | Adreno 642L at 550 MHz, the most this phone's GPU is rated for (`adreno_speed=3`, the default) |
| User space | the Darwin 16.5 user space, laid out from your own IPSW |
| Panel | 1080 x 2400 at 120 Hz |
| Rendered | 1125 x 2436, scaled onto the panel by the driver |
| The run | `tools/metal-run.sh`: eight cores, `fb_hz=120 fb_threads=6 touch_poll_us=4000 wallpaper_freeze=1 metal_defer=1`, the round of `rc.jobs.bench` four times |

## The results

Frames a second, 3 and 4 November 2026. hakios-metal as the last run of 4 November had it: `wallpaper_freeze=1 metal_defer=1 fb_beam=1`.
metal2vulkan as measured on 3 November, before those.



| Motion | hakios-metal | metal2vulkan |
|---|---|---|
| Page swipe | 101 (100 to 104 over the runs) | 50 to 57 |
| Settings' scroll | 89 to 91 (109 in one run of six, not repeated) | 41 |
| Opening an app | about 90 | not recorded |
| Home button | 92 | 41 to 57 |
| Frames over 16.7 ms | 4% | not recorded |
| GPU time a frame | about 10 ms at the home screen, 3 November | 14 to 21 ms |

Both draw the system correctly. Not one of these is 120.

**hakios-metal, inside a swipe.** Once the finger has lifted, 185 of the animation's 205 frames take 8.3 ms, one refresh of the panel.
While the finger drags, frames come at 75 to 80 a second, and the window server waits 8 to 14 ms on GPU fences. The 100 to 104 in the
table covers both: `tools/frames.py` counts a gesture from the touch going down.

**metal2vulkan.** `tu_debug=gmem` and `tu_debug=sysmem` gave the same rates. Each frame renders to a tiled image and merges back into
the IOSurface with a compute pass. The linear attachment path (`VK_NV_linear_color_attachment`) stays unused: the pass has a second
attachment that is not linear, and the extension wants every colour attachment linear. With `tu_debug=perf`, no barrier turned GMEM
off and no texture was shadowed.


### Under real fingers (5 November)

Frames per second do not show what the eye calls jerking: the touch screen was read only when its interrupt line was seen low, and a report
that line was missed for waited for the look of every 80 ms.

| | Before | After (`drivers/input/hakios.goodix.c`) |
|---|---|---|
| A finger's lift after its last move | 88 to 169 ms | 5 ms, at most 6 |
| Between moves, over 13 ms apart | some | none of 164, at most 6 ms |

12 strokes kept in that log; `touch: N strokes` in the kernel's log now sums them up for a whole session. What is left of the jerking
at the start of a gesture is SpringBoard's main thread, before its commit: turns of 100 to 300 ms, 40 to 100 ms after the finger comes down
(`tl: t` in the log has its stack, with `touch_lat=1`). A share of a frame's rows late for its scan is counted too: 19 to 115 in a session.

### The iPhone X's screen at 2 pixels a point (4 November)

`fbscale=2`, the default of `tools/metal-run.sh`: 750x1624, stretched to the panel by the CPU, the layout of the iPhone X's 375 x 812 points with 2.25
times fewer pixels for the GPU. The picture is softer than at 1125x2436, nearest neighbour while something moves and bilinear once it is still. A main
pass is 5 ms in 21 tiles. UIKit has no status bar for this screen: SpringBoard (`inject_sb.c`) makes its fallback the iPhone X's.

| Gesture (`rc.jobs.bench`, 4 runs) | Frames a second |
|---|---|
| Settings' scroll | 118 to 120 |
| Page swipe | 107 to 118 |
| Opening Settings | 107 to 108 |
| Home button | 95 to 111 |
| Frames over 16.7 ms | 1.1 to 1.2% |

The scroll is at the panel's rate. The home button and the opening of an application are held by the GPU: two passes of 7 to 8 ms for a frame, more than the
8.33 ms of a refresh, so those frames come a refresh late. The hitches at the start of a gesture are SpringBoard's main thread: 10 of its 4745 turns in a run
were over 30 ms, the longest 101. These are synthetic gestures (`rwtouch`); fingers cost more.

The framebuffer logs, for each thread's share of the rows, its time and how often it was late for the scan: 1 to 9 torn of about 49 000 shares in a run, all in the
first two shares, whose rows the scan comes to first. The last shares take 2 to 3 ms and were never late. This counts against the scan as the interface's
counters report it; what the panel shows has not been measured independently, and a phone's camera sees lines of its own on a panel refreshing at 120.

### The screen as the iPhone XR's (4 November)

`fbwidth=828 fbheight=1792 fbscale=2 fbsubtype=1792`, the default until the iPhone X's at 2 replaced it (under real fingers the bottom edge opened a sheet here), stretched to the panel by the CPU. 1.85 times fewer
pixels for the GPU; the picture is softer than at 1125x2436. The poster draws nothing on this screen: `wallpaper_freeze=1` shows the picture a
boot at the iPhone X's screen kept in `/var/mobile/Library/hakios-wallpaper.raw`.

| Gesture (`rc.jobs.bench.xr`) | Frames a second | At 1125x2436 |
|---|---|---|
| Settings' scroll | 118 | 89 to 91 |
| Page swipe | 110 to 115 | 101 to 103 |
| Home button | 106 | 89 to 92 |
| Opening Settings | 86 | about 95 |
| Frames over 16.7 ms | 1% | 4 to 6% |

While something moves, half the frames are 8.33 ms apart and most of the rest one refresh more. What keeps the averages under 120: SpringBoard's main
thread at the start of a gesture (36 to 57 ms) and of an application (104 ms), frames the GPU delivers a refresh late now and then, and the
measured stretch ending in the slow ticks of a still screen. These are synthetic gestures (`rwtouch`).

## Tried, and it did not help

| What | Arguments | Result |
|---|---|---|
| The threads that copy frames real-time, with the scan as their deadline | a build with a time-constraint policy, since removed | 684 shares late in a session, against 115 |
| Bilinear on every frame, so that nothing jumps when motion starts or stops | `fb_filter=1` | under real fingers it jerks as much, and 125 shares late against 19 to 43 |
| The stretch written by runs of a source column, a row the same as the one above it copied from there | in `MiniIOMobileFramebuffer` | worse: 8.7 ms in the driver a frame against 7 to 8, every swap waiting for the frame before, 102 frames a second against 110 |
| Touch samples at 250 a second, not 125 | `touch_poll_us=4000`, `rwtouch` every 4 ms | swipes 100 to 102: unchanged |
| Surfaces let go of as soon as their pixels are on the panel, not when the next frame comes | in `MiniIOMobileFramebuffer` | unchanged |
| The iPhone XR's screen class, 1.85 times fewer pixels | `fbwidth=828 fbheight=1792 fbscale=2 fbsubtype=1792` | idle GPU time 2.2 ms, not 6.8; gestures not faster; the wallpaper black |
| The iPhone 12 mini's screen class | `fbwidth=`, `fbheight=`, `fbscale=`, `fbsubtype=` | 103 to 107, with the red rdar://45025538 status bar |
| The wallpaper hidden, for swipes | `wallpaper_freeze=2` | 101 to 103, as with it: the wallpaper is not what holds swipes under 120. It is what held the home button: 78 hidden, against 28 with `wallpaper_cache=1` |
| The wallpaper's picture through `-drawViewHierarchyInRect:` | `wallpaper_freeze=1`, first version | one colour; with all of SpringBoard's windows hidden the screen itself was black. It now reads the IOSurface on the panel |

## What did help

On hakios-metal, each as the commit that made the change measured it, newest first.

## metal2vulkan, on the way

| When (3 November) | What | Result |
|---|---|---|

| `m2v_test` | the Metal device alone | a full-screen clear committed and waited for in 1.08 ms |

The first window-server numbers are higher than the later ones because less was being drawn. They are here so that nobody takes them
for a result.

## OpenGL ES, for comparison

The default path, which is not Metal: Settings scrolled at 107 to 114 a second on the four big cores (`cpus=4`, `fb_hz=120 ca_vbl=1`,
31 October, [hakios-sm7325](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-sm7325) `a8e7a87`). The conditions differ from the table above in the core count and in the day's kernel, so that is a reference point and not
a comparison run.

## Tearing

The panel reads the very buffer the driver writes. It takes the scan 8.3 ms to read it and the driver about 3 ms to write it, so a frame
written across the line being read came out torn: a piece of the last frame and a piece of this one, moving bands with doubled icons and
text wherever something moved. Seen on the phone.

`fb_beam=1`, the default, writes each thread's rows behind the scan line, read from the interface's own `INTF_LINE_COUNT`, so that the next
scan reads all of the new frame. The scan measured 2433 lines, 8338 us. It is looked at a minute after the driver starts; if the counter
does not count as a line counter should, frames stay on their beat, and the log says so. 2 to 16 frames in 5 s miss their scan.

The bands were gone to the eye. That is the only evidence: `xl screenshot` cannot tell, because it sends live memory in pieces of 1 MiB, and
the bands in its pictures are 243 rows apart.

It costs no frames. The same run otherwise, 4 November:



| | `fb_beam=1` | `fb_beam=0` |
|---|---|---|
| Page swipe | 101 | 99 |
| Settings' scroll | 91 | 89 |
| Home button | 92 | 81 |
| Frames over 16.7 ms | 4% | 6% |

`docs/reference/metal.md`:

```md
# Metal on the Adreno

Two implementations of Metal draw the window server on the phone's Adreno 642L. This page says what each is, how to build, run and
measure it, and what is not known. The numbers: [Metal measurements](metal-measurements.md). How it got here, step by step:
[the plan](../metal-plan.md).

**Status, POCO X5 Pro 5G, 3 and 4 November 2026.** Both paths draw the system correctly. hakios-metal is the faster: page swipes 100
to 104 frames a second, Settings' scroll about 90, the home button about 90 at the full 1125x2436; rendering at 750x1624, stretched to the panel (`fbscale=2`, the default of `tools/metal-run.sh`), scroll 118 to 120, swipes 107 to 118, home button 95 to 111, about 110 over the bench as a whole. metal2vulkan: swipes 50 to 57, scroll 41. **120 frames a second has not been
reached on either.** Neither is on by default: without `metal=1` the window server draws through OpenGL ES, as it always has.


## The two paths

| | hakios-metal | metal2vulkan |
|---|---|---|
| Route | Metal, `HakiosMetalCA`, hakios-metal (the Adreno's own PM4 packets), HakiosGPU | Metal, AdrenoMetal's frontend, metal2vulkan, Turnip, `hakios-drm`, HakiosGPU |
| Shaders | AIR to NIR to ir3, by Mesa's compiler inside the process | AIR through metal2vulkan into Vulkan pipelines, which Turnip compiles |
| Where the code is | `userland/src/HakiosMetalCA.m` and `hakios-metal/` here | `tools/mk-turnip.sh`, `tools/mk-m2v.sh`, `tools/m2v/`, `tools/mesa/`; the rest fetched by those scripts |
| Whose | ours; the plug-in began as vcvkk's (origin **to verify**, [third-party licenses](../../THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md)) | [UniXNU](https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU)'s stack, ported from the Adreno 740 and a later system |
| Build | `METAL_PLUGIN=ca` | `METAL_PLUGIN=ca TURNIP=1 M2V=1` |
| Boot arguments | `gpu=1 metal=1 ca_metallib=...` | the same and `metal_m2v=1` |
| Page swipe, frames a second | 100 to 104 | 50 to 57 |
| GPU time a frame | about 10 ms at the home screen | 14 to 21 ms |
| In `prebuilt/` | no | no, and it must not be without the check below ([Licenses](#licenses)) |

The third path is the default one, and it is not Metal: CoreAnimation's OpenGL ES renderer through Mesa's freedreno (`gpu=1`, an image
built with `GL=1`).

## Interfaces

### HakiosGPU (`drivers/gpu/hakios.gpu.cpp`)

The kernel's GPU driver serves all three paths through the same IOKit user client. Its requests are Linux's msm DRM requests by
number, and two of its own:

| Request | Takes | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `0x7e` | an IOSurface's ID | a buffer over the surface; asked with `kHakiosDescribe`, only what it would be like |
| `0x7d` | an address and a size in whole pages of the caller's own (`struct hakios_user_memory`) | a buffer over those pages, Linux's userptr. Wired through an `IOMemoryDescriptor` over the caller's task for as long as the buffer lives, entered into the GPU's address space, pushed out of the CPU's cache by physical address at every submission naming them. Read-only pages are taken as such: a window server's view of another program's backing store. Unwired when the buffer goes, and never kept for reuse. Each refusal is logged with its reason |

### Turnip on Darwin (`tools/mesa/turnip-darwin.patch`, `tools/mesa/hakios-drm/`)

Mesa 25.0.7's Vulkan driver, cross-built with its msm backend and no DRM window system.

- `hakios-drm` stands in for libdrm. Requests become calls of HakiosGPU's user client. DRM syncobjs, which Turnip makes its fences and
  semaphores of, are kept in the process over the kernel's fences: timelines, waits, signal, query, transfer. There is one GPU and
  one connection in a process, which is why that is enough.
- `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`: an IOSurface's pointer is imported by the surface's ID (the frontend says which surface is mapped
  where, `hakios_drm_host_surface`), any other page-aligned pointer through request `0x7d`.
- `VK_NV_linear_color_attachment`: linear tiling already had every feature of optimal tiling in Turnip; the extension says so.
- `vkGetInstanceProcAddr` is exported: there is no Vulkan loader, and metal2vulkan opens the driver by that entry point.
- The cache line size comes from `hw.cachelinesize`, since `CTR_EL0` traps in user space; buffers are mapped through `hakios_drm_map`.

### The window server (`userland/src/HakiosMetalCA.m`)

QuartzCore on this system has its uber shaders only as specialised variants inside `default.pipelinelib`, and no `default.metallib` at
all. Two things follow, on either path:

- `tools/ca-metallib.py` makes the `default.metallib` the window server asks for, from QuartzCore's own variants and a later
  CoreAnimation's library that you supply. It stays on your machine, and `ca_metallib=` names it at boot.
- The plug-in picks the variant by the pipeline's label. For metal2vulkan that goes through `native_bridge_metal_variant_hook`, which
  `tools/m2v/adrenometal-ios16.patch` adds to the frontend. `HakiosMetalCA` also gives the metal2vulkan device its own opening of
  QuartzCore's pipeline library and a `targetDeviceInfo`: without them the pictures came out as grey shapes.

## Build

Everything runs on Linux or in WSL 2 (commands for Windows: [Windows](../windows.md#metal-a-run-measured-from-windows)). Neither path
works from `prebuilt/` alone: `PREBUILT=1` compiles nothing, and `prebuilt/userland` has no Metal plug-in, so these need the cross
toolchain of `xnu-deps/setup.sh`.

The library the window server asks for, for either path:

```sh
CA_QC_METALLIB=/path/to/default.metallib tools/ca-metallib.py ~/ca-share    # off a Mac; on a Mac it reads the Mac's own
```

**hakios-metal.** It is in this tree, in `hakios-metal/`; `HAKIOS_METAL=` names another copy:

```sh
(cd hakios-metal && make ios MESA=1)         # needs tools/mk-mesa.sh's tree
METAL_PLUGIN=ca RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.bench EXTRA_SHARE=~/ca-share REST=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh
```

**metal2vulkan.** Nothing of it is in `prebuilt/`: you fetch and build it yourself. You need what `tools/mk-mesa.sh` needs,
`glslangValidator` (apt: `glslang-tools`), rustup's cargo with Rust 1.98 and its `aarch64-apple-ios` target, `llvm-as` of LLVM 21
(apt: `llvm-21`), clang, and the theos iPhoneOS 16.5 SDK.

```sh
tools/mk-mesa.sh      # Mesa 25.0.7 with tools/mesa/*.patch
tools/mk-turnip.sh    # xnu-deps/build/mesa/out/libvulkan_freedreno.dylib
tools/mk-m2v.sh       # xnu-deps/build/m2v/out/: frontend.o, libadreno_metal_bridge.a
METAL_PLUGIN=ca TURNIP=1 M2V=1 RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.bench EXTRA_SHARE=~/ca-share REST=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh
```

Build these before the image: `userland/build.sh` links metal2vulkan into the plug-in only if `xnu-deps/build/m2v/out` is already there.
`tools/mk-m2v.sh` pins [UniXNU/AdrenoMetal](https://github.com/UniXNU/AdrenoMetal) at `243d63c` and
[steelbrain/metal2vulkan](https://github.com/steelbrain/metal2vulkan) at `624bab3` with AdrenoMetal's 30 patches, and adds
`tools/m2v/`. Programs and libraries over 4 MB go into the system image, with a link in the small one (`/usr/local/redwood`).

Two programs check the path before the window server is involved:

| Image | Boot | The program | On the phone (3 November) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TURNIP=1 RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.vktest` | `gpu=1` | `userland/src/vk_test.c`: Turnip once round | `Adreno 7c+ Gen 3`, Vulkan 1.3.305, a 4 MB `vkCmdFillBuffer` checked word by word, a submission and its fence wait 0.5 ms at best, 2.0 on average: PASS |
| `TURNIP=1 M2V=1 RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.m2vtest` | `gpu=1` | `userland/src/m2v_test.m`: the Metal device, a blit, a clear, surfaces and own pages as textures | the device in 134 ms, a 4 MB blit fill and a 1080 x 2400 clear checked word by word and pixel by pixel, a full-screen clear committed and waited for in 1.08 ms: PASS |

## Boot arguments

Every argument is in [the catalogue](../boot-args.md), which is made from the source; this table says what the ones of Metal do.

| Argument | Layer | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `metal=1` | kernel, plug-in | the accelerator names the Metal plug-in; without it the window server finds no device and stays on OpenGL ES, saying nothing. With `METAL_PLUGIN=ca` the window server alone is shown the device (`metal_all=1`: every process) |
| `ca_metallib=PATH` | `inject.c` | QuartzCore's library for the window server |
| `metal_m2v=1` | plug-in | the window server's device is metal2vulkan's. Needs an image built with `M2V=1` |
| `tu_debug=FLAGS` | plug-in | Turnip's `TU_DEBUG` in the window server (`sysmem`, `gmem`, `perf`, ...); with `metal_m2v=1` |
| `m2v_utrace=1` | plug-in | Turnip's GPU trace of every render pass into a file; the 30 commonest events of each 5 s printed. With `metal_m2v=1` |
| `metal_fps=1` | plug-in | frame and pass counters every 5 s: what `tools/metal-run.sh` sets |
| `metal_fps=passes` | plug-in | also every pass of one slow command buffer in 200, with its attached and touched colour attachments |
| `metal_fps=mainpass` | plug-in | also the draws of a pass of 40 draws or more over 4 ms (in sysmem, where draws are timed) |
| `metal_fps=draws` | plug-in | also each draw of a sysmem pass timed alone, and the time counted by program |
| `metal_defer=1` | plug-in | the window server's command buffers recorded on a thread of hakios-metal's own: a draw costs its render thread about 5 us instead of about 40. `tools/metal-run.sh` sets it |
| `metal_luma_boost=1` | plug-in | draws `luma_boost`, which is otherwise left out where the library has its own |
| `wallpaper_cache=1` | SpringBoard | the wallpaper's window rasterized by the window server |
| `wallpaper_freeze=1` | SpringBoard | the wallpaper as one still picture: at the home screen the window of the icons is hidden for a moment (they blink once a boot), the pixels of the IOSurface on the panel (`kern.hakios.fb_surface`) become one opaque view in the wallpaper's window, and its layers are hidden. It gives up: the wallpaper does not change until the next boot, and the lock screen shows the same picture. `tools/metal-run.sh` sets it |
| `wallpaper_freeze=2` | SpringBoard | the wallpaper hidden: what it costs, measured |
| `ui_lite=1`, `ui_lite=0` | SpringBoard | Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion on, off again. Without it the settings are left alone |
| `fb_intf=` | framebuffer | the physical address of the display interface's registers, for a port: `fb_beam` and `fb_measure` read them. Without it they are known for sc7280 only (`CONFIG_SOC`); on another SoC nothing is read and frames stay on their beat |
| `fbwidth=`, `fbheight=`, `fbscale=`, `fbsubtype=` | framebuffer | another iPhone's screen class: `fbscale=2` alone is the iPhone X's layout at 750x1624 (the default of `tools/metal-run.sh`); `fbwidth=828 fbheight=1792 fbscale=2 fbsubtype=1792` is the XR's |
| `touch_poll_us=N` | touch driver | the touch screen read every N microseconds. The driver's default is 8000; `tools/metal-run.sh` sets 4000 |
| `fb_hz=120`, `fb_threads=6`, `fb_measure=1` | framebuffer | the driver's beat at the panel's rate, six processors scaling a frame onto the panel, the panel's own rate measured once |
| `fb_beam=1` | framebuffer | the default: each thread's rows are written behind the panel's scan line. `fb_beam=0`: whenever the beat comes, as before. [Tearing](metal-measurements.md#tearing) |

And one sysctl: `kern.hakios.fb_surface`, the IOSurface last put on the panel.

## Measure

```sh
tools/metal-run.sh                          # 180 s, hakios-metal; the summary in logs/<time>-metal.txt
MORE="metal_m2v=1" tools/metal-run.sh       # the same on metal2vulkan
MORE="wallpaper_cache=1" tools/metal-run.sh # any argument beside the defaults
```

An image built with `RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.bench` unlocks, waits a minute for the start-up work to end, and does the same round four times:
Settings opened from its icon, its list scrolled, the home button, a page swipe there and back. So each kind of motion is measured
four times in the same state of the system, and runs can be compared.

`tools/metal-run.sh` takes the phone from Android, its bootloader or the loader, uploads the system image, runs, and writes a summary:
`tools/frames.py`'s frames per gesture, the plug-in's `fps:` lines, what was refused, the frames on the panel, the shader cache and any
crash. It sets `gpu=1 metal=1 metal_fps=1 touch_lat=1 touchscreen=1 gpu_recover=1 anim_max=1 bootcpu=7 cpus=8 cpufreq=1 fb_hz=120
fb_measure=1 fb_threads=6 touch_poll_us=4000 wallpaper_freeze=1 metal_defer=1`, the path of QuartzCore's library, and (unless `PERSIST=0`) `ufs=2 ufs_write=1
var_store=1`, which keeps `/private/var` in your `darwin` partition so that shader stages are compiled once.

`MORE=` adds arguments at the end, and a default of the same name goes: `MORE="wallpaper_freeze=0 metal_defer=0"` runs without those two.

`tools/frames.py RUN.log [MORE.log ...]` on its own reads the `tl:` lines of `touch_lat=1`. For each gesture it gives the frames a
second while frames came, the share of frame steps over 16.7 ms, 33 ms and 8.3 ms, and where a slow frame's time went. A window server
drawing through Metal says no `tl: g`: its frames are counted by the swap that handed each over, so `draw` and `idle` are 0 there,
meaning unknown.

## Known gaps

- **Under 120.** While a finger drags, the window server waits 8 to 14 ms on GPU fences and frames come at 75 to 80 a second; after
  the finger lifts, 185 of 205 frames of a swipe take 8.3 ms. The cause of the wait is not established.
- **The wallpaper is frozen to get the home button's rate.** 92 frames a second with `wallpaper_freeze=1`, 50 without it or
  `wallpaper_cache=1`, 28 with `wallpaper_cache=1`. It is many full-screen layers from another process, and rasterizing its window does
  not stop them being composed again. A wallpaper that moves or changes costs that, and it is not solved.
- **metal2vulkan renders each frame to a tiled image and merges it back with a compute pass.** The linear attachment path stays unused
  because a second, non-linear attachment is in the pass, and the extension wants every colour attachment linear.
- **Tearing.** The panel reads the one buffer the driver writes. `fb_beam` writes behind the scan; 2 to 16 frames in 5 s still miss
  their scan, and whether the panel tears less is so far for the eye: [Tearing](metal-measurements.md#tearing).
- **Not the same stack as UniXNU's.** Theirs runs on the Adreno 740 with its own kernel driver, [Adreno740](https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU/blob/main/docs/drivers/adreno740.md),
  and a newer system. Only the part above that driver was taken. What is measured here says nothing about theirs.
- **Other systems' libraries.** The window server's library takes the rest of its shaders from a later CoreAnimation than this
  system's, because this system has none. That it behaves the same as a matched one is not shown.
- **Shaders chosen by their labels.** This system's QuartzCore holds its uber shaders as 451 specialised variants. A pipeline CoreAnimation
  makes at run time that is not among them gets the nearest of the same kind (`hm_ca_nearest()`, `HakiosMetalCA.m`): sampling, blend and
  varyings the same, then the fewest inputs changed. Before that it got one fixed variant, which was the red top of the default wallpaper,
  the white band behind the status bar and the opaque Weather widget. What the letters of a label mean is read from the labels, so a
  stand-in can differ in a flag; the log says each (`... stands in for it`).

## What is not verified

- The results are of one phone, a POCO X5 Pro 5G. No other Adreno has run either path, and QEMU has no GPU.
- They are of the bench's runs, 180 s by default. They do not say how the rates hold over a longer run or with a hot phone, and they
  take the GPU's clock as the 550 MHz it is set to, not as read back frame by frame.
- The only client they describe is the system's own interface. Nothing here shows that a Metal program in general runs, and games
  are not claimed.
- The build commands above were written from the scripts and were not re-run on a clean machine when this page was written.
- HakiosGPU's request `0x7d` lets a client wire its own pages. It has not been through a [driver review](../driver-review/gpu-display.md).
- The frame rates are what `tools/frames.py` counts from the window server's swaps and the driver's frames, not a camera on the panel.

metal2vulkan is `GPL-2.0-or-later OR LGPL-3.0-or-later`. `M2V=1` links its runtime statically into the plug-in and `m2v_test`, so a
binary built that way has obligations whichever you choose. Whether and how such a binary may be distributed is **to verify**, and none
is distributed: [third-party licenses](../../THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md), [compliance](../../COMPLIANCE.md).

`docs/ru/cellular.md`:

```md
# Сотовая связь: состояние и план порта

Сейчас сотовая связь в HakiOS **не работает**, но модем уже запускается из XNU (см. «21 октября» ниже). Wi-Fi использует WPSS и свой GLINK/QRTR; модем MPSS — отдельный процессор с другим каналом. `hakios.qmi.c` кодирует сообщения QMI и теперь позволяет привязать клиент к заданному транспорту QRTR, но канал к MPSS ещё не реализован. У Darwin также нет драйверов AppleBaseband и AppleIPAppender для этого аппаратного пути. Запуск `CommCenter` без них уже проверялся: он завершается аварийно (см. README, раздел «Телефония»).

Проверка `python3 devices/redwood/tools/modem_firmware.py --dtb devices/redwood/prebuilt/device-tree.dtb --firmware-dir fw-modem --node /soc/qcom,mss@4080000` сопоставила 28 сегментов штатной прошивки с областью `mpss@8b800000` (PAS ID 4). `MODEM=1 SYSTEM=1 ... userland/build.sh` теперь может положить эти локальные файлы в системный APFS после проверки. Это только подготовка образа: наличие прошивки в `/fw` не запускает MPSS. Исходник `hakios.nas.c` содержит клиент QMI NAS для заданного транспорта QRTR: он ищет службу, запрашивает регистрацию и силу сигнала, разбирает ответы и сбрасывает состояние при исчезновении службы. Уровень `bars` остаётся нулевым без подтверждённой регистрации. MPSS-транспорта в XNU пока нет, поэтому этот клиент ещё не получает сообщения с телефона и не подключён к статус-бару Darwin. Форматы NAS сверены с [описанием libqmi](https://github.com/linux-mobile-broadband/libqmi/blob/main/data/qmi-service-nas.json).

## Проверка на телефоне, 20 октября 2026

На redwood через `fastboot boot` временно запущены xnuloader и образ Darwin userland 16.5. Системный APFS загружен в ОЗУ; разделы телефона не прошивались. `launchd` запустил `SpringBoard`, и на дисплее открылся интерфейс «Настройки». Это подтверждает загрузку Darwin и работу экрана, но не работу модема. В журнале `mg_test` показывает `telephony = true` и `cellular-data = false`; запросы `com.apple.commcenter.xpc` и `com.apple.basebandd.xpc` остаются без службы. Значение `telephony = true` — ответ MobileGestalt о возможностях устройства, а не регистрация в сети. Тест выполнен с готовым ядром из `prebuilt`, поэтому изменения QMI в исходниках XNU в этой загрузке **не проверялись**. Дальнейший аппаратный тест требует сборки ядра с MPSS/QRTR и интеграции с Darwin.

## Что установлено по redwood

`devices/redwood/prebuilt/device-tree.dtb` содержит зарезервированную память `mpss@8b800000`, `qcom,smp2p-modem`, `qcom,glink/modem/qcom,modem_qrtr`, `qcom,ipa@1e00000` и `qcom,rmnet-ipa`. Это разные части тракта: запуск прошивки модема, сигнализация, управляющий QMI-канал и передача IP-пакетов. Дерево Android [redwood](https://github.com/Redwood-AOSP/android_device_xiaomi_redwood) включает `full_base_telephony.mk`; его `init.qcom.rc` запускает `vendor.qcrild` и `vendor.qcrild2`. [Ветка araxys с ядром/DTB](https://github.com/Redwood-AOSP/android_device_xiaomi_redwood-kernel/tree/araxys) пригодна как аппаратный справочник. Бинарники Android RIL нельзя просто запустить в Darwin: им нужны Android binder, HAL, службы и ABI.

Проверка по USB 20 октября 2026 года: fastboot определил продукт `redwood` и разблокированный загрузчик; Android сообщил `ro.boot.hardware.sku=redwood`, `ro.soc.model=SM7325`. Под Android подсистема `modem` и прошивка `yupik_ipa_fws` были `ONLINE`, `vendor.qcrild`, `vendor.qcrild2`, `vendor.qrtr-ns` — `running`; присутствовали `rmnet_ipa0` и `rmnet_data0`–`rmnet_data5`. Состояние SIM: `ABSENT,LOADED` для двух слотов. Временная загрузка `xnuloader` через `fastboot boot` и его `selftest` прошли (`selftest-ok`); это проверка загрузчика, а не сотовой связи в XNU.

Android `dmesg` уточняет последовательность: сначала поднимается `yupik_ipa_fws`, затем MPSS загружает `modem.mdt` и сегменты в `0x8b800000..0x9ae00000`, получает `Power/Clock ready`, после чего QRTR фиксирует готовность QMI. Штатные `modem.mdt`/`modem.b*` (около 85 МиБ) сохранены локально в игнорируемом Git каталоге `fw-modem/` и не входят в исходники. Их ELF-заголовок содержит 30 программных заголовков и 28 загружаемых сегментов; все файлы совпали по размеру, а сегменты лежат в зарезервированном окне. Загрузчик WPSS ограничен 16 сегментами; путь ADSP рассчитан на 48, но использует собственные ресурсы памяти, SMP2P и GLINK и не может запускать MPSS простым изменением имени прошивки.

## Границы общей реализации

Общими для устройств должны быть контракт транспорта QRTR, разбор QMI, состояние SIM/сети и интерфейс передачи IP-пакетов. Запуск прошивки MPSS, ресурсы памяти, прерывания, SMMU, IPA и прошивки остаются в профиле и драйвере конкретного SoC/устройства. По наличию `qcom,glink` нельзя объявлять поддержку всех Qualcomm или других телефонов.

Порядок доведения до работающей связи:

1. На подключённом Android собрать отчёт `python3 devices/redwood/tools/cellular_probe.py --adb` и сверить DTB, версию прошивки и активные службы. Скрипт читает только открытые свойства и не собирает IMEI, IMSI и номера SIM.
2. Поднять MPSS в XNU с собственным GLINK/QRTR-каналом, отдельным от WPSS; проверить обнаружение QMI-служб, не отправляя команд регистрации или передачи данных.
3. Реализовать QMI DMS/UIM/NAS/WDS и состояние SIM/сети; отдельно включить путь IPA/rmnet для мобильных данных.
4. Подключить эти возможности к CoreTelephony/CommCenter через совместимый сервис и аппаратный драйвер, затем проверить SIM, регистрацию, входящие/исходящие вызовы, SMS и мобильные данные на телефоне. VoLTE/IMS — отдельная работа.

Пока пункт 2 не подтверждён на устройстве, не включать узел `baseband` и не переключать систему на cellular `CommCenter`: это создаёт аварийные циклы без радио.

## Команды до и после подключения

```sh
python3 devices/redwood/tools/cellular_probe.py > modem-dtb.json
# После подключения телефона с разрешённой USB-отладкой:
python3 devices/redwood/tools/cellular_probe.py --adb > modem-android.json
```

Для другого устройства передать его DTB через `--dtb PATH`; прошивку на телефон инструмент не записывает.

## 21 октября 2026: модем запущен из XNU

Ядро теперь собирается на этом Mac (см. `xnu/README.md`, «Сборка на macOS»), и драйвер
`drivers/modem/hakios.mpss.c` — копия пути аудио‑DSP (`hakios.adsp.c`) с числами модема — проверен
на телефоне через `xl run` с `modem_step=11 modem_return=1`:

- шаги 1–10 проходят: прошивка `modem.*` из `/fw` системного образа (85 МБ, 28 сегментов)
  записана в `0x8b800000` и прочитана обратно без расхождений; TrustZone принял подпись
  (образ 4) и область `0xf600000` байт; шины CX и MSS запрошены у RPMh на уровне 384; AOP
  получил `modem: on`; через 63 мс после старта модем сказал `slave-kernel = 0x6` (поднялся и
  взял питание сам); GLINK согласован, канал `IPCRTR` открыт в обе стороны; QRTR: hello в обе
  стороны, модем — узел 0;
- модем объявил только две службы: 43 (SSCTL, экземпляр 18) и 66 (реестр служб). DMS и NAS
  не появились за 40 с, поэтому шаг 11 (DMS «online», опрос NAS) не выполнен;
- по просьбе модем остановился за 43 мс (`0x10e`), TrustZone выключил его, AOP получил
  `modem: off`; телефон вернулся в загрузчик штатно.

Причина отсутствия DMS/NAS — у модема нет доступа к своим файловым системам: на Android их
отдаёт демон `rmtfs` (служба QMI 14 поверх QRTR, [linux-msm/rmtfs](https://github.com/linux-msm/rmtfs)).
В драйвер добавлена такая служба: четыре раздела (`modemst1`, `modemst2`, `fsc`, `fsg`)
читаются при старте шагов целиком в память ядра через `hakios_ufs_read_partition()`
(нужен `ufs=2` в аргументах ядра — блочная служба загрузчика), модем открывает их по путям
`/boot/modem_fs1` и т. д., получает буфер 2,5 МБ (`qcom,rmtfs_sharedmem@0`), в который
TrustZone пускает модем вызовом `SCM MP ASSIGN` (HLOS + MSS_MSA, чтение и запись), и читает
или пишет секторы через него. Записи остаются в памяти ядра: **разделы телефона не
записываются**. Служба объявляется модему в ответ на hello и на lookup (наша сторона
сервиса имён QRTR). Это ещё **не проверено на телефоне**: после предыдущего прогона телефон
исчез с USB (сторожевой таймер загрузчика), нужен ручной перезапуск в fastboot.

Запуск теста:

```sh
./xl enter && ./xl ramdisk userland/system.apfs    # образ с MODEM=1 SYSTEM=1 (один раз после входа в загрузчик)
XL_CMDLINE="debug=0x8 rd=md0 hv_wdt_pet=1 bootcpu=7 cpus=8 cpufreq=1 sb_delay=600 ufs=2 modem_step=11 modem_return=1 modem_new=12 modem_nas_wait=60" XL_SECS=300 XL_FOLLOW=3 ./xl run
```

`modem=1` в обычной загрузке делает всё то же на своём потоке и оставляет модем включённым,
опрашивая NAS каждые две секунды; результат — в `sysctl kern.hakios.cellular_up`,
`cellular_registered`, `cellular_bars`, `cellular_dbm`, `cellular_radio`. Палочки в
статус‑баре Darwin из этого ещё не получаются: нужна либо часть CommCenter, либо подмена
элемента статус‑бара в `libhakios.sb.dylib` по этим sysctl (следующий шаг).

## 23 октября 2026: буфер RMTFS и перезапуски телефона

Ночные прогоны (`tools/macos-bin`: adb из platform-tools r34 — сервер adb 37.0.1 на этом Mac
убивается через две секунды после запуска; `xl` возвращает телефон в Android после каждого
прогона) показали:

- буфер RMTFS должен лежать **ниже 4 ГБ**: адреса в запросах модема 32‑битные (с буфером
  `0x197508000` модем пишет «xpu lock failed» по усечённому адресу и сдаётся);
- память CDSP (`0x9c700000`) не годится: после её передачи TrustZone отказывается запускать
  модем (`-3145799`); память видеокодека (`0x8ae00000`) и `ramoops` (`0xb0000000`) —
  модем стартует, но телефон сбрасывается при первой нашей записи сектора; свободная память
  UEFI (`0xa8000000`, `modem_buffer=`) — то же, пока буфер отдан только HLOS и MSS;
- Android отдаёт буфер трём владельцам: HLOS, MSS_MSA (15) и NAV (0x2b) — в DTB телефона у
  `qcom,rmtfs_sharedmem@0` стоит `qcom,vm-nav-path`. С тремя владельцами запись в буфер после
  «замка» модема проходит без сброса (цикл 2: сектор записан, модему отказано — ядро вернулось
  штатно). Обратная передача (`{HLOS, MSS, NAV} → {HLOS}`) при остановке отказывает
  (`-2`, ответ `0x56`): видимо, пока держится замок модема; на перезагрузку это не влияет;
- опыты включаются ключами `modem_share_test=1` (пробная запись после передачи),
  `modem_rmtfs_rw_off=1` (отказ в чтении), `modem_rmtfs_rw_fake=1` (запись есть, ответ «нет»),
  `modem_rmtfs_delay=S` (пауза перед первым чтением), `modem_share_off=1`, `modem_no_nav=1`.

Паника `copyio.c:89 Assertion failed: pan != 0` в пользовательских процессах Darwin встречалась в
двух прогонах с модемом; её причина не найдена.

## 23 октября 2026, вечер: модем читает файлы, выходит в ONLINE

С буфером в `0xa8000000`, отданным HLOS, MSS и NAV, модем читает свои файловые системы и за
~30 с объявляет все службы (88 объявлений: DMS 2, NAS 3, UIM 11, WDS 1, ...). Дальше он стоит в
режиме **OFFLINE** и на `DMS Set Operating Mode = online` отвечает «устройство не готово» (52),
на `low power` — «недопустимый переход» (60): он ждёт двух служб процессора приложений, которые
на Android дают демоны `pd-mapper` и `tqftpserv`:

- **реестр служб** (QMI 64, версия 257): модем спрашивает, где `tms/servreg` и другие; ответ —
  домены (`msm/modem/root_pd`, экземпляр 180) из `*.jsn` раздела прошивки;
- **TFTP поверх QRTR** (QMI 4096): модем пишет `/readwrite/server_check.txt`, читает
  `/readonly/firmware/image/modem_pr/so/665_0_0.mbn` кусками (опции `rsize`, `seek`, `wsize`,
  `blksize`), просит `/readwrite/ota_firewall/ruleset` (нет — не страшно).

Обе службы теперь в `hakios.mpss.c` (разделы «TFTP over QRTR» и «the service registry's
locator»): файлы берутся из `/fw/image` системного образа (`fw-modem/image` — копия
`/vendor/firmware_mnt/image` телефона, снятая `adb pull`; `MODEM=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh`
кладёт её в образ), записи модема хранятся в памяти ядра на время прогона. Сервер имён QRTR
объявляет наши службы модему при hello и отвечает на его lookup.

Результат (прогон 23:00): после обслуживания файлов модем **согласился перейти в ONLINE**, NAS
ответил «не зарегистрирован, CS/PS отключены», и через несколько секунд модем упал в задаче
`enl2_dl` (LTE L2, downlink) с нулевым адресом. Предположительно при выходе в сеть он обращается
к IPA, которого с нашей стороны нет; проверяется ответ «IPA недоступен» через SMP2P
(`modem_ipa=1`), дальше — либо запуск прошивки IPA и его тактов, либо иной обход.

## 24 октября 2026: IPA — прошивка, такт, SMMU

Падение `enl2_dl` повторяется в каждом прогоне через несколько секунд после ONLINE. Гипотеза —
модему нужен работающий IPA (пакетный ускоритель, через него идут данные LTE), и в
`hakios.mpss.c` появился его минимальный драйвер («the IPA» в файле), по образцу
`drivers/net/ipa` Linux (версия IPA 4.11, sc7280):

- **такт**: без голоса RPMh за BCM `IP0` (`ipa_clock()`) TrustZone отвечает на
  `AUTH_AND_RESET` образа 15 «Unhandled implementation specific error»; с голосом прошивка
  `yupik_ipa_fws` (перемещаемый ELF, кладётся от `0x8b700000`) стартует, микроконтроллер
  отвечает «booted» (`ipa_status()`);
- **память IPA**: `ipa_memory_init()` обнуляет локальную память (0x3000), пишет канарейки и базу
  контекстов обработки; раскладка — `ipa_data-v4.11.c`;
- **QMI 0x31**: наш хост (экземпляр 1) посылает модемному драйверу IPA `INIT_DRIVER` с раскладкой
  памяти (таблиц маршрутов 15, иначе модем падает на `num_indices >= rtng_tbl_max`), модем
  подписывается на индикацию; ответ `INIT_COMPLETE` ещё не дождались;
- **SMMU**: IPA ходит в память через SMMU процессора приложений потоками `0x480` (AP) и `0x482`
  (микроконтроллер). Поток без совпадения даёт отказ, обход (bypass) гипервизор не даёт.
  Контекст с нашими таблицами (тождественное отображение гигабайта DDR от `0x80000000` и imem
  `0x146a8000`) гипервизор принял (`sctlr` стал `0x127`, `s2cr` — наш), но **регистр
  совпадения с потоком `0x480` и маской `0x2` он сбросил в 0**. У Wi-Fi (`0x1c00`, маска 1,
  как в дереве устройств) прошло. В дереве устройств у потоков IPA маска 0 — гипервизор, видимо,
  сверяет пару (поток, маска) со списком хозяев. Прогон 21: по регистру совпадения на каждый
  поток, маска 0.

Телефон после каждого прогона возвращается в Android (`cycle.sh`); разделы не пишутся.

### 24 октября, ночь: что говорит сам Android

Android телефона рутован (KernelSU), и его `dmesg`, debugfs (`/d/ipa`, `/d/gsi`) и IPC-логи
(`/d/ipc_logging/ipa/log`, `gsi/log`) читаются по adb. По ним:

- SMMU: прогон 21 подтвердил догадку — **гипервизор принял по регистру совпадения на поток**
  (`0x480` и `0x482`, маска 0, оба в контекст 7), отказов IPA не было;
- модем **не отвечал на INIT_DRIVER** вовсе (13 с до падения `enl2_dl`). У Android ответ
  приходит через 11 мс, и запрос другой: `platform_type 3` (мы слали 1 — «data card»),
  `num_indices 7` (мы 14), область модема `0x27d8` размером `0x800` (мы `0x1f18/0x100c`,
  раскладка upstream v4.11 не совпадает с раскладкой `ipa_4_11_mem_part` из techpack/dataipa),
  контексты обработки `0xad0` размером `0xac0`, статистика квот `0x1d00/0x30`, дропов
  `0x27b0/0x20`; TLV 0x18 (`is_ssr_bootup`) при первой загрузке не посылается;
- после ответа модем шлёт `INIT_MODEM_DRIVER_CMPLT` (0x35), `CONFIG` (0x27),
  `INSTALL_FILTER_RULE` (0x23), `FILTER_INSTALLED_NOTIF` (0x24) — Android отвечает успехом;
  индикацию `INIT_COMPLETE` (0x22) шлёт сразу после ответа на INIT_DRIVER;
- микроконтроллер IPA загружает **модем** (его события «booted» приходят после ответа), нам его
  область (0x0..0x288) трогать не надо;
- прошивка IPA у Android кладётся с `0x8b710000` (reserved `ipa_fw@8b700000` 0x10000,
  `ipa_gsi@8b710000` 0xa000); окно SRAM — `ipa-base + 0x40000 + 0x10000 = 0x1e50000`, 0x3000
  байт (блок в драйвере был отображён на 4 КБ — исправлено на 0x4000).

Источник раскладки и обработчиков: `techpack/dataipa/drivers/platform/msm/ipa/ipa_v3`
(`ipa_utils.c: ipa_4_11_mem_part`, `ipa_qmi_service.c`), ядро
Atom-X-Devs/android_kernel_xiaomi_sm7325 (у MiCode ветка `hakios-s-oss`).

### Прогон 23 (01:11): служба IPA модема отвечает — но не на INIT_DRIVER

Пробный запрос (сообщение 0x7fff) на порт службы IPA модема получает ответ через 1 мс
(result 1, error 0x39 — неизвестное сообщение): транспорт в обе стороны работает. INIT_DRIVER
(0x21), посланный тем же портом за мгновение до того, ответа не получает ни разу — модем его
декодирует (иначе был бы ответ об ошибке) и **зависает в обработчике**, то есть на обращении к
железу IPA (свои GSI-каналы, таблицы через команды, загрузка микроконтроллера). Регистры,
которые Android пишет до модема (QSB, Qtime, COMP_CFG, группы ресурсов, маршрут), теперь
выставлены (`ipa_hardware_init()`), это не помогло. Следующие кандидаты: GSI со стороны
модема (Android регистрирует GSI и поднимает свои каналы до модема — возможно, модему нужны
прерывания/`GSI_EE` общие регистры), голоса шины `SN8`/`SH0`/`MC0`/`ACV` (имена есть в cmd_db) на
время рукостискания, и чтение через adb того, что делает модем Android в первые 11 мс после
INIT_DRIVER (`/d/ipc_logging/gsi/log` вокруг 33.31 с).

### Прогони 24–26 (ранок 24 жовтня)

- 24 (`skip_uc_load=1`): модем падає інакше — `ipa_qsh.c:1241: IPA_QSH failed to send analysis to
  IPA_CTL msgQ`: черга задачі IPA_CTL переповнена, задача стоїть незалежно від мікроконтролера.
- 25: TrustZone кладе сегменти образу IPA у внутрішню пам'ять GSI (0x1e1f000) і мікроконтролера
  (0x1e81000) байт у байт (перевірено читанням), `GSI_CFG` = 0x205 — як пише `gsi_enable_fw()`.
  Прошивка GSI увімкнена, адреса образу в DDR (0x8b700000 чи 0x8b710000, як у Android) ні на що не
  впливає. Сегмент мікроконтролера — лише 0x3c8 байт: завантажувальний стаб; повну прошивку йому
  дає модем. Пробний запит службі IPA модема відповідається за 1 мс, INIT_DRIVER — ніколи.
- 26: Android при старті драйвера виділяє в SMEM (розділ apps–modem) елемент
  `SMEM_IPA_FILTER_TABLE` (497) на 0x9000 байт (`qcom,ipa-q6-smem-size`) і відображає його в
  SMMU-контекст IPA: модем кладе туди свої таблиці фільтрів. Тепер елемент робиться на кроці 6
  (раніше, 22 жовтня, його вимкнули: без працюючого IPA модем, знайшовши елемент, падав до появи
  служб). `modem_ipa_item=0` — не робити.

### Прогін 28 (08:49): РУКОСТИСКАННЯ IPA ПРОЙШЛО

Розгадка — у рядках образу модема: `IPA_SMP2P: Could not wait for inbound SMP2P channel
readiness`. Драйвер IPA модема при ініціалізації чекає, поки в елементі SMP2P процесора
застосунків з'явиться запис «ipa» (у Android він є з завантаження: `qcom,smp2p-ipa-1-out`), і без
нього задача IPA_CTL стоїть вічно — звідси мовчання на INIT_DRIVER і падіння `enl2_dl`. З
`modem_ipa=3` (запис «ipa» = біт 0 «відповідь дійсна» + біт 1 «такт IPA увімкнено») модем за 10 мс
**прийняв INIT_DRIVER**, надіслав INIT_MODEM_DRIVER_CMPLT, CONFIG і 27 правил фільтрів
(INSTALL_FILTER_RULE). Впав на звірці ідентифікаторів правил з нашої відповіді
(`ipa_ipfltr.c:6246`): `rule_id` у структурі правила лежить на зміщенні 168, не 163 — виправлено
(прогін 29). Елемент SMEM 497 і голоси за шини (SN8, SH0, MC0, ACV) лишаються.

### Прогони 29–30: модем живе, але не шукає мережу — SIM у другому слоті

- 29: з вірними `rule_id` модем пережив установку правил, вийшов в ONLINE і прожив усі 120 с
  опитування NAS, зупинився коректно. NAS: «registration 0 (none), CS 2, PS 2», радіоінтерфейс 0
  (немає сервісу), сигналу нема — модем навіть не шукає.
- 30: додані запити після ONLINE (`sim_probe()`): UIM Get Card Status (0x2f) — **слот 1: карта
  ERROR (код 3), слот 2: PRESENT, USIM READY**; NAS Get System Selection Preference (0x34): режим
  GSM|UMTS|LTE, вибір автоматичний; NAS Initiate Network Register (0x22) — відмова, помилка 37.
  Android бачить ту саму SIM (Kyivstar, ICCID 8938…4340) активною. Первинна підписка (NAS, що
  опитуємо) прив'язана до логічного слота 1 без картки — звідси «no service». Прогін 31: UIM
  Switch Slot (0x46): логічний слот 1 → фізичний слот 2, потім повторні запити.
- Прогони з `modem_step=11` тримають SpringBoard 600 с (телефон стоїть на логотипі Apple);
  тепер `tools/modem-cycle.sh` бере `XL_SB_DELAY` з оточення, і прогін 31 — повне завантаження
  Darwin з модемом у фоні (`modem=1`).

### Прогін 31 (09:12): повне завантаження Darwin, перемикання слота, ПЕРШИЙ СИГНАЛ

`XL_SB_DELAY=8` + `modem=1`: SpringBoard стартує одразу (телефон більше не стоїть на логотипі
Apple під час тестів), модем піднімається у фоні. Після UIM Switch Slot (логічний 1 → фізичний 2)
картка з'явилась у слоті 1 у стані «detected», і NAS уперше прочитав сигнал: **-80…-87 dBm,
UMTS** — радіо працює, модем бачить мережу; реєстрації ще нема (помилка 37 на Initiate Network
Register = `UIM_UNINITIALIZED`: SIM ще ініціалізується після перемикання). Тепер крок 11 раз на
10 с питає стан картки та NAS Get System Info (0x4d).

Статус-бар: у SpringBoard Darwin userland 16.5 стільникові пункти заповнює `SBStatusBarStateAggregator`
через `_updateSignalStrengthItem:withData:SIMInfo:barsGetter:barsSetter:` і `_setItem:enabled:`
(селектори знайдені в кеші dyld). `inject_sb.c` тепер перехоплює цей метод: коли
`kern.hakios.cellular_registered`, виставляє палички через barsSetter і вмикає пункт; раз на 3 с
просить пункт оновитися, коли стан у ядрі змінюється; список методів агрегатора пишеться в лог.

### Прогін 32 (25 жовтня): хук статус-бару живий; підписка ні до чого не прив'язана

- Хук у SpringBoard працює: `_updateSignalStrengthItem:withData:SIMInfo:barsGetter:barsSetter:`
  викликається для пунктів 4 (основна SIM) і 5 (друга), setter-и передаються, і за нашим
  проханням пункт оновлюється; повний список методів агрегатора є в лозі
  (`_postItem:withState:inList:`, `_updateBatteryItems`, …).
- UIM після перемикання слота: USIM у логічному слоті 1 READY, PIN1 вимкнений, але **первинний
  GW-додаток — 0xffff (немає)**, і NAS System Info показує service 4 (power save) по всіх радіо.
  Тобто підписці не призначено USIM. Прогін 33: UIM Change Provisioning Session (0x38): primary GW,
  activate, слот 1 + AID USIM, потім повторне Initiate Network Register.
- Прогони з самим модемом не вмикали решту заліза: GPU (`gpu=1`), DSP/батарея (`adsp=1`),
  вібро (`haptic=5`), Wi-Fi (`wifi=1`) — звідси «no GPU to draw with», `SOC=-1%`, без вібрації.
  Прогін 33 — з усім разом. Тач працює, коли екран увімкнений (Darwin гасить його через ~25 с
  бездіяльності; кнопка живлення будить).
