`docs/u-boot.md`:

```md
# U-Boot

HakiOS's loader can be started by **Das U-Boot** instead of Project Silicium's UEFI. The phone's own bootloader (ABL) starts
U-Boot from RAM with `fastboot boot`, U-Boot finds the loader and its payload **in memory** and starts the loader as a UEFI
application. Nothing is flashed: not `boot`, not any other partition, and a reboot gives the phone back to Android.

Status in one line: **works on the POCO X5 Pro and in QEMU, the whole chain to the kernel's user space, with `xl` as it was.**
The sections below say exactly what was run.

## Why

| | Silicium (`mkxnuimg.py`) | U-Boot (`tools/mkubootimg.py`) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is made of | Mu-Silicium and the **phone vendor's own UEFI drivers**, which are not in the repositories: you extract them from your own phone first | open source only: U-Boot's Qualcomm support and the phone's device tree |
| Where the loader comes from | the payload the boot shim copies to `0xF0000000` | the boot image's ramdisk, or U-Boot's own fastboot: the hakios command copies the payload to `0xF0000000` |
| A new loader or payload | a new boot image and `fastboot boot` through ABL again | the same, or sent to the running U-Boot over USB (below), without going back through ABL |
| `xl` (run, ramdisk, log, screenshot) | yes | yes: U-Boot provides the same USB protocol the loader uses under Qualcomm's UEFI |

## The chain

```
ABL ──fastboot boot──> U-Boot (RAM) ──hakios load──> payload at 0xF0000000, loader.efi ──bootefi──> loader ──> XNU
                         │                               ▲
                         └── no payload in the image ────┘ fastboot stage x.hkub; fastboot oem run:hakios load fastboot
```

- **The boot image** (`tools/mkubootimg.py`): the kernel is `gzip(u-boot.bin)` with the phone's Android device tree appended,
  exactly what ABL expects for Silicium's image (header version 1); the ramdisk is an `HKUB` container with the loader and a payload,
  or nothing.
- **U-Boot's device tree** (`devices/redwood/u-boot/files/dts/upstream/src/arm64/qcom/sm7325-xiaomi-redwood.dts`): the panel's
  framebuffer at `0xE1000000` as ABL left it (the loader knows the phone by that address), the keys, USB as a device, UFS, and every
  carve-out of the Android device tree and of Silicium's memory map. The size of RAM is not in it: ABL writes it into the device
  tree it hands over and U-Boot reads it from there.
- **`0xF0000000`, 64 MiB** is reserved in that device tree (`hakios-payload`): nothing in U-Boot takes it, the hakios command
  writes the payload there, and the loader's memory window stays clear of it, as under Silicium.
- **The hakios command** (`uefi/u-boot/files/cmd/hakios.c`):

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | `hakios load` | from the ramdisk ABL loaded (the device tree ABL handed over says where) |
  | `hakios load fastboot` | what the host sent last with `fastboot stage` |
  | `hakios load ADDR [SIZE]` | from anywhere in RAM; a container or a payload says its own size |
  | `hakios boot` | `bootefi` the loader |
  | `hakios info` | what is in memory |

  It takes an `HKUB` container, a bare XNUP payload or a bare `loader.efi`. A payload with an entry `loader.efi` (the one
  `xl enter` makes) brings its loader with it. Every entry of a container carries a CRC-32, and a damaged one is never started.
- **Qualcomm's USB device protocol** (`uefi/u-boot/files/lib/efi_loader/efi_qcom_usb.c`): the loader talks fastboot to the host
  through `EFI_USB_DEVICE_PROTOCOL`, the interface of Qualcomm's UEFI (published in its open-source ABL). U-Boot provides it on its
  own USB gadget stack: the control endpoint is answered from the loader's descriptors, the loader sees its bulk transfers and the
  cable's state. So `xl` works unchanged.
- **What U-Boot will not do**: write the phone's storage. Capsule updates are off (they flash a partition) and U-Boot's watchdog is
  not started (the loader has its own, and keeps U-Boot's boot services while the kernel runs).

## Build

```sh
tools/hakios-device.py sync          # devices/redwood and uefi/, as for everything else
make u-boot                          # = uefi/u-boot/apply.sh (U-Boot at uefi/u-boot/BASE into u-boot/) + uefi/u-boot/build.sh redwood
```

`uefi/u-boot/build.sh` needs an AArch64 GCC (`aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc`, or Arm's `aarch64-none-elf-gcc` from
developer.arm.com; `CROSS_COMPILE=` to name another). The result is `u-boot/build-redwood/u-boot.bin`.

## Run

**With `xl`**, as always:

```sh
XL_FIRMWARE=u-boot ./xl enter        # without XL_FIRMWARE: Silicium when its image is built, else U-Boot
./xl ramdisk userland/system.apfs
./xl run
```

**One image, loader and payload inside:**

```sh
xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o payload.bin kernel=hakios-kernel ramdisk=userland/hello --cmdline "-v"
make u-boot-img UBOOT_PAYLOAD=payload.bin        # hakios-u-boot.img
fastboot boot hakios-u-boot.img
```

**U-Boot first, then anything over its fastboot** (no new boot image for a new kernel):

```sh
make u-boot-img                                   # no payload: U-Boot waits for the host
fastboot boot hakios-u-boot.img
tools/mkubootimg.py -p payload.bin -c x.hkub      # the container alone
fastboot stage x.hkub
fastboot oem run:"hakios load fastboot"
fastboot continue                                 # hakios boot
```

U-Boot's fastboot shows as Google's `18d1:4ee0` (the loader's own is `18d1:d00d`); `fastboot oem console` reads U-Boot's log.
Hold **volume down** while U-Boot starts for its menu (start, fastboot, what is in memory, a shell over USB serial): the volume
keys move, the power key chooses.

## What the screen says

U-Boot writes what it does on the phone's screen, each line marked **`[oosexgang]`**: what the hakios command took and where it put
it, and, once the loader talks to the host, the cable coming and going, every command of the host (the `getvar` polls of a run
aside), every download and upload with its size, progress and speed, and every `FAIL` the loader answers:

```
[oosexgang] hakios: payload of 66216 bytes at 0xf0000000
[oosexgang] usb: the host is connected
[oosexgang] host: upload
[oosexgang] sending 22 KiB
[oosexgang] sent 22 KiB in 4 ms (5500 KiB/s)
[oosexgang] host: oem screenshot
[oosexgang] host: upload
[oosexgang] sending 10125 KiB
[oosexgang]   30%
```

(lines from the phone's screen after `xl run` and `xl screenshot`)

`setenv hakios_status 0` (U-Boot's shell, or the environment file) turns it off. `hakios_usb_debug=1` shows much more: every
control request, endpoint and transfer of the USB device protocol, which is how the faults below were found.

## Try it in QEMU (nothing of Apple's)

```sh
make qemu-u-boot          # make qemu-open's kernel, loader and hello, booted by U-Boot: qemu/run-u-boot.sh
```

`qemu/run-u-boot.sh` puts an `HKUB` container at `0x50000000` (where a phone's ABL would have put the ramdisk) and boots
`u-boot/build-qemu/u-boot.bin` (`devices/qemu/u-boot/files/configs/hakios_qemu_defconfig`). What it printed (U-Boot 2026.07, the
prebuilt kernel and `hello`):

```
hakios: payload of 16825792 bytes at 0xf0000000
hakios: loader of 65536 bytes at 0x1bd510000
== XNULOADER v3 ==
platform qemu-virt
phys window f4000000 size c8000000, claim status 0
Hello from user space on Darwin!
kernel returned: log at f7bdc9c0, 21629 bytes
```

The same as under edk2 (`qemu/run.sh`), line for line where they are comparable. A bare payload with `loader.efi` in it was run the
same way and gave the same.

## On the phone: what is known and what is not

Run on a POCO X5 Pro 5G (`redwood`, bootloader unlocked, Android on slot b), from Windows' platform-tools, 29 October 2026:

- ABL starts the boot image with `fastboot boot`; U-Boot comes up on the panel, takes the size of RAM from ABL's device tree and
  brings UFS up (SK hynix, six LUNs).
- `./xl enter` (`XL_FIRMWARE` unset, no Silicium image): `xl: loader is up` in about 7 s. The loader finds the phone by its
  framebuffer (`platform redwood`), arms its watchdog, and its fastboot answers (`product: xnuloader`, `version: 0.5`).
- `./xl memmap`: every carve-out of the device tree reserved, the payload area as U-Boot's, and 5.4 GiB free above `0xF4000000`
  for the kernel's window.
- Ten `getvar` and 1 MiB `stage` in turn, all answered; the 16 MiB run payload in 0.55 s.
- `XL_RAMDISK=prebuilt/userland/hello ./xl run`: the prebuilt kernel boots, `Hello from user space on Darwin!`, `initproc` exits
  (that is what `hello` does) and the kernel returns: `result: returned 22037 0`. The loader's log is written to `logdump` and read
  back the same.
- `./xl screenshot`: the kernel's last screen, with U-Boot's `[oosexgang]` lines under it.
- **Darwin userland 16.5**, the images built from the IPSW (`sysimage/unpack.sh`, `PREBUILT=1 REST=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh`, `make
  loader`), no firmware of the phone yet (no GPU: drawn in software): `./xl ramdisk userland/system.apfs` takes 2361 MB in 71 s
  (33 MB/s) through U-Boot, and `XL_CMDLINE="debug=0x8 rd=md0 hv_wdt_pet=1 bootcpu=7 cpus=8 cpufreq=1 ufs=2 touchscreen=1" ./xl run`
  brings the home screen in under a minute (the screenshot at 60 s), with touch.
- The way through U-Boot's own fastboot (`stage`, `oem run:hakios load fastboot`, `continue`): U-Boot takes the container and
  starts the loader, but **the loader's USB then does not come up on the bus**: the controller, released by U-Boot's fastboot and
  taken again by the loader, does not connect. Until that is fixed, put the loader and the payload in the boot image (`xl enter`
  does).

What it took on the phone, each seen there first (`hakios_usb_debug=1` and photographs of the screen):

| Fault | Fix |
|---|---|
| The loader's descriptors (USB 2.10 and a BOS) promise Link Power Management, which U-Boot's DWC3 does not do: the device left the bus 3 s after it came | USB 2.0 and no BOS, as U-Boot's own gadgets |
| U-Boot's endpoint autoconfig ORs the endpoint number into the address it is given (`0x01` became `0x03`) and writes a full-speed packet size (64) | only the direction goes in; the caller's packet size (512) comes back |
| U-Boot's DWC3 starts a bulk transfer only on the XferNotReady the host's next token brings | it starts on queue, and the next one when one completes, as Linux's dwc3 |
| U-Boot's DWC3 clears a stall with a transfer started (WinUSB clears the halt of a pipe it opens) | the transfer ends first and starts again after, as Linux's dwc3 |
| `fastboot oem console`: every response dequeued a request that was not queued; the error went into the console it was sending, for ever | only a request in flight is dequeued |
| The loader's log buffer was not aligned to the block size U-Boot's block I/O wants | aligned (`xnuloader/loader.c`) |
| A download the host gave up half-way left the loader waiting for good | 20 s without a byte and it is given up |

If U-Boot hangs, the menu (volume down) and `fastboot oem console` are the ways in;
[U-Boot's own notes on phones](https://docs.u-boot.org/en/latest/board/qualcomm/phones.html) say how to bisect a hang.
- What the loader asks Qualcomm's UEFI for and U-Boot does not have: the charger protocols (the loader goes on without the battery
  reading) and `EFI_CPU_ARCH_PROTOCOL` (the loader's exception hook is not installed; a fault in the loader resets the phone instead of
  being logged).

## Installed beside Android: a menu at every start

What was done on the POCO X5 Pro, 29 October 2026, in this order, each step checked before the next:

1. **Backup** (`tools/backup-partitions.py --yes`, read only, as root): the boot partitions of both slots, `vbmeta*`, `misc`,
   `devinfo`, `persist`, `modemst1/2`, `fsg`, the first and last 8 blocks of every unit (sda...sdf), each proven by three
   SHA-256s; a second copy kept off the working tree.
2. **`darwin`** (`tools/userdata-carve.py --wipe DIR 20`): userdata shortened, `darwin` (sda34, 20 GiB, APFS container
   type) at the end of LUN 0, two entries changed, both copies of the table checked here and with `sfdisk --sector-size
   4096`; written from Android (root) with `dd`, read back; then `fastboot -w` (**Android's data is erased**).
3. **The Darwin volume** into `darwin`: Apple's root volume of the IPSW (`tools/apfs/dmg.py extract`), the OS and App cryptexes
   after it, as the port's own layout (`docs/ru/notes.md`, "Криптексы на флеше"): 8.4 GB as 11 sparse pieces
   (`tools/sparse-split.py`: Google's fastboot for Windows runs out of memory on one 8 GB image), read back by U-Boot
   (`hakios sum darwin 0 2042368`) with the image's own sum.
4. **Darwin from `darwin`, still from RAM**: `CRYPTEXES=flash FLASHBOOT=1 userland/build.sh`, `xl ramdisk userland/flashboot.apfs`,
   `root_apfs=ufs_darwin ufs=2`: the Darwin volume is the root, SpringBoard up.
5. **The boot image of slot a** (`tools/mkubootimg.py --install`): U-Boot, the loader, a payload with the kernel, `root.apfs`
   and `flashboot.apfs` as its `resident` image (the loader puts it where `xl ramdisk` would), the flash-root command line,
   and `devices/redwood/u-boot/install.env`; `fastboot flash boot_a`, `fastboot set_active a`.

At every start: U-Boot marks slot a successful and shows the menu; **Android** (the default after 10 s) marks slot a
unbootable and restarts, and ABL makes slot b active itself; `fastboot set_active a` (or `hakios-menu.sh` in Android, with
root) brings the menu back. Seen on the phone: the menu, and Android from it.

### The data volume: /private/var kept, the size of the space

Without it `/private/var` is a memory filesystem: empty at every start, and Darwin shows the size of that (a quarter of
the RAM, "1 GB") as the phone's storage. With it, `/private/var` is HFS Plus in `darwin` after the Darwin volume and the
cryptexes (block 2042368 to the end, 12.2 GB): kept between starts, journaled, and what Darwin shows is its size.

- the kernel: HFS Plus is built in (Apple's `hfs-627.100.6`, `bsd/hfs`); with `ufs_write=1` the UFS driver gives that
  stretch out as `/dev/ufs_darwin_data`, which reads and writes through the loader (each write flushed and read back);
- `init`: `var_hfs=ufs_darwin_data` mounts it on `/private/var`, a memory filesystem as before if it does not mount;
- the empty volume, once: `tools/mkdatavol.py data.simg` and `fastboot flash darwin data.simg` (53 KB: the image says
  DONT_CARE for the Darwin volume and the cryptexes, and for every block the volume does not use). Flashing it again
  empties the volume;
- the payload's command line gains `ufs_write=1 var_hfs=ufs_darwin_data`;
- the loader serves writes to any phone's `darwin` (name, type, place, size, LUN 0; the unique GUID, which
  `userdata-carve.py` makes new on every phone, only printed): until then it compared the first phone's GUID, and on
  this one the volume never mounted (`/dev/ufs_darwin_data: No such file or directory`, a memory filesystem instead);
- the volume's writes are only written (`BLOCK_OP_WRITE_FAST`), the flash's cache flushed when the journal asks
  (`DKIOCSYNCHRONIZE` -> `BLOCK_OP_FLUSH`): a flush and a read back after each 4 KB write made the system crawl.

The rest of the installed image's command line is the configuration's (`tools/hakios-config.py args`) without
`adsp`, `sound` and `haptic`, which stopped the phone under U-Boot: `gpu=1 wifi=1 modem=1 modem_again=1
modem_buffer=0xa8000000 socinfo=1 thermal=1`. And `userland/build.sh` with `GL=1` (Mesa: `tools/mk-mesa.sh`): without
`libhakios.gl.dylib` in the image CoreAnimation draws with its software renderer whatever the GPU does -- slow, and
the wallpaper black ("Failed to initialize Metal or OpenGLES contexts!"). And `REST=1`: without it the image has
25 of the system's jobs and none of the launch angels, so PosterBoard (the wallpaper) never starts and the applications
that need one of the other services do not open: `GL=1 REST=1 CRYPTEXES=flash FLASHBOOT=1 userland/build.sh`.

Tried in QEMU first (`qemu/run-hfs-test.sh`; Darwin with `virtio_blk=2 var_hfs=rvblk0`): written, stopped hard, the journal
replayed at the next mount, the files there. The volume's root has to be root's (`mkfs.hfsplus -U 0 -G 0 -M 755`, as
`mkdatavol.py` makes it): with another owner Darwin takes it for a data volume to migrate and stays at the progress bar.

### Which slot is active is never U-Boot's to change

On these phones a slot being active is three things that ABL's `SetActiveSlot()` changes together: the bits of
`boot_a`/`boot_b`, the type GUIDs of every `_a`/`_b` pair (23 on LUN 4, `vbmeta_system` on LUN 0: the active slot's carry
the real types, the other's `77036cd4-...`, which XBL loads by), and the UFS boot LUN (1 for a, 2 for b). At every boot
`ValidateSlotGuids()` refuses a slot whose `boot_X` and `abl_X` carry the same GUID or whose LUN does not match:
`Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Device Error`, for every image, Android's too.

A first version of `hakios slot b` changed the bits alone. After it no image started, and no ABL command could help: every
`set_active` swaps the GUIDs *and* moves the bits, so the two stay apart. What brought the phone back:

- **not** `fastboot flash partition:N` with a stock table set blindly: ABL's `WriteGpt()` calls `ErasePartition()` on the
  whole unit first. On this phone that erase left the data as it was (every partition read back the same), but the code
  says otherwise and LUN 4 holds `abl`, `tz`, `hyp`, `modem` and the phone's own `secdata`, `storsec`, `tzsc`;
- `fastboot flash partition:4` with **this phone's own** LUN 4 table from step 1, in ABL's `gpt_both` layout
  (`work/gptboth.py`: what ABL's `PatchGpt()` makes of it was computed first: every block as it was but the backup header's
  `my_lba`, which ABL always sets to 1), then `fastboot set_active b` (the slot already active: ABL sets the boot LUN only);
- then the hashes of `boot_b`, `vendor_boot_b`, `dtbo_b`, `vbmeta_a/b` read by U-Boot: those of the backup.

So `hakios slot` changes only the active slot's own bits, as ABL does (`successful`, `unbootable`), and only ABL or
Android's boot control HAL change which slot is active. LUN 0's `vbmeta_system` pair was swapped by ABL three times
during this and is the other way round from LUN 4 now; nothing that starts reads it by type, and it is left so.

```

`docs/uefi-boot.md`:

```md
# UEFI boot

HakiOS can start the way a UEFI operating system starts: the firmware runs `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI` from a volume,
that loader reads the kernel from the same volume, and nothing else is needed: no fastboot, no host computer.

Status in one line: **works in QEMU (checked); not tried on a phone.** The sections below say exactly what was run.

## Three ways a payload reaches the loader

The payload is what the loader starts: the kernel, a small root image, the command line and `kernel.ver`
(`xnuloader/mkpayload.py`). The loader takes a payload that is already in memory first, and looks on the volume
only when there is none.

| Way | How | Where | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fastboot boot` | `./xl enter`: a boot image holding Project Silicium's UEFI, a shim and the payload; the shim copies the payload to `0xF0000000` | the phone | yes: the loader started on the attached phone, its banner was read back from the screen and from the log |
| a loader device | QEMU's `-device loader` puts the payload at `0xF0000000` (`make qemu-open`) | QEMU | yes |
| **a file of the volume** | the loader opens the volume it was started from and reads `\EFI\hakios\payload.bin` itself | any UEFI that starts the loader from a volume | **in QEMU only** (AAVMF) |

## The volume

```
EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI       the loader, where an AArch64 UEFI boots a removable volume from
EFI/hakios/payload.bin      the payload
EFI/hakios/kernel.ver       the version, as text, for a person to read
```

`make esp` makes the tree in `build/esp` (`tools/mkesp.py`, which refuses what the loader would refuse: not a payload,
no kernel in it, over 63 MiB, a loader that is not an EFI application, a directory that is not empty). Copy it to a
FAT32 volume, or serve it to QEMU.

## Try it (QEMU, nothing of Apple's closed software: `make doctor` first)

```sh
make qemu-open                    # builds the kernel, the open loader, hello, and boots them (the payload device)
QEMU_ESP=1 qemu/run.sh 90         # the same payload, but as the file \EFI\hakios\payload.bin: no loader device
make esp                          # the tree for a real volume: build/esp
```

What `QEMU_ESP=1` prints under the banner: `payload: 15306944 bytes from \EFI\hakios\payload.bin on the volume this
loader was started from`, then the kernel boots and `hello` reads the same version through `sysctl kern.hakios.version`.
A file that is not a payload gives `is not a payload (no XNUP at its start)`, and no file gives `there is no
\EFI\hakios\payload.bin on the volume`, each with `kernel.ver=unknown` and no crash (both were run).

## Limits

- **63 MiB.** The loader's payload region is 64 MiB and its last MiB holds the panic log. The kernel is about 15 MiB;
  the **big Darwin system image (2.5 GB) does not come this way**. It comes over USB (`xl ramdisk`, once per loader
  session) or, in the flash recipe, from the partition `darwin` (`docs/install.md`).
- **The region has to be free.** The loader takes all 64 MiB of it with `AllocatePages(AllocateAddress)` (not only the
  pages the file fills: a payload sent over USB later, and the panic log, are written into the rest). A firmware that
  keeps it reserved refuses, and the loader says so and goes on without a payload, as it always did. A file that
  cannot be read to its end is dropped, and its header is wiped, so a half-read payload is never started.
- **Nothing is signed.** The loader is not signed and no Secure Boot is involved.

## On a phone: what is known and what is not

- Project Silicium's Boot Manager, in this port, is changed to start the XNU loader **from the container the shim
  leaves in memory instead of a menu** (`uefi/README.md`). It does not look for a loader on a
  volume. So the file-of-the-volume way has **not** been tried on the phone, and it needs a change to the Boot
  Manager (or a UEFI that boots from a volume) before it can be.
- Whether Silicium leaves `0xF0000000` free at the point where the loader runs is not known.
- The way to a phone that does not need a host today is the boot image itself, in a boot slot: `docs/install.md`.
- Another UEFI on the phone, all of it open source: HakiOS's U-Boot, started from RAM by ABL, which takes the loader and the
  payload from memory and starts the loader with `bootefi` ([U-Boot](u-boot.md)).

```

`docs/versioning.md`:

```md
# The kernel's version

An Android kernel says `5.4.147-android12-9-...-g1a2b3c4d`: the Linux it is built on, the vendor's branch, and the
commit. This kernel says the same kind of thing about itself:

```
2.3.4-hakios-darwin22.5-sc7280-g1a2b3c4d[-dirty]
│ │  │  │      │          │      └ the commit; "-dirty" if a tracked file differs from it
│ │  │  │      │          └ the SoC family the configuration is for (CONFIG_SOC)
│ │  │  │      └ the Darwin it is built on (22.5.0, Apple's open xnu-8796.121.2)
│ │  │  └ EXTRAVERSION: what the tree is called
│ │  └ SUBLEVEL
│ └ PATCHLEVEL
└ VERSION
```

## Where it is shown

1. **The loader's banner** (`xnuloader/`), under `HAKIOS`: `hello hakios-kernel!` and `kernel.ver=<the string>`.
2. **The kernel**: a line in the boot log, and `sysctl kern.hakios.version` (`userland/src/hello.c` prints it).
3. **The payload**: `xnuloader/mkpayload.py` puts it in as the entry `kernel.ver`; the loader hands it to the kernel on
   its command line as `hakios_kver=`. A kernel started some other way (no loader) says `unknown`: it does not guess.

Darwin's own `uname -v` ("Darwin Kernel Version 22.5.0: ...") is Apple's and stays as it is, as Linux's `uname -r` stays
in an Android kernel next to the vendor's own string.

## Where it comes from

`VERSION`, at the top of the repository, in the form of the Makefile of Linux (`VERSION`, `PATCHLEVEL`, `SUBLEVEL`,
`EXTRAVERSION`, `NAME`, plus `DARWIN` and `XNU`: the release this port sits on). `tools/kernel-version.py` makes the
string from it, from `CONFIG_SOC` of the `.config` (see [configs.md](configs.md)) and from git:

```bash
tools/kernel-version.py            # 2.3.4-hakios-darwin22.5-sc7280-g1a2b3c4d (the -sc7280 part is there with a .config)
tools/kernel-version.py --short    # 2.3.4
tools/kernel-version.py --release  # 2.3.4-hakios: what a tag is called (v2.3.4-hakios)
tools/kernel-version.py --all      # every part, for a build log
```

`HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX` in the environment replaces the git part (a reproducible build, or a tree that is not a
checkout).

The kernel is told its version and does not carry it, on purpose: it is built once from Apple's open source plus this
port, and the payload is made in a second. A version that is only the commit, or the SoC of one configuration, then does
not need the Mach-O rebuilt.

## When a number moves

| | moves when | example |
|---|---|---|
| **VERSION** (2) | a change that breaks what a user, a port or a boot image relies on | the payload format, the meaning of a boot-argument, the layout of the partition `darwin` |
| **PATCHLEVEL** (3) | a feature | a driver, a device, a tool |
| **SUBLEVEL** (4) | a fix | a bug in a driver, a wrong default |
| **EXTRAVERSION** | the tree is somebody's branch | a vendor writes its own here, as Android's `-android12-9` |

A boot-argument that is removed or changes its meaning is a **VERSION** change, which is why
[boot-args.md](boot-args.md) is made from the source and checked in CI: it is the list of what a version promises.

## Honest limits

- The number says which source the kernel was built from. It does not say that any given phone boots it; what has
  been seen to boot is in the README's status table and in [port-pkg110.md](port-pkg110.md).
- `-dirty` means a tracked file differs from the commit. A build from a modified tree says so.
- `Darwin 22.5` is a name for the open-source xnu release the kernel is built on. The kernel is not Apple's `kernel`
  and is not Darwin's.

```

`docs/windows.md`:

```md
# HakiOS on a Windows machine

How to build and run HakiOS with a Windows PC and a phone. It works, with each tool where it fits.
Everything here was done on a real machine and phone; `tools/doctor.sh` checks the same things for you.

## What runs where

| Job | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Build the images (`sysimage/unpack.sh`, `userland/build.sh`) | **WSL 2, in its own filesystem** (`~/hakios`) | `unpack.sh` makes files named `NAME:com.apple.decmpfs`; NTFS forbids `:`. The Windows drive is also slow for tens of thousands of small files. |
| Drive the phone (`./xl`, `tools/modem-cycle-win.sh`) | **Git Bash**, in your Windows checkout | `fastboot` and `adb` are Windows programs that see the phone's USB; WSL 2 does not, without usbipd. |

So: build in WSL, copy `userland/root.apfs` and `userland/system.apfs` to the Windows checkout, run `xl`
from Git Bash.

## Setup

1. **Platform-tools:** unpack Google's Android platform-tools to `C:\platform-tools` (adb, fastboot).
   fastboot worked here without a separate USB driver.
2. **WSL 2 Ubuntu:** `sudo apt install 7zip clang lld lz4 python3 git make` (7-Zip must be 23 or newer).
3. **Git Bash** (Git for Windows). Check your Windows checkout and WSL both with:
   ```sh
   tools/doctor.sh           # in Git Bash (host checks for the xl side, and the phone)
   tools/doctor.sh           # in WSL, in ~/hakios (host checks for the build side)
   ```
4. **In Git Bash**, before using `xl`: `export PATH="$PWD/tools/win-bin:/c/platform-tools:$PATH"`.
   `tools/win-bin/flock` replaces util-linux's `flock`, which Git Bash does not have and `xl` needs.

## The phone

- Turn on USB debugging. Unlock the bootloader (yours to do; it wipes the phone).
- **Trust the device tree, not the product name.** Some units report a different brand and model than
  the board they really are (root-hiding modules fake the identity and even the bootloader's
  "locked" state). `tools/doctor.sh` prints both. The supported platform is `redwood` / SM7325.
- **Firmware needs root on some ROMs.** If `devices/redwood/pull-firmware.sh` reports every file
  "not on the phone" but `doctor` says the firmware is readable only by root, use
  `devices/redwood/pull-firmware-root.sh`. It copies under `su` to a staging directory, pulls, and
  removes the staging directory; nothing on the phone is changed.

## Build and run

```sh
# WSL, in ~/hakios (a clone in WSL's own filesystem, with fw-*/ copied in):
sysimage/unpack.sh ~/iPhone10,3,iPhone10,6_16.5_20F66_Restore.ipsw   # your own IPSW, ~5 min
PREBUILT=1 REST=1 MODEM=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh     # root.apfs + system.apfs, ~4 min, no theos needed
cp userland/root.apfs userland/system.apfs /mnt/d/.../hakios/userland/

# Git Bash, in the Windows checkout:
./xl enter                  # Android -> fastboot -> the loader in RAM (also the unlock test)
./xl screenshot logs/s.png  # what the loader put on the screen
./xl log                    # the loader's log
./xl reload                 # restart the phone and enter the loader again
./xl reboot                 # back to Android
```

Nothing is flashed: everything is booted from RAM, and a reboot brings Android back.

## When something goes wrong

- **`xl state` says `absent`** for more than three minutes: the phone is not on USB at all. Check the
  cable and the screen; hold power about 15 seconds to restart it into Android. `doctor` shows whether
  Windows sees any device.
- **`Failed to mount root device`** from a run: it was started without a root image. A run needs
  `system.apfs` built with `MODEM=1` if it uses the modem (`tools/modem-cycle-win.sh`).
- **`tools/modem-cycle.sh` fails under Git Bash:** use `tools/modem-cycle-win.sh`; the original puts the
  macOS helpers in `tools/macos-bin` first on `PATH`, and they do not run on Windows.

## Metal: a run, measured, from Windows

The window server drawing through Metal (`METAL_PLUGIN=ca`) and the frame-rate bench, with one command in Git Bash. What the two paths
are and what the arguments do: [Metal on the Adreno](reference/metal.md).

The plug-in is compiled, so the build needs the cross toolchain (`xnu-deps/setup.sh`) and `hakios-metal/` of this tree
beside the checkout; `PREBUILT=1` compiles nothing, and `prebuilt/userland` has no plug-in.

```sh
# WSL, in ~/hakios: QuartzCore's library for CoreAnimation, then the image with the Metal plug-in and the bench.
# Off a Mac, name a later CoreAnimation's library to take the rest of its shaders from (a Mac's
# QuartzCore.framework/Versions/A/Resources/default.metallib copied over, or a later system's out of its IPSW):
CA_QC_METALLIB=/mnt/c/.../default.metallib tools/ca-metallib.py ~/ca-share
(cd hakios-metal && make ios MESA=1)
METAL_PLUGIN=ca RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.bench EXTRA_SHARE=~/ca-share REST=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh
cp userland/root.apfs userland/system.apfs /mnt/d/.../hakios/userland/

# Git Bash, in the Windows checkout (the phone in Android is fine: the script takes it into the loader):
tools/metal-run.sh                       # 180 s; the summary in logs/<time>-metal.txt
MORE="metal_gmem=1" tools/metal-run.sh   # with tiled rendering (each pass left in sysmem says why)
MORE="wallpaper_cache=1" tools/metal-run.sh   # any boot-argument beside the defaults
SHOTS=20 tools/metal-run.sh              # and a screenshot every 20 s, logs/<time>-shots/
```

For UniXNU's Metal on Vulkan, build its pieces in WSL first, then the same image with two more options, and name it at boot. It takes
rustup's cargo with Rust 1.98 and the `aarch64-apple-ios` target, `llvm-as` of LLVM 21, `glslang-tools`, and the theos iPhoneOS 16.5 SDK:

```sh
# WSL, in ~/hakios:
tools/mk-mesa.sh && tools/mk-turnip.sh && tools/mk-m2v.sh
METAL_PLUGIN=ca TURNIP=1 M2V=1 RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.bench EXTRA_SHARE=~/ca-share REST=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh
cp userland/root.apfs userland/system.apfs /mnt/d/.../hakios/userland/

# Git Bash:
MORE="metal_m2v=1" tools/metal-run.sh
MORE="metal_m2v=1 tu_debug=perf" tools/metal-run.sh   # and Turnip's own account of its render passes
```

The summary's frames per gesture come from `tools/frames.py`, which runs anywhere Python does: `python tools/frames.py logs/last.log`.

`tools/metal-run.sh` keeps `/private/var` between boots by default (`ufs=2 ufs_write=1 var_store=1`, the partition
`darwin` only; `PERSIST=0` for none), so the shader stages the window server compiles are compiled once. To put them
into the image, so that not even the first boot compiles them: with the phone back in Android,

```sh
tools/metal-cache-seed.sh                # reads darwin (read only, adb + root) into userland/hakios-metal-cache
```

and copy `userland/hakios-metal-cache` to WSL's `userland/` before the next `userland/build.sh`.

```

`drivers/README.md`:

```md
# Drivers

The kernel's own drivers, by subsystem, the way Linux keeps `drivers/`. They are files of Apple's XNU tree
(`bsd/dev/`, `iokit/Kernel/`), kept here so that they can be found and reviewed by what they do.

| Where | Is |
|---|---|
| `drivers/map` | the list: for each file, its subsystem and the path it has in Apple's tree |
| `drivers/<subsystem>/conf` | which drivers there are and which files each one is: `CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>` in a defconfig builds it in ([docs/drivers-config.md](../docs/drivers-config.md)) |
| `xnu/apply.sh` | lays Apple's tag, `xnu/hakios.patch`, `xnu/files/` and these drivers into one tree |
| `xnu/export.sh` | the reverse, run before committing; refuses a new `hakios.*` file that `drivers/map` does not list |
| `tools/drivers-check.py` | CI: the map and the directories agree, nothing is listed twice, nothing is kept in two places |

Adding a driver: put it in `drivers/<subsystem>/`, add a line to `drivers/map`, a `driver` block (or a `standard` line) to
`drivers/<subsystem>/conf`, `python3 tools/drivers-check.py`. The `bsd/conf/files` and `iokit/conf/files` lines are made from
the conf files (`tools/hakios-config.py kernel`); if the rest of the kernel calls the driver, a stand-in for when it is left out
goes into `core/hakios.stubs.c`. A driver that is started by a boot argument
has to be in `docs/boot-args.md` (`python3 tools/boot-args.py --check`).

## Subsystems

| Directory | Drivers | Boot arguments | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input/` | `hakios.goodix.c`, `hakios.input.c`, `hakios.buttons.c`, `hakios.virtio_input.c` | `touchscreen=` | the touch controller, the event queue behind `/dev/hakios-touch`, the buttons, QEMU's virtio input |
| `storage/` | `hakios.ufs.c`, `hakios.ufshc.c/.h`, `hakios.sparse.c`, `hakios.image.c`, `hakios.apfs_check.c`, `hakios.virtio_blk.c` | `ufs=`, `ufs_write=`, `ufs_native=` | the phone's flash (UFS), the sparse and image devices, the checks of the APFS read path, QEMU's virtio-blk. **The only code of the kernel that may write to the phone**: see `tools/provenance.allow` |
| `gpu/` | `hakios.adreno.c`, `hakios.gpu.cpp` | `gpu=`, `adreno=` | the Adreno GPU bring-up and the IOKit object user space talks to |
| `camera/` | `hakios.camera.c`, `hakios.torch.c` | `cam=`, `torch=` | the camera sensors and ISP interface, the flashlight LED |
| `haptic/` | `hakios.haptic.c` | `haptic=` | the vibration motor |
| `audio/` | `hakios.adsp.c`, `hakios.audio.c`, `hakios.sound.c`, `hakios.guard.c`, `hakios.speaker.c`, `hakios.mic.c`, `hakios.virtio_sound.c` | `adsp=`, `sound=`, `mic=` | the audio DSP loader, `/dev/hakios-audio`, the speaker amplifiers and their guard (`hakios.guard.c`, until now in `storage/`), the microphone, QEMU's virtio sound |
| `power/` | `hakios.battery.c/.cpp`, `hakios.cpufreq.c`, `hakios.thermal.c`, `hakios.pmic.c`, `hakios.battguard.c` | `cpufreq=`, `battmgr=`, `thermal=`, `pmic=`, `battery_stop=` | battery readings (through the DSP), CPU frequency, temperature limits that hand control back to the loader, the PMIC, and an end to an unwatched run before the battery is flat (compiled only: see its head for what it was checked against) |
| `wifi/` | `hakios.wifi.c`, `hakios.wlfw.c`, `hakios.lx.c`, `hakios.sta.c`, `hakios.apple80211.c`, `hakios.wlan.cpp` | `wifi=`, `wifi_step=` | the Wi-Fi subsystem's bring-up, the WLAN firmware service, the Linux-driver layer (`wifi/lx/`) and the surface the Darwin Wi-Fi service expects |
| `bluetooth/` | `hakios.bt.c` | `bt=` | Bluetooth of the WCN6750 radio chip: step one, a look at its three pins, read only (compiled only; the rest is written down in the file's head as what it needs) |
| `modem/` | `hakios.mpss.c`, `hakios.cell.c`, `hakios.qmi.c`, `hakios.nas.c`, `hakios.ipa.c` | `modem=` | the cellular modem path (research; not reviewed in `docs/driver-review/`) |
| `net/` | `hakios.net.c`, `hakios.virtio_net.c` | | the `enN` network interface and QEMU's virtio-net |
| `core/` | `hakios.version.c`, `hakios.platform.c`, `hakios.stubs.c`, `hakios.socinfo.c` | `hakios_kver=`, `socinfo=` | `kern.hakios.version`; what the drivers share (the hardware locks several take turns at, the `kern.hakios` node, `kern.hakios.drivers`); what the kernel calls in a driver that is left out; the SoC's identity as the hardware reports it |

## Reviews

`docs/driver-review/` has one read-only audit per group (what was checked, what was found, how sure). They are
findings to verify, not a certificate: read the report before relying on a driver, and fix findings in the driver,
not in the report.

The head of each driver says what was checked about it (compiled, run in QEMU, run on the phone) and what is a guess.

The kernel is built from the C and C++ files only; the drivers need no files that are not in this repository,
except the touch firmware header (`input/hakios.focaltech_fw.h`), which `tools/provenance.allow` marks as pending.

`drivers/audio/hakios.adsp.c`:

```c
/*
 * The audio DSP of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood), started, and spoken to: step 1 of sound. Every
 * address below belongs to this phone, and nothing here is touched unless a boot-arg asks for it.
 *
 * The SoC's audio (LPASS: its clocks, its I2S and SoundWire, the codec's macros) does not belong
 * to the application processor. It is the audio DSP's -- a Hexagon of its own inside LPASS,
 * Android's "adsp" -- which stays in reset until somebody loads it, exactly as the Wi-Fi's does
 * (hakios.wifi.c): the phone's own signed image, adsp.mdt and adsp.b02 to adsp.b36 from
 * /vendor/firmware_mnt/image of its Android (20 MB: in the system image under /fw, or with ADSP=1 in
 * the small one, see image_file()), goes into the 64 MB reserved for it, TrustZone is
 * asked to authenticate and start it, and from there everything is conversation through the
 * shared memory: SMP2P for "up", "given up", "stopped"; GLINK for channels; QRTR on the channel
 * "IPCRTR" for the services the DSP offers. (Reading an LPASS clock register from here ends the
 * kernel with an external abort: the DSP owns that block, and talks about it only this way.)
 * What audio needs of it later -- the audio services, the codec, the speaker's path -- is for the
 * steps after this one; this file only brings the DSP up and the link with it.
 *
 * The way is the Wi-Fi DSP's, taken over from hakios.wifi.c with the audio DSP's numbers: its
 * comments say why each thing is done so. What is different is said here:
 *   - processor 2 (not 13) in the shared memory; its SMP2P items 443 (its) and 429 (ours), its
 *     last words in item 423; GLINK's three items in our partition with it
 *   - its doorbells are IPCC client 3 (LPASS): signal 0 GLINK, signal 2 SMP2P
 *   - TrustZone knows it as image 1; its memory is 0x86700000, 64 MB (dt: qcom,lpass@3700000,
 *     reserved-memory adsp@86700000), every byte of which the image takes
 *   - the always-on processor is told of it as "adsp"
 *   - the Wi-Fi DSP may be running at the same time (wifi=1): the mailbox to the always-on
 *     processor and the lock for allocating in the shared memory are the two things both use,
 *     each behind a lock both take (hakios.wifi.c); the doorbells are only counted here, and
 *     only the audio DSP's are cleared from here
 * The code is a copy, not a shared library, for now: step 1 is not to change what the Wi-Fi does.
 *
 * Boot-arg adsp_step=N performs steps 1 to N and stops; as with wifi_step, a step says what it is
 * about to touch before it touches it, and a step that does not find what it needs ends the
 * sequence. adsp=1 is all of them, on a thread beside the system's start.
 *
 *   1  reads   the shared memory: our partition with the DSP, its items, whether it has run
 *              since the phone was started (its SMP2P item is there if so), its last words
 *   2  reads   the firmware in the small image: is it whole, does it fit the reserved memory
 *   3  writes  the always-on processor's mailbox open, unless it is (the Wi-Fi may have opened it)
 *   4  asks    TrustZone to take the image's header (image 1) and where the image will be; a
 *              DSP that a kernel before this one left running is asked to stop and shut down first
 *   5  writes  the image into the DSP's memory, and reads it back
 *   6  writes  our SMP2P item (429) into the shared memory, and our two marks of GLINK to zero
 *   7  asks    RPMh for the DSP's rails, writes "adsp: on" to the always-on processor, asks
 *              TrustZone to authenticate and start the DSP, and watches for its first words
 *              (answering in our item what SMP2P has us answer)
 *   8  reads   GLINK's queues
 *   9  writes  our side of GLINK: the versions, the channel "IPCRTR" opened both ways, our intents;
 *              from here a thread of ours listens to the DSP
 *  10  talks   QRTR on that channel: hello both ways, and the services the DSP tells of, written
 *              down for adsp_listen seconds (default 3)
 *  11  talks   APR, on the channel apr_audio_svc that the DSP opens and we answer as well: whether
 *              the audio services are up, and which there are (see step_apr())
 *
 * Once everything is up with adsp=1, the sound's path takes over (hakios.sound.c, boot-arg sound=N):
 * hakios_adsp_apr() is how it speaks to the audio services (any service, port and token; what
 * nobody waits for goes to its handler of events), and it is stopped before the DSP is.
 *
 * What is started is stopped: when the steps are over (unless adsp_keep=1, and then when the run
 * ends), and on a panic's way back to the loader. The DSP is asked first (bit 0 of our entry
 * "master-kernel"), then TrustZone shuts it down, then the always-on processor hears "adsp: off".
 * A DSP that a kernel before this one left running is found by its item and treated the same way
 * before this one is started; one that was shut down without having said it stopped is not
 * started again unless adsp_again=1 (the Wi-Fi DSP reset the phone, twice, when that was tried).
 *
 * More boot-args: adsp_new=K (steps K on have not been seen to work, and wait adsp_pause=MS after
 * each announcement, default 2200: what the loader needs to note the end of the log), adsp_wait=S
 * (how long step 7 watches for "up", default 10), adsp_keep=1, adsp_again=1, adsp_return=1 (back
 * to the loader when the steps are over).
 *
 * Nothing here writes a clock or changes a pin. One request goes to RPMh, as Linux makes it: the
 * DSP's two rails, LCX and LMX, at level 384 while it boots, given back when it says it has asked
 * for its own (see rails()).
 *
 * Addresses are from the phone's own device tree (qcom,lpass@3700000, qcom,smp2p-adsp,
 * qcom,glink/adsp, qcom,ipcc@408000, power-controller@c300000, reserved-memory), layouts from
 * Linux (see hakios.wifi.c for the files).
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <os/atomic_private.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <vm/memory_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/kauth.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/vnode.h>
#include <sys/vnode_internal.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>
#include <sys/hakios.audio.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map_unmappable(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size, unsigned int flags);
extern void ml_io_unmap(vm_offset_t addr, vm_size_t sz);
extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);
extern void loader_return(void);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern vm_offset_t pe_arm_get_soc_base_phys(void);
extern dev_t mdevlookup(int devid);
extern int mdevgetkernelrange(dev_t dev, vm_offset_t *base, uint64_t *size);

/* What the Wi-Fi's DSP and this one both use (hakios.wifi.c). */
extern lck_mtx_t hakios_aop_mailbox_lock;
extern lck_mtx_t hakios_smem_alloc_lock;
extern lck_mtx_t hakios_rsc_lock;            /* RPMh's sequencer, shared with the other DSP's driver */

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(adsp_lock_group, "hakios-adsp");

#define STEPS                   11
#define HAKIOS_SOC_BASE        0x00400000ul    /* where the loader says the phone's peripherals begin */

static uint32_t last_step, pause_ms = 2200, listen_seconds = 3;
static uint32_t step;                   /* the one being performed */
static uint32_t new_from;               /* the first of the steps that have not been seen to work: they wait */
static char last_write[96] = "nothing written";
static bool leaving;                    /* on the way back to the loader after a panic: no lock is taken, nothing sleeps */

/*
 * Every line goes to the log the loader reads from another core as well (as in hakios.wifi.c);
 * with adsp=1 only the few that say how it went (tell()), the rest to the kernel's own log.
 */
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(say_lock, &adsp_lock_group);
static bool quiet;

static void
say_line(const char *line, bool aloud)
{
	if (leaving) {
		for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
			loader_log_putc(*c);
		}
		return;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&say_lock);
	if (!quiet || aloud) {
		for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
			loader_log_putc(*c);
		}
	}
	printf("%s", line);
	lck_mtx_unlock(&say_lock);
}

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);
static int tell(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	say_line(line, false);
	return length;
}

static int
tell(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	say_line(line, true);
	return length;
}
#define printf say

static void
sleep_us(uint32_t us)
{
	delay_for_interval(us, NSEC_PER_USEC);
}

static void
sleep_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
}

static uint64_t
now_us(void)
{
	uint64_t nanoseconds;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &nanoseconds);
	return nanoseconds / 1000;
}

/* Until every write to memory so far has been carried out. */
static void
settle(void)
{
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy");
}

static bool
option(const char *name)
{
	uint32_t value = 0;

	return PE_parse_boot_argn(name, &value, sizeof(value)) && value != 0;
}

/* ---- register access (as in hakios.wifi.c) ------------------------------------------------------- */

static uint32_t __attribute__((noinline))
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	uint32_t value;

	__asm__ volatile ("ldr %w0, [%1]" : "=r" (value) : "r" (address) : "memory");
	return value;
}

static void __attribute__((noinline))
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	__asm__ volatile ("str %w0, [%1]" : : "r" (value), "r" (address) : "memory");
}

struct block {
	const char *name;
	uint32_t phys, size;
	vm_offset_t base;
};

static void
need(struct block *b)
{
	if (b->base == 0) {
		b->base = ml_io_map(b->phys, b->size);
	}
}

/* Time for the loader to note what has just been said, where it is not yet known to be harmless. */
static void
hold(void)
{
	if (step >= new_from && pause_ms && !leaving) {
		sleep_ms(pause_ms);
	}
}

static void
announce(const char *what)
{
	printf("adsp: step %u: %s\n", step, what);
	hold();
}

static uint32_t
get(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset)
{
	uint32_t value;

	need(b);
	value = rd(b->base + offset);
	printf("adsp: %u: %s %s (%#x) = %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
	return value;
}

static void
put(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
	need(b);
	printf("adsp: %u: about to write %s %s at %#x: %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
	snprintf(last_write, sizeof(last_write), "step %u wrote %#x to %s %s at %#x", step, value, b->name, name, b->phys + offset);
	wr(b->base + offset, value);
}

/* ---- the shared memory (hakios.wifi.c, step 1) --------------------------------------------------- */

#define SMEM_PHYS               0x80900000UL
#define SMEM_SIZE               0x00200000u
#define SMEM_US                 0
#define SMEM_ADSP               2               /* dt: qcom,remote-pid of qcom,smp2p-adsp and qcom,glink/adsp */
#define SMEM_GLOBAL             0xfffe
#define SMEM_CANARY             0xa5a5

struct smem_table_entry {
	uint32_t offset, size, flags;
	uint16_t host0, host1;
	uint32_t cacheline, reserved[7];
};
struct smem_table {
	uint8_t magic[4];
	uint32_t version, count, reserved[5];
};
struct smem_partition {
	uint8_t magic[4];
	uint16_t host0, host1;
	uint32_t size, free_uncached, free_cached, reserved[3];
};
struct smem_entry {
	uint16_t canary, item;
	uint32_t size;
	uint16_t padding_data, padding_header;
	uint32_t reserved;
};
struct smem_item {
	uint32_t item, offset, size;
};

/*
 * The DSP's items (dt: qcom,smem of qcom,smp2p-adsp, <443 429>: the item the DSP writes first, then
 * ours -- the Wi-Fi's <617 616> are in the same order; taken the other way round, the DSP made
 * our item its own and never said "up" --, and qcom,smem-id of qcom,lpass@3700000).
 */
#define ITEM_SMP2P_OURS         429
#define ITEM_SMP2P_THEIRS       443
#define ITEM_CRASH_REASON       423

static const volatile uint8_t *smem;

static bool
smem_peek(uint64_t offset, void *to, uint32_t size)
{
	if (smem == NULL) {
		smem = (const volatile uint8_t *)ml_io_map_unmappable(SMEM_PHYS, SMEM_SIZE, VM_WIMG_WCOMB);
	}
	if (offset + size > SMEM_SIZE) {
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
		((uint8_t *)to)[i] = smem[offset + i];
	}
	return true;
}

static void
smem_poke(uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
	wr((vm_offset_t)smem + offset, value);
}

static uint32_t
smem_word(uint32_t offset)
{
	return rd((vm_offset_t)smem + offset);
}

static uint32_t
smem_partition(uint16_t one, uint16_t other, uint32_t *cacheline, uint32_t *size)
{
	struct smem_table table;
	struct smem_table_entry entry;
	struct smem_partition header;

	if (!smem_peek(SMEM_SIZE - 0x1000, &table, sizeof(table)) || memcmp(table.magic, "$TOC", 4) != 0 || table.version != 1 ||
	    table.count > 64) {
		return 0;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < table.count; i++) {
		if (!smem_peek(SMEM_SIZE - 0x1000 + sizeof(table) + i * sizeof(entry), &entry, sizeof(entry)) || entry.offset == 0 ||
		    entry.size == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!((entry.host0 == one && entry.host1 == other) || (entry.host0 == other && entry.host1 == one))) {
			continue;
		}
		if ((uint64_t)entry.offset + entry.size > SMEM_SIZE - 0x1000 || !smem_peek(entry.offset, &header, sizeof(header)) ||
		    memcmp(header.magic, "$PRT", 4) != 0 || header.size != entry.size) {
			return 0;
		}
		*cacheline = entry.cacheline;
		*size = entry.size;
		return entry.offset;
	}
	return 0;
}

static unsigned
smem_items(uint32_t partition, uint32_t cacheline, struct smem_item *found, unsigned max)
{
	struct smem_partition header;
	struct smem_entry entry;
	uint32_t at, step_back;
	unsigned count = 0;

	if (partition == 0 || !smem_peek(partition, &header, sizeof(header)) || header.free_uncached > header.size ||
	    header.free_cached > header.size) {
		return 0;
	}
	for (at = sizeof(header); at + sizeof(entry) <= header.free_uncached;) {
		if (!smem_peek(partition + at, &entry, sizeof(entry)) || entry.canary != SMEM_CANARY || entry.size > header.size) {
			break;
		}
		/*
		 * The DSP can write this header: padding larger than the item would make the size below wrap to about 4 GB,
		 * and an item that ends beyond its partition would send the readers out of the shared memory. Stop at it.
		 */
		if (entry.padding_data > entry.size ||
		    (uint64_t)at + sizeof(entry) + entry.padding_header + entry.size > header.size) {
			break;
		}
		if (count < max) {
			found[count].item = entry.item;
			found[count].offset = partition + at + sizeof(entry) + entry.padding_header;
			found[count].size = entry.size - entry.padding_data;
		}
		count++;
		at += sizeof(entry) + entry.padding_header + entry.size;
	}
	if (cacheline == 0 || (cacheline & (cacheline - 1))) {
		return count;
	}
	step_back = ((uint32_t)sizeof(entry) + cacheline - 1) & ~(cacheline - 1);
	for (at = header.size - step_back; at > header.free_cached && at < header.size;) {
		/* (padding larger than the item would make the size below wrap to about 4 GB) */
		if (!smem_peek(partition + at, &entry, sizeof(entry)) || entry.canary != SMEM_CANARY || entry.size > at ||
		    entry.padding_data > entry.size) {
			break;
		}
		if (count < max) {
			found[count].item = entry.item;
			found[count].offset = partition + at - entry.size;
			found[count].size = entry.size - entry.padding_data;
		}
		count++;
		if (entry.size + step_back > at) {
			break;
		}
		at -= entry.size + step_back;
	}
	return count;
}

/* An item the DSP and we share: in the partition of the two, or else in the global one. Where it is; 0: nowhere. */
static uint32_t
smem_item(uint32_t item, uint32_t *size)
{
	static struct smem_item found[256];
	static const uint16_t hosts[2][2] = { { SMEM_US, SMEM_ADSP }, { SMEM_GLOBAL, SMEM_GLOBAL } };

	for (unsigned h = 0; h < 2; h++) {
		uint32_t cacheline = 0, partition_size = 0;
		uint32_t partition = smem_partition(hosts[h][0], hosts[h][1], &cacheline, &partition_size);
		unsigned count = smem_items(partition, cacheline, found, 256);

		for (unsigned i = 0; i < count && i < 256; i++) {
			if (found[i].item == item) {
				*size = found[i].size;
				return found[i].offset;
			}
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

static void
show_partition(void)
{
	static struct smem_item found[256];
	struct smem_partition header;
	uint32_t cacheline = 0, size = 0, partition = smem_partition(SMEM_US, SMEM_ADSP, &cacheline, &size);
	unsigned count;
	char line[320];

	if (partition == 0 || !smem_peek(partition, &header, sizeof(header))) {
		printf("adsp: %u: there is no partition for us and the audio DSP (0 and 2)\n", step);
		return;
	}
	count = smem_items(partition, cacheline, found, 256);
	printf("adsp: %u: the partition for us and the audio DSP (0 and 2): at %#lx, %#x bytes, of which %#x free; %u items\n", step,
	    SMEM_PHYS + partition, size, header.free_cached - header.free_uncached, count);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count && i < 256;) {
		int at = 0;

		for (unsigned n = 0; n < 12 && i < count && i < 256; n++, i++) {
			at += snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - (size_t)at, " %u (%u)", found[i].item, found[i].size);
		}
		printf("adsp: %u:   items (bytes):%s\n", step, line);
	}
}

/* ---- SMP2P ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

struct smp2p {
	uint32_t magic;
	uint32_t version;
	uint16_t local, remote, total, valid;
	uint32_t flags;
	struct {
		char name[16];
		uint32_t value;
	} entry[16];
};
#define SMP2P_MAGIC             0x504d5324
#define SMP2P_VERSION           1
#define SMP2P_RESTART_ACKS      1u
#define SMP2P_RESTART_DONE      (1u << 0)
#define SMP2P_RESTART_ACK       (1u << 1)
#define SMP2P_AT_VERSION        4
#define SMP2P_AT_PROCESSORS     8
#define SMP2P_AT_COUNTS         12
#define SMP2P_AT_FLAGS          16
#define SMP2P_AT_NAME(i)        (20 + 20 * (i))
#define SMP2P_AT_VALUE(i)       (36 + 20 * (i))

/* The bits of the DSP's entry "slave-kernel" (dt: the interrupts of qcom,lpass@3700000). */
#define DSP_FATAL               (1u << 0)
#define DSP_READY               (1u << 1)
#define DSP_HANDOVER            (1u << 2)
#define DSP_STOP_ACK            (1u << 3)
#define DSP_SHUTDOWN_ACK        (1u << 7)

/* Our entry (dt: the child "master-kernel" of qcom,smp2p-adsp; "qcom,force-stop" of qcom,lpass@3700000). */
#define OUR_ENTRY_STOP          "master-kernel"
#define DSP_STOP                (1u << 0)

static bool
dsp_words(struct smp2p *words)
{
	static uint32_t at;
	uint32_t size = 0;

	if (at == 0) {
		at = smem_item(ITEM_SMP2P_THEIRS, &size);
		if (at == 0 || size < sizeof(*words)) {
			at = 0;
			return false;
		}
	}
	return smem_peek(at, words, sizeof(*words)) && words->magic == SMP2P_MAGIC;
}

static int
smp2p_entry(const struct smp2p *words, const char *name)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < words->valid && i < 16; i++) {
		if (strncmp(words->entry[i].name, name, sizeof(words->entry[i].name)) == 0) {
			return (int)i;
		}
	}
	return -1;
}

static uint32_t
dsp_state(const struct smp2p *words)
{
	int entry = smp2p_entry(words, "slave-kernel");

	return entry < 0 ? 0 : words->entry[entry].value;
}

static void
show_words(const char *prefix, const struct smp2p *words)
{
	char line[320];
	int at = 0;

	line[0] = 0;
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < words->valid && i < 16 && at < (int)sizeof(line) - 40; i++) {
		at += snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - (size_t)at, " %.16s = %#x;", words->entry[i].name, words->entry[i].value);
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: %s: SMP2P version %u, features %#x, from processor %u to %u, flags %#x, %u of %u entries:%s\n", step, prefix,
	    words->version & 0xff, words->version >> 8, words->local, words->remote, words->flags, words->valid, words->total, line);
}

static void
show_crash_reason(void)
{
	char text[81];
	uint32_t size = 0, at = smem_item(ITEM_CRASH_REASON, &size);

	if (at == 0 || size == 0) {
		printf("adsp: %u: item %u, the DSP's last words: not there\n", step, ITEM_CRASH_REASON);
		return;
	}
	bzero(text, sizeof(text));
	smem_peek(at, text, size < sizeof(text) - 1 ? size : sizeof(text) - 1);
	if (text[0] == 0) {
		printf("adsp: %u: item %u, the DSP's last words (%u bytes): none\n", step, ITEM_CRASH_REASON, size);
	} else {
		printf("adsp: %u: THE AUDIO DSP'S LAST WORDS (item %u, %u bytes): \"%s\"\n", step, ITEM_CRASH_REASON, size, text);
	}
}

/* ---- the doorbells, and the mailbox to the always-on processor (hakios.wifi.c, steps 2 and 7) ------ */

#define QMP_MAGIC               0x00
#define QMP_MAGIC_VALUE         0x4d41494c
#define QMP_VERSION             0x04
#define QMP_THEIR_LINK          0x0c
#define QMP_THEIR_LINK_ACK      0x10
#define QMP_THEIR_CHANNEL       0x14
#define QMP_THEIR_CHANNEL_ACK   0x18
#define QMP_OUR_LINK            0x24
#define QMP_OUR_LINK_ACK        0x28
#define QMP_OUR_CHANNEL         0x2c
#define QMP_OUR_CHANNEL_ACK     0x30
#define QMP_OUR_BOX_SIZE        0x34
#define QMP_OUR_BOX             0x38
#define QMP_UP                  0x0000ffffu
#define QMP_DOWN                0xffff0000u
#define QMP_MESSAGE             64

static struct block aoss = { "mailbox", 0x0c300000, 0x400 };

#define IPCC_SEND               0x0c
#define IPCC_RECEIVED           0x10
#define IPCC_ENABLE             0x14
#define IPCC_DISABLE            0x18
#define IPCC_CLEAR              0x1c
#define IPCC_NOBODY             0xffffffffu
#define IPCC_AOP                0u
#define IPCC_LPASS              3u              /* dt: mboxes of qcom,smp2p-adsp and qcom,glink/adsp */
#define IPCC_GLINK              0u
#define IPCC_SMP2P              2u

static struct block ipcc = { "ipcc", 0x00408000, 0x1000 };

static struct {
	uint32_t glink, smp2p, said;
	uint64_t since;
} doorbell;

/*
 * The audio DSP's rings, counted and cleared. Another's ring (the Wi-Fi DSP's, the always-on
 * processor's) is left for whoever listens for it: IPCC names the same one until it is cleared,
 * so the look ends there.
 */
static void
doorbells(void)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
		uint32_t who = rd(ipcc.base + IPCC_RECEIVED);

		if (who == IPCC_NOBODY || who >> 16 != IPCC_LPASS) {
			return;
		}
		wr(ipcc.base + IPCC_CLEAR, who);
		doorbell.glink += (who & 0xffff) == IPCC_GLINK;
		doorbell.smp2p += (who & 0xffff) == IPCC_SMP2P;
		if (doorbell.said < 24) {
			uint64_t now = now_us() - doorbell.since;

			doorbell.said++;
			printf("adsp: doorbell: +%llu.%03llu ms: signal %u of the audio DSP; heard and cleared\n", now / 1000, now % 1000,
			    who & 0xffff);
		}
	}
}

static uint32_t our_box;                /* where in the message memory our mailbox is; 0: not open */

static bool
mailbox_wait(uint32_t offset, uint32_t value, uint32_t ms)
{
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < ms * 10; i++) {
		if (rd(aoss.base + offset) == value) {
			return true;
		}
		sleep_us(100);
	}
	return rd(aoss.base + offset) == value;
}

static void
ring_aop(void)
{
	wr(ipcc.base + IPCC_SEND, IPCC_AOP << 16 | 0);
}

/* Linux's qmp_open(), as hakios.wifi.c does it; what is done already is found done. Under the mailbox's lock. */
static bool
mailbox_open(void)
{
	uint32_t box, size;

	need(&aoss);
	need(&ipcc);
	if (get(&aoss, "magic", QMP_MAGIC) != QMP_MAGIC_VALUE || get(&aoss, "version", QMP_VERSION) != 1) {
		printf("adsp: %u: not a mailbox this knows\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	box = get(&aoss, "our mailbox", QMP_OUR_BOX);
	size = get(&aoss, "our mailbox's size", QMP_OUR_BOX_SIZE);
	/* (box and size come from the always-on processor: "box + size" could wrap in 32 bits and pass, so it is compared as a difference) */
	if (size < QMP_MESSAGE + 4 || box < 0x3c || box >= aoss.size || size > aoss.size - box || (box & 3)) {
		printf("adsp: %u: our mailbox is not where a message fits\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	if (rd(aoss.base + QMP_OUR_LINK) == QMP_UP && rd(aoss.base + QMP_OUR_LINK_ACK) == QMP_UP &&
	    rd(aoss.base + QMP_OUR_CHANNEL) == QMP_UP && rd(aoss.base + QMP_THEIR_CHANNEL) == QMP_UP &&
	    rd(aoss.base + QMP_OUR_CHANNEL_ACK) == QMP_UP) {
		printf("adsp: %u: the mailbox is open already (the Wi-Fi's start, or a kernel before this one, opened it)\n", step);
		our_box = box;
		return true;
	}
	put(&aoss, "their link, seen by us", QMP_THEIR_LINK_ACK, rd(aoss.base + QMP_THEIR_LINK));
	put(&aoss, "our link", QMP_OUR_LINK, QMP_UP);
	ring_aop();
	if (!mailbox_wait(QMP_OUR_LINK_ACK, QMP_UP, 1000)) {
		printf("adsp: %u: THE ALWAYS-ON PROCESSOR DOES NOT ACKNOWLEDGE OUR LINK within a second; taken down again\n", step);
		put(&aoss, "our link", QMP_OUR_LINK, QMP_DOWN);
		ring_aop();
		return false;
	}
	put(&aoss, "our channel", QMP_OUR_CHANNEL, QMP_UP);
	ring_aop();
	if (!mailbox_wait(QMP_THEIR_CHANNEL, QMP_UP, 1000)) {
		printf("adsp: %u: THE ALWAYS-ON PROCESSOR DOES NOT OPEN ITS CHANNEL within a second; ours is taken down again\n", step);
		put(&aoss, "our channel", QMP_OUR_CHANNEL, QMP_DOWN);
		put(&aoss, "our link", QMP_OUR_LINK, QMP_DOWN);
		ring_aop();
		return false;
	}
	put(&aoss, "their channel, seen by us", QMP_THEIR_CHANNEL_ACK, QMP_UP);
	ring_aop();
	if (!mailbox_wait(QMP_OUR_CHANNEL_ACK, QMP_UP, 1000)) {
		printf("adsp: %u: THE ALWAYS-ON PROCESSOR DOES NOT ACKNOWLEDGE OUR CHANNEL within a second; taken down again\n", step);
		put(&aoss, "our channel", QMP_OUR_CHANNEL, QMP_DOWN);
		put(&aoss, "our link", QMP_OUR_LINK, QMP_DOWN);
		ring_aop();
		return false;
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: THE MAILBOX TO THE ALWAYS-ON PROCESSOR IS OPEN\n", step);
	our_box = box;
	return true;
}

/* A message to the always-on processor (Linux's qmp_send()), under the lock the Wi-Fi's start takes too. */
static bool
mailbox_send(const char *text)
{
	uint32_t words[QMP_MESSAGE / 4] = { 0 };
	bool sent = false;

	if (!leaving) {
		lck_mtx_lock(&hakios_aop_mailbox_lock);
	}
	if (our_box == 0 && (leaving || !mailbox_open())) {
		goto out;
	}
	strlcpy((char *)words, text, sizeof(words));
	printf("adsp: %u: about to tell the always-on processor \"%s\"\n", step, text);
	snprintf(last_write, sizeof(last_write), "step %u sent the always-on processor a message", step);
	if (rd(aoss.base + our_box) != 0) {
		printf("adsp: %u: our mailbox still holds a message of %u bytes: not sent\n", step, rd(aoss.base + our_box));
		goto out;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < QMP_MESSAGE / 4; i++) {
		wr(aoss.base + our_box + 4 + 4 * i, words[i]);
	}
	wr(aoss.base + our_box, QMP_MESSAGE);
	(void)rd(aoss.base + our_box);
	ring_aop();
	if (!mailbox_wait(our_box, 0, 1000)) {
		printf("adsp: %u: THE ALWAYS-ON PROCESSOR DOES NOT TAKE THE MESSAGE within a second; it is taken back\n", step);
		wr(aoss.base + our_box, 0);
		goto out;
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: the always-on processor has taken it\n", step);
	sent = true;
out:
	if (!leaving) {
		lck_mtx_unlock(&hakios_aop_mailbox_lock);
	}
	return sent;
}

/* ---- RPMh: the DSP's two rails, asked for while it boots ------------------------------------------------ */

/*
 * The audio DSP's logic and memories run from LPASS's own rails, LCX and LMX (dt: vdd_cx and
 * vdd_mx of qcom,lpass@3700000 are PM7325 L5 and L4 "level" regulators, RPMh resources lcx.lvl and
 * lmx.lvl), which the boot loader leaves at retention (16). Linux and Android ask for level 384
 * while the DSP boots, until it says it has asked for its own (bit 2, "proxy-unvote"); without it
 * the DSP rang once and left "SFR Init: wdog or kernel error suspected." in its last words.
 *
 * A request goes to RPMh through the application processor's sequencer (dt: rsc@18200000, DRV 2,
 * qcom,tcs-offset 0xd00, qcom,tcs-config: TCSs 0 and 1 are for requests made at once), as Linux's
 * rpmh-rsc.c writes one: the command's message id, address and value into a TCS that is idle, the
 * command enabled and marked to be waited for, the TCS put in "active" mode and triggered, and its
 * bit in the status of completions looked for. A rail asked for by level is asked by position in
 * the list of its levels that the boot loader's command database keeps (cmd-db.c), the first
 * position at or above the level wanted.
 */
#define CMD_DB_PHYS             0x80860000UL
#define CMD_DB_SIZE             0x20000UL

struct cmd_db_slave {
	uint16_t id, header_offset, data_offset, count, version, reserved[3];
};
struct cmd_db_header {
	uint32_t version;
	uint8_t magic[4];
	struct cmd_db_slave slave[8];
	uint32_t checksum, reserved;
	uint8_t data[];
};
struct cmd_db_entry {
	char id[8];
	uint32_t priority[2];
	uint32_t address;
	uint16_t length, offset;
};

static const struct cmd_db_header *cmd_db;

static struct block rsc = { "rsc", 0x18220000, 0x10000 };
#define RSC_TCS_BASE            0xd00
#define RSC_IRQ_STATUS          (RSC_TCS_BASE + 0x04)   /* a bit per TCS: done */
#define RSC_IRQ_CLEAR           (RSC_TCS_BASE + 0x08)
#define RSC_TCS(n)              (RSC_TCS_BASE + 672 * (n))
#define TCS_WAIT_FOR_DONE       0x10
#define TCS_CONTROL             0x14
#define TCS_STATUS              0x18                    /* not zero: idle */
#define TCS_ENABLED             0x1c
#define TCS_COMMAND(c)          (0x30 + 20 * (c))       /* message id, address, value, status */
#define TCS_ACTIVE_MODE         (1u << 16)
#define TCS_TRIGGER             (1u << 24)
#define MSGID_WRITE_WAITED      (8u | 1u << 8 | 1u << 16)       /* four bytes, an answer wanted, a write */
#define RPMH_TCS                0                       /* the first of the two for requests made at once */

/* The level position RPMh takes for that rail and level; -1: not found. */
static int
rail_position(const char *name, uint32_t level, uint32_t *address)
{
	char id[8] = { 0 };

	if (cmd_db == NULL) {
		cmd_db = (const struct cmd_db_header *)ml_io_map_unmappable(CMD_DB_PHYS, CMD_DB_SIZE, VM_WIMG_WCOMB);
	}
	if (!(cmd_db->magic[0] == 0xdb && cmd_db->magic[1] == 0x30 && cmd_db->magic[2] == 0x03 && cmd_db->magic[3] == 0x0c)) {
		printf("adsp: %u: the boot loader's command database is not there\n", step);
		return -1;
	}
	strlcpy(id, name, sizeof(id));
	for (unsigned s = 0; s < 8; s++) {
		const struct cmd_db_slave *slave = &cmd_db->slave[s];
		const struct cmd_db_entry *entry = (const struct cmd_db_entry *)(cmd_db->data + slave->header_offset);

		if (slave->id == 0 || slave->count > 512) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < slave->count; i++) {
			const uint8_t *data;
			char levels[160];
			int at;

			if (memcmp(entry[i].id, id, sizeof(id)) != 0) {
				continue;
			}
			if ((unsigned)slave->data_offset + entry[i].offset + entry[i].length > CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000) {
				return -1;
			}
			data = cmd_db->data + slave->data_offset + entry[i].offset;
			at = snprintf(levels, sizeof(levels), "%s at %#x, levels:", name, entry[i].address);
			for (unsigned l = 0; l < entry[i].length / 2u && l < 16; l++) {
				unsigned value = data[2 * l] | data[2 * l + 1] << 8;

				if (l > 0 && value == 0) {
					break;
				}
				at += snprintf(levels + at, sizeof(levels) - (size_t)at, " %u", value);
			}
			printf("adsp: %u: RPMh has %s\n", step, levels);
			for (unsigned l = 0; l < entry[i].length / 2u && l < 16; l++) {
				if ((uint32_t)(data[2 * l] | data[2 * l + 1] << 8) >= level) {
					*address = entry[i].address;
					return (int)l;
				}
			}
			return -1;
		}
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: RPMh has no \"%s\"\n", step, name);
	return -1;
}

/* The two rails at that level (Linux's proxy request), or given back (level 0). True: RPMh has said done. */
static bool
rails(uint32_t level)
{
	static const char *const names[2] = { "lcx.lvl", "lmx.lvl" };
	uint32_t addresses[2] = { 0, 0 }, values[2] = { 0, 0 }, done = 0;
	uint64_t began;

	for (unsigned r = 0; r < 2; r++) {
		int position = level == 0 ? 0 : rail_position(names[r], level, &addresses[r]);

		if (level == 0) {
			rail_position(names[r], 0, &addresses[r]);
		}
		if (position < 0 || addresses[r] == 0) {
			printf("adsp: %u: no position for %s at level %u: the rails are not asked\n", step, names[r], level);
			return false;
		}
		values[r] = (uint32_t)position;
	}
	need(&rsc);
	/* (on a panic's way back to the loader no lock is taken: the other processors are stopped, and one of them may hold this one for good) */
	if (!leaving) {
		lck_mtx_lock(&hakios_rsc_lock);
	}
	/* (the boot loader leaves the trigger set after its last request, done: idle is what the status says) */
	if (rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_STATUS) == 0) {
		printf("adsp: %u: TCS %u of the sequencer is busy (status %#x, control %#x): the rails are not asked\n", step, RPMH_TCS,
		    rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_STATUS), rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL));
		if (!leaving) {
			lck_mtx_unlock(&hakios_rsc_lock);
		}
		return false;
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: about to ask RPMh, through TCS %u, for lcx.lvl (%#x) = %u and lmx.lvl (%#x) = %u (level %u%s)\n", step,
	    RPMH_TCS, addresses[0], values[0], addresses[1], values[1], level, level == 0 ? ": given back" : "");
	snprintf(last_write, sizeof(last_write), "step %u asked RPMh for the audio DSP's rails at level %u", step, level);
	hold();
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_IRQ_CLEAR, 1u << RPMH_TCS);
	for (unsigned r = 0; r < 2; r++) {
		wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_COMMAND(r), MSGID_WRITE_WAITED);
		wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_COMMAND(r) + 4, addresses[r]);
		wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_COMMAND(r) + 8, values[r]);
	}
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_WAIT_FOR_DONE, 3);
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_ENABLED, 3);
	settle();
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL, rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL) & ~TCS_TRIGGER);
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL, rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL) | TCS_ACTIVE_MODE);
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL, rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL) | TCS_TRIGGER);
	began = now_us();
	while (now_us() - began < 100000) {
		done = rd(rsc.base + RSC_IRQ_STATUS) & (1u << RPMH_TCS);
		if (done) {
			break;
		}
		sleep_us(50);
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: RPMh %s after %llu us; the commands' status %#x %#x, the TCS's %#x\n", step, done ? "HAS DONE IT" :
	    "HAS NOT SAID DONE", now_us() - began, rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_COMMAND(0) + 12),
	    rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_COMMAND(1) + 12), rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_STATUS));
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_IRQ_CLEAR, 1u << RPMH_TCS);
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL, rd(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_CONTROL) & ~(TCS_TRIGGER | TCS_ACTIVE_MODE));
	wr(rsc.base + RSC_TCS(RPMH_TCS) + TCS_ENABLED, 0);
	if (!leaving) {
		lck_mtx_unlock(&hakios_rsc_lock);
	}
	return done != 0;
}

/* ---- step 1: the shared memory --------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static bool
step_survey(void)
{
	struct smp2p words;
	uint32_t size = 0;

	announce("read our partition with the audio DSP in the shared memory (0x80900000), and its items");
	show_partition();
	if (dsp_words(&words)) {
		show_words("the DSP's item (443) is there: it has run since the phone was started", &words);
	} else {
		printf("adsp: %u: the DSP's SMP2P item (443) is not there: it has not run since the phone was started\n", step);
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: our SMP2P item (429): %s; GLINK's descriptor (478): %s, our queue (479): %s, the DSP's (480): %s\n", step,
	    smem_item(ITEM_SMP2P_OURS, &size) ? "there" : "not there", smem_item(478, &size) ? "there" : "NOT THERE",
	    smem_item(479, &size) ? "there" : "NOT THERE", smem_item(480, &size) ? "there" : "not there (the DSP makes it)");
	show_crash_reason();
	need(&ipcc);
	printf("adsp: %u: the doorbells say %#x\n", step, rd(ipcc.base + IPCC_RECEIVED));
	return smem_partition(SMEM_US, SMEM_ADSP, &size, &size) != 0;
}

/* ---- step 2: the firmware -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define ADSP_MEMORY             0x86700000u     /* dt: reserved-memory adsp@86700000, memory-region of qcom,lpass@3700000 */
#define ADSP_MEMORY_SIZE        0x04000000u
#define PAS_ADSP                1               /* dt: qcom,pas-id */


/*
 * A file of /fw on the root file system, read whole into memory of ours: the system image, where
 * userland/build.sh puts fw-audio/ when it makes that image. It is compressed there, which the file
 * system undoes and the reading of the small image's memory below does not; and it is there only
 * once the root is mounted, so only adsp=1, which waits for that on its own thread, finds it so.
 */
static const uint8_t *
root_file(const char *name, uint64_t *size)
{
	char path[64];
	vfs_context_t context = vfs_context_kernel();
	vnode_t vnode = NULLVP;
	struct vnode_attr attributes;
	uint8_t *data;
	int left = 0, error;

	if (rootvnode == NULLVP) {
		return NULL;
	}
	snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/fw/%s", name);
	if (vnode_lookup(path, 0, &vnode, context) != 0) {
		return NULL;
	}
	VATTR_INIT(&attributes);
	VATTR_WANTED(&attributes, va_data_size);
	if (vnode_getattr(vnode, &attributes, context) != 0 || attributes.va_data_size == 0 ||
	    attributes.va_data_size > ADSP_MEMORY_SIZE) {
		vnode_put(vnode);
		return NULL;
	}
	data = kalloc_data(attributes.va_data_size, Z_WAITOK);
	if (data == NULL) {
		vnode_put(vnode);
		return NULL;
	}
	error = vn_rdwr(UIO_READ, vnode, (caddr_t)data, (int)attributes.va_data_size, 0, UIO_SYSSPACE, 0,
	    vfs_context_ucred(context), &left, vfs_context_proc(context));
	vnode_put(vnode);
	if (error != 0 || left != 0) {
		printf("adsp: %u: %s: read error %d, %d bytes left\n", step, path, error, left);
		kfree_data(data, attributes.va_data_size);
		return NULL;
	}
	*size = attributes.va_data_size;
	return data;
}

static bool from_root;                  /* the image is in memory of ours (root_file()), to be given back once written */

/* For the sound (hakios.sound.c): a file of /fw on the root, read whole into memory of ours, and given back. */
const uint8_t *
hakios_adsp_fw_file(const char *name, uint64_t *size)
{
	return root_file(name, size);
}

void
hakios_adsp_fw_free(const uint8_t *data, uint64_t size)
{
	uint8_t *ours = __DECONST(uint8_t *, data);

	kfree_data(ours, size);
}

/* A file of fw/ in the small image (ADSP=1 userland/build.sh puts fw-audio/ there), else of /fw on the root (above). */
extern const uint8_t *hakios_image_file(const char *dir, const char *name, uint64_t *size, int *disk_out);
static const uint8_t *
image_file(const char *name, uint64_t *size)
{
	{
		const uint8_t *data = hakios_image_file("fw", name, size, NULL);  /* (hakios.image.c) */

		if (data != NULL) {
			return data;
		}
	}
	{
		const uint8_t *data = root_file(name, size);

		if (data != NULL) {
			from_root = true;
			return data;
		}
	}
	printf("adsp: %u: no fw/%s in the small image nor on the root: put the phone's /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/%s into "
	    "fw-audio/ and run SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh (or ADSP=1, for the small image)\n", step, name, name);
	return NULL;
}


#define MDT_HASH(flags)         (((flags) >> 24 & 7) == 2)
#define MAX_SEGMENTS            48

struct elf_segment {
	uint32_t type, offset, vaddr, paddr, file_size, memory_size, flags, align;
};

static struct {
	const uint8_t *header;
	uint64_t header_size;
	struct {
		uint32_t at;
		uint32_t file_size, memory_size;
		const uint8_t *file;
	} segment[MAX_SEGMENTS];
	unsigned segments;
	uint32_t size;
} image;

/* The image's files given back, if they were read into memory of ours. */
static void
image_forget(void)
{
	if (!from_root) {
		return;
	}
	if (image.header != NULL) {
		void *data = (void *)(uintptr_t)image.header;

		kfree_data(data, image.header_size);
	}
	for (unsigned s = 0; s < image.segments; s++) {
		if (image.segment[s].file != NULL) {
			void *data = (void *)(uintptr_t)image.segment[s].file;

			kfree_data(data, image.segment[s].file_size);
		}
	}
	bzero(&image, sizeof(image));
	from_root = false;
}

static bool
step_firmware(void)
{
	struct elf_segment segment;
	const uint8_t *header;
	uint64_t size = 0, files = 0;
	uint32_t count, hashes = 0, lowest = ~0u, highest = 0;
	uint8_t first[4] = { 0 };

	announce("find the audio DSP's image in the small image or on the root, and check it against its own header");
	image_forget();
	image.segments = 0;
	header = image_file("adsp.mdt", &size);
	if (header == NULL) {
		return false;
	}
	image.header = header;
	image.header_size = size;
	count = size >= 52 + 2 * 32 ? header[44] | header[45] << 8 : 0;
	/* (a file of 1 to 4 bytes is shorter than what is compared and printed: both look only at what is there) */
	memcpy(first, header, size < sizeof(first) ? size : sizeof(first));
	if (size < 5 || memcmp(header, "\177ELF\1", 5) != 0 || count < 3 || count > MAX_SEGMENTS || 52 + 32 * count > size ||
	    size > PAGE_SIZE) {
		printf("adsp: %u: fw/adsp.mdt is not such a header (%02x %02x %02x %02x, %u segments, %llu bytes)\n", step, first[0],
		    first[1], first[2], first[3], count, size);
		goto fail;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		char name[16];

		memcpy(&segment, header + 52 + 32 * i, sizeof(segment));
		if (MDT_HASH(segment.flags)) {
			hashes = segment.file_size;
		}
		if (segment.type != 1 || MDT_HASH(segment.flags) || segment.memory_size == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (segment.paddr < ADSP_MEMORY || segment.file_size > segment.memory_size ||
		    (uint64_t)segment.paddr + segment.memory_size > (uint64_t)ADSP_MEMORY + ADSP_MEMORY_SIZE) {
			printf("adsp: %u: segment %u (%#x, %#x bytes) is not within the DSP's memory\n", step, i, segment.paddr,
			    segment.memory_size);
			goto fail;
		}
		image.segment[image.segments].at = segment.paddr - ADSP_MEMORY;
		image.segment[image.segments].file_size = segment.file_size;
		image.segment[image.segments].memory_size = segment.memory_size;
		image.segment[image.segments].file = NULL;
		if (segment.file_size != 0) {
			uint64_t file_size = 0;
