```c
		}
	}
	/* (the amplifiers are faded in before the tone begins: they fade in on silence, and the tone starts at that level) */
	if (level >= 3 && !hakios_speaker_volume(below, 50)) {
		goto out;
	}
	if (level >= 3) {
		say("sound: THE TONE PLAYS NOW for %u s: 1 kHz at -20 dBFS, both speakers, %u.%03u dB under Android's level\n",
		    seconds, below / 8, below % 8 * 125);
	}
	say_when("the tone begins");
	ok = play(seconds * 1000, level >= 3);
	say_when("the tone has ended");
	space_faults();
out:
	if (acf != NULL) {
		hakios_adsp_fw_free(acf, acf_size);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sound_lock);
	take_down();
	say("sound: %s; last: %s\n", ok ? "LEVEL DONE" : "STOPPED SHORT", last_write);
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
hakios_sound_dsp_up(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("sound", &level, sizeof(level)) || level == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (level > 4) {
		level = 4;
	}
	PE_parse_boot_argn("sound_secs", &seconds, sizeof(seconds));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("sound_below", &below, sizeof(below));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("sound_pause", &pause_ms, sizeof(pause_ms));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("sound_guard_as", &guard_as, sizeof(guard_as));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("sound_gain", &gain, sizeof(gain));
	if (gain > HAKIOS_GUARD_MAX_GAIN) {
		gain = HAKIOS_GUARD_MAX_GAIN;
	}
	hakios_guard_configure(true, gain);
	if (level >= 2 && level <= 3 && seconds > 3) {
		seconds = 3;            /* the test tone: three seconds at most */
	}
	running = true;
	if (kernel_thread_start(sound_thread, NULL, &thread) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		running = false;
		say("sound: no thread\n");
		return;
	}
	thread_deallocate(thread);
}

void
hakios_sound_dsp_down(void)
{
	if (running) {
		take_down();
	}
}

void
hakios_sound_quiesce(void)
{
	hakios_speaker_quiesce();
}

```

`drivers/audio/hakios.speaker.c`:

```c
/*
 * The speakers of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): their two amplifiers. Every address below belongs
 * to this phone, and nothing here is touched unless a boot-arg asks for it.
 *
 * Each speaker has an amplifier of its own, an Awinic AW88261 (chip ID 0x2113, a "smart PA"),
 * set up over I2C -- the bus of the SoC's serial engine 3, GPIO 12 data and 13 clock, on which
 * Android's device tree and its running kernel have these two and nothing else -- and fed by
 * the SoC's first TDM interface ("MI2S 0": GPIO 97 bit clock, 100 frame sync, 99 data out),
 * which the audio DSP drives (hakios.sound.c). In Android's tree the amplifier at 0x35 is
 * "sound-channel 0" and takes slot 0 of the frame (the left channel), the one at 0x34 is
 * channel 1 and takes slot 1; neither has a reset pin.
 *
 * Two uses:
 *
 *   speaker_probe=1    reads registers and nothing else: the pins, the power names (below)
 *   speaker_probe=2    ... and asks the amplifiers who they are (I2C, below)
 *
 *   hakios_speaker_prepare() and the rest (sys/hakios.audio.h), for boot-arg sound=3 of
 *   hakios.sound.c: the amplifiers set up and run exactly as Android's own driver does it
 *   (Xiaomi's hakios-s-oss kernel, techpack/audio/asoc/codecs/aw88263s_m20: aw882xx_device.c,
 *   aw882xx_init.c and aw882xx_pid_2113_reg.h; the phone runs its version 2.0.0), with the
 *   registers' values from Android's own configuration file -- /vendor/etc/aw882xx_acf.bin of
 *   the phone, which userland/build.sh puts into /fw of the system image from fw-audio/ and
 *   which is not in this repository. Its "Music" profile is what Android plays the speakers
 *   with (tinymix: aw_dev_0_prof, aw_dev_1_prof); 55 of its 57 registers read back from the
 *   idle chips under Android exactly as the file has them, and the other two as the driver
 *   leaves them (0x04 powered down and muted, 0x08 with the feedback off).
 *
 * What the driver does and this does the same way, per amplifier:
 *
 *   prepare  reads the chip ID and the four fuse registers; a soft reset (0x55aa into
 *            register 0); the profile's registers, every one but three as the file has them:
 *            0x04 keeps the power-down, amplifier power-down and mute bits as they are and
 *            sets the mute of the power stage ("ULS"), 0x08 has the feedback off, and 0x05 (the
 *            volume) is turned down to the lowest, -90 dB, right after; 0x50 gets the value the
 *            driver works out from the fuses (8192 * (1000 + icalk) / (1000 + vcalk)), which for
 *            this phone's two chips is the value Android left in them
 *   start    only while the TDM clock runs: power-down off, 2 ms, the PLL locked (status bits 0
 *            and 4); amplifier power-down off, 1 ms, the status as the driver wants it (bits 0, 4,
 *            8, 9); the feedback on; the two mutes off; the interrupts read away; the volume
 *            stays at the lowest
 *   volume   stepwise, 6 dB a step (the driver takes one every 100 us), to `below' eighths of a dB
 *            under Android's own level (the profile's 0x05, -2.1 dB, with Android's
 *            aw_dev_N_volume 0) and never above it
 *   stop     the power stage muted, the volume stepped down to the lowest, muted, the feedback
 *            off, 1 ms, amplifier power-down, power-down
 *
 * Every write is said in the log and read back; a value that does not read back as written, a
 * byte nobody acknowledges, or a fault in the status register (under-voltage, over-current of
 * the boost or the output, over-temperature, no clock, the watchdog, over-voltage) has both
 * amplifiers powered down at once (amplifier power-down and power-down, bits 1 and 0 of 0x04)
 * and nothing more done. What is not done, compared with Android: the DSP's Awinic algorithm,
 * which protects the speakers with their calibration (aw882xx_rx_switch); in its place the
 * samples go through hakios.guard.c on their way here. The driver's monitor is done
 * (hakios_speaker_monitor(), below): once a second the chips' temperature and the battery's
 * voltage, and the reduction that the file's table asks for at either.
 *
 * I2C is done by hand: a pin is either pulled low or let go (and the pull-ups raise it), at 100
 * kHz at most. For each register read or written the two pins are taken from the serial engine
 * (function qup03) as GPIOs and given back as they were found right after.
 *
 * Register layouts: the files above, and Linux's sound/soc/codecs/aw88261.c; pins:
 * drivers/pinctrl/qcom/pinctrl-yupik.c of the same kernel and the phone's own device tree.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/hakios.audio.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map_wcomb(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static vm_offset_t tlmm, gcc, cmd_db;
static uint32_t probe_level;
static bool leaving;                    /* on a panic's way out: nothing sleeps, nothing is said but to the loader */

/* Every line to the loader's log as well: what is written to the amplifiers should be known even if the kernel dies. */
static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (!leaving) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
	return length;
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

/* Waits without sleeping (also with interrupts off, on a panic's way out). */
static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static void
wait_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	if (leaving) {
		spin_us(ms * 1000);
	} else {
		delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

/* ---- pins ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define TLMM_PHYS               0x0f100000UL
#define TLMM_SIZE               0x100000UL
#define GPIO_CFG(n)             (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n))         /* [1:0] pull, [5:2] function, [8:6] drive, [9] output */
#define GPIO_IO(n)              (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n) + 4)     /* bit 0 in, bit 1 out */
#define CFG_PULL_UP             3
#define CFG_OUTPUT              (1u << 9)

#define PIN_SDA                 12      /* the serial engine's first pin is the data line, the second the clock */
#define PIN_SCL                 13

static const struct {
	unsigned pin;
	const char *what;
} pins[] = {
	{ 12, "I2C data" }, { 13, "I2C clock" }, { 97, "MI2S 0 bit clock" }, { 100, "MI2S 0 word select" },
	{ 98, "MI2S 0 data 0" }, { 99, "MI2S 0 data 1" }, { 102, "the amplifier 0x35's interrupt" },
	{ 45, "the amplifier 0x34's interrupt" },
};

static void
show_pins(void)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(pins) / sizeof(pins[0]); i++) {
		uint32_t cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(pins[i].pin)), io = rd(GPIO_IO(pins[i].pin));

		say("speaker: gpio%u (%s): function %u, pull %u, %u mA, %s, reads %u\n", pins[i].pin, pins[i].what,
		    (cfg >> 2) & 15, cfg & 3, (((cfg >> 6) & 7) + 1) * 2, (cfg & CFG_OUTPUT) ? (io & 2 ? "drives high" : "drives low") :
		    "input", io & 1);
	}
}

/* ---- I2C by hand ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
half_bit(void)
{
	spin_us(5);                     /* 100 kHz at most, I2C's standard mode; the bus does not mind slower */
}

/* A line is pulled low (the pin drives 0) or let go (the pin is an input and the pull-up raises it). */
static void
line(unsigned pin, bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(pin), 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(pin), CFG_PULL_UP | (high ? 0 : CFG_OUTPUT));
}

static bool
level(unsigned pin)
{
	return rd(GPIO_IO(pin)) & 1;
}

static void
i2c_start(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	half_bit();
}

static void
i2c_stop(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	half_bit();
}

/* One bit out (the other side's bit in, if we let the data line go): the clock goes up and down once. */
static bool
i2c_bit(bool out)
{
	bool in;

	line(PIN_SDA, out);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	for (unsigned stretched = 0; !level(PIN_SCL) && stretched < 100; stretched++) {
		half_bit();             /* (a device may hold the clock low until it is ready) */
	}
	half_bit();
	in = level(PIN_SDA);
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	return in;
}

/* Returns true if the byte was acknowledged. */
static bool
i2c_write(uint8_t byte)
{
	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		i2c_bit((byte >> bit) & 1);
	}
	return !i2c_bit(true);
}

static uint8_t
i2c_read(bool more)
{
	uint8_t byte = 0;

	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		byte = (uint8_t)(byte << 1 | i2c_bit(true));
	}
	i2c_bit(!more);                 /* acknowledge all but the last byte */
	return byte;
}

/*
 * The two pins taken from the serial engine for one transaction, and given back as found. False
 * if the bus is not at rest: then nothing is driven.
 */
static uint32_t taken_cfg[2], taken_io[2];

static bool
bus_take(void)
{
	taken_cfg[0] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA));
	taken_cfg[1] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL));
	taken_io[0] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA));
	taken_io[1] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL));
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	if (!level(PIN_SDA) || !level(PIN_SCL)) {
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static void
bus_give_back(void)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
}

/* A 16-bit register of an Awinic amplifier, most significant byte first. Returns false if nobody answers. */
static bool
register_read(uint8_t address, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *value)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		say("speaker: the I2C bus is not at rest (gpio%u reads %u, gpio%u reads %u): not touched\n", PIN_SDA,
		    level(PIN_SDA), PIN_SCL, level(PIN_SCL));
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write((uint8_t)(address << 1)) && i2c_write(reg);
	if (answered) {
		i2c_start();
		answered = i2c_write((uint8_t)(address << 1 | 1));
	}
	if (answered) {
		*value = (uint16_t)(i2c_read(true) << 8);
		*value |= i2c_read(false);
	}
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

static bool
register_write(uint8_t address, uint8_t reg, uint16_t value)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		say("speaker: the I2C bus is not at rest (gpio%u reads %u, gpio%u reads %u): not touched\n", PIN_SDA,
		    level(PIN_SDA), PIN_SCL, level(PIN_SCL));
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write((uint8_t)(address << 1)) && i2c_write(reg) && i2c_write((uint8_t)(value >> 8)) &&
	    i2c_write((uint8_t)value);
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

static const char *
amplifier_name(uint16_t id)
{
	switch (id) {
	case 0x1852: return "AW88194/AW88195";
	case 0x2013: return "AW88264";
	case 0x2032: return "AW88266";
	case 0x2049: return "AW88395";
	case 0x2055: return "AW88256";
	case 0x2066: return "AW88166";
	case 0x2071: return "AW88350";
	case 0x2113: return "AW88261";
	case 0x2183: return "AW88399";
	case 0x2308: return "AW88230";
	}
	return "an amplifier this list does not know";
}

/* ---- the amplifiers, as Android's driver runs them -------------------------------------------------- */

#define AW_ID                   0x00            /* reads the chip ID; 0x55aa written resets the chip */
#define AW_ID_AW88261           0x2113
#define AW_SOFT_RESET           0x55aa
#define AW_SYSST                0x01
#define AW_SYSINT               0x02            /* read: cleared */
#define AW_SYSINTM              0x03
#define AW_SYSCTRL              0x04
#define AW_SYSCTRL2             0x05            /* [9:0] the volume, attenuation: [9:6] 6 dB steps, [5:0] eighths of a dB */
#define AW_I2SCTRL3             0x08
#define AW_VBAT                 0x21            /* [9:0] the battery's voltage as the amplifier sees it: x 6025 / 1023 mV */
#define AW_TEMP                 0x22            /* [9:0] the amplifier's temperature, degrees Celsius, two's complement */
#define AW_PVDD                 0x23            /* [9:0] its boosted supply */
#define AW_ISNDAT               0x24            /* the current and voltage sense, as last measured */
#define AW_VSNDAT               0x25
#define AW_DBGCTRL              0x14
#define AW_VSNTM1               0x50
#define AW_EFRH4                0x78
#define AW_EFRH3                0x79
#define AW_EFRL4                0x7c
#define AW_EFRL3                0x7d

#define SYSCTRL_PWDN            (1u << 0)
#define SYSCTRL_AMPPD           (1u << 1)
#define SYSCTRL_HMUTE           (1u << 8)
#define SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE       (1u << 14)
#define I2SCTRL3_TXEN           (1u << 6)
#define DBGCTRL_EF_OR           (1u << 3)       /* the fuses' two copies are or-ed; else and-ed */
#define SYSINTM_DEFAULT         0xffff

#define SYSST_PLLS              (1u << 0)
#define SYSST_OTHS              (1u << 1)
#define SYSST_OCDS              (1u << 3)
#define SYSST_CLKS              (1u << 4)
#define SYSST_NOCLKS            (1u << 5)
#define SYSST_WDS               (1u << 6)
#define SYSST_SWS               (1u << 8)
#define SYSST_BSTS              (1u << 9)
#define SYSST_BSTOCS            (1u << 11)
#define SYSST_UVLS              (1u << 14)
#define SYSST_OVP2S             (1u << 15)
#define SYSST_PLL_CHECK         (SYSST_CLKS | SYSST_PLLS)
#define SYSST_CHECK             (SYSST_BSTS | SYSST_SWS | SYSST_CLKS | SYSST_PLLS)
#define SYSST_FAULTS            (SYSST_OVP2S | SYSST_UVLS | SYSST_BSTOCS | SYSST_WDS | SYSST_NOCLKS | SYSST_OCDS | SYSST_OTHS)

#define VOLUME_LOWEST           (90 * 8)        /* the driver's "mute volume", in eighths of a dB */
#define VOLUME_STEP             (6 * 8)
#define STATUS_TRIES            10              /* the driver's AW_DEV_SYSST_CHECK_MAX, 2 ms apart */

/* Android's configuration file ("ACF", Awinic's format; Linux: sound/soc/codecs/aw88395/aw88395_lib.c) */
#define ACF_PROFILE_MUSIC       0
#define ACF_DATA_REGISTERS      4               /* a block with a header of its own and registers in it */
#define ACF_DATA_MONITOR        10              /* the driver's "monitor": what to do when the chip is cold or the battery low */
#define MONITOR_ROWS            8
#define ACF_BLOCK_HEADER        0x3c

struct amplifier {
	uint8_t address;
	unsigned device;                /* the file's device number for it (Android's sound-channel) */
	const char *where;
	uint16_t profile[64][2];        /* register, value */
	unsigned count;
	uint16_t sysctrl;               /* what the profile has for 0x04, 0x08 and 0x05 */
	uint16_t i2sctrl3;
	uint16_t volume_at;             /* Android's level: from the profile's 0x05, in eighths of a dB of attenuation */
	uint16_t volume;                /* where it is now */
	uint16_t volume_high;           /* the profile's bits 15:10 of 0x05, which the volume leaves as they are */
	bool prepared, started;
	/* the monitor's tables (from the file) and what was last seen */
	struct { int16_t min, max; uint16_t less; } temp_rows[MONITOR_ROWS], vbat_rows[MONITOR_ROWS];
	unsigned temp_count, vbat_count, looks;
	int temps[3], vbats[3];
	int temp_row, vbat_row;
};

static struct amplifier amplifiers[2] = {
	{ .address = 0x35, .device = 0, .where = "0x35, slot 0", .temp_row = -1, .vbat_row = -1 },
	{ .address = 0x34, .device = 1, .where = "0x34, slot 1", .temp_row = -1, .vbat_row = -1 },
};
static bool broken;                     /* something went wrong: both have been powered down, nothing more is done */

static uint32_t
le32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return (uint32_t)p[0] | (uint32_t)p[1] << 8 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24;
}

/*
 * The driver's monitor for one amplifier (Android has it on: aw_dev_N_monitor), from the file: every second it
 * reads the chip's temperature and the battery's voltage, and a table says what to do for each range of them.
 * This file's: at 7 to 100 degrees nothing; at 2 to 5 degrees 3 dB less, at -2 to 0 4.5 dB, at -50 to -5 8 dB (and
 * a lower current limit for the boost, which is not done here); from 3.85 V nothing, at 3.65 to 3.75 V and up to
 * 3.55 V a lower "vmax" for the DSP's algorithm, which does not run here. In its temperature rows a vmax goes with
 * each reduction of the volume, so the battery rows' vmax is turned into a volume reduction in the same proportion
 * (the first temperature row's: 3 dB for its vmax): 1.6 and 3.1 dB. Between the ranges the last one holds.
 *   block: checksum (of the bytes after it), version, chip name[16], ui version, the time and count of looks,
 *   switches, then for the temperatures and for the voltages each: a value, the number of rows, a row's size and
 *   the rows' offset; a row: int16 lowest, int16 highest, uint16 boost current, uint16 reduction (eighths of a
 *   dB), int32 vmax
 */
static void
acf_monitor(uint16_t device, const uint8_t *block, uint32_t length)
{
	struct amplifier *a = NULL;
	uint32_t sum = 0, temp_count, temp_size, temp_at, vbat_count, vbat_size, vbat_at;
	int64_t per_eighth = 0;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		if (amplifiers[i].device == device) {
			a = &amplifiers[i];
		}
	}
	if (a == NULL || length < 0x48) {
		return;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 4; i < length; i++) {
		sum += block[i];
	}
	temp_count = le32(block + 0x2c);
	temp_size = le32(block + 0x30);
	temp_at = le32(block + 0x34);
	vbat_count = le32(block + 0x3c);
	vbat_size = le32(block + 0x40);
	vbat_at = le32(block + 0x44);
	/* (the end of each table is worked out in 64 bits: in 32 a crafted size or offset wraps and the check passes, and the
	   rows read below would then lie gigabytes outside the file's buffer) */
	if (sum != le32(block) || temp_size < 12 || vbat_size < 12 || temp_count > MONITOR_ROWS || vbat_count > MONITOR_ROWS ||
	    (uint64_t)temp_at + (uint64_t)temp_count * temp_size > length ||
	    (uint64_t)vbat_at + (uint64_t)vbat_count * vbat_size > length) {
		say("speaker: device %u's monitor table is not of the shape known: not used\n", device);
		return;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < temp_count; i++) {
		const uint8_t *row = block + temp_at + i * temp_size;
		int32_t vmax = (int32_t)le32(row + 8);

		a->temp_rows[i].min = (int16_t)(row[0] | row[1] << 8);
		a->temp_rows[i].max = (int16_t)(row[2] | row[3] << 8);
		a->temp_rows[i].less = (uint16_t)(row[6] | row[7] << 8);
		if (per_eighth == 0 && a->temp_rows[i].less != 0 && vmax < 0) {
			per_eighth = -(int64_t)vmax / a->temp_rows[i].less;
		}
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < vbat_count; i++) {
		const uint8_t *row = block + vbat_at + i * vbat_size;
		int32_t vmax = (int32_t)le32(row + 8);

		a->vbat_rows[i].min = (int16_t)(row[0] | row[1] << 8);
		a->vbat_rows[i].max = (int16_t)(row[2] | row[3] << 8);
		a->vbat_rows[i].less = (uint16_t)(row[6] | row[7] << 8);
		if (vmax < 0 && per_eighth > 0) {
			/* (saturating: a huge vmax in the file must not wrap the 16-bit reduction round to a small one) */
			int64_t more = (-(int64_t)vmax + per_eighth / 2) / per_eighth;

			a->vbat_rows[i].less = (uint16_t)(more > 0xffff - a->vbat_rows[i].less ? 0xffff : a->vbat_rows[i].less + more);
		}
	}
	a->temp_count = temp_count;
	a->vbat_count = vbat_count;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < temp_count; i++) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s's monitor: at %d to %d degrees, %u.%03u dB less\n", a->where, a->temp_rows[i].min,
		    a->temp_rows[i].max, a->temp_rows[i].less / 8, a->temp_rows[i].less % 8 * 125);
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < vbat_count; i++) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s's monitor: at %d to %d mV, %u.%03u dB less\n", a->where, a->vbat_rows[i].min,
		    a->vbat_rows[i].max, a->vbat_rows[i].less / 8, a->vbat_rows[i].less % 8 * 125);
	}
}

/* The "Music" profile of every amplifier, from the file; false if the file is not of the shape known. */
static bool
acf_profiles(const uint8_t *acf, uint64_t size)
{
	uint32_t entry_size, entries, at;

	if (size < 0x50 || size > 0x100000) {
		say("speaker: the configuration file is %llu bytes: not one of Awinic's\n", size);
		return false;
	}
	entry_size = le32(acf + 0x34);
	entries = le32(acf + 0x38);
	at = le32(acf + 0x3c);
	if (entries == 0 || entries > 64 || entry_size % entries != 0 || entry_size / entries < 0x30 ||
	    (uint64_t)at + entry_size > size) {
		say("speaker: the configuration file's table (%u entries, %u bytes at %#x) is not of a shape known\n", entries,
		    entry_size, at);
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t e = 0; e < entries; e++) {
		const uint8_t *entry = acf + at + e * (entry_size / entries);
		char name[17];
		uint16_t device = (uint16_t)(entry[20] | entry[21] << 8), profile = (uint16_t)(entry[26] | entry[27] << 8);
		uint32_t kind = le32(entry + 28), length = le32(entry + 32), offset = le32(entry + 36);
		uint32_t checksum, sum = 0, data_length, count;
		const uint8_t *block = acf + offset;
		struct amplifier *a = NULL;

		memcpy(name, entry + 4, 16);
		name[16] = 0;
		if (kind == ACF_DATA_MONITOR) {
			acf_monitor(device, acf + offset, (uint64_t)offset + length <= size ? length : 0);
			continue;
		}
		if (kind != ACF_DATA_REGISTERS || profile != ACF_PROFILE_MUSIC || strcmp(name, "aw88261") != 0) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
			if (amplifiers[i].device == device) {
				a = &amplifiers[i];
			}
		}
		if (a == NULL || (uint64_t)offset + length > size || length < ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + 4) {
			say("speaker: the configuration file's entry %u (device %u) does not fit\n", e, device);
			return false;
		}
		checksum = le32(block);
		data_length = le32(block + 0x10);
		count = le32(block + ACF_BLOCK_HEADER);
		if (ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + data_length > length || data_length != 4 + 4 * count || count > 64 ||
		    le32(block + 0x20) != 2 || le32(block + 0x24) != 2) {
			say("speaker: device %u's Music profile is not a list of 16-bit registers (%u bytes, %u registers)\n", device,
			    data_length, count);
			return false;
		}
		for (uint32_t i = 4; i < ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + data_length; i++) {
			sum += block[i];
		}
		if (sum != checksum) {
			say("speaker: device %u's Music profile does not add up (%#x, the file says %#x)\n", device, sum, checksum);
			return false;
		}
		a->count = count;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			const uint8_t *pair = block + ACF_BLOCK_HEADER + 4 + 4 * i;

			a->profile[i][0] = (uint16_t)(pair[0] | pair[1] << 8);
			a->profile[i][1] = (uint16_t)(pair[2] | pair[3] << 8);
		}
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		bool have[3] = { false, false, false };

		for (unsigned r = 0; r < a->count; r++) {
			uint16_t reg = a->profile[r][0], value = a->profile[r][1];

			if (reg == AW_SYSCTRL) {
				a->sysctrl = value;
				have[0] = true;
			} else if (reg == AW_I2SCTRL3) {
				a->i2sctrl3 = value;
				have[1] = true;
			} else if (reg == AW_SYSCTRL2) {
				/* the driver's aw_pid_2113_reg_val_to_db() */
				a->volume_at = (uint16_t)(((value & 0x3ff) >> 6) * VOLUME_STEP + (value & 0x3f));
				a->volume_high = value & 0xfc00;
				have[2] = true;
			} else if (reg == AW_ID || reg >= 0x70) {
				say("speaker: device %u's Music profile writes register %#x, which is not one of the configuration's\n",
				    a->device, reg);
				return false;
			}
		}
		if (a->count == 0 || !have[0] || !have[1] || !have[2] || a->volume_at >= VOLUME_LOWEST) {
			say("speaker: no usable Music profile for device %u (the amplifier at %#x) in the configuration file\n",
			    a->device, a->address);
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: Music profile of %u registers; Android's volume there is -%u.%03u dB (%#x)\n", a->where,
		    a->count, a->volume_at / 8, a->volume_at % 8 * 125, a->volume_at);
	}
	return true;
}

/* Both powered down at once, without the driver's ceremony: a fault, or a value that did not stick. */
static void
power_down_now(const char *why)
{
	broken = true;
	say("speaker: %s: BOTH AMPLIFIERS ARE POWERED DOWN AT ONCE (0x04: amplifier power-down and power-down set)\n", why);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t value = 0, after = 0;

		if (!a->prepared && !a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!register_read(a->address, AW_SYSCTRL, &value)) {
			value = a->sysctrl;
		}
		value |= SYSCTRL_PWDN | SYSCTRL_AMPPD | SYSCTRL_HMUTE;
		if (!register_write(a->address, AW_SYSCTRL, value) || !register_read(a->address, AW_SYSCTRL, &after)) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: 0x04 <- %#06x NOT ACKNOWLEDGED\n", a->where, value);
			/* (`started' stays set: the amplifier may still be up, and hakios_speaker_quiesce() tries again only for an
			   amplifier that is not known to be off) */
			continue;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: 0x04 <- %#06x, reads %#06x\n", a->where, value, after);
		a->started = false;
	}
}

/* One register written, said and read back; false (and both powered down) if it did not stick. */
static bool
put(struct amplifier *a, uint8_t reg, uint16_t value)
{
	uint16_t after = 0;

	if (broken) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!register_write(a->address, reg, value)) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x <- %#06x NOT ACKNOWLEDGED\n", a->where, reg, value);
		power_down_now("a write was not acknowledged");
		return false;
	}
	if (!register_read(a->address, reg, &after)) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x <- %#06x, NOT READ BACK\n", a->where, reg, value);
		power_down_now("a register could not be read back");
		return false;
	}
	say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x <- %#06x, reads %#06x%s\n", a->where, reg, value, after, after == value ? "" :
	    ": NOT AS WRITTEN");
	if (after != value) {
		power_down_now("a register did not read back as written");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static bool
get(struct amplifier *a, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *value)
{
	if (!register_read(a->address, reg, value)) {
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %#04x NOT READ\n", a->where, reg);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* The bits of 0x04 named in `bits' set or cleared, the rest as they read. */
static bool
sysctrl(struct amplifier *a, uint16_t bits, bool set)
{
	uint16_t value;

	if (broken || !get(a, AW_SYSCTRL, &value)) {
		return false;
	}
	return put(a, AW_SYSCTRL, set ? (value | bits) : (value & ~bits));
}

/* The volume register at `volume' eighths of a dB of attenuation (the driver's aw_pid_2113_set_volume()). */
static bool
set_volume(struct amplifier *a, uint16_t volume)
{
	uint16_t value;

	if (volume > VOLUME_LOWEST) {
		volume = VOLUME_LOWEST;
	}
	if (volume < a->volume_at) {
		volume = a->volume_at;  /* never louder than Android */
	}
	/* (the other bits as the profile has them and as they were written: not read first, for a quick fade) */
	value = (uint16_t)(a->volume_high | (volume / VOLUME_STEP) << 6 | volume % VOLUME_STEP);
	if (broken || !put(a, AW_SYSCTRL2, value)) {
		return false;
	}
	a->volume = volume;
	return true;
}

/* What the status register says, and whether it says a fault. */
static bool
faulty(struct amplifier *a, uint16_t *status)
{
	if (!get(a, AW_SYSST, status)) {
		return true;
	}
	return (*status & SYSST_FAULTS) != 0;
}

bool
hakios_speaker_prepare(const uint8_t *acf, uint64_t size)
{
	if (tlmm == 0) {
		tlmm = ml_io_map(TLMM_PHYS, TLMM_SIZE);
	}
	broken = false;
	say("speaker: the amplifiers are prepared as Android's driver prepares them; the I2C pins as found:\n");
	show_pins();
	if (!acf_profiles(acf, size)) {
		return false;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t id = 0, h4 = 0, h3 = 0, l4 = 0, l3 = 0, icalk_bits, vcalk_bits;
		int icalk, vcalk;
		uint16_t vcalb, ef_or = 0;

		if (!get(a, AW_ID, &id)) {
			say("speaker: nobody at I2C address %#x: not powered, or not there\n", a->address);
			power_down_now("an amplifier does not answer");
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: chip ID %#06x, %s\n", a->where, id, amplifier_name(id));
		if (id != AW_ID_AW88261) {
			return false;
		}
		if (!get(a, AW_EFRH4, &h4) || !get(a, AW_EFRH3, &h3) || !get(a, AW_EFRL4, &l4) || !get(a, AW_EFRL3, &l3)) {
			return false;
		}
		for (unsigned r = 0; r < a->count; r++) {
			if (a->profile[r][0] == AW_DBGCTRL) {
				ef_or = a->profile[r][1] & DBGCTRL_EF_OR;
			}
		}
		/* the driver's aw_dev_get_icalk(), aw_dev_get_vcalk() and aw_dev_set_vcalb() */
		icalk_bits = ef_or ? ((h4 & 0x3ff) | (l4 & 0x3ff)) : ((h4 & 0x3ff) & (l4 & 0x3ff));
		vcalk_bits = ef_or ? ((h3 & 0x3ff) | (l3 & 0x3ff)) : ((h3 & 0x3ff) & (l3 & 0x3ff));
		icalk = 1000 + ((icalk_bits & 0x200) ? (int)icalk_bits - 0x400 : (int)icalk_bits);
		vcalk = 1000 + ((vcalk_bits & 0x200) ? (int)vcalk_bits - 0x400 : (int)vcalk_bits);
		if (vcalk <= 0 || icalk <= 0) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: fuses %#x %#x %#x %#x make no sense\n", a->where, h4, h3, l4, l3);
			return false;
		}
		vcalb = (uint16_t)(8192 * icalk / vcalk);
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: fuses %#06x %#06x %#06x %#06x: icalk %d, vcalk %d, so 0x50 is to be %#06x\n", a->where,
		    h4, h3, l4, l3, icalk, vcalk, vcalb);

		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: soft reset (0x00 <- 0x55aa), as the driver does it first\n", a->where);
		a->prepared = true;
		if (!register_write(a->address, AW_ID, AW_SOFT_RESET)) {
			power_down_now("the soft reset was not acknowledged");
			return false;
		}
		wait_ms(2);
		for (unsigned r = 0; r < a->count; r++) {
			uint8_t reg = (uint8_t)a->profile[r][0];
			uint16_t value = a->profile[r][1], now;

			switch (reg) {
			case AW_SYSINTM:
				value = SYSINTM_DEFAULT;
				break;
			case AW_SYSCTRL:
				/* the three power and mute bits stay as they are; the power stage's mute on */
				if (!get(a, AW_SYSCTRL, &now)) {
					power_down_now("0x04 could not be read");
					return false;
				}
				value = (uint16_t)((value & ~(SYSCTRL_PWDN | SYSCTRL_AMPPD | SYSCTRL_HMUTE)) |
				    (now & (SYSCTRL_PWDN | SYSCTRL_AMPPD | SYSCTRL_HMUTE)) | SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE);
				break;
			case AW_I2SCTRL3:
				value &= (uint16_t)~I2SCTRL3_TXEN;
				break;
			case AW_VSNTM1:
				continue;
			}
			if (!put(a, reg, value)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		if (!put(a, AW_VSNTM1, vcalb) || !set_volume(a, VOLUME_LOWEST)) {
			return false;
		}
	}
	say("speaker: BOTH AMPLIFIERS ARE CONFIGURED as Android's Music profile has them: powered down, muted, at the lowest volume\n");
	return true;
}

bool
hakios_speaker_start(void)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t status = 0, interrupts = 0;
		unsigned tries;

		if (broken || !a->prepared) {
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: power-down off\n", a->where);
		a->started = true;
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_PWDN, false)) {
			return false;
		}
		wait_ms(2);
		for (tries = 0; tries < STATUS_TRIES; tries++) {
			if (!get(a, AW_SYSST, &status)) {
				power_down_now("the status could not be read");
				return false;
			}
			if ((status & SYSST_PLL_CHECK) == SYSST_PLL_CHECK) {
				break;
			}
			wait_ms(2);
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x: its PLL %s\n", a->where, status, tries < STATUS_TRIES ?
		    "IS LOCKED to the bit clock" : "DOES NOT LOCK: no clock?");
		if (tries == STATUS_TRIES) {
			power_down_now("an amplifier's PLL does not lock");
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: amplifier power-down off\n", a->where);
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_AMPPD, false)) {
			return false;
		}
		wait_ms(1);
		for (tries = 0; tries < STATUS_TRIES; tries++) {
			if (faulty(a, &status)) {
				break;
			}
			if ((status & SYSST_CHECK) == SYSST_CHECK) {
				break;
			}
			wait_ms(2);
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
		if ((status & SYSST_FAULTS) != 0 || (status & SYSST_CHECK) != SYSST_CHECK) {
			power_down_now((status & SYSST_FAULTS) ? "an amplifier reports a fault" : "an amplifier's status is not as "
			    "the driver wants it");
			return false;
		}
		if (!put(a, AW_I2SCTRL3, a->i2sctrl3) ||        /* the feedback on, as the profile has it */
		    !sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE, false) || !sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_HMUTE, false)) {
			return false;
		}
		if (!get(a, AW_SYSINT, &interrupts) || !get(a, AW_SYSINT, &interrupts) || !put(a, AW_SYSINTM, SYSINTM_DEFAULT)) {
			power_down_now("the interrupts could not be read");
			return false;
		}
		if (faulty(a, &status)) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
			power_down_now("an amplifier reports a fault");
			return false;
		}
		say("speaker: THE AMPLIFIER %s RUNS, unmuted at the lowest volume (status %#06x)\n", a->where, status);
	}
	return true;
}

bool
hakios_speaker_volume(uint32_t below, uint32_t step_ms)
{
	uint16_t status;

	/* Nothing is quieter than the driver's mute volume. Without this a huge `below' wraps volume_at + below to a level
	   under volume_at, which the fade loop below can never reach (set_volume() never goes louder than Android), so it
	   would spin forever with the amplifiers at their loudest. */
	if (below > VOLUME_LOWEST) {
		below = VOLUME_LOWEST;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint32_t target = a->volume_at + below;

		if (broken || !a->started) {
			return false;
		}
		if (target > VOLUME_LOWEST) {
			target = VOLUME_LOWEST;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s: the volume to -%u.%03u dB (Android's level less %u.%03u dB), 6 dB a step every %u ms\n",
		    a->where, target / 8, target % 8 * 125, (target - a->volume_at) / 8, (target - a->volume_at) % 8 * 125, step_ms);
	}
	/* both together, a step every step_ms, the status looked at after every step */
	for (;;) {
		bool moved = false;

		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
			struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
			uint32_t target = a->volume_at + below, next;

			if (target > VOLUME_LOWEST) {
				target = VOLUME_LOWEST;
			}
			if (a->volume == target) {
				continue;
			}
			next = a->volume > target ? (a->volume - target > VOLUME_STEP ? a->volume - VOLUME_STEP : target) :
			    (target - a->volume > VOLUME_STEP ? a->volume + VOLUME_STEP : target);
			if (!set_volume(a, (uint16_t)next)) {
				return false;
			}
			/* (a slow fade looks at the status after every step, a quick one once it is over) */
			if (step_ms >= 10 && faulty(a, &status)) {
				say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
				power_down_now("an amplifier reports a fault");
				return false;
			}
			moved = true;
		}
		if (!moved) {
			break;
		}
		if (step_ms) {
			wait_ms(step_ms);
		}
	}
	return hakios_speaker_healthy();
}

bool
hakios_speaker_healthy(void)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t status;

		if (broken) {
			return false;
		}
		if (!a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		if (faulty(a, &status)) {
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: status %#06x\n", a->where, status);
			power_down_now("an amplifier reports a fault");
			return false;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

/* the row of a monitor table that a value falls in; between rows, the one before */
static int
monitor_row(const struct amplifier *a, bool temperature, int value, int before)
{
	unsigned count = temperature ? a->temp_count : a->vbat_count;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		int min = temperature ? a->temp_rows[i].min : a->vbat_rows[i].min;
		int max = temperature ? a->temp_rows[i].max : a->vbat_rows[i].max;

		if (value >= min && value <= max) {
			return (int)i;
		}
	}
	return before;
}

/*
 * The driver's monitor, once: the temperature and the battery voltage of every amplifier that runs (the average of
 * the last three looks, as the file's count says), and the reduction their tables ask for, the larger of the two
 * amplifiers'. With `tell', what was read (also the boosted supply and the current and voltage sense, raw).
 */
uint32_t
hakios_speaker_monitor(bool tell)
{
	uint32_t wanted = 0;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];
		uint16_t vbat = 0, temp = 0, pvdd = 0, isn = 0, vsn = 0;
		int t = 0, v = 0;
		uint32_t less = 0;

		if (broken || !a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!get(a, AW_VBAT, &vbat) || !get(a, AW_TEMP, &temp)) {
			continue;
		}
		a->temps[a->looks % 3] = (temp & 0x200) ? (int)(temp & 0x3ff) - 0x400 : (int)(temp & 0x3ff);
		a->vbats[a->looks % 3] = (int)(vbat & 0x3ff) * 6025 / 1023;
		a->looks++;
		for (unsigned k = 0; k < 3 && k < a->looks; k++) {
			t += a->temps[k];
			v += a->vbats[k];
		}
		t /= (int)(a->looks < 3 ? a->looks : 3);
		v /= (int)(a->looks < 3 ? a->looks : 3);
		a->temp_row = monitor_row(a, true, t, a->temp_row);
		a->vbat_row = monitor_row(a, false, v, a->vbat_row);
		less = (a->temp_row >= 0 ? a->temp_rows[a->temp_row].less : 0) + (a->vbat_row >= 0 ? a->vbat_rows[a->vbat_row].less : 0);
		if (less > wanted) {
			wanted = less;
		}
		if (tell) {
			(void)get(a, AW_PVDD, &pvdd);
			(void)get(a, AW_ISNDAT, &isn);
			(void)get(a, AW_VSNDAT, &vsn);
			say("speaker: the amplifier %s: %d degrees, the battery %d mV (%#05x, %#05x; supply %#05x, sense %#06x %#06x): "
			    "%u.%03u dB less\n", a->where, t, v, temp, vbat, pvdd, isn, vsn, less / 8, less % 8 * 125);
		}
	}
	return wanted;
}

/*
 * A step of the stop sequence failed. A failed write has already powered both down (put()), but a failed read in
 * sysctrl() has not: without this the stop gave up half way, with this amplifier (and the other, not yet reached)
 * still up and the caller about to stop the clock they run on. Both powered down at once, as for any fault.
 */
static void
stop_failed(void)
{
	if (!broken) {
		power_down_now("a step of the stop failed");
	}
}

void
hakios_speaker_stop(void)
{
	if (broken) {
		return;                 /* (already powered down) */
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		struct amplifier *a = &amplifiers[i];

		if (!a->started) {
			continue;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s is stopped as Android's driver stops it\n", a->where);
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_ULS_HMUTE, true)) {
			stop_failed();
			return;
		}
		while (a->volume < VOLUME_LOWEST) {
			if (!set_volume(a, (uint16_t)(a->volume + VOLUME_STEP > VOLUME_LOWEST ? VOLUME_LOWEST : a->volume +
			    VOLUME_STEP))) {
				stop_failed();
				return;
			}
			wait_ms(1);
		}
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_HMUTE, true) || !put(a, AW_I2SCTRL3, (uint16_t)(a->i2sctrl3 & ~I2SCTRL3_TXEN))) {
			stop_failed();
			return;
		}
		wait_ms(1);
		if (!sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_AMPPD, true) || !sysctrl(a, SYSCTRL_PWDN, true)) {
			stop_failed();
			return;
		}
		a->started = false;
		say("speaker: THE AMPLIFIER %s IS POWERED DOWN\n", a->where);
	}
}

void
hakios_speaker_quiesce(void)
{
	bool any = false;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		any |= amplifiers[i].started;
	}
	if (!any || tlmm == 0) {
		return;
	}
	leaving = true;
	power_down_now("the kernel is on its way out");
}

/* ---- speaker_probe=N: a look ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

static void
show_amplifiers(void)
{
	/* the chip ID, then registers that every chip of the family has at the same place and that reading does not change */
	static const struct {
		uint8_t reg;
		const char *name;
	} more[] = { { 0x01, "status" }, { 0x04, "system control" }, { 0x06, "I2S control" } };

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		uint16_t id = 0, value = 0;

		if (!register_read(amplifiers[i].address, AW_ID, &id)) {
			say("speaker: nobody at I2C address %#x: not powered, or not there\n", amplifiers[i].address);
			continue;
		}
		say("speaker: the amplifier %s is there: chip ID %#06x, %s\n", amplifiers[i].where, id, amplifier_name(id));
		for (unsigned r = 0; r < sizeof(more) / sizeof(more[0]); r++) {
			if (register_read(amplifiers[i].address, more[r].reg, &value)) {
				say("speaker:   register %#04x (%s) = %#06x\n", more[r].reg, more[r].name, value);
			}
		}
	}
}

/* ---- power names of the audio subsystem ------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define CMD_DB_PHYS             0x80860000UL
#define CMD_DB_SIZE             0x20000UL
#define GCC_PHYS                0x00100000UL
#define GCC_SIZE                0x60000UL

struct cmd_db_slave {
	uint16_t id, header_offset, data_offset, count, version, reserved[3];
};
struct cmd_db_header {
	uint32_t version;
	uint8_t magic[4];
	struct cmd_db_slave slave[8];
	uint32_t checksum, reserved;
	uint8_t data[];
};
struct cmd_db_entry {
	char id[8];
	uint32_t priority[2];
	uint32_t address;
	uint16_t length, offset;
};

/* The RPMh address of a resource by its name in the command database the boot loader left; 0 = none. */
static uint32_t
rpmh_address(const char *name)
{
	const struct cmd_db_header *db = (const struct cmd_db_header *)cmd_db;
	char id[8] = { 0 };

	if (db->magic[0] != 0xdb || db->magic[1] != 0x30 || db->magic[2] != 0x03 || db->magic[3] != 0x0c) {
		return 0;
	}
	strlcpy(id, name, sizeof(id));
	for (unsigned s = 0; s < 8; s++) {
		const struct cmd_db_slave *slave = &db->slave[s];
		const struct cmd_db_entry *entry = (const struct cmd_db_entry *)(db->data + slave->header_offset);

		if (slave->id == 0 || slave->header_offset >= CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000 || slave->count > 512) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < slave->count; i++) {
			if (memcmp(entry[i].id, id, sizeof(id)) == 0) {
				return entry[i].address;
			}
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

static void
show_power(void)
{
	/* the subsystem's two supplies and, for the DSP, the processor's own two and the crystal */
	static const char *const supplies[] = { "lcx.lvl", "lmx.lvl", "cx.lvl", "mx.lvl", "xo.lvl" };

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(supplies) / sizeof(supplies[0]); i++) {
		uint32_t address = rpmh_address(supplies[i]);

		if (address) {
			say("speaker: supply \"%s\" can be asked for at RPMh address %#x\n", supplies[i], address);
		} else {
			say("speaker: no supply \"%s\" in the command database\n", supplies[i]);
		}
	}
	/*
	 * (The audio subsystem's bus clock, GCC_CFG_NOC_LPASS_CBCR, is not read: on the phone that read
	 * stops the kernel with a synchronous external abort -- the register is not the main processors'
	 * to read while the audio subsystem belongs to its DSP.)
	 */
}

static void
probe_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	if (tlmm == 0) {
		tlmm = ml_io_map(TLMM_PHYS, TLMM_SIZE);
	}
	gcc = ml_io_map(GCC_PHYS, GCC_SIZE);
	cmd_db = ml_io_map_wcomb(CMD_DB_PHYS, CMD_DB_SIZE);      /* memory, not registers: no alignment rules */
	say("speaker: a look at the phone's sound hardware (level %u; nothing is switched on)\n", probe_level);
	show_pins();
	show_power();
	if (probe_level >= 2) {
		show_amplifiers();
	}
	say("speaker: done\n");
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
hakios_speaker_init(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("speaker_probe", &probe_level, sizeof(probe_level)) || probe_level == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (kernel_thread_start(probe_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}

```

`drivers/audio/hakios.virtio_sound.c`:

```c
/*
 * A virtio sound device as the sink of /dev/hakios-audio (see sys/hakios.audio.h).
 *
 * Under QEMU's "virt" machine a "virtio-sound-device" plays what Darwin plays: through the host's
 * sound system, or into a file ("-audiodev wav"), whichever back end QEMU is given. Like the
 * input devices (hakios.virtio_input.c) it sits on the machine's virtio-mmio bus, which must
 * be the current one, not "legacy". Only with boot-arg virtio_sound=1: the bus address is
 * QEMU's and means nothing on the phone.
 *
 * The device has four queues; two are used. Over the control queue its first output stream is
 * set to the one format of /dev/hakios-audio and started, once and for good: a started stream
 * that is given nothing plays nothing. The samples go out over the transmit queue, a hundredth
 * of a second to a buffer. The device gives a buffer back when it has played it, which is what
 * paces us: what does not fit into the buffers waits in a ring, and what does not fit into the
 * ring is lost.
 *
 * No interrupt is used; while there is sound on its way the queue is looked at 200 times a
 * second, otherwise not at all.
 *
 * The protocol: Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO) Version 1.2, section 5.14 "Sound Device".
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/hakios.audio.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);       /* pmap_paddr_t */

#define VIRTIO_BUS              0x0a000000UL    /* QEMU virt: 32 transports of 0x200 bytes */
#define VIRTIO_SLOTS            32
#define VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE        0x200

#define VIRTIO_MAGIC            0x000           /* "virt" */
#define VIRTIO_VERSION          0x004
#define VIRTIO_DEVICE_ID        0x008
#define VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES  0x020
#define VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL 0x024
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_SEL        0x030
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX    0x034
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM        0x038
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_READY      0x044
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY     0x050
#define VIRTIO_STATUS           0x070
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DESC       0x080
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DRIVER     0x090
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DEVICE     0x0a0
#define VIRTIO_CONFIG           0x100

#define VIRTIO_ID_SOUND         25
#define STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE      1
#define STATUS_DRIVER           2
#define STATUS_DRIVER_OK        4
#define STATUS_FEATURES_OK      8

#define QUEUE_CONTROL           0
#define QUEUE_TX                2
#define QUEUE_SIZE              64
#define DESC_F_NEXT             1
#define DESC_F_WRITE            2
#define AVAIL_F_NO_INTERRUPT    1

struct vq_desc {
	uint64_t addr;
	uint32_t len;
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t next;
};
struct vq_avail {
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t idx;
	uint16_t ring[QUEUE_SIZE];
};
struct vq_used {
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t idx;
	struct {
		uint32_t id;
		uint32_t len;
	} ring[QUEUE_SIZE];
};

/* the sound device's own messages */
#define SND_R_PCM_INFO          0x0100
#define SND_R_PCM_SET_PARAMS    0x0101
#define SND_R_PCM_PREPARE       0x0102
#define SND_R_PCM_START         0x0104
#define SND_S_OK                0x8000
#define SND_D_OUTPUT            0
#define SND_PCM_FMT_S16         5
#define SND_PCM_RATE_48000      7

struct snd_query_info {
	uint32_t code;
	uint32_t start_id, count, size;
};
#define SND_PCM_INFO_SIZE       32              /* hda_fn_nid, features, formats (64 bits), rates (64 bits), ... */
#define SND_PCM_INFO_DIRECTION  24              /* ... direction, channels_min, channels_max (a byte each) */
struct snd_pcm_hdr {
	uint32_t code;
	uint32_t stream_id;
};
struct snd_pcm_set_params {
	uint32_t code;
	uint32_t stream_id;
	uint32_t buffer_bytes, period_bytes;
	uint32_t features;
	uint8_t  channels, format, rate, padding;
};
struct snd_pcm_status {
	uint32_t status;
	uint32_t latency_bytes;
};

#define PERIOD_FRAMES           (HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE / 100)
#define PERIOD_BYTES            (PERIOD_FRAMES * HAKIOS_AUDIO_FRAME)
#define TX_BUFFERS              (QUEUE_SIZE / 2)        /* two descriptors each: 0.32 s in the device at most */
#define RING_FRAMES             16384                   /* a power of two: 0.34 s more */
#define MAX_STREAMS             8

/* one transmit buffer: what the device reads, then what it writes */
struct tx_buffer {
	uint32_t stream_id;
	int16_t  frames[PERIOD_FRAMES * HAKIOS_AUDIO_CHANNELS];
	struct snd_pcm_status status;
};

/* what the device reads and writes: the two queues' rings in the first page, then the buffers */
#define OFFSET_DESC(q)          ((q) ? 0x2000 : 0x0000)
#define OFFSET_AVAIL(q)         ((q) ? 0x2400 : 0x0400)
#define OFFSET_USED(q)          ((q) ? 0x2800 : 0x0800)
#define OFFSET_CONTROL          0x1000                  /* a request, and at +0x800 the answer */
#define OFFSET_TX               0x4000
#define SHARED_SIZE             round_page(OFFSET_TX + TX_BUFFERS * sizeof(struct tx_buffer))

struct queue {
	struct vq_desc *        desc;
	struct vq_avail *       avail;
	struct vq_used *        used;
	uint16_t                seen;           /* how far the used ring has been read */
};

static vm_offset_t regs;
static vm_offset_t shared;
static uint64_t shared_phys;
static struct queue control, tx;
static uint32_t stream;

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(sound_lck_grp, "hakios-virtio-sound");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(sound_lock, &sound_lck_grp);
static int16_t ring[RING_FRAMES * HAKIOS_AUDIO_CHANNELS];
static uint32_t ring_head, ring_tail;           /* in frames; play from head, add at tail */
static uint16_t tx_free[TX_BUFFERS];
static uint32_t tx_free_count;
static thread_call_t poll_call;
static bool poll_armed;

static inline uint32_t
reg_read(uint32_t reg)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)(regs + reg);
}

static inline void
reg_write(uint32_t reg, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)(regs + reg) = value;
}

static inline void
reg_write64(uint32_t reg, uint64_t value)
{
	reg_write(reg, (uint32_t)value);
	reg_write(reg + 4, (uint32_t)(value >> 32));
}

static bool
queue_setup(struct queue *q, uint32_t index, int which)
{
	q->desc = (struct vq_desc *)(shared + OFFSET_DESC(which));
	q->avail = (struct vq_avail *)(shared + OFFSET_AVAIL(which));
	q->used = (struct vq_used *)(shared + OFFSET_USED(which));
	q->avail->flags = AVAIL_F_NO_INTERRUPT;
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_SEL, index);
	if (reg_read(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX) < QUEUE_SIZE) {
		printf("virtio-sound: queue %u of %u\n", index, reg_read(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX));
		return false;
	}
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM, QUEUE_SIZE);
	reg_write64(VIRTIO_QUEUE_DESC, shared_phys + OFFSET_DESC(which));
	reg_write64(VIRTIO_QUEUE_DRIVER, shared_phys + OFFSET_AVAIL(which));
	reg_write64(VIRTIO_QUEUE_DEVICE, shared_phys + OFFSET_USED(which));
	__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);         /* ISH */
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_READY, 1);
	return true;
}

/* Hand the device the descriptor chain that starts at `first`. */
static void
queue_add(struct queue *q, uint32_t index, uint16_t first)
{
	q->avail->ring[q->avail->idx % QUEUE_SIZE] = first;
	__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
	q->avail->idx++;
	__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY, index);
}

/*
 * One request over the control queue; the answer begins with a status word. Only while the
 * driver starts: the answer is waited for.
 */
static bool
control_request(const void *request, uint32_t request_size, void *answer, uint32_t answer_size)
{
	uint8_t *out = (uint8_t *)(shared + OFFSET_CONTROL), *in = out + 0x800;

	memcpy(out, request, request_size);
	bzero(in, answer_size);
	control.desc[0] = (struct vq_desc){ .addr = shared_phys + OFFSET_CONTROL, .len = request_size, .flags = DESC_F_NEXT, .next = 1 };
	control.desc[1] = (struct vq_desc){ .addr = shared_phys + OFFSET_CONTROL + 0x800, .len = answer_size, .flags = DESC_F_WRITE };
	queue_add(&control, QUEUE_CONTROL, 0);
	for (int tries = 0; control.seen == *(volatile uint16_t *)&control.used->idx; tries++) {
		if (tries == 1000) {
			printf("virtio-sound: no answer to request %#x\n", *(const uint32_t *)request);
			return false;
		}
		delay_for_interval(1, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
	control.seen++;
	memcpy(answer, in, answer_size);
	if (*(const uint32_t *)answer != SND_S_OK) {
		printf("virtio-sound: request %#x refused: %#x\n", *(const uint32_t *)request, *(const uint32_t *)answer);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* With sound_lock held: take back the buffers the device has played, give it what waits in the ring. */
static void
sound_pump(void)
{
	while (tx.seen != *(volatile uint16_t *)&tx.used->idx) {
		uint32_t n;

		/* (the device wrote the ring entry before it moved idx: read it only after idx, not ahead of it) */
		__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
		n = tx.used->ring[tx.seen++ % QUEUE_SIZE].id / 2;
		/* (the id is the device's: one that is not one of our buffers, or more buffers than there are, would write outside
		   tx_free[] and the shared area below; such an entry is dropped) */
		if (n >= TX_BUFFERS || tx_free_count >= TX_BUFFERS) {
			continue;
		}
		tx_free[tx_free_count++] = (uint16_t)n;
	}
	while (tx_free_count != 0 && ring_tail - ring_head >= PERIOD_FRAMES) {
		uint16_t n = tx_free[--tx_free_count];
		struct tx_buffer *buffer = (struct tx_buffer *)(shared + OFFSET_TX) + n;

		buffer->stream_id = stream;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < PERIOD_FRAMES; i++, ring_head++) {
			buffer->frames[2 * i] = ring[2 * (ring_head % RING_FRAMES)];
			buffer->frames[2 * i + 1] = ring[2 * (ring_head % RING_FRAMES) + 1];
		}
		queue_add(&tx, QUEUE_TX, (uint16_t)(2 * n));
	}
}

static void
sound_poll(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	uint64_t deadline;

	lck_mtx_lock(&sound_lock);
	sound_pump();
	/* as long as the device has buffers of ours, or there is a whole one to give it */
	poll_armed = tx_free_count != TX_BUFFERS || ring_tail - ring_head >= PERIOD_FRAMES;
	if (poll_armed) {
		clock_interval_to_deadline(5, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(poll_call, deadline);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sound_lock);
}

/* The sink: see sys/hakios.audio.h. */
static uint32_t
sound_play(const int16_t *frames, uint32_t count)
{
	uint32_t room, taken;
	uint64_t deadline;

	lck_mtx_lock(&sound_lock);
	room = RING_FRAMES - (ring_tail - ring_head);
	taken = count < room ? count : room;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < taken; i++, ring_tail++) {
		ring[2 * (ring_tail % RING_FRAMES)] = frames[2 * i];
		ring[2 * (ring_tail % RING_FRAMES) + 1] = frames[2 * i + 1];
	}
	sound_pump();
	if (!poll_armed) {
		poll_armed = true;
		clock_interval_to_deadline(5, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(poll_call, deadline);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&sound_lock);
	return taken;
}

static bool
sound_attach(int slot)
{
	uint8_t streams[sizeof(uint32_t) + MAX_STREAMS * SND_PCM_INFO_SIZE];     /* a status word, then the streams */
	struct snd_query_info query = { .code = SND_R_PCM_INFO, .size = SND_PCM_INFO_SIZE };
	struct snd_pcm_set_params params = { .code = SND_R_PCM_SET_PARAMS, .buffer_bytes = TX_BUFFERS * PERIOD_BYTES,
		                             .period_bytes = PERIOD_BYTES, .channels = HAKIOS_AUDIO_CHANNELS,
		                             .format = SND_PCM_FMT_S16, .rate = SND_PCM_RATE_48000 };
	struct snd_pcm_hdr command = { 0 };
	uint32_t status, count;

	if (kmem_alloc_contig(kernel_map, &shared, SHARED_SIZE, PAGE_MASK, 0, 0, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_ZERO | KMA_DATA,
	    VM_KERN_MEMORY_IOKIT) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		return false;
	}
	shared_phys = kvtophys(shared);

	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, 0);            /* reset */
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL, 0);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, 0);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL, 1);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, 1);   /* bit 32: VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1 */
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER | STATUS_FEATURES_OK);
	if (!(reg_read(VIRTIO_STATUS) & STATUS_FEATURES_OK)) {
		printf("virtio-sound: slot %d: features refused\n", slot);
		return false;
	}
	if (!queue_setup(&control, QUEUE_CONTROL, 0) || !queue_setup(&tx, QUEUE_TX, 1)) {
		return false;
	}
	/* every transmit buffer is a chain of two descriptors that never changes */
	for (uint16_t n = 0; n < TX_BUFFERS; n++) {
		uint64_t buffer = shared_phys + OFFSET_TX + (uint64_t)n * sizeof(struct tx_buffer);

		tx.desc[2 * n] = (struct vq_desc){ .addr = buffer, .len = offsetof(struct tx_buffer, status), .flags = DESC_F_NEXT,
			                           .next = (uint16_t)(2 * n + 1) };
		tx.desc[2 * n + 1] = (struct vq_desc){ .addr = buffer + offsetof(struct tx_buffer, status),
			                               .len = sizeof(struct snd_pcm_status), .flags = DESC_F_WRITE };
		tx_free[tx_free_count++] = n;
	}
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER | STATUS_FEATURES_OK | STATUS_DRIVER_OK);

	/* the first stream that plays */
	count = *(volatile uint32_t *)(regs + VIRTIO_CONFIG + 4);
	if (count > MAX_STREAMS) {
		count = MAX_STREAMS;
	}
	query.count = count;
	if (count == 0 || !control_request(&query, sizeof(query), streams, sizeof(uint32_t) + count * SND_PCM_INFO_SIZE)) {
		return false;
	}
	for (stream = 0; stream < count; stream++) {
		if (streams[sizeof(uint32_t) + stream * SND_PCM_INFO_SIZE + SND_PCM_INFO_DIRECTION] == SND_D_OUTPUT) {
			break;
		}
	}
	if (stream == count) {
		printf("virtio-sound: slot %d: no output stream among %u\n", slot, count);
		return false;
	}
	params.stream_id = command.stream_id = stream;
	if (!control_request(&params, sizeof(params), &status, sizeof(status))) {
		return false;
	}
	command.code = SND_R_PCM_PREPARE;
	if (!control_request(&command, sizeof(command), &status, sizeof(status))) {
		return false;
	}
	command.code = SND_R_PCM_START;
	return control_request(&command, sizeof(command), &status, sizeof(status));
}

void
hakios_virtio_sound_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0;
	vm_offset_t bus;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("virtio_sound", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	bus = ml_io_map(VIRTIO_BUS, VIRTIO_SLOTS * VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE);
	for (int slot = 0; slot < VIRTIO_SLOTS; slot++) {
		regs = bus + (vm_offset_t)slot * VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE;
		if (reg_read(VIRTIO_MAGIC) != 0x74726976 || reg_read(VIRTIO_DEVICE_ID) != VIRTIO_ID_SOUND) {
			continue;
		}
		if (reg_read(VIRTIO_VERSION) != 2) {
			printf("virtio-sound: slot %d is a legacy transport; start QEMU with -global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false\n", slot);
			continue;
		}
		if (sound_attach(slot)) {
			printf("virtio-sound: device in slot %d, stream %u\n", slot, stream);
			poll_call = thread_call_allocate(sound_poll, NULL);
			hakios_audio_set_sink("the virtio sound device", sound_play);
		}
		return;
	}
	printf("virtio-sound: no sound device\n");
}
```

`drivers/bluetooth/hakios.bt.c`:

```c
/*
 * Bluetooth of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): STEP ONE, a look. Only with boot-arg bt=1, and it only READS.
 *
 * The phone's radio chip is a Qualcomm WCN6750, one chip for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth (the phone's device tree: the node
 * bt_wcn6750, compatible qcom,wcn6750-bt; the Wi-Fi half is drivers/wifi/hakios.wifi.c). What the device tree says
 * about the Bluetooth half, and what this file takes from it (numbers, not text):
 *
 *   qcom,bt-reset-gpio     GPIO 85    the Bluetooth half's reset / enable line
 *   qcom,bt-sw-ctrl-gpio   GPIO 86    the line that tells the radio's switch which half has the antenna
 *   qcom,wl-reset-gpio     GPIO 84    the Wi-Fi half's reset line, listed here too: the chip comes up as a whole
 *   the supplies (qcom,bt-vdd-*-supply, each with a -config of minimum and maximum microvolts; read out of the
 *   device tree by script, not by eye), the same for both halves:
 *       io 1800000..2000000    aon, dig, rfacmn, rfa-0p8 824000..1120000    rfa1 1872000..2040000
 *       rfa2 1256000..1500000  ipa-2p2 2200000..2210000                     asd 2800000..3544000
 *     (which regulator each supply is, is a phandle in the tree; nothing here writes any of them)
 *
 * What this does. At boot-arg bt=1 it reads the three pins' configuration and level out of the TLMM (the same
 * registers the haptic driver reads for its pins) and prints them, once at the start and once bt_again seconds later
 * (default 30), to see whether the Wi-Fi bring-up (wifi=1) moved the reset lines in between. It writes NOTHING: no
 * pin, no supply, no clock, no serial engine. Reading a pin's configuration is a plain load from the TLMM, which the
 * haptic and thermal drivers do on this phone without trouble.
 *
 * What is NOT here, and what it needs. Bluetooth on this chip, as Android and Linux (hci_qca, btqca) do it:
 *   1. the supplies on (they are shared with Wi-Fi: wifi=1 already raises what the Wi-Fi half needs),
 *   2. the reset line high, and the chip given a moment,
 *   3. the UART of the Bluetooth half opened at 115200 baud (a Qualcomm serial engine, "hsuart0" in the device tree:
 *      its clocks and its pins have to be set up first, and an access to an engine whose clock is off hangs the bus),
 *   4. the chip's own firmware loaded over that UART with Qualcomm's vendor commands (a rampatch and an NVM file out of
 *      /vendor/firmware on the phone: NOT in the repository, and not pulled by devices/redwood/pull-firmware.sh yet; Linux
 *      names them qca/msbtfw*.mbn and qca/msnv*.bin for the WCN6750, as I remember it, which is NOT verified here),
 *   5. the baud rate raised, then H4 packets (HCI) in both directions.
 * None of 1 to 5 is written, because none of it could be checked: the phone was not on the desk when this was written, and
 * the register numbers and command bytes for a chip are not the kind of thing to write from memory and ship. Each step comes
 * with a boot-arg level the way haptic=N and wifi_step=N did: the next one is bt=2 (supplies and reset line, seen on the
 * pins), after this one has been run and its output compared with a phone that is running Android.
 *
 * Status: COMPILED ONLY. Not run in QEMU (it has no such TLMM, and bt=1 must not be given there: a load from an address it
 * does not map faults) and not run on the phone.
 *
 * Boot-args:
 *   bt=1           the look
 *   bt_again=<s>   the second look this many seconds later (0: no second look; 30)
 */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[200];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	return printf("%s", line);
}

#define TLMM_PHYS               0x0f100000UL
#define TLMM_SIZE               0x100000UL
#define GPIO_CFG(n)             (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n))         /* [1:0] pull, [5:2] function, [8:6] drive, [9] output */
#define GPIO_IO(n)              (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n) + 4)     /* bit 0 in, bit 1 out */
#define CFG_OUTPUT              (1u << 9)

static vm_offset_t tlmm;
static uint32_t again_seconds = 30;
static thread_call_t again_call;

/* The three pins of the device tree's bt_wcn6750 node. */
static const struct {
	unsigned pin;
	const char *what;
} pins[] = {
	{ 84, "qcom,wl-reset-gpio: the Wi-Fi half's reset" },
	{ 85, "qcom,bt-reset-gpio: the Bluetooth half's reset" },
	{ 86, "qcom,bt-sw-ctrl-gpio: the antenna switch" },
};

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

/* One look at the pins: what the TLMM says each is set to, and the level it reads. Nothing is written. */
static void
look(const char *when)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(pins) / sizeof(pins[0]); i++) {
		uint32_t cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(pins[i].pin)), io = rd(GPIO_IO(pins[i].pin));

		say("bt: %s: gpio%u (%s): function %u, pull %u, %u mA, %s, reads %u\n", when, pins[i].pin, pins[i].what, (cfg >> 2) & 15,
		    cfg & 3, (((cfg >> 6) & 7) + 1) * 2, (cfg & CFG_OUTPUT) ? (io & 2 ? "drives high" : "drives low") : "input", io & 1);
	}
}

static void
look_again(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	look("again");
}

__startup_func
static void
bt_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0, value;
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("bt", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("bt_again", &value, sizeof(value)) && value <= 3600) {
		again_seconds = value;
	}
	tlmm = ml_io_map(TLMM_PHYS, TLMM_SIZE);
	if (tlmm == 0) {
		say("bt: could not map the TLMM; off\n");
		return;
	}
	say("bt: level 1: a look, reading only (WCN6750; nothing is written)\n");
	look("at start");
	if (again_seconds != 0) {
		again_call = thread_call_allocate(look_again, NULL);
		clock_interval_to_deadline(again_seconds, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(again_call, deadline);
	}
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, bt_init);
```

`drivers/camera/hakios.camera.c`:

```c
/*
 * The cameras of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): the macro one, an OmniVision OV02B10 (2 MP, Android's
 * camera 2, "hakios_aac_ov02b10_macro"), the wide one, a Samsung S5KHM2SD (108 MP, Android's
 * camera 0, "hakios_sunny_s5khm2sd_wide"), the front one and the ultra-wide one. Every address and
 * number below belongs to this phone, from Android's own device tree (cam-sensor0 to cam-sensor3 and
 * what they point to), the sensors' module files of Android's camera stack (/vendor/lib64/camera/com.qti.sensormodule.hakios_*.bin: the
 * slave address, the chip ID and where it is read, the power sequence, the tables) and the drivers
 * of the phone's kernel (MiCode hakios-s-oss: cam_sensor_util.c, qcom_pm8008-regulator.c,
 * camcc-yupik.c, gdsc-regulator.c, pinctrl-yupik.c, pinctrl-spmi-gpio.c, cam_csiphy_*), read as
 * data. The macro one (the others' differences are in sensors[] below and capture_sensor()):
 *
 *   the sensor     on CCI 1, master 0 (GPIO 73 data, 74 clock, function cci_i2c, internal pull-ups),
 *                  slave address 0x3c; done by hand here, as the other drivers do their I2C (the
 *                  two pins taken for each transaction and given back as they were found)
 *   chip ID        Android reads it as a 16-bit register at the 16-bit address 0x0203 and wants
 *                  0x002b (mask 0xffff); done the same way here
 *   reset          GPIO 77, high = running
 *   MCLK           camcc's mclk2 (RCG 0xe038, branch 0xe050) at 19.2 MHz on GPIO 66 (function
 *                  cam_mclk, 4 mA); Android takes the 19.2 MHz from camcc's PLL2 (M/N 1/75), here
 *                  it is the crystal's own 19.2 MHz (the RCG's source 0), with no PLL to start.
 *                  Before it Android switches on the camera's top power domain ("cam_clk":
 *                  titan_top_gdsc, camcc 0xc194), and so does this.
 *   VDIG (DOVDD)   PM8008i's LDO6 at 1.8 V; VANA (AVDD) its LDO7 at 2.8 V (the device tree's
 *                  voltages, normal power mode for the load Android asks). The PM8008i is on the
 *                  serial engine 1's I2C (GPIO 4 data, 5 clock; addresses 0x08 for the chip, 0x09
 *                  for the regulators, 16-bit registers), done by hand too; its reset pin is
 *                  PM8350C GPIO 3 (output high, as Android's pinctrl "pm8008i_active" has it)
 *   power-up       (the module file's): reset low, 1 ms; VDIG on; VANA on, 2 ms; MCLK on, 4 ms;
 *                  reset high, 9 ms. Power-down: MCLK off; reset low, 1 ms; VANA off, 7 ms; VDIG off.
 *                  (Both are read from the sensor's table at run time, as the wide one's are.)
 *
 * The wide one: CCI 0 master 1 (GPIO 71/72), slave address 0x20, chip ID 0xfad2 at 0x0000, reset
 * GPIO 21, MCLK1 (RCG 0xe01c, branch 0xe034, GPIO 65); VDIG the PM8008i's LDO1 at 1.0 V, VIO its
 * LDO5 at 1.8 V, VANA a fixed 2.8 V regulator that GPIO 106 switches; three C-PHY trios into
 * CSIPHY 1.
 *
 * The front one, an OmniVision OV16A1Q (16 MP, cam-sensor1): CCI 0 master 0 (GPIO 69/70), slave
 * 0x10, chip ID 0x1641 at 0x300b, reset GPIO 20, MCLK0 (GPIO 64); VANA LDO3 at 2.8 V, VDIG LDO2 at
 * 1.2 V, VIO LDO5 at 1.8 V; four D-PHY lanes into CSIPHY 0.
 *
 * The ultra-wide one, a Samsung S5K4H7 (8 MP, cam-sensor3): CCI 1 master 1 (GPIO 75/76), slave
 * 0x2d, chip ID 0x487b at 0x0000, reset GPIO 78, MCLK3 (GPIO 67) at the 24 MHz its module file
 * asks for, from camcc's PLL2 (Android's 1440 MHz Zonda configuration); VANA LDO4 at 2.8 V, VIO
 * LDO5 at 1.8 V, VDIG a fixed 1.2 V regulator that GPIO 108 switches; four D-PHY lanes into CSIPHY 3.
 *
 * Nothing here is done unless a boot-arg asks for it:
 *
 *   cam=1   a look, reading only: the camera's clocks and power domain as they are, the pins, the
 *           PM8008i's reset pin, and if it is out of reset the PM8008i itself (its chip enable and
 *           the two LDOs)
 *   cam=2   ... and the sensor powered up as Android powers it, its chip ID read, and powered
 *           down again (every write read back)
 *   cam=3   the CSID's test pattern through RDI 0 and IFE-lite 0 into memory, which the loader hands
 *           to the host after the run (xl camera): the camera subsystem's rails, PLL, clocks, SMMU
 *           and blocks without the sensor (capture_tpg() below)
 *   cam=4   the sensor's own frames that way, through its CSIPHY (capture_sensor() below)
 *
 * Boot-arg cam_sensor=wide picks the wide sensor; without it, the macro one.
 *
 * Limits, whatever asks: Android's voltages only (the device tree's: 1.8 and 2.8 V for the macro
 * one, 1.0 and 1.8 V for the wide one, 1.2, 1.8 and 2.8 V for the front one, 1.8 and 2.8 V for the
 * ultra-wide one; nothing else is ever written to the LDOs' set points); only the registers named above are written (a list each, checked at every
 * write) and each is read back; any write that does not read back, a regulator that is not ready
 * in time or reports over-current, a byte nobody acknowledges, and everything is switched off again
 * in the power-down's order and nothing more is done. At the run's end (and on a panic's way out)
 * whatever was switched on is switched off. Everything that was found switched on is left on.
 * The camera subsystem's own registers (camcc's PLL0 and the clocks named there, the sensor's CSIPHY,
 * CSID-lite 0, IFE-lite 0, one match register and context of the SMMU) are written the same way, read back
 * where they keep what they are given, and taken back in the reverse order.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <vm/memory_types.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <sys/hakios.audio.h>
#include <sys/hakios.camera.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static uint32_t level;
static bool broken, leaving;

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

/* every line to the loader's log as well (and to the console when that may be written) */
static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != '\0'; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (!leaving && ml_get_interrupts_enabled()) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
	return length;
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static void
wait_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	if (leaving) {
		spin_us(ms * 1000);
	} else {
		delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

static void
give_up(const char *why)
{
	if (!broken) {
		broken = true;
		say("camera: %s: nothing more is written in this run\n", why);
	}
}

/* ---- pins ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define TLMM_PHYS               0x0f100000UL
#define TLMM_SIZE               0x100000UL
#define GPIO_CFG(n)             (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n))         /* [1:0] pull, [5:2] function, [8:6] drive, [9] output */
#define GPIO_IO(n)              (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n) + 4)     /* bit 0 in, bit 1 out */
#define CFG_PULL_UP             3
#define CFG_OUTPUT              (1u << 9)
#define CFG_FUNCTION(f)         ((uint32_t)(f) << 2)
#define CFG_DRIVE_MA(ma)        ((uint32_t)((ma) / 2 - 1) << 6)

#define PIN_PMIC_SDA            4       /* the serial engine 1's I2C: the PM8008i */
#define PIN_PMIC_SCL            5

static vm_offset_t tlmm;

/*
 * The four sensors, as Android's device tree has them (cam-sensor2 the macro, cam-sensor0 the wide,
 * cam-sensor1 the front, cam-sensor3 the ultra-wide): the pins of their CCI master (taken by hand),
 * the reset, MCLK (camcc RCG and branch, the pin and its function 1, cam_mclk, at 4 mA), the supplies
 * the module file's power sequence switches (a PM8008i LDO at the device tree's voltage, or a GPIO
 * that switches a fixed regulator), the CSIPHY with its clocks, and how the sensor's exposure
 * registers are laid out. Boot-arg cam_sensor=macro|wide|front|ultra picks one (default: the macro,
 * and for cam=5 the wide).
 */
enum { SUPPLY_NONE, SUPPLY_LDO, SUPPLY_GPIO };
struct supply {
	uint8_t         kind, ldo;      /* SUPPLY_LDO: PM8008i LDO n ... */
	uint16_t        mv;             /* ... at this set point (the device tree's) */
	uint16_t        gpio, ramp_us;  /* SUPPLY_GPIO: the pin, active high, and the regulator's ramp */
};
struct sensor_hw {
	const char *    name;
	const char *    tab;            /* in fw/ of the small image (tools/camsensor.py) */
	const char *    bus_name;
	unsigned        sda, scl, reset;
	uint32_t        mclk_cmd, mclk_cbcr;
	unsigned        mclk_pin;
	struct supply   vana, vdig, vio;
	unsigned        csiphy;
	uint32_t        phy_cbcr, timer_cmd, timer_cbcr;
	uint8_t         regs;           /* the exposure registers: REGS_OV_PAGED, REGS_SMIA or REGS_OV16 */
	uint8_t         bayer;          /* the picture's order as it comes here (camraw.py's codes: 1 GRBG, 3 BGGR) */
	uint8_t         pattern_bayer;  /* ... and its own colour bars' (its module file's "tpgon") */
	const char *    chip;           /* for the frames' header */
	uint16_t        gain_unity, gain_max;   /* the analog gain register's 1x, and the most it is given */
};
enum {
	REGS_OV_PAGED,                  /* OmniVision, 8-bit registers in pages (0xfd): exposure 0x0e/0x0f, gain 0x22, VTS 0x14/0x15 */
	REGS_SMIA,                      /* SMIA: frame length 0x0340, coarse integration 0x0202, analog gain 0x0204, hold 0x0104 */
	REGS_OV16,                      /* OmniVision, 16-bit addresses: exposure 0x3500.., gain 0x3508, VTS 0x380e, hold 0x3208 */
};
static const struct sensor_hw sensors[] = {
	{       /* cam-sensor2: OV02B10, CCI 1 master 0 (GPIO 73/74), reset GPIO 77, MCLK2 (GPIO 66), csiphy 2 */
		.name = "macro (OV02B10)", .tab = "camera-ov02b10.tab", .bus_name = "CCI 1 master 0", .sda = 73, .scl = 74, .reset = 77,

		.csiphy = 2, .phy_cbcr = 0xe110, .timer_cmd = 0xe0f4, .timer_cbcr = 0xe10c, .regs = REGS_OV_PAGED, .bayer = 3,
		.pattern_bayer = 2, .chip = "OV02B10", .gain_unity = 16, .gain_max = 0xf8,
	},
	{       /* cam-sensor0: S5KHM2SD, CCI 0 master 1 (GPIO 71/72), reset GPIO 21, MCLK1 (GPIO 65), csiphy 1;
		 * VANA: camera_wide_vana_ldo, a fixed 2.8 V regulator from BOB switched by GPIO 106 (ramp 135 us) */
		.name = "wide (S5KHM2SD)", .tab = "camera-s5khm2sd.tab", .bus_name = "CCI 0 master 1", .sda = 71, .scl = 72, .reset = 21,

static const struct sensor_hw *hw = &sensors[0];
static unsigned hw_index;

static void
show_pin(unsigned pin, const char *what)
{
	uint32_t cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(pin)), io = rd(GPIO_IO(pin));

	say("camera: gpio%u (%s): function %u, pull %u, %u mA, %s, reads %u\n", pin, what, (cfg >> 2) & 15, cfg & 3,
	    (((cfg >> 6) & 7) + 1) * 2, (cfg & CFG_OUTPUT) ? (io & 2 ? "drives high" : "drives low") : "input", io & 1);
}

/* The pins written while powered up, as they were found, to be put back: the reset pin, MCLK's, a supply's. */
static uint32_t found_reset_cfg, found_reset_io, found_mclk_cfg, found_vana_cfg, found_vana_io;
static bool pins_found;

/* the sensor's reset and MCLK pins as they are now (to be put back when it is powered down) */
static void
find_pins(void)
{
	found_reset_cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(hw->reset));
	found_reset_io = rd(GPIO_IO(hw->reset));
	found_mclk_cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(hw->mclk_pin));
	pins_found = true;
}

static void
reset_pin(bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(hw->reset), high ? 2 : 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(hw->reset), CFG_OUTPUT | CFG_DRIVE_MA(2));         /* GPIO, no pull, 2 mA: Android's cam_sensor_active_* */
}

/* ---- I2C by hand (as in hakios.haptic.c) ---------------------------------------------------------- */

struct bus {
	const char *    name;
	unsigned        sda, scl;
	uint32_t        cfg[2], io[2];  /* the pins as they were found, while taken */
};
static struct bus pmic_bus = { .name = "the PM8008i's I2C", .sda = PIN_PMIC_SDA, .scl = PIN_PMIC_SCL };
static struct bus cci_bus;              /* the sensor's (from hw) */

static void
half_bit(void)
{
	spin_us(5);                     /* 100 kHz at most */
}

static void
line(unsigned pin, bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(pin), 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(pin), CFG_PULL_UP | (high ? 0 : CFG_OUTPUT));
}

static bool
level_of(unsigned pin)
{
	return rd(GPIO_IO(pin)) & 1;
}

static void
i2c_start(struct bus *b)
{
	line(b->sda, true);
	line(b->scl, true);
	half_bit();
	line(b->sda, false);
	half_bit();
	line(b->scl, false);
	half_bit();
}

static void
i2c_stop(struct bus *b)
{
	line(b->sda, false);
	half_bit();
	line(b->scl, true);
	half_bit();
	line(b->sda, true);
	half_bit();
}

static bool
i2c_bit(struct bus *b, bool out)
{
	bool in;

	line(b->sda, out);
	half_bit();
	line(b->scl, true);
```
