```c
	problem = wait_done(channel);
	data[0] = rd(channel + OBSERVER_DATA0);
	data[1] = count > 4 ? rd(channel + OBSERVER_DATA1) : 0;
	unlock();
	if (problem != NULL) {
		return problem;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		bytes[i] = (uint8_t)(data[i / 4] >> (8 * (i % 4)));
	}
	return NULL;
}

/* ---- the flash LED module -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define FLASH_REVISION1         0x00
#define FLASH_TYPE              0x04            /* 0x18: a flash LED module */
#define FLASH_SUBTYPE           0x05            /* 0x07: four channels */
#define FLASH_STATUS1           0x06            /* a channel open or shorted */
#define FLASH_STATUS2           0x07
#define  STATUS2_OTST1          0x20            /* over-temperature, the first and the second threshold */
#define  STATUS2_OTST2          0x10
#define  STATUS2_VPH_LOW        0x01            /* the supply drooped */
#define FLASH_INT_RT_STS        0x10
#define  RT_STS_FAULT           0x01            /* open, short, or its supply not ready */
#define FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0     0x3e            /* [7] on */
#define FLASH_ITARGET0          0x42            /* [6:0]: (code + 1) x the resolution */
#define FLASH_MODULE_EN         0x46            /* [7] */
#define FLASH_IRESOLUTION       0x49            /* a bit per channel: 0 12.5 mA, 1 5 mA */
#define FLASH_STROBE_CTRL0      0x4a            /* [6:4] hardware strobe's kind, [2] hardware strobe */
#define FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL       0x4e            /* a bit per channel */
#define FLASH_OTST2_CFG1        0x78
#define FLASH_OTST1_CFG1        0x7a

#define ALARM_SUBTYPE           0x05            /* 0x08: the first generation, 0x09 the second */
#define ALARM_STATUS            0x08            /* the over-temperature stage: [1:0] (first generation) or [6:4] */

#define ANDROID_TORCH_MA        125             /* led:torch_0 while Android's flashlight is on */
#define IRES_UA                 12500           /* its resolution ("qcom,ires-ua") */
#define ANDROID_ITARGET         9               /* round(125000 / 12500) - 1: the most ever written */
#define HOTTEST_BATTERY_C       45

static const uint8_t writable_regs[] = {
	FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0, FLASH_ITARGET0, FLASH_MODULE_EN, FLASH_IRESOLUTION, FLASH_STROBE_CTRL0, FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL,
};

static void
give_up(const char *why)
{
	if (!broken) {
		broken = true;
		note("%s: no more writing to the flash module for the rest of the run", why);
	}
}

/*
 * One register of the flash module (and of the six above only) written and read back: false, and
 * no more writing, if it cannot be or does not read back.
 */
static bool
put(uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
{
	const char *problem;
	uint8_t back = 0xff;
	bool allowed = false;

	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(writable_regs); i++) {
		allowed |= writable_regs[i] == reg;
	}
	/* (the latch does not stop dark(): after a failed write the final "off" would otherwise do nothing and the LED stay on) */
	if ((broken && !forcing) || !allowed || !flash.writable || flash.write == 0 || flash.id != 0x2ee) {
		give_up(allowed ? "a write that may not be made" : "a register that is not to be written");
		return false;
	}
	/* (the channel is still the module's: its entry in the arbiter's table is looked at again) */
	if (((rd(arb_core + ARB_CHANNEL(flash.channel)) >> 8) & 0xfff) != flash.id) {
		give_up("the arbiter's channel is no longer the flash module's");
		return false;
	}
	for (int tries = 0; tries < 3; tries++) {
		lock();
		wr(flash.write + CHANNEL_WDATA0, value);
		wr(flash.write + CHANNEL_COMMAND, COMMAND_WRITE | (uint32_t)reg << 4);
		problem = wait_done(flash.write);
		unlock();
		if (problem == NULL || strcmp(problem, DROPPED) != 0) {
			break;          /* (a dropped write has not been made: asked for again, then read back) */
		}
	}
	if (problem != NULL || (problem = spmi_read(&flash, reg, &back, 1)) != NULL) {
		say("torch: %#04x <- %#04x: %s\n", reg, value, problem);
		give_up("a write that failed");
		return false;
	}
	if (back != value) {
		say("torch: %#04x <- %#04x, but it reads %#04x\n", reg, value, back);
		give_up("a register that did not read back as written");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static bool
get(const struct peripheral *p, uint8_t reg, uint8_t *value)
{
	const char *problem = spmi_read(p, reg, value, 1);

	if (problem != NULL) {
		say("torch: reading %#04x of %s: %s\n", reg, p->name, problem);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* only the bits of `mask' changed, as the driver's masked writes do */
static bool
put_bits(uint8_t reg, uint8_t mask, uint8_t value)
{
	uint8_t now;

	if (!get(&flash, reg, &now)) {
		give_up("a read that failed");
		return false;
	}
	return (now & mask) == (value & mask) || put(reg, (uint8_t)((now & ~mask) | (value & mask)));
}

static void
find_channel(struct peripheral *p, uint32_t channels)
{
	for (uint32_t n = 0; n < channels; n++) {
		uint32_t map = rd(arb_core + ARB_CHANNEL(n)), owner;

		if (map == 0 || ((map >> 8) & 0xfff) != p->id) {
			continue;
		}
		owner = rd(arb_cnfg + ARB_OWNER(n)) & 7;
		say("torch: channel %u is %s (%#x); written by system %u%s\n", n, p->name, map, owner,
		    owner == ARB_SYSTEM ? ", which is us" : "");
		if (!p->found || owner == ARB_SYSTEM) {
			p->found = true;
			p->channel = (uint16_t)n;
			p->writable = owner == ARB_SYSTEM;
		}
	}
	if (!p->found) {
		say("torch: no channel of the arbiter is %s\n", p->name);
	}
}

static void
show_registers(void)
{
	uint8_t r[8];
	char line[200];

	for (unsigned base = 0; base < 0x100; base += 0x20) {
		int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "torch: %#04x:", base);

		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 0x20; i += 8) {
			if (spmi_read(&flash, (uint8_t)(base + i), r, 8) != NULL) {
				n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " (unreadable)");
				continue;
			}
			for (unsigned j = 0; j < 8; j++) {
				n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " %02x", r[j]);
			}
		}
		say("%s\n", line);
	}
}

/* What would make the light go off now, or NULL. */
static const char *
trouble(void)
{
	static char why[180];
	uint8_t rt = 0, status1 = 0, status2 = 0, alarm_status = 0, stage;

	if (!get(&flash, FLASH_INT_RT_STS, &rt) || !get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS1, &status1) ||
	    !get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS2, &status2) || (alarm.found && !get(&alarm, ALARM_STATUS, &alarm_status))) {
		return "a read of the flags that failed";
	}
	stage = alarm_subtype == 0x08 ? alarm_status & 0x03 : (alarm_status >> 4) & 0x07;
	if ((rt & RT_STS_FAULT) || status1 != 0 || (status2 & (STATUS2_OTST1 | STATUS2_OTST2 | STATUS2_VPH_LOW)) || stage != 0) {
		uint8_t more[8] = { 0 }, latched[2] = { 0 };

		(void)spmi_read(&flash, 0x06, more, 8);
		(void)spmi_read(&flash, 0x18, latched, 2);
		snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "the module says fault %#x, channels %#x, temperature and supply %#x (0x06-0x0d: %02x %02x %02x "
		    "%02x %02x %02x %02x %02x, latched %#x); the PMIC's temperature stage %u", rt, status1, status2, more[0], more[1],
		    more[2], more[3], more[4], more[5], more[6], more[7], latched[0], stage);
		return why;
	}
	if (hakios_battery_temperature() >= HOTTEST_BATTERY_C) {
		snprintf(why, sizeof(why), "the battery is at %d C", hakios_battery_temperature());
		return why;
	}
	return NULL;
}

static bool configured, lit;

/* Android's probe, once: channel 0 strobed by software, its safety timer off. */
static bool
configure(void)
{
	if (!configured && put_bits(FLASH_STROBE_CTRL0, 0x74, 0x00) && put_bits(FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0, 0x80, 0x00)) {
		configured = true;
	}
	return configured;
}

/* The light at `permille' of Android's current: its writes in its order. */
static bool
light(uint32_t permille)
{
	uint32_t ua = ANDROID_TORCH_MA * 1000 * permille / 1000, code;
	const char *why;

	if (ua < IRES_UA) {
		ua = IRES_UA;           /* (the driver's least: one step) */
	}
	code = (ua + IRES_UA / 2) / IRES_UA - 1;
	if (code > ANDROID_ITARGET) {
		code = ANDROID_ITARGET;
	}
	if (!lit && (why = trouble()) != NULL) {
		note("not lit: %s", why);
		give_up("trouble before the light");
		return false;
	}
	if (!configure() || !put_bits(FLASH_IRESOLUTION, 0x01, 0x00) || !put_bits(FLASH_ITARGET0, 0x7f, (uint8_t)code)) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!lit) {
		/* lit is set before the enabling writes: one that lands but fails its read-back must still get a dark() later */
		lit = true;
		if (!put(FLASH_MODULE_EN, 0x80) || !put_bits(FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, 0x01, 0x01)) {
			return false;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

/* Off, in Android's order: the channel, the module, the target current, the timer's bit. */
static bool
dark(void)
{
	bool ok;

	/* every step is tried even if an earlier one failed, and none is stopped by `broken': a half-done "off" leaves the LED on */
	forcing = true;
	ok = put_bits(FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, 0x01, 0x00);
	ok = put(FLASH_MODULE_EN, 0x00) && ok;
	ok = put_bits(FLASH_ITARGET0, 0x7f, 0x00) && ok;
	ok = put_bits(FLASH_SAFETY_TIMER0, 0x80, 0x00) && ok;
	forcing = false;
	lit = !ok && lit;
	return ok;
}

/* ---- torch=3: the light for Darwin --------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static volatile uint32_t wanted;                /* the level asked for last, 0 to 1000 */
static volatile uint32_t asked;                 /* how many times one was */
static uint32_t max_secs = 30;

static int
torch_write(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	uint32_t value;
	int error;

	while (uio_resid(uio) >= (user_ssize_t)sizeof(value)) {
		if ((error = uiomove((caddr_t)&value, sizeof(value), uio)) != 0) {
			return error;
		}
		wanted = value > 1000 ? 1000 : value;
		asked++;
	}
	return 0;
}

/* what is lit now: the level, 0 if nothing */
static uint32_t shown;

static int
torch_read(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	uint32_t value = shown;

	return uiomove((caddr_t)&value, (int)MIN(sizeof(value), (size_t)uio_resid(uio)), uio);
}

static int
torch_open(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int type, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static const struct cdevsw torch_cdevsw = {
	.d_open = torch_open, .d_close = torch_open, .d_read = torch_read, .d_write = torch_write,
	.d_ioctl = eno_ioctl, .d_stop = eno_stop, .d_reset = eno_reset, .d_select = eno_select,
	.d_mmap = eno_mmap, .d_strategy = eno_strat, .d_type = 0
};

static uint64_t
now_ms(void)
{
	uint64_t ns;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &ns);
	return ns / NSEC_PER_MSEC;
}

static void
serve(void)
{
	uint32_t applied = 0, times = 0, cut = 0;
	uint64_t since = 0, last_look = 0;
	bool waiting_for_off = false;           /* cut at the limit: dark until Darwin asks for 0 */
	int major = cdevsw_add(-1, &torch_cdevsw);

	if (major < 0 || devfs_make_node(makedev(major, 0), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "hakios-torch") == NULL) {
		say("torch: /dev/hakios-torch cannot be made\n");
		return;
	}
	say("torch: THE LIGHT IS DARWIN'S (/dev/hakios-torch) from here on, until the run ends: at most Android's %u mA, at most %u s "
	    "at a time\n", ANDROID_TORCH_MA, max_secs);
	while (!broken) {
		uint32_t want = wanted;
		uint64_t now = now_ms();

		if (want == 0) {
			waiting_for_off = false;
		}
		if (waiting_for_off) {
			want = 0;
		}
		if (want != applied) {
			if (want == 0 ? dark() : light(want)) {
				if (applied == 0) {
					since = now;
					times++;
				}
				if (want == 0) {
					note("off (Darwin asked for 0)");
				} else {
					note("ON (Darwin asked for %u of 1000; the battery %d C)", wanted, hakios_battery_temperature());
				}
				applied = want;
				shown = want;
			} else {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (applied != 0 && now - since >= max_secs * 1000ull) {
			cut++;
			note("on for %u s, the limit: off until Darwin asks again", max_secs);
			waiting_for_off = true;
			if (!dark()) {
				break;
			}
			applied = 0;
			shown = 0;
			continue;
		}
		if (applied != 0 && now - last_look >= 100) {
			const char *why;

			last_look = now;
			if ((why = trouble()) != NULL) {
				note("OFF: %s", why);
				(void)dark();
				give_up("trouble while lit");
				break;
			}
		}
		wait_ms(20);
	}
	if (lit) {
		(void)dark();
	}
	shown = 0;
	say("torch: the light is given up on (%u times lit, %u cut at %u s)\n", times, cut, max_secs);
}

/* ---- the start ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
torch_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	uint32_t version, channels;
	uint8_t id[2] = { 0, 0 }, revision = 0, alarm_status = 0;

	say("torch: level %u: %s\n", level, level == 1 ? "a look, reading only" : level == 2 ? "the light on once" :
	    "the light for Darwin");
	arb_core = ml_io_map(ARB_CORE_PHYS, ARB_CORE_SIZE);
	arb_cnfg = ml_io_map(ARB_CNFG_PHYS, ARB_CNFG_SIZE);
	arb_observer = ml_io_map(ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS, ARB_OBSERVER_SIZE);
	version = rd(arb_core + ARB_VERSION);
	channels = rd(arb_core + ARB_FEATURES) & 0x7ff;
	if (version < ARB_VERSION_5 || version >= ARB_VERSION_7) {
		say("torch: PMIC arbiter version %#x, not 5: nothing done\n", version);
		goto out;
	}
	if (channels == 0 || channels > ARB_MAX_CHANNELS) {
		channels = ARB_MAX_CHANNELS;
	}
	find_channel(&flash, channels);
	find_channel(&alarm, channels);
	if (!flash.found || spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_TYPE, id, 2) != NULL || spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_REVISION1, &revision, 1) != NULL) {
		say("torch: the flash module cannot be read\n");
		goto out;
	}
	say("torch: the module says type %#x, subtype %#x, revision %#x%s\n", id[0], id[1], revision,
	    id[0] == 0x18 && id[1] == 0x07 ? ": a flash LED module of four channels, as Android's driver expects" : ": NOT WHAT WAS EXPECTED");
	show_registers();
	if (alarm.found && get(&alarm, ALARM_SUBTYPE, &alarm_subtype) && get(&alarm, ALARM_STATUS, &alarm_status)) {
		uint8_t stage = alarm_subtype == 0x08 ? alarm_status & 0x03 : (alarm_status >> 4) & 0x07;

		say("torch: the PMIC's temperature alarm (subtype %#x) says %#x: stage %u%s\n", alarm_subtype, alarm_status, stage,
		    stage == 0 ? " (all is well)" : "");
	} else {
		alarm.found = false;
	}
	if (id[0] != 0x18 || id[1] != 0x07 || level < 2) {
		goto out;
	}
	if (!flash.writable) {
		say("torch: the channel is not ours to write through: nothing written\n");
		goto out;
	}
	flash.write = ml_io_map(ARB_CHNLS_PHYS + 0x10000UL * flash.channel, 0x1000);
	PE_parse_boot_argn("torch_max_s", &max_secs, sizeof(max_secs));
	max_secs = max_secs < 1 ? 1 : max_secs > 120 ? 120 : max_secs;
	if (level == 2) {
		uint32_t secs = 2;
		uint64_t until;
		const char *why = NULL;

		PE_parse_boot_argn("torch_secs", &secs, sizeof(secs));
		secs = secs < 1 ? 1 : secs > max_secs ? max_secs : secs;
		say("torch: the light ON at Android's %u mA (ITARGET %u, 12.5 mA steps) for %u s\n", ANDROID_TORCH_MA, ANDROID_ITARGET,
		    secs);
		if (light(1000)) {
			uint8_t rt = 0, s1 = 0, s2 = 0;

			wait_ms(50);
			(void)get(&flash, FLASH_INT_RT_STS, &rt);
			(void)get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS1, &s1);
			(void)get(&flash, FLASH_STATUS2, &s2);
			note("lit at Android's %u mA; 50 ms on: interrupt status %#x (%s), channels %#x, temperature and supply %#x",
			    ANDROID_TORCH_MA, rt, (rt & 0x10) ? "ramped up" : "NOT ramped up", s1, s2);
			show_registers();
			for (until = now_ms() + secs * 1000ull; now_ms() < until && (why = trouble()) == NULL;) {
				wait_ms(100);
			}
			if (why != NULL) {
				note("OFF early: %s", why);
			}
			if (dark()) {
				note("off again after %u s", secs);
			}
			show_registers();
		} else if (lit) {
			/* light() failed after it may have enabled the channel: switch it off again */
			(void)dark();
		}
	} else {
		serve();
	}
out:
	say("torch: done\n");
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
hakios_torch_init(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("torch", &level, sizeof(level)) || level == 0) {
		return;
	}
	level = level > 3 ? 3 : level;
	if (kernel_thread_start(torch_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}

/* At the run's end and on a panic's way out: the light off, if it was ever lit. */
void
hakios_torch_quiesce(void)
{
	uint8_t module = 0xff, channels = 0xff, target = 0xff;

	if (level < 2 || flash.write == 0) {
		return;
	}
	leaving = true;
	if (lit) {
		broken = false;         /* (one last time, whatever went before) */
		say("torch: at the run's end: the light %s\n", dark() ? "switched off" : "COULD NOT BE SWITCHED OFF");
	}
	say("torch: what happened in this run (%u events):\n", noted);
	for (unsigned i = noted > NOTES ? noted - NOTES : 0; i < noted; i++) {
		say("torch:   %s\n", notes[i % NOTES]);
	}
	(void)spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_MODULE_EN, &module, 1);
	(void)spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_EN_LED_CTRL, &channels, 1);
	(void)spmi_read(&flash, FLASH_ITARGET0, &target, 1);
	say("torch: at the run's end the module reads: enable %#04x, channels %#04x, target %#04x%s\n", module, channels, target,
	    module == 0 && (channels & 0x01) == 0 && target == 0 ? " (dark)" : " (NOT DARK)");
}

```

`drivers/core/conf`:

```
# drivers/core/conf: what is part of every kernel of this port, and the chip's identity.
# CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y in a defconfig builds a driver into the kernel; "standard" files are always built.
# tools/hakios-config.py reads this file; docs/drivers-config.md says what each word means and how it reaches XNU.

standard bsd/dev/hakios.version.c
	help    kern.hakios.version, and the version in the boot log

standard bsd/dev/hakios.platform.c
	help    what the drivers share (the locks of the PMIC arbiter, the always-on processor, RPMh and the SMMU), and
	help    kern.hakios.drivers, the list of the drivers built in

standard bsd/dev/hakios.stubs.c
	help    what the rest of the kernel calls in a driver that is left out: nothing, and "not there"

standard iokit/Kernel/hakios.stubs.cpp iokitcpp
	help    the same, for the calls that are C++ (the display asking whether the GPU is done with a surface)

driver SOCINFO
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.socinfo.c
	help    the chip's identity from the firmware's shared memory: kern.hakios.soc_* (socinfo=1). Any Qualcomm SoC
	help    that keeps SMEM item 137; where the shared memory is comes from soc_smem=

```

`drivers/core/hakios.platform.c`:

```c
/*
 * What the drivers share, kept apart from any one of them, so that each can be left out of the kernel on its own
 * (drivers/<subsystem>/conf, CONFIG_HAKIOS_*: docs/drivers-config.md).
 *
 *   the locks      of the hardware several drivers take turns at: the PMIC arbiter (the buttons, the flashlight, the
 *                  camera's regulators, the PMIC survey), the always-on processor's mailbox, the shared memory's
 *                  allocation and RPMh's sequencer (the Wi-Fi, audio DSP and modem bring-ups, the touch screen's
 *                  supply), and the SMMU's free match registers (Wi-Fi, sound, camera, modem). They were in
 *                  hakios.buttons.c and hakios.wifi.c, which the others then needed in the kernel to link.
 *   kern.hakios    the sysctl node the drivers hang theirs under (it was hakios.battery.c's)
 *   the list       of the drivers this kernel was built with: sysctl kern.hakios.drivers, and a line in the boot log,
 *                  so that a run says what was in it (hakios.drivers.h is made by tools/hakios-config.py kernel).
 */
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

#include "hakios.drivers.h"

/* kern.hakios: the node every driver of this port hangs its sysctls under (it was hakios.battery.c's) */
SYSCTL_NODE(_kern, OID_AUTO, hakios, CTLFLAG_RW | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, 0, "redwood phone bits");

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(hakios_platform_lock_group, "hakios-platform");

/*
 * One transfer at a time through the PMIC arbiter for this system, whoever asks: with two at once the arbiter drops
 * one ("the transfer was dropped"), as Linux never lets happen (one lock for the bus). A spin lock: it is taken
 * around a transfer of some tens of microseconds.
 */
static LCK_SPIN_DECLARE(spmi_lock, &hakios_platform_lock_group);

void
hakios_spmi_lock(void)
{
	lck_spin_lock(&spmi_lock);
}

void
hakios_spmi_unlock(void)
{
	lck_spin_unlock(&spmi_lock);
}

/*
 * What the DSPs' starts use while another may be at work beside them: the mailbox to the always-on processor, one
 * message at a time, and the allocation of items in the shared memory (whose hardware lock both take under the same
 * number, so it does not keep the two apart); RPMh's sequencer (TCS 0 of the RSC); a free match register and context
 * of the SMMU, found and taken.
 */
LCK_MTX_DECLARE(hakios_aop_mailbox_lock, &hakios_platform_lock_group);
LCK_MTX_DECLARE(hakios_smem_alloc_lock, &hakios_platform_lock_group);
LCK_MTX_DECLARE(hakios_rsc_lock, &hakios_platform_lock_group);
LCK_MTX_DECLARE(hakios_smmu_lock, &hakios_platform_lock_group);

static char hakios_drivers_string[] = HAKIOS_DRIVERS_LIST;

SYSCTL_STRING(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, drivers, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, hakios_drivers_string, 0,
    "the drivers this kernel was built with (CONFIG_HAKIOS_* of its configuration, lowercase)");

static void
hakios_platform_init(void)
{
	printf("hakios-kernel: %d drivers built in (%s): %s\n", HAKIOS_DRIVERS_COUNT, HAKIOS_DRIVERS_CONFIG, hakios_drivers_string);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, hakios_platform_init);

```

`drivers/core/hakios.socinfo.c`:

```c
/*
 * What chip this is, from the chip itself: sysctl kern.hakios.soc_*. Only with boot-arg socinfo=1.
 *
 * Android's /sys/devices/soc0/{soc_id,revision,serial_number,machine,family,...} come from one item of the
 * SoC's shared memory ("SMEM"), which the boot firmware fills before anything else runs: the "socinfo"
 * structure (SMEM item 137). Linux's drivers/soc/qcom/socinfo.c reads it; so does this. It says which
 * chip and revision this is, which board (hardware platform and its subtype), which foundry made the die,
 * and the chip's serial number. (The structure also lists the board's power-management chips; this does not
 * read that part yet.) A kernel that is built for one SoC family can then check the phone it was put on really is one, instead of
 * trusting that the device tree handed to it came from this phone (docs/port-pkg110.md: a phone that
 * reports itself as another model is the case that made this worth writing).
 *
 * THIS DRIVER ONLY READS. The SMEM region is firmware's: 0x200000 bytes at soc_smem (the phone's device tree
 * reserves it as smem@80900000, no-map). It is read with byte loads only, because the memory is mapped as
 * device memory here and an unaligned or wide load of it would fault; every offset is checked against the
 * region before it is read, and a header that is not what it should be ends the search with a line that says
 * what was found instead.
 *
 * Where things are in SMEM (Linux drivers/soc/qcom/smem.c):
 *   - a table of "partitions" in the last 4 KB of the region ("$TOC"), one of which is the GLOBAL one (host
 *     0xfffe on both sides): a header ("$PRT") and, from its start, a chain of items, each a 16-byte entry
 *     (0xa5a5 canary, item number, size, padding) and then its data;
 *   - or, on the older layout, a header at the start of the region with a fixed table of 512 items.
 * Both are tried, the partition table first.
 *
 * The structure grows by appending; a field is read only when the item is long enough to hold it.
 *
 * Status (what has and has not been seen): written from Linux's smem.c and socinfo.c as remembered, not from a
 * copy of them. RUN ON THE PHONE (POCO X5 Pro, 2026-10-27, five runs): the item is found in the global partition and
 * says format 0xf, SoC 475 (the device tree's msm-id 0x1db), revision 1.0, board platform 11, foundry 1, 272 bytes, raw id
 * 402. What the first runs got wrong, and the diagnostic that found it: a partition-table entry is 48 bytes, not 32;
 * the older table at the start of the region is not there on this phone (its words are text), so the lookup in it
 * finds nothing and that is harmless. The firmware build string came out empty, and the PMIC list at the end of the
 * structure is not read. Not run in QEMU: QEMU has no SMEM, and the driver then says so and does nothing.
 *
 * Boot-args:
 *   socinfo=1        read it
 *   soc_smem=<pa>    where SMEM is (also the modem driver's argument; 0x80900000 on the reference phone)
 *   soc_smem_size=<n> its size (0x200000)
 */
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

SYSCTL_DECL(_kern_hakios);

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	return printf("%s", line);
}

#define SMEM_DEFAULT_PA         0x80900000UL
#define SMEM_DEFAULT_SIZE       0x200000UL
#define SMEM_HW_SW_BUILD_ID     137             /* the socinfo structure */

#define PTABLE_MAGIC            0x434f5424u     /* "$TOC" */
#define PART_MAGIC              0x54525024u     /* "$PRT" */
#define PTABLE_ENTRY            48              /* offset, size, flags, host0, host1, cacheline, reserved[7] (Linux smem.c) */
#define GLOBAL_HOST             0xfffeu
#define PRIVATE_CANARY          0xa5a5u
#define LEGACY_ITEMS            512
#define LEGACY_TOC_OFFSET       208             /* 4 proc_comm (64) + version[32] (128) + 4 words (16) */
#define LEGACY_SBL_VERSION      7               /* version[7]: 12 means the partitioned layout */

static vm_offset_t smem;
static vm_size_t smem_size;

static bool
inside(uint64_t offset, uint64_t length)
{
	return offset <= smem_size && length <= smem_size - offset;
}

static uint8_t
b8(uint64_t offset)
{
	return inside(offset, 1) ? *(volatile uint8_t *)(smem + offset) : 0;
}

static uint32_t
le16(uint64_t offset)
{
	return b8(offset) | (uint32_t)b8(offset + 1) << 8;
}

static uint32_t
le32(uint64_t offset)
{
	return le16(offset) | le16(offset + 2) << 16;
}

/*
 * Item `item` of the shared memory: its offset and length in the region, or false. `how` says
 * which layout it was found in, for the log.
 */
static bool
smem_item(uint32_t item, uint64_t *offset, uint64_t *length, const char **how)
{
	uint64_t table = smem_size - 0x1000;

	if (smem_size >= 0x2000 && le32(table) == PTABLE_MAGIC) {
		uint32_t entries = le32(table + 8);

		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < entries && i < 32; i++) {
			uint64_t entry = table + 32 + PTABLE_ENTRY * (uint64_t)i;
			uint32_t part_offset = le32(entry), part_size = le32(entry + 4);

			if (le16(entry + 12) != GLOBAL_HOST || le16(entry + 14) != GLOBAL_HOST || part_size == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			if (!inside(part_offset, part_size) || le32(part_offset) != PART_MAGIC) {
				say("socinfo: the global partition (offset %#x, size %#x) has no \"$PRT\" header (%#x)\n", part_offset,
				    part_size, inside(part_offset, 4) ? le32(part_offset) : 0);
				continue;
			}
			uint64_t at = part_offset + 32, end = part_offset + le32(part_offset + 16);       /* offset_free_uncached */

			if (end > (uint64_t)part_offset + part_size) {
				end = (uint64_t)part_offset + part_size;
			}
			while (at + 16 <= end) {
				uint32_t size = le32(at + 4), padding_hdr = le16(at + 10), padding_data = le16(at + 8);
				uint64_t data = at + 16 + padding_hdr;

				if (le16(at) != PRIVATE_CANARY) {
					say("socinfo: item chain broken at %#llx (canary %#x)\n", (unsigned long long)at, le16(at));
					break;
				}
				if (le16(at + 2) == item && size >= padding_data && inside(data, size - padding_data)) {
					*offset = data;
					*length = size - padding_data;
					*how = "the global partition";
					return true;
				}
				at = data + size;
			}
		}
	}
	/*
	 * The older layout, which Linux's qcom_smem_get_global() uses for every item that is not in a partition (and the
	 * socinfo is one): a header at the start of the region with a fixed table of 512 items. Not gated on the
	 * firmware's version word: the partitioned layout keeps this table for the items it has not moved.
	 */
	if (item < LEGACY_ITEMS) {
		uint64_t entry = LEGACY_TOC_OFFSET + 16 * (uint64_t)item;

		if (le32(entry) != 0 && inside(le32(entry + 4), le32(entry + 8))) {
			*offset = le32(entry + 4);
			*length = le32(entry + 8);
			*how = "the legacy table";
			return true;
		}
	}
	return false;
}

/* For a layout that is not what was expected: which items the legacy table has allocated (item number, size). */
static void
list_items(void)
{
	char line[200];
	unsigned shown = 0;

	line[0] = 0;
	for (uint32_t item = 0; item < LEGACY_ITEMS && shown < 24; item++) {
		uint64_t entry = LEGACY_TOC_OFFSET + 16 * (uint64_t)item;
		char one[24];

		if (le32(entry) == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		snprintf(one, sizeof(one), " %u:%u@%#x", item, le32(entry + 8), le32(entry + 4));
		strlcat(line, one, sizeof(line));
		shown++;
	}
	say("socinfo: the legacy table has allocated:%s%s; the partition table has %u entries\n", line[0] ? line : " nothing", shown == 24 ? " ..." : "",
	    le32(smem_size - 0x1000 + 8));
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < le32(smem_size - 0x1000 + 8) && i < 12; i++) {
		uint64_t entry = smem_size - 0x1000 + 32 + PTABLE_ENTRY * (uint64_t)i;

		say("socinfo:   partition %u: offset %#x size %#x hosts %#x/%#x, header magic there %#x\n", i, le32(entry), le32(entry + 4),
		    le16(entry + 12), le16(entry + 14), inside(le32(entry), 4) ? le32(le32(entry)) : 0);
	}
	say("socinfo: the first words of the region: %08x %08x %08x %08x %08x %08x %08x %08x\n", le32(0), le32(4), le32(8), le32(12),
	    le32(16), le32(20), le32(24), le32(28));
}

/* ---- what the structure holds ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static struct {
	bool            valid;
	uint32_t        fmt, id, version, raw_id, raw_version, hw_platform, platform_version, hw_subtype, foundry, serial,
	    family, raw_family, raw_num;
	char            build[33];
} soc;

static const struct { uint32_t id; const char *name; } known[] = {
	{ 415, "SM8350" }, { 439, "SM8350" }, { 457, "SM8450" }, { 475, "SC7280 (SM7325, \"yupik\")" },
	{ 487, "SC7280" }, { 497, "QCM6490" }, { 498, "QCS6490" }, { 483, "SM6350" }, { 434, "SM6350" },
	{ 480, "SM7225" }, { 459, "SM7225" }, { 416, "SM8250" }, { 356, "SM8250" },
};

static const char *
soc_name(uint32_t id)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(known) / sizeof(known[0]); i++) {
		if (known[i].id == id) {
			return known[i].name;
		}
	}
	return "an SoC this driver has no name for";
}

static void
parse(uint64_t at, uint64_t length)
{
	/*
	 * Offsets of the fields in struct socinfo (Linux socinfo.c). The structure grew by appending, so a field is
	 * read only when the item is long enough to hold it; one that is not there stays 0. (Linux does the same:
	 * it tests offsetof() against the item's size, not the format number.)
	 */
	#define FIELD(offset) (length >= (offset) + 4 ? le32(at + (offset)) : 0)

	soc.fmt = FIELD(0);
	soc.id = FIELD(4);
	soc.version = FIELD(8);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 32 && length >= 12 + i + 1; i++) {
		uint8_t c = b8(at + 12 + i);

		if (c == 0) {
			break;
		}
		soc.build[i] = (c >= 0x20 && c < 0x7f) ? (char)c : '?';
	}
	soc.raw_id = FIELD(44);
	soc.raw_version = FIELD(48);
	soc.hw_platform = FIELD(52);
	soc.platform_version = FIELD(56);
	soc.hw_subtype = FIELD(64);
	soc.foundry = FIELD(92);
	soc.serial = FIELD(96);
	soc.family = FIELD(108);
	soc.raw_family = FIELD(112);
	soc.raw_num = FIELD(116);
	#undef FIELD
}

static char soc_name_text[64] = "unknown";
static char soc_serial_text[16] = "";
static char soc_build_text[40] = "";
static int soc_id_value = -1;
static int soc_revision_value = -1;
static int soc_platform_value = -1;
static int soc_subtype_value = -1;
static int soc_foundry_value = -1;

SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_id, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &soc_id_value, 0,
    "the SoC's number in the firmware's table (475: SC7280/SM7325); -1: not read");
SYSCTL_STRING(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_name, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, soc_name_text, 0, "the SoC's name, as this kernel knows that number");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_revision, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &soc_revision_value, 0,
    "the chip revision, major << 16 | minor (0x10000 is 1.0)");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_platform, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &soc_platform_value, 0, "the board's hardware platform number");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_platform_subtype, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &soc_subtype_value, 0, "its subtype");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_foundry, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &soc_foundry_value, 0, "the foundry that made the die");
SYSCTL_STRING(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_serial, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, soc_serial_text, 0,
    "the chip's serial number (hex). It is this unit's, so it is not written to the log");
SYSCTL_STRING(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, soc_build, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, soc_build_text, 0, "the firmware's build id");

__startup_func
static void
socinfo_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0, pa = (uint32_t)SMEM_DEFAULT_PA, size = (uint32_t)SMEM_DEFAULT_SIZE;
	uint64_t offset, length;
	const char *how;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("socinfo", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	(void)PE_parse_boot_argn("soc_smem", &pa, sizeof(pa));
	(void)PE_parse_boot_argn("soc_smem_size", &size, sizeof(size));
	if (size < 0x2000 || size > 0x1000000) {
		say("socinfo: soc_smem_size=%#x is not a size SMEM can have; not read\n", size);
		return;
	}
	smem_size = size;
	smem = ml_io_map(pa, size);
	if (smem == 0) {
		say("socinfo: could not map %#x bytes at %#x\n", size, pa);
		return;
	}
	if (!smem_item(SMEM_HW_SW_BUILD_ID, &offset, &length, &how)) {
		say("socinfo: item %d is not in the shared memory at %#x (partition table magic %#x, legacy version word %#x)\n",
		    SMEM_HW_SW_BUILD_ID, pa, le32(smem_size - 0x1000), le32(4 * 4 * 4 + 4 * LEGACY_SBL_VERSION));
		list_items();
		return;
	}
	if (length < 56) {
		say("socinfo: item %d is %llu bytes, too short for a socinfo structure\n", SMEM_HW_SW_BUILD_ID, (unsigned long long)length);
		return;
	}
	parse(offset, length);
	soc.valid = true;
	soc_id_value = (int)soc.id;
	soc_revision_value = (int)soc.version;
	soc_platform_value = (int)soc.hw_platform;
	soc_subtype_value = (int)soc.hw_subtype;
	soc_foundry_value = (int)soc.foundry;
	strlcpy(soc_name_text, soc_name(soc.id), sizeof(soc_name_text));
	strlcpy(soc_build_text, soc.build, sizeof(soc_build_text));
	snprintf(soc_serial_text, sizeof(soc_serial_text), "%08x", soc.serial);
	say("socinfo: in %s: format %#x, SoC %u = %s, revision %u.%u, board platform %u (version %u, subtype %u), foundry %u,"
	    " %llu bytes, firmware build \"%s\"\n", how, soc.fmt, soc.id, soc_name_text, soc.version >> 16, soc.version & 0xffff,
	    soc.hw_platform, soc.platform_version, soc.hw_subtype, soc.foundry, (unsigned long long)length, soc.build);
	say("socinfo: raw id %u, raw version %#x; serial number ...%04x (all of it in kern.hakios.soc_serial)\n", soc.raw_id,
	    soc.raw_version, soc.serial & 0xffff);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, socinfo_init);

```

`drivers/core/hakios.stubs.c`:

```c
/*
 * What the rest of the kernel calls in a driver that is left out of it (CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME> not set: drivers/<subsystem>/conf,
 * docs/drivers-config.md), the way XNU keeps bsd/kern/bsd_stubs.c for its own parts that a configuration leaves out.
 *
 * The callers are the places that start the drivers (hakios.input.c, hakios.audio.c, bsd_init.c), that stop them on
 * the way back to the loader or out of a panic (loader_return.c, the thermal and battery guards, machine_routines.c)
 * and the few that ask a driver something on the way (is this device one of the storage's, what the battery's
 * temperature is). Each of them calls the driver unconditionally, as it did when every driver was always built; here,
 * for a driver that is not, is what each call then does: nothing, and the answer "no", "not known" or "not there".
 * A driver that is built gets none of this: every block below is for one driver, and empty when that one is in.
 *
 * What is not here, on purpose: a call from one driver to another that it cannot work without. That is a `requires`
 * of its conf (SOUND requires ADSP and SPEAKER, MODEM requires QMI and UFS, ...), and tools/hakios-config.py refuses
 * the configuration that would need a stand-in for it.
 */
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
```

`drivers/core/hakios.version.c`:

```c
/*
 * The version of this kernel: sysctl kern.hakios.version, and a line in the boot log.
 *
 * Where the string comes from. VERSION (at the top of the repository) holds VERSION.PATCHLEVEL.SUBLEVEL and
 * EXTRAVERSION, in the form of the Makefile of Linux; tools/kernel-version.py makes the whole string from it,
 * from the Darwin the kernel is built on, from CONFIG_SOC of the active configuration and from git
 * (2.3.4-hakios-darwin22.5-sc7280-g1a2b3c4d). xnuloader/mkpayload.py puts it into the payload as the entry
 * kernel.ver, the loader prints it under its banner ("kernel.ver=") and hands it to this kernel on its
 * command line as hakios_kver.
 *
 * Why the kernel is told and does not carry it itself: the kernel is built from Apple's open xnu plus this port,
 * once, and its Mach-O would have to be rebuilt for a version that is only the commit or the SoC of the
 * configuration; the payload is made in a second, so one kernel binary can be shipped with the version of the
 * release that carries it. The cost is that a kernel started some other way (no loader, no hakios_kver) says
 * "unknown": it does not guess.
 *
 * Android's kernels give theirs in uname; Darwin's "Darwin Kernel Version 22.5.0: ..." is Apple's and stays.
 */
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/hakios.version.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

SYSCTL_DECL(_kern_hakios);

#define HAKIOS_VERSION_MAX      64

/* "unknown" until the loader says; one string, written once at boot and then only read */
static char hakios_version_string[HAKIOS_VERSION_MAX] = "unknown";

SYSCTL_STRING(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, version, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, hakios_version_string, 0,
    "the version of this kernel, as the loader printed it under its banner (kernel.ver=)");

void
hakios_version_init(void)
{
	char value[HAKIOS_VERSION_MAX];

	/* the loader leaves it out of the command line when it does not fit: the string stays "unknown" then */
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("hakios_kver", value, sizeof(value)) && value[0] != '\0') {
		strlcpy(hakios_version_string, value, sizeof(hakios_version_string));
	}
	printf("hakios-kernel: version %s\n", hakios_version_string);
}
```

`drivers/gpu/hakios.adreno.c`:

```c
/*
 * The GPU of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood), an Adreno 642L, woken step by step up to a picture that
 * it fills and the panel shows. Every address below belongs to this phone, and nothing here is
 * touched unless a boot-arg asks for it.
 *
 * Boot-arg gpu=1, on the phone and with the GPU's firmware in the small image: the GPU is
 * started while the system starts and kept for the window server to draw with (the service
 * HakiosGPU; "the GPU kept on" below). Should a step fail, one line says which, and the system
 * draws in software as it does without the boot-arg.
 *
 * The steps are how this was found out, and they stay for looking: how much of the GPU a kernel
 * under Qualcomm's hypervisor may reach was not known, and an access the hypervisor does not
 * like ends the run, at once or a quarter of a minute later, and often without a word. adreno=N
 * performs steps 1 to N and stops; a step says what it is about to touch before it touches it
 * and what it found after, reads come before writes, and a step that does not find what it
 * needs ends the sequence instead of going on blind.
 *
 *   1  reads   what feeds the GPU from outside: its clocks in the global clock controller, and
 *              the names RPMh knows its supplies by
 *   2  reads   the fuses that say which GPU this is
 *   3  reads   the GPU's own clock controller, as the boot loader left it
 *   4  writes  the "CX" power switch on: the half of the GPU block that is not the 3D core --
 *              the power management processor ("GMU"), the bus interface, the GPU's SMMU
 *   5  writes  the clocks of that half on, and measures with the SoC's frequency counter whether
 *              they run: the control register of one of them does not say
 *   6  reads   the first words from the GPU block itself: registers of the GMU (among them a
 *              counter that should be seen counting) and of the bus interface
 *   7  reads   the GMU's own channel to RPMh
 *   8  reads   the SMMU in front of the GPU: its ID registers, and which stream goes where
 *   9  reads   that SMMU's first translation context
 *  10  writes  two words into the GMU's memory and reads them back: the way its firmware goes
 *  11  asks    TrustZone questions that pass no memory: whether it takes calls from this kernel,
 *              and which firmware images it says it authenticates
 *  12  asks    TrustZone to check the signature of the GPU's "zap shader", the signed image
 *              without which the 3D core stays locked in secure mode: its header goes from the
 *              small image (fw/a660_zap.mdt) into memory of ours that TrustZone is pointed at
 *  13  writes  page tables for the memory the GMU's firmware asks for, and the SMMU: a
 *              translation context with those tables, and the GMU's requests sent through it
 *  14  writes  the GMU's firmware (fw/a660_gmu.bin) into its own memory and into that memory
 *  15  writes  the GMU's configuration, and lets its processor out of reset: the firmware runs
 *  16  writes  the GMU's connection to RPMh; starts its message queues ("HFI")
 *  17  talks   to the GMU: the tables it needs, and the request to power the 3D core, whose
 *              registers are then read
 *  18  writes  the 3D core's translation context, with its ring and its microcode
 *              (fw/a660_sqe.fw) in it
 *  19  asks    TrustZone to load the zap shader (and first to give up the one a kernel before
 *              this one may have left; the stop at the end of a run asks for that too)
 *  20  writes  the 3D core's registers; starts its command processor and gives it its first
 *              command
 *  21  commands the 3D core out of secure mode, and to write a word into a page of ours
 *  22  commands a picture filled with three colours, and shows it on the panel
 * When the steps are over, what they started is stopped again, in reverse, and the CX half
 * switched off: nothing of the GPU block outlives the run (its SMMU contexts point into this
 * kernel's memory), and the next one starts from what the phone's own start leaves.
 *
 * The firmware is the phone's own, from /vendor/firmware of its Android. There is no register that holds the chip ID (0x06030500,
 * "qcom,chipid" in the device tree): the fuses of step 2 are all the hardware says about
 * itself, and the GMU's version is a property of its firmware.
 *
 * More boot-args:
 *   adreno_only=K      step K alone (what steps 6 to 10 need, they check for themselves: within
 *                      one session of the loader, power and clocks stay as an earlier run left them)
 *   adreno_skip=MASK   leave out the steps whose bits are set (bit 2 = step 2)
 *   adreno_pause=MS    how long the newest step waits after announcing a group of accesses
 *                      (default 2200). The loader, watching from another core (bootcpu=N), writes
 *                      the end of our log to storage every two seconds, and after a silent reset
 *                      that note is all there is.
 *   adreno_fine=1      the newest step waits like that before every single access
 *   adreno_keep=1      with adreno=21: the GPU is not stopped again but kept for the system to draw
 *                      with, through the service HakiosGPU (see "the GPU kept on" below); it is
 *                      given back when the run ends (adreno_dirty=1: left as a panic leaves it)
 *   adreno_speed=N     step 17 asks the GMU for the 3D core's Nth speed: 1 315 MHz, 2 450 MHz,
 *                      3 550 MHz (the default: the most this phone's GPU is rated for)
 *   adreno_blind=1     step 20 starts the command processor with its microcode nowhere, and
 *   adreno_stream1=N   step 18 leaves the core's second stream out (0) or gives it an empty
 *                      context of its own (2): what the SMMU then records shows what the core
 *                      asks for. With 0 and the microcode in place the phone resets.
 *   adreno_watch=S     after the last step, say once a second for S seconds (default 20) that
 *                      the machine is still alive, and what was written last
 *   adreno_return=1    when all is over, go back to the loader instead of starting the system
 *   display_probe=1    before any step: read what the firmware left the display controller
 *                      doing (display_probe() below; two clocks are turned on, nothing else written)
 * The system does not go on starting until all of this is over, so that the end of the log is
 * ours; the touch screen driver's start would talk across it (leave touchscreen=1 out).
 *
 * Addresses are from the phone's own device tree ("dt:" below; the nodes qcom,kgsl-3d0@3d00000,
 * qcom,gmu@3d69000, clock-controller@3d90000, qcom,gdsc@3d9106c, kgsl-smmu@3da0000,
 * qfprom@780000), register layouts from Linux, where SC7280 is this SoC: drivers/clk/qcom/
 * {gcc,gpucc}-sc7280.c, gdsc.c, clk-rcg2.c, drivers/gpu/drm/msm/adreno/a6xx_gmu.c with
 * registers/adreno/a6xx{,_gmu}.xml, drivers/iommu/arm/arm-smmu/arm-smmu.h, drivers/soc/qcom/
 * cmd-db.c, drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm{,-smc}.c, drivers/soc/qcom/mdt_loader.c. The phone's
 * vendor kernel agrees on every offset used here, and is the only source for the frequency counter.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map_wcomb(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);       /* pmap_paddr_t */

static uint32_t last_step, skip_steps, pause_ms = 2200, fine, watch_seconds = 20;
static uint32_t step;                   /* the one being performed */
static uint32_t speed_bin;              /* which of the GPUs of this kind the fuses say this is (step 2) */
static uint32_t newest_step;            /* the highest one asked for: the one that has not been seen to work */
static char last_write[96] = "nothing written";
static bool quiet;                      /* repeating accesses that have been announced and seen to work: say nothing */

/*
 * The kernel's log reaches the loader when a run is over, and a run that ends in a reset
 * without a word leaves none. The loader also reads a log of the kernel's from another core
 * while it runs (loader_return.c; xl keeps it with XL_FOLLOW): every line said here goes there
 * as well, before the next register is touched.
 */
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	return printf("%s", line);
}
#define printf say

static void
sleep_us(uint32_t us)
{
	delay_for_interval(us, NSEC_PER_USEC);
}

static void
sleep_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
}

/* ---- register access ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * One access is one plain load or store of a general register. Some of what is touched here (the
 * SMMU at least) is not the hardware but the hypervisor's imitation of it: the access traps and
 * is carried out on our behalf, which works for the simplest instruction forms only, and the
 * vendor's SMMU driver warns that this imitation "goes horribly wrong" for a store of the zero
 * register. So the compiler does not get to choose the instruction.
 */
static uint32_t __attribute__((noinline))
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	uint32_t value;

	__asm__ volatile ("ldr %w0, [%1]" : "=r" (value) : "r" (address) : "memory");
	return value;
}

static uint32_t __attribute__((noinline))
rd8(vm_offset_t address)
{
	uint32_t value;

	__asm__ volatile ("ldrb %w0, [%1]" : "=r" (value) : "r" (address) : "memory");
	return value;
}

static void __attribute__((noinline))
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	__asm__ volatile ("str %w0, [%1]" : : "r" (value), "r" (address) : "memory");
}

/* A stretch of registers; mapped when a step first needs it. */
struct block {
	const char *name;
	uint32_t phys, size;
	vm_offset_t base;
};

static void
need(struct block *b)
{
	if (b->base == 0) {
		b->base = ml_io_map(b->phys, b->size);
	}
}

/* Time for the loader to note what has just been said, where it is not yet known to be harmless. */
static void
hold(bool single_access)
{
	if (step == newest_step && pause_ms && (!single_access || fine)) {
		sleep_ms(pause_ms);
	}
}

/* What a step is about to do, in a line. */
static void
announce(const char *what)
{
	printf("adreno: step %u: %s\n", step, what);
	hold(false);
}

static uint32_t
get(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset)
{
	uint32_t value;

	need(b);
	if (quiet) {
		return rd(b->base + offset);
	}
	if (step == newest_step) {
		printf("adreno: %u: about to read %s %s at %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset);
		hold(true);
	}
	value = rd(b->base + offset);
	printf("adreno: %u: %s %s (%#x) = %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
	return value;
}

static void
put(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
	need(b);
	if (!quiet) {
		printf("adreno: %u: about to write %s %s at %#x: %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
		snprintf(last_write, sizeof(last_write), "step %u wrote %#x to %s %s at %#x", step, value, b->name, name,
		    b->phys + offset);
		hold(true);
	}
	wr(b->base + offset, value);
}

/* Set bits of a register unless they are set. Returns what the register holds afterwards. */
static uint32_t
set(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset, uint32_t bits)
{
	uint32_t was = get(b, name, offset);

	if ((was & bits) == bits) {
		return was;
	}
	put(b, name, offset, was | bits);
	return get(b, name, offset);
}

/* Look at a register that has been read before until the masked bits have the value, for so many milliseconds. */
static bool
wait_for(struct block *b, uint32_t offset, uint32_t mask, uint32_t value, uint32_t ms)
{
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < ms * 10; i++) {
		if ((rd(b->base + offset) & mask) == value) {
			return true;
		}
		sleep_us(100);
	}
	return (rd(b->base + offset) & mask) == value;
}

/* ---- step 1: the clocks from outside, and RPMh's names ------------------------------------------------ */

/*
 * dt: clock-controller@100000 (qcom,yupik-gcc). The GPU's clocks there, by the names the GPU's
 * nodes give them: gcc_gpu_memnoc_gfx and gcc_gpu_snoc_dvm_gfx (its two bus connections),
 * "axi_clk" = gcc_ddrss_gpu_axi (memory), gcc_gpu_cfg_ahb (the registers of its clock controller);
 * and the two taps of the 600 MHz PLL that its clock controller takes as inputs. None of them is
 * among that node's protected-clocks, the ones the hypervisor keeps to itself. Offsets:
 * gcc-sc7280.c. The touch screen driver uses this controller too.
 */
static struct block gcc = { "gcc", 0x00100000, 0x80000 };
#define GCC_PLL_VOTE            0x52000         /* bit 15: gcc_gpu_gpll0_clk_src (600 MHz), bit 16: ..._div_clk_src (300 MHz) */
#define GCC_PLL_VOTE_GPU_DIV    (1u << 16)
#define GCC_GPU_CFG_AHB_CBCR    0x71004
#define GCC_GPU_MEMNOC_GFX_CBCR 0x7100c
#define GCC_GPU_SNOC_DVM_GFX_CBCR 0x71018
#define GCC_DDRSS_GPU_AXI_CBCR  0x71154
#define CBCR_ENABLE             (1u << 0)       /* a clock's control register: on */
#define CBCR_OFF                (1u << 31)      /* ... and whether it is in fact off */

/* dt: reserved-memory cmd_db@80860000: the boot loader's list of what RPMh can switch (cmd-db.c) */
#define CMD_DB_PHYS             0x80860000UL
#define CMD_DB_SIZE             0x20000UL

struct cmd_db_slave {
	uint16_t id, header_offset, data_offset, count, version, reserved[3];
};
struct cmd_db_header {
	uint32_t version;
	uint8_t magic[4];
	struct cmd_db_slave slave[8];
	uint32_t checksum, reserved;
	uint8_t data[];
};
struct cmd_db_entry {
	char id[8];
	uint32_t priority[2];
	uint32_t address;
	uint16_t length, offset;
};

static const struct cmd_db_header *cmd_db;

/*
 * Where RPMh has a resource (0: nowhere) and, for a supply rail, the levels it knows: the GMU's
 * firmware is told the levels by their position in this list.
 */
static uint32_t
rpmh_resource(const char *name, uint16_t *levels, unsigned *level_count)
{
	const struct cmd_db_header *db = cmd_db;
	char id[8] = { 0 };

	if (level_count != NULL) {
		*level_count = 0;
	}
	if (db == NULL) {
		db = cmd_db = (const struct cmd_db_header *)ml_io_map_wcomb(CMD_DB_PHYS, CMD_DB_SIZE);  /* memory, not registers */
	}
	if (db->magic[0] != 0xdb || db->magic[1] != 0x30 || db->magic[2] != 0x03 || db->magic[3] != 0x0c) {
		return 0;
	}
	strlcpy(id, name, sizeof(id));
	for (unsigned s = 0; s < 8; s++) {
		const struct cmd_db_slave *slave = &db->slave[s];
		const struct cmd_db_entry *entry = (const struct cmd_db_entry *)(db->data + slave->header_offset);

		if (slave->id == 0 || slave->count > 512) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < slave->count; i++) {
			const uint8_t *data = db->data + slave->data_offset + entry[i].offset;
			unsigned count = entry[i].length / 2u;

			if (memcmp(entry[i].id, id, sizeof(id)) != 0) {
				continue;
			}
			if ((unsigned)slave->data_offset + entry[i].offset + entry[i].length > CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000) {
				count = 0;
			}
			for (unsigned l = 0; levels != NULL && l < count && l < 16; l++) {
				levels[l] = (uint16_t)(data[2 * l] | data[2 * l + 1] << 8);
				if (l > 0 && levels[l] == 0) {
					break;
				}
				*level_count = l + 1;
			}
			return entry[i].address;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

static void
show_rpmh_resource(const char *name)
{
	uint16_t level[16];
	unsigned count = 0;
	uint32_t address = rpmh_resource(name, level, &count);
	char levels[160];
	int at = 0;

	if (address == 0) {
		printf("adreno: %u: RPMh has no \"%s\"\n", step, name);
		return;
	}
	levels[0] = 0;
	for (unsigned l = 0; l < count && at < (int)sizeof(levels) - 8; l++) {
		at += snprintf(levels + at, sizeof(levels) - (size_t)at, " %u", level[l]);
	}
	printf("adreno: %u: RPMh has \"%s\" at %#x; levels:%s\n", step, name, address, levels);
}

static bool
step_outside(void)
{
	announce("read the GPU's clocks in the global clock controller (registers the touch screen driver uses too)");
	get(&gcc, "pll votes", GCC_PLL_VOTE);
	get(&gcc, "gpu_cfg_ahb", GCC_GPU_CFG_AHB_CBCR);
	get(&gcc, "gpu_memnoc_gfx", GCC_GPU_MEMNOC_GFX_CBCR);
	get(&gcc, "gpu_snoc_dvm_gfx", GCC_GPU_SNOC_DVM_GFX_CBCR);
	get(&gcc, "ddrss_gpu_axi", GCC_DDRSS_GPU_AXI_CBCR);

	announce("look up the GPU's supply rails in the boot loader's list of RPMh resources (memory at 0x80860000)");
	show_rpmh_resource("gfx.lvl");          /* the 3D core's own rail (dt: VDD_GFX_LEVEL, PM8350C S7) */
	show_rpmh_resource("cx.lvl");           /* the rail of the CX half, shared with most of the SoC */
	show_rpmh_resource("mx.lvl");           /* memories */
	return true;
}

/* ---- step 2: the fuses ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * dt: qfprom@780000 with gpu_speed_bin@1e9 (two bytes, 8 bits from bit 5) and gpu_gaming_bin@1f5
 * (bit 5). Linux has the same cell 0x4000 further on, in the error-corrected copy of the fuses
 * (sc7280.dtsi: efuse@784000), and that is the copy it reads under this hypervisor on sibling
 * boards; so that one first.
 */
static struct block qfprom = { "qfprom", 0x00780000, 0x7000 };
#define QFPROM_CORRECTED        0x4000
#define QFPROM_GPU_SPEED_BIN    0x1e9
#define QFPROM_GPU_GAMING_BIN   0x1f5

static uint32_t
get8(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset)
{
	uint32_t value;

	need(b);
	if (step == newest_step) {
		printf("adreno: %u: about to read %s %s at %#x (a byte)\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset);
		hold(true);
	}
	value = rd8(b->base + offset);
	printf("adreno: %u: %s %s (%#x) = %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
	return value;
}

static bool
step_fuses(void)
{
	uint32_t bin, gaming;

	announce("read the GPU's fuses in the error-corrected copy (0x784000), which Linux reads");
	bin = get8(&qfprom, "speed bin, low", QFPROM_CORRECTED + QFPROM_GPU_SPEED_BIN);
	bin |= get8(&qfprom, "speed bin, high", QFPROM_CORRECTED + QFPROM_GPU_SPEED_BIN + 1) << 8;
	bin = bin >> 5 & 0xff;
	speed_bin = bin;
	gaming = get8(&qfprom, "gaming bin", QFPROM_CORRECTED + QFPROM_GPU_GAMING_BIN) >> 5 & 1;
	/* dt: qcom,gpu-models: 0xac and 0xbe are sold as Adreno 643, anything else is the 642L */
	printf("adreno: %u: speed bin %u: an Adreno %s; gaming bin %u\n", step, bin, bin == 0xac || bin == 0xbe ? "643" : "642L",
	    gaming);

	announce("read the same fuses where the phone's device tree has them (0x780000)");
	bin = get8(&qfprom, "raw speed bin, low", QFPROM_GPU_SPEED_BIN);
	bin |= get8(&qfprom, "raw speed bin, high", QFPROM_GPU_SPEED_BIN + 1) << 8;
	printf("adreno: %u: raw speed bin %u\n", step, bin >> 5 & 0xff);
	return true;
}

/* ---- step 3: the GPU's clock controller ----------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * dt: clock-controller@3d90000 (qcom,yupik-gpucc), 0x9000 long; offsets: gpucc-sc7280.c. Its
 * registers answer only while gcc_gpu_cfg_ahb runs, which Linux turns on for good when it
 * starts (gcc-sc7280.c, the end of the probe function).
 */
static struct block gpucc = { "gpucc", 0x03d90000, 0x9000 };
#define GPUCC_PLL0_MODE         0x0000          /* the 3D core's PLL: bit 31 locked, bit 0 output on; +4: times 19.2 MHz */
#define GPUCC_PLL1_MODE         0x0100          /* a 500 MHz PLL, an alternative source for the GMU's clock */
#define GPUCC_CXO_AON_CBCR      0x1004
#define GPUCC_GX_SW_RESET       0x1008          /* dt: gpu_gx_sw_reset */
#define GPUCC_GX_GDSCR          0x100c          /* dt: gpu_gx_gdsc, the 3D core's power switch: the GMU's to operate */
#define GPUCC_GX_GMU_CBCR       0x1064
#define GPUCC_CX_GDSCR          0x106c          /* dt: gpu_cx_gdsc */
#define GPUCC_AHB_CBCR          0x1078          /* gpu_cc_ahb_clk: the register bus inside the GPU block */
#define GPUCC_CX_GMU_CBCR       0x1098          /* gpu_cc_cx_gmu_clk: the GMU */
#define GPUCC_CXO_CBCR          0x109c          /* gpu_cc_cxo_clk: the crystal, for the GMU's timers */
#define GPUCC_GMU_RCGR          0x1120          /* gpu_cc_gmu_clk_src: +0 command, +4 source and divider */
#define GPUCC_CB_CBCR           0x1170          /* gpu_cc_cb_clk: Linux keeps it on always */
#define GPUCC_HUB_AON_CBCR      0x1178          /* gpu_cc_hub_aon_clk */
#define GPUCC_HUB_RCGR          0x117c          /* gpu_cc_hub_clk_src */
#define GPUCC_HUB_CX_INT_CBCR   0x1204          /* gpu_cc_hub_cx_int_clk */
#define GPUCC_CX_HW_CTRL        0x1540          /* dt: gpu_cx_hw_ctrl: bit 31 is where the vendor's driver sees CX come on */
#define GPUCC_GX_DOMAIN_MISC    0x158c          /* dt: gpu_gx_domain_addr */
#define GPUCC_SMMU_VOTE_CBCR    0x5000          /* gpu_cc_hlos1_vote_gpu_smmu_clk: our vote for the SMMU's clock */

#define GDSC_SW_COLLAPSE        (1u << 0)       /* a power switch's control register (gdsc.c): off, by software */
#define GDSC_HW_CONTROL         (1u << 1)       /* something else than software operates it */
#define GDSC_POWER_ON           (1u << 31)

static bool
step_gpucc(void)
{
	announce("make sure the clock of the GPU clock controller's registers runs (gcc_gpu_cfg_ahb)");
	if ((set(&gcc, "gpu_cfg_ahb", GCC_GPU_CFG_AHB_CBCR, CBCR_ENABLE) & CBCR_OFF) &&
	    !wait_for(&gcc, GCC_GPU_CFG_AHB_CBCR, CBCR_OFF, 0, 10)) {
		printf("adreno: %u: it stays off (%#x): the GPU's clock controller would not answer\n", step,
		    rd(gcc.base + GCC_GPU_CFG_AHB_CBCR));
		return false;
	}

	announce("read the GPU's clock controller (0x3d90000) as it is: the first access to the GPU's part of the SoC");
	get(&gpucc, "cx_gdscr", GPUCC_CX_GDSCR);
	get(&gpucc, "cx_hw_ctrl", GPUCC_CX_HW_CTRL);
	get(&gpucc, "gx_gdscr", GPUCC_GX_GDSCR);
	get(&gpucc, "gx_sw_reset", GPUCC_GX_SW_RESET);
	get(&gpucc, "gx_domain_misc", GPUCC_GX_DOMAIN_MISC);
	get(&gpucc, "pll0 mode", GPUCC_PLL0_MODE);
	get(&gpucc, "pll0 multiplier", GPUCC_PLL0_MODE + 4);
	get(&gpucc, "pll1 mode", GPUCC_PLL1_MODE);
	get(&gpucc, "pll1 multiplier", GPUCC_PLL1_MODE + 4);
	get(&gpucc, "gmu_clk_src command", GPUCC_GMU_RCGR);
	get(&gpucc, "gmu_clk_src source", GPUCC_GMU_RCGR + 4);
	get(&gpucc, "hub_clk_src command", GPUCC_HUB_RCGR);
	get(&gpucc, "hub_clk_src source", GPUCC_HUB_RCGR + 4);
	get(&gpucc, "cxo_aon", GPUCC_CXO_AON_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "gx_gmu", GPUCC_GX_GMU_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "ahb", GPUCC_AHB_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "cx_gmu", GPUCC_CX_GMU_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "cxo", GPUCC_CXO_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "cb", GPUCC_CB_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "hub_aon", GPUCC_HUB_AON_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "hub_cx_int", GPUCC_HUB_CX_INT_CBCR);
	get(&gpucc, "smmu vote", GPUCC_SMMU_VOTE_CBCR);
	return true;
}

/* ---- step 4: CX power --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Not to touch the GPU's clock controller without the clock of its registers: where step 3 has not been. */
static bool
gpucc_answers(void)
{
	need(&gcc);
	need(&gpucc);
	if (rd(gcc.base + GCC_GPU_CFG_AHB_CBCR) & CBCR_OFF) {
		printf("adreno: %u: the GPU clock controller's registers have no clock (gcc gpu_cfg_ahb %#x): step 3\n", step,
		    rd(gcc.base + GCC_GPU_CFG_AHB_CBCR));
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static bool
cx_is_on(void)
{
	return (rd(gpucc.base + GPUCC_CX_GDSCR) | rd(gpucc.base + GPUCC_CX_HW_CTRL)) & GDSC_POWER_ON;
}

static void stale_stop(void);

/*
 * The switch hangs on the rail "cx.lvl", which is up for as long as the SoC runs at all; the
 * vendor's driver (gdsc-regulator.c) clears the collapse bit and waits for bit 31 of the register
 * the device tree calls hw-ctrl-addr, Linux for bit 31 of the control register itself.
 */
static bool
step_cx_power(void)
{
	uint32_t gdscr;

	if (!gpucc_answers()) {
		return false;
	}
	announce("switch the CX half of the GPU block on (gpu_cx_gdsc): clear the collapse bit of its power switch");
	gdscr = get(&gpucc, "cx_gdscr", GPUCC_CX_GDSCR);
	get(&gpucc, "cx_hw_ctrl", GPUCC_CX_HW_CTRL);
	if (cx_is_on()) {
		/*
		 * A kernel that kept the GPU for the system to use (adreno_keep) leaves it running when
		 * its run ends. What it left -- the GMU's processor, the 3D core's power, the GMU's
		 * votes in RPMh, the SMMU's contexts pointing into memory that is somebody else's now --
		 * is taken down as gpu_block_stop() would have, and the start is from nothing.
		 */
		printf("adreno: %u: CX is on already: an earlier kernel left the GPU block running; stopping it first\n", step);
		stale_stop();
		if (cx_is_on()) {
			printf("adreno: %u: CX stays on: going on with it as it is\n", step);
			return true;
		}
		gdscr = rd(gpucc.base + GPUCC_CX_GDSCR);
	}
	if (gdscr & GDSC_HW_CONTROL) {
		printf("adreno: %u: the switch is under hardware control: not ours to operate\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	put(&gpucc, "cx_gdscr", GPUCC_CX_GDSCR, gdscr & ~GDSC_SW_COLLAPSE);
	for (int i = 0; i < 500 && !cx_is_on(); i++) {
		sleep_us(100);
	}
	get(&gpucc, "cx_gdscr", GPUCC_CX_GDSCR);
	get(&gpucc, "cx_hw_ctrl", GPUCC_CX_HW_CTRL);
	if (!cx_is_on()) {
		printf("adreno: %u: CX does not come on\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	printf("adreno: %u: CX is on\n", step);
	if (rd(gpucc.base + GPUCC_GX_GDSCR) & GDSC_POWER_ON) {
		/*
		 * The 3D core kept its power while the rest of the block lost it: an ending that went
		 * wrong (a GMU that did not answer, before gpu_block_stop() switched the core off
		 * itself). Such a core is where it was, in the middle of things, and does not take the
		 * steps' commands (seen: step 21); switching it off from here has hung the whole phone
		 * (seen once). Left alone: no GPU until the phone has been restarted.
		 */
		printf("adreno: %u: THE 3D CORE HAS POWER ALREADY, left on by an earlier kernel: not usable until the phone is "
		    "restarted\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* ---- step 5: clocks ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define RCG_UPDATE              (1u << 0)       /* command register (clk-rcg2.c): take the new source and divider */
#define RCG_SOURCE_MASK         0x371fu         /* [4:0] 2*divider-1, [10:8] source, [13:12] mode */
#define RCG_GPLL0_DIV(twice)    (6u << 8 | ((twice) - 1))       /* source 6: the 300 MHz tap; twice the divider wanted */

/* Turn a clock on and see it run. Not every clock's status can be believed (halt_check in Linux): `must` says which. */
static bool
clock_on(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t cbcr, bool must)
{
	if (!(set(b, name, cbcr, CBCR_ENABLE) & CBCR_OFF) || wait_for(b, cbcr, CBCR_OFF, 0, 10)) {
		return true;
	}
	printf("adreno: %u: %s %s stays off (%#x)%s\n", step, b->name, name, rd(b->base + cbcr),
	    must ? "" : "; its status bit is not one to rely on, going on");
	return !must;
}

static bool
clock_source(const char *name, uint32_t rcgr, uint32_t source)
{
	uint32_t was = get(&gpucc, name, rcgr + 4);

	if ((was & RCG_SOURCE_MASK) == source) {
		return true;
	}
	put(&gpucc, name, rcgr + 4, (was & ~RCG_SOURCE_MASK) | source);
	put(&gpucc, name, rcgr, rd(gpucc.base + rcgr) | RCG_UPDATE);
	if (!wait_for(&gpucc, rcgr, RCG_UPDATE, 0, 10)) {
		printf("adreno: %u: %s does not take its new source (command %#x)\n", step, name, rd(gpucc.base + rcgr));
		return false;
	}
	get(&gpucc, name, rcgr + 4);
	return true;
}

static bool measure_clocks(void);

/*
 * The clocks the device tree gives the GMU and the SMMU, at the rates both the vendor's driver
 * and Linux bring the GMU up with: 200 MHz for the GMU, 150 MHz for the "hub" (a6xx_gmu_resume).
 * Both come from the 300 MHz tap of the global 600 MHz PLL, which runs anyway: no PLL of the
 * GPU's own has to be started.
 */
static bool
step_clocks(void)
{
	if (!gpucc_answers()) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!cx_is_on()) {
		printf("adreno: %u: CX is off: step 4\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	announce("in the global clock controller: ask for the 300 MHz tap for the GPU; the GPU's bus and memory clocks on");
	set(&gcc, "pll votes", GCC_PLL_VOTE, GCC_PLL_VOTE_GPU_DIV);
	if (!clock_on(&gcc, "gpu_memnoc_gfx", GCC_GPU_MEMNOC_GFX_CBCR, false) ||
	    !clock_on(&gcc, "gpu_snoc_dvm_gfx", GCC_GPU_SNOC_DVM_GFX_CBCR, true) ||
	    !clock_on(&gcc, "ddrss_gpu_axi", GCC_DDRSS_GPU_AXI_CBCR, false)) {
		return false;
	}

	announce("in the GPU's clock controller: the GMU's clock to 200 MHz, the hub's to 150 MHz");
	if (!clock_source("gmu_clk_src", GPUCC_GMU_RCGR, RCG_GPLL0_DIV(3)) ||       /* 300 MHz / 1.5 */
	    !clock_source("hub_clk_src", GPUCC_HUB_RCGR, RCG_GPLL0_DIV(4))) {       /* 300 MHz / 2 */
		return false;
	}

	announce("in the GPU's clock controller: the clocks of the GMU and of the SMMU on");
	if (!clock_on(&gpucc, "cb", GPUCC_CB_CBCR, false) ||
	    !clock_on(&gpucc, "cxo", GPUCC_CXO_CBCR, true) ||
	    !clock_on(&gpucc, "ahb", GPUCC_AHB_CBCR, false) ||
	    !clock_on(&gpucc, "hub_aon", GPUCC_HUB_AON_CBCR, true) ||
	    !clock_on(&gpucc, "hub_cx_int", GPUCC_HUB_CX_INT_CBCR, true) ||
	    !clock_on(&gpucc, "cx_gmu", GPUCC_CX_GMU_CBCR, true) ||
	    !clock_on(&gpucc, "smmu vote", GPUCC_SMMU_VOTE_CBCR, false)) {
		return false;
	}
	return measure_clocks();
}

/*
 * Whether a clock runs is not always to be had from its control register: the one of the register
 * bus inside the GPU block, gpu_cc_ahb, reads 0 on this phone before and after its enable bit is
 * written (Linux, for which it has "no bit to check", writes the bit and waits 10 us). The SoC can
 * measure instead: a clock controller can put any of its clocks on a debug output, and the global
 * controller counts what it is given there against the crystal. The vendor's kernel shows the
 * result as "clk_measure"; registers, selections and procedure are its debugcc-yupik.c and
 * clk-debug.c (mainline Linux has no counterpart).
 */
#define GCC_DEBUG_MUX           0x62000         /* [9:0] which clock goes to the counter */
#define GCC_DEBUG_MUX_GPUCC     0x146           /* ... the debug output of the GPU's clock controller */
#define GCC_DEBUG_DIV           0x62004         /* [3:0] divider - 1; both controllers divide by 2 */
#define GCC_DEBUG_CBCR          0x62008
#define GCC_XO_DIV4_CBCR        0x6200c         /* the counter's time base: the crystal / 4, 4.8 MHz */
#define GCC_MEASURE_CTL         0x62038         /* [19:0] how many ticks of the time base to count for */
#define MEASURE_RUN             (1u << 20)
#define MEASURE_CLEAR           (1u << 21)
#define GCC_MEASURE_STATUS      0x6203c         /* [24:0] the count */
#define MEASURE_DONE            (1u << 25)
#define MEASURE_BRIEF           0x1000          /* ticks: a millisecond */
#define MEASURE_FULL            0x20000         /* 27 ms */
#define MEASURE_FAILED          0xffffffffu
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_DIV         0x10fc
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_CBCR        0x1100
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_MUX         0x1568          /* [7:0] which of the GPU's clocks */
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_CXO_AON     0x0b
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_GX_GFX3D    0x0d            /* the 3D core's own clock */
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_GX_GMU      0x11
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_AHB         0x12
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_CX_GMU      0x1a
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_CXO         0x1b
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_HUB_CX_INT  0x1c
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_CB          0x26
#define GPUCC_DEBUG_HUB_AON     0x27

/* Let the counter run for so many ticks of its time base; what it counted of the clock on its input. */
static uint32_t
count_clock(uint32_t ticks)
{
	uint32_t control = get(&gcc, "measure control", GCC_MEASURE_CTL) & ~(MEASURE_RUN | MEASURE_CLEAR | 0xfffffu);
	uint32_t status = 0;

	put(&gcc, "measure control", GCC_MEASURE_CTL, control | MEASURE_CLEAR);
	sleep_us(10);
	put(&gcc, "measure control", GCC_MEASURE_CTL, control | ticks);
	put(&gcc, "measure control", GCC_MEASURE_CTL, control | ticks | MEASURE_RUN);
	for (int i = 0; i < 2000 && !(status & MEASURE_DONE); i++) {
		sleep_us(100);
		status = rd(gcc.base + GCC_MEASURE_STATUS);
	}
	put(&gcc, "measure control", GCC_MEASURE_CTL, control | ticks);
	return status & MEASURE_DONE ? get(&gcc, "measure status", GCC_MEASURE_STATUS) & 0x1ffffff : MEASURE_FAILED;
}

/*
 * The rate in Hz of one of the GPU clock controller's clocks; 0 if it does not run, MEASURE_FAILED
 * if the counter does not finish. Everything that is changed for it is put back.
 */
static uint32_t
measure(uint32_t select)
{
	uint32_t gpu_mux = get(&gpucc, "debug mux", GPUCC_DEBUG_MUX), gpu_div = get(&gpucc, "debug divider", GPUCC_DEBUG_DIV);
	uint32_t gpu_cbcr = get(&gpucc, "debug output", GPUCC_DEBUG_CBCR), mux = get(&gcc, "debug mux", GCC_DEBUG_MUX);
	uint32_t div = get(&gcc, "debug divider", GCC_DEBUG_DIV), cbcr = get(&gcc, "debug input", GCC_DEBUG_CBCR);
	uint32_t base = get(&gcc, "crystal/4", GCC_XO_DIV4_CBCR), control = get(&gcc, "measure control", GCC_MEASURE_CTL);
	uint32_t brief, full;

	put(&gpucc, "debug mux", GPUCC_DEBUG_MUX, (gpu_mux & ~0xffu) | select);
	put(&gpucc, "debug divider", GPUCC_DEBUG_DIV, (gpu_div & ~0xfu) | 1);
	put(&gpucc, "debug output", GPUCC_DEBUG_CBCR, gpu_cbcr | CBCR_ENABLE);
	put(&gcc, "debug mux", GCC_DEBUG_MUX, (mux & ~0x3ffu) | GCC_DEBUG_MUX_GPUCC);
	put(&gcc, "debug divider", GCC_DEBUG_DIV, (div & ~0xfu) | 1);
	put(&gcc, "debug input", GCC_DEBUG_CBCR, cbcr | CBCR_ENABLE);
	put(&gcc, "crystal/4", GCC_XO_DIV4_CBCR, base | CBCR_ENABLE);
	/* a counter whose input stands still keeps its last count: the two counts differ only if the clock runs */
	brief = count_clock(MEASURE_BRIEF);
	full = brief == MEASURE_FAILED ? MEASURE_FAILED : count_clock(MEASURE_FULL);
	put(&gcc, "measure control", GCC_MEASURE_CTL, control);
	put(&gcc, "crystal/4", GCC_XO_DIV4_CBCR, base);
	put(&gcc, "debug input", GCC_DEBUG_CBCR, cbcr);
	put(&gcc, "debug divider", GCC_DEBUG_DIV, div);
	put(&gcc, "debug mux", GCC_DEBUG_MUX, mux);
	put(&gpucc, "debug output", GPUCC_DEBUG_CBCR, gpu_cbcr);
	put(&gpucc, "debug divider", GPUCC_DEBUG_DIV, gpu_div);
	put(&gpucc, "debug mux", GPUCC_DEBUG_MUX, gpu_mux);

	if (full == MEASURE_FAILED) {
		return MEASURE_FAILED;
	}
	if (full == brief) {
		return 0;
	}
	/* the vendor's formula; times 4 for the two dividers on the way to the counter */
	return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)full * 10 + 15) * 4800000 / ((uint64_t)MEASURE_FULL * 10 + 35) * 4);
}

static uint32_t
measure_quietly(uint32_t select)
{
	uint32_t hz;

	quiet = true;
	hz = measure(select);
	quiet = false;
	return hz;
}

/*
 * Measure the clocks step 5 has turned on. The crystal's comes first and aloud: its rate is known,
 * so it shows whether the counter can be believed; one that is off (the 3D core's) comes last.
 */
static bool
measure_clocks(void)
{
	static const struct {
		const char *name;
		uint32_t select;
	} clocks[] = {
		{ "cx_gmu (200 MHz was asked for)", GPUCC_DEBUG_CX_GMU }, { "hub_cx_int (from 150 MHz)", GPUCC_DEBUG_HUB_CX_INT },
		{ "hub_aon", GPUCC_DEBUG_HUB_AON }, { "cb", GPUCC_DEBUG_CB }, { "cxo_aon", GPUCC_DEBUG_CXO_AON },
		{ "gx_gmu (should be off)", GPUCC_DEBUG_GX_GMU }, { "ahb, THE ONE IN QUESTION,", GPUCC_DEBUG_AHB },
	};
	uint32_t hz, ahb_hz = MEASURE_FAILED;

	announce("measure the GPU block's clocks with the SoC's frequency counter (debug registers at gcc 0x162000.., "
	    "gpucc 0x3d910fc, 0x3d91100, 0x3d91568)");
	hz = measure(GPUCC_DEBUG_CXO);
	if (hz == MEASURE_FAILED) {
		printf("adreno: %u: the counter did not finish: it cannot be used as it is set up here\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	printf("adreno: %u: measured: cxo runs at %u Hz (the crystal: 19200000)\n", step, hz);
	if (hz < 18600000 || hz > 19800000) {
		printf("adreno: %u: the counter does not show the crystal's rate: nothing it says can be used\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(clocks) / sizeof(clocks[0]); i++) {
		hz = measure_quietly(clocks[i].select);
		if (hz == MEASURE_FAILED) {
			printf("adreno: %u: measured: %s: the counter did not finish\n", step, clocks[i].name);
		} else {
			printf("adreno: %u: measured: %s runs at %u Hz\n", step, clocks[i].name, hz);
		}
		if (clocks[i].select == GPUCC_DEBUG_AHB) {
			ahb_hz = hz;
		}
	}
	if (ahb_hz != MEASURE_FAILED && ahb_hz >= 1000000) {
		printf("adreno: %u: THE REGISTER BUS OF THE GPU BLOCK HAS ITS CLOCK, whatever its control register says\n", step);
		return true;
	}
	/* for study: what else is there in the clock controller that could be its switch */
	printf("adreno: %u: the register bus of the GPU block has no clock; what is not 0 in gpucc 0x1000..0x15fc:\n", step);
	for (uint32_t offset = 0x1000; offset < 0x1600; offset += 16) {
		uint32_t row[4] = { rd(gpucc.base + offset), rd(gpucc.base + offset + 4), rd(gpucc.base + offset + 8),
			            rd(gpucc.base + offset + 12) };

		if (row[0] | row[1] | row[2] | row[3]) {
			printf("adreno: %u: gpucc %#x: %#x %#x %#x %#x\n", step, gpucc.phys + offset, row[0], row[1], row[2],
			    row[3]);
		}
	}
	return false;
}

/*
 * What every later step stands on: CX powered, the GMU's clock running by its control register,
 * and the register bus's clock running by measurement (see above).
 */
static bool
cx_ready(void)
{
	uint32_t gmu_clock, ahb_hz;

	if (!gpucc_answers()) {
		return false;
	}
	gmu_clock = rd(gpucc.base + GPUCC_CX_GMU_CBCR);
	if (!cx_is_on() || (gmu_clock & (CBCR_ENABLE | CBCR_OFF)) != CBCR_ENABLE) {
		printf("adreno: %u: needs CX on (it is %s) and the GMU's clock running (cx_gmu %#x): steps 4 and 5\n", step,
		    cx_is_on() ? "on" : "off", gmu_clock);
		return false;
	}
	ahb_hz = measure_quietly(GPUCC_DEBUG_AHB);
	if (ahb_hz == MEASURE_FAILED) {
		printf("adreno: %u: the frequency counter did not finish (step 5 shows whether it works)\n", step);
	} else {
		printf("adreno: %u: the GPU block's register bus clock (ahb) measures %u Hz\n", step, ahb_hz);
	}
	if (ahb_hz == MEASURE_FAILED || ahb_hz < 1000000) {
		printf("adreno: %u: without that clock a register of the GPU block would not answer: not touching it\n", step);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* ---- step 6: the first words from the GPU block ------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * dt: qcom,gmu "kgsl_gmu_reg" at 0x3d6a000, 0x34000 long. Offsets in a6xx_gmu.xml are in words.
 */
static struct block gmu = { "gmu", 0x03d6a000, 0x34000 };
#define GMU_WORD(n)             (4u * (n))
#define GMU_DTCM                GMU_WORD(0x1c00)        /* the processor's 16K of data memory (its code: 0x0c00) */
#define GMU_DTCM_VERSIONS       GMU_WORD(0x1c00 + 0xff8) /* five words where loaded firmware carries its versions */
#define GMU_CM3_SYSRESET        GMU_WORD(0x5000)        /* 1: the processor is held in reset */
#define GMU_CM3_BOOT_CONFIG     GMU_WORD(0x5001)
#define GMU_CM3_FW_INIT_RESULT  GMU_WORD(0x501c)        /* 0xbabeface once firmware has started */
#define GMU_CM3_CFG             GMU_WORD(0x502d)
#define GMU_ALWAYS_ON_COUNTER_L GMU_WORD(0x5088)        /* counts the 19.2 MHz crystal */
#define GMU_ALWAYS_ON_COUNTER_H GMU_WORD(0x5089)
#define GMU_SPTPRAC_PWR_CLK_STATUS GMU_WORD(0x50d0)     /* bit 6: the 3D core has no power, bit 7: no clock */
#define GMU_RPMH_POWER_STATE    GMU_WORD(0x50ec)
#define GMU_HFI_CTRL_STATUS     GMU_WORD(0x5180)
#define GMU_HFI_VERSION_INFO    GMU_WORD(0x5181)
#define GMU_GENERAL_7           GMU_WORD(0x51cc)
#define GMU_AO_HOST_INTERRUPT_STATUS GMU_WORD(0x9305)
#define GMU_RSCC_CONTROL_ACK    GMU_WORD(0x9308)
#define GMU_AO_GPU_CX_BUSY_STATUS GMU_WORD(0x930c)
#define GMU_AHB_FENCE_STATUS    GMU_WORD(0x9313)

/*
 * dt: qcom,kgsl-3d0 "kgsl_3d0_reg_memory" at 0x3d00000 is the 3D core, and without power (the GMU
 * gives it) not to be touched -- except its bus interface ("GBIF", words 0x3c00 on in a6xx.xml),
 * which is in the CX half: the vendor's driver writes GBIF_HALT before it starts the GMU.
 * "cx_misc" at 0x3d9e000 is a page of odds and ends in the CX half.
 */
static struct block gbif = { "gbif", 0x03d00000 + 4 * 0x3c00, 0x1000 };
#define GBIF_SCACHE_CNTL0       (4 * 0x01)
#define GBIF_HALT               (4 * 0x45)
#define GBIF_HALT_ACK           (4 * 0x46)
static struct block cx_misc = { "cx_misc", 0x03d9e000, 0x1000 };
#define CX_MISC_SYSTEM_CACHE_CNTL_0 (4 * 1)
#define CX_MISC_SYSTEM_CACHE_CNTL_1 (4 * 2)

static bool
step_first_words(void)
{
	uint64_t start, nanos;
	uint32_t before, hz;

	if (!cx_ready()) {
		return false;
	}
	announce("read registers of the GMU (0x3d6a000): the first words from the GPU block itself");
	get(&gmu, "cm3_sysreset", GMU_CM3_SYSRESET);
	get(&gmu, "cm3_boot_config", GMU_CM3_BOOT_CONFIG);
	get(&gmu, "cm3_fw_init_result", GMU_CM3_FW_INIT_RESULT);
	get(&gmu, "cm3_cfg", GMU_CM3_CFG);
	get(&gmu, "hfi_ctrl_status", GMU_HFI_CTRL_STATUS);
	get(&gmu, "hfi_version_info", GMU_HFI_VERSION_INFO);
	get(&gmu, "general_7", GMU_GENERAL_7);
	get(&gmu, "rpmh_power_state", GMU_RPMH_POWER_STATE);
	get(&gmu, "sptprac_pwr_clk_status", GMU_SPTPRAC_PWR_CLK_STATUS);
```
