```cpp
	uint64_t data;
	uint32_t id, param, len, pad;
};
struct drm_gem_close {
	uint32_t handle, pad;
};
struct hakios_user_memory {
	uint64_t address, size;                 /* in the caller, in whole pages */
	uint32_t handle;                        /* back: the buffer */
	uint32_t flags;
};
struct hakios_surface {
	uint32_t surface;                       /* the IOSurface's ID */
	uint32_t handle;                        /* kHakiosDescribe: no buffer is wanted; else, back: the buffer, */
	uint64_t size;                          /* how big it is, */
	uint32_t offset, rowBytes;              /* where the pixels start in it and how long a row of them is, */
	uint32_t width, height, pixelFormat, planes;    /* and what they are */
};
struct hakios_show {
	uint64_t pixels;
	uint32_t width, height, rowBytes, pad;
};

#define kHakiosDescribe        0xffffffffu

#define MSM_INFO_GET_OFFSET     0
#define MSM_INFO_GET_IOVA       1
#define MSM_INFO_SET_NAME       2
#define MSM_INFO_GET_FLAGS      5
#define MSM_BO_GPU_READONLY     0x00000002
#define MSM_PREP_NOSYNC         0x04
#define MSM_SUBMIT_CMD_BUF      1
#define MSM_SUBMIT_FENCE_FD_OUT 0x20000000

#define GPU_BUFFERS             8192            /* a client's, at most */
#define GPU_BUFFER_MAX          (256u << 20)
#define GPU_SUBMIT_CMDS         128
#define GPU_SUBMIT_BOS          8192
#define GPU_PATIENCE_MS         5000            /* for a buffer or a submission that somebody waits for without a limit */
#define GPU_ASK_AGAIN_US        200             /* while waiting for the core: how long between two looks at how far it is */
#define GPU_PUSH_AGAIN_MS       4               /* a surface is pushed out of the cache again for a submission this long after the last */

static IOLock * gGPULock;                       /* around everything that is the GPU's (hakios_gpu_...) */
static bool gGPUReported;
static bool gGPUCached;                         /* boot-arg gpu_cached=1 */

/* What the last seconds' submissions were and cost here, for the log. */
static struct {
	uint64_t since, flushing, waiting, taking;      /* times of the processor's clock */
	uint64_t flushed;                       /* bytes sent out of the cache */
	uint32_t submissions, commands, buffers, surfaces, waits, over;
	uint32_t made, given_again;             /* buffers of their own made for programs, and of those kept ones given again */
	uint64_t making;                        /* ... and the time it took to make the others */
} gGPUStat;

/* Wait for the 3D core to be done with submission `fence`; with the lock held, which is let go of while waiting. */
static bool
gpuWait(uint32_t fence, uint64_t milliseconds)
{
	uint64_t began = mach_absolute_time(), patience;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(milliseconds * NSEC_PER_MSEC, &patience);
	for (bool waited = false;; waited = true) {
		if (hakios_gpu_done(fence)) {
			if (waited) {
				gGPUStat.waits++;
				gGPUStat.waiting += mach_absolute_time() - began;
			}
			return true;
		}
		if (mach_absolute_time() - began >= patience || gGPUReported) {
			break;                  /* (a GPU that has stopped answering is not waited for again) */
		}
		IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
		delay_for_interval(GPU_ASK_AGAIN_US, NSEC_PER_USEC);
		IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	}
	if (milliseconds >= 1000 && !gGPUReported) {
		gGPUReported = true;
		hakios_gpu_report("no answer");
	}
	return false;
}

bool
MiniIOSurfaceDrawn(MiniIOSurface * surface, uint64_t milliseconds)
{
	uint32_t fence = surface->drawn;
	bool done = true;

	if (fence != 0 && gGPULock != NULL) {
		IOLockLock(gGPULock);
		done = !hakios_gpu_ready() || gpuWait(fence, milliseconds);
		IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	}
	return done;
}

/*
 * Boot-arg touch_lat=1: a line for every wait of a program's for the GPU that took a millisecond or
 * more ("tl: f KIND US at US"), for telling apart what holds a frame up (tools/frames.py).
 */
static TUNABLE(uint32_t, gWaitLines, "touch_lat", 0);

static void
slowWait(const char * kind, uint64_t began)
{
	uint64_t now = mach_absolute_time(), ns, at;

	if (!gWaitLines) {
		return;
	}
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now - began, &ns);
	if (ns >= NSEC_PER_MSEC) {
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now, &at);
		hakios_tl("tl: f %s %llu at %llu\n", kind, ns / 1000, at / 1000);
	}
}

/* How long from now a time of msm's is, in milliseconds; 0: now or past. */
static uint64_t
millisecondsUntil(const struct msm_timespec * when)
{
	uint64_t now;
	int64_t left, end;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_continuous_time(), &now);
	/* the seconds are the caller's: a number too big to be nanoseconds is a time far ahead (or far behind), not a wrapped one */
	if (__builtin_mul_overflow(when->seconds, (int64_t) NSEC_PER_SEC, &end) || __builtin_add_overflow(end, when->nanoseconds, &end)) {
		return when->seconds > 0 && when->nanoseconds >= 0 ? GPU_PATIENCE_MS : 0;
	}
	if (end <= 0) {
		return 0;                       /* (the clock's reading is never negative: this is past) */
	}
	left = end - (int64_t) now;
	if (left <= 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	return (uint64_t) left / NSEC_PER_MSEC > GPU_PATIENCE_MS ? GPU_PATIENCE_MS : (uint64_t) left / NSEC_PER_MSEC;
}

/*
 * A wait that was to end at a time that had passed when it was asked for, and the GPU was not
 * done: whoever asked goes on as if it were (a picture is shown half drawn). That is what comes
 * of a caller whose clock is not this one, so the first few are told.
 */
static void
waitOver(const struct msm_timespec * when, uint32_t fence)
{
	static uint32_t told;
	uint64_t now;

	gGPUStat.over++;
	if (told < 4) {
		told++;
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_continuous_time(), &now);
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: a wait for submission %u, which is not done, until %lld.%09lld s, asked for at %llu.%09llu s: "
		    "over before it began\n", fence, when->seconds, when->nanoseconds, now / NSEC_PER_SEC, now % NSEC_PER_SEC);
	}
}

/* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * */

class HakiosGPU : public IOService
{
	OSDeclareDefaultStructors(HakiosGPU);

public:
	virtual bool start(IOService * provider) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
};

OSDefineMetaClassAndStructors(HakiosGPU, IOService);

bool
HakiosGPU::start(IOService * provider)
{
	if (!IOService::start(provider)) {
		return false;
	}
	setProperty(kIOUserClientClassKey, "HakiosGPUUserClient");
	setName("HakiosGPU");
	registerService();
	return true;
}

void
HakiosGPUStart(void)
{
	IOService * provider = IOService::getPlatform();
	HakiosGPU * gpu;
	uint32_t cached = 0;

	gGPUCached = PE_parse_boot_argn("gpu_cached", &cached, sizeof(cached)) && cached != 0;
	gGPULock = IOLockAlloc();
	gpu = OSTypeAlloc(HakiosGPU);
	if (gpu == NULL || provider == NULL || !gpu->init() || !gpu->attach(provider)) {
		OSSafeReleaseNULL(gpu);
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: cannot create the service\n");
		return;
	}
	if (!gpu->start(provider)) {
		gpu->detach(provider);
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: the service did not start\n");
	}
	gpu->release();
}

/* The run is ending (hakios.adreno.c): nobody is in the middle of anything when the GPU goes. */
void
HakiosGPUStop(void)
{
	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	hakios_gpu_stop();
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
}

/* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * */

struct gpu_buffer {
	IOMemoryDescriptor *            memory;         /* NULL: this handle is free */
	uint8_t *                       kernel;         /* where it is in the kernel */
	MiniIOSurface *                 surface;        /* whose memory it is, when not its own */
	bool                            client;         /* the client's own pages (no kernel view: out of the cache by their physical addresses) */
	uint64_t                        address;        /* the GPU's for it */
	uint64_t                        size;
	uint32_t                        flags;
	uint32_t                        seed;           /* the surface's when it was last pushed out of the cache, */
	uint64_t                        pushed;         /* ... and when that was */
	bool                            seen;           /* by the program: mapped, and from then on written by it */
	uint32_t                        fence;          /* the last submission that names it (0: none has) */
};

/*
 * A buffer given back while the GPU is still at it: its memory and its place in the GPU's
 * address space are kept until the submission is done, and nobody waits for that. (A window
 * server that makes a surface for every frame gives the last frame's back while the GPU draws
 * this one: waiting there, for all the GPU had been given, cost it some five milliseconds a
 * frame.)
 */
struct gpu_left {
	IOMemoryDescriptor *            memory;
	MiniIOSurface *                 surface;
	bool                            client;
	uint64_t                        address, size;
	uint32_t                        fence, flags;
};
#define GPU_LEFT                64

/*
 * A buffer of the program's own given back, and done with: kept, memory and place in the GPU's
 * address space, for the next one of the same size and kind. CoreAnimation makes a new texture to
 * draw a blur into for every frame of an animation with one (Search: 1082 x 1226, 6 MB with Mesa's
 * rounding), and gives them back only later, a score at a time; Mesa keeps what is given back for
 * a second and then lets it go. Each made afresh here took 2 to 3.5 ms of the window server's frame
 * (memory got, cleared, made write-combined, and entered page by page into the GPU's address
 * space). A buffer kept is given again as it is, not cleared: it was the same program's (Mesa's own
 * cache gives buffers back the same way). At most GPU_KEPT_BYTES are kept (the one kept longest
 * makes way), none for longer than GPU_KEPT_SECONDS. rc.jobs.fps, Search: 8 such textures made
 * slowly instead of 77, the window server's frames drawn in 6.8 ms instead of 9.3-10 (median).
 */
struct gpu_kept {
	IOMemoryDescriptor *            memory;         /* NULL: this place is free */
	uint8_t *                       kernel;
	uint64_t                        address, size, since;
	uint32_t                        flags;
};
#define GPU_KEPT                48
#define GPU_KEPT_BYTES          (160ull << 20)
#define GPU_KEPT_SECONDS        60              /* a buffer not asked for again in so long is let go */
#define GPU_KEEP_FROM           (256u << 10)    /* bytes: smaller ones are not worth it */
static TUNABLE(uint32_t, gGPUKeep, "gpu_keep", 1);      /* boot-arg gpu_keep=0 (a test): none kept; gpu_keep=2: kept ones cleared when given again */

class HakiosGPUUserClient : public IOUserClient
{
	OSDeclareDefaultStructors(HakiosGPUUserClient);

	task_t                  fTask;
	struct gpu_buffer *     fBuffers;               /* handle n is fBuffers[n - 1] */
	uint32_t                fNextQueue;
	uint32_t                fNextBuffer;            /* where the search for a free handle starts: one given back is not the next given */
	uint32_t                fBufferCount;
	uint64_t                fBufferBytes;
	uint32_t                fSubmits;
	uint32_t                fStrangers;             /* requests that named a buffer the client does not have */
	struct gpu_left         fLeft[GPU_LEFT];
	uint32_t                fLeftCount;
	struct gpu_kept         fKept[GPU_KEPT];
	uint64_t                fKeptBytes;

	struct gpu_buffer * buffer(uint32_t handle);
	struct gpu_buffer * newBuffer(IOMemoryDescriptor * memory, uint64_t from, uint64_t size, uint32_t flags, uint32_t * handle);
	void freeBuffer(struct gpu_buffer * b);
	bool keep(IOMemoryDescriptor * memory, uint8_t * kernel, uint64_t address, uint64_t size, uint32_t flags);
	void dropKept(struct gpu_kept * k);
	void reap(void);
	IOReturn gemNew(struct msm_gem_new * request);
	IOReturn surfaceBuffer(struct hakios_surface * request);
	IOReturn userBuffer(struct hakios_user_memory * request);
	IOReturn gemInfo(struct msm_gem_info * request);
	IOReturn submit(struct msm_gem_submit * request);
	IOReturn show(const struct hakios_show * request);

public:
	virtual bool initWithTask(task_t owningTask, void * securityID, UInt32 type, OSDictionary * properties) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual bool start(IOService * provider) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual IOReturn clientClose(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual void free(void) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual IOReturn clientMemoryForType(UInt32 type, IOOptionBits * options, IOMemoryDescriptor ** memory) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
	virtual IOReturn externalMethod(uint32_t selector, IOExternalMethodArguments * args,
	    IOExternalMethodDispatch * dispatch, OSObject * target, void * reference) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
};

OSDefineMetaClassAndStructors(HakiosGPUUserClient, IOUserClient);

bool
HakiosGPUUserClient::initWithTask(task_t owningTask, void * securityID, UInt32 type, OSDictionary * properties)
{
	if (!IOUserClient::initWithTask(owningTask, securityID, type, properties)) {
		return false;
	}
	fTask = owningTask;
	return true;
}

bool
HakiosGPUUserClient::start(IOService * provider)
{
	if (!hakios_gpu_ready() || !IOUserClient::start(provider)) {
		return false;
	}
	fBuffers = IONewZero(struct gpu_buffer, GPU_BUFFERS);
	return fBuffers != NULL;
}

/*
 * With the lock held, and the GPU done with everything it has been given (`idle`). If it is
 * not -- it has stopped answering -- the buffer's memory stays the GPU's for good: it may yet be
 * written, and must not be somebody else's by then.
 */
void
HakiosGPUUserClient::freeBuffer(struct gpu_buffer * slot)
{
	/*
	 * gpuWait() below lets go of the lock: take the buffer out of its handle first and work on a copy, so that
	 * a second close of the same handle (or the client's closing) cannot free the same memory and address twice.
	 */
	struct gpu_buffer saved = *slot;
	struct gpu_buffer * b = &saved;

	slot->memory = NULL;
	slot->surface = NULL;
	slot->client = false;
	fBufferCount--;
	fBufferBytes -= b->size;

	bool busy = hakios_gpu_ready() && b->fence != 0 && !hakios_gpu_done(b->fence);

	if (busy && fLeftCount == GPU_LEFT) {
		busy = !gpuWait(b->fence, 1000);        /* (nowhere to keep it: this one is waited for) */
	}
	if (busy && fLeftCount < GPU_LEFT) {
		struct gpu_left * left = &fLeft[fLeftCount++];

		left->memory = b->memory;
		left->surface = b->surface;
		left->client = b->client;
		left->address = b->address;
		left->size = b->size;
		left->fence = b->fence;
		left->flags = b->flags;
	} else {
		if (busy) {
			static uint32_t said;

			if (b->surface == NULL) {
				b->memory->retain();
			} else {
				b->surface->memory->retain();
			}
			if (said++ < 8) {
				IOLog("HakiosGPU: the GPU is not done with what it was given: a buffer of %llu bytes stays its own\n", b->size);
			}
		} else if (b->surface == NULL && !b->client && hakios_gpu_ready() &&
		    keep(b->memory, b->kernel, b->address, b->size, b->flags)) {
			b->memory = NULL;               /* (now the kept one's) */
		} else if (hakios_gpu_ready()) {
			hakios_gpu_unmap(b->address, b->size);
			hakios_gpu_address_free(b->address, b->size);
		}
		if (b->memory != NULL) {
			b->memory->release();
		}
		if (b->surface != NULL) {
			MiniIOSurfaceDrop(b->surface);
		}
	}
}

/* The buffers that were given back early and that the GPU is done with now: freed. With the lock held. */
void
HakiosGPUUserClient::reap(void)
{
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < fLeftCount;) {
		struct gpu_left * left = &fLeft[i];

		if (hakios_gpu_ready() && !hakios_gpu_done(left->fence)) {
			i++;
			continue;
		}
		if (left->surface == NULL && !left->client && hakios_gpu_ready() &&
		    keep(left->memory, NULL, left->address, left->size, left->flags)) {
			left->memory = NULL;
		} else if (hakios_gpu_ready()) {
			hakios_gpu_unmap(left->address, left->size);
			hakios_gpu_address_free(left->address, left->size);
		}
		if (left->memory != NULL) {
			left->memory->release();
		}
		if (left->surface != NULL) {
			MiniIOSurfaceDrop(left->surface);
		}
		*left = fLeft[--fLeftCount];
	}
}

IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::clientClose(void)
{
	if (fBuffers != NULL) {
		IOLockLock(gGPULock);
		/* what the client had the GPU do last may still be going on, in these buffers */
		if (hakios_gpu_ready()) {
			gpuWait(hakios_gpu_last(), 1000);
		}
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < GPU_BUFFERS; i++) {
			if (fBuffers[i].memory != NULL) {
				freeBuffer(&fBuffers[i]);
			}
		}
		reap();
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < GPU_KEPT; i++) {
			dropKept(&fKept[i]);
		}
		if (fLeftCount != 0) {
			IOLog("HakiosGPU: the GPU is not done with %u buffers of a program that is gone: they stay its own\n", fLeftCount);
		}
		IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	}
	if (!isInactive()) {
		terminate();
	}
	return kIOReturnSuccess;
}

void
HakiosGPUUserClient::free(void)
{
	if (fBuffers != NULL) {
		IODelete(fBuffers, struct gpu_buffer, GPU_BUFFERS);
		fBuffers = NULL;
	}
	IOUserClient::free();
}

struct gpu_buffer *
HakiosGPUUserClient::buffer(uint32_t handle)
{
	if (handle == 0 || handle > GPU_BUFFERS || fBuffers[handle - 1].memory == NULL) {
		/* (a program that names a buffer it has given back draws into somebody else's next: worth knowing) */
		if (handle != 0 && fStrangers++ < 16) {
			IOLog("HakiosGPU: buffer %u is asked for and is not there\n", handle);
		}
		return NULL;
	}
	return &fBuffers[handle - 1];
}

/*
 * A handle and addresses of the GPU's for `size` bytes of a memory descriptor, from byte `from`
 * of it on (wired memory; both in whole pages). With the lock held; NULL: there is no room.
 */
struct gpu_buffer *
HakiosGPUUserClient::newBuffer(IOMemoryDescriptor * memory, uint64_t from, uint64_t size, uint32_t flags, uint32_t * handle)
{
	struct gpu_buffer * b = NULL;
	bool mapped = true;

	for (uint32_t n = 0; n < GPU_BUFFERS; n++) {
		uint32_t i = (fNextBuffer + n) % GPU_BUFFERS;

		if (fBuffers[i].memory == NULL) {
			b = &fBuffers[i];
			*handle = i + 1;
			fNextBuffer = i + 1;
			break;
		}
	}
	if (b == NULL || (b->address = hakios_gpu_address(size)) == 0) {
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: no %s left for a buffer of %llu bytes\n", b ? "addresses" : "handles", size);
		return NULL;
	}
	for (uint64_t offset = 0; offset < size && mapped; offset += 4096) {
		IOByteCount length = 0;
		addr64_t phys = memory->getPhysicalSegment(from + offset, &length, kIOMemoryMapperNone);

		mapped = phys != 0 && hakios_gpu_map(b->address + offset, phys, flags & MSM_BO_GPU_READONLY);
	}
	hakios_gpu_mapped();
	if (!mapped) {
		hakios_gpu_unmap(b->address, size);
		hakios_gpu_address_free(b->address, size);
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: a buffer of %llu bytes cannot be entered into the GPU's address space\n", size);
		return NULL;
	}
	b->size = size;
	b->flags = flags;
	b->seed = 0;
	b->pushed = 0;
	b->seen = false;
	b->fence = 0;
	b->surface = NULL;
	b->client = false;
	fBufferCount++;
	fBufferBytes += size;
	return b;
}

/* With the lock held. */
void
HakiosGPUUserClient::dropKept(struct gpu_kept * k)
{
	if (k->memory == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	if (hakios_gpu_ready()) {
		hakios_gpu_unmap(k->address, k->size);
		hakios_gpu_address_free(k->address, k->size);
	}
	k->memory->release();
	k->memory = NULL;
	fKeptBytes -= k->size;
}

/* With the lock held, the GPU done with the buffer: kept if it is worth it (those kept longest make way). */
bool
HakiosGPUUserClient::keep(IOMemoryDescriptor * memory, uint8_t * kernel, uint64_t address, uint64_t size, uint32_t flags)
{
	struct gpu_kept * place = NULL;

	if (gGPUKeep == 0 || size < GPU_KEEP_FROM || size > GPU_KEPT_BYTES / 4 || memory == NULL ||
	    (kernel == NULL && OSDynamicCast(IOBufferMemoryDescriptor, memory) == NULL)) {
		return false;
	}
	for (;;) {
		struct gpu_kept * oldest = NULL;

		place = NULL;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < GPU_KEPT; i++) {
			if (fKept[i].memory == NULL) {
				place = place != NULL ? place : &fKept[i];
			} else if (oldest == NULL || fKept[i].since < oldest->since) {
				oldest = &fKept[i];
			}
		}
		if (place != NULL && fKeptBytes + size <= GPU_KEPT_BYTES) {
			break;
		}
		dropKept(oldest);
	}
	place->memory = memory;
	place->kernel = kernel != NULL ? kernel : (uint8_t *) OSDynamicCast(IOBufferMemoryDescriptor, memory)->getBytesNoCopy();
	place->address = address;
	place->size = size;
	place->flags = flags;
	place->since = mach_absolute_time();
	fKeptBytes += size;
	return true;
}

IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::gemNew(struct msm_gem_new * request)
{
	uint64_t size = round_page_64(request->size), began = mach_absolute_time();
	struct gpu_buffer * b;
	IOBufferMemoryDescriptor * memory;

	if (size == 0 || size > GPU_BUFFER_MAX) {
		return kIOReturnBadArgument;
	}
	/* one kept of this size and kind, if there is one (the one kept last: likeliest still in the caches' way) */
	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	struct gpu_kept * found = NULL;
	uint64_t old;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(GPU_KEPT_SECONDS * NSEC_PER_SEC, &old);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < GPU_KEPT; i++) {
		struct gpu_kept * k = &fKept[i];

		if (k->memory != NULL && began - k->since > old) {
			dropKept(k);
		}

		if (k->memory != NULL && k->size == size && k->flags == request->flags && (found == NULL || k->since > found->since)) {
			found = k;
		}
	}
	for (uint32_t n = 0; found != NULL && n < GPU_BUFFERS; n++) {
		uint32_t h = (fNextBuffer + n) % GPU_BUFFERS;

		if (fBuffers[h].memory == NULL) {
			b = &fBuffers[h];
			bzero(b, sizeof(*b));
			b->memory = found->memory;
			b->kernel = found->kernel;
			b->address = found->address;
			b->size = found->size;
			b->flags = found->flags;
			fNextBuffer = h + 1;
			fBufferCount++;
			fBufferBytes += size;
			request->handle = h + 1;
			found->memory = NULL;
			fKeptBytes -= size;
			gGPUStat.given_again++;
			IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
			if (gGPUKeep == 2) {
				bzero(b->kernel, (size_t) b->size);
			}
			return kIOReturnSuccess;
		}
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	/* (the memory comes zeroed, and making it write-combined pushes the zeroes out of the cache) */
	memory = IOBufferMemoryDescriptor::inTaskWithOptions(kernel_task, kIODirectionInOut | kIOMemoryKernelUserShared |
	    (gGPUCached ? 0 : kIOMapWriteCombineCache), (vm_size_t) size, PAGE_SIZE);
	if (memory == NULL) {
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: no memory for a buffer of %llu bytes (%u buffers, %llu MB with this client)\n", size, fBufferCount,
		    fBufferBytes >> 20);
		return kIOReturnNoMemory;
	}
	if (gGPUCached) {
		hakios_gpu_to_memory(memory->getBytesNoCopy(), size);
	}

	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	b = newBuffer(memory, 0, size, request->flags, &request->handle);
	if (b != NULL) {
		b->memory = memory;
		b->kernel = (uint8_t *) memory->getBytesNoCopy();
		gGPUStat.made++;
		gGPUStat.making += mach_absolute_time() - began;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	if (b == NULL) {
		memory->release();
		return kIOReturnNoMemory;
	}
	return kIOReturnSuccess;
}

/*
 * The memory of an IOSurface as a buffer: its pixels, from the page after the surface's shared
 * state on (MiniIOSurface.h). The surface is held for as long as the buffer is there. A surface
 * that is a buffer of this client's already is that buffer again, as with Linux's handles: so
 * the client must not be giving that buffer back at the same moment (freedreno asks under the
 * lock it gives buffers back under). Asked only to describe (kHakiosDescribe), no buffer is made.
 */
IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::surfaceBuffer(struct hakios_surface * request)
{
	MiniIOSurface * s = MiniIOSurfaceCopy(request->surface);
	struct gpu_buffer * b = NULL;
	IOMemoryDescriptor * memory;
	uint64_t size, began = mach_absolute_time();

	if (s == NULL) {
		return kIOReturnNotFound;
	}
	if (s->client != NULL) {
		/* (memory of a program's own with a surface made around it: not in whole pages, and seldom in rows the GPU takes) */
		MiniIOSurfaceDrop(s);
		return kIOReturnUnsupported;
	}
	size = round_page_64(s->info.allocSize);
	memory = IOSubMemoryDescriptor::withSubRange(s->memory, PAGE_SIZE, size, kIODirectionInOut);
	if (memory == NULL || size == 0 || size > GPU_BUFFER_MAX) {
		OSSafeReleaseNULL(memory);
		MiniIOSurfaceDrop(s);
		return kIOReturnNoMemory;
	}
	request->size = size;
	request->offset = s->info.offset;
	request->rowBytes = s->info.bytesPerRow;
	request->width = s->info.width;
	request->height = s->info.height;
	request->pixelFormat = s->info.pixelFormat;
	request->planes = s->info.planeCount;
	if (request->handle == kHakiosDescribe) {
		request->handle = 0;
		memory->release();
		MiniIOSurfaceDrop(s);
		return kIOReturnSuccess;
	}

	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < GPU_BUFFERS; i++) {
		if (fBuffers[i].memory != NULL && fBuffers[i].surface == s) {
			b = &fBuffers[i];
			request->handle = i + 1;
			break;
		}
	}
	if (b != NULL) {
		memory->release();
		MiniIOSurfaceDrop(s);
	} else if ((b = newBuffer(s->memory, PAGE_SIZE, size, 0, &request->handle)) != NULL) {
		b->memory = memory;
		b->kernel = s->kbase + PAGE_SIZE;
		b->surface = s;
		gGPUStat.surfaces++;
	}
	gGPUStat.taking += mach_absolute_time() - began;
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	if (b == NULL) {
		memory->release();
		MiniIOSurfaceDrop(s);
		return kIOReturnNoMemory;
	}
	return kIOReturnSuccess;
}

/*
 * Pages of the client's own as a buffer, as Linux's userptr: wired for as long as the buffer is there,
 * entered into the GPU's address space, and seen by the kernel through a mapping of its own (for the
 * cache: they are ordinary memory, pushed out of this processor's cache at every submission that
 * names them). Vulkan's VK_EXT_external_memory_host over it (Turnip, tools/mesa/hakios-drm): Metal's
 * no-copy buffers, CoreAnimation's backing stores.
 */
IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::userBuffer(struct hakios_user_memory * request)
{
	IOMemoryDescriptor * memory = NULL;
	struct gpu_buffer * b;
	uint64_t began = mach_absolute_time();

	if ((request->address & PAGE_MASK) || (request->size & PAGE_MASK) || request->size == 0 ||
	    request->size > GPU_BUFFER_MAX) {
		static uint32_t said;

		if (said++ < 8) {
			IOLog("HakiosGPU: pages at %#llx (%llu bytes) of the client's: not whole pages of %u bytes\n",
			    request->address, request->size, (unsigned) PAGE_SIZE);
		}
		return kIOReturnBadArgument;
	}
	/* pages the client may only read (a window server's view of another program's backing store): the GPU reads them only */
	IOReturn prepared = kIOReturnNoMemory;
	for (int pass = 0; pass < 2 && prepared != kIOReturnSuccess; pass++) {
		memory = IOMemoryDescriptor::withAddressRange(request->address, request->size,
		    pass == 0 ? kIODirectionInOut : kIODirectionOut, fTask);
		if (memory == NULL) {
			IOLog("HakiosGPU: pages at %#llx (%llu bytes) of the client's: no descriptor\n", request->address, request->size);
			return kIOReturnNoMemory;
		}
		prepared = memory->prepare();
		if (prepared != kIOReturnSuccess) {
			memory->release();
			memory = NULL;
		} else if (pass == 1) {
			request->flags |= MSM_BO_GPU_READONLY;
		}
	}
	if (memory == NULL) {
		static uint32_t said;

		if (said++ < 8) {
			IOLog("HakiosGPU: pages at %#llx (%llu bytes) of the client's cannot be wired: %#x\n",
			    request->address, request->size, prepared);
		}
		return kIOReturnVMError;
	}
	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	b = newBuffer(memory, 0, request->size, request->flags, &request->handle);
	if (b != NULL) {
		b->memory = memory;             /* (its pages unwired as it goes: IOGeneralMemoryDescriptor::free) */
		b->kernel = NULL;
		b->client = true;
		b->seen = true;
		gGPUStat.surfaces++;
	}
	gGPUStat.taking += mach_absolute_time() - began;
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	if (b == NULL) {
		static uint32_t said;

		if (said++ < 8) {
			IOLog("HakiosGPU: pages at %#llx (%llu bytes) of the client's: no room for them in the GPU\n",
			    request->address, request->size);
		}
		memory->complete();
		memory->release();
		return kIOReturnNoMemory;
	}
	return kIOReturnSuccess;
}

IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::gemInfo(struct msm_gem_info * request)
{
	struct gpu_buffer * b;
	IOReturn ret = kIOReturnSuccess;

	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	b = buffer(request->handle);
	if (b == NULL) {
		ret = kIOReturnBadArgument;
	} else if (request->info == MSM_INFO_GET_OFFSET) {
		request->value = (uint64_t) request->handle << 32;      /* nobody maps by it here */
	} else if (request->info == MSM_INFO_GET_IOVA) {
		request->value = b->address;
	} else if (request->info == MSM_INFO_GET_FLAGS) {
		request->value = b->flags;
	} else if (request->info != MSM_INFO_SET_NAME) {            /* a name for somebody's debugger: not kept */
		ret = kIOReturnUnsupported;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	return ret;
}

IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::submit(struct msm_gem_submit * request)
{
	struct msm_gem_submit_bo * bos = NULL;
	struct msm_gem_submit_cmd * cmds = NULL;
	uint64_t addresses[GPU_SUBMIT_CMDS];
	uint32_t words[GPU_SUBMIT_CMDS], count = 0;
	uint64_t began, nanos, again;
	IOReturn ret = kIOReturnBadArgument;

	if (request->nr_cmds == 0 || request->nr_cmds > GPU_SUBMIT_CMDS || request->nr_bos == 0 || request->nr_bos > GPU_SUBMIT_BOS) {
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: a submission of %u command buffers in %u buffers: not taken\n", request->nr_cmds, request->nr_bos);
		return kIOReturnBadArgument;
	}
	bos = IONew(struct msm_gem_submit_bo, request->nr_bos);
	cmds = IONew(struct msm_gem_submit_cmd, request->nr_cmds);
	if (bos == NULL || cmds == NULL) {
		ret = kIOReturnNoMemory;
		goto out;
	}
	if (copyin((user_addr_t) request->bos, bos, request->nr_bos * sizeof(*bos)) != 0 ||
	    copyin((user_addr_t) request->cmds, cmds, request->nr_cmds * sizeof(*cmds)) != 0) {
		ret = kIOReturnVMError;
		goto out;
	}
	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	/*
	 * The GPU reads memory and writes memory. What this processor's cache holds of an IOSurface
	 * (somebody has written it, or has read it, as the display's driver does, and the GPU is to
	 * draw into it again) goes out of the cache now: when the surface is said to have changed
	 * (its seed: who writes one is to lock it, and so does a program that has had the GPU draw
	 * into one: userland/src/eagl.c), and in any case once in a few milliseconds, which is once
	 * a frame and not once a submission: not everybody who draws into a surface says so (an
	 * application drawing a picture that is on the screen meanwhile). A surface this program
	 * has mapped, every time. The buffers made here need none of that, unless they are
	 * ordinary memory (gpu_cached=1).
	 */
	began = mach_absolute_time();
	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(GPU_PUSH_AGAIN_MS * NSEC_PER_MSEC, &again);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < request->nr_bos; i++) {
		struct gpu_buffer * b = buffer(bos[i].handle);

		if (b == NULL) {
			continue;
		}
		if (b->surface != NULL) {
			uint32_t seed = b->surface->shared()->seed;

			if (seed == b->seed && !b->seen && began - b->pushed < again) {
				continue;
			}
			b->seed = seed;
			b->pushed = began;
		} else if (b->client) {
			/* the client's own pages are ordinary memory: out of the cache every time, by their physical addresses */
			for (uint64_t offset = 0; offset < b->size;) {
				IOByteCount length = 0;
				addr64_t phys = b->memory->getPhysicalSegment(offset, &length, kIOMemoryMapperNone);

				if (phys == 0 || length == 0) {
					break;
				}
				length = MIN(length, b->size - offset);
				flush_dcache64(phys, (unsigned) length, TRUE);
				offset += length;
			}
			gGPUStat.flushed += b->size;
			continue;
		} else if (!b->seen || !gGPUCached) {
			continue;
		}
		hakios_gpu_to_memory(b->kernel, b->size);
		gGPUStat.flushed += b->size;
	}
	hakios_gpu_to_memory(NULL, 0);                 /* (and what was written last is in memory: a barrier) */
	gGPUStat.flushing += mach_absolute_time() - began;
	gGPUStat.buffers += request->nr_bos;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < request->nr_cmds; i++) {
		struct gpu_buffer * b = cmds[i].submit_idx < request->nr_bos ? buffer(bos[cmds[i].submit_idx].handle) : NULL;

		if (cmds[i].type != MSM_SUBMIT_CMD_BUF) {
			continue;                               /* the other kinds are for a GPU shared between address spaces */
		}
		if (b == NULL || cmds[i].nr_relocs != 0 || (cmds[i].size & 3) || (cmds[i].submit_offset & 3) ||
		    (uint64_t) cmds[i].submit_offset + cmds[i].size > b->size) {
			IOLog("HakiosGPU: command buffer %u of a submission: buffer %u, offset %u, %u bytes, %u relocations: not taken\n",
			    i, cmds[i].submit_idx, cmds[i].submit_offset, cmds[i].size, cmds[i].nr_relocs);
			IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
			goto out;
		}
		addresses[count] = b->address + cmds[i].submit_offset;
		words[count++] = cmds[i].size / 4;
	}
	request->fence = hakios_gpu_submit(addresses, words, count);
	if (gpu_log && request->fence != 0) {
		/* "tl: Q FENCE at US: N buffers, B of 4 MB or more, W words of commands": what was given (tl: q: what it took) */
		uint32_t big = 0, all_words = 0;
		uint64_t ns;

		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < request->nr_bos; i++) {
			struct gpu_buffer * b = buffer(bos[i].handle);

			big += b != NULL && b->size >= (4u << 20);
		}
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			all_words += words[i];
		}
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &ns);
		hakios_tl("tl: Q %u at %llu: %u buffers, %u big, %u words\n", request->fence, ns / 1000, request->nr_bos, big, all_words);
	}
	if (request->flags & MSM_SUBMIT_FENCE_FD_OUT) {
		request->fence_fd = -1;
	}
	/*
	 * The surfaces named are being drawn into, or read, until this submission is done: the
	 * display's driver waits for that before it puts one on the panel (MiniIOSurfaceDrawn()).
	 * (freedreno names every buffer for reading and writing alike, so which it is cannot be
	 * told; the last submission of a frame names the surface the frame is drawn into.)
	 */
	for (uint32_t i = 0; request->fence != 0 && i < request->nr_bos; i++) {
		struct gpu_buffer * b = buffer(bos[i].handle);

		if (b != NULL) {
			b->fence = request->fence;
			if (b->surface != NULL) {
				b->surface->drawn = request->fence;
			}
		}
	}
	reap();
	if (request->fence == 0 && !gGPUReported) {
		gGPUReported = true;
		hakios_gpu_report("the ring is full");
	}
	if (fSubmits++ < 4) {
		/* (addresses and words are only set up to `count`: with no command buffer among the commands, the first would be stack garbage) */
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: submission %u: %u command buffers, the first at %#llx, %u words\n", request->fence, count,
		    count != 0 ? addresses[0] : 0ull, count != 0 ? words[0] : 0u);
	}
	/* every five seconds in which something was submitted: how much, and what it cost here */
	gGPUStat.submissions++;
	gGPUStat.commands += count;
	if (gGPUStat.since == 0) {
		gGPUStat.since = began;
	}
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - gGPUStat.since, &nanos);
	if (nanos >= 5 * NSEC_PER_SEC) {
		uint64_t flushing, waiting, taking, worked;
		uint32_t timed, by[7];

		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(gGPUStat.flushing, &flushing);
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(gGPUStat.waiting, &waiting);
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(gGPUStat.taking, &taking);
		hakios_gpu_worked(&worked, &timed, by);
		uint64_t making;

		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(gGPUStat.making, &making);
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: buffers: %u made in %llu us each, %u kept ones given again (%llu MB kept)\n", gGPUStat.made,
		    gGPUStat.made ? making / NSEC_PER_USEC / gGPUStat.made : 0, gGPUStat.given_again, fKeptBytes >> 20);
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: %u submissions in %llu ms: %u command buffers and %u buffers named, %llu KB out of the cache "
		    "in %llu us a submission; the GPU worked %llu us on each of %u (%u under 0.1 ms, %u under 0.25, %u under 0.5, "
		    "%u under 1, %u under 2, %u under 4, %u longer; %llu ms in all); %u waits of %llu us, %u over before they "
		    "began; %u IOSurfaces taken as buffers in %llu us each; %u buffers, %llu MB\n",
		    gGPUStat.submissions, nanos / NSEC_PER_MSEC, gGPUStat.commands, gGPUStat.buffers,
		    (gGPUStat.flushed >> 10) / gGPUStat.submissions, flushing / NSEC_PER_USEC / gGPUStat.submissions,
		    timed ? worked / timed : 0, timed, by[0], by[1], by[2], by[3], by[4], by[5], by[6], worked / 1000,
		    gGPUStat.waits, gGPUStat.waits ? waiting / NSEC_PER_USEC / gGPUStat.waits : 0, gGPUStat.over,
		    gGPUStat.surfaces, gGPUStat.surfaces ? taking / NSEC_PER_USEC / gGPUStat.surfaces : 0, fBufferCount,
		    fBufferBytes >> 20);
		bzero(&gGPUStat, sizeof(gGPUStat));
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	ret = request->fence != 0 ? kIOReturnSuccess : kIOReturnTimeout;
out:
	if (bos != NULL) {
		IODelete(bos, struct msm_gem_submit_bo, request->nr_bos);
	}
	if (cmds != NULL) {
		IODelete(cmds, struct msm_gem_submit_cmd, request->nr_cmds);
	}
	return ret;
}

/* Pixels of the caller's (32 bits each, blue first) copied to the panel: for a test to show what it has drawn. */
IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::show(const struct hakios_show * request)
{
	uint64_t size = (uint64_t) request->rowBytes * request->height;
	uint8_t * pixels;
	IOReturn ret = kIOReturnSuccess;

	if (request->width == 0 || request->width > 4096 || request->height == 0 || request->height > 4096 ||
	    request->rowBytes < 4 * request->width) {
		return kIOReturnBadArgument;
	}
	/* rowBytes is the caller's own number: without a limit it asks for terabytes of wired memory (no more than a buffer may be) */
	if (size > GPU_BUFFER_MAX) {
		return kIOReturnBadArgument;
	}
	pixels = (uint8_t *) IOMallocData(size);
	if (pixels == NULL) {
		return kIOReturnNoMemory;
	}
	if (copyin((user_addr_t) request->pixels, pixels, size) != 0) {
		ret = kIOReturnVMError;
	} else {
		MiniIOMobileFramebufferShow(pixels, request->width, request->height, request->rowBytes);
	}
	IOFreeData(pixels, size);
	return ret;
}

IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::clientMemoryForType(UInt32 type, IOOptionBits * options, IOMemoryDescriptor ** memory)
{
	struct gpu_buffer * b;
	IOReturn ret = kIOReturnBadArgument;

	IOLockLock(gGPULock);
	b = buffer(type);
	if (b != NULL) {
		b->memory->retain();
		b->seen = true;
		*memory = b->memory;
		*options = 0;
		ret = kIOReturnSuccess;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
	return ret;
}

IOReturn
HakiosGPUUserClient::externalMethod(uint32_t selector, IOExternalMethodArguments * args,
    IOExternalMethodDispatch * dispatch, OSObject * target, void * reference)
{
	union {
		struct msm_param param;
		struct msm_gem_new gemNew;
		struct msm_gem_info gemInfo;
		struct msm_gem_cpu_prep cpuPrep;
		struct msm_gem_submit submit;
		struct msm_wait_fence waitFence;
		struct msm_gem_madvise madvise;
		struct msm_submitqueue queue;
		struct msm_submitqueue_query query;
		struct drm_gem_close close;
		struct hakios_surface surface;
		struct hakios_user_memory user;
		struct hakios_show show;
	} r;
	size_t size = args->structureInputSize;
	struct gpu_buffer * b;
	IOReturn ret = kIOReturnSuccess;
	uint64_t zero = 0, patience, waitBegan;

	if (args->structureInput == NULL || size > sizeof(r) || fBuffers == NULL) {
		return kIOReturnBadArgument;
	}
	if (!hakios_gpu_ready() && selector != kHakiosShow) {
		return kIOReturnNotReady;                       /* given back: the run is ending */
	}
	bzero(&r, sizeof(r));
	memcpy(&r, args->structureInput, size);

	switch (selector) {
	case kMsmGetParam:
		ret = hakios_gpu_parameter(r.param.param, &r.param.value) ? kIOReturnSuccess : kIOReturnBadArgument;
		break;
	case kMsmSetParam:                              /* the program's name, for Linux's lists of who uses the GPU */
	case kMsmGemCpuFini:
	case kMsmSubmitQueueClose:
		break;
	case kMsmGemNew:
		ret = gemNew(&r.gemNew);
		break;
	case kMsmGemInfo:
		ret = gemInfo(&r.gemInfo);
		break;
	case kMsmGemCpuPrep:                            /* is the GPU done with a buffer: with all it has been given, here */
		waitBegan = mach_absolute_time();
		IOLockLock(gGPULock);
		patience = (r.cpuPrep.op & MSM_PREP_NOSYNC) ? 0 : millisecondsUntil(&r.cpuPrep.timeout);
		if (!gpuWait(hakios_gpu_last(), patience)) {
			ret = kIOReturnBusy;
			if (patience == 0 && !(r.cpuPrep.op & MSM_PREP_NOSYNC)) {
				waitOver(&r.cpuPrep.timeout, hakios_gpu_last());
			}
		}
		IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
		slowWait("cpu-prep", waitBegan);
		break;
	case kMsmGemSubmit:
		ret = submit(&r.submit);
		break;
	case kMsmWaitFence:
		waitBegan = mach_absolute_time();
		IOLockLock(gGPULock);
		/* a fence that was never issued is never done: refuse it, so that waiting for it cannot make gpuWait() declare the GPU dead for every client */
		if ((int32_t)(r.waitFence.fence - hakios_gpu_last()) > 0) {
			IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
			ret = kIOReturnBadArgument;
			break;
		}
		patience = millisecondsUntil(&r.waitFence.timeout);
		if (!gpuWait(r.waitFence.fence, patience)) {
			ret = kIOReturnTimeout;
			if (patience == 0) {
				waitOver(&r.waitFence.timeout, r.waitFence.fence);
			}
		}
		IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
		slowWait("fence", waitBegan);
		break;
	case kMsmGemMadvise:
		r.madvise.retained = 1;
		break;
	case kMsmSubmitQueueNew:
		r.queue.id = ++fNextQueue;
		break;
	case kMsmSubmitQueueQuery:                      /* how often the GPU has faulted on this client's commands */
		if (r.query.data != 0 && r.query.len >= sizeof(zero)) {
			copyout(&zero, (user_addr_t) r.query.data, sizeof(zero));
		}
		break;
	case kDrmGemClose:
		IOLockLock(gGPULock);
		b = buffer(r.close.handle);
		if (b == NULL) {
			ret = kIOReturnBadArgument;
		} else {
			freeBuffer(b);
			reap();
		}
		IOLockUnlock(gGPULock);
		break;
	case kHakiosSurface:
		ret = surfaceBuffer(&r.surface);
		break;
	case kHakiosUserMemory:
		ret = userBuffer(&r.user);
		break;
	case kHakiosShow:
		ret = show(&r.show);
		break;
	default:
		IOLog("HakiosGPU: request %#x (%zu bytes) is not known here\n", selector, size);
		ret = kIOReturnUnsupported;
		break;
	}
	if (ret == kIOReturnSuccess && args->structureOutput != NULL) {
		if (args->structureOutputSize > size) {
			args->structureOutputSize = (uint32_t) size;
		}
		memcpy(args->structureOutput, &r, args->structureOutputSize);
	}
	return ret;
}

```

`drivers/haptic/conf`:

```
# drivers/haptic/conf: the vibration motor.
# CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y in a defconfig builds a driver into the kernel; "standard" files are always built.
# tools/hakios-config.py reads this file; docs/drivers-config.md says what each word means and how it reaches XNU.

driver HAPTIC
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.haptic.c
	help    the vibration motor: an Awinic AW86927 driving a linear resonant actuator (haptic=N), its waveforms
	help    from fw-haptic/

```

`drivers/haptic/hakios.haptic.c`:

```c
/*
 * The vibration motor of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood): a linear resonant actuator driven by an
 * Awinic AW86927 (chip ID 0x9270), Android's "haptic_hv" (Xiaomi's driver aw8692x, version 1.7.0).
 * Every address and number below belongs to this phone, from Android's own device tree, its
 * kernel's log and the chip's registers as Android leaves them (read from sysfs, read-only):
 *
 *   I2C        the serial engine 9 (qupv3_se9_i2c at 0xa84000, function qup11 on GPIO 36 data and
 *              37 clock, internal pull-ups, 400 kHz under Android), address 0x5a; done by hand here
 *              as for the amplifiers (hakios.speaker.c), the two pins taken for each transaction
 *              and given back as they were found
 *   reset      GPIO 35, high = running (Android: low for 5 ms, then high, at its driver's start)
 *   interrupt  GPIO 18, pulled up, low when the chip has something to say (not used: polled)
 *   the motor  f0 175.5 Hz as Android calibrated it (f0_pre 170.0 Hz, calibration data 0x0d)
 *   effects    Android's RAM waveforms, /vendor/firmware/aw8697_haptic.bin of the phone (fw-haptic/
 *              here, not in the repository; userland/build.sh puts it into /fw of the system image):
 *              eleven of them, 1..10 short (Android's effects 0..9), 11 the one looped for a
 *              vibration of some length
 *
 * Nothing here is done unless a boot-arg asks for it:
 *
 *   haptic=1   a look, reading only: the pins, and whether the chip answers (its ID and registers,
 *              against what Android leaves in them). Out of Android's bootloader the reset pin is an
 *              input with a pull-down: the chip is held in reset and does not answer.
 *   haptic=2   ... and the reset released as Android's driver releases it (low 5 ms, then high; it
 *              stays released until the run ends), and the chip's registers read as they come out
 *              of reset, against Android's. Nothing is written to the chip.
 *   haptic=3   ... and Android's configuration written (every write read back), Android's
 *              waveforms loaded into its RAM and read back; then standby. Nothing moves.
 *   haptic=4   ... and one short effect played (haptic_effect=N, default 1: Android's effect 0)
 *   haptic=5   ... configured and loaded as for 3, and instead of the effect the motor for Darwin until
 *              the run ends: what Darwin plays on its "Actuator" device (the HAL plug-in's,
 *              userland/src/audio_plugin.c: the system's feedbacks and vibrations, CoreHaptics'
 *              patterns, UIKit's feedbacks) is written to /dev/hakios-haptic as samples of one
 *              channel, and the motor plays Android's waveforms by it: each waveform of Darwin's (a
 *              stretch of samples after a pause) a short tap (waveform 1), and one that goes on for
 *              longer than a tap the waveform Android loops for vibrations (11), until it ends -- or
 *              for HAPTIC_MAX_MS at most, after which the motor rests for as long before it plays
 *              again. The gain follows how loud Darwin's waveform is: Android's own (0x80) from a third
 *              of full scale up, five eighths of it for the softest, never above it (gain_for()).
 *
 * Limits, whatever asks: Android's own values only (its gain 0x80, its boost and drive levels, its
 * waveforms); no effect longer than HAPTIC_MAX_MS, and the chip is told to stop and put into
 * standby when that is over whether it has stopped or not; any fault the chip reports (under-
 * voltage, over-current, over-temperature, the boost's short circuit or over-voltage), a write that
 * does not read back or a byte nobody acknowledges, and the chip is put into reset and nothing more
 * is done for the rest of the run. At the run's end (and on a panic's way out) the chip goes back
 * into reset. Nothing is written anywhere but to the chip's registers and its RAM.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <sys/hakios.audio.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern kern_return_t thread_terminate(thread_t thread);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static vm_offset_t tlmm;
static uint32_t level;
static bool broken, released, leaving;

/* every line to the loader's log as well (and to the console when that may be written) */
static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (!leaving && ml_get_interrupts_enabled()) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
	return length;
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

static void
spin_us(uint32_t us)
{
	uint64_t until;

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime((uint64_t)us * NSEC_PER_USEC, &until);
	until += mach_absolute_time();
	while (mach_absolute_time() < until) {
	}
}

static void
wait_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	if (leaving) {
		spin_us(ms * 1000);
	} else {
		delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

/* ---- pins ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define TLMM_PHYS               0x0f100000UL
#define TLMM_SIZE               0x100000UL
#define GPIO_CFG(n)             (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n))         /* [1:0] pull, [5:2] function, [8:6] drive, [9] output */
#define GPIO_IO(n)              (tlmm + 0x1000UL * (n) + 4)     /* bit 0 in, bit 1 out */
#define CFG_PULL_UP             3
#define CFG_OUTPUT              (1u << 9)

#define PIN_SDA                 36      /* the serial engine's first pin is the data line, the second the clock */
#define PIN_SCL                 37
#define PIN_RESET               35
#define PIN_INT                 18

static void
show_pins(void)
{
	static const struct {
		unsigned pin;
		const char *what;
	} pins[] = { { PIN_SDA, "I2C data" }, { PIN_SCL, "I2C clock" }, { PIN_RESET, "reset" }, { PIN_INT, "interrupt" } };

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(pins) / sizeof(pins[0]); i++) {
		uint32_t cfg = rd(GPIO_CFG(pins[i].pin)), io = rd(GPIO_IO(pins[i].pin));

		say("haptic: gpio%u (%s): function %u, pull %u, %u mA, %s, reads %u\n", pins[i].pin, pins[i].what, (cfg >> 2) & 15,
		    cfg & 3, (((cfg >> 6) & 7) + 1) * 2, (cfg & CFG_OUTPUT) ? (io & 2 ? "drives high" : "drives low") : "input", io & 1);
	}
}

/* the reset pin as an output of the GPIO function, driving `high' (2 mA, no pull, as Android has it) */
static void
reset_pin(bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_RESET), high ? 2 : 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_RESET), CFG_OUTPUT);
	released = high;
}

/* ---- I2C by hand (as in hakios.speaker.c) ---------------------------------------------------------- */

static void
half_bit(void)
{
	spin_us(5);                     /* 100 kHz at most */
}

static void
line(unsigned pin, bool high)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(pin), 0);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(pin), CFG_PULL_UP | (high ? 0 : CFG_OUTPUT));
}

static bool
level_of(unsigned pin)
{
	return rd(GPIO_IO(pin)) & 1;
}

static void
i2c_start(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	half_bit();
}

static void
i2c_stop(void)
{
	line(PIN_SDA, false);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	half_bit();
}

static bool
i2c_bit(bool out)
{
	bool in;

	line(PIN_SDA, out);
	half_bit();
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	for (unsigned stretched = 0; !level_of(PIN_SCL) && stretched < 100; stretched++) {
		half_bit();
	}
	half_bit();
	in = level_of(PIN_SDA);
	line(PIN_SCL, false);
	return in;
}

static bool
i2c_write(uint8_t byte)
{
	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		i2c_bit((byte >> bit) & 1);
	}
	return !i2c_bit(true);
}

static uint8_t
i2c_read(bool more)
{
	uint8_t byte = 0;

	for (int bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--) {
		byte = (uint8_t)(byte << 1 | i2c_bit(true));
	}
	i2c_bit(!more);
	return byte;
}

static uint32_t taken_cfg[2], taken_io[2];

static bool
bus_take(void)
{
	taken_cfg[0] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA));
	taken_cfg[1] = rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL));
	taken_io[0] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA));
	taken_io[1] = rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL));
	line(PIN_SDA, true);
	line(PIN_SCL, true);
	half_bit();
	if (!level_of(PIN_SDA) || !level_of(PIN_SCL)) {
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
		wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
		say("haptic: the I2C bus is not at rest (gpio%u reads %u, gpio%u reads %u): not touched\n", PIN_SDA,
		    level_of(PIN_SDA), PIN_SCL, level_of(PIN_SCL));
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static void
bus_give_back(void)
{
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SDA), taken_io[0] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_IO(PIN_SCL), taken_io[1] & 2);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SDA), taken_cfg[0]);
	wr(GPIO_CFG(PIN_SCL), taken_cfg[1]);
}

#define AW_ADDRESS              0x5a

/* `count' 8-bit registers from `reg' on (the chip's address counts up, but for its RAM data port) */
static bool
regs_read(uint8_t reg, uint8_t *values, unsigned count)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write(AW_ADDRESS << 1) && i2c_write(reg);
	if (answered) {
		i2c_start();
		answered = i2c_write(AW_ADDRESS << 1 | 1);
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; answered && i < count; i++) {
		values[i] = i2c_read(i + 1 < count);
	}
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

static bool
regs_write(uint8_t reg, const uint8_t *values, unsigned count)
{
	bool answered;

	if (!bus_take()) {
		return false;
	}
	i2c_start();
	answered = i2c_write(AW_ADDRESS << 1) && i2c_write(reg);
	for (unsigned i = 0; answered && i < count; i++) {
		answered = i2c_write(values[i]);
	}
	i2c_stop();
	bus_give_back();
	return answered;
}

/* ---- the chip -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define AW_RSTCFG               0x00            /* 0xaa: a soft reset */
#define AW_SYSST                0x01
#define AW_SYSINT               0x02            /* read: cleared */
#define AW_SYSINTM              0x03
#define AW_PLAYCFG1             0x06            /* [7] boost on, [6:0] its voltage */
#define AW_PLAYCFG2             0x07            /* the gain */
#define AW_PLAYCFG3             0x08            /* [1:0] the play mode: 0 RAM */
#define AW_PLAYCFG4             0x09            /* [1] stop, [0] go */
#define AW_WAVCFG1              0x0a            /* the first waveform to play, 1..127 (0: the end) */
#define AW_WAVCFG2              0x0b
#define AW_WAVCFG9              0x12            /* [7:4] how often the first is repeated, 15: until told to stop */
#define AW_BASEADDRH            0x2d
#define AW_BASEADDRL            0x2e
#define AW_GLBRD5               0x3f            /* [3:0] the state: 0 standby */
#define AW_RAMADDRH             0x40
#define AW_RAMADDRL             0x41
#define AW_RAMDATA              0x42
#define AW_SYSCTRL3             0x45            /* [5] standby, [2] the RAM open for loading */
#define AW_TMCFG                0x5b            /* 0x7d opens the analog registers 0x70.. for writing, 0 closes them */
#define AW_TRIM_LRA             0x79            /* the motor's f0 calibration */
#define AW_CHIPIDH              0x57
#define AW_CHIPIDL              0x58
#define AW_CHIPID               0x9270

#define SYSINT_FAULTS           0xe6            /* boost short circuit and over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current, over-temperature */
#define HAPTIC_MAX_MS           1000

static void
give_up(const char *why)
{
	broken = true;
	say("haptic: %s: THE CHIP IS PUT INTO RESET (gpio%u low) and nothing more is done\n", why, PIN_RESET);
	if (tlmm != 0) {
		reset_pin(false);
	}
}

static bool
get(uint8_t reg, uint8_t *value)
{
	if (!regs_read(reg, value, 1)) {
		say("haptic: %#04x NOT READ\n", reg);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* One register written and read back. */
static bool
put(uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
{
	uint8_t after = 0;

	if (broken) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!regs_write(reg, &value, 1)) {
		say("haptic: %#04x <- %#04x NOT ACKNOWLEDGED\n", reg, value);
		give_up("a write was not acknowledged");
		return false;
	}
	if (!regs_read(reg, &after, 1)) {
		give_up("a register could not be read back");
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: %#04x <- %#04x, reads %#04x%s\n", reg, value, after, after == value ? "" : ": NOT AS WRITTEN");
	if (after != value) {
		give_up("a register did not read back as written");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* The chip's interrupt flags (reading clears them): false, and the chip given up on, if one is a fault. */
static bool
healthy(const char *when)
{
	uint8_t flags = 0;

	if (!get(AW_SYSINT, &flags)) {
		give_up("the flags could not be read");
		return false;
	}
	if (flags & SYSINT_FAULTS) {
		say("haptic: %s: the chip reports %#04x:%s%s%s%s%s\n", when, flags, flags & 0x80 ? " BOOST SHORT CIRCUIT" : "",
		    flags & 0x40 ? " BOOST OVER-VOLTAGE" : "", flags & 0x20 ? " UNDER-VOLTAGE" : "", flags & 0x04 ? " OVER-CURRENT" : "",
		    flags & 0x02 ? " OVER-TEMPERATURE" : "");
		give_up("a fault");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* Android's registers as its driver leaves them, read from the phone's sysfs (fw-haptic/android/haptic-sysfs.txt) */
static const uint8_t android_regs[0x7d] = {
	[0x00] = 0x82, [0x01] = 0x10, [0x02] = 0x11, [0x03] = 0x59, [0x04] = 0x09, [0x05] = 0x00, [0x06] = 0x47, [0x07] = 0x80,
	[0x08] = 0x07, [0x09] = 0x00, [0x0a] = 0x0b, [0x12] = 0xf0, [0x18] = 0x1e, [0x19] = 0x8d, [0x1a] = 0x71, [0x1b] = 0x06,
	[0x1c] = 0x58, [0x1d] = 0xcf, [0x1e] = 0x28, [0x1f] = 0x04, [0x20] = 0x06, [0x21] = 0x08, [0x22] = 0x0c, [0x23] = 0x0c,
	[0x24] = 0x62, [0x25] = 0x08, [0x26] = 0xa0, [0x27] = 0x08, [0x28] = 0x8c, [0x2d] = 0x08, [0x2f] = 0x46, [0x33] = 0x01,
	[0x34] = 0x01, [0x35] = 0x01, [0x36] = 0x02, [0x37] = 0x02, [0x38] = 0x02, [0x3b] = 0x05, [0x3c] = 0x08, [0x3e] = 0x1b,
	[0x40] = 0x08, [0x41] = 0x03, [0x45] = 0x12, [0x46] = 0x09, [0x47] = 0x5a, [0x49] = 0x28, [0x4a] = 0xbf, [0x4b] = 0x32,
	[0x4d] = 0x24, [0x4e] = 0x04, [0x4f] = 0x0a, [0x51] = 0x07, [0x57] = 0x92, [0x58] = 0x70, [0x59] = 0x04, [0x5a] = 0x98,
	[0x5d] = 0xf5, [0x5e] = 0x0d, [0x5f] = 0xf5, [0x60] = 0x41, [0x61] = 0xf6, [0x62] = 0x5c, [0x63] = 0x0e, [0x64] = 0xf9,
	[0x68] = 0x05, [0x69] = 0x21, [0x6b] = 0x02, [0x6c] = 0x15, [0x6d] = 0x89, [0x6e] = 0xc2, [0x6f] = 0x48, [0x70] = 0x0f,
	[0x71] = 0x93, [0x72] = 0x69, [0x73] = 0xa4, [0x74] = 0x89, [0x75] = 0x88, [0x77] = 0x40, [0x79] = 0x0d,
};

/* What the chip holds now, against Android's (registers 0x00..0x7c; 0x32 and 0x42 are data ports, not read). */
static void
show_registers(void)
{
	unsigned differ = 0;

	for (unsigned reg = 0; reg <= 0x7c; reg++) {
		uint8_t value = 0;

		if (reg == 0x32 || reg == 0x42) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!regs_read((uint8_t)reg, &value, 1)) {
			say("haptic: %#04x NOT READ\n", reg);
			return;
		}
		if (value != android_regs[reg]) {
			differ++;
			say("haptic: %#04x = %#04x (Android leaves %#04x)\n", reg, value, android_regs[reg]);
		}
	}
	say("haptic: %u registers differ from what Android leaves in them\n", differ);
}

static bool
chip_answers(void)
{
	uint8_t id[2] = { 0, 0 };

	if (!regs_read(AW_CHIPIDH, id, 2)) {
		say("haptic: nobody answers at %#x on the bus of gpio%u/%u\n", AW_ADDRESS, PIN_SDA, PIN_SCL);
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: the chip at %#x is %#06x%s\n", AW_ADDRESS, id[0] << 8 | id[1], (id[0] << 8 | id[1]) == AW_CHIPID ? ", an AW86927" :
	    ": NOT THE AW86927 EXPECTED");
	return (id[0] << 8 | id[1]) == AW_CHIPID;
}

/*
 * Android's configuration: the registers its driver sets (and the mainline Linux driver aw86927.c sets the
 * same way), with Android's values -- those that differ from the chip's own after a reset, as the phone
 * showed (haptic=2). Not written: the status and interrupt flags, the RAM's address and data ports, the
 * results of the chip's measurements (0x25..0x28: they do not take what is written, they are what its f0
 * tracking found under Android; 0x4f, 0x51, 0x59, 0x5a likewise), and what is set for each playing (0x08 the mode,
 * 0x0a/0x12 the waveform and its repeats). The values are all read from the chip as Android leaves it.
 */
static const uint8_t android_config[][2] = {
	{ 0x03, 0x59 },         /* the interrupt mask */
	{ 0x06, 0x47 },         /* PLAYCFG1: the boost in bypass, its voltage setting 0x47 (Android's vmax 7938 mV) */
	{ 0x1a, 0x71 },         /* CONTCFG3 */
	{ 0x1d, 0xcf },         /* CONTCFG6: f0 tracking on, the first drive level 0x4f */
	{ 0x1e, 0x28 },         /* CONTCFG7: the second drive level */
	{ 0x2f, 0x46 },         /* the FIFO's thresholds */
	{ 0x36, 0x02 }, { 0x37, 0x02 }, { 0x38, 0x02 },  /* the trigger pins' waveforms (the triggers stay off) */
	{ 0x39, 0x00 }, { 0x3a, 0x00 },  /* ... and off */
	{ 0x46, 0x09 },         /* SYSCTRL4: 24 kHz waveforms, the gain applied as it is */
	{ 0x47, 0x5a },
};
/*
 * ... and the analog ones, behind AW_TMCFG (the boost: skip mode, peak current 3.45 A, peak back, slew).
 * These too are Android's: what the phone's registers hold under Android (they differ from the chip's
 * own after a reset, so Android's driver set them); mainline Linux's aw86927.c sets the same values.
 */
static const uint8_t android_analog[][2] = {
	{ 0x70, 0x0f }, { 0x71, 0x93 }, { 0x72, 0x69 }, { 0x74, 0x89 }, { 0x75, 0x88 },
	{ AW_TRIM_LRA, 0x0d },  /* Android's f0 calibration of this motor (its log: "f0_cali_data = 0x0D") */
};

/* The analog registers opened or closed for writing (AW_TMCFG reads back as 0 either way: what tells is that the writes stick). */
static bool
unlock(bool open)
{
	uint8_t value = open ? 0x7d : 0x00;

	if (broken || !regs_write(AW_TMCFG, &value, 1)) {
		give_up("the analog registers could not be opened");
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: %#04x <- %#04x (the analog registers %s)\n", AW_TMCFG, value, open ? "opened" : "closed");
	return true;
}

static bool
configure(void)
{
	say("haptic: Android's configuration is written\n");
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(android_config) / sizeof(android_config[0]); i++) {
		if (!put(android_config[i][0], android_config[i][1])) {
			return false;
		}
	}
	if (!unlock(true)) {
		return false;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(android_analog) / sizeof(android_analog[0]); i++) {
		if (!put(android_analog[i][0], android_analog[i][1])) {
			(void)unlock(false);
			return false;
		}
	}
	return unlock(false) && healthy("after the configuration");
}

static uint32_t states_seen;           /* the GLBRD5 states seen by the last wait, a bit each */

/* until the chip says it is in standby (GLBRD5 state 0), at most `ms' */
static bool
wait_standby(unsigned ms)
{
	states_seen = 0;
	for (unsigned waited = 0; waited <= ms; waited += 2) {
		uint8_t state = 0xff;

		if (!get(AW_GLBRD5, &state)) {
			return false;
		}
		states_seen |= 1u << (state & 0x0f);
		if ((state & 0x0f) == 0) {
			return true;
		}
		wait_ms(2);
	}
	return false;
}

/*
 * Android's waveforms into the chip's RAM: the file is a checksum (16 bits, of all that follows), the
 * address the RAM's contents begin at (0x0800), and those contents -- a version byte, the start and end
 * address of each waveform, the waveforms. Written through the data port with the address counting up,
 * then read back the same way and compared.
 */
static bool
load_waveforms(void)
{
	uint64_t size = 0;
	const uint8_t *file = hakios_image_file("fw", "aw8697_haptic.bin", &size, NULL);
	uint32_t sum = 0, base, length;
	uint8_t address[2], back[64];

	if (file == NULL || size < 8) {
		say("haptic: no aw8697_haptic.bin in fw/ of the small image (fw-haptic/ when it is built)\n");
		return false;
	}
	for (uint64_t i = 2; i < size; i++) {
		sum += file[i];
	}
	if ((sum & 0xffff) != (uint32_t)(file[0] << 8 | file[1])) {
		say("haptic: aw8697_haptic.bin does not add up (%#x, it says %#x): not loaded\n", sum & 0xffff, file[0] << 8 | file[1]);
		return false;
	}
	base = (uint32_t)(file[2] << 8 | file[3]);
	length = (uint32_t)size - 4;
	say("haptic: Android's waveforms: %u bytes from %#x on, %u waveforms\n", length, base, (unsigned)(((file[5] << 8 | file[6]) -
	    base - 1) / 4));
	if (!wait_standby(250) || !put(AW_SYSCTRL3, (uint8_t)(android_regs[AW_SYSCTRL3] | 0x04))) {
		give_up("the RAM could not be opened");
		return false;
	}
	address[0] = (uint8_t)(base >> 8);
	address[1] = (uint8_t)base;
	if (!put(AW_BASEADDRH, address[0]) || !put(AW_BASEADDRL, address[1]) || !regs_write(AW_RAMADDRH, address, 2)) {
		give_up("the RAM's address could not be set");
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t at = 0; at < length; at += 32) {
		unsigned n = length - at < 32 ? length - at : 32;

		if (!regs_write(AW_RAMDATA, file + 4 + at, n)) {
			give_up("the RAM could not be written");
			return false;
		}
	}
	if (!regs_write(AW_RAMADDRH, address, 2)) {
		give_up("the RAM's address could not be set again");
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t at = 0; at < length; at += sizeof(back)) {
		unsigned n = length - at < sizeof(back) ? length - at : sizeof(back);

		if (!regs_read(AW_RAMDATA, back, n) || memcmp(back, file + 4 + at, n) != 0) {
			say("haptic: the RAM reads back differently at %#x\n", base + at);
			give_up("the waveforms did not load");
			return false;
		}
	}
	if (!put(AW_SYSCTRL3, android_regs[AW_SYSCTRL3])) {
		return false;
	}
	say("haptic: Android's waveforms are in the chip's RAM and read back as written\n");
	return healthy("after the waveforms");
}

/* One waveform played once (Android's effect `effect' - 1), stopped at HAPTIC_MAX_MS at the latest. */
static bool
play_effect(unsigned effect)
{
	uint64_t began = mach_absolute_time(), ended;
	bool done;

	say("haptic: waveform %u is played once, at Android's gain %#x\n", effect, android_regs[AW_PLAYCFG2]);
	if (!wait_standby(250) || !put(AW_PLAYCFG3, 0x04) || !put(AW_WAVCFG1, (uint8_t)effect) || !put(AW_WAVCFG2, 0x00) ||
	    !put(AW_WAVCFG9, 0x00) || !put(AW_PLAYCFG2, android_regs[AW_PLAYCFG2]) || !healthy("before playing")) {
		return false;
	}
	{
		uint8_t go = 0x01;

		if (!regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &go, 1)) {
			give_up("the start was not acknowledged");
			return false;
		}
	}
	wait_ms(2);
	done = wait_standby(HAPTIC_MAX_MS);
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &ended);
	if (!done) {
		uint8_t stop = 0x02;

		say("haptic: STILL PLAYING after %u ms: stopped\n", HAPTIC_MAX_MS);
		(void)regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &stop, 1);
		if (!wait_standby(50)) {
			give_up("it does not stop");
			return false;
		}
	}
	say("haptic: the waveform has played: back in standby after %llu ms (states seen meanwhile: %#x, a bit each; 0 is "
	    "standby)\n", ended / NSEC_PER_MSEC, states_seen);
	return healthy("after playing");
}

/* ---- haptic=5: the motor for Darwin ------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define ACTIVE_US               30000           /* a write that was not silence counts for this long */
#define SILENT_BELOW            256             /* of 32768: samples no larger are silence */
#define TAP_US                  60000           /* longer than this, and it is a vibration, not a tap */
#define SETTLE_US               8000            /* how long Darwin's waveform is listened to before a tap: its loudness */
#define FOLLOW_US               20000           /* how often a vibration's strength follows Darwin's */

#define TOLD_EVENTS             24              /* the first so many taps and vibrations are each said */

static volatile uint64_t heard_us;              /* when the last write that was not silence came */
static volatile uint64_t quiet_us;              /* when the last write that was silence came */
static volatile uint64_t onset_us;              /* when Darwin's last waveform began: the first write not silence after a pause */
static volatile uint32_t heard_peak;            /* the largest sample of that waveform, or since the service last looked */
static uint64_t written_frames;
static unsigned taps, loops, capped;            /* what has been played, for the run's end */

static uint64_t
now_us(void)
{
	uint64_t ns;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &ns);
	return ns / NSEC_PER_USEC;
}

/* From the audio server's I/O thread: never waits. */
static int
haptic_write(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	int16_t samples[256];
	int error = 0;

	while (uio_resid(uio) >= 2) {
		user_ssize_t bytes = uio_resid(uio);
		uint32_t peak = 0;

		if (bytes > (user_ssize_t)sizeof(samples)) {
			bytes = sizeof(samples);
		}
		bytes &= ~(user_ssize_t)1;
		if ((error = uiomove((caddr_t)samples, (int)bytes, uio)) != 0) {
			break;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < bytes / 2; i++) {
			uint32_t v = samples[i] < 0 ? (uint32_t)-(int32_t)samples[i] : (uint32_t)samples[i];

			peak = v > peak ? v : peak;
		}
		written_frames += (uint64_t)bytes / 2;
		if (peak > SILENT_BELOW) {
			uint64_t now = now_us();

			if (heard_us == 0 || quiet_us > heard_us || now - heard_us >= ACTIVE_US) {
				onset_us = now;
				heard_peak = 0;
			}
			heard_us = now;
			if (peak > heard_peak) {
				heard_peak = peak;
			}
		} else {
			quiet_us = now_us();
		}
	}
	return error;
}

/*
 * A test's stand-in for Darwin's waveform (hakios.mic.c, mic_tap=1: the microphone hears the motor): as if
 * a write of this loudness (of 32767) had just come, or silence for 0. The service plays it with all its
 * own limits, as it plays Darwin's.
 */
void
hakios_haptic_pretend(uint32_t peak)
{
	uint64_t now = now_us();

	if (peak <= SILENT_BELOW) {
		quiet_us = now;
		return;
	}
	if (heard_us == 0 || quiet_us > heard_us || now - heard_us >= ACTIVE_US) {
		onset_us = now;
		heard_peak = 0;
	}
	heard_us = now;
	if (peak > heard_peak) {
		heard_peak = peak;
	}
}

static int
haptic_open(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int type, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static const struct cdevsw haptic_cdevsw = {
	.d_open = haptic_open, .d_close = haptic_open, .d_read = eno_rdwrt, .d_write = haptic_write,
	.d_ioctl = eno_ioctl, .d_stop = eno_stop, .d_reset = eno_reset, .d_select = eno_select,
	.d_mmap = eno_mmap, .d_strategy = eno_strat, .d_type = 0
};

/* Start a waveform without waiting for it: once, or (`forever') until stopped. */
static bool
start_waveform(unsigned waveform, bool forever, uint8_t gain)
{
	uint8_t go = 0x01;

	if (!put(AW_PLAYCFG3, 0x04) || !put(AW_WAVCFG1, (uint8_t)waveform) || !put(AW_WAVCFG2, 0x00) ||
	    !put(AW_WAVCFG9, forever ? 0xf0 : 0x00) || !put(AW_PLAYCFG2, gain)) {
		return false;
	}
	if (!regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &go, 1)) {
		give_up("the start was not acknowledged");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static bool
stop_waveform(void)
{
	uint8_t stop = 0x02;

	if (!regs_write(AW_PLAYCFG4, &stop, 1) || !wait_standby(50)) {
		give_up("it does not stop");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* the chip's state (GLBRD5: 0 standby, 7 and 11 seen while a waveform plays), 0xff if it cannot be read */
static unsigned
chip_state(void)
{
	uint8_t state = 0xff;

	return get(AW_GLBRD5, &state) ? state & 0x0f : 0xff;
}

/*
 * How strong to play what Darwin plays. Darwin drives its Taptic Engine with waveforms far under full
 * scale for most feedbacks (a tap's peak anywhere from 1000 to 33000 of 32768, a vibration's
 * about 17000), and followed in proportion (gain = Android's * peak / full scale) most of them came
 * out at a tenth of Android's gain or less: not felt at all. Android plays its own clicks and
 * vibrations at its gain, 0x80. So: Android's gain from a third of full scale up, and below that
 * down to five eighths of it for the softest -- never above Android's.
 */
static uint8_t
gain_for(uint32_t peak)
{
	uint32_t top = android_regs[AW_PLAYCFG2], low = top * 5 / 8, third = 32767 / 3;

	return (uint8_t)(peak >= third ? top : low + (top - low) * peak / third);
}

static void
serve(void)
{
	enum { IDLE, TAP, LOOP, REST } state = IDLE;
	uint64_t since = 0, rest_until = 0, last_look = 0, tap_onset = 0, followed = 0;
	uint8_t playing_gain = 0;
	unsigned follows = 0;                   /* how often the vibration playing now has changed strength */
	int major = cdevsw_add(-1, &haptic_cdevsw);

	if (major < 0 || devfs_make_node(makedev(major, 0), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "hakios-haptic") == NULL) {
		say("haptic: /dev/hakios-haptic cannot be made\n");
		return;
	}
	say("haptic: THE MOTOR PLAYS WHAT DARWIN PLAYS ON ITS ACTUATOR (/dev/hakios-haptic) from here on, until the run ends\n");
	while (!broken) {
		uint64_t now = now_us();
		bool active = heard_us != 0 && now - heard_us < ACTIVE_US;
		uint32_t peak = heard_peak;
		uint8_t gain = gain_for(peak);

		switch (state) {
		case IDLE:
		case TAP:
			/*
			 * A waveform of Darwin's that has begun (after a pause: a tap of a series is a tap of its own) is
			 * a tap -- once its first milliseconds are heard: a waveform begins softly, and they say how
			 * loud it is; one that goes on without a pause, a vibration.
			 */
			if (active && onset_us != tap_onset && now - onset_us >= SETTLE_US) {
				uint64_t began = onset_us;

				if (state == TAP && !wait_standby(0) && !stop_waveform()) {
					break;
				}
				if (!start_waveform(1, false, gain ? gain : 1)) {
					break;
				}
				state = TAP;
				since = now;
				tap_onset = began;
				taps++;
				if (taps + loops <= TOLD_EVENTS) {
					wait_ms(4);
					say("haptic: tap %u: Darwin's waveform peaks at %u of 32768: Android's waveform 1 at gain %#04x; the "
					    "chip's state %u\n", taps, peak, gain ? gain : 1, chip_state());
				}
				break;
			}
			if (state == IDLE) {
				break;
			}
			if (active && quiet_us < tap_onset && now - since > TAP_US) {
				if (stop_waveform() && start_waveform(11, true, gain ? gain : 1)) {
					state = LOOP;
					since = followed = now;
					playing_gain = gain ? gain : 1;
					follows = 0;
					loops++;
					heard_peak = 0;
					if (taps + loops <= TOLD_EVENTS) {
						wait_ms(4);
						say("haptic: vibration %u: Darwin goes on playing (peak %u): Android's waveform 11 over and over at "
						    "gain %#04x, %u ms at most; the chip's state %u\n", loops, peak, gain ? gain : 1,
						    HAPTIC_MAX_MS, chip_state());
					}
				}
			} else if (!active && now - since > TAP_US) {
				state = wait_standby(0) || stop_waveform() ? IDLE : state;
			}
			break;
		case LOOP:
			/* as strong as Darwin's waveform is now (Android's gain at full scale, never more) */
			if (active && now - followed >= FOLLOW_US) {
				followed = now;
				heard_peak = 0;
				if (peak != 0 && (gain > playing_gain + 8 || gain + 8 < playing_gain)) {
					if (!put(AW_PLAYCFG2, gain)) {
						break;
					}
					playing_gain = gain;
					follows++;
				}
			}
			if (!active || now - since > HAPTIC_MAX_MS * 1000ull) {
				bool cut = now - since > HAPTIC_MAX_MS * 1000ull;

				if (cut) {
					capped++;
					rest_until = now + HAPTIC_MAX_MS * 1000ull;
				}
				if (stop_waveform()) {
					state = rest_until > now ? REST : IDLE;
					if (taps + loops <= TOLD_EVENTS + 1) {
						say("haptic: vibration %u: %s after %llu ms (its strength changed %u times, last to gain %#04x); "
						    "the chip is in standby\n", loops, cut ? "CUT at the limit" : "Darwin stopped, and so does the motor",
						    (now - since) / 1000, follows, playing_gain);
					}
				}
			}
			break;
		case REST:
			if (now >= rest_until) {
				state = IDLE;
			}
			break;
		}
		if (state != IDLE && state != REST && now - last_look > 50000) {
			last_look = now;
			if (!healthy("while playing")) {
				break;
			}
		}
		wait_ms(4);
	}
	say("haptic: the motor is given up on (%u taps and %u vibrations played, %u cut at %u ms)\n", taps, loops, capped,
	    HAPTIC_MAX_MS);
}

static void
haptic_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	bool loaded = false;

	tlmm = ml_io_map(TLMM_PHYS, TLMM_SIZE);
	say("haptic: level %u: %s\n", level, level == 1 ? "a look, reading only" : level == 2 ? "the reset released, registers read" :
	    level == 3 ? "the chip configured and its waveforms loaded, nothing played" : level == 4 ? "one effect played" :
	    "the motor for Darwin");
	show_pins();
	if (level >= 2 && !((rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_RESET)) & CFG_OUTPUT) && (rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_RESET)) & 2))) {
		/* (Android's driver: the pin low, 5 ms, high, and the chip ready for I2C 8 ms later) */
		say("haptic: the reset is released: gpio%u low for 5 ms, then high\n", PIN_RESET);
		reset_pin(false);
		wait_ms(5);
		reset_pin(true);
		wait_ms(8);
	}
	if (!chip_answers()) {
		say("haptic: (the reset pin %s)\n", (rd(GPIO_CFG(PIN_RESET)) & CFG_OUTPUT) && (rd(GPIO_IO(PIN_RESET)) & 2) ?
		    "drives high: the chip should answer" : "does not drive high: the chip is held in reset or not powered");
		if (released) {
			give_up("the chip does not answer");
		}
	} else {
		show_registers();
		/* (kept apart from `level == 4' so that level 5 can tell that the waveforms are really in the RAM) */
		loaded = level >= 3 && configure() && load_waveforms();
		if (loaded && level == 4) {
			uint32_t effect = 1;

			PE_parse_boot_argn("haptic_effect", &effect, sizeof(effect));
			if (effect < 1 || effect > 10) {
				effect = 1;     /* (the short ones only) */
			}
			(void)play_effect(effect);
		} else if (level == 5 && !broken && loaded) {
			/* (not started when the waveforms did not load: it would play whatever the RAM held) */
			serve();
		} else if (level == 5 && !broken) {
			give_up("the waveforms are not loaded");
		}
	}
	say("haptic: done\n");
	thread_terminate(current_thread());
}

void
hakios_haptic_init(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("haptic", &level, sizeof(level)) || level == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (level > 5) {
		level = 5;
	}
	if (kernel_thread_start(haptic_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}

/* At the run's end and on a panic's way out: the chip back into reset, if it was let out. */
void
hakios_haptic_quiesce(void)
{
	if (released && tlmm != 0) {
		leaving = true;
		reset_pin(false);
		if (level == 5) {
			say("haptic: at the run's end: %u taps and %u vibrations played (%u cut at %u ms), from %llu frames Darwin "
			    "wrote; the chip is held in reset\n", taps, loops, capped, HAPTIC_MAX_MS, written_frames);
		}
	}
}
```

```
# drivers/input/conf: touch, buttons, and the queue they post to.
# CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y in a defconfig builds a driver into the kernel; "standard" files are always built.
# tools/hakios-config.py reads this file; docs/drivers-config.md says what each word means and how it reaches XNU.

standard bsd/dev/hakios.input.c
	help    /dev/hakios-touch, the queue of touches and buttons, and where the phone's drivers are started from

driver VIRTIO_INPUT
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.virtio_input.c
	help    QEMU's virtio tablet and keyboard as the touch screen and the buttons (virtio_input=1). QEMU only

driver GOODIX
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.goodix.c
	help    the touch screen: a Goodix GT9916 ("Berlin-D") or a FocalTech FT3680 on SPI (touchscreen=1). The bus,
	help    pins and supplies are the POCO X5 Pro's; another phone with one of these controllers changes those

driver BUTTONS
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.buttons.c
	help    the power and volume keys, read from the PMIC through the SPMI arbiter (buttons=1)
```
