`drivers/input/hakios.input.c`:

```c
/*
 * /dev/hakios-touch: a queue of touch samples (see sys/hakios.input.h).
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/proc.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>

#define TOUCH_QUEUE     512             /* records; a power of two */

/*
 * Boot-arg touch_lat=1: for measuring how long a touch takes to reach the panel, a line for every
 * sample posted ("tl: p TYPE FINGER X Y at US", the time in microseconds of mach_absolute_time),
 * to be matched with the window server's lines about reading it (userland/src/inject.c), drawing
 * (eagl.c) and the display driver's about the frame (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp): see
 * tools/latency.py.
 */
static uint32_t touch_lat = 2;          /* 2: not yet looked up */

extern void loader_log_line(const char *line);

/*
 * A "tl:" line, for the kernel's drivers: into the loader's log as it is written -- the kernel's own
 * log keeps only the last of a run, and a live look at the loader's (XL_FOLLOW) then misses nothing.
 */
void hakios_tl(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

void
hakios_tl(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[192];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	loader_log_line(line);
}

static bool
latency_lines(void)
{
	if (touch_lat == 2) {
		uint32_t on = 0;

		touch_lat = PE_parse_boot_argn("touch_lat", &on, sizeof(on)) && on != 0;
	}
	return touch_lat != 0;
}

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(touch_lck_grp, "hakios-touch");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(touch_lock, &touch_lck_grp);
static struct hakios_touch touch_queue[TOUCH_QUEUE];
static uint32_t touch_head, touch_tail;        /* read from head, add at tail */

/*
 * The way out when nothing else is at hand: five fingers held on the screen for a second and a
 * half end the run -- control goes back to the loader, as when loader_return_after expires.
 * Only a driver's fingers count, not samples a program writes to the device.
 */
#define EXIT_FINGERS    5
#define EXIT_HOLD_MS    1500

extern void loader_return(void);

static thread_call_t exit_call;
static uint32_t fingers_down;           /* one bit for each finger a driver says is down */

static void
exit_hold_elapsed(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	printf("\n--- %d fingers held on the screen for %d ms: back to the loader ---\n", EXIT_FINGERS, EXIT_HOLD_MS);
	hakios_adreno_stop();
	loader_return();
}

/* With touch_lock held. */
static void
count_fingers(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger)
{
	int before = __builtin_popcount(fingers_down), now;
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (finger >= 32 || exit_call == NULL || (type != HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN && type != HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP)) {
		return;
	}
	if (type == HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN) {
		fingers_down |= 1u << finger;
	} else {
		fingers_down &= ~(1u << finger);
	}
	now = __builtin_popcount(fingers_down);
	if (now >= EXIT_FINGERS && before < EXIT_FINGERS) {
		clock_interval_to_deadline(EXIT_HOLD_MS, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(exit_call, deadline);
	} else if (now < EXIT_FINGERS && before >= EXIT_FINGERS) {
		thread_call_cancel(exit_call);
	}
}

/*
 * What the fingers' samples were like, said every 8 strokes: the lines of touch_lat=1 are many, and a long run's log keeps only its
 * beginning and its end. From the first move after a finger came down, between moves, and from the last move to its lift.
 */
static struct {
	uint64_t last;
	uint32_t strokes, moves, firsts, slow_moves, longest_move, first_sum, first_longest, lift_sum, lift_longest;
	uint32_t finger;
	bool down, moved;
} touch_feel;

static void
touch_feel_add(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger, uint64_t now)
{
	uint64_t nanos;
	uint32_t ms;

	if (type == HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN && !touch_feel.down) {
		touch_feel.down = true;
		touch_feel.moved = false;
		touch_feel.finger = finger;
		touch_feel.last = now;
		return;
	}
	if (!touch_feel.down || finger != touch_feel.finger) {
		return;
	}
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now - touch_feel.last, &nanos);
	ms = (uint32_t)(nanos / 1000000);
	touch_feel.last = now;
	if (type == HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP) {
		touch_feel.down = false;
		touch_feel.strokes++;
		touch_feel.lift_sum += ms;
		touch_feel.lift_longest = ms > touch_feel.lift_longest ? ms : touch_feel.lift_longest;
		if (touch_feel.strokes % 8 == 0) {
			printf("touch: %u strokes: first move after %u ms on average, %u at most; %u moves, %u of them over 13 ms apart, %u at most; "
			    "the lift %u ms after the last move on average, %u at most\n", touch_feel.strokes,
			    touch_feel.firsts != 0 ? touch_feel.first_sum / touch_feel.firsts : 0, touch_feel.first_longest, touch_feel.moves,
			    touch_feel.slow_moves, touch_feel.longest_move, touch_feel.lift_sum / touch_feel.strokes, touch_feel.lift_longest);
		}
	} else if (!touch_feel.moved) {
		touch_feel.moved = true;
		touch_feel.firsts++;
		touch_feel.first_sum += ms;
		touch_feel.first_longest = ms > touch_feel.first_longest ? ms : touch_feel.first_longest;
	} else {
		touch_feel.moves++;
		touch_feel.slow_moves += ms > 13;
		touch_feel.longest_move = ms > touch_feel.longest_move ? ms : touch_feel.longest_move;
	}
}

static void
touch_post(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger, uint32_t x, uint32_t y, bool from_driver)
{
	struct hakios_touch *t;

	lck_mtx_lock(&touch_lock);
	if (touch_tail - touch_head == TOUCH_QUEUE) {
		touch_head++;                   /* nobody reads: drop the oldest */
	}
	t = &touch_queue[touch_tail++ % TOUCH_QUEUE];
	t->time = mach_absolute_time();
	if (from_driver) {
		touch_feel_add(type, finger, t->time);
	}
	if (latency_lines()) {
		uint64_t ns;

		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(t->time, &ns);
		hakios_tl("tl: p %u %u %u %u at %llu\n", type, finger, x, y, ns / 1000);
	}
	t->type = type;
	t->finger = finger;
	t->x = x > 65535 ? 65535 : x;
	t->y = y > 65535 ? 65535 : y;
	if (from_driver) {
		count_fingers(type, finger);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
	wakeup(&touch_queue);
}

void
hakios_touch_post(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger, uint32_t x, uint32_t y)
{
	touch_post(type, finger, x, y, true);
}

static int
touch_open(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int devtype, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static int
touch_close(__unused dev_t dev, __unused int flags, __unused int devtype, __unused struct proc *p)
{
	return 0;
}

static int
touch_read(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	struct hakios_touch t;
	int error = 0, moved = 0;

	/* a buffer smaller than one record can never be served: say so, instead of blocking for data and then returning 0 (end of file) */
	if (uio_resid(uio) == 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	if (uio_resid(uio) < (user_ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
		return EINVAL;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&touch_lock);
	while (touch_head == touch_tail) {
		error = msleep(&touch_queue, &touch_lock, PZERO | PCATCH, "hakios-touch", NULL);
		if (error) {
			lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
			return error;
		}
	}
	while (touch_head != touch_tail && uio_resid(uio) >= (user_ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
		t = touch_queue[touch_head++ % TOUCH_QUEUE];
		lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
		error = uiomove((caddr_t)&t, sizeof(t), uio);
		lck_mtx_lock(&touch_lock);
		if (error) {
			/* the copy-out failed: put the record back at the head so a lost DOWN or UP does not leave a finger stuck (only if the ring still has room for it) */
			if (touch_tail - touch_head < TOUCH_QUEUE) {
				touch_queue[--touch_head % TOUCH_QUEUE] = t;
			}
			break;
		}
		moved++;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&touch_lock);
	return moved ? 0 : error;
}

static int
touch_write(__unused dev_t dev, struct uio *uio, __unused int ioflag)
{
	struct hakios_touch t;
	int error = 0;

	while (uio_resid(uio) >= (user_ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
		error = uiomove((caddr_t)&t, sizeof(t), uio);
		if (error) {
			break;
		}
		if (t.type < HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN || t.type > HAKIOS_BUTTON_UP) {
			return EINVAL;
		}
		touch_post(t.type, t.finger, t.x, t.y, false);
	}
	return error;
}

static const struct cdevsw touch_cdevsw = {
	.d_open = touch_open, .d_close = touch_close, .d_read = touch_read, .d_write = touch_write,
	.d_ioctl = eno_ioctl, .d_stop = eno_stop, .d_reset = eno_reset, .d_select = eno_select,
	.d_mmap = eno_mmap, .d_strategy = eno_strat, .d_type = 0
};

void
hakios_input_init(void)
{
	int major = cdevsw_add(-1, &touch_cdevsw);

	if (major < 0 || devfs_make_node(makedev(major, 0), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, "hakios-touch") == NULL) {
		printf("hakios-touch: cannot create the device\n");
	}
	exit_call = thread_call_allocate(exit_hold_elapsed, NULL);
	hakios_cpufreq_init();
	hakios_virtio_input_init();
	hakios_goodix_init();
	hakios_buttons_init();
	hakios_battery_init();
	hakios_ufs_init();
	hakios_net_init();
	hakios_adreno_init();
	hakios_wifi_init();
	hakios_adsp_init();
	hakios_mpss_init();
}
```

`drivers/input/hakios.virtio_input.c`:

```c
/*
 * Virtio input devices as a source of touches and buttons (see sys/hakios.input.h).
 *
 * Under QEMU's "virt" machine a "virtio-tablet-device" stands for the touch screen (the pointer
 * with its button held is a finger) and a "virtio-keyboard-device" for the phone's buttons. They
 * sit on the machine's virtio-mmio bus, which must be the current one, not "legacy"
 * (-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false). Only with boot-arg virtio_input=1: the bus address
 * is QEMU's and means nothing on the phone.
 *
 * No interrupt is used; the event queues are looked at 125 times a second.
 *
 * The keyboard is also a way to tell the kernel something from the host while the system runs:
 * F12, a process name, Enter prints where every thread of that process is (ustacks_now(); the
 * host side is "qemu/touch.py stacks NAME"). F11 is five fingers on the screen for as long as it
 * is held, which is how the way out in hakios.input.c is tried ("qemu/touch.py key fivefingers 2000").
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);       /* pmap_paddr_t */

#define VIRTIO_BUS              0x0a000000UL    /* QEMU virt: 32 transports of 0x200 bytes */
#define VIRTIO_SLOTS            32
#define VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE        0x200

#define VIRTIO_MAGIC            0x000           /* "virt" */
#define VIRTIO_VERSION          0x004
#define VIRTIO_DEVICE_ID        0x008
#define VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES  0x020
#define VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL 0x024
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_SEL        0x030
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX    0x034
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM        0x038
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_READY      0x044
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY     0x050
#define VIRTIO_STATUS           0x070
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DESC       0x080
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DRIVER     0x090
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DEVICE     0x0a0

#define VIRTIO_ID_INPUT         18
#define STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE      1
#define STATUS_DRIVER           2
#define STATUS_DRIVER_OK        4
#define STATUS_FEATURES_OK      8
#define STATUS_FAILED           0x80

#define QUEUE_SIZE              64
#define DESC_F_WRITE            2
#define AVAIL_F_NO_INTERRUPT    1

struct vq_desc {
	uint64_t addr;
	uint32_t len;
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t next;
};
struct vq_avail {
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t idx;
	uint16_t ring[QUEUE_SIZE];
};
struct vq_used {
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t idx;
	struct {
		uint32_t id;
		uint32_t len;
	} ring[QUEUE_SIZE];
};
struct input_event {
	uint16_t type;
	uint16_t code;
	uint32_t value;
};

/* everything the device reads and writes is in one page */
#define OFFSET_DESC             0x0000
#define OFFSET_AVAIL            0x0400
#define OFFSET_USED             0x0800
#define OFFSET_EVENTS           0x1000

/* Linux input event numbers, which is what virtio input speaks */
#define EV_SYN                  0
#define EV_KEY                  1
#define EV_ABS                  3
#define ABS_X                   0
#define ABS_Y                   1
#define ABS_RANGE               0x7fff          /* QEMU's tablet: 0..0x7fff across the screen */
#define BTN_LEFT                0x110
#define BTN_TOUCH               0x14a

struct input_device {
	vm_offset_t             regs;
	struct vq_avail *       avail;
	struct vq_used *        used;
	struct input_event *    events;
	uint16_t                seen;           /* how far the used ring has been read */
	/* the pointer */
	uint32_t                x, y;
	bool                    pressed, touching, moved;
};

#define MAX_DEVICES     4
static struct input_device devices[MAX_DEVICES];
static int device_count;
static thread_call_t poll_call;

static inline uint32_t
reg_read(struct input_device *d, uint32_t reg)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)(d->regs + reg);
}

static inline void
reg_write(struct input_device *d, uint32_t reg, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)(d->regs + reg) = value;
}

static inline void
reg_write64(struct input_device *d, uint32_t reg, uint64_t value)
{
	reg_write(d, reg, (uint32_t)value);
	reg_write(d, reg + 4, (uint32_t)(value >> 32));
}

extern void ustacks_now(const char *name);

#define KEY_ENTER               28
#define KEY_LEFTSHIFT           42
#define KEY_RIGHTSHIFT          54
#define KEY_F11                 87
#define KEY_F12                 88

/* F12 NAME Enter: the keys in between spell a process name. Returns true if the key was taken. */
static bool
command_key(uint16_t key, uint32_t value)
{
	static const char plain[] =
	    "\0\0001234567890-=\0\0qwertyuiop[]\0\0asdfghjkl;'`\0\\zxcvbnm,./\0\0\0 ";
	static char name[32];
	static unsigned length;
	static bool active, shift;

	if (key == KEY_F12) {
		if (value == 1) {
			active = true;
			length = 0;
		}
		return true;
	}
	if (!active) {
		return false;
	}
	if (key == KEY_LEFTSHIFT || key == KEY_RIGHTSHIFT) {
		shift = value != 0;
	} else if (value != 1) {
		/* a release or a repeat */
	} else if (key == KEY_ENTER) {
		active = false;
		name[length] = 0;
		if (length) {
			printf("virtio-input: stacks of \"%s\" asked for\n", name);
			ustacks_now(name);
		}
	} else if (key < sizeof(plain) - 1 && plain[key] != 0 && length < sizeof(name) - 1) {
		char c = plain[key];

		if (shift && c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') {
			c -= 'a' - 'A';
		} else if (shift && c == '-') {
			c = '_';
		}
		name[length++] = c;
	}
	return true;
}

/* Which of the phone's buttons a key stands for; 0 = none. */
static uint32_t
button_for_key(uint16_t key)
{
	switch (key) {
	case 116: /* KEY_POWER */
	case 38:  /* KEY_L */
		return HAKIOS_BUTTON_LOCK;
	case 115: /* KEY_VOLUMEUP */
	case 103: /* KEY_UP */
		return HAKIOS_BUTTON_VOLUME_UP;
	case 114: /* KEY_VOLUMEDOWN */
	case 108: /* KEY_DOWN */
		return HAKIOS_BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN;
	case 102: /* KEY_HOME */
	case 35:  /* KEY_H */
		return HAKIOS_BUTTON_HOME;
	}
	return 0;
}

static void
input_event(struct input_device *d, const struct input_event *e)
{
	uint32_t button;

	switch (e->type) {
	case EV_ABS:
		if (e->code == ABS_X) {
			d->x = e->value * 65535 / ABS_RANGE;
			d->moved = true;
		} else if (e->code == ABS_Y) {
			d->y = e->value * 65535 / ABS_RANGE;
			d->moved = true;
		}
		break;
	case EV_KEY:
		if (e->code == BTN_LEFT || e->code == BTN_TOUCH) {
			d->pressed = e->value != 0;
		} else if (command_key(e->code, e->value)) {
			break;
		} else if (e->code == KEY_F11 && e->value < 2) {
			/* five more fingers, for as long as the key is held: the way out of hakios.input.c */
			for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
				hakios_touch_post(e->value ? HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN : HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP, 5 + i, 13107 + 9830 * i, 32768);
			}
		} else if ((button = button_for_key(e->code)) != 0 && e->value < 2) {   /* 2 = key repeat */
			hakios_touch_post(e->value ? HAKIOS_BUTTON_DOWN : HAKIOS_BUTTON_UP, button, 0, 0);
		}
		break;
	case EV_SYN:
		if (d->pressed && !d->touching) {
			hakios_touch_post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN, 0, d->x, d->y);
		} else if (d->pressed && d->moved) {
			hakios_touch_post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_MOVE, 0, d->x, d->y);
		} else if (!d->pressed && d->touching) {
			hakios_touch_post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP, 0, d->x, d->y);
		}
		d->touching = d->pressed;
		d->moved = false;
		break;
	}
}

static void
input_poll(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	uint64_t deadline;

	for (int i = 0; i < device_count; i++) {
		struct input_device *d = &devices[i];
		bool returned = false;

		while (d->seen != *(volatile uint16_t *)&d->used->idx) {
			/* the ring entry and the event must be read after the index that announced them (arm64 does not order those loads by itself) */
			__builtin_arm_dmb(0x9);         /* ISHLD */
			uint32_t id = d->used->ring[d->seen++ % QUEUE_SIZE].id % QUEUE_SIZE;

			input_event(d, &d->events[id]);
			/* give the buffer back */
			d->avail->ring[d->avail->idx % QUEUE_SIZE] = (uint16_t)id;
			__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);         /* ISH */
			d->avail->idx++;
			returned = true;
		}
		if (returned) {
			__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
			reg_write(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY, 0);
		}
	}
	clock_interval_to_deadline(8, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(poll_call, deadline);
}

static bool
input_attach(struct input_device *d, int slot)
{
	vm_offset_t page = 0;
	struct vq_desc *desc;
	uint64_t phys;

	if (kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &page, PAGE_SIZE, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_ZERO | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_IOKIT) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		return false;
	}
	phys = kvtophys(page);
	desc = (struct vq_desc *)(page + OFFSET_DESC);
	d->avail = (struct vq_avail *)(page + OFFSET_AVAIL);
	d->used = (struct vq_used *)(page + OFFSET_USED);
	d->events = (struct input_event *)(page + OFFSET_EVENTS);

	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, 0);         /* reset */
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL, 0);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, 0);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL, 1);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, 1);        /* bit 32: VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1 */
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER | STATUS_FEATURES_OK);
	if (!(reg_read(d, VIRTIO_STATUS) & STATUS_FEATURES_OK)) {
		printf("virtio-input: slot %d: features refused\n", slot);
		/* the device never got this page: give it back and tell the device the driver gave up, so the failing slot costs nothing */
		reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_FAILED);
		kmem_free(kernel_map, page, PAGE_SIZE);
		return false;
	}

	/* queue 0 brings the events: hand the device all the buffers */
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_SEL, 0);
	if (reg_read(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX) < QUEUE_SIZE) {
		printf("virtio-input: slot %d: event queue of %u\n", slot, reg_read(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX));
		/* same as above: the queue was never given to the device */
		reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_FAILED);
		kmem_free(kernel_map, page, PAGE_SIZE);
		return false;
	}
	for (int i = 0; i < QUEUE_SIZE; i++) {
		desc[i].addr = phys + OFFSET_EVENTS + (uint64_t)i * sizeof(struct input_event);
		desc[i].len = sizeof(struct input_event);
		desc[i].flags = DESC_F_WRITE;
		d->avail->ring[i] = (uint16_t)i;
	}
	d->avail->flags = AVAIL_F_NO_INTERRUPT;
	d->avail->idx = QUEUE_SIZE;
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM, QUEUE_SIZE);
	reg_write64(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_DESC, phys + OFFSET_DESC);
	reg_write64(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_DRIVER, phys + OFFSET_AVAIL);
	reg_write64(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_DEVICE, phys + OFFSET_USED);
	__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_READY, 1);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER | STATUS_FEATURES_OK | STATUS_DRIVER_OK);
	reg_write(d, VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY, 0);
	return true;
}

void
hakios_virtio_input_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0;
	vm_offset_t bus;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("virtio_input", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	bus = ml_io_map(VIRTIO_BUS, VIRTIO_SLOTS * VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE);
	for (int slot = 0; slot < VIRTIO_SLOTS && device_count < MAX_DEVICES; slot++) {
		struct input_device *d = &devices[device_count];

		d->regs = bus + (vm_offset_t)slot * VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE;
		if (reg_read(d, VIRTIO_MAGIC) != 0x74726976 || reg_read(d, VIRTIO_DEVICE_ID) != VIRTIO_ID_INPUT) {
			continue;
		}
		if (reg_read(d, VIRTIO_VERSION) != 2) {
			printf("virtio-input: slot %d is a legacy transport; start QEMU with -global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false\n", slot);
			continue;
		}
		if (input_attach(d, slot)) {
			printf("virtio-input: device in slot %d\n", slot);
			device_count++;
		}
	}
	if (device_count) {
		poll_call = thread_call_allocate(input_poll, NULL);
		input_poll(NULL, NULL);
	} else {
		printf("virtio-input: no input devices\n");
	}
}
```

`drivers/modem/hakios.cell.c`:

```c
/*
 * en1: the modem's packets as a network interface Darwin will use.
 *
 * Darwin's own cellular interface (pdp_ip0) is made by its baseband stack, which is not here. What
 * is here is the kernel's Ethernet-looking interface (hakios.net.c) and configd, which treats an
 * Ethernet interface whose link comes up the way it treats a USB Ethernet adapter: it runs DHCP
 * on it, takes the address, the router and the DNS servers it is given, and routes through it.
 * So the modem's IP packets (hakios.ipa.c, QMAP mux 1) are shown as Ethernet frames between two
 * made-up stations, the interface's and "the router's", and this file answers, in the kernel,
 * what the stack asks of the router: ARP for any address (everything is behind the router) and
 * DHCP with the data session's settings (the address and DNS servers the modem got from the
 * network, hakios.mpss.c, QMI WDS). Packets to the router go to the modem; packets from the modem
 * come from the router. IPv6 is not carried (the session is IPv4).
 *
 * The mask and the router given to DHCP are not the modem's: a cellular session is a point-to-point
 * link, and its "gateway" need not be in any subnet with the address, which DHCP cannot express.
 * The interface gets a /24 around its address with the router at its .1 (or .2): any router will
 * do, since every packet goes to the modem anyway.
 */
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/kpi_mbuf.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/hakios.net.h>
#include <sys/hakios.ipa.h>

#define CELL_UNIT               1
#define CELL_MUX                1               /* the QMAP mux id the session is bound to (WDS Bind Mux Data Port) */

static const uint8_t cell_mac[6] = { 0x02, 0x68, 0x61, 0x6b, 0x69, 0x01 };      /* locally administered: "haki", 1 */
static const uint8_t router_mac[6] = { 0x02, 0x68, 0x61, 0x6b, 0x69, 0xfe };

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(cell_lock_group, "hakios-cell");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(cell_lock, &cell_lock_group);
static struct {
	bool            up;
	uint32_t        address, mask, router, dns1, dns2, mtu;        /* host order; what DHCP gives out */
	uint32_t        modem_mask, modem_gateway;                      /* what the modem said, for the log */
} session;
static struct {
	uint64_t        arp, dhcp, to_modem, from_modem, dropped_out, dropped_in, not_ip4;
} cell_count;
static bool cell_attached, cell_trace;

static inline uint32_t
get32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return (uint32_t)p[0] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 8 | p[3];
}

static inline void
put32(uint8_t *p, uint32_t v)
{
	p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16); p[2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); p[3] = (uint8_t)v;
}

static inline void
put16(uint8_t *p, uint32_t v)
{
	p[0] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); p[1] = (uint8_t)v;
}

static uint16_t
checksum(const uint8_t *data, size_t length)
{
	uint32_t sum = 0;

	for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < length; i += 2) {
		sum += (uint32_t)data[i] << 8 | data[i + 1];
	}
	if (length & 1) {
		sum += (uint32_t)data[length - 1] << 8;
	}
	while (sum >> 16) {
		sum = (sum & 0xffff) + (sum >> 16);
	}
	return (uint16_t)~sum;
}

/* ---- ARP: the router answers for everything ---------------------------------------------------- */

static bool
arp_answer(const uint8_t *frame, size_t length)
{
	const uint8_t *arp = frame + 14;
	uint8_t reply[42];

	/* Ethernet/IPv4, a request, not for our own address */
	if (length < 42 || get32(arp) != 0x00010800 || arp[4] != 6 || arp[5] != 4 || arp[7] != 1 || get32(arp + 24) == session.address) {
		return false;
	}
	memcpy(reply, frame + 6, 6);                    /* to the asker */
	memcpy(reply + 6, router_mac, 6);
	put16(reply + 12, 0x0806);
	put32(reply + 14, 0x00010800);
	reply[18] = 6; reply[19] = 4;
	put16(reply + 20, 2);                           /* a reply */
	memcpy(reply + 22, router_mac, 6);              /* "that address is me" */
	memcpy(reply + 28, arp + 24, 4);
	memcpy(reply + 32, arp + 8, 10);                /* the asker's addresses */
	cell_count.arp++;
	if (cell_trace) {
		printf("cell: ARP: %u.%u.%u.%u is the router\n", arp[24], arp[25], arp[26], arp[27]);
	}
	hakios_net_input_unit(CELL_UNIT, reply, sizeof(reply));
	return true;
}

/* ---- DHCP: the session's settings ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define DHCP_DISCOVER           1
#define DHCP_OFFER              2
#define DHCP_REQUEST            3
#define DHCP_ACK                5
#define DHCP_NAK                6

/* Is this a DHCP request (UDP 68 -> 67)? `udp` is set to its UDP header. */
static bool
dhcp_request(const uint8_t *frame, size_t length, const uint8_t **udp)
{
	const uint8_t *ip = frame + 14;
	size_t ihl;

	if (length < 14 + 20 + 8 + 240 || (ip[0] >> 4) != 4 || ip[9] != 17) {
		return false;
	}
	ihl = 4 * (ip[0] & 0xf);
	if (ihl < 20 || 14 + ihl + 8 + 240 > length) {
		return false;
	}
	*udp = ip + ihl;
	return ((*udp)[2] << 8 | (*udp)[3]) == 67;
}

/* The answer to a DHCP request: an offer for a discover, an acknowledgement for a request, with the session's settings. */
static bool
dhcp_answer(const uint8_t *frame, size_t length, const uint8_t *udp)
{
	const uint8_t *request = udp + 8, *end = frame + length, *option;
	uint8_t reply[14 + 20 + 8 + 240 + 64], *ip = reply + 14, *rudp = ip + 20, *bootp = rudp + 8, *o;
	uint32_t type = 0, wanted = 0, kind;
	size_t size;

	if (request[0] != 1 || request[1] != 1 || request[2] != 6 || get32(request + 236) != 0x63825363) {
		return false;
	}
	/* the options: the message type, the address asked for */
	for (option = request + 240; option + 2 <= end && *option != 255; option += option[0] == 0 ? 1 : 2 + option[1]) {
		if (option[0] == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (option + 2 + option[1] > end) {
			break;
		}
		if (option[0] == 53 && option[1] == 1) {
			type = option[2];
		} else if (option[0] == 50 && option[1] == 4) {
			wanted = get32(option + 2);
		}
	}
	if (type != DHCP_DISCOVER && type != DHCP_REQUEST) {
		return false;
	}
	kind = type == DHCP_DISCOVER ? DHCP_OFFER : wanted != 0 && wanted != session.address ? DHCP_NAK : DHCP_ACK;
	bzero(reply, sizeof(reply));
	/* BOOTP */
	bootp[0] = 2; bootp[1] = 1; bootp[2] = 6;      /* a reply, Ethernet */
	memcpy(bootp + 4, request + 4, 4);              /* the transaction */
	memcpy(bootp + 10, request + 10, 2);            /* the flags (broadcast) */
	if (kind != DHCP_NAK) {
		put32(bootp + 16, session.address);     /* yiaddr */
		put32(bootp + 20, session.router);      /* siaddr */
	}
	memcpy(bootp + 28, request + 28, 16);           /* the client's hardware address */
	put32(bootp + 236, 0x63825363);
	o = bootp + 240;
	*o++ = 53; *o++ = 1; *o++ = (uint8_t)kind;
	*o++ = 54; *o++ = 4; put32(o, session.router); o += 4;      /* the server: the router */
	if (kind != DHCP_NAK) {
		*o++ = 51; *o++ = 4; put32(o, 86400); o += 4;           /* a day's lease */
		*o++ = 1; *o++ = 4; put32(o, session.mask); o += 4;
		*o++ = 3; *o++ = 4; put32(o, session.router); o += 4;
		if (session.dns1 != 0 || session.dns2 != 0) {
			*o++ = 6; *o++ = (uint8_t)(4 * ((session.dns1 != 0) + (session.dns2 != 0)));
			if (session.dns1 != 0) { put32(o, session.dns1); o += 4; }
			if (session.dns2 != 0) { put32(o, session.dns2); o += 4; }
		}
		if (session.mtu >= 576 && session.mtu <= 1500) {
			*o++ = 26; *o++ = 2; put16(o, session.mtu); o += 2;
		}
	}
	*o++ = 255;
	size = (size_t)(o - bootp);
	if (size < 300) {
		size = 300;                             /* the traditional minimum, padded with zeros */
	}
	/* UDP 67 -> 68, no checksum */
	put16(rudp, 67); put16(rudp + 2, 68); put16(rudp + 4, (uint32_t)(8 + size)); put16(rudp + 6, 0);
	/* IPv4 from the router to everyone */
	ip[0] = 0x45; ip[1] = 0;
	put16(ip + 2, (uint32_t)(20 + 8 + size));
	put16(ip + 4, 0); put16(ip + 6, 0);
	ip[8] = 64; ip[9] = 17;
	put32(ip + 12, session.router);
	put32(ip + 16, 0xffffffff);
	put16(ip + 10, checksum(ip, 20));
	/* Ethernet to the client */
	memcpy(reply, request + 28, 6);
	memcpy(reply + 6, router_mac, 6);
	put16(reply + 12, 0x0800);
	cell_count.dhcp++;
	printf("cell: DHCP %s answered with %s: %u.%u.%u.%u/%u.%u.%u.%u, router %u.%u.%u.%u, DNS %u.%u.%u.%u %u.%u.%u.%u, MTU %u\n",
	    type == DHCP_DISCOVER ? "discover" : "request", kind == DHCP_OFFER ? "an offer" : kind == DHCP_ACK ? "an acknowledgement" : "a refusal",
	    session.address >> 24, (session.address >> 16) & 0xff, (session.address >> 8) & 0xff, session.address & 0xff,
	    session.mask >> 24, (session.mask >> 16) & 0xff, (session.mask >> 8) & 0xff, session.mask & 0xff,
	    session.router >> 24, (session.router >> 16) & 0xff, (session.router >> 8) & 0xff, session.router & 0xff,
	    session.dns1 >> 24, (session.dns1 >> 16) & 0xff, (session.dns1 >> 8) & 0xff, session.dns1 & 0xff,
	    session.dns2 >> 24, (session.dns2 >> 16) & 0xff, (session.dns2 >> 8) & 0xff, session.dns2 & 0xff, session.mtu);
	hakios_net_input_unit(CELL_UNIT, reply, 14 + 20 + 8 + size);
	return true;
}

/* ---- the link ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* A frame from the stack: answered here, or its IP packet to the modem. */
static bool
cell_transmit(mbuf_t packet, size_t length)
{
	uint8_t frame[HAKIOS_NET_FRAME_MAX];
	const uint8_t *udp;
	uint32_t type;
	bool ok;

	if (length < 14 || length > sizeof(frame) || mbuf_copydata(packet, 0, length, frame) != 0) {
		return false;
	}
	type = (uint32_t)frame[12] << 8 | frame[13];
	lck_mtx_lock(&cell_lock);
	if (type == 0x0806) {
		ok = arp_answer(frame, length);
	} else if (type == 0x0800 && dhcp_request(frame, length, &udp)) {
		ok = session.up && dhcp_answer(frame, length, udp);
	} else if (type == 0x0800) {
		ok = session.up && hakios_ipa_transmit(CELL_MUX, frame + 14, length - 14);
		if (ok) {
			cell_count.to_modem++;
		} else {
			cell_count.dropped_out++;
		}
	} else {
		cell_count.not_ip4++;                   /* IPv6 and the rest: not carried */
		ok = false;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&cell_lock);
	return ok;
}

/* A packet from the modem: an Ethernet frame from the router made around it. */
static void
cell_receive(uint8_t mux, const uint8_t *packet, size_t length)
{
	uint8_t frame[HAKIOS_NET_FRAME_MAX];
	uint32_t version = length > 0 ? packet[0] >> 4 : 0;

	if (length < 20 || length + 14 > sizeof(frame) || (version != 4 && version != 6)) {
		cell_count.dropped_in++;
		return;
	}
	if (cell_trace) {
		printf("cell: %zu bytes from the modem on mux %u (IPv%u)\n", length, mux, version);
	}
	memcpy(frame, cell_mac, 6);
	memcpy(frame + 6, router_mac, 6);
	put16(frame + 12, version == 4 ? 0x0800 : 0x86dd);
	memcpy(frame + 14, packet, length);
	cell_count.from_modem++;
	hakios_net_input_unit(CELL_UNIT, frame, 14 + length);
}

static unsigned
cell_poll(void)
{
	static unsigned ticks;
	unsigned got = hakios_ipa_poll(cell_receive);

	if (++ticks % 30000 == 0 && (cell_count.to_modem != 0 || cell_count.from_modem != 0 || cell_count.dropped_out != 0)) {
		char line[256];

		hakios_ipa_status(line, sizeof(line));
		printf("cell: so far %llu packets to the modem, %llu from it; dropped %llu out, %llu in; %llu not IPv4; ARP %llu, DHCP %llu; "
		    "IPA: %s\n", cell_count.to_modem, cell_count.from_modem, cell_count.dropped_out, cell_count.dropped_in, cell_count.not_ip4,
		    cell_count.arp, cell_count.dhcp, line);
	}
	return got;
}

static struct hakios_net_link cell_link = {
	.name = "the modem through the IPA",
	.unit = CELL_UNIT,
	.address = { 0x02, 0x68, 0x61, 0x6b, 0x69, 0x01 },
	.wireless = false,
	.up = false,
	.transmit = cell_transmit,
	.poll = cell_poll,
};

void
hakios_cell_session(bool up, uint32_t address, uint32_t mask, uint32_t gateway, uint32_t dns1, uint32_t dns2, uint32_t mtu)
{
	uint32_t router;

	lck_mtx_lock(&cell_lock);
	session.modem_mask = mask;
	session.modem_gateway = gateway;
	/* a /24 around the address, with the router in it (see the top of the file) */
	mask = 0xffffff00;
	router = (address & mask) | 1;
	if (router == address) {
		router = (address & mask) | 2;
	}
	session.address = address;
	session.mask = mask;
	session.router = router;
	session.dns1 = dns1;
	session.dns2 = dns2;
	session.mtu = mtu;
	session.up = up && address != 0;
	lck_mtx_unlock(&cell_lock);
	printf("cell: the data session is %s: %u.%u.%u.%u (the modem's mask %u.%u.%u.%u and gateway %u.%u.%u.%u; en1 is told /24 and router "
	    "%u.%u.%u.%u), DNS %u.%u.%u.%u %u.%u.%u.%u, MTU %u%s\n", session.up ? "UP" : "down",
	    address >> 24, (address >> 16) & 0xff, (address >> 8) & 0xff, address & 0xff,
	    session.modem_mask >> 24, (session.modem_mask >> 16) & 0xff, (session.modem_mask >> 8) & 0xff, session.modem_mask & 0xff,
	    gateway >> 24, (gateway >> 16) & 0xff, (gateway >> 8) & 0xff, gateway & 0xff,
	    router >> 24, (router >> 16) & 0xff, (router >> 8) & 0xff, router & 0xff,
	    dns1 >> 24, (dns1 >> 16) & 0xff, (dns1 >> 8) & 0xff, dns1 & 0xff, dns2 >> 24, (dns2 >> 16) & 0xff, (dns2 >> 8) & 0xff, dns2 & 0xff,
	    mtu, cell_attached ? "" : " (no en1: the IPA's data path is not up)");
	if (cell_attached) {
		hakios_net_link_state_unit(CELL_UNIT, session.up);
	}
}

void
hakios_cell_attach(void)
{
	uint32_t t = 0;

	if (cell_attached || !hakios_ipa_data_ready()) {
		return;
	}
	PE_parse_boot_argn("modem_ipa_data_trace", &t, sizeof(t));
	cell_trace = t != 0;
	cell_attached = hakios_net_attach(&cell_link);
	if (cell_attached && session.up) {
		hakios_net_link_state_unit(CELL_UNIT, true);
	}
}

```

`drivers/modem/hakios.ipa.c`:

```c
/*
 * The IPA's data path for this processor: GSI rings, the IPA's endpoints for the application
 * processor, and the immediate commands that give the IPA its tables.
 *
 * The IPA (Qualcomm's "IP accelerator", here IPA 4.11 with GSI 2.11) moves packets between the
 * modem and this processor. Each side has "endpoints" (pipes) in the IPA and "channels" in the
 * GSI (the DMA engine beside it): a channel is a ring of transfer elements (TREs: address, length,
 * flags; 16 bytes) that this processor fills and the hardware consumes, and an event ring the
 * hardware fills with one event per finished TRE. Writing a doorbell register tells the hardware
 * how far the ring is filled; the event ring's write pointer, read from a register, tells us how
 * far the hardware got. No interrupt is used: the interface's thread polls (hakios.cell.c).
 *
 * What this processor needs, as Linux's driver sets them up for IPA 4.11 (drivers/net/ipa,
 * ipa_data-v4.11.c, gsi.c, ipa_endpoint.c, ipa_cmd.c, ipa_table.c; the register layout from
 * reg/gsi_reg-v4.11.c and reg/ipa_reg-v4.11.c):
 *   - the command endpoint (7, channel 5): immediate commands to the IPA itself, which is how it
 *     is told where its filter and route tables and its header table are;
 *   - the "LAN" receive endpoint (9, channel 14): the IPA's default route (what matches no rule)
 *     and its exceptions end here; it is looked at and dropped;
 *   - the modem transmit endpoint (2, channel 2): IP packets to the modem, each behind a QMAP
 *     header (4 bytes: pad length, mux id, packet length, big-endian);
 *   - the modem receive endpoint (16, channel 7): IP packets from the modem, QMAP-framed, several
 *     per buffer (the IPA aggregates them until 12 KB or 500 us).
 * No checksum offload, no status packets: the network stack computes its checksums itself and
 * the modem is told QMAP without checksum (hakios.mpss.c, WDA Set Data Format).
 *
 * All of this is done before the modem starts (Linux does the same): the tables the commands
 * write hold pointers to one "zero rule", and the modem then writes its own rules into its part
 * of them. The IPA reaches this memory through the SMMU context the modem driver gave it, which
 * shows DDR as it is (physical addresses). The memory is cached for us, so every buffer is
 * written back and dropped from the cache (dc civac) before the hardware looks at it and before
 * we look at what the hardware wrote.
 *
 * modem_ipa_data_off=1: none of this. modem_ipa_data_trace=1: a line per packet.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>
#include <sys/hakios.ipa.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);
extern void FlushPoC_DcacheRegion(vm_offset_t va, size_t length);

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(ipa_lock_group, "hakios-ipa");
static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(ipa_lock, &ipa_lock_group);

/* ---- the registers ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * Where the IPA and the GSI are. These are the values of the first phone (POCO X5 Pro, SM7325),
 * which another Qualcomm phone overrides from its own device tree: the "reg" of the node whose
 * compatible is "qcom,ipa" (reg-names "ipa-base" and "gsi-base"), passed as boot-args soc_ipa_base
 * and soc_gsi_base (tools/soc-args.py reads them off the phone's fdt). The IPA driver has one
 * execution environment's worth of GSI registers mapped, from the inter-EE masks to the scratch.
 */
#define IPA_REGS_PHYS_DEFAULT   0x01e40000ull
#define GSI_PHYS_DEFAULT        0x01e04000ull
#define IPA_REGS_SIZE           0x1000
#define GSI_FROM                0xc000          /* what is used of the GSI's registers: from the inter-EE masks (0xc020) to the scratch (0x12400) */
#define GSI_SIZE                0x7000

static uint64_t ipa_regs_phys = IPA_REGS_PHYS_DEFAULT, gsi_phys = GSI_PHYS_DEFAULT;
static vm_offset_t ipa_regs, gsi_regs;         /* gsi_regs maps gsi_phys + GSI_FROM */

static inline uint32_t
ipa_rd(uint32_t offset)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)(ipa_regs + offset);
}

static inline void
ipa_wr(uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)(ipa_regs + offset) = value;
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy" ::: "memory");
}

static inline uint32_t
gsi_rd(uint32_t offset)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)(gsi_regs + (offset - GSI_FROM));
}

static inline void
gsi_wr(uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)(gsi_regs + (offset - GSI_FROM)) = value;
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy" ::: "memory");
}

/* The GSI's registers for our execution environment (EE 0; another EE's are 0x4000 further) */
#define CH_CNTXT(c, n)          (0xf000 + 0x80 * (c) + 4 * (n))        /* n 0..3: type/dir/event ring/state, length, address */
#define CH_QOS(c)               (0xf05c + 0x80 * (c))
#define CH_SCRATCH(c, n)        (0xf060 + 0x80 * (c) + 4 * (n))
#define EV_CNTXT(e, n)          (0x10000 + 0x80 * (e) + 4 * (n))       /* n 0..13: type/state, length, address, read/write pointers, moderation, MSI */
#define CH_DOORBELL(c)          (0x11000 + 8 * (c))
#define EV_DOORBELL(e)          (0x11100 + 8 * (e))
#define GSI_STATUS              0x12000
#define CH_CMD                  0x12008
#define EV_CH_CMD               0x12010
#define CNTXT_TYPE_IRQ          0x12080
#define CNTXT_TYPE_IRQ_MSK      0x12088
#define CNTXT_SRC_CH_IRQ        0x12090
#define CNTXT_SRC_EV_CH_IRQ     0x12094
#define CNTXT_SRC_CH_IRQ_MSK    0x12098
#define CNTXT_SRC_EV_CH_IRQ_MSK 0x1209c
#define CNTXT_SRC_CH_IRQ_CLR    0x120a0
#define CNTXT_SRC_EV_CH_IRQ_CLR 0x120a4
#define CNTXT_SRC_IEOB_IRQ      0x120b0
#define CNTXT_SRC_IEOB_IRQ_MSK  0x120b8
#define CNTXT_SRC_IEOB_IRQ_CLR  0x120c0
#define CNTXT_GLOB_IRQ_STTS     0x12100
#define CNTXT_GLOB_IRQ_EN       0x12108
#define CNTXT_GLOB_IRQ_CLR      0x12110
#define CNTXT_GSI_IRQ_STTS      0x12118
#define CNTXT_GSI_IRQ_EN        0x12120
#define CNTXT_GSI_IRQ_CLR       0x12128
#define CNTXT_INTSET            0x12180
#define ERROR_LOG               0x12200
#define ERROR_LOG_CLR           0x12210
#define INTER_EE_SRC_CH_IRQ_MSK 0xc020
#define INTER_EE_SRC_EV_CH_IRQ_MSK 0xc024

#define GSI_CH_ALLOCATE         0x0     /* channel commands (CH_CMD bits 31:24; the channel in 7:0) */
#define GSI_CH_START            0x1
#define GSI_CH_STOP             0x2
#define GSI_CH_RESET            0x9
#define GSI_CH_DE_ALLOC         0xa
#define GSI_EVT_ALLOCATE        0x0     /* event ring commands (EV_CH_CMD, the same layout) */
#define GSI_EVT_RESET           0x9
#define GSI_EVT_DE_ALLOC        0xa
#define CH_STATE_NOT_ALLOCATED  0       /* CH_CNTXT 0 bits 23:20 */
#define CH_STATE_ALLOCATED      1
#define CH_STATE_STARTED        2
#define CH_STATE_STOPPED        3
#define EV_STATE_NOT_ALLOCATED  0       /* EV_CNTXT 0 bits 23:20 */
#define EV_STATE_ALLOCATED      1
#define GSI_CHANNEL_TYPE_GPI    2
#define ELEMENT_SIZE            16

/* The IPA's endpoint registers (0x70 apart) */
#define ENDP_INIT_CFG(ep)       (0x808 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_NAT(ep)       (0x80c + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_HDR(ep)       (0x810 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_HDR_EXT(ep)   (0x814 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_HDR_METADATA_MASK(ep) (0x818 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_MODE(ep)      (0x820 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_AGGR(ep)      (0x824 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_HOL_BLOCK_EN(ep) (0x82c + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_DEAGGR(ep)    (0x834 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_RSRC_GRP(ep)  (0x838 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_INIT_SEQ(ep)       (0x83c + 0x70 * (ep))
#define ENDP_STATUS(ep)         (0x840 + 0x70 * (ep))
#define IPA_SHARED_MEM_SIZE     0x54            /* bits 31:16: the local memory's offset in 8-byte units */
#define IPA_FILT_ROUT_HASH_FLUSH 0x14c

/* ---- memory the hardware reads and writes ------------------------------------------------------ */

struct dma {
	vm_offset_t     virt;
	uint64_t        phys;
};

/* One page (16 KB), zeroed, written out of the cache; false if there is none. */
static bool
dma_page(struct dma *d)
{
	vm_offset_t virt = 0;

	if (kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &virt, PAGE_SIZE, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_ZERO | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_IOKIT) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		return false;
	}
	d->virt = virt;
	d->phys = kvtophys(virt);
	FlushPoC_DcacheRegion(virt, PAGE_SIZE);
	return true;
}

/* Written back and dropped from the cache: before the hardware reads it, and before we read what the hardware wrote. */
static inline void
dma_sync(vm_offset_t virt, size_t size)
{
	vm_offset_t from = virt & ~63ul;

	FlushPoC_DcacheRegion(from, ((virt + size + 63) & ~63ul) - from);
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy" ::: "memory");
}

/* ---- the channels ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

struct tre {
	uint64_t        addr;
	uint16_t        len_opcode;     /* bytes to transfer, or the immediate command's opcode */
	uint16_t        reserved;
	uint32_t        flags;          /* TRE_* */
};
#define TRE_CHAIN               (1u << 0)
#define TRE_IEOT                (1u << 9)       /* an event when done */
#define TRE_BEI                 (1u << 10)      /* ... but no interrupt for it */
#define TRE_TYPE_XFER           (2u << 16)
#define TRE_TYPE_COMMAND        (3u << 16)

struct event {
	uint64_t        xfer;           /* the address of the TRE that finished */
	uint16_t        len;            /* bytes moved (what a receive buffer got) */
	uint8_t         reserved1;
	uint8_t         code;
	uint16_t        reserved2;
	uint8_t         type;
	uint8_t         chid;
};

struct channel {
	const char *    name;
	uint8_t         id, ring_id, endpoint;  /* the channel, its event ring, the IPA's endpoint */
	bool            to_ipa, command, qmap, aggregate, close_eof;
	uint32_t        slots;          /* TREs in the ring, and buffers (a power of two; they fit one page: at most 1024) */
	uint32_t        tlv;            /* the endpoint's TLV FIFO: how many TREs may be outstanding (ipa_data-v4.11.c tlv_count) */
	uint32_t        buffer_size;    /* bytes per slot (a divisor or a multiple of the page size) */
	struct dma      tre_ring, event_ring;
	struct dma *    pages;          /* the buffers, slot by slot */
	uint32_t        page_count;
	uint32_t        next;           /* the next TRE to fill (counts up; the slot is next % slots) */
	uint32_t        done;           /* the next TRE whose completion is awaited (transmit) */
	uint32_t        events;         /* the next event to read (counts up) */
	bool            started;
	uint64_t        packets, bytes, dropped, errors;
};

/*
 * The four: numbers from Linux's ipa_data-v4.11.c (channel, endpoint, TLV counts, which has
 * QMAP and aggregation). Rings here are smaller than Linux's; the buffers are a page for a receive
 * slot (the IPA aggregates into it) and 2 KB for a transmit slot (one packet and its header).
 */
static struct channel command = { "command", 5, 0, 7, true, true, false, false, false, 16, 20, 64 };
#define RECEIVE_BUFFER          16384           /* a page: the IPA aggregates into it */
static struct channel lan_rx = { "lan-rx", 14, 1, 9, false, false, false, true, false, 16, 9, RECEIVE_BUFFER };
static struct channel modem_tx = { "modem-tx", 2, 2, 2, true, false, true, false, false, 64, 16, 2048 };
static struct channel modem_rx = { "modem-rx", 7, 3, 16, false, false, true, true, true, 64, 9, RECEIVE_BUFFER };
static struct channel *channels[] = { &command, &lan_rx, &modem_tx, &modem_rx };
#define AGGR_LIMIT_KB           12              /* the IPA closes a receive buffer once this much is in it (a page holds another 4 KB packet) */
#define AGGR_TIME_TICKS         5               /* ... or after 5 ticks of the first pulse generator: 500 us (TIMERS_PULSE_GRAN_CFG gran 0 = 100 us) */

static bool ready, trace;
static uint32_t mem_offset;                     /* the local memory's offset within the IPA's shared memory */
static struct dma table, zero;                  /* the tables' page (below) and a page of zeros */

static inline vm_offset_t
slot_virt(const struct channel *ch, uint32_t slot)
{
	uint64_t at = (uint64_t)slot * ch->buffer_size;

	return ch->pages[at / PAGE_SIZE].virt + at % PAGE_SIZE;
}

static inline uint64_t
slot_phys(const struct channel *ch, uint32_t slot)
{
	uint64_t at = (uint64_t)slot * ch->buffer_size;

	return ch->pages[at / PAGE_SIZE].phys + at % PAGE_SIZE;
}

static inline struct tre *
tre_at(const struct channel *ch, uint32_t index)
{
	return (struct tre *)(ch->tre_ring.virt + (index % ch->slots) * ELEMENT_SIZE);
}

static bool
channel_memory(struct channel *ch)
{
	uint64_t bytes = (uint64_t)ch->slots * ch->buffer_size;

	ch->page_count = (uint32_t)((bytes + PAGE_SIZE - 1) / PAGE_SIZE);
	ch->pages = kalloc_type(struct dma, ch->page_count, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
	if (ch->pages == NULL || !dma_page(&ch->tre_ring) || !dma_page(&ch->event_ring)) {
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t p = 0; p < ch->page_count; p++) {
		if (!dma_page(&ch->pages[p])) {
			return false;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

static void
gsi_error(const char *what)
{
	uint32_t log = gsi_rd(ERROR_LOG);

	printf("ipa: %s: GSI status %#x, error log %#x (code %u, type %u, EE %u, index %u, args %#x), global %#x, general %#x\n", what,
	    gsi_rd(GSI_STATUS), log, (log >> 12) & 0xf, (log >> 24) & 0xf, log >> 28, (log >> 19) & 0x1f, log & 0xfff,
	    gsi_rd(CNTXT_GLOB_IRQ_STTS), gsi_rd(CNTXT_GSI_IRQ_STTS));
	if (log != 0) {
		gsi_wr(ERROR_LOG, 0);
		gsi_wr(ERROR_LOG_CLR, ~0u);
	}
}

static inline uint32_t
channel_state(const struct channel *ch)
{
	return (gsi_rd(CH_CNTXT(ch->id, 0)) >> 20) & 0xf;
}

static inline uint32_t
event_ring_state(const struct channel *ch)
{
	return (gsi_rd(EV_CNTXT(ch->ring_id, 0)) >> 20) & 0xf;
}

/* A command to the GSI about a channel or an event ring; true once the state is `wanted` (within 50 ms). */
static bool
gsi_command(struct channel *ch, bool event, uint32_t opcode, uint32_t wanted)
{
	uint32_t state = 0, number = event ? ch->ring_id : ch->id;

	gsi_wr(event ? EV_CH_CMD : CH_CMD, number | opcode << 24);
	for (unsigned us = 0; us < 50000; us += 100) {
		state = event ? event_ring_state(ch) : channel_state(ch);
		if (state == wanted) {
			break;
		}
		delay_for_interval(100, NSEC_PER_USEC);
	}
	/* (the completion is also flagged as an interrupt source, masked: cleared) */
	gsi_wr(event ? CNTXT_SRC_EV_CH_IRQ_CLR : CNTXT_SRC_CH_IRQ_CLR, 1u << number);
	if (state != wanted) {
		printf("ipa: %s: command %#x on %s %u leaves it in state %u, not %u\n", ch->name, opcode, event ? "event ring" : "channel", number,
		    state, wanted);
		gsi_error(ch->name);
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* As Linux's gsi_irq_setup(): interrupts, not MSIs; every source masked (nothing is handled here: the rings are polled). */
static void
gsi_interrupts_off(void)
{
	gsi_wr(CNTXT_INTSET, 1);
	gsi_wr(CNTXT_TYPE_IRQ_MSK, 0);
	gsi_wr(CNTXT_SRC_CH_IRQ_MSK, 0);
	gsi_wr(CNTXT_SRC_EV_CH_IRQ_MSK, 0);
	gsi_wr(CNTXT_GLOB_IRQ_EN, 0);
	gsi_wr(CNTXT_SRC_IEOB_IRQ_MSK, 0);
	gsi_wr(INTER_EE_SRC_CH_IRQ_MSK, 0);
	gsi_wr(INTER_EE_SRC_EV_CH_IRQ_MSK, 0);
	gsi_wr(CNTXT_GSI_IRQ_EN, 0);
}

/* As Linux's gsi_evt_ring_program() and gsi_channel_program(), for the GPI protocol. */
static bool
channel_setup(struct channel *ch)
{
	uint32_t e = ch->ring_id, c = ch->id, value;

	if (!gsi_command(ch, true, GSI_EVT_ALLOCATE, EV_STATE_ALLOCATED)) {
		return false;
	}
	gsi_wr(EV_CNTXT(e, 0), GSI_CHANNEL_TYPE_GPI | 1u << 16 /* INTYPE: interrupt, not MSI */ | ELEMENT_SIZE << 24);
	gsi_wr(EV_CNTXT(e, 1), ch->slots * ELEMENT_SIZE);
	gsi_wr(EV_CNTXT(e, 2), (uint32_t)ch->event_ring.phys);
	gsi_wr(EV_CNTXT(e, 3), (uint32_t)(ch->event_ring.phys >> 32));
	gsi_wr(EV_CNTXT(e, 8), 32 /* moderation: 1 ms at 32 kHz */ | 1u << 16 /* MODC */);
	for (unsigned n = 9; n <= 13; n++) {
		gsi_wr(EV_CNTXT(e, n), 0);              /* no MSI, no read pointer updates */
	}
	/* "the last processed event": the ring's last entry, as nothing has been processed */
	gsi_wr(EV_DOORBELL(e), (uint32_t)(ch->event_ring.phys + (ch->slots - 1) * ELEMENT_SIZE));

	if (!gsi_command(ch, false, GSI_CH_ALLOCATE, CH_STATE_ALLOCATED)) {
		return false;
	}
	gsi_wr(CH_CNTXT(c, 0), GSI_CHANNEL_TYPE_GPI | (ch->to_ipa ? 1u << 3 : 0) | e << 14 | ELEMENT_SIZE << 24);
	gsi_wr(CH_CNTXT(c, 1), ch->slots * ELEMENT_SIZE);
	gsi_wr(CH_CNTXT(c, 2), (uint32_t)ch->tre_ring.phys);
	gsi_wr(CH_CNTXT(c, 3), (uint32_t)(ch->tre_ring.phys >> 32));
	/* QOS: the command channel gets the lowest round-robin weight and no escape buffer; the doorbell counts bytes */
	value = (ch->command ? 0xf : 0) | (ch->command ? 0 : 1u << 10 /* PREFETCH_MODE: escape buffer only */) | 1u << 24;
	gsi_wr(CH_QOS(c), value);
	/* the GPI scratch: the most outstanding TREs (in bytes), the threshold 2 TREs */
	gsi_wr(CH_SCRATCH(c, 0), (ch->tlv * ELEMENT_SIZE) << 16);
	gsi_wr(CH_SCRATCH(c, 1), (2 * ELEMENT_SIZE) << 16);
	gsi_wr(CH_SCRATCH(c, 2), 0);
	gsi_wr(CH_SCRATCH(c, 3), gsi_rd(CH_SCRATCH(c, 3)) & 0xffff);
	return true;
}

/* As Linux's ipa_endpoint_program() for IPA 4.11, with no checksum offload and no status. */
static void
endpoint_program(const struct channel *ch)
{
	uint32_t ep = ch->endpoint, value;

	ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_CFG(ep), 0);                   /* no fragment or checksum offload */
	ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_NAT(ep), 0);                   /* NAT bypassed */
	value = 0;
	if (ch->qmap) {
		value = 4 /* HDR_LEN */ | 1u << 6 /* HDR_OFST_METADATA_VALID, at 0 */;
		if (!ch->to_ipa) {
			/* where the IPA writes the mux id (byte 1) and the packet's length (bytes 2-3) of the header it makes */
			value |= 1u << 7 /* HDR_OFST_METADATA */ | 1u << 19 /* HDR_OFST_PKT_SIZE_VALID */ | 2u << 20 /* HDR_OFST_PKT_SIZE */;
		}
	}
	ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_HDR(ep), value);
	value = 0;
	if (ch->qmap) {
		value = 1 /* HDR_ENDIANNESS: big */;
		if (!ch->to_ipa) {
			value |= 1u << 1 /* HDR_TOTAL_LEN_OR_PAD_VALID (pad) */ | 1u << 3 /* HDR_PAYLOAD_LEN_INC_PADDING */;
		}
	}
	ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_HDR_EXT(ep), value);
	if (!ch->to_ipa) {
		ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_HDR_METADATA_MASK(ep), ch->qmap ? 0xff000000 : 0);   /* the metadata's low byte, big-endian */
	} else {
		/* the command endpoint moves its data to the LAN receive endpoint (DMA mode); the rest is basic */
		ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_MODE(ep), ch->command ? 3 | (uint32_t)lan_rx.endpoint << 4 : 0);
	}
	if (!ch->to_ipa && ch->aggregate) {
		value = 1 /* AGGR_EN: aggregate */ | 4u << 2 /* AGGR_TYPE: generic */ | AGGR_LIMIT_KB << 5 | AGGR_TIME_TICKS << 12 |
		    (ch->close_eof ? 1u << 23 /* SW_EOF_ACTIVE */ : 0);
	} else if (ch->to_ipa && ch->qmap) {
		value = 2 /* AGGR_EN: deaggregate */ | 6u << 2 /* AGGR_TYPE: QCMAP */;
	} else {
		value = 0;
	}
	ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_AGGR(ep), value);
	if (!ch->to_ipa) {
		ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_HOL_BLOCK_EN(ep), 0);  /* no head-of-line blocking drops */
	} else {
		ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_DEAGGR(ep), 0);
	}
	ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_RSRC_GRP(ep), 0);              /* resource group 0: UL/DL (the only one with limits) */
	if (ch->to_ipa) {
		ipa_wr(ENDP_INIT_SEQ(ep), ch->command ? 0 /* DMA */ : 4 /* 2_PASS_SKIP_LAST_UC */);
	}
	ipa_wr(ENDP_STATUS(ep), 0);                     /* no status packets */
}

/* The TRE at `index` of the channel's ring, filled and written out; the doorbell is rung separately. */
static void
tre_fill(struct channel *ch, uint32_t index, uint64_t addr, uint16_t len_opcode, uint32_t flags)
{
	struct tre *t = tre_at(ch, index);

	t->addr = addr;
	t->len_opcode = len_opcode;
	t->reserved = 0;
	t->flags = flags;
	dma_sync((vm_offset_t)t, sizeof(*t));
}

static inline void
channel_doorbell(struct channel *ch)
{
	gsi_wr(CH_DOORBELL(ch->id), (uint32_t)(ch->tre_ring.phys + (ch->next % ch->slots) * ELEMENT_SIZE));
}

/*
 * The events the hardware has written since last time, each to `each`. The event ring's write
 * pointer is in its context register 4; the doorbell afterwards tells the hardware the last event
 * read, which makes room.
 */
static unsigned
channel_events(struct channel *ch, void (*each)(struct channel *, const struct event *, void *), void *context)
{
	uint32_t wp = gsi_rd(EV_CNTXT(ch->ring_id, 4)), base = (uint32_t)ch->event_ring.phys, index;
	unsigned n = 0;

	if (wp < base || wp >= base + ch->slots * ELEMENT_SIZE) {
		if (ch->errors++ == 0) {
			printf("ipa: %s: the event ring's write pointer %#x is outside the ring at %#x\n", ch->name, wp, base);
		}
		return 0;
	}
	index = (wp - base) / ELEMENT_SIZE;
	while (ch->events % ch->slots != index) {
		struct event *e = (struct event *)(ch->event_ring.virt + (ch->events % ch->slots) * ELEMENT_SIZE);

		dma_sync((vm_offset_t)e, sizeof(*e));
		each(ch, e, context);
		ch->events++;
		n++;
	}
	if (n != 0) {
		gsi_wr(EV_DOORBELL(ch->ring_id), (uint32_t)(ch->event_ring.phys + ((ch->events - 1) % ch->slots) * ELEMENT_SIZE));
	}
	return n;
}

/* ---- immediate commands ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define IPA_CMD_IP_V4_FILTER_INIT 0x3
#define IPA_CMD_IP_V6_FILTER_INIT 0x4
#define IPA_CMD_IP_V4_ROUTING_INIT 0x7
#define IPA_CMD_IP_V6_ROUTING_INIT 0x8
#define IPA_CMD_HDR_INIT_LOCAL  0x9
#define IPA_CMD_DMA_SHARED_MEM  0x13

struct command_done {
	uint64_t        tre;
	bool            done;
	uint8_t         code;
};

static void
command_event(__unused struct channel *ch, const struct event *e, void *context)
{
	struct command_done *waiting = context;

	if (e->xfer == waiting->tre) {
		waiting->done = true;
		waiting->code = e->code;
	}
	command.done++;
}

/* One immediate command, waited for (up to 200 ms). The payload is copied into the slot's buffer. */
static bool
ipa_command(const char *what, uint8_t opcode, const void *payload, size_t size)
{
	uint32_t slot = command.next % command.slots;
	struct command_done waiting = { .tre = command.tre_ring.phys + slot * ELEMENT_SIZE };

	if (size > command.buffer_size || command.next - command.done >= command.slots - 1) {
		return false;
	}
	memcpy((void *)slot_virt(&command, slot), payload, size);
	dma_sync(slot_virt(&command, slot), size);
	tre_fill(&command, command.next, slot_phys(&command, slot), opcode, TRE_TYPE_COMMAND | TRE_IEOT);
	command.next++;
	channel_doorbell(&command);
	for (unsigned us = 0; us < 200000 && !waiting.done; us += 200) {
		channel_events(&command, command_event, &waiting);
		if (!waiting.done) {
			delay_for_interval(200, NSEC_PER_USEC);
		}
	}
	if (!waiting.done) {
		printf("ipa: the command %s (opcode %#x) is not answered in 200 ms; channel state %u\n", what, opcode, channel_state(&command));
		gsi_error(what);
		return false;
	}
	if (trace) {
		printf("ipa: the command %s (opcode %#x) done, code %u\n", what, opcode, waiting.code);
	}
	return true;
}

/*
 * The tables, as Linux's ipa_table_init() lays them out in one buffer: a "zero rule" (8 bytes of
 * zero, which every table entry points at until somebody installs a rule), then the filter
 * table's bitmap of the endpoints that filter (bit n+1 for endpoint n: 2, 5 and 8 -- our modem
 * transmit endpoint and two of the modem's), then as many entries as the longest table (15: the
 * route tables' size, 0x78 bytes), each the zero rule's address. The filter table is the bitmap
 * and 3 entries from offset 8; a route table the 15 entries from offset 16.
 *
 * The IPA's local memory, in the layout the modem driver zeroed (Android's ipa_4_11_mem_part,
 * the same offsets as Linux's ipa_mem_local_data for these): IPv4 filter hashed 0x288, not
 * hashed 0x308, IPv6 0x388/0x408; IPv4 route 0x488/0x508, IPv6 0x588/0x608; the modem's and our
 * headers 0x688, 0x440 bytes in all.
 */
#define FILTERED_ENDPOINTS      ((1ull << 2) | (1ull << 5) | (1ull << 8))
#define FILTER_ENTRIES          4               /* the bitmap and one per filtering endpoint */
#define ROUTE_ENTRIES           15

static bool
table_init(const char *what, uint8_t opcode, bool filter, uint32_t hashed_offset, uint32_t offset)
{
	struct {
		uint64_t hash_rules_addr, flags, nhash_rules_addr;
	} payload;
	uint32_t entries = filter ? FILTER_ENTRIES : ROUTE_ENTRIES, size = entries * 8;
	uint64_t source = table.phys + (filter ? 8 : 16);

	payload.hash_rules_addr = source;
	payload.nhash_rules_addr = source;
	payload.flags = (uint64_t)size | (uint64_t)(mem_offset + hashed_offset) << 12 | (uint64_t)size << 28 |
	    (uint64_t)(mem_offset + offset) << 40;
	return ipa_command(what, opcode, &payload, sizeof(payload));
}

static bool
tables_setup(void)
{
	uint64_t *t = (uint64_t *)table.virt;
	struct {
		uint64_t hdr_table_addr;
		uint32_t flags, reserved;
	} headers;

	t[0] = 0;                                       /* the zero rule */
	t[1] = FILTERED_ENDPOINTS << 1;                 /* the filter bitmap */
	for (unsigned n = 0; n < ROUTE_ENTRIES; n++) {
		t[2 + n] = table.phys;
	}
	dma_sync(table.virt, (2 + ROUTE_ENTRIES) * 8);
	if (!table_init("IPv4 route table init", IPA_CMD_IP_V4_ROUTING_INIT, false, 0x488, 0x508) ||
	    !table_init("IPv6 route table init", IPA_CMD_IP_V6_ROUTING_INIT, false, 0x588, 0x608) ||
	    !table_init("IPv4 filter table init", IPA_CMD_IP_V4_FILTER_INIT, true, 0x288, 0x308) ||
	    !table_init("IPv6 filter table init", IPA_CMD_IP_V6_FILTER_INIT, true, 0x388, 0x408)) {
		return false;
	}
	headers.hdr_table_addr = zero.phys;
	headers.flags = 0x440 | (mem_offset + 0x688) << 12;
	headers.reserved = 0;
	if (!ipa_command("header table init", IPA_CMD_HDR_INIT_LOCAL, &headers, sizeof(headers))) {
		return false;
	}
	ipa_wr(IPA_FILT_ROUT_HASH_FLUSH, 0x1111);      /* the hashed tables' caches, flushed */
	return true;
}

/* ---- receiving and sending ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* A receive slot handed to the hardware (one TRE for the whole buffer). */
static void
receive_post(struct channel *ch, uint32_t slot)
{
	tre_fill(ch, ch->next, slot_phys(ch, slot), (uint16_t)(ch->buffer_size > 0xffff ? 0xffff : ch->buffer_size), TRE_TYPE_XFER | TRE_IEOT);
	ch->next++;
}

struct receive_context {
	void            (*receive)(uint8_t mux, const uint8_t *packet, size_t length);
	unsigned        packets;
};

/* A receive buffer is full (or closed): the QMAP packets in it, one by one; then the slot is posted again. */
static void
receive_event(struct channel *ch, const struct event *e, void *context)
{
	struct receive_context *rc = context;
	uint32_t slot = (uint32_t)((e->xfer - ch->tre_ring.phys) / ELEMENT_SIZE), length = e->len;
	const uint8_t *buffer;

	if (slot >= ch->slots || e->xfer < ch->tre_ring.phys) {
		if (ch->errors++ < 4) {
			printf("ipa: %s: an event for TRE %#llx, outside the ring at %#llx\n", ch->name, e->xfer, ch->tre_ring.phys);
		}
		return;
	}
	/* receives complete in order; ch->done is the next expected slot, ch->next the next to post (slots-1 ahead) */
	if (slot != ch->done % ch->slots) {
		if (ch->errors++ < 4) {
			printf("ipa: %s: slot %u finished while slot %u was expected\n", ch->name, slot, ch->done % ch->slots);
		}
	}
	ch->done++;
	buffer = (const uint8_t *)slot_virt(ch, slot);
	if (length > ch->buffer_size) {
		length = ch->buffer_size;
	}
	dma_sync((vm_offset_t)buffer, length);
	ch->bytes += length;
	if (trace) {
		printf("ipa: %s: slot %u: %u bytes (code %u): %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x ...\n", ch->name, slot, length, e->code,
		    buffer[0], buffer[1], buffer[2], buffer[3], buffer[4], buffer[5], buffer[6], buffer[7]);
	}
	if (ch->qmap) {
		for (uint32_t at = 0; at + 4 <= length;) {
			uint32_t pad = buffer[at] & 0x3f, cmd = buffer[at] & 0x80, mux = buffer[at + 1];
			uint32_t packet = (uint32_t)buffer[at + 2] << 8 | buffer[at + 3];

			if (packet == 0 || at + 4 + packet > length || pad > packet) {
				break;
			}
			if (cmd == 0) {
				ch->packets++;
				rc->packets++;
				if (rc->receive != NULL) {
					rc->receive((uint8_t)mux, buffer + at + 4, packet - pad);
				}
			} else if (trace) {
				printf("ipa: %s: a QMAP command (%u bytes) on mux %u\n", ch->name, packet, mux);
			}
			at += 4 + packet;
		}
	} else {
		ch->packets++;                          /* the LAN endpoint: looked at, dropped */
	}
	/* the slot posted again -- the one at the ring's next TRE, which is this one while the hardware finishes in order */
	receive_post(ch, ch->next % ch->slots);
	channel_doorbell(ch);
}

static void
transmit_event(struct channel *ch, const struct event *e, __unused void *context)
{
	uint32_t slot = (uint32_t)((e->xfer - ch->tre_ring.phys) / ELEMENT_SIZE);

	if (slot != ch->done % ch->slots && ch->errors++ < 4) {
		printf("ipa: %s: slot %u finished while slot %u was expected (code %u)\n", ch->name, slot, ch->done % ch->slots, e->code);
	}
	ch->done++;
}

bool
hakios_ipa_transmit(uint8_t mux, const void *packet, size_t length)
{
	struct channel *ch = &modem_tx;
	uint32_t slot;
	uint8_t *buffer;

	if (!ready || length == 0 || length + 4 > ch->buffer_size) {
		return false;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&ipa_lock);
	channel_events(ch, transmit_event, NULL);
	if (ch->next - ch->done >= ch->slots - 1) {     /* one slot always left free: write==read means empty */
		ch->dropped++;
		lck_mtx_unlock(&ipa_lock);
		return false;
	}
	slot = ch->next % ch->slots;
	buffer = (uint8_t *)slot_virt(ch, slot);
	buffer[0] = 0;                                  /* no pad, not a command */
	buffer[1] = mux;
	buffer[2] = (uint8_t)(length >> 8);
	buffer[3] = (uint8_t)length;
	memcpy(buffer + 4, packet, length);
	dma_sync((vm_offset_t)buffer, length + 4);
	tre_fill(ch, ch->next, slot_phys(ch, slot), (uint16_t)(length + 4), TRE_TYPE_XFER | TRE_IEOT | TRE_BEI);
	ch->next++;
	channel_doorbell(ch);
	ch->packets++;
	ch->bytes += length;
	if (trace) {
		printf("ipa: %s: slot %u: %zu bytes on mux %u\n", ch->name, slot, length, mux);
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&ipa_lock);
	return true;
}

unsigned
hakios_ipa_poll(void (*receive)(uint8_t mux, const uint8_t *packet, size_t length))
{
	struct receive_context rc = { receive, 0 };

	if (!ready) {
		return 0;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&ipa_lock);
	channel_events(&modem_rx, receive_event, &rc);
	channel_events(&lan_rx, receive_event, &rc);
	channel_events(&modem_tx, transmit_event, NULL);
	lck_mtx_unlock(&ipa_lock);
	return rc.packets;
}

void
hakios_ipa_modem_endpoints(uint32_t *to_modem, uint32_t *from_modem)
{
	*to_modem = modem_tx.endpoint;          /* 2: what Linux exports as modem/tx_endpoint_id */
	*from_modem = modem_rx.endpoint;        /* 16: modem/rx_endpoint_id */
}

bool
hakios_ipa_data_ready(void)
{
	return ready;
}

void
hakios_ipa_status(char *to, size_t size)
{
	snprintf(to, size, "to the modem %llu packets (%llu bytes, %llu dropped), from it %llu (%llu bytes), %llu to the LAN endpoint; "
	    "errors %llu/%llu/%llu; channels %u/%u/%u/%u", modem_tx.packets, modem_tx.bytes, modem_tx.dropped, modem_rx.packets, modem_rx.bytes,
	    lan_rx.packets, modem_tx.errors, modem_rx.errors, lan_rx.errors, channel_state(&command), channel_state(&lan_rx),
	    channel_state(&modem_tx), channel_state(&modem_rx));
}

/* ---- setting up ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

bool
hakios_ipa_data_setup(void)
{
	uint32_t status, shared;
	char line[256];

	if (ready) {
		return true;
	}
	{
		uint32_t off = 0;

		if (PE_parse_boot_argn("modem_ipa_data_off", &off, sizeof(off)) && off != 0) {
			printf("ipa: no data path (modem_ipa_data_off)\n");
			return false;
		}
		PE_parse_boot_argn("modem_ipa_data_trace", &off, sizeof(off));
		trace = off != 0;
	}
	if (PAGE_SIZE != RECEIVE_BUFFER) {
		printf("ipa: pages of %lu bytes, not %u: no data path\n", (unsigned long)PAGE_SIZE, RECEIVE_BUFFER);
		return false;
	}
	if (ipa_regs == 0) {
		PE_parse_boot_argn("soc_ipa_base", &ipa_regs_phys, sizeof(ipa_regs_phys));
		PE_parse_boot_argn("soc_gsi_base", &gsi_phys, sizeof(gsi_phys));
		ipa_regs = ml_io_map(ipa_regs_phys, IPA_REGS_SIZE);
		gsi_regs = ml_io_map(gsi_phys + GSI_FROM, GSI_SIZE);
	}
	if (ipa_regs == 0 || gsi_regs == 0) {
		printf("ipa: the registers cannot be mapped: no data path\n");
		return false;
	}
	status = gsi_rd(GSI_STATUS);
	shared = ipa_rd(IPA_SHARED_MEM_SIZE);
	mem_offset = 8 * (shared >> 16);
	if ((status & 1) == 0) {
		printf("ipa: the GSI is not enabled (status %#x): no data path\n", status);
		return false;
	}
	if (!dma_page(&table) || !dma_page(&zero)) {
		printf("ipa: no memory for the tables: no data path\n");
		return false;
	}
	for (unsigned n = 0; n < 4; n++) {
		if (!channel_memory(channels[n])) {
			printf("ipa: no memory for the %s channel: no data path\n", channels[n]->name);
			return false;
		}
	}
	printf("ipa: setting up this processor's data path: GSI status %#x, local memory at %#x; rings and buffers in DDR from %#llx "
	    "(the tables at %#llx)\n", status, mem_offset, modem_rx.pages[0].phys, table.phys);
	gsi_interrupts_off();
	for (unsigned n = 0; n < 4; n++) {
		struct channel *ch = channels[n];

		if (!channel_setup(ch)) {
			printf("ipa: the %s channel (%u, event ring %u) cannot be set up: no data path\n", ch->name, ch->id, ch->ring_id);
			return false;
		}
		endpoint_program(ch);
	}
	for (unsigned n = 0; n < 4; n++) {
		struct channel *ch = channels[n];

		if (!gsi_command(ch, false, GSI_CH_START, CH_STATE_STARTED)) {
			printf("ipa: the %s channel does not start: no data path\n", ch->name);
			return false;
		}
		ch->started = true;
		if (!ch->to_ipa) {
			/* one short of the ring: the doorbell is the write pointer, and writing it level with
			 * the read pointer (base) would mean "empty", not "full" */
			for (uint32_t slot = 0; slot + 1 < ch->slots; slot++) {
				receive_post(ch, slot);
			}
			channel_doorbell(ch);
		}
	}
	if (!tables_setup()) {
		printf("ipa: the IPA does not take its tables: no data path (the channels stay)\n");
		return false;
	}
	ready = true;
	hakios_ipa_status(line, sizeof(line));
	printf("ipa: THE DATA PATH IS UP: endpoints %u (commands), %u (LAN in), %u (to the modem), %u (from the modem); the tables set; %s\n",
	    command.endpoint, lan_rx.endpoint, modem_tx.endpoint, modem_rx.endpoint, line);
	return true;
}

```

`drivers/modem/hakios.mpss.c`:

```c
/*
 * The modem of the POCO X5 Pro (redwood), started, and asked about the network: step 1 of
 * cellular. Every address below belongs to this phone, and nothing here is touched unless a
 * boot-arg asks for it.
 *
 * The modem ("MPSS", Android's "modem") is a Hexagon of its own inside the SoC, exactly as the
 * Wi-Fi's and the audio's are (hakios.wifi.c, hakios.adsp.c): it stays in reset until somebody
 * loads its signed image -- modem.mdt and modem.b00 to modem.b29 from /vendor/firmware_mnt/image
 * of its Android, 85 MB, in the system image under /fw (MODEM=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh, from
 * fw-modem/) -- into the 246 MB reserved for it and asks TrustZone to authenticate and start it.
 * From there everything is conversation through the shared memory: SMP2P for "up", "given up",
 * "stopped"; GLINK for channels; QRTR on the channel "IPCRTR" for the modem's services, which
 * speak QMI (drivers/modem/hakios.qmi.c knows the protocol; here only two of its messages are made by
 * hand): the device management service is asked to put the modem online, and the network access
 * service what network it is on and how strong the signal is (drivers/modem/hakios.nas.c). What this
 * learns goes to sysctl kern.hakios.cellular_* for the rest of the system; calls, SMS and data
 * are for the steps after this one.
 *
 * The way is the modem's, which is the Wi-Fi DSP's: hakios.adsp.c's comments say why each
 * thing is done so; this file is that one with the modem's numbers (dt: qcom,mss@4080000,
 * qcom,smp2p-modem, qcom,glink/modem, reserved-memory mpss@8b800000):
 *   - processor 1 in the shared memory; its SMP2P items 435 (its) and 428 (ours); its last words
 *     in item 421; GLINK's three items in our partition with it
 *   - its doorbells are IPCC client 2 (MPSS): signal 0 GLINK, signal 2 SMP2P
 *   - TrustZone knows it as image 4; its memory is 0x8b800000, 246 MB, of which the image takes
 *     the first 85 (TrustZone is told of all of it: the modem uses the rest)
 *   - its rails are CX and MSS (cx.lvl and mss.lvl), asked for at level 384 while it boots
 *   - the always-on processor is told of it as "modem"
 *   - the channel is IPCRTR only; the modem's others (DS, DATA*, glink_ssr) are left unanswered
 *   - the ports of QRTR are the Wi-Fi driver's (sys/hakios.qrtr.h): what the NAS client needs
 * The modem and the Wi-Fi DSP may run at the same time: the mailbox to the always-on
 * processor and the lock for allocating in the shared memory are shared, each behind a lock.
 *
 * Boot-arg modem_step=N performs steps 1 to N and stops; modem=1 is all of them, on a thread
 * beside the system's start, and the modem stays on, its network state asked every two seconds.
 *
 *   1  reads   the shared memory: our partition with the modem, its items, whether it has run
 *   2  reads   the firmware on the root (or in the small image): is it whole, does it fit
 *   3  writes  the always-on processor's mailbox open, unless it is
 *   4  asks    TrustZone to take the image's header (image 4) and where the image will be; a
 *              modem that a kernel before this one left running is asked to stop and shut down first
 *   5  writes  the image into the modem's memory, and reads it back
 *   6  writes  our SMP2P item (428) into the shared memory, and our two marks of GLINK to zero
 *   7  asks    RPMh for the modem's rails, writes "modem: on" to the always-on processor, asks
 *              TrustZone to authenticate and start the modem, and watches for its first words
 *   8  reads   GLINK's queues
 *   9  writes  our side of GLINK: the versions, the channel "IPCRTR" opened both ways, our intents;
 *              from here a thread of ours listens to the modem
 *  10  talks   QRTR on that channel: hello both ways, and the services the modem tells of
 *  11  talks   QMI: DMS "operating mode online" (modem_online=0: not), then NAS "serving system"
 *              and "signal info" every second for modem_nas_wait seconds (default 30), or until
 *              the modem says it is registered and how strong the signal is
 *
 * What is started is stopped: when the steps are over (unless modem_keep=1, and then when the run
 * ends), and on a panic's way back to the loader. More boot-args: modem_new=K, modem_pause=MS,
 * modem_wait=S (step 7's watch, default 10), modem_listen=S (step 10, default 3), modem_again=1,
 * modem_return=1, as the modem's.
 *
 * Nothing here writes a clock or changes a pin. One request goes to RPMh (the two rails), as
 * Linux's remoteproc makes it; the SIM is not touched, no call is made, no data session opened.
 */

extern lck_mtx_t hakios_aop_mailbox_lock;

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(mpss_lock_group, "hakios-mpss");

/* the modem's file systems, served from here (rmtfs, below) */
static bool rmtfs_buffer_make(void);
static bool ipa_firmware_load(void);
static void ipa_firmware_stop(void);

#define STEPS                   11
#define HAKIOS_SOC_BASE        0x00400000ul    /* where the loader says the phone's peripherals begin */

static uint32_t last_step, pause_ms = 2200, listen_seconds = 3;
static uint32_t step;                   /* the one being performed */
static uint32_t new_from;               /* the first of the steps that have not been seen to work: they wait */
static char last_write[96] = "nothing written";
static bool leaving;                    /* on the way back to the loader after a panic: no lock is taken, nothing sleeps */

/*
 * Every line goes to the log the loader reads from another core as well (as in hakios.wifi.c);
 * with modem=1 only the few that say how it went (tell()), the rest to the kernel's own log.
 */
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);

static LCK_MTX_DECLARE(say_lock, &mpss_lock_group);
static bool quiet;

static void
say_line(const char *line, bool aloud)
{
	if (leaving) {
		for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
			loader_log_putc(*c);
		}
		return;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&say_lock);
	if (!quiet || aloud) {
		for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
			loader_log_putc(*c);
		}
	}
	printf("%s", line);
	lck_mtx_unlock(&say_lock);
}

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);
static int tell(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	say_line(line, false);
	return length;
}

static int
tell(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;
	int length;

	va_start(list, format);
	length = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	say_line(line, true);
	return length;
}
#define printf say

static void
sleep_us(uint32_t us)
{
	delay_for_interval(us, NSEC_PER_USEC);
}

static void
sleep_ms(uint32_t ms)
{
	delay_for_interval(ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
}

static uint64_t
now_us(void)
{
	uint64_t nanoseconds;

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &nanoseconds);
	return nanoseconds / 1000;
}

/* Until every write to memory so far has been carried out. */
static void
settle(void)
{
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy");
}

static bool
option(const char *name)
{
	uint32_t value = 0;

	return PE_parse_boot_argn(name, &value, sizeof(value)) && value != 0;
}

/* ---- register access (as in hakios.wifi.c) ------------------------------------------------------- */

static uint32_t __attribute__((noinline))
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	uint32_t value;

	__asm__ volatile ("ldr %w0, [%1]" : "=r" (value) : "r" (address) : "memory");
	return value;
}

static void __attribute__((noinline))
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	__asm__ volatile ("str %w0, [%1]" : : "r" (value), "r" (address) : "memory");
}

struct block {
	const char *name;
	uint32_t phys, size;
	vm_offset_t base;
};

static void
need(struct block *b)
{
	if (b->base == 0) {
		b->base = ml_io_map(b->phys, b->size);
	}
}

/* Time for the loader to note what has just been said, where it is not yet known to be harmless. */
static void
hold(void)
{
	if (step >= new_from && pause_ms && !leaving) {
		sleep_ms(pause_ms);
	}
}

static void
announce(const char *what)
{
	printf("mpss: step %u: %s\n", step, what);
	hold();
}

static uint32_t
get(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset)
{
	uint32_t value;

	need(b);
	value = rd(b->base + offset);
	printf("mpss: %u: %s %s (%#x) = %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
	return value;
}

static void
put(struct block *b, const char *name, uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
	need(b);
	printf("mpss: %u: about to write %s %s at %#x: %#x\n", step, b->name, name, b->phys + offset, value);
	snprintf(last_write, sizeof(last_write), "step %u wrote %#x to %s %s at %#x", step, value, b->name, name, b->phys + offset);
	wr(b->base + offset, value);
}

/* ---- the shared memory (hakios.wifi.c, step 1) --------------------------------------------------- */

#define SMEM_PHYS_DEFAULT       0x80900000u   /* dt: reg of /soc/qcom,smem */
static uint32_t smem_phys = SMEM_PHYS_DEFAULT;
#define SMEM_SIZE               0x00200000u
#define SMEM_US                 0
#define SMEM_MPSS               1               /* dt: qcom,remote-pid of qcom,smp2p-modem and qcom,glink/modem */
#define SMEM_GLOBAL             0xfffe
#define SMEM_CANARY             0xa5a5

struct smem_table_entry {
	uint32_t offset, size, flags;
	uint16_t host0, host1;
	uint32_t cacheline, reserved[7];
};
struct smem_table {
	uint8_t magic[4];
	uint32_t version, count, reserved[5];
};
struct smem_partition {
	uint8_t magic[4];
	uint16_t host0, host1;
	uint32_t size, free_uncached, free_cached, reserved[3];
};
struct smem_entry {
	uint16_t canary, item;
	uint32_t size;
	uint16_t padding_data, padding_header;
	uint32_t reserved;
};
struct smem_item {
	uint32_t item, offset, size;
};

/*
 * The DSP's items (dt: qcom,smem of qcom,smp2p-modem, <435 428>: the item the DSP writes first, then
 * ours -- the Wi-Fi's <617 616> are in the same order; taken the other way round, the DSP made
 * our item its own and never said "up" --, and qcom,smem-id of qcom,mss@4080000).
 */
#define ITEM_SMP2P_OURS         428
#define ITEM_SMP2P_THEIRS       435
#define ITEM_CRASH_REASON       421

static const volatile uint8_t *smem;

static bool
smem_peek(uint64_t offset, void *to, uint32_t size)
{
	if (smem == NULL) {
		smem = (const volatile uint8_t *)ml_io_map_unmappable(smem_phys, SMEM_SIZE, VM_WIMG_WCOMB);
	}
	if (offset + size > SMEM_SIZE) {
		return false;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
		((uint8_t *)to)[i] = smem[offset + i];
	}
	return true;
}

static void
smem_poke(uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
	wr((vm_offset_t)smem + offset, value);
}

static uint32_t
smem_word(uint32_t offset)
{
	return rd((vm_offset_t)smem + offset);
}

static uint32_t
smem_partition(uint16_t one, uint16_t other, uint32_t *cacheline, uint32_t *size)
{
	struct smem_table table;
	struct smem_table_entry entry;
	struct smem_partition header;

	if (!smem_peek(SMEM_SIZE - 0x1000, &table, sizeof(table)) || memcmp(table.magic, "$TOC", 4) != 0 || table.version != 1 ||
	    table.count > 64) {
		return 0;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < table.count; i++) {
		if (!smem_peek(SMEM_SIZE - 0x1000 + sizeof(table) + i * sizeof(entry), &entry, sizeof(entry)) || entry.offset == 0 ||
		    entry.size == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!((entry.host0 == one && entry.host1 == other) || (entry.host0 == other && entry.host1 == one))) {
			continue;
		}
		if ((uint64_t)entry.offset + entry.size > SMEM_SIZE - 0x1000 || !smem_peek(entry.offset, &header, sizeof(header)) ||
```
