```c
			next.bars = next.registered && next.has_signal ? bars_for(next.dbm) : 0;
			serving = true;
		} else if (message == 0x24 && type == 0x10 && size >= 5 && size >= (size_t)5 + value[4]) {
			/* the current PLMN: MCC, MNC (16 bits each), the description's length and bytes */
			unsigned n = value[4] < sizeof(next.operator_name) - 1 ? value[4] : sizeof(next.operator_name) - 1;

			next.mcc = le16(value);
			next.mnc = le16(value + 2);
			memcpy(next.operator_name, value + 5, n);
			next.operator_name[n] = 0;
		} else if ((message == 0x4f || message == 0x51) && type == 0x17 && size >= 4) {
			level = (int16_t)le16(value); radio = 12; signal = true;
		} else if ((message == 0x4f || message == 0x51) && type == 0x14 && size >= 6 && radio != 12) {
			level = (int16_t)le16(value + 2); radio = 8; signal = true;
		} else if ((message == 0x4f || message == 0x51) && type == 0x13 && size >= 3 && !signal) {
			level = (int8_t)value[0]; radio = 5; signal = true;
		} else if ((message == 0x4f || message == 0x51) && type == 0x12 && size >= 1 && !signal) {
			level = (int8_t)value[0]; radio = 4; signal = true;
		}
	}
	if (data[0] == 2 && (!result_seen || !success)) return 0;
	if (signal && level >= -150 && level <= -30) {
		next.has_signal = true;
		next.dbm = level;
		next.radio_interface = radio;
		next.bars = next.registered ? bars_for(level) : 0;
	}
	if (!serving && !signal) return 0;
	if (next.registered == state->registered && next.has_signal == state->has_signal && next.mcc == state->mcc && next.mnc == state->mnc &&
	    strcmp(next.operator_name, state->operator_name) == 0 &&
	    next.radio_interface == state->radio_interface && next.dbm == state->dbm && next.bars == state->bars) return 0;
	*state = next;
	return 1;
}

static void
nas_receive(void *context, uint32_t node, uint32_t port, const void *data, size_t length)
{
	struct hakios_nas_client *client = context;

	if (!client->connected || node != client->peer_node || port != client->peer_port) return;
	client->answers++;
	if (hakios_nas_apply(&client->state, data, length) == 1 && client->changed != NULL)
		client->changed(client->context, &client->state);
}

static void
nas_server(void *context, bool arrived, uint32_t service, uint32_t version, uint32_t instance,
    uint32_t node, uint32_t port)
{
	struct hakios_nas_client *client = context;
	(void)version;
	(void)instance;
	if (service != 3) return; /* QMI NAS */
	if (arrived && !client->connected) {
		client->connected = true;
		client->peer_node = node;
		client->peer_port = port;
		if (client->port != NULL) (void)hakios_nas_client_poll(client);
	} else if (!arrived && client->connected && node == client->peer_node && port == client->peer_port) {
		client->connected = false;
		client->state = (struct hakios_nas_state){0};
		if (client->changed != NULL) client->changed(client->context, &client->state);
	}
}

int
hakios_nas_client_open(struct hakios_nas_client *client, const struct hakios_qrtr_ops *transport,
    void (*changed)(void *, const struct hakios_nas_state *), void *context)
{
	int error;
	if (client == NULL || transport == NULL || transport->open == NULL || transport->lookup == NULL ||
	    transport->send == NULL || transport->close == NULL) return -1;
	*client = (struct hakios_nas_client){0};
	client->transport = transport;
	client->changed = changed;
	client->context = context;
	client->port = transport->open(nas_receive, nas_server, client);
	if (client->port == NULL) return -1;
	error = transport->lookup(client->port, 3, 0, 0);
	if (error != 0) {
		hakios_nas_client_close(client);
		return error;
	}
	return 0;
}

int
hakios_nas_client_poll(struct hakios_nas_client *client)
{
	uint8_t request[7] = {0};
	const uint16_t messages[2] = {0x24, 0x4f};
	int error;
	if (client == NULL || client->port == NULL || !client->connected) return -1;
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		client->transaction++;
		if (client->transaction == 0) client->transaction++;
		request[1] = (uint8_t)client->transaction;
		request[2] = (uint8_t)(client->transaction >> 8);
		request[3] = (uint8_t)messages[i];
		request[4] = (uint8_t)(messages[i] >> 8);
		error = client->transport->send(client->port, client->peer_node, client->peer_port, request, sizeof(request));
		if (error != 0) return error;
	}
	return 0;
}

void
hakios_nas_client_close(struct hakios_nas_client *client)
{
	if (client != NULL && client->port != NULL) {
		client->transport->close(client->port);
		client->port = NULL;
		client->connected = false;
	}
}

```

`drivers/modem/hakios.qmi.c`:

```c
/*
 * QMI: the helpers of sys/hakios.qmi.h -- messages coded by tables, a handle on the IPC router,
 * requests as transactions, indications to handlers.
 *
 * The interface is that of Linux's QMI helpers, because the driver that uses it (ath11k's qmi.c)
 * was written for them and is compiled as it is. The code is not Linux's: it is written from the
 * interface's meaning and from the public descriptions of the wire format (a 7-byte header, then
 * type-length-value triples; see below at "the coding").
 *
 * Where it deliberately does not behave as Linux's does, each of them for a message that is not
 * well formed (a message Linux decodes right is decoded the same here):
 *   - a TLV is taken to be as long as it says: what its element does not use is skipped, and an
 *     element that needs more than its TLV has is an error. (Linux reads on past the TLV.)
 *   - a TLV of a type the table does not have is skipped, whatever its type. (Linux refuses the
 *     message if the type is below 0x10.)
 *   - a string that would fill its C buffer to the last byte is an error: the buffer is elem_len
 *     bytes and ends with a zero. (Linux writes the zero one byte past it.)
 *
 * The same file is compiled into the kernel and, for its tests, on the machine that builds it
 * (tools/qmi-test): the few things it needs from an operating system are in the first section.
 */
#include <sys/hakios.qmi.h>
#include <sys/hakios.qrtr.h>

/* ---- what is needed of the operating system ---------------------------------------------------- */

#ifdef KERNEL

#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/param.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/time.h>

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(qmi_lck_grp, "hakios-qmi");

struct os_lock {
	lck_mtx_t mutex;
};

static void *
os_alloc(size_t size)
{
	return kalloc_data(size, Z_WAITOK | Z_ZERO);
}

static void
os_free(void *memory, size_t size)
{
	kfree_data(memory, size);
}

static void
os_lock_init(struct os_lock *l)
{
	lck_mtx_init(&l->mutex, &qmi_lck_grp, LCK_ATTR_NULL);
}

static void
os_lock_destroy(struct os_lock *l)
{
	lck_mtx_destroy(&l->mutex, &qmi_lck_grp);
}

static void
os_lock(struct os_lock *l)
{
	lck_mtx_lock(&l->mutex);
}

static void
os_unlock(struct os_lock *l)
{
	lck_mtx_unlock(&l->mutex);
}

static uint64_t
os_now_ms(void)
{
	uint64_t now, ns;

	clock_get_uptime(&now);
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now, &ns);
	return ns / NSEC_PER_MSEC;
}

/* With the lock held: sleep until os_wake(what) or for that long. */
static void
os_wait(struct os_lock *l, void *what, uint64_t ms)
{
	struct timespec ts = { .tv_sec = (time_t)(ms / 1000), .tv_nsec = (long)(ms % 1000) * NSEC_PER_MSEC };

	msleep(what, &l->mutex, PZERO, "hakios-qmi", &ts);
}

static void
os_wake(__unused struct os_lock *l, void *what)
{
	wakeup(what);
}

#define os_log(...)     printf(__VA_ARGS__)

#else /* a program on the machine that builds this: the tests */

#include <errno.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

struct os_lock {
	pthread_mutex_t mutex;
	pthread_cond_t woken;
};

static void *
os_alloc(size_t size)
{
	return calloc(1, size ? size : 1);
}

static void
os_free(void *memory, size_t size)
{
	(void)size;
	free(memory);
}

static void
os_lock_init(struct os_lock *l)
{
	pthread_mutex_init(&l->mutex, NULL);
	pthread_cond_init(&l->woken, NULL);
}

static void
os_lock_destroy(struct os_lock *l)
{
	pthread_mutex_destroy(&l->mutex);
	pthread_cond_destroy(&l->woken);
}

static void
os_lock(struct os_lock *l)
{
	pthread_mutex_lock(&l->mutex);
}

static void
os_unlock(struct os_lock *l)
{
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&l->mutex);
}

static uint64_t
os_now_ms(void)
{
	struct timespec ts;

	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
	return (uint64_t)ts.tv_sec * 1000 + (uint64_t)ts.tv_nsec / 1000000;
}

static void
os_wait(struct os_lock *l, void *what, uint64_t ms)
{
	struct timespec until;

	(void)what;                     /* one condition for all: whoever is woken looks again */
	clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &until);
	until.tv_sec += (time_t)(ms / 1000);
	until.tv_nsec += (long)(ms % 1000) * 1000000;
	if (until.tv_nsec >= 1000000000) {
		until.tv_sec++;
		until.tv_nsec -= 1000000000;
	}
	pthread_cond_timedwait(&l->woken, &l->mutex, &until);
}

static void
os_wake(struct os_lock *l, void *what)
{
	(void)what;
	pthread_cond_broadcast(&l->woken);
}

#define os_log(...)     fprintf(stderr, __VA_ARGS__)

#endif

/* ---- the coding -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * A message: the header, then TLVs -- type (1 byte), length (2), value -- in any order. Numbers
 * are little-endian. A table describes the C structure a message is coded from or into, top
 * level element by element; elements of one TLV follow each other and share its type:
 *
 *   [QMI_OPT_FLAG]   a byte in C that says whether the TLV is in the message at all
 *   [QMI_DATA_LEN]   the count of the array that follows. In C it is always a 32-bit number,
 *                    whatever the element's elem_size says (the tables are made by a tool that
 *                    writes "uint32_t x_len" for every count, and Linux reads and writes four
 *                    bytes there); elem_size is its size in the message: 1 byte if it is 1, else 2
 *   the value        numbers of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes; a string (at the top level just its
 *                    characters: the TLV's length is the string's); a structure, which is its
 *                    own elements one after the other with nothing in between; or an array of
 *                    any of these
 *
 * Inside a structure there are no TLVs and nothing is optional: a count if the element is a
 * variable array, a length before a string (1 byte if the string's C buffer is at most 255
 * bytes, else 2), then the values.
 */
#define TLV_HEADER      3

struct writer {
	uint8_t *at, *end;
};

struct reader {
	const uint8_t *at, *end;
};

static bool
put(struct writer *w, const void *bytes, size_t count)
{
	if ((size_t)(w->end - w->at) < count) {
		return false;
	}
	memcpy(w->at, bytes, count);
	w->at += count;
	return true;
}

static bool
put_number(struct writer *w, uint64_t value, unsigned size)
{
	uint8_t bytes[8];

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < size; i++) {
		bytes[i] = (uint8_t)(value >> (8 * i));
	}
	return put(w, bytes, size);
}

static bool
get_number(struct reader *r, uint64_t *value, unsigned size)
{
	if ((size_t)(r->end - r->at) < size) {
		return false;
	}
	*value = 0;
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < size; i++) {
		*value |= (uint64_t)r->at[i] << (8 * i);
	}
	r->at += size;
	return true;
}

/* A number of the C structure, of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes, as the machine keeps it. */
static uint64_t
load(const void *from, unsigned size)
{
	uint8_t v8;
	uint16_t v16;
	uint32_t v32;
	uint64_t v64;

	switch (size) {
	case 1: memcpy(&v8, from, 1); return v8;
	case 2: memcpy(&v16, from, 2); return v16;
	case 4: memcpy(&v32, from, 4); return v32;
	default: memcpy(&v64, from, 8); return v64;
	}
}

static void
store(void *to, uint64_t value, unsigned size)
{
	uint8_t v8 = (uint8_t)value;
	uint16_t v16 = (uint16_t)value;
	uint32_t v32 = (uint32_t)value;

	switch (size) {
	case 1: memcpy(to, &v8, 1); break;
	case 2: memcpy(to, &v16, 2); break;
	case 4: memcpy(to, &v32, 4); break;
	default: memcpy(to, &value, 8); break;
	}
}

static bool
is_number(const struct qmi_elem_info *e)
{
	return e->data_type >= QMI_UNSIGNED_1_BYTE && e->data_type <= QMI_SIGNED_4_BYTE_ENUM &&
	       (e->elem_size == 1 || e->elem_size == 2 || e->elem_size == 4 || e->elem_size == 8);
}

static unsigned
count_size(const struct qmi_elem_info *count)
{
	return count->elem_size == 1 ? 1 : 2;
}

static int encode_structure(struct writer *w, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, const uint8_t *structure);

/* `count` entries of one element. */
static int
encode_value(struct writer *w, const struct qmi_elem_info *e, const uint8_t *from, uint32_t count, bool top)
{
	if (is_number(e)) {
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			if (!put_number(w, load(from + (size_t)i * e->elem_size, e->elem_size), e->elem_size)) {
				return -EMSGSIZE;
			}
		}
		return 0;
	}
	if (e->data_type == QMI_STRUCT && e->ei_array != NULL) {
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			int error = encode_structure(w, e->ei_array, from + (size_t)i * e->elem_size);

			if (error) {
				return error;
			}
		}
		return 0;
	}
	if (e->data_type == QMI_STRING && count == 1) {
		size_t length = strnlen((const char *)from, e->elem_len);

		if (length >= e->elem_len) {
			return -EINVAL;                 /* no zero in the buffer */
		}
		if (!top && !put_number(w, length, e->elem_len <= 255 ? 1 : 2)) {
			return -EMSGSIZE;
		}
		return put(w, from, length) ? 0 : -EMSGSIZE;
	}
	return -EINVAL;
}

/*
 * The count and the entries of the element at *e (a QMI_DATA_LEN first, if the element is a variable
 * array); leaves *e at the last element used.
 */
static int
encode_counted(struct writer *w, const struct qmi_elem_info **e, const uint8_t *structure, bool top)
{
	uint32_t count = 1;

	if ((*e)->data_type == QMI_DATA_LEN) {
		const struct qmi_elem_info *length = (*e)++;

		count = (uint32_t)load(structure + length->offset, sizeof(uint32_t));
		if ((*e)->array_type != VAR_LEN_ARRAY || count > (*e)->elem_len || (count_size(length) == 1 && count > 255)) {
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		if (!put_number(w, count, count_size(length))) {
			return -EMSGSIZE;
		}
	} else if ((*e)->array_type == STATIC_ARRAY) {
		count = (*e)->elem_len;
	} else if ((*e)->array_type != NO_ARRAY) {
		return -EINVAL;                         /* a variable array nothing counts */
	}
	return encode_value(w, *e, structure + (*e)->offset, count, top);
}

static int
encode_structure(struct writer *w, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, const uint8_t *structure)
{
	for (const struct qmi_elem_info *e = ei; e->data_type != QMI_EOTI; e++) {
		int error = e->data_type == QMI_OPT_FLAG ? -EINVAL : encode_counted(w, &e, structure, false);

		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

int
hakios_qmi_encode(uint8_t type, uint16_t message, uint16_t transaction, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, const void *structure,
    void *buffer, size_t size)
{
	struct writer w = { .at = buffer, .end = (uint8_t *)buffer + size };
	uint8_t *start = buffer, *tlv;
	const struct qmi_elem_info *e;

	if (size < QMI_HEADER_SIZE) {
		return -EMSGSIZE;
	}
	w.at += QMI_HEADER_SIZE;
	for (e = structure != NULL ? ei : NULL; e != NULL && e->data_type != QMI_EOTI; e++) {
		uint8_t tlv_type = e->tlv_type;
		int error;

		if (e->data_type == QMI_OPT_FLAG) {
			if (!load((const uint8_t *)structure + e->offset, 1)) {
				/* not there: on to the next element of another TLV */
				while (e[1].data_type != QMI_EOTI && e[1].tlv_type == tlv_type) {
					e++;
				}
				continue;
			}
			e++;
			if (e->data_type == QMI_EOTI || e->tlv_type != tlv_type) {
				return -EINVAL;
			}
		}
		tlv = w.at;
		if ((size_t)(w.end - w.at) < TLV_HEADER) {
			return -EMSGSIZE;
		}
		w.at += TLV_HEADER;
		error = encode_counted(&w, &e, structure, true);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
		if (w.at - tlv - TLV_HEADER > 0xffff) {
			return -EMSGSIZE;
		}
		tlv[0] = tlv_type;
		tlv[1] = (uint8_t)(w.at - tlv - TLV_HEADER);
		tlv[2] = (uint8_t)((w.at - tlv - TLV_HEADER) >> 8);
	}
	if (w.at - start - QMI_HEADER_SIZE > 0xffff) {
		return -EMSGSIZE;
	}
	start[0] = type;
	start[1] = (uint8_t)transaction;
	start[2] = (uint8_t)(transaction >> 8);
	start[3] = (uint8_t)message;
	start[4] = (uint8_t)(message >> 8);
	start[5] = (uint8_t)(w.at - start - QMI_HEADER_SIZE);
	start[6] = (uint8_t)((w.at - start - QMI_HEADER_SIZE) >> 8);
	return (int)(w.at - start);
}

static int decode_structure(struct reader *r, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, uint8_t *structure);

static int
decode_value(struct reader *r, const struct qmi_elem_info *e, uint8_t *to, uint32_t count, bool top)
{
	uint64_t value;

	if (is_number(e)) {
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			if (!get_number(r, &value, e->elem_size)) {
				return -EINVAL;
			}
			store(to + (size_t)i * e->elem_size, value, e->elem_size);
		}
		return 0;
	}
	if (e->data_type == QMI_STRUCT && e->ei_array != NULL) {
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			int error = decode_structure(r, e->ei_array, to + (size_t)i * e->elem_size);

			if (error) {
				return error;
			}
		}
		return 0;
	}
	if (e->data_type == QMI_STRING && count == 1) {
		value = (uint64_t)(r->end - r->at);             /* at the top level: all of the TLV */
		if (!top && !get_number(r, &value, e->elem_len <= 255 ? 1 : 2)) {
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		if (value >= e->elem_len || value > (uint64_t)(r->end - r->at)) {
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		memcpy(to, r->at, (size_t)value);
		to[value] = 0;
		r->at += value;
		return 0;
	}
	return -EINVAL;
}

static int
decode_counted(struct reader *r, const struct qmi_elem_info **e, uint8_t *structure, bool top)
{
	uint32_t count = 1;

	if ((*e)->data_type == QMI_DATA_LEN) {
		const struct qmi_elem_info *length = (*e)++;
		uint64_t value;

		if (!get_number(r, &value, count_size(length))) {
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		if ((*e)->array_type != VAR_LEN_ARRAY || value > (*e)->elem_len) {
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		store(structure + length->offset, value, sizeof(uint32_t));
		count = (uint32_t)value;
	} else if ((*e)->array_type == STATIC_ARRAY) {
		count = (*e)->elem_len;
	} else if ((*e)->array_type != NO_ARRAY) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	return decode_value(r, *e, structure + (*e)->offset, count, top);
}

static int
decode_structure(struct reader *r, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, uint8_t *structure)
{
	for (const struct qmi_elem_info *e = ei; e->data_type != QMI_EOTI; e++) {
		int error = e->data_type == QMI_OPT_FLAG ? -EINVAL : decode_counted(r, &e, structure, false);

		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

int
hakios_qmi_decode(const void *buffer, size_t length, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, void *structure)
{
	const uint8_t *start = buffer;
	struct reader r;
	size_t said;

	if (buffer == NULL || length < QMI_HEADER_SIZE || ei == NULL || structure == NULL) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	said = start[5] | (size_t)start[6] << 8;
	if (said > length - QMI_HEADER_SIZE) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	r.at = start + QMI_HEADER_SIZE;
	r.end = r.at + said;
	while (r.at < r.end) {
		const struct qmi_elem_info *e;
		struct reader value;
		uint8_t tlv_type;
		int error;

		if (r.end - r.at < TLV_HEADER) {
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		tlv_type = r.at[0];
		value.at = r.at + TLV_HEADER;
		value.end = value.at + (r.at[1] | (size_t)r.at[2] << 8);
		if (value.end > r.end) {
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		r.at = value.end;
		for (e = ei; e->data_type != QMI_EOTI && e->tlv_type != tlv_type; e++) {
		}
		if (e->data_type == QMI_EOTI) {
			continue;                       /* nothing we know: a newer firmware's, say */
		}
		if (e->data_type == QMI_OPT_FLAG) {
			store((uint8_t *)structure + e->offset, 1, 1);
			e++;
			if (e->data_type == QMI_EOTI || e->tlv_type != tlv_type) {
				return -EINVAL;
			}
		}
		error = decode_counted(&value, &e, structure, true);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
	}
	return (int)(QMI_HEADER_SIZE + said);
}

const struct qmi_elem_info qmi_response_type_v01_ei[] = {
	{
		.data_type = QMI_SIGNED_2_BYTE_ENUM, .elem_len = 1, .elem_size = sizeof(uint16_t), .array_type = NO_ARRAY,
		.tlv_type = QMI_COMMON_TLV_TYPE, .offset = offsetof(struct qmi_response_type_v01, result),
	},
	{
		.data_type = QMI_SIGNED_2_BYTE_ENUM, .elem_len = 1, .elem_size = sizeof(uint16_t), .array_type = NO_ARRAY,
		.tlv_type = QMI_COMMON_TLV_TYPE, .offset = offsetof(struct qmi_response_type_v01, error),
	},
	{ .data_type = QMI_EOTI },
};

/* ---- handles ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* What stands behind a handle (its `sock` points here). */
struct qmi_state {
	struct qmi_handle *handle;
	const struct hakios_qrtr_ops *transport;
	struct hakios_qrtr_port *port;
	struct os_lock lock;                    /* the lists below and the transactions in them */
	struct qmi_ops ops;
	const struct qmi_msg_handler *handlers;
	size_t largest;
	struct qmi_txn *transactions;
	uint16_t last_id;
	struct qmi_service *services;
	bool connected;
	uint32_t peer_node, peer_port;
	/* said in the log once each, so that a firmware that talks a lot cannot fill it */
	bool said_malformed, said_undecoded, said_unknown;
};

static const struct hakios_qrtr_ops *qmi_transport;

void
hakios_qmi_set_transport(const struct hakios_qrtr_ops *ops)
{
	qmi_transport = ops;
}

static struct qmi_state *
state_of(struct qmi_handle *qmi)
{
	return qmi != NULL ? (struct qmi_state *)(void *)qmi->sock : NULL;
}

/* With the lock held. */
static struct qmi_txn **
find_transaction(struct qmi_state *s, const struct qmi_txn *txn, uint16_t id)
{
	struct qmi_txn **p;

	for (p = &s->transactions; *p != NULL; p = &(*p)->next) {
		if (txn != NULL ? *p == txn : (*p)->id == id) {
			return p;
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

/* A message that is not the reply somebody waits for: to its handler, if it has one. */
static void
to_handler(struct qmi_state *s, uint8_t type, uint16_t id, uint16_t message, uint32_t node, uint32_t port, const void *data,
    size_t length)
{
	const struct qmi_msg_handler *h;
	struct sockaddr_qrtr from = { .sq_family = AF_QIPCRTR, .sq_node = node, .sq_port = port };
	struct qmi_txn txn = { .qmi = s->handle, .id = id };
	void *decoded;
	int result;

	for (h = s->handlers; h != NULL && h->fn != NULL; h++) {
		if (h->type == type && h->msg_id == message) {
			break;
		}
	}
	if (h == NULL || h->fn == NULL) {
		if (!s->said_unknown) {
			s->said_unknown = true;
			os_log("qmi: a message nobody handles: type %u, id %#x, %zu bytes (said once)\n", type, message, length);
		}
		return;
	}
	decoded = os_alloc(h->decoded_size);
	if (decoded == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	result = hakios_qmi_decode(data, length, h->ei, decoded);
	if (result < 0) {
		if (!s->said_undecoded) {
			s->said_undecoded = true;
			os_log("qmi: message %#x (type %u, %zu bytes) cannot be decoded: %d (said once)\n", message, type, length, result);
		}
	} else {
		h->fn(s->handle, &from, &txn, decoded);
	}
	os_free(decoded, h->decoded_size);
}

/* The router has a datagram for us. */
static void
qmi_receive(void *context, uint32_t node, uint32_t port, const void *data, size_t length)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = context;
	const uint8_t *header = data;
	struct qmi_txn **found, *txn;
	uint16_t id, message;
	uint8_t type;

	if (length < QMI_HEADER_SIZE || length > s->largest + QMI_HEADER_SIZE ||
	    (size_t)(header[5] | header[6] << 8) > length - QMI_HEADER_SIZE) {
		if (!s->said_malformed) {
			s->said_malformed = true;
			os_log("qmi: a datagram of %zu bytes from %u:%u is no message we take (said once)\n", length, node, port);
		}
		return;
	}
	type = header[0];
	id = (uint16_t)(header[1] | header[2] << 8);
	message = (uint16_t)(header[3] | header[4] << 8);
	if (type == QMI_RESPONSE) {
		os_lock(&s->lock);
		found = find_transaction(s, NULL, id);
		txn = found != NULL ? *found : NULL;
		if (txn != NULL && !txn->done && txn->ei != NULL && txn->dest != NULL) {
			txn->result = hakios_qmi_decode(data, length, txn->ei, txn->dest);
			txn->done = true;
			os_wake(&s->lock, txn);
			os_unlock(&s->lock);
			return;
		}
		os_unlock(&s->lock);
		if (txn == NULL) {
			return;                         /* a reply to nothing: late, after its transaction was given up */
		}
	}
	to_handler(s, type, id, message, node, port, data, length);
}

/* The router says a server we asked about is there, or is gone. */
static void
qmi_server(void *context, bool arrived, uint32_t service, uint32_t version, uint32_t instance, uint32_t node, uint32_t port)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = context;
	struct qmi_service *svc, **p;

	os_lock(&s->lock);
	for (p = &s->services; *p != NULL; p = &(*p)->next) {
		if ((*p)->node == node && (*p)->port == port) {
			break;
		}
	}
	svc = *p;
	if (!arrived && svc != NULL) {
		*p = svc->next;
	}
	os_unlock(&s->lock);

	if (arrived && svc == NULL) {
		svc = os_alloc(sizeof(*svc));
		if (svc == NULL) {
			return;
		}
		svc->service = service;
		svc->version = version;
		svc->instance = instance;
		svc->node = node;
		svc->port = port;
		if (s->ops.new_server != NULL && s->ops.new_server(s->handle, svc) < 0) {
			os_free(svc, sizeof(*svc));
			return;
		}
		os_lock(&s->lock);
		svc->next = s->services;
		s->services = svc;
		os_unlock(&s->lock);
	} else if (!arrived && svc != NULL) {
		if (s->ops.del_server != NULL) {
			s->ops.del_server(s->handle, svc);
		}
		os_free(svc, sizeof(*svc));
	}
}

int
hakios_qmi_handle_init_transport(struct qmi_handle *qmi, size_t largest, const struct qmi_ops *ops,
    const struct qmi_msg_handler *handlers, const struct hakios_qrtr_ops *transport)
{
	struct qmi_state *s;

	qmi->sock = NULL;
	if (transport == NULL) {
		return -ENXIO;
	}
	s = os_alloc(sizeof(*s));
	if (s == NULL) {
		return -ENOMEM;
	}
	s->handle = qmi;
	s->transport = transport;
	s->largest = largest;
	s->handlers = handlers;
	if (ops != NULL) {
		s->ops = *ops;
	}
	os_lock_init(&s->lock);
	qmi->sock = (struct socket *)(void *)s;         /* before the port: callbacks may come at once */
	s->port = transport->open(qmi_receive, qmi_server, s);
	if (s->port == NULL) {
		qmi->sock = NULL;
		os_lock_destroy(&s->lock);
		os_free(s, sizeof(*s));
		return -ENXIO;
	}
	return 0;
}

int
qmi_handle_init(struct qmi_handle *qmi, size_t largest, const struct qmi_ops *ops, const struct qmi_msg_handler *handlers)
{
	return hakios_qmi_handle_init_transport(qmi, largest, ops, handlers, qmi_transport);
}

/* Nobody may be waiting in qmi_txn_wait() on this handle any more. */
void
qmi_handle_release(struct qmi_handle *qmi)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = state_of(qmi);
	struct qmi_service *svc;

	if (s == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	s->transport->close(s->port);                   /* no callback after this */
	while ((svc = s->services) != NULL) {
		s->services = svc->next;
		os_free(svc, sizeof(*svc));
	}
	qmi->sock = NULL;
	os_lock_destroy(&s->lock);
	os_free(s, sizeof(*s));
}

int
qmi_add_lookup(struct qmi_handle *qmi, unsigned int service, unsigned int version, unsigned int instance)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = state_of(qmi);
	int error;

	if (s == NULL) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	error = s->transport->lookup(s->port, service, version, instance);
	return error > 0 ? -error : error;
}

int
hakios_qmi_connect(struct socket *sock, uint32_t node, uint32_t port)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = (struct qmi_state *)(void *)sock;

	if (s == NULL) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	os_lock(&s->lock);
	s->peer_node = node;
	s->peer_port = port;
	s->connected = true;
	os_unlock(&s->lock);
	return 0;
}

int
qmi_txn_init(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct qmi_txn *txn, const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, void *structure)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = state_of(qmi);
	uint16_t id;

	memset(txn, 0, sizeof(*txn));
	if (s == NULL) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	txn->qmi = qmi;
	txn->ei = ei;
	txn->dest = structure;
	os_lock(&s->lock);
	/* the next number nobody else has (0 to 65534, round and round) */
	for (id = (uint16_t)(s->last_id + 1);; id++) {
		if (id == 0xffff) {
			id = 0;
		}
		if (find_transaction(s, NULL, id) == NULL) {
			break;
		}
		if (id == s->last_id) {
			os_unlock(&s->lock);
			return -ENOMEM;                 /* 65535 of them at once */
		}
	}
	s->last_id = id;
	txn->id = id;
	txn->next = s->transactions;
	s->transactions = txn;
	os_unlock(&s->lock);
	return id;
}

int
qmi_send_request(struct qmi_handle *qmi, struct sockaddr_qrtr *sq, struct qmi_txn *txn, int msg_id, size_t largest,
    const struct qmi_elem_info *ei, const void *structure)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = state_of(qmi);
	uint32_t node, port;
	bool connected;
	size_t size = largest + QMI_HEADER_SIZE;
	void *buffer;
	int length, error;

	if (s == NULL || txn == NULL) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	os_lock(&s->lock);
	connected = s->connected;
	node = s->peer_node;
	port = s->peer_port;
	os_unlock(&s->lock);
	if (sq != NULL) {
		node = sq->sq_node;
		port = sq->sq_port;
	} else if (!connected) {
		return -ENOTCONN;
	}
	buffer = os_alloc(size);
	if (buffer == NULL) {
		return -ENOMEM;
	}
	length = hakios_qmi_encode(QMI_REQUEST, (uint16_t)msg_id, txn->id, ei, structure, buffer, size);
	if (length < 0) {
		os_free(buffer, size);
		return length;
	}
	error = s->transport->send(s->port, node, port, buffer, (size_t)length);
	os_free(buffer, size);
	return error > 0 ? -error : error;
}

void
qmi_txn_cancel(struct qmi_txn *txn)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = state_of(txn->qmi);
	struct qmi_txn **found;

	if (s == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	os_lock(&s->lock);
	found = find_transaction(s, txn, 0);
	if (found != NULL) {
		*found = txn->next;
	}
	os_unlock(&s->lock);
}

int
hakios_qmi_txn_wait_ms(struct qmi_txn *txn, uint64_t milliseconds)
{
	struct qmi_state *s = state_of(txn->qmi);
	uint64_t now = os_now_ms(), until = now + milliseconds;
	struct qmi_txn **found;
	int result;

	if (s == NULL) {
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	os_lock(&s->lock);
	while (!txn->done && now < until) {
		os_wait(&s->lock, txn, until - now);
		now = os_now_ms();
	}
	found = find_transaction(s, txn, 0);
	if (found != NULL) {
		*found = txn->next;
	}
	result = txn->done ? txn->result : -ETIMEDOUT;
	os_unlock(&s->lock);
	return result;
}
```

```
# drivers/net/conf: the network interfaces.
# CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y in a defconfig builds a driver into the kernel; "standard" files are always built.
# tools/hakios-config.py reads this file; docs/drivers-config.md says what each word means and how it reaches XNU.

standard bsd/dev/hakios.net.c
	help    en0, an interface that is Ethernet to the rest of the kernel, for whatever link carries its frames

driver VIRTIO_NET
	file    bsd/dev/hakios.virtio_net.c
	help    QEMU's virtio network device as the link behind en0 (virtio_net=1). QEMU only
```

`drivers/net/hakios.net.c`:

```c
/*
 * en0: a network interface that is Ethernet as far as the rest of the kernel and Darwin can tell.
 *
 * Darwin expects its interfaces from IONetworkingFamily, which this kernel does not have; the BSD
 * half of the kernel does not need it. The interface is made with the kernel's own interface
 * KPI, the way bsd/net/if_fake.c makes its "feth": family Ethernet, the stock Ethernet framing
 * and demultiplexing, one function that is given a frame to send and one call to hand a frame
 * that has arrived to the stack. What Darwin's user space makes of an interface that has no
 * IOKit object behind it is another matter: see userland/src/net_test.m.
 *
 * What carries the frames is a link driver's business; sys/hakios.net.h is all that the two
 * know of each other. The first link is QEMU's virtio network device (hakios.virtio_net.c).
 * There can be two interfaces: en0 for the Wi-Fi (or virtio), en1 for the modem's packets
 * through the IPA (hakios.cell.c); each has its link, its state and its thread.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <net/bpf.h>
#include <net/ethernet.h>
#include <net/if.h>
#include <net/if_ether.h>
#include <net/if_media.h>
#include <net/if_types.h>
#include <net/kpi_interface.h>
#include <netinet/in.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/kern_event.h>
#include <sys/kpi_mbuf.h>
#include <sys/proc.h>
#include <sys/hakios.net.h>
#include <sys/sockio.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern void HakiosWLANStart(const char *interface, const uint8_t *address);  /* drivers/wifi/hakios.wlan.cpp */

static LCK_GRP_DECLARE(net_lck_grp, "hakios-net");

/* One interface: enN on its link. */
struct net_if {
	unsigned        unit;
	const struct hakios_net_link *link;
	bool            up;             /* the link says frames can pass */
	ifnet_t         ifp;
	lck_mtx_t       tx_lock;        /* one frame at a time to the link */
	/* What has gone through: said once a minute while anything moves. */
	struct {
		uint64_t sent, received, sent_bytes, received_bytes, dropped_out, dropped_in;
	} count;
};
static struct net_if net_ifs[HAKIOS_NET_UNITS];

static inline struct net_if *
net_if_of(ifnet_t ifp)
{
	return ifnet_softc(ifp);
}

/* The interface on unit `unit`, once attached; NULL before. */
static struct net_if *
net_if_unit(unsigned unit)
{
	return unit < HAKIOS_NET_UNITS && net_ifs[unit].ifp != NULL ? &net_ifs[unit] : NULL;
}

/*
 * Boot-arg net_trace=N: a line in the log for each of the first N frames, either way.
 * Boot-arg net_names=1: a line for every name asked of a DNS server and for every TCP connection
 * begun from here -- which is how to see what a system that has just been given a network does
 * with it (up to NAMES_MAX lines).
 */
#define NAMES_MAX       3000
static uint32_t net_trace, net_names;

static void
trace_frame(const char *way, const uint8_t *frame, size_t length, size_t whole)
{
	static uint32_t said, names;
	const uint8_t *end = frame + length, *ip = frame + ETHER_HDR_LEN, *l4;
	uint16_t type;
	bool ports;

	if (length < ETHER_HDR_LEN + 28 || (said >= net_trace && (!net_names || names >= NAMES_MAX))) {
		return;
	}
	type = (uint16_t)(frame[12] << 8 | frame[13]);
	l4 = ip + 4 * (ip[0] & 0xf);
	ports = type == ETHERTYPE_IP && (ip[9] == IPPROTO_TCP || ip[9] == IPPROTO_UDP) && l4 + 4 <= end;
	if (net_names && names < NAMES_MAX && ports && way[0] == 'o') {
		if (ip[9] == IPPROTO_UDP && (l4[2] << 8 | l4[3]) == 53 && l4 + 8 + 12 < end) {
			char name[128];
			const uint8_t *label = l4 + 8 + 12;
			size_t n = 0;

			/* the question: lengths and labels, up to a zero */
			while (label < end && *label != 0 && *label < 64 && label + 1 + *label < end && n + *label + 2 < sizeof(name)) {
				memcpy(name + n, label + 1, *label);
				n += *label;
				name[n++] = '.';
				label += 1 + *label;
			}
			name[n ? n - 1 : 0] = 0;
			names++;
			printf("net: asks for the name %s (type %u)\n", name, label + 2 < end ? label[1] << 8 | label[2] : 0);
		} else if (ip[9] == IPPROTO_TCP && l4 + 14 <= end && (l4[13] & 0x12) == 0x02) {
			names++;
			printf("net: connects to %u.%u.%u.%u port %u\n", ip[16], ip[17], ip[18], ip[19], l4[2] << 8 | l4[3]);
		}
	}
	if (said >= net_trace) {
		return;
	}
	said++;
	if (type == ETHERTYPE_IP) {
		printf("net: %s %zu bytes: IPv4 %s %u.%u.%u.%u:%u -> %u.%u.%u.%u:%u%s\n", way, whole, ip[9] == IPPROTO_TCP ? "TCP" :
		    ip[9] == IPPROTO_UDP ? "UDP" : ip[9] == IPPROTO_ICMP ? "ICMP" : "protocol?", ip[12], ip[13], ip[14], ip[15],
		    ports ? l4[0] << 8 | l4[1] : 0, ip[16], ip[17], ip[18], ip[19], ports ? l4[2] << 8 | l4[3] : 0,
		    ip[9] == IPPROTO_TCP && ports && l4 + 14 <= end ? (l4[13] & 2 ? " SYN" : l4[13] & 1 ? " FIN" : l4[13] & 4 ? " RST" : "") : "");
	} else {
		printf("net: %s %zu bytes: %s (type %#x) to %02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x\n", way, whole, type == ETHERTYPE_ARP ? "ARP" :
		    type == ETHERTYPE_IPV6 ? "IPv6" : "?", type, frame[0], frame[1], frame[2], frame[3], frame[4], frame[5]);
	}
}

/* ... of a frame on its way out: the start of it is enough */
static void
trace_packet(mbuf_t packet, size_t length)
{
	uint8_t start[192];
	size_t have = length < sizeof(start) ? length : sizeof(start);

	if ((net_trace || net_names) && mbuf_copydata(packet, 0, have, start) == 0) {
		trace_frame("out", start, have, length);
	}
}

/* ---- the interface -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* The stack has a frame to send (a chain of mbufs that starts with the Ethernet header). */
static errno_t
net_output(ifnet_t ifp, mbuf_t packet)
{
	struct net_if *n = net_if_of(ifp);
	size_t length = mbuf_pkthdr_len(packet);
	bool sent = false;

	if (length <= HAKIOS_NET_FRAME_MAX && n->up) {
		bpf_tap_out(ifp, DLT_EN10MB, packet, NULL, 0);
		trace_packet(packet, length);
		lck_mtx_lock(&n->tx_lock);
		sent = n->link->transmit(packet, length);
		lck_mtx_unlock(&n->tx_lock);
	}
	if (sent) {
		n->count.sent++;
		n->count.sent_bytes += length;
		ifnet_stat_increment_out(ifp, 1, (uint32_t)length, 0);
	} else {
		n->count.dropped_out++;
		ifnet_stat_increment_out(ifp, 0, 0, 1);
	}
	mbuf_freem(packet);
	return 0;
}

/* A frame has arrived on unit `unit`. */
void
hakios_net_input_unit(unsigned unit, const uint8_t *frame, size_t length)
{
	struct net_if *n = net_if_unit(unit);
	struct ifnet_stat_increment_param stats = { .packets_in = 1, .bytes_in = (uint32_t)length };
	unsigned int chunks = 1;
	mbuf_t packet = NULL;
	char *header;

	if (n == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	trace_frame("in ", frame, length, length);
	if (length < ETHER_HDR_LEN || length > HAKIOS_NET_FRAME_MAX || mbuf_allocpacket(MBUF_DONTWAIT, length, &chunks, &packet) != 0) {
		n->count.dropped_in++;
		return;
	}
	if (mbuf_copyback(packet, 0, length, frame, MBUF_DONTWAIT) != 0) {
		mbuf_freem(packet);
		n->count.dropped_in++;
		return;
	}
	/* as every Ethernet driver hands a frame up: the header noted and stepped over */
	header = mbuf_data(packet);
	mbuf_pkthdr_setrcvif(packet, n->ifp);
	mbuf_pkthdr_setheader(packet, header);
	mbuf_pkthdr_adjustlen(packet, -ETHER_HDR_LEN);
	mbuf_setdata(packet, header + ETHER_HDR_LEN, length - ETHER_HDR_LEN);
	bpf_tap_in(n->ifp, DLT_EN10MB, packet, header, ETHER_HDR_LEN);
	n->count.received++;
	n->count.received_bytes += length;
	ifnet_input(n->ifp, packet, &stats);
}

void
hakios_net_input(const uint8_t *frame, size_t length)
{
	hakios_net_input_unit(0, frame, length);
}

static unsigned net_ioctls_said;

static errno_t
net_ioctl(ifnet_t ifp, u_long command, void *data)
{
	struct net_if *n = net_if_of(ifp);
	/* (a radio says it is one here too: IO80211.framework lists the interfaces whose media is 802.11) */
	const int media[] = { (n->link->wireless ? IFM_IEEE80211 : IFM_ETHER) | IFM_AUTO };
	struct ifreq *request = data;
	struct ifmediareq *media_request = data;
	user_addr_t list;
	errno_t error = 0;

	if (n->link->wireless && net_ioctls_said < 80) {
		char who[32] = "?";

		/* (while Darwin's Wi-Fi side is being got to talk to this: who asks the interface what) */
		proc_selfname(who, sizeof(who));
		if (strcmp(who, "configd") != 0) {
			net_ioctls_said++;
			printf("net: en0 is asked %#lx by %s\n", command, who);
		}
	}
	switch (command) {
	case SIOCSIFADDR:
		ifnet_set_flags(ifp, IFF_UP, IFF_UP);
		break;
	case SIOCSIFFLAGS:
		/* running whenever it is up: the link is there or it is not, nothing is switched on */
		ifnet_set_flags(ifp, (ifnet_flags(ifp) & IFF_UP) ? IFF_RUNNING : 0, IFF_RUNNING);
		break;
	case SIOCGIFMEDIA32:
	case SIOCGIFMEDIA64:
		/* what configd asks to learn whether the cable is in */
		list = command == SIOCGIFMEDIA64 ? ((struct ifmediareq64 *)media_request)->ifmu_ulist :
		    CAST_USER_ADDR_T(((struct ifmediareq32 *)media_request)->ifmu_ulist);
		media_request->ifm_active = media_request->ifm_current = media[0];
		media_request->ifm_mask = 0;
		media_request->ifm_status = IFM_AVALID | (n->up ? IFM_ACTIVE : 0);
		if (list != USER_ADDR_NULL && media_request->ifm_count > 0) {
			error = copyout(media, list, sizeof(media));
		}
		media_request->ifm_count = 1;
		break;
	case SIOCGIFDEVMTU:
		request->ifr_devmtu.ifdm_current = ifnet_mtu(ifp);
		request->ifr_devmtu.ifdm_max = ETHERMTU;
		request->ifr_devmtu.ifdm_min = IF_MINMTU;
		break;
	case SIOCSIFMTU:
		error = request->ifr_mtu > ETHERMTU || request->ifr_mtu < IF_MINMTU ? EINVAL : ifnet_set_mtu(ifp, request->ifr_mtu);
		break;
	case SIOCADDMULTI:
	case SIOCDELMULTI:
		break;                          /* the link hands us everything anyway */
	default:
		/* what Darwin's Wi-Fi side asks of a radio's interface: drivers/wifi/hakios.apple80211.c */
		error = n->link->wireless ? hakios_apple80211_ioctl(command, data) : EOPNOTSUPP;
		break;
	}
	return error;
}

/* Tell whoever listens for kernel events (configd does) that the link is up, or down. */
static void
net_link_event(ifnet_t ifp, uint32_t code)
{
	_Alignas(struct kern_event_msg) char message[sizeof(struct kern_event_msg) + sizeof(struct net_event_data)] = { 0 };
	struct kern_event_msg *header = (struct kern_event_msg *)message;
	struct net_event_data *about = (struct net_event_data *)(header + 1);

	header->total_size = sizeof(message);
	header->vendor_code = KEV_VENDOR_APPLE;
	header->kev_class = KEV_NETWORK_CLASS;
	header->kev_subclass = KEV_DL_SUBCLASS;
	header->event_code = code;
	about->if_family = ifnet_family(ifp);
	about->if_unit = ifnet_unit(ifp);
	strlcpy(about->if_name, ifnet_name(ifp), IFNAMSIZ);
	ifnet_event(ifp, header);
}

void
hakios_net_link_state_unit(unsigned unit, bool up)
{
	struct net_if *n = net_if_unit(unit);

	if (n == NULL || up == n->up) {
		return;
	}
	n->up = up;
	printf("net: en%u's link (%s) is %s\n", n->unit, n->link->name, up ? "up" : "down");
	net_link_event(n->ifp, up ? KEV_DL_LINK_ON : KEV_DL_LINK_OFF);
}

void
hakios_net_link_state(bool up)
{
	hakios_net_link_state_unit(0, up);
}

/* The interface's own thread: for a link that wants to be asked, and for the minute's line in the log. */
static void
net_thread(void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	struct net_if *n = parameter;
	uint64_t said = 0, total;
	unsigned quiet = 0;

	for (unsigned tick = 1;; tick++) {
		quiet = n->link->poll != NULL && n->link->poll() ? 0 : quiet + 1;
		/* about once a minute, if anything has moved since */
		total = n->count.sent + n->count.received + n->count.dropped_out + n->count.dropped_in;
		if (tick % 8192 == 0 && total != said) {
			said = total;
			printf("net: en%u so far %llu frames sent (%llu bytes), %llu received (%llu bytes); dropped: %llu out, %llu in\n",
			    n->unit, n->count.sent, n->count.sent_bytes, n->count.received, n->count.received_bytes,
			    n->count.dropped_out, n->count.dropped_in);
		}
		delay_for_interval(quiet < 100 ? 2 : 10, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

bool
hakios_net_attach(const struct hakios_net_link *link)
{
	unsigned unit = link->unit;
	struct net_if *n = unit < HAKIOS_NET_UNITS ? &net_ifs[unit] : NULL;
	char uniqueid[16];
	struct ifnet_init_eparams init = {
		.ver = IFNET_INIT_CURRENT_VERSION,
		.len = sizeof(init),
		/*
		 * The simple model: every frame straight to net_output(). And no Skywalk "nexus" made for
		 * the interface by itself: sockets are all that is asked of it so far.
		 */
		.flags = IFNET_INIT_LEGACY | IFNET_INIT_NX_NOAUTO,
		.uniqueid = uniqueid,
		.uniqueid_len = 11,
		.name = "en",
		.unit = unit,
		.softc = n,
		.family = IFNET_FAMILY_ETHERNET,
		.subfamily = link->wireless ? IFNET_SUBFAMILY_WIFI : IFNET_SUBFAMILY_ANY,
		.type = IFT_ETHER,
		.output = net_output,
		.demux = ether_demux,
		.add_proto = ether_add_proto,
		.del_proto = ether_del_proto,
		.check_multi = ether_check_multi,
		.framer_extended = ether_frameout_extended,
		.ioctl = net_ioctl,
		.broadcast_addr = etherbroadcastaddr,
		.broadcast_len = ETHER_ADDR_LEN,
	};
	const uint8_t *address = link->address;
	ifnet_t ifp = NULL;
	thread_t thread;
	errno_t error;

	if (n == NULL) {
		printf("net: there is no unit %u for %s\n", unit, link->name);
		return false;
	}
	if (n->link != NULL) {
		printf("net: en%u is on %s already; %s is not attached\n", unit, n->link->name, link->name);
		return false;
	}
	snprintf(uniqueid, sizeof(uniqueid), "hakios-en%u", unit);
	n->unit = unit;
	n->link = link;
	n->up = link->up;
	lck_mtx_init(&n->tx_lock, &net_lck_grp, LCK_ATTR_NULL);
	error = ifnet_allocate_extended(&init, &ifp);
	if (error != 0) {
		printf("net: the interface en%u cannot be made: error %d\n", unit, error);
		n->link = NULL;
		return false;
	}
	ifnet_set_capabilities_enabled(ifp, 0, -1);
	ifnet_set_addrlen(ifp, ETHER_ADDR_LEN);
	ifnet_set_baudrate(ifp, 100 * 1000 * 1000);
	ifnet_set_mtu(ifp, ETHERMTU);
	ifnet_set_flags(ifp, IFF_BROADCAST | IFF_MULTICAST | IFF_SIMPLEX, 0xffff);
	ifnet_set_hdrlen(ifp, ETHER_HDR_LEN);
	ifnet_set_offload(ifp, 0);
	error = ifnet_attach(ifp, NULL);
	if (error != 0) {
		printf("net: the interface en%u cannot be attached: error %d\n", unit, error);
		ifnet_release(ifp);
		n->link = NULL;
		return false;
	}
	ifnet_set_lladdr(ifp, address, ETHER_ADDR_LEN);
	bpfattach(ifp, DLT_EN10MB, ETHER_HDR_LEN);
	n->ifp = ifp;
	if (n->up) {
		net_link_event(ifp, KEV_DL_LINK_ON);
	}
	if (link->wireless) {
		/* (a radio's address is the phone's own: not for the log; and Darwin's Wi-Fi side finds the interface by a service) */
		printf("net: en%u attached on %s (a radio), link %s\n", unit, link->name, n->up ? "up" : "down");
		HakiosWLANStart(uniqueid + 7, address);
	} else {
		printf("net: en%u attached on %s, address %02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x, link %s\n", unit, link->name, address[0],
		    address[1], address[2], address[3], address[4], address[5], n->up ? "up" : "down");
	}
	if (kernel_thread_start(net_thread, n, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
	return true;
}

void
hakios_net_init(void)
{
	PE_parse_boot_argn("net_trace", &net_trace, sizeof(net_trace));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("net_names", &net_names, sizeof(net_names));
	hakios_virtio_net_init();
}
```

`drivers/net/hakios.virtio_net.c`:

```c
/*
 * QEMU's virtio network device as the link behind en0 (see sys/hakios.net.h for what a link is).
 *
 * "-device virtio-net-device" on the virt machine's virtio-mmio bus, which must be the current
 * one, not "legacy" (-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false), with any "-netdev" behind it;
 * qemu/run-darwin.sh does that with QEMU_NET=1. Only with boot-arg virtio_net=1: the bus address is
 * QEMU's and means nothing on the phone.
 *
 * Nothing of what the device offers is taken (no checksums or segmentation left to it, no
 * merged receive buffers): a 12-byte header nobody reads, then the frame, one buffer each.
 * No interrupt is used; the interface's thread asks (virtio_poll()).
 */
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <net/ethernet.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/kpi_mbuf.h>
#include <sys/hakios.net.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern uint64_t kvtophys(vm_offset_t va);       /* pmap_paddr_t */

#define VIRTIO_BUS              0x0a000000UL    /* QEMU virt: 32 transports of 0x200 bytes */
#define VIRTIO_SLOTS            32
#define VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE        0x200

#define VIRTIO_MAGIC            0x000           /* "virt" */
#define VIRTIO_VERSION          0x004
#define VIRTIO_DEVICE_ID        0x008
#define VIRTIO_DEVICE_FEATURES  0x010
#define VIRTIO_DEVICE_FEATURES_SEL 0x014
#define VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES  0x020
#define VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL 0x024
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_SEL        0x030
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX    0x034
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM        0x038
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_READY      0x044
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY     0x050
#define VIRTIO_STATUS           0x070
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DESC       0x080
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DRIVER     0x090
#define VIRTIO_QUEUE_DEVICE     0x0a0
#define VIRTIO_CONFIG           0x100           /* the device's own: for a network device, its address first */

#define VIRTIO_ID_NET           1
#define VIRTIO_NET_F_MAC        (1u << 5)       /* the device has an address of its own */
#define STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE      1
#define STATUS_DRIVER           2
#define STATUS_DRIVER_OK        4
#define STATUS_FEATURES_OK      8

#define QUEUE_SIZE              64              /* descriptors, and buffers, per queue */
#define QUEUE_RECEIVE           0
#define QUEUE_TRANSMIT          1
#define BUFFER_SIZE             2048            /* a buffer never crosses a page: one address will do for it */
#define DESC_F_WRITE            2
#define AVAIL_F_NO_INTERRUPT    1

struct vq_desc {
	uint64_t addr;
	uint32_t len;
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t next;
};
struct vq_avail {
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t idx;
	uint16_t ring[QUEUE_SIZE];
};
struct vq_used {
	uint16_t flags;
	uint16_t idx;
	struct {
		uint32_t id;
		uint32_t len;
	} ring[QUEUE_SIZE];
};
/* before every frame, either way; nothing of it is used (no checksum or segmentation is left to the device) */
struct virtio_net_header {
	uint8_t flags, gso_type;
	uint16_t header_length, gso_size, checksum_start, checksum_offset, buffers;
};

/* the rings of a queue are in one page */
#define OFFSET_DESC             0x0000
#define OFFSET_AVAIL            0x0400
#define OFFSET_USED             0x0800

struct queue {
	struct vq_desc *        desc;
	struct vq_avail *       avail;
	struct vq_used *        used;
	uint8_t *               buffers;        /* QUEUE_SIZE of BUFFER_SIZE */
	uint16_t                seen;           /* how far the used ring has been read */
	uint16_t                free[QUEUE_SIZE];       /* transmit: the buffers the device does not have */
	unsigned                free_count;
};

static vm_offset_t virtio;                      /* the device's registers */
static struct queue receive_queue, transmit_queue;

static inline uint32_t
reg_read(uint32_t reg)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)(virtio + reg);
}

static inline void
reg_write(uint32_t reg, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)(virtio + reg) = value;
}

static inline void
reg_write64(uint32_t reg, uint64_t value)
{
	reg_write(reg, (uint32_t)value);
	reg_write(reg + 4, (uint32_t)(value >> 32));
}

static bool
queue_make(struct queue *q, uint32_t index, bool device_writes)
{
	vm_offset_t rings = 0, buffers = 0;

	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_SEL, index);
	if (reg_read(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX) < QUEUE_SIZE) {
		printf("net: virtio queue %u holds only %u\n", index, reg_read(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM_MAX));
		return false;
	}
	if (kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &rings, PAGE_SIZE, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_ZERO | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_IOKIT) != KERN_SUCCESS ||
	    kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &buffers, round_page(QUEUE_SIZE * BUFFER_SIZE), KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_ZERO | KMA_DATA,
	    VM_KERN_MEMORY_IOKIT) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		return false;
	}
	q->desc = (struct vq_desc *)(rings + OFFSET_DESC);
	q->avail = (struct vq_avail *)(rings + OFFSET_AVAIL);
	q->used = (struct vq_used *)(rings + OFFSET_USED);
	q->buffers = (uint8_t *)buffers;
	for (int i = 0; i < QUEUE_SIZE; i++) {
		q->desc[i].addr = kvtophys(buffers + (vm_offset_t)i * BUFFER_SIZE);
		q->desc[i].len = BUFFER_SIZE;
		q->desc[i].flags = device_writes ? DESC_F_WRITE : 0;
		if (device_writes) {
			q->avail->ring[i] = (uint16_t)i;         /* the device gets them all, to fill */
		} else {
			q->free[q->free_count++] = (uint16_t)i;
		}
	}
	q->avail->flags = AVAIL_F_NO_INTERRUPT;
	q->avail->idx = device_writes ? QUEUE_SIZE : 0;
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NUM, QUEUE_SIZE);
	reg_write64(VIRTIO_QUEUE_DESC, kvtophys(rings) + OFFSET_DESC);
	reg_write64(VIRTIO_QUEUE_DRIVER, kvtophys(rings) + OFFSET_AVAIL);
	reg_write64(VIRTIO_QUEUE_DEVICE, kvtophys(rings) + OFFSET_USED);
	__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);         /* ISH */
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_READY, 1);
	return true;
}

/* A frame to send. */
static bool
virtio_transmit(mbuf_t packet, size_t length)
{
	struct queue *q = &transmit_queue;
	uint8_t *buffer;
	uint16_t id;

	/* the buffers the device has done with */
	while (q->seen != *(volatile uint16_t *)&q->used->idx) {
		q->free[q->free_count++] = (uint16_t)(q->used->ring[q->seen++ % QUEUE_SIZE].id % QUEUE_SIZE);
	}
	if (q->free_count == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	id = q->free[--q->free_count];
	buffer = q->buffers + (size_t)id * BUFFER_SIZE;
	bzero(buffer, sizeof(struct virtio_net_header));
	if (mbuf_copydata(packet, 0, length, buffer + sizeof(struct virtio_net_header)) != 0) {
		q->free[q->free_count++] = id;
		return false;
	}
	q->desc[id].len = (uint32_t)(sizeof(struct virtio_net_header) + length);
	q->avail->ring[q->avail->idx % QUEUE_SIZE] = id;
	__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
	q->avail->idx++;
	__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY, QUEUE_TRANSMIT);
	return true;
}

/* Hand up what has arrived; returns how many frames that was. */
static unsigned
virtio_poll(void)
{
	struct queue *q = &receive_queue;
	unsigned frames = 0;

	while (q->seen != *(volatile uint16_t *)&q->used->idx) {
		uint32_t id = q->used->ring[q->seen % QUEUE_SIZE].id % QUEUE_SIZE;
		uint32_t length = q->used->ring[q->seen % QUEUE_SIZE].len;

		q->seen++;
		if (length > sizeof(struct virtio_net_header) && length <= BUFFER_SIZE) {
			hakios_net_input(q->buffers + (size_t)id * BUFFER_SIZE + sizeof(struct virtio_net_header),
			    length - sizeof(struct virtio_net_header));
		}
		/* give the buffer back */
		q->avail->ring[q->avail->idx % QUEUE_SIZE] = (uint16_t)id;
		__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
		q->avail->idx++;
		frames++;
	}
	if (frames) {
		__builtin_arm_dmb(0xb);
		reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY, QUEUE_RECEIVE);
	}
	return frames;
}

static bool
virtio_net_start(uint8_t address[ETHER_ADDR_LEN])
{
	vm_offset_t bus = ml_io_map(VIRTIO_BUS, VIRTIO_SLOTS * VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE);
	uint32_t features;
	int slot;

	for (slot = 0; slot < VIRTIO_SLOTS; slot++) {
		virtio = bus + (vm_offset_t)slot * VIRTIO_SLOT_SIZE;
		if (reg_read(VIRTIO_MAGIC) == 0x74726976 && reg_read(VIRTIO_DEVICE_ID) == VIRTIO_ID_NET) {
			break;
		}
	}
	if (slot == VIRTIO_SLOTS) {
		printf("net: no virtio network device (start QEMU with -device virtio-net-device)\n");
		return false;
	}
	if (reg_read(VIRTIO_VERSION) != 2) {
		printf("net: slot %d is a legacy transport; start QEMU with -global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false\n", slot);
		return false;
	}
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, 0);            /* reset */
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DEVICE_FEATURES_SEL, 0);
	features = reg_read(VIRTIO_DEVICE_FEATURES);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL, 0);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, features & VIRTIO_NET_F_MAC);         /* and nothing else of what it offers */
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES_SEL, 1);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_DRIVER_FEATURES, 1);   /* bit 32: VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1 */
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER | STATUS_FEATURES_OK);
	if (!(reg_read(VIRTIO_STATUS) & STATUS_FEATURES_OK)) {
		printf("net: slot %d: features refused (the device offers %#x)\n", slot, features);
		return false;
	}
	if (!queue_make(&receive_queue, QUEUE_RECEIVE, true) || !queue_make(&transmit_queue, QUEUE_TRANSMIT, false)) {
		return false;
	}
	if (features & VIRTIO_NET_F_MAC) {
		for (int i = 0; i < ETHER_ADDR_LEN; i++) {
			address[i] = *(volatile uint8_t *)(virtio + VIRTIO_CONFIG + i);
		}
	}
	reg_write(VIRTIO_STATUS, STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGE | STATUS_DRIVER | STATUS_FEATURES_OK | STATUS_DRIVER_OK);
	reg_write(VIRTIO_QUEUE_NOTIFY, QUEUE_RECEIVE);
	printf("net: virtio network device in slot %d (it offers features %#x)\n", slot, features);
	return true;
}

static struct hakios_net_link virtio_link = {
	.name = "QEMU's virtio network device",
	.address = { 0x02, 'r', 'e', 'd', 'w', 'd' },   /* if the device has none: one "locally administered" */
	.up = true,
	.transmit = virtio_transmit,
	.poll = virtio_poll,
};

void
hakios_virtio_net_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("virtio_net", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	if (!virtio_net_start(virtio_link.address) || !hakios_net_attach(&virtio_link)) {
		printf("net: no network interface\n");
	}
}
```

```
# drivers/power/conf: the battery, the processor's clock, temperatures, the PMICs, the guards of a run left alone.
# CONFIG_HAKIOS_<NAME>=y in a defconfig builds a driver into the kernel; "standard" files are always built.
# tools/hakios-config.py reads this file; docs/drivers-config.md says what each word means and how it reaches XNU.

	file    iokit/Kernel/hakios.battery.cpp iokitcpp

	help    (the state comes from the audio DSP's battery manager, with adsp=1)

	help    loader when the phone gets too hot (thermal_stop=)

	help    the run handed back to the loader before the battery is flat (battery_stop=<percent>)
```

`drivers/power/hakios.battery.c`:

```c
/*
 * Battery monitor for Xiaomi redwood (POCO X5 Pro).
 *
 * The phone selects PM7325B and qcom,battery-charger over PMIC GLINK/ADSP, not
 * the local PM7250B/QG layout.  The resident UEFI contains the matching
 * Qualcomm charger drivers.  xnuloader owns that firmware context on core 0,
 * polls it, and publishes a read-only cache; XNU only consumes that cache.
 * Charger limits and JEITA protection therefore remain firmware-owned.
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);

#define LOADER_BATTERY_MAGIC            0x2154544142574452ULL
#define LOADER_BATTERY_VERSION          1
#define LOADER_BATTERY_VALID            (1u << 0)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_PRESENT          (1u << 1)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGER_PRESENT  (1u << 2)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_VOLTAGE_VALID    (1u << 3)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGING         (1u << 4)
#define LOADER_BATTERY_SOC_ESTIMATED    (1u << 5)
#define LOADER_PAGE_SIZE                0x4000UL

struct loader_battery {
	uint64_t magic;
	uint32_t version, size;
	volatile uint32_t sequence;
	uint32_t flags;
	int32_t soc_percent, voltage_mv, current_ma, temperature_c;
	uint32_t charger_action, polls, failures, reserved;
};

static volatile struct loader_battery *shared_battery;
static int battery_soc_percent = -1, battery_voltage_mv = -1, battery_current_ma;
static int battery_temperature_c = -273, battery_present, battery_charger_present;
static int battery_charging, battery_soc_estimated, battery_charger_action = -1;
static uint64_t battery_updates, battery_failures;

/* for others in the kernel (the flashlight's thermal guard): -273 while it is not known */
int
hakios_battery_temperature(void)
{
	return battery_temperature_c;
}

SYSCTL_DECL(_kern_hakios);              /* the node is drivers/core/hakios.platform.c's: every driver hangs its sysctls there */
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_soc, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_soc_percent, 0, "battery state of charge, 0..100 percent, or -1 if unknown");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_voltage_mv, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_voltage_mv, 0, "battery voltage in millivolts, or -1 if unknown");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_current_ma, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_current_ma, 0, "battery current reported by Qualcomm firmware, in milliamps");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_temperature_c, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_temperature_c, 0, "battery temperature reported by Qualcomm firmware, in Celsius");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_present, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_present, 0, "1 if Qualcomm firmware reports a battery");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_charger_present, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_charger_present, 0, "1 if Qualcomm firmware reports an attached charger");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_charging, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_charging, 0, "1 while an attached charger is charging a non-full battery");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_soc_estimated, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_soc_estimated, 0, "1 only when SOC had to be estimated from voltage");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_charger_action, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_charger_action, 0, "last Qualcomm charger action, for diagnostics");

static bool
battery_snapshot(struct loader_battery *out)
{
	uint32_t before, after;

	for (unsigned retry = 0; retry < 4; retry++) {
		before = shared_battery->sequence;
		if (before & 1) continue;
		__asm__ volatile ("dmb ishld" ::: "memory");
		memcpy(out, (const void *)(uintptr_t)shared_battery, sizeof(*out));
		__asm__ volatile ("dmb ishld" ::: "memory");
		after = shared_battery->sequence;
		if (before == after && !(after & 1)) return true;
	}
	return false;
}

static void
battery_poll(void)
{
	struct loader_battery sample;

	if (!battery_snapshot(&sample) || sample.magic != LOADER_BATTERY_MAGIC ||
	    sample.version != LOADER_BATTERY_VERSION || sample.size < sizeof(sample) ||
	    !(sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_VALID) || sample.soc_percent < 0 || sample.soc_percent > 100) {
		battery_failures++;
		return;
	}
	battery_soc_percent = sample.soc_percent;
	battery_voltage_mv = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_VOLTAGE_VALID) ? sample.voltage_mv : -1;
	battery_current_ma = sample.current_ma;
	battery_temperature_c = sample.temperature_c;
	battery_present = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_PRESENT) != 0;
	battery_charger_present = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGER_PRESENT) != 0;
	battery_charging = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_CHARGING) != 0;
	battery_soc_estimated = (sample.flags & LOADER_BATTERY_SOC_ESTIMATED) != 0;
	battery_charger_action = (int)sample.charger_action;
	battery_updates++;
}

/*
 * What the audio DSP's battery manager says (drivers/audio/hakios.adsp.c, with adsp=1 unless battmgr=0):
 * the values that Android shows, from where Android takes them. They are kept here for the sysctls
 * and passed on to the power source that Darwin reads (drivers/power/hakios.battery.cpp).
 */
static int battery_full_uah, battery_design_uah, battery_cycles, battery_source_dsp;

SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_full_uah, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_full_uah, 0, "the battery's full charge as the fuel gauge has learnt it, in uAh (0 if unknown)");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_design_uah, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_design_uah, 0, "the battery's charge as designed, in uAh (0 if unknown)");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_cycles, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_cycles, 0, "the battery's charge cycles (0 if unknown)");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, battery_from_dsp, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED,
    &battery_source_dsp, 0, "1 when the values come from the audio DSP's battery manager");

extern void HakiosBatteryReport(const void *state, unsigned size);     /* drivers/power/hakios.battery.cpp */

void
hakios_battery_report(const struct hakios_battery_state *b)
{
	/* (rounded in 64 bits: the DSP's value near INT32_MAX plus 50 would overflow an int, and a full battery would read 0%) */
	int percent = (int)(((int64_t)b->percent_hundredths + 50) / 100);

	battery_soc_percent = percent < 0 ? 0 : percent > 100 ? 100 : percent;
	battery_voltage_mv = b->voltage_uv / 1000;
	battery_current_ma = b->current_ua / 1000;
	/* (in 64 bits for the same reason: an overflow here would make a hot battery read as cold) */
	battery_temperature_c = (int)(((int64_t)b->temperature_hundredths + 50) / 100);
	battery_present = b->present != 0;
	battery_charger_present = b->external != 0;
	battery_charging = b->status == 1;      /* POWER_SUPPLY_STATUS_CHARGING */
	battery_soc_estimated = 0;
	battery_charger_action = b->status;
	if (b->full_uah > 0) {
		battery_full_uah = b->full_uah;
	}
	if (b->design_uah > 0) {
		battery_design_uah = b->design_uah;
	}
	if (b->cycles > 0) {
		battery_cycles = b->cycles;
	}
	battery_source_dsp = 1;
	battery_updates++;
	HakiosBatteryReport(b, sizeof(*b));
}

static void
battery_thread(__unused void *parameter, __unused wait_result_t result)
{
	for (unsigned tick = 0;; tick++) {
		battery_poll();
		if (tick % 12 == 0) {
			printf("battery: SOC=%d%%%s, V=%d mV, I=%d mA, T=%d C, battery=%d charger=%d charging=%d "
			    "action=%d (%llu reads, %llu failed)\n", battery_soc_percent,
			    battery_soc_estimated ? " (voltage estimate)" : "", battery_voltage_mv,
			    battery_current_ma, battery_temperature_c, battery_present, battery_charger_present,
			    battery_charging, battery_charger_action, battery_updates, battery_failures);
		}
		delay_for_interval(5000, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
}

void
hakios_battery_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0;
	uint64_t shared_pa = 0;
	vm_offset_t page;
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("battery", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) return;
	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("battery_shared_pa", &shared_pa, sizeof(shared_pa)) || shared_pa == 0) {
		printf("battery: xnuloader did not provide battery_shared_pa\n");
		return;
	}
	/* The cache must lie inside the one page that is mapped: an address near its end would be read past the mapping. */
	if ((shared_pa & (LOADER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)) + sizeof(struct loader_battery) > LOADER_PAGE_SIZE) {
		printf("battery: battery_shared_pa %#llx: the cache would cross the end of its page\n", shared_pa);
		return;
	}
	page = ml_io_map((vm_offset_t)(shared_pa & ~(LOADER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)), LOADER_PAGE_SIZE);
	shared_battery = (volatile struct loader_battery *)(page + (shared_pa & (LOADER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)));
	if (shared_battery->magic != LOADER_BATTERY_MAGIC || shared_battery->version != LOADER_BATTERY_VERSION ||
	    shared_battery->size < sizeof(struct loader_battery)) {
		printf("battery: bad xnuloader cache at %#llx (magic %#llx version %u size %u)\n", shared_pa,
		    shared_battery->magic, shared_battery->version, shared_battery->size);
		return;
	}
	printf("battery: Qualcomm UEFI cache at pa %#llx; polling every 5 seconds\n", shared_pa);
	if (kernel_thread_start(battery_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) thread_deallocate(thread);
}
```

`drivers/power/hakios.battery.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * HakiosBattery: the phone's battery as Darwin looks for it, an IOPMPowerSource.
 *
 * powerd finds every service of the class IOPMPowerSource (it calls the first "InternalBattery-0"),
 * listens for its kIOPMMessageBatteryStatusHasChanged and then reads its properties: whether a
 * battery is installed, CurrentCapacity and MaxCapacity (without both it gives up on the battery),
 * whether a charger is connected and charging, voltage, current, cycles, the charger's details.
 * From them it makes the power sources list (IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo) and posts its notifications,
 * and everything else follows from that: the status bar's battery, the lock screen's "Charging",
 * the Batteries widget, Settings > Battery.
 *
 * What the values are comes from the audio DSP's battery manager (drivers/audio/hakios.adsp.c,
 * with adsp=1, unless battmgr=0), by way of drivers/power/hakios.battery.c, which calls
 * HakiosBatteryReport() with every reading; the first one makes the service. Nothing here asks
 * the charger anything or tells it anything.
 *
 * As on Apple's newer batteries, CurrentCapacity is the percentage that the fuel gauge shows (and
 * MaxCapacity 100); the charges in mAh are AppleRawCurrentCapacity, AppleRawMaxCapacity (what the
 * gauge has learnt a full charge to be), NominalChargeCapacity and DesignCapacity.
 */

#include <IOKit/IOLib.h>
#include <IOKit/IOPlatformExpert.h>
#include <IOKit/pwr_mgt/IOPM.h>
#include <IOKit/pwr_mgt/IOPMPowerSource.h>
#include <libkern/c++/OSBoolean.h>
#include <libkern/c++/OSDictionary.h>
#include <libkern/c++/OSNumber.h>
#include <libkern/c++/OSSymbol.h>

/* The same as struct hakios_battery_state in bsd/sys/hakios.input.h, which is not seen from here. */
struct hakios_battery_state {
	uint32_t size;
	int32_t percent_hundredths;
	int32_t voltage_uv;
	int32_t current_ua;             /* more than 0 while the battery takes charge */
	int32_t temperature_hundredths;
	int32_t present, external, status;
	int32_t charge_uah, full_uah, design_uah, cycles;
	int32_t usb_type;
	int32_t usb_voltage_uv, usb_current_ua;
};

extern "C" void HakiosBatteryReport(const void * state, unsigned size);

class HakiosBattery : public IOPMPowerSource
{
	OSDeclareDefaultStructors(HakiosBattery);

public:
	void report(const struct hakios_battery_state * b);

private:
	void number(const char * key, long long value);
	void flag(const char * key, bool value);
	void object(const char * key, OSObject * value);
};

OSDefineMetaClassAndStructors(HakiosBattery, IOPMPowerSource);

static HakiosBattery * battery;

void
HakiosBattery::number(const char * key, long long value)
{
	const OSSymbol * symbol = OSSymbol::withCString(key);
	OSNumber * n = OSNumber::withNumber((unsigned long long) value, 32);

	if (symbol != NULL && n != NULL) {
		setPSProperty(symbol, n);
	}
	OSSafeReleaseNULL(n);
	OSSafeReleaseNULL(symbol);
}

void
HakiosBattery::flag(const char * key, bool value)
{
	const OSSymbol * symbol = OSSymbol::withCString(key);

	if (symbol != NULL) {
		setPSProperty(symbol, value ? kOSBooleanTrue : kOSBooleanFalse);
	}
	OSSafeReleaseNULL(symbol);
}

void
HakiosBattery::object(const char * key, OSObject * value)
{
	const OSSymbol * symbol = OSSymbol::withCString(key);

	if (symbol != NULL && value != NULL) {
		setPSProperty(symbol, value);
	}
	OSSafeReleaseNULL(symbol);
}

/*
 * What Darwin calls the charger by (IOPSKeysPrivate.h's kIOPSFamilyCode*, iokit_family_err(sub_iokit_usb, n)),
 * from Linux's POWER_SUPPLY_USB_TYPE_*, as the DSP gives it.
 */
static unsigned
family_code(int usb_type)
{
	switch (usb_type) {
	case 1: return 0xe0004000;      /* SDP, a computer's port: kIOPSFamilyCodeUSBHost */
	case 2: return 0xe0004004;      /* DCP, a charger: kIOPSFamilyCodeUSBChargingPortDedicated */
	case 3: return 0xe0004005;      /* CDP, a computer's charging port: kIOPSFamilyCodeUSBChargingPortDownstream */
	case 5: return 0xe0004009;      /* USB-C: kIOPSFamilyCodeUSBCTypeC */
	case 6: case 7: case 8: return 0xe000400a;      /* USB Power Delivery: kIOPSFamilyCodeUSBCPD */
	default: return 0xe0004007;     /* kIOPSFamilyCodeUSBUnknown */
	}
}

void
HakiosBattery::report(const struct hakios_battery_state * b)
{
	/* (rounded in 64 bits: the DSP's value near INT32_MAX plus 50 would overflow an int) */
	int percent = (int) (((int64_t) b->percent_hundredths + 50) / 100);
	bool charging = b->external && b->status == 1;          /* POWER_SUPPLY_STATUS_CHARGING */

	percent = percent < 0 ? 0 : percent > 100 ? 100 : percent;
	setBatteryInstalled(b->present != 0);
	setExternalConnected(b->external != 0);
	setExternalChargeCapable(b->external != 0);
	setIsCharging(charging);
	flag("FullyCharged", b->external && (b->status == 4 || percent == 100));    /* POWER_SUPPLY_STATUS_FULL */
	flag("AppleRawExternalConnected", b->external != 0);
	setCurrentCapacity((unsigned) percent);
	setMaxCapacity(100);
	/* (a negative voltage from the DSP would become about 4 million mV as an unsigned number: 0 instead) */
	setVoltage(b->voltage_uv > 0 ? (unsigned) (b->voltage_uv / 1000) : 0);
	setAmperage(b->current_ua / 1000);
	number("InstantAmperage", b->current_ua / 1000);
	number("Temperature", b->temperature_hundredths);
	if (b->charge_uah > 0) {
		number("AppleRawCurrentCapacity", b->charge_uah / 1000);
	}
	if (b->full_uah > 0) {
		number("AppleRawMaxCapacity", b->full_uah / 1000);
		number("NominalChargeCapacity", b->full_uah / 1000);
	}
	if (b->design_uah > 0) {
		number("DesignCapacity", b->design_uah / 1000);
	}
	if (b->cycles > 0) {
		setCycleCount((unsigned) b->cycles);
	}

	if (b->external) {
		OSDictionary * adapter = OSDictionary::withCapacity(6);
		long long mv = b->usb_voltage_uv / 1000, ma = b->usb_current_ua / 1000;
		OSNumber * n;

		if (adapter != NULL) {
			if ((n = OSNumber::withNumber((unsigned long long) ((mv * ma + 500000) / 1000000), 32)) != NULL) {
				adapter->setObject(kIOPMPSAdapterDetailsWattsKey, n);
				n->release();
			}
			if ((n = OSNumber::withNumber((unsigned long long) ma, 32)) != NULL) {
				adapter->setObject(kIOPMPSAdapterDetailsAmperageKey, n);
				n->release();
			}
			if ((n = OSNumber::withNumber((unsigned long long) mv, 32)) != NULL) {
				adapter->setObject(kIOPMPSAdapterDetailsVoltage, n);
				n->release();
			}
			if ((n = OSNumber::withNumber((unsigned long long) family_code(b->usb_type), 32)) != NULL) {
				adapter->setObject(kIOPMPSAdapterDetailsFamilyKey, n);
				n->release();
			}
			adapter->setObject("IsWireless", kOSBooleanFalse);
			object(kIOPMPSAdapterDetailsKey, adapter);
			adapter->release();
		}
	} else {
		OSDictionary * none = OSDictionary::withCapacity(1);
		OSNumber * n = OSNumber::withNumber(0ULL, 32);    /* kIOPSFamilyCodeDisconnected */

		if (none != NULL && n != NULL) {
			none->setObject(kIOPMPSAdapterDetailsFamilyKey, n);
			object(kIOPMPSAdapterDetailsKey, none);
		}
		OSSafeReleaseNULL(n);
		OSSafeReleaseNULL(none);
	}
	updateStatus();
}

/* With every reading of the battery (drivers/power/hakios.battery.c); the first one makes the service. One caller at a time. */
void
HakiosBatteryReport(const void * state, unsigned size)
{
	const struct hakios_battery_state * b = (const struct hakios_battery_state *) state;
	IOService * platform;

	if (size != sizeof(struct hakios_battery_state) || b->size != sizeof(struct hakios_battery_state)) {
		static bool said;

		if (!said) {
			said = true;
			IOLog("HakiosBattery: the battery's state is %u bytes, not %lu: bsd/sys/hakios.input.h and this file disagree\n",
			    size, sizeof(struct hakios_battery_state));
		}
		return;
	}
	if (battery == NULL) {
		HakiosBattery * made = OSTypeAlloc(HakiosBattery);

		if ((platform = IOService::getPlatform()) == NULL || made == NULL || !made->init()) {
			OSSafeReleaseNULL(made);
			return;
		}
		made->report(b);        /* (the properties are there before anybody finds the service) */
		if (!made->attach(platform)) {
			made->release();
			return;
		}
		made->setName("HakiosBattery");
		if (!made->start(platform)) {
			made->detach(platform);
			made->release();
			return;
		}
		made->registerService();
		battery = made;
		/* (64-bit rounding, as in report(): no signed overflow on a large value from the DSP) */
		IOLog("HakiosBattery: the battery's power source is up: %d%%, %s\n", (int) (((int64_t) b->percent_hundredths + 50) / 100),
		    b->external ? (b->status == 1 ? "charging" : "on a charger, not charging") : "not on a charger");
		return;
	}
	battery->report(b);
}
```
