`drivers/power/hakios.battguard.c`:

```c
/*
 * A run nobody watches must not empty the battery: with boot-arg battery_stop=<percent>, hand control back to the boot loader
 * when the charge is at or below that for three looks in a row, the way drivers/power/hakios.thermal.c does for heat.
 *
 * Why. The phone is not charged while HakiOS runs (the kernel has no charging path yet: docs/install-safe.md), and a session
 * left going overnight ends with a flat battery, which is a phone that has gone off USB until somebody plugs it in. This is the
 * protection that costs nothing: at 15 percent the run ends, the loader has the log, and (xl with XL_REBOOT_AFTER=1) the phone
 * goes back to Android, which charges it.
 *
 * What it believes. It asks the battery driver's own numbers (sysctl kern.hakios.battery_soc, ..._present, ..._charger_present;
 * they come from the loader's charger page or, with adsp=1, from the audio DSP's battery service) and acts only on a reading that is
 * between 0 and 100 with a battery present and NO charger attached. An unknown charge (-1), no battery, or a charger on the cable
 * is never a reason to stop. It does not read any hardware itself.
 *
 * Status (what has and has not been seen): COMPILED ONLY. It was written while the phone was off USB, so it has not run on one;
 * whether the numbers it reads are filled in when a kernel runs without adsp=1 is not known (the battery driver's header says
 * where they come from; the first run that sets battery_stop will print its "battguard:" line and say). Not run in QEMU.
 *
 * Boot-args:
 *   battery_stop=<percent>   stop at this charge or below (0: never, the default; 1 to 99)
 *   battery_stop_poll=<s>    how often to look (5 to 600; 20)
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern void loader_log_putc(char c);
extern void loader_return(void);
extern void hakios_var_save_on_return(void);
extern void hakios_adreno_stop(void);
extern void hakios_wifi_stop(void);
extern void hakios_adsp_stop(void);
extern int kernel_sysctlbyname(const char *name, void *oldp, size_t *oldlenp, void *newp, size_t newlen);

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[300];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	return printf("%s", line);
}

static thread_call_t call;
static uint32_t stop_percent, poll_seconds = 20, looks, strikes, last_said_minute = ~0u;
static bool stopping;

static bool
read_int(const char *name, int *value)
{
	size_t size = sizeof(*value);

	return kernel_sysctlbyname(name, value, &size, NULL, 0) == 0 && size == sizeof(*value);
}

static void
tick(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	int soc = -1, present = 0, charger = 0;
	uint64_t deadline;
	bool known = read_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc", &soc) && read_int("kern.hakios.battery_present", &present) &&
	    read_int("kern.hakios.battery_charger_present", &charger) && soc >= 0 && soc <= 100 && present && !charger;
	uint32_t minute = (uint32_t)(++looks * poll_seconds / 300);       /* a line every five minutes, and the first */

	if (minute != last_said_minute || looks == 1) {
		last_said_minute = minute;
		say("battguard: charge %d%% (battery %s, charger %s); stop at or below %u%%%s\n", soc, present ? "present" : "not reported",
		    charger ? "attached: the guard waits" : "not attached", stop_percent, known ? "" : " -- not a reading it acts on");
	}
	strikes = (known && (uint32_t)soc <= stop_percent) ? strikes + 1 : 0;
	if (strikes >= 3 && !stopping) {
		stopping = true;
		say("\n--- battguard: the charge is %d%%, at or below battery_stop=%u three looks in a row: back to the loader ---\n", soc,
		    stop_percent);
		hakios_var_save_on_return();
		hakios_adreno_stop();
		hakios_wifi_stop();
		hakios_adsp_stop();
		loader_return();
	}
	clock_interval_to_deadline(poll_seconds, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(call, deadline);
}

__startup_func
static void
battguard_init(void)
{
	uint32_t value;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("battery_stop", &stop_percent, sizeof(stop_percent)) || stop_percent == 0 || stop_percent > 99) {
		return;
	}
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("battery_stop_poll", &value, sizeof(value)) && value >= 5 && value <= 600) {
		poll_seconds = value;
	}
	say("battguard: on, looking every %u s; the run ends at %u%% or less (and only with a battery, a known charge and no charger)\n",
	    poll_seconds, stop_percent);
	uint64_t deadline;

	call = thread_call_allocate(tick, NULL);

	clock_interval_to_deadline(poll_seconds, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(call, deadline);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, battguard_init);

```

`drivers/power/hakios.cpufreq.c`:

```c
/*
 * The clock speed of the processor cores the kernel runs on, on the POCO X5 Pro (redwood).
 * Only with boot-arg cpufreq=1: the addresses are this phone's.
 *
 * The boot loader leaves each group of cores at a modest frequency and expects the operating
 * system to ask for more. On this SoC that is one register write: the hardware ("EPSS") has
 * a table of frequencies per group and switches the clock source and the supply voltage by
 * itself when told which row is wanted. There is no reason for us ever to want less than the
 * top row, for every group that has a core of ours in it (one core, unless boot-arg cpus=N
 * says more).
 *
 * Register layout: Linux drivers/cpufreq/qcom-cpufreq-hw.c ("epss" variant).
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <os/atomic_private.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/hakios.input.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map_wcomb(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);
extern void hakios_tl(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);
extern bool ml_cpu_idle_time(int cpu_id, uint64_t *idle);

/*
 * The loader's log as well: this runs early, and the kernel's own log of a run keeps only its end. With
 * interrupts off -- on the way back to the loader (hakios_ddr_quiesce()) -- the loader's log only: the
 * kernel's console may not be written there, and printf was a panic ("Console I/O from interrupt-disabled
 * context") at the end of every run once the memory vote was taken away on the way back.
 */
static void
tell(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static void
tell(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[256];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	if (ml_get_interrupts_enabled()) {
		printf("%s", line);
	}
}

#define EPSS_PHYS               0x18591000UL    /* three groups ("domains") of 0x1000: small cores, big, biggest */
#define EPSS_DOMAIN_SIZE        0x1000UL
#define EPSS_DOMAINS            3
#define EPSS_FREQ_TABLE         0x100           /* a word per row: [31:30] clock source, [7:0] multiple of 19.2 MHz */
#define EPSS_TABLE_ROWS         40
#define EPSS_PERF_STATE         0x320           /* the row that is wanted */
#define XO_KHZ                  19200
#define ALTERNATE_KHZ           300000          /* source 0: a fixed 300 MHz */

/* How fast a simple loop runs, in thousands of iterations per millisecond. */
static uint32_t
loop_speed(void)
{
	volatile uint64_t sink = 0;
	uint64_t start = mach_absolute_time(), nanos;

	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 2000000; i++) {
		sink += i;
	}
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - start, &nanos);
	return nanos ? (uint32_t)(2000000ULL * 1000 / nanos) : 0;
}

/* The group of the core with that number in its MPIDR (the device tree's "reg": the number is the second field). */
static uint32_t
domain_of(uint32_t phys_id)
{
	uint32_t core = (phys_id >> 8) & 0xff;

	return core < 4 ? 0 : core < 7 ? 1 : 2;
}

static void
raise_domain(uint32_t domain, uint32_t cores)
{
	uint32_t top = 0, top_khz = 0, was;
	vm_offset_t base;

	base = ml_io_map(EPSS_PHYS + domain * EPSS_DOMAIN_SIZE, EPSS_DOMAIN_SIZE);
	for (uint32_t row = 0; row < EPSS_TABLE_ROWS; row++) {
		uint32_t entry = *(volatile uint32_t *)(base + EPSS_FREQ_TABLE + 4 * row);
		uint32_t khz = (entry >> 30) ? XO_KHZ * (entry & 0xff) : ALTERNATE_KHZ;

		if (row > 0 && khz <= top_khz) {
			break;                  /* the table ends by repeating its last row */
		}
		top = row;
		top_khz = khz;
	}
	was = *(volatile uint32_t *)(base + EPSS_PERF_STATE);
	*(volatile uint32_t *)(base + EPSS_PERF_STATE) = top;
	delay_for_interval(20, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	tell("cpufreq: group %u (%u of our cores): row %u -> %u of the frequency table, %u MHz\n", domain, cores, was, top,
	    top_khz / 1000);
}

/*
 * Boot-arg membench=1: how fast this processor reads, writes and copies memory, in MB a second
 * (32 MB at a time, far more than any cache): what the memory's clock allows a processor, which
 * nobody here asks to be raised.
 */
static void
memory_bench(void)
{
	const vm_size_t size = 32u << 20;
	vm_offset_t a = 0, b = 0;
	uint64_t began, ns[3] = { 0, 0, 0 };
	volatile uint64_t sum = 0;

	if (kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &a, size, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_DIAG) != KERN_SUCCESS ||
	    kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &b, size, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_DIAG) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		printf("membench: no memory\n");
		return;
	}
	memset((void *)a, 1, size);
	memset((void *)b, 2, size);
	for (int round = 0; round < 4; round++) {
		uint64_t t;

		began = mach_absolute_time();
		memset((void *)a, round, size);
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &t);
		ns[0] += t;
		began = mach_absolute_time();
		for (const uint64_t *p = (const uint64_t *)b, *end = (const uint64_t *)(b + size); p < end; p += 8) {
			sum += p[0] + p[1] + p[2] + p[3] + p[4] + p[5] + p[6] + p[7];
		}
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &t);
		ns[1] += t;
		began = mach_absolute_time();
		memcpy((void *)b, (const void *)a, size);
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &t);
		ns[2] += t;
	}
	tell("membench: on core %llu: writing %llu MB/s, reading %llu MB/s, copying %llu MB/s\n",
	    (__builtin_arm_rsr64("MPIDR_EL1") >> 8) & 0xff, 4ull * (size >> 20) * 1000000000ull / ns[0],
	    4ull * (size >> 20) * 1000000000ull / ns[1], 4ull * (size >> 20) * 1000000000ull / ns[2]);
	kmem_free(kernel_map, a, size);
	kmem_free(kernel_map, b, size);
}

/*
 * Boot-arg membench=2: the same on every core of ours at once (a thread each, started together, 16 MB
 * at a time), 2 s after this starts, so that all the cores are up: the sum of what they get is what
 * the memory gives at the clock it has been left at.
 */
#define BENCH_THREADS   8
static struct {
	volatile uint32_t ready, go, done;
	uint64_t ns[BENCH_THREADS][3];
	uint32_t core[BENCH_THREADS];
} bench;

static void
bench_thread(void *arg, wait_result_t wr __unused)
{
	const vm_size_t size = 16u << 20;
	uintptr_t index = (uintptr_t)arg;
	vm_offset_t a = 0, b = 0;
	volatile uint64_t sum = 0;

	if (kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &a, size, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_DIAG) != KERN_SUCCESS ||
	    kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &b, size, KMA_KOBJECT | KMA_DATA, VM_KERN_MEMORY_DIAG) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		os_atomic_inc(&bench.ready, relaxed);
		os_atomic_inc(&bench.done, relaxed);
		return;
	}
	memset((void *)a, 1, size);
	memset((void *)b, 2, size);
	os_atomic_inc(&bench.ready, relaxed);
	while (!os_atomic_load(&bench.go, acquire)) {
	}
	bench.core[index] = (uint32_t)(__builtin_arm_rsr64("MPIDR_EL1") >> 8) & 0xff;
	for (int round = 0; round < 4; round++) {
		uint64_t began, t;

		began = mach_absolute_time();
		memset((void *)a, round, size);
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &t);
		bench.ns[index][0] += t;
		began = mach_absolute_time();
		for (const uint64_t *p = (const uint64_t *)b, *end = (const uint64_t *)(b + size); p < end; p += 8) {
			sum += p[0] + p[1] + p[2] + p[3] + p[4] + p[5] + p[6] + p[7];
		}
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &t);
		bench.ns[index][1] += t;
		began = mach_absolute_time();
		memcpy((void *)b, (const void *)a, size);
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time() - began, &t);
		bench.ns[index][2] += t;
	}
	os_atomic_inc(&bench.done, release);
	kmem_free(kernel_map, a, size);
	kmem_free(kernel_map, b, size);
}

static void
bench_all(void *arg __unused, wait_result_t wr __unused)
{
	const uint32_t threads = MIN(ml_get_topology_info()->num_cpus, BENCH_THREADS);
	const uint64_t mb = 4 * 16;                     /* per thread and test */
	uint64_t total[3] = { 0, 0, 0 };

	delay_for_interval(2000, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	for (uintptr_t i = 0; i < threads; i++) {
		thread_t thread;

		if (kernel_thread_start(bench_thread, (void *)i, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
			thread_deallocate(thread);
		} else {
			os_atomic_inc(&bench.ready, relaxed);
			os_atomic_inc(&bench.done, relaxed);
		}
	}
	while (os_atomic_load(&bench.ready, relaxed) < threads) {
		delay_for_interval(1, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
	os_atomic_store(&bench.go, 1, release);
	while (os_atomic_load(&bench.done, acquire) < threads) {
		delay_for_interval(1, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < threads; i++) {
		tell("membench: all at once: core %u: writing %llu MB/s, reading %llu MB/s, copying %llu MB/s\n", bench.core[i],
		    bench.ns[i][0] ? mb * 1000000000ull / bench.ns[i][0] : 0, bench.ns[i][1] ? mb * 1000000000ull / bench.ns[i][1] : 0,
		    bench.ns[i][2] ? mb * 1000000000ull / bench.ns[i][2] : 0);
		for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
			total[k] += bench.ns[i][k] ? mb * 1000000000ull / bench.ns[i][k] : 0;
		}
	}
	tell("membench: all %u at once, together: writing %llu MB/s, reading %llu MB/s, copying %llu MB/s\n", threads, total[0],
	    total[1], total[2]);
}

/*
 * Boot-arg cpuload=MS: every MS milliseconds, how busy each of our cores was meanwhile, in
 * percent, to the loader's log (tools/frames.py shows it per gesture):
 *   tl: u at US 7:NN 6:NN ... 1:NN      the core's number (as in its MPIDR), then its share
 * of the time it was not idle (interrupts included).
 */
static uint32_t load_every_ms;

static void
load_thread(void *arg __unused, wait_result_t wr __unused)
{
	const ml_topology_info_t *topology = ml_get_topology_info();
	uint64_t idle_before[MAX_CPUS] = { 0 }, then = mach_absolute_time();

	for (;;) {
		char line[192];
		int at;
		uint64_t now, us;

		delay_for_interval(load_every_ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
		now = mach_absolute_time();
		absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now, &us);
		at = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "tl: u at %llu", us / 1000);
		for (unsigned int i = 0; i < topology->num_cpus && i < MAX_CPUS; i++) {
			uint64_t idle = 0, busy;

			if (!ml_cpu_idle_time((int)i, &idle)) {
				continue;
			}
			busy = (now - then) > (idle - idle_before[i]) ? (now - then) - (idle - idle_before[i]) : 0;
			idle_before[i] = idle;
			if (at < (int)sizeof(line) - 12) {
				at += snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - at, " %u:%llu", (topology->cpus[i].phys_id >> 8) & 0xff,
				    100 * busy / (now - then));
			}
		}
		then = now;
		hakios_tl("%s\n", line);
	}
}

static void
load_start(void)
{
	thread_t thread;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("cpuload", &load_every_ms, sizeof(load_every_ms)) || load_every_ms == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (kernel_thread_start(load_thread, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		thread_deallocate(thread);
	}
}

/*
 * Boot-arg ddr=1: the memory's bus clock managers ("BCM") in the command database the boot loader
 * left, with what is needed to vote for bandwidth on them -- only read. (membench=2 says the cores
 * together get no more from memory than one alone: 12 GB/s; nobody here votes for more.)
 */
#define CMD_DB_PHYS             0x80860000UL
#define CMD_DB_SIZE             0x20000UL
#define CMD_DB_BCM              5               /* the kind of resource in a slave's id: bus clock managers */

struct cmd_db_slave {
	uint16_t id, header_offset, data_offset, count, version, reserved[3];
};
struct cmd_db_header {
	uint32_t version;
	uint8_t magic[4];
	struct cmd_db_slave slave[8];
	uint32_t checksum, reserved;
	uint8_t data[];
};
struct cmd_db_entry {
	char id[8];
	uint32_t priority[2];
	uint32_t address;
	uint16_t length, offset;
};
struct cmd_db_bcm {                             /* a BCM's auxiliary data (Linux: struct bcm_db) */
	uint32_t unit;
	uint16_t width;
	uint8_t vcd, reserved;
};

/* (the same condition as the cores' clocks: the addresses are this phone's) */
static bool
cpufreq_wanted(void)
{
	uint32_t on = 0;

	return PE_parse_boot_argn("cpufreq", &on, sizeof(on)) && on != 0;
}

static void
ddr_look(void)
{
	/* (memory, not registers: mapped so that reads of any size and alignment are allowed) */
	const struct cmd_db_header *db = (const struct cmd_db_header *)ml_io_map_wcomb(CMD_DB_PHYS, CMD_DB_SIZE);

	if (db->magic[0] != 0xdb || db->magic[1] != 0x30 || db->magic[2] != 0x03 || db->magic[3] != 0x0c) {
		tell("ddr: no command database\n");
		return;
	}
	for (unsigned s = 0; s < 8; s++) {
		const struct cmd_db_slave *slave = &db->slave[s];
		const struct cmd_db_entry *entry = (const struct cmd_db_entry *)(db->data + slave->header_offset);

		if (slave->id != CMD_DB_BCM || slave->header_offset >= CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000 || slave->count > 512) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < slave->count; i++) {
			struct cmd_db_bcm aux = { 0 };
			char name[9] = { 0 };

			memcpy(name, entry[i].id, 8);
			/* (the data starts after the header, so the header counts: this keeps the read inside the mapped database) */
			if (entry[i].length >= sizeof(aux) &&
			    sizeof(*db) + slave->data_offset + entry[i].offset + sizeof(aux) <= CMD_DB_SIZE) {
				memcpy(&aux, db->data + slave->data_offset + entry[i].offset, sizeof(aux));
			}
			tell("ddr: BCM %-8s at %#x: unit %u, width %u, vcd %u (aux %u bytes)\n", name, entry[i].address, aux.unit,
			    aux.width, aux.vcd, entry[i].length);
		}
	}
}

/*
 * ... and what the boot loader's firmware left in the application processor's RPMh command slots
 * ("DRV 2"; Linux: rpmh-rsc.c): 2 active, 3 sleep, 3 wake slot sets and a control one, of 16 commands
 * each (sc7280's qcom,tcs-config): every command with an address, and which of them go to the BCMs
 * above -- the bandwidth it asked for, and that is in force whenever the processors are awake.
 */
#define RSC_PHYS                0x18220000UL
#define RSC_SIZE                0x10000UL
#define RSC_TCS(n, reg)         (0xd00 + 0x2a0 * (n) + (reg))
#define RSC_TCS_COUNT           9
#define RSC_CMDS                16

static void
ddr_slots(void)
{
	vm_offset_t rsc = ml_io_map(RSC_PHYS, RSC_SIZE);

	for (unsigned t = 0; t < RSC_TCS_COUNT; t++) {
		uint32_t enabled = *(volatile uint32_t *)(rsc + RSC_TCS(t, 0x1c));

		for (unsigned c = 0; c < RSC_CMDS; c++) {
			uint32_t msgid = *(volatile uint32_t *)(rsc + RSC_TCS(t, 0x30 + 20 * c));
			uint32_t address = *(volatile uint32_t *)(rsc + RSC_TCS(t, 0x34 + 20 * c));
			uint32_t data = *(volatile uint32_t *)(rsc + RSC_TCS(t, 0x38 + 20 * c));

			if (address == 0 && data == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			tell("ddr: slot set %u (%s) command %u%s: message %#x, address %#x, data %#x%s\n", t,
			    t < 2 ? "active" : t < 5 ? "sleep" : t < 8 ? "wake" : "control", c, enabled & (1u << c) ? " (on)" : "",
			    msgid, address, data, (address >> 16 & 0xf) == CMD_DB_BCM ? " <- a BCM" : "");
		}
	}
}

/*
 * The memory's bandwidth (on by default; boot-arg ddr=0: not): a vote through RPMh -- the most there
 * is -- on the bus clock managers of the memory controller (MC0: the memory's clock) and of the
 * shared hub in front of it with the system cache (SH0), as Linux's interconnect driver casts for
 * a busy GPU (icc-bcm-voter.c: a BCM command is commit, valid, the average and the peak, 14 bits each,
 * in the BCM's units; the BCM takes the highest of its levels the vote reaches), and the memory kept
 * on for this processor (ACV, bit 3, which the boot loader's firmware had set already, the same).
 * All cores together got 12.4 GB/s writing without it (membench=2: what one core gets alone), 14.8
 * with it; frames over 16.7 ms 28% instead of 34-36%. ddr_vote=N: N instead of the most (16383).
 * When the kernel goes back to the loader (hakios_ddr_quiesce(), on every way back, a panic's too)
 * the vote goes down to ddr_rest=N (default 1024). What the firmware had voted cannot be read back,
 * but what the cores get from memory can be measured (membench=2, writing): with any vote from 4
 * to 4096 12.0 to 12.4 GB/s, as before the first vote (12.4); with the most, 15.4; with none at all
 * ("no request", valid clear: what Linux sends for nothing) 0.2 -- the memory at its floor, and the
 * loader's USB transfers at 8 MB/s instead of 30. So the firmware had a vote of its own in our name,
 * of that middle range, and one from the middle of it is left.
 */
#define BCM_COMMIT              (1u << 30)
#define BCM_VALID               (1u << 29)
#define BCM_VOTE(x, y)          (BCM_COMMIT | BCM_VALID | ((uint32_t)(x) & 0x3fff) << 14 | ((uint32_t)(y) & 0x3fff))
#define TCS_REG(reg)            (ddr_rsc + 0xd00 + (reg))       /* command slot set 0, an "active" one */
#define BCM_ACV_APPS            8
#define DDR_REST                1024            /* the vote left for the loader (ddr_rest=N); see hakios_ddr_quiesce() */

static vm_offset_t ddr_rsc;
static uint32_t ddr_mc0, ddr_sh0, ddr_acv;
static bool ddr_voted;

static uint32_t
cmd_db_address(const char *name)
{
	const struct cmd_db_header *db = (const struct cmd_db_header *)ml_io_map_wcomb(CMD_DB_PHYS, CMD_DB_SIZE);
	char id[8] = { 0 };

	if (db->magic[0] != 0xdb || db->magic[1] != 0x30 || db->magic[2] != 0x03 || db->magic[3] != 0x0c) {
		return 0;
	}
	strlcpy(id, name, sizeof(id));
	for (unsigned s = 0; s < 8; s++) {
		const struct cmd_db_slave *slave = &db->slave[s];
		const struct cmd_db_entry *entry = (const struct cmd_db_entry *)(db->data + slave->header_offset);

		if (slave->id != CMD_DB_BCM || slave->header_offset >= CMD_DB_SIZE - 0x1000 || slave->count > 512) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < slave->count; i++) {
			if (memcmp(entry[i].id, id, sizeof(id)) == 0) {
				return entry[i].address;
			}
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

/* Up to three writes through command slot set 0, and the wait until RPMh has done them (as drivers/input/hakios.goodix.c) */
static bool
ddr_rpmh_write(const uint32_t *address, const uint32_t *data, unsigned count)
{
	uint32_t irq_enable = *(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x00);
	bool done = false;

	for (int i = 0; *(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x18) == 0; i++) {
		if (i > 2000) {
			tell("ddr: RPMh: the command slots stay busy\n");
			return false;
		}
		delay_for_interval(100, NSEC_PER_USEC);
	}
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x14) &= ~(1u << 24);
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x14) &= ~(1u << 16);
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x08) = 1;
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x30 + 20 * i) = 0x10008 | 0x100;        /* a 4-byte write, with a response */
		*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x34 + 20 * i) = address[i];
		*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x38 + 20 * i) = data[i];
	}
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x10) = (1u << count) - 1;
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x1c) = (1u << count) - 1;
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x00) = irq_enable | 1;
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x14) = 1u << 16;
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x14) = 1u << 16 | 1u << 24;
	for (int i = 0; i < 2000 && !done; i++) {
		done = (*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x04) & 1) != 0;
		if (!done) {
			delay_for_interval(100, NSEC_PER_USEC);
		}
	}
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x14) &= ~(1u << 24);
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x14) &= ~(1u << 16);
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x1c) = 0;
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x10) = 0;
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x08) = 1;
	*(volatile uint32_t *)TCS_REG(0x00) = irq_enable;
	if (!done) {
		tell("ddr: RPMh: no answer to the vote\n");
	}
	return done;
}

static bool
ddr_vote(uint32_t vote)
{
	uint32_t address[3] = { ddr_mc0, ddr_sh0, ddr_acv };
	uint32_t data[3] = { BCM_VOTE(vote, vote), BCM_VOTE(vote, vote), BCM_VOTE(0, BCM_ACV_APPS) };

	return ddr_rpmh_write(address, data, 3);
}

static void
ddr_raise(void)
{
	uint32_t vote = 0x3fff;

	PE_parse_boot_argn("ddr_vote", &vote, sizeof(vote));
	ddr_mc0 = cmd_db_address("MC0");
	ddr_sh0 = cmd_db_address("SH0");
	ddr_acv = cmd_db_address("ACV");
	if (ddr_mc0 == 0 || ddr_sh0 == 0 || ddr_acv == 0 || vote == 0 || vote > 0x3fff) {
		tell("ddr: no vote (MC0 %#x, SH0 %#x, ACV %#x, vote %u)\n", ddr_mc0, ddr_sh0, ddr_acv, vote);
		return;
	}
	ddr_rsc = ml_io_map(RSC_PHYS, RSC_SIZE);
	ddr_voted = ddr_vote(vote);
	tell("ddr: memory bandwidth vote %u on MC0 (%#x) and SH0 (%#x)%s\n", vote, ddr_mc0, ddr_sh0, ddr_voted ? "" : ": FAILED");
}

/* On the way back to the loader (osfmk/arm64/loader_return.c: loader_return(), whatever the reason; the other processors are stopped) */
void hakios_ddr_quiesce(void);

void
hakios_ddr_quiesce(void)
{
	uint32_t address[2] = { ddr_mc0, ddr_sh0 };
	uint32_t rest = DDR_REST, data[2];
	bool done;

	if (!ddr_voted) {
		return;
	}
	ddr_voted = false;
	PE_parse_boot_argn("ddr_rest", &rest, sizeof(rest));
	rest = MIN(rest, 0x3fff);
	data[0] = data[1] = rest != 0 ? BCM_VOTE(rest, rest) : BCM_COMMIT;     /* 0: no request */
	done = ddr_rpmh_write(address, data, 2);
	tell("ddr: memory bandwidth vote %u for the loader: %s\n", rest, done ? "done" : "FAILED");
}

void
hakios_cpufreq_init(void)
{
	const ml_topology_info_t *topology = ml_get_topology_info();
	uint32_t enabled = 0, membench = 0, cores[EPSS_DOMAINS] = { 0 }, before, here;

	load_start();
	enabled = 2;
	PE_parse_boot_argn("ddr", &enabled, sizeof(enabled));
	if (enabled == 1) {
		ddr_look();
		ddr_slots();
	} else if (enabled == 2 && cpufreq_wanted()) {
		ddr_raise();
	}
	enabled = 0;
	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("cpufreq", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	for (unsigned int i = 0; i < topology->num_cpus; i++) {
		cores[domain_of(topology->cpus[i].phys_id)]++;
	}
	/* (whichever core this thread happens to be on, and stays on or not: it only goes to the log) */
	here = (uint32_t)(__builtin_arm_rsr64("MPIDR_EL1") >> 8) & 0xff;
	before = loop_speed();
	for (uint32_t domain = 0; domain < EPSS_DOMAINS; domain++) {
		if (cores[domain] != 0) {
			raise_domain(domain, cores[domain]);
		}
	}
	printf("cpufreq: on core %u a loop ran at %u, now at %u\n", here, before, loop_speed());
	/* membench has its own variable: when the boot-arg is absent, the cpufreq value (2 means on) must not start the benchmark */
	PE_parse_boot_argn("membench", &membench, sizeof(membench));
	if (membench == 1) {
		memory_bench();
	} else if (membench == 2) {
		thread_t thread;

		if (kernel_thread_start(bench_all, NULL, &thread) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
			thread_deallocate(thread);
		}
	}
}
```

`drivers/power/hakios.pmic.c`:

```c
/*
 * What is on the phone's power-management chips, and what time their clock says. Only with boot-arg pmic=1.
 *
 * The phone's PMICs (the PMK8350 and PM7325 beside the SoC, with a PM8350C and others on the board) hang on
 * one serial bus, SPMI, and the SoC reaches them through the "PMIC arbiter" (dt: qcom,spmi@c440000). Each chip
 * is a set of small blocks ("peripherals", 256 registers each) with a type and a subtype in registers 0x04
 * and 0x05: a GPIO, a regulator, the power-on block, a temperature alarm, a flash LED driver, a charger, the
 * real-time clock. Android's drivers find theirs from the device tree. This one asks the arbiter what it has
 * and what each block says it is, and puts the answer in the log: an inventory, so that the next driver to
 * be written for one of these blocks starts from what the phone really has instead of from what a table
 * for another phone says (this phone's device tree has no node for its real-time clock, for instance).
 *
 * THIS DRIVER ONLY READS. It reads through the arbiter's "observer" channels exactly as drivers/input/hakios.buttons.c
 * does, one bus transfer at a time under the same lock (hakios_spmi_lock()), and writes only the command word
 * that asks the arbiter for a read. Nothing is written to a PMIC: they make the phone's supplies. Where the arbiter
 * answers "denied" or "failed" for a block, the line says so and the driver goes on.
 *
 * Register layout and the version (5) of the arbiter: Linux drivers/spmi/spmi-pmic-arb.c, as drivers/input/hakios.buttons.c
 * has it and has run it on this phone. A phone whose arbiter is another version gets one line and nothing else.
 *
 * The clock. The PMICs have a real-time clock that Android sets, and keeps while the phone is off (Linux:
 * rtc-pm8xxx.c). When the inventory finds a block of type 0x07 (the clock) it reads four bytes at register 0x48 of
 * the one with subtype 0x01 -- the seconds since 1970, little-endian, as Linux reads them -- twice, a little over a
 * second apart, and says whether the second is later than the first (it ticks), how many days that is, and what the
 * kernel's own time (the loader gives the kernel the host's time in epoch=) minus it comes to. The value is kept as
 * kern.hakios.rtc_seconds. The kernel's own clock is NOT set from it. (The first run on the phone showed why: the
 * counter reads 60110539 seconds, 695 days of counting, which as a date is 1971. It is a counter, not wall-clock time; see
 * the comment at the report.)
 *
 * Status (what has and has not been seen): RUN ON THE PHONE (POCO X5 Pro, 2026-10-27, four runs): the arbiter is version 0x50020000
 * (5.2) with 512 channels, 444 distinct peripherals; slaves 0 to 3 answer (0, 1 and 2 are the PMK8350, PM7325 and PM8350C, as the buttons and flashlight drivers have them), the
 * peripherals of slaves 4, 8 and 9 answer "failed" (no chip there: 98 of them); the clock is found where Linux has it
 * (slave 0 0x6100, type 0x07 subtype 0x01) and ticks once a second. The access is the buttons driver's, which is
 * known to work on this phone; what is new is the walk over all channels and the clock's registers (0x48 for the read), taken from Linux's rtc-pm8xxx.c
 * as remembered. The first run on the phone (2026-10-27) found the clock's blocks where Linux has them: slave 0 0x6100 is type 0x07
 * subtype 0x01 (the write block) and 0x6200 type 0x07 subtype 0x03 (the alarm); the type is 0x07, not the 0x06 first assumed. Nothing here has a recorded run on the phone until a
 * line below says so; it is not run in QEMU, which has no arbiter.
 *
 * Boot-args:
 *   pmic=1            do it (once, from a thread of its own)
 *   pmic_list=0       only the clock, not the inventory of every block
 */
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);
extern void hakios_spmi_lock(void);
extern void hakios_spmi_unlock(void);

SYSCTL_DECL(_kern_hakios);

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	return printf("%s", line);
}

static inline uint32_t
rd(vm_offset_t address)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)address;
}

static inline void
wr(vm_offset_t address, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)address = value;
}

/* the arbiter, as drivers/input/hakios.buttons.c maps it */
#define ARB_CORE_PHYS           0x0c440000UL
#define ARB_CORE_SIZE           0x1100UL
#define ARB_CNFG_PHYS           0x0c40a000UL
#define ARB_CNFG_SIZE           0x1000UL
#define ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS       0x0e600000UL
#define ARB_OBSERVER_SIZE       0x10000UL
#define ARB_SYSTEM              0
#define ARB_VERSION             0x000
#define ARB_VERSION_5           0x50000000u
#define ARB_VERSION_7           0x70000000u
#define ARB_FEATURES            0x004
#define ARB_CHANNEL(n)          (0x900 + 4 * (n))               /* [19:8] slave and peripheral */
#define ARB_MAX_CHANNELS        512
#define OBSERVER_COMMAND        0x00
#define OBSERVER_STATUS         0x08
#define OBSERVER_DATA0          0x18
#define OBSERVER_DATA1          0x1c
#define STATUS_DONE             0x1
#define STATUS_FAILURE          0x2
#define STATUS_DENIED           0x4
#define STATUS_DROPPED          0x8
#define COMMAND_READ            (1u << 27)
#define READ_TIMEOUT_US         2000

static vm_offset_t arb_core, arb_observer;

/* Read `count` (1 to 8) registers of the peripheral at channel `channel`, from register `reg`; NULL, or what went wrong. */
static const char *
spmi_read(uint32_t channel, uint8_t reg, uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t count)
{
	vm_offset_t ch = arb_observer + 0x10000UL * ARB_SYSTEM + 0x80UL * channel;
	uint64_t start = mach_absolute_time(), now, interval;
	uint32_t status, data[2];

	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(READ_TIMEOUT_US * (uint64_t)NSEC_PER_USEC, &interval);
	hakios_spmi_lock();
	wr(ch + OBSERVER_COMMAND, COMMAND_READ | (uint32_t)reg << 4 | (count - 1));
	do {
		status = rd(ch + OBSERVER_STATUS);
		now = mach_absolute_time();
	} while (!(status & STATUS_DONE) && now - start < interval);
	data[0] = rd(ch + OBSERVER_DATA0);
	data[1] = count > 4 ? rd(ch + OBSERVER_DATA1) : 0;
	hakios_spmi_unlock();

	if (!(status & STATUS_DONE)) {
		return "no answer";
	} else if (status & STATUS_DENIED) {
		return "denied";
	} else if (status & STATUS_FAILURE) {
		return "failed";
	} else if (status & STATUS_DROPPED) {
		return "dropped";
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		bytes[i] = (uint8_t)(data[i / 4] >> (8 * (i % 4)));
	}
	return NULL;
}

/* ---- the inventory --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define REG_TYPE                0x04
#define RTC_TYPE                0x07
#define RTC_SUBTYPE_WRITE       0x01
#define RTC_REG_READ            0x48

static int64_t rtc_seconds_value = -1;
static int pmic_peripherals_value;
SYSCTL_QUAD(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, rtc_seconds, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &rtc_seconds_value,
    "the PMIC real-time clock, seconds since 1970 as it read once at boot; -1: not read");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, pmic_peripherals, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &pmic_peripherals_value, 0,
    "how many blocks of the power-management chips the arbiter showed us");

static uint8_t seen_type[ARB_MAX_CHANNELS][2];

static bool
read_clock(uint32_t channel, uint32_t *seconds)
{
	uint8_t b[4];
	const char *problem = spmi_read(channel, RTC_REG_READ, b, 4);

	if (problem != NULL) {
		say("pmic: the clock's seconds: %s\n", problem);
		return false;
	}
	*seconds = b[0] | (uint32_t)b[1] << 8 | (uint32_t)b[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)b[3] << 24;
	return true;
}

static void
clock_report(uint32_t channel)
{
	uint32_t first, second;
	clock_sec_t kernel_seconds;
	clock_usec_t kernel_micro;

	if (!read_clock(channel, &first)) {
		return;
	}
	delay_for_interval(1100, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
	if (!read_clock(channel, &second)) {
		return;
	}
	clock_get_calendar_microtime(&kernel_seconds, &kernel_micro);
	rtc_seconds_value = second;
	/*
	 * What this counter is, as the first run on the phone showed: it ticks once a second, and it is NOT wall-clock time (it
	 * read 60110539, which as a date is in 1971). Qualcomm phones keep the clock as a free-running counter in the PMIC, and
	 * Android's time service keeps the offset to real time in a file of its own; the counter's use to this kernel is a
	 * count of seconds that goes on through a reboot and a flat battery's worth of power-off. If the kernel was given the
	 * host's time (epoch=), the difference printed is that offset, which can be compared with the file's.
	 */
	say("pmic: the real-time clock reads %u, then %u a second and a tenth later (%s); that is %u days of counting, not a date;"
	    " the kernel's time minus it is %lld s\n", first, second, second > first ? "it ticks" : "IT DOES NOT TICK", second / 86400,
	    (long long)kernel_seconds - (long long)second);
}

static bool list_all = true;

static void
pmic_run(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	bool list = list_all;
	uint32_t version, channels, found = 0, rtc_channel = 0;
	bool rtc_found = false;
	uint16_t ppids[ARB_MAX_CHANNELS];
	uint16_t channel_of[ARB_MAX_CHANNELS];

	arb_core = ml_io_map(ARB_CORE_PHYS, ARB_CORE_SIZE);
	arb_observer = ml_io_map(ARB_OBSERVER_PHYS, ARB_OBSERVER_SIZE);
	if (arb_core == 0 || arb_observer == 0) {
		say("pmic: could not map the PMIC arbiter\n");
		goto out;
	}
	version = rd(arb_core + ARB_VERSION);
	channels = rd(arb_core + ARB_FEATURES) & 0x7ff;
	say("pmic: PMIC arbiter version %#x, %u channels\n", version, channels);
	if (version < ARB_VERSION_5 || version >= ARB_VERSION_7) {
		say("pmic: this driver knows version 5 of the arbiter only: nothing read\n");
		goto out;
	}
	if (channels == 0 || channels > ARB_MAX_CHANNELS) {
		channels = ARB_MAX_CHANNELS;
	}
	/* one entry for each distinct slave/peripheral, with the first channel that reaches it */
	for (uint32_t n = 0; n < channels; n++) {
		uint32_t map = rd(arb_core + ARB_CHANNEL(n));
		uint16_t ppid = (uint16_t)((map >> 8) & 0xfff);
		bool again = false;

		if (map == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < found; i++) {
			if (ppids[i] == ppid) {
				again = true;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (!again) {
			ppids[found] = ppid;
			channel_of[found] = (uint16_t)n;
			found++;
		}
	}
	pmic_peripherals_value = (int)found;
	say("pmic: %u distinct peripherals in the arbiter's table; reading the type of each\n", found);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < found; i++) {
		uint8_t is[2] = { 0xff, 0xff };
		const char *problem = spmi_read(channel_of[i], REG_TYPE, is, 2);

		seen_type[i][0] = is[0];
		seen_type[i][1] = is[1];
		if (list) {
			if (problem != NULL) {
				say("pmic:   slave %u 0x%02x00 (channel %u): %s\n", ppids[i] >> 8, ppids[i] & 0xff, channel_of[i], problem);
			} else {
				say("pmic:   slave %u 0x%02x00 (channel %u): type %#04x subtype %#04x\n", ppids[i] >> 8, ppids[i] & 0xff,
				    channel_of[i], is[0], is[1]);
			}
		}
		if (problem == NULL && is[0] == RTC_TYPE && is[1] == RTC_SUBTYPE_WRITE && !rtc_found) {
			rtc_found = true;
			rtc_channel = channel_of[i];
			say("pmic: the real-time clock is slave %u 0x%02x00 (type %#x, subtype %#x)\n", ppids[i] >> 8, ppids[i] & 0xff,
			    is[0], is[1]);
		}
	}
	if (rtc_found) {
		clock_report(rtc_channel);
	} else {
		say("pmic: none of the %u blocks says it is a real-time clock (type %#x, subtype %#x): none read\n", found, RTC_TYPE,
		    RTC_SUBTYPE_WRITE);
	}
out:
	return;
}

__startup_func
static void
pmic_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0, list = 1;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("pmic", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	(void)PE_parse_boot_argn("pmic_list", &list, sizeof(list));
	list_all = list != 0;
	/* once, from a thread call: the reads wait on the bus, and that is no place for the startup thread */
	thread_call_enter(thread_call_allocate(pmic_run, NULL));
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, pmic_init);
```

`drivers/power/hakios.thermal.c`:

```c
/*
 * The SoC's temperature sensors: sysctl kern.hakios.thermal_*, a line in the log, and a stop for a phone that is
 * getting too hot to be left alone. Only with boot-arg thermal=1.
 *
 * What is here. The chip has two blocks of temperature sensors ("TSENS", dt: tsens@c222000 and tsens@c223000,
 * compatible qcom,tsens26xx, which Linux's tsens-v2.c drives): 15 sensors in the first (the CPU cores, the CPU
 * subsystem, the always-on block) and 12 in the second (the GPU, the neural processors, video, memory, the
 * modem, the camera). The blocks measure by themselves, all the time, and keep the last reading of each sensor in
 * a status word that anyone may read: bits [11:0] the temperature in tenths of a degree, signed, and bit 21 set
 * when there is a reading. THIS DRIVER ONLY READS those words (one 32-bit load each); it writes nothing, it
 * takes no interrupt and it sets no threshold. Calibration is the firmware's: the blocks are calibrated from the
 * fuses by the secure side before the operating system runs (Linux's tsens does it too, from the QFPROM, for its
 * own use of the raw codes; the status words used here are already degrees).
 *
 * What a temperature is worth. A reading is believed when it has its valid bit and lies between -40 and 160
 * degrees; anything else is a sensor that is not connected, or not yet measured, and is left out of the maximum.
 * The table of sensors (names, which block, which number, and the temperatures at which the vendor slows
 * things down and gives up) is the phone's own device tree's thermal-zones, made by tools/dt-thermal.py: the
 * numbers are the vendor's, not ours.
 *
 * What it does with them.
 *   - every thermal_poll milliseconds (default 2000) it reads all sensors;
 *   - sysctl kern.hakios.thermal_max_mc (the hottest, in millidegrees), thermal_hottest (its name),
 *     thermal_sensors ("cpu-0-0=41.2 ... " in degrees), thermal_reads;
 *   - a line in the log (and the loader's log) every thermal_log seconds (default 60) and at once when the
 *     hottest sensor crosses a multiple of 5 degrees upwards from 60;
 *   - the stop: when the hottest valid sensor reads at least thermal_stop degrees three times in a row (default
 *     105; thermal_stop=0 turns the stop off), it says so and hands control back to the boot loader the way
 *     "xl stop" does (the GPU, Wi-Fi and audio DSP given back first). The vendor starts to slow the CPU at 108 to
 *     112 degrees; 105 is below that on purpose, because nothing here slows anything down: the stop is the whole
 *     protection, and it is for a phone left running unattended. It is a stop of the run, not a repair: a hot phone
 *     is hot for minutes after.
 *
 * Status (what has and has not been seen): RUN ON THE PHONE (POCO X5 Pro, 2026-10-27, four runs): the status-word layout
 * (from Linux's tsens-v2.c as remembered, the same as drivers/gpu/hakios.adreno.c reads for the GPU's two sensors) is right:
 * 27 of 27 sensors have a reading, 33.3 to 39.5 degrees on a phone at rest, the CPU cores a degree or two above the rest, the
 * values move between runs; kern.hakios.thermal_* are read from user space (userland/src/hello.c with hello_wait=). NOT yet
 * seen: the stop (thermal_stop) firing, a phone under load, a reading above 40 degrees. The sensors are the device tree's; whether
 * the phone's own tree is the reference one (devices/redwood/prebuilt/device-tree.dtb) was not compared sensor by sensor.
 * Not run in QEMU, and thermal=1 must not be given there: it has no such blocks, and a load from an address it does not map faults.
 *
 * Boot-args:
 *   thermal=1          read the sensors
 *   thermal_poll=<ms>  how often (200 to 60000; 2000)
 *   thermal_log=<s>    a summary line this often (0: only on a rise; 60)
 *   thermal_stop=<C>   stop the run at this temperature (0: never; 105)
 *   thermal_tm0=<pa>, thermal_tm1=<pa>  the two blocks' readings, when this is not the reference phone
 *                      (0xc263000 and 0xc265000)
 */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>

extern vm_offset_t ml_io_map(vm_offset_t phys_addr, vm_size_t size);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);
extern void loader_return(void);
extern void hakios_var_save_on_return(void);
extern void hakios_adreno_stop(void);
extern void hakios_wifi_stop(void);
extern void hakios_adsp_stop(void);

SYSCTL_DECL(_kern_hakios);

static int say(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

static int
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[700];                                 /* the line of all the sensors is the long one */
	va_list list;

	va_start(list, format);
	vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, list);
	va_end(list);
	for (const char *c = line; *c != 0; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	return printf("%s", line);
}

#define TM_SIZE                 0x200
#define TM_STATUS(sensor)       (0xa0 + 4 * (sensor))           /* one word a sensor */
#define TM_VALID                (1u << 21)
#define TEMP_MIN_TENTHS         (-400)
#define TEMP_MAX_TENTHS         1600

/* made by tools/dt-thermal.py from the phone's device tree: name, block, sensor, slow down at, gives up at (millidegrees) */
static const struct sensor_info {
	const char *    name;
	uint32_t        tm;
	uint32_t        number;
	int32_t         slow_mc;
	int32_t         limit_mc;
} sensors[] = {
	{ "aoss-0", 0xc263000, 0, 115000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-0-0", 0xc263000, 1, 110000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-0-1", 0xc263000, 2, 110000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-0-2", 0xc263000, 3, 110000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-0-3", 0xc263000, 4, 110000, 125000 },
	{ "cpuss-0", 0xc263000, 5, 115000, 125000 },
	{ "cpuss-1", 0xc263000, 6, 115000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-0", 0xc263000, 7, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-1", 0xc263000, 8, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-2", 0xc263000, 9, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-3", 0xc263000, 10, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-4", 0xc263000, 11, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-5", 0xc263000, 12, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-6", 0xc263000, 13, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "cpu-1-7", 0xc263000, 14, 108000, 125000 },
	{ "aoss-1", 0xc265000, 0, 115000, 125000 },
	{ "gpuss-0", 0xc265000, 1, 95000, 125000 },
	{ "gpuss-1", 0xc265000, 2, 95000, 125000 },
	{ "nspss-0", 0xc265000, 3, 100000, 125000 },
	{ "nspss-1", 0xc265000, 4, 100000, 125000 },
	{ "video", 0xc265000, 5, 100000, 125000 },
	{ "ddr", 0xc265000, 6, 115000, 125000 },
	{ "mdmss-0", 0xc265000, 7, 95000, 125000 },
	{ "mdmss-1", 0xc265000, 8, 95000, 125000 },
	{ "mdmss-2", 0xc265000, 9, 95000, 125000 },
	{ "mdmss-3", 0xc265000, 10, 95000, 125000 },
	{ "camera-0", 0xc265000, 11, 100000, 125000 },
};
#define NSENSORS        ((unsigned)(sizeof(sensors) / sizeof(sensors[0])))
#define REFERENCE_TM0   0xc263000u
#define REFERENCE_TM1   0xc265000u

static vm_offset_t tm_va[2];
static uint32_t tm_pa[2] = { REFERENCE_TM0, REFERENCE_TM1 };
static int32_t tenths[NSENSORS];                /* the last good reading; INT32_MIN: none yet */
static uint32_t poll_ms = 2000, log_seconds = 60, stop_celsius = 105;
static uint64_t last_log, reads;
static int strikes, last_step;
static bool stopping;

static int thermal_max_mc = -273000;
static char thermal_hottest[16] = "";
static char thermal_list[NSENSORS * 16 + 8];
static int thermal_reads_value;

SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, thermal_max_mc, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &thermal_max_mc, 0,
    "the hottest valid temperature sensor of the SoC, in millidegrees (-273000: none read)");
SYSCTL_STRING(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, thermal_hottest, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, thermal_hottest, 0, "the name of that sensor");
SYSCTL_STRING(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, thermal_sensors, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, thermal_list, 0,
    "every sensor and its temperature in degrees: \"cpu-0-0=41.2 gpuss-0=38.0 ...\"");
SYSCTL_INT(_kern_hakios, OID_AUTO, thermal_reads, CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, &thermal_reads_value, 0, "how many times the sensors were read");

/* For other drivers (a GPU or modem that wants to back off): the hottest temperature, in millidegrees; -273000: not read. */
int
hakios_thermal_max_mc(void)
{
	return thermal_max_mc;
}

static thread_call_t call;

static void
text_of(char *out, size_t size, int32_t tenth)
{
	int whole = tenth / 10, frac = tenth % 10;

	snprintf(out, size, "%s%d.%d", (tenth < 0 && whole == 0) ? "-" : "", whole, frac < 0 ? -frac : frac);
}

static void
look(void)
{
	int32_t hottest = INT32_MIN;
	unsigned hot = 0, good = 0;
	char list[sizeof(thermal_list)], one[16];

	list[0] = 0;
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < NSENSORS; i++) {
		uint32_t status = *(volatile uint32_t *)(tm_va[sensors[i].tm == REFERENCE_TM0 ? 0 : 1] + TM_STATUS(sensors[i].number));
		int32_t value = (int32_t)(status << 20) >> 20;

		if (!(status & TM_VALID) || value < TEMP_MIN_TENTHS || value > TEMP_MAX_TENTHS) {
			continue;
		}
		tenths[i] = value;
		good++;
		if (value > hottest) {
			hottest = value;
			hot = i;
		}
		text_of(one, sizeof(one), value);
		if (strlen(list) + strlen(sensors[i].name) + strlen(one) + 3 < sizeof(list)) {
			strlcat(list, sensors[i].name, sizeof(list));
			strlcat(list, "=", sizeof(list));
			strlcat(list, one, sizeof(list));
			strlcat(list, " ", sizeof(list));
		}
	}
	reads++;
	thermal_reads_value = (int)reads;
	if (good == 0) {
		return;
	}
	strlcpy(thermal_list, list, sizeof(thermal_list));
	strlcpy(thermal_hottest, sensors[hot].name, sizeof(thermal_hottest));
	thermal_max_mc = hottest * 100;

	uint64_t now = mach_absolute_time(), seconds;
	int step = hottest >= 600 ? hottest / 50 : 0;           /* a step each 5 degrees from 60 */

	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(now - last_log, &seconds);
	seconds /= NSEC_PER_SEC;
	if (step > last_step || last_log == 0 || (log_seconds != 0 && seconds >= log_seconds)) {
		text_of(one, sizeof(one), hottest);
		say("thermal: %u of %u sensors read; hottest %s at %s C; %s\n", good, NSENSORS, sensors[hot].name, one, thermal_list);
		last_log = now;
	}
	last_step = step;

	if (stop_celsius != 0 && hottest >= (int32_t)stop_celsius * 10) {
		strikes++;
	} else {
		strikes = 0;
	}
	if (strikes >= 3 && !stopping) {
		stopping = true;
		text_of(one, sizeof(one), hottest);
		say("\n--- thermal: %s reads %s C, at or above thermal_stop=%u three times in a row: back to the loader ---\n",
		    sensors[hot].name, one, stop_celsius);
		hakios_var_save_on_return();
		hakios_adreno_stop();
		hakios_wifi_stop();
		hakios_adsp_stop();
		loader_return();
	}
}

static void
tick(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	uint64_t deadline;

	look();
	clock_interval_to_deadline(poll_ms, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(call, deadline);
}

__startup_func
static void
thermal_init(void)
{
	uint32_t enabled = 0, value;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("thermal", &enabled, sizeof(enabled)) || !enabled) {
		return;
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < NSENSORS; i++) {
		tenths[i] = INT32_MIN;
	}
	(void)PE_parse_boot_argn("thermal_tm0", &tm_pa[0], sizeof(tm_pa[0]));
	(void)PE_parse_boot_argn("thermal_tm1", &tm_pa[1], sizeof(tm_pa[1]));
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("thermal_poll", &value, sizeof(value)) && value >= 200 && value <= 60000) {
		poll_ms = value;
	}
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("thermal_log", &value, sizeof(value)) && value <= 86400) {
		log_seconds = value;
	}
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("thermal_stop", &value, sizeof(value)) && value <= 160) {
		stop_celsius = value;
	}
	for (unsigned b = 0; b < 2; b++) {
		tm_va[b] = ml_io_map(tm_pa[b], TM_SIZE);
		if (tm_va[b] == 0) {
			say("thermal: could not map the sensors' block at %#x; off\n", tm_pa[b]);
			return;
		}
	}
	say("thermal: %u sensors in two blocks (%#x, %#x), every %u ms; stop at %u C%s\n", NSENSORS, tm_pa[0], tm_pa[1], poll_ms,
	    stop_celsius, stop_celsius ? "" : " (off)");
	call = thread_call_allocate(tick, NULL);
	tick(NULL, NULL);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, thermal_init);
```
