```hpp
    return (znearClipDisable ? A6XX_GRAS_CL_CNTL_ZNEAR_CLIP_DISABLE : 0u) | (zfarClipDisable ? A6XX_GRAS_CL_CNTL_ZFAR_CLIP_DISABLE : 0u) |
           (zClampEnable ? A6XX_GRAS_CL_CNTL_Z_CLAMP_ENABLE : 0u) | (zeroGbScaleZ ? A6XX_GRAS_CL_CNTL_ZERO_GB_SCALE_Z : 0u) |
           (vpClipCodeIgnore ? A6XX_GRAS_CL_CNTL_VP_CLIP_CODE_IGNORE : 0u);
}
constexpr uint32_t grasSuPointMinmax(uint32_t minSixteenths, uint32_t maxSixteenths) {
    return A6XX_GRAS_SU_POINT_MINMAX_MIN(minSixteenths) | A6XX_GRAS_SU_POINT_MINMAX_MAX(maxSixteenths);
}
constexpr uint32_t grasSuPointSize(uint32_t sixteenths) { return A6XX_GRAS_SU_POINT_SIZE(sixteenths); }


// --- the 2D engine: a solid-colour fill of the colour target, turnip's sysmem clear (r2d_*, tu_clear_blit.cc:145-570) ----
//
// A render pass with loadAction Clear begins with one CP_BLIT over the render area: turnip clears a single-sampled
// sysmem attachment with the 2D engine, not with a draw (clear_sysmem_attachment, tu_clear_blit.cc:4402-4444, which
// picks r3d only for MSAA). The 2D engine has its own copies of the format and the destination (RB_2D_DST_*), so the
// clear does not read RB_MRT or any shader state.

// the intermediate format the 2D engine converts the solid colour through (format_to_ifmt, tu_clear_blit.cc:41-71)
enum a6xx_2d_ifmt : uint32_t {
    R2D_UNORM8_SRGB = 1,           // a6xx.xml.h:1125  an sRGB target: the engine encodes, the clear value stays linear-packed (r2d_setup_common)
    R2D_FLOAT16 = 3,               // a6xx.xml.h:1124  16-bit float channels: the value as halfs
    R2D_FLOAT32 = 4,               // a6xx.xml.h:1123  32-bit float channels: the value's bits
    R2D_INT8 = 5,                  // a6xx.xml.h:1122
    R2D_INT16 = 6,                 // a6xx.xml.h:1121
    R2D_INT32 = 7,                 // a6xx.xml.h:1120  32-bit integer channels: the value as integers
    R2D_UNORM8 = 16,               // a6xx.xml.h:1119  8-bit unorm channels: each value rounded to 0..255 (tu_pack_float32_for_unorm)
};

// RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL and GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL take the same word (r2d_setup_common writes one value to both)
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL = 0x8c00;                                // a6xx.xml.h:6555
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_ROTATE__MASK = 0x00000007;                   // a6xx.xml: a6xx_rotation, bits 0..2
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_SOLID_COLOR = 128;                           // a6xx.xml.h:6569
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK = 0x0000ff00;             // a6xx.xml.h:6570
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT__SHIFT = 8;                     // a6xx.xml.h:6571
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK__MASK = 0x00f00000;                     // a6xx.xml.h:6584
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK__SHIFT = 20;                            // a6xx.xml.h:6585
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT__MASK = 0x1f000000;                     // a6xx.xml.h:6590
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT__SHIFT = 24;                            // a6xx.xml.h:6591
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL = 0x8400;                              // a6xx.xml.h:5087
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_SOLID_COLOR = 128;                         // a6xx.xml.h:5101
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK = 0x0000ff00;           // a6xx.xml.h:5102
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK__MASK = 0x00f00000;                   // a6xx.xml.h:5116
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT__MASK = 0x1f000000;                   // a6xx.xml.h:5122
static_assert(A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_SOLID_COLOR == A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_SOLID_COLOR &&
                  A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK == A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK &&
                  A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK__MASK == A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK__MASK && A6XX_GRAS_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT__MASK == A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT__MASK,
              "one blit word serves both copies");
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT(uint32_t v) {
    return field(v, A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT__SHIFT, A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK);
}
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK(uint32_t v) { return field(v, A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK__SHIFT, A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK__MASK); }
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT(uint32_t v) { return field(v, A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT__SHIFT, A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT__MASK); }

// SP_2D_DST_FORMAT: the format again for the SP side of the engine, UINT/SINT for the pure-integer formats
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT = 0xacc0;                               // a6xx.xml.h:9521
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_SINT = 2;                                   // a6xx.xml.h:9523
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_UINT = 4;                                   // a6xx.xml.h:9524
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK = 0x000007f8;            // a6xx.xml.h:9525
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_COLOR_FORMAT__SHIFT = 3;                    // a6xx.xml.h:9526
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_SRGB = 0x00000800;                          // a6xx.xml.h:9531
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_MASK__MASK = 0x0000f000;                    // a6xx.xml.h:9532
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_MASK__SHIFT = 12;                           // a6xx.xml.h:9533
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_RB_2D_UNKNOWN_8C01 = 0x8c01;                             // a6xx.xml.h:6605
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_TL = 0x8405;                                 // a6xx.xml.h:5173
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_BR = 0x8406;                                 // a6xx.xml.h:5188
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_TL_X__MASK = 0x00003fff;                         // a6xx.xml.h:5174
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_TL_Y__MASK = 0x3fff0000;                         // a6xx.xml.h:5180
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_BR_X__MASK = 0x00003fff;                         // a6xx.xml.h:5189
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_BR_Y__MASK = 0x3fff0000;                         // a6xx.xml.h:5195
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_RB_2D_SRC_SOLID_C0 = 0x8c2c;                             // a6xx.xml.h:6693
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_COLOR_FORMAT(uint32_t v) {
    return field(v, A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_COLOR_FORMAT__SHIFT, A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK);
}
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_MASK(uint32_t v) { return field(v, A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_MASK__SHIFT, A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_MASK__MASK); }

// the destination: INFO, BASE lo/hi, PITCH as one pkt4 from RB_2D_DST_INFO (r2d_dst, tu_clear_blit.cc:396-413), then
// the flag buffer's three words from RB_2D_DST_FLAGS (0: no UBWC)
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO = 0x8c17;                                 // a6xx.xml.h:6608
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK = 255;                     // a6xx.xml.h:6609
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__SHIFT = 0;                      // a6xx.xml.h:6610
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_TILE_MODE__MASK = 0x00000300;                 // a6xx.xml.h:6615
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_TILE_MODE__SHIFT = 8;                         // a6xx.xml.h:6616
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__MASK = 0x00000c00;                // a6xx.xml.h:6621
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__SHIFT = 10;                       // a6xx.xml.h:6622
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_SRGB = 0x00002000;                            // a6xx.xml.h:6628
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST = 0x8c18;                                      // a6xx.xml.h:6638
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH = 0x8c1a;                                // a6xx.xml.h:6641
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH__MASK = 0x0000ffff;                          // a6xx.xml.h:6642
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH__SHIFT = 0;                                  // a6xx.xml.h:6643
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST_FLAGS = 0x8c20;                                // a6xx.xml.h:6667
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_FLAGS = 0x00001000;                          // a6xx.xml.h:6627  the destination is UBWC
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_FLAGS_PITCH(uint32_t v) { return (v >> 6) & 0xffu; }          // a6xx.xml.h:6673
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH__SCALE = 6;                                  // a6xx.xml.h:6644  the encoder's val >> 6
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT(uint32_t v) {
    return field(v, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__SHIFT, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK);
}
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_TILE_MODE(uint32_t v) { return field(v, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_TILE_MODE__SHIFT, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_TILE_MODE__MASK); }
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_SWAP(uint32_t v) { return field(v, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__SHIFT, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__MASK); }
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH(uint32_t v) { return field(v >> A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH__SCALE, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH__SHIFT, A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH__MASK); }
static_assert(REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST == REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO + 1 && REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST_PITCH == REG_A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO + 3,
              "INFO, BASE lo, BASE hi, PITCH are four consecutive registers: one pkt4");
static_assert(A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_TL_X__MASK == A6XX_GRAS_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL_X__MASK && A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_TL_Y__MASK == A6XX_GRAS_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL_Y__MASK &&
                  A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_BR_X__MASK == A6XX_GRAS_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL_X__MASK && A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_BR_Y__MASK == A6XX_GRAS_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL_Y__MASK,
              "GRAS_2D_DST_TL/BR are a6xx_reg_xy: regXY encodes them");

// CP_BLIT, one word: the operation (r2d_run, tu_clear_blit.cc:551-570; RB_DBG_ECO_CNTL needs no switch around it on
// this chip: its _blit value is the plain one, freedreno_devices.py's A635 entry)
inline constexpr uint32_t BLIT_OP_SCALE = 3;                                                 // adreno_pm4.xml.h:505
inline constexpr uint32_t CP_BLIT_0_OP__MASK = 0x0000000f;                                   // adreno_pm4.xml.h:2439
inline constexpr uint32_t CP_BLIT_0_OP__SHIFT = 0;                                           // adreno_pm4.xml.h:2440

// the blit word of a solid fill of FMT through IFMT, all four channels written (r2d_setup_common: rotate 0, no scissor,
// no d24s8)
constexpr uint32_t rb2dBlitCntlClear(uint32_t fmt, uint32_t ifmt) {
    return A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_SOLID_COLOR | A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT(fmt) | A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK(0xf) | A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT(ifmt);
}
constexpr uint32_t sp2dDstFormat(uint32_t fmt, bool sint, bool uint, bool srgb) {
    return (sint ? A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_SINT : 0u) | (uint ? A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_UINT : 0u) | A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_COLOR_FORMAT(fmt) |
           (srgb ? A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_SRGB : 0u) | A6XX_SP_2D_DST_FORMAT_MASK(0xf);
}
constexpr uint32_t rb2dDstInfo(uint32_t fmt, uint32_t tileMode, uint32_t swap, bool srgb) {
    return A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT(fmt) | A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_TILE_MODE(tileMode) | A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_COLOR_SWAP(swap) |
           (srgb ? A6XX_RB_2D_DST_INFO_SRGB : 0u);
}
constexpr uint32_t cpBlit0(uint32_t op) { return field(op, CP_BLIT_0_OP__SHIFT, CP_BLIT_0_OP__MASK); }

// The 2D engine's source, for a copy or a scaled copy (r2d_src, tu_clear_blit.cc:268-301; fdl6_view_init's
// SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO/SIZE, fd6_view.c:320-334): the image as INFO (format, tile, swap, sRGB, FILTER for a linear scale,
// and the two UNK bits every view sets), SIZE, the base and the pitch as one pkt4 of five, the flag buffer's three
// words 0; the rectangle read in GRAS_2D_SRC_TL/BR X and Y, integer pixels at bit 8, BR inclusive (r2d_coords,
// tu6_blit_image)
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_TL_X = 0x8401;                               // a6xx.xml.h:5137
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_BR_X = 0x8402;                               // a6xx.xml.h:5146
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_TL_Y = 0x8403;                               // a6xx.xml.h:5155
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_BR_Y = 0x8404;                               // a6xx.xml.h:5164
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_TL_X__MASK = 0x01ffff00;                         // a6xx.xml.h:5138
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_TL_X__SHIFT = 8;                                 // a6xx.xml.h:5139
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO = 0xb4c0;                              // a6xx.xml.h:9836
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK = 0x000000ff;           // a6xx.xml.h:9837
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_TILE_MODE__MASK = 0x00000300;              // a6xx.xml.h:9843
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_TILE_MODE__SHIFT = 8;                      // a6xx.xml.h:9844
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__MASK = 0x00000c00;             // a6xx.xml.h:9849
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__SHIFT = 10;                    // a6xx.xml.h:9850
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SRGB = 0x00002000;                         // a6xx.xml.h:9856
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SAMPLES__MASK = 0x0000c000;                // a6xx.xml.h:9857
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SAMPLES__SHIFT = 14;                       // a6xx.xml.h:9858
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SAMPLES(a3xx_msaa_samples v) { return field(v, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SAMPLES__SHIFT, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SAMPLES__MASK); }
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_FILTER = 0x00010000;                       // a6xx.xml.h:9863
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SAMPLES_AVERAGE = 0x00040000;              // a6xx.xml.h:9865
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_UNK20 = 0x00100000;                        // a6xx.xml.h:9867
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_UNK22 = 0x00400000;                        // a6xx.xml.h:9869
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE = 0xb4c1;                              // a6xx.xml.h:9880
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE_WIDTH__MASK = 0x00007fff;                  // a6xx.xml.h:9881
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE_HEIGHT__MASK = 0x3fff8000;                 // a6xx.xml.h:9887
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE_HEIGHT__SHIFT = 15;                        // a6xx.xml.h:9888
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC = 0xb4c2;                                   // a6xx.xml.h:9895
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_PITCH = 0xb4c4;                             // a6xx.xml.h:9898
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_PITCH_PITCH__MASK = 0x00fffe00;                 // a6xx.xml.h:9905
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_PITCH_PITCH__SHIFT = 9;                         // a6xx.xml.h:9906
inline constexpr uint32_t REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_FLAGS = 0xb4ca;                             // a6xx.xml.h:10017
static_assert(REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE == REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO + 1 && REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC == REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO + 2 &&
                  REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_PITCH == REG_A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO + 4 && REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_DST_TL == REG_A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_BR_Y + 1,
              "INFO, SIZE, BASE lo, hi, PITCH are one pkt4; the four source coordinates run on into GRAS_2D_DST_TL");
constexpr uint32_t gras2dSrc(uint32_t v) { return field(v, A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_TL_X__SHIFT, A6XX_GRAS_2D_SRC_TL_X__MASK); }
constexpr uint32_t sp2dSrcInfo(uint32_t fmt, uint32_t swap, bool srgb, bool filter) {
    return field(fmt, 0, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK) | field(TILE6_LINEAR, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_TILE_MODE__SHIFT, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_TILE_MODE__MASK) |
           field(swap, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__SHIFT, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_COLOR_SWAP__MASK) | (srgb ? A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_SRGB : 0u) |
           (filter ? A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_FILTER : 0u) | A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_UNK20 | A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_INFO_UNK22;
}
constexpr uint32_t sp2dSrcSize(uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {
    return field(w, 0, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE_WIDTH__MASK) | field(h, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE_HEIGHT__SHIFT, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_SIZE_HEIGHT__MASK);
}
constexpr uint32_t sp2dSrcPitch(uint32_t pitchBytes) { return field(pitchBytes >> 6, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_PITCH_PITCH__SHIFT, A6XX_SP_PS_2D_SRC_PITCH_PITCH__MASK); }
// the blit word of a copy (r2d_setup_common with clear false)
constexpr uint32_t rb2dBlitCntlCopy(uint32_t fmt, uint32_t ifmt) {
    return A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_COLOR_FORMAT(fmt) | A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_MASK(0xf) | A6XX_RB_2D_BLIT_CNTL_IFMT(ifmt);
}

// --- a UBO descriptor: what an ldc reads through (fd6_emit_ubos, fd6_const.cc:266-296) ------------------------------------
// two dwords per UBO, loaded as ST6_UBO into the stage's shader block from the packet (8 bytes a unit): the address,
// and in the high dword the size in vec4 (A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE, bits 17..31 above the address's 17 high bits)
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE__MASK = 0xfffe0000;                                // a6xx.xml.h:11544
inline constexpr uint32_t A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE__SHIFT = 17;                                       // a6xx.xml.h:11545
constexpr uint32_t A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE(uint32_t v) { return field(v, A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE__SHIFT, A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE__MASK); }
inline constexpr uint32_t kUboMaxVec4 = A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE__MASK >> A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE__SHIFT;   // not-in-headers: the 15-bit field's largest size
constexpr void uboDescriptor(uint64_t address, uint32_t sizeVec4, uint32_t out[2]) {
    out[0] = uint32_t(address);
    out[1] = uint32_t(address >> 32) | A6XX_UBO_1_SIZE(sizeVec4);
}

}  // namespace hakios::metal::a6xx

```

`hakios-metal/include/hakios-metal/command.hpp`:

```hpp
// Metal's command model on the GPU: a queue, the command buffers committed to it in order, and the blit work the
// command processor can do on its own. It is what MTLCommandQueue, MTLCommandBuffer and MTLBlitCommandEncoder are
// in the plug-in (objc/), and it is testable without them.
//
//   CommandQueue        a submission queue of the driver's own; its command buffers complete in commit order, and
//                       a thread of its own waits for their fences and runs their completed handlers in that order
//   CommandBuffer       Metal's states (not enqueued, enqueued, committed, scheduled, completed, error); its
//                       packets go into a buffer of the queue's (returned to the queue once the GPU is done with it)
//   BlitEncoder         copy and fill of buffers, by the command processor: CP_MEMCPY and CP_MEM_WRITE (pm4.hpp).
//                       Offsets and lengths are in bytes and must be multiples of 4: the command processor moves
//                       words. Metal on macOS asks the same of copies; a blit that is not aligned is refused with
//                       the reason, and the command buffer ends in the error state, as Metal's does on a bad blit.
#pragma once

#include <atomic>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstdint>
#include <deque>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <algorithm>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

#include "hakios-metal/compute.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/render.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/gpu.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/pm4.hpp"

namespace hakios::metal {

class CommandQueue;
class Texture;

// a buffer a program sees: a GEM object with its length (MTLBuffer's -length may be less than the object's size)
class Buffer {
public:
    Buffer(std::unique_ptr<Bo> bo, uint64_t length) : bo_(std::move(bo)), length_(length) {}
    uint64_t length() const { return length_; }
    void* contents() const { return bo_->cpu(); }
    uint64_t gpuAddress() const { return bo_->gpuAddress(); }
    const Bo& bo() const { return *bo_; }

private:
    std::unique_ptr<Bo> bo_;
    uint64_t length_;
};

std::shared_ptr<Buffer> newBuffer(Gpu& gpu, uint64_t length, std::string* why);
// the live Buffer whose memory holds GPU address ADDRESS, and *OFFSET its offset in it; nullptr when none does. An
// argument buffer names a buffer member by the address it was encoded with (setBuffer:offset:atIndex:, or the
// gpuAddress an application writes itself), and this is how the draw finds the Buffer to bind and keep.
std::shared_ptr<Buffer> bufferAt(uint64_t address, uint64_t* offset);
// IOSurface SURFACE_ID's memory as a Buffer, *INFO what the kernel says of the surface. One Buffer per surface while it
// lives: a second ask for the same surface gets the same Buffer (the kernel's handle for it is one), so that the
// handle is closed once, by the last owner. nullptr with *why.
std::shared_ptr<Buffer> surfaceBuffer(Gpu& gpu, uint32_t surfaceId, SurfaceInfo* info, std::string* why);

class CommandBuffer : public std::enable_shared_from_this<CommandBuffer> {
public:
    enum Status { kNotEnqueued, kEnqueued, kCommitted, kScheduled, kCompleted, kError };

    Status status() const { return status_.load(); }
    const std::string& error() const { return error_; }

    // run after completion (or error), on the queue's thread, in the order of commit; only before commit
    void addCompletedHandler(std::function<void(CommandBuffer&)> handler);
    void enqueue();
    void commit();
    void waitUntilCompleted();
    // how long the GPU had it: from commit to the fence, in nanoseconds (Metal's GPUStartTime..GPUEndTime, roughly)
    int64_t gpuNanoseconds() const { return completedAt_ - committedAt_; }

    // --- the blit encoder's work, recorded into this command buffer ---
    bool copy(const Buffer& from, uint64_t fromOffset, const Buffer& to, uint64_t toOffset, uint64_t length);
    bool fill(const Buffer& buffer, uint64_t offset, uint64_t length, uint8_t value);
    // --- the compute encoder's work (compute.hpp): KERNEL over GROUPS work groups of LOCAL threads each (nullptr:
    // the kernel's own size), BUFFERS bound by index, IMMEDIATES in place of the kernel's constants (nullptr: its own).
    // The program and the descriptors go into buffers of their own that live until this completes.
    bool dispatch(const Kernel& kernel, const uint32_t groups[3], const uint32_t* local, const std::vector<Binding>& buffers,
                  const uint32_t* immediates = nullptr, const compute::Options& options = compute::Options{});
    // the same with textures and samplers (compute.hpp: Bindings); the textures' memory is used and kept as buffers are
    bool dispatch(const Kernel& kernel, const uint32_t groups[3], const uint32_t* local, const Bindings& bindings,
                  const uint32_t* immediates = nullptr, const compute::Options& options = compute::Options{});
    // the group counts three 32-bit words in ARGS at OFFSET (a multiple of 4), read when the GPU runs it
    bool dispatchIndirect(const Kernel& kernel, const Buffer& args, uint64_t offset, const uint32_t* local, const Bindings& bindings,
                          const uint32_t* immediates = nullptr, const compute::Options& options = compute::Options{});
    // --- the render encoder's work (render.hpp): one draw of PROGRAM into PASS's colour target, one complete pass per
    // call (begin, state, draw, end). The two programs' words and the pass's table go into buffers of their own that live
    // until this completes; the target's memory is used for write and kept. False with the reason recorded (render::encode's).
    bool draw(const Program& program, const RenderPass& pass, const Draw& draw, const Bindings& vsBindings, const Bindings& fsBindings,
              const render::Options& options = render::Options{});
    // a pass with no draw whose load action is Clear (render::encodeClear): the target filled with the clear colour, a
    // complete pass of its own. What an encoder that recorded no draw needs at its end; anything else is refused.
    bool clear(const RenderPass& pass, const render::Options& options = render::Options{});
    // -copyFromTexture:...toTexture:... and the scaled copies under it: rectangle S of SRC's mip level SL into rectangle D
    // of DST's level DL by the 2D engine, a pass of its own (render::encodeBlit says what it takes)
    bool blit(const Texture& src, uint32_t srcLevel, render::BlitRect s, const Texture& dst, uint32_t dstLevel, render::BlitRect d, bool linear,
              const render::Options& options = render::Options{});
    // the compressed textures among B's sampled ones made current (Texture::staging); a draw and a dispatch do it first
    bool freshen(const Bindings& b, const render::Options& options = {});
private:
    bool blitInto(const Texture& src, uint32_t srcLevel, render::BlitRect s, const Texture& dst, uint32_t dstLevel, render::BlitRect d, bool linear,
                  const render::Options& options);
public:
    // -generateMipmapsForTexture:: every level past 0 made from the one above it, halved with linear filtering, in order
    bool generateMipmaps(const Texture& texture, const render::Options& options = render::Options{});
    // a blit the caller could not record (a buffer not in the GPU's memory, say): the buffer ends in the error state
    void refuse(const std::string& why) { fail(why); }
    // a buffer it uses, kept alive until it completes (the owner may let go of it before that)
    void keep(std::shared_ptr<const Buffer> b) { kept_.push_back(std::move(b)); }
    // anything else it uses (a compiled kernel's words), the same way
    void keepAlive(std::shared_ptr<const void> p) { keptAny_.push_back(std::move(p)); }
    // OTHER's recorded work after this one's, as if it had been recorded here: its packets, what it names and what it
    // keeps alive -- a parallel render encoder's sub-encoders each record into a command buffer of their own, from any
    // thread in any order, and are appended in the order they were made. OTHER is left empty and is not committed; an
    // error it ended in is this one's. False after commit (of either).
    bool append(CommandBuffer& other);
    // What becomes of a draw, dispatch, copy or clear the encoder refuses (a binding it cannot serve, a shape it does not
    // take): by default the command buffer ends in error with the reason, as every test here expects; with skipRefused
    // that one piece of work is left out, counted and its reason kept, and the rest of the buffer still runs. Apple's
    // driver validates nothing and runs a frame whatever is wrong in it; a game whose every frame has one dispatch this
    // does not serve otherwise shows nothing at all (Resident Evil 4). Running out of memory, or work after commit,
    // still fails the buffer either way.
    void setSkipRefused(bool on) { skipRefused_ = on; }
    uint32_t skipped() const { return skipped_; }
    const std::string& lastSkipped() const { return lastSkipped_; }
    // the encoder's refusal of one piece of work, by the rule above: false either way
    bool refuseWork(const std::string& why);
    // What the buffer holds, counted as it is recorded: passes opened (each a pass start, its flushes and the wait for
    // idle at its tail, which is a fixed cost whatever is drawn), the draws in them, and dispatches, copies and clears
    // (each a pass of its own). What a frame's GPU time goes to is read off these beside the time (metal_fps).
    struct Counts { uint32_t passes = 0, draws = 0, dispatches = 0, copies = 0, clears = 0, gmemPasses = 0, tiles = 0, binnedPasses = 0; };   // (gmemPasses of the passes drawn in tiles, binnedPasses of those binned)
    const Counts& counts() const { return counts_; }
    // With profiling on, the command processor writes its always-on counter (CP_ALWAYS_ON_COUNTER, 19.2 MHz) at the start
    // of each pass and after its tail -- whose wait for idle makes the end the end -- for the first kMaxProfiled passes:
    // what each costs, beside what it was (a draw pass with its target's size and its draws, a copy, a clear, a
    // dispatch). Read once the buffer has completed. metal_fps names a frame's slowest passes with it.
    enum PassKind : uint32_t { kPassDraw = 0, kPassCopy = 1, kPassClear = 2, kPassDispatch = 3 };
    struct PassTime { PassKind kind; uint32_t width, height, draws; double us; uint32_t tiles = 0; uint64_t tuneKey = 0; uint8_t attached = 0, touched = 0; std::string sysmemWhy; };   // ATTACHED / TOUCHED: the colour attachments set, and those its draws wrote or read (a GMEM pass's)   // tiles 0: in sysmem; tuneKey: CommandQueue::preferGmem's
    static constexpr uint32_t kMaxProfiled = 64;
    void setProfile(bool on) { profile_ = on; }
    // ...and each draw of a sysmem pass on its own, the first kMaxProfiledDraws: a wait for idle before it and after it,
    // the counter at both (so the draws no longer overlap: what each costs alone), with its program's name. Which
    // draws of a heavy frame are heavy is read off these (metal_fps=draws).
    struct DrawTime { std::string name; double us; uint32_t pass = 0, area[4] = {}; };   // PASS: its pass among passTimes'; AREA render::drawArea's
    static constexpr uint32_t kMaxProfiledDraws = 512;
    void setProfileDraws(bool on) { profileDraws_ = on; }
    std::vector<DrawTime> drawTimes() const;
    // render::Options::gmem for this buffer's draws besides each draw's own (both must allow it): the C API's switch
    void setGmem(bool on) { gmem_ = on; }
    // GMEM's refinements off, for a bisect on the phone: kGmemWholeArea tiles the whole window whatever the draws touch,
    // kGmemEveryAttachment loads and stores every attachment, kGmemFetchBarrier orders a fetch by the barrier
    enum : uint32_t { kGmemWholeArea = 1, kGmemEveryAttachment = 2, kGmemFetchBarrier = 4 };
    void setGmemOff(uint32_t bits) { gmemOff_ = bits; }
    // GMEM or sysmem for each pass by CommandQueue::preferGmem (each pass stamped for it) rather than GMEM whenever a
    // pass can have it: what the plug-in asks; off by default, so that a test gets the mode it asks for
    void setGmemTuned(bool on) { tuning_ = on; }
    // GMEM for a pass of at least DRAWS draws, sysmem for one of fewer; 0: not by the draws. The draws are counted as
    // they come, so the pass is recorded both ways until it closes. SpringBoard's passes of 63 to 161 draws took 13 to
    // 22 ms in GMEM against 17 to 31 in sysmem, its passes of 45 to 49 draws 8 to 10 against 6 to 8, its light ones 5
    // against 0.13.
    void setGmemMinDraws(uint32_t draws) { gmemMinDraws_ = draws; }
    // render::Options::gmemBinning for this buffer's draws besides each draw's own (either asks for it)
    void setGmemBinning(bool on) { gmemBinning_ = on; }
    // every fragment texture the null texture (1x1, always in the texture cache): wrong pictures, but a draw's time then
    // says what its shader costs without its texture reads -- a measurement switch, as setGmemOff is a bisect's
    void setNullFsTextures(bool on) { nullFsTextures_ = on; }
    // why the last pass that could not be drawn in GMEM was not (gmemPlan's or gmemDrawOk's reason), empty when none was refused
    const std::string& gmemRefusal() const { return gmemWhy_; }
    // the words recorded so far (what the command processor will read)
    size_t streamWords() const { return stream_.words().size(); }
    std::vector<PassTime> passTimes() const;
    // why profiled pass I of a draw was drawn in sysmem ("" for a GMEM pass, or one not profiled); valid while the buffer lives
    const char* passSysmemWhy(size_t i) const { return i < profiled_.size() ? profiled_[i].sysmemWhy.c_str() : ""; }

private:
    friend class CommandQueue;
    explicit CommandBuffer(CommandQueue& queue) : queue_(queue) {}
public:
    ~CommandBuffer();   // (its stamp buffers back to the queue: read until the last reader lets go, which is now)
private:
    bool fail(const std::string& why);
    bool skipRefused_ = false;
    Counts counts_;
    bool profile_ = false;
    bool tuning_ = false;     // setGmemTuned's (cleared by a failed stamp buffer too)
    bool profileDraws_ = false;
    std::vector<DrawTime> drawsProfiled_;
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> drawStamps_;
    void drawStamp(uint32_t slot);
    bool gmem_ = true;
    uint32_t gmemOff_ = 0;
    uint32_t gmemMinDraws_ = 0;
    bool gmemBinning_ = false;
    bool nullFsTextures_ = false;
    uint32_t gmemClears_ = 0, gmemClearWords_[kMaxColorOutputs][4] = {};   // (draw's, for the pass it opens)
    std::string gmemWhy_;
    std::unordered_map<uint64_t, uint32_t> ordinals_;   // passes opened so far into each kind of target
    std::vector<PassTime> profiled_;   // as recorded; us filled in by passTimes from the stamps
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> profileStamps_;
    // the counter into stamp slot SLOT (two a pass: start, end), when profiling and there is room
    void stamp(uint32_t slot);
    void stampStart(PassKind kind, uint32_t width, uint32_t height);
    void stampEnd();
    uint32_t skipped_ = 0;
    std::string lastSkipped_;
    // dispatch and dispatchIndirect: GROUPS, or (GROUPS null) the counts at OFFSET of ARGS
    bool dispatchAny(const Kernel& kernel, const uint32_t* groups, const Buffer* args, uint64_t offset, const uint32_t* local, const Bindings& bindings,
                     const uint32_t* immediates, const compute::Options& options);
    // the end of it, however it ends: the status, the handlers (which see that status), and only then the waiters
    void finish(Status s);
    void use(const Buffer& b, bool write) { uses_.push_back(BoUse{&b.bo(), write}); }
public:
    // What each register written in a pass holds, for appendDeduped: a draw writes some 500 of them and almost all
    // hold their value already, so each is looked up once, in an open-addressed table of its own (std::unordered_map's
    // find and insert, two lookups and a node a register, were most of a draw's 20 us of deduplication on the phone)
    class RegShadow {
    public:
        // whether REG held VALUE; it holds VALUE from now on
        bool hold(uint32_t reg, uint32_t value) {
            if (keys_.empty() || 2 * (used_ + 1) > keys_.size()) grow();
            const size_t mask = keys_.size() - 1;
            for (size_t i = (reg * 2654435761u) & mask;; i = (i + 1) & mask) {
                if (keys_[i] == reg) {
                    const bool same = values_[i] == value;
                    values_[i] = value;
                    return same;
                }
                if (keys_[i] == kEmpty) {
                    keys_[i] = reg;
                    values_[i] = value;
                    used_++;
                    return false;
                }
            }
        }
        void clear() {
            std::fill(keys_.begin(), keys_.end(), kEmpty);
            used_ = 0;
        }
    private:
        static constexpr uint32_t kEmpty = ~0u;
        void grow() {
            std::vector<uint32_t> keys = std::move(keys_), values = std::move(values_);
            keys_.assign(std::max<size_t>(1024, keys.size() * 2), kEmpty);
            values_.assign(keys_.size(), 0);
            used_ = 0;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < keys.size(); i++) {
                if (keys[i] != kEmpty) hold(keys[i], values[i]);
            }
        }
        std::vector<uint32_t> keys_, values_;
        size_t used_ = 0;
    };

private:
    // the pass draws are joining (render.cpp: draw), closed by its tail before anything else is recorded or it is submitted
    struct OpenPass {
        RenderPass pass;
        render::Options options;
        uint64_t table;   // the GPU address of the pass's table: a piece (below), kept by the command buffer
        RegShadow regs;   // what each register written in the pass holds (render.cpp: appendDeduped)
        std::vector<uint8_t> staticKey;   // what decided the last draw's program-and-pass state (render.cpp: draw)
        // A pass drawn in GMEM (gmemPlan and every draw gmemDrawOk) is recorded rather than streamed: its draws gather
        // in BODIES, deduplicated among themselves from nothing (BODY_REGS) since each tile replays them after the
        // tile's own register writes, and closePass puts them in the tiles.
        bool gmem = false;
        render::GmemPlan plan;
        pm4::Stream bodies;
        RegShadow bodyRegs;
        // what the draws touch: the render area (X0 Y0 X1 Y1, the union of render::drawArea's) and the attachments they
        // write and read (a framebuffer fetch), as masks -- what closePass tiles, loads and stores
        uint32_t area[4] = {~0u, ~0u, 0, 0};
        uint32_t written = 0, read = 0;
        // Both ways at once (setGmemMinDraws): the draws gathered for tiles in BODIES and, beside them, as a sysmem pass in
        // SYS_STREAM (its head included, deduplicated through REGS), the GMEM head held in HEAD_GMEM; closePass takes the
        // one the pass's draws call for, now that they are known
        bool dual = false;
        pm4::Stream sysStream, headGmem;
        uint32_t clears = 0;        // the attachments a GMEM pass clears in its tiles (render::gmemClearWords), and their words
        uint32_t clearWords[kMaxColorOutputs][4] = {};
        uint64_t kind = 0;          // render::tuneKeyOf the pass and its ordinal in the buffer among passes of that kind
        uint32_t ordinal = 0, draws = 0;
        bool lastFetched = false;   // the last draw read its attachments (render::encodeInPass's AFTER_FETCH for the next)
    };
    void closePass();
    void useAttachments(const RenderPass& pass);
    std::unique_ptr<OpenPass> open_;
    // A piece of a larger buffer, for a draw's or a dispatch's table and a program's words. A buffer of its own for each
    // was three requests to the kernel for every draw, which on the phone cost about 200 us a draw (probe 9r) while the
    // GPU spent 3 us on it. A piece is the command buffer's: written once, used for writing, kept until completion.
    struct Piece {
        std::shared_ptr<Buffer> buffer;
        uint64_t offset = 0;
        uint64_t gpuAddress() const { return buffer->gpuAddress() + offset; }
        uint8_t* contents() const { return static_cast<uint8_t*>(buffer->contents()) + offset; }
    };
    bool piece(uint64_t bytes, Piece* out, std::string* why);
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> slab_;
    uint64_t slabUsed_ = 0;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Buffer>> slabs_;   // every slab this buffer took, given back to the queue when it is done
    // A program's words where they are already in this command buffer, so that every draw with the program does not
    // upload them again. Found by the caller's pointer, but taken only when the words still look the same: the pointer
    // is the caller's to free and reuse. They are compared at every 64th word and the last, not all: the whole compare,
    // once a draw, was 7-10 us of a draw's 50 on the phone, and CoreAnimation's uber shader is 31 000 words. (The copy
    // compared is a CPU one: reading the piece back is uncached memory.)
    struct Uploaded {
        std::vector<uint32_t> words;
        uint64_t gpuAddress;
    };
    // the GPU address of K's words in this buffer, uploading them when they are not there; 0 with *WHY when out of memory
    uint64_t programAddress(const Kernel& k, std::string* why);
    std::unordered_multimap<const uint32_t*, Uploaded> uploaded_;

    CommandQueue& queue_;
    std::atomic<Status> status_{kNotEnqueued};
    std::string error_;
    pm4::Stream stream_;
    std::vector<BoUse> uses_;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const Buffer>> kept_;   // the buffers it uses stay alive until it completes
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const void>> keptAny_;
    std::vector<std::function<void(CommandBuffer&)>> handlers_;
    std::mutex lock_;
    std::condition_variable done_;
    bool finished_ = false;                             // (under lock_) the handlers have run: waitUntilCompleted returns
    uint32_t fence_ = 0;
    uint64_t faultsAtCommit_ = 0;                       // the GPU's reset count then: one more by completion = given up, not run
    std::unique_ptr<Bo> commands_;
    int64_t committedAt_ = 0, completedAt_ = 0;
};

class CommandQueue {
public:
    // a queue of its own with the driver; nullptr with *why when the driver has none to give
    static std::unique_ptr<CommandQueue> make(Gpu& gpu, std::string* why);
    ~CommandQueue();

    std::shared_ptr<CommandBuffer> commandBuffer();
    Gpu& gpu() { return gpu_; }
    // the buffers kept for command streams, idle (to see that they are given back and used again)
    size_t idleCommandBuffers();
    // What a draw binds at the slot the front end reserves for Metal's null texture (Kernel: KernelTexture::isNull): a
    // 1x1 RGBA8Unorm texture of zeros, made at the first ask, the same for every draw of the queue. Zero is an
    // assumption, not a reading -- nothing reachable says what Apple's null texture samples as (nir_air.h) -- and this
    // is the one place it lives; a probe may write the texel to see which instructions read it. nullptr with *why.
    std::shared_ptr<Texture> nullTexture(std::string* why);
    // Private memory for a stage that wants BYTES a fiber in the PERWAVE layout: one buffer for every program of the
    // queue, as turnip keeps one a device (tu_setup_pvtmem, tu_shader.cc:2132-2190) -- a buffer a pipeline is 4 MiB for
    // 512 bytes a fiber on this GPU -- grown to the next power of two when a program wants more. A grown-out buffer is
    // kept as long as the queue: a draw recorded against it may still be in flight. The buffer and *OUT its layout;
    // nullptr with *why.
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> privateMemory(uint32_t bytes, bool perWave, PrivateMemory* out, std::string* why);
    // GMEM or sysmem for a pass into the target at KEY (its memory's address), by what the GPU spent on such passes:
    // each mode's time kept as a running average from the passes' own counter stamps (tuned), the cheaper one taken,
    // the other tried again now and then, sysmem tried first and GMEM next -- turnip's autotune, by time instead of samples.
    // GMEM is no gain for a pass that touches a corner of the screen (its tiles load and store the whole target: 23
    // draws of CoreAnimation took 5 ms so, 0.1 ms in sysmem), nor for one of framebuffer fetches (the texture unit
    // reads GMEM at a quarter of the rate it reads memory: probe "full-screen cost").
    // the visibility streams' memory binned GMEM passes share (render::vscBytes): one is enough, the GPU running one
    // submission at a time and each pass's binning before its tiles; nullptr with *why
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> vscBuffer(std::string* why);
    // K's words in a buffer of their own, made the first time a command buffer of this queue draws with them and kept
    // for the next: copying them into each command buffer was most of a draw's first cost (CoreAnimation's uber shader is
    // 124 KB, into write-combined memory). Found by the words' pointer and taken only when every word is the same -- a
    // freed program's pointer may come back with other words, and then its entry goes. nullptr with *why.
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> programBuffer(const Kernel& k, std::string* why);
    // A slab for draw tables (CommandBuffer::piece): one a completed command buffer gave back, zeroed as a new one comes,
    // or a new one. The kernel's making of a 256 KB buffer, once every 32 draws, was most of a draw's CPU time on the
    // phone (40 us a draw on a fast core, where the same encoding on the host takes 5).
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> takeSlab(uint64_t bytes, std::string* why);
    void giveSlabs(std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Buffer>>* slabs);
    // ...and any other buffer a command buffer makes for itself (a large piece, its counter stamps): BYTES rounded up to
    // a power of two from 4 KB, zeroed; given back the same way, 32 MB of them kept at most
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> takeBuffer(uint64_t bytes, std::string* why);
    void giveBuffer(std::shared_ptr<Buffer> b);
    // whether GMEM passes may still be binned: no pass's visibility streams have overrun their pitch (render::kVscOverflowAt,
    // read by checkVsc once a buffer with a binned pass has completed)
    bool binningOk() const { return !vscOverflowed_.load(); }
    void checkVsc();
    bool preferGmem(uint64_t key);
    void tuned(uint64_t key, bool gmem, double us);
    // What tells passes into one kind of target apart: the draws the pass at that place in a command buffer (the Nth into
    // this kind of target) had the last time, which preferGmem's key takes in as a class (a frame of CoreAnimation is
    // the same passes in the same order as the one before it, light or heavy). 0 when not seen yet.
    uint32_t lastDraws(uint64_t kind, uint32_t ordinal);
    // ...and the most it had in the times since its peak, the peak let go after 16 times below it: a pass that is heavy
    // only now and then (CoreAnimation's: light frames between the heavy ones of an animation) counts as heavy
    uint32_t peakDraws(uint64_t kind, uint32_t ordinal);
    void noteDraws(uint64_t kind, uint32_t ordinal, uint32_t draws);


private:
    friend class CommandBuffer;
    CommandQueue(Gpu& gpu, uint32_t id) : gpu_(gpu), id_(id) {}
    void submit(std::shared_ptr<CommandBuffer> cb);
    void waiter();
    std::unique_ptr<Bo> takeCommandBo(size_t bytes, int* error);

    Gpu& gpu_;
    std::shared_ptr<Texture> null_;   // (under lock_) nullTexture's
    std::shared_ptr<Buffer> vsc_;     // (under lock_) vscBuffer's
    // (under poolLock_, a lock of its own: a command buffer gives its stamps back as it is destroyed, which can be under
    // lock_ -- the queue letting go of the last one in flight -- and lock_ there was the window server hung at boot)
    std::mutex poolLock_;
    std::unordered_map<uint64_t, std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Buffer>>> freeBuffers_;   // by size: giveSlabs', giveBuffer's
    uint64_t freeBytes_ = 0;
    struct Resident { std::vector<uint32_t> words; std::shared_ptr<Buffer> buffer; };
    std::unordered_multimap<const uint32_t*, Resident> resident_;   // (under lock_) programBuffer's
    uint64_t residentBytes_ = 0;
    std::atomic<bool> vscOverflowed_{false};
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Buffer>> private_[2];   // (under lock_) privateMemory's, by layout, the last the current one
    uint32_t privatePerFiber_[2] = {0, 0};
    uint32_t id_;
    std::mutex lock_;
    struct Tune { double us[2] = {0, 0}; uint32_t runs[2] = {0, 0}; uint32_t passes = 0; };
    std::unordered_map<uint64_t, Tune> tune_;   // (under lock_) preferGmem's, by target
    std::unordered_map<uint64_t, uint32_t> lastDraws_;   // (under lock_) noteDraws', by kind and ordinal
    struct Peak { uint32_t draws = 0, below = 0; };
    std::unordered_map<uint64_t, Peak> peakDraws_;        // (under lock_) noteDraws' too: peakDraws'
    std::condition_variable changed_;
    std::deque<std::shared_ptr<CommandBuffer>> inFlight_;
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Bo>> idle_;
    bool quit_ = false;
    std::thread thread_;
};

}  // namespace hakios::metal
```

`hakios-metal/include/hakios-metal/compiler.hpp`:

```hpp
// The shader compiler inside the driver: AIR (the bitcode of one Metal function) to NIR by hakios's front end, NIR to
// ir3 by Mesa's compiler, for this chip, in this process. It is what turns a function of a .metallib into a Kernel the
// dispatch can run, on the host for the tests and on the phone for the image's own libraries, so that nothing of
// Apple's has to leave the phone to be compiled.
//
// It is the same road tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch gives Mesa's ir3_compiler, step for step (load_air, the three lowering
// passes the consumer owes, ir3_finalize_nir, the hand-built variant, ir3_compile_shader_nir, ir3_shader_assemble, the
// fields as the fixture writes them), so that a kernel compiled here is the fixture compiled there, byte for byte: the
// test says so for fill_id.ll against tests/fixtures/fill_id_air.hpp.
//
// A build without Mesa's libraries (make test with no MESA_BUILD) has this as a refusal by name, nothing else.
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "hakios-metal/kernel.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/render.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/texture.hpp"

namespace hakios::metal {

// what a kernel binds, as the front end read it off the function's metadata: the runtime's half of the match
struct Resource {
    enum Kind { kConstantBuffer, kDeviceBuffer, kThreadgroupBuffer, kTexture, kImage, kSampler } kind;
    uint32_t index;         // Metal's [[buffer(n)]], [[texture(n)]], [[sampler(n)]]
    uint32_t sizeBytes;     // air.buffer_size when the metadata gives one (a `constant T&`), else 0
    bool read, write;       // Apple's declaration (air.read, air.write, air.read_write)
    bool irWrite;           // whether the translated code stores through it, which is a different fact
    // textures, images and samplers (the other kinds leave these at their zeros): the shape the kernel's instructions
    // address the index with, as Kernel::textures[index] carries it, and what Apple declared it as (air.arg_type_name,
    // e.g. "texture2d<half, write>": the declaration is the one to judge a bound format by, the instructions' type is
    // the transport -- a half image is stored with a 16-bit stib into whatever format is bound)
    uint8_t textureDim;     // KernelTextureDim
    uint8_t textureArray;   // 1 for the array forms
    uint8_t element;        // KernelElement
    bool nullTexture;       // the front end's reserved slot for air.get_null_texture_*: not served by the dispatch yet
    bool inlineSampler;     // a constexpr sampler (air_resource.inline_sampler): its state below, bound by the runtime at INDEX
    std::string typeName;   // air.arg_type_name as declared
    // a member of an argument buffer (air_resource.argbuf_*): the set's own Metal [[buffer(n)]] and the member's byte
    // offset in it; INDEX is then the binding the front end allocated it, not a Metal index. ~0u: not a member
    uint32_t argbufSet = ~0u;
    uint32_t argbufOffset = 0;
};

// Argument buffers: every member among RESOURCES bound into B from what its set holds -- the eight bytes at the
// member's offset in the buffer bound at the set's Metal index, which MTLArgumentEncoder (or the application itself)
// wrote: a buffer's GPU address (bufferAt), a texture's or a sampler's resource id. Each lands at the member's own
// index; KEPT gets what must live until the GPU is done. The words are read now, on the processor: a set the GPU
// writes before this work runs is not seen. A zero word, or one naming nothing alive, leaves the slot empty -- the
// draw or dispatch then refuses it if the shader reads it. False with *why: a set not bound, or shorter than a member.
bool bindArgumentBuffers(const std::vector<Resource>& resources, Bindings* b, std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const void>>* kept, std::string* why);

// What MTLFunction's -newArgumentEncoderWithBufferIndex: lays out for the argument buffer at Metal [[buffer(SET)]] of
// the function in BITCODE: every member the set declares, used by the function or not, as (its [[id(n)]], its byte
// offset in the set), in id order. Metal's own answer comes from the reflection Apple's compiler writes, which no
// function here has; the front end reads the same members off the metadata (one air_resource each, whatever reads
// them), and only the front end runs. False with *why: the front end refused the function, or it has no set there.
bool argumentBufferLayout(const void* bitcode, size_t size, uint32_t set, std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>>* members, std::string* why);

// a kernel compiled here, owning what its Kernel points into
struct CompiledKernel {
    Kernel kernel{};
    std::vector<uint32_t> words;
    std::vector<uint32_t> immediates;
    std::vector<Resource> resources;
    // the constexpr samplers the function declares itself, made from the front end's decoded state at compile time:
    // the dispatch or draw puts each at its index (after the API's own samplers, where the front end placed it)
    std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, Sampler>> inlineSamplers;
    std::string name;       // the entry point's
    std::string listing;    // ir3's disassembly, for the record and for the eye
    uint32_t threadgroupBytes = 0;   // static threadgroup memory the kernel declares
    // a [[threadgroup(0)]] argument the encoder sizes: it starts threadgroupArgBase bytes in, past the static arrays
    bool hasThreadgroupArg = false;
    uint32_t threadgroupArgBase = 0;
};

// a vertex or fragment function compiled here (render.hpp's Stage), owning what its Stage points into
struct CompiledStage {
    Stage stage{};
    std::vector<uint32_t> words;
    std::vector<uint32_t> immediates;
    std::vector<Resource> resources;
    std::vector<std::string> varyingNames;   // the front end's names of the varyings, VS outputs or FS inputs, in slot order (VAR0 first)
    std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, Sampler>> inlineSamplers;   // as CompiledKernel's
    uint32_t iboBase = 0;                    // compileStage's IBO_BASE, as it took effect (0 for a stage with no device buffers)
    bool writesMemory = true;                // the NIR stores to or does atomics on a device buffer (or global memory); false only when it was looked at and does not
    std::string name;
    std::string listing;
};

// a VS and an FS linked for one colour format (render.hpp's Program), owning both stages
struct CompiledProgram {
    Program program{};
    std::shared_ptr<CompiledStage> vs, fs;
    std::string name;   // "vs+fs"
};

// whether a compiler is in this build
bool hasCompiler();

// A function constant's value as the pipeline supplies it (MTLFunctionConstantValues): INDEX is the module's
// [[function_constant(n)]], BITS the value as the bits of its type -- a bool 0 or 1, an integer or a float its own bits
// in the low end, a vector's component i at bit i * its width (nir_air.h: air_constant_value). A constant not supplied
// is told to the module as not defined (air.is_function_constant_defined) and reads as zero. An index the module does
// not declare is no error: Metal specialises a function with a pipeline's whole set, and the set may name others'.
struct FunctionConstant {
    uint32_t index;
    uint64_t bits;
};
using FunctionConstants = std::vector<FunctionConstant>;

// One AIR module holding a vertex or a fragment function, compiled for this chip: the lowering turnip runs
// (nir_lower_system_values, ir3_nir_lower_io_to_temporaries on variables, ir3_finalize_nir, ir3_nir_post_finalize --
// which does the nir_lower_io -- then ir3), the Stage filled from the variant (inputs, outputs, the sysval regids, the
// FS's ij/face/coord regids, colour outputs, flags). nullptr with *why: not a vertex or fragment function (a kernel goes
// through compileAir), the front end's or ir3's refusal by name, or no compiler in this build. The fixture writer
// (tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch) runs the same passes in the same order, so a Stage compiled here equals its fixture.
// IBO_BASE moves a fragment stage's device buffers that far up the 3D pipeline's one IBO table, past the vertex stage's
// (its [[buffer(n)]] addressed as slot IBO_BASE + n), so that the two stages' buffers at one index do not collide
// What a stage's constant buffer at [[buffer(BINDING)]] holds for the draws a stage is compiled for: its reads of that
// buffer at constant offsets inside BYTES compiled as those values, so that the branches they decide are decided once,
// here, rather than in every fragment. CoreAnimation's uber shader (fixed_frag_lph_cpf) picks its path through 15 000
// instructions by the 52 bytes of its FragmentShaderConfig: compiled for one configuration it is 16 to 48 instructions.
struct KnownBuffer {
    uint32_t binding = 0;
    std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
};
std::unique_ptr<CompiledStage> compileStage(const void* bitcode, size_t size, std::string* why, const FunctionConstants& constants = {},
                                           uint32_t iboBase = 0, const KnownBuffer* known = nullptr);
// compileStage's choice for a stage that spilled with ir3's preamble (WITH) and was compiled again without it (WITHOUT):
// the one that spills less, then the one with fewer registers; WITH on a tie. (CoreAnimation's fixed_frag_lph_cpf: 48
// registers and 512 bytes of spills with the preamble, 21 and none without; its draws 6.6 ms each so, 2.6 without.)
bool preferWithoutPreamble(const Kernel& with, const Kernel& without);

// VS and FS linked (render::link, and with Mesa present cross-checked against ir3_link_shaders) for a colour target of
// COLOR0's format. nullptr with *why: the refusals render.hpp names for a stage (attributes, several colour outputs,
// depth/stencil/sample-mask writes, framebuffer fetch, buffers/textures/samplers in either stage, a varying the VS does
// not write, a colour output class the format does not take, the pipeline constlen budget).
std::unique_ptr<CompiledProgram> linkProgram(std::shared_ptr<CompiledStage> vs, std::shared_ptr<CompiledStage> fs, PixelFormat color0,
                                             std::string* why);

// One AIR module (the bitcode of one function, as metallib.hpp hands it out, or a .bc) compiled for this chip.
// nullptr with *why: the front end's refusal, named by stage ("intrinsic: air.simd_sum not handled"), or ir3's, or
// "not a compute kernel", or that no compiler is in this build.
std::unique_ptr<CompiledKernel> compileAir(const void* bitcode, size_t size, std::string* why, const FunctionConstants& constants = {});

}  // namespace hakios::metal
```
