```cpp
                        fault("RM6_BIN_RENDER_END outside a tile");
                        return false;
                    }
                    inTile_ = false;
                }
                break;
            case CP_SET_BIN_DATA5_OFFSET: {
                // a tile's streams, at offsets from VSC_DRAW_STRM_ADDRESS, VSC_DRAW_STRM_SIZE_ADDRESS and VSC_PRIM_STRM_ADDRESS
                if (h.count != 4 || !inTile_ || at(reg64(REG_A6XX_VSC_DRAW_STRM_ADDRESS) + p[1], 4) == nullptr ||
                    at(reg64(REG_A6XX_VSC_DRAW_STRM_SIZE_ADDRESS) + p[2], 4) == nullptr || at(reg64(REG_A6XX_VSC_PRIM_STRM_ADDRESS) + p[3], 4) == nullptr) {
                    fault("CP_SET_BIN_DATA5_OFFSET not of 4 words, outside a tile, or its streams outside every buffer");
                    return false;
                }
                // The phone's command processor holds two tiles' streams: a third handed over before RM6_BIN_END_OF_DRAWS
                // let one go hangs it, its draws stuck in PC (probe --bin-trace: tiles 0 and 1 drew, 2 hung, the same
                // counted from the last tile)
                if (binQueued_ >= 2) {
                    fault("a third tile's streams with two not let go by RM6_BIN_END_OF_DRAWS: the phone hangs here");
                    return false;
                }
                binQueued_++;
                stats_.binData++;
                break;
            }
            case CP_COND_WRITE5: {
                // a register (POLL 0) or word compared with REF under MASK; the word at the write address set when true
                if (h.count != 8 || (p[0] & 7u) != WRITE_GE || ((p[0] >> 4) & 3u) != POLL_REGISTER || (p[0] & (1u << 8)) == 0) {
                    fault("CP_COND_WRITE5 not of 8 words or not a register's WRITE_GE into memory (the one form modelled)");
                    return false;
                }
                const uint32_t v = regs_[p[1] & 0xffffu] & p[4];
                if (v >= p[3]) {
                    uint8_t* to = at(p[5] | uint64_t(p[6]) << 32, 4);
                    if (to == nullptr) {
                        fault("CP_COND_WRITE5 into no buffer");
                        return false;
                    }
                    memcpy(to, &p[7], 4);
                }
                break;
            }
            case CP_SET_MODE:
            case CP_SKIP_IB2_ENABLE_GLOBAL:
            case CP_SKIP_IB2_ENABLE_LOCAL:
            case CP_SET_VISIBILITY_OVERRIDE:
                // one word each (tu_cmd_buffer.cc:2134-2142); what they do the XML does not say, so nothing is judged of the value
                if (h.count != 1) {
                    fault(text("opcode 0x%02llx of %llu words, not 1", h.opcode, h.count));
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            case CP_SET_DRAW_STATE: {
                // only the 3-word disable-all form both batch starts send (fd6_emit_restore; tu_disable_draw_states): this
                // driver writes its registers directly, and a state group with an address would apply at the draw over them
                if (h.count != 3 || (p[0] & CP_SET_DRAW_STATE__0_DISABLE_ALL_GROUPS) == 0 ||
                    fieldOf(p[0], CP_SET_DRAW_STATE__0_COUNT__MASK, CP_SET_DRAW_STATE__0_COUNT__SHIFT) != 0 || p[1] != 0 || p[2] != 0) {
                    fault("draw-state groups are not what this GPU model runs: registers are written directly (only CP_SET_DRAW_STATE's 3-word disable-all form is taken)");
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            }
            case CP_DRAW_INDIRECT_MULTI: {
                // one draw (DRAW_COUNT 1), its words read from memory as the packet runs (tu_CmdDrawIndirect's layout:
                // Vulkan's draw commands, Metal's indirect arguments): the CP sets VFD_INDEX_OFFSET and
                // VFD_INSTANCE_START_OFFSET from them and the draw goes on as CP_DRAW_INDX_OFFSET's would, checked the same
                const uint32_t op = p[1] & 0xfu;
                const bool indexed = op == INDIRECT_OP_INDEXED;
                if ((op != INDIRECT_OP_NORMAL && !indexed) || h.count != (indexed ? 9u : 6u) || p[2] != 1) {
                    fault(text("CP_DRAW_INDIRECT_MULTI of %llu words, opcode %llu, draw count %llu: one draw, NORMAL in 6 words or INDEXED in 9", h.count, op, p[2]));
                    return false;
                }
                const uint64_t a = indexed ? (p[6] | uint64_t(p[7]) << 32) : (p[3] | uint64_t(p[4]) << 32);
                const uint8_t* m = at(a, indexed ? 20 : 16);
                if (m == nullptr || a % 4 != 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_DRAW_INDIRECT_MULTI's arguments at %#llx: outside every buffer or not 4-aligned", a));
                    return false;
                }
                uint32_t w[5] = {};
                memcpy(w, m, indexed ? 20 : 16);
                if (indexed) {
                    // indexCount, instanceCount, firstIndex, vertexOffset, firstInstance
                    const uint32_t size = fieldOf(p[0], CP_DRAW_INDX_OFFSET_0_INDEX_SIZE__MASK, CP_DRAW_INDX_OFFSET_0_INDEX_SIZE__SHIFT) == INDEX4_SIZE_32_BIT ? 4 : 2;
                    const uint64_t base = (p[3] | uint64_t(p[4]) << 32) + uint64_t(w[2]) * size;
                    regs_[REG_A6XX_VFD_INDEX_OFFSET] = w[3];
                    regs_[REG_A6XX_VFD_INSTANCE_START_OFFSET] = w[4];
                    uint32_t d[7] = {p[0], w[1], w[0], 0, uint32_t(base), uint32_t(base >> 32), w[2] <= p[5] ? p[5] - w[2] : 0};
                    if (!execDraw(d, 7)) return false;
                } else {
                    // vertexCount, instanceCount, firstVertex, firstInstance
                    regs_[REG_A6XX_VFD_INDEX_OFFSET] = w[2];
                    regs_[REG_A6XX_VFD_INSTANCE_START_OFFSET] = w[3];
                    uint32_t d[3] = {p[0], w[1], w[0]};
                    if (!execDraw(d, 3)) return false;
                }
                break;
            }
            case CP_DRAW_INDX_OFFSET:
                if (!execDraw(p, h.count)) {
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            case CP_BLIT:
                if (!execBlit(p, h.count)) {
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            case CP_EVENT_WRITE: {
                // 1 word: the event; 4: and the address and value written when it completes (at once here: the model
                // is in order, so what a later wait reads is what an earlier event wrote)
                if (h.count != 1 && h.count != 4) {
                    fault(text("CP_EVENT_WRITE of %llu words, not 1 or 4", h.count));
                    return false;
                }
                // ZPASS_DONE: the running sample count, 64 bits, where RB_SAMPLE_COUNT_ADDR points, when
                // RB_SAMPLE_COUNT_CONTROL.COPY asks for it (turnip's occlusion query, A6XX path)
                if (h.count == 1 && fieldOf(p[0], CP_EVENT_WRITE_0_EVENT__MASK, CP_EVENT_WRITE_0_EVENT__SHIFT) == BLIT && !eventBlit()) {
                    return false;
                }
                if (h.count == 1 && fieldOf(p[0], CP_EVENT_WRITE_0_EVENT__MASK, CP_EVENT_WRITE_0_EVENT__SHIFT) == ZPASS_DONE) {
                    if ((reg(REG_A6XX_RB_SAMPLE_COUNT_CONTROL) & A6XX_RB_SAMPLE_COUNT_CONTROL_COPY) == 0) {
                        fault("ZPASS_DONE without RB_SAMPLE_COUNT_CONTROL.COPY: no count is written");
                        return false;
                    }
                    const uint64_t to = reg64(REG_A6XX_RB_SAMPLE_COUNT_ADDR);
                    uint8_t* d = at(to, 8);
                    if (d == nullptr || to % 8 != 0) {
                        fault(text("ZPASS_DONE's sample count at %#llx: outside every buffer or not 8-aligned", to));
                        return false;
                    }
                    memcpy(d, &samples_, 8);
                }
                if (h.count == 4) {
                    uint64_t to = p[1] | uint64_t(p[2]) << 32;
                    // With the TIMESTAMP bit the GPU writes a timestamp of its own, not the packet's value (the XML says so,
                    // and on the phone a wait for the value then never ended: 28 October, every dispatch); here a 64-bit
                    // count no wait for a small value can match, 8 bytes as the GPU's timestamp is.
                    bool timestamp = (p[0] & CP_EVENT_WRITE_0_TIMESTAMP) != 0;
                    uint8_t* d = at(to, timestamp ? 8 : 4);
                    if (d == nullptr || to % 4 != 0) {
                        fault(text("CP_EVENT_WRITE's timestamp at %#llx: outside every buffer", to));
                        return false;
                    }
                    if (timestamp) {
                        uint64_t ticks = 0x0001000000000000ull + stats_.packets;
                        memcpy(d, &ticks, 8);
                    } else {
                        memcpy(d, p + 3, 4);
                    }
                    // what a draw needs after it: the colour CCU flushed to memory (tu6_emit_flushes / fd6_emit_flushes: the
                    // 4-word form with an address, freedreno_gpu_event.h:60-85 needs_seqno) and then the cache flush
                    uint32_t ev = fieldOf(p[0], CP_EVENT_WRITE_0_EVENT__MASK, CP_EVENT_WRITE_0_EVENT__SHIFT);
                    if (ev == PC_CCU_FLUSH_COLOR_TS) drawsWithoutCcuFlush_ = 0;
                    if (ev == PC_CCU_FLUSH_DEPTH_TS) drawsWithoutDepthFlush_ = 0;
                    if (ev == CACHE_FLUSH_TS) drawsWithoutCacheFlush_ = 0;
                }
                break;
            }
            case CP_MEM_TO_MEM: {
                // the five-word form with no flags: one 32-bit word from SRC to DST (an indirect dispatch's counts
                // into its table, as turnip copies them, tu_cmd_buffer.cc:6723-6728)
                if (h.count == 5 && p[0] == 0) {
                    const uint64_t dst = p[1] | uint64_t(p[2]) << 32, src = p[3] | uint64_t(p[4]) << 32;
                    const uint8_t* from = at(src, 4);
                    uint8_t* to = at(dst, 4);
                    if (from == nullptr || to == nullptr || src % 4 != 0 || dst % 4 != 0) {
                        fault(text("CP_MEM_TO_MEM of a word from %#llx to %#llx: outside every buffer or not 4-aligned", src, dst));
                        return false;
                    }
                    memmove(to, from, 4);
                    break;
                }
                // DST = A + B + C over 64-bit values, each of A, B, C negated by its NEG flag (an occlusion query's result
                // += end - begin); 32-bit sums are not what this driver emits, and are refused
                if (h.count != 9 || (p[0] & CP_MEM_TO_MEM_0_DOUBLE) == 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_MEM_TO_MEM of %llu words or without DOUBLE: the 64-bit three-source form is what this model runs", h.count));
                    return false;
                }
                uint64_t addr[4], v[3];
                for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) addr[i] = p[1 + 2 * i] | uint64_t(p[2 + 2 * i]) << 32;
                for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
                    const uint8_t* m = at(addr[1 + i], 8);
                    if (m == nullptr || addr[1 + i] % 8 != 0) {
                        fault(text("CP_MEM_TO_MEM's source at %#llx: outside every buffer or not 8-aligned", addr[1 + i]));
                        return false;
                    }
                    memcpy(&v[i], m, 8);
                    if ((p[0] >> i) & 1) v[i] = uint64_t(0) - v[i];   // NEG_A, NEG_B, NEG_C
                }
                uint8_t* out = at(addr[0], 8);
                if (out == nullptr || addr[0] % 8 != 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_MEM_TO_MEM's destination at %#llx: outside every buffer or not 8-aligned", addr[0]));
                    return false;
                }
                const uint64_t sum = v[0] + v[1] + v[2];
                memcpy(out, &sum, 8);
                break;
            }
            case CP_WAIT_REG_MEM: {
                if (h.count != 6) {
                    fault(text("CP_WAIT_REG_MEM of %llu words, not 6", h.count));
                    return false;
                }
                if (fieldOf(p[0], CP_WAIT_REG_MEM_0_POLL__MASK, CP_WAIT_REG_MEM_0_POLL__SHIFT) != POLL_MEMORY) {
                    fault("CP_WAIT_REG_MEM on a register: not what this GPU model runs");
                    return false;
                }
                uint64_t a = p[1] | uint64_t(p[2]) << 32;
                const uint8_t* m = at(a, 4);
                if (m == nullptr || a % 4 != 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_WAIT_REG_MEM on %#llx: outside every buffer", a));
                    return false;
                }
                uint32_t value;
                memcpy(&value, m, 4);
                value &= p[4];
                uint32_t ref = p[3];
                bool holds = false;
                switch (fieldOf(p[0], CP_WAIT_REG_MEM_0_FUNCTION__MASK, CP_WAIT_REG_MEM_0_FUNCTION__SHIFT)) {
                case WRITE_ALWAYS: holds = true; break;
                case WRITE_LT: holds = value < ref; break;
                case WRITE_LE: holds = value <= ref; break;
                case WRITE_EQ: holds = value == ref; break;
                case WRITE_NE: holds = value != ref; break;
                case WRITE_GE: holds = value >= ref; break;
                case WRITE_GT: holds = value > ref; break;
                default: break;
                }
                if (!holds) {
                    // nothing after this packet can change the word, so the real command processor would spin forever
                    fault(text("CP_WAIT_REG_MEM would wait forever: the word at %#llx is %#llx, the reference %#llx", a, value, ref));
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            }
            case CP_REG_TO_MEM: {
                // what a profiled command buffer stamps: CP_ALWAYS_ON_COUNTER as one 64-bit value (CNT 2, 64B); the fake
                // writes a count of the stamps it has carried out, so that the order of two is the order they ran in
                if (h.count != 3) {
                    fault(text("CP_REG_TO_MEM of %llu words, not 3", h.count));
                    return false;
                }
                const uint32_t reg = p[0] & CP_REG_TO_MEM_0_REG__MASK;
                const uint64_t to = p[1] | uint64_t(p[2]) << 32;
                uint8_t* d = at(to, 8);
                if (reg != 0x0980 || !(p[0] & CP_REG_TO_MEM_0_64B) || d == nullptr || to % 8 != 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_REG_TO_MEM of register %#x to %#llx: the fake serves CP_ALWAYS_ON_COUNTER, 64-bit, into a buffer", reg, to));
                    return false;
                }
                const uint64_t now = ++alwaysOn_;
                memcpy(d, &now, 8);
                break;
            }
            case CP_WAIT_MEM_GTE: {
                if (h.count != 4) {
                    fault(text("CP_WAIT_MEM_GTE of %llu words, not 4", h.count));
                    return false;
                }
                uint64_t a = p[1] | uint64_t(p[2]) << 32;
                const uint8_t* m = at(a, 4);
                if (m == nullptr || a % 4 != 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_WAIT_MEM_GTE on %#llx: outside every buffer", a));
                    return false;
                }
                uint32_t value;
                memcpy(&value, m, 4);
                if (int32_t(value - p[3]) < 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_WAIT_MEM_GTE would wait forever: the word at %#llx is %#llx, below %#llx", a, value, p[3]));
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            }
            case CP_EXEC_CS:
                if (!execCs(p, h.count)) {
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            case CP_EXEC_CS_INDIRECT: {
                // the counts are read from memory as the packet runs, what is there then (written by the CPU or by an
                // earlier dispatch); the local size in word 3 must be NDRANGE_0's, which the dispatch also ran with
                if (h.count != 4) {
                    fault(text("CP_EXEC_CS_INDIRECT of %llu words, not 4", h.count));
                    return false;
                }
                const uint64_t a = p[1] | uint64_t(p[2]) << 32;
                const uint8_t* m = at(a, 12);
                if (m == nullptr || a % 4 != 0) {
                    fault(text("CP_EXEC_CS_INDIRECT's counts at %#llx: outside every buffer or not 4-aligned", a));
                    return false;
                }
                const uint32_t nd0 = reg(REG_A6XX_HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0);
                const uint32_t want = execCsIndirect3(fieldOf(nd0, A6XX_HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0_LOCALSIZEX__MASK, A6XX_HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0_LOCALSIZEX__SHIFT) + 1,
                                                      fieldOf(nd0, A6XX_HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0_LOCALSIZEY__MASK, A6XX_HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0_LOCALSIZEY__SHIFT) + 1,
                                                      fieldOf(nd0, A6XX_HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0_LOCALSIZEZ__MASK, A6XX_HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0_LOCALSIZEZ__SHIFT) + 1);
                if (p[3] != want) {
                    fault(text("CP_EXEC_CS_INDIRECT's local size word %#llx is not HLSQ_CS_NDRANGE_0's (%#llx)", p[3], want));
                    return false;
                }
                uint32_t w[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
                memcpy(w + 1, m, 12);
                if (!execCs(w, 4, true)) {
                    return false;
                }
                break;
            }
            default: {
                fault(text("opcode 0x%02llx is not one this GPU model runs", h.opcode));
                return false;
            }
            }
        }
        lastWasWfi_ = h.kind == pm4::Header::kCommand && h.opcode == pm4::kWaitForIdle;
        i += 1 + h.count;
    }
    return true;
}

// A submission the GPU never finishes, as the kernel treats it. With recovery, the GPU is reset and everything it
// had been given is given up as done: the fence word is set to the last submission's number (hakios_gpu_recover),
// so every wait ends, the hung submission's own with the timeout it was found by, and FAULTS says it happened.
// Without recovery nothing is waited for again in this run.
void FakeGpu::hung() {
    jobs_.clear();
    if (recovers_) {
        stats_.recoveries++;
        completed_ = submitted_;
    } else {
        wedged_ = true;
    }
}

void FakeGpu::run(const Job& job) {
    stats_.submits++;
    // a submission starts with nothing loaded and no pass begun: the hardware keeps no state across them that this models
    // (the registers it does keep, regs_, stay)
    cs_ = CsState{};
    vs_ = StageLoads{};
    fs_ = StageLoads{};
    gfxIbosLoaded_ = false;
    gfxIbosFrom_ = 0;
    gfxIboUnits_ = 0;
    passBegun_ = ccuCntlWritten_ = ccuCntlAfterWfi_ = lastWasWfi_ = inTile_ = binning_ = false;
    drawsInSubmission_ = drawsWithoutCcuFlush_ = drawsWithoutCacheFlush_ = drawsWithoutDepthFlush_ = 0;
    written_.clear();
    bool ok = execute(job.address, job.words, 0);
    if (ok && drawsInSubmission_ != 0) {
        // the colour a draw wrote sits in the CCU until PC_CCU_FLUSH_COLOR_TS (the kernel's own end-of-submit fence
        // flushes the UCHE, not the CCU: hakios.adreno.c:3496-3516), and what the CCU flushed sits in the UCHE until
        // CACHE_FLUSH_TS: a stream that draws and ends without both would complete with the target unchanged
        if (drawsWithoutCcuFlush_ != 0) {
            fault("the colour stays in the CCU: no PC_CCU_FLUSH_COLOR_TS (4-word) after the draw");
            ok = false;
        } else if (drawsWithoutDepthFlush_ != 0) {
            fault("the depth stays in the CCU: no PC_CCU_FLUSH_DEPTH_TS (4-word) after a draw that writes depth");
            ok = false;
        } else if (drawsWithoutCacheFlush_ != 0) {
            fault("the colour may stay in the cache: no CACHE_FLUSH_TS (4-word) after the draw");
            ok = false;
        }
        stats_.lastDraw.ccuFlushed = drawsWithoutCcuFlush_ == 0;
        stats_.lastDraw.cacheFlushed = drawsWithoutCacheFlush_ == 0;
    }
    if (ok) {
        completed_ = job.fence;
        return;
    }
    hungFences_.insert(job.fence);
    hung();
}

void FakeGpu::worker() {
    std::unique_lock<std::mutex> g(lock_);
    for (;;) {
        changed_.wait(g, [this] { return quit_ || (!paused_ && !jobs_.empty()); });
        if (quit_ && jobs_.empty()) {
            return;
        }
        if (paused_) {
            continue;
        }
        Job job = jobs_.front();
        jobs_.pop_front();
        if (delayUs_ != 0) {
            g.unlock();
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(delayUs_));
            g.lock();
        }
        run(job);
        changed_.notify_all();
    }
}

int FakeGpu::call(uint32_t request, void* data, size_t size) {
    std::unique_lock<std::mutex> g(lock_);
    switch (request) {
    case kGetParam: {
        if (size != sizeof(MsmParam)) return EINVAL;
        auto* p = static_cast<MsmParam*>(data);
        // the kernel's table (bsd/dev/hakios.adreno.c, hakios_gpu_parameter), number for number
        switch (p->param) {
        case kParamGpuId: p->value = 0; return 0;                   // "none, the chip ID says it"
        case kParamGmemSize: p->value = kGmemBytes; return 0;
        case kParamChipId: p->value = kChipId | kSpeedBin << 32; return 0;
        case kParamMaxFreq: p->value = kMaxFrequencyHz; return 0;
        case kParamTimestamp: p->value = uint64_t(nowNs()); return 0;
        case kParamGmemBase: p->value = 0; return 0;
        case kParamPriorities: p->value = 1; return 0;
        case kParamPpPgtable: p->value = 0; return 0;
        case kParamFaults: p->value = stats_.recoveries; return 0;
        case kParamSuspends: p->value = 0; return 0;
        case kParamHighestBankBit: p->value = 14; return 0;
        case kParamRaytracing: p->value = 0; return 0;
        case kParamUbwcSwizzle: p->value = 6; return 0;
        case kParamMacrotileMode: p->value = 1; return 0;
        default: return EINVAL;                                      // (kIOReturnBadArgument there: VA_START, VA_SIZE among them)
        }
    }
    case kGemNew: {
        if (size != sizeof(MsmGemNew)) return EINVAL;
        auto* n = static_cast<MsmGemNew*>(data);
        if (n->size == 0 || n->size > (256ull << 20)) return EINVAL;
        Buffer b{nextIova_, std::vector<uint8_t>(n->size)};
        nextIova_ += (n->size + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull;
        n->handle = nextHandle_++;
        buffers_.emplace(n->handle, std::move(b));
        return 0;
    }
    case kGemInfo: {
        if (size != sizeof(MsmGemInfo)) return EINVAL;
        auto* i = static_cast<MsmGemInfo*>(data);
        auto b = buffers_.find(i->handle);
        if (b == buffers_.end()) return ENOENT;
        if (i->info == kInfoGetIova) { i->value = b->second.iova; return 0; }
        if (i->info == kInfoGetOffset) { i->value = 0; return 0; }
        return EINVAL;
    }
    case kGemClose: {
        if (size != sizeof(DrmGemClose)) return EINVAL;
        const uint32_t handle = static_cast<DrmGemClose*>(data)->handle;
        auto sb = bufferSurface_.find(handle);
        if (sb != bufferSurface_.end()) {
            // the surface keeps its pixels: the buffer was a view of them
            Surface& s = surfaces_.at(sb->second);
            s.bytes = std::move(buffers_.at(handle).bytes);
            s.handle = 0;
            bufferSurface_.erase(sb);
        }
        return buffers_.erase(handle) ? 0 : ENOENT;
    }
    case kHakiosSurface: {
        if (size != sizeof(HakiosSurface)) return EINVAL;
        auto* r = static_cast<HakiosSurface*>(data);
        auto it = surfaces_.find(r->surface);
        if (it == surfaces_.end()) return ENOENT;          // kIOReturnNotFound
        Surface& s = it->second;
        if (s.client) return ENOTSUP;                      // kIOReturnUnsupported: memory of a program's own
        r->size = (uint64_t(s.offset) + uint64_t(s.rowBytes) * s.height + (s.planes == 2 ? uint64_t(s.rowBytes) * ((s.height + 1) / 2) : 0) + 0xfff) &
                  ~0xfffull;
        r->offset = s.offset;
        r->rowBytes = s.rowBytes;
        r->width = s.width;
        r->height = s.height;
        r->pixelFormat = s.pixelFormat;
        r->planes = s.planes;
        if (r->handle == kHakiosDescribe) {
            r->handle = 0;
            return 0;
        }
        if (s.handle != 0) {
            r->handle = s.handle;                          // the same buffer again, as the kernel answers it
            return 0;
        }
        s.bytes.resize(r->size);
        Buffer b{nextIova_, std::move(s.bytes)};
        nextIova_ += (r->size + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull;
        r->handle = s.handle = nextHandle_++;
        buffers_.emplace(r->handle, std::move(b));
        bufferSurface_[r->handle] = r->surface;
        return 0;
    }
    case kSubmitQueueNew: {
        if (size != sizeof(MsmSubmitQueue)) return EINVAL;
        auto* q = static_cast<MsmSubmitQueue*>(data);
        q->id = nextQueue_++;
        queues_.insert(q->id);
        return 0;
    }
    case kSubmitQueueClose:
        return 0;
    case kGemSubmit: {
        if (size != sizeof(MsmGemSubmit)) return EINVAL;
        auto* s = static_cast<MsmGemSubmit*>(data);
        if (s->nr_cmds != 1 || s->nr_bos == 0 || (s->queueid != 0 && queues_.count(s->queueid) == 0)) return EINVAL;
        auto* bos = reinterpret_cast<const MsmSubmitBo*>(uintptr_t(s->bos));
        auto* cmd = reinterpret_cast<const MsmSubmitCmd*>(uintptr_t(s->cmds));
        if (cmd->submit_idx >= s->nr_bos || cmd->type != kSubmitCmdBuf || cmd->size % 4 != 0) return EINVAL;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < s->nr_bos; i++) {
            if (buffers_.count(bos[i].handle) == 0) return ENOENT;   // a buffer the GPU would not know: refused
        }
        Buffer& c = buffers_.at(bos[cmd->submit_idx].handle);
        if (uint64_t(cmd->submit_offset) + cmd->size > c.bytes.size()) return EINVAL;
        Job job{++submitted_, c.iova + cmd->submit_offset, cmd->size / 4};
        s->fence = job.fence;
        // (a wedged GPU still takes submissions, as the kernel's ring does until it is full: they are never run)
        if (wedged_) {
            return 0;
        }
        if (async_) {
            jobs_.push_back(job);
            changed_.notify_all();
        } else {
            run(job);
        }
        return 0;
    }
    case kWaitFence: {
        if (size != sizeof(MsmWaitFence)) return EINVAL;
        auto* w = static_cast<MsmWaitFence*>(data);
        if (w->queueid != 0 && queues_.count(w->queueid) == 0) return EINVAL;
        if (w->fence > submitted_) {
            // The kernel does not know this fence was never handed out: it waits the caller's whole patience for a word
            // that never comes, and that is a hang like any other. Here it is one at once.
            fault("a fence that was never handed out was waited for");
            hung();
            return ETIMEDOUT;
        }
        if (wedged_ || hungFences_.count(w->fence) != 0) {
            // (the kernel takes the caller's whole patience to say so; the fake knows already)
            return ETIMEDOUT;
        }
        int64_t deadline = w->timeout.seconds * 1000000000 + w->timeout.nanoseconds;
        while (completed_ < w->fence) {
            int64_t left = deadline - nowNs();
            if (left <= 0) return ETIMEDOUT;
            changed_.wait_for(g, std::chrono::nanoseconds(left));
            if (wedged_ || hungFences_.count(w->fence) != 0) return ETIMEDOUT;
        }
        return 0;
    }
    case kGemCpuPrep:
    case kGemCpuFini:
        return 0;
    default:
        return ENOSYS;
    }
}

}  // namespace hakios::metal

```

`hakios-metal/src/gpu.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "hakios-metal/gpu.hpp"

#include <cerrno>
#include <cstring>

namespace hakios::metal {

namespace {
constexpr uint64_t kPage = 0x4000;  // Darwin's page; the driver rounds to its own (4 KB) inside it

MsmTimespec deadline(Transport& t, int64_t ns) {
    // the driver takes a deadline, not a length: a time of the clock that goes on while the machine sleeps
    // (mach_continuous_time, which is Darwin's CLOCK_MONOTONIC), as Linux's msm takes one of CLOCK_MONOTONIC
    if (ns < 0) {
        ns = 0;
    }
    int64_t at = t.nowNs() + ns;
    return MsmTimespec{at / 1000000000, at % 1000000000};
}
}  // namespace

int Gpu::param(uint32_t which, uint64_t* value) {
    MsmParam p{};
    p.pipe = kPipe3D;
    p.param = which;
    int e = t_->call(kGetParam, &p, sizeof(p));
    if (e == 0) {
        *value = p.value;
    }
    return e;
}

uint32_t Gpu::chipId() {
    uint64_t v = 0;
    return param(kParamChipId, &v) == 0 ? uint32_t(v) : 0;
}

uint64_t Gpu::faults() {
    uint64_t v = 0;
    return param(kParamFaults, &v) == 0 ? v : 0;
}

std::unique_ptr<Bo> Gpu::newBo(uint64_t size, uint32_t flags, int* error) {
    *error = 0;
    if (size == 0) {
        *error = EINVAL;
        return nullptr;
    }
    MsmGemNew n{};
    n.size = (size + kPage - 1) & ~(kPage - 1);
    n.flags = flags;
    if ((*error = t_->call(kGemNew, &n, sizeof(n))) != 0) {
        return nullptr;
    }
    MsmGemInfo info{};
    info.handle = n.handle;
    info.info = kInfoGetIova;
    if ((*error = t_->call(kGemInfo, &info, sizeof(info))) != 0) {
        DrmGemClose c{n.handle, 0};
        t_->call(kGemClose, &c, sizeof(c));
        return nullptr;
    }
    void* cpu = t_->map(n.handle, n.size);
    if (cpu == nullptr) {
        DrmGemClose c{n.handle, 0};
        t_->call(kGemClose, &c, sizeof(c));
        *error = ENOMEM;
        return nullptr;
    }
    std::unique_ptr<Bo> bo(new Bo(*this, n.handle, n.size, info.value, cpu));
    bo->counted_ = true;
    allocated_ += n.size;
    return bo;
}

std::unique_ptr<Bo> Gpu::surfaceBo(uint32_t surfaceId, SurfaceInfo* out, int* error) {
    HakiosSurface s{};
    s.surface = surfaceId;
    if ((*error = t_->call(kHakiosSurface, &s, sizeof(s))) != 0) {
        return nullptr;
    }
    MsmGemInfo info{};
    info.handle = s.handle;
    info.info = kInfoGetIova;
    if ((*error = t_->call(kGemInfo, &info, sizeof(info))) != 0) {
        DrmGemClose c{s.handle, 0};
        t_->call(kGemClose, &c, sizeof(c));
        return nullptr;
    }
    *out = SurfaceInfo{s.size, s.offset, s.rowBytes, s.width, s.height, s.pixelFormat, s.planes};
    return std::unique_ptr<Bo>(new Bo(*this, s.handle, s.size, info.value, t_->map(s.handle, s.size)));
}

void Gpu::disown(std::unique_ptr<Bo> bo) {
    if (bo == nullptr) return;
    if (bo->cpu_ != nullptr) {
        t_->unmap(bo->handle_, bo->cpu_);
        bo->cpu_ = nullptr;
    }
    bo->owned_ = false;
    if (bo->counted_) {
        allocated_ -= bo->size_;
        bo->counted_ = false;
    }
}

Bo::~Bo() { gpu_.release(*this); }

void Gpu::release(Bo& bo) {
    if (!bo.owned_) {
        return;
    }
    if (bo.counted_) {
        allocated_ -= bo.size_;
        bo.counted_ = false;
    }
    if (bo.cpu_ != nullptr) {
        t_->unmap(bo.handle_, bo.cpu_);
    }
    DrmGemClose c{bo.handle_, 0};
    t_->call(kGemClose, &c, sizeof(c));
}

int Gpu::newQueue(uint32_t priority, uint32_t* id) {
    MsmSubmitQueue q{0, priority, 0};
    int e = t_->call(kSubmitQueueNew, &q, sizeof(q));
    if (e == 0) {
        *id = q.id;
    }
    return e;
}

void Gpu::closeQueue(uint32_t id) {
    if (id != 0) {
        uint32_t q = id;
        t_->call(kSubmitQueueClose, &q, sizeof(q));
    }
}

int Gpu::submit(uint32_t queue, const Bo& commands, uint32_t offsetBytes, uint32_t words, const std::vector<BoUse>& uses,
                uint32_t* fence) {
    if (words == 0 || offsetBytes % 4 != 0 || offsetBytes + 4ull * words > commands.size()) {
        return EINVAL;
    }
    // the command buffer is the first of the buffers; the others follow it once each, read or written
    std::vector<MsmSubmitBo> bos;
    bos.push_back(MsmSubmitBo{kSubmitBoRead, commands.handle(), commands.gpuAddress()});
    for (const BoUse& u : uses) {
        if (u.bo == &commands) {
            continue;
        }
        bool seen = false;
        for (MsmSubmitBo& b : bos) {
            if (b.handle == u.bo->handle()) {
                b.flags |= u.write ? kSubmitBoWrite : kSubmitBoRead;
                seen = true;
            }
        }
        if (!seen) {
            bos.push_back(MsmSubmitBo{u.write ? kSubmitBoWrite : kSubmitBoRead, u.bo->handle(), u.bo->gpuAddress()});
        }
    }
    MsmSubmitCmd cmd{};
    cmd.type = kSubmitCmdBuf;
    cmd.submit_idx = 0;
    cmd.submit_offset = offsetBytes;
    cmd.size = words * 4;
    MsmGemSubmit s{};
    s.flags = kPipe3D;
    s.nr_bos = uint32_t(bos.size());
    s.nr_cmds = 1;
    s.bos = uint64_t(uintptr_t(bos.data()));
    s.cmds = uint64_t(uintptr_t(&cmd));
    s.fence_fd = -1;
    s.queueid = queue;
    int e = t_->call(kGemSubmit, &s, sizeof(s));
    if (e == 0) {
        *fence = s.fence;
    }
    return e;
}

int Gpu::wait(uint32_t queue, uint32_t fence, int64_t timeoutNs) {
    MsmWaitFence w{};
    w.fence = fence;
    w.timeout = deadline(*t_, timeoutNs);
    w.queueid = queue;
    return t_->call(kWaitFence, &w, sizeof(w));
}

int Gpu::cpuPrep(const Bo& bo, uint32_t op, int64_t timeoutNs) {
    MsmGemCpuPrep p{bo.handle(), op, deadline(*t_, timeoutNs)};
    return t_->call(kGemCpuPrep, &p, sizeof(p));
}

void Gpu::cpuFini(const Bo& bo) {
    MsmGemCpuFini f{bo.handle()};
    t_->call(kGemCpuFini, &f, sizeof(f));
}

}  // namespace hakios::metal
```

`hakios-metal/src/iokit_transport.cpp`:

```cpp
// The kernel's GPU driver (HakiosGPU) through its IOKit user client: the requests as struct-method calls whose
// selector is the request's number, and a buffer's memory as the client memory of the type that is its handle. The
// same as hakios's tools/mesa/hakios-drm/hakios.drm.c does for freedreno.
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>

#include <cerrno>
#include <cstdio>

#include "hakios-metal/gpu.hpp"

namespace hakios::metal {

namespace {

class KernelGpu : public Transport {
public:
    explicit KernelGpu(io_connect_t c) : c_(c) { mach_timebase_info(&timebase_); }
    ~KernelGpu() override { IOServiceClose(c_); }

    int call(uint32_t request, void* data, size_t size) override {
        size_t returned = size;
        kern_return_t r = IOConnectCallStructMethod(c_, request, data, size, data, &returned);
        switch (r) {
        case KERN_SUCCESS: return 0;
        case kIOReturnNoMemory: return ENOMEM;
        case kIOReturnBadArgument: return EINVAL;
        case kIOReturnTimeout: return ETIMEDOUT;
        case kIOReturnBusy: return EBUSY;
        case kIOReturnNotFound: return ENOENT;
        case kIOReturnUnsupported: return ENOSYS;
        default:
            // the kernel's own answer would be lost in a plain EIO: a code no case names is a failure nobody has
            // looked at yet, so it is printed where it happens
            fprintf(stderr, "hakios-metal: the driver's request %u answered %#x\n", request, unsigned(r));
            return EIO;
        }
    }

    void* map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t) override {
        mach_vm_address_t address = 0;
        mach_vm_size_t size = 0;
        // as the driver made the memory: write-combined, the way Linux hands it to freedreno
        if (IOConnectMapMemory64(c_, handle, mach_task_self(), &address, &size, kIOMapAnywhere) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
            return nullptr;
        }
        return reinterpret_cast<void*>(uintptr_t(address));
    }

    void unmap(uint32_t handle, void* address) override {
        IOConnectUnmapMemory64(c_, handle, mach_task_self(), mach_vm_address_t(uintptr_t(address)));
    }

    int64_t nowNs() override {
        // the driver's deadlines are of mach_continuous_time (drivers/gpu/hakios.gpu.cpp, millisecondsUntil)
        return int64_t(mach_continuous_time() * timebase_.numer / timebase_.denom);
    }

private:
    io_connect_t c_;
    mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase_{};
};

}  // namespace

std::unique_ptr<Transport> openKernelGpu(std::string* why) {
    io_service_t s = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("HakiosGPU"));
    if (s == 0) {
        *why = "no HakiosGPU service: the kernel has not started the GPU (gpu=1, the firmware in fw-gpu/, the phone)";
        return nullptr;
    }
    io_connect_t c = 0;
    kern_return_t r = IOServiceOpen(s, mach_task_self(), 0, &c);
    IOObjectRelease(s);
    if (r != KERN_SUCCESS) {
        *why = "HakiosGPU would not open: error " + std::to_string(r);
        return nullptr;
    }
    return std::unique_ptr<Transport>(new KernelGpu(c));
}

}  // namespace hakios::metal
```

`hakios-metal/src/link.cpp`:

```cpp
// render::link -- the VS to FS link as ir3_link_shaders computes it (Mesa 25.0.7, src/freedreno/ir3/ir3_shader.h:
// ir3_link_add at 1289-1308, ir3_link_shaders at 1311-1361), ported over the plain data of render.hpp's Stage so that a
// build without Mesa can compute it and a fixture can carry it; with MESA=1, compiler_test holds this port to Mesa's own
// function over the same two tables (src/compiler.cpp: linkProgram).
//
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
//
// What the link decides, and which register reads it (turnip tu6_emit_vpc, tu_pipeline.cc:890-1070; fd6_program.cc
// setup_stateobj's linkage block): the FRAGMENT stage's bary inputs set the VPC locations ("what the hw calls outloc
// is taken from the inloc of the frag shader", ir3_shader.h:729-735), each paired with the VERTEX output of the same
// slot for SP_VS_OUT_REG (regid, compmask) and SP_VS_VPC_DST_REG (loc); the position is appended after them at
// max_loc (VPC_VS_PACK.POSITIONLOC) with compmask 0xf; max_loc is the stride (VPC_VS_PACK / PC_VS_OUT_CNTL
// .STRIDE_IN_VPC); varmask, the FS's varying locations without the position's, is the complement of VPC_VAR_DISABLE;
// cnt is SP_VS_PRIMITIVE_CNTL.OUT.
//
// Where this port is stricter than Mesa: ir3_link_shaders gives an FS varying that no VS output serves the register
// regid(63, 0) (default_regid with pack_vs_out) and the FS then reads zeros through it -- a quiet black. Here that is
// refused by slot, so that a vertex function and a fragment function whose varyings do not match are told apart from
// a draw that happened. The COL/BFC fallback of ir3_find_output (ir3_shader.h:1197-1215, GL's two-sided colour) is
// not ported: hakios's front end assigns VARYING_SLOT_VAR0 + n to every Metal varying and never COL0/BFC0
// (air_to_nir.c translate_output / translate_input), so the fallback could never fire on a Stage from it.
#include "hakios-metal/render.hpp"

#include "hakios-metal/a6xx.hpp"

namespace hakios::metal::render {

namespace {

// gl_varying_slot numbers the Stage tables use (Mesa src/compiler/shader_enums.h:320, 359): POS is 0 and the generic
// varyings start at 32, VARn = 32 + n; the slots between are GL's fixed-function ones, which the front end never emits
constexpr uint8_t kVaryingSlotPos = 0;
constexpr uint8_t kVaryingSlotVar0 = 32;
constexpr uint8_t kVaryingSlotPsiz = 12;   // gl_varying_slot's VARYING_SLOT_PSIZ: a VS's [[point_size]]
constexpr uint8_t kVaryingSlotPntc = 25;   // [[point_coord]] (compiler.cpp lowers it to this input), filled by the VPC

// VPC_VARYING_INTERP_MODE's two-bit field per component: INTERP_SMOOTH 0, INTERP_FLAT 1, INTERP_ZERO 2, INTERP_ONE 3
// (a6xx.xml.h enum a6xx_varying_interp_mode); 16 components per register (tu_pipeline.cc tu6_emit_vpc_varying_modes)
constexpr uint32_t kInterpFlat = 1;
constexpr uint32_t kInterpZero = 2;
constexpr uint32_t kInterpOne = 3;
// VPC_VARYING_PS_REPL_MODE's: the point sprite's S and T (a6xx.xml.h enum a6xx_varying_ps_repl_mode)
constexpr uint32_t kPsReplS = 1;
constexpr uint32_t kPsReplT = 2;

std::string slotName(uint8_t slot) {
    if (slot == kVaryingSlotPos) return "POS";
    if (slot >= kVaryingSlotVar0) return "VAR" + std::to_string(slot - kVaryingSlotVar0);
    return "slot " + std::to_string(slot);
}

// util_last_bit over a compmask: how many components the mask spans, counting from .x
uint32_t lastBit(uint32_t mask) {
    uint32_t n = 0;
    while (mask != 0) {
        n++;
        mask >>= 1;
    }
    return n;
}

// ir3_find_output (ir3_shader.h:1190-1196), without the COL/BFC fallback (see the file comment)
int findOutput(const Stage& vs, uint8_t slot) {
    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < vs.numOutputs; j++) {
        if (vs.outputs[j].slot == slot) return int(j);
    }
    return -1;
}

// ir3_link_add (ir3_shader.h:1289-1308): the location's components into varmask, max_loc raised past them, and an
// entry in var[] when the VS has a register for it. False when var[] is full (ir3 asserts; here a refusal upstream).
bool linkAdd(Linkage& l, uint8_t slot, uint32_t regid, uint8_t compmask, uint8_t loc) {
    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < lastBit(compmask); j++) {
        uint32_t comploc = loc + j;
        l.varmask[comploc / 32] |= 1u << (comploc % 32);
    }
    uint32_t end = loc + lastBit(compmask);
    if (end > l.maxLoc) l.maxLoc = end;
    if (regid != a6xx::kRegidNone) {
        if (l.cnt >= kMaxStageOutputs) return false;
        l.var[l.cnt] = Linkage::Var{slot, uint8_t(regid), compmask, loc};
        l.cnt++;
    }
    return true;
}

bool refuse(std::string* why, const std::string& text) {
    if (why != nullptr) *why = text;
    return false;
}

}  // namespace

bool link(const Stage& vs, const Stage& fs, Linkage* out, std::string* why) {
    if (vs.kind != kStageVertex) return refuse(why, std::string(vs.k.name ? vs.k.name : "the first stage") + " is not a vertex stage");
    if (fs.kind != kStageFragment) return refuse(why, std::string(fs.k.name ? fs.k.name : "the second stage") + " is not a fragment stage");
    Linkage l{};
    // --- ir3_link_shaders' walk: the FS's bary inputs (ir3_next_varying: compmask && bary, ir3_shader.h:1222-1229),
    // each within total_in (:1338-1346; an input past it is a varying ir3 allocated and then found unread), each
    // paired with the VS output of its slot
    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < fs.numInputs; j++) {
        const StageInput& in = fs.inputs[j];
        if (in.compmask == 0 || !in.bary) continue;
        if (in.inloc >= fs.totalIn) continue;
        if (in.slot == kVaryingSlotPntc) {
            // no VS register: the VPC writes S and T for a point sprite, and the z and w a vec4 read would see as 0 and
            // 1, at the input's packed components (tu6_vpc_varying_mode). Metal's point_coord has its origin at the
            // top left, as Vulkan's has, so T and not ONE_MINUS_T. On a primitive that is not a point Metal leaves
            // the value undefined.
            if (!linkAdd(l, in.slot, a6xx::kRegidNone, in.compmask, in.inloc)) {
                return refuse(why, "the link holds " + std::to_string(kMaxStageOutputs) + " entries and the fragment stage reads more varyings than that");
            }
            uint32_t loc = in.inloc;
            const uint32_t repl[2] = {kPsReplS, kPsReplT}, interp[2] = {kInterpZero, kInterpOne};
            for (uint32_t c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
                if (((in.compmask >> c) & 1) == 0) continue;
                if (c < 2) l.psReplMode[loc / 16] |= repl[c] << ((loc % 16) * 2);
                else l.interpMode[loc / 16] |= interp[c - 2] << ((loc % 16) * 2);
                loc++;
            }
            continue;
        }
        int k = findOutput(vs, in.slot);
        if (k < 0) {
            return refuse(why, "the fragment stage reads varying slot " + std::to_string(in.slot) + " (" + slotName(in.slot) +
                                   "), which the vertex stage does not write");
        }
        if (!linkAdd(l, in.slot, vs.outputs[k].regid, in.compmask, in.inloc)) {
            return refuse(why, "the link holds " + std::to_string(kMaxStageOutputs) + " entries and the fragment stage reads more varyings than that");
        }
        // VPC_VARYING_INTERP_MODE: INTERP_FLAT for each component of a flat input, at two bits per location
        // (tu_pipeline.cc tu6_emit_vpc_varying_modes; fd6_program.cc emit_interp_state); smooth is the zero
        if (in.flat) {
            for (uint32_t c = 0; c < lastBit(in.compmask); c++) {
                if (((in.compmask >> c) & 1) == 0) continue;
                uint32_t loc = in.inloc + c;
                l.interpMode[loc / 16] |= kInterpFlat << ((loc % 16) * 2);
            }
        }
    }
    // --- the position, appended at max_loc with every component (tu_pipeline.cc:938-950, fd6_program.cc:707-710)
    if (vs.positionRegid == a6xx::kRegidNone) {
        return refuse(why, std::string(vs.k.name ? vs.k.name : "the vertex stage") + " writes no position: nothing to rasterize");
    }
    if (vs.positionRegid > 0xff) {
        // ir3_get_output_regid's HALF_REG_ID (0x100): a half-precision position has no place in SP_VS_OUT_REG's 8-bit regid
        return refuse(why, std::string(vs.k.name ? vs.k.name : "the vertex stage") + " writes its position in a half register: not served");
    }
    // varmask is the FS's varyings only: VPC_VAR_DISABLE is ~varmask and neither driver disables the position's
    // locations through it -- turnip builds the mask from the FS's bary inputs alone (tu_shader.cc:1790-1803), fd6
    // takes linkage.varmask BEFORE the position is appended (fd6_program.cc:654-658); ir3_link_add would set the
    // position's bits too, so they are taken back after it
    uint32_t varyingsOnly[4] = {l.varmask[0], l.varmask[1], l.varmask[2], l.varmask[3]};
    l.positionLoc = l.maxLoc;
    if (!linkAdd(l, kVaryingSlotPos, vs.positionRegid, 0xf, uint8_t(l.maxLoc))) {
        return refuse(why, "the link holds " + std::to_string(kMaxStageOutputs) + " entries and has no room left for the position");
    }
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) l.varmask[i] = varyingsOnly[i];
    // --- the point size after it, one component, when the VS writes one (tu6_emit_vpc, tu_pipeline.cc:944-947): what a
    // point is rasterized at; a line or a triangle ignores it
    if (vs.pointSizeRegid != a6xx::kRegidNone) {
        l.psizeLoc = l.maxLoc;
        if (!linkAdd(l, kVaryingSlotPsiz, uint8_t(vs.pointSizeRegid), 0x1, uint8_t(l.maxLoc))) {
            return refuse(why, "the link holds " + std::to_string(kMaxStageOutputs) + " entries and has no room left for the point size");
        }
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) l.varmask[i] = varyingsOnly[i];
    }
    // --- the colour outputs: 0xf per target written (SP_FS_RENDER_COMPONENTS / RB_RENDER_COMPONENTS, tu_shader.cc:1877-1891)
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < fs.numColorOutputs && i < kMaxColorOutputs; i++) {
        if (fs.colorRegid[i] != a6xx::kRegidNone) l.mrtComponents |= 0xfu << (i * 4);
    }
    // psReplMode is zero but for a [[point_coord]] input's (above); fd6 writes all eight registers so (render.hpp)
    *out = l;
    return true;
}

}  // namespace hakios::metal::render
```

`hakios-metal/src/metallib.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "hakios-metal/metallib.hpp"

#include <cstring>

namespace hakios::metal {

namespace {
uint16_t u16(const uint8_t* p) { return uint16_t(p[0] | p[1] << 8); }
uint32_t u32(const uint8_t* p) { return uint32_t(p[0]) | uint32_t(p[1]) << 8 | uint32_t(p[2]) << 16 | uint32_t(p[3]) << 24; }
uint64_t u64(const uint8_t* p) { return uint64_t(u32(p)) | uint64_t(u32(p + 4)) << 32; }
uint32_t be32(const uint8_t* p) { return uint32_t(p[0]) << 24 | uint32_t(p[1]) << 16 | uint32_t(p[2]) << 8 | p[3]; }
// [offset, offset + length) inside SIZE, without the sum wrapping
bool inside(uint64_t offset, uint64_t length, uint64_t size) { return offset <= size && length <= size - offset; }

constexpr size_t kHeader = 0x58;
constexpr uint32_t kFat = 0xcafebabe;
constexpr uint32_t kAir64 = 0x01000017;
}  // namespace

const MetalFunction* MetalLibrary::find(std::string_view name) const {
    for (const MetalFunction& f : functions_) {
        if (f.name == name) {
            return &f;
        }
    }
    return nullptr;
}

bool MetalLibrary::parse(const uint8_t* data, size_t size) {
    functions_.clear();
    why_.clear();
    // a universal file: the AIR64 slice, which is what a GPU that is not Apple's can use
    if (size >= 8 && be32(data) == kFat) {
        uint32_t count = be32(data + 4);
        bool found = false;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count && i < 64; i++) {
            uint64_t at = 8 + 20ull * i;
            if (!inside(at, 20, size)) {
                break;
            }
            if (be32(data + at) == kAir64) {
                uint32_t offset = be32(data + at + 8), length = be32(data + at + 12);
                if (!inside(offset, length, size)) {
                    return refuse("a universal metallib whose AIR64 slice is not inside it");
                }
                data += offset;
                size = length;
                found = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!found) {
            return refuse("a universal metallib with no AIR64 slice (only code for Apple's own GPUs)");
        }
    }
    data_ = data;
    size_ = size;
    if (size < kHeader || memcmp(data, "MTLB", 4) != 0) {
        return refuse("not a metallib (no MTLB at the start, or shorter than its header)");
    }
    version_[0] = u16(data + 4);
    version_[1] = u16(data + 6);
    uint64_t list = u64(data + 0x18), listLength = u64(data + 0x20);
    uint64_t modules = u64(data + 0x48), modulesLength = u64(data + 0x50);
    if (!inside(list, 4, size) || !inside(list + 4, listLength, size)) {
        return refuse("the function list is not inside the file");
    }
    if (!inside(modules, modulesLength, size)) {
        return refuse("the modules are not inside the file");
    }
    uint64_t end = list + 4 + listLength, p = list + 4;
    uint32_t count = u32(data + list);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (!inside(p, 4, end)) {
            return refuse("the function list ends before its count of functions");
        }
        uint64_t entry = u32(data + p);
        if (entry < 4 || !inside(p, entry, end)) {
            return refuse("a function's entry is not inside the function list");
        }
        uint64_t entryEnd = p + entry;
        MetalFunction f;
        bool haveOffset = false, haveSize = false, haveName = false;
        for (uint64_t q = p + 4; q + 4 <= entryEnd && memcmp(data + q, "ENDT", 4) != 0;) {
            if (!inside(q, 6, entryEnd)) {
                return refuse("a tag runs past the end of its function's entry");
            }
            uint16_t length = u16(data + q + 4);
            if (!inside(q + 6, length, entryEnd)) {
                return refuse("a tag's value runs past the end of its function's entry");
            }
            const uint8_t* v = data + q + 6;
            if (memcmp(data + q, "NAME", 4) == 0) {
                size_t n = length;
                while (n > 0 && v[n - 1] == 0) {
                    n--;
                }
                f.name.assign(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(v), n);
                haveName = true;
            } else if (memcmp(data + q, "TYPE", 4) == 0 && length >= 1) {
                f.type = v[0];
            } else if (memcmp(data + q, "VERS", 4) == 0 && length >= 8) {
                for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
                    f.air[k] = u16(v + 2 * k);
                }
            } else if (memcmp(data + q, "OFFT", 4) == 0 && length >= 24) {
                f.moduleOffset = u64(v + 16);
                haveOffset = true;
            } else if (memcmp(data + q, "MDSZ", 4) == 0 && length >= 8) {
                f.moduleSize = u64(v);
                haveSize = true;
            }
            q += 6 + uint64_t(length);
        }
        if (!haveName || !haveOffset || !haveSize) {
            return refuse("a function has no NAME, OFFT or MDSZ");
        }
        if (!inside(f.moduleOffset, f.moduleSize, modulesLength)) {
            return refuse("a function's module is not inside the modules");
        }
        f.moduleOffset += modules;
        functions_.push_back(std::move(f));
        p = entryEnd;
    }
    return true;
}

bool MetalLibrary::bitcode(const MetalFunction& f, const uint8_t** bytes, uint64_t* length) const {
    if (!inside(f.moduleOffset, f.moduleSize, size_)) {
        return false;
    }
    const uint8_t* m = data_ + f.moduleOffset;
    if (f.moduleSize >= 16 && u32(m) == 0x0B17C0DEu) {
        uint32_t offset = u32(m + 8), wrapped = u32(m + 12);
        if (!inside(offset, wrapped, f.moduleSize)) {
            return false;
        }
        *bytes = m + offset;
        *length = wrapped;
        return true;
    }
    *bytes = m;
    *length = f.moduleSize;
    return true;
}

}  // namespace hakios::metal
```

`hakios-metal/src/pm4.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "hakios-metal/pm4.hpp"

#include <cassert>

namespace hakios::metal::pm4 {

Header decode(uint32_t word) {
    Header h;
    switch (word >> 28) {
    case 4:
        h.count = word & 0x7f;
        h.reg = (word >> 8) & 0x3ffff;
        if (((word >> 7) & 1) == oddParity(h.count) && ((word >> 27) & 1) == oddParity(h.reg)) {
            h.kind = Header::kRegisters;
        }
        break;
    case 7:
        h.count = word & 0x3fff;
        h.opcode = (word >> 16) & 0x7f;
        if (((word >> 15) & 1) == oddParity(h.count) && ((word >> 23) & 1) == oddParity(h.opcode)) {
            h.kind = Header::kCommand;
        }
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }
    return h;
}

void Stream::command(uint32_t opcode, uint32_t count) {
    assert(count <= kMaxType7Count);
    words_.push_back(type7(opcode, count));
}

void Stream::registers(uint32_t reg, const uint32_t* values, uint32_t count) {
    // more than a header can count goes as several packets, each starting where the one before stopped
    while (count > 0) {
        uint32_t n = count < kMaxType4Count ? count : kMaxType4Count;
        words_.push_back(type4(reg, n));
        words_.insert(words_.end(), values, values + n);
        reg += n;
        values += n;
        count -= n;
    }
}

void Stream::nop(uint32_t words) {
    command(kNop, words);
    words_.insert(words_.end(), words, 0u);
}

void Stream::waitForIdle() { command(kWaitForIdle, 0); }
void Stream::waitMemWrites() { command(kWaitMemWrites, 0); }
void Stream::waitForMe() { command(kWaitForMe, 0); }

void Stream::memWrite(uint64_t a, const uint32_t* values, uint32_t count) {
    while (count > 0) {
        uint32_t n = count < kMaxType7Count - 2 ? count : kMaxType7Count - 2;
        command(kMemWrite, 2 + n);
        address(a);
        words_.insert(words_.end(), values, values + n);
        a += 4ull * n;
        values += n;
        count -= n;
    }
}

void Stream::memcpy(uint64_t destination, uint64_t source, uint32_t words) {
    command(kMemcpy, 5);
    words_.push_back(words);
    address(source);
    address(destination);
}

void Stream::indirect(uint64_t a, uint32_t words) {
    command(kIndirectBuffer, 3);
    address(a);
    words_.push_back(words);
}

void Stream::packet(uint32_t opcode, const uint32_t* words, uint32_t count) {
    command(opcode, count);
    words_.insert(words_.end(), words, words + count);
}

}  // namespace hakios::metal::pm4

```

`hakios-metal/src/render.cpp`:

```cpp
// The render path (render.hpp): ONE draw of a Program into ONE colour target in SYSMEM mode, as compute.cpp encodes a
// dispatch -- the refusals first, by name, then the table, then the stream group by group under render::Options'
// switches. The register sequence is turnip's sysmem pass and r3d path with fd6 as the second witness (render.hpp's
// file comment names the functions); every value here cites the line it was read at. Nothing of this has run on the
// phone: the fake GPU (fake_gpu.cpp) holds the stream together, hakios-metal-probe stage 9 is what measures it.
//
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#include "hakios-metal/render.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstring>
#include <initializer_list>
#include <tuple>

#include "hakios-metal/a6xx.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/command.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/texture.hpp"

namespace hakios::metal {

namespace render {

namespace {

using namespace a6xx;

std::string n(uint64_t v) { return std::to_string(v); }

// what the RB, SP_FS_MRT and the 2D engine's destination are given: the colour column of fd6_format_table.c, which
// differs from the TP's FMT for RGB10A2 (10_10_10_2_UNORM_DEST)
a6xx_format colorFmt(const FormatInfo& f) { return f.rbFmt != FMT6_NONE ? f.rbFmt : f.fmt6; }

bool refuse(std::string* why, const std::string& text) {
    if (why != nullptr) *why = text;
    return false;
}

const char* stageName(const Stage& s) { return s.k.name != nullptr ? s.k.name : s.kind == kStageVertex ? "the vertex stage" : "the fragment stage"; }

void reg(pm4::Stream& st, uint32_t r, uint32_t v) { st.registers(r, &v, 1); }

void reg64(pm4::Stream& st, uint32_t r, uint64_t a) {
    uint32_t v[2] = {uint32_t(a), uint32_t(a >> 32)};
    st.registers(r, v, 2);
}

// consecutive registers from R on, one type-4 (turnip's pkt4 of several)
void regs(pm4::Stream& st, uint32_t r, std::initializer_list<uint32_t> values) {
    uint32_t v[16];
    uint32_t count = 0;
    for (uint32_t x : values) v[count++] = x;
    st.registers(r, v, count);
}

// a type-7 packet of one word
void command1(pm4::Stream& st, uint32_t opcode, uint32_t word) { st.packet(opcode, &word, 1); }

void event(pm4::Stream& st, vgt_event_type e) {
    uint32_t w = eventWrite0(e, false);
    st.packet(CP_EVENT_WRITE, &w, 1);
}

// the 4-word event: VALUE written to ADDRESS when it has completed. turnip's form (tu_emit_raw_event_write,
// tu_cmd_buffer.cc:48-70) has no TIMESTAMP bit; with it the GPU writes a timestamp instead and the wait below never
// ends (28 October, every compute dispatch). The bit is here for the fake GPU's test of that alone.
void eventTimestamp(pm4::Stream& st, vgt_event_type e, uint64_t address, uint32_t value, bool timestampBit) {
    uint32_t w[4] = {eventWrite0(e, timestampBit), uint32_t(address), uint32_t(address >> 32), value};
    st.packet(CP_EVENT_WRITE, w, 4);
}

void waitForWord(pm4::Stream& st, uint64_t address, uint32_t value) {
    uint32_t w[6] = {waitRegMem0(WRITE_EQ, POLL_MEMORY), uint32_t(address), uint32_t(address >> 32), value, ~0u, kDelayLoopCycles};
    st.packet(CP_WAIT_REG_MEM, w, 6);
}

void waitForWordNot(pm4::Stream& st, uint64_t address, uint32_t value) {
    uint32_t w[6] = {waitRegMem0(WRITE_NE, POLL_MEMORY), uint32_t(address), uint32_t(address >> 32), value, ~0u, kDelayLoopCycles};
    st.packet(CP_WAIT_REG_MEM, w, 6);
}

void waitForWordAtLeast(pm4::Stream& st, uint64_t address, uint32_t value) {
    uint32_t w[4] = {0, uint32_t(address), uint32_t(address >> 32), value};
    st.packet(CP_WAIT_MEM_GTE, w, 4);
}

// CP_LOAD_STATE6_GEOM for the vertex stage's loads, _FRAG for the fragment stage's (tu6_stage2opcode, tu_shader.cc:1349;
// fd6_stage2opcode, fd6_emit.h:331-334): the program from GPU memory (ST6_SHADER, 128-byte units) or constants in
// the packet (ST6_CONSTANTS, vec4 units, the two address words zero as Mesa writes them)
uint32_t loadOpcode(const Stage& s) { return s.kind == kStageVertex ? uint32_t(CP_LOAD_STATE6_GEOM) : uint32_t(CP_LOAD_STATE6_FRAG); }
a6xx_state_block shaderBlock(const Stage& s) { return s.kind == kStageVertex ? SB6_VS_SHADER : SB6_FS_SHADER; }

void loadIndirect(pm4::Stream& st, const Stage& s, a6xx_state_type type, uint32_t dstOff, uint32_t units, uint64_t from) {
    uint32_t w[3] = {loadState6_0(dstOff, type, SS6_INDIRECT, shaderBlock(s), units), CP_LOAD_STATE6_1_EXT_SRC_ADDR(uint32_t(from)),
                     CP_LOAD_STATE6_2_EXT_SRC_ADDR_HI(uint32_t(from >> 32))};
    st.packet(loadOpcode(s), w, 3);
}

void loadDirect(pm4::Stream& st, const Stage& s, a6xx_state_type type, uint32_t dstOff, uint32_t units, const uint32_t* data, uint32_t dwords) {
    std::vector<uint32_t> w;
    w.reserve(3 + dwords);
    w.push_back(loadState6_0(dstOff, type, SS6_DIRECT, shaderBlock(s), units));
    w.push_back(0);
    w.push_back(0);
    w.insert(w.end(), data, data + dwords);
    st.packet(loadOpcode(s), w.data(), uint32_t(w.size()));
}

// The colour target as RB_MRT[0], SP_FS_MRT_REG[0] and the sRGB registers name it, off the Texture's own fields: the
// format's .rb column is its .tex one for every served format (fd6_format_table.c's VTC rows: RGBA8 :163, BGRA8 :174,
// R32Uint :132, R32Float :136, RGBA16F :249, RGBA32F :284, so FormatInfo::fmt6 and swap are the colour ones too), the
// pitch is the layout's (texturePitch), the layer size the buffer's length (layerBytes2d, 4096-aligned, fdl6_view_init's
// layer_size at fd6_view.c:192), the base the buffer's address (64-aligned by the layout), BASE_GMEM 0 in sysmem
// (r3d_dst, tu_clear_blit.cc:1400). COLOR_UINT/SINT for the pure-integer formats (fd6_view.c:415-418). (texture.hpp
// declares no method for this; texture_test holds the same fields through the same encoders to the 64x64 literals.)
struct MrtWords {
    uint32_t bufInfo, pitch, arrayPitch, baseLo, baseHi, baseGmem, spFsMrtReg;
    bool srgb;
    uint32_t flagLo = 0, flagHi = 0, flagPitch = 0;   // a compressed target's flag buffer (RB_MRT_FLAG_BUFFER), 0 for a linear one
};

// the format RB_MRT_BUF_INFO names (GRAS_LRZ_MRT_BUF_INFO_0 repeats attachment 0's)
a6xx_format mrtFormatOf(uint32_t bufInfo) {
    return a6xx_format((bufInfo & A6XX_RB_MRT_BUF_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__MASK) >> A6XX_RB_MRT_BUF_INFO_COLOR_FORMAT__SHIFT);
}

// (at mip level LEVEL: its address and its pitch -- fdl6_view_init's base_miplevel, the RB told the level alone)
MrtWords mrtWords(const Texture& t, uint32_t level, uint32_t slice = 0) {
    const FormatInfo& f = t.info();
    const TextureLevel L = t.level(level);
    MrtWords m{};
    // (a layer, a face or a depth plane: the slices are one 2D layout each, sliceBytes apart -- fd6_layout.c's layer_size)
    const uint64_t base = t.levelAddress(level) + (slice != 0 ? uint64_t(slice) * t.sliceBytes() : 0);
    m.bufInfo = rbMrtBufInfo(colorFmt(f), t.compressed() ? TILE6_3 : TILE6_LINEAR, f.swap);
    if (t.compressed()) {
        // its flag buffer, as tu6_emit_mrt / fd6 emit_mrt write it (fd6_view.c's FLAG_BUFFER_PITCH: the pitch, the layer
        // size over 4); RB_RENDER_CNTL.FLAG_MRTS turns its use on
        m.flagLo = uint32_t(t.flagAddress());
        m.flagHi = uint32_t(t.flagAddress() >> 32);
        m.flagPitch = A6XX_RB_MRT_FLAG_BUFFER_PITCH_PITCH(t.flagPitch()) | A6XX_RB_MRT_FLAG_BUFFER_PITCH_ARRAY_PITCH(t.flagLayerSize() >> 2);
    }
    m.pitch = rbMrtPitch(uint32_t(L.pitch));
    m.arrayPitch = rbMrtArrayPitch(uint32_t(t.buffer()->length()));
    m.baseLo = uint32_t(base);
    m.baseHi = uint32_t(base >> 32);
    m.baseGmem = 0;
    m.spFsMrtReg = spFsMrtReg(colorFmt(f), f.element == kElemInt, f.element == kElemUint);
    m.srgb = f.srgb;
    return m;
}

// what both stages share with a compute Kernel, refused as compute.cpp refuses it, plus what the first draw does not
// serve in either stage (render.hpp's list)
bool checkStage(const Stage& s, std::string* why) {
    const Kernel& k = s.k;
    auto name = [&s]() { return std::string(stageName(s)); };   // (built only for a refusal: a string a draw is an allocation a draw)
    if (k.instrlen == 0 || uint64_t(k.numWords) * 4 < uint64_t(k.instrlen) * 128) {
        return refuse(why, name() + ": " + n(k.numWords) + " words do not hold its instrlen of " + n(k.instrlen) + " units");
    }
    if (k.numSamp > 31) {
        return refuse(why, name() + ": numSamp " + n(k.numSamp) + " does not fit SP_xS_CONFIG.NSAMP's 5 bits (31 at most)");
    }
    // A `constant` buffer is a range ir3 pushes or an ldc through a UBO descriptor (uboDescriptors); a `device` one an
    // SSBO through the 3D pipeline's IBO table (gfxIbos), its slots the Metal buffer indices; images there are not served
    if (k.numIbos > k.numSsbos || k.numSsbos > kMaxVertexBuffers) {
        return refuse(why, name() + " has " + n(k.numIbos) + " IBO slots for " + n(k.numSsbos) + " device buffer(s): images in a draw are not served");
    }
    if (k.numUbos > kMaxVertexBuffers) {
        return refuse(why, name() + " indexes " + n(k.numUbos) + " constant buffers: Metal's buffer table has " + n(kMaxVertexBuffers));
    }
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxTextureSlots; i++) {
        if (k.textures[i].kind == kTexImage) {
            // an image is an IBO of the 3D pipe, the same table a device buffer needs (above)
            return refuse(why, name() + " stores through texture " + n(i) + " as an image: images in a draw (the 3D IBO table) are not served");
        }
    }
    if (k.numTextureSlots > kMaxTextureSlots || (k.samplerMask >> kMaxTextureSlots) != 0) {
        return refuse(why, name() + " names texture or sampler indices past " + n(kMaxTextureSlots - 1) + ": the tables hold " + n(kMaxTextureSlots));
    }
    for (uint32_t i = k.numTextureSlots; i < kMaxTextureSlots; i++) {
        if (k.textures[i].kind == kTexSampled) {
            return refuse(why, name() + " samples texture " + n(i) + " past its numTextureSlots of " + n(k.numTextureSlots) + ": the stage's tables disagree");
        }
    }
    if (k.driverParamsOffsetVec4 >= 0 && s.kind != kStageVertex) {
        // an FS's driver params (subgroup size, the fragment density words) are not worked out here
        return refuse(why, name() + " reads driver params at vec4 " + n(uint32_t(k.driverParamsOffsetVec4)) + ": only a vertex stage's are served");
    }
    if (k.driverParamsOffsetVec4 >= 0 && uint32_t(k.driverParamsOffsetVec4) + 1 > k.constlen) {
        return refuse(why, name() + ": its driver params at vec4 " + n(uint32_t(k.driverParamsOffsetVec4)) + " run past its constlen of " + n(k.constlen));
    }
    if (k.constantDataSize != 0 && (k.constantDataUbo == 0 || uint64_t(k.constantDataOffset) + k.constantDataSize > 4ull * k.numWords)) {
        return refuse(why, name() + " carries " + n(k.constantDataSize) + " bytes of constant data that no UBO of ir3's reads, or outside its words");
    }
    uint32_t immUnits = (k.numImmediates + 3) / 4;
    if (immUnits != 0 && k.immediatesOffsetVec4 + immUnits > k.constlen) {
        return refuse(why, name() + ": " + n(immUnits) + " vec4 of constants at " + n(k.immediatesOffsetVec4) + " run past its constlen of " + n(k.constlen));
    }
    return true;
}

// A pushed constant range of a stage as the GPU reads it: DST_OFF, units and the address in the bound buffer -- or, when
// that address is not a multiple of 16, the words themselves. CP_LOAD_STATE6 reads an indirect source from the address
// rounded down to 16 bytes (probe 9o4: bound at 4, 8 or 120 the consts held the 4, 8 or 8 bytes before the colour;
// at 16 the colour), while Metal binds a constant buffer at any multiple of 4 and CoreAnimation binds its uniforms at
// multiples of 8. Such a range is loaded direct from the bytes as they are when the draw is encoded: a snapshot, which
// is what -setFragmentBytes: gives anyway, and what a caller that writes its uniforms before encoding cannot tell apart.
struct PushedRange {
    uint32_t offsetVec4, units;
    uint64_t from;
    std::vector<uint32_t> words;   // non-empty: load these direct instead of reading FROM
    // FROM not a multiple of 16: copied by the command processor to the draw's table at COPY_AT first and loaded from
    // there (placeCopies), or, past the table's room, read by this processor into WORDS. The buffers are write-combined
    // for this processor, and its reads of them go to memory one by one: CoreAnimation binds its uniforms at multiples
    // of 8, and copying them so took 50-160 us a draw on the phone, most of a draw's encoding
    bool copy = false;
    uint32_t copyAt = 0;
    const Buffer* buffer = nullptr;
    uint64_t bufferOffset = 0;
};

// The stage's pushed ranges against its own [[buffer(n)]] table, by compute's rules (compute.cpp: the range is ir3's,
// in whole vec4 and padded -- a 16-byte float4 is pushed as 64 bytes -- so the read must stay inside the bound object's
// pages, not inside the length bound; it must land inside the stage's constlen). False with *why naming the stage.
bool pushedRanges(const Stage& s, const Bindings& b, std::vector<PushedRange>* out, std::string* why) {
    const Kernel& k = s.k;
    auto name = [&s]() { return std::string(stageName(s)); };   // (built only for a refusal: a string a draw is an allocation a draw)
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < k.numUboRanges; i++) {
        const KernelUboRange& r = k.uboRanges[i];
        // the constant data's range (a module's constant table, kernel.hpp: constantDataUbo): its words direct, from
        // the program's own, past their end zeros (ir3 pushes whole vec4, the table need not fill the last)
        if (k.constantDataUbo != 0 && r.block == k.constantDataUbo - 1) {
            if (r.offsetVec4 + r.sizeDwords / 4 > k.constlen) {
                return refuse(why, name() + ": its constant data's range at vec4 " + n(r.offsetVec4) + " runs past its constlen of " + n(k.constlen));
            }
            PushedRange p{r.offsetVec4, r.sizeDwords / 4, 0, std::vector<uint32_t>(r.sizeDwords, 0u)};
            for (uint32_t d = 0; d < r.sizeDwords; d++) {
                const uint64_t at = uint64_t(r.startDword + d) * 4;
                if (at + 4 <= k.constantDataSize) p.words[d] = k.words[k.constantDataOffset / 4 + r.startDword + d];
            }
            out->push_back(std::move(p));
            continue;
        }
        if (r.block >= b.buffers.size() || b.buffers[r.block].buffer == nullptr) {
            return refuse(why, name() + ": no buffer bound at index " + n(r.block) + " (its constant buffer)");
        }
        const Binding& x = b.buffers[r.block];
        if (x.offset % 4 != 0 || x.offset > x.buffer->length()) {
            return refuse(why, name() + ": buffer " + n(r.block) + ": offset " + n(x.offset) + " is not a multiple of 4 inside it");
        }
        uint64_t bytes = x.buffer->length() - x.offset, mapped = x.buffer->bo().size() - x.offset;
        if (r.sizeDwords == 0 || r.sizeDwords % 4 != 0) {
            return refuse(why, name() + ": a constant range of " + n(r.sizeDwords) + " dwords, not a whole number of vec4");
        }
        if (uint64_t(r.startDword) * 4 + uint64_t(r.sizeDwords) * 4 > mapped) {
            return refuse(why, name() + " reads " + n(r.sizeDwords * 4) + " bytes at " + n(r.startDword * 4) + " of constant buffer " + n(r.block) + "; " +
                                   n(bytes) + " are bound and " + n(mapped) + " mapped behind the offset");
        }
        if (r.offsetVec4 + r.sizeDwords / 4 > k.constlen) {
            return refuse(why, name() + ": constant buffer " + n(r.block) + "'s range at vec4 " + n(r.offsetVec4) + " runs past its constlen of " + n(k.constlen));
        }
        PushedRange p{r.offsetVec4, r.sizeDwords / 4, x.buffer->gpuAddress() + x.offset + 4ull * r.startDword, {}};
        if (p.from % 16 != 0) {
            p.copy = true;
            p.buffer = x.buffer;
            p.bufferOffset = x.offset + 4ull * r.startDword;
        }
        out->push_back(std::move(p));
    }
    return true;
}

// gl_vert_attrib's VERT_ATTRIB_GENERIC0 (Mesa shader_enums.h): a VS input at this slot + n is [[attribute(n)]]
constexpr uint32_t kVertAttribGeneric0 = 15;

// The served MTLVertexFormats as the fetch reads them: fd6_format_table.c's vertex column (VTC/VT_ rows), the bytes one
// element takes, and whether the decoded value is a float (VFD_DECODE_INSTR.FLOAT: set unless the format is a pure

struct VertexFormatInfo {
    VertexFormat format;
    a6xx_format fmt6;

    {VertexFormat::kFloat2, FMT6_32_32_FLOAT, WZYX, 8, true, "Float2"},   // fd6_format_table.c:258

    {VertexFormat::kFloat4, FMT6_32_32_32_32_FLOAT, WZYX, 16, true, "Float4"},   // fd6_format_table.c:284
    {VertexFormat::kInt, FMT6_32_SINT, WZYX, 4, false, "Int"},   // fd6_format_table.c:133
    {VertexFormat::kInt2, FMT6_32_32_SINT, WZYX, 8, false, "Int2"},   // fd6_format_table.c:255
    {VertexFormat::kInt3, FMT6_32_32_32_SINT, WZYX, 12, false, "Int3"},   // fd6_format_table.c:269
    {VertexFormat::kInt4, FMT6_32_32_32_32_SINT, WZYX, 16, false, "Int4"},   // fd6_format_table.c:280
    {VertexFormat::kUInt, FMT6_32_UINT, WZYX, 4, false, "UInt"},   // fd6_format_table.c:132
    {VertexFormat::kUInt2, FMT6_32_32_UINT, WZYX, 8, false, "UInt2"},   // fd6_format_table.c:254
    {VertexFormat::kUInt3, FMT6_32_32_32_UINT, WZYX, 12, false, "UInt3"},   // fd6_format_table.c:268
    {VertexFormat::kUInt4, FMT6_32_32_32_32_UINT, WZYX, 16, false, "UInt4"},   // fd6_format_table.c:278
    {VertexFormat::kUChar4Normalized_BGRA, FMT6_8_8_8_8_UNORM, WXYZ, 4, true, "UChar4Normalized_BGRA"},   // fd6_format_table.c:174
    {VertexFormat::kUChar, FMT6_8_UINT, WZYX, 1, false, "UChar"},   // fd6_format_table.c:46
    {VertexFormat::kChar, FMT6_8_SINT, WZYX, 1, false, "Char"},   // fd6_format_table.c:47
    {VertexFormat::kUCharNormalized, FMT6_8_UNORM, WZYX, 1, true, "UCharNormalized"},   // fd6_format_table.c:44
    {VertexFormat::kCharNormalized, FMT6_8_SNORM, WZYX, 1, true, "CharNormalized"},   // fd6_format_table.c:45
    {VertexFormat::kUShort, FMT6_16_UINT, WZYX, 2, false, "UShort"},   // fd6_format_table.c:72
    {VertexFormat::kShort, FMT6_16_SINT, WZYX, 2, false, "Short"},   // fd6_format_table.c:73
    {VertexFormat::kUShortNormalized, FMT6_16_UNORM, WZYX, 2, true, "UShortNormalized"},   // fd6_format_table.c:70
    {VertexFormat::kShortNormalized, FMT6_16_SNORM, WZYX, 2, true, "ShortNormalized"},   // fd6_format_table.c:71
    {VertexFormat::kHalf, FMT6_16_FLOAT, WZYX, 2, true, "Half"},   // fd6_format_table.c:76
};
const VertexFormatInfo* vertexFormatInfo(VertexFormat f) {
    for (const VertexFormatInfo& i : kVertexFormats) {
        if (i.format == f) return &i;
    }
    return nullptr;
}

// What the vertex fetch registers get: decode entry n per [[attribute(n)]] up to the highest one the VS reads (holes
// zero, as turnip writes them), fetch entry b per Metal buffer index used.
struct VertexFetch {
    uint32_t count = 0;            // VFD_CONTROL_0.FETCH_CNT = DECODE_CNT (turnip writes both as the attribute count)
    uint32_t decode[kMaxVertexAttributes] = {};
    uint32_t stepRate[kMaxVertexAttributes] = {};
    uint32_t dest[kMaxVertexAttributes] = {};
    bool used[kMaxVertexBuffers] = {};
    uint64_t base[kMaxVertexBuffers] = {};
    uint32_t size[kMaxVertexBuffers] = {};
    uint32_t stride[kMaxVertexBuffers] = {};
};

// The VS's attributes against the descriptor and the VS's own [[buffer(n)]] table. Refused by name: an attribute the
// descriptor does not describe, a format not served, an offset or stride past the 12-bit fields (a6xx.xml:4620-4634),
// a step other than per vertex, a stride of 0, no buffer bound at the layout's index, and a fetch that reads past the
// bound length for the draw's last vertex (Metal requires the bytes to be there; the GPU would read whatever follows).
bool vertexFetch(const Stage& vs, const VertexDescriptor& vd, const Draw& draw, const Bindings& b, VertexFetch* f, std::string* why) {
    const std::string name = stageName(vs);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < vs.numInputs; i++) {
        const StageInput& in = vs.inputs[i];
        if (in.sysval || in.regid == kRegidNone) continue;
        if (in.slot < kVertAttribGeneric0 || in.slot - kVertAttribGeneric0 >= kMaxVertexAttributes) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": an input at slot " + n(in.slot) + " that is not a [[stage_in]] attribute");
        }
        const uint32_t loc = in.slot - kVertAttribGeneric0;
        const VertexAttribute& a = vd.attributes[loc];
        if (a.format == VertexFormat::kInvalid) {
            return refuse(why, name + " reads [[attribute(" + n(loc) + ")]], which the vertex descriptor does not describe");
        }
        const VertexFormatInfo* fi = vertexFormatInfo(a.format);
        if (fi == nullptr) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": [[attribute(" + n(loc) + ")]] is MTLVertexFormat " + n(uint32_t(a.format)) +
                                   ": the 1010102, RG11B10 and RGB9E5 formats are not served");
        }
        if (a.bufferIndex >= kMaxVertexBuffers) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": [[attribute(" + n(loc) + ")]] is fetched from buffer " + n(a.bufferIndex) + ": the layouts are 0 to 30");
        }
        if (a.offset > 0xfff) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": [[attribute(" + n(loc) + ")]] at offset " + n(a.offset) + ": VFD_DECODE_INSTR.OFFSET holds 12 bits");
        }
        const VertexLayout& l = vd.layouts[a.bufferIndex];
        const bool perInstance = l.step == VertexStep::kPerInstance;
        if (l.step != VertexStep::kPerVertex && !perInstance) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": buffer " + n(a.bufferIndex) + " steps " + (l.step == VertexStep::kConstant ? "constantly" : "in an unknown way") +
                                   ": per-vertex and per-instance fetch are served");
        }
        if (perInstance && l.stepRate == 0) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": buffer " + n(a.bufferIndex) + " steps per instance at a rate of 0: Metal's step rate is 1 or more");
        }
        if (l.stride == 0 || l.stride > 0xfff) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": buffer " + n(a.bufferIndex) + "'s stride of " + n(l.stride) + ": 1 to 4095 bytes (VFD_FETCH_STRIDE holds 12 bits)");
        }
        if (a.bufferIndex >= b.buffers.size() || b.buffers[a.bufferIndex].buffer == nullptr) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": no buffer bound at index " + n(a.bufferIndex) + " (the vertex buffer of [[attribute(" + n(loc) + ")]])");
        }
        const Binding& x = b.buffers[a.bufferIndex];
        if (x.offset > x.buffer->length()) {
            return refuse(why, name + ": buffer " + n(a.bufferIndex) + ": offset " + n(x.offset) + " lies past its end");
        }
        const uint64_t bytes = x.buffer->length() - x.offset;
        // the last element the draw fetches: for a per-instance attribute baseInstance + (instanceCount - 1) / stepRate
        // (VFD_INSTANCE_START_OFFSET is added after the divisor, as Vulkan's firstInstance is); for a per-vertex
        // one the last vertex, which an indexed draw names only in its index buffer -- there the check is the GPU's own
        // (VFD_FETCH_SIZE bounds the fetch: an index past it reads zeros, robust-buffer style, not what follows)
        // (an indirect draw's counts are the GPU's to read: every attribute is bounded by the fetch size alone, as above)
        if ((!perInstance && draw.indexBuffer != nullptr) || draw.indirect != nullptr) {
            f->decode[loc] = vfdDecodeInstr(a.bufferIndex, a.offset, perInstance, fi->fmt6, fi->swap, fi->isFloat);
            f->stepRate[loc] = perInstance ? l.stepRate : 0;
        } else {
            const uint64_t last = perInstance ? uint64_t(draw.baseInstance) + uint64_t(draw.instanceCount == 0 ? 0 : draw.instanceCount - 1) / l.stepRate
                                              : uint64_t(draw.vertexStart) + (draw.vertexCount == 0 ? 0 : draw.vertexCount - 1);
            const uint64_t need = last * l.stride + a.offset + fi->bytes;
            if (need > bytes) {
                return refuse(why, name + ": [[attribute(" + n(loc) + ")]] of " + (perInstance ? "instance step " : "vertex ") + n(uint32_t(last)) + " ends at byte " +
                                       n(need) + " of buffer " + n(a.bufferIndex) + "; " + n(bytes) + " are bound");
            }
```
