`hakios-metal/tools/check-a6xx.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Checks every constant in include/hakios-metal/a6xx.hpp against Mesa's generated register headers.

    python3 -I tools/check-a6xx.py [MESA_GEN_DIR] [A6XX_HPP]

MESA_GEN_DIR is the directory with a6xx.xml.h, adreno_pm4.xml.h and adreno_common.xml.h, as Mesa's build writes
them (build/src/freedreno/registers/adreno/); when it is not given, the environment variable HAKIOS_MESA_GEN is.
A6XX_HPP defaults to the header of the project this script is in.

What is checked, by name:
  - every `constexpr <type> NAME = VALUE;` and every enumerator `NAME = VALUE,` in a6xx.hpp is looked up among the
    headers' #defines and enumerators, and the values must be equal;
  - a NAME__SCALE constant is compared with the right shift Mesa's encoder NAME(val) applies in its body
    (`val >> N`; 0 when there is none);
  - a NAME__MUL constant is compared with the multiplier Mesa's encoder NAME(val) applies in its body
    (`val * N.0`, the fixed-point fields: GRAS_SU_CNTL.LINEHALFWIDTH is quarter pixels, the point sizes sixteenths;
    0 when there is none);
  - a register array NAME (a `#define NAME(i0) (BASE + STRIDE*i0)` or an inline `NAME(uint32_t i0)` in the
    headers, with or without the `__attribute__((deprecated))` two of them carry) is checked as NAME = BASE and
    NAME__STRIDE = STRIDE;
  - a `// not-in-headers: why` comment marks a constant the headers cannot check; it is listed, not checked.
Anything else is an error: a constant the headers do not have, a value that differs, a constant without a
`file.xml.h:line` comment saying where it comes from. The exit status is 0 only when every constant was checked or
marked. A line comment that does not point at the constant's own line in the header is reported as a warning (the
line numbers are those of one Mesa version's output; the name check is what matters).
"""
import ast
import os
import re
import sys

HEADERS = ("a6xx.xml.h", "adreno_pm4.xml.h", "adreno_common.xml.h")


def read_headers(gen_dir):
    """#defines, enumerators and encoder shifts of the generated headers, each with where it is."""
    defines = {}  # name -> [(value, file, line)]
    enums = {}
    scales = {}  # encoder name -> (shift, file, line)
    muls = {}  # encoder name -> (multiplier, file, line)
    arrays = {}  # register array name -> (base, stride, file, line)
    text = {}  # file -> its lines
    array_re = r"\(\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|\d+)\s*\+\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|\d+)\s*\*\s*i0\s*\)"
    for fname in HEADERS:
        path = os.path.join(gen_dir, fname)
        try:
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                lines = f.read().split("\n")
        except OSError as e:
            sys.exit(f"cannot read {path}: {e}")
        text[fname] = lines
        in_enum = False
        fn = None
        body = []
        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
            m = re.match(r"#define\s+(\w+)\s+(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|\d+)\s*$", line)
            if m:
                defines.setdefault(m.group(1), []).append((int(m.group(2), 0), fname, i))
                continue
            m = re.match(r"#define\s+(\w+)\(i0\)\s+" + array_re + r"\s*$", line)
            if m:
                arrays[m.group(1)] = (int(m.group(2), 0), int(m.group(3), 0), fname, i)
                continue
            m = re.match(r"static inline (?:__attribute__\(\(deprecated\)\)\s+)?uint32_t (\w+)\(uint32_t i0\)\s*\{\s*return\s+" +
                         r"(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|\d+)\s*\+\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|\d+)\s*\*\s*i0;\s*\}", line)
            if m:
                arrays[m.group(1)] = (int(m.group(2), 0), int(m.group(3), 0), fname, i)
                continue
            if re.match(r"enum\s+\w+\s*\{", line):
                in_enum = True
                continue
            if in_enum:
                if line.startswith("}"):
                    in_enum = False
                    continue
                m = re.match(r"\s*(\w+)\s*=\s*(-?0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|-?\d+)\s*,?\s*$", line)
                if m:
                    enums.setdefault(m.group(1), []).append((int(m.group(2), 0), fname, i))
                continue
            # a multi-line encoder: `static inline uint32_t NAME(type val)` then its body to the closing brace
            m = re.match(r"static inline uint32_t (\w+)\(.*\)\s*$", line)
            if m:
                fn = (m.group(1), i)
                body = []
                continue
            if fn is not None:
                if line.startswith("}"):
                    s = re.search(r"val\s*>>\s*(\d+)", " ".join(body))
                    scales[fn[0]] = (int(s.group(1)) if s else 0, fname, fn[1])
                    s = re.search(r"val\s*\*\s*(\d+)\.0", " ".join(body))
                    muls[fn[0]] = (int(s.group(1)) if s else 0, fname, fn[1])
                    fn = None
                else:
                    body.append(line)
    return defines, enums, scales, muls, arrays, text


def evaluate(expr, env):
    """A C++ constant expression made of literals, names defined earlier in the header, and | & << >> + - * ~."""
    expr = re.sub(r"\b(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|\d+)[uU]?[lL]{0,2}\b", r"\1", expr)
    expr = re.sub(r"\btrue\b", "True", expr)
    expr = re.sub(r"\bfalse\b", "False", expr)
    ops = {
        ast.BitOr: lambda a, b: a | b,
        ast.BitAnd: lambda a, b: a & b,
        ast.LShift: lambda a, b: a << b,
        ast.RShift: lambda a, b: a >> b,
        ast.Add: lambda a, b: a + b,
        ast.Sub: lambda a, b: a - b,
        ast.Mult: lambda a, b: a * b,
    }

    def ev(n):
        if isinstance(n, ast.Expression):
            return ev(n.body)
        if isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, (int, bool)):
            return int(n.value)
        if isinstance(n, ast.Name):
            if n.id in env:
                return env[n.id]
            raise ValueError(f"unknown name {n.id}")
        if isinstance(n, ast.BinOp) and type(n.op) in ops:
            return ops[type(n.op)](ev(n.left), ev(n.right))
        if isinstance(n, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(n.op, ast.USub):
            return -ev(n.operand)
        if isinstance(n, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(n.op, ast.Invert):
            return ~ev(n.operand)
        raise ValueError(f"cannot evaluate {ast.dump(n)}")

    return ev(ast.parse(expr, mode="eval"))


def read_hpp(path):
    """Every constant of a6xx.hpp: name, value, its line, the header line its comment names, its marker."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            lines = f.read().split("\n")
    except OSError as e:
        sys.exit(f"cannot read {path}: {e}")
    items = []
    env = {}
    in_enum = False
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        code, _, comment = line.partition("//")
        marker = re.search(r"not-in-headers:\s*(.*)", comment)
        src = re.search(r"(\w+\.xml\.h):(\d+)", comment)
        m = re.match(r"\s*(?:inline\s+)?constexpr\s+\w+\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*(.+?)\s*;\s*$", code)
        if not m:
            if re.match(r"\s*enum\s+\w+(\s*:\s*\w+)?\s*\{", code):
                in_enum = True
                continue
            if in_enum:
                if code.strip().startswith("}"):
                    in_enum = False
                    continue
                m = re.match(r"\s*(\w+)\s*=\s*(.+?)\s*,?\s*$", code)
            if not m:
                continue
        name, expr = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        try:
            value = evaluate(expr, env)
        except (ValueError, SyntaxError) as e:
            sys.exit(f"{path}:{i}: cannot evaluate `{expr}` for {name}: {e}")
        env[name] = value
        items.append({
            "name": name,
            "value": value,
            "line": i,
            "src": (src.group(1), int(src.group(2))) if src else None,
            "marker": marker.group(1).strip() if marker else None,
        })
    return items


def main(argv):
    gen_dir = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else os.environ.get("HAKIOS_MESA_GEN")
    if not gen_dir:
        sys.exit(__doc__.strip())
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    hpp = argv[2] if len(argv) > 2 else os.path.join(here, "..", "include", "hakios-metal", "a6xx.hpp")

    defines, enums, scales, muls, arrays, text = read_headers(gen_dir)
    items = read_hpp(hpp)
    if not items:
        sys.exit(f"{hpp}: no constants found; the parser or the file is wrong")

    checked_values = 0
    checked_scales = 0
    checked_muls = 0
    checked_arrays = 0
    unchecked = []
    mismatches = []
    missing = []
    uncommented = []
    drift = []

    for it in items:
        name, value = it["name"], it["value"]
        if it["marker"] is not None:
            unchecked.append(it)
            continue
        if it["src"] is None:
            uncommented.append(it)
        if name.endswith("__SCALE"):
            base = name[: -len("__SCALE")]
            if base not in scales:
                missing.append((it, f"no encoder {base}(val) in the headers"))
                continue
            expected, f, l = scales[base]
            if expected != value:
                mismatches.append((it, expected, f, l))
                continue
            checked_scales += 1
            lookup = base
        elif name.endswith("__MUL"):
            base = name[: -len("__MUL")]
            if base not in muls:
                missing.append((it, f"no encoder {base}(val) in the headers"))
                continue
            expected, f, l = muls[base]
            if expected != value:
                mismatches.append((it, expected, f, l))
                continue
            checked_muls += 1
            lookup = base
        elif name.endswith("__STRIDE"):
            base = name[: -len("__STRIDE")]
            if base not in arrays:
                missing.append((it, f"no register array {base}(i0) in the headers"))
                continue
            _, stride, f, l = arrays[base]
            if stride != value:
                mismatches.append((it, stride, f, l))
                continue
            checked_arrays += 1
            lookup = base
        else:
            found = defines.get(name, []) + enums.get(name, [])
            if name in arrays:
                b, _, f, l = arrays[name]
                found = found + [(b, f, l)]
            if not found:
                missing.append((it, "not a #define, an enumerator or a register array in the headers"))
                continue
            if all(v != value for v, _, _ in found):
                v, f, l = found[0]
                mismatches.append((it, v, f, l))
                continue
            checked_values += 1
            lookup = name
        if it["src"] is not None:
            f, l = it["src"]
            lines = text.get(f)
            if lines is None or not (1 <= l <= len(lines)) or not re.search(r"\b%s\b" % re.escape(lookup), lines[l - 1]):
                drift.append((it, lookup))

    print(f"checked {checked_values + checked_scales + checked_muls + checked_arrays} constants of {os.path.relpath(hpp)} "
          f"against {gen_dir}: {checked_values} values, {checked_scales} encoder shifts, {checked_muls} encoder "
          f"multipliers, {checked_arrays} array strides")
    if unchecked:
        print(f"not checkable, and why ({len(unchecked)}):")
        for it in unchecked:
            print(f"  {it['name']} = {it['value']:#x} -- {it['marker']}")
    if drift:
        print(f"warning: {len(drift)} line comments do not point at the constant's line in the header:")
        for it, lookup in drift:
            print(f"  a6xx.hpp:{it['line']} {it['name']} says {it['src'][0]}:{it['src'][1]}")

    failed = False
    if mismatches:
        failed = True
        it, v, f, l = mismatches[0]
        print(f"MISMATCH: {it['name']} is {it['value']:#x} in a6xx.hpp:{it['line']} but {v:#x} in {f}:{l}"
              + (f" ({len(mismatches)} mismatches in all)" if len(mismatches) > 1 else ""))
    for it, why in missing:
        failed = True
        print(f"NOT FOUND: {it['name']} (a6xx.hpp:{it['line']}): {why}")
    for it in uncommented:
        failed = True
        print(f"NO SOURCE: {it['name']} (a6xx.hpp:{it['line']}) has no `file.xml.h:line` comment")
    print("FAIL" if failed else "ok")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`hakios-metal/tools/compiler-smoke.cc`:

```cc
// compiler-smoke: does Mesa's compiler link into a program of ours, and does
// it compile an AIR kernel in-process -- the path src/compiler.cpp takes.
//
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
//
//   compiler-smoke [--chip-id 0x06030500] kernel.bc
//
// It does, in order, what the driver will do: look the chip up in Mesa's
// device table, create an ir3 compiler for it, translate the bitcode with the
// AIR front end (air_to_nir, with the options the patched ir3_cmdline.c uses in
// load_air), print the NIR, then lower it as ir3_cmdline.c does and compile and
// assemble it with ir3, printing the listing. Every library of the link is
// exercised: libair, libnir, libcompiler, libfreedreno_ir3 with its encoder and
// decoder, libfreedreno_common, libmesa_util.
//
// The same source builds for the host (tools/compiler.mk: compiler-smoke) and
// for iOS (ios-compiler-smoke), so it uses nothing but the C library and
// Mesa; it does not run on the phone from here, the link is what is checked.

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>

#include "nir_air.h"

#include "common/freedreno_dev_info.h"
#include "ir3/ir3_compiler.h"
#include "ir3/ir3_nir.h"
#include "ir3/ir3_shader.h"
#include "util/ralloc.h"

namespace {

[[noreturn]] void die(const char* what, const char* detail = nullptr)
{
    fprintf(stderr, "compiler-smoke: %s%s%s\n", what, detail ? ": " : "", detail ? detail : "");
    exit(1);
}

std::string readFile(const char* path)
{
    FILE* f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f)
        die("cannot open", path);
    std::string s;
    char buf[4096];
    size_t n;
    while ((n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, f)) > 0)
        s.append(buf, n);
    fclose(f);
    return s;
}

const char* resourceKind(enum air_resource_kind k)
{
    switch (k) {
    case AIR_RESOURCE_CONSTANT_BUFFER: return "constant buffer (UBO)";
    case AIR_RESOURCE_DEVICE_BUFFER: return "device buffer (SSBO)";
    case AIR_RESOURCE_THREADGROUP_BUFFER: return "threadgroup buffer";
    case AIR_RESOURCE_TEXTURE: return "texture";
    case AIR_RESOURCE_IMAGE: return "image";
    case AIR_RESOURCE_SAMPLER: return "sampler";
    }
    return "?";
}

} // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    uint64_t chipId = 0x06030500;
    const char* path = nullptr;
    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
        if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--chip-id") && i + 1 < argc)
            chipId = strtoull(argv[++i], nullptr, 0);
        else if (!path)
            path = argv[i];
        else
            die("usage: compiler-smoke [--chip-id ID] kernel.bc");
    }
    if (!path)
        die("usage: compiler-smoke [--chip-id ID] kernel.bc");

    // 1. The device row (libfreedreno_common).
    struct fd_dev_id devId = {};
    devId.chip_id = chipId;
    const struct fd_dev_info* devInfo = fd_dev_info_raw(&devId);
    if (!devInfo)
        die("chip id not in Mesa's device table");
    printf("device: %s, chip id 0x%llx, gen %u, threadsize_base %u, %u SP cores\n", fd_dev_name(&devId),
           static_cast<unsigned long long>(chipId), devInfo->chip, devInfo->threadsize_base,
           devInfo->num_sp_cores);

    // 2. The compiler (libfreedreno_ir3).
    struct ir3_compiler_options copts = {};
    struct ir3_compiler* compiler = ir3_compiler_create(nullptr, &devId, devInfo, &copts);
    if (!compiler)
        die("ir3_compiler_create failed");
    printf("ir3 compiler: gen %u, max_const_compute %u, branchstack %u\n", compiler->gen,
           compiler->max_const_compute, compiler->branchstack_size);

    // 3. AIR -> NIR (libair), as load_air in the patched ir3_cmdline.c: the
    // module's function constants taken as zero, and the library wrapper on,
    // which is inert for a kernel entry point (it only wraps air.visible functions).
    std::string bc = readFile(path);
    struct air_constant_value* fc = nullptr;
    unsigned numFc = air_module_function_constants(nullptr, bc.data(), bc.size(), &fc);
    struct air_to_nir_options aopts = {};
    aopts.constants = fc;
    aopts.num_constants = numFc;
    aopts.library_wrapper = true;
    struct air_shader_info info = {};
    const char* err = nullptr;
    nir_shader* nir = air_to_nir(nullptr, bc.data(), bc.size(), nullptr, &aopts, ir3_get_compiler_options(compiler),
                                 &info, &err);
    if (!nir)
        die("air_to_nir refused it", err);

    printf("AIR: entry %s, %u function constants, %u resources, %u varyings, %u render targets\n",
           info.entry_point, numFc, info.num_resources, info.num_varyings, info.num_render_targets);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < info.num_resources; i++) {
        const struct air_resource* r = &info.resources[i];
        printf("  resource %u: %s at index %u, size %u, %s%s%s\n", i, resourceKind(r->kind), r->index, r->size,
               r->read ? "read" : "", r->read && r->write ? "+" : "", r->write ? "write" : "");
    }
    printf("NIR: %s \"%s\", workgroup %u x %u x %u%s, %u ubos, %u ssbos, %u images, %u textures\n",
           _mesa_shader_stage_to_string(nir->info.stage), nir->info.name ? nir->info.name : "",
           nir->info.workgroup_size[0], nir->info.workgroup_size[1], nir->info.workgroup_size[2],
           nir->info.workgroup_size_variable ? " (variable)" : "", nir->info.num_ubos, nir->info.num_ssbos,
           nir->info.num_images, nir->info.num_textures);
    nir_print_shader(nir, stdout);

    // 4. NIR -> ir3, the lowering ir3_cmdline.c applies after load_air, then the
    // variant as ir3_shader.c's alloc_variant would set it up.
    nir_lower_system_values(nir);
    nir_lower_compute_system_values(nir, nullptr);
    nir_lower_io(nir, static_cast<nir_variable_mode>(nir_var_shader_in | nir_var_shader_out), ir3_glsl_type_size,
                 nir_lower_io_use_interpolated_input_intrinsics);
    const struct ir3_shader_nir_options nopts = {};
    ir3_nir_lower_io_to_temporaries(nir);
    ir3_finalize_nir(compiler, &nopts, nir);

    struct ir3_shader* shader = static_cast<struct ir3_shader*>(rzalloc_size(nullptr, sizeof(*shader)));
    shader->compiler = compiler;
    shader->type = nir->info.stage;
    shader->nir = nir;
    ir3_nir_post_finalize(shader);

    struct ir3_shader_variant* v = static_cast<struct ir3_shader_variant*>(rzalloc_size(shader, sizeof(*v)));
    v->type = shader->type;
    v->compiler = compiler;
    v->const_state = static_cast<struct ir3_const_state*>(rzalloc_size(v, sizeof(*v->const_state)));
    v->mergedregs = compiler->gen >= 6;
    v->num_ssbos = nir->info.num_ssbos;
    v->num_ibos = nir->info.num_ssbos + nir->info.num_images;
    v->name = ralloc_strdup(v, nir->info.name);
    shader->variants = v;
    shader->variant_count = 1;

    if (ir3_compile_shader_nir(compiler, shader, v))
        die("ir3_compile_shader_nir failed");
    uint32_t* bin = static_cast<uint32_t*>(ir3_shader_assemble(v));
    if (!bin)
        die("ir3_shader_assemble failed");

    const struct ir3_const_state* cs = ir3_const_state(v);
    printf("ir3: %u bytes (%u instruction dwords), instrlen %u, constlen %u vec4, maxReg %d, "
           "local id r%u.%c, workgroup id r%u.%c, %u immediates at vec4 %u, driver params %s, %u UBO ranges, "
           "%u ssbos, %u ibos\n",
           v->info.size, v->info.sizedwords, v->instrlen, v->constlen, v->info.max_reg,
           ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_LOCAL_INVOCATION_ID) >> 2,
           "xyzw"[ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_LOCAL_INVOCATION_ID) & 3],
           ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_WORKGROUP_ID) >> 2,
           "xyzw"[ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_WORKGROUP_ID) & 3], cs->immediates_count,
           cs->allocs.max_const_offset_vec4,
           ir3_const_can_upload(&cs->allocs, IR3_CONST_ALLOC_DRIVER_PARAMS, v->constlen) ? "yes" : "no",
           cs->ubo_state.num_enabled, v->num_ssbos, v->num_ibos);
    ir3_shader_disasm(v, bin, stdout);

    ralloc_free(shader);
    ir3_compiler_destroy(compiler);
    puts("compiler-smoke: ok");
    return 0;
}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/compiler.mk`:

```mk
# tools/compiler.mk: Mesa's compiler libraries linked into the driver, on the
# host (the tests) and for iOS (the phone compiles the image's own .metallib
# files where they are). Included by the main Makefile.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
#   make compiler-smoke       build out/host/compiler-smoke against the host Mesa build and run it on
#                             tools/kernels/fill_id.ll: device row, AIR -> NIR, NIR -> ir3, the listing
#   make ios-compiler-smoke   cross-compile the same program and link it with the iOS archives into
#                             out/ios/compiler-smoke (a Mach-O; not run: there is no phone here)
#
# What the main Makefile takes from here:
#   HAKIOS_METAL_MESA_CXXFLAGS      the -isystem includes (source + generated dirs, src/compiler/air among
#                                   them) and the -D set the host Mesa build compiled its own objects with
#   HAKIOS_METAL_MESA_LIBS          libair + the ir3/nir/util archives of that build, -lz -lm -pthread
#   HAKIOS_METAL_IOS_MESA_CXXFLAGS  the same for the iOS cross build (its own -D set: no glibc, has sysctl)
#   HAKIOS_METAL_IOS_MESA_LIBS      the same archives of the cross build, -lz -lm (ld64 needs no group)
#
# The host half reuses kernels.mk's variables (MESA_SRC, MESA_BUILD, MESA_DEFS,
# MESA_INC, MESA_ARCHIVE_PATHS, MESA_LIBS): that file is included here when the
# Makefile has not done so already, and nothing in it is redefined. The iOS half
# mirrors them with IOS_ names against the cross build.
ifeq ($(origin MESA_INC), undefined)
include tools/kernels.mk
endif

# --- host ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The front end's own include dir: `#include "nir_air.h"` as the Mesa tools do.
HAKIOS_METAL_MESA_CXXFLAGS = $(MESA_DEFS) $(MESA_INC) -isystem $(MESA_SRC)/src/compiler/air
# libair first in the group: it needs nir and util, nothing needs it but the driver.
HAKIOS_METAL_MESA_LIBS = -Wl,--start-group $(MESA_BUILD)/src/compiler/air/libair.a $(MESA_ARCHIVES) -Wl,--end-group -lz -lm -pthread

# --- iOS ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cross build: Mesa built for arm64 iOS by hakios's tools/mk-mesa.sh (meson
# cross file xnu-deps/build/mesa/cross.ini, the same xnu-clang the Makefile
# uses), with the AIR front end from hakios's tools/mesa/air copied in. Its
# libair.a is not a target of the default build (nothing of libOSMesa links it):
# `ninja -C <build> src/compiler/air/libair.a` once after mk-mesa.sh. Override
# IOS_MESA_SRC and IOS_MESA_BUILD for a build elsewhere.
IOS_MESA_ROOT  ?= $(abspath $(HAKIOS))/xnu-deps/build/mesa
IOS_MESA_SRC   ?= $(IOS_MESA_ROOT)/mesa-25.0.7
IOS_MESA_BUILD ?= $(IOS_MESA_ROOT)/build-softpipe-freedreno

# Its -D set, read the same way as the host's (kernels.mk): off the ir3.c.o line
# of its ninja file. It differs from the host's where the libc does (no
# HAVE_SECURE_GETENV, HAVE_BSD_QSORT_R instead of GNU's, HAVE_SYS_SYSCTL_H,
# NDEBUG), and a header compiled with the host's set would declare things the
# iOS objects do not have.
ifeq ($(origin IOS_MESA_DEFS), undefined)
IOS_MESA_DEFS := $(shell grep -m1 -A4 '^build src/freedreno/ir3/libfreedreno_ir3.a.p/ir3.c.o:' $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/build.ninja \
	| grep -m1 ' ARGS = ' | tr ' ' '\n' | grep '^-D' | tr '\n' ' ')
# an empty set compiles Mesa's headers for the wrong libc (c11/threads.h: "Not supported on this platform"): say so
ifeq ($(strip $(IOS_MESA_DEFS)),)
$(warning tools/compiler.mk: no -D set for the iOS Mesa build in $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/build.ninja (not built, or HAKIOS unset?); make ios MESA=1 will not compile)
endif
endif

IOS_MESA_INC = \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/src -isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/include \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/src/freedreno -isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/src/freedreno/common \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/src/compiler -isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/src/compiler/nir \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/src/compiler/air \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_SRC)/src/gallium/include \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/src -isystem $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/src/compiler -isystem $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/src/compiler/nir \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/src/freedreno -isystem $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/src/freedreno/common \
	-isystem $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/src/freedreno/isa

HAKIOS_METAL_IOS_MESA_CXXFLAGS = $(IOS_MESA_DEFS) $(IOS_MESA_INC)
# The same archive list as the host's, under the cross build (libmesa_util_sse41.a
# exists there too, empty on arm64, and is harmless). ld64 resolves across all
# archives whatever their order, so there is no group to open. zlib and libm are
# in the iOS SDK (libz.tbd, libm as part of libSystem); nothing in this set
# needs a framework -- those come with libfreedreno_drm, which the driver does
# not link.
HAKIOS_METAL_IOS_MESA_LIBS = $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/src/compiler/air/libair.a $(addprefix $(IOS_MESA_BUILD)/,$(MESA_ARCHIVE_PATHS)) -lz -lm

# The cross compiler as the main Makefile names it; these are no-ops when it is
# included from there, and let `make -f tools/compiler.mk` work alone.
HAKIOS    ?= ../workspace
SDK       ?= $(abspath $(firstword $(wildcard $(THEOS)/sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk $(HAKIOS)/xnu-deps/theos-mac/sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk $(HOME)/theos/sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk)))
IOS_CXX   ?= $(abspath $(HAKIOS))/xnu-deps/host/bin/xnu-clang++ -arch arm64 -isysroot $(SDK) -miphoneos-version-min=16.0

# --- the smoke program ----------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: compiler-smoke ios-compiler-smoke

out/host/compiler-smoke: tools/compiler-smoke.cc tools/compiler.mk tools/kernels.mk
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O1 -g -Iinclude $(HAKIOS_METAL_MESA_CXXFLAGS) -o $@ tools/compiler-smoke.cc $(HAKIOS_METAL_MESA_LIBS)

compiler-smoke: out/host/compiler-smoke out/host/kernels/fill_id.bc
	out/host/compiler-smoke --chip-id $(CHIP_ID) out/host/kernels/fill_id.bc

out/ios/compiler-smoke: tools/compiler-smoke.cc tools/compiler.mk tools/kernels.mk
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(IOS_CXX) -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -Iinclude $(HAKIOS_METAL_IOS_MESA_CXXFLAGS) -o $@ tools/compiler-smoke.cc $(HAKIOS_METAL_IOS_MESA_LIBS)

ios-compiler-smoke: out/ios/compiler-smoke
	file $<

```

`hakios-metal/tools/ir3-kernel.cc`:

```cc
// ir3-kernel: assemble a text ir3 kernel for the Adreno and write it out as a
// hakios::metal::Kernel fixture.
//
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
//
//   ir3-kernel [--chip-id 0x06030500] [--name NAME] [-o fixture.hpp] kernel.asm
//
// The assembler is Mesa's own (ir3_parse_asm, the one computerator uses), run
// against the device table's row for the chip id, so the words and every
// layout field are what Mesa's compiler would hand freedreno for this GPU.
// What comes out:
//
//   * on stdout, the device row that matched and every field of the Kernel;
//   * in the fixture, constexpr arrays of the words and the immediates, a
//     constexpr Kernel filling every field of include/hakios-metal/kernel.hpp
//     in order, and, as comments, the disassembly (ir3_shader_disasm) and the
//     kernel text itself;
//   * a round trip: the words are disassembled (ir3_isa_disasm) and the
//     instructions compared with the source, so that an operand the assembler
//     read differently from how it was written fails here and not on the phone.
//
// Why C++ and not C: the fixture is C++ and this tool is built by the same
// Makefile with the same -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror. Mesa's ir3 headers
// compile as C++ (computerator is C++ too, and they are BEGINC/ENDC-wrapped),
// but they are not warning-clean under -Wextra, so kernels.mk hands them in
// with -isystem rather than -I: that keeps -Werror for this file and silences
// nothing in it.

#include <cctype>
#include <cerrno>
#include <cstdarg>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "common/freedreno_dev_info.h"
#include "ir3/ir3_assembler.h"
#include "ir3/ir3_compiler.h"
#include "ir3/ir3_shader.h"
#include "isa/ir3-isa.h"

#include "hakios-metal/kernel.hpp"

namespace {

[[noreturn]] void die(const char* fmt, ...)
{
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    fputs("ir3-kernel: ", stderr);
    vfprintf(stderr, fmt, ap);
    fputc('\n', stderr);
    va_end(ap);
    exit(1);
}

std::string readFile(const char* path)
{
    FILE* f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f)
        die("%s: %s", path, strerror(errno));
    std::string s;
    char buf[4096];
    size_t n;
    while ((n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, f)) > 0)
        s.append(buf, n);
    fclose(f);
    return s;
}

// The kernel's name from its file name: the stem, with anything that is not
// an identifier character turned into '_'.
std::string nameFromPath(const char* path)
{
    std::string s = path;
    size_t slash = s.find_last_of('/');
    if (slash != std::string::npos)
        s = s.substr(slash + 1);
    size_t dot = s.find_last_of('.');
    if (dot != std::string::npos && dot > 0)
        s = s.substr(0, dot);
    for (char& ch : s)
        if (!isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)))
            ch = '_';
    if (s.empty() || isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[0])))
        s = "k_" + s;
    return s;
}

// Everything a function that prints into a FILE* produced, as a string.
template <typename F>
std::string capture(F fn)
{
    char* data = nullptr;
    size_t size = 0;
    FILE* f = open_memstream(&data, &size);
    if (!f)
        die("open_memstream failed");
    fn(f);
    fclose(f);
    std::string s(data, size);
    free(data);
    return s;
}

// One instruction line, normalised for the round-trip comparison: the comment
// cut off, lower-cased, whitespace removed, and the disassembler's "(nopN)"
// delay annotation dropped (the source spells delays as nop instructions, and
// the words carry them as such; the annotation is the decoder's reading of the
// same field). Labels ("name:") and directives are skipped by the caller.
std::string normalizeInstr(std::string line)
{
    size_t semi = line.find(';');
    if (semi != std::string::npos)
        line.resize(semi);
    std::string out;
    for (char ch : line)
        if (!isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)))
            out += static_cast<char>(tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)));
    for (;;) {
        size_t p = out.find("(nop");
        if (p == std::string::npos)
            break;
        size_t q = out.find(')', p);
        if (q == std::string::npos)
            break;
        out.erase(p, q - p + 1);
    }
    return out;
}

std::vector<std::string> instructionsOf(const std::string& text, bool isSource)
{
    std::vector<std::string> v;
    size_t pos = 0;
    while (pos < text.size()) {
        size_t nl = text.find('\n', pos);
        if (nl == std::string::npos)
            nl = text.size();
        std::string line = text.substr(pos, nl - pos);
        pos = nl + 1;
        std::string n = normalizeInstr(line);
        if (n.empty())
            continue;
        if (isSource && n[0] == '@')
            continue; // a directive
        if (n.back() == ':')
            continue; // a label
        v.push_back(n);
    }
    return v;
}

void emitWords(FILE* out, const char* name, const uint32_t* words, uint32_t count)
{
    fprintf(out, "constexpr uint32_t %s[] = {", name);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (i % 4 == 0)
            fputs("\n   ", out);
        fprintf(out, " 0x%08x,", words[i]);
    }
    fputs("\n};\n", out);
}

void emitCommentBlock(FILE* out, const std::string& text)
{
    size_t pos = 0;
    while (pos < text.size()) {
        size_t nl = text.find('\n', pos);
        if (nl == std::string::npos)
            nl = text.size();
        fprintf(out, "// %.*s\n", static_cast<int>(nl - pos), text.c_str() + pos);
        pos = nl + 1;
    }
}

} // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    uint64_t chipId = 0x06030500;
    const char* outPath = nullptr;
    const char* nameArg = nullptr;
    const char* inPath = nullptr;

    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
        if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--chip-id") || !strcmp(argv[i], "-c")) {
            if (++i >= argc)
                die("--chip-id needs a value");
            chipId = strtoull(argv[i], nullptr, 0);
        } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "-o")) {
            if (++i >= argc)
                die("-o needs a file");
            outPath = argv[i];
        } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--name") || !strcmp(argv[i], "-n")) {
            if (++i >= argc)
                die("--name needs a value");
            nameArg = argv[i];
        } else if (argv[i][0] == '-' && argv[i][1] != '\0') {
            die("usage: ir3-kernel [--chip-id ID] [--name NAME] [-o fixture.hpp] kernel.asm");
        } else if (!inPath) {
            inPath = argv[i];
        } else {
            die("one kernel at a time");
        }
    }
    if (!inPath)
        die("usage: ir3-kernel [--chip-id ID] [--name NAME] [-o fixture.hpp] kernel.asm");

    // The device row. gpu_id 0 makes the lookup go by chip id, where the
    // 0xffff06030500 row matches any fuse id (freedreno_dev_info.c's
    // WILDCARD_FUSE_ID), which is how 0x06030500 lands on the A635 family.
    struct fd_dev_id devId = {};
    devId.gpu_id = 0;
    devId.chip_id = chipId;
    const struct fd_dev_info* devInfo = fd_dev_info_raw(&devId);
    if (!devInfo)
        die("chip id 0x%llx is not in Mesa's device table", static_cast<unsigned long long>(chipId));
    const char* devName = fd_dev_name(&devId);
    printf("device: %s (chip id 0x%llx, gen %u)\n", devName,
           static_cast<unsigned long long>(chipId), devInfo->chip);

    struct ir3_compiler_options opts = {};
    struct ir3_compiler* compiler = ir3_compiler_create(nullptr, &devId, devInfo, &opts);
    if (!compiler)
        die("ir3_compiler_create failed");

    std::string source = readFile(inPath);
    std::string name = nameArg ? std::string(nameArg) : nameFromPath(inPath);

    // The assembler reads a FILE*; fmemopen keeps the text in hand for the fixture.
    FILE* in = fmemopen(const_cast<char*>(source.data()), source.size(), "r");
    if (!in)
        die("fmemopen failed");
    struct ir3_kernel_info kinfo = {};
    struct ir3_shader* shader = ir3_parse_asm(compiler, &kinfo, in);
    fclose(in);
    if (!shader)
        die("%s: the assembler refused it", inPath);
    struct ir3_shader_variant* v = shader->variants;
    const struct ir3_const_state* cs = ir3_const_state(v);
    const uint32_t* bin = static_cast<const uint32_t*>(v->bin);

    // --- the fields -------------------------------------------------------
    hakios::metal::Kernel k = {};
    k.words = bin;
    k.numWords = v->info.size / 4;
    k.instrlen = v->instrlen;
    k.constlen = v->constlen;
    k.maxReg = v->info.max_reg;
    k.maxHalfReg = v->info.max_half_reg;
    k.doubleThreadsize = v->info.double_threadsize;
    k.mergedRegs = v->mergedregs;
    k.earlyPreamble = v->early_preamble;
    k.branchstackHw = ir3_shader_branchstack_hw(v);
    k.sharedSize = v->shared_size;
    k.pvtmemSize = v->pvtmem_size;
    k.pvtmemPerWave = v->pvtmem_per_wave;
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
        k.localSize[i] = v->local_size[i];
    k.localSizeVariable = v->local_size_variable;
    k.localIdRegid = ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_LOCAL_INVOCATION_ID);
    k.workGroupIdRegid = ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_WORKGROUP_ID);
    k.immediates = cs->immediates;
    k.numImmediates = cs->immediates_count;
    k.immediatesOffsetVec4 = cs->allocs.max_const_offset_vec4;
    k.driverParamsOffsetVec4 =
        ir3_const_can_upload(&cs->allocs, IR3_CONST_ALLOC_DRIVER_PARAMS, v->constlen)
            ? static_cast<int32_t>(cs->allocs.consts[IR3_CONST_ALLOC_DRIVER_PARAMS].offset_vec4)
            : -1;
    k.numUbos = cs->num_ubos;
    k.numSsbos = v->num_ssbos;
    k.numIbos = v->num_ibos;
    k.numSamp = v->num_samp;
    if (cs->ubo_state.num_enabled > hakios::metal::kMaxUboRanges)
        die("%u UBO ranges, the Kernel struct holds %u", cs->ubo_state.num_enabled,
            hakios::metal::kMaxUboRanges);
    k.numUboRanges = cs->ubo_state.num_enabled;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < k.numUboRanges; i++) {
        const struct ir3_ubo_range* r = &cs->ubo_state.range[i];
        k.uboRanges[i].block = r->ubo.block;
        k.uboRanges[i].offsetVec4 = r->offset / 16;
        k.uboRanges[i].startDword = r->start / 4;
        k.uboRanges[i].sizeDwords = (r->end - r->start) / 4;
    }
    if (kinfo.num_bufs > hakios::metal::kMaxBufs)
        die("%u @bufs, the Kernel struct holds %u", kinfo.num_bufs, hakios::metal::kMaxBufs);
    k.numBufs = kinfo.num_bufs;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < k.numBufs; i++) {
        k.bufs[i].sizeBytes = kinfo.buf_sizes[i] * 4; // the assembler counts dwords
        k.bufs[i].constRegid = kinfo.buf_addr_regs[i] == INVALID_REG
                                   ? hakios::metal::kNoConstRegid
                                   : kinfo.buf_addr_regs[i];
        if (kinfo.buf_init_data[i])
            die("@buf %u has initial data; the fixture has no field for it (computerator's buf-init)", i);
    }
    k.numwgConstRegid = kinfo.numwg == INVALID_REG ? hakios::metal::kNoConstRegid : kinfo.numwg;
    k.constantDataOffset = v->info.constant_data_offset;
    k.constantDataSize = v->constant_data_size;
    k.name = name.c_str();
    k.source = source.c_str();

    // --- the listing and the round trip -----------------------------------
    std::string listing = capture([&](FILE* f) { ir3_shader_disasm(v, v->bin, f); });
    struct isa_decode_options dopts = {};
    dopts.gpu_id = compiler->gen * 100;
    dopts.show_errors = true;
    dopts.branch_labels = true;
    std::string disasm = capture([&](FILE* f) {
        ir3_isa_disasm(v->bin, v->info.sizedwords * 4, f, &dopts);
    });
    std::vector<std::string> want = instructionsOf(source, true);
    std::vector<std::string> got = instructionsOf(disasm, false);
    // The decoder reads the padding after `end` as nops; the source stops at end.
    while (got.size() > want.size() && got.back() == "nop")
        got.pop_back();
    bool roundTrip = want == got;
    if (!roundTrip) {
        fprintf(stderr, "round trip: the disassembly differs from the source\n");
        size_t n = want.size() > got.size() ? want.size() : got.size();
        for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            const char* a = i < want.size() ? want[i].c_str() : "(none)";
            const char* b = i < got.size() ? got[i].c_str() : "(none)";
            if (strcmp(a, b))
                fprintf(stderr, "  %zu: source %-40s disasm %s\n", i, a, b);
        }
    }

    // --- stdout -----------------------------------------------------------
    printf("kernel: %s (%s)\n", k.name, inPath);
    printf("  numWords %u (info.size %u bytes, %u instruction dwords)\n", k.numWords, v->info.size,
           v->info.sizedwords);
    printf("  instrlen %u  constlen %u (vec4)\n", k.instrlen, k.constlen);
    printf("  maxReg %d  maxHalfReg %d\n", k.maxReg, k.maxHalfReg);
    printf("  doubleThreadsize %d  mergedRegs %d  earlyPreamble %d  branchstackHw %u\n",
           k.doubleThreadsize, k.mergedRegs, k.earlyPreamble, k.branchstackHw);
    printf("  sharedSize %u  pvtmemSize %u  pvtmemPerWave %d\n", k.sharedSize, k.pvtmemSize,
           k.pvtmemPerWave);
    printf("  localSize %u %u %u  localSizeVariable %d\n", k.localSize[0], k.localSize[1],
           k.localSize[2], k.localSizeVariable);
    printf("  localIdRegid 0x%02x  workGroupIdRegid 0x%02x\n", k.localIdRegid, k.workGroupIdRegid);
    printf("  immediates %u dwords at vec4 %u\n", k.numImmediates, k.immediatesOffsetVec4);
    printf("  driverParamsOffsetVec4 %d\n", k.driverParamsOffsetVec4);
    printf("  numUbos %u  numSsbos %u  numIbos %u  numSamp %u  numUboRanges %u\n", k.numUbos,
           k.numSsbos, k.numIbos, k.numSamp, k.numUboRanges);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < k.numUboRanges; i++)
        printf("    ubo range %u: block %u -> c%u.x, dwords %u..+%u\n", i, k.uboRanges[i].block,
               k.uboRanges[i].offsetVec4, k.uboRanges[i].startDword, k.uboRanges[i].sizeDwords);
    printf("  numBufs %u\n", k.numBufs);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < k.numBufs; i++)
        printf("    buf %u: %u bytes, constRegid 0x%02x\n", i, k.bufs[i].sizeBytes,
               k.bufs[i].constRegid);
    printf("  numwgConstRegid 0x%02x\n", k.numwgConstRegid);
    printf("  constantDataOffset %u  constantDataSize %u\n", k.constantDataOffset,
           k.constantDataSize);
    printf("  round trip: %s\n", roundTrip ? "ok, the disassembly matches the source"
                                           : "MISMATCH (see stderr)");
    fputs(listing.c_str(), stdout);

    // --- the fixture ------------------------------------------------------
    if (outPath) {
        FILE* out = fopen(outPath, "w");
        if (!out)
            die("%s: %s", outPath, strerror(errno));
        fprintf(out,
                "// %s: hakios::metal::Kernel fixture, generated by tools/ir3-kernel from %s\n"
                "// for %s (chip id 0x%llx, gen %u). Do not edit; edit the .asm and rebuild.\n"
                "// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n"
                "#pragma once\n\n"
                "#include \"hakios-metal/kernel.hpp\"\n\n"
                "namespace hakios::metal::kernels {\n\n",
                k.name, inPath, devName, static_cast<unsigned long long>(chipId), devInfo->chip);

        std::string wordsName = name + "_words";
        emitWords(out, wordsName.c_str(), bin, k.numWords);
        fputc('\n', out);
        std::string immName = name + "_immediates";
        if (k.numImmediates) {
            emitWords(out, immName.c_str(), k.immediates, k.numImmediates);
            fputc('\n', out);
        }

        fprintf(out, "constexpr Kernel %s = {\n", name.c_str());
        fprintf(out, "    /* .words = */ %s,\n", wordsName.c_str());
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numWords = */ %u,\n", k.numWords);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .instrlen = */ %u,\n", k.instrlen);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .constlen = */ %u,\n", k.constlen);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .maxReg = */ %d,\n", k.maxReg);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .maxHalfReg = */ %d,\n", k.maxHalfReg);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .doubleThreadsize = */ %s,\n", k.doubleThreadsize ? "true" : "false");
        fprintf(out, "    /* .mergedRegs = */ %s,\n", k.mergedRegs ? "true" : "false");
        fprintf(out, "    /* .earlyPreamble = */ %s,\n", k.earlyPreamble ? "true" : "false");
        fprintf(out, "    /* .branchstackHw = */ %u,\n", k.branchstackHw);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .sharedSize = */ %u,\n", k.sharedSize);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .pvtmemSize = */ %u,\n", k.pvtmemSize);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .pvtmemPerWave = */ %s,\n", k.pvtmemPerWave ? "true" : "false");
        fprintf(out, "    /* .localSize = */ {%u, %u, %u},\n", k.localSize[0], k.localSize[1],
                k.localSize[2]);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .localSizeVariable = */ %s,\n", k.localSizeVariable ? "true" : "false");
        fprintf(out, "    /* .localIdRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", k.localIdRegid);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .workGroupIdRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", k.workGroupIdRegid);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .immediates = */ %s,\n", k.numImmediates ? immName.c_str() : "nullptr");
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numImmediates = */ %u,\n", k.numImmediates);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .immediatesOffsetVec4 = */ %u,\n", k.immediatesOffsetVec4);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .driverParamsOffsetVec4 = */ %d,\n", k.driverParamsOffsetVec4);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numUbos = */ %u,\n", k.numUbos);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numSsbos = */ %u,\n", k.numSsbos);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numIbos = */ %u,\n", k.numIbos);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numSamp = */ %u,\n", k.numSamp);
        fputs("    /* .uboRanges = */ {", out);
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < hakios::metal::kMaxUboRanges; i++)
            fprintf(out, "%s{%u, %u, %u, %u}", i ? ", " : "", k.uboRanges[i].block,
                    k.uboRanges[i].offsetVec4, k.uboRanges[i].startDword, k.uboRanges[i].sizeDwords);
        fputs("},\n", out);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numUboRanges = */ %u,\n", k.numUboRanges);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numBufs = */ %u,\n", k.numBufs);
        fputs("    /* .bufs = */ {", out);
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < hakios::metal::kMaxBufs; i++)
            fprintf(out, "%s{%u, 0x%02x}", i ? ", " : "", k.bufs[i].sizeBytes,
                    i < k.numBufs ? k.bufs[i].constRegid : hakios::metal::kNoConstRegid);
        fputs("},\n", out);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .numwgConstRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", k.numwgConstRegid);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .constantDataOffset = */ %u,\n", k.constantDataOffset);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .constantDataSize = */ %u,\n", k.constantDataSize);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .name = */ \"%s\",\n", k.name);
        fprintf(out, "    /* .source = */ R\"ir3(%s)ir3\",\n", k.source);
        // a text kernel addresses no textures: the fields are zero, but written so that -Wextra sees every member initialized
        fprintf(out, "    /* .textures = */ {},\n    /* .numTextureSlots = */ 0,\n    /* .samplerMask = */ 0,\n    /* .constantDataUbo = */ 0,\n");
        fputs("};\n\n", out);

        fputs("// The disassembly (ir3_shader_disasm), and whether it read back as the source:\n", out);
        fprintf(out, "// round trip: %s\n", roundTrip ? "ok" : "MISMATCH");
        emitCommentBlock(out, listing);
        fputs("\n} // namespace hakios::metal::kernels\n", out);
        fclose(out);
        printf("wrote %s\n", outPath);
    }

    return roundTrip ? 0 : 2;
}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels.mk`:

```mk
# tools/kernels.mk: the host-side kernel tooling. Included by the main Makefile.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
#   make ir3-kernel      build out/host/ir3-kernel against a Mesa host build
#   make fixtures        regenerate tests/fixtures/*.hpp from tools/kernels/*.asm
#   make air-fixtures    regenerate tests/fixtures/*_air.hpp from tools/kernels/*.ll, with out/host/ir3_compiler:
#                        Mesa's ir3_compiler carrying tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch, built here from the host build
#
# The tool links Mesa's ir3 assembler, so it needs a Mesa source tree and a
# meson build of it (the static libraries, and the generated headers). Point
# MESA_SRC and MESA_BUILD at them. The default is a host build in the kernel's tree (xnu-deps/build/mesa-host: a meson build
# of Mesa with the AIR front end, tools/mk-mesa.sh's sources), recognised by its libair.a. Nothing of it is copied, only linked
# against. Without it the tests that need the compiler cannot be built: `make ios` needs only the cross build.
MESA_HOST  ?= $(abspath $(HAKIOS))/xnu-deps/build/mesa-host
MESA_SRC   ?= $(MESA_HOST)/mesa-25.0.7
MESA_BUILD ?= $(MESA_HOST)/build

# The chip id the fixtures are assembled for: the phone's Adreno 7c+ Gen 3
# (A635). Mesa's table matches it through its 0xffff06030500 wildcard row.
CHIP_ID    ?= 0x06030500

# Mesa's headers want the same -D flags its own objects were compiled with
# (HAVE_* for what the host has, _GNU_SOURCE, and so on): a header compiled
# with a different set declares things differently. They are read from the
# build's ninja file, off one ir3 object, rather than copied here, so that a
# build on another machine or of another Mesa gets its own.
ifeq ($(origin MESA_DEFS), undefined)
MESA_DEFS := $(shell grep -m1 -A4 '^build src/freedreno/ir3/libfreedreno_ir3.a.p/ir3.c.o:' $(MESA_BUILD)/build.ninja \
	| grep -m1 ' ARGS = ' | tr ' ' '\n' | grep '^-D' | tr '\n' ' ')
endif

# -isystem, not -I: Mesa's headers are not clean under -Wextra, and the tool is
# built -Werror. Both the source and the build tree are needed: the build tree
# has the generated headers (ir3-isa.h, nir_opcodes.h, freedreno_devices.h).
MESA_INC = \
	-isystem $(MESA_SRC)/src -isystem $(MESA_SRC)/include \
	-isystem $(MESA_SRC)/src/freedreno -isystem $(MESA_SRC)/src/freedreno/common \
	-isystem $(MESA_SRC)/src/compiler -isystem $(MESA_SRC)/src/compiler/nir \
	-isystem $(MESA_SRC)/src/gallium/include \
	-isystem $(MESA_BUILD)/src -isystem $(MESA_BUILD)/src/compiler -isystem $(MESA_BUILD)/src/compiler/nir \
	-isystem $(MESA_BUILD)/src/freedreno -isystem $(MESA_BUILD)/src/freedreno/common \
	-isystem $(MESA_BUILD)/src/freedreno/isa

# The link line is ir3_disasm's (src/freedreno/ir3/meson.build, the smallest
# ir3 consumer Mesa builds), read off the build's ninja file: ir3 and its
# encoder/decoder, nir (ir3 pulls its headers and a few symbols), the util
# library and its parts, and the device table. No gallium, no drm.
# The archives as paths under a build directory, so that compiler.mk can take
# the same list from the iOS cross build (MESA_ARCHIVE_PATHS) and add libair.
MESA_ARCHIVE_PATHS = \
	src/freedreno/ir3/libfreedreno_ir3.a \
	src/freedreno/isa/libir3encode.a \
	src/freedreno/isa/libir3decode.a \
	src/compiler/isaspec/libisaspec.a \
	src/compiler/nir/libnir.a \
	src/compiler/libcompiler.a \
	src/freedreno/fdl/libfreedreno_layout.a \
	src/freedreno/common/libfreedreno_common.a \
	src/util/libmesa_util.a \
	src/util/libmesa_util_sse41.a \
	src/util/blake3/libblake3.a \
	src/c11/impl/libmesa_util_c11.a
MESA_ARCHIVES = $(addprefix $(MESA_BUILD)/,$(MESA_ARCHIVE_PATHS))
MESA_LIBS = -Wl,--start-group $(MESA_ARCHIVES) -Wl,--end-group -lz -lm -pthread

KERNEL_ASM      = $(wildcard tools/kernels/*.asm)
KERNEL_FIXTURES = $(patsubst tools/kernels/%.asm,tests/fixtures/%.hpp,$(KERNEL_ASM))

.PHONY: ir3-kernel fixtures

ir3-kernel: out/host/ir3-kernel

out/host/ir3-kernel: tools/ir3-kernel.cc include/hakios-metal/kernel.hpp tools/kernels.mk
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O1 -g -Iinclude $(MESA_DEFS) $(MESA_INC) -o $@ tools/ir3-kernel.cc $(MESA_LIBS)

tests/fixtures/%.hpp: tools/kernels/%.asm out/host/ir3-kernel
	out/host/ir3-kernel --chip-id $(CHIP_ID) -o $@ $<

fixtures: $(KERNEL_FIXTURES)

# The AIR path. A Metal kernel written as LLVM IR (tools/kernels/*.ll) goes
# through llvm-as, then through Mesa's ir3_compiler with the AIR front end --
# built with tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch applied, which gives it -o (the fixture),
# -s (the text to carry) and -n (its name): the stock ir3_compiler, and the one
# in MESA_BUILD, prints a listing and nothing else. The patched one is built
# here, as out/host/ir3_compiler, from MESA_BUILD's own compile and link lines
# for that program (read off its build.ninja, as MESA_DEFS is) over a copy of
# ir3_cmdline.c with the patch applied: one object and one link, no Mesa
# rebuild, and nothing written into the Mesa tree. IR3_COMPILER= names another
# (a Mesa build that carries the patch itself).
LLVM_AS      ?= llvm-as
IR3_COMPILER ?= out/host/ir3_compiler
IR3_CMDLINE_C = $(MESA_SRC)/src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/ir3/ir3_cmdline.c
IR3_CMDLINE_ARGS = $(shell grep -m1 -A4 '^build src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/ir3_compiler.p/ir3_ir3_cmdline.c.o:' $(MESA_BUILD)/build.ninja \
	| grep -m1 ' ARGS = ' | sed 's/^ ARGS = //')
IR3_COMPILER_LINK_ARGS = $(shell grep -m1 -A4 '^build src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/ir3_compiler:' $(MESA_BUILD)/build.ninja \
	| grep -m1 ' LINK_ARGS = ' | sed 's/^ LINK_ARGS = //')
KERNEL_LL        = $(wildcard tools/kernels/*.ll)
KERNEL_BC        = $(patsubst tools/kernels/%.ll,out/host/kernels/%.bc,$(KERNEL_LL))
KERNEL_AIR_FIXTURES = $(patsubst tools/kernels/%.ll,tests/fixtures/%_air.hpp,$(KERNEL_LL))

out/host/ir3-dump/ir3_cmdline.c: tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch $(IR3_CMDLINE_C)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	patch -s -o $@ $(IR3_CMDLINE_C) tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch

# The compile runs in MESA_BUILD because the -I paths of its ninja line are relative to it; the object and the program
# land here. $(CC) and $(CXX) stand in for the build's `ccache cc` and `c++`.
out/host/ir3_compiler: out/host/ir3-dump/ir3_cmdline.c tools/kernels.mk
	@test -n "$(IR3_CMDLINE_ARGS)" || { echo "tools/kernels.mk: no compile line for ir3_cmdline.c in $(MESA_BUILD)/build.ninja"; exit 1; }
	cd $(MESA_BUILD) && $(CC) $(IR3_CMDLINE_ARGS) -c $(abspath $<) -o $(abspath out/host/ir3-dump/ir3_cmdline.o)
	cd $(MESA_BUILD) && $(CXX) -o $(abspath $@) $(abspath out/host/ir3-dump/ir3_cmdline.o) $(IR3_COMPILER_LINK_ARGS)

.PHONY: air-fixtures
# keep the .bc: make would otherwise delete it as an intermediate and re-run llvm-as each time
.SECONDARY:

out/host/kernels/%.bc: tools/kernels/%.ll
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(LLVM_AS) -o $@ $<

tests/fixtures/%_air.hpp: out/host/kernels/%.bc tools/kernels/%.ll $(IR3_COMPILER)
	$(IR3_COMPILER) --chip-id $(CHIP_ID) -o $@ -s tools/kernels/$*.ll -n $*_air $< > out/host/kernels/$*.listing

air-fixtures: $(KERNEL_AIR_FIXTURES)

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/argbuf_res.ll`:

```ll
; argbuf_res, the AIR side: a kernel whose every resource is a member of one
; argument buffer at [[buffer(0)]] -- the output buffer, a sampler and two
; textures -- generated by workspace-air's tools/air/argbufcheck.py (its
; argbuf_resources case: build(), chain()) and kept as it came out:
;     out[tid] = (uint(t0.sample(s, 1.5).x) << 16) + uint(t1.read(uint2(1, 1)).x)
; Hand-written by that script, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata is
; Apple's convention.
; Why it exists: the runtime reads each member's eight bytes out of the set (a
; buffer's GPU address, a texture's or sampler's resource id) and binds it at
; the index the front end allocated; with t0 all 7 and t1 all 1000 the word is
; 7 << 16 | 1000, and two textures swapped, or a member not bound, give another.
source_filename = "argbuf_res"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios14.0.0"

%"struct.metal::sampler" = type { ptr addrspace(2) }
%"struct.metal::texture2d" = type { ptr addrspace(1) }
%struct.spvDescriptorSetBuffer0 = type { ptr addrspace(1), %"struct.metal::sampler", %"struct.metal::texture2d", %"struct.metal::texture2d" }
declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32) local_unnamed_addr
declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, i32, i32) local_unnamed_addr

define void @argbuf_res(ptr addrspace(2) %0, i32 %1) local_unnamed_addr {
  %outa = getelementptr inbounds %struct.spvDescriptorSetBuffer0, ptr addrspace(2) %0, i64 0, i32 0
  %out = load ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2) %outa, align 8
  %sampa = getelementptr inbounds %struct.spvDescriptorSetBuffer0, ptr addrspace(2) %0, i64 0, i32 1, i32 0
  %samp = load ptr addrspace(2), ptr addrspace(2) %sampa, align 8
  %t0a = getelementptr inbounds %struct.spvDescriptorSetBuffer0, ptr addrspace(2) %0, i64 0, i32 2
  %t0b = getelementptr inbounds %"struct.metal::texture2d", ptr addrspace(2) %t0a, i64 0, i32 0
  %t0 = load ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2) %t0b, align 8
  %t1a = getelementptr inbounds %struct.spvDescriptorSetBuffer0, ptr addrspace(2) %0, i64 0, i32 3
  %t1b = getelementptr inbounds %"struct.metal::texture2d", ptr addrspace(2) %t1a, i64 0, i32 0
  %t1 = load ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2) %t1b, align 8
  %sr = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t0, ptr addrspace(2) %samp, <2 x float> <float 1.500000000e+00, float 1.500000000e+00>, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.0, float 0.0, i32 0)
  %sv = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %sr, 0
  %s0 = extractelement <4 x float> %sv, i64 0
  %rr = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t1, <2 x i32> <i32 1, i32 1>, i32 0, i32 0)
  %rv = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %rr, 0
  %r0 = extractelement <4 x float> %rv, i64 0
  %si = fptoui float %s0 to i32
  %ri = fptoui float %r0 to i32
  %hi = shl i32 %si, 16
  %r = add i32 %hi, %ri
  %oi = zext i32 %1 to i64
  %op = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %oi
  store i32 %r, ptr addrspace(1) %op, align 4

  ret void
}

!llvm.module.flags = !{!0}
!air.version = !{!1}
!air.language_version = !{!2}
!air.kernel = !{!3}

!0 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
!1 = !{i32 2, i32 3, i32 0}
!2 = !{!"Metal", i32 2, i32 3, i32 0}
!3 = !{ptr @argbuf_res, !4, !5}
!4 = !{}
!5 = !{!6, !100}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.indirect_buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 32, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.struct_type_info", !7, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 32, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 8, !"air.arg_type_name", !"spvDescriptorSetBuffer0", !"air.arg_name", !"spvDescriptorSet0"}
!7 = !{i32 0, i32 8, i32 0, !"ty_devrw_0", !"devrw0", !"air.indirect_argument", !10, i32 8, i32 8, i32 0, !"ty_sampler_1", !"sampler1", !"air.indirect_argument", !11, i32 16, i32 8, i32 0, !"ty_texture_2", !"texture2", !"air.indirect_argument", !12, i32 24, i32 8, i32 0, !"ty_texture_3", !"texture3", !"air.indirect_argument", !13}
!10 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"ty_devrw_0", !"air.arg_name", !"devrw0"}
!11 = !{i32 1, !"air.sampler", !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"ty_sampler_1", !"air.arg_name", !"sampler1"}
!12 = !{i32 2, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 2, i32 1, !"air.sample", !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"ty_texture_2", !"air.arg_name", !"texture2"}
!13 = !{i32 3, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 3, i32 1, !"air.sample", !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"ty_texture_3", !"air.arg_name", !"texture3"}
!100 = !{i32 1, !"air.thread_index_in_threadgroup", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"tid"}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/ballot_id.ll`:

```ll
; ballot_id: a SIMD-group ballot, the LLVM IR a Metal compiler emits for
;
;     kernel void ballot_id(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       ulong m = (ulong)simd_ballot(gid % 3 == 0);
;       out[gid] = (gid & 1) ? uint(m >> 32) : uint(m);
;     }
;
; Dispatched in groups of 64, one group of 64 lanes each (hakios-metal keeps ir3 to its single threadsize), so the
; mask's bit l is (group base + l) % 3 == 0: a pattern that differs from group to group, and a high half that is not
; zero -- a 32-lane mask or a truncated one reads 0 in every odd word. Resident Evil 4's culling passes elect a lane
; with a ballot, which the front end refused. Hand-written, ours, MIT; the metadata's shape is Apple's convention, as
; in fill_id.ll.

source_filename = "ballot_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare i64 @air.simd_ballot.i64(i1)

define void @ballot_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %r = urem i32 %gid, 3
  %c = icmp eq i32 %r, 0
  %m = tail call i64 @air.simd_ballot.i64(i1 %c)
  %hi64 = lshr i64 %m, 32
  %hi = trunc i64 %hi64 to i32
  %lo = trunc i64 %m to i32
  %odd = and i32 %gid, 1
  %isodd = icmp ne i32 %odd, 0
  %v = select i1 %isodd, i32 %hi, i32 %lo
  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64
  %po = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  store i32 %v, ptr addrspace(1) %po, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @ballot_id, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/bytes_id.ll`:

```ll
; bytes_id: a word taken apart into its bytes and put back, the AIR a Metal compiler emits for
;
;     kernel void bytes_id(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       uchar4 b = as_type<uchar4>(gid * 0x9E3779B1u);
;       out[gid] = uint(b.x) + uint(b.y) + uint(b.z) + uint(b.w) + (as_type<uint>(b.wzyx) & 0xff00u);
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT; the metadata's shape is Apple's convention, as in fill_id.ll. The bitcast from 1 x 32 bits
; to 4 x 8 (and back) is what mediaserverd's hbf_compute_residual_error_kernel did, which the front end refused --
; and MPS aborted the process on the refusal, over and over.

source_filename = "bytes_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define void @bytes_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %m = mul i32 %gid, -1640531535
  %b = bitcast i32 %m to <4 x i8>
  %b0 = extractelement <4 x i8> %b, i64 0
  %b1 = extractelement <4 x i8> %b, i64 1
  %b2 = extractelement <4 x i8> %b, i64 2
  %b3 = extractelement <4 x i8> %b, i64 3
  %z0 = zext i8 %b0 to i32
  %z1 = zext i8 %b1 to i32
  %z2 = zext i8 %b2 to i32
  %z3 = zext i8 %b3 to i32
  %s1 = add i32 %z0, %z1
  %s2 = add i32 %s1, %z2
  %s3 = add i32 %s2, %z3
  %r = shufflevector <4 x i8> %b, <4 x i8> poison, <4 x i32> <i32 3, i32 2, i32 1, i32 0>
  %w = bitcast <4 x i8> %r to i32
  %k = and i32 %w, 65280
  %v = add i32 %s3, %k
  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64
  %po = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  store i32 %v, ptr addrspace(1) %po, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @bytes_id, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}

```

```ll
;
;     kernel void chain160(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &c [[buffer(1)]],
;                            uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     { uint v = gid ^ c; for each step i: v = rotl((v ^ X[i]) * M[i], R[i]); out[gid] = v; }
```

```ll
;
;     kernel void chain220(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &c [[buffer(1)]],
;                            uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     { uint v = gid ^ c; for each step i: v = rotl((v ^ X[i]) * M[i], R[i]); out[gid] = v; }
;
; Its point is its length: ir3 makes more than 127 instruction units of it, past what CP_LOAD_STATE6 preloads,
; so the GPU fetches the rest from SP_CS_OBJ_START while it runs. Hand-written generator, ours, MIT.
```

```ll
;
;     kernel void chain_fs(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &c [[buffer(1)]],
;                            uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     { uint v = gid ^ c; for each step i: v = rotl((v ^ X[i]) * M[i], R[i]); out[gid] = v; }
;
; Its point is its length: ir3 makes more than 127 instruction units of it, past what CP_LOAD_STATE6 preloads,
; so the GPU fetches the rest from SP_CS_OBJ_START while it runs. Hand-written generator, ours, MIT.
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/fill_id.asm`:

```asm
; fill_id: out[gid] = gid * K + c, for every invocation of the grid.
;
; SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT. Ours, written for hakios-metal; nothing of Apple's.
; The shape (directives, then a value stored through stib into IBO 0 at the
; invocation's own index, then end) is the pattern of Mesa's computerator
; example invocationid.asm (MIT), which is where this syntax is documented by
; use; that file is not copied here.
;
; K = 0x9E3779B1 is odd, so gid -> gid*K is a bijection on 32-bit values and
; every slot of the buffer gets a value no other invocation could have written:
; a readback checks WHICH invocation wrote each word, not only that one did.
; c comes from a const: c0.x, which the driver may overwrite in the immediates
; before uploading them (its default below is deliberately not 0, so a dispatch
; that forgot the constants cannot pass by reading zeros).
;
; The multiply. The a6xx has no 32x32 -> 32 multiply instruction: mul.u24
; takes 24-bit operands and K needs 32, so this is ir3's own lowering of a
; 32-bit imul (ir3_nir_imul.py, and what ir3_compiler emits for fill_id.ll):
;
;   mull.u    t, a, b        t  = lo16(a) * lo16(b)
;   madsh.m16 t, a, b, t     t += (lo16(a) * hi16(b)) << 16
;   madsh.m16 t, b, a, t     t += (lo16(b) * hi16(a)) << 16
;
; which is a*b modulo 2^32: the hi16*hi16 term is shifted out.
;
; The grid. @localsize fixes 64 invocations per workgroup, one wave of 64 on
; this GPU (threadsize_base 64, so ir3 keeps THREAD64 for it), and the buffer
; is 1024 words, so the driver dispatches 16 workgroups along x. The hardware
; hands each invocation its local id in r0.xyz (@invocationid) and its
; workgroup id in r48.xyz (@wgid; on gen 6 the workgroup id lands in a shared
; register, which is why it must be r48 or above), and the kernel forms
;
;   gid = wgid.x * 64 + lid.x       (shl.b by 6, then add.u)
;
; itself. @numwg is not used: the grid's size is not needed to form gid, so no
; const slot is reserved for it (numwgConstRegid is kNoConstRegid in the fixture).
;
; Delays. The assembler schedules nothing: on the a6xx an ALU result is ready
; for another ALU instruction 3 cycles later (ir3 delay_slots.alu_to_alu) and
; for a memory instruction 6 cycles later (delay_slots.non_alu), so a (rpt2)nop
; sits between dependent ALU instructions and a (rpt5)nop before the store,
; as the computerator examples do.

@localsize 64, 1, 1
@buf 1024                        ; g[0]: 1024 dwords = 4096 bytes, IBO 0
@const(c0.x) 0x00001234, 0, 0, 0 ; c in c0.x; the driver sets it (immediates[0])
@wgid(r48.x)                     ; r48.xyz = workgroup id
@invocationid(r0.x)              ; r0.xyz = local invocation id

shl.b r1.x, r48.x, 6             ; r1.x = wgid.x * 64
mov.u32u32 r2.x, 0x9e3779b1      ; r2.x = K (fills one of the three delay slots)
(rpt1)nop
add.u r1.x, r1.x, r0.x           ; r1.x = gid
(rpt2)nop
mull.u r3.x, r1.x, r2.x          ; lo16(gid) * lo16(K)
(rpt2)nop
madsh.m16 r3.x, r1.x, r2.x, r3.x ; += (lo16(gid) * hi16(K)) << 16
(rpt2)nop
madsh.m16 r3.x, r2.x, r1.x, r3.x ; += (lo16(K) * hi16(gid)) << 16  -> gid*K mod 2^32
(rpt2)nop
add.u r3.x, r3.x, c0.x           ; + c
(rpt5)nop
stib.b.untyped.1d.u32.1.imm r3.x, r1.x, 0   ; out[gid] = r3.x (IBO 0, element r1.x)
end

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/fill_id.ll`:

```ll
; fill_id, the AIR side: the same kernel as tools/kernels/fill_id.asm, written as
; the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void fill_id(device uint *out        [[buffer(0)]],
;                         constant uint &c        [[buffer(1)]],
;                         uint gid                [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       out[gid] = gid * 0x9E3779B1u + c;
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple. Only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention (the air.kernel node, the per-argument nodes,
; the version nodes), which is what the AIR front end reads; the values are
; this kernel's own.
;
; The two paths meet on the buffer contents: out[gid] must come out identical
; whether the Adreno ran the words of fill_id.asm or the words ir3 compiled
; from this file. What DIFFERS is everything around the words -- see
; tests/fixtures/fill_id.hpp against tests/fixtures/fill_id_air.hpp.
;
;   llvm-as tools/kernels/fill_id.ll -o fill_id.bc
;   air2nir fill_id.bc                               (the NIR)
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 fill_id.bc     (the Adreno listing)

source_filename = "fill_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

; addrspace(1) is Metal's `device`, addrspace(2) its `constant`: the front end
; turns the first into an SSBO at the buffer index and the second into a UBO at
; the buffer index (air_to_nir.c, the air.address_space switch).
define void @fill_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, ptr addrspace(2) %c, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %cv = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c, align 4
  ; 0x9E3779B1 is odd, so gid -> gid*K is a bijection on 32-bit values: no two
  ; invocations can write the same word, which is what makes a readback of the
  ; buffer a check of WHICH invocation wrote each slot and not only that one did.
  %m = mul i32 %gid, -1640531535
  %v = add i32 %m, %cv
  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64
  %po = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  store i32 %v, ptr addrspace(1) %po, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @fill_id, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6, !7}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 4, !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"c"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/gen-long-chain.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Writes tools/kernels/long_chain.ll: a compute kernel longer than the 127 instruction units the A6xx preloads.

    python3 -I tools/kernels/gen-long-chain.py > tools/kernels/long_chain.ll
    python3 -I tools/kernels/gen-long-chain.py STEPS NAME > tools/kernels/NAME.ll   (the shorter ones that bracket 127)
    python3 -I tools/kernels/gen-long-chain.py 700 chain_fs fs > tools/kernels/chain_fs.ll   (the same as a fragment function)

The fragment form starts from the pixel's y * 64 + x and the constant 0x1234 in place of the buffer, and returns the
chain's low three bytes as red, green and blue over 255, which an RGBA8Unorm target stores as the bytes themselves.

Each of STEPS steps mixes the running value with xor, a multiply and a rotate built from two shifts; the value starts
from the invocation's id and a constant read from a buffer, so nothing can be folded at compile time and every step
stays an instruction sequence of its own. long_chain_reference() in tools/probe.cpp computes the same chain on the
processor. Hand-written generator, MIT; the metadata's shape is the AIR convention fill_id.ll describes.
"""
import sys

STEPS = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 700
NAME = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "long_chain"
FRAGMENT = len(sys.argv) > 3 and sys.argv[3] == "fs"


def k(i):
    # per-step constants from a fixed odd-multiplier sequence: odd multipliers keep each step a bijection
    x = (0x9E3779B1 * (i + 1)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return x ^ 0x5BD1E995, (x | 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF, 5 + i % 23


def s32(v):
    return v - (1 << 32) if v >= 1 << 31 else v


lines = []
lines.append("; %s: %d dependent xor/multiply/rotate steps on (gid, c), written out by gen-long-chain.py; do not edit." % (NAME, STEPS))
lines.append(";")
lines.append(";     kernel void %s(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &c [[buffer(1)]]," % NAME)
lines.append(";                            uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])")
lines.append(";     { uint v = gid ^ c; for each step i: v = rotl((v ^ X[i]) * M[i], R[i]); out[gid] = v; }")
lines.append(";")
lines.append("; Its point is its length: ir3 makes more than 127 instruction units of it, past what CP_LOAD_STATE6 preloads,")
lines.append("; so the GPU fetches the rest from SP_CS_OBJ_START while it runs. Hand-written generator, ours, MIT.")
lines.append("")
lines.append('source_filename = "%s"' % NAME)
lines.append('target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"')
lines.append('target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"')
lines.append("")
if not FRAGMENT:
    lines.append("define void @%s(" % NAME + "ptr addrspace(1) %out, ptr addrspace(2) %c, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {")
    lines.append("  %cv = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c, align 4")
    lines.append("  %v0 = xor i32 %gid, %cv")
else:
    lines.append("define <4 x float> @%s(<4 x float> %%pos) local_unnamed_addr {" % NAME)
    lines.append("  %px = extractelement <4 x float> %pos, i32 0")
    lines.append("  %py = extractelement <4 x float> %pos, i32 1")
    lines.append("  %x = fptoui float %px to i32")
    lines.append("  %y = fptoui float %py to i32")
    lines.append("  %ys = shl i32 %y, 6")
    lines.append("  %gid = add i32 %ys, %x")
    lines.append("  %v0 = xor i32 %gid, 4660")
for i in range(STEPS):
    x, m, r = k(i)
    lines.append("  %%a%d = xor i32 %%v%d, %d" % (i, i, s32(x)))
    lines.append("  %%b%d = mul i32 %%a%d, %d" % (i, i, s32(m)))
    lines.append("  %%l%d = shl i32 %%b%d, %d" % (i, i, r))
    lines.append("  %%h%d = lshr i32 %%b%d, %d" % (i, i, 32 - r))
    lines.append("  %%v%d = or i32 %%l%d, %%h%d" % (i + 1, i, i))
if not FRAGMENT:
    lines.append("  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64")
    lines.append("  %po = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t")
    lines.append("  store i32 %%v%d, ptr addrspace(1) %%po, align 4" % STEPS)
    lines.append("  ret void")
else:
    v = "%%v%d" % STEPS
    lines.append("  %%out_r = and i32 %s, 255" % v)
    lines.append("  %%out_g0 = lshr i32 %s, 8" % v)
    lines.append("  %out_g = and i32 %out_g0, 255")
    lines.append("  %%out_b0 = lshr i32 %s, 16" % v)
    lines.append("  %out_b = and i32 %out_b0, 255")
    for ch in "rgb":
        lines.append("  %%out_%sf = uitofp i32 %%out_%s to float" % (ch, ch))
        lines.append("  %%out_%sn = fdiv float %%out_%sf, 2.550000e+02" % (ch, ch))
    lines.append("  %c0 = insertelement <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %out_rn, i32 0")
    lines.append("  %c1 = insertelement <4 x float> %c0, float %out_gn, i32 1")
    lines.append("  %c2 = insertelement <4 x float> %c1, float %out_bn, i32 2")
    lines.append("  ret <4 x float> %c2")
lines.append("}")
lines.append("")
lines.append("!air.version = !{!0}")
lines.append("!air.language_version = !{!1}")
if not FRAGMENT:
    lines.append("!air.kernel = !{!2}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}")
    lines.append('!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}')
    lines.append("!2 = !{ptr @%s, !3, !4}" % NAME)
    lines.append("!3 = !{}")
    lines.append("!4 = !{!5, !6, !7}")
    lines.append('!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}')
    lines.append('!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 4, !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"c"}')
    lines.append('!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}')
else:
    lines.append("!air.fragment = !{!2}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}")
    lines.append('!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}')
    lines.append("!2 = !{ptr @%s, !3, !5}" % NAME)
    lines.append("!3 = !{!4}")
    lines.append('!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}')
    lines.append("!5 = !{!6}")
    lines.append('!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.position", !"air.center", !"air.no_perspective", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"pos"}')
print("\n".join(lines))
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/hole_vs.ll`:

```ll
; hole_vs: a vertex function that declares an output it never writes, ahead of its position: the LLVM IR a Metal
; compiler would emit for
;
;     struct Vary { float4 color; float2 unused; float4 position [[position]]; };
;     vertex Vary hole_vs(float4 position [[attribute(0)]], float4 color [[attribute(1)]])
;     {
;       Vary v;
;       v.color = color;
;       v.position = position;
;       return v;            // v.unused left undef
;     }
;
; The front end gives every declared output a driver_location before NIR sees which are written, and ir3 places outputs
; by it, so the unwritten one is a hole in ir3's output table: slot 0 and no register. Slot 0 is VARYING_SLOT_POS, and
; Resident Evil 4's VSGUI (its TexCoord1 undef) was refused as writing no position because the lookup found the hole.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT; only the shape of the metadata is Apple's convention (tri_pos_vs.ll).

source_filename = "hole_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <{ <4 x float>, <2 x float>, <4 x float> }> @hole_vs(<4 x float> %pos, <4 x float> %color) local_unnamed_addr {
  %r0 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <2 x float>, <4 x float> }> undef, <4 x float> %color, 0
  %r1 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <2 x float>, <4 x float> }> %r0, <4 x float> %pos, 2
  ret <{ <4 x float>, <2 x float>, <4 x float> }> %r1
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.vertex = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @hole_vs, !3, !7}
!3 = !{!4, !5, !6}
!4 = !{!"air.vertex_output", !"generated(5colorDv4_f)", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"color"}
!5 = !{!"air.vertex_output", !"generated(6unusedDv2_f)", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float2", !"air.arg_name", !"unused"}
!6 = !{!"air.position", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"position"}
!7 = !{!8, !9}
!8 = !{i32 0, !"air.vertex_input", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"position"}
!9 = !{i32 1, !"air.vertex_input", !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"color"}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/long_chain.ll`:
