```ll
; long_chain: 700 dependent xor/multiply/rotate steps on (gid, c), written out by gen-long-chain.py; do not edit.
;
;     kernel void long_chain(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &c [[buffer(1)]],
;                            uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     { uint v = gid ^ c; for each step i: v = rotl((v ^ X[i]) * M[i], R[i]); out[gid] = v; }
;
; Its point is its length: ir3 makes more than 127 instruction units of it, past what CP_LOAD_STATE6 preloads,
; so the GPU fetches the rest from SP_CS_OBJ_START while it runs. Hand-written generator, ours, MIT.

source_filename = "long_chain"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/many_ubo_id.ll`:

```ll
; many_ubo_id: a kernel reading one word from each of ten constant buffers, the LLVM IR a Metal compiler emits for
;
;     kernel void many_ubo_id(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &c0 [[buffer(1)]], ...,
;                             constant uint &c9 [[buffer(10)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       out[gid] = gid + c0 * 1 + c1 * 2 + ... + c9 * 10;
;     }
;
; ir3 pushes each constant buffer it reads at a known offset as a range of its own, so this kernel has ten: more than
; the eight a Kernel held, which refused Resident Evil 4's tonemap (11) and deferred lighting (9) after ir3 had
; compiled them. Hand-written, ours, MIT; the metadata's shape is Apple's convention, as in fill_id.ll.

source_filename = "many_ubo_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define void @many_ubo_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, ptr addrspace(2) %c0, ptr addrspace(2) %c1, ptr addrspace(2) %c2, ptr addrspace(2) %c3, ptr addrspace(2) %c4, ptr addrspace(2) %c5, ptr addrspace(2) %c6, ptr addrspace(2) %c7, ptr addrspace(2) %c8, ptr addrspace(2) %c9, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %v0 = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c0, align 4
  %m0 = mul i32 %v0, 1
  %s0 = add i32 %gid, %m0
  %v1 = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c1, align 4
  %m1 = mul i32 %v1, 2
  %s1 = add i32 %s0, %m1
  %v2 = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c2, align 4
  %m2 = mul i32 %v2, 3
  %s2 = add i32 %s1, %m2
  %v3 = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c3, align 4
  %m3 = mul i32 %v3, 4
  %s3 = add i32 %s2, %m3
  %v4 = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c4, align 4
  %m4 = mul i32 %v4, 5
  %s4 = add i32 %s3, %m4
  %v5 = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c5, align 4
  %m5 = mul i32 %v5, 6
  %s5 = add i32 %s4, %m5
  %v6 = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c6, align 4
  %m6 = mul i32 %v6, 7
  %s6 = add i32 %s5, %m6
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/pack_id.ll`:

```ll
; pack_id: four bytes of gid as halves in 0..1, packed back with pack_float_to_unorm4x8, the AIR a Metal compiler
; emits for
;
;     kernel void pack_id(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       half4 c = half4(gid & 255, (gid >> 2) & 255, 255 - (gid & 255), 128) / 255.0h;
;       out[gid] = pack_float_to_unorm4x8(c);
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT; the metadata's shape is Apple's convention, as in fill_id.ll. n / 255 in a half is within
; 0.12 of a step of n, so the round to nearest gives n back exactly: every word is the four bytes, component 0 low.
; VideoToolbox's scaler (the live wallpaper's) packs so, which the front end refused.

source_filename = "pack_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare i32 @air.pack.unorm4x8.v4f16(<4 x half>)

define void @pack_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %a = and i32 %gid, 255
  %s = lshr i32 %gid, 2
  %b = and i32 %s, 255
  %c = sub i32 255, %a
  %fa = uitofp i32 %a to half
  %fb = uitofp i32 %b to half
  %fc = uitofp i32 %c to half
  %v0 = insertelement <4 x half> poison, half %fa, i64 0
  %v1 = insertelement <4 x half> %v0, half %fb, i64 1
  %v2 = insertelement <4 x half> %v1, half %fc, i64 2
  %v3 = insertelement <4 x half> %v2, half 0xH5800, i64 3
  %n = fdiv <4 x half> %v3, <half 0xH5BF8, half 0xH5BF8, half 0xH5BF8, half 0xH5BF8>
  %p = call i32 @air.pack.unorm4x8.v4f16(<4 x half> %n)
  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64
  %po = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  store i32 %p, ptr addrspace(1) %po, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/ptr_phi.ll`:

```ll
; ptr_phi, the AIR side: pointer phis into one buffer at offsets known only at run
; time, as the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void ptr_phi(device const uint* in [[buffer(0)]], device uint* out [[buffer(1)]],
;                         uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       device const uint* row = (gid & 1) ? in + gid : in + gid + 64;   // a branch, then a phi
;       out[2 * gid] = *row;
;       uint s = 0;
;       device const uint* p = in + gid;                                // stepped round a loop
;       for (uint i = 0; i < 4; i++, p++) s += *p;
;       out[2 * gid + 1] = s;
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention.
;
; Why it exists: the front end resolves a pointer phi while translating, and
; refused one whose operands it could not prove to be the same place -- two
; offsets into one buffer, or an operand over a loop's back edge. Both now carry
; the offset in a register. With in[w] = 3w + 7, out[2g] is in[g] for odd g and
; in[g + 64] for even g, and out[2g + 1] the sum of in[g .. g + 3]: an offset
; register stuck at its first value, or the wrong edge's offset, moves them.
source_filename = "ptr_phi"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define void @ptr_phi(ptr addrspace(1) %in, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
entry:
  %odd = and i32 %gid, 1
  %isodd = icmp ne i32 %odd, 0
  br i1 %isodd, label %a, label %b

a:
  %pa = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 %gid
  br label %join

b:
  %g64 = add i32 %gid, 64
  %pb = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 %g64
  br label %join

join:
  %row = phi ptr addrspace(1) [ %pa, %a ], [ %pb, %b ]
  %rv = load i32, ptr addrspace(1) %row, align 4
  %o0 = shl i32 %gid, 1
  %q0 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %o0
  store i32 %rv, ptr addrspace(1) %q0, align 4
  %p0 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 %gid
  br label %loop

loop:
  %p = phi ptr addrspace(1) [ %p0, %join ], [ %pn, %loop ]
  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %join ], [ %in1, %loop ]
  %s = phi i32 [ 0, %join ], [ %sn, %loop ]
  %w = load i32, ptr addrspace(1) %p, align 4
  %sn = add i32 %s, %w
  %pn = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %p, i32 1
  %in1 = add i32 %i, 1
  %more = icmp ult i32 %in1, 4
  br i1 %more, label %loop, label %done

done:
  %o1 = add i32 %o0, 1
  %q1 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %o1
  store i32 %sn, ptr addrspace(1) %q1, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @ptr_phi, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6, !7}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"in"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/pvt_fill.ll`:

```ll
; pvt_fill, the AIR side: a kernel with a dynamically indexed array, which ir3
; keeps in private memory (stp/ldp), as the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void pvt_fill(device uint* out [[buffer(0)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       uint a[128];
;       for (uint i = 0; i < 128; i++) a[i] = 3 * i + (gid >> 7) + 1;
;       out[gid] = a[gid & 127];
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention.
;
; Why it exists: the dispatch refused any kernel that spills (pvtmemSize) until
; it learnt to bind the queue's private memory as a draw does. Each thread's
; array depends on its own gid, so a fiber reading another fiber's array, or
; zeros, or nothing at all, gives a word other than 3 (gid & 127) + (gid >> 7) + 1.
source_filename = "pvt_fill"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define void @pvt_fill(ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
entry:
  %a = alloca [128 x i32], align 4
  %hi = lshr i32 %gid, 7
  %base = add i32 %hi, 1
  br label %fill

fill:
  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %entry ], [ %next, %fill ]
  %t = mul i32 %i, 3
  %v = add i32 %t, %base
  %p = getelementptr inbounds [128 x i32], ptr %a, i32 0, i32 %i
  store i32 %v, ptr %p, align 4
  %next = add i32 %i, 1
  %more = icmp ult i32 %next, 128
  br i1 %more, label %fill, label %read

read:
  %k = and i32 %gid, 127
  %q = getelementptr inbounds [128 x i32], ptr %a, i32 0, i32 %k
  %w = load i32, ptr %q, align 4
  %o = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid
  store i32 %w, ptr addrspace(1) %o, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @pvt_fill, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}

!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tex_col16.ll`:

```ll
; tex_col16: what a texture's layout costs a blur. Sixteen reads down a column, 8 rows apart, per thread:
;
;     kernel void tex_col16(texture2d<float, access::read> in [[texture(0)]],
;                           device float *out                 [[buffer(0)]],
;                           uint2 gid                         [[thread_position_in_grid]],
;                           uint2 grid                        [[threads_per_grid]])
;     {
;       float s = 0;
;       for (uint k = 0; k < 16; k++) s += in.read(uint2(gid.x, gid.y + 8 * k)).x;
;       out[gid.y * grid.x + gid.x] = s;
;     }
;
; over a texture 128 rows taller than the grid. A blur's taps fall in other rows, which a linear layout puts a pitch
; apart (other cache lines for every tap) and a tiled one beside each other: the probe times it over a linear R32Float
; texture and a tiled Depth32Float one of the same size.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the shape of the metadata and of the intrinsic signature is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tex_col16"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, i32, i32)

  %c3a = insertelement <2 x i32> undef, i32 %gx, i32 0
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tex_copy.ll`:

```ll
; tex_copy, the AIR side: a texture read and a texture write in one compute
; kernel, written as the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void tex_copy(texture2d<uint, access::read>  in   [[texture(1)]],
;                          texture2d<uint, access::write> out  [[texture(0)]],
;                          uint2 gid                           [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       out.write(in.read(gid), gid);
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple. Only the SHAPE of the
; metadata and of the two intrinsic signatures is Apple's convention (the
; air.kernel node, the per-argument air.texture nodes, the version nodes, the
; argument order of air.read_texture_2d and air.write_texture_2d as the AIR
; front end reads them, src/compiler/air/air_intrinsics.c "-- textures --");
; the values are this kernel's own.
;
; What the two paths must meet on: texel (x, y) of `out` equals texel (x, y) of
; `in` for every (x, y) the grid covers, and nothing else of `out` changes. The
; input is the caller's: the reference is the input itself (a copy has no
; arithmetic to get wrong), so the test's input must make every texel distinct
; -- (x + 16*y, 0x100 + x, 0x200 + y, 0x300) or any other injective pattern --
; so that a wrong coordinate, a wrong slot or a wrong channel cannot read back
; as the right answer.
;
; The front end turns `in` (air.texture + air.read) into a TEXTURE resource at
; index 1 and `out` (air.texture + air.write) into an IMAGE resource at index 0
; (air_to_nir.c, translate_input's air.texture branch); the read becomes a
; nir_tex_instr txf with texture_index 1 and the write a nir_image_store with
; image index 0 (air_intrinsics.c, texture_op). ir3 then fetches through texture
; slot 1 (isaml t#1, s#0) and stores through IBO slot num_ssbos + 0 = 0 (stib).
; The indices are chosen so that the image lands at IBO slot 0 with no slot
; before it (an unaddressed IBO slot is a thing no Mesa driver emits) and the
; unused texture slot 0 falls in the texture table, where Gallium's own
; dummy_view is a zero descriptor too.
;
;   llvm-as tex_copy.ll -o tex_copy.bc
;   air2nir tex_copy.bc                               (the NIR)
;   air2nir --interface tex_copy.bc                   (what the runtime binds)
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tex_copy.bc     (the Adreno listing)

source_filename = "tex_copy"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

; The signatures follow Apple's own declarations as the corpus carries them
; (read off a .metallib of the device image with `air2nir --ll`, names only):
;   { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, i32, i32)
;   void @air.write_texture_2d.v4f16(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, <4 x half>, i32, i32)
; with the `.u` part naming an unsigned result (air.read_texture_2d.i16.u.v4i32
; is in the same library). A texture handle is a pointer in address space 1.
; Arguments after the coordinate: read = (lod, flags), write = (value, lod, flags).
declare { <4 x i32>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d.u.v4i32(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, i32, i32)
declare void @air.write_texture_2d.u.v4i32(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, <4 x i32>, i32, i32)

define void @tex_copy(ptr addrspace(1) %in, ptr addrspace(1) %out, <2 x i32> %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %r = tail call { <4 x i32>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d.u.v4i32(ptr addrspace(1) %in, <2 x i32> %gid, i32 0, i32 0)
  ; field 1 is Metal's sparse-residency byte; nothing reads it
  %v = extractvalue { <4 x i32>, i8 } %r, 0
  tail call void @air.write_texture_2d.u.v4i32(ptr addrspace(1) %out, <2 x i32> %gid, <4 x i32> %v, i32 0, i32 0)
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tex_copy, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6, !7}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.arg_type_name", !"texture2d<uint, read>", !"air.arg_name", !"in"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.write", !"air.arg_type_name", !"texture2d<uint, write>", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint2", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tex_fill.ll`:

```ll
; tex_fill, the AIR side: a kernel that only WRITES a texture, written as the
; LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void tex_fill(texture2d<uint, access::write> out [[texture(0)]],
;                          constant uint &c                    [[buffer(0)]],
;                          uint2 gid                           [[thread_position_in_grid]],
;                          uint2 grid                          [[threads_per_grid]])
;     {
;       uint i = gid.y * grid.x + gid.x;
;       out.write(uint4(i * 0x9E3779B1u + c, gid.x, gid.y, 0xdead), gid);
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata and of the intrinsic signature is Apple's convention.
;
; Why a write-only kernel comes first: it adds exactly one new mechanism to a
; dispatch -- a 2D storage descriptor at an IBO slot, written by stib -- and
; none of the others: no texture table, no sampler, no isam coordinate mode.
; The image is [[texture(0)]] of a kernel with no device buffer, so it lands at
; IBO slot num_ssbos + 0 = 0 and no slot before it is left unaddressed; c is a
; pushed constant (a `constant T&`), so no UBO descriptor is needed either.
;
; The first component is fill_id's word for pixel i (an odd multiplier makes
; i -> i*K a bijection, so a readback tells WHICH invocation wrote each pixel),
; the next two are the pixel's own coordinates and the last a constant, so that
; a four-channel format (RGBA32Uint) checks every lane and a one-channel format
; (R32Uint) checks that only .x lands and the other lanes go nowhere.
;
;   llvm-as tex_fill.ll -o tex_fill.bc
;   air2nir tex_fill.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tex_fill.bc

source_filename = "tex_fill"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare void @air.write_texture_2d.u.v4i32(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, <4 x i32>, i32, i32)

define void @tex_fill(ptr addrspace(1) %out, ptr addrspace(2) %c, <2 x i32> %gid, <2 x i32> %grid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %cv = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %c, align 4
  %gx = extractelement <2 x i32> %gid, i32 0
  %gy = extractelement <2 x i32> %gid, i32 1
  %nx = extractelement <2 x i32> %grid, i32 0
  %row = mul i32 %gy, %nx
  %i = add i32 %row, %gx
  %m = mul i32 %i, -1640531535
  %v = add i32 %m, %cv
  %v0 = insertelement <4 x i32> undef, i32 %v, i32 0
  %v1 = insertelement <4 x i32> %v0, i32 %gx, i32 1
  %v2 = insertelement <4 x i32> %v1, i32 %gy, i32 2
  %v3 = insertelement <4 x i32> %v2, i32 57005, i32 3
  tail call void @air.write_texture_2d.u.v4i32(ptr addrspace(1) %out, <2 x i32> %gid, <4 x i32> %v3, i32 0, i32 0)
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tex_fill, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6, !7, !8}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.write", !"air.arg_type_name", !"texture2d<uint, write>", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 4, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"c"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint2", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}
```

```ll
; tex_fill_3d, the AIR side: a 3D image written by a compute kernel, one slice a grid slice, as the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
; kernel void tex_fill_3d(texture3d<uint, access::write> out [[texture(0)]],
;                         uint3 gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
; {
;   out.write(uint4(gid.x, gid.y, gid.z, 0xdead), gid);
; }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata and of the intrinsic
; signature is Apple's convention.
;
; Every texel gets its own (x, y, layer) triple and 0xdead, so a layer stored
; at the wrong pitch, or every layer landing on the first, leaves texels that
; are canary or name another layer -- not one plausible-looking fill.
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tex_fill_h.ll`:

```ll
; tex_fill_h, the AIR side: a HALF image written by a compute kernel, as the
; LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void tex_fill_h(texture2d<half, access::write> out [[texture(0)]],
;                            uint2 gid                           [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       out.write(half4(half(gid.x) / 64.0h, half(gid.y) / 32.0h, 0.5h, 1.0h), gid);
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata and of the intrinsic
; signature is Apple's convention (air.write_texture_2d.v4f16, as the image's
; libraries declare it).
;
; Why it exists: Apple's half kernels (MetalFaceMask_Clear and most of the
; image's texture kernels) store through texture2d<half, write>, and the front
; end carries a half as 16 bits the ir3 stib names as an integer type while the
; descriptor says FMT6_16_16_16_16_FLOAT. Whether the TP converts the integer
; or stores the bits is the question this kernel answers: every value below is
; exact in half (x/64 and y/32 for x < 64, y < 32; 0.5; 1.0), so the expected
; pixel is the four IEEE half bit patterns and nothing else.
source_filename = "tex_fill_h"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare void @air.write_texture_2d.v4f16(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, <4 x half>, i32, i32)

define void @tex_fill_h(ptr addrspace(1) %out, <2 x i32> %gid) local_unnamed_addr {

  %gy = extractelement <2 x i32> %gid, i32 1

  %v3 = insertelement <4 x half> %v2, half 0xH3C00, i32 3
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tex_sample_gid.ll`:

```ll
; tex_sample_gid, the AIR side: tex_sample with the coordinate computed from the
; thread's position instead of loaded from a constant buffer, written as the
; LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void tex_sample_gid(texture2d<float, access::sample> in [[texture(0)]],
;                                sampler s                           [[sampler(0)]],
;                                device float4 *out                  [[buffer(0)]],
;                                uint2 gid                           [[thread_position_in_grid]],
;                                uint2 grid                          [[threads_per_grid]])
;     {
;       out[gid.y * grid.x + gid.x] = in.sample(s, (float2(gid) + 0.5) / float2(grid));
;     }
;
; Why this variant exists beside tex_sample.ll: there `coords[gid]` is a load from
; a constant buffer at an offset that depends on the thread, which ir3 leaves as
; an `ldc` through UBO descriptor 1 rather than pushing it into the constant
; file -- and hakios-metal's dispatch binds pushed ranges only (compute.hpp: "a
; constant buffer (a UBO range)"), no UBO descriptor table. A texture test should
; not also carry that gap, so here every input is a system value or a texture.
; With a grid of W x H threads over a W x H texture, thread (x, y) samples the
; centre of texel (x, y) in normalized coordinates and writes it to out[y*W + x]:
; under nearest/clamp_to_edge the expectation is the texel itself, exactly.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata and of the intrinsic signature is Apple's convention.
;
;   llvm-as tex_sample_gid.ll -o tex_sample_gid.bc
;   air2nir tex_sample_gid.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tex_sample_gid.bc

source_filename = "tex_sample_gid"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)

define void @tex_sample_gid(ptr addrspace(1) %in, ptr addrspace(2) %s, ptr addrspace(1) %out, <2 x i32> %gid, <2 x i32> %grid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %gf = uitofp <2 x i32> %gid to <2 x float>
  %gc = fadd <2 x float> %gf, <float 5.000000e-01, float 5.000000e-01>
  %nf = uitofp <2 x i32> %grid to <2 x float>
  %c = fdiv <2 x float> %gc, %nf
  %r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %in, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <2 x float> %c, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r, 0
  %gx = extractelement <2 x i32> %gid, i32 0
  %gy = extractelement <2 x i32> %gid, i32 1
  %nx = extractelement <2 x i32> %grid, i32 0
  %row = mul i32 %gy, %nx
  %idx = add i32 %row, %gx
  %t = zext i32 %idx to i64
  %po = getelementptr inbounds <4 x float>, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  store <4 x float> %v, ptr addrspace(1) %po, align 16
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tex_sample_gid, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6, !7, !8, !9}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.sample", !"air.arg_type_name", !"texture2d<float, sample>", !"air.arg_name", !"in"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.sampler", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.arg_type_name", !"sampler", !"air.arg_name", !"s"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 16, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 16, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!8 = !{i32 3, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint2", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}
```

```ll
; tex_size_h, the AIR side: a half texture sampled and then asked its size, as
; the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void tex_size_h(texture2d<half, access::sample> in  [[texture(0)]],
;                            sampler                         s   [[sampler(0)]],
;                            texture2d<half, access::write>  out [[texture(1)]],
;                            uint2 gid                           [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       half4 c = in.sample(s, float2(gid) / 64.0);
;       out.write(c * half(in.get_width()), gid);
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata and of the intrinsic
; signatures is Apple's convention.
;
; Why it exists: a size query is a tex instruction too (txs), and its result is
; an integer whatever the texture holds. A walk that took the texture's class
; from every tex would call this half texture int when the query is the last
; tex to name it -- the order here -- and refuse a kernel whose declaration and
; instructions agree.
source_filename = "tex_size_h"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { <4 x half>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f16(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)
declare i32 @air.get_width_texture_2d(ptr addrspace(1), i32)
declare void @air.write_texture_2d.v4f16(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, <4 x half>, i32, i32)

define void @tex_size_h(ptr addrspace(1) %in, ptr addrspace(2) %s, ptr addrspace(1) %out, <2 x i32> %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %gf = uitofp <2 x i32> %gid to <2 x float>
  %uv = fmul <2 x float> %gf, <float 1.562500e-02, float 1.562500e-02>
  %r = tail call { <4 x half>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f16(ptr addrspace(1) %in, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <2 x float> %uv, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %c = extractvalue { <4 x half>, i8 } %r, 0
  %w = tail call i32 @air.get_width_texture_2d(ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 0)
  %wf = uitofp i32 %w to half
  %w0 = insertelement <4 x half> undef, half %wf, i32 0
  %ws = shufflevector <4 x half> %w0, <4 x half> undef, <4 x i32> zeroinitializer
  %v = fmul <4 x half> %c, %ws
  tail call void @air.write_texture_2d.v4f16(ptr addrspace(1) %out, <2 x i32> %gid, <4 x half> %v, i32 0, i32 0)
  ret void
}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tg_arg.ll`:

```ll
; tg_arg, the AIR side: a static threadgroup array beside a threadgroup argument
; the encoder sizes, as the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     kernel void tg_arg(device uint* out [[buffer(0)]], threadgroup uint* t [[threadgroup(0)]],
;                        uint lid [[thread_position_in_threadgroup]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       threadgroup uint s[64];
;       s[lid] = lid + 1000;
;       t[lid * 32] = lid + 2000;
;       threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
;       uint n = (lid + 1) & 63;
;       out[2 * gid] = s[n];
;       out[2 * gid + 1] = t[n * 32];
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata and of the intrinsic
; signature is Apple's convention.
;
; Why it exists: the argument has to start past s, which the front end lays out
; from offset 0 -- at 0 the two share their first bytes and s[n] reads t's word.
; t's words lie 128 bytes apart, so 64 threads reach 8 KiB into it: the dispatch
; has to be given the encoder's length, not the 2 KiB floor, or the far ones are
; lost. Each word read is a neighbour's, so it is written by another thread and
; the barrier is what makes it there.
source_filename = "tg_arg"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

@s = internal addrspace(3) global [64 x i32] undef, align 4

declare void @air.wg.barrier(i32, i32)

define void @tg_arg(ptr addrspace(1) %out, ptr addrspace(3) %t, i32 %lid, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %sv = add i32 %lid, 1000
  %sp = getelementptr inbounds [64 x i32], ptr addrspace(3) @s, i32 0, i32 %lid
  store i32 %sv, ptr addrspace(3) %sp, align 4
  %tv = add i32 %lid, 2000
  %ti = mul i32 %lid, 32
  %tp = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(3) %t, i32 %ti
  store i32 %tv, ptr addrspace(3) %tp, align 4
  tail call void @air.wg.barrier(i32 2, i32 1)
  %l1 = add i32 %lid, 1
  %n = and i32 %l1, 63
  %sq = getelementptr inbounds [64 x i32], ptr addrspace(3) @s, i32 0, i32 %n
  %sr = load i32, ptr addrspace(3) %sq, align 4
  %ni = mul i32 %n, 32
  %tq = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(3) %t, i32 %ni
  %tr = load i32, ptr addrspace(3) %tq, align 4
  %o0 = shl i32 %gid, 1
  %p0 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %o0
  store i32 %sr, ptr addrspace(1) %p0, align 4
  %o1 = add i32 %o0, 1
  %p1 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %o1
  store i32 %tr, ptr addrspace(1) %p1, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tg_arg, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6, !7, !8}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 3, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"t"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_position_in_threadgroup", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"lid"}
!8 = !{i32 3, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_attr_vs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_attr_vs, the AIR side: a vertex function whose position and colour come from [[stage_in]] attributes, written as
; the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     struct In  { float2 position [[attribute(0)]]; float4 color [[attribute(1)]]; };
;     struct Out { float4 position [[position]]; float4 color; };
;     vertex Out tri_attr_vs(In in [[stage_in]])
;     {
;       return Out{ float4(in.position, 0, 1), in.color };
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention (air.vertex_input nodes with
; air.location_index, as the image's own vertex functions carry them; the same two outputs as tri_color_vs).
;
; Why it exists: it is the first vertex fetch. What the attributes are in memory is not in the shader but in the
; pipeline's vertex descriptor: here one interleaved buffer of 12-byte vertices, the position as Float2 at offset 0
; and the colour as UChar4Normalized at offset 8 -- two formats, two offsets, one stride -- decoded by VFD_DECODE_INSTR
; into the registers VFD_DEST_CNTL_INSTR names. With the colour varying it links to tri_color_fs, so the pixels tell
; whether both attributes arrived: positions wrong move the triangles, colours wrong change the bytes.
;
;   llvm-as tri_attr_vs.ll -o tri_attr_vs.bc
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_base_vs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_base_vs, a vertex function that reads the draw's own numbers: the LLVM IR a
; Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     struct out { float4 position [[position]]; float4 color; };
;     vertex out tri_base_vs(uint vid [[vertex_id]], uint bv [[base_vertex]],
;                            uint iid [[instance_id]])
;     {
;       out o;
;       o.position = tri_color_vs's corner (vid - bv);  // the pair, wherever the draw starts
;       o.color = float4(bv / 255.0, iid / 255.0, 0, 1);
;       return o;
;     }
;
; which is the shape of QuartzCore's path_blit_vert_lph: Metal's [[instance_id]]
; counts from the base instance, so the front end reads it as the hardware's
; zero-based id plus base_instance, and [[base_vertex]] as first_vertex -- both
; driver params, which the draw uploads every time. Paired with tri_color_fs.
; A draw of vertices 3..8, two instances from base instance 7, must give every
; pixel 03 08 00 ff: the second instance (7 + 1) drawn last. Params not uploaded
; read 0: the corners land elsewhere and the colour is 00 01 00 ff; the hardware's
; id not added, 03 07 00 ff.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata (air.base_vertex and air.instance_id among the vertex inputs) is
; Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_base_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> @tri_base_vs(i32 %vid, i32 %bv, i32 %iid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %l = sub i32 %vid, %bv
  %c4 = icmp eq i32 %l, 4
  %c3 = icmp eq i32 %l, 3
  %c2 = icmp eq i32 %l, 2
  %c1 = icmp eq i32 %l, 1
  %c0 = icmp eq i32 %l, 0
  %p4 = select i1 %c4, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %p3 = select i1 %c3, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p4
  %p2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p3
  %p1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p2
  %p0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p1
  %rf = uitofp i32 %bv to float
  %gf = uitofp i32 %iid to float
  %rn = fdiv float %rf, 2.550000e+02
  %gn = fdiv float %gf, 2.550000e+02
  %k0 = insertelement <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %rn, i32 0
  %k1 = insertelement <4 x float> %k0, float %gn, i32 1
  %r0 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> undef, <4 x float> %p0, 0
  %r1 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> %r0, <4 x float> %k1, 1
  ret <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> %r1
}

!4 = !{!"air.position", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"position"}

!6 = !{!7, !8, !9}
!7 = !{i32 0, !"air.vertex_id", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"vid"}
!8 = !{i32 1, !"air.base_vertex", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"bv"}
```

```ll
; tri_color_fs, the AIR side of the per-vertex-colour fragment function: the
; LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     struct Vary { float4 position [[position]]; float4 color; };
;     fragment float4 tri_color_fs(Vary in [[stage_in]])
;     {
;       return in.color;   // [[color(0)]], interpolated
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple. Only the SHAPE is
; Apple's convention: AIR has no stage-in struct, each member the function reads
; is a parameter of its own carrying an air.fragment_input node with the
; mangled varying name and the interpolation keys (air.center, air.perspective:
; centre-sampled, perspective-correct, which is Metal's default), as QuartzCore's
; upsample_frag_lpf spells them. A member nothing reads (the position here) is
; left out of the parameter list, as Apple's compiler leaves out what the body
; does not use when the member is not [[position]].
;
; What the front end makes of it: a shader_in variable at VARYING_SLOT_VAR0 with
; INTERP_MODE_SMOOTH, which ir3 reads with bary.f through the ij_pixel
; barycentrics (SYSTEM_VALUE_BARYCENTRIC_PERSP_PIXEL), so the variant carries
; one bary input at inloc 0 (compmask 0xf) and total_in 4. The name the front end
; records for this side is air.arg_name ("color"), not the mangled string; a
; by-name link has to read the latter (air-vs-fs.md, the varying-names gap).
;
;   llvm-as tri_color_fs.ll -o tri_color_fs.bc
;   air2nir tri_color_fs.bc
;   air2nir --interface tri_color_fs.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_color_fs.bc
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_color_vs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_color_vs, the AIR side of the per-vertex-colour vertex function: the LLVM
; IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     struct Vary { float4 position [[position]]; float4 color; };
;     vertex Vary tri_color_vs(uint vid [[vertex_id]])
;     {
;       Vary v;                        // the six positions of tri_flat_vs ...
;       switch (vid) {
;         case 0:  v.position = float4(-1, -1, 0, 1); v.color = float4(1, 0, 0, 1); break;   // red
;         case 1:  v.position = float4( 1, -1, 0, 1); v.color = float4(0, 1, 0, 1); break;   // green
;         case 2:  v.position = float4(-1,  1, 0, 1); v.color = float4(0, 0, 1, 1); break;   // blue
;         case 3:  v.position = float4( 1, -1, 0, 1); v.color = float4(1, 0, 0, 1); break;   // red
;         case 4:  v.position = float4( 1,  1, 0, 1); v.color = float4(0, 1, 0, 1); break;   // green
;         default: v.position = float4(-1,  1, 0, 1); v.color = float4(0, 0, 1, 1); break;   // blue: vertex 5, and every vid past it
;       }
;       return v;                      // ... and a colour varying beside each
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple. Only the SHAPE is
; Apple's convention: the returned struct is spelled packed (<{ }>) and its
; fields carry one output node each, air.position for the first and
; air.vertex_output with the mangled varying name for the second, as
; QuartzCore's std_vert0_lpf spells them. The varying's name
; "generated(5colorDv4_f)" is what a by-name link would match to the fragment
; side; the slot is the order of appearance (VARYING_SLOT_VAR0 here,
; air_to_nir.c translate_output), and with one varying both sides land on VAR0
; without a link step.
;
; No buffer in either stage (the contract's first decision): both the position
; and the colour are literals chosen by icmp eq + select on the vertex id, the
; shape of tri_flat_vs. Red at 0 and 3, green at 1 and 4, blue at 2 and 5, so
; that a pixel's colour is its barycentric weights in the triangle that painted
; it: (bary_A, bary_B, bary_C, 1) for either triangle.
;
;   llvm-as tri_color_vs.ll -o tri_color_vs.bc
;   air2nir tri_color_vs.bc
;   air2nir --interface tri_color_vs.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_color_vs.bc

source_filename = "tri_color_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> @tri_color_vs(i32 %vid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %c4 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 4
  %c3 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 3
  %c2 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 2
  %c1 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 1
  %c0 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 0
  ; the position, from vertex 4 down to vertex 0 over vertex 5's default
  %p4 = select i1 %c4, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %p3 = select i1 %c3, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p4
  %p2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p3
  %p1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p2
  %p0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p1
  ; the colour, the same way: green at 4, red at 3, blue at 2, green at 1, red at 0, blue by default
  %k4 = select i1 %c4, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %k3 = select i1 %c3, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k4
  %k2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k3
  %k1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k2
  %k0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k1
  %r0 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> undef, <4 x float> %p0, 0
  %r1 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> %r0, <4 x float> %k0, 1
  ret <{ <4 x float>, <4 x float> }> %r1
}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_ctex_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_ctex_fs, a fragment function with a sampler of its own: the LLVM IR a Metal
; compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_ctex_fs(Vary in [[stage_in]], texture2d<float> t [[texture(0)]])
;     {
;       constexpr sampler s(address::repeat, filter::nearest);
;       return t.sample(s, in.color.xy * 4.0);   // [[color(0)]]
;     }
;
; A constexpr sampler is no argument: it is a module global, @__air_sampler_state,
; holding the sampler's state word (air_to_nir.c air_decode_sampler_state: the
; address modes s, t, r at bits 0, 3, 6, the filters, the lod range as two halves at
; 24 and 40), named in !air.sampler_states. This one is repeat on s and t, clamp to
; edge on r, nearest, mip none, lod [0, 65504]: 34901797600493650. The front end gives it the
; sampler index after the API's (0 here), and the runtime makes and binds it.
;
; The coordinate is the varying times 4, a computed value, so the sample is an
; ordinary sam rather than tri_tex_fs's prefetch -- and with tri_color_vs's (red,
; green) it runs over 0..4, where repeat and clamp to edge give different texels:
; repeat reads texel floor(16 u) mod 4, clamp would read texel 3 past u = 0.25.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; global and of the metadata is Apple's convention.
;
;   llvm-as tri_ctex_fs.ll -o tri_ctex_fs.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_ctex_fs.bc

source_filename = "tri_ctex_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

@__air_sampler_state = internal addrspace(2) constant i64 34901797600493650, align 8

declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)

define <4 x float> @tri_ctex_fs(<4 x float> %color, ptr addrspace(1) %t) local_unnamed_addr {
  %uv = shufflevector <4 x float> %color, <4 x float> poison, <2 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1>
  %uv4 = fmul <2 x float> %uv, <float 4.000000e+00, float 4.000000e+00>
  %r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) @__air_sampler_state, <2 x float> %uv4, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r, 0
  ret <4 x float> %v
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}
!air.sampler_states = !{!10}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_ctex_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6, !7}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.fragment_input", !"generated(5colorDv4_f)", !"air.center", !"air.perspective", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"color"}
!7 = !{i32 1, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.sample", !"air.arg_type_name", !"texture2d<float, sample>", !"air.arg_name", !"t"}
!10 = !{!"air.sampler_state", ptr addrspace(2) @__air_sampler_state}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_cuba_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_cuba_fs, the AIR side: a cube array sampled along a direction from a
; constant buffer, the cube chosen by its second vec4, as the LLVM IR a Metal
; compiler would emit for
;     fragment float4 tri_cuba_fs(constant float4 *c [[buffer(0)]],
;                                 texturecube_array<float> t [[texture(0)]], sampler s [[sampler(0)]])
;     { return t.sample(s, c[0].xyz, uint(c[1].x)); }
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: only the SHAPE of the metadata and of the intrinsic
; signature is Apple's convention.
; Why it exists: a cube array's view is TYPE CUBE with DEPTH the cubes, each six
; faces ARRAY_PITCH apart; the probe gives every face of every cube its own
; colour, so a wrong cube or a wrong face reads another one.
source_filename = "tri_cuba_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_cube_array.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <3 x float>, i32, i1, float, float, i32)

define <4 x float> @tri_cuba_fs(ptr addrspace(2) %c, ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s) local_unnamed_addr {
  %d = load <4 x float>, ptr addrspace(2) %c, align 16
  %xyz = shufflevector <4 x float> %d, <4 x float> poison, <3 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1, i32 2>
  %p1 = getelementptr inbounds <4 x float>, ptr addrspace(2) %c, i32 1
  %e = load <4 x float>, ptr addrspace(2) %p1, align 16
  %lf = extractelement <4 x float> %e, i32 0
  %l = fptoui float %lf to i32
  %r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_cube_array.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <3 x float> %xyz, i32 %l, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r, 0
  ret <4 x float> %v
}
```

```ll
; tri_dpos_vs, vertex pulling from a device buffer: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler
; would emit for
;
;     vertex float4 tri_dpos_vs(device const float2 *pos [[buffer(0)]],
;                               uint vid                 [[vertex_id]])
;     {
;       return float4(pos[vid], 0.0, 1.0);   // [[position]]
;     }
;
; tri_upos_vs with the buffer in device memory (address space 1) instead of
; constant (2): the front end makes it an SSBO, and ir3 reads it with ldib through
; IBO 0 -- the 3D pipeline's IBO table (SB6_IBO, SP_IBO), one table for every
; graphics stage, which the draw must load. Paired with tri_flat_fs and given the
; pair's six positions the picture is 9b's pair, as tri_upos_vs's is.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention.
;
;   llvm-as tri_dpos_vs.ll -o tri_dpos_vs.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_dpos_vs.bc

source_filename = "tri_dpos_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <4 x float> @tri_dpos_vs(ptr addrspace(1) %pos, i32 %vid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %i = zext i32 %vid to i64
  %p = getelementptr inbounds <2 x float>, ptr addrspace(1) %pos, i64 %i
  %xy = load <2 x float>, ptr addrspace(1) %p, align 8
  %x = extractelement <2 x float> %xy, i32 0
  %y = extractelement <2 x float> %xy, i32 1
  %v0 = insertelement <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %x, i32 0
  %v1 = insertelement <4 x float> %v0, float %y, i32 1
  ret <4 x float> %v1
}
```

```ll
; tri_fb_fs, a fragment function that reads its own colour target (framebuffer
; fetch): the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_fb_fs(float4 c [[color(0)]])
;     {
;       return float4(c.g, c.b, c.r, 1);   // [[color(0)]]
;     }
;
; which is the shape of QuartzCore's luma_boost_lph (a layer re-coloured in place
; from what is under it), the pipeline CoreAnimation's window server exits on when
; it cannot be made. Paired with tri_flat_vs. Over a target cleared to 40 80 bf ff
; one draw leaves 80 bf 40 ff, and a second draw in the same pass bf 40 80 ff: the
; second must read what the first wrote, not the clear colour a stale cache would
; still hold, and a fetch that read nothing would give 00 00 00 ff.

; metadata (an air.render_target among the fragment inputs) is Apple's convention.

target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

  %v = shufflevector <4 x float> %c, <4 x float> <float 0.0, float 0.0, float 0.0, float 1.0>, <4 x i32> <i32 1, i32 2, i32 0, i32 7>
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_fc_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_fc_fs, a fragment function specialised by the pipeline's function constants:
; the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     constant int  fc_value [[function_constant(0)]];   // guarded: may be absent
;     constant bool fc_opaque [[function_constant(1)]];  // read as it is: the pipeline must supply it
;     fragment float4 tri_fc_fs()
;     {
;       return float4(float(fc_value) / 255, is_function_constant_defined(fc_value) ? 1 : 0, 0.25,
;                     fc_opaque ? 1 : 0.25);   // [[color(0)]]
;     }
;
; Paired with tri_flat_vs. As RGBA8Unorm bytes, each set of constants gives its
; own pixel, so the pipeline's values and the "was it supplied" answer are both
; read off the target:
;
;     nothing supplied        00 00 40 40   (the guarded one absent, the bool zero)
;     0 = 7, 1 = true         07 ff 40 ff
;     0 = 0                   00 ff 40 40   (supplied, and zero: not the same as absent)
;     1 = true                00 00 40 ff
;
; The declarations end in `i1 false` for the guarded constant and `i1 true` for
; the one read without asking, which is how Metal marks a constant the pipeline
; may leave out against one it must give.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata (!air.function_constants, the air.fc_initializer globals) and of the
; intrinsic's signature is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_fc_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

@fc_value.MTL_FC_INIT_0_i = internal addrspace(2) externally_initialized constant i32 undef, section "air.fc_initializer", align 4
@fc_opaque.MTL_FC_INIT_1_b = internal addrspace(2) externally_initialized constant i8 undef, section "air.fc_initializer", align 1

declare i1 @air.is_function_constant_defined(ptr addrspace(2) nocapture) local_unnamed_addr

define <4 x float> @tri_fc_fs() local_unnamed_addr {
  %v = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) @fc_value.MTL_FC_INIT_0_i, align 4
  %d = tail call i1 @air.is_function_constant_defined(ptr addrspace(2) @fc_value.MTL_FC_INIT_0_i)
  %ob = load i8, ptr addrspace(2) @fc_opaque.MTL_FC_INIT_1_b, align 1
  %o = trunc i8 %ob to i1
  %vf = uitofp i32 %v to float
  %r = fdiv float %vf, 2.550000e+02
  %g = select i1 %d, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00
  %a = select i1 %o, float 1.000000e+00, float 2.500000e-01
  %c0 = insertelement <4 x float> undef, float %r, i32 0
  %c1 = insertelement <4 x float> %c0, float %g, i32 1
  %c2 = insertelement <4 x float> %c1, float 2.500000e-01, i32 2
  %c3 = insertelement <4 x float> %c2, float %a, i32 3
  ret <4 x float> %c3
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}
!air.function_constants = !{!6, !7}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_fc_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{}
!6 = !{ptr addrspace(2) @fc_value.MTL_FC_INIT_0_i, !"int", !"fc_value", i32 0, i1 false}
!7 = !{ptr addrspace(2) @fc_opaque.MTL_FC_INIT_1_b, !"bool", !"fc_opaque", i32 1, i1 true}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_flat_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_flat_fs, the AIR side of the first draw's fragment function: the LLVM IR
; a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_flat_fs()
;     {
;       return float4(32.0 / 255.0, 64.0 / 255.0, 128.0 / 255.0, 1.0);   // [[color(0)]]
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple. Only the SHAPE of
; the metadata is Apple's convention -- the air.fragment node and the
; air.render_target output node (target 0, dual-source index 0) as QuartzCore's
; path_blit_frag_lpf spells them; the input list is empty, as a function with
; no parameters has it.
;
; The colour is a literal and not a `constant float4&`: the first draw binds no
; buffer in either stage (the contract's first decision, hakios-metal 4c8c901),
; so this FS has constlen 0 and pushes nothing. The four values are exactly the
; RGBA8Unorm bytes 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0xff after the hardware's round-to-nearest
; (n/255 for integral n is reproduced by UNORM conversion without ambiguity), so
; the probe compares pixels for equality and not within a tolerance. The
; literals are written in LLVM's hex form because 32/255 has no exact decimal
; spelling as a float: 0x3FC0101020000000 is the float nearest 0.12549019607843137
; (bits 0x3e008081), 0x3FD0101020000000 the one nearest 0.25098039215686274
; (0x3e808081), 0x3FE0101020000000 the one nearest 0.5019607843137255 (0x3f008081).
;
;   llvm-as tri_flat_fs.ll -o tri_flat_fs.bc
;   air2nir tri_flat_fs.bc
;   air2nir --interface tri_flat_fs.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_flat_fs.bc

source_filename = "tri_flat_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <4 x float> @tri_flat_fs() local_unnamed_addr {
  ret <4 x float> <float 0x3FC0101020000000, float 0x3FD0101020000000, float 0x3FE0101020000000, float 1.000000e+00>
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_flat_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_flat_vs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_flat_vs, the AIR side of the first draw's vertex function: the LLVM IR a
; Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     vertex float4 tri_flat_vs(uint vid [[vertex_id]])
;     {
;       switch (vid) {                 // two triangles, six vertices, no buffer
;         case 0:  return float4(-1, -1, 0, 1);
;         case 1:  return float4( 1, -1, 0, 1);
;         case 2:  return float4(-1,  1, 0, 1);
;         case 3:  return float4( 1, -1, 0, 1);
;         case 4:  return float4( 1,  1, 0, 1);
;         default: return float4(-1,  1, 0, 1);   // vertex 5, and every vid past it
;       }
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple. Only the SHAPE of
; the metadata is Apple's convention -- the air.vertex node (function, outputs,
; inputs), the air.position output node and the air.vertex_id input node as
; QuartzCore's path_blit_vert_lpf spells them -- which is what the AIR front end
; reads; the values are this shader's own.
;
; Why the positions are literals chosen by compare-and-select and not read from
; a buffer: the first draw binds NO buffer in either stage (the contract's first
; decision, hakios-metal 4c8c901). No Mesa 25.0.7 driver drives the graphics
; IBO table non-bindless, so a `device float2 *p` indexed by vid would need a
; load state no witness emits; turnip's own clear path draws from exactly this
; shape of VS (nir_load_vertex_id and bcsel of load_const, tu_clear_blit.cc:
; 629-664). The chain is scalar icmp eq against each vid and a select of whole
; float4 literals, which the front end makes bcsel of (air_to_nir.c, the
; AIR_OP_SELECT case: a 1-component condition is broadcast over the vector).
;
; Under Metal's orientation (NDC y up, row 0 at the top) vertices 0,1,2 are the
; LOWER-LEFT half of the target (T1) and 3,4,5 its complement (T2): a draw of
; 3 vertices paints T1, a draw of 6 paints both and tests the shared diagonal.
;
;   llvm-as tri_flat_vs.ll -o tri_flat_vs.bc
;   air2nir tri_flat_vs.bc                               (the NIR)
;   air2nir --interface tri_flat_vs.bc                   (what the pipeline must serve)
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_flat_vs.bc     (the Adreno listing)

source_filename = "tri_flat_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <4 x float> @tri_flat_vs(i32 %vid) local_unnamed_addr {
  ; the chain runs from vertex 4 down to vertex 0 so that the default (vertex 5's
  ; position) is also what every vid of 6 or more gets
  %c4 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 4
  %p4 = select i1 %c4, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %c3 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 3
  %p3 = select i1 %c3, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p4
  %c2 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 2
  %p2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p3
  %c1 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 1
  %p1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p2
  %c0 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 0
  %p0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p1
  ret <4 x float> %p0
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.vertex = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_flat_vs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.position", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.vertex_id", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"vid"}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_fw_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_fw_fs, a fragment function that takes the screen-space derivative of a
; varying, in float and in half: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_fw_fs(float4 color [[stage_in]])
;     {
;       float f = fwidth(color.r);
;       half h = fwidth(half(color.r));
;       return float4(f * 32, float(h) * 32, 0, 1);
;     }
;
; which is the shape of CoreAnimation's rounded-rect coverage (fwidth of a half
; texcoord in fixed_frag). Paired with tri_color_vs, whose red is (y - x) / 64 in
; T1 and y / 64 in T2: fwidth is 1/64 + 1/64 = 1/32 in T1 and 1/64 in T2, so
; every pixel away from the diagonal is ff ff 00 ff in T1 and 80 80 00 ff in T2.
; A derivative read across lanes that do not hold the quad's other pixels gives
; anything else, and one of 0 gives 00 00 00 ff.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_fw_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare float @air.fwidth.f32(float)
declare half @air.fwidth.f16(half)

define <4 x float> @tri_fw_fs(<4 x float> %color) local_unnamed_addr {
  %u = extractelement <4 x float> %color, i32 0
  %f = tail call fast float @air.fwidth.f32(float %u)
  %uh = fptrunc float %u to half
  %h = tail call fast half @air.fwidth.f16(half %uh)
  %hf = fpext half %h to float
  %a = fmul fast float %f, 3.200000e+01
  %b = fmul fast float %hf, 3.200000e+01
  %c0 = insertelement <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %a, i32 0
  %c1 = insertelement <4 x float> %c0, float %b, i32 1
  ret <4 x float> %c1
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_fw_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.fragment_input", !"generated(5colorDv4_f)", !"air.center", !"air.perspective", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"color"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_half_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_half_fs, a fragment function that reads halfs out of a constant buffer at
; offsets that are not all multiples of 4: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would
; emit for
;
;     struct U { half pad[32]; half a, b, c, d; };   // a at byte 64, b 66, c 68, d 70
;     fragment float4 tri_half_fs(constant U& u [[buffer(0)]])
;     {
;       return float4(u.a, u.b, u.d, u.c);
;     }
;
; which is the shape of CoreAnimation's noise_scale, a half at byte 70 of its
; uniforms that fixed_frag multiplies its noise texture by. With a = 0.25,
; b = 0.5, d = 0.75 and c = 1 every pixel is 40 80 bf ff; a load that took the
; other half of its dword reads c for d or b for a, which are other values. A
; buffer with every other half 0.125 (0x3000) says which neighbour was read.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_half_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <4 x float> @tri_half_fs(ptr addrspace(2) %u) local_unnamed_addr {
  %pa = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr addrspace(2) %u, i64 64
  %pb = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr addrspace(2) %u, i64 66
  %pc = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr addrspace(2) %u, i64 68
  %pd = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr addrspace(2) %u, i64 70
  %a = load half, ptr addrspace(2) %pa, align 2
  %b = load half, ptr addrspace(2) %pb, align 2
  %c = load half, ptr addrspace(2) %pc, align 2
  %d = load half, ptr addrspace(2) %pd, align 2
  %fa = fpext half %a to float
  %fb = fpext half %b to float
  %fc = fpext half %c to float
  %fd = fpext half %d to float
  %v0 = insertelement <4 x float> undef, float %fa, i32 0
  %v1 = insertelement <4 x float> %v0, float %fb, i32 1
  %v2 = insertelement <4 x float> %v1, float %fd, i32 2
  %v3 = insertelement <4 x float> %v2, float %fc, i32 3
  ret <4 x float> %v3
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_half_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 72, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 72, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_name", !"U", !"air.arg_name", !"u"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_hc_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_hc_fs, a fragment function whose half arithmetic reads a constant buffer's
; half straight from the const file: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_hc_fs(float4 color [[stage_in]], constant half& s [[buffer(0)]])
;     {
;       return float4(float(half(color.r) * s) * 4, 0, 0, 1);
;     }
;
; which is the shape of CoreAnimation's noise dither (noise_scale, a half in a
; buffer of its own). ir3 pushes the half, its preamble widens it to f32 into a
; const register, and the main code reads it as a half operand (hc): right only
; when the SP demotes a const read at half precision (SP_MODE_CONTROL's
; CONSTANT_DEMOTION_ENABLE). With s = 0.25 the red is tri_color's red again; the
; f32 bits' low half read as a half would be 0 for 0.25.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_hc_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <4 x float> @tri_hc_fs(<4 x float> %color, ptr addrspace(2) %s) local_unnamed_addr {
  %u = extractelement <4 x float> %color, i32 0
  %uh = fptrunc float %u to half
  %sh = load half, ptr addrspace(2) %s, align 2
  %m = fmul fast half %uh, %sh
  %mf = fpext half %m to float
  %r = fmul fast float %mf, 4.000000e+00
  %c = insertelement <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %r, i32 0
  ret <4 x float> %c
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_hc_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6, !7}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.fragment_input", !"generated(5colorDv4_f)", !"air.center", !"air.perspective", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"color"}
!7 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 2, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_name", !"half", !"air.arg_name", !"s"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_hcolor_vs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_hcolor_vs, tri_color_vs with its colour a half4: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler
; would emit for tri_color_vs with `half4 color` in its output struct, which is the
; shape of CoreAnimation's fixed_vert (its colour and texcoords are half). Paired
; with tri_hcolor_fs, which returns the half4 it is given: tri_color's picture.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_hcolor_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <{ <4 x float>, <4 x half> }> @tri_hcolor_vs(i32 %vid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %c4 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 4
  %c3 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 3
  %c2 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 2
  %c1 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 1
  %c0 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 0
  %p4 = select i1 %c4, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %p3 = select i1 %c3, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p4
  %p2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p3
  %p1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p2
  %p0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float -1.000000e+00, float -1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p1
  %k4 = select i1 %c4, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %k3 = select i1 %c3, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k4
  %k2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k3
  %k1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k2
  %k0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %k1
  %kh = fptrunc <4 x float> %k0 to <4 x half>
  %r0 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <4 x half> }> undef, <4 x float> %p0, 0
  %r1 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, <4 x half> }> %r0, <4 x half> %kh, 1
  ret <{ <4 x float>, <4 x half> }> %r1
}

!3 = !{!4, !5}

!5 = !{!"air.vertex_output", !"generated(5colorDv4_Dh)", !"air.arg_type_name", !"half4", !"air.arg_name", !"color"}
```

```ll
; tri_mrt_fs, a fragment function that writes two colour targets: the LLVM IR a
; Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     struct Out { float4 c0 [[color(0)]]; float4 c1 [[color(1)]]; };
;     fragment Out tri_mrt_fs()
;     {
;       return Out{ float4(0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0xff) / 255,   // tri_flat_fs's colour
;                   float4(1, 0, 0.25, 0.75) };

target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define { <4 x float>, <4 x float> } @tri_mrt_fs() local_unnamed_addr {
  ret { <4 x float>, <4 x float> } { <4 x float> <float 0x3FC0101020000000, float 0x3FD0101020000000, float 0x3FE0101020000000, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float 1.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 2.500000e-01, float 7.500000e-01> }
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_ms_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_ms_fs, a fragment function that reads one sample of a multisample texture: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would
; emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_ms_fs(float4 pos [[position]], constant uint &which [[buffer(0)]],
;                               texture2d_ms<float> t [[texture(0)]])
;     {
;       return t.read(uint2(pos.xy), which);
;     }
;
; Each pixel copies sample WHICH of its own pixel of a 4x texture: where a triangle's edge split a pixel's samples,
; different WHICH give different colours, which a read that ignored the sample (or read the pixel as one sample of a
; wider texture) does not.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_ms_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d_ms.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), <2 x i32>, i32, i32)

define <4 x float> @tri_ms_fs(<4 x float> %pos, ptr addrspace(2) %which, ptr addrspace(1) %t) local_unnamed_addr {
  %xy = shufflevector <4 x float> %pos, <4 x float> poison, <2 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1>
  %c = fptoui <2 x float> %xy to <2 x i32>
  %s = load i32, ptr addrspace(2) %which, align 4
  %r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.read_texture_2d_ms.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t, <2 x i32> %c, i32 %s, i32 0)
  %v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r, 0
  ret <4 x float> %v
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_ms_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6, !7, !8}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.position", !"air.center", !"air.no_perspective", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"pos"}
!7 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 4, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"which"}
!8 = !{i32 2, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.arg_type_name", !"texture2d_ms<float, read>", !"air.arg_name", !"t"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_null_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_null_fs, Metal's null texture sampled as 2D and as 3D through the one slot:
; the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     struct Vary { float4 position [[position]]; float4 color; };
;     fragment float4 tri_null_fs(Vary in [[stage_in]], sampler s [[sampler(0)]])
;     {
;       float4 a = texture2d<float>(/* null */).sample(s, in.color.xy);
;       float4 b = texture3d<float>(/* null */).sample(s, float3(in.color.xy, 0.5));
;       return float4(a.x, a.y, b.x, b.y);   // [[color(0)]]
;     }
;
; which is the shape of QuartzCore's YCbCr uber shaders, whose one reserved slot
; the front end makes of air.get_null_texture_2d and _3d alike (nir_air.h:
; air_resource.null_texture). The slot has one descriptor and the draw binds a
; 2D 1x1 texture there; the question this answers is whether a 3D sample through
; that descriptor reads its texel. The probe writes the texel with a value that
; is not zero, so a sample that reads nothing (a zero) and one that reads the
; texel come out different: red and green are the 2D sample's, blue and alpha
; the 3D one's, and all four are the texel's red and green when both read it.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata and of the intrinsic signatures is Apple's convention (tri_tex_fs.ll).

source_filename = "tri_null_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare ptr addrspace(1) @air.get_null_texture_2d()
declare ptr addrspace(1) @air.get_null_texture_3d()
declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)
declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_3d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <3 x float>, i1, <3 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)

define <4 x float> @tri_null_fs(<4 x float> %color, ptr addrspace(2) %s) local_unnamed_addr {
  %t2 = tail call ptr addrspace(1) @air.get_null_texture_2d()
  %t3 = tail call ptr addrspace(1) @air.get_null_texture_3d()
  %uv = shufflevector <4 x float> %color, <4 x float> poison, <2 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1>
  %uvw = shufflevector <4 x float> %color, <4 x float> <float 0.0, float 0.0, float 0.5, float 0.0>, <3 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1, i32 6>
  %ra = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t2, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <2 x float> %uv, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %rb = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_3d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t3, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <3 x float> %uvw, i1 true, <3 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %a = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %ra, 0
  %b = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %rb, 0
  %v = shufflevector <4 x float> %a, <4 x float> %b, <4 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1, i32 4, i32 5>
  ret <4 x float> %v
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_null_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6, !8}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.fragment_input", !"generated(5colorDv4_f)", !"air.center", !"air.perspective", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"color"}
!8 = !{i32 1, !"air.sampler", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.arg_type_name", !"sampler", !"air.arg_name", !"s"}
```
