`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_nullfb_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_nullfb_fs, a fragment function that both samples the front end's null texture and reads its render target: the
; shape of CoreAnimation's fixed_frag_lph_cpf, written as the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_nullfb_fs(float4 c [[color(0)]], texture2d<float> t [[texture(14)]], sampler s [[sampler(0)]])
;     {
;       float4 z = texture2d<float>().sample(s, float2(0));   // the null texture: zeros
;       return float4(c.g, c.b, c.r, 1) + z + t.sample(s, float2(0));
;     }
;
; A texture is sampled at slot 14, as CoreAnimation's reach that high, and the null texture's slot is the front end's
; next to it (15); the framebuffer read needs a slot of its own too. It used to be "one past the highest sampled
; slot" -- 16 here, past the table -- and is now the lowest free one.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_nullfb_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare ptr addrspace(1) @air.get_null_texture_2d()
declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)

define <4 x float> @tri_nullfb_fs(<4 x float> %c, ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s) local_unnamed_addr {
  %t2 = tail call ptr addrspace(1) @air.get_null_texture_2d()
  %r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t2, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <2 x float> zeroinitializer, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %z = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r, 0
  %v = shufflevector <4 x float> %c, <4 x float> <float 0.0, float 0.0, float 0.0, float 1.0>, <4 x i32> <i32 1, i32 2, i32 0, i32 7>
  %r15 = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <2 x float> zeroinitializer, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %s15 = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r15, 0
  %o0 = fadd <4 x float> %v, %z
  %o = fadd <4 x float> %o0, %s15
  ret <4 x float> %o
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_nullfb_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6, !8, !7}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.render_target", i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"c"}
!8 = !{i32 1, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 14, i32 1, !"air.sample", !"air.arg_type_name", !"texture2d<float, sample>", !"air.arg_name", !"t"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.sampler", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.arg_type_name", !"sampler", !"air.arg_name", !"s"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_oldcb_vs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_oldcb_vs, a vertex function in the shape of AIR 2.3 (Metal 2.3, iOS 14): its buffer's metadata carries no
; air.address_space, which later AIR writes on every buffer. The LLVM IR a Metal compiler of that version would emit for
;
;     vertex float4 tri_oldcb_vs(uint vid [[vertex_id]], constant float4 *at [[buffer(1)]]) { return at[vid]; }
;
; The address space is then the pointer's own (addrspace(2), a constant buffer). tri_oldcb_vs and tri_olddb_vs differ
; in nothing else, so a front end that took one kind for every buffer without the key gets one of the two wrong.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_oldcb_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios14.0.0"

define <{ <4 x float> }> @tri_oldcb_vs(i32 %vid, ptr addrspace(2) %at) local_unnamed_addr {
  %i = zext i32 %vid to i64
  %p = getelementptr inbounds <4 x float>, ptr addrspace(2) %at, i64 %i
  %v = load <4 x float>, ptr addrspace(2) %p, align 16
  %r = insertvalue <{ <4 x float> }> undef, <4 x float> %v, 0
  ret <{ <4 x float> }> %r
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.vertex = !{!2}

!5 = !{!6, !7}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.vertex_id", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"vid"}
```

```ll
;
;     struct P { float4 position [[position]]; float size [[point_size]]; };
;     vertex P tri_pt_vs(uint vid [[vertex_id]])

; up -- each 8 pixels across: drawn as points, 4 squares of 8x8 and nothing else.

  %c2 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 2
  %c1 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 1
  %c0 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 0
  %p2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float -5.000000e-01, float -5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float 5.000000e-01, float -5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %p1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 5.000000e-01, float 5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p2
  %p0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float -5.000000e-01, float 5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p1
  %r0 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, float }> undef, <4 x float> %p0, 0
  %r1 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, float }> %r0, float 8.000000e+00, 1
  ret <{ <4 x float>, float }> %r1
}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_pvt_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_pvt_fs, a fragment function whose array lives in private memory: the LLVM
; IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_pvt_fs(float4 pos [[position]])
;     {
;       uint x = uint(pos.x), y = uint(pos.y);
;       uint a[128];
;       for (uint i = 0; i < 128; i++) a[i] = 3 * i + y + 1;
;       return float4(a[x & 127] / 255.0, 0, 0, 1);
;     }
;
; which is the shape of CoreAnimation's path_exterior_fragment (512 bytes of
; private memory a fiber). 128 words are past the 256 bytes ir3 keeps in
; registers (nir_lower_vars_to_scratch in ir3_nir.c), the index is the pixel's,
; and the fill depends on y so that nir_opt_large_constants cannot make the array
; a constant table. Paired with tri_flat_vs. Pixel (i, j) must have red
; 3i + j + 1 (at most 253): private memory not bound or laid out wrong reads
; zeros or another fiber's words.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_pvt_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <4 x float> @tri_pvt_fs(<4 x float> %pos) local_unnamed_addr {
entry:
  %a = alloca [128 x i32], align 4
  %px = extractelement <4 x float> %pos, i32 0
  %py = extractelement <4 x float> %pos, i32 1
  %x = fptoui float %px to i32
  %y = fptoui float %py to i32
  %base = add i32 %y, 1
  br label %fill

fill:
  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %entry ], [ %next, %fill ]
  %t = mul i32 %i, 3
  %v = add i32 %t, %base
  %p = getelementptr inbounds [128 x i32], ptr %a, i32 0, i32 %i
  store i32 %v, ptr %p, align 4
  %next = add i32 %i, 1
  %more = icmp ult i32 %next, 128
  br i1 %more, label %fill, label %read

read:
  %k = and i32 %x, 127
  %q = getelementptr inbounds [128 x i32], ptr %a, i32 0, i32 %k
  %w = load i32, ptr %q, align 4
  %f = uitofp i32 %w to float
  %r = fdiv float %f, 2.550000e+02
  %c = insertelement <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %r, i32 0
  ret <4 x float> %c
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.fragment = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @tri_pvt_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}
!5 = !{!6}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.position", !"air.center", !"air.no_perspective", !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4", !"air.arg_name", !"pos"}
```

```ll
; tri_shadow_fs, a fragment function that compares a depth texture with a value: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would
; emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_shadow_fs(float4 pos [[position]], constant float &ref [[buffer(0)]],
;                                   depth2d<float> t [[texture(0)]], sampler s [[sampler(0)]])
;     {
;       return float4(t.sample_compare(s, pos.xy / 64.0, ref), 0, 0, 1);
;     }
;
; Each pixel of a 64x64 target compares its own texel of a 64x64 depth texture (a shadow map's lookup, nearest) with
; REF under the sampler's compare function: red 1 where the comparison passes, 0 where it fails. A depth texture
; holding two depths either side of REF splits the target along where they meet; one that was never read, or read as
; a colour texture, does not.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention (the
; depth form's i32 after the sampler as Apple's declaration of air.sample_depth_2d has it).

source_filename = "tri_shadow_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { float, i8 } @air.sample_compare_depth_2d.f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), i32, <2 x float>, float, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)

define <4 x float> @tri_shadow_fs(<4 x float> %pos, ptr addrspace(2) %ref, ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s) local_unnamed_addr {
  %xy = shufflevector <4 x float> %pos, <4 x float> poison, <2 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1>
  %uv = fmul <2 x float> %xy, <float 1.562500e-02, float 1.562500e-02>
  %r = load float, ptr addrspace(2) %ref, align 4
  %c = tail call { float, i8 } @air.sample_compare_depth_2d.f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s, i32 1, <2 x float> %uv, float %r, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %v = extractvalue { float, i8 } %c, 0
  %o0 = insertelement <4 x float> <float poison, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %v, i32 0
  ret <4 x float> %o0
}

!2 = !{ptr @tri_shadow_fs, !3, !5}
!3 = !{!4}
!4 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float4"}

!7 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 4, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float", !"air.arg_name", !"ref"}
```

```ll
; tri_tex39_fs, a fragment function that samples two textures at slots other than
; 0 with two samplers: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     fragment float4 tri_tex39_fs(texture2d<float> a [[texture(3)]],
;                                  texture2d<float> b [[texture(9)]],
;                                  sampler sa [[sampler(0)]], sampler sb [[sampler(1)]])
;     {
;       return float4(a.sample(sa, float2(0.5)).r, b.sample(sb, float2(0.5)).g, 0, 1);
;     }
;
; which is the shape of CoreAnimation's fixed_frag with a noise texture: its image at
; [[texture(3)]] and its noise at [[texture(9)]], each with a sampler of its own. With
; a 1x1 texture of ff 00 00 ff at 3 and one of 00 80 00 ff at 9 every pixel is
; ff 80 00 ff; the two read the other way round give 00 00 00 ff, and the same one
; twice ff 00 00 ff or 00 80 00 ff.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention.
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_tex_fs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_tex_fs, the first fragment function that samples: the LLVM IR a Metal
; compiler would emit for
;
;     struct Vary { float4 position [[position]]; float4 color; };
;     fragment float4 tri_tex_fs(Vary in [[stage_in]],
;                                texture2d<float> t [[texture(0)]],
;                                sampler s          [[sampler(0)]])
;     {
;       return t.sample(s, in.color.xy);   // [[color(0)]]
;     }
;
; Paired with tri_color_vs, whose colour varying is red at v0/v3, green at v1/v4
; and blue at v2/v5: its red and green components, interpolated, ARE a texture
; coordinate -- (1, 0) at one corner, (0, 1) at the next, (0, 0) at the third --
; so every pixel samples a texel the probe can name from the barycentric rule it
; already has (tri_color's), with no new vertex function. Under nearest/clamp the
; expectation is that texel exactly.
;
; Why the coordinate is the varying itself and nothing computed from it: that is
; the shape ir3 turns into a prefetch (ir3_nir_lower_tex_prefetch: a 2D sample
; whose coordinate is an interpolated input, nothing else), the sample the FS
; issues before its first instruction through SP_FS_PREFETCH_CMD. The prefetch is
; what the fragment path needs first: most of what Metal's clients draw is a
; textured quad sampled at a varying, the shape every compositor's blit has.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata and of the intrinsic signature is Apple's convention (tri_color_fs.ll
; for the varying, tex_sample_gid.ll for the sample).
;
;   llvm-as tri_tex_fs.ll -o tri_tex_fs.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_tex_fs.bc

source_filename = "tri_tex_fs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)

define <4 x float> @tri_tex_fs(<4 x float> %color, ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s) local_unnamed_addr {
  %uv = shufflevector <4 x float> %color, <4 x float> poison, <2 x i32> <i32 0, i32 1>
  %r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <2 x float> %uv, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r, 0
  ret <4 x float> %v
}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/tri_upos_vs.ll`:

```ll
; tri_upos_vs, vertex pulling from a constant buffer: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler
; would emit for
;
;     vertex float4 tri_upos_vs(constant float2 *pos [[buffer(0)]],
;                               uint vid             [[vertex_id]])
;     {
;       return float4(pos[vid], 0.0, 1.0);   // [[position]]
;     }
;
; The index is the vertex id, which no compile-time analysis bounds, so ir3 cannot
; push the buffer into the constant file (that is what tri_cflat_fs's fixed-offset
; read gets): it leaves an ldc through UBO descriptor 0, which the draw must load
; (ST6_UBO into the vertex stage's block, Gallium's fd6_emit_ubos). Paired with
; tri_flat_fs, and given tri_flat_vs's six positions in the buffer, the picture is
; 9b's pair exactly: positions read wrong would move the triangles.
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the
; metadata is Apple's convention (tri_cflat_fs.ll for the buffer, tri_flat_vs.ll
; for the vertex id).
;
;   llvm-as tri_upos_vs.ll -o tri_upos_vs.bc
;   ir3_compiler --chip-id 0x06030500 tri_upos_vs.bc

source_filename = "tri_upos_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define <4 x float> @tri_upos_vs(ptr addrspace(2) %pos, i32 %vid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %i = zext i32 %vid to i64
  %p = getelementptr inbounds <2 x float>, ptr addrspace(2) %pos, i64 %i
  %xy = load <2 x float>, ptr addrspace(2) %p, align 8
  %x = extractelement <2 x float> %xy, i32 0
  %y = extractelement <2 x float> %xy, i32 1
  %v0 = insertelement <4 x float> <float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, float %x, i32 0
  %v1 = insertelement <4 x float> %v0, float %y, i32 1
  ret <4 x float> %v1
}

!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.vertex = !{!2}
```

```ll
; tri_vtex_vs, a vertex function that samples a texture: the LLVM IR a Metal compiler would emit for
;
;     struct P { float4 position [[position]]; float size [[point_size]]; float4 color; };
;     vertex P tri_vtex_vs(uint vid [[vertex_id]], texture2d<float> t [[texture(0)]], sampler s [[sampler(0)]])
;     {
;       const float2 at[4] = { float2(-0.5, 0.5), float2(0.5, 0.5), float2(-0.5, -0.5), float2(0.5, -0.5) };
;       return P{ float4(at[vid], 0, 1), 8.0, t.sample(s, float2((vid + 0.5) / 4, 0.5), level(0)) };
;     }
;
; tri_pt_vs's four points, each the colour of texel VID of a 4x1 texture under a nearest sampler: with tri_color_fs
; each 8x8 square is its own texel, so a vertex stage that read nothing, or one texel for all four, or the texels in
; another order, draws something else. A vertex stage samples at an explicit level, Metal's rule, hence level(0).
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT: nothing in it comes from Apple; only the SHAPE of the metadata is Apple's convention.

source_filename = "tri_vtex_vs"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1), ptr addrspace(2), <2 x float>, i1, <2 x i32>, i1, float, float, i32)

define <{ <4 x float>, float, <4 x float> }> @tri_vtex_vs(i32 %vid, ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s) local_unnamed_addr {
  %c2 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 2
  %c1 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 1
  %c0 = icmp eq i32 %vid, 0
  %p2 = select i1 %c2, <4 x float> <float -5.000000e-01, float -5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> <float 5.000000e-01, float -5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>
  %p1 = select i1 %c1, <4 x float> <float 5.000000e-01, float 5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p2
  %p0 = select i1 %c0, <4 x float> <float -5.000000e-01, float 5.000000e-01, float 0.000000e+00, float 1.000000e+00>, <4 x float> %p1
  %vf = uitofp i32 %vid to float
  %vh = fadd float %vf, 5.000000e-01
  %u = fmul float %vh, 2.500000e-01
  %uv0 = insertelement <2 x float> <float poison, float 5.000000e-01>, float %u, i32 0
  %r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32(ptr addrspace(1) %t, ptr addrspace(2) %s, <2 x float> %uv0, i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 true, float 0.000000e+00, float 0.000000e+00, i32 0)
  %k = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %r, 0
  %r0 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, float, <4 x float> }> undef, <4 x float> %p0, 0
  %r1 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, float, <4 x float> }> %r0, float 8.000000e+00, 1
  %r2 = insertvalue <{ <4 x float>, float, <4 x float> }> %r1, <4 x float> %k, 2
  ret <{ <4 x float>, float, <4 x float> }> %r2
}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/undef_phi_id.ll`:

```ll
; undef_phi_id: a pointer split into one phi per path, each undef over the other path's edge -- the shape LLVM leaves
; when only one path uses each copy:
;
;     kernel void undef_phi_id(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       if (gid & 1) out[gid] = gid * 3;
;       else         out[gid] = gid ^ 0x5a5a;
;     }
;
; after the optimiser has hoisted the two address computations above a join and sunk the stores below it. Hand-written,
; ours, MIT; the metadata's shape is Apple's convention, as in fill_id.ll. MPS's cnnConvArray_* kernels carry two such
; threadgroup pointers, and the front end counted the undef as a second resource and refused them, which took
; mediaserverd down in a loop. The two values differ for every gid, so a store through the wrong copy shows.

source_filename = "undef_phi_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define void @undef_phi_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
entry:
  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64
  %odd = trunc i32 %gid to i1
  br i1 %odd, label %a, label %b

a:
  %pa = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  br label %join

b:
  %pb = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  br label %join

join:
  %p1 = phi ptr addrspace(1) [ %pa, %a ], [ undef, %b ]
  %p2 = phi ptr addrspace(1) [ undef, %a ], [ %pb, %b ]
  br i1 %odd, label %s1, label %s2

s1:
  %v1 = mul i32 %gid, 3
  store i32 %v1, ptr addrspace(1) %p1, align 4
  br label %end

s2:
  %v2 = xor i32 %gid, 23130
  store i32 %v2, ptr addrspace(1) %p2, align 4
  br label %end

end:
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @undef_phi_id, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/uniform_id.ll`:

```ll
; uniform_id: simd_is_uniform over a value every lane of a SIMD group shares, and over one they do not:
;
;     kernel void uniform_id(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
;     {
;       out[gid] = 2 * uint(simd_is_uniform(ushort(gid >> 8))) + uint(simd_is_uniform(gid & 1));
;     }
;
; Hand-written, ours, MIT; the metadata's shape is Apple's convention, as in fill_id.ll. gid >> 8 is one value over
; 256 consecutive threads, which hold a whole group of this hardware's 64 or 128 lanes; gid & 1 differs between
; neighbours. Every word is 2. air.is_uniform is what mediaserverd's CNN kernels call, which the front end refused.

source_filename = "uniform_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare i1 @air.is_uniform.i16(i16)
declare i1 @air.is_uniform.i32(i32)

define void @uniform_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid) local_unnamed_addr {
  %hi = lshr i32 %gid, 8
  %h16 = trunc i32 %hi to i16
  %u1 = call i1 @air.is_uniform.i16(i16 %h16)
  %lo = and i32 %gid, 1
  %u2 = call i1 @air.is_uniform.i32(i32 %lo)
  %z1 = zext i1 %u1 to i32
  %z2 = zext i1 %u2 to i32
  %d = shl i32 %z1, 1
  %v = add i32 %d, %z2
  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64
  %po = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  store i32 %v, ptr addrspace(1) %po, align 4
  ret void
}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/kernels/width_id.ll`:

```ll
; width_id: the thread execution width a kernel is given, the LLVM IR a Metal compiler emits for
;
;     kernel void width_id(device uint *out [[buffer(0)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]],
;                          uint width [[thread_execution_width]])
;     {
;       out[gid] = width * 1000 + (gid & 63);
;     }
;
; The width is the SIMD-group's: 64 on the A635 in every stage (hakios-metal keeps ir3 to its single threadsize), the
; number the device reports as the pipeline's threadExecutionWidth. Resident Evil 4's mainCS and
; CS_MiniClusterCompaction take it, which the front end refused as an input it did not know. The gid term makes every
; word differ, so a kernel that wrote one word for all would show. Hand-written, ours, MIT; the metadata's shape is
; Apple's convention, as in fill_id.ll.

source_filename = "width_id"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

define void @width_id(ptr addrspace(1) %out, i32 %gid, i32 %width) local_unnamed_addr {
  %w = mul i32 %width, 1000
  %l = and i32 %gid, 63
  %v = add i32 %w, %l
  %t = zext i32 %gid to i64
  %po = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %out, i64 %t
  store i32 %v, ptr addrspace(1) %po, align 4
  ret void
}

!air.version = !{!0}
!air.language_version = !{!1}
!air.kernel = !{!2}

!0 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!1 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!2 = !{ptr @width_id, !3, !4}
!3 = !{}
!4 = !{!5, !6, !7}
!5 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{i32 1, !"air.thread_position_in_grid", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"gid"}
!7 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_execution_width", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"width"}
```

`hakios-metal/tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch`:

```patch
Teach ir3_compiler to write the variant out: -o FILE, a hakios::metal::Kernel fixture.

ir3_compiler prints a listing of what it compiled and keeps the binary to itself.
hakios-metal dispatches kernels with raw PM4, as Mesa's computerator does, and
needs the words together with the layout ir3 chose around them: where the driver
params go, which UBO ranges were pushed to consts and to where, the immediates
and their offset, the register ids of the ids the hardware loads, constlen,
instrlen, the register footprint. No listing carries all of that, and the AIR
path has no other place where the variant exists -- the frontend is reached only
through this tool. So -o FILE writes the variant as the same C++ fixture that
hakios-metal's tools/ir3-kernel writes for a text kernel (its
include/hakios-metal/kernel.hpp documents every field and the register that
reads it), and -s FILE carries the kernel text (the .ll) into it for the record.

The variant is assembled once: ir3_shader_assemble frees the constant data it
appends to the binary, so dump_info now takes the binary rather than calling it.

Applies after air-frontend.patch, air-ir3.patch and ir3-round-default.patch
(tools/air/mk-host.sh's order) on mesa-25.0.7, with the AIR frontend copied in.

-o also writes the Kernel's texture fields (textures[], numTextureSlots,
samplerMask) from a walk of the NIR before ir3 lowers it: which Metal texture
index the code samples (sam/saml/isaml through the texture table) or stores
to as an image (stib/ldib at IBO slot num_ssbos + index), with what dimension
and element class and width, and which sampler indices it names. The dispatch
sizes its tables from these, not from ir3's num_samp, which counts textures and
images together and ignores sampler indices (ir3_compiler_nir.c), nor from the
front end's resource list, which says what was declared and not what the code
does. The same walk lives in hakios-metal's src/compiler.cpp, and compiler_test
holds the two to each other over tools/kernels/*.ll. A sampled slot the front
end reserved for Metal's null texture (air_resource.null_texture) is marked as
such: the draw binds its own texture there, whatever the application bound.

-o is stage-aware (29 October): a VERTEX or FRAGMENT variant is written as a
hakios::metal::Stage (include/hakios-metal/render.hpp) -- the Kernel as its
first member, then inputs[] (slot, regid, compmask, inloc, sysval, bary, flat,
half) and outputs[] (slot, regid, half, and the output's declared class in the
pad: float or integer, read off the NIR's shader_out variables before lowering)
straight from ir3_shader_variant, and the regids and flags turnip's
tu6_emit_vpc / tu6_emit_fs_inputs / tu6_emit_fs_outputs read (vertex id,
position, the ij barycentrics, frag coord, face, the colour outputs with
ir3_get_output_regid's HALF_REG_ID split, depth/stencil/sample mask, total_in,
has_kill, per_samp...). The vertex-only and fragment-only fields are read from
their own stage only, because the slot namespaces collide (VARYING_SLOT_POS and
FRAG_RESULT_DEPTH are both 0). A compute variant is written as the Kernel it
was, byte for byte; any other stage is refused by name, where before 29 October
a VS came out as a compute-shaped Kernel and the tool exited 0.

For a vertex or fragment AIR input the NIR is lowered in turnip's order:
ir3_nir_lower_io_to_temporaries on the IO VARIABLES, nir_lower_io inside
ir3_nir_post_finalize (ir3_nir.c:755; tu_shader.cc:2527). The AIR path used to
lower IO first, so io_to_temporaries found nothing to copy and left orphan
temporaries whose undef stores nir_opt_undef happened to remove; a second
store_output to one slot would have won in ir3's setup_output. Compute keeps
the old order (it has no IO variables) and its fixtures do not change.
hakios-metal's compileStage runs the same passes in the same order, and
compiler_test holds each Stage compiled there to the fixture written here.

+/* -o FILE: the compiled variant written out as a hakios::metal::Kernel fixture,
+ * in the format hakios-metal's tools/ir3-kernel writes for a text kernel (its
+ * include/hakios-metal/kernel.hpp documents every field and the register that
+ * reads it): constexpr arrays of the words and the immediates, a constexpr
+ * Kernel with every field in order, and the listing as comments. The two
+ * writers are kept in step by hand; a field added to the struct is added to
+ * both. It lives here because this is the only place where an AIR kernel's
+ * variant exists: ir3_compiler has no binary output of its own, and the driver
+ * needs the words together with the layout ir3 chose for them -- where the
+ * driver params and the pushed UBO ranges go -- which no listing carries whole.
+ */
+static void
+emit_words(FILE *out, const char *name, const uint32_t *words, uint32_t count)
+{
+   fprintf(out, "constexpr uint32_t %s[] = {", name);
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+      if (i % 4 == 0)
+         fputs("\n   ", out);
+      fprintf(out, " 0x%08x,", words[i]);
+   }
+   fputs("\n};\n", out);
+}
+
+static void
+emit_comment_block(FILE *out, const char *text)
+{
+   while (*text) {
+      const char *nl = strchr(text, '\n');
+      size_t len = nl ? (size_t)(nl - text) : strlen(text);
+      fprintf(out, "// %.*s\n", (int)len, text);
+      text += len + (nl ? 1 : 0);
+   }
+}
+
+/* -o: the kernel's textures, images and samplers as its INSTRUCTIONS address
+ * them (kernel.hpp: Kernel::textures, numTextureSlots, samplerMask), read off
+ * the NIR the front end produced, before ir3 lowers it. ir3's own num_samp
+ * counts sampled textures and images together and never looks at a sampler
+ * index (ir3_compiler_nir.c: num_samp = last texture used + 1 + num_images),
+ * so the dispatch cannot size its tables from it; and the front end's resource
+ * list says what was declared, not what the code does with it. The walk is the
+ * one hakios-metal's compileAir makes in-process (src/compiler.cpp), so that a
+ * fixture and an in-process compile agree field for field (compiler_test):
+ *
+ *   nir_tex_instr          slot texture_index, kind sampled (1): sam/saml with
+ *                          a sampler, isaml for texture.read (txf). dim from
+ *                          sampler_dim, element from dest_type -- but not from
+ *                          a query (txs, lod, query_levels...), whose int
+ *                          result is not the texture's class. The ops that take
+ *                          a sampler (tex, txb, txl, txd, tg4, lod:
+ *                          nir_tex_instr_need_sampler) set the sampler's bit;
+ *                          txf, txf_ms and the queries do not.
+ *   image_load/store       slot src[0] (always an immediate from the front end),
+ *                          kind image (2): ldib/stib at IBO slot num_ssbos +
+ *                          index (ir3_image.c:50-52). element from dest_type /
+ *                          src_type and the WIDTH from the value's bit size, as
+ *                          ir3_get_type_for_image_intrinsic reads them
+ *                          (ir3_image.c:96-141): a half image is a 16-bit stib
+ *                          into whatever descriptor is bound.
+ *   image_atomic(_swap)    the same, read and written, the atomic op's type.
+ *   image_size/levels/samples   the slot's kind and dimension only.
+ *
+ * A texture or sampler chosen at run time, an index at or past the Kernel's
+ * sixteen slots, a dimension or element class the Kernel has no name for, or
+ * one index used two ways are refused by name: the Kernel has no field for them.
+ */
+#define FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS 16   /* kernel.hpp's kMaxTextureSlots */
+
+struct fixture_texture {
+   uint8_t kind, dim, is_array, element, bits, read, write, is_null, fb_target;   /* KernelTexture */
+};
+
+struct fixture_textures {
+   struct fixture_texture slot[FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS];
+   unsigned num_slots;      /* highest SAMPLED index + 1: Kernel::numTextureSlots */
+   uint32_t sampler_mask;   /* Kernel::samplerMask */
+};
+
+static uint8_t
+fixture_dim(enum glsl_sampler_dim dim, const char *what, unsigned index)
+{
+   switch (dim) {
+   case GLSL_SAMPLER_DIM_1D:   return 1;   /* kTexDim1D */
+   case GLSL_SAMPLER_DIM_2D:
+   case GLSL_SAMPLER_DIM_RECT: return 2;   /* kTexDim2D */
+   case GLSL_SAMPLER_DIM_3D:   return 3;   /* kTexDim3D */
+   case GLSL_SAMPLER_DIM_CUBE: return 4;   /* kTexDimCube */
+   case GLSL_SAMPLER_DIM_MS:   return 5;   /* kTexDimMS */
+   default:
+      errx(1, "-o: %s %u has a dimension (glsl_sampler_dim %d) KernelTextureDim has no name for",
+           what, index, (int)dim);
+   }
+}
+
+static uint8_t
+fixture_element(nir_alu_type type, const char *what, unsigned index)
+{
+   switch (nir_alu_type_get_base_type(type)) {
+   case nir_type_float: return 0;   /* kElemFloat */
+   case nir_type_uint:  return 1;   /* kElemUint */
+   case nir_type_int:   return 2;   /* kElemInt */
+   default:
+      errx(1, "-o: %s %u moves values of nir_alu_type %d, which is not float, uint or int",
+           what, index, (int)type);
+   }
+}
+
+static struct fixture_texture *
+fixture_slot(struct fixture_textures *t, unsigned index, uint8_t kind, const char *what)
+{
+   if (index >= FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS)
+      errx(1, "-o: %s index %u: the Kernel holds %u texture slots", what, index,
+           FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS);
+   struct fixture_texture *s = &t->slot[index];
+   if (s->kind && s->kind != kind)
+      errx(1, "-o: texture index %u is both sampled and addressed as an image", index);
+   s->kind = kind;
+   return s;
+}
+
+/* The front end's reading of the function's metadata, kept from load_air for
+ * the check below: what Apple DECLARED each texture argument as. */
+static struct air_shader_info fixture_air_info;
+
+/* The element class a declaration names: the scalar type between the first '<'
+ * and the next ',' or '>' of air.arg_type_name ("texture2d<half, write>").
+ * -1 when the name has none (src/compiler.cpp: declaredElement, the same rule). */
+static int
+fixture_declared_element(const char *type_name)
+{
+   const char *lt = strchr(type_name, '<');
+   if (!lt)
+      return -1;
+   const char *b = lt + 1;
+   while (*b == ' ')
+      b++;
+   const char *e = b;
+   while (*e && *e != ',' && *e != '>' && *e != ' ')
+      e++;
+   size_t n = e - b;
+#define IS(word) (n == strlen(word) && !strncmp(b, word, n))
+   if (IS("half") || IS("float") || IS("bfloat"))
+      return 0;
+   if (IS("uint") || IS("ushort") || IS("uchar"))
+      return 1;
+   if (IS("int") || IS("short") || IS("char"))
+      return 2;
+#undef IS
+   return -1;
+}
+
+static void
+walk_textures(nir_shader *nir, struct fixture_textures *t)
+{
+   memset(t, 0, sizeof(*t));
+   nir_foreach_function_impl(impl, nir) {
+      nir_foreach_block(block, impl) {
+         nir_foreach_instr(instr, block) {
+            if (instr->type == nir_instr_type_tex) {
+               nir_tex_instr *tex = nir_instr_as_tex(instr);
+               if (nir_tex_instr_src_index(tex, nir_tex_src_texture_offset) >= 0 ||
+                   nir_tex_instr_src_index(tex, nir_tex_src_sampler_offset) >= 0 ||
+                   nir_tex_instr_src_index(tex, nir_tex_src_texture_handle) >= 0 ||
+                   nir_tex_instr_src_index(tex, nir_tex_src_sampler_handle) >= 0)
+                  errx(1, "-o: a texture or sampler chosen at run time: the Kernel addresses them by Metal's own indices only");
+               struct fixture_texture *s = fixture_slot(t, tex->texture_index, 1, "texture");
+               s->dim = fixture_dim(tex->sampler_dim, "texture", tex->texture_index);
+               s->is_array = tex->is_array;
+               s->read = 1;
+               if (!nir_tex_instr_is_query(tex))
+                  s->element = fixture_element(tex->dest_type, "texture", tex->texture_index);
+               if (nir_tex_instr_need_sampler(tex)) {
+                  if (tex->sampler_index >= FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS)
+                     errx(1, "-o: sampler index %u: the Kernel holds %u sampler slots",
+                          tex->sampler_index, FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS);
+                  t->sampler_mask |= 1u << tex->sampler_index;
+               }
+               if (tex->texture_index + 1 > t->num_slots)
+                  t->num_slots = tex->texture_index + 1;
+            } else if (instr->type == nir_instr_type_intrinsic) {
+               nir_intrinsic_instr *in = nir_instr_as_intrinsic(instr);
+               nir_alu_type type = nir_type_invalid;
+               bool read = false, write = false, typed = true;
+               switch (in->intrinsic) {
+               case nir_intrinsic_image_load:
+                  type = nir_intrinsic_dest_type(in);
+                  read = true;
+                  break;
+               case nir_intrinsic_image_store:
+                  type = nir_intrinsic_src_type(in);
+                  write = true;
+                  break;
+               case nir_intrinsic_image_atomic:
+               case nir_intrinsic_image_atomic_swap:
+                  type = nir_atomic_op_type(nir_intrinsic_atomic_op(in));
+                  read = write = true;
+                  break;
+               case nir_intrinsic_image_size:
+               case nir_intrinsic_image_levels:
+               case nir_intrinsic_image_samples:
+                  typed = false;
+                  break;
+               default:
+                  continue;
+               }
+               if (!nir_src_is_const(in->src[0]))
+                  errx(1, "-o: an image chosen at run time: the Kernel addresses images by Metal's own indices only");
+               unsigned index = nir_src_as_uint(in->src[0]);
+               struct fixture_texture *s = fixture_slot(t, index, 2, "image");
+               s->dim = fixture_dim(nir_intrinsic_image_dim(in), "image", index);
+               s->is_array = nir_intrinsic_image_array(in);
+               s->read |= read;
+               s->write |= write;
+               if (typed) {
+                  const nir_intrinsic_info *info = &nir_intrinsic_infos[in->intrinsic];
+                  unsigned bits = info->has_dest ? in->def.bit_size : nir_src_bit_size(in->src[3]);
+                  uint8_t element = fixture_element(type, "image", index);
+                  if (s->bits && (s->bits != bits || s->element != element))
+                     errx(1, "-o: image %u is addressed as %u-bit values of element class %u and as %u-bit values of class %u",
+                          index, s->bits, s->element, bits, element);
+                  s->element = element;
+                  s->bits = bits;
+               }
+            }
+         }
+      }
+   }
+   /* The declaration and the instructions must name the same class. They did
+    * not for every half or float image until 29 October: the front end typed
+    * a texture write by the call's return type (void, so uint), and ir3 then
+    * emitted stib.b.typed.*.u16/u32 for half and float values, which a typed
+    * store converts as integers. src/compiler.cpp refuses the same, so that a
+    * fixture and a kernel compiled on the phone agree in refusing it. */
+   static const char *const class_names[] = { "float", "uint", "int" };
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < fixture_air_info.num_resources; i++) {
+      const struct air_resource *r = &fixture_air_info.resources[i];
+      if ((r->kind != AIR_RESOURCE_TEXTURE && r->kind != AIR_RESOURCE_IMAGE) ||
+          r->index >= FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS || !r->type_name)
+         continue;
+      const struct fixture_texture *s = &t->slot[r->index];
+      if (!s->kind)
+         continue;
+      int declared = fixture_declared_element(r->type_name);
+      if (declared >= 0 && declared != s->element)
+         errx(1, "-o: texture %u is declared %s but its instructions move %s values through it: "
+                 "the front end's typing of the access is off",
+              r->index, r->type_name, class_names[s->element]);
+   }
+   /* The front end's reserved slot for Metal's null texture (air_resource.null_texture),
+    * when the code samples it: the draw binds its own texture there. A slot declared
+    * and not sampled is no slot, as for any texture. */
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < fixture_air_info.num_resources; i++) {
+      const struct air_resource *r = &fixture_air_info.resources[i];
+      if (r->kind == AIR_RESOURCE_TEXTURE && r->null_texture && r->index < FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS &&
+          t->slot[r->index].kind == 1)
+         t->slot[r->index].is_null = 1;
+   }
+}
+
+static int read_file(const char *filename, void **ptr, size_t *size);
+
+/* A framebuffer fetch lowered before ir3_nir_post_finalize would, with the
+ * layer and the sample it reads made 0 -- what hakios-metal's compiler does
+ * (src/compiler.cpp: lowerFbReadSingleLayer, which says why), so that its
+ * fixtures and its compiles agree. Only the reads the lowering added: the
+ * shader's own are counted first and left alone. */
+struct fixture_fb_counts {
+   unsigned layer, sample;
+};
+
+static bool
+fixture_count_layer_sample(nir_builder *b, nir_intrinsic_instr *in, void *data)
+{
+   struct fixture_fb_counts *c = data;
+   (void)b;
+   c->layer += in->intrinsic == nir_intrinsic_load_layer_id;
+   c->sample += in->intrinsic == nir_intrinsic_load_sample_id;
+   return false;
+}
+
+static bool
+fixture_zero_layer_sample(nir_builder *b, nir_intrinsic_instr *in, void *data)
+{
+   const struct fixture_fb_counts *own = data;
+   if (!((in->intrinsic == nir_intrinsic_load_layer_id && own->layer == 0) ||
+         (in->intrinsic == nir_intrinsic_load_sample_id && own->sample == 0)))
+      return false;
+   b->cursor = nir_before_instr(&in->instr);
+   nir_def_rewrite_uses(&in->def, nir_imm_intN_t(b, 0, in->def.bit_size));
+   nir_instr_remove(&in->instr);
+   return true;
+}
+
+/* ...and each fetch then an ordinary texel fetch of a slot of its target's own,
+ * one past the highest sampled slot plus the target's index, marked in the
+ * fixture's slot table (src/compiler.cpp: lowerFbRead, which says why). */
+/* whether the lowering below made a fetch slot: the stage reads its targets,
+ * which ir3's fb_read no longer says (it sees no txf_ms_fb) */
+static bool fixture_fb_lowered;
+
+/* src/compiler.cpp: fixPrefetchSamplers */
+static bool
+fix_prefetch_samplers(nir_shader *nir, struct ir3_shader_variant *v)
+{
+   uint8_t sampler_of[32];
+   memset(sampler_of, 0xfe, sizeof(sampler_of));
+   nir_foreach_function_impl (impl, nir) {
+      nir_foreach_block (block, impl) {
+         nir_foreach_instr (instr, block) {
+            if (instr->type != nir_instr_type_tex)
+               continue;
+            nir_tex_instr *tex = nir_instr_as_tex(instr);
+            if (!nir_tex_instr_need_sampler(tex) || tex->texture_index >= 32)
+               continue;
+            uint8_t *s = &sampler_of[tex->texture_index];
+            *s = *s == 0xfe ? (uint8_t)tex->sampler_index : *s == tex->sampler_index ? *s : 0xff;
+         }
+      }
+   }
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < v->num_sampler_prefetch; i++) {
+      struct ir3_sampler_prefetch *p = &v->sampler_prefetch[i];
+      if (p->bindless || p->tex_id >= 32 || sampler_of[p->tex_id] == 0xfe)
+         continue;
+      if (sampler_of[p->tex_id] == 0xff)
+         return false;
+      p->samp_id = sampler_of[p->tex_id];
+   }
+   return true;
+}
+
+/* src/compiler.cpp: widenHalfVarying */
+static bool
+widen_half_varyings(nir_builder *b, nir_intrinsic_instr *intr, void *data)
+{
+   const bool store = intr->intrinsic == nir_intrinsic_store_output && b->shader->info.stage == MESA_SHADER_VERTEX;
+   const bool load = (intr->intrinsic == nir_intrinsic_load_interpolated_input || intr->intrinsic == nir_intrinsic_load_input) &&
+                     b->shader->info.stage == MESA_SHADER_FRAGMENT;
+   if (store) {
+      if (nir_src_bit_size(intr->src[0]) != 16)
+         return false;
+      nir_alu_type base = nir_alu_type_get_base_type(nir_intrinsic_src_type(intr));
+      b->cursor = nir_before_instr(&intr->instr);
+      nir_def *w = base == nir_type_float ? nir_f2f32(b, intr->src[0].ssa) : base == nir_type_int ? nir_i2i32(b, intr->src[0].ssa) : nir_u2u32(b, intr->src[0].ssa);
+      nir_src_rewrite(&intr->src[0], w);
+      nir_intrinsic_set_src_type(intr, (nir_alu_type)(base | 32));
+      return true;
+   }
+   if (load) {
+      if (intr->def.bit_size != 16)
+         return false;
+      nir_alu_type base = nir_alu_type_get_base_type(nir_intrinsic_dest_type(intr));
+      nir_intrinsic_instr *wide = nir_instr_as_intrinsic(nir_instr_clone(b->shader, &intr->instr));
+      wide->def.bit_size = 32;
+      nir_intrinsic_set_dest_type(wide, (nir_alu_type)(base | 32));
+      b->cursor = nir_before_instr(&intr->instr);
+      nir_builder_instr_insert(b, &wide->instr);
+      nir_def *n = base == nir_type_float ? nir_f2f16(b, &wide->def) : nir_u2u16(b, &wide->def);
+      nir_def_rewrite_uses(&intr->def, n);
+      nir_instr_remove(&intr->instr);
+      return true;
+   }
+   return false;
+}
+
+/* src/compiler.cpp: lowerHalfDerivative */
+static bool
+lower_half_derivatives(nir_builder *b, nir_intrinsic_instr *intr, void *data)
+{
+   switch (intr->intrinsic) {
+   case nir_intrinsic_ddx: case nir_intrinsic_ddx_fine: case nir_intrinsic_ddx_coarse:
+   case nir_intrinsic_ddy: case nir_intrinsic_ddy_fine: case nir_intrinsic_ddy_coarse:
+      break;
+   default:
+      return false;
+   }
+   if (intr->def.bit_size != 16)
+      return false;
+   b->cursor = nir_before_instr(&intr->instr);
+   nir_def *wide = nir_f2f32(b, intr->src[0].ssa);
+   nir_intrinsic_instr *d = nir_intrinsic_instr_create(b->shader, intr->intrinsic);
+   d->num_components = intr->num_components;
+   d->src[0] = nir_src_for_ssa(wide);
+   nir_def_init(&d->instr, &d->def, intr->num_components, 32);
+   nir_builder_instr_insert(b, &d->instr);
+   nir_def_rewrite_uses(&intr->def, nir_f2f16(b, &d->def));
+   nir_instr_remove(&intr->instr);
+   return true;
+}
+
+static bool
+lower_point_coord(nir_builder *b, nir_intrinsic_instr *intr, void *data)
+{
+   (void)data;
+   if (intr->intrinsic != nir_intrinsic_load_point_coord)
+      return false;
+   nir_variable *pc = nir_find_variable_with_location(b->shader, nir_var_shader_in, VARYING_SLOT_PNTC);
+   if (!pc)
+      pc = nir_create_variable_with_location(b->shader, nir_var_shader_in, VARYING_SLOT_PNTC, glsl_vec_type(2));
+   b->cursor = nir_before_instr(&intr->instr);
+   nir_def_rewrite_uses(&intr->def, nir_load_var(b, pc));
+   nir_instr_remove(&intr->instr);
+   return true;
+}
+
+static void
+fixture_lower_fb_read(nir_shader *nir, struct fixture_textures *t)
+{
+   if (nir->info.stage != MESA_SHADER_FRAGMENT || !nir->info.fs.uses_fbfetch_output)
+      return;
+   struct fixture_fb_counts own = { 0 };
+   nir_shader_intrinsics_pass(nir, fixture_count_layer_sample, nir_metadata_all, &own);
+   nir_lower_fb_read(nir);
+   nir_shader_intrinsics_pass(nir, fixture_zero_layer_sample, nir_metadata_control_flow, &own);
+   /* a target's slot: the lowest the function does not sample, in the order the targets are first read (not one past
+    * the highest sampled: the null texture sits high, and a target beside it would need a 17th) */
+   int slot_of[FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS];
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS; i++)
+      slot_of[i] = -1;
+   unsigned next_free = 0;
+   nir_foreach_function_impl (impl, nir) {
+      nir_builder b = nir_builder_create(impl);
+      nir_foreach_block (block, impl) {
+         nir_foreach_instr_safe (instr, block) {
+            if (instr->type != nir_instr_type_tex)
+               continue;
+            nir_tex_instr *fb = nir_instr_as_tex(instr);
+            if (fb->op != nir_texop_txf_ms_fb)
+               continue;
+            int h = nir_tex_instr_src_index(fb, nir_tex_src_texture_handle);
+            int c = nir_tex_instr_src_index(fb, nir_tex_src_coord);
+            unsigned target = h >= 0 && nir_src_is_const(fb->src[h].src) ? nir_src_as_uint(fb->src[h].src) : 0;
+            if (target >= FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS || c < 0)
+               errx(1, "-o: a framebuffer fetch of target %u, or one without a coordinate", target);
+            if (slot_of[target] < 0) {
+               while (next_free < FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS && BITSET_TEST(nir->info.textures_used, next_free))
+                  next_free++;
+               if (next_free >= FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS)
+                  errx(1, "-o: a framebuffer fetch needs a slot and all of the Kernel's %u are sampled", FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS);
+               slot_of[target] = (int)next_free++;
+            }
+            unsigned slot = (unsigned)slot_of[target];
+            b.cursor = nir_before_instr(instr);
+            nir_tex_instr *tx = nir_tex_instr_create(nir, 2);
+            tx->op = nir_texop_txf;
+            tx->sampler_dim = GLSL_SAMPLER_DIM_2D;
+            tx->coord_components = 2;
+            tx->dest_type = nir_type_float32;
+            tx->texture_index = slot;
+            tx->sampler_index = 0;
+            tx->src[0] = nir_tex_src_for_ssa(nir_tex_src_coord, nir_trim_vector(&b, fb->src[c].src.ssa, 2));
+            tx->src[1] = nir_tex_src_for_ssa(nir_tex_src_lod, nir_imm_int(&b, 0));
+            nir_def_init(&tx->instr, &tx->def, 4, 32);
+            nir_builder_instr_insert(&b, &tx->instr);
+            nir_def_rewrite_uses(&fb->def, &tx->def);
+            nir_instr_remove(instr);
+            BITSET_SET(nir->info.textures_used, slot);
+            fixture_fb_lowered = true;
+            if (t) {
+               struct fixture_texture *s = &t->slot[slot];
+               memset(s, 0, sizeof(*s));
+               s->kind = 1;      /* sampled */
+               s->dim = 2;       /* kTexDim2D */
+               s->element = 0;   /* float */
+               s->read = 1;
+               s->fb_target = target + 1;
+               if (slot + 1 > t->num_slots)
+                  t->num_slots = slot + 1;
+            }
+         }
+      }
+      nir_metadata_preserve(impl, nir_metadata_control_flow);
+   }
+}
+
+/* -o for a vertex or fragment stage: the class of each output's declared type,
+ * read off the NIR's shader_out variables before nir_lower_io, because ir3's
+ * outputs[] knows a register and a slot and not whether the shader meant the
+ * bits as a float or as an integer -- which is what a colour target's format
+ * must agree with (render.hpp: StageOutput). The front end types a float or
+ * half output as a float vector and EVERY integer output as GLSL_TYPE_INT
+ * (air_to_nir.c make_io_var: uint4 and int4 are both <4 x i32> in LLVM and it
+ * does not read air.arg_type_name for outputs), so the classes here are float
+ * (0, kElemFloat) and integer (1, kElemUint: the class of the Uint formats, the
+ * only integer formats served); a signed format would need the type name.
+ * Indexed by the output's location: gl_varying_slot for a VS, gl_frag_result
+ * for an FS, both below 64 + 32.
+ */
+#define FIXTURE_OUTPUT_LOCATIONS 96
+
+struct fixture_output_classes {
+   uint8_t class[FIXTURE_OUTPUT_LOCATIONS];
+   bool known[FIXTURE_OUTPUT_LOCATIONS];
+};
+
+static void
+walk_output_classes(nir_shader *nir, struct fixture_output_classes *oc)
+{
+   memset(oc, 0, sizeof(*oc));
+   if (nir->info.stage != MESA_SHADER_VERTEX && nir->info.stage != MESA_SHADER_FRAGMENT)
+      return;
+   nir_foreach_shader_out_variable(var, nir) {
+      unsigned loc = var->data.location;
+      if (loc >= FIXTURE_OUTPUT_LOCATIONS)
+         errx(1, "-o: an output at location %u, past the %u the fixture indexes", loc,
+              FIXTURE_OUTPUT_LOCATIONS);
+      const struct glsl_type *t = glsl_without_array(var->type);
+      oc->class[loc] = glsl_type_is_float_16_32_64(t) ? 0 : 1;
+      oc->known[loc] = true;
+   }
+}
+
+/* The Kernel's fields, as the initializer of a `constexpr Kernel` or of the
+ * `.k` of a `constexpr Stage` (render.hpp), one line each with the field's
+ * name beside its value, INDENT spaces in. The compute-only fields of a
+ * vertex or fragment stage (localSize, localIdRegid, workGroupIdRegid, bufs,
+ * numwgConstRegid) come out at their zeros / 0xfc / 0xff from the same code,
+ * which is what render.hpp says a Stage's Kernel holds there.
+ */
+static void
+emit_kernel_fields(FILE *out, const char *indent, struct ir3_shader_variant *v,
+                   const char *name, uint32_t num_words, const char *words_name,
+                   const char *imm_name, const void *source, size_t source_size,
+                   const struct fixture_textures *tex)
+{
+   const struct ir3_const_state *cs = ir3_const_state(v);
+   const unsigned max_ubo_ranges = 32;  /* kernel.hpp's kMaxUboRanges */
+   const unsigned max_bufs = 4;         /* kMaxBufs */
+   const unsigned no_const_regid = 0xff;
+   uint32_t local_id = ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_LOCAL_INVOCATION_ID);
+   uint32_t wg_id = ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_WORKGROUP_ID);
+   int32_t driver_params =
+      ir3_const_can_upload(&cs->allocs, IR3_CONST_ALLOC_DRIVER_PARAMS, v->constlen)
+         ? (int32_t)cs->allocs.consts[IR3_CONST_ALLOC_DRIVER_PARAMS].offset_vec4
+         : -1;
+
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .words = */ %s,\n", indent, words_name);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numWords = */ %u,\n", indent, num_words);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .instrlen = */ %u,\n", indent, v->instrlen);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .constlen = */ %u,\n", indent, v->constlen);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .maxReg = */ %d,\n", indent, v->info.max_reg);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .maxHalfReg = */ %d,\n", indent, v->info.max_half_reg);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .doubleThreadsize = */ %s,\n", indent, v->info.double_threadsize ? "true" : "false");
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .mergedRegs = */ %s,\n", indent, v->mergedregs ? "true" : "false");
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .earlyPreamble = */ %s,\n", indent, v->early_preamble ? "true" : "false");
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .branchstackHw = */ %u,\n", indent, ir3_shader_branchstack_hw(v));
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .sharedSize = */ %u,\n", indent, v->shared_size);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .pvtmemSize = */ %u,\n", indent, v->pvtmem_size);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .pvtmemPerWave = */ %s,\n", indent, v->pvtmem_per_wave ? "true" : "false");
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .localSize = */ {%u, %u, %u},\n", indent, v->local_size[0], v->local_size[1],
+           v->local_size[2]);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .localSizeVariable = */ %s,\n", indent, v->local_size_variable ? "true" : "false");
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .localIdRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", indent, local_id);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .workGroupIdRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", indent, wg_id);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .immediates = */ %s,\n", indent, cs->immediates_count ? imm_name : "nullptr");
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numImmediates = */ %u,\n", indent, cs->immediates_count);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .immediatesOffsetVec4 = */ %u,\n", indent, cs->allocs.max_const_offset_vec4);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .driverParamsOffsetVec4 = */ %d,\n", indent, driver_params);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numUbos = */ %u,\n", indent, cs->num_ubos);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numSsbos = */ %u,\n", indent, v->num_ssbos);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numIbos = */ %u,\n", indent, v->num_ibos);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numSamp = */ %d,\n", indent, v->num_samp);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .uboRanges = */ {", indent);
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < max_ubo_ranges; i++) {
+      if (i < cs->ubo_state.num_enabled) {
+         const struct ir3_ubo_range *r = &cs->ubo_state.range[i];
+         fprintf(out, "%s{%u, %u, %u, %u}", i ? ", " : "", r->ubo.block, r->offset / 16,
+                 r->start / 4, (r->end - r->start) / 4);
+      } else {
+         fprintf(out, "%s{0, 0, 0, 0}", i ? ", " : "");
+      }
+   }
+   fputs("},\n", out);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numUboRanges = */ %u,\n", indent, cs->ubo_state.num_enabled);
+   /* @buf and @numwg are the text assembler's; a compiled kernel binds its
+    * buffers as SSBOs/UBOs and reads its grid from the driver params.
+    */
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numBufs = */ 0,\n", indent);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .bufs = */ {", indent);
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < max_bufs; i++)
+      fprintf(out, "%s{0, 0x%02x}", i ? ", " : "", no_const_regid);
+   fputs("},\n", out);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numwgConstRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", indent, no_const_regid);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .constantDataOffset = */ %u,\n", indent, v->info.constant_data_offset);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .constantDataSize = */ %u,\n", indent, v->constant_data_size);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .name = */ \"%s\",\n", indent, name);
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .source = */ R\"ir3(%.*s)ir3\",\n", indent, (int)source_size,
+           source ? (const char *)source : "");
+   /* The texture slots: `{}` when the kernel addresses none (the text kernels'
+    * form, tools/ir3-kernel.cc), else every slot up to the highest addressed,
+    * all eight members of each (the pad too) so that -Wextra sees them
+    * initialized, with what each is in words beside it.
+    */
+   unsigned last_slot = 0;
+   bool any_slot = false;
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < FIXTURE_TEXTURE_SLOTS; i++) {
+      if (tex->slot[i].kind) {
+         any_slot = true;
+         last_slot = i;
+      }
+   }
+   if (!any_slot) {
+      fprintf(out, "%s/* .textures = */ {},\n", indent);
+   } else {
+      static const char *const dims[] = { "?", "1D", "2D", "3D", "cube" };
+      static const char *const elements[] = { "float", "uint", "int" };
+      fprintf(out, "%s/* .textures = */ {\n", indent);
+      for (unsigned i = 0; i <= last_slot; i++) {
+         const struct fixture_texture *s = &tex->slot[i];
+         fprintf(out, "%s    /* [%u] */ {%u, %u, %u, %u, %u, %u, %u, %u, %u},", indent, i, s->kind, s->dim,
+                 s->is_array, s->element, s->bits, s->read, s->write, s->is_null, s->fb_target);
+         if (!s->kind)
+            fputs("   // not addressed\n", out);
+         else
+            fprintf(out, "   // %s %s%s of %s%s%s%s\n", s->kind == 1 ? "sampled" : "image",
+                    dims[s->dim], s->is_array ? " array" : "", elements[s->element],
+                    s->bits == 16 ? " as 16-bit" : s->bits ? " as 32-bit" : "",
+                    s->read ? ", read" : "", s->write ? ", written" : "");
+         if (s->is_null)
+            fprintf(out, "%s              // ...the null texture's slot\n", indent);
+         if (s->fb_target)
+            fprintf(out, "%s              // ...framebuffer fetch of colour attachment %u\n", indent, s->fb_target - 1u);
+      }
+      fprintf(out, "%s},\n", indent);
+   }
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .numTextureSlots = */ %u,\n", indent, tex->num_slots);
+   if (tex->sampler_mask)
+      fprintf(out, "%s/* .samplerMask = */ 0x%x,\n", indent, tex->sampler_mask);
+   else
+      fprintf(out, "%s/* .samplerMask = */ 0,\n", indent);
+   /* the UBO ir3 reads the constant data through (consts_ubo), plus one: 0 is none, and so is a fixture written before
+    * the field was (kernel.hpp: Kernel::constantDataUbo) */
+   fprintf(out, "%s/* .constantDataUbo = */ %d,\n", indent,
+           ir3_const_state(v)->consts_ubo.idx >= 0 ? ir3_const_state(v)->consts_ubo.idx + 1 : 0);
+}
+
+/* r<n>.<c> for a comment, or "none" for regid(63, 0) */
+static const char *
+regid_name(uint32_t r, char *buf, size_t size)
+{
+   if (r == regid(63, 0))
+      return "none";
+   snprintf(buf, size, "%sr%u.%c", (r & HALF_REG_ID) ? "h" : "", (r & 0xff) >> 2, "xyzw"[r & 3]);
+   return buf;
+}
+
+/* -o for a VERTEX or FRAGMENT variant: the fields of render.hpp's Stage after
+ * its Kernel, in the struct's order, each with a comment, from the variant the
+ * way turnip and fd6 read them (the field comments in render.hpp name the
+ * register each feeds). The same semantics live in hakios-metal's compileStage
+ * (src/compiler.cpp), and compiler_test holds the two to each other field for
+ * field, so a rule changed here is changed there. Slot namespaces differ by
+ * stage -- VARYING_SLOT_POS and FRAG_RESULT_DEPTH are both 0, PSIZ and
+ * STENCIL both 1 -- so the vertex-only fields are read from a VS only and the
+ * fragment-only ones from an FS only; a sysval lookup (ir3_find_sysval_regid
+ * filters on the sysval bit, gl_system_value numbering) is the same for both.
+ */
+static void
+emit_stage_fields(FILE *out, struct ir3_shader_variant *v,
+                  const struct fixture_output_classes *oc)
+{
+   const bool vs = v->type == MESA_SHADER_VERTEX;
+   const unsigned max_inputs = 34;     /* render.hpp's kMaxStageInputs = ir3's inputs[32 + 2] */
+   const unsigned max_outputs = 32;    /* kMaxStageOutputs */
+   const unsigned max_colors = 8;      /* kMaxColorOutputs */
+   const unsigned ij_count = 7;        /* kIjCount = ir3's IJ_COUNT */
+   const uint32_t none = regid(63, 0);
+   char rb[16];
+
+   if (v->inputs_count > max_inputs)
+      errx(1, "-o: %u inputs, the Stage holds %u", v->inputs_count, max_inputs);
+   if (v->outputs_count > max_outputs)
+      errx(1, "-o: %u outputs, the Stage holds %u", v->outputs_count, max_outputs);
+
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .kind = */ %u,   // %s\n", vs ? 0 : 1, vs ? "kStageVertex" : "kStageFragment");
+   fputs("    /* .pad0 = */ {0, 0, 0},\n", out);
+
+   /* inputs[]: {slot, regid, compmask, inloc, sysval, bary, flat, half} */
+   if (!v->inputs_count) {
+      fputs("    /* .inputs = */ {},\n", out);
+   } else {
+      fputs("    /* .inputs = */ {\n", out);
+      for (unsigned i = 0; i < v->inputs_count; i++) {
+         const __typeof__(v->inputs[0]) *in = &v->inputs[i];
+         const char *slot_name = in->sysval ? gl_system_value_name(in->slot)
+                                 : vs ? gl_vert_attrib_name(in->slot)
+                                      : gl_varying_slot_name_for_stage(in->slot, v->type);
+         fprintf(out, "        /* [%u] */ {%u, 0x%02x, 0x%x, %u, %u, %u, %u, %u},   // %s %s cm=%x il=%u%s%s%s%s\n",
+                 i, in->slot, in->regid, in->compmask, in->inloc, in->sysval, in->bary, in->flat,
+                 in->half, slot_name, regid_name(in->regid, rb, sizeof(rb)), in->compmask, in->inloc,
+                 in->sysval ? " sysval" : "", in->bary ? " bary" : "", in->flat ? " flat" : "",
+                 in->half ? " half" : "");
+      }
+      fputs("    },\n", out);
+   }
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .numInputs = */ %u,\n", v->inputs_count);
+
+   /* outputs[]: {slot, regid, half, pad}; pad carries the output's declared
+    * class (0 float, 1 integer: walk_output_classes) until render.hpp names
+    * the field -- it is what a colour target's format is judged against.
+    */
+   if (!v->outputs_count) {
+      fputs("    /* .outputs = */ {},\n", out);
+   } else {
+      fputs("    /* .outputs = */ {\n", out);
+      for (unsigned i = 0; i < v->outputs_count; i++) {
+         const struct ir3_shader_output *o = &v->outputs[i];
+         const char *slot_name = vs ? gl_varying_slot_name_for_stage(o->slot, v->type)
+                                    : gl_frag_result_name(o->slot);
+         unsigned class = o->slot < FIXTURE_OUTPUT_LOCATIONS && oc->known[o->slot] ? oc->class[o->slot] : 0;
+         fprintf(out, "        /* [%u] */ {%u, 0x%02x, %u, %u},   // %s %s%s, %s\n", i, o->slot,
+                 o->regid, o->half, class, slot_name, regid_name(o->regid, rb, sizeof(rb)),
+                 o->half ? " half" : "", class ? "integer" : "float");
+      }
+      fputs("    },\n", out);
+   }
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .numOutputs = */ %u,\n", v->outputs_count);
+
+   /* --- a vertex stage --- */
+   unsigned num_attributes = 0;
+   bool writes_layer = false, writes_viewport = false;
+   uint32_t position = none, point_size = none;
+   if (vs) {
+      for (unsigned i = 0; i < v->inputs_count; i++)
+         if (!v->inputs[i].sysval && v->inputs[i].regid != none)
+            num_attributes++;
+      position = ir3_find_output_regid(v, VARYING_SLOT_POS);
+      point_size = ir3_find_output_regid(v, VARYING_SLOT_PSIZ);
+      writes_layer = ir3_find_output(v, VARYING_SLOT_LAYER) >= 0;
+      writes_viewport = ir3_find_output(v, VARYING_SLOT_VIEWPORT) >= 0;
+   }
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .numAttributes = */ %u,\n", num_attributes);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .vertexIdRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_VERTEX_ID));
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .instanceIdRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_INSTANCE_ID));
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .positionRegid = */ 0x%02x,   // %s\n", position, regid_name(position, rb, sizeof(rb)));
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .pointSizeRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", point_size);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .clipMask = */ 0x%x, /* .cullMask = */ 0x%x, /* .writesLayer = */ %u, /* .writesViewport = */ %u,\n",
+           v->clip_mask, v->cull_mask, writes_layer, writes_viewport);
+
+   /* --- a fragment stage --- */
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .totalIn = */ %u,\n", v->total_in);
+   uint32_t frag_coord = ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_FRAG_COORD);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .fragCoordRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", frag_coord);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .fragcoordCompmask = */ 0x%x,\n", v->fragcoord_compmask);
+   fputs("    /* .pad1 = */ {0, 0, 0},\n", out);
+   fputs("    /* .ijRegid = */ {", out);
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < ij_count; i++)
+      fprintf(out, "%s0x%02x", i ? ", " : "",
+              ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_BARYCENTRIC_PERSP_PIXEL + i));
+   fputs("},   // ir3's IJ order: persp pixel, sample, centroid, centre rhw; linear pixel, centroid, sample\n", out);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .faceRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n", ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_FRONT_FACE));
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .sampleIdRegid = */ 0x%02x, /* .sampleMaskInRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n",
+           ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_SAMPLE_ID),
+           ir3_find_sysval_regid(v, SYSTEM_VALUE_SAMPLE_MASK_IN));
+   uint32_t color[8], color_half[8];
+   unsigned num_colors = 0;
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < max_colors; i++) {
+      color[i] = none;
+      color_half[i] = 0;
+      if (!vs) {
+         int k = ir3_find_output(v, FRAG_RESULT_DATA0 + i);
+         if (k >= 0) {

+            color[i] = v->outputs[k].regid;
+            color_half[i] = v->outputs[k].half;
+            num_colors = i + 1;

+      }
+   }
+   fputs("    /* .colorRegid = */ {", out);
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < max_colors; i++)
+      fprintf(out, "%s0x%02x", i ? ", " : "", color[i]);
+   fputs("},\n", out);
+   fputs("    /* .colorHalf = */ {", out);
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < max_colors; i++)
+      fprintf(out, "%s%u", i ? ", " : "", color_half[i]);
+   fputs("},\n", out);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .numColorOutputs = */ %u,\n", num_colors);
+   uint32_t depth = none, sample_mask = none, stencil_ref = none;
+   if (!vs) {
+      depth = ir3_find_output_regid(v, FRAG_RESULT_DEPTH);
+      sample_mask = ir3_find_output_regid(v, FRAG_RESULT_SAMPLE_MASK);
+      stencil_ref = ir3_find_output_regid(v, FRAG_RESULT_STENCIL);
+   }
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .depthRegid = */ 0x%02x, /* .sampleMaskRegid = */ 0x%02x, /* .stencilRefRegid = */ 0x%02x,\n",
+           depth, sample_mask, stencil_ref);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .writesPos = */ %u, /* .writesSmask = */ %u, /* .writesStencilref = */ %u, /* .dualSrcBlend = */ %u,\n",
+           v->writes_pos, v->writes_smask, v->writes_stencilref, v->dual_src_blend);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .hasKill = */ %u, /* .perSamp = */ %u, /* .readsPrimid = */ %u, /* .fbRead = */ %u,\n",
+           v->has_kill, v->per_samp, v->reads_primid, v->fb_read || fixture_fb_lowered);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .needPixlod = */ %u, /* .needFullQuad = */ %u,\n", v->need_pixlod, v->need_full_quad);
+   fputs("    /* .pad2 = */ {0, 0},\n", out);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .numSamplerPrefetch = */ %u,\n", v->num_sampler_prefetch);
+   fputs("    /* .prefetch = */ {\n", out);

+      bool used = i < v->num_sampler_prefetch;
+      fprintf(out, "        /* [%u] */ {0x%02x, %u, %u, 0x%02x, 0x%x, %u, %u, %u},%s\n", i, used ? p->src : 0, used ? p->samp_id : 0,
+              used ? p->tex_id : 0, used ? p->dst : 0, used ? p->wrmask : 0, used ? p->half_precision : 0,
+              used && p->tex_opc == OPC_SAM ? 1 : 0, used ? p->bindless : 0, used ? "   // src, samp, tex, dst, wrmask, half, cmd, bindless" : "");
+   }
+   fputs("    },\n", out);
+   fprintf(out, "    /* .prefetchEndOfQuad = */ %u,\n", v->prefetch_end_of_quad);
+   fputs("    /* .pad3 = */ {0, 0, 0},\n", out);

+static void
+dump_fixture(struct ir3_shader_variant *v, uint32_t *bin, const char *path,
+             const char *in_path, const char *source_path,
+             const char *kernel_name, const struct fd_dev_id *dev_id,
+             const struct fixture_textures *tex,
+             const struct fixture_output_classes *output_classes)
+{
+   const struct ir3_const_state *cs = ir3_const_state(v);
+   const struct fd_dev_info *dev_info = fd_dev_info_raw(dev_id);
+   const unsigned max_ubo_ranges = 32;  /* kernel.hpp's kMaxUboRanges */
+
+   /* What the fixture is: a Kernel for a compute variant, a Stage (render.hpp:
+    * a Kernel plus what the 3D registers read) for a vertex or fragment one.
+    * The other stages have no struct here: refused by name, not written as a
+    * compute-shaped Kernel, which is what this did for a VS until 29 October.
+    */
+   bool stage_fixture;
+   switch (v->type) {
+   case MESA_SHADER_COMPUTE:
+   case MESA_SHADER_KERNEL:
+      stage_fixture = false;
+      break;
+   case MESA_SHADER_VERTEX:
+   case MESA_SHADER_FRAGMENT:
+      stage_fixture = true;
+      break;
+   default:
+      errx(1, "-o: a %s shader: the fixtures hold a compute Kernel or a vertex/fragment Stage, nothing else",
+           gl_shader_stage_name(v->type));
+   }
+
+   /* The kernel's name: -n, else the entry point's (nir->info.name); made an identifier. */
+   char name[128];
+   const char *nir_name = kernel_name ? kernel_name : "kernel";
+   unsigned n = 0;
+   for (const char *c = nir_name; *c && n + 1 < sizeof(name); c++)
+      name[n++] = isalnum((unsigned char)*c) ? *c : '_';
+   name[n] = 0;
+   if (!n || isdigit((unsigned char)name[0]))
+      errx(1, "-o: cannot name the kernel after \"%s\"", nir_name);
+
+   /* The kernel text, when given (-s): the .ll of an AIR kernel, for the record. */
+   void *source = NULL;
+   size_t source_size = 0;
+   if (source_path && read_file(source_path, &source, &source_size))
+      errx(1, "-s %s: cannot read it", source_path);
+
+   if (cs->ubo_state.num_enabled > max_ubo_ranges)
+      errx(1, "-o: %u UBO ranges, the Kernel struct holds %u",
+           cs->ubo_state.num_enabled, max_ubo_ranges);
+
+   char *listing = NULL;
+   size_t listing_size = 0;
+   FILE *ls = open_memstream(&listing, &listing_size);
+   ir3_shader_disasm(v, bin, ls);
+   fclose(ls);
+
+   FILE *out = fopen(path, "w");
+   if (!out)
+      errx(1, "%s: cannot write it", path);
+
+   uint32_t num_words = v->info.size / 4;
+
+   fprintf(out,
+           "// %s: hakios::metal::%s fixture, generated by ir3_compiler -o (tools/mesa/ir3-dump.patch)\n"
+           "// from %s for %s (chip id 0x%" PRIx64 ", gen %u). Do not edit; recompile the %s.\n"
+           "// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n"
+           "#pragma once\n\n"
+           "#include \"hakios-metal/%s.hpp\"\n\n"
+           "namespace hakios::metal::kernels {\n\n",
+           name, stage_fixture ? "Stage" : "Kernel", in_path, fd_dev_name(dev_id), dev_id->chip_id,
+           dev_info->chip, stage_fixture ? "shader" : "kernel", stage_fixture ? "render" : "kernel");
+
+   char words_name[160], imm_name[160];
+   snprintf(words_name, sizeof(words_name), "%s_words", name);
+   snprintf(imm_name, sizeof(imm_name), "%s_immediates", name);
+   emit_words(out, words_name, bin, num_words);
+   fputc('\n', out);
+   if (cs->immediates_count) {
+      emit_words(out, imm_name, cs->immediates, cs->immediates_count);
+      fputc('\n', out);
+   }
+
+   if (!stage_fixture) {
+      fprintf(out, "constexpr Kernel %s = {\n", name);
+      emit_kernel_fields(out, "    ", v, name, num_words, words_name, imm_name, source, source_size, tex);
+   } else {
+      fprintf(out, "constexpr Stage %s = {\n", name);
+      fputs("    /* .k = */ {\n", out);
+      emit_kernel_fields(out, "        ", v, name, num_words, words_name, imm_name, source, source_size, tex);
+      fputs("    },\n", out);
+      emit_stage_fields(out, v, output_classes);
+   }
+   fputs("};\n\n", out);
+
+   fputs("// The listing (ir3_shader_disasm):\n", out);
+   emit_comment_block(out, listing);
+   fputs("\n} // namespace hakios::metal::kernels\n", out);
+   fclose(out);
+   free(listing);
+   printf("wrote %s\n", path);
+}
```

```cpp
// hakios-metal-probe: the driver's core on the phone's real GPU. What the tests check against the fake GPU, done by
// the Adreno: a copy of a megabyte, fills of every awkward length, a chain of command buffers whose handlers must run
// in order, how fast a copy goes, kernels of our own over buffers and then over textures (an image written through the
// IBO table, a texture read through the texture table, a sampler), each result compared with the kernel's own rule;
// then the first draw (stage 9): one triangle, the pair, per-vertex colours, into a 64x64 target, each pixel against
// the rule the probe computes from the shaders' text.
// One line per check, "probe: ok ..." or "probe: FAIL ...", and a last line with the count; the exit status is the
// number of failures. Run it from a job list (hakios: RC_JOBS, EXTRA=).
#include <algorithm>

using namespace hakios::metal;

static int failures = 0;

static void report(bool ok, const std::string& what) {
    std::printf("probe: %s %s\n", ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL", what.c_str());
    std::fflush(stdout);
    failures += !ok;
}

// fill_id's answer for one invocation: gid * K + c, modulo 2^32 (K odd: no two invocations write the same word)
static uint32_t expectedWord(uint32_t gid, uint32_t c) { return gid * 0x9E3779B1u + c; }

// A value no invocation of a grid of WORDS can write with this C, so that a word still holding it was not written: a
// dispatch that did not run then reads as "did not run" and not as a result. (Checked, not assumed: K is a bijection,
// so the candidate collides with exactly one gid of all 2^32, and that gid may be inside the grid.)
static uint32_t canaryFor(uint32_t words, uint32_t c) {
    uint32_t canary = 0xa5a5a5a5u;
    for (;;) {
        bool clash = false;
        for (uint32_t gid = 0; gid < words && !clash; gid++) clash = expectedWord(gid, c) == canary;
        if (!clash) return canary;
        canary += 0x01010101u;
    }
}

// What a buffer holds after a dispatch, against the kernel's answer for WRITTEN words and the canary beyond them
// tools/kernels/gen-long-chain.py's chain on the processor: STEPS steps of v = rotl((v ^ X) * M, R) from gid ^ c
uint32_t long_chain_reference(uint32_t gid, uint32_t c, unsigned steps) {
    uint32_t v = gid ^ c;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < steps; i++) {
        const uint32_t x = 0x9E3779B1u * (i + 1);
        const uint32_t m = x | 1, r = 5 + i % 23;
        const uint32_t b = (v ^ (x ^ 0x5BD1E995u)) * m;
        v = (b << r) | (b >> (32 - r));
    }
    return v;
}

struct Readback {
    uint32_t right = 0, canary = 0, wrong = 0;   // of the WRITTEN words
    uint32_t beyondCanary = 0, beyondOther = 0;  // of the words after them
    uint32_t firstWrongAt = 0, firstWrongValue = 0;
};

static Readback readBack(const Buffer& b, uint32_t written, uint32_t c, uint32_t canaryValue) {
    std::vector<uint32_t> back(b.length() / 4);
    memcpy(back.data(), b.contents(), b.length());   // one read of the write-combined memory, in order
    Readback r;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < back.size(); i++) {
        if (i < written) {
            if (back[i] == expectedWord(i, c)) {
                r.right++;
            } else if (back[i] == canaryValue) {
                r.canary++;
            } else {
                if (r.wrong == 0) {
                    r.firstWrongAt = i;
                    r.firstWrongValue = back[i];
                }
                r.wrong++;
            }
        } else {
            (back[i] == canaryValue ? r.beyondCanary : r.beyondOther)++;
        }
    }
    return r;
}

static std::string describe(const Readback& r, uint32_t written, uint32_t beyond) {
    char text[200];
    snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%u of %u words as the kernel computes them, %u still canary, %u wrong%s; beyond them %u of %u canary", r.right,
             written, r.canary, r.wrong, r.wrong ? (" (first at " + std::to_string(r.firstWrongAt) + ": 0x" + [&] {
                                                        char h[12];
                                                        snprintf(h, sizeof h, "%08x", r.firstWrongValue);
                                                        return std::string(h);
                                                    }() + ")")
                                                           .c_str()
                                                     : "",
             r.beyondCanary, beyond);
    return text;
}

static std::string status(const CommandBuffer& cb, Gpu& gpu) {
    return (cb.error().empty() ? "" : " (" + cb.error() + ")") + ", " + std::to_string(cb.gpuNanoseconds() / 1000) + " us, FAULTS " +
           std::to_string(gpu.faults());
}

static std::string hex8(uint32_t v) {
    char h[12];
    snprintf(h, sizeof h, "0x%08x", v);
    return h;
}
static std::string hex2(uint8_t v) {
    char h[4];
    snprintf(h, sizeof h, "%02x", v);
    return h;
}

// FNV-1a over bytes: the hash the --metallib lines print per buffer and per texture, so that a host reference running
// the same kernel over the same canary-filled memory can print the same line and the two logs diff
static uint64_t fnv1a(const void* data, size_t bytes) {
    const auto* p = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(data);
    uint64_t hash = 0xcbf29ce484222325ull;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < bytes; i++) {
        hash ^= p[i];
        hash *= 0x100000001b3ull;
    }
    return hash;
}

// --- textures ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
