```cpp
    // (hakios's kernelref.py has no texture path); that is the next instrument, not this one.
    for (const auto& [path, function] : metallibs) {
        std::string what = function + " of " + path;
        if (!hasCompiler()) {
            report(false, what + ": no compiler in this build (MESA=1)");
            continue;
        }
        std::vector<uint8_t> file;
        {
            FILE* f = fopen(path.c_str(), "rb");
            if (f == nullptr) {
                report(false, what + ": cannot open the file");
                continue;
            }
            uint8_t chunk[65536];
            size_t n;
            while ((n = fread(chunk, 1, sizeof chunk, f)) > 0) file.insert(file.end(), chunk, chunk + n);
            fclose(f);
        }
        MetalLibrary lib;
        if (!lib.parse(file.data(), file.size())) {
            report(false, what + ": " + lib.why());
            continue;
        }
        const MetalFunction* fn = lib.find(function);
        const uint8_t* bitcode = nullptr;
        uint64_t length = 0;
        if (fn == nullptr || !lib.bitcode(*fn, &bitcode, &length)) {
            report(false, what + ": no such function in its " + std::to_string(lib.functions().size()));
            continue;
        }
        std::string why3;
        auto k = compileAir(bitcode, size_t(length), &why3);
        if (k == nullptr) {
            report(false, "compile " + what + ": " + why3);
            continue;
        }
        uint32_t deviceBuffers = 0, constantBuffers = 0, textures = 0, images = 0, samplers = 0, threadgroupBuffers = 0;
        uint32_t highest = 0, highestTexture = 0, highestSampler = 0;
        for (const Resource& r : k->resources) {
            if (r.kind == Resource::kDeviceBuffer) deviceBuffers++;
            else if (r.kind == Resource::kConstantBuffer) constantBuffers++;
            else if (r.kind == Resource::kTexture) textures++;
            else if (r.kind == Resource::kImage) images++;
            else if (r.kind == Resource::kSampler) samplers++;
            else threadgroupBuffers++;
            if (r.kind == Resource::kDeviceBuffer || r.kind == Resource::kConstantBuffer) highest = std::max(highest, r.index);
            if (r.kind == Resource::kTexture || r.kind == Resource::kImage) highestTexture = std::max(highestTexture, r.index);
            if (r.kind == Resource::kSampler) highestSampler = std::max(highestSampler, r.index);
        }
        report(true, "compile " + what + ": " + std::to_string(k->kernel.numWords) + " words, instrlen " + std::to_string(k->kernel.instrlen) +
                         ", constlen " + std::to_string(k->kernel.constlen) + ", " + std::to_string(deviceBuffers) + " device and " +
                         std::to_string(constantBuffers) + " constant buffers, " + std::to_string(textures) + " textures, " + std::to_string(images) +
                         " images, " + std::to_string(samplers) + " samplers, " + std::to_string(threadgroupBuffers) + " threadgroup buffers, " +
                         std::to_string(k->threadgroupBytes) + " bytes of threadgroup memory" +
                         (k->kernel.localSizeVariable ? "" : ", a fixed threadgroup"));
        if (threadgroupBuffers != 0) {
            report(false, what + ": binds a threadgroup buffer, which this driver does not serve yet; not dispatched");
            continue;
        }
        // the buffers: a constant one as long as its metadata says (or a page), a device one of a megabyte, every slot
        // up to the highest index bound so that the descriptor table has no hole, all of them canary
        const uint32_t canary = 0xa5a5a5a5u;
        std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Buffer>> owned;
        std::vector<Binding> bindings(highest + 1);
        bool ok = true;
        for (uint32_t index = 0; index <= highest && ok; index++) {
            uint64_t bytes = 4096;
            for (const Resource& r : k->resources) {
                if ((r.kind == Resource::kDeviceBuffer || r.kind == Resource::kConstantBuffer) && r.index == index) {
                    bytes = r.kind == Resource::kDeviceBuffer ? (1u << 20) : std::max<uint64_t>(r.sizeBytes, 4096);
                }
            }
            auto b = newBuffer(gpu, bytes, &why);
            if (b == nullptr) {
                report(false, what + ": a buffer of " + std::to_string(bytes) + " bytes for index " + std::to_string(index) + ": " + why);
                ok = false;
                break;
            }
            auto* w = static_cast<uint32_t*>(b->contents());
            for (uint64_t i = 0; i < bytes / 4; i++) w[i] = canary;
            bindings[index] = Binding{b.get(), 0};
            owned.push_back(b);
        }
        if (!ok) continue;
        // the textures: a canary-filled 64x64 one at each declared texture index, readable and writable, of the element
        // class the kernel's own instructions address it with (Kernel::textures, the core's walk of the NIR, which is
        // what the dispatch checks a binding against): R32Uint for uint, R32Float for float; int has no served format
        // and a dimension other than 2D no served texture, so those are refused here by name. A default sampler at each
        // declared sampler index.
        std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Texture>> ownedTextures;
        std::vector<Sampler> ownedSamplers(samplers ? highestSampler + 1 : 0);
        Bindings all;
        all.buffers = bindings;
        all.textures.assign((textures + images) ? highestTexture + 1 : 0, nullptr);
        all.samplers.assign(ownedSamplers.size(), nullptr);
        for (const Resource& r : k->resources) {
            if (!ok) break;
            if (r.kind == Resource::kTexture || r.kind == Resource::kImage) {
                std::string texture = "texture " + std::to_string(r.index) + " (" + r.typeName + ")";
                if (r.index >= kMaxTextureSlots) {
                    report(false, what + ": " + texture + " is past the Kernel's " + std::to_string(kMaxTextureSlots) + " slots; not dispatched");
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                const KernelTexture& t = k->kernel.textures[r.index];
                if (t.kind != kTexNone && t.dim != kTexDim2D) {
                    report(false, what + ": " + texture + " is addressed as a " + dimName(t.dim) + " texture: only 2D is served; not dispatched");
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                if (t.element == kElemInt) {
                    report(false, what + ": " + texture + " is addressed as int: no served format carries ints; not dispatched");
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                TextureDesc d;
                d.format = t.element == kElemFloat ? PixelFormat::kR32Float : PixelFormat::kR32Uint;
                d.width = d.height = 64;
                d.usage = kTextureUsageRead | kTextureUsageWrite;
                auto tex = Texture::make(gpu, d, &why);
                if (tex == nullptr) {
                    report(false, what + ": a 64x64 texture for index " + std::to_string(r.index) + ": " + why);
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                fillBo(*tex, canary);
                all.textures[r.index] = tex.get();
                ownedTextures.push_back(tex);
            } else if (r.kind == Resource::kSampler) {
                SamplerDesc sd;
                if (r.index >= ownedSamplers.size() || !makeSampler(sd, &ownedSamplers[r.index], &why)) {
                    report(false, what + ": a default sampler for index " + std::to_string(r.index) + ": " + why);
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                all.samplers[r.index] = &ownedSamplers[r.index];
            }
        }
        if (!ok) continue;
        const uint32_t g[3] = {1, 1, 1}, local[3] = {64, 1, 1};
        auto cb = queue->commandBuffer();
        if (!cb->dispatch(k->kernel, g, k->kernel.localSizeVariable ? local : nullptr, all, nullptr, chosen)) {
            report(false, "dispatch " + what + ": " + cb->error());
            continue;
        }
        cb->commit();
        cb->waitUntilCompleted();
        std::string written;
        for (uint32_t index = 0; index <= highest; index++) {
            const Buffer& b = *bindings[index].buffer;
            std::vector<uint32_t> back(b.length() / 4);
            memcpy(back.data(), b.contents(), b.length());
            uint32_t changed = 0, first = 0;
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < back.size(); i++) {
                if (back[i] != canary) {
                    if (changed == 0) first = i;
                    changed++;
                }
            }
            // FNV-1a over the whole buffer, so that a host reference (tools/air/kernelref.py in hakios) running the same
            // kernel through LLVM over the same canary-filled buffers can print the same line and the two be compared
            uint64_t hash = fnv1a(back.data(), back.size() * 4);
            char text[240];
            if (changed == 0) {
                snprintf(text, sizeof text, "; buffer %u: untouched", index);
            } else {
                snprintf(text, sizeof text, "; buffer %u: %u words written from %u on, fnv1a %016llx, the first 0x%08x 0x%08x 0x%08x 0x%08x 0x%08x 0x%08x 0x%08x 0x%08x",
                         index, changed, first, (unsigned long long)hash, back[first], first + 1 < back.size() ? back[first + 1] : 0,
                         first + 2 < back.size() ? back[first + 2] : 0, first + 3 < back.size() ? back[first + 3] : 0,
                         first + 4 < back.size() ? back[first + 4] : 0, first + 5 < back.size() ? back[first + 5] : 0,
                         first + 6 < back.size() ? back[first + 6] : 0, first + 7 < back.size() ? back[first + 7] : 0);
            }
            written += text;
        }
        // per texture: how many of its 64x64 pixels changed, and the hash of its whole Bo -- a reading, not a comparison,
        // until the host reference has a texture path
        for (uint32_t index = 0; index < all.textures.size(); index++) {
            const Texture* t = all.textures[index];
            if (t == nullptr) continue;
            std::vector<uint8_t> bo = textureBo(*t);
            uint32_t changed = 0;
            for (uint32_t y = 0; y < t->height(); y++) {
                for (uint32_t x = 0; x < t->width(); x++) {
                    uint32_t word;
                    memcpy(&word, bo.data() + y * t->bytesPerRow() + uint64_t(x) * 4, 4);
                    changed += word != canary;
                }
            }
            char text[160];
            snprintf(text, sizeof text, "; texture %u (%s 64x64, %s): %u pixels written, fnv1a %016llx", index, t->info().name,
                     k->kernel.textures[index].kind == kTexImage ? "image" : k->kernel.textures[index].kind == kTexSampled ? "sampled" : "not addressed",
                     changed, (unsigned long long)fnv1a(bo.data(), bo.size()));
            written += text;
        }
        report(cb->status() == CommandBuffer::kCompleted,
               "dispatch " + what + ", 1 group of 64: " + (cb->status() == CommandBuffer::kCompleted ? "completed" : "did NOT complete") + written +
                   status(*cb, gpu));
    }

    // 11. (--bisect) end_only under each part of the dispatch stream switched off in turn, and under none of them: when
    // every dispatch hangs (28 October: HLSQ busy, SP idle, the CP through its IB), this says which part the hang needs,
    // one boot for all of it, each hang costing the kernel one reset. A variant that completes is the finding.
    if (bisect) {
        struct Variant {
            const char* name;
            compute::Options o;
        };
        compute::Options minimal;
        minimal.prelude = minimal.invalidateCmd = minimal.hlsqCopies = minimal.pvtmemZero = minimal.invalidate = minimal.marker = minimal.tail = false;
        std::vector<Variant> variants = {{"the whole stream", compute::Options{}}};
        auto without = [&](const char* name, void (*off)(compute::Options&)) {
            compute::Options o;
            off(o);
            variants.push_back(Variant{name, o});
        };
        // 28 October, first round: every variant with the end hung, both without it completed. So the end it is; now its parts.
        without("without the end (RB_DONE_TS, CACHE_FLUSH_TS and their waits)", [](compute::Options& o) { o.tail = false; });
        without("with the end, the TIMESTAMP bit off (computerator's form)", [](compute::Options& o) { o.tailTimestampBit = false; });
        without("with only RB_DONE_TS and its wait", [](compute::Options& o) { o.tailCacheFlush = false; });
        without("with only CACHE_FLUSH_TS and its wait", [](compute::Options& o) { o.tailRbDone = false; });
        without("with only CACHE_FLUSH_TS and its wait, TIMESTAMP bit off", [](compute::Options& o) {
            o.tailRbDone = false;
            o.tailTimestampBit = false;
        });
        without("with only RB_DONE_TS and its wait, TIMESTAMP bit off", [](compute::Options& o) {
            o.tailCacheFlush = false;
            o.tailTimestampBit = false;
        });
        variants.push_back(Variant{"with none of those: the registers, the loads, NDRANGE, CP_EXEC_CS, CP_WAIT_FOR_IDLE", minimal});
        const uint32_t one[3] = {1, 1, 1};
        for (const Variant& v : variants) {
            auto cb = queue->commandBuffer();
            cb->dispatch(kernels::end_only, one, nullptr, std::vector<Binding>{}, nullptr, v.o);
            cb->commit();
            cb->waitUntilCompleted();
            bool ok = cb->status() == CommandBuffer::kCompleted;
            report(ok, std::string("bisect: end_only ") + v.name + ": " + (ok ? "COMPLETED" : "hung") + status(*cb, gpu));
        }
    }

    // 12. (--recover) the GPU is hung on purpose, and the kernel must bring it back. The hang is the measured one:
    // 4 Mi words in one CP_MEMCPY stopped the command processor on 27 October (125 000 took 4.2 ms), and the run and
    // the system with it. With boot-arg gpu_recover=1 the kernel resets the core when a wait of a second or more
    // comes to nothing, FAULTS rises by one, and the next command buffer is the core's own again. This goes last,
    // because without that boot-arg it is the end of the run; the line says which it was.
    if (recover) {
        auto big1 = newBuffer(gpu, 16 * mb, &why), big2 = newBuffer(gpu, 16 * mb, &why);
        if (big1 && big2) {
            memset(b->contents(), 0x33, 4096);
            uint64_t before = gpu.faults();
            pm4::Stream s;
            s.memcpy(big2->gpuAddress(), big1->gpuAddress(), 4u << 20);
            s.waitForIdle();
            int e = 0;
            auto commands = gpu.newBo(4096, kBoGpuReadOnly | kBoWriteCombined, &e);
            memcpy(commands->cpu(), s.words().data(), 4 * s.words().size());
            uint32_t fence = 0;
            int64_t began = gpu.transport().nowNs();
            int sub = gpu.submit(0, *commands, 0, uint32_t(s.words().size()), {BoUse{&big1->bo(), false}, BoUse{&big2->bo(), true}},
                                 &fence);
            int w = sub == 0 ? gpu.wait(0, fence, 2000000000) : -1;   // 2 s: over the kernel's one-second line
            int64_t took = (gpu.transport().nowNs() - began) / 1000000;
            uint64_t after = gpu.faults();
            if (sub != 0) {
                report(false, "hang on purpose: the submission was refused: " + std::string(strerror(sub)));
            } else if (w == 0) {
                report(false, "hang on purpose: 4 Mi words in one CP_MEMCPY COMPLETED in " + std::to_string(took) +
                                  " ms; the 27 October hang did not reproduce, so nothing here tests the recovery");
            } else {
                report(after == before + 1, "hang on purpose: the wait ended with " + std::string(strerror(w)) + " after " +
                                                std::to_string(took) + " ms, FAULTS " + std::to_string(before) + " -> " +
                                                std::to_string(after) +
                                                (after == before + 1 ? " (the kernel reset the GPU)"
                                                 : after == before ? " (NO reset: gpu_recover=1 missing, or recovery failed)"
                                                                   : " (MORE than one reset)"));
            }
            // and after it: a command buffer committed now must run, and its bytes must land
            auto cb = queue->commandBuffer();
            cb->fill(*b, 0, 4096, 0xc3);
            cb->commit();
            cb->waitUntilCompleted();
            std::vector<uint8_t> back(4096);
            memcpy(back.data(), b->contents(), 4096);
            bool ok = cb->status() == CommandBuffer::kCompleted;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < 4096; i++) ok = ok && back[i] == 0xc3;
            report(ok, "after the hang: a fill of 4096 bytes " + std::string(ok ? "ran and landed" : "did NOT land") +
                           (cb->error().empty() ? "" : " (" + cb->error() + ")") + ", FAULTS now " + std::to_string(gpu.faults()));
        } else {
            report(false, "two buffers of 16 MB for the hang: " + why);
        }
    }

    std::printf("probe: %d failure%s\n", failures, failures == 1 ? "" : "s");
    return failures;
}

```

`hakios-metal/tools/sweep.cpp`:

```cpp
// sweep: how much of a metallib's code the driver's compiler takes. Every function of each library named on the
// command line goes through the compiler a draw or a dispatch would use (compileAir for a kernel, compileStage for a
// vertex or fragment function), and the run ends with the counts and the refusals grouped by their sentence, the
// commonest first -- the list of what the front end and the draw do not serve yet, by how often real code meets it.
//
// Each function is compiled in a child process: a front end or ir3 that aborts on one (this host build keeps Mesa's
// assertions; the phone's is release, where the same input fails another way) is then a counted cause with the
// assertion's text, not the end of the sweep.
//
// The libraries are read where they lie (a phone's or an image's /System/Library/...): nothing of them is copied,
// kept or printed but function names, counts and the compiler's own sentences.
//
//   sweep [-v] [-f FUNCTION] [-c INDEX=VALUE]... LIBRARY.metallib...
//     -v: a line per function; -f: that function alone; -c: a function constant's value, as a pipeline supplies
//     it (with IR3_SHADER_DEBUG=disasm the listing of one specialisation is what comes out)
//
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <fstream>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "hakios-metal/compiler.hpp"
#include "hakios-metal/metallib.hpp"

using namespace hakios::metal;

namespace {
// compile in a child: true when it compiled; else *why is the refusal, or "the compiler aborted: " and the last line
// the child printed (Mesa's assertion)
FunctionConstants gConstants;

bool compileApart(bool kernel, const uint8_t* bc, uint64_t len, std::string* why) {
    int fds[2];
    if (pipe(fds) != 0) {
        *why = "no pipe";
        return false;
    }
    std::fflush(stdout);
    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid == 0) {
        close(fds[0]);
        dup2(fds[1], 2);   // the child's assertion text goes up the pipe too
        std::string w;
        bool ok = kernel ? compileAir(bc, len, &w, gConstants) != nullptr : compileStage(bc, len, &w, gConstants) != nullptr;
        std::string msg = std::string(ok ? "OK\n" : "NO\n") + w;
        (void)!write(fds[1], msg.data(), msg.size());
        _exit(0);
    }
    close(fds[1]);
    std::string out;
    char buf[4096];
    ssize_t n;
    while ((n = read(fds[0], buf, sizeof buf)) > 0) out.append(buf, size_t(n));
    close(fds[0]);
    int status = 0;
    waitpid(pid, &status, 0);
    if (WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 0 && out.rfind("OK\n", 0) == 0) return true;
    if (WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 0 && out.rfind("NO\n", 0) == 0) {
        *why = out.substr(3);
        return false;
    }
    // aborted: keep the assertion's line (the last line holding "Assertion" or "error", else the last one)
    std::string last;
    size_t at = 0;
    while (at < out.size()) {
        size_t e = out.find('\n', at);
        std::string line = out.substr(at, e == std::string::npos ? std::string::npos : e - at);
        if (line.find("Assertion") != std::string::npos || (last.empty() && !line.empty())) last = line;
        if (e == std::string::npos) break;
        at = e + 1;
    }
    size_t src = last.find("../mesa");
    if (src != std::string::npos) last = last.substr(src);
    *why = "the compiler aborted (signal " + std::to_string(WIFSIGNALED(status) ? WTERMSIG(status) : -1) + "): " + last;
    return false;
}

// a refusal's sentence without the function's own name and numbers, so that one cause counts once however many
// functions meet it: digits become '#', and the text up to the first ':' is dropped when it names the function
std::string causeOf(const std::string& why, const std::string& name) {
    std::string s = why;
    for (const std::string& n : {name, name + "_air"}) {
        size_t at;
        while ((at = s.find(n)) != std::string::npos) s.replace(at, n.size(), "F");
    }
    std::string out;
    for (char c : s) {
        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
            if (out.empty() || out.back() != '#') out += '#';
        } else {
            out += c;
        }
    }
    if (out.size() > 200) out = out.substr(0, 200) + "...";
    return out;
}
}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    bool verbose = false;
    std::string only;
    std::vector<std::string> files;
    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
        if (std::strcmp(argv[i], "-v") == 0) {
            verbose = true;
        } else if (std::strcmp(argv[i], "-f") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
            only = argv[++i];
        } else if (std::strcmp(argv[i], "-c") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
            unsigned index = 0;
            unsigned long long value = 0;
            if (std::sscanf(argv[++i], "%u=%llu", &index, &value) != 2) {
                std::fprintf(stderr, "sweep: -c takes INDEX=VALUE, not %s\n", argv[i]);
                return 2;
            }
            gConstants.push_back(FunctionConstant{index, value});
        } else {
            files.push_back(argv[i]);
        }
    }
    if (files.empty()) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "usage: sweep [-v] LIBRARY.metallib...\n");
        return 2;
    }
    if (!hasCompiler()) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "sweep: no compiler in this build (make MESA=1)\n");
        return 2;
    }
    const char* typeName[] = {"vertex", "fragment", "kernel"};
    uint32_t seen[3] = {}, taken[3] = {};
    std::map<std::string, uint32_t> causes;
    std::map<std::string, std::string> example;
    for (const std::string& path : files) {
        std::ifstream in(path, std::ios::binary);
        std::vector<uint8_t> data((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
        MetalLibrary lib;
        if (data.empty() || !lib.parse(data.data(), data.size())) {
            std::printf("sweep: %s: not read as a metallib: %s\n", path.c_str(), data.empty() ? "empty or missing" : lib.why().c_str());
            continue;
        }
        uint32_t here[3] = {}, hereTaken[3] = {};
        for (const MetalFunction& f : lib.functions()) {
            int t = f.type == MetalFunction::kVertex ? 0 : f.type == MetalFunction::kFragment ? 1 : f.type == MetalFunction::kKernel ? 2 : -1;
            if (t < 0 || (!only.empty() && f.name != only)) continue;
            const uint8_t* bc = nullptr;
            uint64_t len = 0;
            std::string why;
            bool ok = false;
            if (!lib.bitcode(f, &bc, &len)) {
                why = "the module's bitcode could not be found";
            } else {
                if (!only.empty()) {
                    uint32_t h = 2166136261u;
                    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < len; i++) h = (h ^ bc[i]) * 16777619u;
                    std::printf("sweep: %s: %llu bytes of bitcode, fnv %08x\n", f.name.c_str(), (unsigned long long)len, h);
                }
                // (one function by name is compiled in this process, so that Mesa's own debug output reaches the terminal)
                if (!only.empty() && t != 2) {
                    // the stage's tables as a draw reads them: what samples what, and through which sampler
                    auto st = compileStage(bc, len, &why, gConstants);
                    ok = st != nullptr;
                    if (ok) {
                        const Kernel& k = st->stage.k;
                        std::printf("sweep: %s: %u texture slots, sampler mask %#x, %u prefetch(es)", f.name.c_str(), k.numTextureSlots, k.samplerMask,
                                    unsigned(st->stage.numSamplerPrefetch));
                        for (unsigned i = 0; i < st->stage.numSamplerPrefetch; i++)
                            std::printf(" [tex %u samp %u]", st->stage.prefetch[i].texId, st->stage.prefetch[i].sampId);
                        for (const auto& [index, smp] : st->inlineSamplers) std::printf(" inline sampler at %u", index);
                        std::printf("\n");
                    }
                } else {
                    ok = !only.empty() ? compileAir(bc, len, &why, gConstants) != nullptr : compileApart(t == 2, bc, len, &why);
                }
            }
            seen[t]++;
            here[t]++;
            if (ok) {
                taken[t]++;
                hereTaken[t]++;
            } else {
                const std::string c = std::string(typeName[t]) + ": " + causeOf(why, f.name);
                if (causes[c]++ == 0) example[c] = f.name;
            }
            if (verbose) std::printf("sweep: %-8s %-60s %s%s\n", typeName[t], f.name.c_str(), ok ? "ok" : "REFUSED: ", ok ? "" : why.c_str());
        }
        std::printf("sweep: %s: vertex %u of %u, fragment %u of %u, kernel %u of %u compiled\n", path.c_str(), hereTaken[0], here[0], hereTaken[1], here[1],
                    hereTaken[2], here[2]);
    }
    std::printf("sweep: in all: vertex %u of %u, fragment %u of %u, kernel %u of %u compiled\n", taken[0], seen[0], taken[1], seen[1], taken[2], seen[2]);
    std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, std::string>> sorted;
    for (const auto& [c, n] : causes) sorted.push_back({n, c});
    std::sort(sorted.begin(), sorted.end(), [](const auto& a, const auto& b) { return a.first > b.first; });
    for (const auto& [n, c] : sorted) std::printf("sweep: %5u x %s  (e.g. %s)\n", n, c.c_str(), example[c].c_str());
    return 0;
}
```

`mkxnuimg.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pack the redwood UEFI (with the hook that starts the XNU loader) and an optional payload
into an Android boot image for `fastboot boot`.

  kernel = gzip(BootShim + UEFI FD + ["XNUP" container]) + DTB

The boot shim copies the FD to its base and the payload to PAYLOAD_BASE.

The UEFI pieces are taken from a Mu-Silicium tree built here (Mu-Silicium/, see uefi/README.md)
or, when there is none, from devices/redwood/prebuilt/.

usage: mkxnuimg.py [-p payload.bin] [-o out.img]
"""
import argparse, gzip, os, subprocess, sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
MU = os.path.join(HERE, 'Mu-Silicium')
PREBUILT = os.path.join(HERE, 'devices', 'redwood', 'prebuilt')
FD_BASE, FD_SIZE = 0x9FD00000, 0x200000
PAYLOAD_BASE, PAYLOAD_MAX = 0xF0000000, 0x04000000

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('-p', '--payload')
ap.add_argument('-o', '--output', default=os.path.join(HERE, 'xnu-redwood.img'))
ap.add_argument('--mode', default='RELEASE')
args = ap.parse_args()

fd_path = os.path.join(MU, f'Build/redwoodPkg/{args.mode}_CLANGPDB/FV/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd')
if os.path.isfile(fd_path):
    shim_dir = os.path.join(MU, 'BootShim')
    for f in ('BootShim.elf', 'BootShim.bin'):
        try: os.unlink(os.path.join(shim_dir, f))
        except FileNotFoundError: pass
    subprocess.check_call(['make', 'REQUIRES_KERNEL_HEADER=1', f'FD_BASE={FD_BASE:#x}', f'FD_SIZE={FD_SIZE:#x}',
                           f'CFLAGS=--target=aarch64-linux-gnu -DPAYLOAD_BASE={PAYLOAD_BASE:#x}'],
                          cwd=shim_dir, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    parts = {'shim': os.path.join(shim_dir, 'BootShim.bin'), 'fd': fd_path,
             'dtb': os.path.join(MU, 'Resources/DTBs/redwood.dtb'), 'ramdisk': os.path.join(MU, 'Resources/ramdisk'),
             'mkbootimg': os.path.join(MU, 'Resources/Scripts/mkbootimg.py')}
else:
    parts = {'shim': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'BootShim.bin'), 'fd': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'SILICIUM_UEFI.fd'),
             'dtb': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'device-tree.dtb'), 'ramdisk': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'ramdisk'),
             'mkbootimg': os.path.join(PREBUILT, 'mkbootimg.py')}
for name, path in parts.items():
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        hint = ''
        if name == 'fd':
            hint = ("\n  The UEFI image is not in the repository: it carries the phone vendor's own drivers, which are not\n"
                    "  redistributed here. Build it from your own phone's firmware: uefi/README.md")
        sys.exit(f'mkxnuimg.py: {path} not found{hint}')
shim = open(parts['shim'], 'rb').read()
fd = open(parts['fd'], 'rb').read()
assert len(fd) == FD_SIZE, hex(len(fd))

blob = shim + fd
if args.payload:
    data = open(args.payload, 'rb').read()
    # the payload file is a complete "XNUP" container (see xnuloader/mkpayload.py)
    assert data[:4] == b'XNUP' and len(data) <= PAYLOAD_MAX - 0x1000, 'bad or oversized payload'
    blob += data
    blob += b'\0' * (-len(blob) % 16)
    print(f'payload: {len(data)} bytes, bytesum={sum(data) & 0xffffffff:08x}')

dtb = open(parts['dtb'], 'rb').read()
kernel = args.output + '.kernel~'
open(kernel, 'wb').write(gzip.compress(blob, 6) + dtb)
try:
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, parts['mkbootimg'], '--kernel', kernel, '--ramdisk', parts['ramdisk'],
                           '--header_version', '1', '-o', args.output])
finally:
    os.unlink(kernel)
print(f'{args.output}: {os.path.getsize(args.output)} bytes (shim {len(shim)}, uncompressed {len(blob)})')

```

`qemu/daemonlog.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Pick one daemon's story out of a run log: its own messages (stderr/os_log on the console), what
# launchd said about it, its failing system calls and crashes.
# usage: daemonlog.sh LOG NAME [max lines]
log=$1 name=$2 max=${3:-60}
sed -n '/== KERNEL LOG ==/,/--- kernel message buffer ---/p' "$log" |
	grep -a -E "(^|\] |[ 0-9:.+-]{20,40} )$name\[|\((system|user/[0-9]+|pid)/[^ ]*$name[^)]*\)|requestor = $name\[" |
	grep -a -v 'internal event\|service state: \(spawn\|xpcproxy\|running\)\|persona\|uncorking\|> created$\|shutting down\|cleaning up\|removing child\|launching: ' |
	cut -c1-${COLS:-250} | awk '!seen[$0]++' | head -"$max"
echo "--- crashes"
grep -a "usertrap: $name\[" -A5 "$log" | sed 's/^\[[^]]*\]: //' | awk '!seen[$0]++' | head -14
echo "--- failing system calls"
grep -a "systrace: $name\[" "$log" | sed 's/^\[[^]]*\]: //; s/\[[0-9]*\]/[]/; s/0x[0-9a-f]*/X/g' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn |
	grep -a -v 'FeatureFlags\|fsgetpath\|getattrlist\|Info.plist\|libdispatch\|gettid\|#535\|__mac_syscall(X, X, X, X) = 103\|timezone\|shm_open' | cut -c1-200 | head -${SYS:-14}
```

`qemu/run-darwin.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Boot the whole system under QEMU: the big system image preloaded at the loader's resident
# address (it becomes /dev/md0, the root) and the small image in the payload (/dev/md1), the
# same arrangement `xl ramdisk` + `xl run` make on the phone.
# usage: run-darwin.sh [seconds] [extra qemu args...]
#
# Counting anything in the log this writes: every console line comes out TWICE, the second copy in a
# block replayed some thousands of lines later (take any launchd line and grep -n it). So `grep -c` gives
# about double, and `sort -u` does not fix it either, because other processes' output interleaves and
# splits one of the two copies. Count distinct events instead -- by timestamp, or by program and pid for
# "Successfully spawned". The phone's logs do not do this; `xl log` fetches the buffer once.
#
# env: ROOT=<small image>, IMG=<system image>, CMDLINE=<extra boot-args>
#      QEMU_RAM_GB=<n>     the guest's RAM, default 7: memory then ends where the phone's does and the
#                          kernel gets the same 4.2 GB window (the system image included) as on the phone.
#                          The host needs about 2.5 GB per running instance.
#      QEMU_NET=1          with a network: a virtio network device, behind it QEMU's own "user" network
#                          (it hands out an address by DHCP, answers DNS and passes connections on to
#                          this machine's network; no privileges needed). The kernel makes en0 of it
#                          (boot-arg virtio_net=1, added here); see userland/src/net_test.m for the rest.
#      AUDIO=<where>       what plays the sound of Darwin: a QEMU audio back end (pipewire, pa, alsa, sdl: each
#                          needs its QEMU module, e.g. the package qemu-audio-pipewire) or FILE.wav to
#                          write it into a file instead. Default: nowhere (the guest plays all the same).
#      QEMU_INSTANCE=<n>   to run several at once: each number has its own monitor and QMP ports
#                          (4444 + 10n, 4445 + 10n); the file qemu/instance sets it for a working copy.
#                          touch.py, screendump.sh and stop.sh follow the same rule.
# The machine has a display (ramfb; without one SpringBoard does not start): the loader sets a mode of the
# size of the phone's screen. qemu/screendump.sh saves a picture of it (through the monitor on port 4444).
# Add "-display gtk" to see it in a window and use it with the mouse: the pointer with the left button
# held is a finger (the keys L, H, Up and Down are the lock, home and volume buttons).
# Touches can also be sent from a script: qemu/touch.py (through the QMP socket on port 4445).
#
# The system image is not read into QEMU: guest RAM is a private mapping of qemu/ram.img, a sparse
# file that holds the image at the right offset (reflinked, so it costs neither disk space nor
# host RAM).
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." || exit 1
K=hakios-kernel
[ -f $K ] || { K=prebuilt/hakios-kernel; echo "run-darwin.sh: no kernel built here, using $K" >&2; }
# Darwin has to be told which iPhone it runs on, and that comes from the user's own IPSW, into the loader at build time
# (xnuloader/mkidentity.sh). The loader in prebuilt/ has no Apple data, so with it Darwin does not start, and the window stays black.
if [ ! -f xnuloader/loader.efi ] && [ -z "$QEMU_PREBUILT_LOADER" ]; then
	echo "run-darwin.sh: no xnuloader/loader.efi: Darwin needs the loader built with the identity of the iPhone from your own IPSW:"
	echo "            make loader        (needs clang and lld; QEMU_PREBUILT_LOADER=1 to run with the one without Apple data anyway)"
	exit 1
fi
IMG=${IMG:-userland/system.apfs}
ROOT=${ROOT:-userland/root.apfs}
[ -f "$IMG" ] && [ -f "$ROOT" ] || { echo "run-darwin.sh: $IMG or $ROOT is missing (userland/build.sh makes them)"; exit 1; }
SECS=${1:-60}; shift
RAM_BASE=0x40000000 RD_ADDR=0xFC000000
RAM_GB=${QEMU_RAM_GB:-7}
RAM_SIZE=$((RAM_GB << 30)) FILE_SIZE=$((12 << 30))
INSTANCE=${QEMU_INSTANCE:-$(cat qemu/instance 2>/dev/null || echo 0)}
# an instance takes 2.5-3 GB of host memory; starting one that does not fit gets something killed
AVAILABLE=$(awk '/^MemAvailable:/ { print int($2 / 1024) }' /proc/meminfo)
if [ "${AVAILABLE:-9999}" -lt 3000 ] && [ -z "$QEMU_FORCE" ]; then
	echo "run-darwin.sh: only $AVAILABLE MB of memory available on this machine: stop another QEMU first (QEMU_FORCE=1 to start anyway)"
	exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f qemu/ram.img ] || [ "$IMG" -nt qemu/ram.img ]; then
	python3 - "$IMG" qemu/ram.img $((RD_ADDR - RAM_BASE)) $FILE_SIZE <<'PY' || exit 1
import os, sys
src = os.open(sys.argv[1], os.O_RDONLY)
dst = os.open(sys.argv[2], os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
offset, size = int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
os.ftruncate(dst, size)
total, done = os.fstat(src).st_size, 0
while done < total:
    done += os.copy_file_range(src, dst, total - done, done, offset + done)
PY
fi
NET=()
if [ -n "$QEMU_NET" ] && [ "$QEMU_NET" != 0 ]; then
	NET=(-netdev user,id=net0 -device virtio-net-device,netdev=net0)
	CMDLINE="virtio_net=1 $CMDLINE"
fi
# the sound device (QEMU 8.2 or newer has one for this machine): the kernel's sink for /dev/hakios-audio
SOUND=()
if qemu-system-aarch64 -device help 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"virtio-sound-device"'; then
	case "${AUDIO:-none}" in
	*.wav) SOUND=(-audiodev "wav,id=snd,path=$(readlink -f "$AUDIO")") ;;
	*) SOUND=(-audiodev "${AUDIO:-none},id=snd") ;;
	esac
	SOUND+=(-device virtio-sound-device,audiodev=snd,streams=1)   # one stream: output, no microphone of the host
	CMDLINE="virtio_sound=1 $CMDLINE"
fi
xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o qemu/payload.bin kernel=$K ramdisk=$ROOT --rdres "$(printf '%x' "$(stat -c %s "$IMG")")" \
	--cmdline "loader_return_after=$SECS epoch=$(date +%s) virtio_input=1 $CMDLINE" >/dev/null || exit 1
QEMU_MEM=${RAM_GB}G exec qemu/run.sh $((SECS + 40)) \
	-object memory-backend-file,id=ram,size=$RAM_SIZE,mem-path="$PWD/qemu/ram.img",share=off \
	-machine memory-backend=ram \
	-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false -device virtio-tablet-device -device virtio-keyboard-device "${NET[@]}" "${SOUND[@]}" \
	-device ramfb -monitor tcp:127.0.0.1:$((4444 + 10 * INSTANCE)),server,nowait \
	-qmp tcp:127.0.0.1:$((4445 + 10 * INSTANCE)),server,nowait "$@"

```

`qemu/run-hfs-test.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# HFS Plus, built into the kernel, on a disk image of its own: userland/src/hfs_test.c as process 1 of a tiny APFS root,
# the volume on a writable virtio disk (virtio_blk=2). Run it twice on the same image to see what the first run wrote
# still there ("boot number 2").
# usage: qemu/run-hfs-test.sh [IMAGE]      (default: a new 256 MB volume in qemu/hfs-test/)
# needs: the kernel built (make kernel), mkfs.hfsplus (hfsprogs) in $PATH or $MKFS
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." || exit 1
W=qemu/hfs-test
mkdir -p $W/root/dev $W/root/mnt $W/root/sbin
IMG=${1:-$W/hfs.img}
if [ ! -f "$IMG" ]; then
	truncate -s 256M "$IMG"
	"${MKFS:-mkfs.hfsplus}" -s -J -U 0 -G 0 -M 755 -v Data "$IMG" || exit 1
fi
. ./xnu-env.sh
xnu-clang -arch arm64 -Os -static -nostdlib -ffreestanding -fno-stack-protector -fno-builtin \
	-Wl,-e,__start -Wl,-pagezero_size,0x100000000 -o $W/root/sbin/launchd userland/src/hfs_test.c || exit 1
python3 tools/apfs/mkapfs.py -o $W/root.apfs Root=$W/root >/dev/null || exit 1
xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o qemu/payload.bin kernel=hakios-kernel ramdisk=$W/root.apfs \
	--cmdline "cpus=1 debug=0x8 rd=md0 virtio_blk=2" >/dev/null || exit 1
qemu/run.sh 60 -global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false \
	-drive file="$IMG",format=raw,if=none,id=hd -device virtio-blk-device,drive=hd | grep -a "hfs_test\|^hfs:\|^jnl:\|virtio-blk\|panic("
```

`qemu/run-u-boot.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Boot the XNU loader + kernel payload under QEMU the way the phone does with HakiOS's U-Boot: U-Boot (not edk2) is
# the firmware, the loader and its payload are in memory before it starts (an HKUB container at 0x50000000, where a
# phone's ABL would have put its ramdisk), and the hakios command puts the payload at 0xF0000000 and starts the loader.
# usage: run-u-boot.sh [seconds] [extra qemu args...]
# env: QEMU_U_BOOT   U-Boot for QEMU (default ../u-boot/build-qemu/u-boot.bin: uefi/u-boot/apply.sh qemu &&
#                    uefi/u-boot/build.sh qemu)
#      QEMU_SMP, QEMU_MEM, QEMU_TB_MB as for run.sh
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
T=${1:-20}; shift
UB=${QEMU_U_BOOT:-../u-boot/build-qemu/u-boot.bin}
[ -f "$UB" ] || { echo "run-u-boot.sh: no $UB (uefi/u-boot/apply.sh qemu && uefi/u-boot/build.sh qemu)"; exit 1; }
[ -f payload.bin ] || { echo "run-u-boot.sh: no payload.bin (make qemu-open makes one)"; exit 1; }
L=../xnuloader/loader.efi; [ -f $L ] || L=../prebuilt/loader.efi
python3 - payload.bin $L u-boot.hkub <<'PY' || exit 1
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join('..', 'tools'))
from mkubootimg import container
payload, loader, out = sys.argv[1:4]
open(out, 'wb').write(container([('payload', open(payload, 'rb').read()), ('loader', open(loader, 'rb').read())]))
PY
timeout "$T" qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt,gic-version=3 -cpu cortex-a76 -smp ${QEMU_SMP:-1} -m ${QEMU_MEM:-6G} \
  -accel tcg,tb-size=${QEMU_TB_MB:-384} \
  -bios "$UB" \
  -device loader,file=u-boot.hkub,addr=0x50000000,force-raw=on \
  -display none -serial stdio -monitor none -no-reboot "$@" 2>&1
```

`qemu/run.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Boot the XNU loader + kernel payload under QEMU (virt, GICv3, UEFI at EL1).
# usage: run.sh [seconds] [extra qemu args...]
# env: QEMU_TB_MB           megabytes for QEMU's cache of translated code (default 384; QEMU's own
#                           default of 1 GB mostly costs host memory)
#      QEMU_SMP             processor cores of the machine (default 1); the kernel uses as many of them as
#                           its boot-arg cpus=N says (CMDLINE="cpus=4" for run-darwin.sh), one without it
#      QEMU_ESP=1           no loader device: the payload is the file \EFI\hakios\payload.bin on the ESP, which the loader
#                           reads itself (UEFI-native boot; what a boot menu or a USB stick does)
#      QEMU_EFI, QEMU_VARS  the UEFI firmware for aarch64 guests (found by itself where Arch's edk2-aarch64
#                           puts it, or Debian/Ubuntu's /usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_CODE.fd and AAVMF_VARS.fd)
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
T=${1:-20}; shift
# the UEFI firmware: where Arch's edk2-aarch64 puts it, or where Debian and Ubuntu's AAVMF does
EFI=${QEMU_EFI-}; VARS_SRC=${QEMU_VARS-}
if [ -z "$EFI" ]; then
	for f in /usr/share/edk2/aarch64/QEMU_EFI.fd /usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_CODE.fd; do [ -f "$f" ] && { EFI=$f; break; }; done
fi
if [ -z "$VARS_SRC" ]; then
	for f in /usr/share/edk2/aarch64/QEMU_VARS.fd /usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_VARS.fd; do [ -f "$f" ] && { VARS_SRC=$f; break; }; done
fi
[ -f "$EFI" ] || { echo "run.sh: no UEFI firmware found (looked for edk2-aarch64's and AAVMF's); set QEMU_EFI and QEMU_VARS"; exit 1; }
cp "$VARS_SRC" vars.fd 2>/dev/null
# the loader is the boot application of the little FAT volume QEMU makes of esp/:
# the one built here, or else the one that comes with the repository
L=../xnuloader/loader.efi; [ -f $L ] || L=../prebuilt/loader.efi
mkdir -p esp/EFI/BOOT && cp -u $L esp/EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI
# The payload (kernel, root image, command line) reaches the loader in one of two ways. By default QEMU's loader
# device puts it in memory at 0xF0000000, as the boot shim does behind Project Silicium's image on the phone.
# With QEMU_ESP=1 it is not put anywhere: it is the file \EFI\hakios\payload.bin of the ESP, and the loader reads it
# itself from the volume it was started from -- UEFI-native boot, what a boot menu or a USB stick does (docs/uefi-boot.md).
PAYLOAD_DEVICE=(-device loader,file=payload.bin,addr=0xF0000000,force-raw=on)
if [ -n "${QEMU_ESP:-}" ]; then
	mkdir -p esp/EFI/hakios && cp payload.bin esp/EFI/hakios/payload.bin
	PAYLOAD_DEVICE=()
fi
timeout "$T" qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt,gic-version=3 -cpu cortex-a76 -smp ${QEMU_SMP:-1} -m ${QEMU_MEM:-6G} \
  -accel tcg,tb-size=${QEMU_TB_MB:-384} \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file="$EFI" \
  -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=vars.fd \
  -drive file=fat:rw:esp,format=raw,if=virtio \
  "${PAYLOAD_DEVICE[@]}" \
  -display none -serial stdio -monitor none -no-reboot "$@" 2>&1

```

`qemu/screendump.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Save the screen of a running QEMU (started with -device ramfb -monitor tcp:127.0.0.1:4444,server,nowait) as a PNG.
# usage: screendump.sh [out.png]      (FULL=1: the whole mode, not only the phone-sized corner)
out=$(realpath -m "${1:-$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/../logs/qemu-screen.png}")   # QEMU writes it: absolute
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out")"
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
python3 - "$out" "${QEMU_INSTANCE:-$(cat "$here/instance" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)}" <<'PY'
import socket, struct, sys, time, zlib, os
out = sys.argv[1]; ppm = out + '.ppm'
s = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 4444 + 10 * int(sys.argv[2]))); s.settimeout(2)
s.sendall(b'\n'); time.sleep(0.3)
s.sendall(f'screendump {ppm}\n'.encode()); time.sleep(1.5)
d = open(ppm, 'rb').read(); os.unlink(ppm)
magic, size, maxval, pix = d.split(b'\n', 3)
w, h = map(int, size.split())
# the kernel uses the top left 1125x2436 of a bigger mode as the phone's screen (boot-args fbwidth/fbheight)
cw, ch = (min(w, 1125), min(h, 2436)) if os.environ.get('FULL') != '1' else (w, h)
# QEMU pads every row of the PPM to a multiple of 4 bytes (wrong for the format, but that is what it writes)
stride = len(pix) // h
rows = b''.join(b'\0' + pix[y * stride:y * stride + cw * 3] for y in range(ch))
w, h = cw, ch
chunk = lambda k, b: struct.pack('>I', len(b)) + k + b + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(k + b))
open(out, 'wb').write(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) +
                      chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(rows, 6)) + chunk(b'IEND', b''))
print(out, w, h)
PY

```

`qemu/sym.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Symbolicate kernel addresses: sym.py 0xaddr [0xaddr ...] (uses kernel.syms from nm -n)."""
import sys, bisect, os, subprocess
syms = []
for l in open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'kernel.syms')):
    p = l.split()
    if len(p) == 3 and p[1] in 'tTsSdDbB':
        syms.append((int(p[0], 16), p[2]))
addrs = [s[0] for s in syms]
for a in sys.argv[1:]:
    v = int(a, 16); i = bisect.bisect_right(addrs, v) - 1
    name = syms[i][1]
    if name.startswith('__Z'):
        name = subprocess.run(['c++filt', name[1:]], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip() or name
    print(f'{a}: {name} + {v - syms[i][0]:#x}')
```

`qemu/symstack.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Put names on the user-space addresses the kernel's bring-up aids print.

usage: symstack.py LOG [PROCESS]

Reads the "ustacks:" (boot-args ustacks=NAME ustacks_at=SECONDS [ustacks_ms=PERIOD]), "usertrap:" and
"userabort:" lines of a console log (and, before a "userabort:", the "First throw call stack" of the exception
that led to it), subtracts the shared cache slide and looks every address up in the Darwin dyld
shared cache with "ipsw dyld a2s". Lookups take a few seconds each, so the answers are kept
in sysimage/a2s.json. Addresses outside the cache (the program itself) are shown as they are.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

BASE = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), 'sysimage')
CACHE = os.path.join(BASE, '20F66__iPhone10,3_6/dyld_shared_cache_arm64')
KNOWN = os.path.join(BASE, 'a2s.json')
CACHE_LOW, CACHE_HIGH = 0x180000000, 0x280000000        # unslid addresses of the shared cache

known = json.load(open(KNOWN)) if os.path.exists(KNOWN) else {}


def name(address, slide):
    unslid = address - slide
    if not CACHE_LOW <= unslid < CACHE_HIGH:
        return f'{address:#x} (not in the shared cache)'
    key = f'{unslid:#x}'
    if key not in known:
        out = subprocess.run(['ipsw', 'dyld', 'a2s', CACHE, key], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        lines = [line for line in out.splitlines() if key in line]
        known[key] = re.sub(r'^\S+:\s*', '', lines[-1]).strip() if lines else '?'
        json.dump(known, open(KNOWN, 'w'), indent=0)
    return known[key]


def main():
    log = sys.argv[1]
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    slide, show = 0, True
    thrown = None                       # the addresses after "*** First throw call stack:", until the abort
    for line in open(log, errors='replace'):
        line = line.rstrip('\n')
        if re.fullmatch(r'\((0x[0-9a-f]+ ?)+\)', line):
            thrown = line[1:-1].split()
            continue
        m = re.search(r'userabort: (\S+)\[(\d+)\] aborts, shared cache slide (0x[0-9a-f]+); called from: (.*)', line)
        if m:
            if only is None or m.group(1) == only:
                print(f'userabort: {m.group(1)}[{m.group(2)}]')
                for text in m.group(4).split():
                    print(f'    {name(int(text, 16), int(m.group(3), 16))}')
                if thrown:
                    print('  the exception was thrown from')
                    for text in thrown:
                        print(f'    {name(int(text, 16), int(m.group(3), 16))}')
            thrown = None
            continue
        m = re.search(r'(ustacks|usertrap): (\S+)\[(\d+)\].*shared cache slide (0x[0-9a-f]+)', line)
        if m:
            slide = int(m.group(4), 16)
            show = only is None or m.group(2) == only
            if show:
                print(line[line.index(m.group(1)):])
            continue
        if not show:
            continue
        m = re.search(r'ustacks:  thread (0x[0-9a-f]+)([^:]*): (.*)', line)
        if m:
            print(f'  thread {m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}')
            for depth, text in enumerate(m.group(3).split()):
                if depth == 1:
                    continue            # the link register: usually stale, the frame chain has the caller
                print(f'    {name(int(text, 16), slide)}')
            continue
        m = re.search(r'usertrap:   called from (0x[0-9a-f]+)', line)
        if m:
            print(f'    {name(int(m.group(1), 16), slide)}')
        elif 'usertrap:   x' in line:
            print('  ' + line[line.index('usertrap:') + 10:])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`qemu/touch.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Touch the screen of the system running under QEMU (qemu/run-darwin.sh), through QMP.

usage: touch.py STEP...
  tap X Y                     a short touch
  hold X Y MS                 touch and stay
  swipe X0 Y0 X1 Y1 [MS]      drag in MS milliseconds (default 300)
  key NAME [MS]               press a button: lock, home, volup, voldown; fivefingers = five fingers on the
                              screen for MS (held 1500 ms they end the run)
  stacks PROCESS              have the kernel print where the threads of that process are (the
                              addresses come out in the log; qemu/symstack.py names them).
                              "stacks top" is something else: which processes have had the processor
                              since it was last asked ("top:" lines in the log)
  wait SECONDS
Positions are fractions of the screen: 0 0 is the top left corner, 1 1 the bottom right.
Example, the "swipe up to open" gesture:  touch.py swipe 0.5 0.98 0.5 0.4 250
"""
import json
import os
import socket
import sys
import time


def instance():
    """Which QEMU: QEMU_INSTANCE, or the number in the file "instance" next to this script, or 0."""
    try:
        return int(os.environ.get('QEMU_INSTANCE') or
                   open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'instance')).read())
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return 0

KEYS = {'lock': 'l', 'home': 'h', 'volup': 'up', 'voldown': 'down', 'fivefingers': 'f11'}


class Qmp:
    def __init__(self, port=None):
        self.sock = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', port or 4445 + 10 * instance()))
        self.file = self.sock.makefile('rw')
        self.file.readline()                        # the greeting
        self.command('qmp_capabilities')

    def command(self, name, **arguments):
        self.file.write(json.dumps({'execute': name, 'arguments': arguments}) + '\n')
        self.file.flush()
        while True:
            reply = json.loads(self.file.readline())
            if 'return' in reply or 'error' in reply:
                if 'error' in reply:
                    sys.exit(f'touch.py: {name}: {reply["error"]["desc"]}')
                return reply['return']

    def events(self, *events):
        self.command('input-send-event', events=list(events))

    def pointer(self, x, y, down=None):
        events = [{'type': 'abs', 'data': {'axis': 'x', 'value': round(x * 0x7fff)}},
                  {'type': 'abs', 'data': {'axis': 'y', 'value': round(y * 0x7fff)}}]
        if down is not None:
            events.append({'type': 'btn', 'data': {'button': 'left', 'down': down}})
        self.events(*events)

    def key(self, name, down):
        self.events({'type': 'key', 'data': {'key': {'type': 'qcode', 'data': name}, 'down': down}})


def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if not args:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    qmp = Qmp()
    while args:
        step = args.pop(0)
        if step == 'wait':
            time.sleep(float(args.pop(0)))
        elif step in ('tap', 'hold'):
            x, y = float(args.pop(0)), float(args.pop(0))
            ms = float(args.pop(0)) if step == 'hold' else 60
            qmp.pointer(x, y)
            qmp.pointer(x, y, True)
            time.sleep(ms / 1000)
            qmp.pointer(x, y, False)
        elif step == 'swipe':
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = (float(args.pop(0)) for _ in range(4))
            ms = float(args.pop(0)) if args and args[0][0].isdigit() else 300
            steps = max(2, int(ms / 16))
            qmp.pointer(x0, y0)
            qmp.pointer(x0, y0, True)
            for i in range(1, steps + 1):
                time.sleep(ms / 1000 / steps)
                qmp.pointer(x0 + (x1 - x0) * i / steps, y0 + (y1 - y0) * i / steps)
            time.sleep(0.016)
            qmp.pointer(x1, y1, False)
        elif step == 'stacks':
            # F12, the name, Enter: the kernel's virtio keyboard driver takes it as a command
            special = {'.': 'dot', '-': 'minus', '_': 'minus', ' ': 'spc'}
            qmp.key('f12', True)
            qmp.key('f12', False)
            for ch in args.pop(0):
                shifted = ch.isupper() or ch == '_'
                code = special.get(ch, ch.lower())
                if shifted:
                    qmp.key('shift', True)
                qmp.key(code, True)
                qmp.key(code, False)
                if shifted:
                    qmp.key('shift', False)
                time.sleep(0.02)
            qmp.key('ret', True)
            qmp.key('ret', False)
        elif step == 'key':
            name = KEYS.get(args.pop(0))
            if name is None:
                sys.exit('touch.py: buttons are: ' + ' '.join(KEYS))
            ms = float(args.pop(0)) if args and args[0][0].isdigit() else 80
            qmp.key(name, True)
            time.sleep(ms / 1000)
            qmp.key(name, False)
        else:
            sys.exit(f'touch.py: bad step "{step}"')
        time.sleep(0.05)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`qemu/where.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Ask a running QEMU (its monitor: port 4444, or 4444 + 10 * QEMU_INSTANCE) where the guest's CPUs are, a few times."""
import socket, time, re, subprocess, sys, os
n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3
try:
    instance = int(os.environ.get('QEMU_INSTANCE') or open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'instance')).read())
except (OSError, ValueError):
    instance = 0
s = socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 4444 + 10 * instance)); s.settimeout(2)
def cmd(c):
    s.sendall(c.encode() + b'\n'); time.sleep(0.4)
    out = b''
    try:
        while True:
            d = s.recv(65536)
            if not d: break
            out += d
    except socket.timeout:
        pass
    return out.decode(errors='replace')
cmd('')
pcs = []
for i in range(n):
    # one block of registers per CPU ("CPU#n"); a machine with one CPU prints no such heading
    for block in re.split(r'(?=CPU#\d+)', cmd('info registers -a')):
        c = re.match(r'CPU#(\d+)', block)
        m = re.search(r'PC=([0-9a-f]+)', block); l = re.search(r'X30=([0-9a-f]+)', block)
        if m: pcs.append((c.group(1) if c else '0', '0x' + m.group(1), '0x' + l.group(1) if l else '0x0'))
    time.sleep(1.0)
for cpu, pc, lr in pcs:
    out = subprocess.run([os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'sym.py'), pc, lr], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip().replace('\n', '   <- lr ')
    print(f'cpu {cpu}: {out}')

```

`sysimage/ipsw-member.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy one member out of an IPSW the user has on their own disk.

usage: ipsw-member.py IPSW MEMBER OUTPUT

An IPSW is a ZIP64 archive; Python's zipfile reads it as it is. The member is streamed to OUTPUT
(inflated if it is compressed), so the 4.7 GB root filesystem image never has to fit in memory.
Nothing is downloaded: the project ships no file of Apple's and fetches none. The IPSW is the
user's, got by the user from wherever they get their firmware.
"""
import shutil
import sys
import zipfile


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 4:
        sys.exit(__doc__.split('\n\n')[1])
    ipsw, member, output = sys.argv[1:]
    try:
        archive = zipfile.ZipFile(ipsw)
    except (OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as error:
        sys.exit(f'ipsw-member.py: {ipsw}: {error}')
    with archive:
        try:
            info = archive.getinfo(member)
        except KeyError:
            sys.exit(f'ipsw-member.py: {member} is not in {ipsw} (is it the Darwin userland 16.5 20F66 IPSW for iPhone10,3/iPhone10,6?)')
        with archive.open(info) as stream, open(output, 'wb') as out:
            shutil.copyfileobj(stream, out, 1 << 20)
    print(f'{member}: {info.file_size} bytes')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`sysimage/mkvarskel.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write the skeleton of the data volume: mkvarskel.py rootfs.slt > var.skel

The Darwin image carries a template of /private/var (the restore process copies it to the data
volume). Our /private/var is an empty memory filesystem at every boot, so init re-creates the
directories of that template, with their owners and modes, from this list. Lines, tab separated:
    d  mode(octal)  uid  gid  path
    l  target  path                      (symbolic link)
The staged applications and assets of the template are left out; a few directories that daemons
expect but only a running Darwin creates are added at the end.
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import stat
import sys

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('select_system', os.path.join(here, 'select-system.py'))
select_system = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(select_system)

SKIP = ('private/var/staged_system_apps', 'private/var/MobileAsset/')
EXTRA = [   # path, mode, uid, gid
    ('/private/var/db/uuidtext', 0o755, 272, 272),                      # logd
    ('/private/var/db/diagnostics/timesync', 0o755, 272, 272),
    ('/private/var/containers', 0o755, 0, 0),                           # containermanagerd
    ('/private/var/containers/Data', 0o755, 0, 0),
    ('/private/var/containers/Shared', 0o755, 0, 0),
    ('/private/var/containers/Bundle', 0o755, 0, 0),
    ('/private/var/mobile/Containers', 0o755, 501, 501),
    ('/private/var/mobile/Containers/Data', 0o755, 501, 501),
    ('/private/var/mobile/Containers/Shared', 0o755, 501, 501),
    ('/private/var/mobile/Library/Caches', 0o755, 501, 501),
    ('/private/var/mobile/Library/Preferences', 0o755, 501, 501),
    ('/private/var/mobile/Library/Logs', 0o755, 501, 501),
    ('/private/var/root/Library/Caches', 0o700, 0, 0),
    ('/private/var/root/Library/Preferences', 0o700, 0, 0),
    ('/private/var/root/Library/Logs', 0o700, 0, 0),
]

dirs, links = {}, []
for e in select_system.entries(sys.argv[1]):
    path = e['Path']
    if not path.startswith('private/var') or path.startswith(SKIP):
        continue
    mode = select_system.mode_bits(e['Mode'])
    if mode is None:
        continue
    if stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
        dirs['/' + path] = (mode & 0o7777, int(e.get('User ID') or 0), int(e.get('Group ID') or 0))
    elif stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
        links.append((e.get('Symbolic Link', ''), '/' + path))
for path, mode, uid, gid in EXTRA:
    dirs.setdefault(path, (mode, uid, gid))
dirs.pop('/private/var', None)          # the mount point itself: init sets it up
for path in sorted(dirs):
    mode, uid, gid = dirs[path]
    print(f'd\t{mode:o}\t{uid}\t{gid}\t{path}')
for target, path in links:
    print(f'l\t{target}\t{path}')
# the time zone database is on the system volume
print('l\t/usr/share/zoneinfo\t/private/var/db/timezone/zoneinfo')

```

`sysimage/select-system.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Choose the part of the Darwin root filesystem that goes into the in-memory system image.

usage: select-system.py rootfs.slt system.files system.manifest

rootfs.slt is the technical listing of the root filesystem image ("7z l -slt rootfs.dmg").
Two files are written:
  system.files      the regular files to extract ("7z x -orootfs rootfs.dmg @system.files")
  system.manifest   every chosen file, directory and symbolic link with its owner, group and mode,
                    tab separated: mode(octal, with the type bits) uid gid path [link target].
                    tools/apfs/mkapfs.py builds the image from the extracted files and this manifest,
                    because extraction on Linux keeps neither owners nor all of the symlinks.

The whole root is 7.9 GB and the kernel on the phone has about 4 GB of RAM for everything, so:
  - programs, libraries and their data outside the framework directories are taken whole;
  - from the framework directories (the code itself is in the dyld shared cache) what a
    program may open at run time and is not huge: property lists, string tables, resources,
    plug-ins, and the XPC services and helper executables bundled with frameworks;
  - the applications (the home screen is made of their icons), without their media; those that Darwin
    keeps in /private/var/staged_system_apps until its first boot installs them (Maps, Notes,
    Weather, ...) are put straight into /Applications, where they are system applications like
    the rest: system.files names them where they are in the image, system.manifest where they go
    (userland/build.sh moves the extracted files);
  - machine-learning models, other languages' localizations, media and GPU shader libraries
    are left out, and so are a few very big daemons that have nothing to do with the display;
  - /Library (the wallpapers, regional tables) without its sounds;
  - of pictures, what the user interface itself is drawn with: small images, asset catalogs of
    moderate size; the fonts, the two biggest (colour emoji and Chinese) made smaller by unpack.sh;
  - the empty LANGUAGE.lproj directories of the bundles whose strings are in one .loctable file
    for all languages: they are how CoreFoundation knows which languages a bundle has, and
    without them every string comes out as its key.
"""
import re
import stat
import sys

WHOLE = ('usr/libexec/', 'usr/sbin/', 'usr/bin/', 'usr/lib/', 'usr/share/', 'sbin/', 'bin/', 'private/etc/',
         'System/Library/', 'Applications/', 'Library/')
# ... except these parts of /System/Library: big, and not needed to get a picture on the screen
# (not OnBoardingBundles, the privacy notices: an application's first screen links to its notice, and
# News refuses to start without its own -- "a legal requirement"; nor Health, the plug-ins the Health
# application and its daemon are made of: both stop with a fatal error when the directory is not there.
# Of Health only the pictures and films of the activity awards are left out, see SKIP_PREFIX and HEALTH)
SKIP_SYSTEM_LIBRARY = ('LinguisticData', 'PreinstalledAssetsV2', 'NanoTimeKit', 'Audio',
                       'Assistant', 'AccessibilityBundles',
                       'VideoProcessors', 'ScreenReader', 'Photos', 'Carrier Bundles', 'NanoPreferenceBundles',
                       'ImagingNetworks', 'ProductDocuments', 'AppPlaceholders', 'UserNotifications',
                       'Caches')
FRAMEWORKS = ('System/Library/Frameworks/', 'System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/')
SMALL = 4 << 20
# never from frameworks: machine-learning models, shader libraries, sound and video, big tables.
# (Not the data models, .mom: an application that keeps its data with Core Data dies without its
# model -- Notes did; nor the animations and vector pictures the interface is drawn with.)
SKIP_EXT = ('.weights', '.weights_nonane', '.metallib', '.mov', '.pcm', '.scnz', '.espresso.net',
            '.espresso.shape', '.caf', '.m4a', '.aiff', '.mp4', '.heic', '.wav', '.art', '.scube',
            '.ds', '.dat', '.bin')
# ... but '.dat' and '.bin' are also what these keep the tables in that the user interface is made with:
# the layouts of the on-screen keyboard, the emoji, the list of public domain suffixes
DATA_FRAMEWORKS = tuple(f'System/Library/{name}.framework/' for name in (
    'PrivateFrameworks/TextInputUI', 'PrivateFrameworks/CoreEmoji', 'Frameworks/CFNetwork'))
# never from applications: their sound, video and 3D content
SKIP_APP_EXT = ('.mov', '.mp4', '.m4a', '.caf', '.wav', '.heic', '.aiff', '.metallib', '.scnz', '.usdz')
# pictures the user interface is drawn with: small images, and asset catalogs up to this size
# (the one with all the SF Symbols alone is 170 MB and is left out)
MAX_ASSET_CATALOG = 4 << 20
# fonts: all but the very big ones; those two -- the colour emoji, 130 MB, and PingFang, the Chinese faces, 74 MB --
# are taken and made smaller after extraction (unpack.sh, ../tools/font_trim.py): the emoji without their biggest
# bitmaps (59 MB), PingFang with the regular and semibold faces for simplified, traditional and Hong Kong Chinese,
# both those programs name and the hidden ones (".PingFangSC-Regular") the system font falls back to
# (26 MB). Without them Safari and the rest drew emoji and Chinese characters as boxes with a question mark.
MAX_FONT = 25 << 20
TRIMMED_FONTS = ('System/Library/Fonts/CoreAddition/AppleColorEmoji-160px.ttc',
                 'System/Library/Fonts/LanguageSupport/PingFang.ttc')
# string tables hold every language; the biggest (Shortcuts' actions, Home) are 5-12 MB
MAX_STRING_TABLE = 16 << 20
# applications waiting here to be installed by the first boot go to /Applications instead
STAGED_APPS = 'private/var/staged_system_apps/'
# frameworks whose pictures are wanted whatever their size
ALL_PICTURES = ('System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ProgressUI.framework/',)
# ... and asset catalogs: the SF Symbols (UIKit crashes on the first system image without them)
BIG_CATALOGS = ('System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SFSymbols.framework/',)
# taken whole in principle, but not these: big and of no use until much later
# (/Library is the wallpapers and a few tables of regional settings, apart from the sounds)
HEALTH = 'System/Library/Health/'
SKIP_PREFIX = ('usr/share/tokenizer/', 'usr/share/firmware/', 'usr/share/mecabra/',
               'usr/standalone/', 'Library/Audio/', 'Library/Ringtones/',
               HEALTH + 'Assets/FitnessUIAssets.bundle/') + \
    tuple(f'System/Library/{name}/' for name in SKIP_SYSTEM_LIBRARY)
BIG_PROGRAM = 10 << 20           # daemons bigger than this (locationd, lskdd, ...) are not on the way to the screen
# sound, outside the directories above: the virtual audio device, a plug-in that all of mediaserverd's
# audio goes through, with its tunings (signal processing chains) for this model and for any, and the
# system's own sounds. Not the neural networks among the tunings, nor the sounds of the watch.
AUDIO = ('Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/', 'Library/Audio/Tunings/D22/', 'Library/Audio/Tunings/Generic/',
         'System/Library/Audio/UISounds/')
SKIP_AUDIO = ('System/Library/Audio/UISounds/nano/',)
KEEP_LANG = ('en', 'Base', 'English', 'en_US', 'en_GB')


def entries(listing):
    """Yield one dict per entry of a 7z technical listing."""
    entry = {}
    for line in open(listing, errors='replace'):
        line = line.rstrip('\n')
        if not line:
            if 'Path' in entry and 'Mode' in entry:
                yield entry
            entry = {}
        elif ' = ' in line or line.endswith(' ='):
            key, _, value = line.partition(' =')
            entry[key] = value[1:] if value.startswith(' ') else value
    if 'Path' in entry and 'Mode' in entry:
        yield entry


def mode_bits(text):
    """'-rwsr-xr-x' -> st_mode"""
    kinds = {'-': stat.S_IFREG, 'd': stat.S_IFDIR, 'l': stat.S_IFLNK}
    if text[0] not in kinds:
        return None
    mode = kinds[text[0]]
    for i, ch in enumerate(text[1:10]):
        if ch in 'rwxst':
            mode |= 0o400 >> i
        if ch in 'sS' and i == 2:
            mode |= stat.S_ISUID
        if ch in 'sS' and i == 5:
            mode |= stat.S_ISGID
        if ch in 'tT' and i == 8:
            mode |= stat.S_ISVTX
        if ch in 'ST':
            mode &= ~(0o400 >> i)
    return mode


def wanted_file(path, size):
    lproj = re.search(r'/([^/]+)\.lproj/', path)
    if lproj and lproj.group(1) not in KEEP_LANG:
        return False
    if path.startswith(AUDIO):
        return not path.startswith(SKIP_AUDIO) and '.espresso.' not in path
    if path.startswith(SKIP_PREFIX):
        return False
    if path.startswith('System/Library/Fonts/'):
        return size <= MAX_FONT or path in TRIMMED_FONTS
    if path.startswith(ALL_PICTURES) and path.lower().endswith('.png'):
        return True
    if path.startswith(('usr/libexec/', 'usr/sbin/')):
        return size <= BIG_PROGRAM
    if path.startswith(('Applications/', HEALTH)):
        return not path.lower().endswith(SKIP_APP_EXT) and '.mlmodelc/' not in path
    if path.startswith(FRAMEWORKS):
        if re.search(r'/(XPCServices|Support|Helpers)/', path):
            return size <= 32 << 20 and not path.lower().endswith(('.png', '.car', '.loctable', '.caml'))
        if path.endswith('.car'):
            return size <= MAX_ASSET_CATALOG or path.startswith(BIG_CATALOGS)
        if path.endswith('.loctable'):
            return size <= MAX_STRING_TABLE
        if path.startswith(DATA_FRAMEWORKS) and path.lower().endswith(('.dat', '.bin')):
            return size <= SMALL
        return size <= SMALL and not path.lower().endswith(SKIP_EXT) and '.mlmodelc/' not in path
    return path.startswith(WHOLE)


def main():
    listing, files_out, manifest_out = sys.argv[1:4]
    meta = {}                   # path in our image -> (mode, uid, gid, target, size)
    source = {}                 # ... -> path in Apple's image, where that is another
    for e in entries(listing):
        mode = mode_bits(e['Mode'])
        path = e['Path']
        if mode is None:
            continue
        if path.startswith(STAGED_APPS):
            source['Applications/' + path[len(STAGED_APPS):]] = path
            path = 'Applications/' + path[len(STAGED_APPS):]
        elif path.startswith('private/var/'):
            continue
        meta[path] = (mode, int(e.get('User ID') or 0), int(e.get('Group ID') or 0),
                      e.get('Symbolic Link', ''), int(e.get('Size') or 0))

    chosen = set()
    for path, (mode, uid, gid, target, size) in meta.items():
        if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
            keep = wanted_file(path, size)
        elif stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
            # a symlink costs nothing: keep every one that lives where we take anything at all
            keep = '/' not in path or path.startswith(WHOLE) and not path.startswith(SKIP_PREFIX)
        else:
            # (the sound plug-ins' too: Library/Audio is skipped but for AUDIO, and without its en.lproj the
            # virtual audio device's port names came out NULL -- mediaserverd died naming the microphone)
            lproj = re.search(r'/([^/]+)\.lproj$', path)
            keep = '/' not in path or path in ('private/var', 'private/tmp', 'private/etc', 'private/preboot',
                                               'private/xarts', 'private') or \
                bool(lproj) and lproj.group(1) in KEEP_LANG and \
                (path.startswith(WHOLE) and not path.startswith(SKIP_PREFIX) or
                 path.startswith(AUDIO) and not path.startswith(SKIP_AUDIO))
        if keep:
            chosen.add(path)
    # every directory on the way to something chosen
    for path in list(chosen):
        while '/' in path:
            path = path.rsplit('/', 1)[0]
            chosen.add(path)

    total = count = 0
    with open(files_out, 'w') as files, open(manifest_out, 'w') as manifest:
        for path in sorted(chosen):
            if path not in meta:
                continue
            mode, uid, gid, target, size = meta[path]
            manifest.write(f'{mode:o}\t{uid}\t{gid}\t{path}\t{target if stat.S_ISLNK(mode) else ""}\n')
            if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
                files.write(source.get(path, path) + '\n')
                total += size
                count += 1
    print(f'select-system: {count} files, {total / 1048576:.0f} MB; {len(chosen)} entries in the manifest')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`sysimage/unpack.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Unpack the files of Darwin userland 16.5 (20F66, iPhone X) that the system image is made of, out of an IPSW
# you have on your own disk, and lay them out the way ../userland/build.sh expects them:
#
#   rootfs/                  the chosen part of the root filesystem (see select-system.py)
#   system.files/.manifest   what was chosen, with owners, modes and symbolic links
#   var.skel                 the skeleton of /private/var (see mkvarskel.py)
#   cryptex/                 the OS cryptex without the dyld shared cache
#   cryptex-app.dmg          the App cryptex as it is in the IPSW (10 MB, an APFS container: Safari's
#                            daemons, its settings and the bundles around it, which the root volume's
#                            launchd jobs and links reach through /System/Cryptexes/App)
#   cryptex-app/             ... and its files
#   20F66__iPhone10,3_6/     the dyld shared cache (arm64)
#   DeviceTree.d22ap.im4p    the device tree, for ../xnuloader/mkidentity.sh
#
# The project ships no file of Apple's and downloads none. The IPSW is yours: get
# iPhone10,3,iPhone10,6_16.5_20F66_Restore.ipsw yourself (6 165 698 198 bytes) and give its path:
#
#   sysimage/unpack.sh ~/Downloads/iPhone10,3,iPhone10,6_16.5_20F66_Restore.ipsw
#   IPSW=... sysimage/unpack.sh              the same, from the environment (make unpack IPSW=...)
#
# The disk images are copied out of the IPSW (ipsw-member.py) and unpacked with 7z. Needs: python3,
# 7z (7-Zip 23 or newer: it reads APFS), cc. About 8 GB of disk while it runs, 5.3 GB afterwards.
#
#   KEEP=1   keep the copied disk images (rootfs.dmg is needed again only after changing
#            select-system.py; with it in place a second run does not read the IPSW for it)
set -e
IPSW=${1:-${IPSW:-}}
if [ -z "$IPSW" ]; then
	sed -n '16,20p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2
	echo "unpack.sh: give the path of your Darwin userland 16.5 IPSW" >&2
	exit 1
fi
[ -f "$IPSW" ] || { echo "unpack.sh: $IPSW: no such file" >&2; exit 1; }
IPSW=$(cd "$(dirname "$IPSW")" && pwd)/$(basename "$IPSW")
size=$(wc -c < "$IPSW" | tr -d ' ')
# select-system.py and the checks below are made for this one build; another IPSW would unpack, then fail somewhere later
if [ "$size" != 6165698198 ] && [ -z "${ANY_IPSW:-}" ]; then
	echo "unpack.sh: $IPSW is $size bytes, not the 6165698198 of Darwin userland 16.5 20F66 for iPhone10,3/10,6 (ANY_IPSW=1 tries it anyway)" >&2
	exit 1
fi
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
ROOTFS_DMG=096-04088-077.dmg                    # the root filesystem, APFS
CRYPTEX_DMG=096-04666-078.dmg                   # the OS cryptex: dyld shared cache and a few libraries
APP_CRYPTEX_DMG=096-03536-083.dmg               # the App cryptex (BuildManifest: Cryptex1,AppOS)
CACHE=20F66__iPhone10,3_6
UNZBM=../xnu-deps/host/bin/unzbm

for tool in python3 7z cc; do
	command -v $tool >/dev/null || { echo "unpack.sh: $tool is not installed"; exit 1; }
done
# 7z leaves files compressed with LZBITMAP as an empty file and two attribute files; unzbm finishes them
if [ ! -x $UNZBM ]; then
	mkdir -p "$(dirname $UNZBM)"
	cc -O2 -w -o $UNZBM ../xnu-deps/build/lzbitmap/unzbm.c ../xnu-deps/build/lzbitmap/libzbitmap.c
fi
unzbm_all() { # unzbm_all DIR: expand every LZBITMAP file below DIR
	find "$1" -type f -name '*:com.apple.decmpfs' | sed 's/:com\.apple\.decmpfs$//' | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 -r -n 200 $UNZBM
	local left
	left=$(find "$1" -name '*:com.apple.*' | wc -l)
	[ "$left" -eq 0 ] || { echo "unpack.sh: $left files in $1 are still compressed"; exit 1; }
}

# --- the root filesystem --------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ ! -f .done-rootfs ] || [ select-system.py -nt .done-rootfs ]; then
	if [ ! -f rootfs.dmg ]; then
		echo "unpack.sh: copying the root filesystem image out of the IPSW (4.7 GB)"
		python3 ipsw-member.py "$IPSW" $ROOTFS_DMG rootfs.dmg.part
		mv rootfs.dmg.part rootfs.dmg
	fi
	echo "unpack.sh: listing the image"
	7z l -slt rootfs.dmg > rootfs.slt
	python3 select-system.py rootfs.slt system.files system.manifest
	python3 mkvarskel.py rootfs.slt > var.skel
	echo "unpack.sh: extracting $(wc -l < system.files) files"
	rm -rf rootfs
	7z x -y -orootfs rootfs.dmg @system.files > extract-system.log
	# the two fonts too big for the image as they are, made smaller in place (see select-system.py)
	python3 ../tools/font_trim.py emoji rootfs/System/Library/Fonts/CoreAddition/AppleColorEmoji-160px.ttc \
		rootfs/System/Library/Fonts/CoreAddition/AppleColorEmoji-160px.ttc 40,64,96
	python3 ../tools/font_trim.py faces rootfs/System/Library/Fonts/LanguageSupport/PingFang.ttc \
		rootfs/System/Library/Fonts/LanguageSupport/PingFang.ttc '^\.?PingFang(SC|TC|HK)-(Regular|Semibold)$'
	touch .done-rootfs
	[ -n "$KEEP" ] || rm -f rootfs.dmg
fi

# --- the OS cryptex -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ ! -f .done-cryptex ]; then
	if [ ! -f cryptex-os.dmg ]; then
		echo "unpack.sh: copying the OS cryptex image out of the IPSW (2.7 GB)"
		python3 ipsw-member.py "$IPSW" $CRYPTEX_DMG cryptex-os.dmg.part
		mv cryptex-os.dmg.part cryptex-os.dmg
	fi
	echo "unpack.sh: extracting the cryptex"
	rm -rf cryptex cryptex.cache $CACHE
	# 7z reports every LZBITMAP file as an error ("Unsupported Method"): expected, unzbm_all checks the result
	7z x -y -ocryptex cryptex-os.dmg '-xr!com.apple.dyld' '-x!System/DriverKit' > extract-cryptex.log 2>&1 || true
	unzbm_all cryptex
	# the dyld shared cache; its .symbols file (0.6 GB) is never mapped and is left out
	7z x -y -ocryptex.cache cryptex-os.dmg System/Library/Caches/com.apple.dyld '-xr!*.symbols*' > extract-dyld.log 2>&1 || true
	unzbm_all cryptex.cache
	mv cryptex.cache/System/Library/Caches/com.apple.dyld $CACHE
	rm -rf cryptex.cache
	[ "$(ls $CACHE | wc -l)" -eq 43 ] || { echo "unpack.sh: the dyld shared cache is incomplete"; exit 1; }
	touch .done-cryptex
	[ -n "$KEEP" ] || rm -f cryptex-os.dmg
fi

# --- the App cryptex ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# kept as it is (the boot off the flash puts it in memory unchanged, ../userland/build.sh FLASHBOOT=1)
# and unpacked (the system image has its files at /System/Cryptexes/App)
if [ ! -f .done-cryptex-app ]; then
	if [ ! -f cryptex-app.dmg ]; then
		echo "unpack.sh: copying the App cryptex image out of the IPSW (10 MB)"
		python3 ipsw-member.py "$IPSW" $APP_CRYPTEX_DMG cryptex-app.dmg.part
		mv cryptex-app.dmg.part cryptex-app.dmg
	fi
	echo "unpack.sh: extracting the App cryptex"
	rm -rf cryptex-app
```
