```sh
	7z x -y -ocryptex-app cryptex-app.dmg > extract-cryptex-app.log 2>&1 || true
	unzbm_all cryptex-app
	[ -f cryptex-app/usr/libexec/webbookmarksd ] || { echo "unpack.sh: the App cryptex is incomplete"; exit 1; }
	touch .done-cryptex-app
fi
# --- the device tree, for xnuloader/mkidentity.sh -----------------------------------------------
[ -f DeviceTree.d22ap.im4p ] || python3 ipsw-member.py "$IPSW" Firmware/all_flash/DeviceTree.d22ap.im4p DeviceTree.d22ap.im4p
echo "unpack.sh: done: $(du -sh rootfs | cut -f1) rootfs, $(du -sh cryptex | cut -f1) cryptex, $(du -sh cryptex-app | cut -f1) App cryptex, $(du -sh $CACHE | cut -f1) dyld shared cache"

```

`tools/air/atomiccheck.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check the atomics with a kernel written for the purpose.

docs/air.md said what was missing and why none of Apple's kernels could supply
it: "a sum written by threads that never raced looks exactly like a sum written
by threads that did. Detecting a lost update needs the expected total to depend
on every thread having contributed -- which needs a kernel whose arithmetic is
known, i.e. one written for the purpose rather than one of Apple's." This is
that kernel.

It is generated as AIR, assembled with llvm-as and dispatched by air_run, which
runs 4x4 threads in one workgroup. Every thread does the same five things to two
device buffers whose initial bytes this script chooses (AIR_RUN_BUFFER).

What each part can show:

  [0] += 1 by every thread                  the total is the thread count
  [1] += the value loaded from [4]          atomic load returns what is there
  [2] = max(thread index)                   signed max, and the right operand
  [3] = min(thread index - 100)             signed min across negatives, which
                                            is where an unsigned min would
                                            answer 0xffffff9c-as-huge instead
  buf1[i] = old*16 + i + 1                  see below

The last one is the only part that can detect a lost update, and it does so
without depending on the order the threads ran in. If fetch_add is atomic, the
sixteen values it returned are the numbers 0..15 in some order -- a permutation
-- because each thread saw a different predecessor count. If two threads read
the same old value, the permutation has a duplicate and a gap, and the gap says
which increment was lost. Serial execution also produces a permutation, so this
passes on software by being correct rather than by being unopposed; what it
cannot do is *prove* atomicity on a machine that never ran the threads at once.
The +1 is so that a slot no thread wrote cannot look like a result, and the
*16 + i is so that a thread writing another thread's slot does not read as
correct either.

The operations tested are only the ones the corpus proves exist, read off its
own declarations: global add.s, load, max.s, min.s and store. air_intrinsics.c
also handles and, or, xor and xchg, and those are not tested here, because the
names Apple would emit for them are a guess and a test of a guessed name is a
test of the guess.

usage: atomiccheck.py [--keep DIR]
"""

import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
AIR_RUN = os.environ.get(
    "AIR_RUN",
    os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/air_run"),
)

THREADS = 16          # air_run dispatches GRID x GRID = 4x4 in one workgroup
LOADED = 7            # what sits in [4] for every thread to read

KERNEL = r'''source_filename = "atomics"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

declare i32 @air.atomic.global.add.s.i32(ptr addrspace(1), i32, i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr
declare i32 @air.atomic.global.load.i32(ptr addrspace(1), i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr
declare i32 @air.atomic.global.max.s.i32(ptr addrspace(1), i32, i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr
declare i32 @air.atomic.global.min.s.i32(ptr addrspace(1), i32, i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr
declare void @air.atomic.global.store.i32(ptr addrspace(1), i32, i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr

define void @atomics(ptr addrspace(1) %0, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i32 %2) local_unnamed_addr {
  ; [0] += 1: the returned old value is this thread's place in the queue
  %c0 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %0, i64 0
  %old = call i32 @air.atomic.global.add.s.i32(ptr addrspace(1) %c0, i32 1, i32 0, i32 2, i1 true)

  ; [1] += whatever [4] holds, loaded atomically
  %c4 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %0, i64 4
  %got = call i32 @air.atomic.global.load.i32(ptr addrspace(1) %c4, i32 0, i32 2, i1 true)
  %c1 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %0, i64 1
  %sum = call i32 @air.atomic.global.add.s.i32(ptr addrspace(1) %c1, i32 %got, i32 0, i32 2, i1 true)

  ; [2] = max(thread index), [3] = min(thread index - 100)
  %c2 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %0, i64 2
  %mx = call i32 @air.atomic.global.max.s.i32(ptr addrspace(1) %c2, i32 %2, i32 0, i32 2, i1 true)
  %neg = sub i32 %2, 100
  %c3 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %0, i64 3
  %mn = call i32 @air.atomic.global.min.s.i32(ptr addrspace(1) %c3, i32 %neg, i32 0, i32 2, i1 true)

  ; buf1[index] = old * 16 + index + 1, stored atomically
  %t0 = mul i32 %old, 16
  %t1 = add i32 %t0, %2
  %t2 = add i32 %t1, 1
  %w = zext i32 %2 to i64
  %p1 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i64 %w
  call void @air.atomic.global.store.i32(ptr addrspace(1) %p1, i32 %t2, i32 0, i32 2, i1 true)
  ret void
}

!llvm.module.flags = !{!0}
!air.version = !{!1}
!air.language_version = !{!2}
!air.kernel = !{!3}

!0 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
!1 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!2 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!3 = !{ptr @atomics, !4, !5}
!4 = !{}
!5 = !{!6, !7, !8}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 64, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"int", !"air.arg_name", !"counters"}
!7 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 64, !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"int", !"air.arg_name", !"queue"}
!8 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_index_in_threadgroup", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"tid"}
'''


# The threadgroup atomics and the barrier, which the kernel above cannot reach:
# they go through nir_shared_atomic and a different path for the memory.
#
# Threadgroup memory is not zeroed at dispatch -- neither Metal nor Mesa
# promises that -- so it has to be initialised, and every thread storing 0 to
# the same two words does it without needing a branch.
#
# Then every thread adds 1 to one word and 1 << its own index to the other, and
# after the second barrier reads both back and writes them to its own slot of
# two device buffers. So each of the sixteen slots must hold 16 and 0xffff:
#
#   a lost add leaves a bit clear in every slot, and the bit names the thread
#   whose increment went missing;
#   a barrier that did not wait leaves a *smaller* number in the slot of the
#   thread that ran ahead, and names that one instead.
LOCAL_KERNEL = r"""source_filename = "local_atomics"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

@tg = internal addrspace(3) global [2 x i32] undef

declare i32 @air.atomic.local.add.u.i32(ptr addrspace(3), i32, i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr
declare i32 @air.atomic.local.load.i32(ptr addrspace(3), i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr
declare void @air.atomic.local.store.i32(ptr addrspace(3), i32, i32, i32, i1) local_unnamed_addr
declare void @air.wg.barrier(i32, i32) local_unnamed_addr

define void @local_atomics(ptr addrspace(1) %0, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i32 %2) local_unnamed_addr {
  %t0 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x i32], ptr addrspace(3) @tg, i64 0, i64 0
  %t1 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x i32], ptr addrspace(3) @tg, i64 0, i64 1

  ; every thread stores 0 to both: idempotent, so no branch is needed to make
  ; one thread the initialiser
  call void @air.atomic.local.store.i32(ptr addrspace(3) %t0, i32 0, i32 0, i32 1, i1 true)
  call void @air.atomic.local.store.i32(ptr addrspace(3) %t1, i32 0, i32 0, i32 1, i1 true)
  call void @air.wg.barrier(i32 2, i32 1)

  %bit = shl i32 1, %2
  %o0 = call i32 @air.atomic.local.add.u.i32(ptr addrspace(3) %t0, i32 1, i32 0, i32 1, i1 true)
  %o1 = call i32 @air.atomic.local.add.u.i32(ptr addrspace(3) %t1, i32 %bit, i32 0, i32 1, i1 true)
  call void @air.wg.barrier(i32 2, i32 1)

  %v0 = call i32 @air.atomic.local.load.i32(ptr addrspace(3) %t0, i32 0, i32 1, i1 true)
  %v1 = call i32 @air.atomic.local.load.i32(ptr addrspace(3) %t1, i32 0, i32 1, i1 true)
  %w = zext i32 %2 to i64
  %p0 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %0, i64 %w
  %p1 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i64 %w
  store i32 %v0, ptr addrspace(1) %p0, align 4
  store i32 %v1, ptr addrspace(1) %p1, align 4
  ret void
}

!llvm.module.flags = !{!0}
!air.version = !{!1}
!air.language_version = !{!2}
!air.kernel = !{!3}

!0 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
!1 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!2 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!3 = !{ptr @local_atomics, !4, !5}
!4 = !{}
!5 = !{!6, !7, !8}
!6 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 64, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"int", !"air.arg_name", !"counts"}
!7 = !{i32 1, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 64, !"air.location_index", i32 1, i32 1, !"air.read_write", !"air.address_space", i32 1, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"int", !"air.arg_name", !"masks"}
!8 = !{i32 2, !"air.thread_index_in_threadgroup", !"air.arg_type_name", !"uint", !"air.arg_name", !"tid"}
"""


def initial_bytes():
    """What both buffers start as. Every word is chosen, none is left to the
    harness's pattern, so a slot nothing wrote reads as something invalid
    rather than as something plausible."""
    words = [0] * 16
    words[0] = 0               # the counter
    words[1] = 0               # the sum of the loaded values
    words[2] = 0               # max starts at 0; every thread index is >= 0
    words[3] = 2147483647      # min starts at INT_MAX
    words[4] = LOADED          # what every thread loads
    return b"".join(struct.pack("<i", w) for w in words)


def parse(out):
    """{buffer index: [words]} from air_run's readback."""
    bufs = {}
    cur = None
    for line in out.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"air_run: device buffer (\d+) after the dispatch", line)
        if m:
            cur = int(m.group(1))
            bufs[cur] = []
            continue
        if cur is not None:
            m = re.match(r"\s*\[\s*(\d+)\]\s+(\d+)\s+0x([0-9a-f]+)", line)
            if m:
                bufs[cur].append(int(m.group(3), 16))
            elif line.startswith("air_run:") and "device buffer" not in line:
                cur = None
    return bufs


def signed(u):
    return u - (1 << 32) if u >> 31 else u


def run_kernel(d, stem, source, data, env_extra=None):
    """Assemble one kernel, dispatch it, and return (buffers, screen, output)."""
    ll, bc, bin_ = (os.path.join(d, stem + e) for e in (".ll", ".bc", ".bin"))
    with open(ll, "w") as f:
        f.write(source)
    with open(bin_, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    q = subprocess.run(["llvm-as", "-o", bc, ll], capture_output=True)
    if q.returncode:
        return None, None, "llvm-as: " + q.stderr.decode().strip()
    q = subprocess.run([AIR_RUN, bc], capture_output=True,
                       env=dict(os.environ, AIR_RUN_BUFFER=bin_))
    out = q.stdout.decode() + q.stderr.decode()
    screen = "an unnamed screen"
    m = re.search(r"air_run: \S+ on (.+?), as a compute kernel", out)
    if m:
        screen = m.group(1)
    return parse(out), screen, out


def check_local(d):
    """The threadgroup atomics and the barrier. Returns a list of complaints."""
    # the initial bytes do not matter here: every slot is written by its own
    # thread and the threadgroup words are initialised by the kernel
    bufs, screen, out = run_kernel(d, "local", LOCAL_KERNEL,
                                   b"\0" * 64)
    if bufs is None or 0 not in bufs or 1 not in bufs:
        tail = "\n      ".join((out or "").strip().splitlines()[-5:])
        return ["the threadgroup kernel did not read both buffers back:\n      " + tail]
    bad = []
    for i in range(THREADS):
        if bufs[0][i] != THREADS:
            bad.append("thread %-2d saw %d of %d increments: the barrier did not wait"
                       % (i, bufs[0][i], THREADS))
        want = (1 << THREADS) - 1
        if bufs[1][i] != want:
            missing = [b for b in range(THREADS) if not bufs[1][i] & (1 << b)]
            bad.append("thread %-2d saw mask 0x%08x, want 0x%08x: nothing from thread%s %s"
                       % (i, bufs[1][i], want, "" if len(missing) == 1 else "s",
                          ", ".join(str(b) for b in missing)))
    return bad


def main(argv):
    keep = None
    if len(argv) >= 2 and argv[0] == "--keep":
        keep = argv[1]
    if not os.path.exists(AIR_RUN):
        print("atomiccheck: no air_run at %s (run tools/air/mk-host.sh)" % AIR_RUN,
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    d = keep or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="atomiccheck.")
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)

    bufs, screen, out = run_kernel(d, "atomics", KERNEL, initial_bytes())
    if bufs is None or 0 not in bufs or 1 not in bufs:
        print("atomiccheck: the dispatch did not read both buffers back:")
        for line in (out or "").strip().splitlines()[-6:]:
            print("  " + line)
        return 1

    c, queue = bufs[0], bufs[1]
    bad = []

    def want(label, got, exp):
        if got != exp:
            bad.append("%-34s got %-12s want %s" % (label, got, exp))

    want("[0] threads that incremented", c[0], THREADS)
    want("[1] sum of the loaded value", c[1], THREADS * LOADED)
    want("[2] max of the thread indices", c[2], THREADS - 1)
    want("[3] min of index - 100", signed(c[3]), -100)
    want("[4] the loaded value, untouched", c[4], LOADED)

    # the permutation: every slot written by its own thread, and the old values
    # the sixteen fetch_adds returned being 0..15 with nothing repeated
    olds = []
    for i in range(THREADS):
        v = queue[i]
        if v == 0:
            bad.append("queue[%-2d] no thread wrote it" % i)
            continue
        if (v - 1) % 16 != i:
            bad.append("queue[%-2d] was written by thread %d" % (i, (v - 1) % 16))
            continue
        o = (v - 1) // 16
        if not 0 <= o < THREADS:
            # the whole set being shifted is what returning the new value
            # instead of the old looks like, so say that rather than leave it
            # to be read off a missing element
            bad.append("queue[%-2d] was given %d, which is not a predecessor count "
                       "of %d threads" % (i, o, THREADS))
        olds.append(o)
    if len(olds) == THREADS and sorted(olds) != list(range(THREADS)):
        seen = {}
        for i, o in enumerate(olds):
            seen.setdefault(o, []).append(i)
        for o in sorted(seen):
            if len(seen[o]) > 1:
                bad.append("fetch_add returned %d to threads %s: a lost update"
                           % (o, ", ".join(str(t) for t in seen[o])))
        for o in range(THREADS):
            if o not in seen:
                bad.append("no thread was given %d: that increment went missing" % o)

    local_bad = check_local(d)
    bad += local_bad

    for line in bad:
        print("WRONG   " + line)
    print()
    if bad:
        print("atomiccheck: %d of the checks failed on %s" % (len(bad), screen))
        return 1
    print("atomiccheck: the eight atomic operations the corpus uses agree, on %s" % screen)
    print("atomiccheck: five on device memory, three on threadgroup memory across two")
    print("atomiccheck: barriers, every thread seeing all sixteen contributions")
    print("atomiccheck: %d threads each incremented once and were given a distinct"
          % THREADS)
    print("atomiccheck: predecessor count, 0 to %d, so no update was lost" % (THREADS - 1))
    if "softpipe" in screen or "software" in screen:
        print("atomiccheck: the two barriers are really under test here: softpipe advances its")
        print("atomiccheck: invocations in groups of four, so with the barrier made a no-op")
        print("atomiccheck: every thread sees 4 of 16 increments and this says so.")
        print("atomiccheck: ATOMICITY still is not tested. Softpipe applies a group's atomic")
        print("atomiccheck: lane by lane, so it cannot lose an update however the lowering is")
        print("atomiccheck: written. That needs the GPU, where sixteen threads really do race.")
    if keep:
        print("atomiccheck: kept in %s" % d)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

```

`tools/air/check.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# The frontend's whole test run, in the order of what it proves (docs/air.md
# section 4): first that the bitcode reader agrees with LLVM on every module of
# the corpus, then how far every module gets through translation and ir3.
#
# This is the project's CI. There is no hosted one -- the corpus is Apple's
# code and stays off the network -- so this runs before every commit that
# touches the frontend, and docs/air-report.md is the report of that commit.
#
#   tools/air/check.sh            check, and write docs/air-report.md
#   tools/air/check.sh -q         only the numbers, write nothing
set -e
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/../.." && pwd)
DARWIN=${DARWIN:-$ROOT/sysimage}
QUIET=0
[ "${1:-}" = "-q" ] && QUIET=1

# The corpus: the MTLB libraries of the device image. The five are named rather
# than searched for, so a missing one is an error and not a smaller corpus.
LIBS=(
	"$DARWIN/rootfs/System/Library/VideoDecoders/AV1SW.metallib"
	"$DARWIN/rootfs/System/Library/Extensions/AppleMetalGLRenderer.bundle/default.metallib"
	"$DARWIN/rootfs/System/Library/CoreImage/PortraitFilters.cifilter/default.metallib"
	"$DARWIN/rootfs/System/Library/CoreImage/PortraitFilters.cifilter/portrait_filters.metallib"
)
# SafariSharedUI's default.metallib is in the corpus list of docs/air.md and is
# deliberately not here: it is 118 bytes and holds no functions at all.
for f in "${LIBS[@]}"; do
	[ -f "$f" ] || { echo "check.sh: missing $f"; exit 1; }
done

AIR2NIR=$ROOT/build/mesa-host/build/src/compiler/air/air2nir
[ -x "$AIR2NIR" ] || { echo "check.sh: run tools/air/mk-host.sh first"; exit 1; }

WORK=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

echo "== the reader against llvm-dis"
for f in "${LIBS[@]}"; do
	python3 "$ROOT/tools/metallib.py" dump "$f" "$WORK/$(basename "$(dirname "$f")")" > /dev/null
done
"$ROOT/tools/air/reader-check.sh" "$WORK" | tail -3
reader_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

echo
echo "== translation and ir3, over the corpus"
if [ "$QUIET" = 1 ]; then
	python3 "$ROOT/tools/air/corpus.py" --ir3 --md /dev/null "${LIBS[@]}"
else
	python3 "$ROOT/tools/air/corpus.py" --ir3 \
		--md "$ROOT/docs/air-report.md" --json "$ROOT/build/air-report.json" "${LIBS[@]}"
	echo "check.sh: wrote docs/air-report.md"
fi

echo
echo "== against LLVM on the processor, and drawn, shader by shader"
# The strongest check there is, and it needs no GPU: LLVM runs the same module
# over the same buffer bytes, our NIR is folded over them, and the numbers are
# compared. Only the class where this is decidable -- an entry point whose
# arguments are all buffers and which returns its result -- is counted; the
# rest say why not. --draw also puts each one through a Gallium driver and
# compares the pixel that comes back, which is M1's acceptance test with
# softpipe standing in for the Adreno. See tools/air/cpuref.py and air_run.c.
cpu_rc=0
for f in "${LIBS[@]}"; do
	echo "$(basename "$(dirname "$f")")/$(basename "$f"):"
	python3 "$ROOT/tools/air/cpuref.py" --all --draw "$f" 2>&1 | tail -3 | sed 's/^/  /' ||
		cpu_rc=1
done

echo
echo "== the air.* operations, one at a time"
# The section above ends with "0 call an air.* function", which is the whole
# reason this one exists: a module that agrees with LLVM proves the reader and
# the instructions, and says nothing about the intrinsics, because LLVM cannot
# evaluate a call it has no body for. So each operation is called on its own
# here, on inputs chosen to break it, against a reference in the script.
python3 "$ROOT/tools/air/intrincheck.py" 2>&1 | tail -8
intrin_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

echo
echo "== the same operations run, not folded"
# A different check and not a slower one: folding asks NIR's constant
# expression, this builds the arguments into a buffer so nothing can be folded
# and hands the shader to a driver that compiles and executes it. That is how
# air.sign(-0) was caught -- NIR's folder keeps the sign of a zero, softpipe
# does not, and nir_fsign promises neither.
#
# --cases 4 and not the whole pool: 612 cases in 79 seconds against 2586 in
# 300, and it still catches that bug, which is how the subset was chosen rather
# than guessed. The full run is `intrincheck.py --run --few`.
python3 "$ROOT/tools/air/intrincheck.py" --run --cases 4 2>&1 | tail -6
run_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

echo
echo "== the atomics, with a kernel written to make a lost update show"
# None of Apple's kernels can test an atomic: a sum written by threads that
# never raced reads the same as one written by threads that did. This one
# dispatches sixteen threads whose fetch_add results must be the numbers 0..15
# with nothing repeated, so a lost update leaves a duplicate and a gap.
python3 "$ROOT/tools/air/atomiccheck.py" 2>&1 | tail -8
atomic_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

echo
echo "== the texture operations, on more than one texel"
# texcheck.sh runs the corpus's own texture shaders, which all sample texel
# (1, 1) because that is where air_run's vertex shader puts the coordinate: a
# lowering that ignored the coordinate and always fetched (1, 1) would pass all
# six of them. These ask for the corners too, so swapping x and y is caught on
# the five asymmetric coordinates and correctly not on the symmetric ones.
python3 "$ROOT/tools/air/texopcheck.py" 2>&1 | tail -10
texop_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

exit $((reader_rc | cpu_rc | intrin_rc | run_rc | atomic_rc | texop_rc))

```

`tools/air/corpus.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The corpus report: how far every module of every .metallib gets.

This is the project's progress meter (docs/air.md section 5). Each module goes
through stages, and each module is counted under the first one it fails:

  container   found in the .metallib and unwrapped
  reader      our bitcode reader read it (and agrees with llvm-dis: that is
              checked separately, by tools/air/reader-check.sh)
  translate   air_to_nir produced a shader and nir_validate passed
  ir3         ir3 compiled it for the Adreno without error

Nothing here says a shader is correct: that needs the CPU reference and a run
on the GPU. A module that reaches ir3 has compiled, which is not the same
thing, and the report never claims otherwise.

usage: corpus.py [--ir3] [--json FILE] [--md FILE] FILE.metallib...
"""
import argparse
import collections
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
AIR2NIR = os.environ.get(
    "AIR2NIR", os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/compiler/air/air2nir"))
IR3 = os.environ.get(
    "IR3", os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/ir3_compiler"))
# the redwood's Adreno 7c+ Gen 3 (A635), as freedreno names it
CHIP_ID = os.environ.get("AIR_CHIP_ID", "0x007506030500")


def refuse_if_stale(prog, what):
    """A tool older than the frontend it contains is measuring the past.

    ir3_compiler is not in the host build's default target, so a plain
    `ninja -C build/mesa-host/build` leaves it as it was while air2nir beside
    it is rebuilt. That produced a column of numbers from the old frontend and
    a translate column from the new one: on 20 October the two read 315 and
    313, and the missing two looked like modules ir3 could not compile. They
    compiled perfectly; the compiler was six hours old. Both columns came from
    the same table and only one of them was current, which is the worst case --
    a stale tool whose output is plausible beside a fresh one.

    So the age is checked rather than assumed, against every source of the
    frontend, and the run is refused instead of warned: a number nobody can
    trust is worse than no number.
    """
    if not os.path.exists(prog):
        return
    src = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools/mesa/air")
    newest, name = 0.0, None
    for f in os.listdir(src):
        if f.endswith((".c", ".h")):
            t = os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(src, f))
            if t > newest:
                newest, name = t, f
    if newest and os.path.getmtime(prog) < newest:
        print("corpus.py: %s is older than tools/mesa/air/%s, so its column would be "
              "the previous frontend's. Build it: ninja -C build/mesa-host/build %s"
              % (what, name, os.path.relpath(prog, os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build"))),
              file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


def read_report(paths):
    """air2nir --report, which forks per module so one crash is one line."""
    rows = []
    for path in paths:
        out = subprocess.run([AIR2NIR, "--report", path], capture_output=True, text=True)
        for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
            if not line.startswith("module="):
                continue
            row = dict(kv.split("=", 1) for kv in line.split("\t") if "=" in kv)
            # two of the five libraries are both called default.metallib, so
            # the label carries the bundle they are in
            row["library"] = os.path.join(os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path)),
                                          os.path.basename(path))
            row["path"] = path
            row["calls"] = [c for c in row.get("calls", "").split(",") if c]
            rows.append(row)
    return rows


def run_ir3(rows):
    """ir3 on every module that translated, one process each."""
    for row in rows:
        if row.get("translate") != "ok":
            continue
        out = subprocess.run([IR3, "--chip-id", CHIP_ID, row["path"], row["module"]],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        if out.returncode == 0:
            row["ir3"] = "ok"
            for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
                # "; FRAG prog 0/0: 5 instr, 0 nops, ..."
                if " prog " in line and " instr," in line:
                    row["ir3_instr"] = int(line.split(":")[1].split()[0])
                    break
        else:
            row["ir3"] = "fail"
            err = (out.stderr or out.stdout).strip().splitlines()
            row["ir3_error"] = err[-1][:200] if err else "no message"


def reason(row):
    if row.get("crash"):
        return "crashed: " + row["crash"]
    if row.get("reader") != "ok":
        return row.get("error", "reader failed")
    if row.get("translate") != "ok":
        return row.get("error", "translation failed")
    if row.get("ir3") == "fail":
        return "ir3: " + row.get("ir3_error", "")
    return None


def short_reason(r):
    """Group reasons so the table ranks causes, not instances."""
    if r is None:
        return None
    r = r.split(" (block ")[0]
    if r.startswith("intrinsic: air."):
        name = r.split("intrinsic: ")[1].split("(")[0].strip()
        # air.sample_texture_2d.v4f16 -> air.sample_texture_2d
        base = name.split(".")
        if len(base) > 2:
            name = ".".join(base[:2]) if base[1] in ("atomic", "wg") else ".".join(base[:2])
        return "intrinsic: " + name
    return r


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("libs", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--ir3", action="store_true", help="also compile through ir3")
    ap.add_argument("--json")
    ap.add_argument("--md")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    rows = read_report(args.libs)
    if not rows:
        sys.exit("corpus.py: no modules; is %s built?" % AIR2NIR)
    if args.ir3:
        refuse_if_stale(IR3, "ir3_compiler")
        run_ir3(rows)

    total = len(rows)
    stages = collections.OrderedDict()
    stages["container"] = total
    stages["reader"] = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("reader") == "ok")
    stages["translate"] = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("translate") == "ok")
    if args.ir3:
        stages["ir3"] = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("ir3") == "ok")

    by_stage = collections.Counter(r.get("stage", "?") for r in rows)
    ok_by_stage = collections.Counter(r.get("stage", "?") for r in rows
                                      if r.get("translate") == "ok")
    ir3_by_stage = collections.Counter(r.get("stage", "?") for r in rows
                                       if r.get("ir3") == "ok")
    reasons = collections.Counter(short_reason(reason(r)) for r in rows
                                  if reason(r) is not None)
    intrinsics = collections.Counter(c for r in rows for c in r["calls"])
    no_intrinsics = [r for r in rows if not r["calls"]]

    out = []
    out.append("# AIR corpus report\n")
    out.append("What every module of the system's Metal libraries does when put through the\n"
               "frontend. Generated by `tools/air/corpus.py`; see docs/air.md section 5 for\n"
               "what the stages mean. **Reaching ir3 means it compiled, not that it is\n"
               "correct**: correctness needs the CPU reference and a run on the GPU.\n")
    out.append("## Stages\n")
    out.append("| stage | modules | of %d |" % total)
    out.append("| --- | --- | --- |")
    for name, n in stages.items():
        out.append("| %s | %d | %.0f%% |" % (name, n, 100.0 * n / total))
    out.append("")

    out.append("## By stage of the shader\n")
    out.append("| what the module is | modules | translate | ir3 |")
    out.append("| --- | --- | --- | --- |")
    for st in sorted(by_stage):
        out.append("| %s | %d | %d | %s |" % (st, by_stage[st], ok_by_stage[st],
                                              ir3_by_stage[st] if args.ir3 else "-"))
    out.append("")

    # The container's TYPE tag and the module's own metadata are two
    # independent statements of what a function is; if they ever disagree, one
    # of the two readings is wrong and the report says so rather than picking.
    same = {"vertex": "vertex", "fragment": "fragment", "kernel": "kernel",
            "visible": "visible"}
    mismatch = [r for r in rows
                if r.get("container") in same and r.get("stage")
                and same[r["container"]] != r.get("stage")]
    out.append("The container's TYPE tag agrees with the module's own metadata on %d of %d; "
               "%d disagree.\n" % (total - len(mismatch), total, len(mismatch)))
    for r in mismatch[:20]:
        out.append("- `%s`: container says %s, metadata says %s" %
                   (r["module"], r["container"], r["stage"]))
    if mismatch:
        out.append("")

    out.append("## By library\n")
    out.append("| library | modules | translate | ir3 |")
    out.append("| --- | --- | --- | --- |")
    for lib in sorted({r["library"] for r in rows}):
        rs = [r for r in rows if r["library"] == lib]
        out.append("| %s | %d | %d | %s |" % (
            lib, len(rs), sum(1 for r in rs if r.get("translate") == "ok"),
            sum(1 for r in rs if r.get("ir3") == "ok") if args.ir3 else "-"))
    out.append("")

    out.append("## Modules that call no `air.*` at all\n")
    out.append("%d of %d (%.0f%%), of which %d translate and %s compile through ir3.\n" % (
        len(no_intrinsics), total, 100.0 * len(no_intrinsics) / total,
        sum(1 for r in no_intrinsics if r.get("translate") == "ok"),
        sum(1 for r in no_intrinsics if r.get("ir3") == "ok") if args.ir3 else "-"))

    if reasons:
        out.append("## What is not handled yet, by how many modules it stops\n")
        out.append("| modules | where it stops |")
        out.append("| --- | --- |")
        for why, n in reasons.most_common():
            out.append("| %d | %s |" % (n, why.replace("|", "\\|")))
        out.append("")

    if intrinsics:
        out.append("## The `air.*` functions the corpus calls\n")
        out.append("%d distinct names in %d modules.\n" % (
            len(intrinsics), sum(1 for r in rows if r["calls"])))
        out.append("| calls | name |")
        out.append("| --- | --- |")
        for name, n in intrinsics.most_common():
            out.append("| %d | `%s` |" % (n, name))
        out.append("")

    text = "\n".join(out)
    if args.md:
        with open(args.md, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
    else:
        print(text)
    if args.json:
        with open(args.json, "w") as f:
            json.dump({"total": total, "stages": stages, "rows": rows}, f, indent=1)

    print("corpus.py: %s" % ", ".join("%s %d/%d" % (k, v, total) for k, v in stages.items()),
          file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/air/cpuref.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The CPU reference: run an AIR shader through LLVM on this machine.

This is the strongest check the project has (docs/air.md section 4) and it
needs no Apple hardware and no GPU. LLVM -- not our reader and not our
translator -- decides what the shader means:

  1. the module's triple is changed to the host's and llc compiles it,
  2. a harness is generated from the entry point's own metadata: one buffer
     per air.buffer argument, filled with a seeded pattern, and the result
     printed field by field,
  3. the same shader goes through our frontend, and the two results are
     compared.

Step 3 is not automatic for every shader: a fragment shader's result depends
on where it is in the buffer, and only the GPU knows that. What is automatic
is the class this covers -- an entry point whose arguments are all constant or
device buffers and whose result is a struct of vectors, which is 256 of the
corpus's 271 fragment shaders. For those the NIR is interpreted here too, by
nir_opt_constant_folding on a shader whose buffer loads have been replaced
with the harness's bytes, so both sides are numbers and the comparison is
exact.

usage: cpuref.py FILE[.metallib] [FUNCTION]      run and print LLVM's result
       cpuref.py --compare FILE [FUNCTION]       and compare against our NIR
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "tools"))
import metallib  # noqa: E402

AIR2NIR = os.environ.get(
    "AIR2NIR", os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/compiler/air/air2nir"))
AIR_RUN = os.environ.get(
    "AIR_RUN",
    os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/air_run"))

# The pattern every buffer is filled with. Arbitrary, but fixed and not all
# zeros: a shader that ignores its input and one that reads it must differ.
def pattern(n):
    return bytes((i * 7 + 13) & 0xff for i in range(n))


class CType:
    """One LLVM type, as C and as a struct.unpack format."""

    def __init__(self, c, fmt, size):
        self.c, self.fmt, self.size = c, fmt, size


SCALARS = {
    "float": CType("float", "f", 4),
    "half": CType("unsigned short", "H", 2),   # no C half; compared as bits
    "double": CType("double", "d", 8),
    "i1": CType("unsigned char", "B", 1),
    "i8": CType("unsigned char", "B", 1),
    "i16": CType("unsigned short", "H", 2),
    "i32": CType("unsigned int", "I", 4),
    "i64": CType("unsigned long long", "Q", 8),
}


def parse_type(t):
    """<4 x float> -> (CType, 4); float -> (CType, 1)."""
    t = t.strip()
    m = re.match(r"<(\d+) x (.+)>$", t)
    if m:
        base = SCALARS.get(m.group(2).strip())
        return (base, int(m.group(1))) if base else (None, 0)
    base = SCALARS.get(t)
    return (base, 1) if base else (None, 0)


def param_type(t):
    """The type out of a define's parameter: "<4 x float> %0" -> "<4 x float>".

    Taken as the leading type rather than by stripping a list of attribute
    words: LLVM has dozens of parameter attributes and they sit between the
    type and the name, so a blacklist misses one -- "returned" was the one that
    made a library function unreadable here, and the next version of LLVM would
    have found another.
    """
    m = re.match(r"\s*(<\s*\d+\s+x\s+[A-Za-z_0-9]+\s*>|\[[^\]]*\]|[A-Za-z_0-9]+)",
                 t)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", m.group(1)).strip() if m else t.strip()


def split_fields(s):
    """The top-level comma-separated members of a struct body."""
    out, depth, cur = [], 0, ""
    for ch in s:
        if ch in "<[{":
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ">]}":
            depth -= 1
        if ch == "," and depth == 0:
            out.append(cur)
            cur = ""
        else:
            cur += ch
    if cur.strip():
        out.append(cur)
    return out


def disassemble(bc_path):
    return subprocess.run(["llvm-dis", "-o", "-", bc_path], capture_output=True,
                          text=True, check=True).stdout


def entry_of(ll):
    """The entry point's name, its parameter types and its result type."""
    stage = None
    for name in ("vertex", "fragment", "kernel", "visible"):
        if re.search(r"^!air\.%s = " % name, ll, re.M):
            stage = name
            break
    m = re.search(r"^define[^@\n]*@([A-Za-z_0-9.$]+)\(([^)]*)\)[^\n]*\{$", ll, re.M)
    if not m:
        return None
    # the LAST define is not necessarily the entry point; find the one the
    # metadata names
    ep = re.search(r"^!air\.(?:vertex|fragment|kernel|visible) = !\{!(\d+)\}", ll, re.M)
    if ep:
        node = re.search(r"^!%s = !\{ptr @([A-Za-z_0-9.$]+)," % ep.group(1), ll, re.M)
        if node:
            want = node.group(1)
            for m2 in re.finditer(r"^define([^@\n]*)@([A-Za-z_0-9.$]+)\(([^)]*)\)[^\n]*\{$",
                                  ll, re.M):
                if m2.group(2) == want:
                    m = m2
                    break
    ret = m.group(1).strip().split()[-1] if m.group(1).strip() else "void"
    # "define <{ <4 x float> }> @f(...)": the return type may contain spaces
    head = ll[m.start():m.start(1) + len(m.group(1))]
    ret = head[len("define"):].strip()
    for word in ("local_unnamed_addr", "internal", "fastcc", "unnamed_addr", "dso_local"):
        ret = ret.replace(word, "").strip()
    return dict(stage=stage, name=m.group(2), params=split_fields(m.group(3)), ret=ret)


def buffer_args(ll, entry):
    """Which parameters are buffers, from the entry-point metadata."""
    ep = re.search(r"^!air\.(?:vertex|fragment|kernel|visible) = !\{!(\d+)\}", ll, re.M)
    if not ep:
        return {}
    node = re.search(r"^!%s = !\{ptr @[^,]+, !(\d+), !(\d+)" % ep.group(1), ll, re.M)
    if not node:
        return {}
    ins = re.search(r"^!%s = !\{([^}]*)\}" % node.group(2), ll, re.M)
    if not ins:
        return {}
    out = {}
    for ref in re.findall(r"!(\d+)", ins.group(1)):
        line = re.search(r"^!%s = !\{(.*)\}$" % ref, ll, re.M)
        if not line:
            continue
        body = line.group(1)
        pm = re.match(r"\s*i32 (\d+)", body)
        if not pm or '"air.buffer"' not in body:
            continue
        size = re.search(r'"air\.buffer_size", i32 (\d+)', body)
        out[int(pm.group(1))] = int(size.group(1)) if size else 256
    return out


# Apple's name for each type, from the air.visible_input/output metadata beside
# a library function. It is a second statement of what the arguments are: the
# LLVM signature says <4 x float>, the metadata says float4, and a harness that
# agrees with only one of them is guessing. parse_type reads the LLVM side; this
# reads Apple's, and the two are checked against each other before anything runs.
APPLE_TYPES = {
    "float": ("float", 1), "float2": ("float", 2),
    "float3": ("float", 3), "float4": ("float", 4),
    "half": ("half", 1), "half2": ("half", 2),
    "half3": ("half", 3), "half4": ("half", 4),
}


def library_types(ll):
    """(inputs, output) as Apple names them, in parameter order."""
    ins = {}
    for body in re.findall(r"^!\d+ = !\{(.*)\}$", ll, re.M):
        if '"air.visible_input"' in body:
            pm = re.match(r"\s*i32 (\d+)", body)
            tn = re.search(r'"air\.arg_type_name", !"([^"]*)"', body)
            if pm and tn:
                ins[int(pm.group(1))] = tn.group(1)
    out = None
    for body in re.findall(r"^!\d+ = !\{(.*)\}$", ll, re.M):
        if '"air.visible_output"' in body:
            tn = re.search(r'"air\.arg_type_name", !"([^"]*)"', body)
            if tn:
                out = tn.group(1)
    return [ins.get(i) for i in range(len(ins))], out


def check_against_metadata(entry, ll):
    """Refuse when the LLVM types and Apple's names do not say the same thing."""
    names, out = library_types(ll)
    if len(names) != len(entry["params"]):
        return ("the metadata names %d arguments and the signature has %d"
                % (len(names), len(entry["params"])))
    for i, (t, name) in enumerate(zip(entry["params"], names)):
        base, n = parse_type(param_type(t))
        if base is None:
            return "argument %d is %s, which this harness cannot make" % (i, param_type(t))
        if name is None:
            return "argument %d has no air.arg_type_name" % i
        want = APPLE_TYPES.get(name)
        if want is None:
            return "argument %d is called %s, a type this harness does not make" % (i, name)
        if (want[0] == "float") != (base.fmt == "f") or want[1] != n:
            return ("argument %d is %s in the signature and %s in the metadata"
                    % (i, param_type(t), name))
    if out is not None and out not in APPLE_TYPES:
        return "the result is called %s, which this harness cannot read" % out
    return None


def build_and_run(ll, entry, bufs, workdir, library=False):
    """Compile the module for this machine and call the entry point.

    The call is made from a wrapper written in LLVM IR, not from C. A shader
    returns a struct of vectors by value, and how llc lowers that is its own
    business -- a C declaration of "the same" struct is not guaranteed to
    agree, and for anything past a single vector it does not. So LLVM compiles
    both sides of that call, the wrapper stores each result field into a flat
    buffer, and the only thing C ever sees is void(const void *, void *).
    """
    ret = entry["ret"].strip()
    body = re.match(r"<?\{(.*)\}>?$", ret)
    members = split_fields(body.group(1)) if body else ([ret] if ret != "void" else [])
    fields = []
    for i, t in enumerate(members):
        base, n = parse_type(t)
        if base is None:
            return None, "result field %d is %s, which this harness cannot read" % (i, t)
        fields.append((base, n, t.strip()))
    if not fields:
        return None, "the entry point returns nothing to compare"

    # A library function takes values, not buffers, so the wrapper reads each
    # argument out of one buffer at byte 16*i -- the same slot the frontend's
    # generated entry point reads it from (wrap_library_function in
    # air_to_nir.c). Both sides read the same offsets, so this comparison
    # cannot catch a slot layout that is wrong in the same way twice; what it
    # does catch is the two sides disagreeing about which slot is which
    # argument, because the pattern makes every slot's bytes different.
    if library:
        wrap_params, call_args, pre = ["ptr %in"], [], []
        for i, t in enumerate(entry["params"]):
            t = param_type(t)
            pre.append("  %%g%d = getelementptr i8, ptr %%in, i64 %d" % (i, 16 * i))
            pre.append("  %%a%d = load %s, ptr %%g%d, align 16" % (i, t, i))
            call_args.append("%s %%a%d" % (t, i))
        return _finish(ll, entry, {0: 16 * max(len(entry["params"]), 1)}, workdir,
                       fields, ret, wrap_params, call_args, pre, True)

    # the wrapper's own arguments: one pointer per buffer, and the output
    wrap_params, call_args, pre = [], [], []
    for i, t in enumerate(entry["params"]):
        t = t.strip()
        if "ptr" in t:
            if i not in bufs:
                return None, "parameter %d is a pointer that is not a buffer" % i
            wrap_params.append("ptr %%in%d" % i)
            m = re.search(r"addrspace\((\d+)\)", t)
            if m:
                pre.append("  %%p%d = addrspacecast ptr %%in%d to ptr addrspace(%s)"
                           % (i, i, m.group(1)))
                call_args.append("ptr addrspace(%s) %%p%d" % (m.group(1), i))
            else:
                call_args.append("ptr %%in%d" % i)
        else:
            base, n = parse_type(t)
            if base is None:
                return None, "parameter %d is %s, which this harness cannot make" % (i, t)
            # a non-buffer argument (a varying, a vertex id) is zero: what it
            # really is only the GPU knows, so such a shader is not compared
            return None, "parameter %d is %s, not a buffer" % (i, t)

    return _finish(ll, entry, bufs, workdir, fields, ret, wrap_params, call_args, pre)


def _finish(ll, entry, bufs, workdir, fields, ret, wrap_params, call_args, pre,
            library=False):
    """Compile the wrapper and the C harness around it, and run them."""
    # store each field at its own 16-byte slot of the output buffer. A shader
    # returns a struct of fields and each one is extracted; a library function
    # returns one value and there is nothing to extract -- extractvalue on a
    # vector is not valid IR, and llc says so with a caret and no sentence.
    is_struct = bool(re.match(r"<?\{", ret.strip()))
    stores, slots = [], []
    for i, (base, n, t) in enumerate(fields):
        if is_struct:
            stores.append("  %%f%d = extractvalue %s %%r, %d" % (i, ret, i))
        else:
            stores.append("  %%f%d = bitcast %s %%r to %s" % (i, t, t))
        stores.append("  %%o%d = getelementptr i8, ptr %%out, i64 %d" % (i, i * 16))
        stores.append("  store %s %%f%d, ptr %%o%d, align 1" % (t, i, i))
        slots.append((base, n))

    wrapper = """
define void @__cpuref_call(%s, ptr %%out) {
%s
  %%r = call %s @%s(%s)
%s
  ret void
}
""" % (", ".join(wrap_params + []) if wrap_params else "ptr %unused",
       "\n".join(pre), ret, entry["name"], ", ".join(call_args), "\n".join(stores))

    host_ll = os.path.join(workdir, "m.ll")
    with open(host_ll, "w") as f:
        f.write(re.sub(r'target triple = "[^"]*"',
                       'target triple = "%s"' % host_triple(), ll))
        f.write(wrapper)
    obj = os.path.join(workdir, "m.o")
    llc = subprocess.run(["llc", "-filetype=obj", "-o", obj, host_ll],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    if llc.returncode:
        last = (llc.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()
        return None, "llc refused it: " + (last[-1][:140] if last else "no message")

    setup, args = [], []
    for i in sorted(bufs):
        setup.append("    static unsigned char buf%d[%d];" % (i, bufs[i]))
        if library:
            # floats, not bytes: these modules are compiled with no-nans and
            # no-infs, so arbitrary bytes put the call outside the contract it
            # was compiled under. The same words air2nir and air_run use
            # (library_byte in both).
            setup.append("    for (int w = 0; w < %d; w++) {"
                         " float f = (float)((w * 13) %% 29 - 14) / 4.0f;"
                         " __builtin_memcpy(buf%d + 4 * w, &f, 4); }"
                         % (bufs[i] // 4, i))
        else:
            setup.append("    for (int i = 0; i < %d; i++) buf%d[i] = (i * 7 + 13) & 0xff;"
                         % (bufs[i], i))
        args.append("buf%d" % i)
    decl = ", ".join(["const void *"] * len(args) + ["void *"]) if args else "void *"

    prints = []
    for i, (base, n) in enumerate(slots):
        for k in range(n):
            at = "out + %d" % (i * 16 + k * base.size)
            if base.fmt == "f":
                prints.append('    { float v; __builtin_memcpy(&v, %s, 4);'
                              ' printf("%%.9g\\n", (double)v); }' % at)
            elif base.fmt == "d":
                prints.append('    { double v; __builtin_memcpy(&v, %s, 8);'
                              ' printf("%%.17g\\n", v); }' % at)
            else:
                prints.append('    { %s v; __builtin_memcpy(&v, %s, %d);'
                              ' printf("%%llu\\n", (unsigned long long)v); }'
                              % (base.c, at, base.size))

    src = """#include <stdio.h>
extern void __cpuref_call(%s);
int main(void) {
%s
    static unsigned char out[%d];
    __cpuref_call(%s);
%s
    return 0;
}
""" % (decl, "\n".join(setup), max(16 * len(fields), 16),
       ", ".join(args + ["out"]) if args else "out", "\n".join(prints))

    csrc = os.path.join(workdir, "harness.c")
    with open(csrc, "w") as f:
        f.write(src)
    exe = os.path.join(workdir, "harness")
    cc = subprocess.run(["cc", "-O0", "-o", exe, csrc, obj, "-lm"],
                        capture_output=True, text=True)
    if cc.returncode:
        last = cc.stderr.strip().splitlines()
        return None, "the harness did not build: " + (last[-1][:140] if last else "?")
    run = subprocess.run([exe], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    if run.returncode:
        return None, "the harness crashed (signal %d)" % -run.returncode
    return [l for l in run.stdout.splitlines() if l], None


def host_triple():
    out = subprocess.run(["llc", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    m = re.search(r"Default target: (\S+)", out)
    return m.group(1) if m else "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("file")
    ap.add_argument("function", nargs="?")
    ap.add_argument("--compare", action="store_true",
                    help="run ours too and compare the numbers")
    ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                    help="every function of the file, comparing each")
    ap.add_argument("--tolerance", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="relative difference allowed (default: none, bit-exact)")
    ap.add_argument("--draw", action="store_true",
                    help="also draw with it (air_run) and compare the pixel")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.all:
        return run_all(args)

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work:
        if args.file.endswith(".metallib"):
            b, header, funcs = metallib.parse(args.file)
            picked = None
            for f in funcs:
                if not args.function or f.get("name") == args.function:
                    picked = f
                    break
            if not picked:
                sys.exit("cpuref.py: no function %s in %s" % (args.function, args.file))
            bc, _ = metallib.bitcode_of(b, header, picked)
            bc_path = os.path.join(work, "m.bc")
            with open(bc_path, "wb") as f:
                f.write(bc)
        else:
            bc_path = args.file

        ll = disassemble(bc_path)
        entry = entry_of(ll)
        if not entry:
            sys.exit("cpuref.py: no entry point found")
        library = entry["stage"] == "visible"
        bufs = buffer_args(ll, entry)
        if library:
            why = check_against_metadata(entry, ll)
            if why:
                print("cpuref: cannot run this one: %s" % why)
                return 1
            bufs = {0: 16 * max(len(entry["params"]), 1)}
            print("cpuref: %s (a library function), %d arguments, each read from "
                  "byte 16*i of one buffer" % (entry["name"], len(entry["params"])))
        else:
            print("cpuref: %s (%s), %d parameters, %d of them buffers" %
                  (entry["name"], entry["stage"], len(entry["params"]), len(bufs)))
        for i, n in sorted(bufs.items()):
            print("  parameter %d: a buffer of %d bytes, filled with %s"
                  % (i, n, "the floats ((w * 13) % 29 - 14) / 4" if library
                     else "(i * 7 + 13) & 0xff"))

        values, why = build_and_run(ll, entry, bufs, work, library)
        if why:
            print("cpuref: cannot run this one: %s" % why)
            return 1
        print("cpuref: LLVM on this machine says the result is:")
        for v in values:
            print("  %s" % v)

        if args.compare:
            ours, why = evaluate_ours(args.file, entry["name"], library)
            if why:
                print("cpuref: ours could not be evaluated: %s" % why)
                return 1
            print("cpuref: and our frontend, folded over the same bytes, says:")
            for v in ours:
                print("  %s" % v)
            bad = compare(values, ours, args.tolerance)
            print("cpuref: %s" % ("they agree" if not bad else "they DIFFER: " + bad))
            return 1 if bad else 0
    return 0


def draw_ours(path, function):
    """air_run: the same shader drawn by a Gallium driver, pixel read back."""
    out = subprocess.run([AIR_RUN, path, function], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode:
        return None, (out.stderr or out.stdout).strip().splitlines()[-1][:160] \
            if (out.stderr or out.stdout).strip() else "air_run failed"
    values, taking = [], False
    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("air_run: the pixel"):
            taking = True
            continue
        if taking and line.startswith("  "):
            values.append(line.strip())
        elif taking:
            break
    return (values, None) if values else (None, "air_run printed no pixel")


def evaluate_ours(path, function, library=False):
    """air2nir --eval: the same shader folded over the same buffer bytes."""
    cmd = [AIR2NIR] + (["--library"] if library else []) + ["--eval", path, function]
    out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode:
        return None, (out.stderr or out.stdout).strip().splitlines()[-1][:160]
    values = []
    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
        if not line.startswith("  ") or line.startswith("  constant") or \
           line.startswith("  device") or line.startswith("  ("):
            continue
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) < 2:
            continue
        if "did not fold" in line:
            return None, "an output did not fold to a constant"
        values.extend(parts[1:])
    return values, None


def compare(theirs, ours, tol):
    """What differs between LLVM's numbers and ours, or None."""
    if len(theirs) != len(ours):
        return "LLVM printed %d values, we printed %d" % (len(theirs), len(ours))
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(theirs, ours)):
        fa, fb = float(a), float(b)
        if fa == fb:
            continue
        if tol > 0:
            scale = max(abs(fa), abs(fb))
            if scale > 0 and abs(fa - fb) / scale <= tol:
                continue
        return "value %d: LLVM %s, ours %s" % (i, a, b)
    return None


def run_all(args):
    """Every function of a .metallib, with a count at the end."""
    b, header, funcs = metallib.parse(args.file)
    agree = differ = skipped = with_air = drawn = not_drawn = 0
    for f in funcs:
        name = f.get("name")
        if not name:
            continue
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work:
            bc, _ = metallib.bitcode_of(b, header, f)
            bc_path = os.path.join(work, "m.bc")
            with open(bc_path, "wb") as fp:
                fp.write(bc)
            try:
                ll = disassemble(bc_path)
                entry = entry_of(ll)
            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
                entry = None
            if not entry:
                skipped += 1
                continue
            theirs, why = build_and_run(ll, entry, buffer_args(ll, entry), work)
            if why:
                print("skip   %-44s LLVM: %s" % (name, why))
                skipped += 1
                continue
        ours, why = evaluate_ours(args.file, name)
        if why:
            print("skip   %-44s ours: %s" % (name, why))
            skipped += 1
            continue
        bad = compare(theirs, ours, args.tolerance)
        drawn_note = ""
        if not bad and args.draw:
            pixel, why = draw_ours(args.file, name)
            if why:
                drawn_note = "  (not drawn: %s)" % why
                not_drawn += 1
            else:
                # the pixel is render target 0, which is the result's first
                # field for every shader of this corpus
                dbad = compare(theirs[:len(pixel)], pixel, args.tolerance)
                if dbad:
                    print("DRAWN DIFFERS %-38s %s" % (name, dbad))
                    differ += 1
                    continue
                drawn += 1
                drawn_note = "  drawn and matching"
        if bad:
            print("DIFFER %-44s %s" % (name, bad))
            differ += 1
        else:
            agree += 1
            if calls_air(b, header, f):
                with_air += 1
            print("agree  %-44s %s%s" % (name, " ".join(theirs[:4]), drawn_note))
    print("\ncpuref: %d agree with LLVM, %d differ, %d could not be compared (of %d)"
          % (agree, differ, skipped, len(funcs)))
    # Which part of the frontend this actually exercised. A shader that calls
    # no air.* checks the reader, the interface and the instructions, and says
    # nothing whatever about air_intrinsics.c.
    print("cpuref: of the %d that agree, %d call an air.* function; %d are plain LLVM IR, "
          "so they test the reader, the interface and the instructions but no intrinsic"
          % (agree, with_air, agree - with_air))
    if args.draw:
        print("cpuref: %d of them were also DRAWN by a Gallium driver and the pixel matched; "
              "%d could not be drawn" % (drawn, not_drawn))
    return 1 if differ else 0


def calls_air(b, header, f):
    """Does this module declare any air.* function?"""
    bc, _ = metallib.bitcode_of(b, header, f)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work:
        p = os.path.join(work, "m.bc")
        with open(p, "wb") as fp:
            fp.write(bc)
        try:
            ll = disassemble(p)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            return False
    return bool(re.search(r"^declare[^@\n]*@air\.", ll, re.M))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/air/intrincheck.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every air.* arithmetic operation the corpus uses against a reference.

The corpus exercises each operation only incidentally: a shader that calls
air.fast_round once and a hundred other things tells us the module translated,
not that the rounding is right. One of these was wrong for a week -- fast_round
was lowered to nir_fround_even, which is rint, and the two differ at every
half-way value -- and nothing in the 456-module corpus could have shown it,
because no module's output was ever compared with a number computed any other
way.

So the operations are tested one at a time, on inputs chosen to break them:

  - air2nir --list over the corpus gives the declarations that are actually
    used (78 arithmetic ones today). Apple's vocabulary in AGXCompilerCore has
    137 names; the ones no module calls are not translated and not tested, and
    this prints that difference rather than hiding it.
  - for each declaration a fragment shader is generated that calls it on
    constant arguments and returns the result as its render target, llvm-as
    assembles it, and `air2nir --eval` folds it. Nothing is read from the
    corpus but the list of names.
  - the reference is this file's Python, which for every exactly-defined
    operation is the IEEE result rounded once to the shader's precision.

What a disagreement means, in order of what it is most likely to be: the
lowering in air_intrinsics.c is the wrong NIR opcode (fast_round); the
reference here is the wrong Metal semantics; NIR's constant folder differs
from libm. The third has never happened yet.

What this does NOT prove, and no amount of it will:

  - The reference for a transcendental is this machine's libm, not Apple's and
    not the Adreno's. Metal's `fast_` prefix *permits* a lower-precision
    implementation, so the printed difference for fast_sin is a measurement,
    not a verdict. Those are reported separately and are never counted as
    exact. The only thing checked there is that the lowering picked an
    operation of the right shape.
  - NIR's constant folder is not the Adreno. A difference between what
    nir_opt_constant_folding computes for nir_ffloor and what the hardware's
    floor instruction computes would be invisible here. Checking that needs
    the phone, and for these operations it has not been done.
  - Denormals. Apple compiles with air.compile.denorms_disable, so the
    hardware may flush where this check does not. Inputs are kept normal.

usage: intrincheck.py [-v] [--decls FILE] [OP ...]           fold it, exhaustively
       intrincheck.py --run [--few] [--cases N] [OP ...]     run it through a real driver
       intrincheck.py --emit DIR [--few] [--cases N]         write it out to carry somewhere
       intrincheck.py --check DIR RUN.LOG                    judge what the runner printed
"""

import json
import math
import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
AIR2NIR = os.environ.get(
    "AIR2NIR", os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/compiler/air/air2nir")
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# precision


def f32(x):
    """x rounded once to float32, the way a shader's float holds it."""
    return struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<f", x))[0]


def f16(x):
    try:
        return struct.unpack("<e", struct.pack("<e", float(x)))[0]
    except (OverflowError, struct.error):
        return math.copysign(float("inf"), x)


def to_f32_bits(x):
    return struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", x))[0]


def wrap(bits, width, signed):
    bits &= (1 << width) - 1
    if signed and bits >> (width - 1):
        bits -= 1 << width
    return bits


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the inputs
#
# Every value here is one that has broken something, in this port or in
# somebody else's: the half-way cases that separate round from rint, the
# largest float below a half-way case (0x1.fffffep-2, which the first fix for
# fast_round got wrong), the powers of two where exponent arithmetic goes
# wrong, zero of both signs, and the first float above 2^24 where consecutive
# integers stop being representable.

FLOATS = [
    0.0,
    -0.0,
    0.5,
    -0.5,
    struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", 0x3EFFFFFF))[0],  # 0x1.fffffep-2
    1.5,
    -1.5,
    2.5,
    -2.5,
    1.0,
    -1.0,
    3.7,
    -3.7,
    0.1,
    -0.1,
    2.0,
    16777216.0,  # 2^24
    16777217.0,  # not representable: becomes 2^24
    1e-8,
    1e8,
    123.456,
    -123.456,
]

# the second and third arguments want their own values, not the same ones, or
# min(a, b) is only ever tested with a == b
# -0.0 belongs here as well as in FLOATS: all four of (+-0, +-0) are separate
# cases for atan2, and three of them were wrong until this pool had them
FLOATS2 = [1.0, -1.0, 0.0, -0.0, 0.25, -0.25, 2.0, 3.0, -3.0, 0.5, 100.0, -100.0, 1e-8]

# inputs where the answer is defined but unusual. Reported separately: a
# disagreement here is worth reading, not necessarily worth fixing, because
# fast-math shaders are allowed to give up on them.
EDGE_FLOATS = [float("inf"), float("-inf"), float("nan")]

INTS = [0, 1, -1, 2, 7, -7, 127, -128, 255, 32767, -32768, 65535, 1000000, -1000000,
        2147483647, -2147483648]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the reference
#
# One entry per base operation: how many arguments, what it computes, and
# whether the result is exactly defined. `exact=False` means the reference is
# this machine's libm and the shader is allowed to differ -- the number is
# printed and nothing is concluded from it.


def _signed_int_result(f):
    """math.floor and friends return a Python int, which cannot hold -0. IEEE
    says floor(-0) is -0, and the shader gets that right, so the reference has
    to as well -- the first thing this check found was its own reference."""
    def g(x):
        if math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x):
            return x
        return math.copysign(float(f(x)), x)
    return g


# The precision the operation under test computes at, set by reference()
# before it calls one of these. An operation on halves rounds every
# intermediate to half: mix(3.7h, 1h, 0.25h) is 3.0234375 that way and
# 3.02441406 with float32 intermediates, and the shader is right.
ROUND = f32


def _mix(a, b, t):
    return ROUND(a + ROUND(ROUND(b - a) * t))


def _fract(x):
    if math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x):
        return x
    # the sign of floor's zero decides the sign of this zero:
    # -0 - (-0) is +0, but -0 - 0 is -0, and Python's math.floor returns an
    # int, which has no -0 to carry
    r = ROUND(x - math.copysign(float(math.floor(x)), x))
    # Metal: "returns a value in [0, 1)", so a result that rounds up to 1 is
    # clamped to the largest value below it in this precision
    return min(r, ROUND(1.0 - ROUND(2.0 ** -12)))


def _sign(x):
    if math.isnan(x):
        return 0.0
    if x > 0:
        return 1.0
    if x < 0:
        return -1.0
    return x  # keeps the sign of zero


def _roundf(x):
    """C roundf: half away from zero, which is Metal's round."""
    if math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x) or x == 0.0:
        return x
    a = math.floor(abs(x) + 0.5)
    # floor(|x| + 0.5) is wrong where |x| + 0.5 rounds up in float; do it the
    # way the shader does, and the way roundf is specified
    t = math.trunc(abs(x))
    a = t + 1 if abs(x) - t >= 0.5 else t
    return math.copysign(a, x)


def _fmin(a, b):
    if math.isnan(a):
        return b
    if math.isnan(b):
        return a
    if a == b == 0.0:  # fmin(+0, -0) may be either; Metal does not say
        return b if math.copysign(1, b) < 0 else a
    return min(a, b)


def _fmax(a, b):
    if math.isnan(a):
        return b
    if math.isnan(b):
        return a
    if a == b == 0.0:
        return b if math.copysign(1, b) > 0 else a
    return max(a, b)


def _clamp_f(x, lo, hi):
    return _fmin(_fmax(x, lo), hi)


def _powr(x, y):
    # powr is pow for x >= 0 only, undefined elsewhere
    if x < 0:
        return float("nan")
    return math.pow(x, y)


# Python raises where C returns a value. Metal's math functions are OpenCL's,
# which keep the IEEE results at the edge of the domain, so raising here would
# silently drop the cases that matter most -- it had already dropped every case
# of air.fast_sqrt.v4f32, whose rotated components always include a negative.
def _sqrt(x):
    if math.isnan(x):
        return x
    return float("nan") if x < 0 else math.sqrt(x)   # sqrt(-0) is -0


def _log(f, zero):
    def g(x):
        if math.isnan(x):
            return x
        if x == 0.0:
            return zero
        return float("nan") if x < 0 else f(x)
    return g


def _rsqrt(x):
    if math.isnan(x):
        return x
    if x == 0.0:
        return math.copysign(float("inf"), x)
    return float("nan") if x < 0 else 1.0 / math.sqrt(x)


def _fmod(x, y):
    if y == 0.0 or math.isnan(x) or math.isnan(y) or math.isinf(x):
        return float("nan")
    return math.fmod(x, y)


def _pow(x, y):
    # C: pow(+-0, y) for a negative odd integer y is +-inf, keeping the zero's
    # sign; for any other negative y it is +inf. Python raises for both, and
    # the fallback that guessed +inf made the shader's correct -inf for
    # pow(-0, -1) look like an infinite-ulp disagreement.
    if x == 0.0 and y < 0:
        odd = y == int(y) and int(y) % 2 != 0
        return math.copysign(float("inf"), x) if odd else float("inf")
    try:
        return math.pow(x, y)
    except ValueError:
        return float("nan")        # x < 0 with a fractional y
    except OverflowError:
        return math.copysign(float("inf"), x if x < 0 and y == int(y)
                             and int(y) % 2 != 0 else 1.0)


def _ldexp(x, n):
    try:
        return math.ldexp(x, n)
    except OverflowError:
        return math.copysign(float("inf"), x)


OPS = {
    # name:        (nargs, fn, exact)
    "floor":       (1, _signed_int_result(math.floor), True),
    "ceil":        (1, _signed_int_result(math.ceil), True),
    "trunc":       (1, _signed_int_result(math.trunc), True),
    "rint":        (1, _signed_int_result(round), True),
    "round":       (1, _roundf, True),
    "fabs":        (1, abs, True),
    "fract":       (1, _fract, True),
    "sign":        (1, _sign, True),
    "saturate":    (1, lambda x: _clamp_f(x, 0.0, 1.0), True),
    "fmin":        (2, _fmin, True),
    "fmax":        (2, _fmax, True),
    "clamp":       (3, _clamp_f, True),
    "mix":         (3, _mix, True),
    "fmod":        (2, _fmod, True),
    "mod":         (2, _fmod, True),
    "divide":      (2, lambda a, b: a / b if b else math.copysign(float("inf"), a) if a else float("nan"), True),
    "sqrt":        (1, _sqrt, True),      # IEEE: exactly rounded
    "fma":         (3, lambda a, b, c: math.fma(a, b, c), True),
    "ldexp":       (2, _ldexp, True),
    # approximate: the reference is libm, the shader is allowed to differ
    "sin":         (1, math.sin, False),
    "cos":         (1, math.cos, False),
    "tan":         (1, math.tan, False),
    "atan2":       (2, math.atan2, False),
    "exp":         (1, math.exp, False),
    "exp2":        (1, lambda x: math.pow(2.0, x), False),
    "exp10":       (1, lambda x: math.pow(10.0, x), False),
    "log":         (1, _log(math.log, float("-inf")), False),
    "log2":        (1, _log(math.log2, float("-inf")), False),
    "log10":       (1, _log(math.log10, float("-inf")), False),
    "pow":         (2, _pow, False),
    "powr":        (2, _powr, False),
    "rsqrt":       (1, _rsqrt, False),
}

# integer operations, by (base name, signed)
IOPS = {
    ("min", True):  lambda w: (2, min),
    ("min", False): lambda w: (2, min),
    ("max", True):  lambda w: (2, max),
    ("max", False): lambda w: (2, max),
    ("clamp", True): lambda w: (3, lambda x, lo, hi: min(max(x, lo), hi)),
    ("clamp", False): lambda w: (3, lambda x, lo, hi: min(max(x, lo), hi)),
}


def ref_elementwise(op, args, argtys, signed):
    """One component of an elementwise operation.

    The arguments must be rounded to the shader's precision first. mix(3.7, 1,
    1) is exactly 1 in float32 and 0.99999994 in double, and this check
    reported the shader wrong for a while because the reference was given
    Python's 3.7 and the shader f32(3.7). Everything insensitive to the low
    bits of its input -- floor, min, clamp -- hid the mistake.
    """
    bty, _ = parse_type(argtys[0])
    if bty.startswith("i"):
        # integer min/max/clamp: no rounding anywhere, and the result is
        # whatever the declared width holds
        w = int(bty[1:])
        fn = {"min": min, "max": max,
              "clamp": lambda x, lo, hi: min(max(x, lo), hi)}[op]
        # air.min.u is an unsigned minimum: umin(0, 0xffff) is 0, not -1, and
        # taking the declaration's `u` for granted as signed made the shader
        # look wrong on 175 of 256 cases
        return wrap(fn(*[wrap(v, w, bool(signed)) for v in args]), w, bool(signed))

    global ROUND
    ROUND = f16 if bty == "half" else f32
    nargs, fn, exact = OPS[op]
    rounded = [ROUND(v) if parse_type(ty)[0] in ("half", "float") else v
               for ty, v in zip(argtys, args)]
    return ROUND(fn(*rounded))


def ref_convert(name, retty, srcty, v):
    """air.convert.<dk>.<dt>.<sk>.<st>(v), one component.

    The two kind letters are not decoration. `s`/`u` on the source say how its
    integer is read, which decides sign- against zero-extension; `s`/`u` on the
    destination say how the result is read, which decides whether a float is
    converted signed or unsigned and what a narrowing wraps to. The corpus has
    air.convert.u.v2i16.s.v2i32 -- a signed 32-bit value narrowed to an
    unsigned 16-bit one -- where getting either letter the wrong way round
    still produces a plausible number.
    """
    parts = name.split(".")
    dk, sk = parts[2], parts[4]
    dbase, _ = parse_type(retty)
    sbase, _ = parse_type(srcty)

    if sbase in ("half", "float"):
        # float -> int: Metal truncates toward zero. Out of the destination's
        # range it is undefined, in C and in the MSL specification both, so
        # those are not cases.
        x = f16(v) if sbase == "half" else f32(v)
        if math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x):
            raise ValueError("not defined")
        w = int(dbase[1:])
        t = math.trunc(x)
        lo, hi = ((-(1 << (w - 1)), (1 << (w - 1)) - 1) if dk == "s"
                  else (0, (1 << w) - 1))
        if t < lo or t > hi:
            raise ValueError("outside the destination's range")
        return wrap(t, w, dk == "s")

    w = int(sbase[1:])
    x = wrap(v, w, sk == "s")
    if dbase in ("half", "float"):
        # int -> float, rounded once to the destination's precision
        return f16(x) if dbase == "half" else f32(x)
    return wrap(x, int(dbase[1:]), dk == "s")


def reference(family, op, name, args, argtys, retty, signed):
    """The reference result for one case, as a list of result components.

    `args` is one list per argument, holding that argument's components.
    """
    rty, rn = parse_type(retty)

    if family == "dot":
        # The inputs are small dyadic rationals, so every product and every
        # partial sum is exact and the answer does not depend on the order the
        # accumulation is taken in. What this pins is which components are
        # paired with which -- a lowering that dropped a component or paired
        # them crosswise gives a different number -- and not the rounding of a
        # general dot product, which it cannot.
        n = parse_type(argtys[0])[1]
        return [f32(sum(f32(args[0][k]) * f32(args[1][k]) for k in range(n)))]

    if family in ("all", "any"):
        n = parse_type(argtys[0])[1]
        v = args[0][:n]
        return [1 if (all(v) if family == "all" else any(v)) else 0]

    if family == "convert":
        return [ref_convert(name, retty, argtys[0], v) for v in args[0][:rn]]

    out = []
    for k in range(rn):
        # a scalar argument of a vector operation would be broadcast; none of
        # the corpus's declarations mix the two, but take component 0 if so
        per = [a[k] if len(a) > k else a[0] for a in args]
        out.append(ref_elementwise(op, per, argtys, signed))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the declarations
#
# air.<op>.<type>                       air.fast_round.f32
# air.<op>.<s|u>.<type>                 air.clamp.s.v2i16
# air.convert.<f|s|u>.<dst>.<f|s|u>.<src>
# air.dot.<type>                        returns a scalar from two vectors

DECL = re.compile(r"^declare\s+(.*?)\s+@(air\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+)\((.*)\)")


def parse_type(s):
    """'<4 x float>' -> ('float', 4); 'i32' -> ('i32', 1)"""
    s = s.strip()
    m = re.match(r"<(\d+) x (.+)>$", s)
    if m:
        return m.group(2).strip(), int(m.group(1))
    return s, 1


def collect_declarations(libs):
    out = set()
    for lib in libs:
        try:
            ll = subprocess.run([AIR2NIR, "--ll", lib], capture_output=True).stdout
        except OSError:
            continue
        for line in ll.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines():
            if line.startswith("declare ") and "@air." in line:
                line = re.sub(r"\s+local_unnamed_addr.*$", "", line)
                line = re.sub(r"\s+#\d+$", "", line)
                out.add(line.strip())
    return sorted(out)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the generated shader

SKELETON = """source_filename = "ic"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

%(decl)s

define <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> @ic() local_unnamed_addr {
%(body)s
  %%r = insertvalue <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> undef, <4 x %(outty)s> %%v3, 0
  ret <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> %%r
}

!llvm.module.flags = !{!0}
!air.version = !{!1}
!air.language_version = !{!2}
!air.fragment = !{!3}

!0 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
!1 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!2 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!3 = !{ptr @ic, !4, !6}
!4 = !{!5}
!5 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"%(outname)s", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{}
"""

# The same shader with its arguments read from a constant buffer instead of
# written in as immediates. That is the only form worth running on a GPU: ir3
# folds, so air.fast_round(0.5) written as a constant is answered by the
# compiler and the hardware never sees the instruction -- the test would pass
# with the GPU switched off. A value loaded from a buffer cannot be folded, and
# air_run puts bytes we choose there (AIR_RUN_BUFFER).
BUF_SKELETON = """source_filename = "ic"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

%(decl)s

define <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> @ic(ptr addrspace(2) %%in) local_unnamed_addr {
%(body)s
  %%r = insertvalue <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> undef, <4 x %(outty)s> %%v3, 0
  ret <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> %%r
}

!llvm.module.flags = !{!0}
!air.version = !{!1}
!air.language_version = !{!2}
!air.fragment = !{!3}

!0 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
!1 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!2 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!3 = !{ptr @ic, !4, !6}
!4 = !{!5}
!5 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"%(outname)s", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{!7}
!7 = !{i32 0, !"air.buffer", !"air.buffer_size", i32 4096, !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"air.read", !"air.address_space", i32 2, !"air.arg_type_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_align_size", i32 4, !"air.arg_type_name", !"float", !"air.arg_name", !"in"}
"""
```
