```sh
		printf 'READER  %s: %s\n' "$2" "$(head -1 "$WORK/ours.err")"
		return
	fi
	llvm-dis -o - "$1" 2>/dev/null | canon > "$WORK/theirs.canon" || true
	if ! canon < "$WORK/ours.ll" > "$WORK/ours.canon"; then
		reject=$((reject + 1))
		printf 'LLVM-AS %s: %s\n' "$2" "$(head -1 "$WORK/as.err")"
		return
	fi
	if cmp -s "$WORK/ours.canon" "$WORK/theirs.canon"; then
		ok=$((ok + 1))
		[ "$VERBOSE" = 1 ] && printf 'ok      %s\n' "$2"
	else
		differ=$((differ + 1))
		printf 'DIFFER  %s\n' "$2"
		[ "$VERBOSE" = 1 ] && diff -u "$WORK/theirs.canon" "$WORK/ours.canon" | head -40
	fi
	return 0
}

for arg in "$@"; do
	if [ -d "$arg" ]; then
		while IFS= read -r f; do check_bc "$f" "${f#"$arg"/}"; done \
			< <(find "$arg" -name '*.bc' | sort)
	elif [ "${arg%.metallib}" != "$arg" ]; then
		dir=$WORK/unpack
		rm -rf "$dir"
		python3 "$ROOT/tools/metallib.py" dump "$arg" "$dir" > /dev/null
		while IFS= read -r f; do
			check_bc "$f" "$(basename "$arg"):$(basename "$f" .bc)"
		done < <(find "$dir" -name '*.bc' | sort)
	else
		check_bc "$arg" "$arg"
	fi
done

printf '\nreader-check: %d modules, %d identical to llvm-dis' "$modules" "$ok"
[ "$readfail" != 0 ] && printf ', %d our reader refused' "$readfail"
[ "$reject" != 0 ] && printf ', %d llvm-as refused' "$reject"
[ "$differ" != 0 ] && printf ', %d differ' "$differ"
printf '\n'
[ "$ok" = "$modules" ]

```

`tools/air/texcheck.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Run every texture shader of the corpus and check the texel it returns.
#
# air_run binds a texture whose texel (x, y, z) is (100+x, 200+y, 300+x+y+z, 400) --
# 4x4 for a 2D sampler, 4x4x4 for a 3D one, because a 3D sample out of a 2D
# texture can come back right by accident and that is not evidence --
# a nearest sampler with clamped addressing, and a coordinate at the centre of
# texel (1, 1). A shader that samples or fetches once must therefore return
# exactly 101 201 302 400 -- an equality, not a tolerance: nearest filtering at
# a texel centre has no weights to round and clamping has no arithmetic.
#
# What this does NOT check is anything that depends on Metal's own sampler
# state: the two modules of the corpus that declare a `constexpr sampler`
# carry it as a 64-bit word that is not decoded (docs/air.md). Here the API
# chooses the sampler, so what is verified is the texture operation and not
# Apple's filtering or addressing.
#
# A shader that combines several samples, or scales the coordinate, will not
# return the bare texel; those are listed as "other" with what they did return,
# which is a thing to read rather than a failure.
#
# usage: texcheck.sh [FILE.metallib ...]
set -u
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/../.." && pwd)
AIR_RUN=${AIR_RUN:-$ROOT/build/mesa-host/build/src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/air_run}
AIR2NIR=${AIR2NIR:-$ROOT/build/mesa-host/build/src/compiler/air/air2nir}
[ -x "$AIR_RUN" ] || { echo "texcheck.sh: run tools/air/mk-host.sh first"; exit 1; }

LIBS=("$@")
if [ ${#LIBS[@]} = 0 ]; then
	LIBS=(
		"$ROOT/sysimage/rootfs/System/Library/VideoDecoders/AV1SW.metallib"
		"$ROOT/sysimage/rootfs/System/Library/Extensions/AppleMetalGLRenderer.bundle/default.metallib"
		"$ROOT/sysimage/rootfs/System/Library/CoreImage/PortraitFilters.cifilter/default.metallib"
		"$ROOT/sysimage/rootfs/System/Library/CoreImage/PortraitFilters.cifilter/portrait_filters.metallib"
	)
fi

exact=0 other=0 refused=0 total=0
for lib in "${LIBS[@]}"; do
	[ -f "$lib" ] || continue
	# the functions that touch a texture at all
	"$AIR2NIR" --report "$lib" 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r line; do
		case "$line" in *$'\t'calls=*texture*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
		printf '%s\n' "${line%%$'\t'*}" | sed 's/^module=//'
	done > /tmp/texcheck.names
	while IFS= read -r fn; do
		[ -n "$fn" ] || continue
		total=$((total + 1))
		out=$("$AIR_RUN" "$lib" "$fn" 2>&1)
		got=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '/came back as/,$p' | sed -n '2,5p' |
			tr -d ' ' | paste -sd' ')
		# air_run knows what it bound, so it says what to expect; the 3D case
		# wants a different texel from the 2D one
		WANT=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^air_run: expected \(.*\)  (the centre.*/\1/p')
		if [ -z "$got" ]; then
			# the reason, not the first line: air_run says why on stderr, and
			# "<name> on softpipe" is only which screen it got
			# -a: a fault dump can carry a NUL, and a binary verdict here would
			# lose the reason and leave "refused" with nothing said about why
			why=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" |
				grep -aE 'this harness|is a .* shader|Assertion|stage: |error|no gallium|does not bind|stores nothing' |
				head -1)
			[ -n "$why" ] || why=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -1)
			printf 'refused %-44s %s\n' "$fn" "${why:0:90}"
			refused=$((refused + 1))
		elif [ -n "$WANT" ] && [ "$got" = "$(echo $WANT | tr ' ' '\n' | paste -sd' ')" ]; then
			printf 'EXACT   %-44s %s\n' "$fn" "$got"
			exact=$((exact + 1))
		else
			printf 'other   %-44s %s\n' "$fn" "$got"
			other=$((other + 1))
		fi
	done < /tmp/texcheck.names
done
rm -f /tmp/texcheck.names

echo
echo "texcheck: $total texture shaders run: $exact returned the expected texel exactly,"
echo "texcheck: $other returned something else, $refused could not be run"
echo "texcheck: the sampler here is the API's (nearest, clamped); Metal's own sampler word"
echo "texcheck: is not decoded, so nothing here verifies Apple's filtering or addressing"

```

`tools/air/texopcheck.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check the texture operations one at a time, on more than one texel.

tools/air/texcheck.sh runs the corpus's own texture shaders, and 6 of its 55
return the exact texel on the Adreno. Two things it cannot do:

  - Most of the other 49 are air.visible library functions, which the harness
    cannot invoke as entry points, so whole operations -- the texel fetch, the
    size queries -- have no coverage at all from it.
  - Every one of them samples the same texel, (1, 1), because that is where
    air_run's vertex shader puts the coordinate. A lowering that ignored the
    coordinate and always fetched (1, 1) would pass all six.

So this generates a fragment shader per (operation, coordinate), the way
tools/air/intrincheck.py does for the arithmetic, and asks for several texels
including the corners. air_run fills texel (x, y, z) of slot n with
(100 + x + 1000n, 200 + y, 300 + x + y + z, 400), so every coordinate has a
different expected answer in all four channels and a confusion between any two
of them gives a wrong number rather than a plausible one.

Nothing is read from the corpus but the list of declarations, and the
coordinates are immediates here rather than loaded from a buffer: a texture
fetch is not constant-folded by either NIR or ir3, so there is nothing for the
compiler to answer in the shader's place. That is the difference from the
arithmetic, where the buffer was necessary.

What is NOT checked, and why:

  - Metal's own sampler state. air_run's sampler is the API's -- nearest,
    clamped -- and the 64-bit constexpr sampler word is not decoded
    (docs/air.md section 3.3). The coordinates here are texel centres, where
    nearest filtering has no weights to round, so this says nothing about
    filtering or addressing.
  - The integer-typed reads and samples (read_texture_2d.s.v4i16,
    sample_texture_2d.u.v4i32 and the rest). air_run binds one
    r32g32b32a32_float texture, and a shader declaring an integer texture
    against it is a type mismatch whose result would say nothing about the
    lowering. Binding a texture whose format follows the declaration is a
    change to air_run that is not made here.
  - write_texture_2d and the multisample reads: the first needs the texture
    read back, which air_run does not do, and the second a multisample
    texture, which it does not bind.
  - The depth sample: air_run binds no depth texture, and a shader reading an
    attachment nothing stored to is one of the four tests this port has
    already had pass for the wrong reason.

usage: texopcheck.py [--keep DIR] [-v]
"""

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
AIR_RUN = os.environ.get(
    "AIR_RUN",
    os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/gallium/drivers/freedreno/air_run"),
)

TEX = 4   # air_run binds a TEX x TEX (x TEX) texture


def texel(x, y, z=0):
    """What air_run put at (x, y, z) of slot 0."""
    return [100 + x, 200 + y, 300 + x + y + z, 400]


SKELETON = """source_filename = "tex"
target datalayout = "e-p:64:64:64-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024-n8:16:32"
target triple = "air64-apple-ios16.5.0"

%(decl)s

define <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> @tex(%(params)s) local_unnamed_addr {
%(body)s
  %%out = insertvalue <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> undef, <4 x %(outty)s> %%v, 0
  ret <{ <4 x %(outty)s> }> %%out
}

!llvm.module.flags = !{!0}
!air.version = !{!1}
!air.language_version = !{!2}
!air.fragment = !{!3}
!0 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
!1 = !{i32 2, i32 5, i32 0}
!2 = !{!"Metal", i32 3, i32 0, i32 0}
!3 = !{ptr @tex, !4, !6}
!4 = !{!5}
!5 = !{!"air.render_target", i32 0, i32 0, !"air.arg_type_name", !"%(outname)s", !"air.arg_name", !"out"}
!6 = !{%(args)s}
%(argmd)s
"""

TEXTURE_MD = ('!{i32 %d, !"air.texture", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, !"%s", '
              '!"air.arg_type_name", !"texture%s", !"air.arg_name", !"t"}')
SAMPLER_MD = ('!{i32 %d, !"air.sampler", !"air.location_index", i32 0, i32 1, '
              '!"air.arg_type_name", !"sampler", !"air.arg_name", !"s"}')


def build(decl, call, needs_sampler, kind, access, outty="float"):
    """One shader: `call` computes %v from %t (and %s), `decl` declares it.

    outty is the render target's component type. It has to follow the
    declaration: air_run picks the texture's format from what the shader
    samples into (its own comment says why -- "a Metal texture2d<uint> read out
    of a float texture gives numbers that are neither right nor obviously
    wrong"), and the render target has to be able to hold the result.
    """
    params = ["ptr addrspace(1) %t"]
    md = [TEXTURE_MD % (0, access, kind)]
    if needs_sampler:
        params.append("ptr addrspace(2) %s")
        md.append(SAMPLER_MD % 1)
    return SKELETON % dict(
        decl=decl, params=", ".join(params), body=call, outty=outty,
        outname="float4" if outty == "float" else "int4",
        args=", ".join("!%d" % (7 + i) for i in range(len(md))),
        argmd="\n".join("!%d = %s" % (7 + i, m) for i, m in enumerate(md)))


def cases(decls):
    """Everything to try: (label, source, expected four floats)."""
    out = []
    have = {}
    for d in decls:
        m = re.match(r"^declare\s+(.*?)\s+@(air\.[A-Za-z0-9_.]+)\((.*)\)", d)
        if m:
            have[m.group(2)] = d

    # -- the texel fetch, at four corners and the middle of the 4x4 ---------
    name = "air.read_texture_2d.v4f32"
    if name in have:
        for (x, y) in [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 3), (3, 3), (3, 0)]:
            body = ('  %%r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                    '<2 x i32> <i32 %d, i32 %d>, i32 0, i32 0)\n'
                    '  %%v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %%r, 0' % (name, x, y))
            out.append(("%s (%d,%d)" % (name, x, y),
                        build(have[name], body, False, "2d<float, access::read>",
                              "air.read"),
                        texel(x, y), False))

    # the same fetch with 16-bit coordinates, which is a separate declaration
    name = "air.read_texture_2d.i16.v4f32"
    if name in have:
        for (x, y) in [(1, 1), (2, 3)]:
            body = ('  %%r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                    '<2 x i16> <i16 %d, i16 %d>, i16 0, i32 0)\n'
                    '  %%v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %%r, 0' % (name, x, y))
            out.append(("%s (%d,%d)" % (name, x, y),
                        build(have[name], body, False, "2d<float, access::read>",
                              "air.read"),
                        texel(x, y), False))

    # -- the size queries ---------------------------------------------------
    for name, want in (("air.get_width_texture_2d", TEX),
                       ("air.get_height_texture_2d", TEX)):
        if name not in have:
            continue
        body = ('  %%n = tail call i32 @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, i32 0)\n'
                '  %%f = sitofp i32 %%n to float\n'
                '  %%v0 = insertelement <4 x float> undef, float %%f, i32 0\n'
                '  %%v1 = insertelement <4 x float> %%v0, float %%f, i32 1\n'
                '  %%v2 = insertelement <4 x float> %%v1, float %%f, i32 2\n'
                '  %%v = insertelement <4 x float> %%v2, float %%f, i32 3' % name)
        out.append((name, build(have[name], body, False,
                                "2d<float, access::read>", "air.read"),
                    [want] * 4, False))

    # -- sampling, at the centre of several texels --------------------------
    name = "air.sample_texture_2d.v4f32"
    if name in have:
        for (x, y) in [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 3), (3, 3)]:
            u, v = (x + 0.5) / TEX, (y + 0.5) / TEX
            body = ('  %%r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                    'ptr addrspace(2) %%s, <2 x float> <float %.9e, float %.9e>, '
                    'i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.0, '
                    'float 0.0, i32 0)\n'
                    '  %%v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %%r, 0' % (name, u, v))
            out.append(("%s (%d,%d)" % (name, x, y),
                        build(have[name], body, True, "2d<float, sample>",
                              "air.sample"),
                        texel(x, y), False))

    name = "air.sample_texture_3d.v4f32"
    if name in have:
        for (x, y, z) in [(0, 0, 0), (1, 1, 1), (2, 3, 1), (3, 3, 3)]:
            u, v, w = ((x + 0.5) / TEX, (y + 0.5) / TEX, (z + 0.5) / TEX)
            body = ('  %%r = tail call { <4 x float>, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                    'ptr addrspace(2) %%s, <3 x float> <float %.9e, float %.9e, '
                    'float %.9e>, i1 true, <3 x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, '
                    'float 0.0, float 0.0, i32 0)\n'
                    '  %%v = extractvalue { <4 x float>, i8 } %%r, 0' % (name, u, v, w))
            out.append(("%s (%d,%d,%d)" % (name, x, y, z),
                        build(have[name], body, True, "3d<float, sample>",
                              "air.sample"),
                        texel(x, y, z), False))
    # -- the integer-typed reads and samples ---------------------------------
    #
    # air_run picks the texture's format from what the shader samples into, so
    # these get an R32G32B32A32_SINT or _UINT texture holding the same numbers
    # cast to int. The render target has to follow too, or the bits come back
    # read the wrong way.
    for name in sorted(have):
        m = re.match(r"^air\.(read|sample)_texture_(2d|3d)"
                     r"(\.i16)?\.([su])\.v4i(16|32)$", name)
        if not m:
            continue
        kindop, nd, narrow_coord, sign, width = m.groups()
        n = 3 if nd == "3d" else 2
        rty = "<4 x i%s>" % width
        decl = have[name]
        for coord in ([(1, 1, 1), (2, 3, 1)] if nd == "3d" else [(1, 1), (2, 3)]):
            if kindop == "read":
                cty = "i16" if narrow_coord else "i32"
                cv = ", ".join("%s %d" % (cty, v) for v in coord[:n])
                body = ('  %%r = tail call { %s, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                        '<%d x %s> <%s>, %s 0, i32 0)\n'
                        % (rty, name, n, cty, cv, cty))
                access, kind = "air.read", "%s<%s, access::read>" % (
                    nd, "int" if sign == "s" else "uint")
            else:
                cv = ", ".join("float %.9e" % ((v + 0.5) / TEX) for v in coord[:n])
                body = ('  %%r = tail call { %s, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                        'ptr addrspace(2) %%s, <%d x float> <%s>, i1 true, '
                        '<%d x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.0, '
                        'float 0.0, i32 0)\n' % (rty, name, n, cv, n))
                access, kind = "air.sample", "%s<%s, sample>" % (
                    nd, "int" if sign == "s" else "uint")
            body += '  %%t0 = extractvalue { %s, i8 } %%r, 0\n' % rty
            if width == "16":
                # widen to the render target, by the declaration's own sign
                body += ('  %%v = %s <4 x i16> %%t0 to <4 x i32>'
                         % ("sext" if sign == "s" else "zext"))
            else:
                body += '  %v = bitcast <4 x i32> %t0 to <4 x i32>'
            out.append(("%s %s" % (name, coord[:n]),
                        build(decl, body, kindop == "sample", kind, access, "i32"),
                        texel(*coord[:3] if nd == "3d" else (coord[0], coord[1])),
                        False))

    # -- the gather ----------------------------------------------------------
    #
    # A gather returns one channel of the four texels around the coordinate.
    # Metal fixes the order they come back in and this does not know it, so the
    # four values are compared as a multiset: that checks the footprint and the
    # channel selection without committing to an order convention, and every
    # channel gives a different multiset, so a wrong channel still shows.
    #
    # The coordinate is 1.75/4, so in texel space it is 1.25 and the footprint
    # is x,y in {1, 2} with nothing ambiguous about the rounding.
    for name in sorted(have):
        m = re.match(r"^air\.gather_texture_2d(\.[su])?\.v4(f32|f16|i32|i16)$", name)
        if not m:
            continue
        sign, width = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        rty = "<4 x %s>" % {"f32": "float", "f16": "half",
                            "i32": "i32", "i16": "i16"}[width]
        outty = "float" if width.startswith("f") else "i32"
        base = {"f32": "float", "f16": "half",
                "i32": "uint" if sign == ".u" else "int",
                "i16": "uint" if sign == ".u" else "int"}[width]
        u = 1.75 / TEX
        for comp in range(4):
            want = sorted(texel(x, y)[comp] for x in (1, 2) for y in (1, 2))
            body = ('  %%r = tail call { %s, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                    'ptr addrspace(2) %%s, <2 x float> <float %.9e, float %.9e>, '
                    'i1 true, <2 x i32> zeroinitializer, i32 %d, i32 0)\n'
                    % (rty, name, u, u, comp))
            body += '  %%g = extractvalue { %s, i8 } %%r, 0\n' % rty
            if width == "f16":
                body += '  %v = fpext <4 x half> %g to <4 x float>'
            elif width == "i16":
                body += ('  %%v = %s <4 x i16> %%g to <4 x i32>'
                         % ("zext" if sign == ".u" else "sext"))
            elif width == "i32":
                body += '  %v = bitcast <4 x i32> %g to <4 x i32>'
            else:
                body += '  %v = bitcast <4 x float> %g to <4 x float>'
            out.append(("%s channel %d" % (name, comp),
                        build(have[name], body, True, "2d<%s, sample>" % base,
                              "air.sample", outty),
                        want, True))

    # -- the half-typed reads and samples ------------------------------------
    #
    # These belong with the rest rather than in a list of things with no case:
    # they are generated, they are correct as far as this can tell, and
    # softpipe sets them aside for the one reason it sets aside every 16-bit
    # operation. On ir3 they are a real question.
    for name in sorted(have):
        m = re.match(r"^air\.(read|sample)_texture_(2d|3d)\.v4f16$", name)
        if not m:
            continue
        kindop, nd = m.groups()
        n = 3 if nd == "3d" else 2
        coord = (1, 1, 1) if nd == "3d" else (1, 1)
        if kindop == "read":
            cv = ", ".join("i32 %d" % v for v in coord[:n])
            body = ('  %%r = tail call { <4 x half>, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                    '<%d x i32> <%s>, i32 0, i32 0)\n' % (name, n, cv))
            access, kind = "air.read", "%s<half, access::read>" % nd
            sampler = False
        else:
            cv = ", ".join("float %.9e" % ((v + 0.5) / TEX) for v in coord[:n])
            body = ('  %%r = tail call { <4 x half>, i8 } @%s(ptr addrspace(1) %%t, '
                    'ptr addrspace(2) %%s, <%d x float> <%s>, i1 true, '
                    '<%d x i32> zeroinitializer, i1 false, float 0.0, float 0.0, '
                    'i32 0)\n' % (name, n, cv, n))
            access, kind = "air.sample", "%s<half, sample>" % nd
            sampler = True
        body += '  %g = extractvalue { <4 x half>, i8 } %r, 0\n'
        body += '  %v = fpext <4 x half> %g to <4 x float>'
        out.append(("%s %s" % (name, coord[:n]),
                    build(have[name], body, sampler, kind, access),
                    texel(*coord[:3]) if nd == "3d" else texel(*coord[:2]), False))

    return out


def collect_declarations():
    air2nir = os.environ.get(
        "AIR2NIR", os.path.join(ROOT, "build/mesa-host/build/src/compiler/air/air2nir"))
    out = set()
    for dirpath, _, names in os.walk(os.path.join(ROOT, "sysimage/rootfs")):
        for n in sorted(names):
            if not n.endswith(".metallib"):
                continue
            ll = subprocess.run([air2nir, "--ll", os.path.join(dirpath, n)],
                                capture_output=True).stdout
            for line in ll.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines():
                if line.startswith("declare ") and "@air." in line:
                    line = re.sub(r"\s+local_unnamed_addr.*$", "", line)
                    out.add(re.sub(r"\s+#\d+$", "", line).strip())
    return sorted(out)


def run(d, i, source):
    ll, bc = os.path.join(d, "t%03d.ll" % i), os.path.join(d, "t%03d.bc" % i)
    with open(ll, "w") as f:
        f.write(source)
    q = subprocess.run(["llvm-as", "-o", bc, ll], capture_output=True)
    if q.returncode:
        return None, "llvm-as: " + q.stderr.decode().strip().splitlines()[0]
    q = subprocess.run([AIR_RUN, bc], capture_output=True)
    out = q.stdout.decode() + q.stderr.decode()
    i = out.find("came back as")
    if i < 0:
        for line in out.splitlines():
            if any(w in line for w in ("this harness", "Assertion", "error",
                                       "does not bind", "stores nothing")):
                return None, line.strip()
        return None, (out.strip().splitlines() or ["no output"])[-1]
    vals = []
    for line in out[i:].splitlines()[1:]:
        t = line.strip()
        if not re.match(r"^-?[0-9]", t):
            break
        vals.append(float(t))
    return vals, None


def main(argv):
    keep = None
    verbose = "-v" in argv
    if "--keep" in argv:
        keep = argv[argv.index("--keep") + 1]
    if not os.path.exists(AIR_RUN):
        print("texopcheck: no air_run at %s (run tools/air/mk-host.sh)" % AIR_RUN,
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    todo = cases(collect_declarations())
    if not todo:
        print("texopcheck: no texture declaration in the corpus has a case here",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    d = keep or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="texopcheck.")
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    exact = other = refused = 0
    narrow = set()
    for i, (label, source, want, unordered) in enumerate(todo):
        got, err = run(d, i, source)
        if got is None:
            # TGSI's registers are 32-bit, so softpipe cannot carry a 16-bit
            # texture result: nir_to_tgsi asserts. That is softpipe's limit and
            # not the frontend's, and it is the same one intrincheck.py sets
            # aside for the narrow arithmetic. ir3 has real 16-bit registers,
            # so these are a question for the phone.
            if "nir_to_tgsi" in err and re.search(r"v4i16|v4f16", label):
                narrow.add(label.split(" ")[0])
                continue
            print("refused %-44s %s" % (label, err[:80]))
            refused += 1
            continue
        g4 = sorted(got[:4]) if unordered else got[:4]
        w4 = sorted(float(w) for w in want) if unordered else [float(w) for w in want]
        if w4 == g4:
            exact += 1
            if verbose:
                print("EXACT   %-44s %s" % (label, " ".join("%g" % g for g in got[:4])))
        else:
            other += 1
            print("WRONG   %-44s got %s  want %s%s"
                  % (label, " ".join("%g" % g for g in g4),
                     " ".join("%g" % w for w in w4),
                     " (in any order)" if unordered else ""))

    print()
    print("texopcheck: %d texture calls run: %d returned exactly what was put there, "
          "%d did not, %d refused" % (len(todo) - sum(1 for l, _, _, _ in todo
                                          if l.split(" ")[0] in narrow),
                          exact, other, refused))
    if narrow:
        print("texopcheck: %d declarations left out: a 16-bit result, and TGSI's registers"
              % len(narrow))
        print("texopcheck: are 32-bit, so softpipe asserts rather than answering wrongly")
    print("texopcheck: the coordinates differ between calls, so a lowering that ignored")
    print("texopcheck: them and always fetched (1,1) would fail here and not in texcheck.sh")
    print("texopcheck: a gather is compared as a multiset: it came back in GL's order,")
    print("texopcheck: (i0j1, i1j1, i1j0, i0j0), but Metal's own order is not established")
    print("texopcheck: here, so the footprint and the channel are checked and not the order")
    print("texopcheck: nothing here tests Metal's sampler state: the sampler is the API's")
    print("texopcheck: (nearest, clamped) and the 64-bit sampler word is not decoded")
    if keep:
        print("texopcheck: kept in %s" % d)
    return 1 if (other or refused) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the small tools that are run on the phone under Android (adb's root shell): static arm64
# Linux binaries with no C library, so nothing beyond clang and lld is needed.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -fno-stack-protector -nostdlib -static \
	-fuse-ld=lld -O1 -Wall -Wl,-e,_start -o f2fs-resize f2fs-resize.c
ls -la f2fs-resize
```

`tools/android/f2fs-resize.c`:

```c
/*
 * f2fs-resize MOUNTPOINT BLOCKS: ask Android's kernel to shrink the mounted f2fs at MOUNTPOINT to
 * BLOCKS blocks of 4 KB (F2FS_IOC_RESIZE_FS). The kernel moves whatever lies past the new end
 * (here nothing does: see tools/userdata-carve.py) and rewrites the superblocks and the
 * checkpoint; the partition itself stays as it is until its GPT entry is changed.
 * "f2fs-resize MOUNTPOINT probe" only asks whether the kernel has that ioctl at all, by asking
 * for a size it must refuse (one block more than there is): EINVAL means it has, ENOTTY not.
 *
 * Built without any C library (raw system calls), for adb's root shell:
 *   tools/android/build.sh
 */
typedef unsigned long u64;

#define F2FS_IOC_RESIZE_FS 0x4008f510UL         /* _IOW(0xf5, 16, __u64) */
#define AT_FDCWD (-100)
#define O_RDONLY_DIRECTORY 040000               /* O_DIRECTORY | O_RDONLY on arm64 */

static long
sys(long n, long a, long b, long c, long d)
{
	register long x8 __asm__("x8") = n, x0 __asm__("x0") = a, x1 __asm__("x1") = b;
	register long x2 __asm__("x2") = c, x3 __asm__("x3") = d;
	__asm__ volatile ("svc 0" : "+r"(x0) : "r"(x8), "r"(x1), "r"(x2), "r"(x3) : "memory");
	return x0;
}

static void
say(const char *s)
{
	long n = 0;
	while (s[n]) {
		n++;
	}
	sys(64, 1, (long)s, n, 0);              /* write */
}

static void
say_num(u64 v)
{
	char b[24];
	int i = 23;
	b[i] = 0;
	do {
		b[--i] = (char)('0' + v % 10);
		v /= 10;
	} while (v);
	say(b + i);
}

static int
equal(const char *a, const char *b)
{
	while (*a && *a == *b) {
		a++;
		b++;
	}
	return *a == *b;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	u64 blocks = 0;
	long fd, r;

	if (argc != 3) {
		say("usage: f2fs-resize MOUNTPOINT BLOCKS|probe\n");
		return 2;
	}
	if (equal(argv[2], "probe")) {
		blocks = (u64)1 << 40;
	} else {
		for (const char *p = argv[2]; *p; p++) {
			if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') {
				say("f2fs-resize: BLOCKS is a number of 4 KB blocks\n");
				return 2;
			}
			blocks = blocks * 10 + (u64)(*p - '0');
		}
	}
	fd = sys(56, AT_FDCWD, (long)argv[1], O_RDONLY_DIRECTORY, 0);   /* openat */
	if (fd < 0) {
		say("f2fs-resize: cannot open ");
		say(argv[1]);
		say(": errno ");
		say_num((u64)-fd);
		say("\n");
		return 1;
	}
	r = sys(29, fd, (long)F2FS_IOC_RESIZE_FS, (long)&blocks, 0);    /* ioctl */
	say("f2fs-resize: F2FS_IOC_RESIZE_FS to ");
	say_num(blocks);
	say(" blocks: ");
	if (r == 0) {
		say("done\n");
	} else {
		say("errno ");
		say_num((u64)-r);
		say(-r == 22 ? " (EINVAL)\n" : -r == 25 ? " (ENOTTY: no such ioctl)\n" : -r == 28 ? " (ENOSPC)\n" :
		    -r == 1 ? " (EPERM)\n" : -r == 30 ? " (EROFS)\n" : -r == 117 ? " (EFSCORRUPTED: fsck first)\n" : "\n");
	}
	sys(57, fd, 0, 0, 0);                   /* close */
	return r == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}

/* the entry point: argc and argv on the stack, as the kernel leaves them */
__attribute__((naked, noreturn)) void
_start(void)
{
	__asm__ volatile (
		"ldr x0, [sp]\n"
		"add x1, sp, #8\n"
		"bl main\n"
		"mov x8, #93\n"         /* exit */
		"svc 0\n");
}

```

`tools/apfs/apfs-tool.c`:

```c
/*
 * Run the kernel's APFS reading code on the build machine.
 *
 * bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_lib.c is built into this program unchanged, so what it says about
 * an image here is what the driver will see.  `census` prints a line per directory entry
 * that tools/apfs/apfs.py can print too, and run-tests.sh diffs the two: the Python
 * reader has already been checked against 7-Zip over the whole volume, so agreeing with
 * it byte for byte is the C code agreeing with the image.
 *
 * Built by tools/apfs/build-tool.sh.
 *
 * usage: apfs-tool info   IMAGE
 *        apfs-tool ls     IMAGE [PATH]
 *        apfs-tool stat   IMAGE PATH
 *        apfs-tool cat    IMAGE PATH
 *        apfs-tool census IMAGE [PATH] [--meta]   (--meta: do not read contents)
 *        apfs-tool lookups IMAGE    (every name looked up by name; see cmd_lookups)
 *        apfs-tool writable IMAGE   (may the volume be written in place, and why not)
 *        apfs-tool write  IMAGE PATH OFFSET FILE|- [--fail-after N | --corrupt-after N]
 *        apfs-tool store  info IMAGE | save IMAGE FILE|- | load IMAGE FILE|-
 *                                   (the store of fixed-length slot files: bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_store.c)
 *                                   (the kernel's apfs_write.c; --fail-after is a power failure,
 *                                    --corrupt-after a device that lies about the write)
 */

/* pread(2) and clock_gettime(2) come with -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE, set by build-tool.sh */
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "apfs_lib.h"
#include "apfs_write.h"
#include "apfs_store.h"

/* ---- the image as a device ---- */

static int
file_read(void *ctx, uint64_t off, void *buf, size_t len)
{
	int fd = (int)(intptr_t)ctx;
	uint8_t *p = buf;

	while (len > 0) {
		ssize_t n = pread(fd, p, len, (off_t)off);

		if (n <= 0) {
			return EIO;
		}
		p += n;
		off += (uint64_t)n;
		len -= (size_t)n;
	}
	return 0;
}

/* The same hash the Python side computes, so contents can be compared without the bytes. */
static uint64_t
fnv1a(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint64_t h)
{
	size_t i;

	for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		h ^= p[i];
		h *= 0x100000001b3ULL;
	}
	return h;
}

#define FNV_INIT 0xcbf29ce484222325ULL

/*
 * APFS_TOOL_THREADS=N: nx->parallel on threads of this program, so that what the kernel
 * does on several processors -- whole pieces of one request read and decompressed at once
 * -- runs here the same way (and can be run under ThreadSanitizer).  A thread per worker
 * per call: slow, and only for checking.
 */
struct host_par {
	int (*fn)(void *arg, uint32_t item, uint32_t worker);
	void *arg;
	uint32_t items;
	atomic_uint next;
	atomic_int error;
};

struct host_par_arg {
	struct host_par *hp;
	uint32_t worker;
};

static void
host_par_work(struct host_par *hp, uint32_t worker)
{
	for (;;) {
		uint32_t item = atomic_fetch_add(&hp->next, 1);
		int error, none = 0;

		if (item >= hp->items) {
			break;
		}
		error = hp->fn(hp->arg, item, worker);
		if (error != 0) {
			atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&hp->error, &none, error);
		}
	}
}

static void *
host_par_thread(void *p)
{
	struct host_par_arg *a = p;

	host_par_work(a->hp, a->worker);
	return NULL;
}

static int
host_parallel(void *ctx, uint32_t items, uint32_t workers,
    int (*fn)(void *arg, uint32_t item, uint32_t worker), void *arg)
{
	struct host_par hp;
	struct host_par_arg a[16];
	pthread_t th[16];
	uint32_t w, started = 1;

	(void)ctx;
	hp.fn = fn;
	hp.arg = arg;
	hp.items = items;
	atomic_init(&hp.next, 0);
	atomic_init(&hp.error, 0);
	for (w = 1; w < workers && w < 16; w++) {
		a[w].hp = &hp;
		a[w].worker = w;
		if (pthread_create(&th[w], NULL, host_par_thread, &a[w]) != 0) {
			break;
		}
		started++;
	}
	host_par_work(&hp, 0);
	for (w = 1; w < started; w++) {
		pthread_join(th[w], NULL);
	}
	return atomic_load(&hp.error);
}

static bool want_lock;                 /* the library under a lock, as in the kernel (walkers, cfrace) */
static void host_locking(struct apfs_nx *nx);
static void op_begin(void);
static void op_end(void);

/*
 * The image opened for writing, and the power failure stood in for: after `write_fail_after`
 * blocks the device refuses every write, as a phone whose battery came out mid-write would.
 * Without it nothing refuses; --fail-after 0 refuses the very first block.
 */
static bool want_write;
static bool write_fails;                /* --fail-after was given; 0 of them is a failure too */
static bool write_corrupts;             /* --corrupt-after: a device that lies about a write */
static uint64_t write_fail_after;
static uint64_t writes_done;

static int
file_write(void *ctx, uint64_t off, const void *buf, size_t len)
{
	int fd = (int)(intptr_t)ctx;
	const uint8_t *p = buf;

	uint8_t *copy = NULL;

	if (write_fails && writes_done >= write_fail_after) {
		return EIO;
	}
	if (write_corrupts && writes_done >= write_fail_after) {
		/*
		 * A device that says the write went through and puts something else on the
		 * platter: the one failure no checking before the write can catch, and what the
		 * read-back comparison in apfs_write.c is there for.
		 */
		copy = malloc(len);
		if (copy == NULL) {
			return EIO;
		}
		memcpy(copy, p, len);
		copy[0] ^= 0xff;
		p = copy;
	}
	writes_done++;
	while (len > 0) {
		ssize_t n = pwrite(fd, p, len, (off_t)off);

		if (n <= 0) {
			free(copy);
			return EIO;
		}
		p += n;
		off += (uint64_t)n;
		len -= (size_t)n;
	}
	free(copy);
	return 0;
}

static int
open_image(const char *path, struct apfs_nx *nx, struct apfs_vol *vol)
{
	struct apfs_dev dev;
	int fd = open(path, want_write ? O_RDWR : O_RDONLY);
	uint32_t i;
	int error;

	if (fd < 0) {
		perror(path);
		return 1;
	}
	memset(&dev, 0, sizeof(dev));
	dev.ctx = (void *)(intptr_t)fd;
	dev.size = (uint64_t)lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END);
	dev.read = file_read;
	dev.read_data = file_read;      /* pread is as good without a lock as with one */
	if (want_write) {
		dev.write = file_write;
	}

	error = apfs_nx_open(nx, &dev);
	if (error) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: cannot read the container: %s\n", strerror(error));
		return 1;
	}
	if (getenv("APFS_TOOL_THREADS") != NULL) {
		long t = strtol(getenv("APFS_TOOL_THREADS"), NULL, 0);

		if (t > 1) {
			nx->parallel = host_parallel;
			nx->parallel_max = (uint32_t)(t < 16 ? t : 16);
		}
	}
	if (getenv("APFS_TOOL_WALKERS") != NULL && strtol(getenv("APFS_TOOL_WALKERS"), NULL, 0) > 1) {
		want_lock = true;
	}
	if (want_lock) {
		/* handed over now, as the kernel's mount does; from here on every call is with the lock */
		host_locking(nx);
		op_begin();
	}
	/* the first volume that has a root directory, like apfs.py picks it; or APFS_TOOL_VOLUME=N */
	for (i = 0; i < APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS; i++) {
		if (getenv("APFS_TOOL_VOLUME") != NULL && (long)i != strtol(getenv("APFS_TOOL_VOLUME"), NULL, 0)) {
			continue;
		}
		struct apfs_inode ino;

		if (nx->fs_oid[i] == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (apfs_vol_open(nx, i, vol) != 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (apfs_inode_get(vol, APFS_ROOT_DIR_INO_NUM, &ino) == 0) {
			if (want_lock) {
				op_end();
			}
			return 0;
		}
	}
	if (want_lock) {
		op_end();
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: no readable volume with a root directory\n");
	return 1;
}

/* ---- info ---- */

static int
cmd_info(const char *path)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	uint32_t i;

	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	printf("%s: APFS container, block size %u, %" PRIu64 " blocks\n", path,
	    nx.block_size, nx.block_count);
	printf("  newest checkpoint xid %" PRIu64 "\n", nx.xid);
	printf("  container omap block %" PRIu64 "\n", nx.omap_addr);
	for (i = 0; i < APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS; i++) {
		struct apfs_vol v;

		if (nx.fs_oid[i] == 0 || apfs_vol_open(&nx, i, &v) != 0) {
			continue;
		}
		printf("  [%u] %s  role 0x%04x  incompatible 0x%" PRIx64 "  fs flags 0x%" PRIx64 "\n",
		    i, v.name, v.role, v.incompat, v.fs_flags);
		printf("       files %" PRIu64 "  dirs %" PRIu64 "  symlinks %" PRIu64
		    "  blocks used %" PRIu64 "\n", v.num_files, v.num_dirs, v.num_symlinks,
		    v.alloc_count);
		printf("       tree: %" PRIu64 " records in %" PRIu64 " nodes, flags 0x%x\n",
		    v.tree.key_count, v.tree.node_count, v.tree.flags);
	}
	printf("  blocks read %" PRIu64 ", cache hits %" PRIu64 "\n", nx.reads, nx.hits);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return 0;
}

/* ---- ls ---- */

struct ls_ctx {
	struct apfs_vol *vol;
};

static const char *
mode_kind(uint16_t mode)
{
	switch (mode & APFS_S_IFMT) {
	case APFS_S_IFDIR:  return "d";
	case APFS_S_IFLNK:  return "l";
	case APFS_S_IFREG:  return "-";
	case APFS_S_IFIFO:  return "p";
	case APFS_S_IFCHR:  return "c";
	case APFS_S_IFBLK:  return "b";
	case APFS_S_IFSOCK: return "s";
	default:            return "?";
	}
}

static int
ls_cb(void *ctx, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint64_t file_id, uint8_t d_type)
{
	struct ls_ctx *lc = ctx;
	struct apfs_inode ino;

	(void)name_len;
	(void)d_type;
	if (apfs_inode_get(lc->vol, file_id, &ino) != 0) {
		printf("?  %20s  %s  (no inode record)\n", "", name);
		return 0;
	}
	printf("%s %06o %4u:%-4u %12" PRIu64 "  %-20" PRIu64 " %s", mode_kind(ino.mode),
	    ino.mode & 07777, ino.owner, ino.group, ino.size, file_id, name);
	if ((ino.mode & APFS_S_IFMT) == APFS_S_IFLNK) {
		char target[1024];
		size_t n = 0;

		if (apfs_readlink(lc->vol, file_id, target, sizeof(target) - 1, &n) == 0) {
			target[n] = '\0';
			printf(" -> %s", target);
		}
	}
	printf("\n");
	return 0;
}

static int
cmd_ls(const char *path, const char *where)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct ls_ctx lc;
	uint64_t id;
	uint8_t dt;
	int error;

	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	error = apfs_path_lookup(&vol, where, &id, &dt);
	if (error) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: %s\n", where, strerror(error));
		return 1;
	}
	lc.vol = &vol;
	if (dt != APFS_DT_DIR) {
		ls_cb(&lc, where, strlen(where), id, dt);
	} else {
		error = apfs_readdir(&vol, id, ls_cb, &lc);
		if (error) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s\n", strerror(error));
			return 1;
		}
	}
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return 0;
}

/* ---- stat ---- */

static int
xattr_print_cb(void *ctx, const char *name, size_t name_len, const struct apfs_xattr *xa)
{
	(void)ctx;
	(void)name_len;
	printf("  xattr %-28s flags 0x%x  %u bytes%s\n", name, xa->flags, xa->data_len,
	    (xa->flags & APFS_XATTR_DATA_STREAM) ? " (in a data stream)" : "");
	return 0;
}

static int
cmd_stat(const char *path, const char *where)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct apfs_inode ino;
	struct apfs_cfile cf;
	uint64_t id;
	uint8_t dt;
	int error;

	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	error = apfs_path_lookup(&vol, where, &id, &dt);
	if (error) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: %s\n", where, strerror(error));
		return 1;
	}
	error = apfs_inode_get(&vol, id, &ino);
	if (error) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: inode %" PRIu64 ": %s\n", id, strerror(error));
		return 1;
	}
	printf("path        %s\n", where);
	printf("inode       %" PRIu64 "  parent %" PRIu64 "  private %" PRIu64 "\n",
	    ino.obj_id, ino.parent_id, ino.private_id);
	printf("mode        %06o  uid %u  gid %u\n", ino.mode, ino.owner, ino.group);
	printf("size        %" PRIu64 "  allocated %" PRIu64 "\n", ino.size,
	    ino.alloced_size);
	printf("flags       internal 0x%" PRIx64 "  bsd 0x%x%s\n", ino.internal_flags,
	    ino.bsd_flags, ino.is_sparse ? "  sparse" : "");
	memset(&cf, 0, sizeof(cf));
	cf.held = APFS_NO_PIECE;
	if (apfs_cfile_init(&vol, &ino, &cf) == 0 && cf.compressed) {
		printf("decmpfs     type %u  uncompressed %" PRIu64 "  %s\n", cf.type, cf.size,
		    cf.in_rsrc ? "in the resource fork" : "in the attribute");
	}
	apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
	apfs_xattr_list(&vol, id, xattr_print_cb, NULL);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return 0;
}

/* ---- cat ---- */

static int
cmd_cat(const char *path, const char *where)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct apfs_inode ino;
	struct apfs_cfile cf;
	uint64_t id, off = 0;
	uint8_t dt;
	uint8_t *buf;
	int error;

	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	error = apfs_path_lookup(&vol, where, &id, &dt);
	if (error == 0) {
		error = apfs_inode_get(&vol, id, &ino);
	}
	if (error) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: %s\n", where, strerror(error));
		return 1;
	}
	buf = malloc(65536);
	if (buf == NULL) {
		return 1;
	}
	memset(&cf, 0, sizeof(cf));
	cf.held = APFS_NO_PIECE;
	{
		uint64_t size = 0;

		/* (a compressed file's size is in its decmpfs header, not its inode) */
		if (apfs_inode_size(&vol, &ino, &size) == 0) {
			ino.size = size;
		}
	}
	while (off < ino.size) {
		size_t got = 0;

		error = apfs_read_file(&vol, &ino, &cf, off, buf, 65536, &got);
		if (error) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: read at %" PRIu64 ": %s\n", off,
			    strerror(error));
			free(buf);
			return 1;
		}
		if (got == 0) {
			break;
		}
		if (fwrite(buf, 1, got, stdout) != got) {
			free(buf);
			return 1;
		}
		off += got;
	}
	apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
	free(buf);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return 0;
}

/*
 * ---- several threads on the library at once, as in the kernel ----
 *
 * The kernel holds one lock round apfs_lib for each operation and lets apfs_lib let go of it
 * in the middle (reading file contents, and a block of metadata not in the cache); a block
 * leaving the cache keeps its memory until no operation that began before can be reading it
 * (apfs_nx_reclaim). The same here, with a pthread mutex, so that it can be run under
 * ThreadSanitizer: op_begin/op_end are the kernel's apfs_lock/apfs_unlock.
 */
static pthread_mutex_t host_lock;      /* error checking: unlocking one not held aborts, as the kernel panics */
static struct apfs_nx *host_nx;

static void
host_lock_check(int error, const char *what)
{
	if (error != 0) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s the library's lock: %s\n", what, strerror(error));
		abort();
	}
}
#define HOST_OPS 64
static struct {
	pthread_t th;
	uint64_t  epoch;
	bool      used;
} host_ops[HOST_OPS];

static void
host_unlock(void *ctx)
{
	(void)ctx;
	host_lock_check(pthread_mutex_unlock(&host_lock), "letting go of");
}

static void
host_relock(void *ctx)
{
	(void)ctx;
	host_lock_check(pthread_mutex_lock(&host_lock), "taking");
}

static void
op_begin(void)
{
	host_lock_check(pthread_mutex_lock(&host_lock), "taking");
	for (int i = 0; i < HOST_OPS; i++) {
		if (!host_ops[i].used) {
			host_ops[i].used = true;
			host_ops[i].th = pthread_self();
			host_ops[i].epoch = host_nx->epoch;
			return;
		}
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: more operations at once than %d\n", HOST_OPS);
	abort();
}

static void
op_end(void)
{
	uint64_t oldest = host_nx->epoch;

	for (int i = 0; i < HOST_OPS; i++) {
		if (host_ops[i].used && pthread_equal(host_ops[i].th, pthread_self())) {
			host_ops[i].used = false;
		} else if (host_ops[i].used && host_ops[i].epoch < oldest) {
			oldest = host_ops[i].epoch;
		}
	}
	apfs_nx_reclaim(host_nx, oldest);
	host_lock_check(pthread_mutex_unlock(&host_lock), "letting go of");
}

static void
host_locking(struct apfs_nx *nx)
{
	pthread_mutexattr_t a;

	pthread_mutexattr_init(&a);
	pthread_mutexattr_settype(&a, PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK);
	pthread_mutex_init(&host_lock, &a);
	host_nx = nx;
	nx->unlock = host_unlock;
	nx->relock = host_relock;
	nx->lock_ctx = NULL;
}

/* ---- census: one line per entry, for diffing against apfs.py ---- */

struct census {
	struct apfs_vol *vol;
	char            *path;          /* the directory being walked, with a trailing / */
	size_t           path_len;
	size_t           path_cap;
	uint8_t         *buf;
	long             max;
	long             seen;
	size_t           chunk;         /* how much each read asks for */
	bool             meta_only;
	int              error;
};

static int census_dir(struct census *cs, uint64_t dir_id);
static int census_parallel(struct apfs_nx *nx, struct apfs_vol *vol, uint64_t start, const char *where,
    size_t chunk, bool meta_only, int n);

static uint64_t
file_hash(struct census *cs, const struct apfs_inode *ino, uint64_t size)
{
	uint64_t h = FNV_INIT, off = 0;
	struct apfs_cfile cf;

	memset(&cf, 0, sizeof(cf));
	cf.held = APFS_NO_PIECE;
	for (;;) {
		size_t got = 0;
		int error = apfs_read_file(cs->vol, ino, &cf, off, cs->buf, cs->chunk, &got);

		if (error) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: read at %" PRIu64 ": %s\n", cs->path,
			    off, strerror(error));
			cs->error = error;
			apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
			return 0;
		}
		if (got == 0) {
			break;
		}
		h = fnv1a(cs->buf, got, h);
		off += got;
		if (off >= size) {
			break;
		}
	}
	apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
	return h;
}

static int
census_cb(void *ctx, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint64_t file_id, uint8_t d_type)
{
	struct census *cs = ctx;
	struct apfs_inode ino;
	size_t saved = cs->path_len;
	uint64_t h = 0, size = 0;
	int error;

	if (cs->max > 0 && cs->seen >= cs->max) {
		return EEXIST;
	}
	/* append "/name" to the path we are at */
	while (cs->path_len + name_len + 2 > cs->path_cap) {
		cs->path_cap *= 2;
		cs->path = realloc(cs->path, cs->path_cap);
		if (cs->path == NULL) {
			return ENOMEM;
		}
	}
	cs->path[cs->path_len++] = '/';
	memcpy(cs->path + cs->path_len, name, name_len);
	cs->path_len += name_len;
	cs->path[cs->path_len] = '\0';

	error = apfs_inode_get(cs->vol, file_id, &ino);
	if (error) {
		printf("%s\t?\tno-inode\n", cs->path);
		cs->error = error;
		goto done;
	}
	cs->seen++;
	if (apfs_inode_size(cs->vol, &ino, &size) != 0) {
		size = ino.size;
	}
	if (!cs->meta_only && ((ino.mode & APFS_S_IFMT) == APFS_S_IFREG ||
	    (ino.mode & APFS_S_IFMT) == APFS_S_IFLNK)) {
		h = file_hash(cs, &ino, size);
	}
	printf("%s\t%u\t%06o\t%u\t%u\t%" PRIu64 "\t%016" PRIx64 "\n", cs->path, d_type,
	    ino.mode, ino.owner, ino.group, size, h);

	if (d_type == APFS_DT_DIR) {
		error = census_dir(cs, file_id);
		if (error) {
			cs->path_len = saved;
			cs->path[cs->path_len] = '\0';
			return error;
		}
	}
done:
	cs->path_len = saved;
	cs->path[cs->path_len] = '\0';
	return 0;
}

static int
census_dir(struct census *cs, uint64_t dir_id)
{
	return apfs_readdir(cs->vol, dir_id, census_cb, cs);
}

static int
cmd_census(const char *path, const char *where, bool meta_only)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct census cs;
	uint64_t start = APFS_ROOT_DIR_INO_NUM;
	uint8_t dt = APFS_DT_DIR;
	int error;

	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	if (where != NULL) {
		int e;

		if (want_lock) {
			op_begin();
		}
		e = apfs_path_lookup(&vol, where, &start, &dt);
		if (want_lock) {
			op_end();
		}
		if (e != 0) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: not found\n", where);
			return 1;
		}
	}
	memset(&cs, 0, sizeof(cs));
	cs.vol = &vol;
	cs.path_cap = 4096;
	cs.path = malloc(cs.path_cap);
	/*
	 * APFS_TOOL_CHUNK: reads of another size than 64 KB (say 4096, or 12345 and 200000,
	 * which never line up with a compressed file's 64 KB pieces), so that the roads through
	 * apfs_read_file the census does not otherwise take are checked over a whole volume too.
	 */
	cs.chunk = 65536;
	if (getenv("APFS_TOOL_CHUNK") != NULL) {
		long c = strtol(getenv("APFS_TOOL_CHUNK"), NULL, 0);

		if (c < 1 || c > 16 * 1024 * 1024) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: APFS_TOOL_CHUNK %ld is not 1..16M\n", c);
			return 2;
		}
		cs.chunk = (size_t)c;
	}
	cs.buf = malloc(cs.chunk);
	cs.max = 0;
	cs.meta_only = meta_only;
	if (cs.path == NULL || cs.buf == NULL) {
		return 1;
	}
	cs.path[0] = '\0';
	if (where != NULL) {
		size_t n = strlen(where);

		while (n > 0 && where[n - 1] == '/') {
			n--;
		}
		memcpy(cs.path, where, n);
		cs.path_len = n;
		cs.path[n] = '\0';
	}
	if (getenv("APFS_TOOL_WALKERS") != NULL && strtol(getenv("APFS_TOOL_WALKERS"), NULL, 0) > 1) {
		long n = strtol(getenv("APFS_TOOL_WALKERS"), NULL, 0);

		return census_parallel(&nx, &vol, start, where, cs.chunk, meta_only, (int)(n > 16 ? 16 : n));
	}
	error = census_dir(&cs, start);
	if (error && error != EEXIST) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: census: %s\n", strerror(error));
		return 1;
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %ld entries, %" PRIu64 " blocks read, %" PRIu64
	    " cache hits; %" PRIu64 " neighbours brought in, %" PRIu64 " of them asked for\n",
	    cs.seen, nx.reads, nx.hits, nx.prefetched, nx.prefetch_used);
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: inflate %" PRIu64 " calls, %" PRIu64 " bytes in, %" PRIu64
	    " bytes out, %" PRIu64 " by zlib\n", nx.inflate_calls, nx.inflate_in, nx.inflate_out,
	    nx.inflate_fallbacks);
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %" PRIu64 " requests of whole pieces, %" PRIu64 " pieces in "
	    "them, on %u threads at most; read ahead %" PRIu64 " times, %" PRIu64 " pieces, %"
	    PRIu64 " of them used\n", nx.batch_calls, nx.batch_pieces,
	    nx.parallel != NULL ? nx.parallel_max : 1, nx.ra_batches, nx.ra_pieces, nx.ra_hits);
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: highest block touched %" PRIu64 " (%.2f GB in), of which "
	    "file contents reach %" PRIu64 " (%.2f GB in)\n", nx.max_addr,
	    nx.max_addr * (double)nx.block_size / 1e9, nx.max_data_addr,
	    nx.max_data_addr * (double)nx.block_size / 1e9);
	free(cs.path);
	free(cs.buf);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return cs.error ? 1 : 0;
}

/*
 * APFS_TOOL_WALKERS=N with census: N threads walk at once, taking directories off one shared
 * stack, each line hashed and the hashes added up (order does not matter): the same sum the
 * kernel's apfs_check prints. Lines are not printed.
 */
struct pjob {
	uint64_t dir_id;
	char    *path;
};

static pthread_mutex_t pmtx = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_cond_t pcond = PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER;
static struct pjob *pstack;
static size_t pcount, pcap;
static int pbusy;

struct pwalker {
	struct apfs_vol *vol;
	const char      *dir;           /* the directory being walked */
	uint8_t         *buf;
	size_t           chunk;
	bool             meta_only;
	uint64_t         sum, entries, bytes;
	int              error;
};

static void
ppush(uint64_t dir_id, const char *path)
{
	pthread_mutex_lock(&pmtx);
	if (pcount == pcap) {
		pcap = pcap ? 2 * pcap : 1024;
		pstack = realloc(pstack, pcap * sizeof(*pstack));
		if (pstack == NULL) {
			abort();
		}
	}
	pstack[pcount].dir_id = dir_id;
	pstack[pcount].path = strdup(path);
	pcount++;
	pthread_cond_signal(&pcond);
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&pmtx);
}

static uint64_t
pfile_hash(struct pwalker *w, const struct apfs_inode *ino, uint64_t size, const char *path)
{
	uint64_t h = FNV_INIT, off = 0;
	struct apfs_cfile cf;

	memset(&cf, 0, sizeof(cf));
	cf.held = APFS_NO_PIECE;
	for (;;) {
		size_t got = 0;
		int error = apfs_read_file(w->vol, ino, &cf, off, w->buf, w->chunk, &got);

		if (error) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: read at %" PRIu64 ": %s\n", path, off, strerror(error));
			w->error = error;
			break;
		}
		if (got == 0) {
			break;
		}
		h = fnv1a(w->buf, got, h);
		off += got;
		w->bytes += got;
		if (off >= size) {
			break;
		}
	}
	apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
	return h;
}

static int
pcensus_cb(void *ctx, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint64_t file_id, uint8_t d_type)
{
	struct pwalker *w = ctx;
	struct apfs_inode ino;
	uint64_t h = 0, size = 0;
	char path[4096], line[4096 + 128];
	int n;

	n = snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/%.*s", w->dir, (int)name_len, name);
	if (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= sizeof(path)) {
		w->error = ENAMETOOLONG;
		return 0;
	}
	if (apfs_inode_get(w->vol, file_id, &ino) != 0) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: no inode\n", path);
		w->error = ENOENT;
		return 0;
	}
	if (apfs_inode_size(w->vol, &ino, &size) != 0) {
		size = ino.size;
	}
	if (!w->meta_only && ((ino.mode & APFS_S_IFMT) == APFS_S_IFREG || (ino.mode & APFS_S_IFMT) == APFS_S_IFLNK)) {
		h = pfile_hash(w, &ino, size, path);
	}
	n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s\t%u\t%06o\t%u\t%u\t%" PRIu64 "\t%016" PRIx64 "\n", path, d_type,
	    ino.mode, ino.owner, ino.group, size, h);
	w->sum += fnv1a((const uint8_t *)line, (size_t)n, FNV_INIT);
	w->entries++;
	if (d_type == APFS_DT_DIR) {
		ppush(file_id, path);
	}
	return 0;
}

static void *
pwalker_thread(void *p)
{
	struct pwalker *w = p;

	for (;;) {
		struct pjob j;
		int error;

		pthread_mutex_lock(&pmtx);
		while (pcount == 0 && pbusy > 0) {
			pthread_cond_wait(&pcond, &pmtx);
		}
		if (pcount == 0) {
			pthread_cond_broadcast(&pcond);
			pthread_mutex_unlock(&pmtx);
			return NULL;
		}
		j = pstack[--pcount];
		pbusy++;
		pthread_mutex_unlock(&pmtx);

		w->dir = j.path;
		op_begin();
		error = apfs_readdir(w->vol, j.dir_id, pcensus_cb, w);
		op_end();
		if (error) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: readdir: %s\n", j.path, strerror(error));
			w->error = error;
		}
		free(j.path);

		pthread_mutex_lock(&pmtx);
		pbusy--;
		pthread_cond_broadcast(&pcond);
		pthread_mutex_unlock(&pmtx);
	}
}

static int
census_parallel(struct apfs_nx *nx, struct apfs_vol *vol, uint64_t start, const char *where, size_t chunk,
    bool meta_only, int n)
{
	struct pwalker w[16];
	pthread_t th[16];
	uint64_t sum = 0, entries = 0, bytes = 0;
	int error = 0;

	ppush(start, where != NULL ? where : "");
	for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		memset(&w[i], 0, sizeof(w[i]));
		w[i].vol = vol;
		w[i].chunk = chunk;
		w[i].meta_only = meta_only;
		w[i].buf = malloc(chunk);
		if (w[i].buf == NULL || pthread_create(&th[i], NULL, pwalker_thread, &w[i]) != 0) {
			abort();
		}
	}
	for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		pthread_join(th[i], NULL);
		sum += w[i].sum;
		entries += w[i].entries;
		bytes += w[i].bytes;
		if (w[i].error) {
			error = w[i].error;
		}
		free(w[i].buf);
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %d walkers: %" PRIu64 " entries, %" PRIu64 " content bytes, line-hash sum %016" PRIx64
	    ", %s\n", n, entries, bytes, sum, error ? "ERRORS" : "no errors");
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: metadata read without the lock %" PRIu64 " times, %" PRIu64 " of them already in; "
	    "retired blocks %" PRIu64 " now, %" PRIu64 " at most\n", nx->unlocked_fills, nx->fill_races, nx->retired_now,
	    nx->retired_most);
	free(pstack);
	{
		int fd = (int)(intptr_t)nx->dev.ctx;

		apfs_nx_close(nx);
		close(fd);
	}
	return error ? 1 : 0;
}

/*
 * cfrace IMAGE N ROUNDS: the compressed files of the volume (up to 400, taken from a walk),
 * each read whole by N threads at once through one shared apfs_cfile -- as two readers of one
 * vnode share it in the kernel -- with the cache emptied before every round, so that setting
 * up the file and its read-ahead let go of the lock in the middle; every read must hash the
 * same as a read on one thread.
 */
struct cf_file {
	uint64_t           id;
	struct apfs_inode  ino;
	uint64_t           size;
	uint64_t           want;        /* the hash on one thread */
	struct apfs_cfile  cf;          /* shared by the threads, touched with the lock held */
};

static struct cf_file *cf_files;
static size_t cf_nfiles;
static struct apfs_vol *cf_vol;
static atomic_uint cf_bad, cf_reads;

static int
cf_collect_cb(void *ctx, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint64_t file_id, uint8_t d_type)
{
	struct apfs_inode ino;
	struct apfs_cfile cf;
	uint64_t size;

	(void)ctx;
	(void)name;
	(void)name_len;
	if (cf_nfiles >= 400) {
		return EEXIST;
	}
	if (d_type == APFS_DT_DIR) {
		return apfs_readdir(cf_vol, file_id, cf_collect_cb, NULL) == EEXIST ? EEXIST : 0;
	}
	if (d_type != APFS_DT_REG || apfs_inode_get(cf_vol, file_id, &ino) != 0 ||
	    apfs_inode_size(cf_vol, &ino, &size) != 0 || size < 3 * 65536) {
		return 0;
	}
	memset(&cf, 0, sizeof(cf));
	cf.held = APFS_NO_PIECE;
	if (apfs_cfile_init(cf_vol, &ino, &cf) == 0 && cf.compressed && cf.in_rsrc) {
		cf_files[cf_nfiles].id = file_id;
		cf_files[cf_nfiles].ino = ino;
		cf_files[cf_nfiles].size = size;
		cf_nfiles++;
	}
	apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
	return 0;
}

static uint64_t
cf_read_whole(struct cf_file *f, struct apfs_cfile *cf, uint8_t *buf, size_t chunk, bool locked)
{
	uint64_t h = FNV_INIT, off = 0;

	while (off < f->size) {
		size_t got = 0;
		int error;

		if (locked) {
			op_begin();
		}
		error = apfs_read_file(cf_vol, &f->ino, cf, off, buf, chunk, &got);
		if (locked) {
			op_end();
		}
		if (error || got == 0) {
			return 0;
		}
		h = fnv1a(buf, got, h);
		off += got;
	}
	return h;
}

static void *
cf_thread(void *p)
{
	uint8_t *buf = malloc(65536);

	(void)p;
	for (size_t i = 0; i < cf_nfiles; i++) {
		uint64_t h = cf_read_whole(&cf_files[i], &cf_files[i].cf, buf, 65536, true);

		atomic_fetch_add(&cf_reads, 1);
		if (h != cf_files[i].want) {
			atomic_fetch_add(&cf_bad, 1);
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: cfrace: inode %" PRIu64 " read DIFFERENTLY\n", cf_files[i].id);
		}
	}
	free(buf);
	return NULL;
}

static int
cmd_cfrace(const char *path, int n, int rounds)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	pthread_t th[16];
	uint8_t *buf = malloc(65536);

	want_lock = true;
	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0 || buf == NULL || n < 2 || n > 16) {
		return 1;
	}
	cf_vol = &vol;
	cf_files = calloc(400, sizeof(*cf_files));
	op_begin();
	(void)apfs_readdir(&vol, APFS_ROOT_DIR_INO_NUM, cf_collect_cb, NULL);
	op_end();
	for (size_t i = 0; i < cf_nfiles; i++) {
		struct apfs_cfile cf;

		memset(&cf, 0, sizeof(cf));
		cf.held = APFS_NO_PIECE;
		cf_files[i].want = cf_read_whole(&cf_files[i], &cf, buf, 65536, true);
		op_begin();
		apfs_cfile_fini(&cf);
		op_end();
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: cfrace: %zu compressed files of 192 KB or more, %d threads, %d rounds\n", cf_nfiles,
	    n, rounds);
	if (nx.parallel == NULL) {
		nx.parallel = host_parallel;    /* read-ahead needs helpers to spare */
		nx.parallel_max = 4;
	}
	for (int r = 0; r < rounds; r++) {
		pthread_mutex_lock(&host_lock);
		for (size_t i = 0; i < cf_nfiles; i++) {
			apfs_cfile_fini(&cf_files[i].cf);
		}
		apfs_nx_cache_flush(&nx);
		pthread_mutex_unlock(&host_lock);
		for (int t = 0; t < n; t++) {
			pthread_create(&th[t], NULL, cf_thread, NULL);
		}
		for (int t = 0; t < n; t++) {
			pthread_join(th[t], NULL);
		}
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: cfrace: %u reads, %u different; metadata read without the lock %" PRIu64
	    " times, %" PRIu64 " of them already in; read ahead %" PRIu64 " times\n", atomic_load(&cf_reads),
	    atomic_load(&cf_bad), nx.unlocked_fills, nx.fill_races, nx.ra_batches);
	/* all given back, so that a leak checker sees only what the library lost */
	for (size_t i = 0; i < cf_nfiles; i++) {
		apfs_cfile_fini(&cf_files[i].cf);
	}
	free(cf_files);
	free(buf);
	{
		int fd = (int)(intptr_t)nx.dev.ctx;

		apfs_nx_close(&nx);
		close(fd);
	}
	return atomic_load(&cf_bad) != 0;
}

/*
 * namehash IMAGE OUT: every directory record's name hashed the way the lookup hashes it,
 * against the hash APFS stored with it; and into OUT, for tools/apfs/test_namehash.py to work
 * out independently, a line per record: directory, the name in hex, the stored hash, the hash
 * as on a case-sensitive volume and as on a case-insensitive one, the file's id.
 */
struct nh_ctx {
	FILE    *out;
	bool     fold;
	uint64_t total, ascii, other, same, differ, unhashable;
};

static int
namehash_cb(void *ctx, uint64_t dir_id, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint32_t stored, uint64_t file_id)
{
	struct nh_ctx *c = ctx;
	uint32_t cs = 0, ci = 0, mine;
	bool ok_cs = apfs_name_hash(name, name_len, false, &cs), ok_ci = apfs_name_hash(name, name_len, true, &ci);
	bool ascii = true;

	for (size_t i = 0; i < name_len; i++) {
		ascii &= (uint8_t)name[i] < 0x80;
	}
	c->total++;
	if (ascii) {
		c->ascii++;
	} else {
		c->other++;
	}
	mine = c->fold ? ci : cs;
	if (!(c->fold ? ok_ci : ok_cs)) {
		c->unhashable++;
	} else if (mine == stored) {
		c->same++;
	} else {
		c->differ++;
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: namehash: dir %" PRIu64 ": %.*s: stored %06x, worked out %06x\n", dir_id,
		    (int)name_len, name, stored, mine);
	}
	if (c->out != NULL) {
		fprintf(c->out, "%" PRIu64 "\t", dir_id);
		for (size_t i = 0; i < name_len; i++) {
			fprintf(c->out, "%02x", (uint8_t)name[i]);
		}
		fprintf(c->out, "\t%06x\t%06x\t%06x\t%" PRIu64 "\n", stored, ok_cs ? cs : 0xffffffu, ok_ci ? ci : 0xffffffu,
		    file_id);
	}
	return 0;
}

static int
cmd_namehash(const char *path, const char *out)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct nh_ctx c;
	int error;

	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	memset(&c, 0, sizeof(c));
	c.fold = (vol.incompat & APFS_INCOMPAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE) != 0;
	c.out = out != NULL ? fopen(out, "w") : NULL;
	error = apfs_dirrec_walk(&vol, namehash_cb, &c);
	if (c.out != NULL) {
		fclose(c.out);
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: namehash: %s volume: %" PRIu64 " directory records (%" PRIu64 " plain ASCII, %" PRIu64
	    " not): hash as stored %" PRIu64 ", not %" PRIu64 ", cannot be hashed %" PRIu64 "%s\n",
	    c.fold ? "case-insensitive" : "case-sensitive", c.total, c.ascii, c.other, c.same, c.differ, c.unhashable,
	    error ? " (WALK FAILED)" : "");
	return (error || c.differ || c.unhashable) ? 1 : 0;
}

/*
 * lookupnames IMAGE LIST: a line of LIST is a directory, a name in hex and what looking it up
 * must give (an id, or "none"); each looked up the way the kernel's vnop_lookup does it.
 */
static int
cmd_lookupnames(const char *path, const char *list)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	FILE *f = fopen(list, "r");
	char line[4096];
	uint64_t total = 0, right = 0, hashed0, scanned0;

	if (f == NULL || open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	hashed0 = nx.lookups_hashed;
	scanned0 = nx.lookups_scanned;
	while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f) != NULL) {
		char hex[2048], want[32], name[1024];
		uint64_t dir, id = 0;
		size_t n = 0;
		uint8_t dt;
		int error;

		if (sscanf(line, "%" SCNu64 " %2047s %31s", &dir, hex, want) != 3) {
			continue;
		}
		for (size_t i = 0; hex[2 * i] != 0 && hex[2 * i + 1] != 0 && n < sizeof(name); i++) {
			unsigned v;

			sscanf(hex + 2 * i, "%2x", &v);
			name[n++] = (char)v;
		}
		total++;
		error = apfs_lookup(&vol, dir, name, n, &id, &dt);
		if ((strcmp(want, "none") == 0 && error == ENOENT) ||
		    (strcmp(want, "none") != 0 && error == 0 && id == strtoull(want, NULL, 0))) {
			right++;
		} else if (total - right <= 20) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: lookupnames: dir %" PRIu64 " %s: want %s, got %s %" PRIu64 "\n", dir, hex, want,
			    error ? strerror(error) : "id", id);
		}
	}
	fclose(f);
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: lookupnames: %" PRIu64 " names, %" PRIu64 " as expected, %" PRIu64 " not; %" PRIu64
	    " found by the hash, %" PRIu64 " by reading the directory\n", total, right, total - right,
	    nx.lookups_hashed - hashed0, nx.lookups_scanned - scanned0);
	return right == total ? 0 : 1;
}

/*
 * Every name in the volume looked up by name, the way the kernel's vnop_lookup does it,
 * against what reading its directory gave; and each name with "#" after it, which must
 * not be found.  Also how long that took against finding each name by reading its
 * directory from the start, which is what apfs_lookup did before it went by the hash.
 */
struct lk_entry {
	char     name[256];
	size_t   len;
	uint64_t id;
	uint8_t  type;
};

struct lk_dir {
	struct lk_entry *e;
	size_t n, cap;
};

static int
lk_collect(void *ctx, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint64_t file_id, uint8_t d_type)
{
	struct lk_dir *d = ctx;

	if (d->n == d->cap) {
		size_t cap = d->cap ? d->cap * 2 : 64;
		struct lk_entry *e = realloc(d->e, cap * sizeof(*e));

		if (e == NULL) {
			return ENOMEM;
		}
		d->e = e;
		d->cap = cap;
	}
	if (name_len >= sizeof(d->e[0].name)) {
		return EIO;
	}
	memcpy(d->e[d->n].name, name, name_len);
	d->e[d->n].name[name_len] = '\0';
	d->e[d->n].len = name_len;
	d->e[d->n].id = file_id;
	d->e[d->n].type = d_type;
	d->n++;
	return 0;
}

struct lk_scan {
	const char *name;
	size_t      len;
	bool        found;
};

static int
lk_scan_cb(void *ctx, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint64_t file_id, uint8_t d_type)
{
	struct lk_scan *sc = ctx;

	(void)file_id;
	(void)d_type;
	if (name_len == sc->len && memcmp(name, sc->name, name_len) == 0) {
		sc->found = true;
		return EEXIST;
	}
	return 0;
}

static double
lk_now(void)
{
	struct timespec ts;

	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
	return (double)ts.tv_sec + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;
}

static int
cmd_lookups(const char *path)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	uint64_t *stack = NULL;
	size_t depth = 0, cap = 0;
	uint64_t dirs = 0, names = 0, good = 0, bad = 0, absent_good = 0, absent_bad = 0;
	double t_hash = 0, t_scan = 0;

	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	stack = malloc(sizeof(*stack) * 64);
	cap = 64;
	stack[depth++] = APFS_ROOT_DIR_INO_NUM;
	while (depth > 0) {
		uint64_t dir = stack[--depth];
		struct lk_dir d = { 0 };
		size_t i;
		int error = apfs_readdir(&vol, dir, lk_collect, &d);

		if (error) {
			fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: readdir %" PRIu64 ": %s\n", dir, strerror(error));
			bad++;
			continue;
		}
		dirs++;
		for (i = 0; i < d.n; i++) {
			struct lk_entry *e = &d.e[i];
			struct lk_scan sc = { e->name, e->len, false };
			char absent[260];
			uint64_t id = 0;
			uint8_t type = 0;
			double t0;

			names++;
			t0 = lk_now();
			error = apfs_lookup(&vol, dir, e->name, e->len, &id, &type);
			t_hash += lk_now() - t0;
			if (error == 0 && id == e->id && type == e->type) {
				good++;
			} else {
				bad++;
				if (bad <= 10) {
					fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: lookup %s in %" PRIu64 ": %d, %" PRIu64
					    " (readdir: %" PRIu64 ")\n", e->name, dir, error, id, e->id);
				}
			}
			t0 = lk_now();
			error = apfs_readdir(&vol, dir, lk_scan_cb, &sc);
			t_scan += lk_now() - t0;
			if (!sc.found) {
				bad++;
			}
			snprintf(absent, sizeof(absent), "%s#", e->name);
			error = apfs_lookup(&vol, dir, absent, e->len + 1, NULL, NULL);
			if (error == ENOENT) {
				absent_good++;
			} else {
				absent_bad++;
			}
			if (e->type == APFS_DT_DIR) {
				if (depth == cap) {
					cap *= 2;
					stack = realloc(stack, sizeof(*stack) * cap);
				}
				stack[depth++] = e->id;
			}
		}
		free(d.e);
	}
	printf("directories %" PRIu64 ", names %" PRIu64 ": found as readdir has them %" PRIu64
	    ", not %" PRIu64 "; with \"#\" after them not found %" PRIu64 ", found %" PRIu64 "\n",
	    dirs, names, good, bad, absent_good, absent_bad);
	printf("time for all of them: apfs_lookup %.0f ms, reading the directory from its start "
	    "%.0f ms\n", t_hash * 1000, t_scan * 1000);
	free(stack);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return (bad == 0 && absent_bad == 0) ? 0 : 1;
}

/*
 * Replace bytes inside a file of the image: the kernel's own apfs_write.c, run here where a
 * ruined image costs nothing.  The bytes come from a file or from standard input.
 * --fail-after N stops the device after N blocks, which is this program's power failure.
 */
static int
cmd_write(const char *path, const char *in_path, const char *at_str, const char *from)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct apfs_write_report rep;
	uint64_t at = strtoull(at_str, NULL, 0);
	uint8_t *data = NULL;
	size_t len = 0, cap = 0;
	uint64_t id = 0;
	uint8_t type = 0;
	FILE *f;
	int error;

	f = strcmp(from, "-") == 0 ? stdin : fopen(from, "rb");
	if (f == NULL) {
		perror(from);
		return 1;
	}
	for (;;) {
		size_t n;

		if (len == cap) {
			cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 65536;
			data = realloc(data, cap);
			if (data == NULL) {
				fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: out of memory\n");
				return 1;
			}
		}
		n = fread(data + len, 1, cap - len, f);
		len += n;
		if (n == 0) {
			break;
		}
	}
	if (f != stdin) {
		fclose(f);
	}

	want_write = true;
	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	if (apfs_path_lookup(&vol, in_path, &id, &type) != 0) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: no such path in the volume\n", in_path);
		return 1;
	}
	error = apfs_write_in_place(&vol, id, at, data, len, &rep);
	printf("%s: %zu bytes at %" PRIu64 " of %s (inode %" PRIu64 "): %s\n", path, len, at,
	    in_path, id, error == 0 ? "written" : (rep.why ? rep.why : strerror(error)));
	printf("  blocks %" PRIu64 " from %" PRIu64 ", of them patched whole %" PRIu64
	    ", writes %" PRIu64 "\n", rep.blocks, rep.first_block, rep.partial, rep.calls);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	free(data);
	return error == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}

/* Would this volume take a write at all, and what does it say about itself? */
static int
cmd_writable(const char *path)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	const char *why = NULL;
	int error;

	want_write = true;
	if (open_image(path, &nx, &vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	error = apfs_write_volume_ok(&vol, &why);
	printf("%s: volume %s: %s\n", path, vol.name, error == 0 ? "writable in place" : why);
	printf("  incompatible 0x%" PRIx64 "  snapshots %" PRIu64 "  integrity metadata %" PRIu64
	    "  extent-reference tree %s\n", vol.incompat, vol.num_snapshots, vol.integrity_meta_oid,
	    vol.extentref_oid ? "yes" : "no");
	printf("  checkpoint rings: descriptor %" PRIu64 "+%u, data %" PRIu64 "+%u; container omap %"
	    PRIu64 "\n", nx.xp_desc_base, nx.xp_desc_blocks, nx.xp_data_base, nx.xp_data_blocks,
	    nx.omap_addr);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return error == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}


/* ---- the store of fixed-length slot files (bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_store.c) ---- */

#define STORE_SCRATCH (1u << 20)

static int
store_open(const char *path, struct apfs_nx *nx, struct apfs_vol *vol, struct apfs_store *st,
    bool for_writing)
{
	const char *why = NULL;

	want_write = for_writing;
	if (open_image(path, nx, vol) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	if (apfs_store_open(vol, st, &why) != 0) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s is not a store: %s\n", path,
		    why != NULL ? why : "no reason given");
		return 1;
	}
	return 0;
}

static int
cmd_store_info(const char *path)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct apfs_store st;
	struct apfs_store_head h;
	uint8_t *scratch;
	int slot, best;

	if (store_open(path, &nx, &vol, &st, false) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	{
		const char *why = NULL;

		printf("%s: store on volume %s: %d slots of %" PRIu64 " bytes, %" PRIu64
		    " of payload; a save here: %s\n", path, vol.name, APFS_STORE_SLOTS,
		    st.slot_bytes, st.payload_max,
		    apfs_store_writable(&st, &why) == 0 ? "would go through" : why);
	}
	for (slot = 0; slot < APFS_STORE_SLOTS; slot++) {
		if (apfs_store_head(&st, slot, &h) != 0) {
			printf("  slot %d (inode %" PRIu64 "): nothing good\n", slot,
			    st.slot_id[slot]);
			continue;
		}
		printf("  slot %d (inode %" PRIu64 "): generation %" PRIu64 ", %" PRIu64
		    " bytes, sum %016" PRIx64 ", note %" PRIu64 ", at %" PRIu64 "\n", slot,
		    st.slot_id[slot], h.generation, h.bytes, h.sum, h.note, h.seconds);
	}
	scratch = malloc(STORE_SCRATCH);
	best = scratch == NULL ? -1 : apfs_store_newest(&st, scratch, STORE_SCRATCH, &h);
	free(scratch);
	if (best < 0) {
		printf("  the newest good slot: none\n");
	} else {
		printf("  the newest good slot: %d, generation %" PRIu64 ", %" PRIu64 " bytes\n",
		    best, h.generation, h.bytes);
	}
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return 0;
}

static int
cmd_store_save(const char *path, const char *from, uint64_t note)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct apfs_store st;
	struct apfs_store_write w;
	uint8_t *data = NULL, *scratch;
	size_t len = 0, cap = 0;
	FILE *f = strcmp(from, "-") == 0 ? stdin : fopen(from, "rb");
	int error;

	if (f == NULL) {
		perror(from);
		return 1;
	}
	for (;;) {
		size_t n;

		if (len == cap) {
			cap = cap ? cap * 2 : (1u << 16);
			data = realloc(data, cap);
			if (data == NULL) {
				fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: out of memory\n");
				return 1;
			}
		}
		n = fread(data + len, 1, cap - len, f);
		len += n;
		if (n == 0) {
			break;
		}
	}
	if (f != stdin) {
		fclose(f);
	}
	if (store_open(path, &nx, &vol, &st, true) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	scratch = malloc(STORE_SCRATCH);
	if (scratch == NULL) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: out of memory\n");
		return 1;
	}
	error = apfs_store_save(&st, data, len, 0, note, scratch, STORE_SCRATCH, &w);
	printf("%s: %zu bytes into slot %d as generation %" PRIu64 ": %s; %" PRIu64 " blocks\n",
	    path, len, w.slot, w.generation, error == 0 ? "saved" : strerror(error), w.blocks);
	free(scratch);
	free(data);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return error == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}

static int
cmd_store_load(const char *path, const char *to)
{
	struct apfs_nx nx;
	struct apfs_vol vol;
	struct apfs_store st;
	struct apfs_store_head h;
	uint8_t *scratch, *buf;
	FILE *f;
	int best, error;

	if (store_open(path, &nx, &vol, &st, false) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	scratch = malloc(STORE_SCRATCH);
	if (scratch == NULL) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: out of memory\n");
		return 1;
	}
	best = apfs_store_newest(&st, scratch, STORE_SCRATCH, &h);
	free(scratch);
	if (best < 0) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: %s: no slot holds anything good\n", path);
		return 1;
	}
	buf = malloc(h.bytes ? (size_t)h.bytes : 1);
	if (buf == NULL) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: out of memory\n");
		return 1;
	}
	error = h.bytes == 0 ? 0 : apfs_store_read(&st, best, 0, buf, (size_t)h.bytes);
	if (error) {
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: slot %d will not read: %s\n", best, strerror(error));
		return 1;
	}
	f = strcmp(to, "-") == 0 ? stdout : fopen(to, "wb");
	if (f == NULL) {
		perror(to);
		return 1;
	}
	if (h.bytes != 0 && fwrite(buf, 1, (size_t)h.bytes, f) != h.bytes) {
		perror(to);
		return 1;
	}
	if (f != stdout) {
		fclose(f);
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "%s: slot %d, generation %" PRIu64 ", %" PRIu64 " bytes, note %" PRIu64
	    "\n", path, best, h.generation, h.bytes, h.note);
	free(buf);
	apfs_nx_close(&nx);
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int i;

	for (i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
		if ((strcmp(argv[i], "--fail-after") == 0 ||
		    strcmp(argv[i], "--corrupt-after") == 0) && i + 1 < argc) {
			write_fail_after = strtoull(argv[i + 1], NULL, 0);
			if (argv[i][2] == 'f') {
				write_fails = true;
			} else {
				write_corrupts = true;
			}
			memmove(&argv[i], &argv[i + 2], (size_t)(argc - i - 2) * sizeof(*argv));
			argc -= 2;
			i--;
		}
	}
	if (argc < 3) {
		fprintf(stderr,
		    "usage: apfs-tool info   IMAGE\n"
		    "       apfs-tool ls     IMAGE [PATH]\n"
		    "       apfs-tool stat   IMAGE PATH\n"
		    "       apfs-tool cat    IMAGE PATH\n"
		    "       apfs-tool census IMAGE [PATH] [--meta]\n"
		    "       apfs-tool write  IMAGE PATH OFFSET FILE|- [--fail-after N | --corrupt-after N]\n"
		    "       apfs-tool writable IMAGE\n"
		    "       apfs-tool store  info IMAGE | save IMAGE FILE|- [NOTE] | load IMAGE FILE|-\n"
		    "       apfs-tool lookups IMAGE\n"
		    "       apfs-tool cfrace IMAGE [THREADS [ROUNDS]]\n"
		    "       apfs-tool namehash IMAGE [OUT]\n"
		    "       apfs-tool lookupnames IMAGE LIST\n");
		return 2;
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "info") == 0) {
		return cmd_info(argv[2]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "ls") == 0) {
		return cmd_ls(argv[2], argc > 3 ? argv[3] : "/");
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "stat") == 0 && argc > 3) {
		return cmd_stat(argv[2], argv[3]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "cat") == 0 && argc > 3) {
		return cmd_cat(argv[2], argv[3]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "census") == 0) {
		return cmd_census(argv[2], (argc > 3 && argv[3][0] == '/') ? argv[3] : NULL,
		    (argc > 3 && strcmp(argv[argc - 1], "--meta") == 0));
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "write") == 0 && argc > 5) {
		return cmd_write(argv[2], argv[3], argv[4], argv[5]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "writable") == 0) {
		return cmd_writable(argv[2]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "store") == 0 && argc > 3) {
		if (strcmp(argv[2], "info") == 0) {
			return cmd_store_info(argv[3]);
		}
		if (strcmp(argv[2], "save") == 0 && argc > 4) {
			return cmd_store_save(argv[3], argv[4],
			    argc > 5 ? strtoull(argv[5], NULL, 0) : 0);
		}
		if (strcmp(argv[2], "load") == 0 && argc > 4) {
			return cmd_store_load(argv[3], argv[4]);
		}
		fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: store: info, save or load\n");
		return 2;
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "lookups") == 0) {
		return cmd_lookups(argv[2]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "namehash") == 0) {
		return cmd_namehash(argv[2], argc > 3 ? argv[3] : NULL);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "lookupnames") == 0 && argc > 3) {
		return cmd_lookupnames(argv[2], argv[3]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "cfrace") == 0) {
		return cmd_cfrace(argv[2], argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 4, argc > 4 ? atoi(argv[4]) : 3);
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "apfs-tool: unknown command %s\n", argv[1]);
	return 2;
}
```
