```py
        # found by the dependency files the compiler wrote, which name the headers each object was built from
        for d, _dirs, files in os.walk(obj):
            for name in files:
                if name.endswith((".d", ".cpd")):
                    text = open(os.path.join(d, name), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
                    if any("/" + h + ".h" in text for h in headers):
                        o = os.path.join(d, name[:-2] + ".o" if name.endswith(".d") else name[:-4] + ".cpo")
                        if os.path.isfile(o):
                            os.remove(o)
                            removed += 1
    return removed


def cmd_kernel(a):
    """kernel [--tree DIR]: put the drivers' choice of the .config (every driver's default if there is no .config) into the
    kernel tree, where XNU's build reads it: config/MASTER.hakios, the HakiOS block of bsd/conf/files and iokit/conf/files,
    bsd/dev/hakios.drivers.h. Files are written only when they change, so an unchanged choice rebuilds nothing."""
    if DRIVERS_ERROR:
        raise ConfigError(DRIVERS_ERROR)
    tree = a.tree or os.environ.get("XNU_SRC") or os.path.join(a.root, "xnu-src", "xnu-8796.121.2")
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tree, "bsd", "conf", "files")):
        raise ConfigError("no kernel tree at %s (xnu/apply.sh makes it)" % tree)
    if os.path.isfile(a.config):
        config, sources = load(a.config), rel(a.root, a.config)
    else:
        config, sources = {}, "the drivers' defaults (no .config)"
    problems = check_drivers(config, {})
    if problems:
        report(problems)
        return 1
    built = drivers_built(config)
    changed = []
    for component in ("bsd", "iokit"):
        path = os.path.join(tree, component, "conf", "files")
        try:
            text = put_block(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read(), files_block(component))
        except ConfigError as e:
            raise ConfigError("%s/conf/files: %s" % (component, e))
        if write_if_changed(path, text):
            changed.append(component + "/conf/files")
    choice_changed = write_if_changed(os.path.join(tree, "config", "MASTER.hakios"), master_hakios(built, sources))
    if choice_changed:
        changed.append("config/MASTER.hakios")
    if write_if_changed(os.path.join(tree, "bsd", "dev", "hakios.drivers.h"), drivers_header(built, sources)):
        changed.append("bsd/dev/hakios.drivers.h")
    removed = stale_objects(tree) if choice_changed and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(tree, "BUILD", "obj")) else 0
    on = [d.name.lower() for d in DRIVERS if built[d.symbol]]
    off = [d.name.lower() for d in DRIVERS if not built[d.symbol]]
    print("hakios-config: kernel: %d of %d drivers built in, from %s%s" % (len(on), len(DRIVERS), sources,
          "; left out: " + " ".join(off) if off else ""))
    if changed:
        print("hakios-config: kernel: %s written%s" % (", ".join(changed), "; %d objects to be built again" % removed if removed else ""))
    return 0


def cmd_external(a):
    """external-files: "<file in a SoC's or device's repository>\t<path in the kernel tree>" for each file of their drivers, for
    xnu/apply.sh and xnu/sync-drivers.sh to copy into the tree and xnu/export.sh to leave where it is (it is not this repository's)."""
    if DRIVERS_ERROR:
        raise ConfigError(DRIVERS_ERROR)
    for d in DRIVERS:
        if d.origin:
            for path, _tags in d.files:
                print("%s\t%s" % (d.source(path), path))
    return 0


def main():
    # --root and --config are accepted before the command and after it
    common = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    common.add_argument("--root", default=argparse.SUPPRESS, help="the top of the repository (tests use another)")
    common.add_argument("--config", default=argparse.SUPPRESS, help="the .config to use (default: .config at the top)")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter, parents=[common])
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("defconfig", parents=[common], help="make .config from a defconfig and fragments")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.add_argument("fragments", nargs="*")
    p.add_argument("-o", "--output")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_defconfig)
    p = sub.add_parser("merge", parents=[common], help="put fragments over the .config")
    p.add_argument("fragments", nargs="+")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_merge)
    p = sub.add_parser("args", parents=[common], help="the kernel's boot-arguments")
    p.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="print them even if the check finds a problem")
    p.add_argument("--defconfig", help="the arguments of this defconfig (and --fragment) instead of the .config's")
    p.add_argument("--fragment", action="append", default=[], help="a fragment over it; more than one is allowed")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_args)
    for name, fn, text in (("check", cmd_check, "validate the .config"), ("show", cmd_show, "say what the .config is"),
                           ("needs", cmd_needs, "which firmware the .config wants, and whether it is there"),
                           ("savedefconfig", cmd_savedefconfig, "the .config as a minimal defconfig"),
                           ("list", cmd_list, "the defconfigs and fragments in configs/")):
        sub.add_parser(name, parents=[common], help=text).set_defaults(fn=fn)
    p = sub.add_parser("listing", parents=[common], help="the documented defconfig of NAME, every symbol, on stdout or into -o FILE")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.add_argument("fragments", nargs="*")
    p.add_argument("-o", dest="output_listing", help="write it here (safe for the file it is made from, as `>` is not)")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_listing)
    p = sub.add_parser("complete", parents=[common], help="a defconfig must name every symbol")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_complete)
    p = sub.add_parser("kernel", parents=[common], help="put the .config's choice of drivers into the kernel tree (make kernel runs it)")
    p.add_argument("--tree", help="the kernel tree (default: $XNU_SRC, else xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2)")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_kernel)
    sub.add_parser("external-files", parents=[common], help="the driver files of SoC and device repositories, and their place in the tree").set_defaults(fn=cmd_external)
    p = sub.add_parser("help", parents=[common], help="what a symbol means")
    p.add_argument("symbol")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_help)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    a.root = os.path.abspath(getattr(a, "root", ROOT))
    a.config = os.path.abspath(getattr(a, "config", os.path.join(a.root, ".config")))
    if getattr(a, "output", None) is None:
        a.output = a.config
    if DRIVERS_ERROR:
        # a conf file that does not read leaves the drivers unknown, and every answer about a configuration would be wrong
        print("hakios-config: %s" % DRIVERS_ERROR, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    try:
        sys.exit(a.fn(a))
    except ConfigError as e:
        print("hakios-config: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`tools/hakios-device-test.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""tools/hakios-device.py and the layers of tools/hakios-config.py: a common repository, a SoC's, a device's with a driver of its own.

Everything happens in a copy made for the test (the tools, configs/, the drivers' conf files, the SoC and device repositories):
  - a device repository's defconfig is found as if it were in configs/; the same name in two repositories is refused
  - its driver (devices/<name>/drivers/<sub>/conf) is a CONFIG_HAKIOS_ symbol like the common ones, goes into the kernel tree's
    conf/files `optional`, and is listed by external-files for apply.sh, sync-drivers.sh and export.sh
  - a device repository cannot declare `standard` files; a driver naming a file that is not there is a problem of `check`
  - `new` makes a device that `check` passes, with the phone drivers left out but the SoC's
  - the real tree's devices and SoCs hold together
"""
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

# (--repo commits: a machine with no git identity of its own is no reason for the test to fail)
for key, value in (("GIT_AUTHOR_NAME", "test"), ("GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL", "test@example.invalid"),
                   ("GIT_COMMITTER_NAME", "test"), ("GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL", "test@example.invalid")):
    os.environ.setdefault(key, value)

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
failures = []


def check(label, ok, detail=""):
    print("%s %s" % ("ok  " if ok else "FAIL", label))
    if not ok:
        failures.append(label)
        if detail:
            print("     " + str(detail).strip().replace("\n", "\n     ")[:800])


def tool(root, name, *args):
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(root, "tools", name), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=root)


work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="hakios-device-test-")
try:
    root = os.path.join(work, "root")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, "tools"))
    for t in ("hakios-config.py", "hakios-device.py", "boot-args.py", "kernel-version.py"):
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(HERE, t), os.path.join(root, "tools", t))
    shutil.copytree(os.path.join(ROOT, "configs"), os.path.join(root, "configs"))
    # a SoC of the test's own, so that the test needs no SoC or device repository checked out (the common one alone runs it)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, "socs", "fakesoc", "configs"))
    open(os.path.join(root, "socs", "fakesoc", "soc.conf"), "w").write("soc fakesoc\n\ttitle       a SoC made for the test\n")
    open(os.path.join(root, "socs", "fakesoc", "configs", "fakesoc.config"), "w").write(
        "# HakiOS fragment: the test's SoC.\nCONFIG_SOC=\"fakesoc\"\nCONFIG_CPUS=8\nCONFIG_THERMAL=y\nCONFIG_HAKIOS_THERMAL=y\n")
    for sub in os.listdir(os.path.join(ROOT, "drivers")):
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(ROOT, "drivers", sub, "conf")):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, "drivers", sub))
            shutil.copy(os.path.join(ROOT, "drivers", sub, "conf"), os.path.join(root, "drivers", sub, "conf"))
    shutil.copytree(os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", "qemu"), os.path.join(root, "devices", "qemu"))

    r = tool(root, "hakios-device.py", "new", "fakephone", "--soc", "fakesoc", "--title", "Fake Phone")
    check("new: a device repository that check passes", r.returncode == 0 and "all hold together" in r.stdout, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    conf = open(os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "configs", "fakephone.config")).read()
    check("new: the phone drivers left out, the SoC's kept, QEMU's untouched",
          "# CONFIG_HAKIOS_GOODIX is not set" in conf and "HAKIOS_THERMAL" not in conf and "HAKIOS_VIRTIO" not in conf, conf)
    r = tool(root, "hakios-device.py", "new", "fakephone", "--soc", "fakesoc", "--title", "x")
    check("new: refuses a device that exists", r.returncode != 0 and "already exists" in r.stderr, r.stderr)
    check("new: the device carries its SoC's layer, a copy of the one there is",
          open(os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "soc", "soc.conf")).read() == open(os.path.join(root, "socs", "fakesoc", "soc.conf")).read())
    r = tool(root, "hakios-device.py", "new", "otherphone", "--soc", "newsoc", "--title", "Other Phone", "--repo")
    check("new: a SoC nobody has yet gets a new layer in the device, and --repo makes the device a git repository",
          r.returncode == 0 and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, "devices", "otherphone", "soc", "configs", "newsoc.config")) and
          os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root, "devices", "otherphone", ".git")) and "git -C devices/otherphone remote add origin" in r.stdout,
          r.stdout + r.stderr)
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(root, "devices", "otherphone"))
    # two copies of one SoC: the same is fine, different is refused
    with open(os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "soc", "configs", "fakesoc.config"), "a") as f:
        f.write("CONFIG_CPUS=4\n")
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "list")
    check("two different copies of one SoC are refused, with both named", r.returncode != 0 and "the SoC fakesoc is in" in r.stderr and
          "differ" in r.stderr, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    shutil.copy(os.path.join(root, "socs", "fakesoc", "configs", "fakesoc.config"), os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "soc", "configs"))
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(root, "socs"))
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "defconfig", "fakephone")
    check("a device that carries its SoC needs nothing else: no socs/ at all", r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr)

    # a driver of the device's own
    d = os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "drivers", "input")
    os.makedirs(d)
    with open(os.path.join(d, "conf"), "w") as f:
        f.write("driver FAKETOUCH\n\tfile    bsd/dev/hakios.faketouch.c\n\thelp    the fake phone's touch controller\n")
    open(os.path.join(d, "hakios.faketouch.c"), "w").write("/* a touch driver */\n")
    with open(os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "configs", "fakephone.config"), "a") as f:
        f.write("CONFIG_HAKIOS_FAKETOUCH=y\n")
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "help", "HAKIOS_FAKETOUCH")
    check("a device's driver is a symbol like the common ones", r.returncode == 0 and "devices/fakephone/drivers/input/conf" in r.stdout, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "external-files")
    check("external-files: its file, and where it goes in the tree",
          r.stdout.strip() == "%s\tbsd/dev/hakios.faketouch.c" % os.path.join(d, "hakios.faketouch.c"), r.stdout + r.stderr)
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "defconfig", "fakephone")
    check("make fakephone_defconfig: found in the device's repository, the driver built", r.returncode == 0 and
          "CONFIG_HAKIOS_FAKETOUCH=y" in open(os.path.join(root, ".config")).read(), r.stdout + r.stderr)
    tree = os.path.join(work, "tree")
    for sub in ("bsd/conf", "iokit/conf", "config", "bsd/dev"):
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(tree, sub))
    open(os.path.join(tree, "bsd/conf/files"), "w").write("bsd/dev/a.c standard\nbsd/dev/hakios.input.c standard\n")
    open(os.path.join(tree, "iokit/conf/files"), "w").write("iokit/Kernel/hakios.gpu.cpp optional iokitcpp\n")
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "kernel", "--tree", tree)
    files = open(os.path.join(tree, "bsd/conf/files")).read()
    check("kernel: the device's driver in conf/files and in the choice", r.returncode == 0 and
          "bsd/dev/hakios.faketouch.c" in files and "optional hakios_faketouch" in files and
          " hakios_faketouch " in open(os.path.join(tree, "config/MASTER.hakios")).read(), r.stdout + r.stderr + files)
    r = tool(root, "hakios-device.py", "check", "fakephone")
    check("check: the device with its driver holds together", r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    os.remove(os.path.join(d, "hakios.faketouch.c"))
    r = tool(root, "hakios-device.py", "check", "fakephone")
    check("check: a driver naming a file that is not there is a problem", r.returncode != 0 and "hakios.faketouch.c" in r.stdout, r.stdout)
    with open(os.path.join(d, "conf"), "a") as f:
        f.write("standard bsd/dev/hakios.everyone.c\n")
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "list")
    check("a device repository cannot declare `standard` files", "a SoC or device repository has drivers, not `standard`" in r.stdout + r.stderr,
          r.stdout + r.stderr)
    os.remove(os.path.join(d, "conf"))
    shutil.copy(os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "soc", "configs", "fakesoc.config"),
                os.path.join(root, "devices", "fakephone", "configs", "fakesoc.config"))
    r = tool(root, "hakios-config.py", "defconfig", "fakephone")
    check("the same configuration name in two repositories is refused", r.returncode != 0 and "more than one repository" in r.stderr, r.stderr)

    # the real tree
    r = tool(ROOT, "hakios-device.py", "check")
    check("the devices and SoCs of this tree hold together", r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    r = tool(ROOT, "hakios-device.py", "list")
    check("list names the QEMU device, which the common repository always has", "qemu" in r.stdout, r.stdout)
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)

if failures:
    sys.exit("hakios-device-test: %d FAILED" % len(failures))
print("hakios-device-test: all passed")

```

`tools/hakios-device.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""HakiOS device and SoC repositories: the common repository (this one), a repository per SoC family, one per device.

The way Android puts a phone's tree together (device/<vendor>/<name>, a <soc>-common, a manifest that names them) and the way XNU
ports keep a board apart from the kernel: what is true of every device lives here (the kernel, the loader, the drivers, the tools);
what is true of a SoC lives in socs/<soc>/; what is true of one device lives in devices/<name>/. Each of those two is a directory of
the same shape that may be its own git repository:

    devices/<name>/device.conf          what the device is, and how far each part of it works (the device's page is made from it)
    devices/<name>/configs/             <name>_defconfig (#include common_defconfig, the SoC's fragment, <name>.config) and fragments
    devices/<name>/drivers/<sub>/conf   drivers of its own, if it has any, in the format of drivers/<sub>/conf (docs/drivers-config.md)
    socs/<soc>/soc.conf, configs/<soc>.config, drivers/...    the same for a SoC family

devices/manifest.conf names every one: `path` for one kept in this tree, `repository` and `revision` for one that is its own
repository, which `sync` clones into place at that revision.

  tools/hakios-device.py list                       the devices and SoCs, where each is, how far each part works
  tools/hakios-device.py check [NAME...]            a device or SoC repository holds together (CI runs it on every one)
  tools/hakios-device.py new NAME --soc SOC ...     a new device repository, with every phone driver left out to begin with
  tools/hakios-device.py sync [NAME...]             clone or update the repositories the manifest names, at their revisions
  tools/hakios-device.py lock NAME                  write the revision checked out into the manifest
  tools/hakios-device.py split NAME DIR             a device kept in this tree as a git repository of its own, with its history

docs/porting/repositories.md is the guide.
"""
import argparse
import importlib.util
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
STATES = ("works", "partial", "missing")
AREAS = ("display", "touch", "buttons", "cpu", "gpu", "storage", "audio", "battery", "haptic", "camera", "torch", "wifi",
         "bluetooth", "cellular", "network", "thermal", "usb", "sensors")
DEVICE_KEYS = {"title", "vendor", "soc", "defconfig", "firmware", "maintainer", "status", "repository", "revision", "path"}
SOC_KEYS = {"title", "vendor", "cores", "gpu", "maintainer", "repository", "revision", "path"}


class Problem(Exception):
    pass


_CONFIG = []


def config_tool():
    if _CONFIG:
        return _CONFIG[0]
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("hakios_config", os.path.join(HERE, "hakios-config.py"))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    _CONFIG.append(module)
    return module


def read_blocks(path, kinds, keys):
    """[(kind, name, {key: [values]}, line)] of a file of blocks: `<kind> <name>` and indented `<key> <value>` lines under it."""
    blocks, block = [], None
    shown = os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)
    for n, raw in enumerate(open(path, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
        line = raw.split("#", 1)[0].rstrip()
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        words = line.split()
        if not raw[0].isspace():
            if words[0] not in kinds or len(words) != 2 or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*", words[1]):
                raise Problem("%s:%d: want `%s NAME` (lowercase), got %r" % (shown, n, " NAME` or `".join(kinds), line.strip()))
            block = (words[0], words[1], {}, n)
            blocks.append(block)
            continue
        if block is None:
            raise Problem("%s:%d: an indented line before any block" % (shown, n))
        key, value = words[0], line.strip()[len(words[0]):].strip()
        allowed = keys[block[0]]
        if key not in allowed:
            raise Problem("%s:%d: %s does not take `%s` (it takes: %s)" % (shown, n, block[0], key, ", ".join(sorted(allowed))))
        block[2].setdefault(key, []).append((value, n))
    return blocks


def one(fields, key, default=None):
    values = fields.get(key)
    return values[-1][0] if values else default


def manifest():
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", "manifest.conf")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return []
    return read_blocks(path, ("device", "soc", "uefi"), {"device": DEVICE_KEYS, "soc": SOC_KEYS, "uefi": {"path", "repository", "revision"}})


def soc_homes():
    """{SoC name: its directory}: socs/<name>/, then the SoC layers devices carry (devices/<device>/soc/), the first of each."""
    out = {}
    base = os.path.join(ROOT, "socs")
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(base)) if os.path.isdir(base) else []:
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(base, name, "soc.conf")):
            out.setdefault(name, os.path.join(base, name))
    base = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices")
    for dev in sorted(os.listdir(base)) if os.path.isdir(base) else []:
        top = os.path.join(base, dev, "soc")
        named = config_tool().soc_name(top)
        if named:
            out.setdefault(named, top)
    return out


def home(kind, name):
    if kind == "uefi":
        return os.path.join(ROOT, "uefi")         # one UEFI for every device: Mu-Silicium with HakiOS's changes (uefi/README.md)
    if kind == "soc":
        return soc_homes().get(name, os.path.join(ROOT, "socs", name))
    return os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", name)


def describe(kind, name):
    """The block of devices/<name>/device.conf or socs/<name>/soc.conf, or None if it is not checked out."""
    path = os.path.join(home(kind, name), "device.conf" if kind == "device" else "soc.conf")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    blocks = read_blocks(path, (kind,), {"device": DEVICE_KEYS, "soc": SOC_KEYS})
    if len(blocks) != 1 or blocks[0][1] != name:
        raise Problem("%s: want one `%s %s` block" % (os.path.relpath(path, ROOT), kind, name))
    return blocks[0][2]


def present():
    """[(kind, name)] of every device and SoC checked out, whether or not the manifest names it."""
    out = [("soc", name) for name in sorted(soc_homes())]
    base = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices")
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(base)) if os.path.isdir(base) else []:
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(base, name, "device.conf")):
            out.append(("device", name))
    return out


def statuses(fields):
    """[(area, state, note)] of a device's `status` lines, checked."""
    out = []
    for value, n in fields.get("status", []):
        parts = value.split(None, 2)
        if len(parts) < 2 or parts[0] not in AREAS or parts[1] not in STATES:
            raise Problem("line %d: want `status <area> works|partial|missing <note>`, the area one of %s (got %r)" %
                          (n, ", ".join(AREAS), value))
        out.append((parts[0], parts[1], parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else ""))
    return out


# ---- commands ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_list(_a):
    named = {(k, n): f for k, n, f, _l in manifest()}
    every = sorted(set(named) | set(present()), key=lambda x: (x[0] != "soc", x[1]))
    for kind, name in every:
        if kind == "uefi":
            where = one(named[(kind, name)], "repository") or one(named[(kind, name)], "path")
            there = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(home(kind, name), "apply.sh"))
            print("%-6s %-10s %-44s %s" % (kind, name, "HakiOS UEFI (Mu-Silicium)" if there else
                                            "NOT CHECKED OUT (tools/hakios-device.py sync %s)" % name, where))
            continue
        fields = describe(kind, name)
        where = one(named.get((kind, name), {}), "repository") or one(named.get((kind, name), {}), "path")
        if not where and kind == "soc" and os.path.basename(home(kind, name)) == "soc":
            where = "carried by %s" % os.path.relpath(os.path.dirname(home(kind, name)), ROOT)
        where = where or "(not in the manifest)"
        if fields is None:
            print("%-6s %-10s NOT CHECKED OUT (tools/hakios-device.py sync %s)  %s" % (kind, name, name, where))
            continue
        line = "%-6s %-10s %-44s %s" % (kind, name, one(fields, "title", "?")[:44], where)
        if kind == "device":
            counts = {s: 0 for s in STATES}
            for _area, state, _note in statuses(fields):
                counts[state] += 1
            line += "  [%d works, %d partial, %d missing]" % (counts["works"], counts["partial"], counts["missing"])
        print(line)
    return 0


def check_one(kind, name, hc):
    problems = []
    try:
        fields = describe(kind, name)
    except Problem as e:
        return [str(e)]
    if fields is None:
        return ["%s %s is not checked out" % (kind, name)]
    top = home(kind, name)
    shown = os.path.relpath(top, ROOT)
    if not one(fields, "title"):
        problems.append("%s: no title" % shown)
    if kind == "device":
        try:
            areas = statuses(fields)
        except Problem as e:
            problems.append("%s/device.conf: %s" % (shown, e))
            areas = []
        if len({a for a, _s, _n in areas}) != len(areas):
            problems.append("%s/device.conf: an area has two status lines" % shown)
        soc = one(fields, "soc")
        if soc is None:
            problems.append("%s/device.conf: no soc (`none` for a machine with no SoC repository)" % shown)
        elif soc != "none" and soc not in soc_homes():
            problems.append("%s/device.conf: soc %s, and neither %s/soc/ nor socs/%s/ has its soc.conf" % (shown, soc, shown, soc))
        defconfig = one(fields, "defconfig")
        path = os.path.join(top, "configs", defconfig or "")
        if not defconfig or not os.path.isfile(path):
            problems.append("%s/device.conf: defconfig %s is not in %s/configs/" % (shown, defconfig, shown))
        else:
            includes = [l.split()[1] for l in open(path, encoding="utf-8") if l.startswith("#include ")]
            if "common_defconfig" not in includes:
                problems.append("%s/configs/%s does not #include common_defconfig: a device is the common kernel plus its own" % (shown, defconfig))
            if soc not in (None, "none") and soc + ".config" not in includes:
                problems.append("%s/configs/%s does not #include %s.config (its SoC's facts)" % (shown, defconfig, soc))
            out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, "hakios-config.py"), "defconfig", defconfig, "-o", os.devnull],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT)
            for l in (out.stdout + out.stderr).splitlines():
                if "PROBLEM" in l or out.returncode != 0 and l.startswith("hakios-config:") and "made from" not in l and "characters" not in l:
                    problems.append("%s/configs/%s: %s" % (shown, defconfig, l.replace("hakios-config: ", "")))
        firmware = one(fields, "firmware")
        if firmware and not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(top, firmware)):
            problems.append("%s/device.conf: firmware %s is not there" % (shown, firmware))
    else:
        fragment = os.path.join(top, "configs", name + ".config")
        if not os.path.isfile(fragment):
            problems.append("%s: no configs/%s.config, the fragment a device with this SoC includes" % (shown, name))
    for d in hc.DRIVERS:
        if d.origin and os.path.abspath(d.origin) == os.path.abspath(top):
            for f, _tags in d.files:
                if not os.path.isfile(d.source(f)):
                    problems.append("%s: the driver %s names %s, which is not there" % (d.where, d.name, os.path.relpath(d.source(f), ROOT)))
    return problems


def cmd_check(a):
    hc = config_tool()
    if hc.DRIVERS_ERROR:
        print("hakios-device: " + hc.DRIVERS_ERROR)
        return 1
    every = present()
    wanted = [(k, n) for k, n in every if not a.names or n in a.names]
    missing = [n for n in a.names if n not in {x[1] for x in every}]
    problems = ["%s: not checked out here" % n for n in missing]
    for kind, name in wanted:
        problems += check_one(kind, name, hc)
    names = {}
    for kind, name in every:
        if name in names:
            problems.append("%s is both a %s and a %s: a configuration name would be ambiguous" % (name, names[name], kind))
        names[name] = kind
    for p in problems:
        print("hakios-device: " + p)
    print("hakios-device: %d repositories checked (%s)%s" % (len(wanted), ", ".join(n for _k, n in wanted),
          ", %d problem(s)" % len(problems) if problems else ", all hold together"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


NEW_README = """# {title} ({name})

A HakiOS device repository: what is true of this device and of no other. The kernel, the loader, the drivers and the tools are
the common repository's; the {soc} family's facts are in `soc/`, carried with the device. How the three are put together:
[docs/porting/repositories.md](https://github.com/oosexgang/hakios-xnu-kernel/blob/main/docs/porting/repositories.md).

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `metal.args` | what `tools/metal-run.sh` gives this phone: its cores, its panel's rate, the threads that copy frames, the touch poll |
| `device.conf` | what the device is, and how far each part of it works: its page in the documentation is made from it |
| `configs/{name}_defconfig` | the common kernel, the SoC's fragment, this device's: `make {name}_defconfig` |
| `configs/{name}.config` | what is this device's own: the drivers built in, the arguments it needs |
| `soc/` | its SoC family's layer ({soc}): `soc.conf`, `configs/{soc}.config`, the SoC's drivers; carried here so that this one repository is all the device needs |
| `drivers/` | drivers of its own, if it needs any (`drivers/<subsystem>/conf`, as in the common repository) |

Every phone driver of the common repository is left out to begin with: their addresses and pins are the phone they were written
for. Put one back in `configs/{name}.config` when it has been made to work here, and say so in `device.conf`.

Check with `tools/hakios-device.py check {name}`.
"""


def cmd_new(a):
    name = a.name
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*", name):
        raise Problem("a device's name is its codename, lowercase: %s" % name)
    top = home("device", name)
    if os.path.exists(top):
        raise Problem("devices/%s already exists" % name)
    if a.fdt or a.adb:
        # the phone's own device tree first: tools/new-device.py makes the directory with soc.args and its README
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, "new-device.py"), name] + (["--fdt", a.fdt] if a.fdt else ["--adb"]),
                             cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
        print(out.stdout.rstrip())
        if out.returncode != 0:
            raise Problem("tools/new-device.py: %s" % (out.stderr.strip() or "failed"))
    if a.soc != "none":
        # the device carries its SoC's layer: a copy of one there is (another device's, synced), or a new one to fill in
        socs = soc_homes()
        os.makedirs(top, exist_ok=True)
        if a.soc in socs:
            shutil.copytree(socs[a.soc], os.path.join(top, "soc"), ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(".git"))
            print("hakios-device: devices/%s/soc/: the %s layer, copied from %s" % (name, a.soc, os.path.relpath(socs[a.soc], ROOT)))
        else:
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(top, "soc", "configs"))
            with open(os.path.join(top, "soc", "soc.conf"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("# the %s SoC family, carried by this device's repository (docs/porting/repositories.md)\n\nsoc %s\n"
                        "\ttitle       %s\n\tvendor      ?\n\tmaintainer  %s\n" % (a.soc, a.soc, a.soc_title or a.soc, a.maintainer))
            with open(os.path.join(top, "soc", "configs", a.soc + ".config"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write('# HakiOS fragment: the %s family -- what is true of the SoC, whatever device it is in.\nCONFIG_SOC="%s"\n' % (a.soc, a.soc))
            print("hakios-device: devices/%s/soc/: a new SoC layer for %s: its cores, addresses and drivers go there" % (name, a.soc))
    hc = config_tool()
    # what a new device begins without: every driver written for one machine (not QEMU's), but the ones its SoC's fragment builds
    soc_fragment = os.path.join(top, "soc", "configs", a.soc + ".config")      # the copy the device now carries
    soc_has = hc.parse(soc_fragment)[0] if a.soc != "none" else {}
    left_out = [d.symbol for d in hc.DRIVERS if not d.name.startswith("VIRTIO_") and soc_has.get(d.symbol) != "y"]
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(top, "configs"), exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(top, "device.conf"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("# devices/%s/device.conf: what this device repository is (docs/porting/repositories.md has every word).\n\n"
                "device %s\n\ttitle       %s\n\tvendor      %s\n\tsoc         %s\n\tdefconfig   %s_defconfig\n"
                "\tmaintainer  %s\n\tstatus      display     partial   UEFI's framebuffer, through the loader (to be checked)\n" %
                (name, name, a.title, a.vendor, a.soc, name, a.maintainer))
    with open(os.path.join(top, "metal.args"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("# what tools/metal-run.sh gives this phone (docs/porting/index.md): its big core and cores, its panel's rate,\n"
                "# how many threads copy frames, how often the touch screen is read. A line of boot-arguments; # is a comment.\n"
                "# fb_intf=<physical> as well, if its SoC's display interface is known: frames are then written behind the scan.\n"
                "fb_hz=60 fb_threads=3\n")
    with open(os.path.join(top, "configs", name + "_defconfig"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("# HakiOS defconfig for the %s (%s): the common kernel, %s, and this device's own.\n#include common_defconfig\n%s"
                "#include %s.config\n" % (a.title, name, "the %s family's facts" % a.soc if a.soc != "none" else "no SoC repository",
                                           "#include %s.config\n" % a.soc if a.soc != "none" else "", name))
    with open(os.path.join(top, "configs", name + ".config"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("# HakiOS fragment: the %s (%s) -- what is true of this device and of no other.\n" % (a.title, name))
        f.write("# Every phone driver is left out until it has been made to work here; the arguments only those drivers read go too.\n")
        f.write('CONFIG_DEVICE="%s"\n' % name)
        for sym in left_out:
            f.write("# CONFIG_%s is not set\n" % sym)
        common = hc.overlay({}, [hc.find_config(ROOT, "common_defconfig")] + ([soc_fragment] if a.soc != "none" else []))
        problems, _ = hc.check(dict(common, **{s: "n" for s in left_out}))
        for p in problems:
            m = re.match(r"CONFIG_([A-Z0-9_]+) gives ", p)
            if m:
                f.write("# CONFIG_%s is not set\n" % m.group(1))
        f.write('# CONFIG_FIRMWARE is "device" in the common kernel: say "none" here until this device\'s firmware is pulled\n')
    readme = os.path.join(top, "README.md")
    if os.path.isfile(readme):              # new-device.py's, about the device tree: the repository's part goes after it
        with open(readme, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("\n## The repository\n\n" + NEW_README.format(title=a.title, name=name, soc=a.soc).split("\n", 2)[2])
    else:
        with open(readme, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(NEW_README.format(title=a.title, name=name, soc=a.soc))
    print("hakios-device: devices/%s made: device.conf, configs/%s_defconfig, configs/%s.config, README.md" % (name, name, name))
    print("hakios-device: %d phone drivers left out to begin with; `make %s_defconfig && make config` shows what is built" % (len(left_out), name))
    print("hakios-device: next: docs/porting/index.md, step by step; tools/new-device.py reads the phone's own device tree")
    if a.repo:
        git("init", "-q", "-b", "main", cwd=top)
        git("add", "-A", cwd=top)
        git("commit", "-q", "-m", "%s: a HakiOS device repository, made by tools/hakios-device.py new" % name, cwd=top)
        print("hakios-device: devices/%s is a git repository; to publish it: make an empty repository (hakios-%s), then\n"
              "    git -C devices/%s remote add origin <its URL> && git -C devices/%s push -u origin main\n"
              "and add its block to devices/manifest.conf (repository, revision) in a pull request" % (name, name, name, name))
    return cmd_check(argparse.Namespace(names=[name]))


def git(*args, cwd=None):
    out = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=cwd or ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode != 0:
        raise Problem("git %s: %s" % (" ".join(args), out.stderr.strip()))
    return out.stdout.strip()


def cmd_sync(a):
    entries = [(k, n, f) for k, n, f, _l in manifest() if not a.names or n in a.names]
    done = 0
    for kind, name, fields in entries:
        repository, revision = one(fields, "repository"), one(fields, "revision")
        if not repository:
            continue                        # kept in this tree (`path`)
        top = home(kind, name)
        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(top, ".git")):
            if os.path.exists(top):
                raise Problem("%s exists and is not a clone of %s: move it away first" % (os.path.relpath(top, ROOT), repository))
            print("hakios-device: %s: cloning %s" % (name, repository))
            git("clone", "-q", repository, top)
        else:
            # the manifest says where the repository is: a clone made before it moved or was renamed follows it
            origin = subprocess.run(["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"], cwd=top, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
            if origin != repository:
                print("hakios-device: %s: origin was %s, now %s (as the manifest says)" % (name, origin or "(none)", repository))
                git("remote", "set-url" if origin else "add", "origin", repository, cwd=top)
            git("fetch", "-q", "origin", cwd=top)
        if revision:
            git("checkout", "-q", revision, cwd=top)
        print("hakios-device: %s %s at %s" % (kind, name, git("rev-parse", "--short=12", "HEAD", cwd=top)))
        done += 1
    print("hakios-device: %d repositories synced%s" % (done, "" if done else " (every one the manifest names is kept in this tree)"))
    return 0


def cmd_lock(a):
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", "manifest.conf")
    lines = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    for kind, name, fields, start in manifest():
        if name != a.name:
            continue
        if not one(fields, "repository"):
            raise Problem("%s is kept in this tree: it has no revision to lock" % name)
        sha = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=home(kind, name))
        if "revision" in fields:
            n = fields["revision"][-1][1] - 1
            lines[n] = re.sub(r"revision\s+\S+", "revision    " + sha, lines[n])
        else:
            lines.insert(start, "\trevision    " + sha)
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write("\n".join(lines))
        print("hakios-device: %s locked at %s" % (name, sha[:12]))
        return 0
    raise Problem("no %s in devices/manifest.conf" % a.name)


def cmd_split(a):
    kinds = {n: k for k, n in present()}
    if a.name not in kinds:
        raise Problem("no device or SoC %s checked out" % a.name)
    prefix = os.path.relpath(home(kinds[a.name], a.name), ROOT)
    if os.path.exists(a.dir):
        raise Problem("%s already exists" % a.dir)
    branch = "split/" + a.name
    try:
        sha = git("subtree", "split", "-q", "--prefix=" + prefix, "-b", branch)
    except Problem:
        sha = None
    if sha:
        git("clone", "-q", "--branch", branch, ROOT, a.dir)
        git("branch", "-D", branch)
        git("remote", "remove", "origin", cwd=a.dir)
        how = "with the history of %s" % prefix
    else:                                   # no git subtree here: the files as they are, in one first commit
        shutil.copytree(os.path.join(ROOT, prefix), a.dir)
        git("init", "-q", cwd=a.dir)
        git("add", "-A", cwd=a.dir)
        git("commit", "-q", "-m", "%s: the device repository, split from the common one" % a.name, cwd=a.dir)
        how = "in one commit (git subtree is not installed: the history stays in the common repository)"
    print("hakios-device: %s is a repository of its own in %s, %s" % (prefix, a.dir, how))
    print("hakios-device: to publish it: make an empty repository (e.g. hakios-%s-%s), then\n"
          "    git -C %s remote add origin <its URL> && git -C %s push -u origin HEAD:main\n"
          "and in devices/manifest.conf replace `path %s` by `repository <its URL>`, then tools/hakios-device.py lock %s" %
          (kinds[a.name], a.name, a.dir, a.dir, prefix, a.name))
    return 0


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("list", help="the devices and SoCs").set_defaults(fn=cmd_list)
    p = sub.add_parser("check", help="a device or SoC repository holds together")
    p.add_argument("names", nargs="*")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_check)
    p = sub.add_parser("new", help="a new device repository")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.add_argument("--soc", required=True, help="its SoC family: copied from a device or socs/ that has it, else a new layer; or none")
    p.add_argument("--soc-title", help="for a new SoC layer: what the family is called")
    p.add_argument("--repo", action="store_true", help="make the device's directory a git repository, ready to push")
    p.add_argument("--title", required=True, help='what it is called ("POCO X5 Pro 5G")')
    p.add_argument("--vendor", default="?")
    p.add_argument("--maintainer", default="?")
    tree = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    tree.add_argument("--fdt", help="the phone's own device tree (adb pull /sys/firmware/fdt): tools/new-device.py reads it first")
    tree.add_argument("--adb", action="store_true", help="... pulled from the phone on adb now")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_new)
    p = sub.add_parser("sync", help="clone or update the repositories the manifest names")
    p.add_argument("names", nargs="*")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_sync)
    p = sub.add_parser("lock", help="write the revision checked out into the manifest")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_lock)
    p = sub.add_parser("split", help="a device or SoC kept in this tree as a repository of its own")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.add_argument("dir")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_split)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    try:
        sys.exit(a.fn(a))
    except Problem as e:
        print("hakios-device: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`tools/jb-preinstall.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Put packages of the repository into the prefix as installed, newest version first.

usage: jb-preinstall.py PREFIX PACKAGES-INDEX DEBS-DIR NAME...
  PREFIX          the prefix tree, the directory that holds var/jb (jb/root of tools/mk-jb.sh)
  PACKAGES-INDEX  the repository's Packages file, already fetched
  DEBS-DIR        where the .deb files are kept (they are fetched into it when missing)
  NAME...         the packages to put in

The bootstrap is a snapshot, and some of what it carries is older than the repository (debianutils,
launchctl). apt on the phone would upgrade them, but only over the network and only after a boot,
and what is in the image is what a first boot has; so the newest version of each is unpacked into
the prefix here and written into dpkg's database, replacing an older entry if there is one.

Nothing of the package's own scripts is run: these are plain file packages, and /var/jb/prep.sh does
the little that the bootstrap's postinst scripts are needed for at every boot.
"""
import os
import re
import lzma
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile


def version_parts(version):
    """A Debian version as (epoch, upstream, revision), each ready for compare_part."""
    epoch, _, rest = version.partition(':') if ':' in version else ('0', '', version)
    if not rest:
        epoch, rest = '0', version
    upstream, _, revision = rest.rpartition('-')
    if not upstream:
        upstream, revision = rest, ''
    return int(epoch or 0), upstream, revision


def compare_part(a, b):
    """Debian's own order for one part: digit runs numerically, and "~" before everything else."""
    def order(c):
        if c == '~':
            return -1
        if c.isalpha():
            return ord(c)
        return ord(c) + 256

    i = j = 0
    while i < len(a) or j < len(b):
        # the stretch that is not digits, character by character
        while (i < len(a) and not a[i].isdigit()) or (j < len(b) and not b[j].isdigit()):
            x = order(a[i]) if i < len(a) and not a[i].isdigit() else 0
            y = order(b[j]) if j < len(b) and not b[j].isdigit() else 0
            if x != y:
                return -1 if x < y else 1
            if i < len(a) and not a[i].isdigit():
                i += 1
            if j < len(b) and not b[j].isdigit():
                j += 1
        # and the stretch that is, as a number
        first, second = i, j
        while i < len(a) and a[i].isdigit():
            i += 1
        while j < len(b) and b[j].isdigit():
            j += 1
        x = int(a[first:i] or 0)
        y = int(b[second:j] or 0)
        if x != y:
            return -1 if x < y else 1
    return 0


def newer(a, b):
    """Is version a newer than version b?"""
    ea, ua, ra = version_parts(a)
    eb, ub, rb = version_parts(b)
    if ea != eb:
        return ea > eb
    for x, y in ((ua, ub), (ra, rb)):
        order = compare_part(x, y)
        if order:
            return order > 0
    return False


def stanzas(text):
    for block in text.split('\n\n'):
        if block.strip():
            yield block.strip('\n')


def field(stanza, name):
    m = re.search(r'(?m)^%s: (.*)$' % name, stanza)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else None


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 5:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    prefix, index_path, debs, names = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4:]
    jb = os.path.join(prefix, 'var/jb')
    status_path = os.path.join(jb, 'Library/dpkg/status')
    index = open(index_path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()

    best = {}
    for stanza in stanzas(index):
        name = field(stanza, 'Package')
        if name in names:
            version = field(stanza, 'Version') or '0'
            if name not in best or newer(version, field(best[name], 'Version') or '0'):
                best[name] = stanza

    status = open(status_path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    installed = {field(s, 'Package'): field(s, 'Version') for s in stanzas(status)}
    done = []
    for name in names:
        if name not in best:
            print('jb-preinstall.py: %s: not in the repository' % name)
            continue
        stanza = best[name]
        version = field(stanza, 'Version')
        have = installed.get(name)
        if have is not None and not newer(version, have):
            print('jb-preinstall.py: %s %s is already there' % (name, have))
            continue
        filename = field(stanza, 'Filename')
        deb = os.path.join(debs, os.path.basename(filename))
        if not os.path.exists(deb):
            url = os.environ.get('MIRROR', 'https://apt.procurs.us').rstrip('/') + '/' + filename
            # curl, as the rest of tools/mk-jb.sh fetches: the repository turns away urllib
            if subprocess.run(['curl', '-sL', '--fail', '-o', deb, url]).returncode != 0:
                sys.exit('jb-preinstall.py: cannot fetch %s' % url)
        # a .deb is an ar archive; its data holds the tree, under ./var/jb for a rootless package.
        # The member is found in the listing: "ar p" says nothing and still succeeds for a name that
        # is not in the archive, so asking for one that may not be there tells us nothing.
        listing = subprocess.run(['ar', 't', deb], capture_output=True, text=True)
        member = next((line.strip() for line in listing.stdout.split('\n') if line.startswith('data.tar')), None)
        if member is None:
            sys.exit('jb-preinstall.py: %s: no data member in %s' % (name, deb))
        data = subprocess.run(['ar', 'p', deb, member], capture_output=True).stdout
        if not data:
            sys.exit('jb-preinstall.py: %s: %s is empty in %s' % (name, member, deb))
        if member.endswith('.zst'):
            data = subprocess.run(['zstd', '-dc'], input=data, capture_output=True).stdout
        elif member.endswith('.lzma'):
            data = lzma.decompress(data, format=lzma.FORMAT_ALONE)
        # .gz, .bz2 and .xz tarfile knows by itself
        tmp = deb + '.tar'
        with open(tmp, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(data)
        with tarfile.open(tmp) as tar:
            for member in tar.getmembers():
                path = os.path.normpath(member.name.lstrip('./'))
                # only into the prefix, and never climbing out of it
                if not path.startswith('var/jb/') or '..' in path.split('/'):
                    continue
                member.name = './' + path
                target = os.path.join(prefix, path)
                if os.path.islink(target) or (os.path.exists(target) and not os.path.isdir(target)):
                    os.unlink(target)                   # the older version's file makes way
                # "fully_trusted": the prefix is full of links to absolute paths of its own
                # (/var/jb/bin/run-parts -> /var/jb/usr/bin/run-parts), which the careful filter
                # refuses; where the files land is checked above instead.
                tar.extract(member, prefix, set_attrs=True, filter='fully_trusted')
        os.unlink(tmp)
        # dpkg's database: the new stanza in place of the old one, or added
        entry = '\n'.join(line for line in stanza.split('\n')
                          if not line.startswith(('Filename:', 'Size:', 'MD5sum:', 'SHA1:', 'SHA256:', 'SHA512:',
                                                  'Description-md5:'))) + '\nStatus: install ok installed\n'
        if have is not None:
            status = '\n\n'.join(entry if field(s, 'Package') == name else s for s in stanzas(status)) + '\n'
        else:
            status = status.rstrip('\n') + '\n\n' + entry + '\n'
        done.append('%s %s%s' % (name, version, ' (was %s)' % have if have else ''))
    # A package that still writes to Cydia Substrate's old directory turns the link ElleKit put there
    # into a real one when it is unpacked here; put the tweaks where they belong and the link back.
    old_dir = os.path.join(jb, 'Library/MobileSubstrate/DynamicLibraries')
    new_dir = os.path.join(jb, 'usr/lib/TweakInject')
    if os.path.isdir(old_dir) and not os.path.islink(old_dir):
        os.makedirs(new_dir, exist_ok=True)
        for entry in sorted(os.listdir(old_dir)):
            os.replace(os.path.join(old_dir, entry), os.path.join(new_dir, entry))
        os.rmdir(old_dir)
        os.symlink('/var/jb/usr/lib/TweakInject', old_dir)
        print('jb-preinstall.py: the tweaks moved to usr/lib/TweakInject, the old directory a link again')
    open(status_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(status)
    if done:
        print('jb-preinstall.py: ' + ', '.join(done))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

`tools/kernel-delta.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# In a workspace made by new-workspace.sh: print, as a patch, what was changed in the kernel tree
# since the workspace was made (new files included). Apply it elsewhere with "git apply".
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/../xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2"
git rev-parse -q --verify refs/redwood/baseline >/dev/null || { echo "kernel-delta.sh: not a workspace (no baseline)" >&2; exit 1; }
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$PWD/.git/index.delta
rm -f "$GIT_INDEX_FILE"
git read-tree refs/redwood/baseline
git add -A . 2>/dev/null
git diff --cached --binary refs/redwood/baseline
rm -f "$GIT_INDEX_FILE"
```

`tools/kernel-version-test.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""tools/kernel-version.py: how the version string is made, and what it refuses.

  the real VERSION file          -> 2.3.4-hakios-darwin22.5-g<8 hex>, in the form Android's kernels have
  a tracked file changed         -> "-dirty"; a new untracked file is not a change (as in Linux's setlocalversion)
  CONFIG_SOC in a .config        -> "-<soc>" between the Darwin and the commit
  HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX          -> replaces the git part
  not a git tree                 -> no git part, and no failure
  a malformed VERSION            -> an error that says which line
"""
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
TOOL = os.path.join(HERE, "kernel-version.py")
failures = []


def check(label, ok, detail=""):
    print("%s %s" % ("ok  " if ok else "FAIL", label))
    if not ok:
        failures.append(label)
        if detail:
            print("     " + detail.strip().replace("\n", "\n     ")[:400])


def run(root, *args, env=None):
    e = dict(os.environ)
    e.pop("HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX", None)
    e.update(env or {})
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, TOOL, "--root", root, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, env=e)


def git(d, *args):
    subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@t", "-C", d, *args], check=True, capture_output=True)


work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="kernel-version-test-")
try:
    # a repository with the real VERSION file, committed
    repo = os.path.join(work, "repo")
    os.makedirs(repo)
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", repo], check=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION"), os.path.join(repo, "VERSION"))
    open(os.path.join(repo, "tracked.txt"), "w").write("one\n")
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "x")

    full = run(repo)
    check("the full string has the Android form", re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+-hakios-darwin22\.5-g[0-9a-f]{8}", full.stdout.strip()) is not None,
          full.stdout + full.stderr)
    check("--short is VERSION.PATCHLEVEL.SUBLEVEL", re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+", run(repo, "--short").stdout.strip()) is not None)
    check("--release adds EXTRAVERSION", run(repo, "--release").stdout.strip() == run(repo, "--short").stdout.strip() + "-hakios")
    check("--name and --darwin", run(repo, "--name").stdout.strip() == "Hello Darwin" and
          run(repo, "--darwin").stdout.split() == ["22.5.0", "xnu-8796.121.2"])
    check("the string starts with the release", full.stdout.startswith(run(repo, "--release").stdout.strip() + "-darwin"))

    open(os.path.join(repo, "untracked.txt"), "w").write("new\n")
    check("an untracked file is not a change", "-dirty" not in run(repo).stdout)
    open(os.path.join(repo, "tracked.txt"), "w").write("two\n")
    check("a changed tracked file makes it -dirty", run(repo).stdout.strip().endswith("-dirty"), run(repo).stdout)
    git(repo, "checkout", "--", "tracked.txt")
    check("restored: clean again", "-dirty" not in run(repo).stdout)

    open(os.path.join(repo, ".config"), "w").write('# a configuration\nCONFIG_SOC="sc7280"\nCONFIG_CPUS=8\n')
    check("CONFIG_SOC of .config goes between the Darwin and the commit",
          re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+-hakios-darwin22\.5-sc7280-g[0-9a-f]{8}", run(repo).stdout.strip()) is not None, run(repo).stdout)
    other = os.path.join(work, "other.config")
    open(other, "w").write('CONFIG_SOC="sm8550"\n')
    check("--config names another configuration", "-sm8550-" in run(repo, "--config", other).stdout, run(repo, "--config", other).stdout)

    check("HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX replaces the git part",
          run(repo, env={"HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX": "-gdeadbeef"}).stdout.strip().endswith("-sc7280-gdeadbeef"))
    check("an empty HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX means no git part", run(repo, env={"HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX": ""}).stdout.strip().endswith("-sc7280"))

    # not a git tree
    plain = os.path.join(work, "plain")
    os.makedirs(plain)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION"), os.path.join(plain, "VERSION"))
    r = run(plain)
    check("not a git tree: no git part, no failure", r.returncode == 0 and r.stdout.strip() == "%s-darwin22.5" % run(plain, "--release").stdout.strip(),
          r.stdout + r.stderr)

    # malformed files
    def with_version(text):
        d = os.path.join(work, "bad%d" % len(os.listdir(work)))
        os.makedirs(d)
        open(os.path.join(d, "VERSION"), "w").write(text)
        return run(d)

    good = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION")).read()
    r = with_version(re.sub(r"SUBLEVEL = \d+", "SUBLEVEL = thirteen", good))
    check("a SUBLEVEL that is not a number: refused", r.returncode != 0 and "SUBLEVEL" in r.stderr, r.stderr)
    r = with_version(good.replace("EXTRAVERSION = -hakios", "EXTRAVERSION = hakios"))
    check("an EXTRAVERSION without its dash: refused", r.returncode != 0 and "EXTRAVERSION" in r.stderr, r.stderr)
    r = with_version(good.replace("NAME = Hello Darwin\n", ""))
    check("a missing key: refused, and named", r.returncode != 0 and "NAME" in r.stderr, r.stderr)
    r = with_version(good + "this is not a setting\n")
    check("a line that is no setting: refused, with its number", r.returncode != 0 and re.search(r"VERSION:\d+", r.stderr), r.stderr)
    r = run(os.path.join(work, "nothing-here"))
    check("no VERSION file: refused", r.returncode != 0 and "no VERSION file" in r.stderr, r.stderr)
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)

if failures:
    sys.exit("kernel-version-test: %d FAILED" % len(failures))
print("kernel-version-test: all passed")

```

`tools/kernel-version.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The version string of the HakiOS kernel, made from VERSION, the active configuration and git.

usage: tools/kernel-version.py [--short | --name | --darwin | --release | --all]
                               [--config FILE] [--root DIR]

  (none)    2.3.4-hakios-darwin22.5-sc7280-g1a2b3c4d[-dirty]   what goes under the banner as kernel.ver=
  --short   2.3.4                                              VERSION.PATCHLEVEL.SUBLEVEL
  --release 2.3.4-hakios                                       with EXTRAVERSION: what a tag is called (v2.3.4-hakios)
  --name    Hello Darwin                                        the release's name
  --darwin  22.5.0 xnu-8796.121.2                               what it is built on
  --all     every part, one per line, for the build log

The parts of the full string, in the order Android's kernels give theirs:
  VERSION.PATCHLEVEL.SUBLEVEL  from the file VERSION
  EXTRAVERSION                 ... likewise
  -darwin<major>.<minor>       the Darwin it is built on (DARWIN in VERSION)
  -<soc>                       CONFIG_SOC of the active configuration, if there is one (`make redwood_defconfig`)
  -g<commit>[-dirty]           git: the commit, and "-dirty" if a tracked file differs from it

HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX in the environment replaces the git part (a reproducible build, or a tree that is
not a git checkout): the string it holds is added as it is.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def read_version(root):
    """VERSION as {KEY: value}: `KEY = value` lines, `#` comments."""
    path = os.path.join(root, "VERSION")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        sys.exit("kernel-version: no VERSION file in %s" % root)
    values = {}
    for n, line in enumerate(open(path, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
        line = line.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        m = re.fullmatch(r"([A-Z]+)\s*=\s*(.*)", line)
        if not m:
            sys.exit("kernel-version: VERSION:%d: want  KEY = value, got %r" % (n, line))
        values[m.group(1)] = m.group(2).strip()
    for key in ("VERSION", "PATCHLEVEL", "SUBLEVEL", "EXTRAVERSION", "NAME", "DARWIN", "XNU"):
        if key not in values:
            sys.exit("kernel-version: VERSION lacks %s" % key)
    for key in ("VERSION", "PATCHLEVEL", "SUBLEVEL"):
        if not values[key].isdigit():
            sys.exit("kernel-version: %s must be a number, got %r" % (key, values[key]))
    if values["EXTRAVERSION"] and not re.fullmatch(r"-[A-Za-z0-9._]+", values["EXTRAVERSION"]):
        sys.exit("kernel-version: EXTRAVERSION is a dash and letters or digits (-hakios), got %r" % values["EXTRAVERSION"])
    return values


def config_soc(path):
    """CONFIG_SOC of a .config, or None: the SoC family the configuration is for."""
    if not path or not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
        m = re.fullmatch(r'CONFIG_SOC="?([a-z0-9]+)"?\s*', line.strip())
        if m:
            return m.group(1)
    return None


def git_part(root):
    """-g<commit>[-dirty], or "" when this is not a git tree (or git is not there)."""
    def git(*args):
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)

    try:
        head = git("rev-parse", "--short=8", "HEAD")
    except OSError:
        return ""
    if head.returncode != 0:
        return ""
    git("update-index", "-q", "--refresh")          # stat data may be stale after a checkout: not a change
    dirty = git("diff-index", "--quiet", "HEAD", "--").returncode != 0
    return "-g" + head.stdout.strip() + ("-dirty" if dirty else "")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    what = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    for flag in ("short", "release", "name", "darwin", "all"):
        what.add_argument("--" + flag, action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--config", help="the configuration to take CONFIG_SOC from (default: .config at the top)")
    ap.add_argument("--root", default=os.path.dirname(HERE))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    root = os.path.abspath(args.root)
    v = read_version(root)
    short = "%s.%s.%s" % (v["VERSION"], v["PATCHLEVEL"], v["SUBLEVEL"])
    release = short + v["EXTRAVERSION"]
    darwin = "-darwin" + ".".join(v["DARWIN"].split(".")[:2])
    soc = config_soc(args.config or os.path.join(root, ".config"))
    suffix = os.environ.get("HAKIOS_VERSION_SUFFIX")
    git = suffix if suffix is not None else git_part(root)
    full = release + darwin + ("-" + soc if soc else "") + git

    if args.short:
        print(short)
    elif args.release:
        print(release)
    elif args.name:
        print(v["NAME"])
    elif args.darwin:
        print(v["DARWIN"], v["XNU"])
    elif args.all:
        print("full=" + full)
        print("short=" + short)
        print("release=" + release)
        print("name=" + v["NAME"])
        print("darwin=" + v["DARWIN"])
        print("xnu=" + v["XNU"])
        print("soc=" + (soc or ""))
        print("git=" + git)
    else:
        print(full)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/latency.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
latency.py RUN.log [MORE.log ...] [RECORDING.raw]: how far behind the finger the phone's screen is.
(More logs: the live ones of the same run, XL_FOLLOW=N XL_FOLLOW_KEEP=1, which keep what the run's log loses.)

A run with boot-arg touch_lat=1 writes a line at every stage a touch passes on its way to the panel,
all in microseconds of mach_absolute_time (the kernel's clock, which user space reads too):

  tl: p TYPE FINGER X Y at US              the kernel posts a sample (drivers/input/hakios.input.c)
  tl: c before US seen US read US          the touch driver finds the interrupt line low and reads the
                                           report (drivers/input/hakios.goodix.c; only for a real finger)
  tl: i TYPE posted US read US sent US     the window server reads it and hands it to the event system
                                           (userland/src/inject.c)
  tl: g FRAME began US ended US DRAWS      the window server draws a frame (userland/src/eagl.c)
  tl: s ID at US                           it hands the frame over (SwapEnd)
  tl: v ID ready US shown US done US       the display driver: the GPU done with it, its beat come, its
                                           pixels in the panel's memory (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp)

With rec_secs=... rec_ring=1 the frames themselves are in the screen recording, each with the time it
was put in the panel's memory. A "zigzag" of rwtouch (the finger up and down over a scrolling list
without letting go) then gives the latency from end to end: the list follows the finger, and the
time by which the list's movement lags the finger's is found by fitting the one to the other (a
constant offset -- the scroll view's slop before it starts to follow -- does not matter; the turns do).
The stages are averaged over the same frames and samples, and what is left between the event
system and the frame -- the application's handling and the wait for the next frame of
CoreAnimation's clock -- is the difference.
"""
import re
import struct
import sys

import numpy as np


def micros_lines(paths):
    """The tl: lines of the logs, once each (the kernel's own also come back in its log at the end)."""
    seen, lines = set(), []
    if isinstance(paths, str):
        paths = [paths]
    for path in paths:
      with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        for raw in f:
            text = raw.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
            at = text.find('tl: ')
            if at < 0:
                continue
            line = text[at:].strip()
            if line not in seen:
                seen.add(line)
                lines.append(line)
    return lines


def parse(lines):
    samples, reads, frames, swaps, shows, chip = [], [], [], {}, {}, []
    for line in lines:
        w = line.split()
        try:
            if w[1] == 'p' and len(w) >= 8:
                samples.append((int(w[7]), int(w[2]), int(w[3]), int(w[4]), int(w[5])))
            elif w[1] == 'i' and len(w) >= 9:
                reads.append((int(w[4]), int(w[6]), int(w[8]), int(w[2])))
            elif w[1] == 'g' and len(w) >= 8:
                frames.append((int(w[4]), int(w[6]), int(w[7])))
            elif w[1] == 's' and len(w) >= 5:
                swaps[int(w[2])] = int(w[4])
            elif w[1] == 'v' and len(w) >= 9:
                shows[int(w[2])] = (int(w[4]), int(w[6]), int(w[8]))
            elif w[1] == 'c' and len(w) >= 8:
                chip.append((int(w[3]), int(w[5]), int(w[7])))
        except ValueError:
            pass
    samples.sort()
    reads.sort()
    frames.sort(key=lambda f: f[1])
    return samples, reads, frames, swaps, shows, chip


def recording(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    magic, width, height, count, oldest = struct.unpack_from('<8sIIII', data, 0)
    if magic != b'RWREC003':
        sys.exit('latency.py: not a recording of the RWREC003 kind')
    began = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, 24)[0]
    size = 8 + width * height * 3
    out = []
    for k in range(count):
        i = (oldest + k) % count
        at = 32 + i * size
        t = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, at)[0]
        pixels = np.frombuffer(data, np.uint8, width * height * 3, at + 8).reshape(height, width, 3)
        out.append(((began + t) // 1000, pixels))
    out.sort(key=lambda f: f[0])
    return out, width, height


def zigzags(samples):
    """Touches with many moves, finger 0: (down time, up time, [(t, y)])."""
    out, current = [], None
    for t, kind, finger, x, y in samples:
        if finger != 0:
            continue
        if kind == 1:
            current = [(t, y)]
        elif kind == 2 and current is not None:
            current.append((t, y))
        elif kind == 3 and current is not None:
            current.append((t, y))
            ys = [p[1] for p in current]
            turns = sum(1 for i in range(1, len(ys) - 1) if (ys[i] - ys[i - 1]) * (ys[i + 1] - ys[i]) < 0)
            if len(current) > 30 and turns >= 3:
                out.append((current[0][0], t, current))
            current = None
    return out


def shift(a, b, most):
    """How far b's content has moved down from a's, in rows: the shift with the least difference."""
    h = a.shape[0]
    best, best_cost = 0, None
    for s in range(-most, most + 1):
        if s >= 0:
            pa, pb = a[0:h - s], b[s:h]
        else:
            pa, pb = a[-s:h], b[0:h + s]
        cost = np.mean(np.abs(pa - pb))
        if best_cost is None or cost < best_cost:
            best, best_cost = s, cost
    return best


def content_offsets(frames, t0, t1, height):
    """The list's position in each frame between t0 and t1, in rows of the recording, relative to the first."""
    chosen = [(t, p) for t, p in frames if t0 <= t <= t1]
    out = []
    if not chosen:
        return out
    top, bottom = int(height * 0.15), int(height * 0.90)
    previous, offset = None, 0
    for t, pixels in chosen:
        grey = pixels[top:bottom, :, :].astype(np.float32).mean(axis=2)
        grey = grey[:, grey.shape[1] // 10: grey.shape[1] * 9 // 10]
        if previous is not None:
            offset += shift(previous, grey, 48)
        out.append((t, offset))
        previous = grey
    return out


def fit_lag(offsets, touch, height):
    """The lag (us) at which the list's position best follows the finger's: least squares with an offset and a gain."""
    tt = np.array([p[0] for p in touch], dtype=np.float64)
    ty = np.array([p[1] for p in touch], dtype=np.float64) / 65535.0 * height
    ft = np.array([o[0] for o in offsets], dtype=np.float64)
    fy = np.array([o[1] for o in offsets], dtype=np.float64)
    best = None
    for lag in range(0, 250001, 500):
        at = ft - lag
        keep = (at >= tt[0]) & (at <= tt[-1])
        if keep.sum() < 10:
            continue
        x = np.interp(at[keep], tt, ty)
        y = fy[keep]
        matrix = np.vstack([x, np.ones_like(x)]).T
        coefficients, residual, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(matrix, y, rcond=None)
        error = float(np.mean((matrix @ coefficients - y) ** 2))
        if best is None or error < best[1]:
            best = (lag, error, coefficients[0], int(keep.sum()))
    return best


def mean(values):
    return sum(values) / len(values) if values else float('nan')


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    logs = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.endswith('.raw')]
    raws = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a.endswith('.raw')]
    samples, reads, frames, swaps, shows, chip = parse(micros_lines(logs))
    print(f'latency.py: {len(samples)} samples, {len(reads)} read by the window server, {len(frames)} frames drawn, '
          f'{len(swaps)} handed over, {len(shows)} shown; {len(chip)} reports read from the touch chip')
    if chip:
        found = [seen - before for before, seen, read in chip if before]
        took = [read - seen for before, seen, read in chip]
        print(f'  touch chip: looked at every {mean(found) / 1000:.2f} ms (a report waits half of that on average); '
              f'reading a report takes {mean(took) / 1000:.2f} ms')
    pictures, width, height = recording(raws[0]) if raws else ([], 0, 0)
    totals = []
    for number, (down, up, touch) in enumerate(zigzags(samples)):
        moves = [p for p in touch[1:-1]]
        print(f'zigzag {number + 1}: {len(touch)} samples over {(up - down) / 1000:.0f} ms')
        result = None
        if pictures:
            offsets = content_offsets(pictures, down, up + 400000, height)
            result = fit_lag(offsets, moves, height) if len(offsets) > 10 else None
        if result is None:
            print('  (no frames of it in the recording)')
            continue
        lag, error, gain, used = result
        print(f'  END TO END: the list follows the finger {lag / 1000:.1f} ms behind, until its pixels are in the panel\'s '
              f'memory (gain {gain:.2f}, misfit {error ** 0.5:.1f} rows, {used} frames)')
        totals.append(lag)
        # the stages, over the samples and frames of this zigzag
        within = [r for r in reads if down <= r[0] <= up]
        inject = [r[1] - r[0] for r in within]
        send = [r[2] - r[1] for r in within]
        rows = []
        for sid in sorted(shows):
            if sid not in swaps or not (down <= shows[sid][2] <= up + 400000):
                continue
            swap = swaps[sid]
            drawn = [f for f in frames if f[1] <= swap]
            if not drawn:
                continue
            began, ended, draws = drawn[-1]
            ready, shown, done = shows[sid]
            rows.append((ended - began, swap - ended, ready - swap, shown - ready, done - shown))
        if rows:
            render, handover, gpu, beat, copy = (mean([r[k] for r in rows]) for k in range(5))
            rest = lag - mean(inject) - mean(send) - render - handover - gpu - beat - copy
            print(f'  kernel to window server (the touch device read):   {mean(inject) / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  window server to event system:                      {mean(send) / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  the application, and the wait for the next frame:   {rest / 1000:6.2f} ms  (what is left)')
            print(f'  the window server drawing the frame (GPU commands):  {render / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  frame drawn to frame handed over (SwapEnd):         {handover / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  waiting for the GPU to finish it:                   {gpu / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  waiting for the display driver\'s beat:              {beat / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  copying (scaling) it into the panel\'s memory:       {copy / 1000:6.2f} ms')
            print(f'  ({len(rows)} frames, {len(within)} samples; then the panel\'s next scan of those rows, '
                  f'0 to 8.3 ms at 120 Hz)')
    if totals:
        print(f'all zigzags: {mean(totals) / 1000:.1f} ms behind the finger on average')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/macos-bin/README.md`:

```md
What `xl` needs of Linux on a Mac: `flock`, GNU `timeout` and `stat` (MacPorts' gtimeout and gstat),
`sha256sum` with GNU's `--quiet` (for tools/mk-mesa.sh; it is `shasum -a 256` underneath), and Android's `fastboot` and `adb` (platform-tools, which `xl` finds here or in $PATH). Put the
```
