```c
/*
 * DRM's synchronisation objects (syncobj), which Turnip's msm backend makes its VkFences and VkSemaphores of, kept in
 * this process: there is one GPU and one connection to it here, so what a syncobj waits for is always one of this
 * process's submissions, a fence number of the kernel's (MSM_WAIT_FENCE tells when it is done). A syncobj is a timeline:
 * the last point known reached, and the points still on their way, each with the submission that reaches it. A binary
 * one is the timeline of point 1 (signalled: 1, reset: 0). A submission's MSM_SUBMIT_SYNCOBJ_IN syncobjs are waited for
 * here, before it goes to the kernel, and its MSM_SUBMIT_SYNCOBJ_OUT ones are given its fence (submit_with_syncobjs).
 * Not here: syncobjs and sync files as file descriptors (nothing outside this process waits for them).
 */
#define SYNCOBJS        4096
#define PENDING         16

struct syncobj {
	bool used;
	uint64_t reached;                       /* the last point known reached */
	unsigned pending;
	struct { uint64_t point; uint32_t fence; } on_the_way[PENDING];
};
static struct syncobj syncobjs[SYNCOBJS];
static pthread_mutex_t syncobj_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_cond_t syncobj_submitted = PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER;

static struct syncobj *
syncobj_of(uint32_t handle)
{
	return handle != 0 && handle < SYNCOBJS && syncobjs[handle].used ? &syncobjs[handle] : NULL;
}

/* whether the kernel is done with submission FENCE: waited for until DEADLINE (absolute CLOCK_MONOTONIC ns; 0: not at all) */
static bool
fence_done(uint32_t fence, int64_t deadline)
{
	struct drm_msm_wait_fence wait = { .fence = fence, .queueid = 0 };

	wait.timeout.tv_sec = deadline / 1000000000;
	wait.timeout.tv_nsec = deadline % 1000000000;
	return call(DRM_COMMAND_BASE + DRM_MSM_WAIT_FENCE, &wait, sizeof(wait)) == 0;
}

static int64_t
now_ns(void)
{
	struct timespec t;

	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &t);
	return (int64_t)t.tv_sec * 1000000000 + t.tv_nsec;
}

/* the points on their way that their submissions have reached since: into REACHED (lock held) */
static void
syncobj_poll(struct syncobj *s)
{
	unsigned kept = 0;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < s->pending; i++) {
		if (fence_done(s->on_the_way[i].fence, 0)) {
			if (s->on_the_way[i].point > s->reached) s->reached = s->on_the_way[i].point;
		} else {
			s->on_the_way[kept++] = s->on_the_way[i];
		}
	}
	s->pending = kept;
}

static void
syncobj_add(struct syncobj *s, uint64_t point, uint32_t fence)
{
	if (s->pending == PENDING) {
		syncobj_poll(s);
	}
	if (s->pending == PENDING) {
		/* (full: the oldest is waited for, its point taken as reached) */
		fence_done(s->on_the_way[0].fence, now_ns() + 10000000000LL);
		if (s->on_the_way[0].point > s->reached) s->reached = s->on_the_way[0].point;
		memmove(&s->on_the_way[0], &s->on_the_way[1], (PENDING - 1) * sizeof(s->on_the_way[0]));
		s->pending--;
	}
	s->on_the_way[s->pending].point = point;
	s->on_the_way[s->pending].fence = fence;
	s->pending++;
}

int
drmSyncobjCreate(int fd, uint32_t flags, uint32_t *handle)
{
	(void)fd;
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	for (uint32_t h = 1; h < SYNCOBJS; h++) {
		if (!syncobjs[h].used) {
			memset(&syncobjs[h], 0, sizeof(syncobjs[h]));
			syncobjs[h].used = true;
			syncobjs[h].reached = (flags & DRM_SYNCOBJ_CREATE_SIGNALED) ? 1 : 0;
			*handle = h;
			pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
			return 0;
		}
	}
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	errno = ENOMEM;
	return -ENOMEM;
}

int
drmSyncobjDestroy(int fd, uint32_t handle)
{
	struct syncobj *s;

	(void)fd;
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	s = syncobj_of(handle);
	if (s != NULL) s->used = false;
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	return s != NULL ? 0 : -EINVAL;
}

int
drmSyncobjReset(int fd, const uint32_t *handles, uint32_t count)
{
	(void)fd;
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		struct syncobj *s = syncobj_of(handles[i]);
		if (s != NULL) s->reached = 0, s->pending = 0;
	}
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	return 0;
}

int
drmSyncobjTimelineSignal(int fd, const uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, uint32_t count)
{
	(void)fd;
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		struct syncobj *s = syncobj_of(handles[i]);
		uint64_t point = points != NULL && points[i] != 0 ? points[i] : 1;
		if (s != NULL && point > s->reached) s->reached = point;
	}
	pthread_cond_broadcast(&syncobj_submitted);
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	return 0;
}

int
drmSyncobjSignal(int fd, const uint32_t *handles, uint32_t count)
{
	return drmSyncobjTimelineSignal(fd, handles, NULL, count);
}

int
drmSyncobjQuery2(int fd, uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, uint32_t count, uint32_t flags)
{
	(void)fd;
	(void)flags;
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		struct syncobj *s = syncobj_of(handles[i]);
		if (s != NULL) syncobj_poll(s);
		points[i] = s != NULL ? s->reached : 0;
	}
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	return 0;
}

int
drmSyncobjQuery(int fd, uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, uint32_t count)
{
	return drmSyncobjQuery2(fd, handles, points, count, 0);
}

/*
 * Wait for each syncobj's point (0 or NULL: 1, a binary one's) -- all of them, or the first (DRM_SYNCOBJ_WAIT_FLAGS_WAIT_ALL
 * clear) -- until DEADLINE (absolute CLOCK_MONOTONIC ns). A point no submission is on its way to yet is waited for to be
 * submitted with DRM_SYNCOBJ_WAIT_FLAGS_WAIT_FOR_SUBMIT, an error without (as Linux answers); WAIT_AVAILABLE: submitted
 * is enough.
 */
int
drmSyncobjTimelineWait(int fd, uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, unsigned count, int64_t deadline, unsigned flags,
    uint32_t *first)
{
	const bool all = (flags & DRM_SYNCOBJ_WAIT_FLAGS_WAIT_ALL) != 0;
	int result = -ETIME;

	(void)fd;
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	for (;;) {
		unsigned reached = 0, unknown = 0;
		uint32_t wait_fence = 0;
		bool have_fence = false;

		for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			struct syncobj *s = syncobj_of(handles[i]);
			uint64_t point = points != NULL && points[i] != 0 ? points[i] : 1;
			bool on_the_way = false;

			if (s == NULL) {
				pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
				return -EINVAL;
			}
			syncobj_poll(s);
			for (unsigned k = 0; k < s->pending; k++) {
				if (s->on_the_way[k].point >= point) {
					on_the_way = true;
					if (!have_fence || (int32_t)(s->on_the_way[k].fence - wait_fence) < 0) wait_fence = s->on_the_way[k].fence;
					have_fence = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (s->reached >= point || (on_the_way && (flags & DRM_SYNCOBJ_WAIT_FLAGS_WAIT_AVAILABLE))) {
				reached++;
				if (!all) {
					if (first != NULL) *first = i;
					pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
					return 0;
				}
			} else if (!on_the_way) {
				unknown++;
			}
		}
		if (reached == count) {
			if (first != NULL) *first = 0;
			pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
			return 0;
		}
		if (unknown != 0 && !(flags & DRM_SYNCOBJ_WAIT_FLAGS_WAIT_FOR_SUBMIT)) {
			pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
			return -EINVAL;
		}
		if (now_ns() >= deadline) {
			break;
		}
		if (have_fence && unknown == 0) {
			/* every point is on its way: the earliest submission among them waited for, without the lock */
			pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
			fence_done(wait_fence, deadline);
			pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
		} else {
			/* some point not submitted yet: until a submission or a signal, in steps of a millisecond at most */
			struct timespec until;
			int64_t step = now_ns() + 1000000;
			struct timeval tv;
			gettimeofday(&tv, NULL);
			int64_t real = (int64_t)tv.tv_sec * 1000000000 + (int64_t)tv.tv_usec * 1000 + (step < deadline ? 1000000 : deadline - now_ns());
			until.tv_sec = real / 1000000000;
			until.tv_nsec = real % 1000000000;
			pthread_cond_timedwait(&syncobj_submitted, &syncobj_lock, &until);
		}
	}
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	return result;
}

int
drmSyncobjWait(int fd, uint32_t *handles, unsigned count, int64_t deadline, unsigned flags, uint32_t *first)
{
	return drmSyncobjTimelineWait(fd, handles, NULL, count, deadline, flags, first);
}

/* DST at DST_POINT (0: binary) gets what SRC at SRC_POINT (0: binary) is or will be */
int
drmSyncobjTransfer(int fd, uint32_t dst, uint64_t dst_point, uint32_t src, uint64_t src_point, uint32_t flags)
{
	struct syncobj *d, *s;
	uint64_t want = src_point != 0 ? src_point : 1, to = dst_point != 0 ? dst_point : 1;

	(void)fd;
	(void)flags;
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	d = syncobj_of(dst);
	s = syncobj_of(src);
	if (d == NULL || s == NULL) {
		pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
		return -EINVAL;
	}
	syncobj_poll(s);
	if (dst_point == 0) d->reached = 0, d->pending = 0;
	if (s->reached >= want) {
		if (to > d->reached) d->reached = to;
	} else {
		for (unsigned k = 0; k < s->pending; k++) {
			if (s->on_the_way[k].point >= want) {
				syncobj_add(d, to, s->on_the_way[k].fence);
				break;
			}
		}
	}
	pthread_cond_broadcast(&syncobj_submitted);
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	return 0;
}

static uint32_t last_fence;     /* the fence of the last submission the kernel took */

static int
submit_with_syncobjs(struct drm_msm_gem_submit *submit, unsigned long size)
{
	const struct drm_msm_gem_submit_syncobj *in = (const void *)(uintptr_t)submit->in_syncobjs;
	const struct drm_msm_gem_submit_syncobj *out = (const void *)(uintptr_t)submit->out_syncobjs;
	const uint32_t stride = submit->syncobj_stride ? submit->syncobj_stride : sizeof(*in);
	const uint32_t nin = (submit->flags & MSM_SUBMIT_SYNCOBJ_IN) ? submit->nr_in_syncobjs : 0;
	const uint32_t nout = (submit->flags & MSM_SUBMIT_SYNCOBJ_OUT) ? submit->nr_out_syncobjs : 0;
	int error;

	/* what it waits for first (this queue's own submissions are in order on the one ring anyway) */
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nin; i++) {
		const struct drm_msm_gem_submit_syncobj *x = (const void *)((const uint8_t *)in + i * stride);
		uint32_t h = x->handle;
		uint64_t p = x->point;
		int r = drmSyncobjTimelineWait(0, &h, &p, 1, now_ns() + 10000000000LL,
		    DRM_SYNCOBJ_WAIT_FLAGS_WAIT_ALL | DRM_SYNCOBJ_WAIT_FLAGS_WAIT_FOR_SUBMIT, NULL);
		if (r != 0) return r;
		if (x->flags & MSM_SUBMIT_SYNCOBJ_RESET) drmSyncobjReset(0, &h, 1);
	}
	submit->flags &= ~(uint32_t)(MSM_SUBMIT_SYNCOBJ_IN | MSM_SUBMIT_SYNCOBJ_OUT);
	submit->in_syncobjs = submit->out_syncobjs = 0;
	submit->nr_in_syncobjs = submit->nr_out_syncobjs = 0;
	if (submit->nr_cmds == 0) {
		/*
		 * Nothing for the GPU (Turnip's submissions that only signal): the kernel takes none, and what it stands for
		 * is done when everything submitted before it is, the last fence -- there is one ring.
		 */
		submit->fence = __atomic_load_n(&last_fence, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
	} else {
		error = call((unsigned)(DRM_COMMAND_BASE + DRM_MSM_GEM_SUBMIT), submit, size);
		if (error != 0) return -error;
		__atomic_store_n(&last_fence, submit->fence, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
	}
	pthread_mutex_lock(&syncobj_lock);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nout; i++) {
		const struct drm_msm_gem_submit_syncobj *x = (const void *)((const uint8_t *)out + i * stride);
		struct syncobj *s = syncobj_of(x->handle);
		if (s == NULL) continue;
		if (x->point == 0) s->reached = 0, s->pending = 0;   /* a binary one: what it holds now is this submission */
		syncobj_add(s, x->point != 0 ? x->point : 1, submit->fence);
	}
	pthread_cond_broadcast(&syncobj_submitted);
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&syncobj_lock);
	return 0;
}

/* Linux's device nodes, which Turnip's lists of devices ask about: one GPU, a render node 128 */
int drmGetNodeTypeFromFd(int fd) { (void)fd; return DRM_NODE_RENDER; }

int drmGetDevices2(uint32_t flags, drmDevicePtr devices[], int max_devices) { (void)flags; (void)devices; (void)max_devices; return 0; }
void drmFreeDevices(drmDevicePtr devices[], int count) { (void)devices; (void)count; }
int drmGetDevice2(int fd, uint32_t flags, drmDevicePtr *device) { (void)fd; (void)flags; *device = NULL; return -ENODEV; }
void drmFreeDevice(drmDevicePtr *device) { (void)device; }

/*
 * The IOSurfaces mapped in this process, by address (hakios_drm_host_surface): a host pointer Turnip is asked to import
 * (VK_EXT_external_memory_host) is the memory of one of them, and the kernel makes a buffer of a surface by its ID
 * (drmPrimeFDToHandle). A surface's mapping lasts as long as the surface; a later surface at the same address replaces it.
 */
#define HOST_SURFACES 1024
static struct { uintptr_t base; uint64_t size; uint32_t surface; } host_surfaces[HOST_SURFACES];
static unsigned host_surfaces_next;
static pthread_mutex_t host_surfaces_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

__attribute__((visibility("default")))     /* (called by AdrenoMetal's frontend, outside Turnip) */
void
hakios_drm_host_surface(const void *base, uint64_t size, uint32_t surface)
{
	unsigned i, free_slot = HOST_SURFACES;

	pthread_mutex_lock(&host_surfaces_lock);
	for (i = 0; i < HOST_SURFACES; i++) {
		if (host_surfaces[i].base == (uintptr_t)base) {
			break;
		}
		if (host_surfaces[i].base == 0 && free_slot == HOST_SURFACES) {
			free_slot = i;
		}
	}
	if (i == HOST_SURFACES) {
		i = free_slot != HOST_SURFACES ? free_slot : host_surfaces_next++ % HOST_SURFACES;
	}
	host_surfaces[i].base = (uintptr_t)base;
	host_surfaces[i].size = size;
	host_surfaces[i].surface = surface;
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&host_surfaces_lock);
}

uint32_t
hakios_drm_host_surface_at(const void *base, uint64_t size)
{
	uint32_t surface = 0;

	pthread_mutex_lock(&host_surfaces_lock);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < HOST_SURFACES; i++) {
		if (host_surfaces[i].base == (uintptr_t)base && host_surfaces[i].size >= size) {
			surface = host_surfaces[i].surface;
			break;
		}
	}
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&host_surfaces_lock);
	return surface;
}

int
hakios_drm_user_memory(int fd, const void *address, uint64_t size, uint32_t *handle)
{
	struct { uint64_t address, size; uint32_t handle, flags; } request = { (uintptr_t)address, size, 0, 0 };
	int error = call(HAKIOS_GPU_USER_MEMORY, &request, sizeof(request));

	(void)fd;
	if (error != 0) {
		errno = error;
		return -1;
	}
	*handle = request.handle;
	return 0;
}
```

`tools/mesa/hakios-drm/xf86drm.h`:

```h
/*
 * What Mesa's freedreno takes from libdrm's xf86drm.h, for a system without Linux's DRM: the
 * declarations here, the functions in hakios.drm.c, which carry the requests to the kernel's
 * GPU driver (the service HakiosGPU; drivers/gpu/hakios.gpu.cpp) as calls of its user client.
 * tools/mk-mesa.sh puts both into Mesa's tree, where they are the "libdrm" freedreno is built
 * against. The request numbers and their structures are Linux's (Mesa's include/drm-uapi).
 */
#ifndef HAKIOS_XF86DRM_H
#define HAKIOS_XF86DRM_H

#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <sys/types.h>

#include "drm-uapi/drm.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#define DRM_NODE_PRIMARY        0
#define DRM_NODE_RENDER         2
#define DRM_CLOEXEC             O_CLOEXEC
#define DRM_RDWR                O_RDWR

typedef struct _drmVersion {
	int version_major, version_minor, version_patchlevel;
	int name_len;
	char *name;
	int date_len;
	char *date;
	int desc_len;
	char *desc;
} drmVersion, *drmVersionPtr;

int drmOpenWithType(const char *name, const char *busid, int type);
int drmIoctl(int fd, unsigned long request, void *arg);
int drmCommandWrite(int fd, unsigned long index, const void *data, unsigned long size);
int drmCommandWriteRead(int fd, unsigned long index, void *data, unsigned long size);
drmVersionPtr drmGetVersion(int fd);
void drmFreeVersion(drmVersionPtr version);
int drmGetCap(int fd, uint64_t capability, uint64_t *value);

/*
 * Buffers and fences as file descriptors: there are none here. But memory that somebody else
 * has made does come in, as Linux's comes in by file descriptor: an IOSurface, by its ID, where
 * freedreno expects the descriptor (see hakios_drm_surface() below).
 */
int drmPrimeHandleToFD(int fd, uint32_t handle, uint32_t flags, int *prime_fd);
int drmPrimeFDToHandle(int fd, int surface, uint32_t *handle);
int drmSyncobjCreate(int fd, uint32_t flags, uint32_t *handle);
```

`tools/mesa/ir3-round-default.patch`:

```patch
ir3: round integer-to-float conversions to nearest when nothing says otherwise.

The a6xx `cov` instruction has a rounding-mode field, and create_cov() sets it
only from float_controls_execution_mode, which is a SPIR-V declaration. When
nothing is declared, nir_get_rounding_mode_from_float_controls returns
nir_rounding_mode_undef, neither branch fires, and the field keeps the zero it
was built with -- ROUND_ZERO in instr-a3xx.h, which is truncation toward zero.

So every shader that does not come from SPIR-V with an explicit rounding mode
gets truncation where IEEE-754, GLSL and OpenCL all require round-to-nearest-even.
On this port that is every shader: the port's OpenGL ES declares nothing, and so
does the AIR frontend. The hardware is not at fault -- it can round, and setting
the field makes it.

Measured on the phone's Adreno 7c+ Gen 3, uint -> float, GLSL ES 3.0 through
OSMesa with the value in a uniform so nothing could be folded on the host
(userland/src/u2f_test.c, RC=rc.u2f), expectations from C on the host:

      input         before        after      C
  0xFFFFFFFF    4294967040   4294967296   4294967296
  0xFFFFFF80    4294967040   4294967296   4294967296
  0x01000001      16777216     16777216     16777216
  0x01000003      16777218     16777220     16777220
  0x7FFFFFFF    2147483520   2147483648   2147483648
  0x00FFFFFF      16777215     16777215     16777215

0x01000003 is the value that identifies the rule rather than merely showing a
disagreement: it is 2^24+3, half way between the representable 2^24+2 and
2^24+4, and both round-half-to-even and round-half-away-from-zero give 2^24+4.
The hardware gave 2^24+2, which is neither -- it is the low bits dropped. The
two inputs that agree before the change are exactly the two where truncation and
rounding coincide, so agreement there is the absence of a question.

Reproduced independently down a second path with no GLSL in it at all: the AIR
frontend's own test suite (tools/air/intrincheck.py, docs/air.md section 4)
compiles one Metal operation per module and executes it on the same GPU, and
air.convert.f.{f32,v2f32,v3f32}.{u,s}.* disagree with C on exactly the inputs
that need rounding -- 5 declarations, and i2f truncates just as u2f does. Two
unrelated front ends reaching the same instruction return the same wrong number.

The case for this change does not need a standard quoted at it, because Mesa
already contains both answers. NIR's own constant folder, with no rounding mode
declared, rounds to nearest even: nir_opcodes.py generates, for the plain f2f16,

    if (nir_is_rounding_mode_rtz(execution_mode, 16))
       dst = _mesa_half_to_float(_mesa_float_to_float16_rtz(src0));
    else
       dst = _mesa_half_to_float(_mesa_float_to_float16_rtne(src0));

-- RTZ only where RTZ was asked for, RTNE otherwise -- and it folds an integer
to float conversion through the host's own, which is also RTNE. The backend, in
the same circumstances, leaves the cov field at ROUND_ZERO and truncates.

So one expression has two answers in one compiler depending on whether NIR could
fold it. That is what the measurements above are: the same operation over the
same inputs, folded by NIR and executed by the hardware, disagreeing. Whatever
any specification requires, these two should not differ from each other, and
making the backend ask for what the folder already assumes is the smaller change
of the two.

Not verified: whether the field is honoured for a 16-bit destination. The branch
covers TYPE_F16 too, and the measurements do not reach it -- this port's harness
packs every half result into a float4, so no shader it generates declares a half
output, and a half render target appears in none of the 456 modules of the corpus
it was built from.

Worth a reviewer's attention rather than hidden: one F16 path through this branch
is pack_half_2x16, and nir_lower_mediump.c says of it "pack_half rounding is
undefined". Where nothing is required, setting ROUND_EVEN changes behaviour
without correcting it -- permitted either way, and not part of the argument here.
If that is unwelcome, the narrower change is to set the default only when the
source is an integer type; the measurements above would be unaffected. I would
not choose it, and the reason is worth stating rather than leaving the two
looking equivalent.

Of everything that reaches this branch, pack_half is the only destination with no
requirement behind it. f2f32 and b2f are exact, so the mode cannot change them.
i2f and u2f require round-to-nearest-even, and are measured above. And plain
nir_op_f2f16 reaches it too -- f2f16_rtne and f2f16_rtz are taken by the two
cases above, so an f32 -> f16 narrowing with no declared mode lands here and
truncates by exactly the same mechanism, in an API that asks for RTE. The
narrower change would leave that one unfixed while fixing its neighbours, which
is a worse place to stop than either end.

That last one is reasoning from the mechanism and is NOT measured here: this
port's harness packs every half result into a float4, so it cannot reach an
f2f16 either. It is offered as a thing to check, not as a result.

Checked against Mesa 25.0.7 (this port's pin), the 26.2.5 release, and main as
fetched on 20 October 2026: the rounding block of create_cov() is 750 characters
in each and character-for-character identical in all three, with no trailing
else. So this is not an artefact of the pin, and not something a newer release
has already addressed. (ROUND_ZERO = 0 in instr-a3xx.h was verified in the pin
and in 26.2.5; only ir3_compiler_nir.c was taken from main, so that header is
not claimed for it.)

The hunk applies to main's own copy of the file without a rebase, tested against
it rather than against the pin: both patch(1) and git apply report "succeeded at
410 (offset 2 lines)" and exit 0. The context matches; only the line number has
moved, so anyone comparing the hunk header's 408 against main will see the two
lines and should not take them for a mismatch.

--- a/src/freedreno/ir3/ir3_compiler_nir.c
+++ b/src/freedreno/ir3/ir3_compiler_nir.c
@@ -408,6 +408,13 @@
          set_cat1_round(cov.rpts, nrpt, ROUND_EVEN);
       else if (rounding_mode == nir_rounding_mode_rtz)
          set_cat1_round(cov.rpts, nrpt, ROUND_ZERO);
+      else
+         /* Nothing declared a mode, and the field defaults to ROUND_ZERO,
+          * which is truncation. IEEE-754, GLSL and OpenCL all require
+          * round-to-nearest-even here, so ask for it rather than letting the
```

`tools/mesa/ir3-shift-split.patch`:

```patch
ir3: moving a shift inside an add changes the number when the constant is
negative.

create_shift() in ir3_nir_lower_io_offsets.c turns the byte offset of an SSBO
access into an element offset. When the offset has the shape `iadd constant,
foo` it rewrites `(C + x) >> s` as `(x >> s) + (C >> s)`, so that
nir_opt_offsets can fold the constant into the instruction's immediate field.

That identity does not hold for a negative constant. `buf[i - 1].field` is
ordinary code, and LLVM hands it over as `iadd 0xfffffffc, i*24` -- a
subtraction. `(i*24 - 4) >> 2` borrows from the bits above the two it drops;
`(i*24 >> 2) + (0xfffffffc >> 2)` adds 0x3fffffff instead of 0xffffffff and
does not. The two differ by 2^30, which puts the element offset a gigabyte past
the end of the buffer, and an out-of-range `ldib` returns zero without saying
so. It also drops the low bits of a constant that is not a whole number of
elements, which is the same mistake in a smaller way.

Measured on the phone's Adreno 7c+ Gen 3. `fbs_bistochastize_iter` of
PortraitFilters.metallib reads `grid_buf[id - 1].n` through exactly this shape
and sums `id + 1` terms when the read returns 0 instead of `id`. With input
built from the module's own metadata (tools/air/kinput.py, docs/air.md section
5) its four outputs should all be 1/sqrt(3) -- one term each -- and on the
device they were:

      word     device        1/sqrt(n)     Apple's own LLVM on the host
       0    0x3f13cd3a       1/sqrt(3)     0x3f13cd3a
       1    0x3f000000       1/sqrt(4)     0x3f13cd3a
       2    0x3ee4f92e       1/sqrt(5)     0x3f13cd3a
       3    0x3ed105ec       1/sqrt(6)     0x3f13cd3a

1/sqrt(3+i) in word i is the signature of the read returning 0 for every
thread, and 0 is what that address returns. The three fbs_* kernels of the
corpus carry this shape; the eight MetalFaceMask_* ones do not.

So split the constant out only when it survives being shifted and cannot be a
subtraction. Everything else keeps the shift outside the add, which is what the
code did before the folding and is always right.

--- a/src/freedreno/ir3/ir3_nir_lower_io_offsets.c
+++ b/src/freedreno/ir3/ir3_nir_lower_io_offsets.c
@@ -126,6 +126,32 @@
    return new_offset;
 }
 
+/* Whether `(c + x) >> shift` and `(x >> shift) + (c >> shift)` are the same
+ * number for every x, which is what moving the shift inside the add assumes.
+ *
+ * They are not, twice over. A constant whose low `shift` bits are set loses
+ * them to `c >> shift`, so the offset comes out short. Worse, a negative
+ * constant -- a struct field reached through `buf[i - 1]`, which is ordinary
+ * code -- is a subtraction, and `(x - 4) >> 2` borrows from the bits above
+ * while `(x >> 2) + (0xfffffffc >> 2)` adds 0x3fffffff and does not: the two
+ * differ by 2^30 and the SSBO read lands outside the buffer, where a6xx
+ * returns zero without saying so.
+ *
+ * That was measured: fbs_bistochastize_iter reads grid_buf[id - 1].n with
+ * exactly this shape, and on an Adreno 7c+ Gen 3 it read 0 for every thread,
+ * which turned 1/sqrt(3) in all four of its outputs into 1/sqrt(3), 1/sqrt(4),
+ * 1/sqrt(5), 1/sqrt(6) (docs/air.md section 5).
+ *
+ * So split only a constant that is a whole number of elements and cannot be a
+ * subtraction. Everything else keeps the shift outside the add, which is what
+ * the code did before the folding was added and is always right.
+ */
+static bool
+shift_splits_over_iadd(uint32_t c, int shift)
+{
+   return (c & BITFIELD_MASK(shift)) == 0 && c < (1u << 31);
+}
+
 static nir_def *
 create_shift(nir_builder *b, nir_def *offset, int shift)
 {
@@ -138,7 +164,9 @@

       if (offset_instr->op == nir_op_iadd &&
-          nir_src_is_const(offset_instr->src[0].src)) {
+          nir_src_is_const(offset_instr->src[0].src) &&
+          shift_splits_over_iadd(
+             nir_src_as_const_value(offset_instr->src[0].src)->u32, shift)) {
          nir_def *new_shift = ir3_nir_try_propagate_bit_shift(
```

`tools/mesa/ir3-ssbo-subdword.patch`:

```patch
ir3: an SSBO is a buffer of dwords to the Gallium driver, so keep sub-dword
access off it.

An SSBO on a6xx/a7xx is reached through an IBO descriptor, and `ldib`/`stib`
take an offset in *that descriptor's* texels -- the hardware multiplies the
index by the texel size the descriptor declares. ir3 does the dividing on the
other side, in ir3_nir_lower_io_offsets.c's lower_offset_for_ssbo(), and it
divides by the size of the *instruction*: shift 2 for a 32-bit access, 1 for
16-bit, 0 for 8-bit. The two only agree when the descriptor's texel is as wide
as the access.

Turnip keeps them agreeing by writing a descriptor per width and picking one:
write_buffer_descriptor_addr() lays down FMT6_16_UINT, FMT6_32_UINT and
FMT6_8_UINT descriptors next to each other, and tu_lower_io()'s
`descriptor_idx + 1` selects the 8-bit one for an 8-bit load or store.

The Gallium driver writes one descriptor per SSBO slot and it is always
PIPE_FORMAT_R32_UINT (fd6_image.cc, fd6_ssbo_descriptor()), with nothing that
selects another. So on that driver a 16-bit SSBO access addresses twice the
byte offset it was given and an 8-bit one four times, and an 8-bit store is
worse than mis-addressed: ir3_a6xx.c emits it as `stib.b.typed...u16.4`, which
is the blob's encoding for an imageBuffer of VK_FORMAT_R8 and means nothing
against a 32-bit descriptor. The driver also leaves
ir3_compiler_options::storage_16bit and storage_8bit false, which is already
how ir3 knows the difference elsewhere -- ir3_nir_lower_ssbo_size() shifts the
buffer length by 1 or 2 depending on exactly that, "a byte length divided by
IBO_0_FMT".

Nothing in GL reaches it, which is why it has stood: a GLSL SSBO member is at
least 32 bits and at least 4-byte aligned, so ir3_mem_access_size_align()'s
`(bytes & 1)` and `(bytes & 2)` cases never fire. A Metal shader is a different
matter -- `ushort` and `uchar` fields in a device buffer are ordinary there,
and the AIR frontend (src/compiler/air) translates them to 16- and 8-bit
load_ssbo/store_ssbo.

Measured on the phone's Adreno 7c+ Gen 3, two of Apple's compute kernels from
PortraitFilters.metallib, given input built from each module's own metadata
(docs/air.md section 5):

  MetalFaceMask_AddSeedPoint    one `uchar` store, to byte 28 of the span
                                table. The dispatch finished and byte 28 was
                                unchanged; the CPU reference over the same
                                bytes writes 0x5a there.
  MetalFaceMask_PropagateParents  walks a linked list of spans, leaving when
                                `nextSpanID` is 0xffff. The dispatch never
                                finished. Its `nextSpanID` reads land four
                                bytes apart instead of two, which turns the
                                lists 0, 1, 2, 3 of the input into the cycle
                                0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 0, and that loop has no end.

The fix is to ask for dwords whenever the descriptor is one, in
ir3_mem_access_size_align(), where every other size decision is already made.
nir_lower_mem_access_bit_sizes then does the work: a narrow load becomes a dword
load at the masked offset plus a shift, and a narrow store becomes the iand/ior
pair of 32-bit SSBO atomics the pass already keeps for this, which is why
may_lower_unaligned_stores_to_atomics has to be set. Atomics rather than a plain
read-modify-write matter here: these kernels have sixteen threads writing `uchar`
fields that share a dword.

Turnip is unaffected where it sets the options, and is fixed by the same change
on a device where it cannot (a6xx without 16-bit storage, where an unaligned
32-bit access is split into 16-bit ones against a 32-bit descriptor).

cb_data was unset at both call sites, so it carries the compiler now; turnip's
other call (push constants, tu_shader.cc) leaves it null and never sees an SSBO
intrinsic, and a null is read as "no sub-dword descriptor" either way.

--- a/src/freedreno/ir3/ir3_nir.c
+++ b/src/freedreno/ir3/ir3_nir.c
@@ -953,6 +953,8 @@
                  uint32_t align_offset, bool offset_is_const,
                  enum gl_access_qualifier access, const void *cb_data)
 {
+   const struct ir3_compiler *compiler = cb_data;
+
    align = nir_combined_align(align, align_offset);
    assert(util_is_power_of_two_nonzero(align));
 
@@ -970,6 +972,29 @@
    if (intrin == nir_intrinsic_load_ubo)
       bit_size = 32;
 
+   /* ldib/stib scale the offset by the texel size of the IBO descriptor, while
+    * lower_offset_for_ssbo() scales it by the size of the access. A driver with
+    * no narrower descriptor to point them at must therefore stay on dwords:
+    * otherwise a 16-bit access reads and writes at twice the byte offset it was
+    * given and an 8-bit one at four times -- and an 8-bit store is emitted as a
+    * typed R8 store, which a 32-bit descriptor does not describe at all.
+    *
+    * nir_lower_mem_access_bit_sizes turns what is left into a dword load plus a
+    * shift, or a store into the pair of 32-bit atomics it keeps for this, so the
+    * narrow access still happens -- it happens through a descriptor that exists.
+    */
+   if ((intrin == nir_intrinsic_load_ssbo || intrin == nir_intrinsic_store_ssbo) &&
+       ((bit_size == 16 && (!compiler || !compiler->options.storage_16bit)) ||
+        (bit_size == 8 && (!compiler || !compiler->options.storage_8bit)))) {
+      bit_size = 32;
+      /* Below a dword of alignment the pass reads with a mask and a shift and
+       * writes with a pair of atomics, and both of those work a dword at a
+       * time -- so ask for one, however many narrow components there were.
+       */
+      if (align < 4)
+         bytes = MIN2(bytes, 4);
+   }
+
    return (nir_mem_access_size_align){
       .num_components = MAX2(1, MIN2(bytes / (bit_size / 8), 4)),
       .bit_size = bit_size,
@@ -1092,6 +1117,12 @@
                nir_var_mem_global | nir_var_mem_shared |
                nir_var_function_temp | nir_var_mem_ssbo,
       .callback = ir3_mem_access_size_align,
+      /* so the callback can ask which descriptors this driver writes */
+      .cb_data = (void *)so->compiler,
+      /* a narrow store the callback widened becomes an iand/ior pair of 32-bit
+       * atomics; threads that share a dword then do not lose each other's bytes
+       */
+      .may_lower_unaligned_stores_to_atomics = true,
    };
 
    progress |= OPT(s, nir_lower_mem_access_bit_sizes, &mem_bit_size_options);
```

`tools/metal-cache-seed.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Metal's compiled shader stages from the last run into the next image: no boot compiles them again.
#
#   tools/metal-cache-seed.sh            the phone in Android (adb, root): read var_store's newest archive off
#                                        darwin (read only), take db/hakios-metal-cache out of it into
#                                        userland/hakios-metal-cache; userland/build.sh puts that into the image
#                                        at /redwood/share/hakios-metal-cache, where the window server looks after
#                                        its own cache (HakiosMetalCA.m: HM_CACHE_SEED)
#   tools/metal-cache-seed.sh --image F  the same from a copy of darwin taken from byte 8589934592
#
# What fills the cache in the first place: a Metal run with var_store=1 ufs_write=1 (tools/metal-run.sh does so by
# default), whose orderly end saves /private/var into darwin. Works under Git Bash on Windows (python3 and adb on PATH).
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.."
PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python)
OUT=userland/hakios-metal-cache
rm -rf "$OUT.new"
"$PY" -I tools/var-store-read.py "$@" extract db/hakios-metal-cache "$OUT.new"
n=$(ls "$OUT.new" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '\.stage$' || true)
if [ "$n" = 0 ]; then
	rm -rf "$OUT.new"
	echo "metal-cache-seed: the store holds no compiled stages (was the run a Metal one, with var_store=1 ufs_write=1?)"
	exit 1
fi
# (a stage half written when the save came is a .tmp: never one of the cache's)
rm -f "$OUT.new"/*.tmp
# what was seeded before and is not in this store is kept: another build's stages are only room
mkdir -p "$OUT"
cp "$OUT.new"/*.stage "$OUT"/
rm -rf "$OUT.new"
echo "metal-cache-seed: $n stages from the phone; $(ls "$OUT" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') in $OUT; rebuild the image (userland/build.sh) to carry them"

```

`tools/metal-plugin-test.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# The Metal plug-in's objects on this Mac (tools/metal_plugin_test.m says what that does and does not show), under the address
# sanitizer, with every .metallib under DIR read as a library (an extracted system: sysimage/rootfs). macOS only.
# usage: tools/metal-plugin-test.sh [DIR]
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
[ "$(uname)" = Darwin ] || { echo "metal-plugin-test: needs macOS (its Metal stands in for Darwin's)"; exit 0; }
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
clang -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -Wall -Wno-unused-parameter -Iuserland/src -framework Foundation -framework Metal -lobjc \
	tools/metal_plugin_test.m userland/src/HakiosMetal.m userland/src/hakios_metallib.c -o "$tmp/metal_test"
files=
if [ -n "$1" ]; then
	# the MTLB ones (the GPU driver's own runtime libraries are another format: tools/metallib-test.sh)
	for f in $(find "$1" -name '*.metallib' -type f); do
		if python3 tools/metallib.py list "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then files="$files $f"; fi
	done
fi
"$tmp/metal_test" $files 2>&1 | grep -v '^.*HakiosMetal: ' || true
"$tmp/metal_test" $files >/dev/null 2>&1

```

`tools/metal-run.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# One Metal run on the phone, measured: the window server drawing through Metal (an image built with METAL_PLUGIN=ca),
# the frame-rate bench driving it, and what came of it in one summary. Git Bash on Windows, macOS and Linux alike.
#
#   tools/metal-run.sh                  the run (the phone may be in Android, in its bootloader or in the loader)
#   SECS=180 tools/metal-run.sh         its length in seconds (default 180: the bench's four rounds; see rc.jobs.bench)
#   MORE="metal_gmem=1" tools/...       boot-args beside the ones below; one of the same name takes a default's place
#   PERSIST=0 tools/metal-run.sh        without var_store: /private/var starts empty and nothing is written to darwin
#   UPLOAD=0 tools/metal-run.sh         keep the system image already in the phone's RAM (default: upload this copy's)
#   (bench at this screen: RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.bench.xr, Settings lies lower; UPLOAD=0 keeps the image in the phone's RAM)
#   SHOTS=N                             a screenshot every N seconds during the run into logs/<stamp>-shots/ (default 0)
#   VERBOSE=1 tools/metal-run.sh        with -v: the kernel's text console drawn over the picture (off by default: the log has it all)
#
# What it needs, built in WSL (docs/windows.md) and copied here: userland/root.apfs and userland/system.apfs from
#   METAL_PLUGIN=ca RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.bench EXTRA_SHARE=<dir of QuartzCore-default.metallib> REST=1 SYSTEM=1 userland/build.sh
# (tools/ca-metallib.py writes that file; off a Mac with CA_QC_METALLIB=...). The kernel: hakios-kernel, else prebuilt/.
#
# Boot-args, and why each:
#   gpu=1 metal_fps=1 touch_lat=1   the GPU on, Metal's frame and pass counters, the "tl:" lines tools/frames.py reads
#   metal=1                         the accelerator names the Metal plug-in (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp): without it
#                                   the window server finds no device and stays on OpenGL ES, saying nothing
#   touchscreen=1                   the bench taps and swipes through the touch screen's driver
#   ca_metallib=...                 QuartzCore's library for the window server (tools/ca-metallib.py)
#   gpu_recover=1                   a GPU hang is reset and counted, not the end of the run
#   anim_max=1                      SpringBoard's animations ask for 80..120 frames a second
#   bootcpu=7 cpus=8 cpufreq=1      the kernel on a big core with all eight and their clocks (docs/u-boot.md): xl's own
#                                   default is one small core, on which the first boot is still compiling CoreAnimation's
#                                   shaders when the bench ends (2 November: first frame at 159 s on one core, 86 s on eight)
#   fb_hz=120 fb_measure=1          the framebuffer's beat at the panel's 120 Hz, not its default 60, and the panel's own
#                                   rate measured once (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp)
#   fb_threads=6                    six processors scale a frame onto the panel, not three: Settings' scroll 75 -> 84 frames
#   touch_poll_us=4000              the touch screen looked at every 4 ms, not 8: a sample in every refresh at 120 Hz
#   wallpaper_freeze=1              the wallpaper one picture once at the home screen (the icons blink once): home button 28 -> 92 frames
#   metal_defer=1                   a command buffer's draws recorded when it is committed, not on the way
#   fbscale=2                       the iPhone X's 375 x 812 points at 2 pixels a point (750 x 1624, 2.25 times fewer pixels), stretched to the panel:
#                                   110 frames a second over the bench's gestures, 1.1% over 16.7 ms (4 runs, 4 November, tools/frames.py). Its status
#                                   bar comes from SpringBoard (inject_sb.c). The iPhone XR's class (fbwidth=828 fbheight=1792 fbsubtype=1792) drew
#                                   a little more and at it the bottom edge opened Control Center under real fingers
#   ufs=2 ufs_write=1 var_store=1   (PERSIST=1, the default) /private/var kept in the partition darwin between boots: the
#                                   compiled shader stages in /var/db/hakios-metal-cache survive, so only the first boot
#                                   ever compiles them (tools/metal-cache-seed.sh then puts them in the image)
# The summary: logs/<stamp>-metal.txt -- tools/frames.py's frames per gesture, the HakiosMetal fps lines (the slowest
# passes, each sysmem one with its reason), refusals counted by kind, and var_store's save.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." || exit 1
case "$(uname -s)" in
MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
	# Git Bash: tools/win-bin's flock, and Google's platform-tools where docs/windows.md puts them
	export PATH="$PWD/tools/win-bin:/c/platform-tools:$PATH"
	PY=$(command -v python || command -v python3) ;;
*)
	PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python) ;;
esac
[ -n "$PY" ] || { echo "metal-run: no python on PATH"; exit 1; }
for f in userland/root.apfs userland/system.apfs; do
	[ -f "$f" ] || { echo "metal-run: $f is missing (build it in WSL: docs/windows.md, METAL_PLUGIN=ca)"; exit 1; }
done
command -v fastboot >/dev/null && command -v adb >/dev/null || { echo "metal-run: adb and fastboot are not on PATH (C:\\platform-tools)"; exit 1; }

SECS=${SECS:-180}
PERSIST=${PERSIST:-1}
UPLOAD=${UPLOAD:-1}
SHOTS=${SHOTS:-0}
CA_METALLIB=${CA_METALLIB:-/redwood/share/ca-share/QuartzCore-default.metallib}
# what is the phone's own: its big core and cores, its panel's rate, how many threads copy frames, how often the touch screen is read.
# DEVICE_ARGS= names them, or devices/<CONFIG_DEVICE>/metal.args (tools/hakios-device.py new makes one). Without either, on a phone that
# is not redwood, what assumes nothing: a wrong bootcpu= does not boot and a wrong fb_hz= shows every frame's beat wrong.
if [ -z "${DEVICE_ARGS:-}" ]; then
	device=$(sed -n 's/^CONFIG_DEVICE="\(.*\)"/\1/p' .config 2>/dev/null)
	if [ -n "$device" ] && [ -f "devices/$device/metal.args" ]; then
		DEVICE_ARGS=$(grep -v '^#' "devices/$device/metal.args" | tr '\n' ' ')
	elif [ -z "$device" ] || [ "$device" = redwood ]; then
		DEVICE_ARGS="bootcpu=7 cpus=8 cpufreq=1 fb_hz=120 fb_threads=6 touch_poll_us=4000"
	else
		DEVICE_ARGS="fb_hz=60 fb_threads=3"
		echo "metal-run: no devices/$device/metal.args: fb_hz=60 and one boot core; docs/porting/index.md" >&2
	fi
fi
ARGS="gpu=1 metal=1 metal_fps=1 touch_lat=1 touchscreen=1 ca_metallib=$CA_METALLIB gpu_recover=1 anim_max=1 $DEVICE_ARGS fb_measure=1 wallpaper_freeze=1 metal_defer=1 fbscale=2"
[ "$PERSIST" = 1 ] && ARGS="$ARGS ufs=2 ufs_write=1 var_store=1"
[ "${VERBOSE:-0}" = 1 ] && ARGS="-v $ARGS"
# (a default of the same name goes: the kernel takes the last of two, the plug-in and SpringBoard the first)
for more in ${MORE:-}; do
	kept=
	for word in $ARGS; do
		[ "${word%%=*}" = "${more%%=*}" ] || kept="$kept $word"
	done
	ARGS=$kept
done
ARGS="$ARGS ${MORE:-}"
stamp=$(date +%H%M%S)
mkdir -p logs
out=logs/$stamp-metal.txt

echo "metal-run: the phone is $(./xl state)"
./xl enter || { echo "metal-run: the phone did not reach the loader (./xl state; docs/windows.md, When something goes wrong)"; exit 1; }
if [ "$UPLOAD" = 1 ]; then
	./xl ramdisk userland/system.apfs || { echo "metal-run: the system image did not upload"; exit 1; }
fi

shots_pid=
if [ "$SHOTS" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
	mkdir -p logs/$stamp-shots
	( sleep 30; i=0; while [ $i -lt $(( SECS / SHOTS )) ]; do ./xl screenshot logs/$stamp-shots/$i.png >/dev/null 2>&1; i=$((i + 1)); sleep "$SHOTS"; done ) &
	shots_pid=$!
fi
echo "metal-run: $SECS s with: $ARGS"
XL_CMDLINE="$ARGS" XL_SECS=$SECS XL_FOLLOW=${XL_FOLLOW:-10} XL_FOLLOW_KEEP=1 ./xl run
status=$?
[ -n "$shots_pid" ] && kill "$shots_pid" 2>/dev/null
log=logs/$(readlink logs/last.log 2>/dev/null || ls -t logs/*-run.log 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xargs -n1 basename)
[ -f "$log" ] || { echo "metal-run: no run log (xl run said $status)"; exit 1; }

{
	echo "metal-run $stamp: $log, $SECS s, xl run $status"
	echo "boot-args: $ARGS"
	echo
	echo "== frames per gesture (tools/frames.py)"
	"$PY" -I tools/frames.py "$log" $(ls "$log".live.* 2>/dev/null) 2>&1 | head -60
	echo
	echo "== HakiosMetal"
	grep -a -E 'HakiosMetal(\[[^]]*\])?: fps:' "$log" | tail -40
	grep -a -E 'HakiosMetal(\[[^]]*\])?: (inplace_copy|CoreAnimation.s .*compiled as)' "$log" | sort | uniq -c | head
	echo
	echo "== refused (count, kind)"
	grep -a -E 'HakiosMetal(\[[^]]*\])?: refused:' "$log" | sed -E 's/.*refused: //; s/[0-9]+ vertices.*: /...: /' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -15
	echo
	echo "== frames on the panel (MiniIOMobileFramebuffer, every 5 s: what the window server drew through Metal)"
	grep -a -E 'MiniIOMobileFramebuffer: the panel:' "$log" | sed 's/^\[[^]]*\]: //'
	grep -a -oE 'MiniIOMobileFramebuffer: [0-9]+ frames in [0-9]+ ms \([0-9]+ a second\), [0-9]+ us each in the driver, after [0-9]+ us waiting for the GPU' "$log" |
		sed -E 's/MiniIOMobileFramebuffer: //' | tail -40
	echo
	echo "== shader cache and var_store"
	grep -a -E 'var_store|hakios-metal-cache' "$log" | tail -12
	echo
	echo "== crashes"
	grep -a -E 'crashed|Assertion failed|abort|panic' "$log" | head -10
} > "$out" 2>&1
cat "$out"
echo
echo "metal-run: the summary is $out; the whole log $log"
[ "$PERSIST" = 1 ] && echo "metal-run: next, with the phone back in Android: tools/metal-cache-seed.sh (the stages into the next image)"
exit $status
```

`tools/metal_plugin_test.m`:

```m
/*
 * The Metal plug-in's objects (userland/src/HakiosMetal.m) on this Mac, against the Mac's own Metal: the same source built for
 * macOS, its device made by hand the way Metal makes it (-initWithAcceleratorPort:), and what a program does with buffers and
 * libraries checked. tools/metal-plugin-test.sh builds and runs it, under the address sanitizer.
 *
 * What this shows and what it does not. Metal's private classes on macOS are not Darwin 16.5's (the plug-in takes _MTLResource,
 * _MTLLibrary and _MTLFunction where they exist, and both systems have them), so this checks the plug-in's own logic -- the
 * classes it makes at run time, their state, the buffers' memory, the reading of a .metallib, every object freed -- not that
 * Darwin's Metal is content with them. That is metal_test's to say, in QEMU (userland/rc.jobs.metal).
 *
 * The binary must be called metal_test: the plug-in shows its device to that program only (metal=1, the level a Mac's
 * kern.bootargs gives, having no metal= in it).
 *
 *   usage: metal_test [FILE.metallib ...]      libraries to read besides the one made here
 */
#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>
#import <Metal/Metal.h>
#import <objc/message.h>
#import <objc/runtime.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static int failures;

static void
check(const char *what, BOOL ok)
{
	printf("%s %s\n", ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL", what);
	failures += !ok;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	@autoreleasepool {
		Class cls = objc_getClass("HakiosMetalDevice");
		id<MTLDevice> device;

		check("the plug-in registered HakiosMetalDevice, a subclass of _MTLDevice",
		    cls != Nil && class_getSuperclass(cls) == objc_getClass("_MTLDevice"));
		if (cls == Nil) {
			return 1;
		}
		device = ((id (*)(id, SEL, unsigned int))objc_msgSend)([cls alloc], sel_registerName("initWithAcceleratorPort:"), 7);
		check("-initWithAcceleratorPort: gives a device that conforms to MTLDevice", device != nil && [(id)device conformsToProtocol:@protocol(MTLDevice)]);
		check("it shares the system's memory", [device hasUnifiedMemory]);
		check("what CoreImage asks of a device's limits is answered (no memory of its own, the system's shared)",
		    [(id)device respondsToSelector:sel_registerName("sharedMemorySize")] &&
		    ((uint64_t (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)((id)device, sel_registerName("sharedMemorySize")) == [[NSProcessInfo processInfo] physicalMemory] &&
		    ((uint64_t (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)((id)device, sel_registerName("dedicatedMemorySize")) == 0 && ![device isLowPower] &&
		    ![device isRemovable] && ![device isHeadless]);

		/* buffers */
		id<MTLBuffer> b = [device newBufferWithLength:10000 options:MTLResourceStorageModeShared | MTLResourceCPUCacheModeWriteCombined];
		check("newBufferWithLength: a buffer of that length, zeroed, conforming to MTLBuffer", b != nil && [b length] == 10000 &&
		    ((uint8_t *)[b contents])[9999] == 0 && [(id)b conformsToProtocol:@protocol(MTLBuffer)]);
		memset([b contents], 0x5a, [b length]);
		check("what is written through -contents reads back", ((uint8_t *)[b contents])[0] == 0x5a && ((uint8_t *)[b contents])[9999] == 0x5a);
		check("its options: shared storage, write-combined", [b storageMode] == MTLStorageModeShared &&
		    [b cpuCacheMode] == MTLCPUCacheModeWriteCombined && [b allocatedSize] >= 10000 && [b device] == device);
		[b setLabel:@"a buffer"];
		check("a label is kept", [[b label] isEqualToString:@"a buffer"]);
		[b release];
		const char text[] = "copied, not kept";
		id<MTLBuffer> c = [device newBufferWithBytes:text length:sizeof(text) options:0];
		check("newBufferWithBytes: a copy", c != nil && [c contents] != text && memcmp([c contents], text, sizeof(text)) == 0);
		[c release];
		check("a buffer longer than maxBufferLength is refused", [device newBufferWithLength:[device maxBufferLength] + 1 options:0] == nil);
		__block int freed = 0;
		void *page = mmap(NULL, 16384, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_ANON | MAP_PRIVATE, -1, 0);
		id<MTLBuffer> n = [device newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:page length:16384 options:0 deallocator:^(void *p, NSUInteger l) {
			freed = (p == page && l == 16384);
			munmap(p, l);
		}];
		check("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: the caller's memory itself", n != nil && [n contents] == page);
		[n release];
		check("... and its deallocator is called when the buffer goes", freed == 1);

		/* libraries */
		NSError *error = nil;
		const char junk[] = "not a metallib at all, and long enough to have a header's worth of bytes in it......";
		dispatch_data_t data = dispatch_data_create(junk, sizeof(junk), NULL, DISPATCH_DATA_DESTRUCTOR_DEFAULT);
		id<MTLLibrary> none = [device newLibraryWithData:data error:&error];
		check("newLibraryWithData: on bytes that are not a metallib: nil, and an error that says why", none == nil &&
		    [[error domain] isEqualToString:MTLLibraryErrorDomain] && [[error localizedDescription] containsString:@"not a metallib"]);
		dispatch_release(data);
		error = nil;
		check("newLibraryWithURL: of no file: nil, and an error", [device newLibraryWithURL:[NSURL fileURLWithPath:@"/nonexistent.metallib"]
		    error:&error] == nil && error != nil);
		for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
			NSString *path = [NSString stringWithUTF8String:argv[i]];
			id<MTLLibrary> library = [device newLibraryWithURL:[NSURL fileURLWithPath:path] error:&error];
			NSArray *names = [library functionNames];
			char label[512];

			/* (a library may have no function at all: SafariSharedUI's default.metallib is 118 bytes of header) */
			snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "%s: a library with its functions' names (%lu)", argv[i], (unsigned long)[names count]);
			check(label, library != nil && names != nil && [(id)library conformsToProtocol:@protocol(MTLLibrary)]);
			if (library == nil || [names count] == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			unsigned typed = 0, bitcode = 0;
			for (NSString *name in names) {
				id<MTLFunction> f = [library newFunctionWithName:name];
				NSData *module = [(id)f performSelector:sel_registerName("hakiosBitcode")];

				typed += f != nil && [[f name] isEqualToString:name] && [f functionType] >= MTLFunctionTypeVertex && [f device] == device;
				/* LLVM bitcode starts with "BC" 0xC0DE */
				bitcode += [module length] > 4 && memcmp([module bytes], "BC\xc0\xde", 4) == 0;
				[f release];
			}
			snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "%s: every function by its name, with its type, and its module is LLVM bitcode", argv[i]);
			check(label, typed == [names count] && bitcode == [names count]);
			check("a name the library does not have: nil", [library newFunctionWithName:@"no such function"] == nil);
			[library release];
		}
		/* the first library again, as a universal file (an Apple-GPU slice, then the AIR64 one) given as data */
		if (argc > 1) {
			NSData *thin = [NSData dataWithContentsOfFile:[NSString stringWithUTF8String:argv[1]]];
			NSMutableData *fat = [NSMutableData dataWithLength:4096];
			uint8_t *h = [fat mutableBytes];
			uint32_t length = (uint32_t)[thin length];
			const uint8_t header[] = { 0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbe, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0x01, 0, 0, 0x13, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x08, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x10, 0, 0, 0, 0,
				0x01, 0, 0, 0x17, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x10, 0, (uint8_t)(length >> 24), (uint8_t)(length >> 16), (uint8_t)(length >> 8),
				(uint8_t)length, 0, 0, 0, 0 };

			memcpy(h, header, sizeof(header));
			[fat appendData:thin];
			dispatch_data_t d = dispatch_data_create([fat bytes], [fat length], NULL, DISPATCH_DATA_DESTRUCTOR_DEFAULT);
			id<MTLLibrary> universal = [device newLibraryWithData:d error:&error];
			id<MTLLibrary> plain = [device newLibraryWithURL:[NSURL fileURLWithPath:[NSString stringWithUTF8String:argv[1]]] error:&error];
			check("a universal metallib given as data: its AIR64 slice, the same functions as the thin file",
			    universal != nil && [[universal functionNames] isEqualToArray:[plain functionNames]]);
			dispatch_release(d);
			[universal release];
			[plain release];
		}
		[device release];
	}
	printf("metal_plugin_test: %s\n", failures ? "FAILED" : "all passed");
	return failures != 0;
}
```

`tools/metallib-test.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# The Metal plug-in's reading of a .metallib (userland/src/hakios_metallib.c) on this machine, under the address and
# undefined-behaviour sanitizers: a file made here and cut and bent every way (each refused, nothing read outside it), then
# every .metallib under DIR read by it and by tools/metallib.py, which must agree on every function.
# usage: tools/metallib-test.sh [DIR]     DIR: an extracted system (sysimage/rootfs); without one, only the made file
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
cc -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Iuserland/src \
	tools/metallib_test.c userland/src/hakios_metallib.c -o "$tmp/metallib_test"
"$tmp/metallib_test" cuts
[ -n "$1" ] || exit 0
n=0
other=0
find "$1" -name '*.metallib' -type f > "$tmp/files"
while IFS= read -r f; do
	if ! python3 tools/metallib.py list "$f" > "$tmp/py.all" 2>/dev/null; then
		# not an MTLB container (the GPU driver's own runtime libraries are another format): the C reading must refuse it too
		if "$tmp/metallib_test" list "$f" > "$tmp/c"; then
			echo "metallib-test: $f: tools/metallib.py cannot read it and the C reading took it"
			exit 1
		fi
		other=$((other + 1))
		continue
	fi
	sed -n '/ functions$/,$p' "$tmp/py.all" > "$tmp/py"
	"$tmp/metallib_test" list "$f" > "$tmp/c" || true
	if ! cmp -s "$tmp/py" "$tmp/c"; then
		echo "metallib-test: $f: the two readings differ"
		diff "$tmp/py" "$tmp/c" | head -5
		exit 1
	fi
	n=$((n + 1))
done < "$tmp/files"
echo "metallib-test: $n files under $1: the C reading and tools/metallib.py agree on every function; $other that are not MTLB refused by both"

```

`tools/metallib.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Take a .metallib apart: the MTLB container, its function list, and each function's LLVM bitcode.

The container was worked out by hand against the files of Darwin userland 16.5; what is in it, and what the
numbers below mean, is written down in docs/metal.md (section 9). Every module of every .metallib
in the extracted system is ordinary LLVM bitcode in the standard 0x0B17C0DE wrapper, so after
"metallib.py dump" an ordinary llvm-dis reads them.

usage: metallib.py list FILE                  the functions, their type, air version, module size
       metallib.py dump FILE OUTDIR [N]       write each function's bitcode as OUTDIR/<name>.bc
"""
import os
import struct
import sys

# The TYPE tag. Corrected against the metadata of all 456 modules: 4 is what
# the 135 stitchable functions of PortraitFilters carry, and every one of them
# says !air.visible, so 4 is "visible" and 3 is not.
TYPES = {0: 'vertex', 1: 'fragment', 2: 'kernel', 3: 'unqualified', 4: 'visible',
         5: 'extern', 6: 'intersection'}


def parse(path):
    b = open(path, 'rb').read()
    assert b[:4] == b'MTLB', 'not a metallib: %r' % b[:4]
    (ver_maj, ver_min) = struct.unpack_from('<HH', b, 4)
    total = struct.unpack_from('<Q', b, 0x10)[0]
    funcs_off = struct.unpack_from('<Q', b, 0x18)[0]
    funcs_end = struct.unpack_from('<Q', b, 0x20)[0]
    pub_off, pub_len = struct.unpack_from('<QQ', b, 0x28)
    prv_off, prv_len = struct.unpack_from('<QQ', b, 0x38)
    bc_off, bc_len = struct.unpack_from('<QQ', b, 0x48)
    header = dict(version=(ver_maj, ver_min), total=total, file=len(b),
                  funcs=(funcs_off, funcs_end), public=(pub_off, pub_len),
                  private=(prv_off, prv_len), bitcode=(bc_off, bc_len))

    p = funcs_off
    count = struct.unpack_from('<I', b, p)[0]
    p += 4
    out = []
    for _ in range(count):
        size = struct.unpack_from('<I', b, p)[0]      # counts from this field itself
        q, end = p + 4, p + size
        f = {}
        while q < end:
            tag = b[q:q + 4]
            if tag == b'ENDT':
                break
            ln = struct.unpack_from('<H', b, q + 4)[0]
            val = b[q + 6:q + 6 + ln]
            if tag == b'NAME':
                f['name'] = val.rstrip(b'\0').decode('utf-8', 'replace')
            elif tag == b'TYPE':
                f['type'] = TYPES.get(val[0], 'type%d' % val[0])
            elif tag == b'OFFT':
                f['offt'] = struct.unpack('<QQQ', val)
            elif tag == b'VERS':
                f['vers'] = struct.unpack('<HHHH', val)
            elif tag == b'MDSZ':
                f['mdsz'] = struct.unpack('<Q', val)[0]
            elif tag == b'HASH':
                f['hash'] = val.hex()[:16]
            q += 6 + ln
        out.append(f)
        p = end
    return b, header, out


def bitcode_of(b, header, f):
    """The function's module, unwrapped from the LLVM bitcode wrapper if it has one."""
    start = header['bitcode'][0] + f['offt'][2]
    blob = b[start:start + f['mdsz']]
    if blob[:4] == bytes((0xde, 0xc0, 0x17, 0x0b)):          # 0x0B17C0DE, little endian
        off, size = struct.unpack_from('<II', blob, 8)
        return blob[off:off + size], True
    return blob, False


if __name__ == '__main__':
    what, path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    b, header, funcs = parse(path)
    if what == 'list':
        for k, v in header.items():
            print('%-10s %s' % (k, v))
        print('%d functions' % len(funcs))
        for f in funcs:
            print('  %-52s %-13s air %s  module %d' % (f.get('name', '?'), f.get('type', '?'),
                                                       '.'.join(map(str, f.get('vers', ()))), f.get('mdsz', 0)))
    elif what == 'dump':
        outdir = sys.argv[3]
        limit = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else len(funcs)
        os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
        for f in funcs[:limit]:
            bc, wrapped = bitcode_of(b, header, f)
            name = f.get('name', 'f%d' % funcs.index(f)).replace('/', '_')[:120]
            with open(os.path.join(outdir, name + '.bc'), 'wb') as fp:
                fp.write(bc)
            print('%-52s %6d bytes %s %s' % (name, len(bc), 'unwrapped' if wrapped else 'raw   ', bc[:4].hex()))

```

`tools/metallib_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * userland/src/hakios_metallib.c on this machine (tools/metallib-test.sh builds it with the address and undefined-behaviour
 * sanitizers and runs it).
 *
 *   metallib_test list FILE    the functions as tools/metallib.py list prints them (name, type, AIR version, module size),
 *                              so that the script can compare the two readings line for line
 *   metallib_test cuts         a small metallib made here, then every way of cutting it short and a set of lengths and offsets
 *                              made to point outside it: each must be refused (or read), never read past the end
 */
#include "hakios_metallib.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static int failures;

static void
put16(uint8_t *p, uint16_t v) { p[0] = (uint8_t)v; p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); }
static void
put32(uint8_t *p, uint32_t v) { for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) p[i] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8 * i); }
static void
put64(uint8_t *p, uint64_t v) { for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) p[i] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8 * i); }

static size_t
tag(uint8_t *p, const char *name, const void *value, uint16_t length)
{
	memcpy(p, name, 4);
	put16(p + 4, length);
	memcpy(p + 6, value, length);
	return 6 + (size_t)length;
}

/* two functions, the second's module in the bitcode wrapper; returns the size */
static size_t
make(uint8_t *b)
{
	size_t list = 0x58, p, entry, modules;
	uint8_t vers[8] = { 2, 0, 8, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0 }, offt[24] = { 0 }, mdsz[8] = { 0 }, type;

	memset(b, 0, 1024);
	memcpy(b, "MTLB", 4);
	put16(b + 4, 0x8001);
	put16(b + 6, 2);
	p = list + 4;
	put32(b + list, 2);
	for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
		entry = p;
		p += 4;
		p += tag(b + p, "NAME", i == 0 ? "first\0" : "second_one\0", i == 0 ? 6 : 11);
		type = i == 0 ? 2 : 1;
		p += tag(b + p, "TYPE", &type, 1);
		p += tag(b + p, "VERS", vers, 8);
		put64(offt + 16, i == 0 ? 0 : 16);
		p += tag(b + p, "OFFT", offt, 24);
		put64(mdsz, i == 0 ? 16 : 40);
		p += tag(b + p, "MDSZ", mdsz, 8);
		memcpy(b + p, "ENDT", 4);
		p += 4;
		put32(b + entry, (uint32_t)(p - entry));
	}
	put64(b + 0x18, list);
	put64(b + 0x20, p - list - 4);
	modules = p;
	memset(b + modules, 0xab, 16);                          /* the first module, bare */
	put32(b + modules + 16, 0x0B17C0DE);                    /* the second, wrapped: 20 bytes of header, then 20 of bitcode */
	put32(b + modules + 16 + 8, 20);
	put32(b + modules + 16 + 12, 20);
	memcpy(b + modules + 36, "BC\xc0\xde", 4);
	put64(b + 0x48, modules);
	put64(b + 0x50, 56);
	put64(b + 0x10, modules + 56);
	return modules + 56;
}

static void
check(const char *what, int ok)
{
	if (!ok) {
		printf("FAIL %s\n", what);
		failures++;
	}
}

static int
cuts(void)
{
	uint8_t good[1024];
	size_t size = make(good);
	struct hakios_metallib info;
	struct hakios_metallib_function f[4];
	const char *why = NULL;
	const uint8_t *bc;
	uint64_t length;

	check("the made file reads", hakios_metallib_parse(good, size, &info, f, 4, &why) == 0 && info.count == 2);
	check("names, types, versions", f[0].name_length == 5 && memcmp(f[0].name, "first", 5) == 0 && f[1].name_length == 10 &&
	    f[0].type == HAKIOS_METALLIB_KERNEL && f[1].type == HAKIOS_METALLIB_FRAGMENT && f[0].air[0] == 2 && f[0].air[1] == 8);
	check("a bare module is itself", hakios_metallib_bitcode(good, size, &f[0], &bc, &length) == 0 && length == 16);
	check("a wrapped one is what the wrapper points at", hakios_metallib_bitcode(good, size, &f[1], &bc, &length) == 0 &&
	    length == 20 && memcmp(bc, "BC\xc0\xde", 4) == 0);
	check("counting without keeping", hakios_metallib_parse(good, size, &info, NULL, 0, &why) == 0 && info.count == 2);

	/* every length short of the whole: refused, and (under the sanitizers) nothing read past it */
	int refused = 0;
	for (size_t cut = 0; cut < size; cut++) {
		uint8_t *copy = malloc(cut ? cut : 1);

		memcpy(copy, good, cut);
		refused += hakios_metallib_parse(copy, cut, &info, f, 4, &why) != 0;
		free(copy);
	}
	check("every file cut short is refused", refused == (int)size);

	/* offsets and lengths made to point outside, each alone */
	static const struct { size_t at; int width; uint64_t value; const char *what; } bad[] = {
		{ 0x18, 8, 0xfffffffffffffff0ull, "the list's start" },
		{ 0x20, 8, 0xffffffffffffffffull, "the list's length" },
		{ 0x48, 8, 0xfffffffffffffff8ull, "the modules' start" },
		{ 0x50, 8, 0x7fffffffffffffffull, "the modules' length" },
		{ 0x58, 4, 0xffffffffu, "the count of functions" },
		{ 0x5c, 4, 0xfffffff0u, "an entry's size" },
		{ 0x5c, 4, 2, "an entry's size, too small" },
	};
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(bad) / sizeof(bad[0]); i++) {
		uint8_t copy[1024];

		memcpy(copy, good, size);
		if (bad[i].width == 8) {
			put64(copy + bad[i].at, bad[i].value);
		} else {
			put32(copy + bad[i].at, (uint32_t)bad[i].value);
		}
		char label[96];
		snprintf(label, sizeof(label), "a bad %s is refused", bad[i].what);
		check(label, hakios_metallib_parse(copy, size, &info, f, 4, &why) != 0);
	}
	/* a tag's length that runs past its entry, and a module past the modules */
	uint8_t copy[1024];
	memcpy(copy, good, size);
	put16(copy + 0x58 + 4 + 4 + 4, 0xffff);                  /* NAME's length of the first function */
	check("a tag running past its entry is refused", hakios_metallib_parse(copy, size, &info, f, 4, &why) != 0);
	memcpy(copy, good, size);
	hakios_metallib_parse(copy, size, &info, f, 4, &why);
	put64(copy + info.file_size - 56 - 1, 0);               /* (no-op: keeps the layout) */
	/* the wrapper of the second module pointing past it */
	memcpy(copy, good, size);
	put32(copy + size - 40 + 12, 1000);
	check("a wrapper pointing past its module is refused", hakios_metallib_parse(copy, size, &info, f, 4, &why) == 0 &&
	    hakios_metallib_bitcode(copy, size, &f[1], &bc, &length) != 0);
	/* a universal file: an Apple-GPU slice first, then the AIR64 one, which is what is taken */
	uint8_t fat[2048] = { 0 };
	const uint8_t *thin;
	size_t thin_size;
	static const uint8_t header[] = { 0xca, 0xfe, 0xba, 0xbe, 0, 0, 0, 2,
		0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x13, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x01, 0x00, 0, 0, 0, 0x10, 0, 0, 0, 0,        /* an Apple GPU's: 16 bytes at 256 */
		0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x17, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x02, 0x00, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 };         /* AIR64 at 512, its length below */
	memcpy(fat, header, sizeof(header));
	fat[8 + 20 + 12] = (uint8_t)(size >> 24);
	fat[8 + 20 + 13] = (uint8_t)(size >> 16);
	fat[8 + 20 + 14] = (uint8_t)(size >> 8);
	fat[8 + 20 + 15] = (uint8_t)size;
	memcpy(fat + 512, good, size);
	check("a universal file: its AIR64 slice is taken, and reads", hakios_metallib_thin(fat, 512 + size, &thin, &thin_size, &why) == 0 &&
	    thin == fat + 512 && thin_size == size && hakios_metallib_parse(thin, thin_size, &info, f, 4, &why) == 0 && info.count == 2);
	check("a thin file is itself", hakios_metallib_thin(good, size, &thin, &thin_size, &why) == 0 && thin == good && thin_size == size);
	check("a universal file cut short of its slice is refused", hakios_metallib_thin(fat, 512 + size - 1, &thin, &thin_size, &why) != 0);
	fat[8 + 20 + 3] = 0x13;                                 /* no AIR64 slice any more */
	check("a universal file with no AIR64 slice is refused", hakios_metallib_thin(fat, 512 + size, &thin, &thin_size, &why) != 0);
	for (size_t cut = 0; cut < 64; cut++) {
		hakios_metallib_thin(fat, cut, &thin, &thin_size, &why);      /* under the sanitizers: nothing read past CUT */
	}
	printf("metallib_test: %s\n", failures ? "FAILED" : "the made file reads, thin and universal; every cut and every bad offset is refused");
	return failures != 0;
}

static int
list(const char *path)
{
	FILE *file = fopen(path, "rb");
	uint8_t *data;
	long size;
	struct hakios_metallib info;
	struct hakios_metallib_function *f;
	const char *why = NULL;

	if (file == NULL || fseek(file, 0, SEEK_END) != 0 || (size = ftell(file)) < 0 || fseek(file, 0, SEEK_SET) != 0) {
		perror(path);
		return 1;
	}
	data = malloc((size_t)size + 1);
	if (fread(data, 1, (size_t)size, file) != (size_t)size) {
		perror(path);
		return 1;
	}
	fclose(file);
	if (hakios_metallib_parse(data, (size_t)size, &info, NULL, 0, &why) != 0) {
		printf("%s: %s\n", path, why);
		return 1;
	}
	f = calloc(info.count ? info.count : 1, sizeof(*f));
	hakios_metallib_parse(data, (size_t)size, &info, f, info.count, &why);
	printf("%u functions\n", info.count);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < info.count; i++) {
		char air[32];
		const uint8_t *bc;
		uint64_t length;

		snprintf(air, sizeof(air), "%u.%u.%u.%u", f[i].air[0], f[i].air[1], f[i].air[2], f[i].air[3]);
		if (hakios_metallib_bitcode(data, (size_t)size, &f[i], &bc, &length) != 0) {
			printf("%.*s: its wrapper points outside its module\n", (int)f[i].name_length, f[i].name);
			return 1;
		}
		printf("  %-52.*s %-13s air %s  module %llu\n", (int)f[i].name_length, f[i].name,
		    f[i].type == HAKIOS_METALLIB_NO_TYPE ? "?" : f[i].type < 7 ? hakios_metallib_type_name(f[i].type) : "type?",
		    air, (unsigned long long)f[i].module_size);
	}
	free(f);
	free(data);
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	if (argc == 3 && strcmp(argv[1], "list") == 0) {
		return list(argv[2]);
	}
	if (argc == 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "cuts") == 0) {
		return cuts();
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "usage: metallib_test list FILE | cuts\n");
	return 2;
}

```

`tools/mk-ath11k.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the driver of the phone's Wi-Fi radio for our kernel: ath11k, Qualcomm's driver for the
# WCN6750 (and its kin) as it is in Linux, unmodified, on a layer that gives it the kernel
# interfaces it expects. Three things meet here, and only the third is in the repository:
#
#   Linux's ath11k        drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath11k of a pinned release of Linux
#                         (BSD-3-Clause-Clear; the one header of ath/ it includes is ISC);
#   FreeBSD's LinuxKPI    the headers with which FreeBSD compiles Linux drivers, with the kernel
#                         headers those are written against (BSD-2-Clause, of a pinned release
#                         of FreeBSD); patched with wifi/lx/patches/*.patch. Its source files
#                         are not used: what they do is done in wifi/lx/src;
#   wifi/lx               ours: the headers LinuxKPI lacks (device tree, platform devices), the
#                         headers of FreeBSD that cannot serve under XNU as they are, and the
#                         functions underneath (locks, sleeping, work, memory, firmware, the
#                         radio's bus) written on the handful of calls that the kernel's
#                         drivers/wifi/hakios.lx.c offers (bsd/sys/hakios.lx.h of the kernel tree).
#
# Not all of the driver is built yet: DRIVER below lists the files that are. What they call in
# the files that are not becomes a function that says its name in the log and answers 0
# (out/stubs.txt lists them), unless wifi/lx/src has one that does more.
#
# Everything is compiled as FreeBSD kernel code for an Apple arm64 kernel and tied into one
# object that shows nothing but its entry points; the kernel links it when it is there
# (xnu-build.sh).
#
#   VERSION   of Linux. 7.0.14: LinuxKPI's 802.11 headers follow the mac80211 of Linux 7.0, and
#             the driver has to be the one they were written for. For the WCN6750 the driver
#             asks the same of firmware and platform as in the 6.6 series.
#   FREEBSD   15.1-RELEASE, the first release whose LinuxKPI is at Linux 7.0.
#
# What comes out, in xnu-deps/build/ath11k:
#   src/ath11k/        the driver's files, untouched       freebsd/sys/   FreeBSD's, patched
#   out/ath11k.o       the object for the kernel           out/stubs.txt  what is not there yet
# Needs on this machine: curl, tar, xz, sha256sum, patch, awk, clang, and the kernel's linker
# (xnu-deps/host/bin/ld64, see xnu-deps/setup.sh). The two archives are 150 and 253 MB and are kept.
#
# usage: tools/mk-ath11k.sh [fetch]        "fetch" stops when the driver's sources are there
set -e
VERSION=7.0.14
SHA256=de9999b784d2293f00d39c62d8f92a08ab8a54bc4e80ffd250a0c09cb07a0f98
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)
B=$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/ath11k
ATH=drivers/net/wireless/ath
mkdir -p "$B"
cd "$B"

if [ "$(cat src/.release 2>/dev/null)" != "$VERSION $SHA256" ]; then
	[ -f linux-$VERSION.tar.xz ] || curl -sL --fail -o linux-$VERSION.tar.xz \
		https://cdn.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/v${VERSION%%.*}.x/linux-$VERSION.tar.xz
	echo "$SHA256  linux-$VERSION.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c --quiet
	rm -rf src unpacked
	mkdir unpacked
	tar xJf linux-$VERSION.tar.xz -C unpacked --strip-components=1 linux-$VERSION/$ATH/ath11k \
		linux-$VERSION/$ATH/spectral_common.h
	# every file must say itself that it may be used so: the licence is checked, not assumed
	for f in unpacked/$ATH/ath11k/*.[ch] unpacked/$ATH/spectral_common.h; do
		case "$(head -6 "$f")" in
		*"SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause-Clear"*) ;;
		*"Permission to use, copy, modify, and/or distribute this software"*) ;;      # (ISC, spelt out)
		*) echo "mk-ath11k.sh: $f does not carry the licence expected" >&2; exit 1 ;;
		esac
	done
	mkdir src
	mv unpacked/$ATH/ath11k src/ath11k
	mv unpacked/$ATH/spectral_common.h src/
	rm -rf unpacked
	echo "$VERSION $SHA256" > src/.release
fi
[ "$1" = fetch ] && { echo "mk-ath11k.sh: ath11k of Linux $VERSION: $B/src/ath11k"; exit 0; }
W=$ROOT/wifi/lx

# --- FreeBSD's LinuxKPI and the kernel headers under it, with our patches on top. When the patches
# change, the tree is taken from the archive again (as tools/mk-mesa.sh does with Mesa's).
FREEBSD=15.1
FREEBSD_SHA256=cf5762da53fd52e1eaf0f9ceee9bf58cbe314c821031d0d9ffa76823185a89e1
FSYS="compat/linuxkpi sys arm64/include net net80211 netinet netinet6 vm kern tools libkern ddb
	security fs/pseudofs crypto opencrypto geom bsm isa cam rpc xdr x86/include ofed/include
	dev/pci dev/ofw dev/fdt dev/acpica dev/usb dev/iicbus dev/backlight
	contrib/ck/include contrib/dev/acpica/include contrib/libnv"
PATCHES=$(cat "$W"/patches/*.patch 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
if [ "$(cat freebsd/.release 2>/dev/null)" != "$FREEBSD $FREEBSD_SHA256 $PATCHES" ]; then
	[ -f freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz ] || curl -sL --fail -o freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz \
		https://download.freebsd.org/releases/amd64/$FREEBSD-RELEASE/src.txz
	echo "$FREEBSD_SHA256  freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz" | sha256sum -c --quiet
	rm -rf freebsd gen obj
	mkdir freebsd
	tar xJf freebsd-$FREEBSD-src.txz -C freebsd --strip-components=2 usr/src/COPYRIGHT \
		$(for d in $FSYS; do echo usr/src/sys/$d; done)
	for p in "$W"/patches/*.patch; do
		[ -f "$p" ] && patch -s --no-backup-if-mismatch -d freebsd -p1 < "$p"
	done
	echo "$FREEBSD $FREEBSD_SHA256 $PATCHES" > freebsd/.release
fi
S=$B/freebsd/sys

# --- what FreeBSD's build would have generated: the interfaces of its device framework, and the
# option headers, which here say only that there is an Internet
if [ ! -d gen ]; then
	mkdir gen
	(
		cd gen
		ln -s $S/arm64/include machine
		for m in kern/device_if.m kern/bus_if.m dev/pci/pci_if.m dev/pci/pci_iov_if.m dev/pci/pcib_if.m \
			dev/iicbus/iicbus_if.m dev/iicbus/iicbb_if.m dev/backlight/backlight_if.m dev/usb/usb_if.m \
			dev/ofw/ofw_bus_if.m; do
			awk -f $S/tools/makeobjops.awk $S/$m -h
		done
		for o in h p q; do awk -f $S/tools/vnode_if.awk $S/kern/vnode_if.src -$o; done
		for o in $(grep -rhoE "opt_[a-z0-9_]+\.h" $S | sort -u) lkpi_iic_if.h; do : > $o; done
		printf '#define INET 1\n#define INET6 1\n' > opt_inet.h
		printf '#define INET6 1\n' > opt_inet6.h
		printf '#define SMP 1\n' > opt_global.h
	)
fi

# --- compile: the driver's files that are built so far, and ours
DRIVER="core hal qmi ce hw fw htc wmi mac reg peer dp dp_rx dp_tx hal_rx hal_tx dbring p2p"
CC="clang -target arm64-apple-ios16.5"
LD=$ROOT/xnu-deps/host/bin/ld64
CFLAGS="-mkernel -mgeneral-regs-only -fno-builtin -fno-common -ffreestanding -fno-strict-aliasing
	-funsigned-char -nostdinc -std=gnu17 -O2 -g -w
	-D__FreeBSD__=15 -D_KERNEL -DKLD_MODULE -DHAVE_KERNEL_OPTION_HEADERS -include opt_global.h
	-I$W/include -Igen -I$S -I$S/contrib/ck/include
	-I$S/compat/linuxkpi/common/include -I$S/compat/linuxkpi/dummy/include
	-include $S/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/kconfig.h -DLINUXKPI_VERSION=70000"
DFLAGS="-Isrc/ath11k -Isrc -include $W/include/lx_prelude.h -DCONFIG_ATH11K_AHB -DCONFIG_ATH11K_DEBUG
	-DKBUILD_MODNAME=\"ath11k\""
# two headers are the kernel's: what it offers this object (wifi/lx/include/lx_os.h), and its QMI
# helpers (wifi/lx/include/linux/soc/qcom/qmi.h)
source "$ROOT/xnu-env.sh"
for h in lx qmi; do
	[ -f "$XNU_SRC/bsd/sys/hakios.$h.h" ] || { echo "mk-ath11k.sh: the kernel tree has no bsd/sys/hakios.$h.h" >&2; exit 1; }
done
DFLAGS="$DFLAGS -DLX_HAKIOS_LX_H=\"$XNU_SRC/bsd/sys/hakios.lx.h\" -DLX_HAKIOS_QMI_H=\"$XNU_SRC/bsd/sys/hakios.qmi.h\""
mkdir -p obj out
rm -f obj/*.err
compile() {		# compile SOURCE OBJECT [FLAGS]: only when the object is older than anything it was made of
	local src=$1 obj=$2
	shift 2
	if [ -f "$obj" ] && [ -f "$obj.d" ] && [ -z "$(find $(sed -e 's/^[^:]*://' -e 's/\\$//' "$obj.d") "$0" -newer "$obj" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]; then
		return
	fi
	$CC $CFLAGS "$@" -MMD -MF "$obj.d" -c "$src" -o "$obj" 2> "$obj.err" || rm -f "$obj"
}
for f in $DRIVER; do compile src/ath11k/$f.c obj/ath11k_$f.o $DFLAGS & done
for f in "$W"/src/*.c; do [ -f "$f" ] && compile "$f" obj/lx_$(basename "$f" .c).o $DFLAGS -I$W/src & done
wait
bad=
for f in obj/*.err; do
	[ -s "$f" ] && [ ! -f "${f%.err}" ] && { echo "--- $(basename "$f" .o.err)"; grep -m6 -A3 "error:" "$f"; bad=1; }
done
[ -z "$bad" ] || exit 1
OBJECTS=$(for f in $DRIVER; do echo obj/ath11k_$f.o; done; for f in "$W"/src/*.c; do echo obj/lx_$(basename "$f" .c).o; done)

# --- tie it all into one object. What it then still wants is one of three things: a call of the
# kernel's (hakios.lx.h; the QMI helpers; the handful of C library functions XNU has under the same
# names with the same meaning), a function of a part of the driver that is not built yet, or a
# mistake. The second kind gets a stub each that says its name and answers 0; anything else
# missing ends the build.
KERNEL="memcmp memcpy memmove memset strcmp strncmp strlen strchr strrchr strlcpy strlcat bzero
	snprintf vsnprintf __stack_chk_fail __stack_chk_guard"
$LD -r -arch arm64 $OBJECTS -o out/all.o 2> out/ld.err || { cat out/ld.err; exit 1; }
llvm-nm -u --format=just-symbols out/all.o | sed 's/^_//' | sort > out/undefined.txt
: > out/stubs.txt
: > out/stubs.s
missing=
for s in $(cat out/undefined.txt); do
	case " $(echo $KERNEL) " in *" $s "*) continue ;; esac
	case $s in
	lx_os_*|qmi_*|hakios_qmi_*|section\$*) continue ;;
	ath11k_*|__ath11k_*) ;;
	*) echo "mk-ath11k.sh: nothing defines $s" >&2; missing=1; continue ;;
	esac
	echo $s >> out/stubs.txt
	printf '\t.globl _%s\n_%s:\n\tadrp x0, 1f@PAGE\n\tadd x0, x0, 1f@PAGEOFF\n\tb _lx_stub\n\t.cstring\n1:\t.asciz "%s"\n\t.text\n\t.p2align 2\n' \
		$s $s $s >> out/stubs.s
done
[ -z "$missing" ] || exit 1
$CC -c out/stubs.s -o out/stubs.o
# four names are shown: where the kernel enters (lx_prepare(), lx_start(), lx_stop() and lx_transmit() of hakios.lx.h)
printf '_lx_prepare\n_lx_start\n_lx_stop\n_lx_transmit\n' > out/exported.txt
$LD -r -arch arm64 -exported_symbols_list out/exported.txt out/all.o out/stubs.o -o out/ath11k.o 2> out/ld.err ||
	{ cat out/ld.err; exit 1; }
rm -f out/all.o
echo "mk-ath11k.sh: out/ath11k.o: $(llvm-size out/ath11k.o | awk 'NR == 2 { print $1 + $2 }') bytes of code and data from" \
	"$(echo $DRIVER | wc -w) of the driver's files; $(wc -l < out/stubs.txt) functions of the others are stubs (out/stubs.txt);" \
	"asks the kernel for $(llvm-nm -u --format=just-symbols out/ath11k.o | grep -vc 'section\$') names"
```
