`tools/new-device-test.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""tools/new-device.py: what it makes and what it refuses.

  the reference phone's own tree   -> "the SAME values", soc.args identical to the reference's
  another SoC's tree               -> says which values differ and which are missing; the README says so too
  not a device tree                -> a clear error, nothing made
  a bad name, an existing directory -> refused (an existing one is written into only with --force)
  --adb, the tree readable by root only (a stand-in adb; not on Windows, where a script is not a program)
                                   -> pulled through su, and the staged copy is removed again
"""
import os
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
from fdtbuild import cells, compat, fdt  # noqa: E402

TOOL = os.path.join(HERE, "new-device.py")
REFERENCE_DTB = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", "redwood", "prebuilt", "device-tree.dtb")
REFERENCE_ARGS = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", "redwood", "soc.args")
failures = []


def run(*args, env=None):
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, TOOL, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)


def check(label, condition, detail=""):
    print("%s %s" % ("ok  " if condition else "FAIL", label))
    if not condition:
        failures.append(label)
        if detail:
            print("     " + detail.strip().replace("\n", "\n     ")[:600])


work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="new-device-test-")
try:
    # 1. the reference phone's own tree
    out = os.path.join(work, "ref")
    r = run("same-soc", "--fdt", REFERENCE_DTB, "--out", out)
    check("the reference tree: exit 0", r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    check("the reference tree: says the SAME values", "the SAME values as the reference" in r.stdout, r.stdout)
    check("the reference tree: soc.args is byte for byte the reference's",
          os.path.exists(os.path.join(out, "soc.args")) and
          open(os.path.join(out, "soc.args"), "rb").read() == open(REFERENCE_ARGS, "rb").read().replace(b"\r\n", b"\n"))
    check("the reference tree: no carriage return in soc.args", b"\r" not in open(os.path.join(out, "soc.args"), "rb").read())
    check("the reference tree: README, pull-soc.sh and soc.args made",
          sorted(os.listdir(out)) == ["README.md", "pull-soc.sh", "soc.args"], str(sorted(os.listdir(out))))
    readme = open(os.path.join(out, "README.md"), encoding="utf-8").read()
    check("the reference tree: README names the board and carries the checklist",
          "Yupik" in readme and "- [ ] **Cellular**" in readme and "the same as the reference" in readme)

    # 2. another SoC: an IPCC at the usual place, the AOSS mailbox elsewhere, nothing else
    other = fdt({"": ({"model": b"Some Phone\0", "compatible": compat("vendor,some-phone", "qcom,sm9999")},
                      {"soc": ({}, {"qcom,ipcc@408000": ({"compatible": compat("qcom,ipcc"), "reg": cells(0x408000, 0x1000)}, {}),
                                    "power-controller@1000000": ({"compatible": compat("qcom,sc7280-aoss-qmp"),
                                                                  "reg": cells(0x1000000, 0x400)}, {})})})})
    other_path = os.path.join(work, "other.dtb")
    open(other_path, "wb").write(other)
    out = os.path.join(work, "other")
    r = run("some-phone", "--fdt", other_path, "--out", out)
    check("another SoC: exit 0", r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    check("another SoC: does not claim to be the reference", "SAME" not in r.stdout and "differs" in r.stdout, r.stdout)
    readme = open(os.path.join(out, "README.md"), encoding="utf-8").read()
    check("another SoC: README says which differs and which are missing",
          "**differs from the reference**" in readme and "**missing**" in readme and "Some Phone" in readme)
    check("another SoC: soc.args holds what was found",
          open(os.path.join(out, "soc.args")).read().split() == ["soc_ipcc=0x408000", "soc_aoss=0x1000000"],
          open(os.path.join(out, "soc.args")).read())

    # 3. refusals
    junk = os.path.join(work, "junk.dtb")
    open(junk, "wb").write(b"not a device tree at all")
    r = run("x", "--fdt", junk, "--out", os.path.join(work, "junk"))
    check("not a device tree: refused with a reason", r.returncode != 0 and "not a flattened device tree" in (r.stdout + r.stderr), r.stdout + r.stderr)
    check("not a device tree: nothing made", not os.path.exists(os.path.join(work, "junk")))
    r = run("Bad Name!", "--fdt", REFERENCE_DTB, "--out", os.path.join(work, "bad"))
    check("a bad name: refused", r.returncode != 0 and "lower case" in (r.stdout + r.stderr), r.stdout + r.stderr)
    r = run("again", "--fdt", REFERENCE_DTB, "--out", os.path.join(work, "ref"))
    check("an existing directory: refused", r.returncode != 0 and "exists" in (r.stdout + r.stderr), r.stdout + r.stderr)
    r = run("again", "--fdt", REFERENCE_DTB, "--out", os.path.join(work, "ref"), "--force")
    check("an existing directory with --force: written", r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr)
    r = run("x", "--fdt", os.path.join(work, "missing.dtb"), "--out", os.path.join(work, "m"))
    check("no such file: refused", r.returncode != 0 and "no such file" in (r.stdout + r.stderr), r.stdout + r.stderr)

    # 4. --adb with the tree readable by root only (a stand-in adb: a shell script, so not on Windows)
    if os.name != "nt":
        fake = os.path.join(work, "bin")
        os.makedirs(fake)
        state = os.path.join(work, "state")
        script = r"""#!/bin/sh
# a phone whose /sys/firmware/fdt only root can read: a plain pull fails; su copies it to a staging file
case "$1" in
pull)
	case "$2" in
	/sys/firmware/fdt) echo "adb: error: failed to stat remote object '/sys/firmware/fdt': Permission denied" >&2; exit 1 ;;
	/data/local/tmp/hakios-fdt) [ -f "$STATE" ] || exit 1; cp "$REF" "$3"; exit 0 ;;
	esac ;;
shell)
	case "$2" in
	*"cat /sys/firmware/fdt >"*) : > "$STATE"; exit 0 ;;
	*"rm -f /data/local/tmp/hakios-fdt"*) rm -f "$STATE"; echo removed >> "$STATE.log"; exit 0 ;;
	esac ;;
esac
exit 1
"""
        adb = os.path.join(fake, "adb")
        open(adb, "w", newline="\n").write(script)
        os.chmod(adb, os.stat(adb).st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)
        env = dict(os.environ, PATH=fake + os.pathsep + os.environ["PATH"], STATE=state, REF=REFERENCE_DTB)
        r = run("from-adb", "--adb", "--out", os.path.join(work, "adb"), env=env)
        check("--adb, root-only tree: pulled through su and recognised", r.returncode == 0 and "the SAME values" in r.stdout, r.stdout + r.stderr)
        check("--adb, root-only tree: README says how it was got",
              "through su" in open(os.path.join(work, "adb", "README.md"), encoding="utf-8").read())
        check("--adb, root-only tree: the staged copy on the phone was removed again",
              os.path.exists(state + ".log") and not os.path.exists(state))
    else:
        print("skip --adb with a stand-in adb (Windows)")
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)

if failures:
    sys.exit("new-device-test: %d FAILED" % len(failures))
print("new-device-test: all passed")

```

`tools/new-device.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Start a port: make devices/NAME/ from a phone's own device tree, and say how far the SoC code carries.

usage: tools/new-device.py NAME [--fdt FILE | --adb] [--out DIR] [--force]

  NAME    the new directory under devices/ (lower case letters, digits and dashes: redwood)
  --fdt   the phone's device tree, a file (adb pull /sys/firmware/fdt; the tree of the phone's own Android)
  --adb   pull it from the phone on adb now (as the shell user, then through su: on some ROMs the file is
          readable by root only)
  --out   where to make the directory (default: devices/NAME beside this tool); tests use it
  --force write into a directory that exists

What it makes, in devices/NAME/:
  soc.args    the soc_* boot-arguments tools/soc-args.py reads out of the tree: the addresses of the modem's,
              the IPA's and the radio's blocks, which the run scripts add to the kernel command line
  README.md   what the tree says the phone is, which arguments were found and which not, which of them
              differ from the reference phone's, and a checklist of what is the phone's own to port, with
              the files whose head says where their numbers came from
  pull-soc.sh pull the tree again and regenerate soc.args

It also compares the result with the reference phone's (devices/redwood): a tree that gives the same
values means the kernel's built-in defaults already fit, and a port is then about the board (display,
touch, UEFI) and not the SoC. Nothing here changes the phone; the only things read from it are its tree.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import importlib.util
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
SOC_ARGS = os.path.join(HERE, "soc-args.py")
REFERENCE = "redwood"
REFERENCE_DTB = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", REFERENCE, "prebuilt", "device-tree.dtb")

# what is the phone's own, and the files whose head says where their numbers came from
CHECKLIST = [
    ("UEFI", "the firmware that starts the loader: devices/%s/uefi/ is a port of Mu-Silicium; the vendor's drivers are "
             "extracted from your own phone (uefi/README.md)" % REFERENCE),
    ("Display, buttons, touch", "drivers/input/hakios.input.c, hakios.buttons.c, hakios.goodix.c (the reference phone's "
                                "controller; another phone has another)"),
    ("Storage", "hakios.ufs.c and hakios.ufshc.c (UFS); a phone with eMMC needs another driver"),
    ("CPU clocks", "hakios.cpufreq.c"),
    ("GPU", "hakios.adreno.c (Adreno 642L here: another generation needs its own firmware and registers)"),
    ("Wi-Fi", "hakios.wifi.c, hakios.lx.c and wifi/lx/ (the WCN6750 radio of the reference phone)"),
    ("Audio and battery", "hakios.adsp.c, hakios.audio.c, hakios.sound.c, hakios.speaker.c, hakios.mic.c, hakios.battery.c"),
    ("Cellular", "hakios.mpss.c, hakios.qmi.c, hakios.nas.c, hakios.ipa.c, hakios.cell.c; soc.args carries the addresses, "
                 "the IPA layout is for IPA 4.11 (docs/cellular.md)"),
    ("Haptics and cameras", "hakios.haptic.c, hakios.camera.c"),
]


def load_soc_args():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("soc_args", SOC_ARGS)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def generate(fdt_path):
    """The lines tools/soc-args.py prints for a tree, or an error message."""
    run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SOC_ARGS, fdt_path], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if run.returncode != 0:
        return None, (run.stderr or run.stdout).strip()
    return [l for l in run.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip()], None


def text_prop(props, name):
    value = props.get(name, b"")
    return [s.decode(errors="replace") for s in value.split(b"\0") if s]


def pull_fdt(dest):
    adb = shutil.which("adb") or shutil.which("adb.exe")
    for candidate in ("C:/platform-tools/adb.exe", "/mnt/c/platform-tools/adb.exe"):
        adb = adb or (candidate if os.path.exists(candidate) else None)
    if not adb:
        sys.exit("new-device: adb not found; put platform-tools on PATH, or pass the tree with --fdt")

    def adb_run(*args):
        return subprocess.run([adb, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)

    if adb_run("pull", "/sys/firmware/fdt", dest).returncode == 0 and os.path.getsize(dest) > 0:
        return "adb pull /sys/firmware/fdt"
    # some ROMs make it readable by root only: copy it under su to a place the shell can read, pull it, remove it
    stage = "/data/local/tmp/hakios-fdt"
    adb_run("shell", "su -c 'cat /sys/firmware/fdt > %s && chmod 644 %s'" % (stage, stage))
    ok = adb_run("pull", stage, dest).returncode == 0 and os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.getsize(dest) > 0
    adb_run("shell", "su -c 'rm -f %s'" % stage)
    if not ok:
        sys.exit("new-device: could not read /sys/firmware/fdt over adb, with or without su")
    return "adb pull through su (the file is readable by root only on this ROM)"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("name")
    source = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    source.add_argument("--fdt")
    source.add_argument("--adb", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*", args.name):
        sys.exit("new-device: NAME is lower case letters, digits and dashes (like redwood), got %r" % args.name)
    out = args.out or os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", args.name)
    if os.path.exists(out) and not args.force:
        sys.exit("new-device: %s exists (--force to write into it)" % out)

    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="new-device-")
    try:
        if args.adb:
            fdt = os.path.join(tmp, "fdt")
            how = pull_fdt(fdt)
        else:
            fdt = args.fdt
            how = "the file %s" % os.path.basename(fdt)
            if not os.path.isfile(fdt):
                sys.exit("new-device: no such file: %s" % fdt)
        lines, error = generate(fdt)
        if lines is None:
            sys.exit("new-device: %s\n  (is this the phone's own device tree? adb pull /sys/firmware/fdt)" % error)

        nodes = load_soc_args().nodes_of(open(fdt, "rb").read())
        root = nodes.get("", {})
        model = (text_prop(root, "model") or ["(the tree has no model)"])[0]
        compatible = text_prop(root, "compatible")
        reference, _ = generate(REFERENCE_DTB) if os.path.exists(REFERENCE_DTB) else (None, None)

        found = dict(l.split("=", 1) for l in lines)
        names = ["soc_ipa_base", "soc_gsi_base", "soc_ipcc", "soc_aoss", "soc_rsc", "soc_apps_smmu", "soc_cmd_db",
                 "soc_mpss_mem", "modem_ipa_fw_at", "soc_smem", "soc_imem", "soc_ipa_stream", "soc_ipa_stream_uc",
                 "soc_pas_mpss", "soc_pas_ipa", "soc_ipa_fw"]
        missing = [n for n in names if n not in found]
        ref = dict(l.split("=", 1) for l in reference) if reference else {}
        differs = [n for n in found if n in ref and ref[n] != found[n]]
        same_as_reference = bool(ref) and not missing and not differs and set(found) == set(ref)

        os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
        open(os.path.join(out, "soc.args"), "w", newline="\n").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        pull = os.path.join(ROOT, "devices", REFERENCE, "pull-soc.sh")
        if os.path.exists(pull):
            shutil.copyfile(pull, os.path.join(out, "pull-soc.sh"))
            os.chmod(os.path.join(out, "pull-soc.sh"), 0o755)

        rows = "\n".join("| `%s` | `%s` | %s |" % (n, found.get(n, "(not found)"),
                         "the same as the reference" if n in found and ref.get(n) == found[n] else
                         ("**differs from the reference** (`%s`)" % ref.get(n) if n in found and n in ref else
                          "**missing**: the tree has no node this was read from; see the table in devices/%s/README.md" % REFERENCE
                          if n not in found else "")) for n in names)
        verdict = (
            "**The tree gives the same %d values as the reference phone (`devices/%s`).** The kernel's built-in defaults "
            "already fit this SoC, so `soc.args` changes nothing here; what is left to port is the board (UEFI, display, "
            "touch, and the rest of the checklist below), not the SoC." % (len(found), REFERENCE)
            if same_as_reference else
            "**This tree differs from the reference phone's** in %d value(s) and lacks %d: %s. Those are this phone's own "
            "addresses; `soc.args` carries them to the kernel and the run scripts add the file to the command line." %
            (len(differs), len(missing), ", ".join("`%s`" % n for n in (differs + missing)) or "none") if ref else
            "No reference tree to compare with (devices/%s/prebuilt/device-tree.dtb is missing)." % REFERENCE)
        checklist = "\n".join("- [ ] **%s**: %s" % (a, b) for a, b in CHECKLIST)
        readme = """# Device: {model} ({name})

Made by `tools/new-device.py` on {date}, from {how}. Edit it as the port goes.

| What | Value |
|---|---|
| Board (the tree's `model`) | {model} |
| Compatible | `{compatible}` |

## The SoC addresses

{verdict}

| Argument | Value | Against the reference |
|---|---|---|
{rows}

`soc.args` is what `tools/soc-args.py` read out of the tree; `pull-soc.sh` makes it again from the phone on
adb. The run scripts add it to the kernel command line. Where each argument comes from in the tree:
`devices/{reference}/README.md`.

## What is this phone's own

The kernel, loader and user space know nothing about a phone: addresses, interrupts, rails and firmware
come from its tree and its Android. What is written for one phone is the list below. The head of each file
says where its numbers came from; that is the map of what to rewrite.

{checklist}

## Configuration

The kernel's settings are layered the way an Android kernel's are: the common kernel, the SoC's, this phone's
(`docs/configs.md`). Two short files make this phone a configuration:

    configs/{name}.config          CONFIG_DEVICE="{name}"   and whatever is true of this phone only
    configs/{name}_defconfig       #include common_defconfig
                                   #include <the SoC's fragment: sc7280.config for the SC7280 family>
                                   #include {name}.config

Then `make {name}_defconfig`. Turn on only what this phone has been shown to do; `tools/hakios-config.py check` says what the
choice needs.

The drivers are part of the configuration too (`docs/drivers-config.md`): every one is built unless a configuration leaves it out,
and the addresses, pins and rails in each are the reference phone's. Leave out in `configs/{name}.config` what has not been
ported to this phone yet (`# CONFIG_HAKIOS_GOODIX is not set`, ...; `configs/qemu_defconfig` leaves out all of them), and put
each one back when it has been made to work here. `tools/hakios-config.py show` lists what is built in.

## Firmware

Pulled from your own phone, never committed: `devices/{reference}/pull-firmware.sh`, or
`pull-firmware-root.sh` where the firmware is readable by root only. Check with `make doctor`.

## Before you open a pull request

`tools/provenance-check.py` must pass: no vendor firmware, no UEFI drivers, no Apple files in the tree.
""".format(model=model, name=args.name, date=datetime.date.today().isoformat(), how=how,
           compatible=" ".join(compatible), verdict=verdict, rows=rows, checklist=checklist, reference=REFERENCE)
        open(os.path.join(out, "README.md"), "w", newline="\n").write(readme)

        print("new-device: %s" % model)
        print("new-device: %d of %d soc_* values read from the tree%s" % (len(found), len(names),
              "" if not missing else "; missing: " + ", ".join(missing)))
        print("new-device: %s" % ("the SAME values as the reference phone (%s): the SoC code already fits" % REFERENCE
              if same_as_reference else "differs from the reference in: %s" % (", ".join(differs + missing) or "nothing")))
        print("new-device: wrote %s" % out)
        for f in sorted(os.listdir(out)):
            print("    " + f)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/new-workspace.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# A second working copy of everything, for working on something else at the same time: its own
# branch of this repository (a git worktree), its own kernel tree and build, its own images and
# its own QEMU instance. What is big is shared with this copy through reflinks and hard links
# (btrfs or xfs), so a workspace costs about 0.5 GB, most of it the kernel's build output.
#
# usage: tools/new-workspace.sh NAME INSTANCE [DIR]
#   NAME      the branch, and the directory ../hakios-NAME unless DIR is given
#   INSTANCE  the QEMU instance number of the copy (1, 2, ...; see qemu/run-darwin.sh)
#
# The kernel tree is copied as it is now, uncommitted work included, and that state is recorded
# (refs/redwood/baseline in the copy's kernel tree): tools/kernel-delta.sh, run in the workspace,
# prints what was changed in the kernel since. Files below sysimage/rootfs, sysimage/cryptex and
# sysimage/cryptex-app are hard links to this copy's: replace them, never edit them in place.
# The phone is not part of a workspace: there is one, and ./xl belongs to the main copy.
set -e
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)
NAME=${1:?usage: new-workspace.sh NAME INSTANCE [DIR]}
INSTANCE=${2:?usage: new-workspace.sh NAME INSTANCE [DIR]}
WS=${3:-$(dirname "$ROOT")/hakios-$NAME}
[ -e "$WS" ] && { echo "new-workspace.sh: $WS already exists"; exit 1; }

git -C "$ROOT" worktree add -q -b "$NAME" "$WS"
cd "$WS"

# the kernel tree, without build output (it is full of absolute paths)
mkdir -p xnu-src
cp -a --reflink=auto "$ROOT/xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2" xnu-src/
K=xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2
rm -rf $K/BUILD
(
	cd $K
	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$PWD/.git/index.baseline
	git add -A . 2>/dev/null
	git update-ref refs/redwood/baseline "$(git commit-tree "$(git write-tree)" -p HEAD -m 'the state the workspace started from')"
	rm -f "$GIT_INDEX_FILE"
)
# what the kernel build needs besides the tree
cp -a --reflink=auto "$ROOT/xnu-deps/." xnu-deps/
# The files of Darwin and the system image made of them. Every one of these is taken only if it is
# there: a main copy that has not built its images yet has no system.apfs nor root.apfs, and
# cryptex-app is unpacked only where somebody has needed it -- under "set -e" a copy of a file that
# is not there used to end the script halfway, leaving a workspace without its QEMU instance number
# and without a kernel. What a missing cryptex-app costs, when there is one to take: the images come
# out with no /System/Cryptexes/App at all, and Safari's daemons and AuthenticationServicesAgent --
# eight jobs -- then look to mkjobs.py like programs nobody has (build.sh at cryptex-app, present()).
for d in rootfs cryptex cryptex-app "20F66__iPhone10,3_6"; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/sysimage/$d" ]; then cp -al "$ROOT/sysimage/$d" sysimage/; fi
done
for f in system.files system.manifest var.skel .done-rootfs .done-cryptex .done-cryptex-app a2s.json; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/sysimage/$f" ]; then cp -a "$ROOT/sysimage/$f" sysimage/; fi
done
for f in rootfs.dmg rootfs.slt cryptex-app.dmg extracted; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/sysimage/$f" ]; then ln -s "$ROOT/sysimage/$f" sysimage/; fi
done
# The firmware the build puts into the images -- the radio's, the audio DSP's, the GPU's. A copy
# without them builds an image with no /fw and says nothing about it: gpu=1 then starts no GPU.
# Links, not copies: there is one set of these on this computer and they are not small.
for d in "$ROOT"/fw-*; do
	if [ -d "$d" ]; then ln -s "$d" ./; fi
done
for f in obj system.apfs root.apfs hello; do
	if [ -e "$ROOT/userland/$f" ]; then cp -a --reflink=auto "$ROOT/userland/$f" userland/; fi
done
[ -f "$ROOT/xnuloader/loader.efi" ] && cp -a "$ROOT/xnuloader/loader.efi" xnuloader/
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu/kernel.syms" ] && cp -a "$ROOT/qemu/kernel.syms" qemu/
echo "$INSTANCE" > qemu/instance
mkdir -p logs

echo "new-workspace.sh: building the kernel in $WS"
./xnu-build.sh -j"$(nproc)" -k > xnu-build.log 2>&1 || true
[ -f $K/BUILD/obj/DEVELOPMENT_ARM64_BCM2837/mach.development.bcm2837 ] ||
	{ echo "new-workspace.sh: the kernel did not build, see $WS/xnu-build.log"; exit 1; }
echo "new-workspace.sh: $WS is ready (branch $NAME, QEMU instance $INSTANCE)"

```

`tools/provenance-check.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every binary file, and every firmware blob hidden in a source file, must say where it came from.

usage: tools/provenance-check.py [--report] [--root DIR]

The rule of this repository is that it holds only what its authors may redistribute: the source of
the project, and files built from that source. Nothing of Apple's closed software (Darwin, its images,
fonts, pictures), nothing of a phone vendor's firmware. A rule like that holds only if a machine
checks it on every push, so this does. It reads the files git tracks and fails when it finds

  - a binary file (an executable, an image, a font, a firmware image, an archive ...) that no entry of
    tools/provenance.allow explains;
  - a source file that is mostly a table of bytes (firmware compiled into a header) with no entry;
  - a file of a kind the project never carries (screenshots, disk images, IPSW or IPA files,
    cryptexes, the dyld shared cache, fonts), with no entry;
  - a file with an entry whose status is `vendor` (proprietary, not cleared for redistribution);
  - a script that would write to the phone's flash (fastboot flash, erase, format, oem unlock, dd to a
    block device): the project boots from RAM and promises not to touch the phone's storage.

tools/provenance.allow has one line per rule:   STATUS  GLOB  reason
  open     redistributable: source-built from this tree, or under an open licence, with the licence named
  pending  known and not settled; the check passes with a warning, and the entry says who must decide
  vendor   proprietary; the check fails until the file is removed from the tree
  flash    a script that is allowed to contain a command that writes to the phone's storage, because a
           person runs it by hand for a one-time job; named here so that it is a decision, not an accident
The first line whose glob matches a path decides. A path no line matches is unexplained.

--report prints the explained files as a Markdown table (docs/provenance.md is made with it).
Exit status: 0 clean, 1 something to fix.
"""
import argparse
import fnmatch
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

# kinds the project never carries; each needs an entry to be allowed at all
NEVER = re.compile(r"\.(png|jpe?g|gif|heic|webp|bmp|tiff?|mov|mp4|m4v|m4a|mp3|aiff?|caf|ttf|ttc|otf|woff2?|"
                   r"ipsw|ipa|dmg|img4|im4p|car|nib|tbd|mobileconfig|strings|zip|tar|tgz|gz|xz|7z)$", re.I)
NEVER_PATH = re.compile(r"cryptex|dyld_shared_cache|\.ipsw|SpringBoard\.app|(^|/)System/Library/", re.I)
# a source file that is mostly 0x.., 0x.., ... lines: firmware compiled into a header
HEXLINE = re.compile(r"^\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]{2},\s*){8,}")
HEX_LINES_LIMIT = 200
# commands that write to a phone's storage; the project's scripts must not contain them
FLASHY = re.compile(r"fastboot\s+(flash|erase|format|flashing|oem\s+unlock|oem\s+lock|set_active)\b|"
                    r"\bdd\s+[^|;&\n]*of=/dev/(block|mmcblk|sd[a-z]|nvme)|\bmke2fs\b.*\b/dev/|"
                    r"\badb\s+(shell\s+)?(su\s+-c\s+)?['\"]?(flash_image|erase_image|blkdiscard)")
# ... and in C: the loader's write to a block device, and the kernel's UFS driver's. Both are limited in code to
# the partitions named in the `flash` lines of tools/provenance.allow, and both are declared there.
FLASHY_C = re.compile(r"\bwrite_blocks\s*\(|\bBLOCK_OP_WRITE\b")
C_WRITERS = re.compile(r"^(xnuloader/[^/]+|drivers/storage/hakios\.ufs[^/]*)\.c$")
SCRIPT_DIRS = ("tools/", "devices/", "qemu/", "sysimage/", "xnuloader/", "userland/build.sh")
SCRIPT_FILES = ("xl", "Makefile", "xnu-build.sh")
# this file, its test and the doctor mention these commands in order to look for them (the test has them as data)
SKIP_SCAN = {"tools/provenance-check.py", "tools/provenance-test.py", "tools/doctor.sh"}


def tracked(root):
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "-z"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return [p.decode() for p in out.split(b"\0") if p]


def load_rules(root):
    rules = []
    path = os.path.join(root, "tools", "provenance.allow")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return rules
    for n, line in enumerate(open(path, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        parts = line.split(None, 2)
        if len(parts) < 3 or parts[0] not in ("open", "pending", "vendor", "flash"):
            sys.exit("provenance.allow:%d: want  open|pending|vendor|flash  GLOB  reason  (got: %s)" % (n, line))
        rules.append((parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], n))
    return rules


def match(rules, path, flash=False):
    """The first rule for `path`: among the `flash` rules when asked for those, among the others if not."""
    for status, glob, reason, _ in rules:
        if (status == "flash") == flash and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(path, glob):
            return status, reason
    return None


def kind_of(head):
    if head[:4] in (b"\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe", b"\xce\xfa\xed\xfe", b"\xca\xfe\xba\xbe"):
        return "Mach-O"
    if head[:2] == b"MZ":
        return "PE/EFI"
    if head[:4] == b"\x7fELF":
        return "ELF"
    if head[:4] == b"\xd0\x0d\xfe\xed":
        return "device tree"
    if head[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n":
        return "PNG"
    if head[:3] == b"\xff\xd8\xff":
        return "JPEG"
    if head[:4] == b"NXSB" or head[32:36] == b"NXSB":
        return "APFS"
    return "binary"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--report", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--root", default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".."))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    root = os.path.abspath(args.root)
    rules = load_rules(root)
    used = set()
    problems, warnings, explained = [], [], []

    files = tracked(root)
    for path in files:
        full = os.path.join(root, path)
        if not os.path.isfile(full) or os.path.islink(full):
            continue
        with open(full, "rb") as f:
            head = f.read(8192)
        binary = b"\0" in head
        why = None
        if binary:
            why = kind_of(head)
        elif NEVER.search(path) or NEVER_PATH.search(path):
            why = "a kind of file the project does not carry"
        elif path.endswith((".h", ".c", ".inc", ".S")):
            with open(full, "r", errors="replace") as f:
                hexlines = sum(1 for line in f if HEXLINE.match(line))
            if hexlines >= HEX_LINES_LIMIT:
                why = "firmware or data compiled into source (%d lines of bytes)" % hexlines
        if why is not None:
            hit = match(rules, path)
            if hit is None:
                problems.append("%s: %s, and no line of tools/provenance.allow explains it" % (path, why))
                continue
            status, reason = hit
            used.add(path)
            explained.append((path, why, status, reason, os.path.getsize(full)))
            if status == "vendor":
                problems.append("%s: %s -- marked vendor (proprietary): remove it from the tree" % (path, why))
            elif status == "pending":
                warnings.append("%s: %s -- pending: %s" % (path, why, reason))
        # scripts, and C code of the loader and the UFS driver, that would write to the phone's storage
        scan_c = bool(C_WRITERS.match(path))
        is_script = (path in SCRIPT_FILES or path.startswith(SCRIPT_DIRS)) and path.endswith((".sh", ".py", "xl", "Makefile"))
        if path not in SKIP_SCAN and (scan_c or is_script):
            try:
                text = open(full, "r", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
                code = line.split("#", 1)[0] if path.endswith((".sh", "xl", "Makefile")) else line
                found = (FLASHY_C if scan_c else FLASHY).search(code)
                if not found:
                    continue
                hit = match(rules, path, flash=True)
                if hit is None:
                    problems.append("%s:%d: writes to the phone's storage (%s): the project boots from RAM; a "
                                    "deliberate exception needs a `flash` line in tools/provenance.allow"
                                    % (path, n, found.group(0).strip()))
                elif path not in used:
                    used.add(path)
                    explained.append((path, "writes to the phone's storage, by a person's hand", "flash", hit[1],
                                      os.path.getsize(full)))
                    warnings.append("%s: declared exception to \"nothing is written to the phone\": %s"
                                    % (path, hit[1]))
                break

    # a declared writer is a statement about a file, so it is listed even if no pattern fired in it today
    for status, glob, reason, _ in rules:
        if status == "flash":
            for p in files:
                if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(p, glob) and p not in used:
                    used.add(p)
                    explained.append((p, "declared writer to the phone's storage", "flash", reason,
                                      os.path.getsize(os.path.join(root, p))))
    # an entry that matches nothing has gone stale: a rule for a file that left the tree is clutter that
    # would explain a file that comes back
    # (a `vendor` line is a tripwire: it stays after the files are gone, so that putting them back fails)
    stale = [(s, g, n) for s, g, _, n in rules if s != "vendor" and not any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(p, g) for p in files)]
    for s, g, n in stale:
        warnings.append("tools/provenance.allow:%d: '%s' matches no tracked file (stale)" % (n, g))

    if args.report:
        print("| File | What | Status | Why it may be here | Bytes |")
        print("|---|---|---|---|---:|")
        for path, why, status, reason, size in sorted(explained):
            print("| `%s` | %s | %s | %s | %d |" % (path, why, status, reason, size))
        return 0

    for w in warnings:
        print("warn: " + w)
    for p in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + p)
    print("provenance: %d tracked files, %d explained binaries or blobs, %d warnings, %d problems"
          % (len(files), len(explained), len(warnings), len(problems)))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/provenance-test.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""tools/provenance-check.py on small repositories of its own: what it lets through and what it stops.

Every kind of violation has a case that must fail and the same case, explained in tools/provenance.allow,
that must pass; a clean tree passes; a `vendor` line is a tripwire that stays quiet while the files are
gone and fails when one comes back; a stale line is reported; a comment that only mentions a flash
command is not a flash command.
"""
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CHECK = os.path.join(HERE, "provenance-check.py")
PNG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + b"x" * 64
MACHO = b"\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe\x07\x00\x00\x01" + b"not really a kernel"
FIRMWARE = ("static const unsigned char fw[] = {\n" + "0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x08,\n" * 250 + "};\n").encode()
failures = []


def repo(files, allow=""):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="provenance-test-")
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", d], check=True)
    files = dict(files)
    files["tools/provenance.allow"] = allow
    for name, data in files.items():
        path = os.path.join(d, name)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
        open(path, "wb").write(data if isinstance(data, bytes) else data.encode())
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", d, "add", "-A"], check=True, capture_output=True)
    return d


def check(label, files, allow, ok, expect=()):
    d = repo(files, allow)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, CHECK, "--root", d], capture_output=True, text=True)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    out = r.stdout + r.stderr
    good = (r.returncode == 0) == ok and all(e in out for e in expect)
    print("%s %s" % ("ok  " if good else "FAIL", label))
    if not good:
        failures.append(label)
        print("     want exit %s and %r; got exit %d:\n     %s" % (0 if ok else 1, list(expect), r.returncode,
                                                              out.strip().replace("\n", "\n     ")[:500]))


SRC = {"src/ok.c": "int main(void) { return 0; }\n"}

check("a clean tree passes", SRC, "", True)

check("a screenshot, unexplained, fails", {**SRC, "docs/home.png": PNG}, "", False, ["docs/home.png"])
check("a screenshot, explained, passes", {**SRC, "docs/home.png": PNG}, "open docs/home.png my own drawing\n", True)

check("an unexplained Mach-O fails", {**SRC, "bin/stray": MACHO}, "", False, ["Mach-O"])
check("a Mach-O built from the tree passes", {**SRC, "bin/stray": MACHO}, "open bin/* built from src/ok.c\n", True)

for kind, data in (("an IPSW", b"PK\x03\x04" + b"\0" * 20), ("a font", b"\0\1\0\0" + b"\0" * 20)):
    name = "x.ipsw" if kind == "an IPSW" else "x.ttf"
    check("%s fails" % kind, {**SRC, name: data}, "", False, [name])

check("a path through a cryptex fails", {**SRC, "sysimage/cryptex/readme.txt": "hi\n"}, "", False, ["cryptex"])

flash_sh = {"tools/flash-it.sh": "#!/bin/sh\nfastboot flash boot x.img\n"}
check("a script that flashes fails", {**SRC, **flash_sh}, "", False, ["writes to the phone"])
check("a script that flashes, declared, passes with a warning", {**SRC, **flash_sh}, "flash tools/flash-it.sh a one-time job\n", True, ["declared exception"])
check("a flash command in a comment is not a flash command", {**SRC, "tools/note.sh": "# never run: fastboot flash boot x.img\necho hi\n"}, "", True)
check("erase and oem unlock are caught too", {**SRC, "tools/a.sh": "fastboot erase userdata\n", "tools/b.sh": "fastboot oem unlock\n"}, "", False, ["tools/a.sh", "tools/b.sh"])

loader = {"xnuloader/loader.c": "void f(void) { bio->write_blocks(bio, 0, 0, 1, b); }\n"}
check("the loader writing blocks, undeclared, fails", {**SRC, **loader}, "", False, ["xnuloader/loader.c"])
check("the loader writing blocks, declared, passes", {**SRC, **loader}, "flash xnuloader/loader.c its log to logdump\n", True, ["xnuloader/loader.c"])
check("a C file elsewhere may use the name", {**SRC, "src/other.c": "int write_blocks(int x);\n"}, "", True)

check("firmware compiled into a header fails", {**SRC, "src/fw.h": FIRMWARE}, "", False, ["src/fw.h"])
check("... explained as pending: passes, with a warning", {**SRC, "src/fw.h": FIRMWARE}, "pending src/fw.h waiting for the vendor\n", True, ["pending"])

vendor_tracked = {**SRC, "vendor/driver.efi": b"MZ\x90\0" + b"\0" * 32}
check("a vendor file tracked fails", vendor_tracked, "vendor vendor/* the vendor's\n", False, ["vendor (proprietary)"])
check("a vendor line with the files gone: quiet, no stale warning", SRC, "vendor vendor/* the vendor's\n", True)
check("an open line that matches nothing is reported as stale", SRC, "open nothing/here/* gone\n", True, ["stale"])

check("a bad status in the allowlist is an error", SRC, "maybe docs/x something\n", False, ["provenance.allow"])
check("the report lists a declared writer", {**SRC, **flash_sh}, "flash tools/flash-it.sh a one-time job\n", True)

if failures:
    sys.exit("provenance-test: %d FAILED" % len(failures))
print("provenance-test: all passed")

```

`tools/provenance.allow`:

```allow
# What may be a binary, or a blob in a source file, in this repository, and why.
# Read by tools/provenance-check.py, which CI runs on every push. Format:  STATUS  GLOB  reason
#   open     redistributable
#   pending  known, not settled: the check passes with a warning
#   vendor   proprietary: the check fails until the file leaves the tree
#   flash    a script allowed to write to the phone's storage, by a person's hand
# The first line that matches a path decides. A file that no line explains fails the check.

# --- built from this repository -----------------------------------------------------------------------
open     prebuilt/hakios-kernel                   the kernel, built from Apple's open xnu-8796.121.2 plus xnu/hakios.patch and xnu/files: APSL-2.0, corresponding source here and at Apple
open     prebuilt/loader.efi                      the boot loader, built from xnuloader/loader.c: MIT
open     prebuilt/userland/*                      our programs and libraries, built from userland/src: MIT
open     devices/redwood/prebuilt/BootShim.bin   built from the shim of Mu-Silicium with our change (uefi/hakios.patch): BSD-2-Clause-Patent

# --- a description of the hardware ------------------------------------------------------------------------
pending  devices/redwood/prebuilt/device-tree.dtb          the phone's device tree, compiled from Linux sources that are GPL-2.0; confirm the headers, or have each user pull it from their own phone as tools/soc-args.py already does
pending  devices/redwood/uefi/files/Resources/DTBs/redwood.dtb   the same device tree, for the UEFI build

# --- the touch controller's firmware, compiled into a driver ---------------------------------------------
pending  drivers/input/hakios.focaltech_fw.h   FocalTech's firmware as a C array, from a blob on the phone: the kernel (hakios.goodix.c) includes it, so it cannot simply be removed; owner to decide between a licence from the vendor and loading the blob from the phone at run time like the rest of the firmware

# --- proprietary: Qualcomm's and Xiaomi's, taken out of the phone's own UEFI; not for a public tree ---------
vendor   devices/redwood/uefi/files/Binaries/redwood/*       UEFI drivers extracted from the vendor's xbl firmware (QcomPkg, MiPkg, RawFiles and the EDK2 modules as the vendor built them)
vendor   devices/redwood/prebuilt/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd           the built UEFI image: carries those drivers

# --- everything that can write to the phone's storage: a short list, each limited in code --------------------
# (the default run writes one thing: the loader's own log into the phone's logdump partition)
flash    xnuloader/loader.c                       the loader writes its own log (a few KB) into the phone's `logdump` partition at the end of a run and, only with ufs_write=1, into the partition `darwin` from BLOCK_WRITE_FIRST on; it REFUSES every other write (BLOCK_OP_WRITE: "not darwin ... never")
flash    drivers/storage/hakios.ufs.c           the kernel's side: no write at all without ufs_write=1, then only /dev/rufs_darwin, whole blocks from UFS_WRITE_FIRST on, and one writer at a time
flash    tools/darwin-write.py                    writes an image into `darwin` from Android (adb, root) after checking the GPT, the partition's identity and the block range, only to /dev/block/by-name/darwin, reading every write back; every attempt is logged
flash    tools/backup-partitions.py               WRITES NOTHING to the phone (only ls, blockdev, dd if= and sha256sum, as root, over adb); it is declared because the restore notes it writes for a person (restore.txt) contain the fastboot lines that would put each partition back, which the scan cannot tell from a command to run
flash    tools/backup-partitions-test.py          the same tool's test, against a stand-in adb: the text it checks for is those notes
flash    tools/userdata-carve.py                 prints the dd commands that cut the `darwin` partition off the end of Android's userdata (a new GPT); a person runs them once, by hand, under Android, and only for the optional persistence; the default run needs no such partition

```

`tools/publish-repos.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Push the repositories tools/split-repos.sh made (and the website's) to GitHub, each as a PRIVATE repository of OWNER (the organization oosexgang by default).
#
#   tools/publish-repos.sh DIR [OWNER]          DIR: where split-repos.sh put them; OWNER: default oosexgang (the organization)
#
# It signs in as nobody: it uses YOUR login. With the GitHub CLI (`gh auth login` once), it makes each repository and pushes it;
# without it, make each one empty and private on github.com first (New repository, the same name, nothing in it), and git asks
# your credential manager when it pushes. Never put a token in this file, in a command line or in a chat.
set -e
DIR=${1:?usage: tools/publish-repos.sh DIR [OWNER]}
OWNER=${2:-oosexgang}
REPOS=${REPOS:-"hakios hakios-sm7325 hakios-uefi hakios-web"}
for r in $REPOS; do
	[ -d "$DIR/$r/.git" ] || { echo "publish-repos: no $DIR/$r (tools/split-repos.sh makes the first four; the website is hakios-web)"; continue; }
	url="https://github.com/$OWNER/$r.git"
	if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 && gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		gh repo view "$OWNER/$r" >/dev/null 2>&1 || gh repo create "$OWNER/$r" --private --description "$(head -1 "$DIR/$r/README.md" | sed 's/^# *//')"
	fi
	git -C "$DIR/$r" remote remove origin 2>/dev/null || true
	git -C "$DIR/$r" remote add origin "$url"
	git -C "$DIR/$r" push -u origin main
	echo "publish-repos: $r -> $url"
done
```

`tools/qmi-test/extract.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Take the message descriptions out of ath11k's qmi.c for the tests of our QMI helpers.

usage: extract.py PATH/TO/ath11k > tables.inc

qmi.c has 36 tables of struct qmi_elem_info, all static, and qmi.h has the C structures
they describe and, for most messages, the length the encoded message can have at most
(QMI_WLANFW_..._MAX_LEN). The tables are copied as they are, and a list is added that names each
message's table, structure and that length, so that the tests can go through all of them.
The output is ath11k's text (BSD-3-Clause-Clear) and is not kept in the repository.
"""
import re
import sys

src = sys.argv[1]
c = open(src + '/qmi.c').read()
h = open(src + '/qmi.h').read()

# every table, in the file's order (a table is used by the ones after it)
found = re.findall(r'static const struct qmi_elem_info \w+\[\] = \{.*?\n\};\n', c, re.S)
tables = '\n'.join(found)
print('/* from ath11k\'s qmi.c, by tools/qmi-test/extract.py: not to be edited, not to be committed */')
print(tables)

structs = set(re.findall(r'^struct (\w+) \{', h, re.M))
defines = set(re.findall(r'^#define (\w+)', h, re.M))
rows = []
for name, body in re.findall(r'static const struct qmi_elem_info (\w+)\[\] = \{(.*?)\n\};', tables, re.S):
    used = re.search(r'offsetof\(struct (\w+),', body)
    struct = used.group(1) if used else name[:-len('_ei')]
    if struct not in structs:
        # the few tables with no element in them: the structure is named a little differently
        guess = [s for s in structs if s.replace('_fw_', '_').replace('wlfw', 'wlanfw') ==
                 name[:-len('_ei')].replace('_fw_', '_').replace('wlfw', 'wlanfw')]
        struct = guess[0] if guess else None
    limit = (struct or '').upper() + '_MAX_LEN'
    rows.append((name, struct, limit if limit in defines else None))

print('static const struct test_message {')
print('\tconst char *name;\n\tconst struct qmi_elem_info *ei;\n\tsize_t size;\n\tint limit;\t/* -1: none given */\n\tbool message;\t/* not a structure inside one */')
print('} ath11k_messages[] = {')
for name, struct, limit in rows:
    size = 'sizeof(struct %s)' % struct if struct else '1'
    print('\t{ "%s", %s, %s, %s, %s },' % (name[:-len('_ei')], name, size, limit or '-1',
                                          'true' if '_msg_' in name else 'false'))
print('};')

```

`tools/qmi-test/run.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build and run the tests of the QMI helpers (drivers/modem/hakios.qmi.c of the kernel tree) on this
# machine, under the address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers.
#
# With ath11k's sources at hand (tools/mk-ath11k.sh fetches them; ATH11K=<directory> to say where
# else they are) its own message tables are tested too; without, only what needs none of them.
# Nothing of ath11k is kept: its tables are taken out of qmi.c into the build directory each time.
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)
K=$ROOT/xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2                 # the kernel tree being worked in, or else the copies that are in git
[ -f "$K/bsd/dev/hakios.qmi.c" ] || K=$ROOT/xnu/files
ATH=${ATH11K:-$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/ath11k/src/ath11k}
B=$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/qmi-test
rm -rf "$B"
mkdir -p "$B/inc/sys"
ln -s "$K/bsd/sys/hakios.qmi.h" "$K/bsd/sys/hakios.qrtr.h" "$B/inc/sys/"
FLAGS="-std=gnu11 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -pthread"
if [ -f "$ATH/qmi.c" ]; then
	"$HERE/extract.py" "$ATH" > "$B/tables.inc"
	${CC:-cc} $FLAGS -I"$B/inc" -I"$B" -I"$HERE/shim" -I"$ATH" -o "$B/test" "$HERE/test_qmi.c" "$K/bsd/dev/hakios.qmi.c"
	echo "qmi-test: with ath11k's tables from $ATH ($(cat "$ATH/../.release" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1))"
else
	echo "qmi-test: no ath11k sources in $ATH: only the tests that need none"
	${CC:-cc} $FLAGS -DNO_ATH11K -I"$B/inc" -o "$B/test" "$HERE/test_qmi.c" "$K/bsd/dev/hakios.qmi.c"
fi
"$B/test"
```
