`tools/recording.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Make a video of a screen recording left by the kernel's display driver (boot-arg rec_secs=N).

usage: recording.py RECORDING OUT.mp4 [--fps N] [--max-hold SECONDS] [--frames FOLDER]

With --max-hold, no picture stays longer than that: the stretches in which nothing changes on the
screen (an emulated machine thinking about starting an application) are cut short, while whatever
moves keeps its real speed.

RECORDING is the piece of memory as the loader hands it over ("xl recording"; under QEMU, the
monitor's pmemsave): a header { "RWREC003", width, height, frames, oldest, began }, then for every
frame the time it was shown (nanoseconds from the first) and width x height pixels of three bytes
(R, G, B). With boot-arg rec_ring=1 the frames are a ring, "oldest" the place of the oldest, and what
is kept begins wherever the run's last frames began; "began" is when the first frame was recorded,
in nanoseconds of the kernel's time. ("RWREC002", a kernel before that, has no "began".)
The frames are not evenly spaced -- one is recorded whenever the screen changes -- so each is
repeated for as long as it stayed on the screen, at 60 pictures a second (--fps: another rate), and
ffmpeg encodes that. 60 because the window server shows at most one frame per 60 Hz beat: at that
rate every frame the screen showed has a picture of its own. The video used to be made at 30, which
threw away every other frame of a smooth 60 and put the rest on a 33 ms grid, so a recording of a
smooth screen played back jerky. The picture is enlarged twice (it was recorded at a third of the panel's resolution).
"""
import os
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

FPS = 60


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    fps = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--fps') + 1]) if '--fps' in sys.argv else FPS
    data = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
    magic, width, height, frames, oldest = struct.unpack_from('<8sIIII', data, 0)
    if magic not in (b'RWREC002', b'RWREC003') or not width or not height:
        sys.exit('recording.py: not a recording')
    began = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, 24)[0] / 1e9 if magic == b'RWREC003' else 0.0
    size = width * height * 3
    times, offsets, at = [], [], 24 if magic == b'RWREC002' else 32
    for _ in range(frames):
        if at + 8 + size > len(data):
            break
        times.append(struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, at)[0] / 1e9)
        offsets.append(at + 8)
        at += 8 + size
    if magic == b'RWREC003' and 0 < oldest < len(times):
        # (rec_ring: the memory went round; the oldest frame is at that place, the newest just before it)
        times = times[oldest:] + times[:oldest]
        offsets = offsets[oldest:] + offsets[:oldest]
    if '--frames' in sys.argv:
        # every frame as a picture of its own (PPM), named by when it was shown in the kernel's time, in
        # milliseconds: what the window server's lines with glframes=1 say ("f N at S.mmm s")
        folder = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--frames') + 1]
        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
        for t, o in zip(times, offsets):
            with open(os.path.join(folder, f'{int((began + t) * 1000):010d}.ppm'), 'wb') as f:
                f.write(b'P6 %d %d 255\n' % (width, height) + data[o:o + size])
        print(f'{folder}: {len(times)} frames, from {began + times[0]:.3f} s to {began + times[-1]:.3f} s of the kernel\'s time')
    first = times[0] if times else 0.0
    if first:
        print(f'recording.py: the frames kept begin at {first:.3f} s of the recording (rec_ring)')
        times = [t - first for t in times]
    if not times:
        sys.exit('recording.py: no frames in the recording')
    real = times[-1]
    if '--max-hold' in sys.argv:
        hold = float(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--max-hold') + 1])
        squeezed = [0.0]
        for a, b in zip(times, times[1:]):
            squeezed.append(squeezed[-1] + min(b - a, hold))
        times = squeezed
    length = times[-1] + 1.0
    scale = f'scale={width * 2}:{height * 2}:flags=lanczos,pad=ceil(iw/2)*2:ceil(ih/2)*2'
    out = sys.argv[2]
    codec = ['-c:v', 'libx264', '-preset', 'slow', '-crf', '20', '-pix_fmt', 'yuv420p', '-movflags', '+faststart']
    ffmpeg = subprocess.Popen(['ffmpeg', '-loglevel', 'error', '-y', '-f', 'rawvideo', '-pix_fmt', 'rgb24',
                               '-s', f'{width}x{height}', '-r', str(fps), '-i', '-', '-vf', scale] + codec + [out],
                              stdin=subprocess.PIPE)
    # Each frame gets a picture of its own: the one nearest to when it was shown or, when a frame shown
    # a little late (the present beat wanders by a few milliseconds) finds that one taken by the frame
    # before, the next. Sampling the screen at the pictures' times instead lost one frame in ten of a
    # steady 60. A frame more than two pictures late is one the screen showed faster than FPS: dropped.
    slot, last, dropped = [], -1, 0
    for t in times:
        want = round(t * fps)
        if max(want, last + 1) - want > 2:
            slot.append(None)
            dropped += 1
            continue
        last = max(want, last + 1)
        slot.append(last)
    current, k = 0, 0
    for n in range(int(length * fps)):
        while k < len(times) and (slot[k] is None or slot[k] <= n):
            if slot[k] is not None:
                current = k
            k += 1
        ffmpeg.stdin.write(data[offsets[current]:offsets[current] + size])
    ffmpeg.stdin.close()
    if ffmpeg.wait() != 0:
        sys.exit('recording.py: ffmpeg failed')
    gaps = sorted(b - a for a, b in zip(times, times[1:]))
    typical = gaps[len(gaps) // 2] if gaps else 0
    print(f'{out}: {len(times)} frames over {real:.1f} s ({len(times) / max(real, 0.001):.1f} a second on average'
          + (f', typically {1 / typical:.0f} a second while something moves' if typical else '') + f'), {width}x{height}'
          + (f'; the video is {times[-1]:.0f} s long' if times[-1] != real else '')
          + (f'; {dropped} frames came faster than {fps} a second and are not in it' if dropped else ''))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/soc-args-test-aoss.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The generator must find the AOSS mailbox however a phone's device tree describes it.

The same SM7325 phone gave soc_aoss from the repository's reference tree and none from the tree the
running phone itself exports (/sys/firmware/fdt): the reference calls the node
qcom,sm8350-aoss-qmp, the phone's Android kernel calls it qcom,qmp-mbox on /soc/qcom,qmp-aop. This test
builds small device trees of its own (no part of a real phone's tree is committed) and checks
tools/soc-args.py on each:

  mainline form                 -> soc_aoss found
  vendor-kernel form            -> soc_aoss found
  both, and a reg-less decoy    -> the one with a reg, and only one line
  neither                       -> no soc_aoss, and no failure
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
SOC_ARGS = os.path.join(HERE, "soc-args.py")


from fdtbuild import cells, compat, fdt  # noqa: E402  (tools/fdtbuild.py)


def soc_with(**nodes):
    return {"": ({}, {"soc": ({}, nodes)})}


def run(tree):
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".dtb", delete=False) as f:
        f.write(fdt(tree))
        path = f.name
    try:
        # an IPCC node is there in every tree, so that the generator has something to print
        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, SOC_ARGS, path], capture_output=True, text=True)
    finally:
        os.unlink(path)


IPCC = ("qcom,ipcc@408000", ({"compatible": compat("qcom,ipcc"), "reg": cells(0x408000, 0x1000)}, {}))
failures = []


def check(label, tree, want):
    got = run(tree)
    lines = [l for l in got.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("soc_aoss=")]
    ok = got.returncode == 0 and lines == want
    print("%s %s" % ("ok  " if ok else "FAIL", label))
    if not ok:
        failures.append(label)
        print("     want %r, got %r (exit %d) %s" % (want, lines, got.returncode, got.stderr.strip()[:120]))


mainline = ("power-controller@c300000", ({"compatible": compat("qcom,sm8350-aoss-qmp"), "reg": cells(0xC300000, 0x400)}, {}))
vendor = ("qcom,qmp-aop@c300000", ({"compatible": compat("qcom,qmp-mbox"), "reg": cells(0xC300000, 0x400)}, {}))
decoy = ("qcom,qmp-aop@dead000", ({"compatible": compat("qcom,qmp-mbox")}, {}))     # no reg: must be ignored
other_soc = ("power-controller@1000000", ({"compatible": compat("qcom,sc7280-aoss-qmp"), "reg": cells(0x1000000, 0x400)}, {}))

check("mainline form", soc_with(**dict([IPCC, mainline])), ["soc_aoss=0xc300000"])
check("vendor-kernel form", soc_with(**dict([IPCC, vendor])), ["soc_aoss=0xc300000"])
check("a reg-less decoy beside the mainline node", soc_with(**dict([IPCC, decoy, mainline])), ["soc_aoss=0xc300000"])
check("a reg-less decoy only", soc_with(**dict([IPCC, decoy])), [])
check("another SoC's compatible (qcom,sc7280-aoss-qmp)", soc_with(**dict([IPCC, other_soc])), ["soc_aoss=0x1000000"])
check("neither: no soc_aoss, no failure", soc_with(**dict([IPCC])), [])

if failures:
    sys.exit("soc-args-test-aoss: %d FAILED" % len(failures))
print("soc-args-test-aoss: all passed")
```

`tools/soc-args.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the modem/IPA SoC addresses of a Qualcomm phone as HakiOS boot-args, from its device tree.

usage: tools/soc-args.py DEVICE-TREE.dtb

The kernel's modem and IPA drivers (drivers/modem/hakios.mpss.c, hakios.ipa.c) carry the first phone's
addresses as defaults and take any that differ from boot-args soc_* (see soc_override there). This
reads a phone's own flattened device tree -- /sys/firmware/fdt on a rooted phone, or the dtb a port
already has -- and prints the soc_* it needs, which devices/<name>/soc.args holds and the run
scripts pass along. Only numbers are read out; no part of the tree is copied.
"""
import struct
import sys


def nodes_of(blob):
    if blob[:4] != b'\xd0\x0d\xfe\xed':
        sys.exit('soc-args.py: not a flattened device tree')
    off_struct, off_strings = struct.unpack('>II', blob[8:16])
    size_strings, = struct.unpack('>I', blob[32:36])
    strings = blob[off_strings:off_strings + size_strings]
    out, path, at = {}, [], off_struct
    while True:
        token, = struct.unpack('>I', blob[at:at + 4])
        at += 4
        if token == 1:                                  # FDT_BEGIN_NODE
            end = blob.index(b'\0', at)
            path.append(blob[at:end].decode())
            at = (end + 4) & ~3
            out['/'.join(path)] = {}
        elif token == 2:                                # FDT_END_NODE
            path.pop()
        elif token == 3:                                # FDT_PROP
            length, name_off = struct.unpack('>II', blob[at:at + 8])
            at += 8
            name = strings[name_off:strings.index(b'\0', name_off)].decode()
            out['/'.join(path)][name] = blob[at:at + length]
            at = (at + length + 3) & ~3
        elif token == 9:                                # FDT_END
            return out
        elif token != 4:                                # 4 = FDT_NOP
            sys.exit(f'soc-args.py: unexpected token {token}')


def find(nodes, compatible):
    for path, props in nodes.items():
        if compatible.encode() in props.get('compatible', b'').split(b'\0'):
            return path, props
    return None, None


def find_named(nodes, leaf):
    """The node whose last path component begins with `leaf` (e.g. apps-smmu@..., several SMMUs share a compatible)."""
    for path, props in nodes.items():
        if path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1].split('@', 1)[0] == leaf:
            return path, props
    return None, None


def u32(value, index=0):
    return struct.unpack_from('>I', value, index * 4)[0]


def aoss_mailbox(nodes):
    """The address of the AOSS QMP mailbox, which one phone's device tree describes in two ways.

    A tree from a mainline-style kernel has a node whose compatible is qcom,<soc>-aoss-qmp (the
    reference tree here: qcom,sm8350-aoss-qmp on /soc/power-controller@c300000). A tree from the
    phone's own Android (vendor) kernel, which is what /sys/firmware/fdt gives on the phone, calls the
    same hardware /soc/qcom,qmp-aop@c300000 with the compatible qcom,qmp-mbox; the reference tree
    even has such a node as well, but without a reg. Both carry the same address. Only a node that
    has a reg counts, and the mainline form is preferred when both are there."""
    for path, props in nodes.items():
        kinds = props.get('compatible', b'').split(b'\0')
        if any(k.startswith(b'qcom,') and k.endswith(b'-aoss-qmp') for k in kinds) and len(props.get('reg', b'')) >= 4:
            return u32(props['reg'], 0)
    for path, props in nodes.items():
        if path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1].split('@', 1)[0] == 'qcom,qmp-aop' and len(props.get('reg', b'')) >= 4:
            return u32(props['reg'], 0)
    return None


def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(newline="\n")        # LF on Windows too: the output becomes a file of boot-args
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    nodes = nodes_of(open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read())
    args = []

    path, ipa = find(nodes, 'qcom,ipa')
    if ipa and 'reg' in ipa and len(ipa['reg']) >= 16:  # reg = ipa-base, size, gsi-base, size (1 address + 1 size cell each)
        ipa_region = u32(ipa['reg'], 0)                 # the IPA region's start; the registers the driver maps are 0x40000 into it
        gsi_base = u32(ipa['reg'], 2)                   # the GSI's base is given directly
        args.append(('soc_ipa_base', ipa_region + 0x40000))
        args.append(('soc_gsi_base', gsi_base))

    def block(compatible, arg, cell=0):                 # these nodes have 1 address + 1 size cell: address at an even index
        _, props = find(nodes, compatible)
        if props and 'reg' in props and len(props['reg']) >= (cell + 1) * 4:
            args.append((arg, u32(props['reg'], cell)))

    block('qcom,ipcc', 'soc_ipcc')                      # cell 0: the address
    aoss = aoss_mailbox(nodes)                          # the AOSS mailbox: see aoss_mailbox() for the two ways it is described
    if aoss is not None:
        args.append(('soc_aoss', aoss))
    block('qcom,rpmh-rsc', 'soc_rsc', cell=4)           # drv-2 (the application processors') is the third addr/size pair (reg-names drv-0/1/2)
    _, smmu = find_named(nodes, 'apps-smmu')            # not by compatible: the GPU's SMMU shares qcom,qsmmu-v500
    if smmu and 'reg' in smmu:
        args.append(('soc_apps_smmu', u32(smmu['reg'], 0)))

    # the memory addresses: the command DB and the modem's region are reserved-memory nodes named by
    # their address; shared memory is the reserved-memory the /soc/qcom,smem node points at; the SoC's
    # internal memory is the msm-imem node rounded down to its 2 MB block (what the IPA's table maps).
    by_phandle = {}
    for path, props in nodes.items():
        if 'phandle' in props:
            by_phandle[u32(props['phandle'])] = (path, props)

    def reserved(leaf, arg):
        _, props = find_named(nodes, leaf)
        if props and 'reg' in props:
            args.append((arg, u32(props['reg'], 1)))    # reserved-memory: 2 address cells, so the low word is cell 1

    reserved('cmd_db', 'soc_cmd_db')
    reserved('mpss', 'soc_mpss_mem')
    reserved('ipa_gsi', 'modem_ipa_fw_at')              # where the IPA's firmware is loaded (the ipa_gsi reservation)
    _, smem = find(nodes, 'qcom,smem')
    if smem and 'memory-region' in smem:
        target = by_phandle.get(u32(smem['memory-region']))
        if target and 'reg' in target[1]:
            args.append(('soc_smem', u32(target[1]['reg'], 1)))
    _, imem = find(nodes, 'qcom,msm-imem')
    if imem and 'reg' in imem:
        args.append(('soc_imem', u32(imem['reg'], 0) & ~0x1fffff))   # the 2 MB block that holds it

    def stream(compatible, arg):
        _, props = find(nodes, compatible)
        if props and 'iommus' in props and len(props['iommus']) >= 8:
            args.append((arg, u32(props['iommus'], 1)))   # iommus = <phandle stream mask>; the stream is the second cell

    stream('qcom,ipa-smmu-ap-cb', 'soc_ipa_stream')
    stream('qcom,ipa-smmu-uc-cb', 'soc_ipa_stream_uc')

    def pas_id(leaf, arg):
        _, props = find_named(nodes, leaf)
        if props and 'qcom,pas-id' in props:
            args.append((arg, u32(props['qcom,pas-id'])))

    pas_id('qcom,mss', 'soc_pas_mpss')
    pas_id('qcom,ipa_fws', 'soc_pas_ipa')

    _, ipa_fws = find_named(nodes, 'qcom,ipa_fws')
    ipa_fw_name = None
    if ipa_fws and 'qcom,firmware-name' in ipa_fws:
        ipa_fw_name = ipa_fws['qcom,firmware-name'].split(b'\0')[0].decode()

    for name, value in args:
        print(f'{name}={value:#x}')
    if ipa_fw_name:
        print(f'soc_ipa_fw={ipa_fw_name}')
    if not args:
        sys.exit('soc-args.py: found none of the expected nodes; is this the phone\'s own device tree?')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# tools/soc-only-changes.sh: the reference's own values are not sent; a port's differences are; CRs do not matter.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
. tools/soc-only-changes.sh
fails=0
check() { # check LABEL WANT GOT
	if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "ok   $1"; else echo "FAIL $1"; echo "     want: [$2]"; echo "     got:  [$3]"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
}
ref=devices/redwood/soc.args
tmp=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

check "the reference phone's own soc.args sends nothing" "" "$(soc_only_changes $ref | tr '\n' ' ')"

# a port: one value differs, one is new, the rest equal the defaults
{ cat $ref | sed 's/^soc_aoss=.*/soc_aoss=0x1000000/'; echo "soc_extra=0x5"; } > "$tmp/port.args"
check "a port sends only its differences" "soc_aoss=0x1000000 soc_extra=0x5 " "$(soc_only_changes "$tmp/port.args" | tr '\n' ' ')"

# the same file with Windows line endings
sed 's/$/\r/' "$tmp/port.args" > "$tmp/port-crlf.args"
got=$(soc_only_changes "$tmp/port-crlf.args" | tr '\n' ' ')
check "CRLF line endings: same result" "soc_aoss=0x1000000 soc_extra=0x5 " "$got"
check "CRLF line endings: no CR in what is sent" "0" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | tr -cd '\r' | wc -c | tr -d ' ')"

# the reference file itself with CRLF still sends nothing
sed 's/$/\r/' $ref > "$tmp/ref-crlf.args"
check "the reference with CRLF sends nothing" "" "$(soc_only_changes "$tmp/ref-crlf.args" | tr '\n' ' ')"

printf '# a comment\n\nsoc_x=0x1\n' > "$tmp/c.args"
check "comments and blank lines are dropped" "soc_x=0x1 " "$(soc_only_changes "$tmp/c.args" | tr '\n' ' ')"
check "a missing file sends nothing, and is not an error" "" "$(soc_only_changes "$tmp/none.args" | tr '\n' ' ')"
check "without a reference file everything is sent" "soc_x=0x1 " "$(SOC_DEFAULTS=$tmp/no-such-ref soc_only_changes "$tmp/c.args" | tr '\n' ' ')"

# what it buys: the command line of a run of the reference phone
all=$(tr -d '\r' < $ref | tr '\n' ' ' | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
echo "info: all 16 soc_* values are $all characters of the kernel's 607; for the reference phone $(soc_only_changes $ref | wc -c | tr -d ' ') are sent"
[ "$fails" -eq 0 ] && echo "soc-only-changes-test: all passed" || { echo "soc-only-changes-test: $fails FAILED"; exit 1; }
```

`tools/soc-only-changes.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# soc_only_changes FILE: the lines of a soc.args that DIFFER from the kernel's built-in defaults.
#
# Sourced by tools/modem-cycle.sh and tools/modem-cycle-win.sh, which add the soc_* arguments of a port to
# the kernel's command line. The kernel carries the reference phone's values as defaults
# (devices/redwood/soc.args holds them): an argument equal to its default changes nothing, and the
# command line has room for 607 characters, of which sixteen soc_* values take about 340. A run with all of
# them lost the end of its command line without a word (the loader now says so). A port that differs from the
# reference in two values sends two.
#
# CRs are dropped (a file checked out on Windows may have them); lines that are blank or comments are dropped.
soc_only_changes() {
	local file=$1 ref=${SOC_DEFAULTS:-devices/redwood/soc.args}
	[ -f "$file" ] || return 0
	if [ -f "$ref" ]; then
		tr -d '\r' < "$file" | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' | grep -vxF -f <(tr -d '\r' < "$ref") || true
	else
		tr -d '\r' < "$file" | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' || true
	fi
}
```

`tools/sound.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Make a WAV file of a sound recording left by the kernel (boot-arg rec_sound=N).

usage: sound.py RECORDING OUT.wav

RECORDING is the piece of memory as the loader hands it over ("xl sound"; under QEMU, the
monitor's pmemsave at the address in the kernel's line "hakios-audio: recording ... at 0x..."):
a header { "RWSND001", rate, channels, blocks }, then for every write to /dev/hakios-audio the
time it was made (nanoseconds since the kernel started), the number of frames and the frames
themselves, 16-bit samples. Darwin writes only while something plays, so the recording holds no
silence: here the blocks are put back where they were in time, with silence in between
(a pause of more than a quarter of a second is a pause; anything shorter is the writer being
early or late, and the blocks are joined).

Says how long and how loud the result is, which is the way to tell sound from nothing without
listening: a file that peaks at -90 dBFS is silence that was "played".
"""
import array
import math
import struct
import sys
import wave

PAUSE = 0.25


def db(level):
    return f'{20 * math.log10(level / 32768):.1f} dBFS' if level > 0 else 'silence'


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    data = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
    magic, rate, channels, blocks, _ = struct.unpack_from('<8sIIII', data, 0)
    if magic != b'RWSND001' or not rate or not channels:
        sys.exit('sound.py: not a sound recording')
    frame = 2 * channels
    out = wave.open(sys.argv[2], 'wb')
    out.setnchannels(channels)
    out.setsampwidth(2)
    out.setframerate(rate)
    at, first, end, played, pauses = 24, None, 0, 0, 0       # end: frames written to the file so far
    samples = array.array('h')
    for _ in range(blocks):
        if at + 16 > len(data):
            break
        nanoseconds, frames, _ = struct.unpack_from('<QII', data, at)
        pcm = data[at + 16:at + 16 + frames * frame]
        at += 16 + frames * frame
        if len(pcm) < frames * frame:
            break
        if first is None:
            first = nanoseconds
        position = (nanoseconds - first) * rate // 10**9
        if position > end + PAUSE * rate:
            out.writeframes(bytes((position - end) * frame))
            end = position
            pauses += 1
        out.writeframes(pcm)
        samples.frombytes(pcm)
        end += frames
        played += frames
    out.close()
    if not played:
        sys.exit('sound.py: the recording is empty: nothing was played')
    peak = max(max(samples), -min(samples))
    rms = math.sqrt(sum(s * s for s in samples) / len(samples))
    print(f'sound.py: {sys.argv[2]}: {end / rate:.1f} s, of which {played / rate:.1f} s of sound in {pauses + 1} '
          f'stretch{"es" if pauses else ""}; peak {db(peak)}, RMS {db(rms)}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/sparse-split.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cut a raw image into Android sparse images that each fit one fastboot download, to flash one after the other.

usage: sparse-split.py IMAGE OUTDIR [MAX_BYTES]          (MAX_BYTES: the phone's max-download-size, default 768 MiB)

Each piece holds one stretch of IMAGE as RAW blocks (all-zero blocks as FILL, which costs nothing to send), and
DONT_CARE before and after it, so that every piece describes the whole image and the bootloader writes only its own
stretch: `fastboot flash PART piece-00.simg`, then 01, ... in any order. This is what fastboot does by itself with an
image larger than one download, done here because Google's fastboot for Windows runs out of memory on an 8 GB one.

What is checked: the pieces put together (RAW and FILL where they say, nothing else) are IMAGE again, byte for byte;
the sha256 of IMAGE is printed for the read-back on the phone.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import struct
import sys

BS = 4096
MAGIC, RAW, FILL, DONT_CARE = 0xED26FF3A, 0xCAC1, 0xCAC2, 0xCAC3


def chunk(kind, blocks, data_size):
    return struct.pack('<HHII', kind, 0, blocks, 12 + data_size)


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) not in (3, 4):
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    image, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    limit = int(sys.argv[3], 0) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 768 << 20
    size = os.path.getsize(image)
    if size % BS:
        sys.exit(f'sparse-split.py: {image} is not a whole number of {BS}-byte blocks')
    total = size // BS
    per = (limit - (1 << 20)) // BS            # room for the headers, and a margin under the limit
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    whole = hashlib.sha256()
    check = hashlib.sha256()
    pieces = 0
    with open(image, 'rb') as f:
        for first in range(0, total, per):
            n = min(per, total - first)
            body = []                           # (kind, blocks, payload)
            run = None
            for b in range(n):
                block = f.read(BS)
                whole.update(block)
                kind = FILL if block == bytes(BS) else RAW
                if run and run[0] == kind:
                    run[1] += 1
                    if kind == RAW:
                        run[2].append(block)
                else:
                    run = [kind, 1, [block] if kind == RAW else []]
                    body.append(run)
            chunks = []
            if first:
                chunks.append(chunk(DONT_CARE, first, 0))
            for kind, blocks, data in body:
                if kind == RAW:
                    chunks.append(chunk(RAW, blocks, blocks * BS) + b''.join(data))
                else:
                    chunks.append(chunk(FILL, blocks, 4) + bytes(4))
            if first + n < total:
                chunks.append(chunk(DONT_CARE, total - first - n, 0))
            head = struct.pack('<IHHHHIIII', MAGIC, 1, 0, 28, 12, BS, total, len(chunks), 0)
            path = os.path.join(out, f'piece-{pieces:02d}.simg')
            with open(path, 'wb') as p:
                p.write(head)
                for c in chunks:
                    p.write(c)
            # what the piece writes, read back from the piece itself
            for kind, blocks, data in body:
                if kind == RAW:
                    for block in data:
                        check.update(block)
                else:
                    check.update(bytes(BS) * blocks)
            print(f'{path}: blocks {first}..{first + n - 1}, {os.path.getsize(path)} bytes, {len(chunks)} chunks')
            pieces += 1
    if check.digest() != whole.digest():
        sys.exit('sparse-split.py: the pieces do not put the image back together')
    print(f'{pieces} pieces; the image: {total} blocks, sha256 {whole.hexdigest()}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/ufs-super.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""What is in the phone's "super" partition, and where in it nothing is.

usage: ufs-super.py [LOG]
  LOG  the loader's log of a run with ufs=1 among XL_CMDLINE (default logs/last.log)

Android's system, vendor, product and the rest are logical partitions inside the GPT partition
"super", laid out by liblp's metadata at its start. With ufs=1 the loader (xnuloader/loader.c,
ufs_dump_super) prints that metadata raw: the geometry, the header of the first slot and its tables.
This checks their SHA-256 sums -- right sums mean the bytes are the metadata as Android wrote it --
lists the logical partitions with their extents and groups, and says which ranges of super no
extent covers. Nothing is read from the phone here; it only reads the log.
"""
import hashlib
import re
import struct
import sys

SECTOR = 512


def blob(text, what):
    rows = re.findall(rf'^ufs: super {what} \+([0-9a-f]+): ([0-9a-f]*)$', text, re.M)
    data = bytearray()
    for at, hexa in rows:
        if int(at, 16) != len(data):
            sys.exit(f'ufs-super.py: the {what} lines are not contiguous at +{at}')
        data += bytes.fromhex(hexa)
    return bytes(data)


def checked(data, at, name):
    """the sum at data[at:at+32] over data with that field zeroed"""
    zeroed = data[:at] + bytes(32) + data[at + 32:]
    right = hashlib.sha256(zeroed).digest() == data[at:at + 32]
    print(f'{name} sha256 {"right" if right else "WRONG"}')
    return right


def cstr(b):
    return b.split(b'\0', 1)[0].decode('ascii', 'replace')


def size(n):
    return f'{n / 2**30:.2f} GB' if n >= 2**30 else f'{n / 2**20:.1f} MB'


def slot(number, header, tables):
    print(f'\n=== metadata slot {number} (as slot _{"ab"[number]} sees super) ===')
    _, major, minor, header_size = struct.unpack_from('<IHHI', header)
    tables_size = struct.unpack_from('<I', header, 44)[0]
    ok = checked(header[:header_size], 12, f'header v{major}.{minor}')
    right = hashlib.sha256(tables).digest() == header[48:80]
    print(f'tables sha256 {"right" if right else "WRONG"} ({tables_size} bytes)')
    ok &= right
    desc = [struct.unpack_from('<III', header, 80 + 12 * i) for i in range(4)]
    flags = struct.unpack_from('<I', header, 128)[0] if header_size >= 132 else 0

    def table(i, fmt):
        offset, count, entry = desc[i]
        return [struct.unpack_from(fmt, tables, offset + k * entry) for k in range(count)]

    partitions = table(0, '<36sIIII')
    extents = table(1, '<QIQI')
    groups = table(2, '<36sIQ')
    devices = table(3, '<QIIQ36sI')

    print(f'block devices (header flags {flags:#x}):')
    for first, align, align_off, dev_size, name, dflags in devices:
        print(f'  {cstr(name)}: {size(dev_size)} ({dev_size} bytes), data from sector {first}, '
              f'alignment {align}, flags {dflags:#x}')
    print('groups:')
    used_in = {}
    for _, attrs, first, count, group in partitions:
        used_in[group] = used_in.get(group, 0) + sum(extents[first + k][0] for k in range(count)) * SECTOR
    for i, (name, gflags, maximum) in enumerate(groups):
        room = f', {size(maximum - used_in.get(i, 0))} of it unused' if maximum else ''
        print(f'  {cstr(name) or "(default)"}: at most {size(maximum) if maximum else "unlimited"}, '
              f'holds {size(used_in.get(i, 0))}{room}')

    print('logical partitions:')
    taken = []
    for name, attrs, first, count, group in partitions:
        parts = []
        for k in range(count):
            sectors, kind, target, source = extents[first + k]
            if kind == 0:
                taken.append((target, target + sectors, cstr(name), source))
                parts.append(f'{sectors * SECTOR / 2**20:.0f} MB at sector {target}')
            else:
                parts.append(f'{sectors * SECTOR / 2**20:.0f} MB of zeros')
        total = sum(extents[first + k][0] for k in range(count)) * SECTOR
        print(f'  {cstr(name):<20} {size(total):>9}  group {cstr(groups[group][0]) or group}, '
              f'attributes {attrs:#x}' + (f': {"; ".join(parts)}' if parts else ', empty'))

    print('what lies where in super (sectors of 512):')
    first_data, dev_end = devices[0][0], devices[0][3] // SECTOR
    print(f'  0 .. {first_data}: liblp metadata ({size(first_data * SECTOR)})')
    at, free = first_data, 0
    for start, end, name, source in sorted(t for t in taken if t[3] == 0):
        if start > at:
            print(f'  {at} .. {start}: FREE, {size((start - at) * SECTOR)}')
            free += start - at
        print(f'  {start} .. {end}: {name}')
        at = max(at, end)
    if at < dev_end:
        print(f'  {at} .. {dev_end}: FREE, {size((dev_end - at) * SECTOR)}')
        free += dev_end - at
    print(f'{size(free * SECTOR)} of {size(devices[0][3])} in super is covered by no extent of slot {number}')
    return ok


def main():
    log_path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'logs/last.log'
    text = open(log_path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    for line in re.findall(r'^ufs: super: .*$', text, re.M):
        print(line)
    geometry = blob(text, 'geometry')
    if not geometry:
        sys.exit(f'ufs-super.py: no "ufs: super" dump in {log_path} (was the run made with ufs=1?)')
    gpt = re.search(r'^ufs: part super: lba (\d+)\.\.(\d+), (\d+) KB$', text, re.M)
    if gpt:
        print(f'GPT: super is lba {gpt[1]}..{gpt[2]}, {size(int(gpt[3]) * 1024)}')

    magic, struct_size = struct.unpack_from('<II', geometry)
    max_size, slots, block_size = struct.unpack_from('<III', geometry, 40)
    ok = checked(geometry[:struct_size], 8, 'geometry')
    print(f'  metadata up to {max_size} bytes, {slots} slots, logical block {block_size}')
    for number in range(2):
        header, tables = blob(text, f'header{number}'), blob(text, f'tables{number}')
        if header:
            ok &= slot(number, header, tables)
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
```

`tools/ufs-survey.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check what the loader read from the phone's storage against the ROM's own images.

usage: ufs-survey.py [LOG] [FW_ZIP]
  LOG     the loader's log of a run with ufs=1 among XL_CMDLINE (default logs/last.log)
  FW_ZIP  the ROM's firmware archive (default fw/fw.zip)

With ufs=1 the loader (xnuloader/loader.c, ufs_survey) lists the phone's logical units and GPT
partitions as Qualcomm's own UFS driver in UEFI sees them, and for the partitions there are images
of in the ROM's firmware-update/ it prints an FNV-1a hash of exactly as many bytes as the image
has. This computes the same hash from the images and says, partition by partition, whether the
two agree: where they do, reading through that driver gives the bytes that are on the flash.
With ufs=2 ufs_check=1 the kernel then reads the same partitions through the loader's page
(drivers/storage/hakios.ufs.c) and prints the same hashes: those are shown as kernel:NAME.
Nothing is read from the phone here; it only reads the log.
"""
import re
import sys
import zipfile


def fnv(data, h=0xcbf29ce484222325):
    for b in data:
        h = ((h ^ b) * 0x100000001b3) & 0xffffffffffffffff
    return h


def main():
    log_path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'logs/last.log'
    zip_path = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'fw/fw.zip'
    text = open(log_path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()

    units = re.findall(r'^ufs: unit (\d+): .*$', text, re.M)
    parts = re.findall(r'^ufs: part (\S+): lba (\d+)\.\.(\d+), (\d+) KB$', text, re.M)
    hashes = re.findall(r'^ufs: (\S+): fnv ([0-9a-f]+) over (\d+) bytes, (\d+) ms$', text, re.M)
    # the same partitions read again by the kernel through the loader's page (ufs=2 ufs_check=1)
    checks = re.findall(r'ufs: check (\S+): fnv ([0-9a-f]+) over (\d+) bytes, (\d+) ms', text)
    hashes += [('kernel:' + name, value, size, ms) for name, value, size, ms in checks]
    errors = re.findall(r'^ufs: (\S+): (reading at block .*|.* the partition is smaller)$', text, re.M)
    if not parts:
        sys.exit(f'ufs-survey.py: no "ufs:" lines in {log_path} (was the run made with ufs=1?)')
    print(f'{len(units)} logical units, {len(parts)} partitions in the log')

    images = {}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        for info in z.infolist():
            m = re.match(r'firmware-update/(.+)\.img$', info.filename)
            if m:
                images[m.group(1)] = info.filename
        agreed = differed = 0
        for name, value, size, ms in hashes:
            base = re.sub(r'_[ab]$', '', name.removeprefix('kernel:'))
            if base not in images:
                print(f'  {name}: no image named {base}.img in {zip_path}')
                continue
            data = z.read(images[base])
            if len(data) != int(size):
                print(f'  {name}: the image has {len(data)} bytes, the loader hashed {size}')
                differed += 1
                continue
            mine = fnv(data)
            same = mine == int(value, 16)
            agreed += same
            differed += not same
            rate = int(size) / max(int(ms), 1) / 1000
            print(f'  {name:<21} {"same" if same else "DIFFERENT":<9} {int(size):>11} bytes '
                  f'in {ms:>5} ms ({rate:.0f} MB/s)  flash {value}  image {mine:x}')
    for name, what in errors:
        print(f'  {name}: {what}')
    print(f'{agreed} agree, {differed} differ, {len(errors)} not read')
    return 0 if differed == 0 and not errors and agreed > 0 else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/update-prebuilt.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Refresh prebuilt/ from what is built in this tree: the kernel, the loader, our user-space programs
# and the pieces of the phone's UEFI. With them somebody without the cross toolchain can still make the
# images and run the system (QEMU or the phone); see README.md.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.."
# KERNEL=... to take the kernel from a tree built elsewhere (xnu/apply.sh makes one anywhere)
K=${KERNEL:-hakios-kernel}
MU=Mu-Silicium
mkdir -p prebuilt/userland devices/redwood/prebuilt
cp $K prebuilt/hakios-kernel
# The loader in prebuilt/ is built with the PLACEHOLDER identity (xnuloader/mkidentity.sh --placeholder: no Apple data), in a
# temporary copy so that the real xnuloader/identity.h of this tree, made from your own IPSW, is left alone and never copied
# here. It boots the open kernel (make qemu-open); to start Darwin, build the loader yourself (make loader).
if command -v lld-link >/dev/null && command -v clang >/dev/null; then
	T=$(mktemp -d)
	mkdir "$T/xnuloader"
	cp xnuloader/loader.c xnuloader/efi.h xnuloader/build.sh xnuloader/mkidentity.sh xnuloader/mkidentity.py xnuloader/im4p.py "$T/xnuloader/"
	( cd "$T/xnuloader" && PLACEHOLDER=1 ./mkidentity.sh >/dev/null && ./build.sh >/dev/null ) && cp "$T/xnuloader/loader.efi" prebuilt/loader.efi ||
		echo "update-prebuilt.sh: the placeholder loader did not build; prebuilt/loader.efi kept"
	rm -rf "$T"
else
	echo "update-prebuilt.sh: no lld-link or clang here; prebuilt/loader.efi kept"
fi
cp userland/hello prebuilt/userland/
for f in init child stage0 hello_dyn svc_test surf_test rwtouch mg_test cpu_test sound_test libhakios.dylib libhakios.sb.dylib \
	libhakios.media.dylib libhakios.app.dylib libhakios.tweaks.dylib HakiosAudio net_test; do
	cp userland/obj/$f prebuilt/userland/
done
if [ -f $MU/Build/redwoodPkg/RELEASE_CLANGPDB/FV/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd ]; then
	cp $MU/Build/redwoodPkg/RELEASE_CLANGPDB/FV/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd $MU/BootShim/BootShim.bin $MU/Resources/DTBs/redwood.dtb \
		$MU/Resources/ramdisk $MU/Resources/Scripts/mkbootimg.py devices/redwood/prebuilt/
fi
{
	echo "Built $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') from this tree."
	echo
	sha256sum prebuilt/hakios-kernel prebuilt/loader.efi prebuilt/userland/* devices/redwood/prebuilt/* 2>/dev/null
} > prebuilt/SHA256SUMS
ls -la prebuilt prebuilt/userland devices/redwood/prebuilt
```

`tools/userdata-carve.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cut a partition of this port's own off the end of Android's userdata: the new GPT, made and checked here.

usage: userdata-carve.py DIR GIB [NAME]
       userdata-carve.py --wipe DIR GIB [NAME]

--wipe: Android's data is to be erased and userdata made again (fastboot -w), so no f2fs is shrunk and none is read:
userdata ends where NAME begins, NAME being the last GIB of the unit (from a 2 MB boundary). Only gpt-head.bin and
gpt-tail.bin are needed in DIR (tools/backup-partitions.py's gpt-sda-head.bin and gpt-sda-tail.bin). Everything else --
the checks of the old and the new table, two entries changed and nothing more -- is as without it.
  DIR   what was saved from the phone under Android (adb's root shell), all read only:
          gpt-head.bin             the first 8 blocks of LUN 0 (dd if=/dev/block/sda bs=4096 count=8)
          gpt-tail.bin             its last 8 blocks (... skip=BLOCKS-8 count=8)
          userdata-meta-before.bin at least the first block of userdata (its f2fs superblock)
          segment_info-before.txt  /proc/fs/f2fs/sda33/segment_info
          sb-after.bin             (once the f2fs is shrunk) the first block of userdata again
  GIB   how much to take off the end of userdata, in GiB (a whole number of f2fs segments)
  NAME  the new partition's name (default darwin)

Android's userdata on this phone is a plain f2fs (no metadata encryption: its superblock lies on the
flash as it is) that fills its partition, the last of LUN 0. Taking GIB off its end takes two steps
on the phone: first the filesystem is shrunk in place, by Android's own kernel
(tools/android/f2fs-resize, F2FS_IOC_RESIZE_FS), and only then the partition, by writing the
GPT this makes: userdata ends exactly where the shrunk f2fs ends, and a new partition NAME (of the
APFS container type) has the rest from the next 2 MB on. The kernel takes whole sections off the
main area and leaves the filesystem's own slack at its end (the blocks past the last whole segment)
as it was, so the shrunk f2fs is the old size less GIB, not the size it was asked for.

Both steps belong to one session of Android, with no reboot between them: at every boot fs_mgr
runs resize.f2fs on userdata, which grows the filesystem to whatever its partition is -- a shrunk
f2fs in the old partition is grown straight back (seen on this phone). With userdata exactly the
filesystem's size there is nothing for it to do. Nothing else in the table changes -- no other entry, no GUID, no
name, no attribute -- and both copies of the table (the primary one at the start of LUN 0, the
backup at its end) are made, each with its CRC-32s, then read back here and checked the same way a
firmware would.

What this writes, into DIR: gpt-head.new and gpt-tail.new (the same 8 blocks, with the change),
and it prints the f2fs size to shrink to and the dd commands that put the two on the phone. It
refuses unless the old table checks out, userdata is the last partition, and no f2fs segment
past the new end holds a single valid block.
"""
import re
import struct
import sys
import uuid
import zlib

BS = 4096
APFS_CONTAINER = uuid.UUID('7c3457ef-0000-11aa-aa11-00306543ecac')


def crc(b):
    return zlib.crc32(b) & 0xffffffff


def header_of(block):
    if block[:8] != b'EFI PART':
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: no GPT header where one should be')
    size = struct.unpack_from('<I', block, 12)[0]
    h = bytearray(block[:size])
    want = struct.unpack_from('<I', h, 16)[0]
    struct.pack_into('<I', h, 16, 0)
    return {
        'size': size, 'crc_right': crc(bytes(h)) == want,
        'my': struct.unpack_from('<Q', block, 24)[0], 'alternate': struct.unpack_from('<Q', block, 32)[0],
        'first_usable': struct.unpack_from('<Q', block, 40)[0], 'last_usable': struct.unpack_from('<Q', block, 48)[0],
        'entries_lba': struct.unpack_from('<Q', block, 72)[0], 'count': struct.unpack_from('<I', block, 80)[0],
        'entry_size': struct.unpack_from('<I', block, 84)[0], 'entries_crc': struct.unpack_from('<I', block, 88)[0],
    }


def seal(block, entries):
    """block with its header's entries CRC and header CRC made right for these entries"""
    b = bytearray(block)
    h = header_of(b)
    struct.pack_into('<I', b, 88, crc(entries))
    struct.pack_into('<I', b, 16, 0)
    struct.pack_into('<I', b, 16, crc(bytes(b[:h['size']])))
    return bytes(b)


def entries_of(blob, h, base):
    """the table bytes and its parsed entries, from blob that starts at LBA base"""
    at = (h['entries_lba'] - base) * BS
    raw = blob[at:at + h['count'] * h['entry_size']]
    if len(raw) != h['count'] * h['entry_size']:
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: the partition table is not within the saved blocks')
    parsed = []
    for i in range(h['count']):
        e = raw[i * h['entry_size']:(i + 1) * h['entry_size']]
        parsed.append({
            'type': uuid.UUID(bytes_le=e[:16]), 'guid': uuid.UUID(bytes_le=e[16:32]),
            'first': struct.unpack_from('<Q', e, 32)[0], 'last': struct.unpack_from('<Q', e, 40)[0],
            'attrs': struct.unpack_from('<Q', e, 48)[0],
            'name': e[56:128].decode('utf-16le').split('\0', 1)[0],
        })
    return raw, parsed, at


def check(name, head, tail, disk):
    """both copies: header CRCs, table CRCs, where each says the other is; the parsed table"""
    ph = header_of(head[BS:2 * BS])
    bh = header_of(tail[7 * BS:8 * BS])
    praw, pe, _ = entries_of(head, ph, 0)
    braw, be, _ = entries_of(tail, bh, disk - 8)
    ok = (ph['crc_right'] and bh['crc_right'] and crc(praw) == ph['entries_crc'] and crc(braw) == bh['entries_crc']
          and ph['my'] == 1 and ph['alternate'] == disk - 1 and bh['my'] == disk - 1 and bh['alternate'] == 1
          and praw == braw and ph['last_usable'] == bh['last_usable'] and ph['first_usable'] == bh['first_usable'])
    print(f'{name}: primary header crc {"right" if ph["crc_right"] else "WRONG"}, table crc '
          f'{"right" if crc(praw) == ph["entries_crc"] else "WRONG"}; backup header crc '
          f'{"right" if bh["crc_right"] else "WRONG"}, table crc {"right" if crc(braw) == bh["entries_crc"] else "WRONG"}; '
          f'the two tables {"the same" if praw == braw else "DIFFER"} -> {"good" if ok else "BAD"}')
    return ok, ph, bh, pe


def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    wipe = '--wipe' in args
    if wipe:
        args.remove('--wipe')
    if len(args) not in (2, 3):
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    d, gib = args[0], int(args[1])
    name = args[2] if len(args) > 2 else 'darwin'
    head = open(f'{d}/gpt-head.bin', 'rb').read()
    tail = open(f'{d}/gpt-tail.bin', 'rb').read()
    if len(head) != 8 * BS or len(tail) != 8 * BS:
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: gpt-head.bin and gpt-tail.bin are to be 8 blocks each')
    # the backup header says where it is: the last block of the unit
    disk = header_of(tail[7 * BS:8 * BS])['my'] + 1
    ok, ph, bh, entries = check('the table now', head, tail, disk)
    if not ok:
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: the table on the phone does not check out; nothing made')

    used = [i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if e['type'].int != 0]
    ud = [i for i in used if entries[i]['name'] == 'userdata']
    if len(ud) != 1:
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: not exactly one partition named userdata')
    u = ud[0]
    if any(entries[i]['last'] > entries[u]['last'] for i in used) or entries[u]['last'] != ph['last_usable']:
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: userdata is not the last partition, reaching to the end of the unit')
    if any(e['name'] == name for e in entries):
        sys.exit(f'userdata-carve.py: there is a partition named {name} already')
    free = [i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if e['type'].int == 0]
    if not free or free[0] < max(used):
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: no free entry after the used ones')
    slot = free[0]

    if wipe:
        new_first = (ph['last_usable'] + 1 - gib * 2**30 // BS) // 512 * 512
        if new_first <= entries[u]['first'] + 256 * 2**20 // BS:
            sys.exit(f'userdata-carve.py: {gib} GiB leaves userdata less than 256 MB')
        part_end = new_first
        print(f'userdata: lba {entries[u]["first"]}..{entries[u]["last"]} -> {entries[u]["first"]}..{part_end - 1} '
              f'({(part_end - entries[u]["first"]) * BS / 2**30:.2f} GiB), to be made again (fastboot -w): its data goes')
    else:
        part_end, new_first = carve_f2fs(d, gib, entries, u, name)
    new_last = ph['last_usable']
    print(f'{name}: lba {new_first}..{new_last} ({(new_last - new_first + 1) * BS / 2**30:.3f} GiB), '
          f'entry {slot} (sda{slot + 1} under Android), type APFS container')
    make_table(d, head, tail, disk, ph, bh, entries, u, slot, name, new_first, new_last, part_end, wipe)


def carve_f2fs(d, gib, entries, u, name):
    """userdata shrunk to its f2fs: (where userdata ends, where NAME begins)"""
    sb = open(f'{d}/userdata-meta-before.bin', 'rb').read(BS)[1024:2048]

    # the f2fs of userdata: where its main area is, and how its segments are filled
    magic, = struct.unpack_from('<I', sb, 0)
    log_bs, log_bps = struct.unpack_from('<I', sb, 16)[0], struct.unpack_from('<I', sb, 20)[0]
    block_count, = struct.unpack_from('<Q', sb, 36)
    segs_main, = struct.unpack_from('<I', sb, 68)
    main_blkaddr, = struct.unpack_from('<I', sb, 92)
    if magic != 0xf2f52010 or log_bs != 12:
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: userdata does not begin with a plain f2fs of 4 KB blocks')
    per_seg = 1 << log_bps
    part_blocks = entries[u]['last'] - entries[u]['first'] + 1
    if block_count > part_blocks:
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: the f2fs is bigger than its partition')
    cut = gib * 2**30 // BS // per_seg            # segments taken off the end
    new_segs = segs_main - cut
    new_blocks = main_blkaddr + new_segs * per_seg  # what F2FS_IOC_RESIZE_FS is asked for
    fs_blocks = block_count - cut * per_seg         # what the f2fs is then: its slack stays
    try:
        after = open(f'{d}/sb-after.bin', 'rb').read(BS)[1024:2048]
    except FileNotFoundError:
        after = None
    if after is not None:
        got, = struct.unpack_from('<Q', after, 36)
        got_main, = struct.unpack_from('<I', after, 68)
        print(f'f2fs on the phone now: {got} blocks, {got_main} segments in its main area')
        if (got, got_main) != (fs_blocks, new_segs):
            sys.exit(f'userdata-carve.py: expected {fs_blocks} blocks and {new_segs} segments after the shrink')
    part_end = entries[u]['first'] + fs_blocks                                        # userdata: exactly the f2fs
    new_start = (part_end + per_seg - 1) // per_seg * per_seg                          # 2 MB from the unit's start
    valid = {}
    for line in open(f'{d}/segment_info-before.txt'):
        m = re.match(r'^(\d+)\s+(.*)$', line)
        if m:
            for k, e in enumerate(m[2].split()):
                valid[int(m[1]) + k] = int(e.split('|')[1])
    if len(valid) != segs_main:
        sys.exit(f'userdata-carve.py: segment_info has {len(valid)} segments, the superblock {segs_main}')
    in_tail = [s for s in range(new_segs, segs_main) if valid[s]]
    last_used = max(s for s in valid if valid[s])
    print(f'f2fs: {block_count} blocks, main area from block {main_blkaddr}, {segs_main} segments of {per_seg} blocks; '
          f'the last segment holding data is {last_used}')
    if in_tail:
        sys.exit(f'userdata-carve.py: {len(in_tail)} segments past the new end hold data; shrink with less, '
                 f'or let the kernel move it first')

    print(f'userdata: lba {entries[u]["first"]}..{entries[u]["last"]} ({part_blocks * BS / 2**30:.2f} GiB) '
          f'-> {entries[u]["first"]}..{part_end - 1} ({fs_blocks * BS / 2**30:.2f} GiB, the f2fs exactly); '
          f'{new_start - part_end} blocks between it and {name} belong to neither')
    carve_f2fs.new_blocks = new_blocks
    return part_end, new_start


def make_table(d, head, tail, disk, ph, bh, entries, u, slot, name, new_first, new_last, part_end, wipe):
    # the new table: userdata's end, and one new entry; every other byte as it was
    praw, _, pat = entries_of(head, ph, 0)
    table = bytearray(praw)
    es = ph['entry_size']
    struct.pack_into('<Q', table, u * es + 40, part_end - 1)
    e = bytearray(es)
    e[:16] = APFS_CONTAINER.bytes_le
    e[16:32] = uuid.uuid4().bytes_le
    struct.pack_into('<QQQ', e, 32, new_first, new_last, 0)
    e[56:56 + 2 * len(name)] = name.encode('utf-16le')
    table[slot * es:(slot + 1) * es] = e
    table = bytes(table)

    new_head = bytearray(head)
    new_head[pat:pat + len(table)] = table
    new_head[BS:2 * BS] = seal(head[BS:2 * BS], table)
    _, _, bat = entries_of(tail, bh, disk - 8)
    new_tail = bytearray(tail)
    new_tail[bat:bat + len(table)] = table
    new_tail[7 * BS:8 * BS] = seal(tail[7 * BS:8 * BS], table)
    new_head, new_tail = bytes(new_head), bytes(new_tail)

    ok, _, _, new_entries = check('the new table', new_head, new_tail, disk)
    changed_blocks = [i for i in range(8) if head[i * BS:(i + 1) * BS] != new_head[i * BS:(i + 1) * BS]]
    changed_tail = [i for i in range(8) if tail[i * BS:(i + 1) * BS] != new_tail[i * BS:(i + 1) * BS]]
    changed = [i for i in range(len(entries)) if entries[i] != new_entries[i]]
    print(f'blocks that differ: head {changed_blocks} (lba {changed_blocks}), tail {changed_tail} '
          f'(lba {[disk - 8 + i for i in changed_tail]}); entries that differ: {changed}')
    if not ok or changed != sorted({u, slot}):
        sys.exit('userdata-carve.py: the new table is not what it should be; nothing made')
    open(f'{d}/gpt-head.new', 'wb').write(new_head)
    open(f'{d}/gpt-tail.new', 'wb').write(new_tail)
    print(f'\nmade {d}/gpt-head.new and {d}/gpt-tail.new\n')
    print('on the phone, in this order (adb root shell):')
    if wipe:
        print('  1. nothing to shrink: userdata is erased and made again in step 3')
    else:
        print(f'  1. /data/local/tmp/f2fs-resize /data {carve_f2fs.new_blocks}     # the filesystem first')
        print(f'     and, with no reboot in between (the boot would grow it back), save its first block as sb-after.bin')
        print(f'     and run this again: it checks the shrunk size and makes the table for it')
    # each copy: its table before its header, so that a write cut short leaves a header whose table
    # CRC is wrong (and the other copy is used) rather than a right header over a half-written table
    tl, tn = ph['entries_lba'], (ph['count'] * ph['entry_size'] + BS - 1) // BS
    print(f'  2. the table: the primary copy, its table (lba {tl}..{tl + tn - 1}) and then its header (lba 1); '
          f'then the backup')
    print(f'     dd if=gpt-head.new of=/dev/block/sda bs={BS} skip={tl} seek={tl} count={tn} conv=notrunc,fsync')
    print(f'     dd if=gpt-head.new of=/dev/block/sda bs={BS} skip=1 seek=1 count=1 conv=notrunc,fsync')
    print(f'     dd if=gpt-tail.new of=/dev/block/sda bs={BS} skip={changed_tail[0]} seek={disk - 8 + changed_tail[0]} '
          f'count={changed_tail[-1] - changed_tail[0] + 1} conv=notrunc,fsync')
    if wipe:
        print('  3. adb reboot bootloader; fastboot -w   (userdata and metadata made again: Android starts as new)')
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/var-store-read.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read what var_store kept of Darwin's /private/var, from the phone's darwin partition, and write nothing.

usage:
  var-store-read.py show                       both slots' headers: generation, entries, bytes, when
  var-store-read.py list [PREFIX]              the newest good archive's entries (under PREFIX, a path in /private/var)
  var-store-read.py extract PREFIX DEST        the files under PREFIX into DEST (directories and files only)
  var-store-read.py selftest                   an archive made here in var_store's format, read back

The store is userland/src/var_store.c's: two slots of 2 GiB from darwin's byte 8589934592, each a header block
(struct head) and then a stream of entries (struct entry, its path, its extended attributes, its contents, padded
to 8 bytes), whose CRC-32 is in the header. The newest slot whose header and stream both check out is read; one
that does not check out is never half used.

Where it reads from, read only, either way:
  --image FILE   a copy of darwin from byte 8589934592 (dd if=/dev/block/by-name/darwin bs=4096 skip=2097152)
  (default)      the phone in Android, over adb, as root: `su -c dd` of /dev/block/by-name/darwin, the blocks
                 needed and no others. Under Git Bash on Windows as anywhere else (adb exec-out passes bytes as
                 they are).

What it is for: tools/metal-cache-seed.sh takes db/hakios-metal-cache (Metal's compiled shader stages) out of
the last run's store, so that the next image carries them and no boot compiles them again.
"""
import os
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import zlib

BLOCK = 4096
STORE_AT = 8589934592
SLOT_BYTES = 0x80000000
SLOTS = 2
HEAD = struct.Struct("<8sIIQQQQII")           # magic version slot generation bytes entries seconds crc head_crc
ENTRY = struct.Struct("<IIIIIIIIqQ")          # kind mode uid gid flags pathlen nxattr mtime_nsec mtime_sec size
MAGIC = b"RDWVAR\0\0"
ENT_DIR, ENT_FILE, ENT_SYMLINK, ENT_HARDLINK, ENT_DIRTIME = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
DEVICE = "/dev/block/by-name/darwin"


class Source:
    """Bytes of darwin counted from STORE_AT."""

    def __init__(self, image=None):
        self.image = image

    def read(self, offset, length):
        if self.image is not None:
            with open(self.image, "rb") as f:
                f.seek(offset)
                return f.read(length)
        first = offset // BLOCK
        count = (offset + length + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK - first
        skip = STORE_AT // BLOCK + first
        # (read only: if= the partition by name, no of=; the device is darwin's or dd fails)
        cmd = ["adb", "exec-out", "su", "-c", f"dd if={DEVICE} bs={BLOCK} skip={skip} count={count} 2>/dev/null"]
        data = subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, check=True).stdout
        if len(data) != count * BLOCK:
            raise SystemExit(f"var-store-read: adb gave {len(data)} bytes where {count * BLOCK} were asked for "
                             "(is the phone in Android, with root for the shell?)")
        start = offset - first * BLOCK
        return data[start:start + length]


def head_crc(raw):
    zeroed = raw[:HEAD.size - 4] + b"\0\0\0\0"
    return zlib.crc32(zeroed) & 0xffffffff


def read_head(src, slot):
    raw = src.read(slot * SLOT_BYTES, HEAD.size)
    if len(raw) < HEAD.size:
        return None
    magic, version, s, generation, nbytes, entries, seconds, crc, hcrc = HEAD.unpack(raw)
    if magic != MAGIC or version != 1 or s != slot or nbytes > SLOT_BYTES - BLOCK or hcrc != head_crc(raw):
        return None
    return dict(slot=slot, generation=generation, bytes=nbytes, entries=entries, seconds=seconds, crc=crc)


def newest(src):
    best = None
    for slot in range(SLOTS):
        h = read_head(src, slot)
        if h is not None and (best is None or h["generation"] > best["generation"]):
            best = h
    return best


def stream_of(src, h):
    data = src.read(h["slot"] * SLOT_BYTES + BLOCK, h["bytes"])
    if len(data) != h["bytes"] or (zlib.crc32(data) & 0xffffffff) != h["crc"]:
        raise SystemExit(f"var-store-read: slot {h['slot']}: the archive's checksum is not its header's: not read")
    return data


def entries(data):
    at = 0
    while at < len(data):
        if len(data) - at < ENTRY.size:
            raise SystemExit("var-store-read: an entry cut short")
        kind, mode, uid, gid, flags, pathlen, nxattr, nsec, sec, size = ENTRY.unpack_from(data, at)
        at += ENTRY.size
        path = data[at:at + pathlen].decode("utf-8", "replace")
        at += pathlen
        if kind != ENT_DIRTIME:
            for _ in range(nxattr):
                namelen, vlen = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, at)
                at += 8 + namelen + vlen
            body = data[at:at + size] if kind != ENT_DIR else b""
            at += size if kind != ENT_DIR else 0
        else:
            body = b""
        at += (-at) % 8
        if at > len(data):
            raise SystemExit("var-store-read: an entry runs past the archive")
        yield dict(kind=kind, mode=mode, path=path, size=size, mtime=sec, body=body)


def under(path, prefix):
    prefix = prefix.strip("/")
    return prefix == "" or path == prefix or path.startswith(prefix + "/")


def main(argv):
    image = None
    if len(argv) > 2 and argv[1] == "--image":
        image = argv[2]
        argv = argv[:1] + argv[3:]
    if len(argv) < 2:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    cmd = argv[1]
    if cmd == "selftest":
        return selftest()
    src = Source(image)
    if cmd == "show":
        for slot in range(SLOTS):
            h = read_head(src, slot)
            print(f"slot {slot}: " + ("nothing good" if h is None else
                  f"generation {h['generation']}, {h['entries']} entries, {h['bytes']} bytes, written at {h['seconds']}"))
        return 0
    h = newest(src)
    if h is None:
        print("var-store-read: no slot holds a good archive (nothing saved yet: var_store=1 ufs_write=1)")
        return 1
    data = stream_of(src, h)
    if cmd == "list":
        prefix = argv[2] if len(argv) > 2 else ""
        for e in entries(data):
            if e["kind"] != ENT_DIRTIME and under(e["path"], prefix):
                print(f"{e['kind']} {e['mode']:04o} {e['size']:10d} {e['path']}")
        return 0
    if cmd == "extract" and len(argv) == 4:
        prefix, dest = argv[2].strip("/"), argv[3]
        n = 0
        for e in entries(data):
            if not under(e["path"], prefix) or e["kind"] not in (ENT_DIR, ENT_FILE):
                continue
            rel = e["path"][len(prefix):].lstrip("/")
            if ".." in rel.split("/"):
                continue
            out = os.path.join(dest, rel) if rel else dest
            if e["kind"] == ENT_DIR:
                os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
            else:
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out) or ".", exist_ok=True)
                with open(out, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(e["body"])
                n += 1
        print(f"var-store-read: generation {h['generation']}: {n} files of {prefix or '/'} into {dest}")
        return 0
    print(__doc__)
    return 2


def selftest():
    def entry(kind, path, body=b"", mode=0o644, xattrs=()):
        x = b"".join(struct.pack("<II", len(k), len(v)) + k + v for k, v in xattrs)
        e = ENTRY.pack(kind, mode, 0, 0, 0, len(path), len(xattrs), 0, 1700000000, len(body) if kind != ENT_DIR else 0)
        b = e + path.encode() + (x if kind != ENT_DIRTIME else b"") + (body if kind not in (ENT_DIR, ENT_DIRTIME) else b"")
        return b

    stream = b""
    for piece in (entry(ENT_DIR, "", mode=0o755), entry(ENT_DIR, "db", mode=0o755),
                  entry(ENT_DIR, "db/hakios-metal-cache", mode=0o755),
                  entry(ENT_FILE, "db/hakios-metal-cache/0123.stage", b"HMCS" + bytes(range(37))),
                  entry(ENT_FILE, "db/hakios-metal-cache/4567.stage", b"HMCS", xattrs=((b"com.x", b"yz"),)),
                  entry(ENT_FILE, "db/other", b"not this one"),
                  entry(ENT_SYMLINK, "db/hakios-metal-cache/link", b"0123.stage"),
                  entry(ENT_DIRTIME, "db/hakios-metal-cache"), entry(ENT_DIRTIME, "db")):
        stream += piece + b"\0" * ((-len(piece)) % 8)
    def head(slot, generation, data):
        raw = HEAD.pack(MAGIC, 1, slot, generation, len(data), 9, 1700000001, zlib.crc32(data) & 0xffffffff, 0)
        return HEAD.pack(MAGIC, 1, slot, generation, len(data), 9, 1700000001, zlib.crc32(data) & 0xffffffff, head_crc(raw))
    failures = 0
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        img = os.path.join(tmp, "store")
        with open(img, "wb") as f:
            # slot 0 an older generation, slot 1 the newest: the newest is read
            f.write(head(0, 1, b"").ljust(BLOCK, b"\0"))
            f.seek(SLOT_BYTES)
            f.write(head(1, 2, stream).ljust(BLOCK, b"\0") + stream)
        src = Source(img)
        h = newest(src)
        failures += h is None or h["slot"] != 1
        dest = os.path.join(tmp, "out")
        main(["x", "--image", img, "extract", "db/hakios-metal-cache", dest])
        got = sorted(os.listdir(dest))
        failures += got != ["0123.stage", "4567.stage"]
        failures += open(os.path.join(dest, "0123.stage"), "rb").read() != b"HMCS" + bytes(range(37))
        # a torn archive (one byte changed) is refused whole, not half read
        with open(img, "r+b") as f:
            f.seek(SLOT_BYTES + BLOCK + 60)
            f.write(b"\xff")
        try:
            stream_of(src, newest(src))
            failures += 1
        except SystemExit:
            pass
        # a header whose own checksum is wrong is not a slot
        with open(img, "r+b") as f:
            f.seek(SLOT_BYTES + 16)
            f.write(b"\x09")
        failures += read_head(src, 1) is not None
    print("var-store-read selftest: " + ("ok" if failures == 0 else f"{failures} failures"))
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`tools/win-bin/flock`:

```
#!/bin/sh
# flock for Git Bash on Windows, where util-linux's flock does not exist. xl (the loader driver)
# wraps every fastboot call in `flock -w SECS LOCKFILE timeout SECS fastboot ...` so that two xl
# invocations (a run in one terminal, a screenshot in another) take turns on the one USB channel.
# Here one xl runs at a time, so the lock buys nothing: the lock options and the lock file are
# dropped and the command is run as it is. To use it: PATH=$PWD/tools/win-bin:$PATH ./xl ...
# (next to C:\platform-tools for fastboot and adb). Not for Linux or macOS, which have the real one.
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
	case $1 in
	-w|-E|--timeout|--conflict-exit-code) shift 2 ;;	# an option that takes a value
	-*) shift ;;						# -n -s -x -u -o and the rest
	*) break ;;						# the lock file
	esac
done
shift								# the lock file itself
exec "$@"
```

`tools/wpa-test/reference.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# The access point's side of the WPA2 handshake, written against Python's own hashlib and hmac
# and the AES key wrap of the "cryptography" package: an implementation that shares nothing with
# wifi/lx/src/lx_wpa.c. For a number of made-up networks it writes down, as C, the messages an
# access point would send and the answers a correct station gives, byte for byte; test_wpa.c
# has lx_wpa.c answer the same messages and compares. (IEEE 802.11-2020, 12.7.)
import hashlib
import hmac
import random
import struct
import sys

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.keywrap import aes_key_wrap

rnd = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1)


def prf(key, label, data, length):
    out = b''
    for i in range((length + 19) // 20):
        out += hmac.new(key, label + b'\0' + data + bytes([i]), hashlib.sha1).digest()
    return out[:length]


def key_message(version, info, replay, nonce, rsc, data, kck):
    body = struct.pack('>BHH8s32s16s8s8s16sH', 2, info, 16 if info & 0x80 else 0, replay, nonce, bytes(16), rsc, bytes(8),
                       bytes(16), len(data)) + data
    frame = bytearray(struct.pack('>BBH', version, 3, len(body)) + body)
    if kck is not None:
        frame[81:97] = hmac.new(kck, bytes(frame), hashlib.sha1).digest()[:16]
    return bytes(frame)


def c_bytes(name, data):
    return 'static const unsigned char %s[] = { %s };\n' % (name, ', '.join('0x%02x' % b for b in data) or '0')


def case(n):
    passphrase = bytes(rnd.choice(b'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 !#') for _ in
                       range(rnd.randint(8, 63)))
    name = bytes(rnd.randrange(32, 127) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 32)))
    ap, station = bytes([2] + [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(5)]), bytes([2] + [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(5)])
    anonce, snonce = rnd.randbytes(32), rnd.randbytes(32)
    rsn = bytes.fromhex('30140100000fac040100000fac040100000fac020000')      # CCMP, CCMP, PSK, no capabilities
    group, group_index, group2 = rnd.randbytes(16), rnd.randint(1, 3), rnd.randbytes(16)
    version = rnd.choice([1, 2])
    counter = rnd.randrange(1 << 40)
    replay = lambda k: struct.pack('>Q', counter + k)

    pmk = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha1', passphrase, name, 4096, 32)
    ptk = prf(pmk, b'Pairwise key expansion', min(ap, station) + max(ap, station) + min(anonce, snonce) + max(anonce, snonce), 48)
    kck, kek, tk = ptk[:16], ptk[16:32], ptk[32:]

    def wrapped(key, index, before=b''):
        # the group key as a "key data encapsulation", padded to a multiple of eight bytes, wrapped with the KEK
        plain = before + bytes([0xdd, 6 + len(key), 0x00, 0x0f, 0xac, 1, index, 0]) + key
        if len(plain) % 8:
            plain += b'\xdd' + bytes(7 - len(plain) % 8)
        return aes_key_wrap(kek, plain)

    rsc = rnd.randbytes(6) + bytes(2)
    m1 = key_message(version, 0x008a, replay(0), anonce, bytes(8), b'', None)
    m2 = key_message(version, 0x010a, replay(0), snonce, bytes(8), rsn, kck)
    m3 = key_message(version, 0x13ca, replay(1), anonce, rsc, wrapped(group, group_index, rsn), kck)
    m4 = key_message(version, 0x030a, replay(1), bytes(32), bytes(8), b'', kck)
    g1 = key_message(version, 0x1382, replay(5), bytes(32), rsc, wrapped(group2, group_index % 3 + 1), kck)
    g2 = key_message(version, 0x0302, replay(5), bytes(32), bytes(8), b'', kck)
    # the same message 3 from an access point that was given another passphrase
    other = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha1', passphrase + b'x', name, 4096, 32)
    other_ptk = prf(other, b'Pairwise key expansion', min(ap, station) + max(ap, station) + min(anonce, snonce) + max(anonce, snonce), 48)
    m3_wrong = key_message(version, 0x13ca, replay(1), anonce, rsc, aes_key_wrap(other_ptk[16:32], bytes(24)), other_ptk[:16])

    text = ''.join(c_bytes('c%d_%s' % (n, k), v) for k, v in (
        ('passphrase', passphrase), ('name', name), ('ap', ap), ('station', station), ('snonce', snonce), ('rsn', rsn),
        ('pmk', pmk), ('tk', tk), ('group', group), ('group2', group2), ('m1', m1), ('m2', m2), ('m3', m3), ('m4', m4),
        ('g1', g1), ('g2', g2), ('m3_wrong', m3_wrong)))
    entry = '{ %s, %d }' % (', '.join('c%d_%s, sizeof(c%d_%s)' % (n, k, n, k) for k in (
        'passphrase', 'name', 'ap', 'station', 'snonce', 'rsn', 'pmk', 'tk', 'group', 'group2', 'm1', 'm2', 'm3', 'm4', 'g1',
        'g2', 'm3_wrong')), group_index)
    return text, entry


count = 12
cases = [case(n) for n in range(count)]
print(''.join(t for t, _ in cases))
print('static const struct handshake handshakes[] = {\n\t%s\n};' % ',\n\t'.join(e for _, e in cases))

# two things for the pieces on their own, from the same independent implementations
key = bytes(range(32, 48))
print(c_bytes('prf_key', key) + c_bytes('prf_out', prf(key, b'A label', bytes(range(70)), 61)))
print(c_bytes('wrap_kek', key) + c_bytes('wrap_out', aes_key_wrap(key, bytes(range(100, 140)))))

```

`tools/wpa-test/run.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build and run the tests of the WPA2 handshake's arithmetic (wifi/lx/src/lx_wpa.c) on this
# machine, under the address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers. Needs Python 3 with the
# "cryptography" package: the access point the handshakes are held with is reference.py.
# usage: tools/wpa-test/run.sh [SEED]      another seed, other made-up networks
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)
B=$ROOT/xnu-deps/build/wpa-test
rm -rf "$B"
mkdir -p "$B"
"$HERE/reference.py" "${1:-1}" > "$B/cases.inc"
${CC:-cc} -std=gnu11 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all \
	-I"$B" -I"$ROOT/wifi/lx/src" -o "$B/test" "$HERE/test_wpa.c"
"$B/test"
```
