`userland/src/apfs_mmap_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * Read files off the APFS mount and hash them, two ways, so that what the driver hands
 * back can be compared with what tools/apfs/apfs.py reads from the same image on the
 * build machine.
 *
 *   mmap   map the file and read it through the mapping.  This is the only way to make
 *          the driver's vnop_pagein run: the walk inside the kernel (boot-arg apfs_check)
 *          goes through vnop_read, and nothing on this volume is executed, so without
 *          this the paging path is never touched at all.
 *   read   read(2) the file in pieces of a given size.  With a small size this is the
 *          case the compressed-file path is worst at -- every read decompresses the whole
 *          64 KB piece it falls in.
 *
 * The hash is FNV-1a over the whole file, which is what verify.py and the in-kernel walk
 * use, so a line here can be compared with a line from either.
 *
 * usage: apfs_mmap_test [-q] mmap [PATH]
 *        apfs_mmap_test [-q] read [PATH] [CHUNK]
 *        apfs_mmap_test drop [PATH]
 * -q: no line for each file, only the files' count, bytes, line-hash sum and time.
 * drop: each file's pages are put out of the page cache (a shared mapping of it, msync with
 * MS_INVALIDATE), so that the next pass over PATH reads it from the volume again: a cold pass
 * without a reboot.  Nothing is hashed, and the driver's counters are left alone.
 * PATH defaults to /private/var/apfs-check/usr, CHUNK to 4096.  PATH may be anywhere on a
 * mounted volume: the lines name files from that volume's mount point (statfs), which is
 * what makes them the host's lines.
 */

#include <dirent.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <limits.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/mount.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define FNV_INIT  0xcbf29ce484222325ULL
#define FNV_PRIME 0x100000001b3ULL

#define MOUNT "/private/var/apfs-check"
static size_t mount_len = sizeof(MOUNT) - 1;   /* the mount point's length in a path */

static const char *tag;         /* what to print each line under */
static int chunk_size = 4096;
static int use_mmap;
static int quiet;               /* -q: no line a file, only what they add up to */
static int drop_mode;           /* drop: out of the page cache, nothing read */

static unsigned long long total_sum;
static unsigned long long total_bytes;
static long total_files, total_errors;

static unsigned long long
fnv1a(const unsigned char *p, size_t n, unsigned long long h)
{
	size_t i;

	for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		h ^= p[i];
		h *= FNV_PRIME;
	}
	return h;
}

/*
 * The driver's own breakdown of where the time went (kern.apfs_stats): waiting for the
 * device, decompressing, and the rest.  Zeroed before a road is walked and printed after,
 * so the numbers belong to that road alone.
 */
static void
stats_reset(void)
{
	char zero = 0;

	if (sysctlbyname("kern.apfs_stats", NULL, NULL, &zero, 1) != 0) {
		printf("%s cannot zero kern.apfs_stats: %s\n", tag, strerror(errno));
	}
}

static void
stats_print(void)
{
	static char buf[16384];
	size_t n = sizeof(buf);
	char *line, *next;

	if (sysctlbyname("kern.apfs_stats", buf, &n, NULL, 0) != 0) {
		printf("%s cannot read kern.apfs_stats: %s\n", tag, strerror(errno));
		return;
	}
	buf[sizeof(buf) - 1] = '\0';
	for (line = buf; line != NULL && *line != '\0'; line = next) {
		next = strchr(line, '\n');
		if (next != NULL) {
			*next++ = '\0';
		}
		/* -q: the totals only (the per-caller and per-process tables are for vol_ls sysctl) */
		if (quiet && strncmp(line, "pagein ", 7) != 0 && strncmp(line, "read ", 5) != 0 &&
		    strncmp(line, "device ", 7) != 0 && strncmp(line, "data ", 5) != 0 &&
		    strncmp(line, "inflate ", 8) != 0 && strncmp(line, "blocks ", 7) != 0 &&
		    !(strncmp(line, "lock ", 5) == 0 && strstr(line, " takes ") != NULL &&
		    strstr(line, "metadata") != NULL)) {
			continue;
		}
		if (*line != '\0') {
			printf("%s kernel: %s\n", tag, line);
		}
	}
}

static double
now_ms(void)
{
	struct timespec ts;

	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
	return ts.tv_sec * 1000.0 + ts.tv_nsec / 1000000.0;
}

/* The bytes of one file, through a mapping. */
static int
hash_mapped(const char *path, off_t size, unsigned long long *out)
{
	int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
	void *map;

	if (fd < 0) {
		return -1;
	}
	if (size == 0) {
		close(fd);
		*out = FNV_INIT;        /* nothing to map, and nothing to hash */
		return 0;
	}
	map = mmap(NULL, (size_t)size, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0);
	close(fd);
	if (map == MAP_FAILED) {
		return -1;
	}
	/* touching every page is what makes the kernel page the file in */
	*out = fnv1a((const unsigned char *)map, (size_t)size, FNV_INIT);
	munmap(map, (size_t)size);
	return 0;
}

/* The bytes of one file, read in pieces. */
static int
hash_read(const char *path, off_t size, unsigned long long *out)
{
	int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
	unsigned long long h = FNV_INIT;
	unsigned char *buf;
	ssize_t n;

	(void)size;
	if (fd < 0) {
		return -1;
	}
	buf = malloc((size_t)chunk_size);
	if (buf == NULL) {
		close(fd);
		return -1;
	}
	while ((n = read(fd, buf, (size_t)chunk_size)) > 0) {
		h = fnv1a(buf, (size_t)n, h);
	}
	free(buf);
	close(fd);
	if (n < 0) {
		return -1;
	}
	*out = h;
	return 0;
}

/* One file's pages out of the page cache: they are the same ones every mapping of it shares. */
static int
drop_file(const char *path, off_t size)
{
	int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
	void *map;
	int rc;

	if (fd < 0) {
		return -1;
	}
	if (size == 0) {
		close(fd);
		return 0;
	}
	map = mmap(NULL, (size_t)size, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
	close(fd);
	if (map == MAP_FAILED) {
		return -1;
	}
	rc = msync(map, (size_t)size, MS_INVALIDATE);
	munmap(map, (size_t)size);
	return rc;
}

static void
do_file(const char *path, off_t size)
{
	unsigned long long h = 0;
	char line[2048];
	int rc;

	if (drop_mode) {
		if (drop_file(path, size) != 0) {
			printf("%s %s: cannot drop it: %s\n", tag, path + mount_len, strerror(errno));
			total_errors++;
			return;
		}
		total_files++;
		total_bytes += (unsigned long long)size;
		return;
	}
	rc = use_mmap ? hash_mapped(path, size, &h) : hash_read(path, size, &h);

	if (rc != 0) {
		printf("%s %s: cannot read it: %s\n", tag, path + mount_len,
		    strerror(errno));
		total_errors++;
		return;
	}
	snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s\t%lld\t%016llx\n", path + mount_len,
	    (long long)size, h);
	if (!quiet) {
		printf("%s %s", tag, line);
	}
	total_sum += fnv1a((const unsigned char *)line, strlen(line), FNV_INIT);
	total_files++;
	total_bytes += (unsigned long long)size;
}

static void
walk(char *path, size_t len)
{
	DIR *d = opendir(path);
	struct dirent *de;

	if (d == NULL) {
		printf("%s %s: cannot open the directory: %s\n", tag,
		    path + mount_len, strerror(errno));
		total_errors++;
		return;
	}
	while ((de = readdir(d)) != NULL) {
		struct stat st;
		size_t n = strlen(de->d_name);

		if (strcmp(de->d_name, ".") == 0 || strcmp(de->d_name, "..") == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (len + n + 2 > PATH_MAX) {
			total_errors++;
			continue;
		}
		path[len] = '/';
		memcpy(path + len + 1, de->d_name, n + 1);
		/* lstat, not stat: a symbolic link is not followed and not read */
		if (lstat(path, &st) != 0) {
			printf("%s %s: lstat failed: %s\n", tag, path + mount_len,
			    strerror(errno));
			total_errors++;
		} else if (S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {
			walk(path, len + 1 + n);
		} else if (S_ISREG(st.st_mode)) {
			do_file(path, st.st_size);
		}
		path[len] = '\0';
	}
	closedir(d);
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	static char path[PATH_MAX];
	const char *where = MOUNT "/usr";
	const char *mode;
	double t0, t1;
	int tries;

	if (argc > 1 && strcmp(argv[1], "-q") == 0) {
		quiet = 1;
		argv++;
		argc--;
	}
	mode = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "mmap";

	drop_mode = (strcmp(mode, "drop") == 0);
	use_mmap = (strcmp(mode, "read") != 0);
	tag = drop_mode ? "apfs-drop:" : use_mmap ? "apfs-mmap:" : "apfs-read:";
	if (argc > 2) {
		where = argv[2];
	}
	if (argc > 3) {
		chunk_size = atoi(argv[3]);
		if (chunk_size <= 0) {
			chunk_size = 4096;
		}
	}
	/* the kernel mounts the volume as soon as /private/var is there; wait for it */
	for (tries = 0; tries < 120; tries++) {
		struct stat st;

		if (stat(where, &st) == 0) {
			break;
		}
		sleep(1);
	}
	{
		struct statfs sf;

		if (statfs(where, &sf) == 0 && strncmp(where, sf.f_mntonname,
		    strlen(sf.f_mntonname)) == 0) {
			mount_len = strcmp(sf.f_mntonname, "/") == 0 ? 0 : strlen(sf.f_mntonname);
			printf("%s %s is %s on %s\n", tag, sf.f_mntonname, sf.f_mntfromname,
			    sf.f_fstypename);
		}
	}

	if (drop_mode) {
		snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s", where);
		t0 = now_ms();
		walk(path, strlen(path));
		t1 = now_ms();
		printf("%s %s: files %ld  bytes %llu  errors %ld, out of the page cache in %.0f ms\n", tag, where,
		    total_files, total_bytes, total_errors, t1 - t0);
		return total_errors ? 1 : 0;
	}
	printf("%s %s, %s%s\n", tag, where, use_mmap ? "through a mapping" : "with read(2)",
	    use_mmap ? "" : " in pieces");
	if (!use_mmap) {
		printf("%s pieces of %d bytes\n", tag, chunk_size);
	}
	snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s", where);
	stats_reset();
	t0 = now_ms();
	walk(path, strlen(path));
	t1 = now_ms();

	printf("%s files %ld  bytes %llu  errors %ld\n", tag, total_files, total_bytes,
	    total_errors);
	printf("%s line-hash sum %016llx\n", tag, total_sum);
	printf("%s done in %.0f ms (%.1f MB/s)\n", tag, t1 - t0,
	    (t1 > t0) ? (double)total_bytes / 1048576.0 / ((t1 - t0) / 1000.0) : 0.0);
	stats_print();
	return total_errors ? 1 : 0;
}
```

`userland/src/audio_plugin.c`:

```c
/*
 * HakiosAudio.driver: the output device of Darwin on this machine.
 *
 * Audio devices reach the audio server's hardware layer (the "HAL" of CoreAudio, inside
 * mediaserverd) in two ways: kernel drivers through IOAudio2 -- that is how an iPhone's own
 * speaker, codec and microphones arrive, and none of it exists here -- and plug-ins in
 * /System/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL, which is how Bluetooth, AirPlay, CarPlay and USB audio
 * arrive. This is such a plug-in. Its interface is the one macOS documents for user-space
 * audio drivers (AudioServerPlugIn: a CFPlugIn with one COM-style table of functions; the HAL
 * asks for objects and their properties, then runs the I/O); the Darwin SDK has no header for it,
 * so what is needed of it is declared below.
 *
 * Above the HAL sits the virtual audio device (/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL/VirtualAudio.plugin),
 * through which everything in Darwin is routed. It knows an iPhone's own devices by their names
 * (their UIDs) and makes a port of each: "Speaker" becomes the speaker port, the route an iPhone
 * with nothing plugged in plays through, with a volume, the volume display and the place in
 * Control Center that go with it. So this presents four devices under those names:
 *
 *   "Speaker"   a stereo output whose samples are written to /dev/hakios-audio, where the
 *               kernel takes them to whatever can play them (see sys/hakios.audio.h), and a
 *               stereo input that is always silent (on an iPhone: what the amplifiers measure)
 *   "Hawking"   one silent input and nothing else. The virtual audio device will not build the
 *               speaker route without a second virtual device of its own (its type 'vhaw', a
 *               mandatory companion of the default one in the iPhone X's routing tables) whose
 *               only port is this input; without it everything stays on the null port.
 *   "Actuator"  one output of one channel: the iPhone's Taptic Engine, on which Darwin plays its
 *               haptics as waveforms (through the chain 'd22_actuator_general'); its samples go to
 *               the kernel's motor driver, /dev/hakios-haptic (see actuator_write())
 *   "Codec"     one input of one channel: on an iPhone, the audio codec that the built-in
 *               microphones are on, of which the virtual audio device makes the built-in microphone
 *               port; its samples come from the kernel, /dev/hakios-mic (the phone's main
 *               microphone, boot-arg mic=4), which listens only while this input runs (see codec_read())
 *
 * CoreAudio's own null device ("Null_Device", described in the framework's Info.plist, playing
 * into nowhere) stays as it is: it is the only device the virtual audio device takes while it
 * starts, and ours are taken a moment later, when it says it allows all devices.
 *
 * What is played through the speaker port passes the iPhone X's chain of effects for its own
 * speakers first ('d22_speaker_general', from /Library/Audio/Tunings/D22: equalisers,
 * compressors, speaker protection), at the volume Darwin has set.
 *
 * The device has no clock but the system's: it claims to play exactly HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE frames
 * a second of mach_absolute_time(), and the HAL's I/O thread paces itself by that.
 *
 * The speaker's output has a volume control, as the iPhone's own speaker has: what is set on it
 * goes to the kernel (ioctl HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME), which sets the amplifiers' level by it -- on
 * the phone, so far under the loudest it allows. Its scale is 48 dB in a straight line of
 * decibels, 3 dB for each of Darwin's sixteen steps; 0 is silence. What Darwin does with it (the phone,
 * 15 October): the virtual audio device sets it once, to its top (0 dB), when it takes the
 * device, and leaves it there -- its routing tables keep the iPhone X's speaker in software volume
 * mode, so the volume buttons and Control Center scale the samples themselves, and at 0 what is
 * written is silence (on which the kernel keeps the amplifiers off).
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreFoundation/CFPlugInCOM.h>
#include <CoreAudioTypes/CoreAudioTypes.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <sys/ioctl.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "hakios.audio.h"

/* ---- the AudioServerPlugIn interface (macOS: CoreAudio/AudioServerPlugIn.h, AudioHardwareBase.h) ---- */

typedef UInt32 AudioObjectID;
typedef struct {
	UInt32 mSelector, mScope, mElement;
} AudioObjectPropertyAddress;
typedef struct {
	AudioStreamBasicDescription mFormat;
	AudioValueRange mSampleRateRange;
} AudioStreamRangedDescription;
typedef struct {
	UInt32 mClientID;
	pid_t mProcessID;
	Boolean mIsNativeEndian;
	CFStringRef mBundleID;
} AudioServerPlugInClientInfo;
typedef struct {
	UInt64 mIOCycleCounter;
	UInt32 mNominalIOBufferFrameSize;
	AudioTimeStamp mCurrentTime, mInputTime, mOutputTime;
	Float64 mMasterHostTicksPerFrame, mDeviceHostTicksPerFrame;
} AudioServerPlugInIOCycleInfo;

typedef struct AudioServerPlugInHostInterface AudioServerPlugInHostInterface;
typedef const AudioServerPlugInHostInterface *AudioServerPlugInHostRef;
struct AudioServerPlugInHostInterface {
	OSStatus (*PropertiesChanged)(AudioServerPlugInHostRef, AudioObjectID, UInt32, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *);
	OSStatus (*CopyFromStorage)(AudioServerPlugInHostRef, CFStringRef, CFPropertyListRef *);
	OSStatus (*WriteToStorage)(AudioServerPlugInHostRef, CFStringRef, CFPropertyListRef);
	OSStatus (*DeleteFromStorage)(AudioServerPlugInHostRef, CFStringRef);
	OSStatus (*RequestDeviceConfigurationChange)(AudioServerPlugInHostRef, AudioObjectID, UInt64, void *);

typedef struct AudioServerPlugInDriverInterface AudioServerPlugInDriverInterface;
typedef AudioServerPlugInDriverInterface **AudioServerPlugInDriverRef;
struct AudioServerPlugInDriverInterface {
	void *_reserved;
	HRESULT (*QueryInterface)(void *, REFIID, LPVOID *);
	ULONG (*AddRef)(void *);
	ULONG (*Release)(void *);
	OSStatus (*Initialize)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioServerPlugInHostRef);
	OSStatus (*CreateDevice)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, CFDictionaryRef, const AudioServerPlugInClientInfo *, AudioObjectID *);
	OSStatus (*DestroyDevice)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID);
	OSStatus (*AddDeviceClient)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, const AudioServerPlugInClientInfo *);
	OSStatus (*RemoveDeviceClient)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, const AudioServerPlugInClientInfo *);
	OSStatus (*PerformDeviceConfigurationChange)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt64, void *);
	OSStatus (*AbortDeviceConfigurationChange)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt64, void *);
	Boolean (*HasProperty)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, pid_t, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *);
	OSStatus (*IsPropertySettable)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, pid_t, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *, Boolean *);
	OSStatus (*GetPropertyDataSize)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, pid_t, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *, UInt32,
	    const void *, UInt32 *);
	OSStatus (*GetPropertyData)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, pid_t, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *, UInt32,
	    const void *, UInt32, UInt32 *, void *);
	OSStatus (*SetPropertyData)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, pid_t, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *, UInt32,
	    const void *, UInt32, const void *);
	OSStatus (*StartIO)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt32);
	OSStatus (*StopIO)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt32);
	OSStatus (*GetZeroTimeStamp)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt32, Float64 *, UInt64 *, UInt64 *);
	OSStatus (*WillDoIOOperation)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt32, UInt32, Boolean *, Boolean *);
	OSStatus (*BeginIOOperation)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt32, UInt32, UInt32,
	    const AudioServerPlugInIOCycleInfo *);
	OSStatus (*DoIOOperation)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, AudioObjectID, UInt32, UInt32, UInt32,
	    const AudioServerPlugInIOCycleInfo *, void *, void *);
	OSStatus (*EndIOOperation)(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef, AudioObjectID, UInt32, UInt32, UInt32,
	    const AudioServerPlugInIOCycleInfo *);
};

#define kAudioServerPlugInTypeUUID CFUUIDGetConstantUUIDWithBytes(NULL, 0x44, 0x3A, 0xBA, 0xB8, 0xE7, 0xB3, 0x49, 0x1A, \
	    0xB9, 0x85, 0xBE, 0xB9, 0x18, 0x70, 0x30, 0xDB)
#define kAudioServerPlugInDriverInterfaceUUID CFUUIDGetConstantUUIDWithBytes(NULL, 0xEE, 0xA5, 0x77, 0x3D, 0xCC, 0x43, \
	    0x49, 0xF1, 0x8E, 0x00, 0x8F, 0x96, 0xE7, 0xD2, 0x3B, 0x17)

enum {
	kAudioHardwareUnknownPropertyError = 'who?', kAudioHardwareBadPropertySizeError = '!siz',
	kAudioHardwareIllegalOperationError = 'nope', kAudioHardwareBadObjectError = '!obj',
	kAudioHardwareUnsupportedOperationError = 'unop', kAudioDeviceUnsupportedFormatError = '!dat',

	kAudioObjectPropertyScopeGlobal = 'glob', kAudioObjectPropertyScopeInput = 'inpt', kAudioObjectPropertyScopeOutput = 'outp',

	kAudioObjectClassID = 'aobj', kAudioPlugInClassID = 'aplg', kAudioDeviceClassID = 'adev', kAudioStreamClassID = 'astr',

	kAudioObjectPropertyBaseClass = 'bcls', kAudioObjectPropertyClass = 'clas', kAudioObjectPropertyOwner = 'stdv',
	kAudioObjectPropertyName = 'lnam', kAudioObjectPropertyManufacturer = 'lmak', kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects = 'ownd',

	kAudioPlugInPropertyBoxList = 'box#', kAudioPlugInPropertyTranslateUIDToBox = 'uidb',
	kAudioPlugInPropertyDeviceList = 'dev#', kAudioPlugInPropertyTranslateUIDToDevice = 'uidd',
	kAudioPlugInPropertyResourceBundle = 'rsrc',

	kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceUID = 'uid ', kAudioDevicePropertyModelUID = 'muid', kAudioDevicePropertyTransportType = 'tran',
	kAudioDevicePropertyRelatedDevices = 'akin', kAudioDevicePropertyClockDomain = 'clkd',
	kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceIsAlive = 'livn', kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceIsRunning = 'goin',
	kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceCanBeDefaultDevice = 'dflt', kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceCanBeDefaultSystemDevice = 'sflt',
	kAudioDevicePropertyLatency = 'ltnc', kAudioDevicePropertyStreams = 'stm#', kAudioObjectPropertyControlList = 'ctrl',
	kAudioDevicePropertySafetyOffset = 'saft', kAudioDevicePropertyNominalSampleRate = 'nsrt',
	kAudioDevicePropertyAvailableNominalSampleRates = 'nsr#', kAudioDevicePropertyIsHidden = 'hidn',
	kAudioDevicePropertyPreferredChannelsForStereo = 'dch2', kAudioDevicePropertyZeroTimeStampPeriod = 'ring',
	kAudioSelectorControlClassID = 'slct', kAudioDataSourceControlClassID = 'dsrc',
	kAudioSelectorControlPropertyCurrentItem = 'scci', kAudioSelectorControlPropertyAvailableItems = 'scai',
	kAudioSelectorControlPropertyItemName = 'scin', kAudioSelectorControlPropertyItemKind = 'clkk',

	kAudioStreamPropertyIsActive = 'sact', kAudioStreamPropertyDirection = 'sdir', kAudioStreamPropertyTerminalType = 'term',
	kAudioStreamPropertyStartingChannel = 'schn', kAudioStreamPropertyLatency = 'ltnc',
	kAudioStreamPropertyVirtualFormat = 'sfmt', kAudioStreamPropertyAvailableVirtualFormats = 'sfma',
	kAudioStreamPropertyPhysicalFormat = 'pft ', kAudioStreamPropertyAvailablePhysicalFormats = 'pfta',

	kAudioStreamTerminalTypeSpeaker = 'spkr', kAudioStreamTerminalTypeMicrophone = 'micr',

	kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationReadInput = 'read', kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationWriteMix = 'rite',

	kAudioLevelControlClassID = 'levl', kAudioVolumeControlClassID = 'vlme',
	kAudioControlPropertyScope = 'cscp', kAudioControlPropertyElement = 'celm',
	kAudioLevelControlPropertyScalarValue = 'lcsv', kAudioLevelControlPropertyDecibelValue = 'lcdv',
	kAudioLevelControlPropertyDecibelRange = 'lcdr', kAudioLevelControlPropertyConvertScalarToDecibels = 'lcsd',
	kAudioLevelControlPropertyConvertDecibelsToScalar = 'lcds',
};

/* ---- the devices ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * Object numbers are ours to choose. A device's streams follow it: its output (if it has one),
 * then its input.
 */
enum {
	OBJECT_PLUGIN = 1,
	OBJECT_SPEAKER, OBJECT_SPEAKER_OUTPUT, OBJECT_SPEAKER_INPUT,
	OBJECT_HAWKING, OBJECT_HAWKING_INPUT,
	OBJECT_ACTUATOR, OBJECT_ACTUATOR_OUTPUT,
	OBJECT_CODEC, OBJECT_CODEC_INPUT,
	OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME,          /* the speaker output's volume control */
	OBJECT_CODEC_SOURCE,            /* the codec input's data source control: its microphones */
	OBJECT_LAST = OBJECT_CODEC_SOURCE
};

#define VOLUME_RANGE_DB         48.0    /* from the loudest the kernel allows down to the quietest step above 0 */

struct device {
	AudioObjectID object;
	CFStringRef uid;                /* the name the virtual audio device knows it by */
	AudioObjectID output, input;    /* its streams; 0 = none */
	UInt32 output_channels, input_channels;
	/* its clock, running while anybody does I/O */
	unsigned running;               /* how many clients have started I/O */
	UInt64 anchor;                  /* mach_absolute_time() when the first of them did */
	UInt64 periods;                 /* whole timestamp periods since */
};

static struct device devices[] = {
	{ .object = OBJECT_SPEAKER, .uid = CFSTR("Speaker"), .output = OBJECT_SPEAKER_OUTPUT, .input = OBJECT_SPEAKER_INPUT,
	  .output_channels = HAKIOS_AUDIO_CHANNELS, .input_channels = 2 },
	{ .object = OBJECT_HAWKING, .uid = CFSTR("Hawking"), .input = OBJECT_HAWKING_INPUT, .input_channels = 1 },
	{ .object = OBJECT_ACTUATOR, .uid = CFSTR("Actuator"), .output = OBJECT_ACTUATOR_OUTPUT, .output_channels = 1 },
	{ .object = OBJECT_CODEC, .uid = CFSTR("Codec"), .input = OBJECT_CODEC_INPUT, .input_channels = 1 },
};
#define DEVICES                 (sizeof(devices) / sizeof(devices[0]))

#define TRANSPORT_BUILT_IN      'bltn'
/*
 * The codec's input has data sources, one for each microphone, and the virtual audio device will not
 * take a codec without them (VirtualAudio asks for kAudioDevicePropertyDataSources on its input, and
 * keeps those it knows: 'imic', 'smic', 'fmic', 'lmic', 'tmic', 'umic', 'imi1' to 'imi4'). A plug-in
 * has them as a data source control on the input, which the HAL answers those properties from. There
 * is one microphone here, at the bottom: 'imic', the iPhone's internal (bottom) one.
 */
#define MIC_SOURCE              'imic'
#define MANUFACTURER            CFSTR("redwood")
/* how often a device says where its clock is, in frames: also the largest I/O buffer the HAL will use */
#define TIMESTAMP_PERIOD        16384

static AudioServerPlugInHostRef host;
static pthread_mutex_t lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static int sink = -1;                   /* /dev/hakios-audio */
static Float64 ticks_per_frame;
static UInt64 written, refused;         /* frames since the speaker's I/O started */
static Boolean inactive[OBJECT_LAST + 1];       /* streams the HAL has switched off */
static Float32 volume = 1.0f;           /* the speaker's volume control, 0 to 1 (Darwin sets it once it routes there) */

static void
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[256];
	va_list ap;
	int n;

	va_start(ap, format);
	n = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, ap);
	va_end(ap);
	if (n > (int)sizeof(line) - 1) {
		n = sizeof(line) - 1;
	}
	write(2, line, (size_t)n);
}

/* The volume control's scale: a straight line of decibels over VOLUME_RANGE_DB. */
static Float32
scalar_to_db(Float32 scalar)
{
	scalar = scalar < 0 ? 0 : scalar > 1 ? 1 : scalar;
	return (Float32)(-VOLUME_RANGE_DB * (1.0 - scalar));
}

static Float32
db_to_scalar(Float32 db)
{
	Float32 scalar = (Float32)(1.0 + db / VOLUME_RANGE_DB);

	return scalar < 0 ? 0 : scalar > 1 ? 1 : scalar;
}

/* The volume, to the kernel. With the lock held. */
static void
volume_to_kernel(void)
{
	struct hakios_audio_volume v = { (uint32_t)lround(-scalar_to_db(volume) * 8), volume <= 0 };

	if (sink < 0 || ioctl(sink, HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME, &v) < 0) {
		say("hakios: audio: the volume %.3f could not be given to the kernel (%s)\n", volume, strerror(errno));
		return;
	}
	say("hakios: audio: the volume is %.3f: %s%.1f dB under the loudest\n", volume, v.muted ? "silence, " : "",
	    v.below / 8.0);
}

/* The device with this object number, or the one this stream belongs to; NULL = neither. */
static struct device *
device_of(AudioObjectID object)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < DEVICES; i++) {
		if (object == devices[i].object || (object != 0 && (object == devices[i].output || object == devices[i].input))) {
			return &devices[i];
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

/* The one format of a stream: 16-bit samples at HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE, so many channels. */
static AudioStreamBasicDescription
format_of(AudioObjectID stream)
{
	const struct device *d = device_of(stream);
	UInt32 channels = stream == d->output ? d->output_channels : d->input_channels;

	return (AudioStreamBasicDescription) {
		       .mSampleRate = HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE, .mFormatID = kAudioFormatLinearPCM,
		       .mFormatFlags = kAudioFormatFlagIsSignedInteger | kAudioFormatFlagIsPacked,
		       .mBytesPerPacket = 2 * channels, .mFramesPerPacket = 1, .mBytesPerFrame = 2 * channels,
		       .mChannelsPerFrame = channels, .mBitsPerChannel = 16,
	};
}

static HRESULT
query_interface(void *driver, REFIID uuid, LPVOID *interface)
{
	CFUUIDRef requested = CFUUIDCreateFromUUIDBytes(NULL, uuid);
	Boolean ours = CFEqual(requested, IUnknownUUID) || CFEqual(requested, kAudioServerPlugInDriverInterfaceUUID);

	CFRelease(requested);
	if (interface == NULL || !ours) {
		return E_NOINTERFACE;
	}
	*interface = driver;            /* one driver, never freed: no counting */
	return S_OK;
}

static ULONG
add_ref(__unused void *driver)
{
	return 1;
}

static ULONG
release(__unused void *driver)
{
	return 1;
}

static OSStatus
initialize(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioServerPlugInHostRef the_host)
{
	mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;

	host = the_host;
	mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
	ticks_per_frame = 1e9 * timebase.denom / timebase.numer / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE;
	sink = open(HAKIOS_AUDIO_DEVICE, O_WRONLY);
	say("hakios: audio: the speaker is with the HAL (%s: %s)\n", HAKIOS_AUDIO_DEVICE, sink < 0 ? strerror(errno) : "open");
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
create_device(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, __unused CFDictionaryRef description,
    __unused const AudioServerPlugInClientInfo *client, __unused AudioObjectID *object)
{
	return kAudioHardwareUnsupportedOperationError;
}

static OSStatus
destroy_device(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, __unused AudioObjectID object)
{
	return kAudioHardwareUnsupportedOperationError;
}

static OSStatus
device_client(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, __unused AudioObjectID object,
    __unused const AudioServerPlugInClientInfo *client)
{
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
configuration_change(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, __unused AudioObjectID object, __unused UInt64 action,
    __unused void *info)
{
	return 0;
}

/* A property's value: `size` bytes of it, or a list with nothing in it, or (neither) no such property. */
struct value {
	UInt32 size;
	bool empty;
	bool string;                    /* a CFString: whoever is given it gets a reference of their own */
	union {
		UInt32 words[4];
		Float64 number;
		Float32 decimal;
		CFStringRef string;
		AudioValueRange range;
		AudioStreamBasicDescription format;
		AudioStreamRangedDescription ranged;
	} u;
};

static struct value
property(AudioObjectID object, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *address, UInt32 qualifier_size, const void *qualifier)
{
	UInt32 selector = address->mSelector, scope = address->mScope;
	const struct device *d = device_of(object);
	struct value v;

	memset(&v, 0, sizeof(v));
#define WORD(x)         (v.u.words[0] = (x), v.size = sizeof(UInt32))
#define LIST(x)         (v.u.words[v.size / sizeof(UInt32)] = (x), v.size += sizeof(UInt32))
#define STRING(x)       (v.u.string = (x), v.string = true, v.size = sizeof(CFStringRef))
#define FLOAT(x)        (v.u.decimal = (x), v.size = sizeof(Float32))
	if (object == OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME) {
		switch (selector) {
		case kAudioObjectPropertyBaseClass:
			WORD(kAudioLevelControlClassID);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyClass:
			WORD(kAudioVolumeControlClassID);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyOwner:
			WORD(OBJECT_SPEAKER);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects:
			v.empty = true;
			break;
		case kAudioControlPropertyScope:
			WORD(kAudioObjectPropertyScopeOutput);
			break;
		case kAudioControlPropertyElement:
			WORD(0);
			break;
		case kAudioLevelControlPropertyScalarValue:
			FLOAT(volume);
			break;
		case kAudioLevelControlPropertyDecibelValue:
			FLOAT(scalar_to_db(volume));
			break;
		case kAudioLevelControlPropertyDecibelRange:
			v.u.range.mMinimum = -VOLUME_RANGE_DB;
			v.u.range.mMaximum = 0;
			v.size = sizeof(AudioValueRange);
			break;
		case kAudioLevelControlPropertyConvertScalarToDecibels:
		case kAudioLevelControlPropertyConvertDecibelsToScalar:
			FLOAT(0);       /* (converts what it is given: get_property_data()) */
			break;
		}
		return v;
	}
	if (object == OBJECT_CODEC_SOURCE) {
		switch (selector) {
		case kAudioObjectPropertyBaseClass:
			WORD(kAudioSelectorControlClassID);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyClass:
			WORD(kAudioDataSourceControlClassID);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyOwner:
			WORD(OBJECT_CODEC);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects:
			v.empty = true;
			break;
		case kAudioControlPropertyScope:
			WORD(kAudioObjectPropertyScopeInput);
			break;
		case kAudioControlPropertyElement:
			WORD(0);
			break;
		case kAudioSelectorControlPropertyCurrentItem:
		case kAudioSelectorControlPropertyAvailableItems:
			WORD(MIC_SOURCE);
			break;
		case kAudioSelectorControlPropertyItemName:
			if (qualifier_size == sizeof(UInt32) && qualifier != NULL && *(const UInt32 *)qualifier == MIC_SOURCE) {
				STRING(CFSTR("Bottom"));
			} else {
				STRING(CFSTR(""));
			}
			break;
		}
		return v;
	}
	if (object != OBJECT_PLUGIN && d == NULL) {
		return v;
	}
	switch (selector) {
	case kAudioObjectPropertyBaseClass:
		WORD(kAudioObjectClassID);
		return v;
	case kAudioObjectPropertyClass:
		WORD(object == OBJECT_PLUGIN ? kAudioPlugInClassID : object == d->object ? kAudioDeviceClassID : kAudioStreamClassID);
		return v;
	case kAudioObjectPropertyOwner:
		WORD(object == OBJECT_PLUGIN ? 0 : object == d->object ? OBJECT_PLUGIN : d->object);
		return v;
	}
	if (object == OBJECT_PLUGIN) {
		switch (selector) {
		case kAudioObjectPropertyManufacturer:
			STRING(MANUFACTURER);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects:
		case kAudioPlugInPropertyDeviceList:
			for (unsigned i = 0; i < DEVICES; i++) {
				LIST(devices[i].object);
			}
			break;
		case kAudioPlugInPropertyBoxList:
			v.empty = true;
			break;
		case kAudioPlugInPropertyTranslateUIDToBox:
			WORD(0);
			break;
		case kAudioPlugInPropertyTranslateUIDToDevice:
			WORD(0);
			for (unsigned i = 0; i < DEVICES; i++) {
				if (qualifier_size == sizeof(CFStringRef) && qualifier != NULL && *(const CFStringRef *)qualifier != NULL &&
				    CFEqual(*(const CFStringRef *)qualifier, devices[i].uid)) {
					WORD(devices[i].object);
				}
			}
			break;
		case kAudioPlugInPropertyResourceBundle:
			STRING(CFSTR(""));
			break;
		}
	} else if (object == d->object) {
		switch (selector) {
		case kAudioObjectPropertyManufacturer:
			STRING(MANUFACTURER);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyName:
		case kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceUID:
		case kAudioDevicePropertyModelUID:
			STRING(d->uid);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyTransportType:
			WORD(TRANSPORT_BUILT_IN);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyRelatedDevices:
			WORD(d->object);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyClockDomain:
		case kAudioDevicePropertyLatency:
		case kAudioDevicePropertySafetyOffset:
		case kAudioDevicePropertyIsHidden:
			WORD(0);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceIsAlive:
			WORD(1);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceCanBeDefaultDevice:
		case kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceCanBeDefaultSystemDevice:
			WORD(d->output != 0);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceIsRunning:
			WORD(d->running != 0);
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects:
		case kAudioDevicePropertyStreams:
			/* the streams of one direction, or of both (and the speaker's volume control, which it owns) */
			if (scope != kAudioObjectPropertyScopeInput && d->output != 0) {
				LIST(d->output);
			}
			if (scope != kAudioObjectPropertyScopeOutput && d->input != 0) {
				LIST(d->input);
			}
			if (selector == kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects && d->object == OBJECT_SPEAKER) {
				LIST(OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME);
			}
			if (selector == kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects && d->object == OBJECT_CODEC && scope != kAudioObjectPropertyScopeOutput) {
				LIST(OBJECT_CODEC_SOURCE);
			}
			v.empty = v.size == 0;
			break;
		case kAudioObjectPropertyControlList:
			if (d->object == OBJECT_SPEAKER) {
				LIST(OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME);
			}
			if (d->object == OBJECT_CODEC) {
				LIST(OBJECT_CODEC_SOURCE);
			}
			v.empty = v.size == 0;
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyNominalSampleRate:
			v.u.number = HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE;
			v.size = sizeof(Float64);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyAvailableNominalSampleRates:
			v.u.range.mMinimum = v.u.range.mMaximum = HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE;
			v.size = sizeof(AudioValueRange);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyPreferredChannelsForStereo:
			v.u.words[0] = 1;
			v.u.words[1] = 2;
			v.size = 2 * sizeof(UInt32);
			break;
		case kAudioDevicePropertyZeroTimeStampPeriod:
			WORD(TIMESTAMP_PERIOD);
			break;
		}
	} else {
		switch (selector) {
		case kAudioStreamPropertyIsActive:
			WORD(!inactive[object]);
			break;
		case kAudioStreamPropertyDirection:
			WORD(object == d->input);
			break;
		case kAudioStreamPropertyTerminalType:
			WORD(object == d->input ? kAudioStreamTerminalTypeMicrophone : kAudioStreamTerminalTypeSpeaker);
			break;
		case kAudioStreamPropertyStartingChannel:
			WORD(1);
			break;
		case kAudioStreamPropertyLatency:
			WORD(0);
			break;
		case kAudioStreamPropertyVirtualFormat:
		case kAudioStreamPropertyPhysicalFormat:
			v.u.format = format_of(object);
			v.size = sizeof(AudioStreamBasicDescription);
			break;
		case kAudioStreamPropertyAvailableVirtualFormats:
		case kAudioStreamPropertyAvailablePhysicalFormats:
			v.u.ranged.mFormat = format_of(object);
			v.u.ranged.mSampleRateRange.mMinimum = v.u.ranged.mSampleRateRange.mMaximum = HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE;
			v.size = sizeof(AudioStreamRangedDescription);
			break;
		}
	}
#undef WORD
#undef LIST
#undef STRING
#undef FLOAT
	return v;
}

/*
 * What the HAL (or the virtual audio device through it) asks of an object that it does not have,
 * the first times for each object, selector and scope: what a device it will not take may lack.
 */
#define UNKNOWN_TOLD            64
static UInt32 unknown_told[UNKNOWN_TOLD][3];
static unsigned unknown_count;

static void
unknown(AudioObjectID object, const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *address)
{
	UInt32 s = address->mSelector, c = address->mScope;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < unknown_count; i++) {
		if (unknown_told[i][0] == object && unknown_told[i][1] == s && unknown_told[i][2] == c) {
			return;
		}
	}
	if (unknown_count >= UNKNOWN_TOLD) {
		return;
	}
	unknown_told[unknown_count][0] = object;
	unknown_told[unknown_count][1] = s;
	unknown_told[unknown_count][2] = c;
	unknown_count++;
	say("hakios: audio: asked of object %u (%s) what it does not have: '%c%c%c%c' (%#x), scope '%c%c%c%c', element %u\n",
	    (unsigned)object, device_of(object) ? CFStringGetCStringPtr(device_of(object)->uid, kCFStringEncodingUTF8) : "-",
	    (int)(s >> 24 & 0xff), (int)(s >> 16 & 0xff), (int)(s >> 8 & 0xff), (int)(s & 0xff), (unsigned)s,
	    (int)(c >> 24 & 0xff), (int)(c >> 16 & 0xff), (int)(c >> 8 & 0xff), (int)(c & 0xff), (unsigned)address->mElement);
}

static Boolean
has_property(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, __unused pid_t client,
    const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *address)
{
	struct value v;

	if (address == NULL) {
		return false;
	}
	v = property(object, address, 0, NULL);
	if (v.size == 0 && !v.empty) {
		unknown(object, address);
	}
	return v.size != 0 || v.empty;
}

static OSStatus
is_property_settable(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, pid_t client,
    const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *address, Boolean *settable)
{
	const struct device *d = device_of(object);

	if (address == NULL || settable == NULL || !has_property(driver, object, client, address)) {
		return kAudioHardwareUnknownPropertyError;
	}
	/* the rate and the formats can be "set", to the ones there are; the volume can be set */
	if (object == OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME) {
		*settable = address->mSelector == kAudioLevelControlPropertyScalarValue ||
		    address->mSelector == kAudioLevelControlPropertyDecibelValue;
	} else if (object == OBJECT_CODEC_SOURCE) {
		*settable = address->mSelector == kAudioSelectorControlPropertyCurrentItem;
	} else if (object == OBJECT_PLUGIN) {
		*settable = false;
	} else if (object == d->object) {
		*settable = address->mSelector == kAudioDevicePropertyNominalSampleRate;
	} else {
		*settable = address->mSelector == kAudioStreamPropertyIsActive ||
		    address->mSelector == kAudioStreamPropertyVirtualFormat || address->mSelector == kAudioStreamPropertyPhysicalFormat;
	}
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
get_property_data_size(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, pid_t client,
    const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *address, UInt32 qualifier_size, const void *qualifier, UInt32 *size)
{
	if (address == NULL || size == NULL || !has_property(driver, object, client, address)) {
		return object < OBJECT_PLUGIN || object > OBJECT_LAST ? kAudioHardwareBadObjectError : kAudioHardwareUnknownPropertyError;
	}
	*size = property(object, address, qualifier_size, qualifier).size;
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
get_property_data(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, pid_t client,
    const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *address, UInt32 qualifier_size, const void *qualifier, UInt32 room, UInt32 *size,
    void *data)
{
	struct value v;

	if (address == NULL || size == NULL || data == NULL || !has_property(driver, object, client, address)) {
		return object < OBJECT_PLUGIN || object > OBJECT_LAST ? kAudioHardwareBadObjectError : kAudioHardwareUnknownPropertyError;
	}
	if (object == OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME && (address->mSelector == kAudioLevelControlPropertyConvertScalarToDecibels ||
	    address->mSelector == kAudioLevelControlPropertyConvertDecibelsToScalar)) {
		/* what is in the buffer, converted where it is */
		if (room < sizeof(Float32)) {
			return kAudioHardwareBadPropertySizeError;
		}
		*(Float32 *)data = address->mSelector == kAudioLevelControlPropertyConvertScalarToDecibels ?
		    scalar_to_db(*(Float32 *)data) : db_to_scalar(*(Float32 *)data);
		*size = sizeof(Float32);
		return 0;
	}
	pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
	v = property(object, address, qualifier_size, qualifier);
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
	if (v.size > room) {
		/* a list may be asked for in part; anything else must fit */
		if (address->mSelector != kAudioObjectPropertyOwnedObjects && address->mSelector != kAudioDevicePropertyStreams &&
		    address->mSelector != kAudioPlugInPropertyDeviceList) {
			return kAudioHardwareBadPropertySizeError;
		}
		v.size = room - room % sizeof(UInt32);
	}
	memcpy(data, &v.u, v.size);
	if (v.string) {
		CFRetain(v.u.string);
	}
	*size = v.size;
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
set_property_data(AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, pid_t client,
    const AudioObjectPropertyAddress *address, __unused UInt32 qualifier_size, __unused const void *qualifier, UInt32 size,
    const void *data)
{
	Boolean settable = false;

	if (address == NULL || data == NULL || is_property_settable(driver, object, client, address, &settable) != 0) {
		return kAudioHardwareUnknownPropertyError;
	}
	if (!settable) {
		return kAudioHardwareIllegalOperationError;
	}
	if (object == OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME) {
		AudioObjectPropertyAddress changed[2] = {
			{ kAudioLevelControlPropertyScalarValue, kAudioObjectPropertyScopeGlobal, 0 },
			{ kAudioLevelControlPropertyDecibelValue, kAudioObjectPropertyScopeGlobal, 0 },
		};
		Float32 wanted;

		if (size != sizeof(Float32)) {
			return kAudioHardwareBadPropertySizeError;
		}
		wanted = *(const Float32 *)data;
		wanted = address->mSelector == kAudioLevelControlPropertyDecibelValue ? db_to_scalar(wanted) :
		    wanted < 0 ? 0 : wanted > 1 ? 1 : wanted;
		pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
		volume = wanted;
		volume_to_kernel();
		pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
		if (host != NULL) {
			host->PropertiesChanged(host, OBJECT_SPEAKER_VOLUME, 2, changed);
		}
		return 0;
	}
	if (object == OBJECT_CODEC_SOURCE) {
		/* the one microphone there is */
		return size == sizeof(UInt32) ? (*(const UInt32 *)data == MIC_SOURCE ? 0 : kAudioHardwareIllegalOperationError) :
		       kAudioHardwareBadPropertySizeError;
	}
	if (address->mSelector == kAudioStreamPropertyIsActive) {
		if (size != sizeof(UInt32)) {
			return kAudioHardwareBadPropertySizeError;
		}
		pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
		inactive[object] = *(const UInt32 *)data == 0;
		pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
		return 0;
	}
	if (address->mSelector == kAudioDevicePropertyNominalSampleRate) {
		return size == sizeof(Float64) && *(const Float64 *)data == HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE ? 0 : kAudioDeviceUnsupportedFormatError;
	}
	/* a format: the one we have, or nothing */
	if (size != sizeof(AudioStreamBasicDescription)) {
		return kAudioHardwareBadPropertySizeError;
	} else {
		const AudioStreamBasicDescription *wanted = data, format = format_of(object);

		return wanted->mSampleRate == format.mSampleRate && wanted->mFormatID == format.mFormatID &&
		       wanted->mChannelsPerFrame == format.mChannelsPerFrame && wanted->mBitsPerChannel == format.mBitsPerChannel &&
		       (wanted->mFormatFlags & kAudioFormatFlagIsSignedInteger) ? 0 : kAudioDeviceUnsupportedFormatError;
	}
}

/*
 * The microphone (the device "Codec"): /dev/hakios-mic is open while the input runs, and the kernel
 * listens only while it is open. A read gives what has come and never waits; what it does not
 * give is silence. Said when it starts and stops, with how much came.
 */
static int mic = -1;
static UInt64 mic_frames, mic_heard, mic_short;
static int mic_peak;

static void
codec_open(void)
{
	mic = open("/dev/hakios-mic", O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK);
	mic_frames = mic_heard = mic_short = 0;
	mic_peak = 0;
	say("hakios: audio: the microphone is listened to (/dev/hakios-mic: %s)\n", mic < 0 ? strerror(errno) : "open");
}

static void
codec_close(void)
{
	say("hakios: audio: the microphone stops: %llu.%02llu s asked for, %llu.%02llu s of it from the kernel (peak %d of 32768), "
	    "%llu reads short\n", mic_frames / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE, mic_frames % HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE * 100 / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE,
	    mic_heard / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE, mic_heard % HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE * 100 / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE, mic_peak, mic_short);
	if (mic >= 0) {
		close(mic);
	}
	mic = -1;
}

static void
codec_read(int16_t *samples, UInt32 frames)
{
	ssize_t got = mic >= 0 ? read(mic, samples, (size_t)frames * 2) : -1;
	UInt32 have = got > 0 ? (UInt32)got / 2 : 0;

	if (have > 0 && mic_heard == 0) {
		say("hakios: audio: the microphone's first samples, %llu.%02llu s after the input started\n",
		    mic_frames / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE, mic_frames % HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE * 100 / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE);
	}
	for (UInt32 i = 0; i < have; i++) {
		int v = samples[i] < 0 ? -samples[i] : samples[i];

		mic_peak = v > mic_peak ? v : mic_peak;
	}
	if (have < frames) {
		memset(samples + have, 0, (size_t)(frames - have) * 2);
		mic_short += mic_heard > 0;
	}
	mic_frames += frames;
	mic_heard += have;
}

static OSStatus
start_io(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, __unused UInt32 client)
{
	struct device *d = device_of(object);

	if (d == NULL || object != d->object) {
		return kAudioHardwareBadObjectError;
	}
	pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
	if (d->running++ == 0) {
		d->anchor = mach_absolute_time();
		d->periods = 0;
		if (d->output != 0) {
			written = refused = 0;
			say("hakios: audio: playing\n");
		}
		if (d->object == OBJECT_CODEC) {
			codec_open();
		}
	}
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
stop_io(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, __unused UInt32 client)
{
	struct device *d = device_of(object);

	if (d == NULL || object != d->object) {
		return kAudioHardwareBadObjectError;
	}
	pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
	if (d->running != 0 && --d->running == 0) {
		if (d->object == OBJECT_CODEC) {
			codec_close();
		} else if (d->output != 0) {
			say("hakios: audio: stopped after %llu.%02llu s (%llu frames not taken by %s)\n", written / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE,
			    written % HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE * 100 / HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE, refused, HAKIOS_AUDIO_DEVICE);
		}
	}
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
	return 0;
}

/* Where the device's clock was last at a multiple of TIMESTAMP_PERIOD frames, and when. */
static OSStatus
get_zero_time_stamp(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, AudioObjectID object, __unused UInt32 client,
    Float64 *sample_time, UInt64 *host_time, UInt64 *seed)
{
	Float64 ticks_per_period = ticks_per_frame * TIMESTAMP_PERIOD;
	UInt64 now = mach_absolute_time();
	struct device *d = device_of(object);

	if (d == NULL) {
		return kAudioHardwareBadObjectError;
	}
	pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
	while (now >= d->anchor + (UInt64)((Float64)(d->periods + 1) * ticks_per_period)) {
		d->periods++;
	}
	*sample_time = (Float64)d->periods * TIMESTAMP_PERIOD;
	*host_time = d->anchor + (UInt64)((Float64)d->periods * ticks_per_period);
	*seed = 1;
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
will_do_io_operation(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, __unused AudioObjectID object, __unused UInt32 client,
    UInt32 operation, Boolean *will_do, Boolean *in_place)
{
	*will_do = operation == kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationReadInput || operation == kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationWriteMix;
	*in_place = true;
	return 0;
}

static OSStatus
begin_end_io_operation(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, __unused AudioObjectID object, __unused UInt32 client,
    __unused UInt32 operation, __unused UInt32 frames, __unused const AudioServerPlugInIOCycleInfo *cycle)
{
	return 0;
}

/*
 * What Darwin plays on the actuator -- the haptics: the system's feedbacks and the ringer's vibration,
 * CoreHaptics' patterns, UIKit's feedbacks, as waveforms of one channel -- goes to the kernel's motor
 * driver (/dev/hakios-haptic, drivers/haptic/hakios.haptic.c, haptic=5), which plays Android's own
 * waveforms on the phone's motor by it. (Darwin plays on this device at all only because the device
 * tree says the phone's haptics are "closed-loop": see mkidentity.py.) Said the first times, with
 * how loud.
 */
static int haptic = -1;          /* the motor driver; -2: not there (the kernel runs without haptic=5) */
static unsigned haptic_said;

static void
actuator_write(const int16_t *samples, UInt32 frames)
{
	int peak = 0;

	for (UInt32 i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
		int v = samples[i] < 0 ? -samples[i] : samples[i];

		peak = v > peak ? v : peak;
	}
	if (haptic == -1) {
		haptic = open("/dev/hakios-haptic", O_WRONLY | O_NONBLOCK);
		haptic = haptic >= 0 ? haptic : -2;
	}
	if (haptic >= 0) {
		(void)write(haptic, samples, (size_t)frames * 2);
	}
	if (peak > 0 && haptic_said < 12) {
		haptic_said++;
		say("hakios: audio: the actuator plays: %u frames, peak %d of 32768%s\n", (unsigned)frames, peak,
		    haptic >= 0 ? "" : " (no /dev/hakios-haptic: not felt)");
	}
}

static OSStatus
do_io_operation(__unused AudioServerPlugInDriverRef driver, __unused AudioObjectID object, AudioObjectID stream,
    __unused UInt32 client, UInt32 operation, UInt32 frames, __unused const AudioServerPlugInIOCycleInfo *cycle, void *buffer,
    __unused void *secondary)
{
	const struct device *d = device_of(stream);

	if (d == NULL) {
		return kAudioHardwareBadObjectError;
	}
	if (operation == kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationReadInput && stream == OBJECT_CODEC_INPUT) {
		codec_read(buffer, frames);
	} else if (operation == kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationReadInput) {
		/* the speaker's and Hawking's inputs: silence */
		memset(buffer, 0, (size_t)frames * 2 * d->input_channels);
	} else if (operation == kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationWriteMix && stream == OBJECT_ACTUATOR_OUTPUT) {
		actuator_write(buffer, frames);
	} else if (operation == kAudioServerPlugInIOOperationWriteMix && stream == d->output) {
		/* the kernel takes it all or leaves it: this thread must not wait */
		if (sink < 0 || write(sink, buffer, (size_t)frames * HAKIOS_AUDIO_FRAME) < 0) {
			refused += frames;
		}
		written += frames;
	}
	return 0;
}

static AudioServerPlugInDriverInterface interface = {
	NULL, query_interface, add_ref, release, initialize, create_device, destroy_device, device_client, device_client,
	configuration_change, configuration_change, has_property, is_property_settable, get_property_data_size,
	get_property_data, set_property_data, start_io, stop_io, get_zero_time_stamp, will_do_io_operation,
	begin_end_io_operation, do_io_operation, begin_end_io_operation,
};
static AudioServerPlugInDriverInterface *driver = &interface;

/* The factory named in the bundle's Info.plist. */
void *
HakiosAudio_Create(__unused CFAllocatorRef allocator, CFUUIDRef type)
{
	return CFEqual(type, kAudioServerPlugInTypeUUID) ? &driver : NULL;
}
```

`userland/src/battery_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * The battery as Darwin sees it: the kernel's power source (the IOPMPowerSource that powerd reads,
 * drivers/power/hakios.battery.cpp) and what powerd has made of it (the power sources list that
 * the status bar, the lock screen and Settings get through IOPS), side by side with the kernel's
 * own numbers (kern.hakios.battery_*).
 *
 *   battery_test            once
 *   battery_test N S        N times, S seconds apart
 *   battery_test open URL   have SpringBoard open a URL, such as prefs:root=BATTERY_USAGE (Settings >
 *                           Battery): for screenshots of a page that is hard to reach by touches alone
 *                           (needs the entitlement in battery_test.entitlements, which build.sh signs in)
 *   battery_test powerlog   what Darwin's power log (aggregated, CurrentPowerlog.PLSQL) has collected: every
 *                           table with rows, how many and over what time; one row of each of the accounting
 *                           tables Settings > Battery reads (the energy per application comes from them)
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <glob.h>
#include <sqlite3.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/* IOKit's IOPowerSources.h and IOPSKeys.h, which the SDK leaves out */
extern CFTypeRef IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo(void);
extern CFArrayRef IOPSCopyPowerSourcesList(CFTypeRef blob);
extern CFDictionaryRef IOPSGetPowerSourceDescription(CFTypeRef blob, CFTypeRef ps);
extern CFStringRef IOPSGetProvidingPowerSourceType(CFTypeRef snapshot);
extern CFDictionaryRef IOPSCopyExternalPowerAdapterDetails(void);
extern double IOPSGetTimeRemainingEstimate(void);
extern int IOPSGetPercentRemaining(int *percent, bool *charging, bool *full);

/* a value in short: a number, yes or no, a string, or a dictionary of them in braces */
static void
put(char *line, size_t size, CFTypeRef value)
{
	size_t used = strlen(line);
	char text[256] = "";

	if (value == NULL) {
		snprintf(line + used, size - used, "-");
	} else if (CFGetTypeID(value) == CFBooleanGetTypeID()) {
		snprintf(line + used, size - used, "%s", CFBooleanGetValue(value) ? "yes" : "no");
	} else if (CFGetTypeID(value) == CFNumberGetTypeID()) {
		long long n = 0;

		CFNumberGetValue(value, kCFNumberLongLongType, &n);
		snprintf(line + used, size - used, "%lld", n);
	} else if (CFGetTypeID(value) == CFStringGetTypeID()) {
		CFStringGetCString(value, text, sizeof(text), kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
		snprintf(line + used, size - used, "\"%s\"", text);
	} else if (CFGetTypeID(value) == CFDictionaryGetTypeID()) {
		CFIndex count = CFDictionaryGetCount(value);
		const void **keys = calloc(count + 1, sizeof(void *)), **values = calloc(count + 1, sizeof(void *));

		CFDictionaryGetKeysAndValues(value, keys, values);
		snprintf(line + used, size - used, "{");
		for (CFIndex i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			used = strlen(line);
			text[0] = 0;
			if (CFGetTypeID(keys[i]) == CFStringGetTypeID()) {
				CFStringGetCString(keys[i], text, sizeof(text), kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
			}
			snprintf(line + used, size - used, "%s%s=", i ? ", " : "", text);
			put(line, size, values[i]);
		}
		used = strlen(line);
		snprintf(line + used, size - used, "}");
		free(keys);
		free(values);
	} else {
		snprintf(line + used, size - used, "(something else)");
	}
}

static void
show(const char *what, CFTypeRef object)
{
	static char line[16384];

	if (object == NULL) {
		printf("%s: none\n", what);
		return;
	}
	line[0] = 0;
	put(line, sizeof(line), object);
	printf("%s: %s\n", what, line);
}

static int
kernel(const char *name)
{
	int value = -1;
	size_t size = sizeof(value);

	sysctlbyname(name, &value, &size, NULL, 0);
	return value;
}

static void
once(void)
{
	io_service_t service = IOServiceGetMatchingService(0, IOServiceMatching("IOPMPowerSource"));
	CFTypeRef blob = IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo();
	CFArrayRef list = blob ? IOPSCopyPowerSourcesList(blob) : NULL;
	CFDictionaryRef adapter = IOPSCopyExternalPowerAdapterDetails();
	int percent = -1;
	bool charging = false, full = false;
	int got = IOPSGetPercentRemaining(&percent, &charging, &full);

	printf("battery_test: the kernel says %d%%, %d mV, %d mA, %d C, battery %d, charger %d, charging %d, from the DSP %d\n",
	    kernel("kern.hakios.battery_soc"), kernel("kern.hakios.battery_voltage_mv"), kernel("kern.hakios.battery_current_ma"),
	    kernel("kern.hakios.battery_temperature_c"), kernel("kern.hakios.battery_present"),
	    kernel("kern.hakios.battery_charger_present"), kernel("kern.hakios.battery_charging"),
	    kernel("kern.hakios.battery_from_dsp"));
	if (service != 0) {
		CFMutableDictionaryRef properties = NULL;
		io_name_t name = "";

		IORegistryEntryGetName(service, name);
		if (IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperties(service, &properties, kCFAllocatorDefault, 0) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
			printf("battery_test: the power source in the kernel is %s\n", name);
			show("battery_test: its properties", properties);
			CFRelease(properties);
		}
		IOObjectRelease(service);
	} else {
		printf("battery_test: there is no IOPMPowerSource in the kernel\n");
	}
	printf("battery_test: IOPSGetPercentRemaining: %d (%#x), %d%%, charging %d, full %d; time remaining %.0f s\n", got, got,
	    percent, charging, full, IOPSGetTimeRemainingEstimate());
	if (blob != NULL) {
		show("battery_test: powered by", IOPSGetProvidingPowerSourceType(blob));
	}
	for (CFIndex i = 0; list != NULL && i < CFArrayGetCount(list); i++) {
		show("battery_test: power source", IOPSGetPowerSourceDescription(blob, CFArrayGetValueAtIndex(list, i)));
	}
	if (list == NULL || CFArrayGetCount(list) == 0) {
		printf("battery_test: powerd lists no power source\n");
	}
	show("battery_test: the power adapter", adapter);
	if (adapter != NULL) CFRelease(adapter);
	if (list != NULL) CFRelease(list);
	if (blob != NULL) CFRelease(blob);
	fflush(stdout);
}

/* SpringBoardServices' way of opening a URL, as a program with the entitlement may */
static int
open_url(const char *text)
{
	void *sbs = dlopen("/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SpringBoardServices.framework/SpringBoardServices", RTLD_NOW);
	int (*open)(CFURLRef, Boolean) = sbs ? (int (*)(CFURLRef, Boolean))dlsym(sbs, "SBSOpenSensitiveURLAndUnlock") : NULL;
	CFURLRef url = CFURLCreateWithBytes(NULL, (const UInt8 *)text, (CFIndex)strlen(text), kCFStringEncodingUTF8, NULL);
	int result;

	if (open == NULL || url == NULL) {
		printf("battery_test: cannot open %s: %s\n", text, open == NULL ? "no SBSOpenSensitiveURLAndUnlock" : "not a URL");
		return 1;
	}
	result = open(url, true);
	printf("battery_test: SpringBoard was asked to open %s: %s\n", text, result ? "it does" : "it REFUSES");
	CFRelease(url);
	return result ? 0 : 1;
}

/* the power log's database, read only (aggregated keeps writing it) */
static int
powerlog(void)
{
	glob_t found;
	sqlite3 *db;
	sqlite3_stmt *tables;

	if (glob("/private/var/containers/Shared/SystemGroup/*/Library/BatteryLife/CurrentPowerlog.PLSQL", 0, NULL, &found) != 0 ||
	    found.gl_pathc == 0) {
		printf("battery_test: no power log database (is aggregated running?)\n");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("battery_test: the power log: %s\n", found.gl_pathv[0]);
	if (sqlite3_open_v2(found.gl_pathv[0], &db, SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
		printf("battery_test: cannot open it: %s\n", sqlite3_errmsg(db));
		return 1;
	}
	sqlite3_busy_timeout(db, 2000);
	if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name", -1, &tables, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
		printf("battery_test: cannot list its tables: %s\n", sqlite3_errmsg(db));
		return 1;
	}
	while (sqlite3_step(tables) == SQLITE_ROW) {
		const char *name = (const char *)sqlite3_column_text(tables, 0);
		char query[512];
		sqlite3_stmt *count;
		long rows = 0;
		double first = 0, last = 0;

		snprintf(query, sizeof(query), "SELECT COUNT(*), MIN(timestamp), MAX(timestamp) FROM \"%s\"", name);
		if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, query, -1, &count, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
			snprintf(query, sizeof(query), "SELECT COUNT(*), 0, 0 FROM \"%s\"", name);
			if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, query, -1, &count, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
				continue;
			}
		}
		if (sqlite3_step(count) == SQLITE_ROW) {
			rows = sqlite3_column_int64(count, 0);
			first = sqlite3_column_double(count, 1);
			last = sqlite3_column_double(count, 2);
		}
		sqlite3_finalize(count);
		if (rows == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		printf("battery_test: powerlog %-70s %6ld rows, %.0f s from the first to the last\n", name, rows, last - first);
		if (strncmp(name, "PLAccountingOperator", 20) == 0 || strncmp(name, "PLBatteryAgent_EventBackward_Battery", 36) == 0) {
			sqlite3_stmt *row;

			snprintf(query, sizeof(query), "SELECT * FROM \"%s\" ORDER BY ID DESC LIMIT 1", name);
			if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, query, -1, &row, NULL) == SQLITE_OK) {
				if (sqlite3_step(row) == SQLITE_ROW) {
					char line[1024] = "";

					for (int c = 0; c < sqlite3_column_count(row) && strlen(line) < sizeof(line) - 80; c++) {
						const unsigned char *v = sqlite3_column_text(row, c);

						snprintf(line + strlen(line), sizeof(line) - strlen(line), " %s=%.40s", sqlite3_column_name(row, c),
						    v ? (const char *)v : "-");
					}
					printf("battery_test: powerlog   the last row:%s\n", line);
				}
				sqlite3_finalize(row);
			}
		}
	}
	sqlite3_finalize(tables);
	sqlite3_close(db);
	globfree(&found);
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	if (argc > 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "open") == 0) {
		return open_url(argv[2]);
	}
	if (argc > 1 && strcmp(argv[1], "powerlog") == 0) {
		return powerlog();
	}
	int times = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 1;
	int seconds = argc > 2 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 10;

	for (int i = 0; i < times; i++) {
		if (i > 0) sleep(seconds);
		once();
	}
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/battery_test.entitlements`:


`userland/src/camera_avtest.m`:

```m
/*
 * camera_avtest: what cameras Darwin lists for applications, as AVFoundation gives them: the video
 * devices, and every format of the default one (on this machine the device is libhakios.media.dylib's
 * in mediaserverd: camera_device.c, the kernel's /dev/hakios-camera, cam=5).
 *
 * usage: camera_avtest
 *
 * Frames are for applications in the foreground, as Darwin has it: a program like this one is not
 * given any (its session is interrupted at once). Camera.app is the test for those (rc.jobs.camera).
 */
#import <AVFoundation/AVFoundation.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int
main(void)
{
	@autoreleasepool {
		setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
#pragma clang diagnostic push
#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wdeprecated-declarations"
		NSArray *devices = [AVCaptureDevice devicesWithMediaType:AVMediaTypeVideo];
#pragma clang diagnostic pop
		printf("camera_avtest: %lu video device(s)\n", (unsigned long)devices.count);
		for (AVCaptureDevice *d in devices) {
			printf("camera_avtest:   %s (%s), position %ld, %lu formats\n", d.localizedName.UTF8String, d.uniqueID.UTF8String,
			    (long)d.position, (unsigned long)d.formats.count);
		}
		AVCaptureDevice *device = [AVCaptureDevice defaultDeviceWithMediaType:AVMediaTypeVideo];
		if (device == nil) {
			printf("camera_avtest: no default video device\n");
			return 1;
		}
		for (AVCaptureDeviceFormat *f in device.formats) {
			printf("camera_avtest:   format %s\n", f.description.UTF8String);
		}
		printf("camera_avtest: the default device's active format: %s\n", device.activeFormat.description.UTF8String);
		return 0;
	}
}
```

`userland/src/camera_device.c`:

```c
/*
 * The phone's cameras as Darwin's capture stack wants them: a FigCaptureDevice with two FigCaptureStreams,
 * the wide camera as the back camera and the front one as the front camera, made for mediaserverd's
 * BWFigCaptureDeviceVendor in place of the device Apple's H10ISP.mediacapture makes of the iPhone's ISP
 * (part of libhakios.media.dylib; inject_media.c gives the vendor our device's create function when
 * the kernel has a camera: cam=5).
 *
 * Both are CoreMedia "derived objects" (CMDerivedObjectCreate): a table of functions for the base
 * class (properties) and one for the device or stream class, as H10ISP's are laid out in Darwin userland 16.5:
 *   device  RequestStreams, RelinquishStreams (and a processing session and Pearl calibration, not here)
 *   stream  Start, Stop, AddAttachmentsToSampleBuffer
 * A stream's frames go to the capture graph through the blocks it is given in its property
 * "VideoOutputHandlers" ({ output: { PixelBufferHandler: ^(CVPixelBufferRef, CMTime) } }), for the
 * outputs "VideoOutputConfigurations" describes (the graph's own buffer pools) and "VideoOutputsEnabled"
 * switches on. A frame: read from the kernel's /dev/hakios-camera (RAW10), made into a picture by
 * camera_isp.c (exposure, white balance kept to the sensor's reference lights, the colour matrix and
 * lens shading of the camera's own tuning, gamma, zoom), one pixel buffer for each output, with the
 * metadata the graph keeps its frame statistics and its zoom by. The kernel gives one sensor's frames
 * at a time: a stream that starts stops the other's frames and has the kernel change sensors.
 *
 * The formats the streams offer are named as the iPhone X's cameras' are in CMCapture's
 * D22/AVCaptureSession.plist (FigCaptureStreamFormats, by the sensor sizes and frame rates the plist
 * matches them by), so that their AVCaptureDevice formats and session presets resolve: the pictures
 * are scaled from the sensor's frames to whatever size is asked for.
 *
 * The shutter: StillImageCaptureNow asks for one frame of the whole sensor on the StillImage output
 * (the time machine's TimeMachineSuspendNow/ResumeNow are taken and ignored). Focus, where there is
 * a lens motor (the wide camera's): by contrast, continuous, and on the window a tap gives (af_frame()).
 *
 * Everything asked of the device and the streams that is not answered here is said in mediaserverd's
 * log ("hakios: camera: ..."), once per property.
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreMedia/CoreMedia.h>
#include <CoreVideo/CoreVideo.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurfaceRef.h>
#include <dispatch/dispatch.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include "camera_isp.h"

void hakios_camera_say(const char *format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));

void
hakios_camera_say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[400];
	va_list ap;
	int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: camera: ");

	va_start(ap, format);
	n += vsnprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, format, ap);
	va_end(ap);
	if (n > (int)sizeof(line) - 2) {
		n = sizeof(line) - 2;
	}
	line[n++] = '\n';
	write(2, line, (size_t)n);
}
#define say hakios_camera_say

/* ---- CoreMedia's derived objects, as Darwin userland 16.5 lays them out ---------------------------------------- */

typedef struct OpaqueCMBaseObject *CMBaseObjectRef;
typedef const void *CMBaseClassID;

struct base_class {
	uint64_t        version;
	uint64_t        storage_size;
	Boolean         (*equal)(CMBaseObjectRef, CMBaseObjectRef);
	OSStatus        (*invalidate)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	void            (*finalize)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	CFStringRef     (*copy_debug_description)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	OSStatus        (*copy_property)(CMBaseObjectRef, CFStringRef, CFAllocatorRef, void *);
	OSStatus        (*set_property)(CMBaseObjectRef, CFStringRef, CFTypeRef);
	OSStatus        (*notification_barrier)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	const void *    protocols;
	const void *    reserved;
};
struct device_class {
	uint64_t        version;                /* 3 */
	void *          processing_session_create;
	OSStatus        (*request_streams)(CMBaseObjectRef, CFArrayRef, CFDictionaryRef);
	OSStatus        (*relinquish_streams)(CMBaseObjectRef, CFArrayRef, CFDictionaryRef);
	void *          pearl_calibration;
};
struct stream_class {
	uint64_t        version;                /* 2 */
	OSStatus        (*start)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	OSStatus        (*stop)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	OSStatus        (*add_attachments)(CMBaseObjectRef, CMSampleBufferRef, CFDictionaryRef);
};
struct vtable {
	const void *    reserved;
	const struct base_class *base;
	const void *    derived;
};

#define ERR_PARAM               (-12780)
#define ERR_NOT_AVAILABLE       (-12783)
#define ERR_UNSUPPORTED         (-12782)

static OSStatus (*derived_create)(CFAllocatorRef, const struct vtable *, CMBaseClassID, CMBaseObjectRef *);
static void *(*derived_storage)(CMBaseObjectRef);
static CMBaseClassID (*device_class_id)(void);
static CMBaseClassID (*stream_class_id)(void);
static CFStringRef port_back;           /* kFigCapturePortType_BackFacingCamera */
static CFStringRef port_front;          /* kFigCapturePortType_FrontFacingCamera */

/*
 * The frames' metadata: what H10ISP's stream attaches to every frame (a dictionary under
 * kFigCaptureSampleBufferAttachmentKey_MetadataDictionary, through the stream's
 * AddAttachmentsToSampleBuffer when the graph defers it), and what the capture device keeps its frame
 * statistics of. -[BWFrameStatisticsByPortType updateWithFrameMetadata:updateFocusDistance:] counts
 * a frame only for a buffer that has it, and -[BWFigVideoCaptureDevice
 * _stillImageCaptureInProgressSubstateForFrameStatisticsByPortType:...] puts a standard photograph
 * off until more than four frames have been counted (then only while AFStatus is 2, a coarse focus
 * scan): without it the shutter's capture was put off on every frame (the retry in
 * _updateStateUsingVideoSampleBuffer:fromCaptureStream:), for ever, and StillImageCaptureNow never
 * came. The dictionary goes on the pixel buffer too, and mutable, as the ISP's does: FigImageControl_Focus
 * (the device's camera controls, on every frame once the sample buffer has metadata) reads it from
 * the pixel buffer with no check that it is there -- CFDictionaryGetValue(NULL, ...): mediaserverd
 * died of SIGSEGV -- and adds its own keys to it. The keys are CoreMedia's; the values come from the
 * frame's header and our ISP's levels, in Apple's units where they are known (the exposure in seconds,
 * gains with 256 for 1x); lux and SNR are rough.
 */
enum {
	MD_PORT, MD_PTS, MD_EXPOSURE, MD_AGC, MD_ISP_DGAIN, MD_SENSOR_DGAIN, MD_ISO_BASE, MD_FRAME_RATE, MD_LUX, MD_SNR,
	MD_AF_STATUS, MD_FOCUSING, MD_AE_STABLE, MD_AE_LOCKED, MD_AWB_STABLE, MD_AWB_LOCKED, MD_AF_LOCKED, MD_ZOOM, MD_KEYS
};
static const char *const md_names[MD_KEYS] = {
	"kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_PortType", "kFigCaptureSampleBufferAttachmentKey_OriginalPresentationTimeStamp",
	"kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_ExposureTime", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_AGC", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_ispDGain",
	"kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_sensorDGain", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_ISOBase", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_CurrentFrameRate",
	"kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_LuxLevel", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_NormalizedSNR", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_AFStatus",
	"kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_FocusingMethod", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_AEStable", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_AELocked",
	"kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_AWBStable", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_AWBLocked", "kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_AFLocked",
	"kFigCaptureStreamMetadata_ZoomFactor",
};
static CFStringRef md_key[MD_KEYS];
static CFStringRef md_attachment;       /* kFigCaptureSampleBufferAttachmentKey_MetadataDictionary */

static bool
find_functions(void)
{
	CFStringRef *port;

	derived_create = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CMDerivedObjectCreate");
	derived_storage = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CMBaseObjectGetDerivedStorage");
	device_class_id = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "FigCaptureDeviceGetClassID");
	stream_class_id = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "FigCaptureStreamGetClassID");
	port = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "kFigCapturePortType_BackFacingCamera");
	port_back = port != NULL ? *port : NULL;
	port = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "kFigCapturePortType_FrontFacingCamera");
	port_front = port != NULL ? *port : NULL;
	port = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "kFigCaptureSampleBufferAttachmentKey_MetadataDictionary");
	md_attachment = port != NULL ? *port : NULL;
	for (int i = 0; i < MD_KEYS; i++) {
		port = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, md_names[i]);
		md_key[i] = port != NULL ? *port : NULL;
		if (md_key[i] == NULL) {
			say("%s is not there: the frames' metadata go without it", md_names[i]);
		}
	}
	if (md_attachment == NULL || md_key[MD_PORT] == NULL) {
		say("kFigCaptureSampleBufferAttachmentKey_MetadataDictionary or the port's key is not there: frames without "
		    "metadata, and the shutter will wait for ever");
		md_attachment = NULL;
	}
	if (derived_create == NULL || derived_storage == NULL || device_class_id == NULL || stream_class_id == NULL || port_back == NULL ||
	    port_front == NULL) {
		say("CoreMedia's or CMCapture's functions are not there: no camera");
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

/* ---- what is asked and not answered: said once per name ------------------------------------------- */

static CFMutableSetRef said_names;
static pthread_mutex_t said_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

static void
say_value(const char *what, CFStringRef key, CFTypeRef value)
{
	char name[160] = "?", text[300] = "";

	CFStringGetCString(key, name, sizeof(name), kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
	if (value != NULL) {
		CFStringRef d = CFCopyDescription(value);

		CFStringGetCString(d, text, sizeof(text), kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
		CFRelease(d);
		for (char *c = text; *c; c++) {
			*c = *c == '\n' ? ' ' : *c;
		}
	}
	say("%s %s%s%s", what, name, value ? " = " : "", text);
}

static void
say_once(const char *what, CFStringRef key, CFTypeRef value)
{
	CFStringRef tag = CFStringCreateWithFormat(NULL, NULL, CFSTR("%s %@"), what, key);

	pthread_mutex_lock(&said_lock);
	if (said_names == NULL) {
		said_names = CFSetCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeSetCallBacks);
	}
	bool first = !CFSetContainsValue(said_names, tag);

	CFSetAddValue(said_names, tag);
	pthread_mutex_unlock(&said_lock);
	CFRelease(tag);
	if (first) {
		say_value(what, key, value);
	}
}

/* ---- numbers and dictionaries ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static CFNumberRef
number_i(int64_t v)
{
	return CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberSInt64Type, &v);
}

static CFNumberRef
number_f(double v)
{
	return CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberDoubleType, &v);
}

static void
put(CFMutableDictionaryRef d, const char *key, CFTypeRef value)
{
	CFStringRef k = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, key, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);

	CFDictionarySetValue(d, k, value);
	CFRelease(k);
	CFRelease(value);
}

static CFDictionaryRef
new_dict(void)
{
	return CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
}

static bool
key_is(CFStringRef key, const char *name)
{
	char buffer[128];

	return CFStringGetCString(key, buffer, sizeof(buffer), kCFStringEncodingUTF8) && strcmp(buffer, name) == 0;
}

/* ---- what the device and the stream say they have ---------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * The capture stack asks only for the properties an object lists in its "SupportedPropertiesDictionary"
 * ({ name: { PropertyType, ReadWriteStatus } }). Listed here: what is answered, and what is taken
 * (and, for now, mostly not acted on) without failing the graph that sets it.
 */
struct prop {
	const char *name, *type, *access;
};

static CFDictionaryRef
supported(const struct prop *p, size_t n)
{
	CFMutableDictionaryRef all = (CFMutableDictionaryRef)new_dict();

	for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		CFMutableDictionaryRef one = (CFMutableDictionaryRef)new_dict();

		put(one, "PropertyType", CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, p[i].type, kCFStringEncodingUTF8));
		put(one, "ReadWriteStatus", CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, p[i].access, kCFStringEncodingUTF8));
		put(all, p[i].name, one);
	}
	return all;
}

/* ---- the formats ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define PF_420F         0x34323066      /* '420f' */
#define PF_420V         0x34323076      /* '420v' */
#define PF_BGRA         0x42475241      /* 'BGRA' */

static CFDictionaryRef
output_info(int width, int height)
{
	CFMutableDictionaryRef o = (CFMutableDictionaryRef)new_dict();
	CFNumberRef pf[3] = { number_i(PF_420F), number_i(PF_420V), number_i(PF_BGRA) };
	CFArrayRef pfs = CFArrayCreate(NULL, (const void **)pf, 3, &kCFTypeArrayCallBacks);

	for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
		CFRelease(pf[i]);
	}
	put(o, "SupportedPixelFormats", pfs);
	put(o, "NativeWidth", number_i(width));
	put(o, "NativeHeight", number_i(height));
	put(o, "MaxDownscaleFactor", number_f(32));
	put(o, "MaxScaleFactor", number_f(1));
	put(o, "MinScaleFactor", number_f(1.0 / 32));
	put(o, "OutputWidthAlignmentRequirement", number_i(16));
	return o;
}

static CFDictionaryRef
format(int sensor_width, int sensor_height, int max_fps, bool binned, double fov)
{
	CFMutableDictionaryRef f = (CFMutableDictionaryRef)new_dict(), outputs = (CFMutableDictionaryRef)new_dict();
	CMVideoFormatDescriptionRef fd = NULL;

	CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreate(NULL, PF_420F, sensor_width, sensor_height, NULL, &fd);
	if (fd != NULL) {
		put(f, "FormatDescription", fd);
	}
	put(f, "VideoMinFrameRate", number_f(2));
	put(f, "VideoMaxFrameRate", number_f(max_fps));
	put(f, "VideoIsBinned", CFRetain(binned ? kCFBooleanTrue : kCFBooleanFalse));
	put(f, "VideoBinningFactorHorizontal", number_i(binned ? 2 : 1));
	put(f, "VideoBinningFactorVertical", number_i(binned ? 2 : 1));
	put(f, "VideoFieldOfView", number_f(fov));
	put(f, "VideoMinIntegrationTime", number_i(100));
	put(f, "VideoMaxIntegrationTime", number_i(1000000 / 15));
	put(f, "VideoRawBitDepth", number_i(10));
	put(f, "VideoMaxWidth", number_i(sensor_width));
	put(f, "VideoMaxHeight", number_i(sensor_height));
	put(f, "Experimental", CFRetain(kCFBooleanFalse));
	put(f, "SensorWidth", number_i(sensor_width));
	put(f, "SensorHeight", number_i(sensor_height));
	put(f, "ISOBase", number_f(32));
	put(f, "DefaultAEMaxGain", number_f(64));

	/*
	 * The sensor crop geometry the capture-graph builder reads off this format to resolve non-zero
	 * output dimensions (confirmed by a hook: -[FigCaptureSourceVideoFormat sensorCropDimensions] /
	 * postGDCCropDimensions] return these). Everything spans the full sensor: no GDC crop.
	 */
	put(f, "SensorCropWidth", number_i(sensor_width));
	put(f, "SensorCropHeight", number_i(sensor_height));
	put(f, "PreGDCSensorCropWidth", number_i(sensor_width));
	put(f, "PreGDCSensorCropHeight", number_i(sensor_height));
	put(f, "PostGDCCropWidth", number_i(sensor_width));
	put(f, "PostGDCCropHeight", number_i(sensor_height));
	put(f, "GeometricDistortionCorrectedNativeWidth", number_i(sensor_width));
	put(f, "GeometricDistortionCorrectedNativeHeight", number_i(sensor_height));

	put(outputs, "PrimaryScaler", output_info(sensor_width, sensor_height));
	put(outputs, "SecondaryScaler", output_info(sensor_width, sensor_height));
	put(outputs, "StillImage", output_info(sensor_width, sensor_height));
	put(f, "SupportedOutputs", outputs);
	return f;
}

/* ---- the stream ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define HELD    3               /* the moving pictures kept from the pool after they are given (see deliver) */

struct output {
	const char *    name;
	CFDictionaryRef config;                 /* from VideoOutputConfigurations */
	bool            enabled;
	void *          handler;                /* a block: ^(CVPixelBufferRef, CMTime) */
	bool            said_shape;
	uint64_t        delivered, refused;
	CVPixelBufferRef held[HELD];            /* the pictures given last, kept from the pool (see deliver) */
	unsigned        held_next;
	bool            said_pool;
};

static void let_go(struct output *out);

#define OUTPUTS 3
static const char *const output_names[OUTPUTS] = { "PrimaryScaler", "SecondaryScaler", "StillImage" };

#define MAX_ZOOM        16              /* (the most the iPhone X's wide camera zooms digitally) */

/*
 * The device's cameras, a stream each, as the iPhone X's are in CMCapture's D22/AVCaptureSession.plist
 * (its devices' uniqueIDs, and the stream formats its formats and presets are matched to by sensor size
 * and frame rate): the wide camera as the back camera, the front one as the front camera. The kernel
 * gives one sensor's frames at a time; a stream's frames start with its own sensor's (see worker()).
 */
static const struct camera {
	uint32_t        sensor;         /* the kernel's (the frames' sensor, HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR) */
	const char      *name, *unique_id;
```
