```c
				if (c == 1 && l / top[c] < darkest) {
					darkest = l / top[c];
				}
			}
		}
	}
	isp->lsc.on = true;
	if (min_ratio != NULL) {
		*min_ratio = darkest;
	}
	return true;
}

/* one module's part of a tuning file (tools/camtuning.py): its ranges, and where each range's values are */
static bool
tune_set(const uint8_t **p, const uint8_t *end, struct isp_tune_set *set, size_t floats)
{
	uint32_t n;

	if (end - *p < 4) {
		return false;
	}
	memcpy(&n, *p, 4);
	*p += 4;
	if (n == 0 || n > TUNE_LIGHTS) {
		return false;
	}
	set->lights = n;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		if (end - *p < 12) {
			return false;
		}
		memcpy(&set->light[i].lux_from, *p, 4);
		memcpy(&set->light[i].lux_to, *p + 4, 4);
		memcpy(&set->light[i].ccts, *p + 8, 4);
		*p += 12;
		if (set->light[i].ccts == 0 || set->light[i].ccts > TUNE_CCTS) {
			return false;
		}
		for (uint32_t j = 0; j < set->light[i].ccts; j++) {
			if ((size_t)(end - *p) < (2 + floats) * 4) {
				return false;
			}
			memcpy(&set->light[i].cct_from[j], *p, 4);
			memcpy(&set->light[i].cct_to[j], *p + 4, 4);
			set->light[i].v[j] = (const float *)(const void *)(*p + 8);     /* (every field is 4 bytes) */
			*p += (2 + floats) * 4;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

bool
isp_load_tuning(struct isp *isp, const char *path)
{
	struct isp_tuning *t = calloc(1, sizeof(*t));
	int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY);
	struct stat st;
	const uint8_t *p, *end;
	bool good = false;

	if (isp->tuning != NULL) {
		free(isp->tuning->file);
		free(isp->tuning);
		isp->tuning = NULL;
	}
	if (t != NULL && fd >= 0 && fstat(fd, &st) == 0 && st.st_size > 8 && st.st_size < (16 << 20) &&
	    (t->file = malloc((size_t)st.st_size)) != NULL && read(fd, t->file, (size_t)st.st_size) == st.st_size) {
		p = t->file;
		end = p + st.st_size;
		good = memcmp(p, "RWCISP02", 8) == 0;
		p += 8;
		good = good && tune_set(&p, end, &t->ccm, 9) && tune_set(&p, end, &t->lsc, 4 * LSC_W * LSC_H) && end - p >= 4;
		if (good) {
			memcpy(&t->refs, p, 4);
			p += 4;
			good = t->refs <= 16 && (size_t)(end - p) >= t->refs * 12;
		}
		if (good) {
			memcpy(t->ref, p, t->refs * 12);
		}
	}
	if (fd >= 0) {
		close(fd);
	}
	if (!good) {
		if (t != NULL) {
			free(t->file);
		}
		free(t);
		return false;
	}
	isp->tuning = t;
	return true;
}

/*
 * Where x falls among ascending ranges [from[i], to[i]]: in one (a = b), or between two (a, b and how
 * far from a's end to b's start, 0 to 1); before the first, the first; after the last, the last.
 */
static void
pick(const float *from, const float *to, uint32_t n, float x, uint32_t *a, uint32_t *b, float *t)
{
	*a = *b = n - 1;
	*t = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		if (x <= to[i]) {
			*a = *b = i;
			if (i > 0 && x < from[i]) {
				*a = i - 1;
				*t = (x - to[i - 1]) / (from[i] - to[i - 1]);
			}
			return;
		}
	}
}

/* a module's values for this light and temperature: those of the ranges they fall in, or between */
static void
tune_blend(const struct isp_tune_set *set, float lux_index, float cct, size_t floats, float *out)
{
	float from[TUNE_LIGHTS], to[TUNE_LIGHTS], tl;
	uint32_t la, lb;

	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < set->lights; i++) {
		from[i] = set->light[i].lux_from;
		to[i] = set->light[i].lux_to;
	}
	pick(from, to, set->lights, lux_index, &la, &lb, &tl);
	memset(out, 0, floats * sizeof(float));
	for (int k = 0; k < 2; k++) {
		uint32_t l = k ? lb : la, ca, cb;
		float w = k ? tl : 1 - tl, tc;

		if (w == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		pick(set->light[l].cct_from, set->light[l].cct_to, set->light[l].ccts, cct, &ca, &cb, &tc);
		for (size_t i = 0; i < floats; i++) {
			out[i] += w * ((1 - tc) * set->light[l].v[ca][i] + tc * set->light[l].v[cb][i]);
		}
	}
}

void
isp_tune(struct isp *isp, float lux_index, float cct)
{
	const struct isp_tuning *t = isp->tuning;
	float m[9], g[4 * LSC_H * LSC_W];
	const int grid = LSC_H * LSC_W;

	if (t == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	tune_blend(&t->ccm, lux_index, cct, 9, m);
	isp_set_ccm(isp, m);
	tune_blend(&t->lsc, lux_index, cct, 4 * (size_t)grid, g);
	for (int gy = 0; gy < LSC_H; gy++) {
		for (int gx = 0; gx < LSC_W; gx++) {
			int at = gy * LSC_W + gx;

			isp->lsc.gain[0][gy][gx] = g[at];
			isp->lsc.gain[1][gy][gx] = (g[grid + at] + g[2 * grid + at]) / 2;
			isp->lsc.gain[2][gy][gx] = g[3 * grid + at];
		}
	}
	isp->lsc.on = true;
}
```

`userland/src/camera_isp.h`:

```h
/*
 * What the phone's ISP would do with the cameras' RAW10 frames, done by the processor instead
 * (src/camera_isp.c): the levels of a frame, the exposure for the next ones (AE), the white balance
 * (AWB), and a picture: each 2x2 Bayer cell one pixel of colour, scaled to the size asked for, or
 * every pixel (bilinear demosaic) at the sensor's own size; lens shading (a grid of gains per
 * colour), the white balance's and AE's gains, a colour matrix, a gamma; as 8-bit YCbCr 4:2:0 (NV12,
 * full range: CoreVideo's 420f, or video range: 420v) or BGRA.
 */
#ifndef CAMERA_ISP_H
#define CAMERA_ISP_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include "hakios.camera.h"

struct isp_stats {
	double          mean[3];        /* R, G, B above black, in 10-bit steps */
	double          bright;         /* the level of green that 1 % of the cells are above */
	uint32_t        hist[64];       /* green above black, 16 steps a bin */
	uint32_t        cells;
	/*
	 * Red over green and blue over green, lens-shaded, each cell's counted once however bright it is:
	 * the mean of the cells none of whose colours is near white or near black, and of those of them
	 * that are grey or nearly with the white balance as it is.
	 */
	double          grey[2], neutral[2];
	uint32_t        grey_cells, neutral_cells;
};

/*
 * Lens shading: a gain for each colour at each point of a grid laid over the sensor (corners on its
 * corners), between the points bilinear. Off until it is given one (isp_lsc_from_flat(), isp_tune()).
 */
#define LSC_W           17
#define LSC_H           13
struct isp_lsc {
	bool            on;
	float           gain[3][LSC_H][LSC_W];
};

/*
 * A camera's colour tuning, as tools/camtuning.py makes it out of the camera's tuning file of Android's
 * camera stack: colour matrices and lens shading grids, each per range of the scene's light (a lux
 * index, Qualcomm's measure: higher is darker) and within that per range of the light's colour
 * temperature.
 */
#define TUNE_LIGHTS     6
#define TUNE_CCTS       6
struct isp_tune_set {
	uint32_t        lights;
	struct {
		float           lux_from, lux_to;
		uint32_t        ccts;
		float           cct_from[TUNE_CCTS], cct_to[TUNE_CCTS];
		const float     *v[TUNE_CCTS];  /* a matrix by rows (9), or R, Gr, Gb and B grids (4 x 13 x 17) */
	} light[TUNE_LIGHTS];
};
struct isp_tuning {
	struct isp_tune_set ccm, lsc;
	/*
	 * The white balance's reference lights, from the bluest to the reddest: each as the sensor sees a
	 * grey under it (red over green, blue over green), and the colour temperature its tables are
	 * picked by (tools/camtuning.py). Between them, the line the white balance keeps to.
	 */
	uint32_t        refs;
	float           ref[16][3];
	void            *file;
};

struct isp {
	float           wb[3];          /* the white balance's gains, green 1 */
	float           digital;        /* more gain, for what AE cannot reach with the sensor's */
	float           zoom;           /* the picture is the middle 1/zoom of the sensor each way (1: the whole of it) */
	bool            turned;         /* the picture turned half round (a sensor mounted the other way up) */
	float           ccm[3][3];      /* the colour matrix, camera RGB (white balanced) to linear sRGB; rows sum to 1 */
	struct isp_lsc  lsc;
	uint8_t         gamma[4096];    /* linear (959 above black is 3836) to 8 bits, sRGB's curve */
	uint32_t        asked_lines, asked_gain, asked_frame_lines;     /* what AE asked for last */
	bool            asked;
	uint32_t        max_frame_lines;        /* the longest frame AE may ask for (0: twice the shortest) */
	struct isp_tuning *tuning;              /* isp_load_tuning()'s, or none */
};

void isp_init(struct isp *isp);
/*
 * How sharp the picture is in a part of the frame (fractions of it, x0 < x1, y0 < y1): the squares of
 * green's steps between neighbouring blocks of 4x4 cells, over green's level squared -- higher is sharper,
 * the same scene at any exposure the same; and green's mean level there (level, may be NULL).
 */
float isp_sharpness(const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, float *level);
/* the levels, from every 4th cell of every 4th pair of lines (with the processor's lens shading and white balance, if isp) */
void isp_measure(const struct isp *isp, const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, struct isp_stats *s);
/* the exposure for the frames to come: true, and the command filled in, when it should change */
bool isp_ae(struct isp *isp, const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const struct isp_stats *s, struct hakios_camera_command *c);
/*
 * The white balance: grey world -- of the nearly grey, when enough is -- kept to the line of the
 * tuning's reference lights when there is one, a little of the way at a time.
 */
void isp_awb(struct isp *isp, const struct isp_stats *s);
/*
 * A picture of the frame, width x height, of the sensor's middle part with the picture's proportions
 * (rows from first_row to end_row only, for doing it in pieces). NV12: y and uv planes, full range (420f) or video
 * range (420v); BGRA: y only.
 */
void isp_render_nv12(const struct isp *isp, const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, uint8_t *y, size_t y_stride,
    uint8_t *uv, size_t uv_stride, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t first_row, uint32_t end_row, bool video_range);
void isp_render_bgra(const struct isp *isp, const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, uint8_t *out, size_t stride,
    uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t first_row, uint32_t end_row);
/*
 * Every pixel at the sensor's own size (f->width x f->height): the two colours a site does not have
 * from the same colour's sites around it (bilinear); rows from first_row to end_row (even), NV12.
 */
/*
 * A photograph, width x height: every pixel of the sensor's part the picture shows (the zoom's, turned as the
 * moving pictures are) demosaiced as isp_render_full_nv12() does, and scaled to the picture between the
 * two nearest lines and pixels; rows from first_row to end_row (even), NV12.
 */
void isp_render_still_nv12(const struct isp *isp, const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, uint8_t *y,
    size_t y_stride, uint8_t *uv, size_t uv_stride, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t first_row, uint32_t end_row,
    bool video_range);
void isp_render_full_nv12(const struct isp *isp, const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, uint8_t *y, size_t y_stride,
    uint8_t *uv, size_t uv_stride, uint32_t first_row, uint32_t end_row, bool video_range);
/*
 * Lens shading measured from a frame of a flat field (a white sheet held over the lens, evenly lit):
 * each colour's level at each grid point (a block's mean) over the brightest of its own; false if
 * the frame is too dark or clipped for it. min_ratio: the darkest point's level over the brightest's.
 */
bool isp_lsc_from_flat(struct isp *isp, const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, float *min_ratio);
void isp_set_ccm(struct isp *isp, const float m[9]);
/* the tuning in PATH (tools/camtuning.py's) in place of the one there was: false, and none, if it is not one */
bool isp_load_tuning(struct isp *isp, const char *path);
/* the colour matrix and lens shading for a scene of this lux index and colour temperature, from the tuning */
void isp_tune(struct isp *isp, float lux_index, float cct);
/* the colour temperature the white balance is at, by the tuning's reference lights (0: there are none) */
float isp_cct(const struct isp *isp);

#endif

```

`userland/src/camera_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * camera_test: the wide camera's frames as a program gets them (cam=5).
 *
 * usage: camera_test raw [FRAMES] [noae] [noawb] [keepraw|full] [ccm M] [sensor N]
 *        camera_test cycle [FRAMES]
 *        camera_test noise [SENSOR|all]
 *   raw: reads FRAMES frames (default 150) from the kernel's /dev/hakios-camera, with src/camera_isp.c's
 *   exposure (unless noae: the kernel's, boot-args cam_shutter and cam_gain) and white balance working
 *   on them, says what came and how fast, and leaves the last one as a picture for the host (xl
 *   camera: logs/, never the repository): one pixel a cell, NV12, or with full every pixel (bilinear
 *   demosaic, at the sensor's size), or with keepraw the frame itself.
 *   With sensor N, another sensor first (0 the macro, 1 the wide, 2 the front, 3 the ultra-wide); with
 *   noawb, no white balance (gains of 1: for colour bars, whose colours are known); with ccm M, the
 *   colour matrix M (nine numbers, row by row, separated by commas: a check of the matrix's path).
 *   cycle: each of the four sensors in turn, FRAMES frames each (default 30), the kernel's exposure:
 *   what came of each, and how long the change from one to the next took.
 *   noise: the sensor's black level and noise in the dark (the lens covered, or a dark room): at the
 *   longest exposure of its usual frame and 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x and its most gain, two frames each: per
 *   site of the 2x2 cell the mean (the black level), the temporal noise (the two frames' difference,
 *   over the square root of 2), the fixed pattern (what is left of the two frames' mean), the rows'
 *   noise (how much whole lines move together); for one sensor (0 to 3) or all four.
 */
#include <dispatch/dispatch.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include "camera_isp.h"

static double
ms_since(uint64_t then)
{
	static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;

	if (tb.denom == 0) {
		mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	}
	return (double)(mach_absolute_time() - then) * tb.numer / tb.denom / 1e6;
}

static double
ticks_ms(uint64_t ticks)
{
	static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;

	if (tb.denom == 0) {
		mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	}
	return (double)ticks * tb.numer / tb.denom / 1e6;
}

static const char *const sensor_names[4] = { "macro", "wide", "front", "ultra-wide" };

/* HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR: the kernel changes to that sensor (its usual mode) before the next frames */
static bool
choose_sensor(int device, unsigned n)
{
	struct hakios_camera_command c = { .command = HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR, .a = n, .b = ~0u };

	if (write(device, &c, sizeof(c)) != (ssize_t)sizeof(c)) {
		printf("camera_test: the %s camera cannot be chosen: %s\n", n < 4 ? sensor_names[n] : "?", strerror(errno));
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}

static int
cycle(int frames)
{
	int device = open(HAKIOS_CAMERA_DEVICE, O_RDWR), failures = 0;
	uint8_t *buffer = NULL;
	size_t size = 0;

	if (device < 0) {
		perror("camera_test: " HAKIOS_CAMERA_DEVICE);
		return 1;
	}
	for (unsigned n = 0; n < 4; n++) {
		struct hakios_camera_frame head, *f = &head;
		uint64_t asked = mach_absolute_time(), first = 0, last_seq = 0, first_seq = 0;
		int got = 0;
		ssize_t r;

		if (!choose_sensor(device, n)) {
			failures++;
			continue;
		}
		for (int tries = 0; (r = read(device, &head, sizeof(head))) < 0 && errno == EAGAIN && tries < 3; tries++) {
		}
		if (r != (ssize_t)sizeof(head) || memcmp(head.magic, HAKIOS_CAMERA_MAGIC, 8) != 0 || head.sensor != n) {
			printf("camera_test: the %s camera: no frames (%s, header of sensor %u)\n", sensor_names[n],
			    r < 0 ? strerror(errno) : "short", r == (ssize_t)sizeof(head) ? head.sensor : 99);
			failures++;
			if (r < 0 && errno == EIO) {
				break;
			}
			continue;
		}
		size_t want = sizeof(head) + (size_t)head.stride * head.height;

		if (want > size) {
			free(buffer);
			buffer = malloc(want);
			size = want;
		}
		double changed_ms = ms_since(asked);
		struct isp_stats s;

		for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
			r = read(device, buffer, want);
			if (r != (ssize_t)want) {
				printf("camera_test: the %s camera: a read gave %zd of %zu bytes (%s)\n", sensor_names[n], r, want,
				    r < 0 ? strerror(errno) : "short");
				break;
			}
			f = (struct hakios_camera_frame *)buffer;
			got++;
			first = first ? first : f->time;
			first_seq = first_seq ? first_seq : f->sequence;
			last_seq = f->sequence;
		}
		if (got == 0) {
			failures++;
			continue;
		}
		isp_measure(NULL, f, buffer + f->header_bytes, &s);
		printf("camera_test: the %s camera (sensor %u): %ux%u, stride %u, Bayer %u; the first frame %.0f ms after it was asked "
		    "for; %d frames of %llu in %.2f s (%.1f a second); R %.1f G %.1f B %.1f above black\n", sensor_names[n], f->sensor,
		    f->width, f->height, f->stride, f->bayer, changed_ms, got, last_seq - first_seq + 1, ticks_ms(f->time - first) / 1000,
		    got > 1 ? (got - 1) * 1000.0 / ticks_ms(f->time - first) : 0.0, s.mean[0], s.mean[1], s.mean[2]);
	}
	free(buffer);
	close(device);
	return failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}

/* the value of pixel x of line y of a RAW10 frame */
static inline int
raw10(const struct hakios_camera_frame *f, const uint8_t *raw, uint32_t x, uint32_t y)
{
	const uint8_t *g = raw + (size_t)y * f->stride + (size_t)(x >> 2) * 5;

	return g[x & 3] << 2 | (g[4] >> ((x & 3) * 2) & 3);
}

/* the next frame whose exposure is the one asked for (up to 12 tries) */
static bool
read_settled(int device, uint8_t *buffer, size_t bytes, uint32_t lines, uint32_t gain)
{
	for (int tries = 0; tries < 12; tries++) {
		const struct hakios_camera_frame *f = (const void *)buffer;

		if (read(device, buffer, bytes) != (ssize_t)bytes) {
			return false;
		}
		if (f->exposure_lines == lines && f->gain == gain) {
			return true;
		}
	}
	return false;
}

static int
noise_one(int device, unsigned n)
{
	struct hakios_camera_frame head;
	uint8_t *a, *b;
	size_t bytes;
	ssize_t r;

	if (!choose_sensor(device, n)) {
		return 1;
	}
	for (int tries = 0; (r = read(device, &head, sizeof(head))) < 0 && errno == EAGAIN && tries < 3; tries++) {
	}
	if (r != (ssize_t)sizeof(head) || head.sensor != n) {
		printf("camera_test: noise: no frames from the %s camera\n", sensor_names[n]);
		return 1;
	}
	bytes = sizeof(head) + (size_t)head.stride * head.height;
	a = malloc(bytes);
	b = malloc(bytes);
	uint32_t lines = head.frame_lines_min - head.margin, gains[5] = { 1, 2, 4, 8, 0 };

	printf("camera_test: noise of the %s camera: %ux%u, black %u, exposure %.1f ms (%u lines); per site of the cell (R, G1, "
	    "G2, B in its order) the mean, temporal noise, fixed pattern, and the rows' noise, in 10-bit steps\n", sensor_names[n],
	    head.width, head.height, head.black, lines * (double)head.line_ns / 1e6, lines);
	for (int k = 0; k < 5; k++) {
		uint32_t gain = gains[k] ? gains[k] * head.gain_unity : head.gain_max;
		struct hakios_camera_command c = { .command = HAKIOS_CAMERA_EXPOSURE, .a = lines, .b = gain, .c = 0 };

		if (gain > head.gain_max) {
			continue;
		}
		if (write(device, &c, sizeof(c)) != (ssize_t)sizeof(c) || !read_settled(device, a, bytes, lines, gain) ||
		    read(device, b, bytes) != (ssize_t)bytes) {
			printf("camera_test: noise: the %s camera at gain %u: no frames with that exposure\n", sensor_names[n], gain);
			continue;
		}
		const struct hakios_camera_frame *f = (const void *)a;
		const uint8_t *ra = a + f->header_bytes, *rb = b + f->header_bytes;
		double sum[4] = { 0 }, sumd2[4] = { 0 }, sumd[4] = { 0 }, summ2[4] = { 0 }, cnt[4] = { 0 };
		double rows = 0, rows2 = 0, nrows = 0;

		for (uint32_t y = 0; y + 1 < f->height; y += 2) {
			double row = 0, rn = 0;

			for (uint32_t x = 0; x + 1 < f->width; x += 8) {
				for (int site = 0; site < 4; site++) {
					uint32_t xx = x + (site & 1), yy = y + (site >> 1);
					int va = raw10(f, ra, xx, yy), vb = raw10(f, rb, xx, yy);
					double m = (va + vb) / 2.0, d = va - vb;

					sum[site] += m;
					summ2[site] += m * m;
					sumd[site] += d;
					sumd2[site] += d * d;
					cnt[site]++;
					row += m;
					rn++;
				}
			}
			row /= rn;
			rows += row;
			rows2 += row * row;
			nrows++;
		}
		char line[300];
		int at = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "camera_test:   gain %5.2fx:", (double)gain / f->gain_unity);

		for (int site = 0; site < 4; site++) {
			double mean = sum[site] / cnt[site], dmean = sumd[site] / cnt[site];
			double temporal = sqrt(sumd2[site] / cnt[site] - dmean * dmean) / sqrt(2.0);
			double spread = summ2[site] / cnt[site] - mean * mean;      /* the two frames' mean: fixed pattern and temporal / 2 */
			double fixed = spread > temporal * temporal / 2 ? sqrt(spread - temporal * temporal / 2) : 0;

			at += snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - (size_t)at, " %.2f/%.2f/%.2f", mean, temporal, fixed);
		}
		double rmean = rows / nrows;

		snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - (size_t)at, "; rows %.3f", sqrt(rows2 / nrows - rmean * rmean));
		printf("%s\n", line);
	}
	free(a);
	free(b);
	return 0;
}

static int
noise(const char *which)
{
	int device = open(HAKIOS_CAMERA_DEVICE, O_RDWR), failures = 0;

	if (device < 0) {
		perror("camera_test: " HAKIOS_CAMERA_DEVICE);
		return 1;
	}
	for (unsigned n = 0; n < 4; n++) {
		if (strcmp(which, "all") == 0 || (unsigned)atoi(which) == n) {
			failures += noise_one(device, n);
		}
	}
	close(device);
	return failures ? 1 : 0;
}

/* a piece of a picture of every pixel (one of 8 bands of lines, each an even number of them) */
struct full_job {
	const struct isp *isp;
	const struct hakios_camera_frame *f;
	const uint8_t *raw;
	uint8_t *y, *uv;
	uint32_t width;
};

static void
full_piece(void *context, size_t i)
{
	struct full_job *j = context;
	uint32_t rows = (j->f->height / 8 + 1) & ~1u, first = (uint32_t)i * rows, end = i == 7 ? j->f->height : first + rows;

	isp_render_full_nv12(j->isp, j->f, j->raw, j->y, j->width, j->uv, j->width, first, end, false);
}

static float ccm[9] = { 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1 };

static int
raw(int frames, bool ae, bool awb, bool keep_raw, bool full, int sensor)
{
	struct hakios_camera_frame head, *f;
	struct isp isp;
	struct isp_stats s;
	uint64_t started = mach_absolute_time(), previous = 0, first_seq = 0;
	size_t bytes;
	int device = open(HAKIOS_CAMERA_DEVICE, O_RDWR), got = 0, failures = 0;
	ssize_t n;

	if (device < 0) {
		perror("camera_test: " HAKIOS_CAMERA_DEVICE);
		return 1;
	}
	if (sensor >= 0 && !choose_sensor(device, (unsigned)sensor)) {
		return 1;
	}
	for (int tries = 0; (n = read(device, &head, sizeof(head))) < 0 && errno == EAGAIN && tries < 3; tries++) {
	}
	if (n != (ssize_t)sizeof(head) || memcmp(head.magic, HAKIOS_CAMERA_MAGIC, 8) != 0) {
		perror("camera_test: the first frame's header");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("camera_test: the first frame after %.0f ms: %ux%u, stride %u, Bayer %u, black %u, %u lines of %u ns a frame "
	    "(%.2f frames/s at the shortest), exposure %u lines, gain %u (%u is 1x)\n", ms_since(started), head.width, head.height,
	    head.stride, head.bayer, head.black, head.frame_lines_min, head.line_ns, 1e9 / ((double)head.frame_lines_min * head.line_ns),
	    head.exposure_lines, head.gain, head.gain_unity);
	bytes = sizeof(head) + (size_t)head.stride * head.height;
	f = malloc(bytes);
	isp_init(&isp);
	isp_set_ccm(&isp, ccm);
	while (got < frames && failures < 5) {
		struct hakios_camera_command c;
		uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time();

		n = read(device, f, bytes);
		if (n != (ssize_t)bytes) {
			printf("camera_test: a read gave %zd of %zu bytes (%s)\n", n, bytes, n < 0 ? strerror(errno) : "short");
			failures++;
			continue;
		}
		double read_ms = ms_since(t0);
		const uint8_t *raw = (const uint8_t *)f + f->header_bytes;

		got++;
		first_seq = first_seq ? first_seq : f->sequence;
		isp_measure(&isp, f, raw, &s);
		if (awb) {
			isp_awb(&isp, &s);
		}
		if (ae && isp_ae(&isp, f, &s, &c) && write(device, &c, sizeof(c)) != (ssize_t)sizeof(c)) {
			perror("camera_test: the exposure");
		}
		if (got <= 3 || got % 15 == 0) {
			printf("camera_test: frame %llu (%d read): %.1f ms after the last, read in %.1f ms; exposure %.2f ms (%u lines), gain "
			    "%.2fx, digital %.2fx, frame %.1f ms; R %.1f G %.1f B %.1f above black, 1 %% above %.0f; wb %.2f %.2f\n",
			    f->sequence, got, previous ? ticks_ms(f->time - previous) : 0.0, read_ms,
			    f->exposure_lines * (double)f->line_ns / 1e6, f->exposure_lines, (double)f->gain / f->gain_unity, isp.digital,
			    f->frame_lines * (double)f->line_ns / 1e6, s.mean[0], s.mean[1], s.mean[2], s.bright, isp.wb[0], isp.wb[2]);
		}
		previous = f->time;
	}
	if (got == 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	printf("camera_test: %d frames of %llu (%llu skipped) in %.1f s\n", got, f->sequence - first_seq + 1,
	    f->sequence - first_seq + 1 - got, ms_since(started) / 1000);

	if (keep_raw) {
		struct hakios_camera_command *k = (struct hakios_camera_command *)((uint8_t *)f + f->header_bytes) - 1;
		uint32_t frame_bytes = f->stride * f->height, w = f->width, h = f->height, stride = f->stride;

		/* (the command goes over the end of the header, just before the frame's bytes) */
		memset(k, 0, sizeof(*k));
		k->command = HAKIOS_CAMERA_KEEP;
		k->bytes = frame_bytes;
		k->a = w;
		k->b = h;
		k->c = stride;
		k->d = 1;
		if (write(device, k, sizeof(*k) + frame_bytes) != (ssize_t)(sizeof(*k) + frame_bytes)) {
			perror("camera_test: the frame for the host");
		} else {
			printf("camera_test: the frame (RAW10) is the host's (xl camera)\n");
		}
		close(device);
		return 0;
	}
	/* the last one, as a picture for the host: one pixel per cell, or every pixel; NV12 */
	uint32_t w = full ? f->width : f->width / 2, h = full ? f->height : f->height / 2;
	size_t picture = (size_t)w * h * 3 / 2;
	struct hakios_camera_command *keep = malloc(sizeof(*keep) + picture);
	uint8_t *y = (uint8_t *)(keep + 1);
	uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time();

	if (full) {
		struct full_job job = { &isp, f, (const uint8_t *)f + f->header_bytes, y, y + (size_t)w * h, w };

		dispatch_apply_f(8, dispatch_get_global_queue(QOS_CLASS_USER_INITIATED, 0), &job, full_piece);
	} else {
		isp_render_nv12(&isp, f, (const uint8_t *)f + f->header_bytes, y, w, y + (size_t)w * h, w, w, h, 0, h, false);
	}
	printf("camera_test: the picture (%ux%u NV12%s) made in %.1f ms\n", w, h, full ? ", every pixel" : "", ms_since(t0));
	memset(keep, 0, sizeof(*keep));
	keep->command = HAKIOS_CAMERA_KEEP;
	keep->bytes = (uint32_t)picture;
	keep->a = w;
	keep->b = h;
	keep->c = w;
	keep->d = 2;
	if (write(device, keep, sizeof(*keep) + picture) != (ssize_t)(sizeof(*keep) + picture)) {
		perror("camera_test: the picture for the host");
	} else {
		printf("camera_test: the picture is the host's (xl camera)\n");
	}
	close(device);
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
	if (argc >= 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "raw") == 0) {
		bool ae = true, awb = true, keep_raw = false, full = false;
		int sensor = -1;

		for (int i = 3; i < argc; i++) {
			ae = ae && strcmp(argv[i], "noae") != 0;
			awb = awb && strcmp(argv[i], "noawb") != 0;
			keep_raw = keep_raw || strcmp(argv[i], "keepraw") == 0;
			full = full || strcmp(argv[i], "full") == 0;
			if (strcmp(argv[i], "ccm") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
				const char *at = argv[++i];

				for (int k = 0; k < 9 && at != NULL; k++) {
					ccm[k] = strtof(at, NULL);
					at = strchr(at, ',');
					at = at != NULL ? at + 1 : NULL;
				}
				printf("camera_test: the colour matrix %.2f %.2f %.2f / %.2f %.2f %.2f / %.2f %.2f %.2f\n", ccm[0], ccm[1],
				    ccm[2], ccm[3], ccm[4], ccm[5], ccm[6], ccm[7], ccm[8]);
			}
			if (strcmp(argv[i], "sensor") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
				sensor = atoi(argv[++i]);
			}
		}
		return raw(argc >= 3 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 150, ae, awb, keep_raw, full, sensor);
	}
	if (argc >= 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "noise") == 0) {
		return noise(argc >= 3 ? argv[2] : "all");
	}
	if (argc >= 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "cycle") == 0) {
		return cycle(argc >= 3 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 30);
	}
	fprintf(stderr, "usage: camera_test raw [FRAMES] [noae] [noawb] [keepraw|full] [ccm M] [sensor N]\n       camera_test cycle [FRAMES]\n       camera_test noise [SENSOR|all]\n");
	return 2;
}
```

`userland/src/cg_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * cg_test: CoreGraphics drawing into an IOSurface, the way WebKit's GPU process draws a web page's
 * tiles (WebCore::IOSurface::createPlatformContext: CGIOSurfaceContextCreate), and the plain way
 * for comparison (a bitmap context on the surface's locked memory). Says, for each, whether a red
 * rectangle drawn and flushed ends up in the surface's memory.
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreGraphics/CoreGraphics.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurfaceRef.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <spawn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>

extern char **environ;

#define SIZE 256

static CFNumberRef
num(int value)
{
	return CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, &value);
}

static IOSurfaceRef
make_surface(void)
{
	CFMutableDictionaryRef props = CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks,
	    &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	CFNumberRef n;
	IOSurfaceRef surface;

	n = num(SIZE); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceWidth, n); CFRelease(n);
	n = num(SIZE); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceHeight, n); CFRelease(n);
	n = num(4); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceBytesPerElement, n); CFRelease(n);
	n = num(SIZE * 4); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceBytesPerRow, n); CFRelease(n);
	n = num('BGRA'); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfacePixelFormat, n); CFRelease(n);
	n = num(SIZE * SIZE * 4); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceAllocSize, n); CFRelease(n);
	surface = IOSurfaceCreate(props);
	CFRelease(props);
	return surface;
}

/* how many pixels are red, and what the one at 10,10 is */
static void
look(const char *what, IOSurfaceRef surface)
{
	uint32_t seed = 0, red = 0, zero = 0, first;
	const uint32_t *pixels;

	IOSurfaceLock(surface, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, &seed);
	pixels = IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface);
	for (int i = 0; i < SIZE * SIZE; i++) {
		red += pixels[i] == 0xffff0000;
		zero += pixels[i] == 0;
	}
	first = pixels[10 * SIZE + 10];
	IOSurfaceUnlock(surface, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, &seed);
	printf("cg_test: %s: %u of %u pixels red, %u zero, the one at 10,10 %#010x (seed %u)\n", what, red, SIZE * SIZE, zero, first,
	    IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface));
}

/* a second process looks the surface up by its number and says what it sees there */
static void
seen_elsewhere(const char *self, IOSurfaceRef surface)
{
	char number[16];
	char *args[] = { (char *)self, "child", number, NULL };
	pid_t pid;
	int status;

	snprintf(number, sizeof(number), "%u", IOSurfaceGetID(surface));
	if (posix_spawn(&pid, self, NULL, NULL, args, environ) == 0) {
		waitpid(pid, &status, 0);
	}
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	if (argc == 3 && strcmp(argv[1], "child") == 0) {
		IOSurfaceRef surface = IOSurfaceLookup((IOSurfaceID)atoi(argv[2]));

		if (surface == NULL) {
			printf("cg_test: (another process) surface %s not found\n", argv[2]);
			return 1;
		}
		look("(another process)", surface);
		return 0;
	}
	CGContextRef (*create)(IOSurfaceRef, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, CGColorSpaceRef, CGBitmapInfo) =
	    (CGContextRef (*)(IOSurfaceRef, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, CGColorSpaceRef, CGBitmapInfo))dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT,
	    "CGIOSurfaceContextCreate");
	CGColorSpaceRef space = CGColorSpaceCreateWithName(kCGColorSpaceSRGB);
	CGBitmapInfo info = kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedFirst | kCGBitmapByteOrder32Little;
	IOSurfaceRef surface = make_surface(), plain = make_surface();
	CGContextRef context;
	uint32_t seed = 0;

	if (surface == NULL || plain == NULL) {
		printf("cg_test: IOSurfaceCreate failed\n");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("cg_test: surfaces %u and %u, %zu bytes a row; CGIOSurfaceContextCreate is %s\n", IOSurfaceGetID(surface),
	    IOSurfaceGetID(plain), IOSurfaceGetBytesPerRow(surface), create ? "there" : "NOT THERE");
	look("before", surface);

	/* WebKit's way */
	if (create != NULL && (context = create(surface, SIZE, SIZE, 8, 32, space, info)) != NULL) {
		CGContextSetRGBFillColor(context, 1, 0, 0, 1);
		CGContextFillRect(context, CGRectMake(0, 0, SIZE, SIZE));
		CGContextFlush(context);
		look("CGIOSurfaceContext, filled and flushed", surface);
		CGContextRelease(context);
		look("CGIOSurfaceContext, released", surface);
		seen_elsewhere(argv[0], surface);
	} else {
		printf("cg_test: CGIOSurfaceContextCreate gave no context\n");
	}

	/* the plain way */
	IOSurfaceLock(plain, 0, &seed);
	context = CGBitmapContextCreate(IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(plain), SIZE, SIZE, 8, IOSurfaceGetBytesPerRow(plain), space, info);
	if (context != NULL) {
		CGContextSetRGBFillColor(context, 1, 0, 0, 1);
		CGContextFillRect(context, CGRectMake(0, 0, SIZE, SIZE));
		CGContextRelease(context);
	}
	IOSurfaceUnlock(plain, 0, &seed);
	look("a bitmap context on the locked memory", plain);
	seen_elsewhere(argv[0], plain);
	return 0;
}
```

```c
/*

 * a status the parent checks.

#include "mini.h"

int
main(int argc, char **argv, char **envp)
{
	printf("  child: pid %d, parent %d, %d arguments:", getpid(), getppid(), argc);
	for (int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
		printf(" [%s]", argv[i]);
	}
	printf("\n  child: environment:");
	for (char **e = envp; *e; e++) {

	}
```

`userland/src/cow_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * cow_test: is what is copied really a copy, and what is written really seen? For each of the ways
 * a picture's bytes go from one place to another -- sent out of line with a virtual copy, vm_copy()
 * into memory that is there already, a memory entry made as a copy (how XPC hands large data over),
 * a file written with write() while it is mapped -- a buffer of an icon's size (180 x 180 x 4) is
 * filled, copied or written, and the source written over afterwards; every 16K page of the result
 * must be what it should be. Page-aligned and 4224 bytes into a page (where the broken Calendar
 * icon's bytes lay: its first and last pages shared with what is around it), from memory of our
 * own, from malloc, from purgeable memory, with the source or the destination wired (mlock), with
 * the received copy made read-only and then wired or with a surface made around it the way
 * CoreAnimation's window server makes one around a picture (MiniIOSurface.cpp), and with a file's
 * mapping wired before it is written: that last one is the Calendar icon's case, which the ramfs
 * got wrong (it threw cached pages away after a write and could not throw away wired ones; see
 * ramfs_refresh_cache()).
 * Run by RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.cow ("cow_test files": only the file cases). Every line should end with
 * no page wrong.
 */
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurfaceRef.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

struct sent {
	mach_msg_header_t header;
	mach_msg_body_t body;
	mach_msg_ool_descriptor_t data;
};

struct got {
	struct sent message;
	mach_msg_trailer_t trailer;
};

static void
one(const char *what, unsigned char *buffer, size_t size, int touch_neighbours)
{
	mach_port_t port;
	struct sent m;
	struct got g;
	kern_return_t kr;
	size_t page = (size_t)getpagesize(), changed = 0, pages = 0;
	char line[512] = "";
	size_t used = 0;

	mach_port_allocate(mach_task_self(), MACH_PORT_RIGHT_RECEIVE, &port);
	mach_port_insert_right(mach_task_self(), port, port, MACH_MSG_TYPE_MAKE_SEND);
	memset(buffer, 0x11, size);
	memset(&m, 0, sizeof(m));
	m.header.msgh_bits = MACH_MSGH_BITS(MACH_MSG_TYPE_COPY_SEND, 0) | MACH_MSGH_BITS_COMPLEX;
	m.header.msgh_size = sizeof(m);
	m.header.msgh_remote_port = port;
	m.body.msgh_descriptor_count = 1;
	m.data.address = buffer;
	m.data.size = (mach_msg_size_t)size;
	m.data.deallocate = 0;
	m.data.copy = MACH_MSG_VIRTUAL_COPY;
	m.data.type = MACH_MSG_OOL_DESCRIPTOR;
	kr = mach_msg(&m.header, MACH_SEND_MSG, sizeof(m), 0, MACH_PORT_NULL, 0, MACH_PORT_NULL);
	if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		printf("cow_test: %s: send failed %#x\n", what, kr);
		return;
	}
	if (touch_neighbours) {
		/* what is before and after it in its first and last page, written first */
		uintptr_t first = (uintptr_t)buffer & ~(page - 1), end = ((uintptr_t)buffer + size + page - 1) & ~(page - 1);

		memset((void *)first, 0x33, (uintptr_t)buffer - first);
		memset(buffer + size, 0x33, end - ((uintptr_t)buffer + size));
	}
	memset(buffer, 0x22, size);
	memset(&g, 0, sizeof(g));
	kr = mach_msg(&g.message.header, MACH_RCV_MSG, 0, sizeof(g), port, 0, MACH_PORT_NULL);
	if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		printf("cow_test: %s: receive failed %#x\n", what, kr);
		return;
	}
	{
		const unsigned char *got = g.message.data.address;
		uintptr_t start = (uintptr_t)got;

		for (size_t at = 0; at < size;) {
			size_t next = ((start + at) & ~(page - 1)) + page - start, end = next < size ? next : size, bad = 0;

			for (size_t i = at; i < end; i++) {
				bad += got[i] != 0x11;
			}
			if (bad != 0 && used < sizeof(line) - 40) {
				used += (size_t)snprintf(line + used, sizeof(line) - used, " page %zu (bytes %zu-%zu): %zu", pages, at, end, bad);
			}
			changed += bad != 0;
			pages++;
			at = end;
		}
		printf("cow_test: %s (%zu bytes, %zu into its page, received %zu into its page): %zu of %zu pages show what was "
		    "written after the send%s%s\n", what, size, (size_t)((uintptr_t)buffer & (page - 1)), (size_t)(start & (page - 1)),
		    changed, pages, changed ? ":" : "", line);
		vm_deallocate(mach_task_self(), (vm_address_t)got, size);
	}
	mach_port_destroy(mach_task_self(), port);
}

/* vm_copy() into memory that is there already (what a picture's copy-on-write snapshot may be made with) */
static void
two(const char *what, unsigned char *from, unsigned char *to, size_t size, int write_after)
{
	size_t page = (size_t)getpagesize(), pages = 0, bad_pages = 0;
	char line[512] = "";
	size_t used = 0;
	kern_return_t kr;

	memset(from, 0x11, size);
	memset(to, 0x44, size);
	kr = vm_copy(mach_task_self(), (vm_address_t)from, size, (vm_address_t)to);
	if (write_after == 1) {
		memset(from, 0x22, size);               /* the source written after the copy */
	} else if (write_after == 2) {
		memset(to + size / 2, 0x55, 1);         /* the copy written in one place */
	}
	for (size_t at = 0; at < size;) {
		size_t next = (((uintptr_t)to + at) & ~(page - 1)) + page - (uintptr_t)to, end = next < size ? next : size, bad = 0;

		for (size_t i = at; i < end; i++) {
			bad += to[i] != 0x11 && !(write_after == 2 && i == size / 2);
		}
		if (bad != 0 && used < sizeof(line) - 40) {
			used += (size_t)snprintf(line + used, sizeof(line) - used, " page %zu (bytes %zu-%zu): %zu", pages, at, end, bad);
		}
		bad_pages += bad != 0;
		pages++;
		at = end;
	}
	if (write_after == 2) {
		size_t leaked = 0;

		for (size_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
			leaked += from[i] != 0x11;
		}
		used += (size_t)snprintf(line + used, sizeof(line) - used, "; the source changed in %zu bytes", leaked);
	}
	printf("cow_test: vm_copy %s (%zu bytes, from %zu into its page to %zu into its): %#x; %zu of %zu pages of the copy wrong%s\n",
	    what, size, (size_t)((uintptr_t)from & (page - 1)), (size_t)((uintptr_t)to & (page - 1)), kr, bad_pages, pages, line);
}

/* sent out of line, received, the copy wired (as a surface around it would be), and only then the source written */
static void
three(const char *what, unsigned char *buffer, size_t size, int surface_mode)
{
	IOSurfaceRef surface = NULL;
	mach_port_t port;
	struct sent m;
	struct got g;
	size_t page = (size_t)getpagesize(), changed = 0, pages = 0;
	char line[512] = "";
	size_t used = 0;
	int locked;

	mach_port_allocate(mach_task_self(), MACH_PORT_RIGHT_RECEIVE, &port);
	mach_port_insert_right(mach_task_self(), port, port, MACH_MSG_TYPE_MAKE_SEND);
	memset(buffer, 0x11, size);
	memset(&m, 0, sizeof(m));
	m.header.msgh_bits = MACH_MSGH_BITS(MACH_MSG_TYPE_COPY_SEND, 0) | MACH_MSGH_BITS_COMPLEX;
	m.header.msgh_size = sizeof(m);
	m.header.msgh_remote_port = port;
	m.body.msgh_descriptor_count = 1;
	m.data.address = buffer;
	m.data.size = (mach_msg_size_t)size;
	m.data.copy = MACH_MSG_VIRTUAL_COPY;
	m.data.type = MACH_MSG_OOL_DESCRIPTOR;
	mach_msg(&m.header, MACH_SEND_MSG, sizeof(m), 0, MACH_PORT_NULL, 0, MACH_PORT_NULL);
	memset(&g, 0, sizeof(g));
	mach_msg(&g.message.header, MACH_RCV_MSG, 0, sizeof(g), port, 0, MACH_PORT_NULL);
	{
		const unsigned char *got = g.message.data.address;
		uintptr_t start = (uintptr_t)got;

		vm_protect(mach_task_self(), (vm_address_t)got & ~(page - 1), ((start + size + page - 1) & ~(page - 1)) - (start & ~(page - 1)), 0, VM_PROT_READ);
		if (!surface_mode) {
			locked = mlock((const void *)((uintptr_t)got & ~(page - 1)), ((start + size + page - 1) & ~(page - 1)) - (start & ~(page - 1)));
		} else {
			/* a surface made around the received copy, as CoreAnimation's window server does with a picture */
			CFMutableDictionaryRef d = CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
			long long address = (long long)start, w = 180, h = 180, row = 720, bpe = 4, alloc = (long long)size, format = 0;
			struct { CFStringRef key; long long *value; } values[] = { { CFSTR("IOSurfaceAddress"), &address },
				{ CFSTR("IOSurfaceWidth"), &w }, { CFSTR("IOSurfaceHeight"), &h }, { CFSTR("IOSurfaceBytesPerRow"), &row },
				{ CFSTR("IOSurfaceBytesPerElement"), &bpe }, { CFSTR("IOSurfaceAllocSize"), &alloc },
				{ CFSTR("IOSurfacePixelFormat"), &format } };

			for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(values) / sizeof(values[0]); i++) {
				CFNumberRef n = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberLongLongType, values[i].value);

				CFDictionarySetValue(d, values[i].key, n);
				CFRelease(n);
			}
			surface = IOSurfaceCreate(d);
			locked = surface != NULL ? 0 : -1;
			CFRelease(d);
		}
		memset(buffer, 0x22, size);
		for (size_t at = 0; at < size;) {
			size_t next = ((start + at) & ~(page - 1)) + page - start, end = next < size ? next : size, bad = 0;

			for (size_t i = at; i < end; i++) {
				bad += got[i] != 0x11;
			}
			if (bad != 0 && used < sizeof(line) - 40) {
				used += (size_t)snprintf(line + used, sizeof(line) - used, " page %zu (bytes %zu-%zu): %zu", pages, at, end, bad);
			}
			changed += bad != 0;
			pages++;
			at = end;
		}
		{
			size_t source_bad = 0;

			for (size_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
				source_bad += buffer[i] != 0x22;
			}
			printf("cow_test: %s (wired or surface made: %d, 0 is yes): %zu of %zu pages of the received copy show what was written after; the source "
			    "itself has %zu bytes that are not what was written to it%s\n", what, locked, changed, pages, source_bad, line);
		}
	}
	if (surface != NULL) {
		CFRelease(surface);
	}
	mach_port_destroy(mach_task_self(), port);
}

/* a memory entry made as a copy of memory (what XPC hands large data over with), mapped, and the source written after */
static void
four(const char *what, unsigned char *buffer, size_t size, int flags)
{
	size_t page = (size_t)getpagesize(), changed = 0, pages = 0;
	memory_object_size_t entry_size = size;
	mach_port_t entry = MACH_PORT_NULL;
	vm_address_t mapped = 0;
	kern_return_t kr, km = KERN_FAILURE;
	char line[512] = "";
	size_t used = 0, offset = (uintptr_t)buffer & (page - 1);

	memset(buffer, 0x11, size);
	kr = mach_make_memory_entry_64(mach_task_self(), &entry_size, (memory_object_offset_t)(uintptr_t)buffer,
	    VM_PROT_READ | flags, &entry, MACH_PORT_NULL);
	if (kr == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		km = vm_map(mach_task_self(), &mapped, entry_size, 0, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE, entry, 0, 0, VM_PROT_READ, VM_PROT_READ,
		    VM_INHERIT_NONE);
	}
	memset(buffer, 0x22, size);
	if (km == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		/* where the bytes are in the mapping: at the entry's own offset if the entry starts on a page, else at 0 */
		const unsigned char *got = (const unsigned char *)mapped + (entry_size >= size + offset ? offset : 0);
		uintptr_t start = (uintptr_t)got;

		for (size_t at = 0; at < size;) {
			size_t next = ((start + at) & ~(page - 1)) + page - start, end = next < size ? next : size, bad = 0;

			for (size_t i = at; i < end; i++) {
				bad += got[i] != 0x11;
			}
			if (bad != 0 && used < sizeof(line) - 40) {
				used += (size_t)snprintf(line + used, sizeof(line) - used, " page %zu (bytes %zu-%zu): %zu", pages, at, end, bad);
			}
			changed += bad != 0;
			pages++;
			at = end;
		}
		vm_deallocate(mach_task_self(), mapped, entry_size);
	}
	printf("cow_test: memory entry, %s (%zu bytes, %zu into its page): entry %#x, %llu bytes, mapped %#x; %zu of %zu pages show "
	    "what was written after%s\n", what, size, offset, kr, (unsigned long long)entry_size, km, changed, pages, line);
	if (entry != MACH_PORT_NULL) {
		mach_port_deallocate(mach_task_self(), entry);
	}
}

/*
 * A file that one program has mapped while another writes it (an icon cache read by SpringBoard and
 * written by iconservicesagent): written with write() at a place that does not start on a page, the
 * mapping must show what was written, in every page of it. `touch`: which pages of the mapping were
 * read before the write (0 none, 1 the first and the last, 2 all).
 */
static void
five(const char *what, const char *path, size_t offset, size_t size, int touch, int twice, int wire)
{
	size_t page = (size_t)getpagesize(), file_size = 16 * page, changed = 0, pages = 0;
	unsigned char *data = malloc(size), *zero = calloc(1, file_size);
	const unsigned char *map;
	char line[512] = "";
	size_t used = 0;
	int fd = open(path, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0600);

	if (fd < 0 || data == NULL || zero == NULL) {
		printf("cow_test: file, %s: cannot open %s\n", what, path);
		return;
	}
	write(fd, zero, file_size);
	map = mmap(NULL, file_size, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
	if (map == MAP_FAILED) {
		printf("cow_test: file, %s: cannot map\n", what);
		close(fd);
		return;
	}
	if (twice) {
		memset(data, 0x33, size);               /* a first version, read through the mapping, then the second */
		pwrite(fd, data, size, (off_t)offset);
		for (size_t at = 0; at < size; at += page / 2) {
			(void)*(volatile const unsigned char *)(map + offset + at);
		}
	}
	for (size_t at = 0; touch && at < file_size; at += page) {
		if (touch == 2 || at == (offset & ~(page - 1)) || at == ((offset + size - 1) & ~(page - 1))) {
			(void)*(volatile const unsigned char *)(map + at);
		}
	}
	if (wire) {
		/* the mapping's pages held in memory, as a surface made around them holds them */
		mlock(map, file_size);
	}
	memset(data, 0x11, size);
	pwrite(fd, data, size, (off_t)offset);
	for (size_t at = 0; at < size;) {
		size_t next = ((offset + at) & ~(page - 1)) + page - offset, end = next < size ? next : size, bad = 0;

		for (size_t i = at; i < end; i++) {
			bad += map[offset + i] != 0x11;
		}
		if (bad != 0 && used < sizeof(line) - 40) {
			used += (size_t)snprintf(line + used, sizeof(line) - used, " page %zu (bytes %zu-%zu): %zu", pages, at, end, bad);
		}
		changed += bad != 0;
		pages++;
		at = end;
	}
	printf("cow_test: file, %s (%zu bytes at %zu in %s): %zu of %zu pages of the mapping do not show what was written%s\n",
	    what, size, offset, path, changed, pages, line);
	if (wire) {
		munlock(map, file_size);
	}
	munmap((void *)map, file_size);
	close(fd);
	unlink(path);
	free(data);
	free(zero);
}

static void
files(size_t size)
{
	five("mapped, nothing read, then written", "/private/var/tmp/cow_test.data", 4224, size, 0, 0, 0);
	five("mapped, its first and last page read, then written", "/private/var/tmp/cow_test.data", 4224, size, 1, 0, 0);
	five("mapped, all read, then written", "/private/var/tmp/cow_test.data", 4224, size, 2, 0, 0);
	five("written, read through the mapping, written again", "/private/var/tmp/cow_test.data", 4224, size, 0, 1, 0);
	five("written, read through the mapping, written again (aligned)", "/private/var/tmp/cow_test.data", 0, size, 0, 1, 0);
	five("mapped, wired, then written", "/private/var/tmp/cow_test.data", 4224, size, 2, 0, 1);
	five("written, read, wired, written again", "/private/var/tmp/cow_test.data", 4224, size, 0, 1, 1);
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	size_t size = 180 * 720, page = (size_t)getpagesize();
	vm_address_t region = 0;

	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
	printf("cow_test: pages of %zu bytes\n", page);
	files(size);                    /* (first: the rest makes surfaces, which a kernel that breaks may not survive) */
	if (argc > 1 && strcmp(argv[1], "files") == 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	vm_allocate(mach_task_self(), &region, size + 4 * page, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE);
	one("a region of our own, page-aligned", (unsigned char *)region, size, 0);
	one("a region of our own, 4224 bytes in", (unsigned char *)region + 4224, size, 0);
	one("a region of our own, 4224 bytes in, neighbours written first", (unsigned char *)region + 4224, size, 1);
	{
		vm_address_t a = 0, b = 0;

		vm_allocate(mach_task_self(), &a, size + 4 * page, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE);
		vm_allocate(mach_task_self(), &b, size + 4 * page, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE);
		memset((void *)b, 0x66, size + 4 * page);       /* (the destination's pages in use already) */
		two("aligned", (unsigned char *)a, (unsigned char *)b, size, 0);
		two("aligned, source written after", (unsigned char *)a, (unsigned char *)b, size, 1);
		two("aligned, copy written after", (unsigned char *)a, (unsigned char *)b, size, 2);
		two("4224 in both", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, (unsigned char *)b + 4224, size, 0);
		two("4224 in both, source written after", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, (unsigned char *)b + 4224, size, 1);
		two("4224 in both, copy written after", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, (unsigned char *)b + 4224, size, 2);
		two("4224 and 2816", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, (unsigned char *)b + 2816, size, 1);
		three("received, made read-only and wired, then the source written (aligned)", (unsigned char *)a, size, 0);
		three("received, made read-only and wired, then the source written (4224 in)", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, size, 0);
		three("received, made read-only, a surface made around it, then the source written (aligned)", (unsigned char *)a, size, 1);
		three("received, made read-only, a surface made around it, then the source written (4224 in)", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, size, 1);
		{
			unsigned char *heap = malloc(size);

			three("malloc, received, made read-only, a surface made around it, then the source written", heap, size, 1);
		}
		{
			vm_address_t p = 0, q = 0;
			kern_return_t kp = vm_allocate(mach_task_self(), &p, size + 4 * page, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE | VM_FLAGS_PURGABLE);
			kern_return_t kq = vm_allocate(mach_task_self(), &q, size + 4 * page, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE | VM_FLAGS_PURGABLE);

			printf("cow_test: purgeable regions: %#x %#x\n", kp, kq);
			two("purgeable source, aligned, source written after", (unsigned char *)p, (unsigned char *)b, size, 1);
			two("purgeable source, 4224 in both, source written after", (unsigned char *)p + 4224, (unsigned char *)b + 4224, size, 1);
			two("purgeable both, 4224 in both, source written after", (unsigned char *)p + 4224, (unsigned char *)q + 4224, size, 1);
			two("purgeable destination, 4224 in both, source written after", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, (unsigned char *)q + 4224, size, 1);
			one("OOL from a purgeable region, 4224 bytes in", (unsigned char *)p + 4224, size, 0);
			three("OOL from a purgeable region, received, a surface made around it, then the source written (4224 in)",
			    (unsigned char *)p + 4224, size, 1);
		}
		four("a copy (MAP_MEM_VM_COPY), aligned", (unsigned char *)a, size, MAP_MEM_VM_COPY);
		four("a copy (MAP_MEM_VM_COPY), 4224 in", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, size, MAP_MEM_VM_COPY);
		four("a copy (MAP_MEM_VM_COPY), 2816 in", (unsigned char *)a + 2816, size, MAP_MEM_VM_COPY);
		printf("cow_test: the source locked in memory (wired): mlock %d\n", mlock((void *)a, size + 4 * page));
		two("wired source, aligned, source written after", (unsigned char *)a, (unsigned char *)b, size, 1);
		two("wired source, 4224 in both, source written after", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, (unsigned char *)b + 4224, size, 1);
		one("OOL from a wired region, 4224 bytes in", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, size, 0);
		munlock((void *)a, size + 4 * page);
		printf("cow_test: the destination locked in memory (wired): mlock %d\n", mlock((void *)b, size + 4 * page));
		two("wired destination, 4224 in both, source written after", (unsigned char *)a + 4224, (unsigned char *)b + 4224, size, 1);
		munlock((void *)b, size + 4 * page);
	}
	{
		unsigned char *heap = malloc(size);

		one("malloc", heap, size, 0);
		one("malloc, neighbours written first", heap, size, 1);
	}
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/cpu_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * How many processors the kernel has, and whether they really work at the same time: a fixed
 * amount of arithmetic on one thread, then the same on each of as many threads as there are
 * processors (two at least), and how much processor time the threads were given between
 * them while that took: with one processor never more than the time that passed, with
 * several of them free several times as much.
 *
 * usage: cpu_test [SECONDS]    without an argument only the numbers; with one, wait that long
 *                             (for a moment when the system is quiet) and then do the work
 */
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <sys/resource.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define ROUNDS  60000000ULL
#define MOST    16

static int
number(const char *name)
{
	int value = -1;
	size_t size = sizeof(value);

	sysctlbyname(name, &value, &size, NULL, 0);
	return value;
}

static uint64_t
milliseconds(void)
{
	static mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;

	if (timebase.denom == 0) {
		mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
	}
	return mach_absolute_time() * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1000000;
}

/* The processor time this process has used so far, in milliseconds. */
static uint64_t
used(void)
{
	struct rusage usage;

	getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &usage);
	return (uint64_t)(usage.ru_utime.tv_sec + usage.ru_stime.tv_sec) * 1000 +
	       (uint64_t)(usage.ru_utime.tv_usec + usage.ru_stime.tv_usec) / 1000;
}

/* The work; says which processor it found itself on at the end. */
static void *
work(void *arg)
{
	volatile uint64_t sum = 0;
	size_t cpu = 0;

	for (uint64_t i = 0; i < ROUNDS; i++) {
		sum += i * i;
	}
	pthread_cpu_number_np(&cpu);
	*(int *)arg = (int)cpu;
	return NULL;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int active = number("hw.activecpu"), threads = active < 2 ? 2 : active > MOST ? MOST : active;
	int where[MOST], seen = 0;
	pthread_t thread[MOST];
	uint64_t start, alone, together, spent;

	if (argc > 1) {
		sleep((unsigned)atoi(argv[1]));
	}
	printf("cpu_test: hw.ncpu %d, hw.activecpu %d, hw.physicalcpu %d, hw.logicalcpu %d\n", number("hw.ncpu"),
	    number("hw.activecpu"), number("hw.physicalcpu"), number("hw.logicalcpu"));
	if (argc < 2) {
		return 0;
	}

	start = milliseconds();
	work(&where[0]);
	alone = milliseconds() - start;

	start = milliseconds();
	spent = used();
	for (int i = 0; i < threads; i++) {
		pthread_create(&thread[i], NULL, work, &where[i]);
	}
	for (int i = 0; i < threads; i++) {
		pthread_join(thread[i], NULL);
		seen |= 1 << where[i];
	}
	spent = used() - spent;
	together = milliseconds() - start;
	if (together == 0) {
		together = 1;
	}

	printf("cpu_test: one thread took %llu ms; %d threads at once took %llu ms and were given %llu ms of processor time: "
	    "%llu.%llu processors at work, seen on", alone, threads, together, spent, spent / together, spent * 10 / together % 10);
	for (int cpu = 0; cpu < 32; cpu++) {
		if (seen & (1 << cpu)) {
			printf(" %d", cpu);
		}
	}
	printf("\n");
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/cputop.c`:

```c
/*
 * Which processes take the processors: every few seconds, the processor time each process was given since the
 * last look (user and system together), the most first, as one line for the run's log:
 *
 *   cputop: 25 s: 412% in all: backboardd[13] 96% SpringBoard[41] 88% WeatherWidget[131] 40% ...
 *
 * (100% is one core's whole time.) tools/frames.py says when the cores were all busy ("cores busy") while the
 * window server's frames came late; this says with whom it shared them. A process born since the last look counts
 * with all the time it has had.
 *
 *   usage: cputop [SECONDS [LOOKS]]     every SECONDS (default 5), LOOKS times (default: until the run ends)
 */
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/* libproc's, which the iPhoneOS SDK does not declare (XNU's bsd/sys/proc_info.h, libsyscall/wrappers/libproc) */
#define PROC_ALL_PIDS           1
#define PROC_PIDTASKINFO        4
struct proc_taskinfo {
	uint64_t pti_virtual_size;
	uint64_t pti_resident_size;
	uint64_t pti_total_user;        /* in mach_absolute_time's units */
	uint64_t pti_total_system;
	uint64_t pti_threads_user;
	uint64_t pti_threads_system;
	int32_t pti_policy;
	int32_t pti_faults;
	int32_t pti_pageins;
	int32_t pti_cow_faults;
	int32_t pti_messages_sent;
	int32_t pti_messages_received;
	int32_t pti_syscalls_mach;
	int32_t pti_syscalls_unix;
	int32_t pti_csw;
	int32_t pti_threadnum;
	int32_t pti_numrunning;
	int32_t pti_priority;
};
int proc_listpids(uint32_t type, uint32_t typeinfo, void *buffer, int buffersize);
int proc_pidinfo(int pid, int flavor, uint64_t arg, void *buffer, int buffersize);
int proc_name(int pid, void *buffer, uint32_t buffersize);

#define MAX_PROCS       2048
#define SHOWN           10

struct sample {
	int pid;
	uint64_t time;                  /* user + system, mach_absolute_time's units */
};

static struct sample last[MAX_PROCS], now[MAX_PROCS];
static int last_count;

struct share {
	int pid;
	uint64_t time;
};

static int
by_time(const void *a, const void *b)
{
	const struct share *x = a, *y = b;

	return x->time < y->time ? 1 : x->time > y->time ? -1 : 0;
}

static uint64_t
time_before(int pid, int *found)
{
	for (int i = 0; i < last_count; i++) {
		if (last[i].pid == pid) {
			*found = 1;
			return last[i].time;
		}
	}
	*found = 0;
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	unsigned seconds = argc > 1 ? (unsigned)atoi(argv[1]) : 5, looks = argc > 2 ? (unsigned)atoi(argv[2]) : 0;
	static int pids[MAX_PROCS];
	static struct share shares[MAX_PROCS];
	mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;
	uint64_t start = mach_absolute_time(), before = start;

	if (seconds == 0) {
		seconds = 5;
	}
	mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
	for (unsigned look = 0; looks == 0 || look <= looks; look++) {
		int bytes = proc_listpids(PROC_ALL_PIDS, 0, pids, sizeof(pids)), count = 0, shown = 0;
		uint64_t at = mach_absolute_time(), all = 0;

		for (int i = 0; i < bytes / (int)sizeof(int) && count < MAX_PROCS; i++) {
			struct proc_taskinfo info;

			if (pids[i] <= 0 || proc_pidinfo(pids[i], PROC_PIDTASKINFO, 0, &info, sizeof(info)) != sizeof(info)) {
				continue;
			}
			now[count].pid = pids[i];
			now[count].time = info.pti_total_user + info.pti_total_system;
			count++;
		}
		if (look > 0) {
			int n = 0;

			for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
				int found;
				uint64_t then = time_before(now[i].pid, &found);

				if (now[i].time > then) {
					shares[n].pid = now[i].pid;
					shares[n].time = now[i].time - then;
					all += shares[n].time;
					n++;
				}
			}
			qsort(shares, (size_t)n, sizeof(shares[0]), by_time);
			/* the shares as percent of one core over the time between the looks (both in mach_absolute_time's units) */
			double span = (double)(at - before);
			printf("cputop: %llu s: %.0f%% in all:", (unsigned long long)((at - start) * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1000000000ull),
			    span > 0 ? 100.0 * (double)all / span : 0);
			for (int i = 0; i < n && shown < SHOWN; i++) {
				char name[64] = "?";
				double percent = span > 0 ? 100.0 * (double)shares[i].time / span : 0;

				if (percent < 1) {
					break;
				}
				proc_name(shares[i].pid, name, sizeof(name));
				printf(" %s[%d] %.0f%%", name, shares[i].pid, percent);
				shown++;
			}
			printf("\n");
		}
		memcpy(last, now, sizeof(now[0]) * (size_t)count);
		last_count = count;
		before = at;
		if (looks != 0 && look == looks) {
			break;
		}
		sleep(seconds);
	}
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/dlopen_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * dlopen_test PATH...: open each library the way dyld would and say what happened -- what the path
 * really leads to, and dlerror() when it will not open. For finding out why a library the kernel
 * inserts into a process (etc/inject.conf) is not there in the end.
 */
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <string.h>

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	{
		const char *inserted = getenv("DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES");

		printf("dlopen_test: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=%s\n", inserted != NULL ? inserted : "(not set)");
	}
	for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
		char real[1024];
		struct stat st;
		void *h;

		printf("dlopen_test: %s\n", argv[i]);
		if (realpath(argv[i], real) != NULL) {
			printf("  leads to %s\n", real);
		} else {
			printf("  realpath: no (%s)\n", strerror(errno));
		}
		if (stat(argv[i], &st) == 0) {
			printf("  %lld bytes, mode %o, uid %d\n", (long long)st.st_size, st.st_mode & 07777, st.st_uid);
		} else {
			printf("  stat: %s\n", strerror(errno));
		}
		h = dlopen(argv[i], RTLD_NOW | RTLD_GLOBAL);
		if (h != NULL) {
			printf("  OPENED\n");
		} else {
			printf("  dlopen failed: %s\n", dlerror());
		}
	}
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/eagl.c`:

```c
/*
 * libhakios.gl.dylib: an OpenGL ES implementation behind Darwin's EAGLContext, inside the window
 * server (backboardd; libhakios.dylib loads this when the image has it: build.sh GL=1).
 *
 * CoreAnimation's render server draws with Metal, or else with OpenGL ES, or else with its own
 * software rasterizer (CA::WindowServer::EAGLServer::renderer()). For OpenGL ES it makes an
 * EAGLContext of API 3 and asks six things of it, all of which are replaced here:
 *
 *   -initWithAPI:properties:   ours makes a context of the OpenGL ES library behind us
 *   -API                       3
 *   -setParameter:to:          noted
 *   -getMacroContextPrivate    a table of functions, called as entry(table[0], arguments...) at
 *                              the offsets of Darwin's own OpenGLES (src/eagl_slots.txt); ours is
 *                              made by mkeagl.py: each entry counts the call and passes it on,
 *                              except the ones written by hand below (my_gl...)
 *   -texImageIOSurface:target:internalFormat:width:height:format:type:plane:invert:
 *                              the texture bound to `target` is to show what the IOSurface holds
 *   -attachImage:toCoreSurface:invertedRender:
 *                              the texture bound to the target ("image") is to BE the IOSurface:
 *                              what is drawn into it (it becomes a framebuffer's colour
 *                              attachment) is the screen; or it is a picture to be shown
 *
 * A GPU's driver does the last two by using the IOSurface's memory as the texture's, and so it
 * is done here where the library can (hakios_gl_surface_texture(); surface_shared()): nothing
 * is copied, and a frame's end waits for the GPU. Where it cannot (a software driver, a surface
 * the GPU cannot address, a picture to be turned over) the texture is an ordinary one, filled
 * from the IOSurface when that has changed (its seed) and read back into it when a frame ends
 * (glFlush, glFinish), with nothing but OpenGL ES calls. Either way this file does not know
 * what draws: the library is reached through its gl* functions and the functions of hakios.gl.h.
 *
 * Where CoreAnimation relies on Darwin's library being what it is, this stands in between:
 * blue-first pixels into a texture called GL_RGBA (internal_format()), shaders that read
 * textures at coordinates in pixels (my_glShaderSource()), and draws made with no program
 * (plain_draw_begin()).
 *
 * What CoreAnimation asks of OpenGL ES is written down as it goes (the log lines "hakios-gl:"):
 * strings and limits it reads, texture formats and sizes, calls and triangles per frame. More
 * with the kernel's boot-args: gltrace=FIRST-LAST writes down every call of those frames (lines
 * "gl:"; with each draw what it is made of -- the texture, the first corners -- and after it a
 * pixel or two of the framebuffer; gltrace_lit=1: and how much of the framebuffer is not black);
 * gltrace_at=SECONDS does so for the first frame that long after the window server started,
 * gltrace_draws=N for the first frame after one of N draws, gltrace_function=N[,K] for the frame
 * after the Kth draw CoreAnimation makes of its function N with no program, gltrace_frames=N for
 * N frames from any of them on; gltrace_place=X0,Y0,X1,Y1 writes down, of those frames, only the draws whose corners
 * reach into that rectangle, a line each (lines "gl-at:"; writing everything down is slow, and a
 * window server that is slow draws other frames), gltrace_look=1 adds the pixel each of them
 * left in the middle of itself; gltrace_shaders=1 writes down the text of the shaders of every
 * program a traced draw uses, the first time it draws, gltrace_uniforms=1 what every traced draw
 * gave its program, by the names the shaders use, gltrace_corners=N how many of a draw's corners
 * to write down (twelve by default); glcensus=1 keeps count of the draws CoreAnimation makes with no
 * program and of the functions it asks for in vain (see census_draw()); glshaders=1 writes down
 * the text of every shader, glshow=TEXTURE (or WxH, with glshow_part=W,H and glshow_zoom=N) puts that texture over the corner of the picture, glplain=0 leaves the
 * draws without a program alone, glskip=N[,N...] leaves out the draws of those programs (see skip_draw()), glcopy=1 copies every IOSurface as if the library could not
 * share one, glwait=1 waits for the GPU at the end of every frame and glwait=0 never (see
 * wait_for_frames), glfetch=0 keeps EXT_shader_framebuffer_fetch from CoreAnimation (see
 * fetch_offered), glgroup=0 leaves vibrant layers inside groups as they were (see group_draw_begin()), glprecision=0 leaves the shaders' "lowp" and "mediump" as they are (see all_highp), glenv=NAME=VALUE puts that into the environment for the library to find
 * (its own switches: FD_MESA_DEBUG=sysmem, say), vblur=0 blurs nothing whose radius varies and
 * vblur=2 paints such blurs by their masks instead (see vblur_on), glframes=1 writes a line for
 * every frame (see frame_end()).
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurfaceRef.h>
#include <libkern/OSByteOrder.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <objc/message.h>
#include <objc/runtime.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "hakios.gl.h"

static void
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[1024];
	va_list ap;
	int n;

	va_start(ap, format);
	n = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, ap);
	va_end(ap);
	if (n > (int)sizeof(line) - 1) {
		n = sizeof(line) - 1;
	}
	write(2, line, (size_t)n);
}

static void
eagl_trace(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[512] = "gl: ";
	va_list ap;
	int n;

	va_start(ap, format);
	n = vsnprintf(line + 4, sizeof(line) - 4, format, ap) + 4;
	va_end(ap);
	write(2, line, n > (int)sizeof(line) - 1 ? sizeof(line) - 1 : (size_t)n);
}

static void
eagl_trace_floats(const float *values, int count)
{
	char line[512] = "gl:    ";
	int n = 7;

	for (int i = 0; i < count && i < 16 && n < 480; i++) {
		n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " %g", (double)values[i]);
	}
	line[n++] = '\n';
	write(2, line, (size_t)n);
}

static uint64_t
now_us(void)
{
	static mach_timebase_info_data_t base;

	if (base.denom == 0) {
		mach_timebase_info(&base);
	}
	return mach_absolute_time() * base.numer / base.denom / 1000;
}

/* ---- a context -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

#define SLOTS           0x440           /* entries of the table: more than Darwin's has (checked below) */

/* (a vibrant layer inside a group: see group_draw_begin()) */

	uint8_t state;                  /* GROUP_FRESH: cleared, nothing drawn in it since; GROUP_VIBRANT: a vibrant layer's coverage */
	GLfloat colours[20];            /* ... and that layer's colour matrix */
};
static int group_vibrant_on = 1;        /* boot-arg glgroup=0 */

/* A texture that stands for an IOSurface. */
struct image {
	GLuint texture;
	IOSurfaceRef surface;
	bool target;                    /* drawn into (attachImage) rather than shown (texImageIOSurface) */
	bool invert, drawn;
	bool shared;                    /* the texture is the surface's memory: nothing to copy */
	GLuint mirror;                  /* a texture that is the surface's memory, which the GPU copies the frame into (blit_targets) */
	bool wrapped;                   /* the surface is memory of somebody's with a surface made around it */
	bool alpha_first;               /* its pixels are opacity, blue, green, red in memory: see my_attachImage() */
	bool painted;                   /* something has been drawn into it (it is a target in fact, not only in name) */
	unsigned looked;                /* ... the frame in which that memory was last looked at, */
	uint64_t sum;                   /* ... and what it added up to */
	unsigned unchanged;             /* ... and how many looks in a row found it the same (surface_changed()) */
	GLenum to, internal, format, type;
	uint32_t plane, seed;
	GLsizei width, height;
};

	} line;
	/* a frame's worth */
	unsigned calls, draws, triangles, uploads, clears, last_draws;

static unsigned trace_first, trace_last;        /* the frames whose calls are written down */

static int trace_function_met;                                  /* ... CoreAnimation makes of its function N with no program */
static float trace_place[4];                    /* boot-arg gltrace_place=X0,Y0,X1,Y1: of those frames, only the draws that touch this */
static int trace_placed, trace_placing;         /* ... is set; ... and this frame is one of them */
static int trace_look;                          /* boot-arg gltrace_look=1: ... and what each of them left in the middle of itself */
static int trace_shaders;                       /* boot-arg gltrace_shaders=1: the text of the shaders of every program that draws */
static int trace_uniforms_on;                   /* boot-arg gltrace_uniforms=1: and what every traced draw gave its program */
static GLsizei trace_corners = 12;              /* boot-arg gltrace_corners=N: how many corners of a traced draw to write down */
static float trace_middle[2];                   /* ... which is here, as CoreAnimation counts */
static int trace_listed;                        /* the draw at hand is one of them */
static int all_shaders;                         /* boot-arg glshaders=1: the text of every shader, not of the first two */
static struct group_texture *group_of(struct eagl *e, GLuint texture);
static __thread struct eagl *current;
static struct eagl *contexts[8];
static uint32_t slot_calls[SLOTS];
static int check_errors = 1;            /* ask the library for an error after every call (the first frames) */
static int share_surfaces = 1;          /* boot-arg glcopy=1: 0 */
/*
 * A frame is not drawn into its surface's memory but into a texture of the library's own, and the
 * GPU copies it into the surface at the frame's end (one blit; the display's driver waits for that
 * submission, as it waited for the frame's last draw). Drawn into the surface's memory directly,
 * frames came out with parts of them missing, every other frame for a while -- Control Center's
 * modules, the home screen's icons -- where CoreAnimation reads the picture it is drawing to draw
 * over it (EXT_shader_framebuffer_fetch, the colour matrix over what is behind: our vibrant program);
 * a texture of the library's own does not show that, as a copy by the processor did not (glcopy=1).
 * Boot-arg glblit=0: the surface's memory, as before.
 */
static int blit_targets = 1;
/*
 * A frame that is handed to the display must have been drawn. The display's driver waits for
 * the GPU itself before it puts a surface on the panel, on a thread of its own, and says so in
 * the registry ("HakiosWaitsForGPU"); the window server is then at its next frame meanwhile.
 * With a driver that does not, the frame is waited for here (glFinish). Boot-arg glwait=1:
 * here in any case; glwait=0: nowhere, to see what the waiting costs (and frames half drawn).
 */
static int wait_for_frames = 1;
static int sync_frames = 1;             /* boot-arg glsync=0 (a test): a frame's end does not push what Mesa holds back (frame_end()) */
/*
 * EXT_shader_framebuffer_fetch -- a fragment shader reads the pixel it is about to write -- is
 * what CoreAnimation draws a number of things with where the library offers it: the shadows
 * under the home screen's labels, when they are of the kind that darkens only what is light,
 * are quads that read the picture and write it back, and a colour matrix over what is there
 * (the Search field's text) is one draw instead of a copy and a draw. Without the extension
 * CoreAnimation does the same with what OpenGL ES always has, at four times the submissions
 * for a home screen. (Mesa's driver for this GPU drew the first triangle of each such quad
 * with pixels of another tile, fragments of other icons under the labels, until it was given a
 * flush before the first draw that reads the picture after one that does not:
 * tools/mesa/freedreno-darwin.patch, fd6_draw.cc.) Boot-arg glfetch=0 keeps the extension from
 * CoreAnimation, to see the difference.
 */
static int fetch_offered = 1;

#define GL_SCISSOR_TEST                 0x0c11
#define GL_SCISSOR_BOX                  0x0c10
#define GL_COLOR_CLEAR_VALUE            0x0c22

static const char *eagl_slot_name(unsigned offset);
static void census_report(void);
static void clear_now(struct eagl *e);

static void
eagl_enter(struct eagl *e, unsigned offset)
{
	if (current != e) {
		if (!hakios_gl_make_current(e->gl)) {
			say("hakios-gl: the context cannot be made this thread's\n");
		}
		current = e;
	}
	slot_calls[offset / 8]++;
	e->calls++;
	if (slow_calls_us != 0) {
		call_began_us = now_us();
	}
}

static void
eagl_leave(struct eagl *e, unsigned offset)
{
	GLenum error;

	if (check_errors && offset != 0x338 && (error = glGetError()) != 0) {
		if (e->errors++ < 60) {
			say("hakios-gl: %s: error %#x\n", eagl_slot_name(offset), error);
		}
	}
	if (slow_calls_us != 0) {
		uint64_t now = now_us();

		/* "tl: slow NAME US at US, frame N": a call that took long, and when it ended (tools/frames.py) */
		if (now - call_began_us >= slow_calls_us) {
			say("tl: slow %s %llu at %llu, frame %u%s\n", eagl_slot_name(offset), now - call_began_us, now, e->frames + 1,
			    e->in_frame ? "" : " (before its first draw)");
		}
	}
}

/* An entry the library has no function for: say so, once an entry. */
static long
eagl_missing(void *context, unsigned offset)
{
	struct eagl *e = context;

	eagl_enter(e, offset);
	if (slot_calls[offset / 8] == 1) {
		say("hakios-gl: CALLED AND NOT THERE: entry %#x, %s\n", offset, eagl_slot_name(offset));
	}
	return 0;
}

static struct eagl *
context_of(id object)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(contexts) / sizeof(contexts[0]); i++) {
		if (contexts[i] != NULL && contexts[i]->object == object) {
			return contexts[i];
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

/* ---- what CoreAnimation asks for: kept for the summary ------------------------------------------- */

struct format_use {
	GLenum internal, format, type;
	unsigned count, widest, tallest;
	const char *how;
};
static struct format_use formats[48];
static unsigned widest_texture, tallest_texture;

static void
note_format(const char *how, GLenum internal, GLenum format, GLenum type, GLsizei width, GLsizei height)
{
	struct format_use *use = NULL;

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(formats) / sizeof(formats[0]); i++) {
		if (formats[i].count == 0 || (formats[i].how == how && formats[i].internal == internal &&
		    formats[i].format == format && formats[i].type == type)) {
			use = &formats[i];
			break;
		}
	}
	if ((unsigned)width > widest_texture) {
		widest_texture = (unsigned)width;
	}
	if ((unsigned)height > tallest_texture) {
		tallest_texture = (unsigned)height;
	}
	if (use == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	if (use->count++ == 0) {
		use->how = how;
		use->internal = internal;
		use->format = format;
		use->type = type;
		say("hakios-gl: a new kind of texture: %s, internal format %#x, format %#x, type %#x, %d x %d\n", how, internal,
		    format, type, width, height);
	}
	if ((unsigned)width > use->widest) {
		use->widest = (unsigned)width;
	}
	if ((unsigned)height > use->tallest) {
		use->tallest = (unsigned)height;
	}
}

static void
summary(struct eagl *e)
{
	unsigned frames = e->frames ? e->frames : 1;

	say("hakios-gl: after %u frames: %llu calls, %llu draws and %llu triangles a frame on average; the most in one: "
	    "%u calls, %u triangles; %llu us a frame, of which %llu handing the commands on, %llu waiting for the picture "
	    "to be drawn and %llu copying it out, and before each %llu making textures of IOSurfaces; %u IOSurfaces were "
	    "the textures' memory, %u had to be copied; %u shaders, %u programs; biggest texture %u x %u; %u errors\n",
	    e->frames, e->all_calls / frames, e->all_draws / frames, e->all_triangles / frames, e->most_calls,
	    e->most_triangles, e->frame_us / frames, e->flush_us / frames, e->wait_us / frames, e->readback_us / frames,
	    e->attach_us / frames, e->shared, e->refused, e->shaders, e->programs, widest_texture, tallest_texture, e->errors);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(formats) / sizeof(formats[0]) && formats[i].count; i++) {
		say("hakios-gl:   textures: %s %#x/%#x/%#x: %u times, up to %u x %u\n", formats[i].how, formats[i].internal,
		    formats[i].format, formats[i].type, formats[i].count, formats[i].widest, formats[i].tallest);
	}
	for (unsigned offset = 8; offset < SLOTS * 8; offset += 8) {
		if (slot_calls[offset / 8]) {
			say("hakios-gl:   %-28s %u\n", eagl_slot_name(offset), slot_calls[offset / 8]);
		}
	}
}

/* ---- IOSurfaces ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static struct image *
image_of(struct eagl *e, GLuint texture)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < e->image_count; i++) {
		if (e->images[i].texture == texture) {
			return &e->images[i];
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

static struct image *
image_new(struct eagl *e, GLuint texture, IOSurfaceRef surface)
{
	struct image *image = image_of(e, texture);

	if (image == NULL) {
		if (e->image_count == sizeof(e->images) / sizeof(e->images[0])) {
			say("hakios-gl: more textures with IOSurfaces than there is room for\n");
			return NULL;
		}
		image = &e->images[e->image_count++];
	} else {
		if (image->mirror != 0) {
			glDeleteTextures(1, &image->mirror);
		}
		CFRelease(image->surface);
	}
	memset(image, 0, sizeof(*image));
	image->texture = texture;
	image->surface = (IOSurfaceRef)CFRetain(surface);
	return image;
}

static void
image_forget(struct eagl *e, GLuint texture)
{
	struct image *image = image_of(e, texture);

	if (image != NULL) {
		if (image->mirror != 0) {
			glDeleteTextures(1, &image->mirror);
		}
		CFRelease(image->surface);
		*image = e->images[--e->image_count];
	}
}

/* Apple's OpenGL ES takes blue-first pixels into a texture called GL_RGBA; everybody else's calls the texture so too. */
static GLenum
internal_format(GLenum internal, GLenum format)
{
	return format == GL_BGRA && internal == GL_RGBA ? GL_BGRA : internal;
}

static unsigned
bytes_a_pixel(GLenum format, GLenum type)
{
```
