`userland/src/gl_osmesa.c`:

```c
/*
 * The OpenGL ES library behind src/eagl.c when that library is Mesa as tools/mk-mesa.sh builds
 * it: any of its drivers that draws into memory, reached through its off-screen interface
 * (OSMesa, given an OpenGL ES profile by tools/mesa/osmesa-es-profile.patch).
 *
 * This file is all that knows which library draws. eagl.c wants four things besides the gl*
 * functions themselves: a context of a version of OpenGL ES, that context made the calling
 * thread's, a context taken away again, and a name for the log. A library with another way to
 * its contexts gets another file like this one.
 */
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "hakios.gl.h"

/* GL/osmesa.h of Mesa */
#define OSMESA_RGBA                     0x1908
#define OSMESA_FORMAT                   0x22
#define OSMESA_DEPTH_BITS               0x30
#define OSMESA_STENCIL_BITS             0x31
#define OSMESA_PROFILE                  0x33
#define OSMESA_CONTEXT_MAJOR_VERSION    0x36
#define OSMESA_CONTEXT_MINOR_VERSION    0x37
#define OSMESA_ES_PROFILE               0x38
#define GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE                0x1401
#define GL_TEXTURE_2D                   0x0de1
#define GL_RENDERER                     0x1f01

typedef struct osmesa_context *OSMesaContext;
extern OSMesaContext OSMesaCreateContextAttribs(const int *attributes, OSMesaContext share);
extern unsigned char OSMesaMakeCurrent(OSMesaContext context, void *buffer, unsigned type, int width, int height);
extern void OSMesaDestroyContext(OSMesaContext context);
extern void (*OSMesaGetProcAddress(const char *name))(void);
extern const unsigned char *glGetString(unsigned name);
extern unsigned glGetError(void);

/*
 * OSMesa draws its "window" into memory handed to it. Nothing here draws into a window (the
 * window server draws into textures of its own, see eagl.c): a few pixels will do.
 */
#define WINDOW  16

struct hakios_gl {
	OSMesaContext context;
	unsigned char window[WINDOW * WINDOW * 4];
};

struct hakios_gl *
hakios_gl_create(int version)
{
	const int attributes[] = {
		OSMESA_FORMAT, OSMESA_RGBA, OSMESA_DEPTH_BITS, 24, OSMESA_STENCIL_BITS, 8,
		OSMESA_PROFILE, OSMESA_ES_PROFILE, OSMESA_CONTEXT_MAJOR_VERSION, version, OSMESA_CONTEXT_MINOR_VERSION, 0,
		0
	};
	struct hakios_gl *gl = calloc(1, sizeof(*gl));

	if (gl != NULL && (gl->context = OSMesaCreateContextAttribs(attributes, NULL)) == NULL) {
		free(gl);
		gl = NULL;
	}
	return gl;
}

int
hakios_gl_make_current(struct hakios_gl *gl)
{
	if (gl == NULL) {
		return OSMesaMakeCurrent(NULL, NULL, 0, 0, 0);
	}
	return OSMesaMakeCurrent(gl->context, gl->window, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, WINDOW, WINDOW);
}

void
hakios_gl_destroy(struct hakios_gl *gl)
{
	OSMesaDestroyContext(gl->context);
	free(gl);
}

const char *
hakios_gl_library(void)
{
	return "Mesa, off-screen (OSMesa)";
}

/*
 * OES_EGL_image, with the IOSurface's ID as the image (tools/mesa/freedreno-darwin.patch: the
 * kernel's GPU driver makes a buffer of the surface's memory). The drivers that draw in memory
 * of their own with this processor are not asked: they refuse every time.
 */
int
hakios_gl_surface_texture(struct hakios_gl *gl, uint32_t surface)
{
	static void (*image_target)(unsigned target, void *image);
	static int asked, software;

	(void)gl;
	if (!asked) {
		const char *renderer = (const char *)glGetString(GL_RENDERER);

		asked = 1;
		image_target = (void (*)(unsigned, void *))OSMesaGetProcAddress("glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES");
		software = renderer == NULL || strstr(renderer, "softpipe") != NULL || strstr(renderer, "llvmpipe") != NULL;
	}
	if (image_target == NULL || software) {
		return 0;
	}
	while (glGetError() != 0) {
	}
	image_target(GL_TEXTURE_2D, (void *)(uintptr_t)surface);
	return glGetError() == 0;
}
```

`userland/src/gl_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * gl_test: one triangle through the OpenGL ES library of the image (lib/libOSMesa.8.dylib: Mesa,
 * with its Adreno driver when the kernel has kept the GPU on -- boot-arg adreno_keep=1 -- and its
 * software one when not), read back and put on the panel. It says which driver drew, how long
 * it took and what a few pixels are, so that the picture need not be seen to be believed.
 *
 *   gl_test [SECONDS [WIDTH HEIGHT]]   keep the picture on the panel for so long (default 6: the
 *                                      window server draws over it with its next frame)
 *   gl_test fill [WIDTH HEIGHT]        no picture: how long the GPU takes over a frame of that size
 *                                      (default 1125 x 2436, what the window server draws), by what
 *                                      is in it -- see fill()
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/* GL/osmesa.h and GLES2/gl2.h of Mesa, as far as they are used here */
typedef struct osmesa_context *OSMesaContext;
extern OSMesaContext OSMesaCreateContextAttribs(const int *attributes, OSMesaContext share);
extern unsigned char OSMesaMakeCurrent(OSMesaContext context, void *buffer, unsigned type, int width, int height);

extern const unsigned char *glGetString(unsigned name);
extern unsigned glGetError(void);
extern void glGenTextures(int n, unsigned *names);
extern void glBindTexture(unsigned target, unsigned texture);
extern void glTexImage2D(unsigned target, int level, int internal, int width, int height, int border, unsigned format,
    unsigned type, const void *pixels);
extern void glTexParameteri(unsigned target, unsigned name, int value);
extern void glGenFramebuffers(int n, unsigned *names);
extern void glBindFramebuffer(unsigned target, unsigned framebuffer);
extern void glFramebufferTexture2D(unsigned target, unsigned attachment, unsigned textarget, unsigned texture, int level);
extern unsigned glCheckFramebufferStatus(unsigned target);
extern void glViewport(int x, int y, int width, int height);
extern void glClearColor(float red, float green, float blue, float alpha);
extern void glClear(unsigned mask);
extern unsigned glCreateShader(unsigned type);
extern void glShaderSource(unsigned shader, int count, const char *const *strings, const int *lengths);
extern void glCompileShader(unsigned shader);
extern void glGetShaderiv(unsigned shader, unsigned name, int *value);
extern unsigned glCreateProgram(void);
extern void glAttachShader(unsigned program, unsigned shader);
extern void glBindAttribLocation(unsigned program, unsigned index, const char *name);
extern void glLinkProgram(unsigned program);
extern void glGetProgramiv(unsigned program, unsigned name, int *value);
extern void glUseProgram(unsigned program);
extern void glVertexAttribPointer(unsigned index, int size, unsigned type, unsigned char normalized, int stride,
    const void *pointer);

extern void glDisable(unsigned what);

extern void glReadPixels(int x, int y, int width, int height, unsigned format, unsigned type, void *pixels);

#define OSMESA_RGBA                     0x1908
#define OSMESA_FORMAT                   0x22
#define OSMESA_PROFILE                  0x33
#define OSMESA_CONTEXT_MAJOR_VERSION    0x36
#define OSMESA_ES_PROFILE               0x38
#define GL_TRIANGLES                    0x0004
#define GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP               0x0005
#define GL_ONE                          1
#define GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA          0x0303
#define GL_BLEND                        0x0be2
#define GL_LINEAR                       0x2601
#define GL_TEXTURE_2D                   0x0de1
#define GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE                0x1401
#define GL_FLOAT                        0x1406
#define GL_RGBA                         0x1908
#define GL_VENDOR                       0x1f00
#define GL_RENDERER                     0x1f01
#define GL_VERSION                      0x1f02
#define GL_NEAREST                      0x2600
#define GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER           0x2800
#define GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER           0x2801
#define GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT             0x4000
#define GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER              0x8b30
#define GL_VERTEX_SHADER                0x8b31
#define GL_COMPILE_STATUS               0x8b81
#define GL_LINK_STATUS                  0x8b82
#define GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE         0x8cd5
#define GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0            0x8ce0
#define GL_FRAMEBUFFER                  0x8d40

/* the kernel's GPU service takes pixels for the panel (drivers/gpu/hakios.gpu.cpp: kHakiosShow) */
struct show {
	uint64_t pixels;
	uint32_t width, height, row_bytes, pad;
};

static uint64_t
now_us(void)
{
	static mach_timebase_info_data_t base;

	if (base.denom == 0) {
		mach_timebase_info(&base);
	}
	return mach_absolute_time() * base.numer / base.denom / 1000;
}

static uint64_t
now_ms(void)
{
	static mach_timebase_info_data_t base;

	if (base.denom == 0) {
		mach_timebase_info(&base);
	}
	return mach_absolute_time() * base.numer / base.denom / 1000000;
}

static unsigned
shader(unsigned type, const char *text)
{
	unsigned name = glCreateShader(type);
	int good = 0;

	glShaderSource(name, 1, &text, NULL);
	glCompileShader(name);
	glGetShaderiv(name, GL_COMPILE_STATUS, &good);
	if (!good) {
		printf("gl_test: a shader does not compile\n");
	}
	return name;
}

/*
 * What a frame costs by what is in it. Each kind of frame is drawn sixteen times into a texture
 * of the size given, each time waited for (glFinish), and the shortest time is the one told:
 * the window server draws its own frames meanwhile, and they are in the way of some.
 *   - nothing but a clear: what a frame costs before anything is drawn in it (the GPU draws a
 *     picture of this size in pieces, in memory of its own, and writes each piece out);
 *   - no clear, one small rectangle: the same, and the picture as it was has to be read in first;
 *   - a clear and 1, 2, 4, 8 rectangles over all of it, in one colour: what covering every pixel
 *     once costs;
 *   - the same with a texture of the same size and blending, which is what a layer of the
 *     window server's is.
 * From these it can be told what a slow frame is slow at: the pieces written to memory and read
 * from it, or the pixels drawn.
 */
static void
fill(int width, int height)
{
	static const float all[] = { -1, -1, 1, -1, -1, 1, 1, 1 }, some[] = { -0.1f, -0.1f, 0.1f, -0.1f, -0.1f, 0.1f, 0.1f, 0.1f };
	static const struct {
		const char *what;
		int clear, layers, textured, small;
	} kinds[] = {
		{ "a clear and nothing else", 1, 0, 0, 0 },
		{ "no clear, one small rectangle", 0, 1, 0, 1 },
		{ "a clear, 1 rectangle over all of it", 1, 1, 0, 0 },
		{ "a clear, 2 rectangles", 1, 2, 0, 0 },
		{ "a clear, 4 rectangles", 1, 4, 0, 0 },
		{ "a clear, 8 rectangles", 1, 8, 0, 0 },
		{ "a clear, 1 rectangle with a texture, blended", 1, 1, 1, 0 },
		{ "a clear, 2 such", 1, 2, 1, 0 },
		{ "a clear, 4 such", 1, 4, 1, 0 },
		{ "a clear, 8 such", 1, 8, 1, 0 },
	};
	unsigned target = 0, source = 0, framebuffer = 0, program;
	uint32_t *pixels = malloc((size_t)width * (size_t)height * 4);
	int textured, colour, good = 0;

	if (pixels == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	for (size_t i = 0; i < (size_t)width * (size_t)height; i++) {
		pixels[i] = 0x80404040u + ((uint32_t)i * 2654435761u >> 28);
	}
	glGenTextures(1, &source);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, source);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);
	glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, width, height, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, pixels);
	free(pixels);
	glGenTextures(1, &target);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, target);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, width, height, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, NULL);
	glGenFramebuffers(1, &framebuffer);
	glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, framebuffer);
	glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, target, 0);
	program = glCreateProgram();
	glAttachShader(program, shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER,
	    "attribute vec2 where; varying vec2 at;\n"
	    "void main() { gl_Position = vec4(where, 0.0, 1.0); at = where * 0.5 + 0.5; }\n"));
	glAttachShader(program, shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER,
	    "precision mediump float; varying vec2 at; uniform sampler2D picture; uniform int textured; uniform vec4 colour;\n"
	    "void main() { gl_FragColor = textured != 0 ? texture2D(picture, at) * colour : colour; }\n"));
	glBindAttribLocation(program, 0, "where");
	glLinkProgram(program);
	glGetProgramiv(program, GL_LINK_STATUS, &good);
	if (!good || glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER) != GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE) {
		printf("gl_test: fill: no program or no framebuffer\n");
		return;
	}
	glUseProgram(program);
	textured = glGetUniformLocation(program, "textured");
	colour = glGetUniformLocation(program, "colour");
	glUniform1i(glGetUniformLocation(program, "picture"), 0);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, source);
	glViewport(0, 0, width, height);
	glEnableVertexAttribArray(0);
	glClearColor(0.1f, 0.1f, 0.2f, 1.0f);
	printf("gl_test: fill: frames of %d x %d (%d KB), the shortest of 16 each:\n", width, height, width * height / 256);
	for (unsigned k = 0; k < sizeof(kinds) / sizeof(kinds[0]); k++) {
		uint64_t least = ~0ull, most = 0;

		glUniform1i(textured, kinds[k].textured);
		if (kinds[k].textured) {
			glEnable(GL_BLEND);
			glBlendFunc(GL_ONE, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
		} else {
			glDisable(GL_BLEND);
		}
		glVertexAttribPointer(0, 2, GL_FLOAT, 0, 0, kinds[k].small ? some : all);
		for (int frame = 0; frame < 16; frame++) {
			uint64_t began = now_us(), took;

			if (kinds[k].clear) {
				glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);
			}
			for (int layer = 0; layer < kinds[k].layers; layer++) {
				glUniform4f(colour, 0.2f + 0.1f * (float)layer, 0.5f, 0.3f, 0.5f);
				glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, 4);
			}
			glFinish();
			took = now_us() - began;
			least = took < least ? took : least;
			most = took > most ? took : most;
		}
		printf("gl_test: fill: %-46s %5llu us (the longest %llu)\n", kinds[k].what, least, most);
	}
	printf("gl_test: fill: error %#x\n", glGetError());
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	static const int attributes[] = { OSMESA_FORMAT, OSMESA_RGBA, OSMESA_PROFILE, OSMESA_ES_PROFILE,
		                          OSMESA_CONTEXT_MAJOR_VERSION, 2, 0 };
	static const float corners[] = {
		/* where, and what colour */
		-0.8f, -0.6f, 1, 0, 0,
		0.8f, -0.6f, 0, 1, 0,
		0.0f, 0.7f, 0, 0, 1,
	};
	static unsigned char window[16 * 16 * 4];
	int seconds = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 6, width = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 1080;
	int height = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 2400;
	unsigned texture = 0, framebuffer = 0, program, coloured = 0;
	uint8_t *drawn, *shown;
	uint64_t began, drew, read;
	io_service_t service;
	io_connect_t connection = 0;
	OSMesaContext context;
	int good = 0;

	context = OSMesaCreateContextAttribs(attributes, NULL);
	if (context == NULL || !OSMesaMakeCurrent(context, window, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, 16, 16)) {
		printf("gl_test: no OpenGL ES context\n");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("gl_test: %s; %s; %s\n", (const char *)glGetString(GL_VENDOR), (const char *)glGetString(GL_RENDERER),
	    (const char *)glGetString(GL_VERSION));
	if (argc > 1 && strcmp(argv[1], "fill") == 0) {
		fill(argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 1125, argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 2436);
		return 0;
	}

	began = now_ms();
	glGenTextures(1, &texture);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, texture);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, width, height, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, NULL);
	glGenFramebuffers(1, &framebuffer);
	glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, framebuffer);
	glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, texture, 0);
	if (glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER) != GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE) {
		printf("gl_test: the framebuffer is not complete\n");
		return 1;
	}
	program = glCreateProgram();
	glAttachShader(program, shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER,
	    "attribute vec2 where; attribute vec3 colour; varying vec3 c;\n"
	    "void main() { gl_Position = vec4(where, 0.0, 1.0); c = colour; }\n"));
	glAttachShader(program, shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER,
	    "precision mediump float; varying vec3 c;\n"
	    "void main() { gl_FragColor = vec4(c, 1.0); }\n"));
	glBindAttribLocation(program, 0, "where");
	glBindAttribLocation(program, 1, "colour");
	glLinkProgram(program);
	glGetProgramiv(program, GL_LINK_STATUS, &good);
	if (!good) {
		printf("gl_test: the program does not link\n");
		return 1;
	}
	glUseProgram(program);
	glViewport(0, 0, width, height);
	glClearColor(0.1f, 0.1f, 0.2f, 1.0f);
	glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);
	glVertexAttribPointer(0, 2, GL_FLOAT, 0, 5 * sizeof(float), corners);
	glVertexAttribPointer(1, 3, GL_FLOAT, 0, 5 * sizeof(float), corners + 2);
	glEnableVertexAttribArray(0);
	glEnableVertexAttribArray(1);
	glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 3);
	glFinish();
	drew = now_ms();

	drawn = malloc((size_t)width * (size_t)height * 4);
	shown = malloc((size_t)width * (size_t)height * 4);
	if (drawn == NULL || shown == NULL) {
		return 1;
	}
	memset(drawn, 0x55, (size_t)width * (size_t)height * 4);
	glReadPixels(0, 0, width, height, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, drawn);
	read = now_ms();
	/* the panel's rows go down and its pixels are blue first */
	for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
		const uint8_t *from = drawn + (size_t)(height - 1 - y) * (size_t)width * 4;
		uint8_t *to = shown + (size_t)y * (size_t)width * 4;

		for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
			to[4 * x] = from[4 * x + 2];
			to[4 * x + 1] = from[4 * x + 1];
			to[4 * x + 2] = from[4 * x];
			to[4 * x + 3] = 255;
			coloured += from[4 * x] > 60 || from[4 * x + 1] > 60 || from[4 * x + 2] > 60;
		}
	}
#define PIXEL(x, y) drawn[((size_t)(y) * (size_t)width + (size_t)(x)) * 4], drawn[((size_t)(y) * (size_t)width + (size_t)(x)) * 4 + 1], \
	    drawn[((size_t)(y) * (size_t)width + (size_t)(x)) * 4 + 2], drawn[((size_t)(y) * (size_t)width + (size_t)(x)) * 4 + 3]
	printf("gl_test: %d x %d drawn in %llu ms, read back in %llu ms; error %#x; red green blue alpha: a corner %u %u %u %u, "
	    "the middle %u %u %u %u, near the red corner %u %u %u %u, near the green %u %u %u %u, near the blue %u %u %u %u; "
	    "%u of %u pixels inside the triangle (%u%%; 26%% by geometry)\n", width, height, drew - began, read - drew,
	    glGetError(), PIXEL(2, 2), PIXEL(width / 2, height / 2), PIXEL(width * 15 / 100, height * 22 / 100),
	    PIXEL(width * 85 / 100, height * 22 / 100), PIXEL(width / 2, height * 80 / 100), coloured,
	    (unsigned)(width * height), (unsigned)((uint64_t)coloured * 100 / (uint64_t)(width * height)));

	service = IOServiceGetMatchingService(0, IOServiceMatching("HakiosGPU"));
	if (service == 0 || IOServiceOpen(service, mach_task_self(), 0, &connection) != 0) {
		printf("gl_test: no GPU service in this kernel to put the picture on the panel with\n");
		return 0;
	}
	for (int i = 0; i < seconds * 5; i++) {
		struct show show = { (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)shown, (uint32_t)width, (uint32_t)height, (uint32_t)width * 4, 0 };
		kern_return_t result = IOConnectCallStructMethod(connection, 0x7f, &show, sizeof(show), NULL, NULL);

		if (i == 0) {
			printf("gl_test: the picture is on the panel (%#x), for %d seconds\n", result, seconds);
		}
		usleep(200000);
	}
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/hakios.audio.h`:

```h
/*
 * /dev/hakios-audio: the sound Darwin plays, on its way to whatever can make it heard.
 *
 * Darwin expects its output devices from Apple's audio drivers through IOAudio2; neither exists
 * here. Instead the audio server (mediaserverd) is given a plug-in of ours that presents one
 * stereo output device, and the plug-in writes what the server has mixed for that device
 * here. In the kernel the samples go to a sink -- a driver for something that plays them --
 * and, if asked for, into a recording that outlives the kernel (see dev/hakios.audio.c).
 *
 *   write(): whole frames in the format below. Never blocks: the writer is the audio server's
 *            real-time thread, which paces itself (48000 frames a second while anything
 *            plays, nothing at all otherwise). What the sink cannot take is dropped.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_HAKIOS_AUDIO_H_
#define _SYS_HAKIOS_AUDIO_H_

#include <stdint.h>

#define HAKIOS_AUDIO_DEVICE    "/dev/hakios-audio"

/* The one format: 16-bit signed little-endian samples, left then right. */
#define HAKIOS_AUDIO_RATE      48000
#define HAKIOS_AUDIO_CHANNELS  2
#define HAKIOS_AUDIO_FRAME     4       /* bytes */

/*
 * ioctl(HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME): the speakers' volume, as Darwin sets it on the plug-in's volume
 * control -- how many eighths of a dB under the loudest they may play, and whether they are
 * muted (Darwin's volume at 0). The loudest is the kernel's to say (on the phone: Android's own
 * level less sound_below, hakios.sound.c); the plug-in only says how far under it.
 */
#include <sys/ioccom.h>

struct hakios_audio_volume {
	uint32_t below;                 /* eighths of a dB */
	uint32_t muted;
};
#define HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME _IOW('r', 1, struct hakios_audio_volume)

#ifdef KERNEL
#include <stdbool.h>

/*
 * For drivers. A sink is offered frames as they are written and says how many it took (the
 * rest are lost); it is called from the writer's thread and must not wait.
 */
typedef uint32_t (*hakios_audio_sink_t)(const int16_t *frames, uint32_t count);

void hakios_audio_set_sink(const char *name, hakios_audio_sink_t sink);
/* The volume Darwin has set last (HAKIOS_AUDIO_SET_VOLUME): false if it has set none; *generation counts the settings. */
bool hakios_audio_volume(uint32_t *below, bool *muted, uint32_t *generation);
void hakios_audio_init(void);
void hakios_virtio_sound_init(void);   /* boot-arg virtio_sound=1: QEMU's virtio sound device */
void hakios_speaker_init(void);        /* boot-arg speaker_probe=N: a look at the phone's speaker amplifiers */

/*
 * The phone's speakers (drivers/audio/hakios.speaker.c): its two Awinic amplifiers, set up as
 * Android's driver sets them up, from Android's own configuration file (see there).
 */
bool hakios_speaker_prepare(const uint8_t *acf, uint64_t size);       /* found, reset, configured: powered down, muted */
bool hakios_speaker_start(void);       /* powered up and unmuted at the lowest volume: only while the I2S clock runs */
bool hakios_speaker_volume(uint32_t below, uint32_t step_ms); /* below Android's level, in eighths of a dB; 6 dB a step */
bool hakios_speaker_healthy(void);     /* no fault reported; on one, both are powered down at once */
void hakios_speaker_stop(void);        /* faded out, muted, powered down, in Android's order */
void hakios_speaker_quiesce(void);     /* powered down at once, without sleeping: on a panic's way out */

/*
 * The audio DSP's services, for the sound's path (drivers/audio/hakios.adsp.c, drivers/audio/hakios.sound.c).
 * hakios_adsp_apr() sends one APR packet to a service of the DSP (AFE 4, ASM 7, ADM 8) with the
 * given port and token (0: one of its own) and, with wait_ms, waits for the packet that carries
 * that token back. What is not waited for goes to the handler of events, if there is one and it
 * takes it (returns true). The handler is called on the link's thread and must not wait.
 */
struct hakios_apr_answer {
	uint32_t opcode, token, length;         /* length: of the payload, in bytes */
	uint32_t words[64];
};
typedef bool (*hakios_apr_events_t)(uint8_t service, uint16_t port, uint32_t opcode, uint32_t token, const uint32_t *payload,
    uint32_t length);

bool hakios_adsp_apr(uint8_t service, uint16_t port, uint32_t token, uint32_t opcode, const void *payload, uint32_t length,
    uint32_t wait_ms, struct hakios_apr_answer *answer);
void hakios_adsp_apr_events(hakios_apr_events_t handler);
const uint8_t *hakios_adsp_fw_file(const char *name, uint64_t *size);        /* /fw/name, read whole; give back with: */
void hakios_adsp_fw_free(const uint8_t *data, uint64_t size);

void hakios_sound_dsp_up(void);        /* the DSP's audio services are up (adsp=1): boot-arg sound=N begins */
void hakios_sound_dsp_down(void);      /* before the DSP is shut down at the run's end: everything of the sound's stopped */
void hakios_sound_quiesce(void);       /* on a panic's way out: the amplifiers off, without sleeping */
#endif

#endif /* _SYS_HAKIOS_AUDIO_H_ */
```

`userland/src/hakios.camera.h`:

```h
/*
 * /dev/hakios-camera: the phone's wide camera for Darwin (boot-arg cam=5; the kernel's drivers/camera/hakios.camera.c,
 * whose bsd/sys/hakios.camera.h this is a copy of).
 *
 *   open()   the first one powers the sensor up and starts its frames (the sensor's mode: boot-arg
 *            cam_mode, else the module file's 4000x3000 one); the last close puts everything down
 *            again, and so does a second without a read.
 *   read()   waits (at most a second) for the newest frame not read yet: a struct
 *            hakios_camera_frame, then as many of the frame's bytes as the buffer has room for.
 *            A buffer of the header's size learns the frame's size and nothing else is copied.
 *            EIO when the camera has had a fault: it stays off for the rest of the run.
 *   write()  commands: a struct hakios_camera_command, then what it says follows.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_HAKIOS_CAMERA_H_
#define _SYS_HAKIOS_CAMERA_H_

#include <stdint.h>

#define HAKIOS_CAMERA_DEVICE           "/dev/hakios-camera"
#define HAKIOS_CAMERA_MAGIC            "RWFRAME1"

struct hakios_camera_frame {
	char            magic[8];       /* HAKIOS_CAMERA_MAGIC */
	uint32_t        header_bytes;   /* this structure's size: the frame's bytes follow */
	uint32_t        width, height;  /* pixels */
	uint32_t        stride;         /* bytes from one line to the next */
	uint32_t        format;         /* 1: MIPI RAW10, four pixels in five bytes */
	uint32_t        bayer;          /* the order of a 2x2 cell: 0 RGGB, 1 GRBG, 2 GBRG, 3 BGGR */
	uint32_t        black;          /* the black level, in 10-bit steps */
	uint64_t        sequence;       /* the frame's number since the sensor started, from 1 */
	uint64_t        time;           /* when the frame was done, in mach_absolute_time()'s units */
	uint32_t        exposure_lines; /* the exposure it was taken with, in lines ... */
	uint32_t        line_ns;        /* ... of this many nanoseconds */
	uint32_t        gain;           /* the sensor's analog gain register ... */
	uint32_t        gain_unity;     /* ... which is this for 1x */
	uint32_t        gain_max;       /* the most it may be given */
	uint32_t        frame_lines;    /* the frame's length in lines (frames a second: 1e9 / (frame_lines * line_ns)) */
	uint32_t        frame_lines_min; /* the mode's own length: the shortest frame */
	uint32_t        frame_lines_max; /* the longest frame it may be given */
	uint32_t        margin;         /* exposure_lines is at most frame_lines - margin */
	uint32_t        sensor;         /* which: 0 the macro, 1 the wide, 2 the front, 3 the ultra-wide camera */
	uint32_t        focus;          /* the lens's position as last set, 0 (the furthest) to 1023: HAKIOS_CAMERA_NO_FOCUS where it
	                                 * has no motor (or it does not answer) */
	uint32_t        reserved[5];
};

#define HAKIOS_CAMERA_NO_FOCUS 0xffffffffu

enum {
	HAKIOS_CAMERA_EXPOSURE = 1,    /* a: lines, b: gain, c: frame lines (0: the shortest that holds the exposure) */
	HAKIOS_CAMERA_KEEP = 2,        /* a picture for the host: a width, b height, c stride, d format (1 the frame's RAW10, 2 NV12,
	                                 * 3 BGRA); bytes follow */
	HAKIOS_CAMERA_SENSOR = 3,      /* another sensor: a which (as in the frames' header), b its mode (~0: the usual one);
	                                 * the frames stop, everything goes down, and the next read starts the other one */
	HAKIOS_CAMERA_FOCUS = 4,       /* the lens to a: 0 (the furthest) to 1023, from the next frame or so */
};

struct hakios_camera_command {
	uint32_t        command;
	uint32_t        bytes;          /* of what follows this structure */
	uint32_t        a, b, c, d;
};

#endif /* _SYS_HAKIOS_CAMERA_H_ */
```

`userland/src/hakios.input.h`:

```h
/*
 * /dev/hakios-touch: touch samples on their way from whoever produces them to the
 * program that turns them into HID events for the window server.
 *
 * Darwin expects touches from Apple's multitouch driver through IOHIDFamily; neither exists
 * here. Instead a producer -- a kernel driver for a real touch controller or for an emulated
 * pointer, or a user program replaying a script -- posts samples, and code of ours running
 * inside backboardd reads them and synthesizes the events. Both sides use the same record.
 *
 *   write(): one or more records (time is ignored; the kernel stamps them)
 *   read():  blocks until there is at least one record, returns as many whole ones as fit
 */
#ifndef _SYS_HAKIOS_INPUT_H_
#define _SYS_HAKIOS_INPUT_H_

#include <stdint.h>

#define HAKIOS_TOUCH_DEVICE    "/dev/hakios-touch"

#define HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN      1       /* a finger has landed */
#define HAKIOS_TOUCH_MOVE      2
#define HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP        3       /* it has lifted (x, y: where it was last) */
#define HAKIOS_BUTTON_DOWN     4       /* a hardware button; `finger` says which (HAKIOS_BUTTON_*), x and y are 0 */
#define HAKIOS_BUTTON_UP       5

#define HAKIOS_BUTTON_LOCK     1       /* the side button */
#define HAKIOS_BUTTON_VOLUME_UP 2
#define HAKIOS_BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN 3
#define HAKIOS_BUTTON_HOME     4

struct hakios_touch {
	uint64_t time;                  /* mach_absolute_time() when the sample was posted */
	uint32_t type;                  /* HAKIOS_TOUCH_* or HAKIOS_BUTTON_DOWN/UP */
	uint32_t finger;                /* which finger, from 0 (or which button) */
	uint32_t x, y;                  /* position on the display, 0 = left/top edge, 65535 = right/bottom edge */
};

#ifdef KERNEL
/* For drivers; not from interrupt context. */
void hakios_touch_post(uint32_t type, uint32_t finger, uint32_t x, uint32_t y);
void hakios_input_init(void);
void hakios_virtio_input_init(void);   /* boot-arg virtio_input=1: QEMU's virtio pointer and keyboard */
void hakios_goodix_init(void);         /* boot-arg touchscreen=1: the phone's touch screen */
void hakios_cpufreq_init(void);        /* boot-arg cpufreq=1: the phone's processor at full speed */
#endif

#endif /* _SYS_HAKIOS_INPUT_H_ */
```

`userland/src/hakios_metallib.c`:

```c
/*
 * The MTLB container (userland/src/hakios_metallib.h): what tools/metallib.py reads, with every offset checked.
 *
 *   0x00  "MTLB"
 *   0x04  u16 u16      the container's version
 *   0x10  u64          the file's size
 *   0x18  u64 u64      the function list: where it starts, and how long it is after its count (tools/metallib.py calls
 *                      the second "funcs_end" and does not use it; on every file of the system, the start plus 4 plus it is
 *                      where the entries end)
 *   0x28  u64 u64      the public metadata (offset, length)        not read here
 *   0x38  u64 u64      the private metadata                        not read here
 *   0x48  u64 u64      the modules: where they start, how long
 *
 * The function list is a u32 count, then one entry per function: a u32 size (counted from the size field itself) and
 * tags until ENDT. A tag is four letters, a u16 length and that many bytes. NAME is the name with its NUL, TYPE one
 * byte, VERS four u16, OFFT three u64 (the last is the module's offset from the start of the modules), MDSZ the
 * module's size.
 */
#include "hakios_metallib.h"

#include <string.h>

#define HEADER_SIZE     0x58

static uint16_t
u16(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return (uint16_t)(p[0] | p[1] << 8);
}

static uint32_t
u32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return (uint32_t)p[0] | (uint32_t)p[1] << 8 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24;
}

static uint64_t
u64(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return (uint64_t)u32(p) | (uint64_t)u32(p + 4) << 32;
}

/* [offset, offset + length) inside a file of SIZE bytes, without the sum wrapping */
static int
inside(uint64_t offset, uint64_t length, uint64_t size)
{
	return offset <= size && length <= size - offset;
}

int
hakios_metallib_parse(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, struct hakios_metallib *info,
    struct hakios_metallib_function *out, uint32_t max, const char **why)
{
	uint64_t list, list_length, list_end, modules, modules_length, p;
	uint32_t count;

	if (size < HEADER_SIZE || memcmp(data, "MTLB", 4) != 0) {
		*why = "not a metallib (no MTLB at the start, or shorter than its header)";
		return -1;
	}
	info->version[0] = u16(data + 4);
	info->version[1] = u16(data + 6);
	info->file_size = u64(data + 0x10);
	list = u64(data + 0x18);
	list_length = u64(data + 0x20);
	modules = u64(data + 0x48);
	modules_length = u64(data + 0x50);
	if (!inside(list, 4, size) || !inside(list + 4, list_length, size)) {
		*why = "the function list is not inside the file";
		return -1;
	}
	if (!inside(modules, modules_length, size)) {
		*why = "the modules are not inside the file";
		return -1;
	}
	list_end = list + 4 + list_length;
	count = u32(data + list);
	info->count = count;
	p = list + 4;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		struct hakios_metallib_function f = { .type = HAKIOS_METALLIB_NO_TYPE };
		uint64_t entry, end, q;
		int have_offset = 0, have_size = 0;

		if (!inside(p, 4, list_end)) {
			*why = "the function list ends before its count of functions";
			return -1;
		}
		entry = u32(data + p);
		if (entry < 4 || !inside(p, entry, list_end)) {
			*why = "a function's entry is not inside the function list";
			return -1;
		}
		end = p + entry;
		for (q = p + 4; q + 4 <= end && memcmp(data + q, "ENDT", 4) != 0;) {
			const uint8_t *value;
			uint16_t length;

			if (!inside(q, 6, end)) {
				*why = "a tag runs past the end of its function's entry";
				return -1;
			}
			length = u16(data + q + 4);
			if (!inside(q + 6, length, end)) {
				*why = "a tag's value runs past the end of its function's entry";
				return -1;
			}
			value = data + q + 6;
			if (memcmp(data + q, "NAME", 4) == 0) {
				f.name = (const char *)value;
				f.name_length = length;
				while (f.name_length > 0 && f.name[f.name_length - 1] == '\0') {
					f.name_length--;
				}
			} else if (memcmp(data + q, "TYPE", 4) == 0 && length >= 1) {
				f.type = value[0];
			} else if (memcmp(data + q, "VERS", 4) == 0 && length >= 8) {
				for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
					f.air[k] = u16(value + 2 * k);
				}
			} else if (memcmp(data + q, "OFFT", 4) == 0 && length >= 24) {
				f.module_offset = u64(value + 16);
				have_offset = 1;
			} else if (memcmp(data + q, "MDSZ", 4) == 0 && length >= 8) {
				f.module_size = u64(value);
				have_size = 1;
			}
			q += 6 + (uint64_t)length;
		}
		if (f.name == NULL || !have_offset || !have_size) {
			*why = "a function has no NAME, OFFT or MDSZ";
			return -1;
		}
		if (!inside(f.module_offset, f.module_size, modules_length)) {
			*why = "a function's module is not inside the modules";
			return -1;
		}
		f.module_offset += modules;
		if (i < max) {
			out[i] = f;
		}
		p = end;
	}
	return 0;
}

#define FAT_MAGIC       0xcafebabeu
#define CPU_TYPE_AIR64  0x01000017u     /* the AIR slice's cputype, as Metal looks for it */

static uint32_t
be32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return (uint32_t)p[0] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 8 | (uint32_t)p[3];
}

int
hakios_metallib_thin(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, const uint8_t **thin, size_t *thin_size, const char **why)
{
	uint32_t count;

	if (size < 8 || be32(data) != FAT_MAGIC) {
		*thin = data;
		*thin_size = size;
		return 0;
	}
	count = be32(data + 4);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count && i < 64; i++) {
		uint64_t at = 8 + 20 * (uint64_t)i;

		if (!inside(at, 20, size)) {
			break;
		}
		if (be32(data + at) == CPU_TYPE_AIR64) {
			uint32_t offset = be32(data + at + 8), length = be32(data + at + 12);

			if (!inside(offset, length, size)) {
				*why = "a universal metallib whose AIR64 slice is not inside it";
				return -1;
			}
			*thin = data + offset;
			*thin_size = length;
			return 0;
		}
	}
	*why = "a universal metallib with no AIR64 slice (only code for Apple's own GPUs)";
	return -1;
}

const char *
hakios_metallib_type_name(uint8_t type)
{
	static const char *const names[] = { "vertex", "fragment", "kernel", "unqualified", "visible", "extern", "intersection" };

	return type < sizeof(names) / sizeof(names[0]) ? names[type] : "?";
}

int
hakios_metallib_bitcode(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, const struct hakios_metallib_function *function,
    const uint8_t **bitcode, uint64_t *length)
{
	const uint8_t *module = data + function->module_offset;
	uint32_t offset, wrapped;

	if (!inside(function->module_offset, function->module_size, size)) {
		return -1;
	}
	if (function->module_size >= 16 && u32(module) == 0x0B17C0DEu) {
		offset = u32(module + 8);
		wrapped = u32(module + 12);
		if (!inside(offset, wrapped, function->module_size)) {
			return -1;
		}
		*bitcode = module + offset;
		*length = wrapped;
		return 0;
	}
	*bitcode = module;
	*length = function->module_size;
	return 0;
}

```

`userland/src/hakios_metallib.h`:

```h
/*
 * A .metallib taken apart: the MTLB container Apple's shader compiler writes, its list of functions, and where each
 * function's module (LLVM bitcode, "AIR") is. The same reading as tools/metallib.py, in C, for the Metal plug-in
 * (userland/src/HakiosMetal.m: -newLibraryWithData:, -newLibraryWithURL:) and for tools/metallib-test.sh, which checks
 * the two against each other on every .metallib of the system.
 *
 * The file is not trusted: a program hands the device whatever bytes it likes. Every offset and length is checked
 * against the size before it is used, and a file that does not hold together is refused with the reason.
 */
#ifndef HAKIOS_METALLIB_H
#define HAKIOS_METALLIB_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* the TYPE tag (tools/metallib.py, checked against the metadata of the system's 456 modules) */
enum hakios_metallib_type {
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_VERTEX = 0,
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_FRAGMENT = 1,
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_KERNEL = 2,
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_UNQUALIFIED = 3,
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_VISIBLE = 4,
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_EXTERN = 5,
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_INTERSECTION = 6,
	HAKIOS_METALLIB_NO_TYPE = 255,          /* the entry has no TYPE tag */
};

struct hakios_metallib_function {
	const char *name;                       /* into the file's bytes, NAME_LENGTH long; not NUL-terminated of itself */
	uint32_t name_length;
	uint8_t type;                           /* enum hakios_metallib_type, or the number as the file has it */
	uint16_t air[4];                        /* VERS: the AIR version (2.8.4.0) */
	uint64_t module_offset;                 /* the module's first byte, from the start of the file */
	uint64_t module_size;
};

struct hakios_metallib {
	uint16_t version[2];                    /* the container's (32769.2 on Darwin userland 16.5) */
	uint64_t file_size;                     /* what the header says the file is */
	uint32_t count;                         /* the functions in the file (more than were kept, if the caller's array was short) */
};

/*
 * Reads DATA (SIZE bytes). Up to MAX functions go into OUT (which may be NULL when MAX is 0, to count them first).
 * 0 on success; -1 on a file that is not a metallib or does not hold together, with *WHY saying where.
 */
int hakios_metallib_parse(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, struct hakios_metallib *info,
    struct hakios_metallib_function *out, uint32_t max, const char **why);

/*
 * The AIR of a universal metallib: a fat container (0xCAFEBABE, big endian, 20-byte entries as Mach-O's) of an AIR64 metallib and
 * a binary for Apple's own GPUs, the way the frameworks of newer systems ship their libraries (QuartzCore's default.metallib on
 * iPadOS 17: UniXNU's AdrenoMetal found it, and takes the AIR64 slice as Metal itself does). A thin metallib is returned as it is.
 * 0 with *THIN and *THIN_SIZE, or -1 (with *WHY) for a fat file with no AIR64 slice or one that is not inside it.
 */
int hakios_metallib_thin(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, const uint8_t **thin, size_t *thin_size, const char **why);

/* the TYPE number as tools/metallib.py names it: "vertex", "fragment", "kernel", ... */
const char *hakios_metallib_type_name(uint8_t type);

/*
 * The function's module without the LLVM bitcode wrapper (0x0B17C0DE: the header that says where the bitcode is in it),
 * if it has one: *BITCODE and *LENGTH, into DATA. 0, or -1 if the wrapper points outside the module.
 */
int hakios_metallib_bitcode(const uint8_t *data, size_t size, const struct hakios_metallib_function *function,
    const uint8_t **bitcode, uint64_t *length);

#endif

```

`userland/src/hello.c`:

```c
/*
 * First user-space program for the Darwin-on-redwood bring-up.
 *
 * A static arm64 Mach-O with no libc and no dyld: it talks to the kernel with
 * raw system calls. The kernel's mockfs presents the ramdisk (this very file)
 * as /sbin/launchd, so this runs as process 1.
 */
typedef unsigned long u64;

/* XNU arm64 system call: number in x16, arguments in x0.., "svc #0x80"; carry set on error */
static long
syscall3(long num, long a, long b, long c)
{
	register long x16 __asm__("x16") = num;
	register long x0 __asm__("x0") = a;
	register long x1 __asm__("x1") = b;
	register long x2 __asm__("x2") = c;
	__asm__ volatile ("svc #0x80" : "+r" (x0) : "r" (x16), "r" (x1), "r" (x2) : "memory", "cc");
	return x0;
}

/* the same with six arguments, for sysctlbyname(name, namelen, old, &oldlen, new, newlen) */
static long
syscall6(long num, long a, long b, long c, long d, long e, long f)
{
	register long x16 __asm__("x16") = num;
	register long x0 __asm__("x0") = a;
	register long x1 __asm__("x1") = b;
	register long x2 __asm__("x2") = c;
	register long x3 __asm__("x3") = d;
	register long x4 __asm__("x4") = e;
	register long x5 __asm__("x5") = f;
	__asm__ volatile ("svc #0x80" : "+r" (x0) : "r" (x16), "r" (x1), "r" (x2), "r" (x3), "r" (x4), "r" (x5) : "memory", "cc");
	return x0;
}

#define SYS_exit    1
#define SYS_write   4
#define SYS_open    5
#define SYS_getpid  20
#define SYS_getuid  24
#define SYS_select  93
#define SYS_sysctlbyname 274
#define O_RDWR      2

static unsigned
length(const char *s)
{
	unsigned n = 0;
	while (s[n]) {
		n++;
	}
	return n;
}

static void
put(int fd, const char *s)
{
	syscall3(SYS_write, fd, (long)s, length(s));
}

static void
put_number(int fd, long v)
{
	char buf[24];
	int i = sizeof(buf);
	buf[--i] = 0;
	do {
		buf[--i] = (char)('0' + v % 10);
		v /= 10;
	} while (v);
	put(fd, buf + i);
}

/* "name=value" for a string sysctl, or nothing at all if the kernel has no such name (the driver is off) */
static void
show_string(int fd, const char *name)
{
	char value[1100];
	u64 size = sizeof(value);

	if (syscall6(SYS_sysctlbyname, (long)name, length(name), (long)value, (long)&size, 0, 0) == 0) {
		put(fd, name);
		put(fd, "=");
		put(fd, value);
		put(fd, "\n");
	}
}

/* ... for an int sysctl (four bytes) */
static void
show_int(int fd, const char *name)
{
	int value = 0;
	u64 size = sizeof(value);

	if (syscall6(SYS_sysctlbyname, (long)name, length(name), (long)&value, (long)&size, 0, 0) == 0) {
		put(fd, name);
		put(fd, "=");
		if (value < 0) {
			put(fd, "-");
			value = -value;
		}
		put_number(fd, value);
		put(fd, "\n");
	}
}

/* hello_wait=N in the kernel's command line (kern.bootargs): N, or 0 */
static long
wait_seconds(void)
{
	char args[700];
	u64 size = sizeof(args);
	long n = 0;

	if (syscall6(SYS_sysctlbyname, (long)"kern.bootargs", 13, (long)args, (long)&size, 0, 0) != 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	for (char *c = args; *c; c++) {
		if (c[0] == 'h' && c[1] == 'e' && c[2] == 'l' && c[3] == 'l' && c[4] == 'o' && c[5] == '_' && c[6] == 'w' &&
		    c[7] == 'a' && c[8] == 'i' && c[9] == 't' && c[10] == '=') {
			for (c += 11; *c >= '0' && *c <= '9'; c++) {
				n = n * 10 + (*c - '0');
			}
			return n;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

void
start(void)
{
	int fd = (int)syscall3(SYS_open, (long)"/dev/console", O_RDWR, 0);

	put(fd, "\nHello from user space on Darwin!\n");
	put(fd, "I am process ");
	put_number(fd, syscall3(SYS_getpid, 0, 0, 0));
	put(fd, ", uid ");
	put_number(fd, syscall3(SYS_getuid, 0, 0, 0));
	put(fd, ", console fd ");
	put_number(fd, fd);
	put(fd, ".\n");

	/*
	 * The kernel's own version: sysctl kern.hakios.version, which the loader gave the kernel on its command line
	 * (hakios_kver, from the payload's kernel.ver). The same string the banner shows under hello hakios-kernel!
	 */
	{
		char version[96];
		u64 size = sizeof(version);
		long failed = syscall6(SYS_sysctlbyname, (long)"kern.hakios.version", 19, (long)version, (long)&size, 0, 0);

		put(fd, "kernel.ver=");
		put(fd, failed ? "(sysctl kern.hakios.version not available)" : version);
		put(fd, "\n");
	}

	/* What the drivers that are on say about the chip, through the same door (a driver that is off has no such name) */
	show_string(fd, "kern.hakios.soc_name");
	show_int(fd, "kern.hakios.soc_id");
	show_int(fd, "kern.hakios.pmic_peripherals");
	show_string(fd, "kern.hakios.thermal_sensors");

	/*
	 * hello_wait=N: stay N seconds, and say once in five how warm the SoC is. Process 1 is not supposed to exit (doing so
	 * panics the kernel, which ends the test run), so this is also how a run is made to last.
	 */
	for (long second = 0, wait = wait_seconds(); second < wait; second++) {
		long tv[2] = { 1, 0 };

		syscall6(SYS_select, 0, 0, 0, 0, (long)tv, 0);
		if (second % 5 == 4) {
			show_int(fd, "kern.hakios.thermal_max_mc");
			show_string(fd, "kern.hakios.thermal_hottest");
		}
	}

	/* Process 1 is not supposed to exit; doing so panics the kernel, which ends the test run. */
	syscall3(SYS_exit, 0, 0, 0);
	for (;;) {
	}
}
```

`userland/src/hello_dyn.c`:

```c
/*
 * The first ordinary program: dynamically linked against the real Darwin
 * libSystem, loaded by the real dyld out of the dyld shared cache.
 */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sys/utsname.h>

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	struct utsname u;
	char *copy = strdup("malloc works");

	printf("Hello from a dynamically linked program! pid %d, %d argument(s)\n", getpid(), argc);
	if (uname(&u) == 0) {
		printf("uname: %s %s %s\n", u.sysname, u.release, u.machine);
	}
	printf("heap: %s (%p), stack near %p, main at %p, printf at %p\n", copy, (void *)copy, (void *)&u, (void *)main, (void *)printf);
	for (int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
		printf("argv[%d] = %s\n", i, argv[i]);
	}
	free(copy);
	return 7;
}
```

`userland/src/hfs_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * hfs_test: HFS Plus, built into the kernel (bsd/hfs), on a disk of its own -- what the data volume on the phone's flash
 * will be asked to do, tried first in QEMU on a virtio disk.
 *
 * A static program with no libc, run as process 1 from a tiny APFS root that has /dev, /mnt and this as
 * /sbin/launchd (qemu/run-hfs-test.sh). It mounts the volume, reads its size, writes a megabyte, reads it back,
 * renames, counts its own boots in a file on the volume, unmounts, mounts again and checks everything is still
 * there. Every step prints one line; the last is "hfs_test: ALL OK" or the step that failed.
 */
typedef unsigned long u64;
typedef unsigned int u32;
typedef unsigned short u16;

static long
sys6(long num, long a, long b, long c, long d, long e, long f)
{
	register long x16 __asm__("x16") = num;
	register long x0 __asm__("x0") = a;
	register long x1 __asm__("x1") = b;
	register long x2 __asm__("x2") = c;
	register long x3 __asm__("x3") = d;
	register long x4 __asm__("x4") = e;
	register long x5 __asm__("x5") = f;
	long carry;
	__asm__ volatile ("svc #0x80\n cset %1, cs" : "+r" (x0), "=r" (carry) : "r" (x16), "r" (x1), "r" (x2), "r" (x3),
	    "r" (x4), "r" (x5) : "memory", "cc");
	return carry ? -x0 : x0;
}
#define sys3(n, a, b, c) sys6(n, (long)(a), (long)(b), (long)(c), 0, 0, 0)

enum { SYS_exit = 1, SYS_read = 3, SYS_write = 4, SYS_open = 5, SYS_close = 6, SYS_unlink = 10, SYS_fsync = 95,
       SYS_rename = 128, SYS_mkdir = 136, SYS_unmount = 159, SYS_mount = 167, SYS_lseek = 199, SYS_statfs64 = 345 };
#define O_RDONLY 0
#define O_RDWR   2
#define O_CREAT  0x200
#define O_TRUNC  0x400

static unsigned long
slen(const char *s)
{
	unsigned long n = 0;
	while (s[n]) {
		n++;
	}
	return n;
}

static long console = -1;

static void
say(const char *s)
{
	sys3(SYS_write, console, s, slen(s));
}

static void
num(long v)
{
	char b[24];
	int i = 23;
	int neg = v < 0;
	b[i] = 0;
	if (neg) {
		v = -v;
	}
	do {
		b[--i] = '0' + v % 10;
		v /= 10;
	} while (v);
	if (neg) {
		b[--i] = '-';
	}
	say(b + i);
}

static void
fail(const char *what, long err)
{
	say("hfs_test: FAILED: ");
	say(what);
	say(" (");
	num(err);
	say(")\n");
	sys3(SYS_exit, 1, 0, 0);
}

/* struct hfs_mount_args as user space passes it (bsd/hfs/hfs_mount.h) */
struct hfs_args {
	const char *fspec;
	u32 uid, gid;
	u16 mask, pad;
	u32 encoding;
	int tz[2];
	int flags, journal_tbuffer_size, journal_flags, journal_disable;
};

static char buf[1 << 20], back[1 << 20];

static long
mount_hfs(void)
{
	struct hfs_args a = { .fspec = "/dev/rvblk0" };
	return sys6(SYS_mount, (long)"hfs", (long)"/mnt", 0, (long)&a, 0, 0);
}

static void
fill(char *p, u32 seed)
{
	for (u32 i = 0; i < sizeof(buf); i++) {
		seed = seed * 1103515245 + 12345;
		p[i] = (char)(seed >> 16);
	}
}

static int
same(const char *a, const char *b, unsigned long n)
{
	for (unsigned long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		if (a[i] != b[i]) {
			return 0;
		}
	}
	return 1;
}

static long
read_all(const char *path, char *into, unsigned long n)
{
	long fd = sys3(SYS_open, path, O_RDONLY, 0), got = 0, r;
	if (fd < 0) {
		return fd;
	}
	while (got < (long)n && (r = sys3(SYS_read, fd, into + got, n - got)) > 0) {
		got += r;
	}
	sys3(SYS_close, fd, 0, 0);
	return got;
}

void
_start(void)
{
	long r, fd;
	unsigned char sfs[2168];

	console = sys3(SYS_open, "/dev/console", O_RDWR, 0);
	say("hfs_test: start\n");
	if ((r = mount_hfs()) < 0) {
		fail("mount hfs /dev/rvblk0 on /mnt", r);
	}
	say("hfs_test: mounted\n");

	if ((r = sys3(SYS_statfs64, "/mnt", sfs, 0)) < 0) {
		fail("statfs /mnt", r);
	}
	u32 bsize = *(u32 *)(sfs + 0);
	u64 blocks = *(u64 *)(sfs + 8), bfree = *(u64 *)(sfs + 16);
	say("hfs_test: statfs: type ");
	say((const char *)(sfs + 72));
	say(", ");
	num((long)(blocks * bsize >> 20));
	say(" MB, free ");
	num((long)(bfree * bsize >> 20));
	say(" MB\n");

	/* the boots this volume has seen: a counter in a file on it */
	char cnt[8] = { 0 };
	long boots = 0;
	if (read_all("/mnt/boots", cnt, 8) == 8) {
		boots = *(long *)cnt;
	}
	boots++;
	*(long *)cnt = boots;
	if ((fd = sys3(SYS_open, "/mnt/boots", O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644)) < 0 || sys3(SYS_write, fd, cnt, 8) != 8 ||
	    sys3(SYS_fsync, fd, 0, 0) < 0) {
		fail("write /mnt/boots", fd);
	}
	sys3(SYS_close, fd, 0, 0);
	say("hfs_test: this volume's boot number ");
	num(boots);
	say("\n");

	sys3(SYS_mkdir, "/mnt/d", 0755, 0);
	fill(buf, (u32)boots);
	if ((fd = sys3(SYS_open, "/mnt/d/f", O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644)) < 0) {
		fail("create /mnt/d/f", fd);
	}
	if ((r = sys3(SYS_write, fd, buf, sizeof(buf))) != (long)sizeof(buf)) {
		fail("write 1 MB", r);
	}
	if ((r = sys3(SYS_fsync, fd, 0, 0)) < 0) {
		fail("fsync", r);
	}
	sys3(SYS_close, fd, 0, 0);
	if ((r = read_all("/mnt/d/f", back, sizeof(back))) != (long)sizeof(back) || !same(buf, back, sizeof(buf))) {
		fail("read the megabyte back", r);
	}
	say("hfs_test: 1 MB written and read back the same\n");
	sys3(SYS_unlink, "/mnt/d/g", 0, 0);
	if ((r = sys3(SYS_rename, "/mnt/d/f", "/mnt/d/g", 0)) < 0) {
		fail("rename", r);
	}

	if ((r = sys3(SYS_unmount, "/mnt", 0, 0)) < 0) {
		fail("unmount", r);
	}
	if ((r = mount_hfs()) < 0) {
		fail("mount again", r);
	}
	for (unsigned long i = 0; i < sizeof(back); i++) {
		back[i] = 0;
	}
	if ((r = read_all("/mnt/d/g", back, sizeof(back))) != (long)sizeof(back) || !same(buf, back, sizeof(buf))) {
		fail("the megabyte after unmount and mount", r);
	}
	if ((r = sys3(SYS_unmount, "/mnt", 0, 0)) < 0) {
		fail("unmount again", r);
	}
	say("hfs_test: after unmount and mount, the same; boots counted ");
	num(boots);
	say("\nhfs_test: ALL OK\n");
	sys3(SYS_exit, 0, 0, 0);
}

```

`userland/src/init.c`:

```c
/*
 * Process 1 of the Darwin bring-up, until it hands over to the real launchd.
 *
 * It lives in the small image mounted on /redwood (see stage0.c) and
 *   - mounts the data volume on /private/var -- HFS Plus on the phone's flash
 *     (var_hfs=DEV), or else a memory filesystem -- and creates the directories
 *     a system expects there;
 *   - checks what the kernel can do for user space, one line per check;
 *   - runs the commands listed in etc/rc of its image: usually just
 *     "exec /sbin/launchd.darwin", which turns process 1 into the Darwin launchd;
 *   - halts the machine if it is still process 1 after that.
 *
 * Started with a file name by anything else, it is a command runner: that is
 * how a launchd job (LaunchDaemons/com.hakios.demo.plist) runs a list of
 * commands.
 */
#include "mini.h"

#define PATTERN_SIZE    300000
#define RB_HALT         0x08

static int checks, failures;

/* Where this program's own image is mounted ("" when it is the root itself). */
static const char *base = "";

/* A path inside our own image; the result is valid until the next call. */
static const char *
in_image(const char *path)
{
	static char buf[256];

	strcpy(buf, base);
	strcpy(buf + strlen(buf), path);
	return buf;
}

/* ---- the Darwin root volume on the phone's flash as the root (boot-arg root_apfs=DEV) ---- */

/* the root is the Darwin volume: its /sbin/launchd is Apple's, there is no launchd.darwin */
static int flash_root_mode;

static void check(int ok, const char *what);

/* dst = a + b + c (each call's result only until the next) */
static const char *
join(const char *a, const char *b, const char *c)
{
	static char buf[1200];
	size_t la = strlen(a), lb = strlen(b), lc = strlen(c);

	if (la + lb + lc >= sizeof(buf)) {
		buf[0] = 0;
		return buf;
	}
	memcpy(buf, a, la);
	memcpy(buf + la, b, lb);
	memcpy(buf + la + lb, c, lc + 1);
	return buf;
}

/* The value of boot-arg NAME on the kernel's command line, or NULL. */
static const char *
boot_arg(const char *name)
{
	static char args[1024], value[128];
	size_t len = sizeof(args) - 1, n = strlen(name);

	if (sysctlbyname("kern.bootargs", args, &len, NULL, 0) != 0) {
		return NULL;
	}
	args[len < sizeof(args) ? len : sizeof(args) - 1] = 0;
	for (char *p = args; *p;) {
		while (*p == ' ') {
			p++;
		}
		if (strncmp(p, name, n) == 0 && p[n] == '=') {
			size_t i = 0;

			for (p += n + 1; *p && *p != ' ' && i < sizeof(value) - 1; p++) {
				value[i++] = *p;
			}
			value[i] = 0;
			return value;
		}
		while (*p && *p != ' ') {
			p++;
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

/* A directory of this image (or anything else) shown in place of one of the volume's: bindfs. */
static int
bind_dir(const char *from, const char *to)
{
	int ok = mount("bindfs", to, MNT_RDONLY, (void *)from) == 0;

	if (!ok) {
		printf("  bindfs %s on %s: %s\n", from, to, strerror(errno));
	}
	return ok;
}

/* An empty directory that is not on the volume, for a mount point (sysctl kern.apfs_synthetic). */
static int
synthetic_dir(const char *path)
{
	int ok = sysctlbyname("kern.apfs_synthetic", NULL, NULL, (void *)path, strlen(path)) == 0;

	if (!ok) {
		printf("  synthetic directory %s: %s\n", path, strerror(errno));
	}
	return ok;
}

/*
 * root_apfs=DEV: the root is to be the Darwin root volume on /dev/DEV -- the phone's flash, read
 * only.  The kernel has started off the boot volume of flashboot.apfs (the resident image, md0,
 * its first container: stage0, firmware, mount points; the OS cryptex with the dyld shared cache
 * is its second container) and stage0 has mounted this image on /redwood.  What the big system image changes in Darwin (userland/build.sh) is put in place on
 * the volume instead, without writing to it:
 *   - our choice of launchd jobs instead of Darwin's 500 (this image's LaunchDaemons, and
 *     nothing for NanoLaunchDaemons, LaunchAngels, nor xpc's launchd.plist, which launchd
 *     would read instead of the directory);
 *   - only our audio device among the audio server's plug-ins;
 *   - the applications Darwin installs on its first boot (private/var/staged_system_apps)
 *     among the system's own in /Applications: another name for each there (a synthetic
 *     entry of the volume -- not a mount, which whatever registers the system's
 *     applications passed over), made before /private/var is covered by a memory
 *     filesystem.
 * Then the volume becomes the root (sysctl kern.hakios_switch_root) and the boot volume
 * goes to its /private/preboot, the cryptexes onto that volume's Cryptexes/OS and App: the Darwin
 * volume's /System/Cryptexes/OS and App point to /private/preboot/Cryptexes/OS and App, and the
 * kernel takes a shared cache from the first.  This
 * image goes along with it, to /private/preboot/redwood, and is bound back on /redwood, a
 * synthetic directory of the volume.  The boot-args stay those of a RAM disk (rd=md0),
 * which is what launchd reads to leave out the boot tasks of a real device.
 */
#ifndef EINVAL
#define EINVAL 22
#endif
/*
 * Mount a cryptex on /private/preboot/Cryptexes/NAME: container C (",c=N") of md0, or, when md0 has
 * no such container (EINVAL: the RAM part of the boot is the boot volume alone), the same container
 * of the device the Darwin volume came from.  Neither: said, and a check fails.
 */
static void
mount_cryptex(const char *name, const char *container, const char *flashdev)
{
	char at[64], spec[128], what[200];
	int err;

	strcpy(at, join("/private/preboot/Cryptexes/", name, ""));
	strcpy(spec, join("/dev/md0", container, ""));
	if (mount("apfs", at, MNT_RDONLY, (void *)spec) != 0) {
		err = errno;
		if (err != EINVAL) {
			printf("  the %s cryptex from %s: %s\n", name, spec, strerror(err));
		}
		strcpy(spec, join(flashdev, container, ""));
		if (mount("apfs", at, MNT_RDONLY, (void *)spec) != 0) {
			printf("  the %s cryptex from %s: %s\n", name, spec, strerror(errno));
			strcpy(what, join("the ", name, " cryptex: in neither md0 nor the flash"));
			check(0, what);
			return;
		}
	}
	strcpy(what, join("the ", name, " cryptex ("));
	strcpy(what, join(what, spec, ") on "));
	strcpy(what, join(what, at, ""));
	check(1, what);
}

static void
flash_root(const char *dev)
{
	static char buf[8192];
	char devpath[96], name[256], from[800], to[400];
	struct stat fw_st;
	off_t pos = 0;
	ssize_t n;
	int fd, ok, apps = 0, bound = 0;

	printf("\n-- the Darwin root volume on /dev/%s as the root --\n", dev);
	strcpy(devpath, join("/dev/", dev, ""));
	ok = mount("apfs", "/flash", MNT_RDONLY, devpath) == 0;
	if (!ok) {
		printf("  mount %s: %s\n", devpath, strerror(errno));
	}
	check(ok, "mount the Darwin volume read only");
	if (!ok) {
		return;
	}
	check(synthetic_dir("/flash/redwood"), "a synthetic /redwood on it, for this image");
	check(bind_dir(in_image("/LaunchDaemons"), "/flash/System/Library/LaunchDaemons") &&
	    bind_dir(in_image("/empty"), "/flash/System/Library/NanoLaunchDaemons") &&
	    bind_dir(in_image("/empty"), "/flash/System/Library/LaunchAngels") &&
	    bind_dir(in_image("/xpc"), "/flash/System/Library/xpc"), "our launchd jobs, not Darwin's");
	check(bind_dir(in_image("/hal"), "/flash/System/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL"),
	    "our audio device, not Apple's plug-ins");
	if (stat("/fw", &fw_st) == 0) {
		/* the audio DSP's firmware and the speakers' configuration, from the RAM image as in a RAM boot */
		check(synthetic_dir("/flash/fw") && bind_dir("/fw", "/flash/fw"), "the firmware on /fw (adsp=1, sound=N)");
	}
	if (stat("/jb-bin", &fw_st) == 0) {
		/*
		 * The package manager's prefix is in the boot volume (/jb), and Sileo runs mv, cp, rm, mkdir
		 * and chmod from /bin, where Darwin has df and ps alone (userland/build.sh, SILEO_BIN): the boot
		 * volume's jb-bin -- those five, links into the prefix -- over the volume's /bin as a union
		 * mount, through which what it does not have is found in the /bin below.
		 */
		ok = mount("bindfs", "/flash/bin", MNT_RDONLY | MNT_UNION, (void *)"/jb-bin") == 0;
		if (!ok) {
			printf("  bindfs /jb-bin on /flash/bin, union: %s\n", strerror(errno));
		}
		check(ok, "Sileo's programs in /bin, over the volume's own");
	}

	fd = open("/flash/private/var/staged_system_apps", O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY, 0);
	while (fd >= 0 && (n = getdirentries(fd, buf, sizeof(buf), &pos)) > 0) {
		for (char *p = buf; p < buf + n;) {
			struct dirent *de = (struct dirent *)(void *)p;
			size_t len = de->d_namlen;

			if (de->d_reclen == 0) {
				break;
			}
			p += de->d_reclen;
			if (len < 5 || len >= sizeof(name) || strncmp(de->d_name + len - 4, ".app", 4) != 0) {
				continue;
			}
			memcpy(name, de->d_name, len);
			name[len] = 0;
			apps++;
			/* another name for it in /Applications, on the same volume: no mount point to skip */
			strcpy(to, join("/flash/Applications/", name, "="));
			strcpy(from, join(to, "/flash/private/var/staged_system_apps/", name));
			if (synthetic_dir(from)) {
				bound++;
			}
		}
	}
	if (fd >= 0) {
		close(fd);
	}
	printf("  %d applications waiting to be installed, %d of them in /Applications\n", apps, bound);
	check(apps > 0 && bound == apps, "the first boot's applications in /Applications");

	ok = sysctlbyname("kern.hakios_switch_root", NULL, NULL, "/flash private/preboot", 22) == 0;
	if (!ok) {
		printf("  switching the root: %s\n", strerror(errno));
	}
	check(ok, "the Darwin volume is the root, the RAM part of the boot on /private/preboot");
	if (!ok) {
		return;
	}
	chdir("/");
	/*
	 * The cryptexes, where Darwin grafts them: the boot volume's empty Cryptexes/OS and Cryptexes/App,
	 * now /private/preboot/Cryptexes/OS and App, where the Darwin volume's /System/Cryptexes/OS and App
	 * point (and the kernel takes a shared cache from the first, bsd/vm/vm_unix.c).  Each from md0 when
	 * the RAM part of the boot has it (flashboot.apfs: the second and third containers), else from
	 * the flash -- darwin, where Apple's images lie as they are after the Darwin volume (containers 1 and 2
	 * of the root's own device).
	 */
	mount_cryptex("OS", ",c=1", devpath);
	mount_cryptex("App", ",c=2", devpath);
	check(bind_dir("/private/preboot/redwood", "/redwood"), "this image back on /redwood");
	flash_root_mode = 1;
}

static void
check(int ok, const char *what)
{
	checks++;
	if (!ok) {
		failures++;
	}
	printf("[%s] %s\n", ok ? " ok " : "FAIL", what);
}

/* Same formula as build.sh uses to generate the file. */
static unsigned char
pattern(unsigned long i)
{
	return (unsigned char)(i * 31 + (i >> 8));
}

static void
show_system(void)
{
	char type[32] = "?", release[32] = "?", machine[32] = "?", version[256] = "?";
	unsigned long long memsize = 0, pagesize = 0;
	int ncpu = 0;
	size_t len;

	len = sizeof(type), sysctlbyname("kern.ostype", type, &len, NULL, 0);
	len = sizeof(release), sysctlbyname("kern.osrelease", release, &len, NULL, 0);
	len = sizeof(version), sysctlbyname("kern.version", version, &len, NULL, 0);
	len = sizeof(machine), sysctlbyname("hw.machine", machine, &len, NULL, 0);
	len = sizeof(memsize), sysctlbyname("hw.memsize", &memsize, &len, NULL, 0);
	len = sizeof(pagesize), sysctlbyname("hw.pagesize", &pagesize, &len, NULL, 0);
	len = sizeof(ncpu), sysctlbyname("hw.ncpu", &ncpu, &len, NULL, 0);

	printf("%s %s %s\n%s\n", type, release, machine, version);
	printf("memory %llu MB, page size %llu, %d cpu\n\n", memsize >> 20, pagesize, ncpu);
	check(strcmp(type, "Darwin") == 0 && memsize != 0, "sysctl: kernel identifies itself");
}

static void
mode_string(unsigned mode, char *out)
{
	static const char bits[] = "rwxrwxrwx";

	out[0] = (mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR ? 'd' : (mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFLNK ? 'l' :
	    (mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFCHR ? 'c' : (mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFBLK ? 'b' : (mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFSOCK ? 's' : '-';
	for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
		out[1 + i] = (mode & (0400 >> i)) ? bits[i] : '-';
	}
	out[10] = 0;
}

/* ls -lR; returns the number of entries seen, or -1 */
static int
list_tree(const char *path, int depth)
{
	static char buf[8192];          /* one directory at a time: the contents are copied out before recursing */
	char names[32][64];
	int count = 0, subdirs = 0, total = 0;
	off_t position = 0;
	ssize_t n;
	int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY, 0);

	if (fd < 0) {
		printf("  %s: %s\n", path, strerror(errno));
		return -1;
	}
	while ((n = getdirentries(fd, buf, sizeof(buf), &position)) > 0) {
		for (ssize_t at = 0; at < n;) {
			struct dirent *de = (struct dirent *)(buf + at);
			char full[256], mode[12], target[128];
			struct stat st;

			at += de->d_reclen;
			if (strcmp(de->d_name, ".") == 0 || strcmp(de->d_name, "..") == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			strcpy(full, path);
			if (full[strlen(full) - 1] != '/') {
				strcpy(full + strlen(full), "/");
			}
			strcpy(full + strlen(full), de->d_name);
			if (lstat(full, &st) != 0) {
				printf("  %s: %s\n", full, strerror(errno));
				close(fd);
				return -1;
			}
			mode_string(st.st_mode, mode);
			printf("  %s %2u %8lld %s", mode, st.st_nlink, st.st_size, full);
			if ((st.st_mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFLNK) {
				ssize_t t = readlink(full, target, sizeof(target) - 1);

				target[t > 0 ? t : 0] = 0;
				printf(" -> %s", target);
			}
			printf("\n");
			count++;
			if (de->d_type == DT_DIR && depth > 0 && subdirs < 32 && strlen(full) < 64) {
				strcpy(names[subdirs++], full);
			}
		}
	}
	close(fd);
	if (n < 0) {
		return -1;
	}
	total = count;
	for (int i = 0; i < subdirs; i++) {
		int sub = list_tree(names[i], depth - 1);

		if (sub < 0) {
			return -1;
		}
		total += sub;
	}
	return total;
}

static void
test_files(void)
{
	static unsigned char buf[65536];
	char text[128];
	struct stat st;
	int fd, good;
	ssize_t n;
	unsigned long done;
	unsigned char *map;

	printf("\n-- read-only filesystem --\n");
	check(list_tree(*base ? base : "/", 3) >= 8, "walk our image (readdir, lstat, readlink)");
	check(stat("/usr/lib/dyld", &st) != 0 || st.st_size > 100000, "the system image has the dynamic linker");

	fd = open(in_image("/etc/motd"), O_RDONLY, 0);
	n = fd >= 0 ? read(fd, text, sizeof(text) - 1) : -1;
	text[n > 0 ? n : 0] = 0;
	close(fd);
	printf("  etc/motd: %s", text);
	check(n > 0 && strncmp(text, "Darwin", 6) == 0, "read a small file");

	check(stat("/tmp", &st) == 0 && (st.st_mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR, "follow a symlink to a directory");
	check(open("/nonexistent", O_RDONLY, 0) < 0 && errno == 2, "missing file gives ENOENT");
	check(open(in_image("/etc/newfile"), O_WRONLY | O_CREAT, 0644) < 0 && errno == 30, "creating a file gives EROFS");

	fd = open(in_image("/share/pattern.bin"), O_RDONLY, 0);
	good = fd >= 0 && fstat(fd, &st) == 0 && st.st_size == PATTERN_SIZE;
	for (done = 0; good && done < PATTERN_SIZE; done += (unsigned long)n) {
		n = read(fd, buf, sizeof(buf));
		if (n <= 0) {
			good = 0;
			break;
		}
		for (ssize_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
			if (buf[i] != pattern(done + (unsigned long)i)) {
				good = 0;
			}
		}
	}
	check(good && done == PATTERN_SIZE, "read a 300 KB file and verify every byte");

	good = fd >= 0 && lseek(fd, 123457, SEEK_SET) == 123457 && read(fd, buf, 1000) == 1000;
	for (int i = 0; good && i < 1000; i++) {
		good = buf[i] == pattern(123457 + (unsigned long)i);
	}
	check(good, "seek into the middle and read");

	map = fd >= 0 ? mmap(NULL, PATTERN_SIZE, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0) : MAP_FAILED;
	good = map != MAP_FAILED;
	for (unsigned long i = 0; good && i < PATTERN_SIZE; i++) {
		good = map[i] == pattern(i);
	}
	check(good, "mmap the file and verify every byte (page-in)");
	if (map != MAP_FAILED) {
		munmap(map, PATTERN_SIZE);
	}
	close(fd);
}

static void
test_memory(void)
{
	const size_t size = 64u << 20, step = 4096;
	unsigned long *mem = mmap(NULL, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANON, -1, 0);
	int good = mem != MAP_FAILED;

	printf("\n-- memory --\n");
	for (size_t off = 0; good && off < size; off += step) {
		mem[off / sizeof(*mem)] = off ^ 0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5aUL;
	}
	for (size_t off = 0; good && off < size; off += step) {
		good = mem[off / sizeof(*mem)] == (off ^ 0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5aUL);
	}
	check(good, "64 MB of anonymous memory: touch every page, read it back");
	check(good && munmap(mem, size) == 0, "unmap it");
}

static void
test_processes(void)
{
	char program[128];
	char *argv[] = { program, "one", "two", NULL };
	char *envp[] = { "GREETING=hello from init", NULL };
	int status = 0, fds[2];
	char text[16] = "";
	pid_t pid;

	strcpy(program, in_image("/bin/child"));
	printf("\n-- processes --\n");
	pid = fork();
	if (pid == 0) {
		execve(argv[0], argv, envp);
		printf("  execve: %s\n", strerror(errno));
		_exit(127);
	}
	check(pid > 1, "fork");
	check(pid > 0 && wait4(pid, &status, 0, NULL) == pid && WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 42,
	    "exec a second program from the image, collect its exit status");

	if (pipe(fds) == 0) {
		pid = fork();
		if (pid == 0) {
			close(fds[0]);
			write(fds[1], "ping", 4);
			_exit(0);
		}
		close(fds[1]);
		read(fds[0], text, sizeof(text) - 1);
		close(fds[0]);
		wait4(pid, &status, 0, NULL);
	}
	check(strcmp(text, "ping") == 0, "pipe from a child process");
}

/*
 * Present only in the image that carries the Darwin dyld and shared cache:
 * an ordinary dynamically linked program.
 */
static void
test_dynamic(void)
{
	char program[128];
	char *argv[] = { program, "from", "init", NULL };
	char *envp[] = { "PATH=/bin:/usr/bin", "HOME=/", NULL };
	struct stat st;
	int status = 0;
	pid_t pid;

	strcpy(program, in_image("/bin/hello_dyn"));
	if (stat(argv[0], &st) != 0 || stat("/usr/lib/dyld", &st) != 0) {
		return;
	}
	printf("\n-- dynamic linking --\n");
	pid = fork();
	if (pid == 0) {
		execve(argv[0], argv, envp);
		printf("  execve: %s\n", strerror(errno));
		_exit(127);
	}
	if (pid > 0 && wait4(pid, &status, 0, NULL) == pid) {
		if (WIFEXITED(status)) {
			printf("  %s exited with status %d\n", argv[0], WEXITSTATUS(status));
		} else {
			printf("  %s was killed by signal %d\n", argv[0], WTERMSIG(status));
		}
	}
	check(pid > 0 && WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 7, "run a program through dyld and the shared cache");
}

/* One line of the skeleton list: fields are separated by tabs. Returns the number of fields found. */
static int
split_tabs(char *line, char **fields, int max)
{
	int n = 0;

	while (n < max) {
		fields[n++] = line;
		line = strchr(line, '\t');
		if (line == NULL) {
			break;
		}
		*line++ = 0;
	}
	return n;
}

static long
parse_number(const char *text, int radix)
{
	long value = 0;

	for (; *text >= '0' && *text < '0' + radix; text++) {
		value = value * radix + (*text - '0');
	}
	return value;
}

/*
 * /private/var is an empty directory of the read-only root: give it a
 * memory-backed filesystem and the directories a system expects there.
 * (/tmp is a symlink to /private/var/tmp, as on Darwin.)
 */
static int
copy_file(const char *from, const char *to, int mode, int uid, int gid)
{
	static char buf[4096];
	int in = open(from, O_RDONLY, 0), out, ok = 0;
	ssize_t n;

	if (in < 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	out = open(to, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, mode);
	if (out >= 0) {
		ok = 1;
		while ((n = read(in, buf, sizeof(buf))) > 0) {
			ok = ok && write(out, buf, (size_t)n) == n;
		}
		close(out);
		ok = ok && n == 0 && chmod(to, mode) == 0 && chown(to, uid, gid) == 0;
	}
	close(in);
	return ok;
}

/*
 * Everything under a directory to one owner: the user's corner of the prefix belongs to mobile, and
 * what an application of the prefix makes there later (caches, databases) must belong to it too.
 */
static int
own_tree(const char *path, int uid)
{
	char buf[4096], child[512];
	struct stat st;
	off_t position = 0;
	ssize_t n;
	int ok, fd;

	/*
	 * A link is left alone: there is no lchown here, and the only links in a grafted tree point
	 * into the image, which is read only (the user's corner is copied for real, GRAFT_COPY).
	 */
	if (lstat(path, &st) != 0 || (st.st_mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFLNK) {
		return 1;
	}
	ok = chown(path, uid, uid) == 0;
	if ((st.st_mode & S_IFMT) != S_IFDIR) {
		return ok;
	}
	if ((fd = open(path, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY, 0)) < 0) {
		return ok;
	}
	while ((n = getdirentries(fd, buf, sizeof(buf), &position)) > 0) {
		for (ssize_t at = 0; at < n; at += ((struct dirent *)(buf + at))->d_reclen) {
			const char *name = ((struct dirent *)(buf + at))->d_name;

			if (strcmp(name, ".") == 0 || strcmp(name, "..") == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			if (strlen(path) + strlen(name) + 2 > sizeof(child)) {
				continue;
			}
			strcpy(child, path);
			strcpy(child + strlen(child), "/");
			strcpy(child + strlen(child), name);
			ok = own_tree(child, uid) && ok;
		}
	}
	close(fd);
	return ok;
}

/*
 * The rootless prefix of a package manager, /var/jb: the Procursus bootstrap with Sileo in it
 * (tools/mk-jb.sh) rides in the system image as /jb (or in the boot volume, /private/preboot/jb,
 * with the root on the flash), an APFS image that cannot be written to, while dpkg and apt must be
 * able to write anywhere in their own prefix.
 *
 * Copying all 124 MB of it into the memory filesystem is more than this machine has to spare (the
 * system image is already 2.8 GB of its 4.3 GB), so the prefix is grafted instead: every directory
 * is made for real, and every file and link in it becomes a symbolic link to its twin in /jb. The
 * directories are then writable -- a package that puts a file in /var/jb/usr/bin puts it in memory,
 * next to the links -- while the 114 MB of programs and libraries stay where they are, read only
 * and shared. What dpkg and apt write over rather than beside (their databases and settings) is
 * copied for real: GRAFT_COPY below.
 */
static int
copy_tree(const char *from, const char *to, int *files)
{
	char buf[4096], f[512], t[512], target[512];
	struct stat st;
	off_t position = 0;
	ssize_t n;
	int ok = 1, fd, mode;

	/* The mode of this directory, kept aside: st is used for its entries below. */
	if (lstat(from, &st) != 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	mode = st.st_mode & 07777;
	if (mkdir(to, mode) != 0 || chown(to, 0, 0) != 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	if ((fd = open(from, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY, 0)) < 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	while (ok && (n = getdirentries(fd, buf, sizeof(buf), &position)) > 0) {
		for (ssize_t at = 0; ok && at < n; at += ((struct dirent *)(buf + at))->d_reclen) {
			const char *name = ((struct dirent *)(buf + at))->d_name;

			if (strcmp(name, ".") == 0 || strcmp(name, "..") == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			if (strlen(from) + strlen(name) + 2 > sizeof(f) || strlen(to) + strlen(name) + 2 > sizeof(t)) {
				printf("  %s/%s: the path is too long\n", from, name);
				ok = 0;
				break;
			}
			strcpy(f, from);
			strcpy(f + strlen(f), "/");
			strcpy(f + strlen(f), name);
			strcpy(t, to);
			strcpy(t + strlen(t), "/");
			strcpy(t + strlen(t), name);
			if (lstat(f, &st) != 0) {
				ok = 0;
			} else if ((st.st_mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR) {
				ok = copy_tree(f, t, files);
			} else if ((st.st_mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFLNK) {
				ssize_t length = readlink(f, target, sizeof(target) - 1);

				target[length > 0 ? length : 0] = 0;
				ok = length > 0 && symlink(target, t) == 0;
				(*files)++;
			} else {
				ok = copy_file(f, t, st.st_mode & 07777, 0, 0);
				(*files)++;
			}
			if (!ok) {
				printf("  %s: %s\n", f, strerror(errno));
			}
		}
	}
	close(fd);
	return ok && chmod(to, mode) == 0;
}

/* The parts of the prefix that are written over, not just added to, and so are copied for real. */
static const char *const graft_copy[] = { "Library", "etc", "var", "tmp" };

static int
graft_tree(const char *from, const char *to, int top, int *made, int *linked)
{
	char buf[4096], f[512], t[512];
	struct stat st;
	off_t position = 0;
	ssize_t n;
	int ok = 1, fd, mode;

	/* The mode of this directory, kept aside: st is used for its entries below. */
	if (lstat(from, &st) != 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	mode = st.st_mode & 07777;
	if (mkdir(to, mode) != 0 || chown(to, 0, 0) != 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	(*made)++;
	if ((fd = open(from, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY, 0)) < 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	while (ok && (n = getdirentries(fd, buf, sizeof(buf), &position)) > 0) {
		for (ssize_t at = 0; ok && at < n; at += ((struct dirent *)(buf + at))->d_reclen) {
			const char *name = ((struct dirent *)(buf + at))->d_name;
			int copy_it = 0;

			if (strcmp(name, ".") == 0 || strcmp(name, "..") == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			if (strlen(from) + strlen(name) + 2 > sizeof(f) || strlen(to) + strlen(name) + 2 > sizeof(t)) {
				printf("  %s/%s: the path is too long\n", from, name);
				ok = 0;
				break;
			}
			strcpy(f, from);
			strcpy(f + strlen(f), "/");
			strcpy(f + strlen(f), name);
			strcpy(t, to);
			strcpy(t + strlen(t), "/");
			strcpy(t + strlen(t), name);
			for (unsigned i = 0; top && i < sizeof(graft_copy) / sizeof(graft_copy[0]); i++) {
				copy_it = copy_it || strcmp(name, graft_copy[i]) == 0;
			}
			if (lstat(f, &st) != 0) {
				ok = 0;
			} else if (copy_it) {
				ok = copy_tree(f, t, linked);
			} else if ((st.st_mode & S_IFMT) == S_IFDIR) {
				ok = graft_tree(f, t, 0, made, linked);
			} else {
				ok = symlink(f, t) == 0;
				(*linked)++;
			}
			if (!ok) {
				printf("  %s: %s\n", f, strerror(errno));
			}
		}
	}
	close(fd);
	return ok && chmod(to, mode) == 0;
}

/*
 * A configuration file read whole into a fixed buffer, and loudly when it does not fit.
 *
 * Three places here read a file of ours this way, and all three used to do it with one
 * read() and no check at all, so a file longer than its buffer simply lost its tail. What
 * that looks like is different every time and never looks like a short read: half a program
 * name handed to kern.exec_inject, which then matches nothing and the insertion quietly does
 * not happen; directories of /private/var that are merely absent, which is what cost the
 * package manager's work a long hunt for a missing /var/mobile/tmp; job lines that do not
 * run, which reads as a test that found nothing.
 *
 * The loop matters as much as the size: read() is allowed to return less than it was asked
 * for without being at the end of the file, so a single read() is not enough even when the
 * file does fit. The buffers are still fixed -- this is an init with no allocator worth the
 * name -- but a file that does not fit now says so instead of going quiet.
 *
 * The length, or -1 if there is no such file.
 */
static ssize_t
read_whole(const char *path, char *buf, size_t size)
{
	int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY, 0);
	size_t got = 0;
	ssize_t n;
	char over;

	if (fd < 0) {
		return -1;
	}
	while (got < size - 1 && (n = read(fd, buf + got, size - 1 - got)) > 0) {
		got += (size_t)n;
	}
	/* one byte left to read means the buffer ended, not the file */
	if (got == size - 1 && read(fd, &over, 1) > 0) {
		printf("init: %s does not fit in %zu bytes: the rest of it is not used\n", path, size - 1);
	}
	close(fd);
	buf[got] = 0;
	return (ssize_t)got;
}

/*
 * The data volume on the phone's flash (boot-arg var_hfs=DEV, DEV a node of /dev: ufs_darwin_data, darwin past the
 * Darwin volume and the cryptexes): HFS Plus, which this kernel has built in, so that what Darwin keeps in /private/var is
 * there at the next boot and its size is the size of the space -- not a memory filesystem's quarter of the RAM.
 * Journaled: a phone reset in the middle of a write finds the volume whole at the next mount. If it does not mount
 * (no volume made there yet, or this kernel cannot write it), the memory filesystem as before.
 */
static int var_kept;            /* /private/var is the volume on the flash: what is in it stays */

static int
mount_data_volume(void)
{
	const char *name = boot_arg("var_hfs");
	static char dev[64];
	/* struct hfs_mount_args (bsd/hfs/hfs_mount.h) */
	struct {
		const char *fspec;
```
