```c
 * does it ask UIKit for a background task (a round trip to another daemon, which can wait for ever if
 * that daemon does not answer), and does it ever start a URL session task, for what address.
 */
static unsigned long (*begin_task)(id, SEL, id);
static void (*resume_task)(id, SEL);

static unsigned long
watched_begin_task(id self, SEL cmd, id handler)
{
	unsigned long task;
	char line[160];
	int n;

	n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: %s: asking UIKit for a background task\n", who);
	say(line, (size_t)(n > 0 ? n : 0));
	task = begin_task(self, cmd, handler);
	n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: %s: the background task is %lu\n", who, task);
	say(line, (size_t)(n > 0 ? n : 0));
	return task;
}

static void
watched_resume_task(id self, SEL cmd)
{
	const char *(*string)(id, SEL) = (const char *(*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend;
	id (*get)(id, SEL) = (id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend;
	const char *url = "?";
	char line[700];
	id request, address, text;
	int n;

	request = get(self, sel_registerName("originalRequest"));
	address = request != NULL ? get(request, sel_registerName("URL")) : NULL;
	text = address != NULL ? get(address, sel_registerName("absoluteString")) : NULL;
	if (text != NULL) {
		url = string(text, sel_registerName("UTF8String"));
	}
	n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: %s: starting a session task for %s\n", who,
	    url != NULL ? url : "?");
	say(line, (size_t)(n > 0 ? n : 0));
	resume_task(self, cmd);
}

/*
 * One setting of Sileo's, set for it at every start: "Show Packages From Canister" (ShowProvisional,
 * on by default). Canister is the search service Sileo asks about packages, and where its servers
 * cannot be reached the asking never stops -- 3810 session tasks in two minutes in one run here,
 * and the download of a package never gets its turn among them. With the setting off Sileo keeps to
 * the repositories themselves, which work. The prefix lives in memory and is new at every boot, so
 * there is nowhere to keep this but here. It is done on the main queue, not here in the library's
 * own initializer: at that point Foundation is loaded but has not run its own initializers yet, and
 * asking it for the defaults then kills the application before it says a word.
 */
static void
keep_to_the_repositories(void)
{
	id (*get)(id, SEL) = (id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend;
	id (*from_text)(id, SEL, const char *) = (id (*)(id, SEL, const char *))objc_msgSend;
	void (*set_bool)(id, SEL, signed char, id) = (void (*)(id, SEL, signed char, id))objc_msgSend;
	id defaults = (id)objc_getClass("NSUserDefaults");
	id key = from_text((id)objc_getClass("NSString"), sel_registerName("stringWithUTF8String:"), "ShowProvisional");

	if (defaults == NULL || key == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	defaults = get(defaults, sel_registerName("standardUserDefaults"));
	if (defaults != NULL) {
		set_bool(defaults, sel_registerName("setBool:forKey:"), 0, key);
		say("hakios: Sileo: its Canister search is turned off (it is not reachable here)\n", 73);
	}
}

/*
 * apt-get install, not its simulation (-s...): the one that ends in "Unable to fetch some archives"
 * when Sileo runs it and installs the package when a terminal runs the same command.
 */
static int
apt_install(char *const argv[])
{
	int install = 0;

	if (argv == NULL || argv[0] == NULL || strcmp(argv[0], "apt-get") != 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	for (int i = 1; argv[i] != NULL; i++) {
		if (argv[i][0] == '-' && argv[i][1] == 's') {
			return 0;
		}
		install |= strcmp(argv[i], "install") == 0;
	}
	return install;
}

/*
 * What apt says goes to Sileo, which shows a line of it at most. Run the same apt-get, with the same
 * descriptors, credential and environment, under a shell that first says on the console who it runs
 * as, what lies in apt's archives and what Sileo's index says of the package, and afterwards how apt
 * ended and what the archives hold then. This is how "Unable to fetch some archives" was found: the
 * archives were empty, Sileo's /bin/mv having never run.
 */
static int
spawn_apt_said(pid_t *pid, const posix_spawn_file_actions_t *actions, const posix_spawnattr_t *attr,
    char *const argv[], char *const envp[])
{
	static char script[] =
	    "exec 7>/dev/console; J=/var/jb\n"
	    "echo \"hakios: apt-get runs as $($J/usr/bin/id), in $(pwd)\" >&7\n"
	    "$J/bin/ls -ln $J/var/cache/apt/archives $J/var/lib/apt/sileolists >&7 2>&1\n"
	    "for a in \"$@\"; do case $a in -*|install) ;; *) p=${a%%=*}\n"
	    "  echo \"hakios: $p in sileolists:\" >&7\n"
	    "  $J/usr/bin/grep -h -A30 \"^Package: $p\\$\" $J/var/lib/apt/sileolists/*Packages 2>&1 | $J/usr/bin/head -40 >&7 ;; esac; done\n"
	    "$J/usr/bin/apt-get \"$@\"\n"
	    "s=$?; echo \"hakios: apt-get exits $s; its archives after:\" >&7\n"
	    "$J/bin/ls -ln $J/var/cache/apt/archives >&7 2>&1; exit $s\n";
	char *wrapped[96];
	int k = 0;

	for (int i = 0; envp != NULL && envp[i] != NULL; i++) {
		char line[600];
		int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: %s: apt-get's environment: %s\n", who, envp[i]);

		say(line, (size_t)(n < (int)sizeof(line) ? n : (int)sizeof(line) - 1));
	}
	wrapped[k++] = "sh";
	wrapped[k++] = "-c";
	wrapped[k++] = script;
	wrapped[k++] = "apt-get";
	for (int i = 1; argv[i] != NULL && k < 95; i++) {
		wrapped[k++] = argv[i];
	}
	wrapped[k] = NULL;
	return posix_spawn(pid, "/var/jb/bin/sh", actions, attr, wrapped, envp);
}

/*
 * Every program the application starts, with its arguments. Sileo does everything to the system by
 * spawning its set-user-ID helper, which execs apt or dpkg; the arguments are the whole question
 * when apt's answer to Sileo differs from apt's answer on the command line.
 */
static int
watched_spawn(pid_t *pid, const char *path, const posix_spawn_file_actions_t *actions,
    const posix_spawnattr_t *attr, char *const argv[], char *const envp[])
{
	char line[1200];
	int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: %s: (uid %d) spawns %s", who, (int)getuid(),
	    path != NULL ? path : "?");

	for (int i = 0; argv != NULL && argv[i] != NULL && n < (int)sizeof(line) - 40; i++) {
		n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " %s", argv[i]);
	}
	/*
	 * The size of what it is about to move, while the file is still there: apt refuses the
	 * package Sileo puts in its archives ("Unable to fetch some archives") and takes the very
	 * same package when apt itself fetched it, so the first thing to know is whether the file
	 * is whole.
	 */
	if (argv != NULL && argv[0] != NULL && strcmp(argv[0], "mv") == 0 && argv[1] != NULL) {
		struct stat st;

		if (stat(argv[1], &st) == 0) {
			n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " [%lld bytes]", (long long)st.st_size);
		} else {
			n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, " [no such file]");
		}
	}
	n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof(line) - (size_t)n, "\n");
	say(line, (size_t)n);
	if (apt_install(argv)) {
		return spawn_apt_said(pid, actions, attr, argv, envp);
	}
	n = posix_spawn(pid, path, actions, attr, argv, envp);
	if (n != 0) {
		char said[300];
		int k = snprintf(said, sizeof(said), "hakios: %s: ... and that spawn failed: %s\n", who, strerror(n));

		say(said, (size_t)(k < (int)sizeof(said) ? k : (int)sizeof(said) - 1));
	}
	return n;
}

/*
 * A file the application moves or copies itself (NSFileManager, under Swift's FileManager), when it
 * fails: from where, to where, and what the error says. Sileo moves each download into place this
 * way, and says only "The operation couldn't be completed. No such file or directory".
 */
static const char *
text_of(id object)
{
	id (*get)(id, SEL) = (id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend;
	const char *(*utf8)(id, SEL) = (const char *(*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend;
	id text;

	if (object == NULL) {
		return "(nil)";
	}
	text = (class_respondsToSelector(object_getClass(object), sel_registerName("path")) ?
	    get(object, sel_registerName("path")) : get(object, sel_registerName("description")));
	return text != NULL ? utf8(text, sel_registerName("UTF8String")) : "?";
}

static signed char (*move_url)(id, SEL, id, id, id *), (*copy_url)(id, SEL, id, id, id *);
static signed char (*move_path)(id, SEL, id, id, id *), (*copy_path)(id, SEL, id, id, id *);

static signed char
file_said(const char *what, signed char ok, id from, id to, id error)
{
	if (!ok) {
		char line[1400];
		int n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: %s: %s %s -> %s failed: %s\n", who, what, text_of(from),
		    text_of(to), error != NULL ? text_of(error) : "(no error given)");

		say(line, (size_t)(n < (int)sizeof(line) ? n : (int)sizeof(line) - 1));
	}
	return ok;
}

static signed char
watched_move_url(id self, SEL cmd, id from, id to, id *error)
{
	id mine = NULL;
	signed char ok = move_url(self, cmd, from, to, error != NULL ? error : &mine);

	return file_said("moveItemAtURL", ok, from, to, error != NULL ? *error : mine);
}

static signed char
watched_copy_url(id self, SEL cmd, id from, id to, id *error)
{
	id mine = NULL;
	signed char ok = copy_url(self, cmd, from, to, error != NULL ? error : &mine);

	return file_said("copyItemAtURL", ok, from, to, error != NULL ? *error : mine);
}

static signed char
watched_move_path(id self, SEL cmd, id from, id to, id *error)
{
	id mine = NULL;
	signed char ok = move_path(self, cmd, from, to, error != NULL ? error : &mine);

	return file_said("moveItemAtPath", ok, from, to, error != NULL ? *error : mine);
}

static signed char
watched_copy_path(id self, SEL cmd, id from, id to, id *error)
{
	id mine = NULL;
	signed char ok = copy_path(self, cmd, from, to, error != NULL ? error : &mine);

	return file_said("copyItemAtPath", ok, from, to, error != NULL ? *error : mine);
}

__attribute__((used)) static struct {
	const void *ours, *theirs;
} spawn_interpose __attribute__((section("__DATA,__interpose"))) = {
	(const void *)watched_spawn, (const void *)posix_spawn
};

/* Put ours in the place of a method, keeping the one that was there. */
static void
watch(const char *name, const char *selector, IMP ours, void *theirs)
{
	Class class = objc_getClass(name);
	Method method = class != NULL ? class_getInstanceMethod(class, sel_registerName(selector)) : NULL;

	if (method != NULL && method_getImplementation(method) != ours) {
		*(IMP *)theirs = method_setImplementation(method, ours);
	}
}

__attribute__((constructor))
static void
hakios_app_init(void)
{
	static const int signals[] = { SIGTRAP, SIGABRT, SIGILL, SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGSYS };
	struct sigaction action = { 0 };
	const char *name = getprogname();
	char line[200];
	size_t length = 0;
	int n;

	if (name == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	who = name;
	slide = (uintptr_t)_dyld_get_shared_cache_range(&length) - CACHE_BASE;
	/*
	 * An application's standard error goes nowhere here, and that is where the Swift runtime says
	 * what it is about to die of ("Fatal error: ..."), so it is pointed at the console.
	 */
	console = open("/dev/console", O_WRONLY);
	if (console >= 0) {
		dup2(console, 2);
	}
	action.sa_sigaction = killed;
	action.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO | SA_NODEFER | SA_RESETHAND;
	sigemptyset(&action.sa_mask);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(signals) / sizeof(signals[0]); i++) {
		sigaction(signals[i], &action, NULL);
	}
	if (strcmp(name, "Sileo") == 0) {
		dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{ keep_to_the_repositories(); });
	}
	watch("UIApplication", "beginBackgroundTaskWithExpirationHandler:", (IMP)watched_begin_task, &begin_task);
	/*
	 * NSURLSessionTask alone: its subclasses inherit the very same method, and watching it twice
	 * would leave ours as the "original" of itself -- a call that never returns.
	 */
	watch("NSURLSessionTask", "resume", (IMP)watched_resume_task, &resume_task);
	watch("NSFileManager", "moveItemAtURL:toURL:error:", (IMP)watched_move_url, &move_url);
	watch("NSFileManager", "copyItemAtURL:toURL:error:", (IMP)watched_copy_url, &copy_url);
	watch("NSFileManager", "moveItemAtPath:toPath:error:", (IMP)watched_move_path, &move_path);
	watch("NSFileManager", "copyItemAtPath:toPath:error:", (IMP)watched_copy_path, &copy_path);
	n = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "hakios: %s: started as uid %d (effective %d), watching for what kills it\n",
	    name, (int)getuid(), (int)geteuid());
	say(line, (size_t)(n > 0 ? n : 0));
}
```

`userland/src/inject_media.c`:

```c
/*
 * libhakios.media.dylib: code of ours inside mediaserverd (see inject.c for how it gets there).
 *
 * mediaserverd is the audio server, and also the camera's: the capture stack of CMCapture lives
 * in the same process. Soon after it starts, that stack "prewarms" the Core Image filters of the
 * portrait mode, for which Core Image wants an OpenGL ES context; there is no GPU, the context
 * has no functions behind it, and the daemon jumps to address 0 -- every time launchd restarts
 * it. Nobody is going to take a portrait here: the prewarming is skipped.
 *
 * What the daemon is wanted for meanwhile is neither sound nor the camera: it is where
 * VideoToolbox decodes for everybody else (the service com.apple.coremedia.decompressionsession),
 * and a HEIC picture is HEVC inside. Without the daemon ImageIO has "no way to decode a HEIC",
 * and the stock wallpaper of Darwin userland 16, whose layers are four such pictures, is its gradient alone.
 * There is no hardware decoder here; VideoToolbox takes its software one (VCPHEVC.videocodec).
 *
 * The flashlight (only where the kernel has one: torch=3, /dev/hakios-torch): Control Center's
 * button and AVFlashlight reach FigFlashlight in here, which asks the capture stack's device vendor
 * (+[BWFigCaptureDeviceVendor sharedCaptureDeviceVendor]) for the camera device and its back
 * camera's stream, and sets the stream's "TorchLevel" (0 to 1). Without a camera there is no
 * vendor (it is nil), every message to it does nothing, and FigFlashlight says it has set the level
 * when nothing has been. So where there is no vendor, FigFlashlight -- and only FigFlashlight,
 * by where it calls from -- is given one of ours, with a device and a stream whose torch level goes
 * to the kernel (see flashlight_*() below). Everybody else still gets none, as before.
 *
 * The camera (only where the kernel has one: cam=5, /dev/hakios-camera): the vendor is made for
 * everybody, with the create function of our capture device (camera_device.c) in place of the
 * one H10ISP.mediacapture would give for the iPhone's ISP; the capture graph is built around it and
 * its frames reach Camera.app's preview (see camera_device.c). Its stream takes the torch level too,
 * so FigFlashlight would need nothing of its own then (not tried yet).
 *
 * What the capture stack asks of hardware this phone has none of is refused here: there is no ISP
 * processing session, so there can be no video stabilization (see video_stabilization_method below).
 *
 * CMCapture is not loaded yet when this library is: the methods are replaced when its image
 * arrives.
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreMedia/CoreMedia.h>
#include <CoreVideo/CoreVideo.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <mach-o/dyld.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <objc/message.h>
#include <objc/runtime.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

static void
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[256];
	va_list ap;
	int n;

	va_start(ap, format);
	n = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, ap);
	va_end(ap);
	if (n > (int)sizeof(line) - 1) {
		n = sizeof(line) - 1;
	}
	write(2, line, (size_t)n);
}

extern const void *_dyld_get_shared_cache_range(size_t *length);

#define CACHE_BASE 0x180000000UL                /* where the cache was built to be, before the slide */

static uintptr_t slide;

/* +[BWCoreImageFilterRenderer prewarmPortraitFilterVersion:semanticStyleFilters:] */
static void
prewarm_portrait_filter(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, __unused int version, __unused BOOL styles)
{
}

/* ---- the flashlight ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static int torch = -1;                  /* /dev/hakios-torch */
static bool camera;                     /* /dev/hakios-camera is there */
extern int hakios_camera_device_create(const void *allocator, const void *options, void **out);
static Class vendor_class, device_class, stream_class;
static IMP original_shared_vendor;
static unsigned torch_said;

/*
 * FigFlashlight's functions that ask for the vendor, unslid (20F66): flashlight_IsAvailable,
 * _NotifyForCurrentState and _setupDevice lie together, _teardownDevice apart.
 */
static const struct { uintptr_t from, to; } flashlight_code[] = {
	{ 0x1a1fb0830UL, 0x1a1fb0c5cUL }, { 0x1a1eee5c0UL, 0x1a1eee6e8UL },
};

/* +[BWFigCaptureDeviceVendor sharedCaptureDeviceVendor] */
static id
shared_vendor(id self, SEL selector)
{
	uintptr_t caller = (uintptr_t)__builtin_return_address(0) - slide;
	id vendor = ((id (*)(id, SEL))original_shared_vendor)(self, selector);
	static id ours, camera_vendor;
	static pthread_mutex_t lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

	if (vendor != NULL) {
		return vendor;
	}
	if (!camera && access("/dev/hakios-camera", F_OK) == 0) {
		camera = true;          /* (should the kernel have made it after mediaserverd started) */
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: the kernel has a camera (/dev/hakios-camera)\n");
	}
	if (camera) {
		pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
		if (camera_vendor == NULL) {
			id made = ((id (*)(Class, SEL))objc_msgSend)(objc_getClass("BWFigCaptureDeviceVendor"), sel_registerName("alloc"));

			camera_vendor = ((id (*)(id, SEL, void *))objc_msgSend)(made, sel_registerName("initWithDeviceCreateFunction:"),
			    (void *)hakios_camera_device_create);
			say("hakios: mediaserverd: the camera's device vendor %s\n", camera_vendor ? "made (camera_device.c)" :
			    "CANNOT BE MADE");
		}
		pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
		return camera_vendor;
	}
	for (size_t i = 0; torch >= 0 && i < sizeof(flashlight_code) / sizeof(flashlight_code[0]); i++) {
		if (caller >= flashlight_code[i].from && caller < flashlight_code[i].to) {
			if (ours == NULL) {
				ours = class_createInstance(vendor_class, 0);
				say("hakios: mediaserverd: no camera, so no device vendor: FigFlashlight gets the flashlight's own\n");
			}
			return ours;
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

static void
flashlight_set(uint32_t level)
{
	ssize_t written = write(torch, &level, sizeof(level));

	if (written != (ssize_t)sizeof(level) || torch_said < 40) {
		torch_said++;
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: the flashlight at %u of 1000%s\n", level, written == (ssize_t)sizeof(level) ? "" :
		    " (NOT TAKEN by /dev/hakios-torch)");
	}
}

/* the vendor's: one client, one device, always available to it */
static int
flashlight_register(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, __unused int pid, __unused id description, __unused int priority,
    __unused BOOL steal, __unused BOOL share, __unused id handler)
{
	return 1;
}

static id
flashlight_copy_device(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, __unused int client, __unused BOOL inform, int *error)
{
	if (error != NULL) {
		*error = 0;
	}
	return class_createInstance(device_class, 0);
}

static id
flashlight_copy_stream(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, __unused int position, __unused int type, id device)
{
	return device != NULL && object_getClass(device) == device_class ? class_createInstance(stream_class, 0) : NULL;
}

static void
flashlight_take_back(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, __unused id device, __unused int client, __unused BOOL inform)
{
	flashlight_set(0);
}

static BOOL
flashlight_active_equals(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, id device)
{
	return device == NULL || object_getClass(device) == device_class;
}

/* the stream's -supportedProperties: none that FigFlashlight looks for ("HighCurrentTorchEnabled") */
static id
flashlight_stream_properties(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector)
{
	static CFDictionaryRef none;

	if (none == NULL) {
		none = CFDictionaryCreate(NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	}
	return (id)none;
}

/* the stream's -setProperty:value: -- "TorchLevel", 0 to 1, as thousandths to the kernel */
static int
flashlight_stream_set(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, id key, id value)
{
	float level = 0;

	if (key != NULL && CFEqual((CFTypeRef)key, CFSTR("TorchLevel"))) {
		if (value != NULL && CFGetTypeID((CFTypeRef)value) == CFNumberGetTypeID()) {
			CFNumberGetValue((CFNumberRef)value, kCFNumberFloatType, &level);
		}
		level = level < 0 ? 0 : level > 1 ? 1 : level;
		flashlight_set((uint32_t)(level * 1000 + 0.5f));
	}
	return 0;
}

/*
 * Video stabilization, of which this hardware has none: the capture graph's VIS node
 * (-[FigCaptureVISPipeline _newVISNodeWithUpstreamOutput:...]) is made with the ISP's processing
 * session, and this device has no such session, so the node comes back nil, the VIS pipeline with
 * it, the movie file sink's tail pipeline with that, and captureSession_buildGraphWithConfiguration
 * tears the whole graph down -- the preview too, for all that the preview has nothing to do with
 * stabilizing a recording. The connection's stabilization method is where the whole stack reads the
 * wish from (+[FigVideoCaptureConnectionConfiguration videoStabilizationMethods:includeIris:] ->
 * cspc_getVideoStabilizationType -> the connections' FigCaptureVideoStabilizationType), and 0 there
 * means none: the graph is then built without a VIS pipeline anywhere
 * (+[FigCaptureVISPipeline visPipelineIsRequiredForFigCaptureVideoStabilizationType:] says no to
 * every type but 2 and 3), and recordings are as steady as the hand that holds the phone.
 */
static int
video_stabilization_method(id self, SEL selector)
{
	(void)self;
	(void)selector;
	return 0;
}

/*
 * The type the stack acts on. The connection configuration arrives from the application's
 * AVFoundation with the type in it, which is read straight out of the object and not computed from
 * the method above (-[FigCaptureSessionParsedConfiguration _computeVideoStabilizationTypes] only
 * fills in what the client left out), so the wish has to be refused here as well.
 */
static int
video_stabilization_type(id self, SEL selector)
{
	(void)self;
	(void)selector;
	return 0;                       /* kFigCaptureVideoStabilizationType_None */
}

/*
 * The microphone, which the capture stack has none of here. A capture session's sound comes through
 * CoreMedia's own capture audio session -- BWAudioSourceNode's start sets its properties and reads
 * its pull format, all of it through a brokered plug-in of the audio HAL -- and that plug-in is not
 * on this phone: the node's start comes back with 'nope', the HAL's word for "no such thing".
 *
 * Camera.app's session has an audio input in it, because it is a session for photographs and for
 * video both. The graph starts its source nodes late (startDeferredSourceNodesIfNeeded) and takes
 * the first error it gets for the whole graph's, so the session reported AVCaptureSessionRuntimeError
 * to the application, which took the session down and built it again, two seconds later, for ever:
 * the camera's preview came in bursts of five frames with the sensor powering down in between.
 *
 * The node is told that it started. It then produces no sound -- which is all a phone with no
 * capture audio has to offer -- and the rest of the graph, the preview and the photograph, runs.
 * Only that one error is swallowed: a microphone that is there and fails for another reason still
 * takes the session down, as it should. (The kernel's own microphone, adsp=1 mic=4, is a different
 * path: AVAudioRecorder and Voice Memos record through it, and nothing here touches it.)
 */
#define ERROR_NO_SUCH_THING     1852797029      /* 'nope' */

static IMP original_audio_source_start;

static BOOL
audio_source_start(id self, SEL selector, id *error)
{
	BOOL started = ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL, id *))original_audio_source_start)(self, selector, error);
	id made = error != NULL ? *error : NULL;
	static bool said;

	if (started || made == NULL || ((long (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(made, sel_registerName("code")) != ERROR_NO_SUCH_THING) {
		return started;
	}
	*error = NULL;                  /* (autoreleased by the capture stack: not ours to give back) */
	if (!said) {
		said = true;
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: there is no capture audio on this phone: the session's audio source gives nothing, "
		    "and the camera runs without it\n");
	}
	return true;
}

/*
 * A photograph's quality prioritization, "speed" at the most. Asked for "balanced" (Camera.app's) or
 * "quality", the capture device takes a scene for a low-light one whenever a frame was exposed at
 * least as long as the sensor's still image stabilization threshold
 * (-[BWFigVideoCaptureDevice _isLowLightSceneUsingFrameStatisticsByPortType:]) -- a threshold from
 * the sensor's tuning in CameraSetup.plist, 0 for a sensor it has no tuning for, as ours -- and
 * then asks the stream for a bracket of four frames for SIS fusion (captureType 4, BWSISNode), which
 * this port has nothing to fuse with: the photograph never came. With "speed" it asks for one frame
 * (-_resolveStillImageCaptureTypeFromStatisticsByPortType:..., captureType 1), which the stream
 * gives (camera_device.c, StillImageCaptureNow).
 */
static IMP original_quality_prioritization;

static int
quality_prioritization(id self, SEL selector)
{
	int asked = ((int (*)(id, SEL))original_quality_prioritization)(self, selector);
	static bool said;

	if (asked > 1 && !said) {
		said = true;
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: a photograph's quality prioritization %d taken as 1 (speed): one frame, no SIS bracket\n",
		    asked);
	}
	return asked > 1 ? 1 : asked;
}

/*
 * A photograph's noise reduction (BWGNRNode, between the still image coordinator and the photo
 * encoder) is a FigSampleBufferProcessor of the iPhone's, which is handed the picture and never
 * hands one back here: the photograph stopped there, with no error, and the request with it (the
 * shutter's second press asked for nothing more). The picture goes past it to the node's output as
 * it came, as with no noise reduction to do.
 */
static void
gnr_render(id self, SEL selector, void *sample_buffer, id input)
{
	id output = ((id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(self, sel_registerName("output"));
	static bool said;

	(void)selector, (void)input;
	if (!said) {
		said = true;
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: a photograph goes past the noise reduction, which has nothing to do it with here\n");
	}
	if (output != nil) {
		((void (*)(id, SEL, void *))objc_msgSend)(output, sel_registerName("emitSampleBuffer:"), sample_buffer);
	}
}

static bool
is_node(id node, const char *name)
{
	return node != nil && strcmp(object_getClassName(node), name) == 0;
}

/*
 * How long a photograph's encoding took, from the picture handed to the photo encoder node to the one
 * it hands on (HEVC in software, see register_hevc_encoder below: the slowest step of a photograph).
 */
static void
time_photo_encoder(id output, CMSampleBufferRef sample_buffer)
{
	CVImageBufferRef image = CMSampleBufferGetImageBuffer(sample_buffer);
	static uint64_t began;
	static mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;
	id connection, input;

	if (image == NULL || CVPixelBufferGetWidth(image) < 2000) {
		return;                 /* not a photograph */
	}
	if (is_node(((id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(output, sel_registerName("node")), "BWPhotoEncoderNode")) {
		if (began != 0) {
			if (timebase.denom == 0) {
				mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
			}
			say("hakios: mediaserverd: a photograph of %zux%zu encoded in %.0f ms\n", CVPixelBufferGetWidth(image),
			    CVPixelBufferGetHeight(image), (double)(mach_absolute_time() - began) * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1e6);
		}
		began = 0;
		return;
	}
	connection = ((id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(output, sel_registerName("connection"));
	input = connection != nil ? ((id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(connection, sel_registerName("input")) : nil;
	if (input != nil && is_node(((id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(input, sel_registerName("node")), "BWPhotoEncoderNode")) {
		began = mach_absolute_time();
	}
}

/*
 * A node's output given no sample buffer at all, which no node takes: the session's audio source
 * (-[BWAudioSourceNode _generateSamples]), whose audio unit never started here (see audio_source_start
 * above), fills the silence by a timer with buffers it fails to make and emits them all the same --
 * NULL. Live Photo's staging node added that to an array (-[BWIrisStagingNode renderSampleBuffer:forInput:])
 * and mediaserverd died of the NSInvalidArgumentException, every half a minute with Live Photo on, the
 * preview black for a second each time. A NULL is not passed on.
 */
static IMP original_emit_sample_buffer;

static void
emit_sample_buffer(id self, SEL selector, CMSampleBufferRef sample_buffer)
{
	static bool said;

	if (sample_buffer == NULL) {
		if (!said) {
			said = true;
			say("hakios: mediaserverd: a node's output was given no sample buffer (the silent audio source's): not passed on\n");
		}
		return;
	}
	time_photo_encoder(self, sample_buffer);
	((void (*)(id, SEL, CMSampleBufferRef))original_emit_sample_buffer)(self, selector, sample_buffer);
}

/*
 * The photograph's encoder. Camera.app asks for HEIC -- HEVC inside a HEIF file, which CMPhoto makes
 * through VideoToolbox -- and VideoToolbox here has no HEVC encoder but the iPhone's hardware ones
 * (com.apple.videotoolbox.videoencoder.hevc and .hevc.gva, behind its AVE): the photo encoder node
 * failed with kVTCouldNotFindVideoEncoderErr (-12908). Apple's software HEVC codec is in the system
 * all the same, VCPHEVC.videocodec, whose decoder VideoToolbox takes here for every HEIC picture (see
 * the top), and there is an encoder in it, HEVCVideoEncoder_CreateInstance, that Darwin never registers:
 * the codec's VCPHEVCRegisterEncoder is an empty function. It is registered here, as the codec
 * registers its decoder (VTRegisterVideoDecoderWithInfo, not hardware accelerated).
 */
static void
register_hevc_encoder(void)
{
	void *codec = dlopen("/System/Library/VideoCodecs/VCPHEVC.videocodec", RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
	void *vt = dlopen("/System/Library/Frameworks/VideoToolbox.framework/VideoToolbox", RTLD_NOW | RTLD_GLOBAL);
	void *create = codec != NULL ? dlsym(codec, "HEVCVideoEncoder_CreateInstance") : NULL;
	int (*register_encoder)(uint32_t, CFDictionaryRef, void *) = vt != NULL ? dlsym(vt, "VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo") : NULL;
	CFStringRef *id_key = vt != NULL ? dlsym(vt, "kVTVideoEncoderList_EncoderID") : NULL;
	CFStringRef *name_key = vt != NULL ? dlsym(vt, "kVTVideoEncoderList_EncoderName") : NULL;
	CFStringRef *hardware_key = vt != NULL ? dlsym(vt, "kVTVideoEncoderList_IsHardwareAccelerated") : NULL;
	int status;

	if (create == NULL || register_encoder == NULL || id_key == NULL || name_key == NULL || hardware_key == NULL) {
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: no software HEVC encoder to register (%s)\n", codec == NULL ? "no VCPHEVC.videocodec" :
		    create == NULL ? "no HEVCVideoEncoder_CreateInstance" : "VideoToolbox without VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo");
		return;
	}
	const void *keys[] = { *id_key, *name_key, *hardware_key };
	const void *values[] = { CFSTR("com.apple.videotoolbox.videoencoder.hevc.vcp"), CFSTR("HEVC (VCPHEVC, software)"),
		kCFBooleanFalse };
	CFDictionaryRef info = CFDictionaryCreate(NULL, keys, values, 3, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks,
	    &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);

	status = register_encoder('hvc1', info, create);
	CFRelease(info);
	say("hakios: mediaserverd: the software HEVC encoder of VCPHEVC.videocodec registered for 'hvc1' (%d)\n", status);
}

struct method_spec {
	const char *selector, *types;
	IMP imp;
};

static Class
make_class(const char *name, const struct method_spec *methods, size_t count)
{
	Class cls = objc_allocateClassPair(objc_getClass("NSObject"), name, 0);

	for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		class_addMethod(cls, sel_registerName(methods[i].selector), methods[i].imp, methods[i].types);
	}
	objc_registerClassPair(cls);
	return cls;
}

static void
flashlight_classes(void)
{
	static const struct method_spec vendor[] = {
		{ "registerClientWithPID:clientDescription:clientPriority:canStealFromClientsWithSamePriority:"
		  "deviceSharingWithOtherClientsAllowed:deviceAvailabilityChangedHandler:", "i@:i@iBB@", (IMP)flashlight_register },
		{ "copyDeviceForClient:informClientWhenDeviceAvailableAgain:error:", "@@:iB^i", (IMP)flashlight_copy_device },
		{ "copyStreamForFlashlightWithPosition:deviceType:forDevice:", "@@:ii@", (IMP)flashlight_copy_stream },
		{ "takeBackDevice:forClient:informClientWhenDeviceAvailableAgain:", "v@:@iB", (IMP)flashlight_take_back },
		{ "activeDeviceEquals:", "B@:@", (IMP)flashlight_active_equals },
	}, stream[] = {
		{ "supportedProperties", "@@:", (IMP)flashlight_stream_properties },
		{ "setProperty:value:", "i@:@@", (IMP)flashlight_stream_set },
	};

	vendor_class = make_class("HakiosFlashlightVendor", vendor, sizeof(vendor) / sizeof(vendor[0]));
	device_class = make_class("HakiosFlashlightDevice", NULL, 0);
	stream_class = make_class("HakiosFlashlightStream", stream, sizeof(stream) / sizeof(stream[0]));
}

/*
 * The class methods replaced, each as soon as its class exists. `expected` is the unslid address
 * of the code in Darwin userland 16.5 (20F66): a method that is not what it was is left alone. `original`, where
 * there is one, keeps what was there (the vendor's: given as it is wherever there is one, and where
 * there is none, ours only with the kernel's camera or flashlight).
 */
static struct replacement {
	const char *class_name, *selector;
	uintptr_t expected;
	IMP replacement, *original;
	bool instance;                  /* an instance method, not a class method */
	bool done;
} replacements[] = {
	{ "BWCoreImageFilterRenderer", "prewarmPortraitFilterVersion:semanticStyleFilters:", 0x1a2115c0cUL,
	  (IMP)prewarm_portrait_filter, NULL, false, false },
	{ "BWFigCaptureDeviceVendor", "sharedCaptureDeviceVendor", 0x1a1ef0d04UL,
	  (IMP)shared_vendor, &original_shared_vendor, false, false },
	{ "BWAudioSourceNode", "start:", 0x1a1eefa18UL, (IMP)audio_source_start, &original_audio_source_start, true, false },
	{ "FigVideoCaptureConnectionConfiguration", "videoStabilizationMethod", 0x1a1e99ef8UL,
	  (IMP)video_stabilization_method, NULL, true, false },
	{ "FigVideoCaptureConnectionConfiguration", "videoStabilizationType", 0x1a20d8f48UL,
	  (IMP)video_stabilization_type, NULL, true, false },
	{ "FigCaptureStillImageSettings", "qualityPrioritization", 0x1a1f533dcUL,
	  (IMP)quality_prioritization, &original_quality_prioritization, true, false },
	{ "BWGNRNode", "renderSampleBuffer:forInput:", 0x1a1ec83b8UL, (IMP)gnr_render, NULL, true, false },
	{ "BWNodeOutput", "emitSampleBuffer:", 0x1a1ea37e0UL, (IMP)emit_sample_buffer, &original_emit_sample_buffer, true, false },
};

static void
image_added(__unused const struct mach_header *header, __unused intptr_t image_slide)
{
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(replacements) / sizeof(replacements[0]); i++) {
		struct replacement *r = &replacements[i];
		Class cls;
		Method method;
		IMP original;

		if (r->done || (cls = objc_getClass(r->class_name)) == NULL) {
			continue;
		}
		r->done = true;
		method = r->instance ? class_getInstanceMethod(cls, sel_registerName(r->selector)) :
		    class_getClassMethod(cls, sel_registerName(r->selector));
		original = method ? method_getImplementation(method) : NULL;
		if (original == NULL || (uintptr_t)original != r->expected + slide) {
			say("hakios: %c[%s %s]: found %#lx, expected %#lx; left alone\n", r->instance ? '-' : '+', r->class_name,
			    r->selector,
			    original ? (uintptr_t)original - slide : 0, r->expected);
			continue;
		}
		if (r->original != NULL) {
			*r->original = original;
		}
		method_setImplementation(method, r->replacement);
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: %c[%s %s] replaced\n", r->instance ? '-' : '+', r->class_name, r->selector);
	}
}

__attribute__((constructor))
static void
hakios_media_init(void)
{
	const char *name = getprogname();
	size_t length = 0;

	if (name == NULL || strcmp(name, "mediaserverd") != 0) {
		return;
	}
	slide = (uintptr_t)_dyld_get_shared_cache_range(&length) - CACHE_BASE;
	torch = open("/dev/hakios-torch", O_WRONLY);
	camera = access("/dev/hakios-camera", F_OK) == 0;
	if (torch >= 0) {
		flashlight_classes();
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: the kernel has a flashlight (/dev/hakios-torch)\n");
	}
	if (camera) {
		say("hakios: mediaserverd: the kernel has a camera (/dev/hakios-camera)\n");
		register_hevc_encoder();
	}
	_dyld_register_func_for_add_image(image_added);         /* also called for every image already there */
}
```

`userland/src/inject_sb.c`:

```c
/*
 * libhakios.sb.dylib: code of ours inside SpringBoard (see inject.c for how it gets there).
 *
 *   - The phone is "activated". SpringBoard asks mobileactivationd, which is not running (and
 *     could not talk to Apple anyway); without an answer it treats the device as bricked and
 *     shows the first-boot setup ("hello") instead of the lock screen.
 *   - The setup assistant is never needed, whatever the reason: nobody is going to go through
 *     it here.
 *   - SpringBoard starts a few seconds late where the kernel's boot-args say so (sb_delay=N;
 *     "xl run" does for the phone). /private/var is empty at every boot, so the applications
 *     are registered anew each time, one after another; one that is registered after
 *     SpringBoard has laid out the home screen ends up on a later page, and which one that is
 *     differs from boot to boot. On the phone that happens; under QEMU, where everything takes
 *     five times as long, it does not -- and there the delay is harmful: for a reason not yet
 *     found the window server then never takes our touch screen service for its own.
 *     (A wrapper program in the launchd job would be the obvious way to wait; launchd panics
 *     the system when a system job runs anything that is not Apple's.)
 *   - The picture SpringBoard keeps of an application that leaves the screen (for the application
 *     switcher and the next launch) is saved as JPEG or PNG, not as an ASTC texture: see
 *     snapshot_output_format().
 *   - Where CoreAnimation draws with its software renderer (QEMU; the phone without gpu=1) the
 *     "vibrant" views draw their content as it is: see plain_vibrancy().
 *   - A press of the side button that is long over is not taken for a long press (Siri) because
 *     SpringBoard was busy waking the display: see lock_long_press().
 *   - A long press on the lock screen's wallpaper does not open the poster switcher, which the
 *     window server here shows as a black screen: see poster_switcher_allowed().
 *   - Darwin notifications as a remote control, for scripts (rwtouch notify NAME):
 *       com.hakios.unlock      what the lock screen does after "swipe up to open"
 *       com.hakios.layers      write down the layers SpringBoard has on the screen: see layers()
 *       com.hakios.switcher    open the switcher of running applications: see switcher()
 *     In any other program given this library (INJECT in build.sh) only the last of them is
 *     answered, with that program's layers.
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreGraphics/CoreGraphics.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurfaceRef.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <Block.h>
#include <dispatch/dispatch.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <notify.h>
#include <objc/message.h>
#include <objc/runtime.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/* where what is said goes: the standard error, which is the console's for SpringBoard (an application's is nowhere) */
static int say_fd = 2;

static void
say(const char *format, ...)
{
	char line[1280];
	va_list ap;
	int n;

	va_start(ap, format);
	n = vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), format, ap);
	va_end(ap);
	if (n > (int)sizeof(line) - 1) {
		n = sizeof(line) - 1;
	}
	write(say_fd, line, (size_t)n);
}

/*
 * Boot-arg touch_lat=1: a line for every turn of SpringBoard's main run loop -- when it woke up (a
 * touch, a timer, the display link ...), when CoreAnimation's commit of what that turn changed
 * began and when it was done (our observers just before and after its own, of order 2000000), in
 * microseconds of mach_absolute_time, as the other "tl:" lines (tools/latency.py, tools/frames.py):
 *   tl: a WOKE COMMIT DONE
 * (a commit with nothing in it takes some microseconds; one that sends changes, a good deal more)
 */
#define CA_COMMIT_ORDER 2000000
static uint64_t main_woke, commit_began;
static volatile uint64_t turn_began;    /* mach_absolute_time at the start of the turn; 0 between turns (stall_watch()) */
static uintptr_t main_stack_top, main_stack_bottom;
static mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;

static uint64_t
now_us(void)
{
	return mach_absolute_time() * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1000;
}

static void
main_loop_turn(__unused CFRunLoopObserverRef observer, CFRunLoopActivity activity, void *info)
{
	if (activity == kCFRunLoopAfterWaiting) {
		main_woke = now_us();
		turn_began = mach_absolute_time();
	} else if (activity == kCFRunLoopBeforeWaiting && info == NULL) {
		commit_began = now_us();
	} else if (activity == kCFRunLoopBeforeWaiting && main_woke != 0) {
		say("tl: a %llu %llu %llu\n", main_woke, commit_began, now_us());
		main_woke = 0;
		turn_began = 0;
	}
}

/*
 * What SpringBoard's main thread is doing when a turn of its run loop takes long (with touch_lat=1): turns of 100 to 300 ms come
 * 40 to 100 ms after a finger comes down, before their commit, and that is what jerks at the start of a swipe. A thread looks every
 * 10 ms; at 25 ms into a turn, and every 50 ms after, it stops the main thread for the moment of walking its frame pointers.
 * "tl: t MS frame frame ...": an image's name and offset, its symbol if it exports one. mach_msg at the top is a wait for a service.
 */
static void
stall_say(thread_t thread, uint64_t ms)
{
	arm_thread_state64_t state;
	mach_msg_type_number_t count = ARM_THREAD_STATE64_COUNT;
	uintptr_t pcs[12];
	unsigned depth = 0;
	char line[1024];
	int at;

	if (thread_suspend(thread) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		return;
	}
	if (thread_get_state(thread, ARM_THREAD_STATE64, (thread_state_t)&state, &count) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		uintptr_t pc = (uintptr_t)arm_thread_state64_get_pc(state), fp = (uintptr_t)arm_thread_state64_get_fp(state);
		pcs[depth++] = pc;
		while (depth < sizeof(pcs) / sizeof(pcs[0]) && fp >= main_stack_bottom && fp + 16 <= main_stack_top && (fp & 15) == 0) {
			uintptr_t next = ((uintptr_t *)fp)[0], lr = ((uintptr_t *)fp)[1];

			if (lr == 0) {
				break;
			}
			pcs[depth++] = lr;
			if (next <= fp) {
				break;
			}
			fp = next;
		}
	}
	thread_resume(thread);
	at = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "tl: t %llu", ms);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < depth && at < (int)sizeof(line) - 96; i++) {
		Dl_info info;

		if (dladdr((void *)pcs[i], &info) != 0 && info.dli_fname != NULL) {
			const char *image = strrchr(info.dli_fname, '/');

			at += info.dli_sname != NULL && pcs[i] - (uintptr_t)info.dli_saddr < 0x4000 ?
			    snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - at, " %s", info.dli_sname) :
			    snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - at, " %s+%#lx", image != NULL ? image + 1 : info.dli_fname, pcs[i] - (uintptr_t)info.dli_fbase);
		} else {
			at += snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - at, " %#lx", pcs[i]);
		}
	}
	say("%s\n", line);
}

static void *
stall_watch(void *argument)
{
	thread_t main_thread = (thread_t)(uintptr_t)argument;
	uint64_t said_turn = 0, next_ms = 25;

	for (;;) {
		uint64_t began = turn_began;

		usleep(10000);
		if (began == 0 || began != turn_began) {
			continue;
		}
		uint64_t ms = (mach_absolute_time() - began) * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1000000;

		if (began != said_turn) {
			said_turn = began;
			next_ms = 25;
		}
		if (ms >= next_ms && ms < 2000) {
			stall_say(main_thread, ms);
			next_ms = ms + 50;
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

static void
watch_main_loop(void)
{
	char args[1024] = "";
	size_t size = sizeof(args) - 1;
	const char *arg;

	if (sysctlbyname("kern.bootargs", args, &size, NULL, 0) != 0 || (arg = strstr(args, "touch_lat=1")) == NULL ||
	    (arg != args && arg[-1] != ' ')) {
		return;
	}
	mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
	{
		pthread_t watcher;

		main_stack_top = (uintptr_t)pthread_get_stackaddr_np(pthread_self());
		main_stack_bottom = main_stack_top - pthread_get_stacksize_np(pthread_self());
		if (pthread_create(&watcher, NULL, stall_watch, (void *)(uintptr_t)mach_thread_self()) == 0) {
			pthread_detach(watcher);
		}
	}
	CFRunLoopAddObserver(CFRunLoopGetMain(), CFRunLoopObserverCreate(NULL, kCFRunLoopAfterWaiting, true, LONG_MIN,
	    main_loop_turn, NULL), kCFRunLoopCommonModes);
	CFRunLoopAddObserver(CFRunLoopGetMain(), CFRunLoopObserverCreate(NULL, kCFRunLoopBeforeWaiting, true, CA_COMMIT_ORDER - 1,
	    main_loop_turn, NULL), kCFRunLoopCommonModes);
	{
		CFRunLoopObserverContext after = { .info = (void *)1 };

		CFRunLoopAddObserver(CFRunLoopGetMain(), CFRunLoopObserverCreate(NULL, kCFRunLoopBeforeWaiting, true,
		    CA_COMMIT_ORDER + 1, main_loop_turn, &after), kCFRunLoopCommonModes);
	}
}

/* ---- methods of SpringBoard's classes, replaced --------------------------------------------------- */

extern const void *_dyld_get_shared_cache_range(size_t *length);

#define CACHE_BASE 0x180000000UL                /* where the cache was built to be, before the slide */

static uintptr_t slide;

/*
 * Replace -[CLASS SELECTOR] (or +[CLASS SELECTOR]: `kind` is that first character), whose code must now
 * be at the unslid address `expected` (Darwin userland 16.5, 20F66: what a replacement does depends on what the
 * original did). Returns the original.
 * (dyld interposing of the C functions underneath does not reach calls made from inside the
 * shared cache: there one library branches straight into the other.)
 */
static IMP
replace_method_of_kind(char kind, const char *class_name, const char *selector, uintptr_t expected, IMP replacement)
{
	Class cls = objc_getClass(class_name);
	Method method = cls == NULL ? NULL : kind == '+' ? class_getClassMethod(cls, sel_registerName(selector)) :
	    class_getInstanceMethod(cls, sel_registerName(selector));
	IMP original = method ? method_getImplementation(method) : NULL;

	if (original == NULL || (uintptr_t)original != expected + slide) {
		say("hakios: %c[%s %s]: found %#lx, expected %#lx; left alone\n", kind, class_name, selector,
		    original ? (uintptr_t)original - slide : 0, expected);
		return NULL;
	}
	method_setImplementation(method, replacement);
	return original;
}

static IMP
replace_method(const char *class_name, const char *selector, uintptr_t expected, IMP replacement)
{
	return replace_method_of_kind('-', class_name, selector, expected, replacement);
}

/*
 * -[SBLockdownManager _setupActivationState] asks MobileActivation and keeps the answer in the
 * int at +8: 2 = activated, 1 = not, 3 = unknown; it stays 0 when there is no answer.
 */
#define LOCKDOWN_STATE(manager)         (*(int *)((char *)(manager) + 8))
#define LOCKDOWN_ACTIVATED              2

static void
setup_activation_state(id self, __unused SEL selector)
{
	LOCKDOWN_STATE(self) = LOCKDOWN_ACTIVATED;
}

/* -[SBSetupManager _setSetupRequiredReason:]: 0 = no need for the setup assistant */
static void (*original_set_setup_required_reason)(id self, SEL selector, long reason);

static void
set_setup_required_reason(id self, SEL selector, long reason)
{
	if (reason != 0) {
		say("hakios: SpringBoard wants the setup assistant (reason %ld); not here\n", reason);
	}
	original_set_setup_required_reason(self, selector, 0);
}

/*
 * +[XBApplicationSnapshotManifestImpl _outputFormatForSnapshot:] chooses the file format of the picture
 * SpringBoard takes of an application that leaves the screen: 0 = PNG, 1 and 2 = ATX (an ASTC texture),
 * 3 = JPEG. A device with a wide colour display that can decode ASTC gets ATX, and Darwin compresses it on
 * the processor: fast with the vector code of Apple's cores, but here it takes one core more than ten
 * seconds per picture (under QEMU; seconds on the phone) -- and all that time the application waits for
 * the answer, until the watchdog for scene updates (10 s, there is no setting to scale it) kills it:
 * no application survived going to the background. JPEG takes a fraction of a second; it has no
 * transparency, so a picture that needs it becomes a PNG (which is what Darwin itself does on a device
 * without ASTC).
 */
#define SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_PNG             0
#define SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_JPEG            3

static long
snapshot_output_format(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, id snapshot)
{
	SEL opaque = sel_registerName("isImageOpaque");

	if (snapshot != NULL && class_getInstanceMethod(object_getClass(snapshot), opaque) != NULL &&
	    ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(snapshot, opaque)) {
		return SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_JPEG;
	}
	return SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_PNG;
}

/* ---- battery state from redwood's Qualcomm charger stack ----------------------------------------- */

/*
 * Darwin reads battery level through UIDevice.batteryLevel and UIDevice.batteryState; SpringBoard's
 * status bar reads it the same way via SBBatteryController. Where the battery has no power source
 * of its own in the kernel (battery=1, the loader's way through Qualcomm's UEFI charger protocols),
 * we hook the UIDevice accessors to return what XNU publishes as kern.hakios.battery_soc (0..100)
 * and kern.hakios.battery_charging.
 * When the sysctl is missing (battery=1 not in boot-args, or the driver never started) we hand
 * back the value the real implementation computed; the status bar then shows whatever Darwin last
 * knew, which is better than crashing.
 * With adsp=1 the battery is a power source (the service HakiosBattery, an IOPMPowerSource:
 * drivers/power/hakios.battery.cpp), which powerd reads like an iPhone's own, and from it Darwin knows
 * everything by itself; once that service is there, the hooks hand everything to Darwin's own code.
 */
static float  (*original_battery_level)(id self, SEL sel);
static long   (*original_battery_state)(id self, SEL sel);
static BOOL   (*original_battery_view_shows_percentage)(id self, SEL sel);
static void   (*original_battery_view_set_shows_percentage)(id self, SEL sel, BOOL shows);
static BOOL   (*original_battery_view_should_show_bolt)(id self, SEL sel);
static double (*original_battery_view_charge_percent)(id self, SEL sel);
static void   (*original_battery_view_set_charge_percent)(id self, SEL sel, double p);
static double (*original_ring_charging_level)(id self, SEL sel);

static int
sysctl_int(const char *name)
{
	int value = -1;
	size_t size = sizeof(value);

	sysctlbyname(name, &value, &size, NULL, 0);
	return value;
}

/* Is the battery a power source that Darwin reads by itself (see above)? Once it is, it stays one. */
static bool
battery_power_source(void)
{
	static bool found;
	io_service_t service;

	if (!found && (service = IOServiceGetMatchingService(0, IOServiceMatching("HakiosBattery"))) != 0) {
		IOObjectRelease(service);
		found = true;
	}
	return found;
}

/* ---- the cellular items of the status bar, from the kernel's modem ------------------------------ */

/*
 * SpringBoard's SBStatusBarStateAggregator fills the raw status bar data from CoreTelephony, which
 * has no baseband here. Its item updaters take the data and a getter and setter for the field
 * (Darwin userland 16.5: -[SBStatusBarStateAggregator _updateSignalStrengthItem:withData:SIMInfo:barsGetter:
 * barsSetter:], and the like for the service string): the signal one is replaced so that, when the
 * kernel's modem is registered (sysctl kern.hakios.cellular_registered, _bars: hakios.mpss.c),
 * the bars are set and the item switched on (-[... _setItem:enabled:]). The aggregator's whole
 * method list is said once in the log, for the posting to be found; and the signal item is asked
 * to update itself every few seconds while the kernel's state changes.
 */
static void (*original_update_signal_item)(id self, SEL sel, long item, void *data, id sim, void *getter, void *setter);
static id cellular_aggregator;
static int cellular_last_bars = -2, cellular_said;

/* The getters and setters are blocks (their type is "@?"): called through the block's own invoke pointer, with the block first. */
struct block_layout {
	void *isa;
	int flags, reserved;
	void (*invoke)(void *, ...);
};
#define BLOCK_CALL(block, type, ...) ((type)((struct block_layout *)(block))->invoke)((block), __VA_ARGS__)

static void
update_signal_item(id self, SEL sel, long item, void *data, id sim, void *getter, void *setter)
{
	int up = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_up"), registered = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_registered");
	int bars = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_bars"), dbm = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_dbm");
	int shown;

	cellular_aggregator = self;
	if (original_update_signal_item) {
		original_update_signal_item(self, sel, item, data, sim, getter, setter);
	}
	if (cellular_said++ < 8) {
		say("hakios: cellular: signal item %ld: data %p, SIM info %p, getter %p, setter %p; the kernel says up %d registered %d bars %d dbm %d\n",
		    item, data, (void *)sim, getter, setter, up, registered, bars, dbm);
	}
	/*
	 * Force the signal item on. Darwin hides it unless its own cellular stack (CommCenter, which is
	 * not here) says there is service, so the bars never appear on their own. The kernel knows
	 * the modem's state, so once it is up the item is shown here with the kernel's bars; when the
	 * kernel has a reading but zero bars (a brief "no signal" sample, or a reading just after
	 * registration) at least one bar is forced so the icon is visibly present rather than empty.
	 * modem_bars_off=1 (as a sysctl) is not honoured; set kern.hakios.cellular_up=0 to hide it.
	 */
	/*
	 * The kernel's NAS state alternates between two reports -- "registered, signal not read" and
	 * "not registered, -86 dBm" -- so at the moments it says registered the dBm reads 0. The last
	 * real reading (within a minute) stands in for it.
	 */
	{
		static int last_dbm;
		static time_t last_dbm_at;
		time_t now = time(NULL);

		if (dbm < 0) {
			last_dbm = dbm;
			last_dbm_at = now;
		} else if (last_dbm < 0 && now - last_dbm_at < 60) {
			dbm = last_dbm;
		}
	}
	shown = bars;
	if (shown <= 0 && dbm < 0) {
		shown = dbm >= -95 ? 4 : dbm >= -105 ? 3 : dbm >= -115 ? 2 : 1;   /* derive from dBm when bars is 0 */
	}
	if (shown <= 0 && (up > 0 || registered > 0)) {
		shown = 1;                      /* up but no reading yet: still show the icon */
	}
	if (shown > 5) {
		shown = 5;
	}
	if ((up > 0 || registered > 0) && shown > 0 && setter != NULL && data != NULL) {
		BLOCK_CALL(setter, void (*)(void *, void *, int), data, shown);
		((void (*)(id, SEL, long, BOOL))objc_msgSend)(self, sel_registerName("_setItem:enabled:"), item, YES);
		if (shown != cellular_last_bars) {
			say("hakios: cellular: %d bars shown (item %ld; kernel bars %d, %d dBm, registered %d)\n", shown, item, bars, dbm, registered);
		}
	}
	cellular_last_bars = shown;
}

static void (*original_update_service_item)(id self, SEL sel, long item, void *data, id sim, id other, void *g1, void *s1, void *g2, void *s2,
    void *g3, void *s3, void *g4, void *s4);

/*
 * The service item ("No SIM", the network's name): once the kernel's modem is registered, the
 * network's name (sysctl kern.hakios.cellular_operator) goes in through the item's string setter
 * and the item is switched on.
 */
static void
update_service_item(id self, SEL sel, long item, void *data, id sim, id other, void *g1, void *s1, void *g2, void *s2, void *g3, void *s3,
    void *g4, void *s4)
{
	static int said;
	static char shown[64];
	char name[64] = "";
	size_t size = sizeof(name) - 1;
	int registered = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_registered");

	if (original_update_service_item) {
		original_update_service_item(self, sel, item, data, sim, other, g1, s1, g2, s2, g3, s3, g4, s4);
	}
	sysctlbyname("kern.hakios.cellular_operator", name, &size, NULL, 0);
	if (said++ < 4) {
		say("hakios: cellular: service item %ld: data %p, SIM info %p, other %p; string getter %p setter %p, content type getter %p "
		    "setter %p; the kernel's network \"%s\"\n", item, data, (void *)sim, (void *)other, g1, s1, g3, s3, name);
	}
	if (registered > 0 && name[0] != 0 && s1 != NULL && data != NULL) {
		CFStringRef string = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, name, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);

		if (string != NULL) {
			BLOCK_CALL(s1, void (*)(void *, void *, CFStringRef), data, string);
			((void (*)(id, SEL, long, BOOL))objc_msgSend)(self, sel_registerName("_setItem:enabled:"), item, YES);
			if (strcmp(shown, name) != 0) {
				snprintf(shown, sizeof(shown), "%s", name);
				say("hakios: cellular: service \"%s\" shown (item %ld)\n", name, item);
			}
			CFRelease(string);
		}
	}
}

/*
 * The bars are drawn by UIKit's signal view, whose "signal mode" says how: inactive (all bars grey),
 * searching, or active (the bars that count dark). Darwin's cellular stack (CommCenter, not here)
 * puts it in active mode once there is service; without it the bars stay grey whatever their
 * number. So for the cellular signal view (not the Wi-Fi one), while the kernel says the modem is
 * registered, the mode is made active. The modes seen are said in the log once each.
 */
static void (*original_set_signal_mode)(id self, SEL sel, long mode);
static long cellular_active_mode = 2;  /* _UIStatusBarSignalView: 0 inactive, 1 searching, 2 active */

static void
set_signal_mode(id self, SEL sel, long mode)
{
	static unsigned said_modes;
	const char *name = object_getClassName(self);
	bool cellular = name != NULL && strstr(name, "Cellular") != NULL;
	long wanted = mode;

	if (cellular && mode < 8 && !(said_modes & (1u << mode))) {
		said_modes |= 1u << mode;
		say("hakios: cellular: %s asked for signal mode %ld\n", name, mode);
	}
	if (cellular && sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_registered") > 0 && mode != cellular_active_mode) {
		wanted = cellular_active_mode;
	}
	original_set_signal_mode(self, sel, wanted);
}

static void
signal_view_hook(void)
{
	static const char *const classes[] = { "_UIStatusBarCellularSignalView", "_UIStatusBarSignalView" };

	for (unsigned c = 0; c < sizeof(classes) / sizeof(classes[0]); c++) {
		Class cls = objc_getClass(classes[c]);
		Method method = cls ? class_getInstanceMethod(cls, sel_registerName("setSignalMode:")) : NULL;

		if (method == NULL) {
			say("hakios: cellular: no -[%s setSignalMode:]\n", classes[c]);
			continue;
		}
		original_set_signal_mode = (void (*)(id, SEL, long))method_getImplementation(method);
		method_setImplementation(method, (IMP)set_signal_mode);
		say("hakios: cellular: -[%s setSignalMode:] replaced (types \"%s\"): active while the kernel says registered\n",
		    classes[c], method_getTypeEncoding(method));
		return;         /* the base class's method serves the subclasses */
	}
}

static void
cellular_hook(void)
{
	signal_view_hook();
	{
		const char *service_selector = "_updateServiceItem:withData:SIMInfo:otherSIMInfo:serviceStringGetter:serviceStringSetter:"
		    "serviceCrossfadeStringGetter:serviceCrossfadeStringSetter:serviceContentTypeGetter:serviceContentTypeSetter:"
		    "serviceBadgeStringGetter:serviceBadgeStringSetter:";
		Class cls = objc_getClass("SBStatusBarStateAggregator");
		Method method = cls ? class_getInstanceMethod(cls, sel_registerName(service_selector)) : NULL;

		if (method) {
			say("hakios: cellular: -[SBStatusBarStateAggregator %s] at %#lx, types \"%s\": looked at\n", service_selector,
			    (uintptr_t)method_getImplementation(method) - slide, method_getTypeEncoding(method));
			original_update_service_item = (void (*)(id, SEL, long, void *, id, id, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *, void *,
			    void *))method_getImplementation(method);
			method_setImplementation(method, (IMP)update_service_item);
		}
	}
	const char *selector = "_updateSignalStrengthItem:withData:SIMInfo:barsGetter:barsSetter:";
	Class cls = objc_getClass("SBStatusBarStateAggregator");
	Method method = cls ? class_getInstanceMethod(cls, sel_registerName(selector)) : NULL;

	if (method == NULL) {
		say("hakios: cellular: no -[SBStatusBarStateAggregator %s]\n", selector);
		return;
	}
	say("hakios: cellular: -[SBStatusBarStateAggregator %s] at %#lx, types \"%s\": replaced\n", selector,
	    (uintptr_t)method_getImplementation(method) - slide, method_getTypeEncoding(method));
	original_update_signal_item = (void (*)(id, SEL, long, void *, id, void *, void *))method_getImplementation(method);
	method_setImplementation(method, (IMP)update_signal_item);
	{
		/* the whole class, once: which updaters and posters there are */
		unsigned count = 0;
		Method *list = class_copyMethodList(cls, &count);
		char line[1024] = "";
		size_t at = 0;

		for (unsigned i = 0; list && i < count; i++) {
			const char *name = sel_getName(method_getName(list[i]));
			size_t n = strlen(name);

			if (at + n + 2 > sizeof(line)) {
				say("hakios: cellular: aggregator methods: %s\n", line);
				line[0] = 0;
				at = 0;
			}
			memcpy(line + at, name, n);
			at += n;
			line[at++] = ' ';
			line[at] = 0;
		}
		if (at) {
			say("hakios: cellular: aggregator methods: %s\n", line);
		}
		free(list);
	}
	/* every 3 s: when the kernel's registration or bars change, the item is asked to update itself */
	dispatch_source_t timer = dispatch_source_create(DISPATCH_SOURCE_TYPE_TIMER, 0, 0, dispatch_get_main_queue());

	dispatch_source_set_timer(timer, dispatch_time(DISPATCH_TIME_NOW, 3 * NSEC_PER_SEC), 3 * NSEC_PER_SEC, NSEC_PER_SEC / 2);
	dispatch_source_set_event_handler(timer, ^{
		static int last_registered = -2, last_bars = -2;
		int registered = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_registered"), bars = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.cellular_bars");

		if ((registered != last_registered || bars != last_bars) && cellular_aggregator != nil) {
			SEL update = sel_registerName("_updateSignalStrengthItem");

			last_registered = registered;
			last_bars = bars;
			if (class_getInstanceMethod(object_getClass(cellular_aggregator), update)) {
				((void (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(cellular_aggregator, update);
				say("hakios: cellular: the signal item asked to update (registered %d, bars %d)\n", registered, bars);
			}
		}
	});
	dispatch_resume(timer);
}

/* UIDevice.batteryLevel: 0.0..1.0; -1.0 if monitoring not enabled */
static float
battery_level(id self, SEL sel)
{
	int soc = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc");

	if (soc < 0 || soc > 100 || battery_power_source()) {
		return original_battery_level ? original_battery_level(self, sel) : -1.0f;
	}
	return (float)soc / 100.0f;
}

/* UIDevice.batteryState: 0=unknown 1=unplugged 2=charging 3=full */
static long
battery_state(id self, SEL sel)
{
	int charging = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_charging");
	int present = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_present");
	int plugged = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_charger_present");
	int soc = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc");

	if (charging == -1 || present == -1 || plugged == -1 || soc < 0 || soc > 100 || battery_power_source()) {
		return original_battery_state ? original_battery_state(self, sel) : 0;
	}
	if (!present) return 0;
	if (plugged && soc >= 100) return 3;
	return charging ? 2 : 1;
}

/*
 * UIKitCore's status-bar view has its own presentation policy, separate from UIDevice. With the power
 * source it is Darwin's own again: the switch Battery Percentage in Settings > Battery, which the image
 * turns on (SBShowBatteryPercentage in userland/var/mobile/Library/Preferences/com.apple.springboard.plist).
 */
static BOOL
battery_view_shows_percentage(id self, SEL sel)
{
	int soc = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc");

	if (soc >= 0 && soc <= 100 && !battery_power_source()) return YES;
	return original_battery_view_shows_percentage ? original_battery_view_shows_percentage(self, sel) : NO;
}

static void
battery_view_set_shows_percentage(id self, SEL sel, BOOL shows)
{
	int soc = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc");

	original_battery_view_set_shows_percentage(self, sel, (soc >= 0 && soc <= 100 && !battery_power_source()) ? YES : shows);
}

static BOOL
battery_view_should_show_bolt(id self, SEL sel)
{
	int charging = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_charging");
	int present = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_present");
	int plugged = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_charger_present");

	if (charging != -1 && present != -1 && plugged != -1 && !battery_power_source()) return charging && present && plugged;
	return original_battery_view_should_show_bolt ? original_battery_view_should_show_bolt(self, sel) : NO;
}

/*
 * The actual number the status bar draws. _UIBatteryView keeps the fill fraction (0.0..1.0) in
 * chargePercent; it is set through setChargePercent: and read back for layout. Darwin feeds it from
 * BatteryCenter / IOPowerSources, which is empty on this phone, so without us it sits near zero
 * (the "1%" the user saw). We override both sides: setChargePercent: so the stored value is ours
 * no matter who writes it, and the getter so any layout path that reads it agrees.
 */
static double
battery_view_charge_percent(id self, SEL sel)
{
	int soc = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc");

	if (soc >= 0 && soc <= 100 && !battery_power_source()) return (double)soc / 100.0;
	return original_battery_view_charge_percent ? original_battery_view_charge_percent(self, sel) : 0.0;
}

static void
battery_view_set_charge_percent(id self, SEL sel, double p)
{
	int soc = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc");

	original_battery_view_set_charge_percent(self, sel, (soc >= 0 && soc <= 100 && !battery_power_source()) ? (double)soc / 100.0 : p);
}

/* The big charging ring on the lock screen (CoverSheet) reads its fill level the same way. */
static double
ring_charging_level(id self, SEL sel)
{
	int soc = sysctl_int("kern.hakios.battery_soc");

	if (soc >= 0 && soc <= 100 && !battery_power_source()) return (double)soc / 100.0;
	return original_ring_charging_level ? original_ring_charging_level(self, sel) : 0.0;
}

/* Keep SpringBoard's normal battery observers awake while the XNU cache changes. */
static void
battery_post_notifications(void)
{
	Class uidev = objc_getClass("UIDevice");
	Class notification_center = objc_getClass("NSNotificationCenter");
	id device = uidev ? ((id (*)(Class, SEL))objc_msgSend)(uidev, sel_registerName("currentDevice")) : nil;
	id center = notification_center ? ((id (*)(Class, SEL))objc_msgSend)(notification_center,
	    sel_registerName("defaultCenter")) : nil;

	if (center != nil && !battery_power_source()) {
		SEL post = sel_registerName("postNotificationName:object:");
		((void (*)(id, SEL, id, id))objc_msgSend)(center, post,
		    (id)CFSTR("UIDeviceBatteryLevelDidChangeNotification"), device);
		((void (*)(id, SEL, id, id))objc_msgSend)(center, post,
		    (id)CFSTR("UIDeviceBatteryStateDidChangeNotification"), device);
	}
	dispatch_after(dispatch_time(DISPATCH_TIME_NOW, 5 * NSEC_PER_SEC), dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{
		battery_post_notifications();
	});
}

/* ---- the lock screen's clock without a GPU ------------------------------------------------------- */

#define HAKIOS_GL "/redwood/lib/libhakios.gl.dylib"

/* Does the window server draw with OpenGL ES? The same question, asked the same way, as opengl_es() in inject.c. */
static bool
gpu_draws(void)
{
	char arguments[1024] = "";
	size_t size = sizeof(arguments) - 1;
	const char *argument;
	io_service_t gpu;

	/* ... or through Metal (boot-arg metal=1 with the GPU kept: HakiosMetal.bundle, an image built with METAL_PLUGIN) */
	if (access("/redwood/lib/HakiosMetal.bundle/HakiosMetal", R_OK) == 0 &&
	    sysctlbyname("kern.bootargs", arguments, &size, NULL, 0) == 0) {
		for (argument = arguments; (argument = strstr(argument, "metal=")) != NULL; argument += 6) {
			if ((argument == arguments || argument[-1] == ' ') && argument[6] != '0') {
				gpu = IOServiceGetMatchingService(0, IOServiceMatching("HakiosGPU"));
				if (gpu != 0) {
					IOObjectRelease(gpu);
					return true;
				}
			}
		}
	}
	size = sizeof(arguments) - 1;
	if (access(HAKIOS_GL, R_OK) != 0) {
		return false;
	}
	if (sysctlbyname("kern.bootargs", arguments, &size, NULL, 0) == 0) {
		for (argument = arguments; (argument = strstr(argument, "gl=")) != NULL; argument += 3) {
			if (argument == arguments || argument[-1] == ' ') {
				return argument[3] != '0';
			}
		}
	}
	gpu = IOServiceGetMatchingService(0, IOServiceMatching("HakiosGPU"));
	if (gpu != 0) {
		IOObjectRelease(gpu);
	}
	return gpu != 0;
}

/*
 * The clock of the lock screen is a "vibrant" view (BSUIVibrancyEffectView in BaseBoardUI): its
 * digits are not drawn, they are a mask -- a copy of them through a colour matrix that keeps red
 * as alpha -- through which the filter vibrantColorMatrix lets the wallpaper behind come out
 * lighter; and a gradient over the whole screen, red at the top, tones the wallpaper down the
 * same way. On the GPU that is what is seen (eagl.c draws the two filters). CoreAnimation's
 * software renderer shows neither: the digits come out red, and the top of the wallpaper as it
 * was. Why was not found out; that renderer is in QuartzCore, not here.
 * Such views have a switch, the user default BSUIVibrancyEffectViewDisabled: with it they show
 * their content as it is drawn, the clock in plain white. It is set for this run of SpringBoard
 * alone (nothing is written), and only where the software renderer draws.
 */
static void
plain_vibrancy(void)
{
	if (gpu_draws()) {
		return;
	}
	CFPreferencesSetAppValue(CFSTR("BSUIVibrancyEffectViewDisabled"), kCFBooleanTrue, kCFPreferencesCurrentApplication);
	say("hakios: SpringBoard: no GPU draws, vibrant views are plain (the lock screen's clock is white)\n");
}

/*
 * Boot-arg ui_lite=1: the system's own "Reduce Transparency" and "Reduce Motion" (Settings, Accessibility), for this
 * boot and, through var_store, the next. CoreAnimation then draws the dock, folders and widgets' platters in plain
 * colours instead of blurring what is behind them every frame, and opens and closes applications with a fade instead
 * of a zoom of the whole home screen -- the two things the Adreno spends a frame's GPU time on through Metal (2
 * November: 6 to 10 ms a frame in motion, ~30 ms for an application's close). ui_lite=0 turns both off again (what
 * var_store kept from a ui_lite=1 boot); without the boot-arg the settings are left alone.
 */
static void
ui_lite(void)
{
	char arguments[1024] = "";
	size_t size = sizeof(arguments) - 1;
	const char *argument;
	CFBooleanRef on;

	if (sysctlbyname("kern.bootargs", arguments, &size, NULL, 0) != 0 ||
	    (argument = strstr(arguments, "ui_lite=")) == NULL || (argument != arguments && argument[-1] != ' ')) {
		return;
	}
	on = argument[8] == '0' ? kCFBooleanFalse : kCFBooleanTrue;
	CFPreferencesSetValue(CFSTR("EnhancedBackgroundContrastEnabled"), on, CFSTR("com.apple.Accessibility"),
	    kCFPreferencesCurrentUser, kCFPreferencesAnyHost);
	CFPreferencesSetValue(CFSTR("ReduceMotionEnabled"), on, CFSTR("com.apple.Accessibility"),
	    kCFPreferencesCurrentUser, kCFPreferencesAnyHost);
	CFPreferencesSynchronize(CFSTR("com.apple.Accessibility"), kCFPreferencesCurrentUser, kCFPreferencesAnyHost);
	notify_post("com.apple.accessibility.cache.enhance.background.contrast");
	notify_post("com.apple.accessibility.cache.reduce.motion");
	say("hakios: SpringBoard: ui_lite=%c: Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion %s\n", argument[8], on == kCFBooleanTrue ? "on" : "off");
}

/* ---- the side button's long press ---------------------------------------------------------------- */

/*
 * -[SBLockHardwareButton longPress:] is what the side button's long press recognizer calls: Siri
 * (here, its "turn on Siri" sheet, nobody having turned it on). The recognizer is a timer of
 * SpringBoard's own: started when the main thread sees the press, stopped when it sees the release
 * -- and a release it has not got round to is no release. A press of the side button with the
 * display off wakes the display from inside the handling of that very press, which on an iPhone
 * takes no time. Here it takes as long as the software renderer needs for the first picture of the
 * lock screen: a tenth of a second on the phone, a second under QEMU. That is longer than a long
 * press, so there every wake by the button (and by a tap, which is a press of that button made in
 * inject.c) ended with Siri's sheet over the lock screen, however short the press had been.
 * Where the button's events come from -- inject.c, in backboardd -- it is known whether the button
 * is still held; a long press of a button that is not is dropped here.
 */
#define GESTURE_BEGAN                   1       /* UIGestureRecognizerState */
#define GESTURE_ENDED                   3       /* and cancelled, failed after it */

static void (*original_lock_long_press)(id self, SEL selector, id recognizer);

static bool
lock_button_held(void)
{
	static int token = NOTIFY_TOKEN_INVALID;
	uint64_t state = 0;

	if (token == NOTIFY_TOKEN_INVALID && notify_register_check("com.hakios.button.lock", &token) != NOTIFY_STATUS_OK) {
		token = NOTIFY_TOKEN_INVALID;
		return true;
	}
	/* 1 = released; held, or not known: as SpringBoard has it */
	return notify_get_state(token, &state) != NOTIFY_STATUS_OK || state != 1;
}

static void
lock_long_press(id self, SEL selector, id recognizer)
{
	static bool dropping;
	SEL state_selector = sel_registerName("state");
	long state = recognizer != NULL && class_getInstanceMethod(object_getClass(recognizer), state_selector) != NULL ?
	    ((long (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(recognizer, state_selector) : 0;

	if (state == GESTURE_BEGAN) {
		dropping = !lock_button_held();
		if (dropping) {
			say("hakios: SpringBoard: a long press of the side button, which was released long ago: dropped\n");
		}
	}
	if (dropping) {
		if (state >= GESTURE_ENDED) {
			dropping = false;
		}
		return;
	}
	original_lock_long_press(self, selector, recognizer);
}

/* ---- remote control ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

#define UNLOCK_SOURCE_COVER_SHEET       24      /* what the lock screen itself passes */

static void
unlock(void)
{
	Class cls = objc_getClass("SBLockScreenManager");
	SEL shared = sel_registerName("sharedInstance"), locked = sel_registerName("isUILocked");
	SEL unlock_ui = sel_registerName("unlockUIFromSource:withOptions:");
	id manager;

	if (cls == NULL || class_getClassMethod(cls, shared) == NULL || class_getInstanceMethod(cls, locked) == NULL ||
	    class_getInstanceMethod(cls, unlock_ui) == NULL) {
		say("hakios: unlock: SBLockScreenManager is not what it was\n");
		return;
	}
	manager = ((id (*)(Class, SEL))objc_msgSend)(cls, shared);
	if (manager == NULL) {
		say("hakios: unlock: no lock screen manager yet\n");
	} else if (!((BOOL (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(manager, locked)) {
		say("hakios: unlock: not locked\n");
	} else {
		BOOL done = ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL, long, id))objc_msgSend)(manager, unlock_ui, UNLOCK_SOURCE_COVER_SHEET, NULL);

		say("hakios: unlock: asked, answer %d\n", done);
	}
}

/*
 * The poster switcher: on Darwin userland 16 a long press on the lock screen's wallpaper shrinks it into a
 * row of posters to choose from or customize. The row is PosterBoard's, an application scene of
 * that process which the lock screen hosts (CSPosterSwitcherViewController, a CALayerHost of the
 * context of PosterBoard's window over an opaque black layer). PosterBoard does lay it out -- its
 * window has the posters, "Customize" and "+", the hosted context is that window's, the scene is
 * in the foreground -- but the window server draws nothing of that context, with either
 * renderer, so what is left is the black layer under it, until a swipe up takes the switcher
 * away. Why is not known: the display is not in secure mode, SpringBoard counts the user as
 * authenticated, the same nesting of hosted contexts works for the wallpaper itself.
 * Until it is, the switcher is not offered, the way SpringBoard itself withholds it where it has
 * none (an iPad, Guided Access): its policy says the capability is not there, and the long press
 * does nothing.
 */
static BOOL
poster_switcher_allowed(__unused id self, __unused SEL selector, id *explanation)
{
	if (explanation != NULL) {
		*explanation = (id)CFSTR("the poster switcher is not shown here (see inject_sb.c)");
	}
	return NO;
}

/*
 * What SpringBoard has put on the screen, as CoreAnimation has it: every layer of every window, a
 * line each -- class and name, place, opacity, what it shows (an image, a colour, another
 * process's layers), and what is done to it: its filters by type with their inputs, in order,
 * the compositing filter, the mask. That is where a picture that comes out wrong on one renderer
 * and right on another is described: the same description goes to both.
 */
#define SEND(type, object, name)        ((type (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)((id)(object), sel_registerName(name))
#define SEND1(type, object, name, argument_type, argument) \
	((type (*)(id, SEL, argument_type))objc_msgSend)((id)(object), sel_registerName(name), argument)

static const char *layers_of = "";               /* in another program than SpringBoard: " of" and its name */

static const char *
text_of(id object)
{
	id text = object ? SEND(id, object, "description") : NULL;

	return text ? SEND(const char *, text, "UTF8String") : "-";
}

/*
 * Boot-arg wallpaper_cache=1: the window that shows the wallpaper rasterized by the window server (CALayer's
 * shouldRasterize), drawn from one texture instead of composed again every frame. iOS 16's Collections poster is
 * eight to twelve full-screen layers blended together (textures of 1271 x 1823, 1326 x 1326, 1326 x 1160, ...), 1.5 to
 * 2.4 ms each on the Adreno through Metal: 15 to 20 ms of every frame in which something moves over it (2 November,
 * metal_fps=mainpass), for a picture that does not change -- nothing here moves it (no parallax without a gyroscope).
 * Looked for every 15 s from 20 s on, for windows whose class names a wallpaper or a poster.
 */
static void
wallpaper_cache_pass(void)
{
	static unsigned listed;
	id app = SEND(id, objc_getClass("UIApplication"), "sharedApplication");
	id windows = app != NULL ? SEND(id, app, "windows") : NULL;
	unsigned long count = windows != NULL ? SEND(unsigned long, windows, "count") : 0;
	id screen = SEND(id, objc_getClass("UIScreen"), "mainScreen");
	double scale = screen != NULL ? ((double (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(screen, sel_registerName("scale")) : 3.0;

	for (unsigned long i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		id window = ((id (*)(id, SEL, unsigned long))objc_msgSend)(windows, sel_registerName("objectAtIndex:"), i);
		const char *name = object_getClassName(window);
		id layer = SEND(id, window, "layer");

		if (listed < 12) {
			id sub = SEND(id, layer, "sublayers");
			say("hakios: SpringBoard: window %lu of %lu: %s, layer %s with %lu sublayers%s\n", i, count, name,
			    layer != NULL ? object_getClassName(layer) : "-", sub != NULL ? SEND(unsigned long, sub, "count") : 0UL,
			    layer != NULL && SEND(BOOL, layer, "shouldRasterize") ? ", rasterized" : "");
		}
		if ((strcasestr(name, "wallpaper") != NULL || strcasestr(name, "poster") != NULL) && layer != NULL &&
		    !SEND(BOOL, layer, "shouldRasterize")) {
			((void (*)(id, SEL, BOOL))objc_msgSend)(layer, sel_registerName("setShouldRasterize:"), YES);
			((void (*)(id, SEL, double))objc_msgSend)(layer, sel_registerName("setRasterizationScale:"), scale);
			say("hakios: SpringBoard: %s rasterized at %g (wallpaper_cache=1)\n", name, scale);
		}
	}
	listed++;
```
