`userland/src/rwtouch.c`:

```c
/*
 * rwtouch: replay touches through /dev/hakios-touch (see hakios.input.h).
 *
 * usage: rwtouch STEP...
 *   wait SECONDS                 pause
 *   tap X Y                      a short touch
 *   swipe X0 Y0 X1 Y1 [MS]       drag from one point to the other in MS milliseconds (default 300)
 *   drag X0 Y0 X1 Y1 MS HOLD [GRAB]
 *                                the same, then stay at the end HOLD milliseconds before letting go
 *                                (what is dragged is held where it was taken, neither flung nor sprung back);
 *                                GRAB milliseconds of staying still first, for what has to be picked up
 *                                before it will move -- an icon of the home screen wants about 700
 *   hold X Y MS                  touch and stay
 *   zigzag X Y0 Y1 MS N [STEP]   touch at Y0, go to Y1 in MS milliseconds and back again, N times, then let go;
 *                                a sample every STEP milliseconds (default 8, what the touch screen gives, as
 *                                swipe and drag give them):
 *                                for measuring how far behind the finger the screen is (tools/latency.py)
 *   button NAME [MS]             press a button: home, lock, volup, voldown
 *   read                         print the samples that arrive, forever (to watch the queue)
 *   notify NAME                  post a Darwin notification (com.hakios.unlock: see inject_sb.c)
 *   clock                        how long short sleeps really take (a check of the kernel's timers)
 * Positions are fractions of the screen: 0 0 is the top left corner, 1 1 the bottom right.
 * Example, "swipe up from the bottom edge two minutes after boot":
 *   rwtouch wait 120 swipe 0.5 0.99 0.5 0.4 250
 */
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <notify.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <sys/qos.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "hakios.input.h"

static int device;

static void
post(uint32_t type, double x, double y)
{
	struct hakios_touch t = { .type = type, .finger = 0, .x = (uint32_t)(x * 65535.0 + 0.5), .y = (uint32_t)(y * 65535.0 + 0.5) };

	if (write(device, &t, sizeof(t)) != (ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
		perror("rwtouch: write");
		exit(1);
	}
}

static void
button(uint32_t which, int ms)
{
	struct hakios_touch t = { .type = HAKIOS_BUTTON_DOWN, .finger = which };

	if (write(device, &t, sizeof(t)) != (ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
		perror("rwtouch: write");
		exit(1);
	}
	usleep((useconds_t)ms * 1000);
	t.type = HAKIOS_BUTTON_UP;
	write(device, &t, sizeof(t));
}

/*
 * A sample every so many milliseconds: 4, a sample in every refresh at 120 Hz (touch_poll_us=4000 for the touch screen
 * itself). Once 8. Measured (4 November): the frame rate of a swipe is the same with either, 100 to 104 a second.
 */
#define SAMPLE_MS       4

static mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;

/* Until `at` microseconds after `start` (mach_absolute_time()): on a clock of its own, not one sleep after another */
static void
sleep_until(uint64_t start, uint64_t at)
{
	uint64_t now_us;

	do {
		now_us = (mach_absolute_time() - start) * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1000;
		if (now_us < at) {
			usleep((useconds_t)(at - now_us));
		}
	} while (now_us < at);
}

/*
 * A sample every SAMPLE_MS on the way, each where the finger would be by then. (Once one sleep of a
 * frame after another: those came out at 21 ms apart, 48 samples a second, fewer than the display's
 * 60 frames, and an application that is moved by the samples drew no more frames than that.)
 */
static void
drag(double x0, double y0, double x1, double y1, int ms, int hold, int grab)
{
	uint64_t start, total_us = (uint64_t)(ms > 0 ? ms : 1) * 1000;

	post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN, x0, y0);
	/*
	 * grab: stay where the finger landed before moving at all. An icon of the home screen is
	 * picked up by a long press and only then dragged, and it has to be one touch throughout --
	 * a press that ends puts up the icon's menu instead.
	 */
	for (int waited = 0; waited < grab; waited += 100) {
		usleep(100000);
		post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_MOVE, x0, y0);
	}
	start = mach_absolute_time();
	for (uint64_t at = SAMPLE_MS * 1000;; at += SAMPLE_MS * 1000) {
		double part;

		if (at > total_us) {
			at = total_us;
		}
		part = (double)at / (double)total_us;
		sleep_until(start, at);
		post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_MOVE, x0 + (x1 - x0) * part, y0 + (y1 - y0) * part);
		if (at == total_us) {
			break;
		}
	}
	usleep(16000);
	if (hold > 0) {
		/* (a sample now and then, as a finger that stays still still gives) */
		for (int waited = 0; waited < hold; waited += 100) {
			usleep(100000);
			post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_MOVE, x1, y1);
		}
	}
	post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP, x1, y1);
}

static void
zigzag(double x, double y0, double y1, int ms, int times, int step_ms)
{
	uint64_t start, legs = (uint64_t)times * 2, total_us = legs * (uint64_t)ms * 1000;

	post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN, x, y0);
	start = mach_absolute_time();
	for (uint64_t at = (uint64_t)step_ms * 1000; at <= total_us; at += (uint64_t)step_ms * 1000) {
		uint64_t leg = at / ((uint64_t)ms * 1000), within = at % ((uint64_t)ms * 1000);
		double part = (double)within / (ms * 1000.0), y;

		if (leg >= legs) {
			leg = legs - 1;
			part = 1;
		}
		y = leg % 2 == 0 ? y0 + (y1 - y0) * part : y1 + (y0 - y1) * part;
		sleep_until(start, at);
		post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_MOVE, x, y);
	}
	usleep(16000);
	post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP, x, y0);
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	/* a gesture is a matter of timing: do not let the rest of a busy system stretch it */
	pthread_set_qos_class_self_np(QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE, 0);
	mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
	device = open(HAKIOS_TOUCH_DEVICE, O_RDWR);
	if (device < 0) {
		perror("rwtouch: " HAKIOS_TOUCH_DEVICE);
		return 1;
	}
	for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
		const char *step = argv[i];
		int left = argc - i - 1;

		if (strcmp(step, "wait") == 0 && left >= 1) {
			usleep((useconds_t)(atof(argv[i + 1]) * 1e6));
			i += 1;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "tap") == 0 && left >= 2) {
			double x = atof(argv[i + 1]), y = atof(argv[i + 2]);

			post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN, x, y);
			usleep(60000);
			post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP, x, y);
			i += 2;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "zigzag") == 0 && left >= 5) {
			int step_ms = left >= 6 && atoi(argv[i + 6]) > 0 ? atoi(argv[i + 6]) : 8;

			zigzag(atof(argv[i + 1]), atof(argv[i + 2]), atof(argv[i + 3]), atoi(argv[i + 4]), atoi(argv[i + 5]), step_ms);
			i += left >= 6 && atoi(argv[i + 6]) > 0 ? 6 : 5;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "hold") == 0 && left >= 3) {
			double x = atof(argv[i + 1]), y = atof(argv[i + 2]);

			post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN, x, y);
			usleep((useconds_t)atoi(argv[i + 3]) * 1000);
			post(HAKIOS_TOUCH_UP, x, y);
			i += 3;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "button") == 0 && left >= 1) {
			const char *name = argv[i + 1];
			uint32_t which = strcmp(name, "home") == 0 ? HAKIOS_BUTTON_HOME : strcmp(name, "lock") == 0 ?
			    HAKIOS_BUTTON_LOCK : strcmp(name, "volup") == 0 ? HAKIOS_BUTTON_VOLUME_UP :
			    strcmp(name, "voldown") == 0 ? HAKIOS_BUTTON_VOLUME_DOWN : 0;
			int ms = left >= 2 && argv[i + 2][0] >= '0' && argv[i + 2][0] <= '9' ? atoi(argv[i + 2]) : 0;

			if (which == 0) {
				fprintf(stderr, "rwtouch: buttons are home, lock, volup and voldown\n");
				return 2;
			}
			button(which, ms ? ms : 80);
			i += ms ? 2 : 1;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "swipe") == 0 && left >= 4) {
			int ms = left >= 5 && argv[i + 5][0] >= '0' && argv[i + 5][0] <= '9' ? atoi(argv[i + 5]) : 0;

			drag(atof(argv[i + 1]), atof(argv[i + 2]), atof(argv[i + 3]), atof(argv[i + 4]), ms ? ms : 300, 0, 0);
			i += ms ? 5 : 4;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "drag") == 0 && left >= 6) {
			int grab = left >= 7 && argv[i + 7][0] >= '0' && argv[i + 7][0] <= '9' ? atoi(argv[i + 7]) : 0;

			drag(atof(argv[i + 1]), atof(argv[i + 2]), atof(argv[i + 3]), atof(argv[i + 4]), atoi(argv[i + 5]),
			    atoi(argv[i + 6]), grab);
			i += grab ? 7 : 6;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "notify") == 0 && left >= 1) {
			uint32_t status = notify_post(argv[i + 1]);

			printf("rwtouch: notification %s: %s\n", argv[i + 1], status == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK ? "posted" : "FAILED");
			i += 1;
		} else if (strcmp(step, "clock") == 0) {
			static const useconds_t lengths[] = { 1000, 16000, 100000 };
			mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;

			mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
			for (unsigned k = 0; k < sizeof(lengths) / sizeof(lengths[0]); k++) {
				uint64_t start = mach_absolute_time(), worst = 0, total;

				for (int n = 0; n < 20; n++) {
					uint64_t before = mach_absolute_time(), took;

					usleep(lengths[k]);
					took = mach_absolute_time() - before;
					worst = took > worst ? took : worst;
				}
				total = (mach_absolute_time() - start) * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1000;
				printf("rwtouch: 20 sleeps of %u us took %llu us (the longest %llu us)\n", lengths[k],
				    (unsigned long long)total, (unsigned long long)(worst * timebase.numer / timebase.denom / 1000));
			}
		} else if (strcmp(step, "read") == 0) {
			struct hakios_touch t;

			while (read(device, &t, sizeof(t)) == (ssize_t)sizeof(t)) {
				if (t.type >= HAKIOS_BUTTON_DOWN) {
					printf("rwtouch: button %u %s\n", t.finger, t.type == HAKIOS_BUTTON_DOWN ? "down" : "up");
					continue;
				}
				printf("rwtouch: %s finger %u at %.3f %.3f\n", t.type == HAKIOS_TOUCH_DOWN ? "down" :
				    t.type == HAKIOS_TOUCH_MOVE ? "move" : "up  ", t.finger, t.x / 65535.0, t.y / 65535.0);
			}
			return 0;
		} else {
			fprintf(stderr, "rwtouch: bad step \"%s\"\n", step);
			return 2;
		}
		usleep(50000);
	}
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/shm_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * shm_test: the two things WebKit's processes talk through besides messages, between two processes of ours
 * (WebKit's IPC::StreamConnection: a shared buffer the web content process writes drawing commands into,
 * and a mach semaphore it signals to wake the GPU process up):
 *   - memory shared through a named entry (mach_make_memory_entry_64, mapped on the other side with
 *     mach_vm_map, as WebKit's SharedMemory does): is what one side writes seen by the other?
 *   - a mach semaphore handed over as a port: does a signal on one side wake a wait on the other?
 *
 *   shm_test [share]       the test (share: the memory entry made as WebKit's SharedMemory makes it, with
 *                          MAP_MEM_VM_SHARE); starts itself again as the second process
 *   shm_test child         (internal) the second process: its ports come through mach_ports_register()
 */
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <spawn.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <unistd.h>

extern char **environ;
/* (the SDK's mach/mach_vm.h refuses to be included on Darwin; the calls are there all the same) */
extern kern_return_t mach_vm_allocate(vm_map_t, mach_vm_address_t *, mach_vm_size_t, int);
extern kern_return_t mach_vm_map(vm_map_t, mach_vm_address_t *, mach_vm_size_t, mach_vm_offset_t, int, mem_entry_name_port_t,
    memory_object_offset_t, boolean_t, vm_prot_t, vm_prot_t, vm_inherit_t);

#define SIZE (2 << 20)          /* WebKit's stream buffer is about this big */

static int
child(void)
{
	mach_port_array_t ports;
	mach_msg_type_number_t count = 0;
	mach_vm_address_t address = 0;
	kern_return_t kr;
	volatile uint32_t *words;

	kr = mach_ports_lookup(mach_task_self(), &ports, &count);
	if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS || count < 3) {
		printf("shm_test child: mach_ports_lookup: %#x, %u ports\n", kr, count);
		return 1;
	}
	kr = mach_vm_map(mach_task_self(), &address, SIZE, 0, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE, ports[0], 0, FALSE, VM_PROT_READ | VM_PROT_WRITE,
	    VM_PROT_READ | VM_PROT_WRITE, VM_INHERIT_NONE);
	if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		printf("shm_test child: mach_vm_map: %#x\n", kr);
		return 1;
	}
	words = (volatile uint32_t *)address;
	printf("shm_test child: the shared memory at %#llx says %#x %#x (the parent wrote 0x1234 and 0x5678)\n", address, words[0],
	    words[SIZE / 4 - 1]);
	fflush(stdout);
	words[1] = 0xc0ffee;
	words[SIZE / 4 - 2] = 0xbeef;
	kr = semaphore_signal(ports[1]);
	printf("shm_test child: wrote 0xc0ffee and 0xbeef, signalled the semaphore: %#x; now waiting on the other one\n", kr);
	fflush(stdout);
	{
		mach_timespec_t wait = { 3, 0 };

		kr = semaphore_timedwait(ports[2], wait);
		printf("shm_test child: the parent's signal %s (%#x)\n", kr == KERN_SUCCESS ? "came" : "DID NOT COME", kr);
	}
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	mach_vm_address_t address = 0;
	memory_object_size_t size = SIZE;
	mach_port_t entry = MACH_PORT_NULL, wake = MACH_PORT_NULL, back = MACH_PORT_NULL, ports[3];
	volatile uint32_t *words;
	kern_return_t kr;
	mach_timespec_t wait = { 3, 0 };
	pid_t pid;
	int status = 0;
	char *args[] = { argv[0], "child", NULL };
	bool share = argc == 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "share") == 0;      /* "shm_test share": the entry made as WebKit makes it */

	if (argc == 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "child") == 0) {
		return child();
	}
	printf("shm_test: the memory entry made %s\n", share ? "with MAP_MEM_VM_SHARE | VM_PROT_IS_MASK, as WebKit's SharedMemory "
	    "makes it" : "plainly");
	if ((kr = mach_vm_allocate(mach_task_self(), &address, SIZE, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE)) != KERN_SUCCESS ||
	    (kr = mach_make_memory_entry_64(mach_task_self(), &size, address, VM_PROT_READ | VM_PROT_WRITE | (share ? VM_PROT_IS_MASK |
	    MAP_MEM_VM_SHARE : 0), &entry, MACH_PORT_NULL))
	    != KERN_SUCCESS || (kr = semaphore_create(mach_task_self(), &wake, SYNC_POLICY_FIFO, 0)) != KERN_SUCCESS ||
	    (kr = semaphore_create(mach_task_self(), &back, SYNC_POLICY_FIFO, 0)) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		printf("shm_test: setting up: %#x\n", kr);
		return 1;
	}
	words = (volatile uint32_t *)address;
	words[0] = 0x1234;
	words[SIZE / 4 - 1] = 0x5678;
	ports[0] = entry;
	ports[1] = wake;
	ports[2] = back;
	if ((kr = mach_ports_register(mach_task_self(), ports, 3)) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		printf("shm_test: mach_ports_register: %#x\n", kr);
		return 1;
	}
	if (posix_spawn(&pid, argv[0], NULL, NULL, args, environ) != 0) {
		printf("shm_test: cannot start the second process\n");
		return 1;
	}
	kr = semaphore_timedwait(wake, wait);
	printf("shm_test: the child's signal %s (%#x); the shared memory now says %#x %#x (the child writes 0xc0ffee and 0xbeef)\n",
	    kr == KERN_SUCCESS ? "came" : "DID NOT COME", kr, words[1], words[SIZE / 4 - 2]);
	fflush(stdout);
	semaphore_signal(back);
	waitpid(pid, &status, 0);
	printf("shm_test: %s\n", kr == KERN_SUCCESS && words[1] == 0xc0ffee && words[SIZE / 4 - 2] == 0xbeef ? "both work" :
	    "SOMETHING DOES NOT WORK");
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/snap_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * snap_test: what the pictures SpringBoard keeps of applications look like -- their launch images
 * and their snapshots (Library/SplashBoard/Snapshots), as files.
 *
 * usage: snap_test DIRECTORY...
 * Every JPEG, PNG or other picture ImageIO can read under the directories is decoded and drawn
 * into 8 x 8 pixels; the line it gets says its size, its average colour and opacity, and how
 * many of those 64 pixels are near black. (A launch image of a light application that comes out
 * black was the question: the zoom that opens an application showed black at its first launch.)
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreGraphics/CoreGraphics.h>
#include <ImageIO/ImageIO.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <fts.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static void
look(const char *path)
{
	CFURLRef url = CFURLCreateFromFileSystemRepresentation(NULL, (const UInt8 *)path, (CFIndex)strlen(path), false);
	CGImageSourceRef source = url != NULL ? CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(url, NULL) : NULL;
	CGImageRef image = source != NULL && CGImageSourceGetCount(source) > 0 ? CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(source, 0, NULL) : NULL;
	uint8_t pixels[8 * 8 * 4];
	unsigned long sum[4] = { 0, 0, 0, 0 };
	unsigned dark = 0;

	if (image == NULL) {
		printf("snap_test: %s: NOT READ\n", path);
	} else {
		CGColorSpaceRef space = CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB();
		CGContextRef context = CGBitmapContextCreate(pixels, 8, 8, 8, 32, space, kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast);

		memset(pixels, 0, sizeof(pixels));
		CGContextDrawImage(context, CGRectMake(0, 0, 8, 8), image);
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
			for (unsigned c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
				sum[c] += pixels[4 * i + c];
			}
			dark += pixels[4 * i] < 16 && pixels[4 * i + 1] < 16 && pixels[4 * i + 2] < 16;
		}
		printf("snap_test: %s: %zu x %zu, average %lu %lu %lu opacity %lu, %u of 64 near black\n", path, CGImageGetWidth(image),
		    CGImageGetHeight(image), sum[0] / 64, sum[1] / 64, sum[2] / 64, sum[3] / 64, dark);
		CGContextRelease(context);
		CGColorSpaceRelease(space);
		CGImageRelease(image);
	}
	if (source != NULL) {
		CFRelease(source);
	}
	if (url != NULL) {
		CFRelease(url);
	}
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	FTS *walk;
	FTSENT *entry;

	if (argc < 2) {
		fprintf(stderr, "usage: snap_test DIRECTORY...\n");
		return 2;
	}
	walk = fts_open(argv + 1, FTS_PHYSICAL | FTS_NOCHDIR, NULL);
	while (walk != NULL && (entry = fts_read(walk)) != NULL) {
		const char *dot = strrchr(entry->fts_name, '.');

		if (entry->fts_info == FTS_F && dot != NULL && (strcmp(dot, ".jpeg") == 0 || strcmp(dot, ".jpg") == 0 ||
		    strcmp(dot, ".png") == 0 || strcmp(dot, ".ktx") == 0 || strcmp(dot, ".atx") == 0)) {
			look(entry->fts_path);
		} else if (entry->fts_info == FTS_F) {
			printf("snap_test: %s: %lld bytes, not a picture by its name\n", entry->fts_path, (long long)entry->fts_statp->st_size);
		}
	}
	if (walk != NULL) {
		fts_close(walk);
	}
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/src/sound_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * sound_test: make Darwin play something, the way a program would.
 *
 * usage: sound_test STEP...
 *   wait SECONDS
 *   springboard                        wait until SpringBoard is up and has said that the ringer is on (at
 *                                      most ten minutes): until then system sounds are "played" in silence,
 *                                      as on an iPhone with its switch on silent
 *   tone SECONDS [LEFT_HZ RIGHT_HZ]    a sine wave in each channel (default 1000 and 440 Hz) at half of
 *                                      full scale, through an audio queue: what a music player does
 *   level PEAK                         the tones after this one at PEAK of full scale (0 to 1) instead
 *                                      (before Darwin's volume, which scales the samples itself)
 *   raw SECONDS                        the same tone written straight to /dev/hakios-audio, past Darwin's own
 *                                      processing and volume (which keep a tone more than 12 dB under full
 *                                      scale even at the top): to try what the kernel does with full scale
 *   system ID                          a system sound by its number (1100 is the lock sound,
 *                                      1104 a keyboard click), as SpringBoard plays them
 *   file PATH                          a sound file, played as a system sound
 *   route                              where Darwin says its sound goes: the audio session's outputs and volume,
 *                                      and the devices of the system's output context
 *   haptic [SECONDS]                   haptics the way an application (and UIKit's feedback generators) plays
 *                                      them, through CoreHaptics: a tap, then a vibration of SECONDS (default
 *                                      0.3, at most 3: the kernel cuts a vibration at 1 s) at half strength, then
 *                                      three taps of falling strength
 *   restart                            kill the audio server (launchd starts it again when it is next asked for):
 *                                      what every program then sees as "media services were reset"
 *
 * The samples come out of /dev/hakios-audio (see sys/hakios.audio.h); a tone is something one
 * can recognize there without ears: two peaks in the spectrum, where they were put.
 */
#include <AudioToolbox/AudioToolbox.h>
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <notify.h>
#include <objc/message.h>
#include <objc/runtime.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define RATE            48000
#define BUFFER_FRAMES   4096

static double frequency[2] = { 1000, 440 }, peak = 0.5;
static uint64_t frame, frames_wanted;

static void
fill(__unused void *context, AudioQueueRef queue, AudioQueueBufferRef buffer)
{
	int16_t *samples = buffer->mAudioData;
	uint32_t count = 0;

	for (; count < BUFFER_FRAMES && frame < frames_wanted; count++, frame++) {
		/* a hundredth of a second to come in and to go out: no click */
		double edge = frame < RATE / 100 ? frame / (RATE / 100.0) :
		    frames_wanted - frame < RATE / 100 ? (frames_wanted - frame) / (RATE / 100.0) : 1;

		for (int channel = 0; channel < 2; channel++) {
			samples[2 * count + channel] = (int16_t)(32767 * peak * edge * sin(2 * M_PI * frequency[channel] * frame / RATE));
		}
	}
	if (count == 0) {
		AudioQueueStop(queue, false);
		return;
	}
	buffer->mAudioDataByteSize = count * 4;
	AudioQueueEnqueueBuffer(queue, buffer, 0, NULL);
}

/* The tone to the kernel's device itself, 10 ms at a time and as fast as it plays (48000 frames a second). */
static int
raw(double seconds)
{
	int device = open("/dev/hakios-audio", O_WRONLY);
	int16_t block[2 * 480];
	uint64_t total = (uint64_t)(seconds * RATE), written = 0, start;
	mach_timebase_info_data_t timebase;

	if (device < 0) {
		printf("sound_test: /dev/hakios-audio: %s\n", strerror(errno));
		return 1;
	}
	mach_timebase_info(&timebase);
	printf("sound_test: a tone of %.0f and %.0f Hz at %.2f of full scale for %.1f s, straight to /dev/hakios-audio\n",
	    frequency[0], frequency[1], peak, seconds);
	fflush(stdout);
	start = mach_absolute_time();
	while (written < total) {
		uint64_t due;
		uint32_t count = total - written < 480 ? (uint32_t)(total - written) : 480;

		for (uint32_t f = 0; f < count; f++) {
			uint64_t n = written + f;
			double edge = n < RATE / 100 ? n / (RATE / 100.0) : total - n < RATE / 100 ? (total - n) / (RATE / 100.0) : 1;

			for (int channel = 0; channel < 2; channel++) {
				block[2 * f + channel] = (int16_t)(32767 * peak * edge * sin(2 * M_PI * frequency[channel] * n / RATE));
			}
		}
		if (write(device, block, count * 4) != (ssize_t)(count * 4)) {
			printf("sound_test: /dev/hakios-audio: a write failed: %s\n", strerror(errno));
			break;
		}
		written += count;
		/* stay 100 ms ahead of the clock, not more: the kernel's ring holds 0.68 s */
		due = start + (written > RATE / 10 ? written - RATE / 10 : 0) * 1000000000ull / RATE * timebase.denom / timebase.numer;
		if (mach_absolute_time() < due) {
			mach_wait_until(due);
		}
	}
	close(device);
	printf("sound_test: %llu frames written straight to the device\n", written);
	return written < total;
}

static int
tone(double seconds)
{
	AudioStreamBasicDescription format = {
		.mSampleRate = RATE, .mFormatID = kAudioFormatLinearPCM,
		.mFormatFlags = kAudioFormatFlagIsSignedInteger | kAudioFormatFlagIsPacked,
		.mBytesPerPacket = 4, .mFramesPerPacket = 1, .mBytesPerFrame = 4, .mChannelsPerFrame = 2, .mBitsPerChannel = 16,
	};
	AudioQueueRef queue;
	OSStatus status;

	frame = 0;
	frames_wanted = (uint64_t)(seconds * RATE);
	/* no run loop given: the queue asks for more on a thread of its own, also while we are busy talking */
	status = AudioQueueNewOutput(&format, fill, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, &queue);
	if (status != 0) {
		printf("sound_test: AudioQueueNewOutput: %d\n", (int)status);
		return 1;
	}
	for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
		AudioQueueBufferRef buffer;

		status = AudioQueueAllocateBuffer(queue, BUFFER_FRAMES * 4, &buffer);
		if (status != 0) {
			printf("sound_test: AudioQueueAllocateBuffer: %d\n", (int)status);
			return 1;
		}
		fill(NULL, queue, buffer);
	}
	status = AudioQueueStart(queue, NULL);
	printf("sound_test: a tone of %.0f and %.0f Hz at %.2f of full scale for %.1f s: AudioQueueStart: %d\n", frequency[0],
	    frequency[1], peak, seconds,
	    (int)status);
	if (status == 0) {
		/* a slow machine may take its time: wait for the end, three times as long as it should take at most */
		for (int tenths = 0; frame < frames_wanted && tenths < 30 * seconds + 100; tenths++) {
			usleep(100000);
		}
		usleep(1500000);                /* the last buffers are still to be played */
		printf("sound_test: %llu of %llu frames handed over\n", frame, frames_wanted);
	}
	AudioQueueDispose(queue, true);
	return status != 0 || frame < frames_wanted;
}

static void
played(SystemSoundID sound, __unused void *context)
{
	printf("sound_test: system sound %u has been played\n", (unsigned)sound);
	CFRunLoopStop(CFRunLoopGetCurrent());
}

static int
system_sound(SystemSoundID sound)
{
	AudioServicesAddSystemSoundCompletion(sound, CFRunLoopGetCurrent(), kCFRunLoopCommonModes, played, NULL);
	printf("sound_test: system sound %u\n", (unsigned)sound);
	AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(sound);
	if (CFRunLoopRunInMode(kCFRunLoopDefaultMode, 15, false) == kCFRunLoopRunTimedOut) {
		printf("sound_test: system sound %u: no word of its end in 15 s\n", (unsigned)sound);
		return 1;
	}
	return 0;
}

/* SpringBoard keeps the state of the ringer switch (1: ring, 0: silent) in a notification of this name. */
static void
wait_for_ringer(void)
{
	uint64_t state = 0;
	int token, seconds;

	if (notify_register_check("com.apple.springboard.ringerstate", &token) != NOTIFY_STATUS_OK) {
		return;
	}
	for (seconds = 0; seconds < 600 && (notify_get_state(token, &state) != NOTIFY_STATUS_OK || state == 0); seconds++) {
		sleep(1);
	}
	printf("sound_test: the ringer is %s after %d s\n", state ? "on" : "still off", seconds);
	notify_cancel(token);
}

/* [object selector] for methods without arguments that return an object. */
static id
send(id object, const char *selector)
{
	return object ? ((id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(object, sel_registerName(selector)) : NULL;
}

static const char *
text(id string)
{
	const char *utf8 = string ? ((const char *(*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(string, sel_registerName("UTF8String")) : NULL;

	return utf8 ? utf8 : "(none)";
}

/*
 * What the audio session of this program says of the route (AVAudioSession, as an application would
 * ask), and what the system's output context holds (AVOutputContext: what Control Center goes by).
 */
static void
route(void)
{
	id session = send((id)objc_getClass("AVAudioSession"), "sharedInstance");
	id outputs = send(send(session, "currentRoute"), "outputs");
	id context = send((id)objc_getClass("AVOutputContext"), "sharedSystemAudioContext");
	id devices = send(context, "outputDevices");
	unsigned long count = outputs ? ((unsigned long (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(outputs, sel_registerName("count")) : 0;

	printf("sound_test: route: %lu output%s, volume %.2f\n", count, count == 1 ? "" : "s",
	    session ? ((float (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(session, sel_registerName("outputVolume")) : -1.0f);
	for (unsigned long i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		id port = ((id (*)(id, SEL, unsigned long))objc_msgSend)(outputs, sel_registerName("objectAtIndex:"), i);

		printf("sound_test: route:   %s \"%s\" (%s)\n", text(send(port, "portType")), text(send(port, "portName")),
		    text(send(port, "UID")));
	}
	count = devices ? ((unsigned long (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(devices, sel_registerName("count")) : 0;
	printf("sound_test: route: the system's output context %s, %lu device%s\n", context ? "is there" : "is missing", count,
	    count == 1 ? "" : "s");
	for (unsigned long i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		id device = ((id (*)(id, SEL, unsigned long))objc_msgSend)(devices, sel_registerName("objectAtIndex:"), i);

		printf("sound_test: route:   \"%s\" (%s)\n", text(send(device, "name")), text(send(device, "ID")));
	}
}

/* CoreHaptics' constants (NSString *) by name, the framework opened when first asked for */
static id
haptics_constant(const char *name)
{
	static void *framework;
	id *constant;

	if (framework == NULL) {
		framework = dlopen("/System/Library/Frameworks/CoreHaptics.framework/CoreHaptics", RTLD_NOW);
	}
	constant = framework ? dlsym(framework, name) : NULL;
	return constant ? *constant : NULL;
}

static id
haptic_parameter(const char *name, float value)
{
	id parameter = send((id)objc_getClass("CHHapticEventParameter"), "alloc");

	return ((id (*)(id, SEL, id, float))objc_msgSend)(parameter, sel_registerName("initWithParameterID:value:"),
	           haptics_constant(name), value);
}

/* A haptic event: transient (a tap) when `duration' is 0, otherwise continuous for that long. */
static id
haptic_event(double at, double duration, float intensity, float sharpness)
{
	const void *parameters[2] = {
		haptic_parameter("CHHapticEventParameterIDHapticIntensity", intensity),
		haptic_parameter("CHHapticEventParameterIDHapticSharpness", sharpness),
	};
	CFArrayRef list = CFArrayCreate(NULL, parameters, 2, &kCFTypeArrayCallBacks);
	id event = send((id)objc_getClass("CHHapticEvent"), "alloc");

	if (duration > 0) {
		event = ((id (*)(id, SEL, id, id, double, double))objc_msgSend)(event,
		    sel_registerName("initWithEventType:parameters:relativeTime:duration:"),
		    haptics_constant("CHHapticEventTypeHapticContinuous"), (id)list, at, duration);
	} else {
		event = ((id (*)(id, SEL, id, id, double))objc_msgSend)(event, sel_registerName("initWithEventType:parameters:relativeTime:"),
		    haptics_constant("CHHapticEventTypeHapticTransient"), (id)list, at);
	}
	CFRelease(list);
	return event;
}

static int
haptic(double seconds)
{
	id error = NULL, engine, pattern, player;
	const void *events[5];
	CFArrayRef list, none = CFArrayCreate(NULL, NULL, 0, &kCFTypeArrayCallBacks);
	BOOL started;

	if (haptics_constant("CHHapticEventTypeHapticTransient") == NULL) {
		printf("sound_test: haptic: no CoreHaptics\n");
		return 1;
	}
	{
		/* what an application asks first, and what UIKit's feedback generators go by */
		id capabilities = send((id)objc_getClass("CHHapticEngine"), "capabilitiesForHardware");
		SEL first = sel_registerName("supports1stPartyHaptics");
		BOOL answers = capabilities && ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL, SEL))objc_msgSend)(capabilities,
		    sel_registerName("respondsToSelector:"), first);

		printf("sound_test: haptic: the hardware %s haptics%s\n", capabilities && ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(capabilities,
		    sel_registerName("supportsHaptics")) ? "supports" : "DOES NOT SUPPORT", !answers ? "" :
		    ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(capabilities, first) ? " (also the system's own, as UIKit's feedbacks)" :
		    " (but NOT the system's own, as UIKit's feedbacks)");
	}
	engine = ((id (*)(id, SEL, id *))objc_msgSend)(send((id)objc_getClass("CHHapticEngine"), "alloc"),
	    sel_registerName("initAndReturnError:"), &error);
	if (engine == NULL) {
		printf("sound_test: haptic: no engine: %s\n", text(send(error, "description")));
		return 1;
	}
	started = ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL, id *))objc_msgSend)(engine, sel_registerName("startAndReturnError:"), &error);
	printf("sound_test: haptic: the engine %s%s\n", started ? "has started" : "DOES NOT START: ",
	    started ? "" : text(send(error, "description")));
	if (!started) {
		return 1;
	}
	events[0] = haptic_event(0, 0, 1.0f, 0.5f);
	events[1] = haptic_event(0.3, seconds, 0.5f, 0.3f);
	events[2] = haptic_event(0.6 + seconds, 0, 1.0f, 0.8f);
	events[3] = haptic_event(0.8 + seconds, 0, 0.6f, 0.8f);
	events[4] = haptic_event(1.0 + seconds, 0, 0.3f, 0.8f);
	list = CFArrayCreate(NULL, events, 5, &kCFTypeArrayCallBacks);
	pattern = ((id (*)(id, SEL, id, id, id *))objc_msgSend)(send((id)objc_getClass("CHHapticPattern"), "alloc"),
	    sel_registerName("initWithEvents:parameters:error:"), (id)list, (id)none, &error);
	player = pattern ? ((id (*)(id, SEL, id, id *))objc_msgSend)(engine, sel_registerName("createPlayerWithPattern:error:"),
	    pattern, &error) : NULL;
	if (player == NULL ||
	    !((BOOL (*)(id, SEL, double, id *))objc_msgSend)(player, sel_registerName("startAtTime:error:"), 0.0, &error)) {
		printf("sound_test: haptic: the pattern does not play: %s\n", text(send(error, "description")));
		return 1;
	}
	printf("sound_test: haptic: playing a tap, %.2f s of vibration at half strength, three taps\n", seconds);
	usleep((useconds_t)((1.5 + seconds) * 1e6));
	((void (*)(id, SEL, id))objc_msgSend)(engine, sel_registerName("stopWithCompletionHandler:"), NULL);
	printf("sound_test: haptic: done\n");
	return 0;
}

extern int proc_listallpids(void *buffer, int size);
extern int proc_name(int pid, void *buffer, uint32_t size);

static void
restart(void)
{
	static int pids[2048];
	int count = proc_listallpids(pids, sizeof(pids));
	char name[64];

	for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		if (proc_name(pids[i], name, sizeof(name)) > 0 && strcmp(name, "mediaserverd") == 0) {
			printf("sound_test: restart: killing mediaserverd[%d]: %s\n", pids[i],
			    kill(pids[i], SIGKILL) == 0 ? "done" : strerror(errno));
			return;
		}
	}
	printf("sound_test: restart: no mediaserverd is running\n");
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int failed = 0;

	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
	for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
		if (strcmp(argv[i], "wait") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			usleep((useconds_t)(atof(argv[++i]) * 1e6));
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "springboard") == 0) {
			wait_for_ringer();
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "route") == 0) {
			route();
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "restart") == 0) {
			restart();
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "haptic") == 0) {
			double seconds = i + 1 < argc && atof(argv[i + 1]) > 0 ? atof(argv[++i]) : 0.3;

			failed |= haptic(seconds > 3 ? 3 : seconds);
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "tone") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			double seconds = atof(argv[++i]);

			if (i + 2 < argc && atof(argv[i + 1]) > 0 && atof(argv[i + 2]) > 0) {
				frequency[0] = atof(argv[++i]);
				frequency[1] = atof(argv[++i]);
			}
			failed |= tone(seconds);
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "raw") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			failed |= raw(atof(argv[++i]));
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "level") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			peak = atof(argv[++i]);
			peak = peak < 0 ? 0 : peak > 1 ? 1 : peak;
			printf("sound_test: the tones from now on at %.2f of full scale\n", peak);
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "system") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			failed |= system_sound((SystemSoundID)atoi(argv[++i]));
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "file") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			CFURLRef url = CFURLCreateFromFileSystemRepresentation(NULL, (const UInt8 *)argv[i + 1],
			    (CFIndex)strlen(argv[i + 1]), false);
			SystemSoundID sound = 0;
			OSStatus status = AudioServicesCreateSystemSoundID(url, &sound);

			i++;
			if (status != 0) {
				printf("sound_test: %s: AudioServicesCreateSystemSoundID: %d\n", argv[i], (int)status);
				failed = 1;
			} else {
				failed |= system_sound(sound);
			}
		} else {
			printf("sound_test: what is \"%s\"?\n", argv[i]);
			return 2;
		}
	}
	return failed;
}
```

`userland/src/stage0.c`:

```c
/*
 * /sbin/launchd of the big system image: the first program the kernel runs.
 *
 * The system image (the Darwin files and the dyld shared cache) takes a minute
 * and a half to upload to the phone, so nothing that changes often lives in
 * it. All of that - the real init, its tests, the list of launchd jobs - is
 * in the small image that travels with the kernel (the second RAM disk,
 * /dev/md1), an APFS container (tools/apfs/mkapfs.py). This program
 * mounts it on /redwood and hands over.
 */
#include "mini.h"

int
main(int argc, char **argv, char **envp)
{
	char *init_argv[] = { "/redwood/sbin/init", NULL };
	int fd = open("/dev/console", O_RDWR, 0);

	(void)argc, (void)argv;
	dup2(fd, 0);
	dup2(fd, 1);
	dup2(fd, 2);
	if (fd > 2) {
		close(fd);
	}

	if (mount("apfs", "/redwood", MNT_RDONLY, (void *)"/dev/md1") != 0) {
		printf("stage0: cannot mount /dev/md1 on /hakios: %s\n", strerror(errno));
	} else {
		execve(init_argv[0], init_argv, envp);
		printf("stage0: cannot run %s: %s\n", init_argv[0], strerror(errno));
	}
	reboot(0x08 /* RB_HALT */);
	return 1;
}
```

`userland/src/surf_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * surf_test: exercises the kernel's IOSurface stand-in through the real IOSurface.framework.
 *
 *   surf_test              the tests; starts itself again as a second process for the sharing part
 *   surf_test child ID     (internal) look surface ID up, check the pattern, change one pixel
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurfaceRef.h>
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <spawn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <unistd.h>

extern char **environ;

static int failed, checks;

#define CHECK(cond, ...) do { \
		checks++; \
		if (!(cond)) { failed++; printf("surf_test: FAILED: " __VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } \
	} while (0)

static CFNumberRef
num(int value)
{
	return CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, &value);
}

static IOSurfaceRef
make_surface(int width, int height, uint32_t format, int bytes_per_element)
{
	CFMutableDictionaryRef props = CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks,
	    &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	CFNumberRef n;
	IOSurfaceRef surface;

	n = num(width); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceWidth, n); CFRelease(n);
	n = num(height); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceHeight, n); CFRelease(n);
	n = num((int) format); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfacePixelFormat, n); CFRelease(n);
	if (bytes_per_element) {
		n = num(bytes_per_element); CFDictionarySetValue(props, kIOSurfaceBytesPerElement, n); CFRelease(n);
	}
	surface = IOSurfaceCreate(props);
	CFRelease(props);
	return surface;
}

static uint32_t
pattern(int x, int y)
{
	return 0xff000000u | (uint32_t) (x * 7 + y * 13) << 8 | (uint32_t) ((x ^ y) & 0xff);
}

static int
child(uint32_t sid)
{
	IOSurfaceRef surface = IOSurfaceLookup(sid);
	uint32_t *row;
	int bad = 0;

	if (surface == NULL) {
		printf("surf_test: child: no surface %u\n", sid);
		return 2;
	}
	IOSurfaceLock(surface, 0, NULL);
	for (int y = 0; y < (int) IOSurfaceGetHeight(surface); y++) {
		row = (uint32_t *) ((char *) IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface) + y * IOSurfaceGetBytesPerRow(surface));
		for (int x = 0; x < (int) IOSurfaceGetWidth(surface); x++) {
			bad += row[x] != pattern(x, y);
		}
	}
	row = (uint32_t *) IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface);
	row[3] = 0x12345678;
	IOSurfaceUnlock(surface, 0, NULL);
	CFRelease(surface);
	printf("surf_test: child: surface %u, %d wrong pixels\n", sid, bad);
	return bad ? 3 : 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	IOSurfaceRef surface, again, yuv;
	uint32_t sid, seed, *row;
	mach_port_t port;
	CFStringRef text;
	CFTypeRef value;

	if (argc == 3 && strcmp(argv[1], "child") == 0) {
		return child((uint32_t) atoi(argv[2]));
	}

	surface = make_surface(64, 48, 'BGRA', 4);
	CHECK(surface != NULL, "IOSurfaceCreate");
	if (surface == NULL) {
		printf("surf_test: no IOSurface service, giving up\n");
		return 1;
	}
	sid = IOSurfaceGetID(surface);
	printf("surf_test: surface %u: %zux%zu, %zu bytes per row, %zu bytes, base %p\n", sid, IOSurfaceGetWidth(surface),
	    IOSurfaceGetHeight(surface), IOSurfaceGetBytesPerRow(surface), IOSurfaceGetAllocSize(surface),
	    IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface));
	CHECK(sid != 0, "surface number");
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetWidth(surface) == 64 && IOSurfaceGetHeight(surface) == 48, "size");
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetBytesPerRow(surface) >= 256, "bytes per row");
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetAllocSize(surface) >= 48 * 256, "alloc size");
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetPixelFormat(surface) == 'BGRA', "pixel format");
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetBytesPerElement(surface) == 4, "bytes per element");
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface) != NULL, "base address");

	seed = IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface);
	CHECK(IOSurfaceLock(surface, 0, NULL) == KERN_SUCCESS, "lock");
	for (int y = 0; y < 48; y++) {
		row = (uint32_t *) ((char *) IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface) + y * IOSurfaceGetBytesPerRow(surface));
		CHECK(row[0] == 0 && row[63] == 0, "new surface not zeroed, row %d", y);
		for (int x = 0; x < 64; x++) {
			row[x] = pattern(x, y);
		}
	}
	CHECK(IOSurfaceUnlock(surface, 0, NULL) == KERN_SUCCESS, "unlock");
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface) != seed, "seed did not change after writing (%u)", seed);
	seed = IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface);
	IOSurfaceLock(surface, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	IOSurfaceUnlock(surface, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	CHECK(IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface) == seed, "seed changed after a read-only lock");

	/* values */
	text = CFSTR("a value");
	IOSurfaceSetValue(surface, CFSTR("redwood.test"), text);
	value = IOSurfaceCopyValue(surface, CFSTR("redwood.test"));
	CHECK(value != NULL && CFEqual(value, text), "value did not come back");
	if (value) {
		CFRelease(value);
	}
	value = num(42);
	IOSurfaceSetValue(surface, CFSTR("redwood.number"), value);
	CFRelease(value);
	value = IOSurfaceCopyAllValues(surface);
	CHECK(value != NULL && CFGetTypeID(value) == CFDictionaryGetTypeID() && CFDictionaryGetCount(value) >= 2,
	    "all values");
	if (value) {
		CFRelease(value);
	}
	IOSurfaceRemoveValue(surface, CFSTR("redwood.test"));
	value = IOSurfaceCopyValue(surface, CFSTR("redwood.test"));
	CHECK(value == NULL, "value still there after removing it");
	value = IOSurfaceCopyValue(surface, CFSTR("redwood.number"));
	CHECK(value != NULL, "the other value is gone");
	if (value) {
		CFRelease(value);
	}

	/* use count */
	CHECK(!IOSurfaceIsInUse(surface), "in use from the start");
	IOSurfaceIncrementUseCount(surface);
	CHECK(IOSurfaceIsInUse(surface), "not in use after increment");
	IOSurfaceDecrementUseCount(surface);
	CHECK(!IOSurfaceIsInUse(surface), "in use after decrement");

	/* the same surface through a Mach port and by number */
	port = IOSurfaceCreateMachPort(surface);
	CHECK(port != MACH_PORT_NULL, "IOSurfaceCreateMachPort");
	again = IOSurfaceLookupFromMachPort(port);
	CHECK(again != NULL && IOSurfaceGetID(again) == sid, "lookup from the Mach port");
	if (again) {
		CHECK(IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(again) == IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface), "second view of the same surface");
		CFRelease(again);
	}
	mach_port_deallocate(mach_task_self(), port);
	again = IOSurfaceLookup(sid);
	CHECK(again != NULL && IOSurfaceGetID(again) == sid, "lookup by number");
	if (again) {
		CFRelease(again);
	}
	CHECK(IOSurfaceLookup(sid + 1000) == NULL, "found a surface that does not exist");

	/* another process */
	{
		char number[16];
		char *args[] = { argv[0], "child", number, NULL };
		pid_t pid;
		int status = -1;

		snprintf(number, sizeof(number), "%u", sid);
		seed = IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface);
		if (posix_spawn(&pid, argv[0], NULL, NULL, args, environ) == 0) {
			waitpid(pid, &status, 0);
		}
		CHECK(WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 0, "second process: status 0x%x", status);
		row = (uint32_t *) IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(surface);
		CHECK(row[3] == 0x12345678, "the pixel written by the second process: 0x%x", row[3]);
		CHECK(IOSurfaceGetSeed(surface) != seed, "seed did not change after the second process wrote");
	}
	CFRelease(surface);
	CHECK(IOSurfaceLookup(sid) == NULL, "surface still exists after the last release");

	/* two planes */
	yuv = make_surface(100, 50, '420v', 0);
	CHECK(yuv != NULL, "IOSurfaceCreate 420v");
	if (yuv) {
		CHECK(IOSurfaceGetPlaneCount(yuv) == 2, "plane count %zu", IOSurfaceGetPlaneCount(yuv));
		CHECK(IOSurfaceGetWidthOfPlane(yuv, 1) == 50 && IOSurfaceGetHeightOfPlane(yuv, 1) == 25, "chroma plane %zux%zu",
		    IOSurfaceGetWidthOfPlane(yuv, 1), IOSurfaceGetHeightOfPlane(yuv, 1));
		CHECK((char *) IOSurfaceGetBaseAddressOfPlane(yuv, 1) >= (char *) IOSurfaceGetBaseAddressOfPlane(yuv, 0) +
		    50 * IOSurfaceGetBytesPerRowOfPlane(yuv, 0), "planes overlap");
		CFRelease(yuv);
	}

	printf("surf_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, failed);
	return failed != 0;
}
```

`userland/src/svc_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * A client of the first real Darwin services: each call below is answered by a
 * daemon that launchd starts on demand.
 *   notifyd   - Darwin notifications (libnotify)
 *   cfprefsd  - preferences (CoreFoundation)
 *   logd      - unified logging (os_log)
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <notify.h>
#include <os/log.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>

static int failures;

static void
check(int ok, const char *what)
{
	failures += !ok;
	printf("[%s] %s\n", ok ? " ok " : "FAIL", what);
	fflush(stdout);
}

int
main(void)
{
	int token = -1, changed = 0;
	uint32_t status;
	uint64_t state = 0;

	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
	printf("svc_test: pid %d, uid %d\n", getpid(), getuid());

	/* notifyd */
	status = notify_register_check("com.hakios.test", &token);
	check(status == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK, "notifyd: register for a notification");
	if (status == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK) {
		notify_check(token, &changed);          /* the first check always reports a change */
		status = notify_set_state(token, 0x1234abcd);
		check(status == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK && notify_get_state(token, &state) == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK && state == 0x1234abcd,
		    "notifyd: store and fetch a state value");
		changed = 0;
		status = notify_post("com.hakios.test");
		usleep(100000);
		check(status == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK && notify_check(token, &changed) == NOTIFY_STATUS_OK && changed,
		    "notifyd: post a notification and see it arrive");
	} else {
		printf("  status %u\n", status);
	}

	/* cfprefsd */
	{
		CFStringRef app = CFSTR("com.hakios.test"), key = CFSTR("greeting");
		CFStringRef value;
		char text[64] = "";

		CFPreferencesSetAppValue(key, CFSTR("hello from preferences"), app);
		check(CFPreferencesAppSynchronize(app), "cfprefsd: write a preference");
		value = CFPreferencesCopyAppValue(key, app);
		if (value != NULL && CFGetTypeID(value) == CFStringGetTypeID()) {
			CFStringGetCString(value, text, sizeof(text), kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
		}
		printf("  greeting = \"%s\"\n", text);
		check(strcmp(text, "hello from preferences") == 0, "cfprefsd: read it back");
	}

	/* logd */
	os_log(OS_LOG_DEFAULT, "svc_test says hello to the unified log (pid %d)", getpid());
	check(1, "logd: os_log does not crash");

	printf("svc_test: %d failed\n", failures);
	return failures;
}
```

`userland/src/torch_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * torch_test: the flashlight the way a program (and Control Center) works it: AVFlashlight, which
 * asks mediaserverd's FigFlashlight, which sets the back camera's torch level (on this machine:
 * libhakios.media.dylib in mediaserverd, the kernel's /dev/hakios-torch, torch=3).
 *
 * usage: torch_test STEP...
 *   wait SECONDS
 *   level L          the flashlight at L (0 to 1; Control Center's steps are fractions of 1)
 *   off              the flashlight off (level 0, then AVFlashlight's turnPowerOff)
 *   state            what the kernel says is lit now (thousandths of Android's current)
 *
 * Says first whether Darwin believes there is a flashlight (AVFlashlight's hasFlashlight: MobileGestalt's
 * camera-flash) and whether it is available.
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <objc/message.h>
#include <objc/runtime.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

static id
send(id object, const char *selector)
{
	return object ? ((id (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(object, sel_registerName(selector)) : NULL;
}

static BOOL
yes(id object, const char *selector)
{
	return object ? ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(object, sel_registerName(selector)) : NO;
}

static const char *
text(id object)
{
	id description = send(object, "description");
	const char *utf8 = description ? ((const char *(*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(description, sel_registerName("UTF8String")) : NULL;

	return utf8 ? utf8 : "(none)";
}

static void
kernel_state(void)
{
	int device = open("/dev/hakios-torch", O_RDONLY);
	uint32_t lit = 0;

	if (device < 0 || read(device, &lit, sizeof(lit)) != (ssize_t)sizeof(lit)) {
		printf("torch_test: the kernel has no flashlight (/dev/hakios-torch)\n");
	} else {
		printf("torch_test: the kernel says: %s%u of 1000\n", lit ? "LIT at " : "dark, ", lit);
	}
	if (device >= 0) {
		close(device);
	}
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	Class flashlight_class = objc_getClass("AVFlashlight");
	id flashlight;
	int failed = 0;

	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
	if (flashlight_class == NULL) {
		printf("torch_test: no AVFlashlight\n");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("torch_test: AVFlashlight says hasFlashlight %s\n", yes((id)flashlight_class, "hasFlashlight") ? "YES" : "NO");
	if (!yes((id)flashlight_class, "hasFlashlight")) {
		/* (AVFlashlight refuses to be made, with an exception, where there is none: the loader adds the flash with torch=N) */
		kernel_state();
		return 1;
	}
	flashlight = send(send((id)flashlight_class, "alloc"), "init");
	printf("torch_test: an AVFlashlight %s; available %s, overheated %s, level %.2f\n", flashlight ? "made" : "NOT MADE",
	    yes(flashlight, "isAvailable") ? "YES" : "NO", yes(flashlight, "isOverheated") ? "YES" : "NO",
	    flashlight ? ((float (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(flashlight, sel_registerName("flashlightLevel")) : -1.0f);
	if (flashlight == NULL) {
		return 1;
	}
	for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
		if (strcmp(argv[i], "wait") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			usleep((useconds_t)(atof(argv[++i]) * 1e6));
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "level") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {
			float level = (float)atof(argv[++i]);
			id error = NULL;
			BOOL done = ((BOOL (*)(id, SEL, float, id *))objc_msgSend)(flashlight, sel_registerName("setFlashlightLevel:withError:"),
			    level, &error);

			printf("torch_test: level %.2f: %s%s; available %s, level now %.2f\n", level, done ? "done" : "FAILED: ",
			    done ? "" : text(error), yes(flashlight, "isAvailable") ? "YES" : "NO",
			    ((float (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(flashlight, sel_registerName("flashlightLevel")));
			failed |= !done;
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "off") == 0) {
			/* (as Control Center does it: level 0, then the power; FigFlashlight powers off only what is dark) */
			id error = NULL;

			((BOOL (*)(id, SEL, float, id *))objc_msgSend)(flashlight, sel_registerName("setFlashlightLevel:withError:"), 0.0f,
			    &error);
			send(flashlight, "turnPowerOff");
			printf("torch_test: off; level now %.2f\n", ((float (*)(id, SEL))objc_msgSend)(flashlight,
			    sel_registerName("flashlightLevel")));
		} else if (strcmp(argv[i], "state") == 0) {
			kernel_state();
		} else {
			printf("torch_test: what is \"%s\"?\n", argv[i]);
			return 2;
		}
	}
	return failed;
}
```

`userland/src/tweaks/redbare.c`:

```c
/*
 * The same as redtest.c, but with nothing linked against it: if this one loads and redtest does not,
 * what fails is the hooking library (ElleKit is Swift and wants /usr/lib/swift from the shared cache),
 * not the loader that found and opened the tweak.
 */
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

__attribute__((constructor))
static void redbare_init(void) {
	int fd = open("/dev/console", O_WRONLY);
	const char *s = "hakios: bare tweak loaded (no libsubstrate)\n";
	if (fd >= 0) { (void)write(fd, s, strlen(s)); close(fd); }
}
```

`userland/src/tweaks/redtest.c`:

```c
/*
 * A tiny tweak, to prove the port loads tweaks: injected into a process by ElleKit's loader
 * (/var/jb/usr/lib/TweakLoader.dylib, which the kernel inserts into the processes named in
 * etc/inject.conf), it says on the console that it is there, and hooks one SpringBoard method
 * with MSHookMessageEx (from libsubstrate -> libellekit) to show that the hooking engine works.
 */
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <objc/message.h>
#include <objc/runtime.h>

extern void MSHookMessageEx(Class cls, SEL sel, IMP imp, IMP *result);

static void say(const char *s) {
	int fd = open("/dev/console", O_WRONLY);
	if (fd >= 0) { (void)write(fd, s, strlen(s)); close(fd); }
}

/* -[SpringBoard applicationDidFinishLaunching:] has already fired by the time we load, so hook
 * something that keeps being called: -[SBIconView setIcon:] runs whenever an icon is laid out. */
static void (*orig_setIcon)(id, SEL, id);
static int hit;
static void my_setIcon(id self, SEL _cmd, id icon) {
	if (!hit) { hit = 1; say("hakios: tweak hook fired: -[SBIconView setIcon:]\n"); }
	orig_setIcon(self, _cmd, icon);
}

__attribute__((constructor))
static void redtest_init(void) {
	say("hakios: test tweak loaded\n");
	Class c = objc_getClass("SBIconView");
	SEL s = sel_registerName("setIcon:");
	if (c && class_getInstanceMethod(c, s)) {
		MSHookMessageEx(c, s, (IMP)my_setIcon, (IMP *)&orig_setIcon);
		say("hakios: tweak hooked -[SBIconView setIcon:]\n");
	} else {
		say("hakios: tweak: no SBIconView setIcon:\n");
	}
}
```

`userland/src/u2f_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * u2f_test: what this GPU makes of an unsigned 32-bit integer turned into a float, through
 * OpenGL ES and nothing of ours.
 *
 * The AIR work found that the Adreno gives 4294967040 for (float)0xFFFFFFFF where C gives
 * 4294967296 -- the low eight bits dropped instead of rounded (docs/air.md). Three things could
 * do that: the a6xx instruction itself, ir3's lowering of it, or our own AIR frontend asking for
 * the wrong thing. This program takes the third out of the question by not involving it: the
 * conversion is written in GLSL ES, compiled by the same Mesa and the same ir3 that the window
 * server's drawing goes through, and run on the same GPU.
 *
 * The value is a uniform, never a constant: a constant would be folded by the compiler on this
 * side and the answer would be the host's, which is the whole thing being asked about.
 *
 * The float comes back as its four bytes through an RGBA8 framebuffer, so the bits are exact:
 * a float render target is not needed and not every driver has one.
 *
 *   u2f_test            the table below
 *   u2f_test HEX...     those values instead (e.g. u2f_test 0xffffffff 0x1000001)
 */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

/* OSMesa and GLES as far as they are used here (see gl_test.c, which does the same) */
typedef struct osmesa_context *OSMesaContext;
extern OSMesaContext OSMesaCreateContextAttribs(const int *attributes, OSMesaContext share);
extern unsigned char OSMesaMakeCurrent(OSMesaContext context, void *buffer, unsigned type, int width, int height);

extern const unsigned char *glGetString(unsigned name);
extern unsigned glGetError(void);
extern void glGenTextures(int n, unsigned *names);
extern void glBindTexture(unsigned target, unsigned texture);
extern void glTexImage2D(unsigned target, int level, int internal, int width, int height, int border, unsigned format,
    unsigned type, const void *pixels);
extern void glTexParameteri(unsigned target, unsigned name, int value);
extern void glGenFramebuffers(int n, unsigned *names);
extern void glBindFramebuffer(unsigned target, unsigned framebuffer);
extern void glFramebufferTexture2D(unsigned target, unsigned attachment, unsigned textarget, unsigned texture, int level);
extern unsigned glCheckFramebufferStatus(unsigned target);
extern void glViewport(int x, int y, int width, int height);
extern unsigned glCreateShader(unsigned type);
extern void glShaderSource(unsigned shader, int count, const char *const *strings, const int *lengths);
extern void glCompileShader(unsigned shader);
extern void glGetShaderiv(unsigned shader, unsigned name, int *value);
extern void glGetShaderInfoLog(unsigned shader, int size, int *length, char *log);
extern unsigned glCreateProgram(void);
extern void glAttachShader(unsigned program, unsigned shader);
extern void glLinkProgram(unsigned program);
extern void glGetProgramiv(unsigned program, unsigned name, int *value);
extern void glGetProgramInfoLog(unsigned program, int size, int *length, char *log);
extern void glUseProgram(unsigned program);
extern int glGetUniformLocation(unsigned program, const char *name);
extern void glUniform1ui(int location, unsigned value);
extern void glDrawArrays(unsigned mode, int first, int count);
extern void glReadPixels(int x, int y, int width, int height, unsigned format, unsigned type, void *pixels);
extern void glFinish(void);
extern void glGenVertexArrays(int n, unsigned *names);
extern void glBindVertexArray(unsigned name);

#define GL_VENDOR                       0x1F00
#define GL_RENDERER                     0x1F01
#define GL_VERSION                      0x1F02
#define GL_TEXTURE_2D                   0x0DE1
#define GL_RGBA                         0x1908
#define GL_RGBA8                        0x8058
#define GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE                0x1401
#define GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER           0x2801
#define GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER           0x2800
#define GL_NEAREST                      0x2600
#define GL_FRAMEBUFFER                  0x8D40
#define GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0            0x8CE0
#define GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE         0x8CD5
#define GL_VERTEX_SHADER                0x8B31
#define GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER              0x8B30
#define GL_COMPILE_STATUS               0x8B81
#define GL_LINK_STATUS                  0x8B82
#define GL_TRIANGLES                    0x0004

#define OSMESA_RGBA                     0x1908
#define OSMESA_FORMAT                   0x22
#define OSMESA_PROFILE                  0x33
#define OSMESA_CONTEXT_MAJOR_VERSION    0x36
#define OSMESA_CONTEXT_MINOR_VERSION    0x37
#define OSMESA_ES_PROFILE               0x38

/*
 * The whole of the question. gl_VertexID makes the triangle, so there are no attributes and no
 * buffers; the conversion is of a uniform, and its result leaves as four bytes.
 */
static const char *const vertex_text =
    "#version 300 es\n"
    "void main() {\n"
    "	vec2 at = vec2((gl_VertexID << 1) & 2, gl_VertexID & 2);\n"
    "	gl_Position = vec4(at * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);\n"
    "}\n";

static const char *const fragment_text =
    "#version 300 es\n"
    "precision highp float;\n"
    "precision highp int;\n"
    "uniform uint value;\n"
    "out vec4 colour;\n"
    "void main() {\n"
    "	uint bits = floatBitsToUint(float(value));\n"
    "	colour = vec4(float((bits >> 24) & 255u), float((bits >> 16) & 255u),\n"
    "	              float((bits >> 8) & 255u), float(bits & 255u)) / 255.0;\n"
    "}\n";

static unsigned
shader(unsigned type, const char *text)
{
	unsigned name = glCreateShader(type);
	char log[1024] = { 0 };
	int good = 0;

	glShaderSource(name, 1, &text, NULL);
	glCompileShader(name);
	glGetShaderiv(name, GL_COMPILE_STATUS, &good);
	if (!good) {
		glGetShaderInfoLog(name, (int)sizeof(log) - 1, NULL, log);
		printf("u2f_test: a shader does not compile: %s\n", log);
	}
	return name;
}

/* the float a C compiler on this machine makes of the same value */
static uint32_t
reference(uint32_t value)
{
	float f = (float)value;
	uint32_t bits;

	memcpy(&bits, &f, sizeof(bits));
	return bits;
}

static float
as_float(uint32_t bits)
{
	float f;

	memcpy(&f, &bits, sizeof(f));
	return f;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	static const int attributes[] = { OSMESA_FORMAT, OSMESA_RGBA, OSMESA_PROFILE, OSMESA_ES_PROFILE,
		                          OSMESA_CONTEXT_MAJOR_VERSION, 3, OSMESA_CONTEXT_MINOR_VERSION, 0, 0 };
	/*
	 * Values where the answer tells the three apart. Rounding only decides where the integer is
	 * not representable: above 2^24 the gaps open, and these sit in them.
	 *   0xffffffff  255 away from one neighbour and 1 from the other: nearest says the far one
	 *   0xffffff80  exactly halfway: nearest-even says 2^32, whose significand is even
	 *   0x01000001  halfway in the first gap of all (2^24 + 1): nearest-even says 2^24
	 *   0x01000003  halfway in the same gap the other way: nearest-even says 2^24 + 4
	 *   0x7fffffff  the signed maximum, 1 away from 2^31
	 *   0x00ffffff  the last integer that is exact: every rule must agree here
	 */
	static const uint32_t table[] = { 0xffffffffu, 0xffffff80u, 0x01000001u, 0x01000003u, 0x7fffffffu, 0x00ffffffu };
	static unsigned char window[16 * 16 * 4];
	const uint32_t *values = table;
	unsigned count = sizeof(table) / sizeof(table[0]);
	uint32_t given[16];
	unsigned texture = 0, framebuffer = 0, program, array = 0;
	int location, good = 0, differ = 0;
	OSMesaContext context;

	/*
	 * Unbuffered: this program is killed where it stands when the session's time is up, and
	 * a buffered line is a line that was never said. The first run of it said nothing at all
	 * -- not even the driver's name, which is printed before any work -- and the reason was
	 * here, not on the GPU.
	 */
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);

	if (argc > 1) {
		count = (unsigned)(argc - 1) > sizeof(given) / sizeof(given[0]) ? sizeof(given) / sizeof(given[0])
		                                                                : (unsigned)(argc - 1);
		for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
			given[i] = (uint32_t)strtoul(argv[1 + i], NULL, 0);
		}
		values = given;
	}

	context = OSMesaCreateContextAttribs(attributes, NULL);
	if (context == NULL || !OSMesaMakeCurrent(context, window, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, 16, 16)) {
		printf("u2f_test: no OpenGL ES 3.0 context\n");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("u2f_test: context made; %s; %s; %s\n", (const char *)glGetString(GL_VENDOR), (const char *)glGetString(GL_RENDERER),
	    (const char *)glGetString(GL_VERSION));

	glGenVertexArrays(1, &array);
	glBindVertexArray(array);
	glGenTextures(1, &texture);
	glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, texture);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
	glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, 1, 1, 0, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, NULL);
	glGenFramebuffers(1, &framebuffer);
	glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, framebuffer);
	glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0, GL_TEXTURE_2D, texture, 0);
	if (glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER) != GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE) {
		printf("u2f_test: the framebuffer is not complete\n");
		return 1;
	}
	glViewport(0, 0, 1, 1);

	program = glCreateProgram();
	glAttachShader(program, shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, vertex_text));
	glAttachShader(program, shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, fragment_text));
	glLinkProgram(program);
	glGetProgramiv(program, GL_LINK_STATUS, &good);
	if (!good) {
		char log[1024] = { 0 };

		glGetProgramInfoLog(program, (int)sizeof(log) - 1, NULL, log);
		printf("u2f_test: the program does not link: %s\n", log);
		return 1;
	}
	glUseProgram(program);
	location = glGetUniformLocation(program, "value");
	if (location < 0) {
		printf("u2f_test: the uniform is gone: the compiler folded what it was asked not to\n");
		return 1;
	}

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		unsigned char pixel[4] = { 0, 0, 0, 0 };
		uint32_t bits, want = reference(values[i]);

		glUniform1ui(location, values[i]);
		glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES, 0, 3);
		glFinish();
		glReadPixels(0, 0, 1, 1, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, pixel);
		bits = (uint32_t)pixel[0] << 24 | (uint32_t)pixel[1] << 16 | (uint32_t)pixel[2] << 8 | pixel[3];
		printf("u2f_test: 0x%08x -> %#010x %-16.9g  C says %#010x %-16.9g  %s\n", values[i], bits, (double)as_float(bits),
		    want, (double)as_float(want), bits == want ? "same" : "DIFFERENT");
		differ += bits != want;
	}
	printf("u2f_test: %u value(s), %d different; error %#x\n", count, differ, glGetError());
	return differ != 0;
}
```
