`userland/src/var_store.c`:

```c
/*
 * The data volume of Darwin between two boots: /private/var packed into the phone's flash and
 * unpacked out of it again.
 *
 * /private/var is a memory filesystem (bsd/miscfs/ramfs), mounted empty by init at every boot and
 * given the directories of the template Darwin ships with (sysimage/mkvarskel.py), so nothing Darwin keeps
 * there outlives the boot that wrote it: no home screen layout, no application data, no baked
 * wallpaper. The kernel's APFS driver reads and does not write, and writing APFS is not the point
 * here -- what is needed is that the bytes come back. So the tree is packed into a plain archive
 * and the archive is written into the one place on the phone's flash this port owns and nothing of
 * it uses: the partition darwin, past the Darwin volume and both cryptexes. The kernel takes those
 * writes on /dev/rufs_darwin alone and refuses anything else (drivers/storage/hakios.ufs.c, ufs_write=1).
 *
 *   var_store save          pack /private/var into the store
 *   var_store load          unpack the newest good store into /private/var (init, at boot)
 *   var_store watch [SECS]  stay and save by itself: when the kernel says the run is ending, and
 *                           every SECS seconds besides (a launchd job of ours does this)
 *   var_store show          what the store holds, both slots
 *   var_store erase         forget both slots (the next boot starts empty again)
 *   var_store stamp PATH    write a line into PATH saying when: a marker for a run
 *
 * Nobody has to remember to save. `watch` registers with the kernel (kern.hakios.var_save), and
 * on the orderly way back to the loader -- the run's time up, or "xl stop" -- the kernel asks it
 * for the volume and waits, bounded, before it goes (drivers/storage/hakios.ufs.c,
 * hakios_var_save_on_return). A save every SECS seconds is there as well but is not the default:
 * one costs seconds of the run and a hundred-odd megabytes of flash, and while it runs the
 * storage is read through the loader rather than through this kernel's own driver.
 *
 * One saver at a time: a write to the store is refused unless the writer holds the claim
 * (kern.hakios.var_busy), so two of them cannot interleave into one slot. Even if they did, the
 * slot being written is never the one holding the newest good archive, and a header is written
 * last and over a zeroed one -- so the worst an interrupted or doubled save can do is lose itself.
 *
 * Two slots, written in turn: the one not holding the newest good archive is the one written, its
 * header first zeroed, the archive next, the header last. So a save that does not finish -- the
 * phone reset in the middle of it -- loses nothing: the other slot still holds the archive from
 * before, and `load` takes the newest slot whose header and contents both check out.
 *
 * `load` reads the archive twice: once to see that its checksum is the one in the header, and only
 * then to make files. A store that was torn or is half a different archive therefore leaves
 * /private/var as init made it rather than half filled.
 *
 * What is left out: sockets and devices, which the daemons of a new boot make for themselves, and
 * the directories in SKIP below, which hold what only this boot can mean (its runtime sockets, its
 * swap, its logs) or what is grafted from a read-only image at every boot anyway.
 */
#include "mini.h"

#define BLOCK           4096
#define BUFFER          (4u << 20)              /* the loader's own buffer: one request a write */
#define STORE_AT        8589934592LL            /* darwin's block 2097152: past the cryptexes, with room to spare */
#define SLOT_BYTES      0x80000000LL            /* 2 GiB a slot, two slots */
#define SLOTS           2
#define DEVICE          "/dev/rufs_darwin"
#define ROOT            "/private/var"
#define MAX_PATH        1024
#define MAX_DEPTH       32
#define MAX_XATTR       (256u << 10)            /* one attribute's value; Darwin keeps small ones */
#define XPACK           (512u << 10)            /* all the attributes of one file, packed */
#define LINKS           8192                    /* names remembered for hard links */
#define LINK_PATH       256
/*
 * The file flags put back: the ones a tree of files can mean. UF_COMPRESSED is not among them
 * (a ramfs file is not a compressed HFS one, and the flag would make it read as empty), nor are
 * the flags only a single-user boot can clear.
 */
#define FLAGS_KEPT      (0x1u | 0x2u | 0x4u | 0x8u | 0x8000u)   /* nodump, immutable, append, opaque, hidden */

/* the directories whose contents are not kept (the directory itself is) */
static const char *const SKIP[] = {
	"tmp",                  /* its name says it */
	"run",                  /* runtime sockets and pid files: this boot's, not the last one's */
	"vm",                   /* the compressor's swap */
	"log", "logs",          /* what the last boot said */
	"db/diagnostics", "db/uuidtext",        /* logd's archive: tens of MB a boot, and remade */
	"jb",                   /* the package prefix, grafted from the read-only image at every boot */
	NULL,
};

enum { ENT_DIR = 1, ENT_FILE = 2, ENT_SYMLINK = 3, ENT_HARDLINK = 4, ENT_DIRTIME = 5 };

#define HEAD_MAGIC      "RDWVAR\0"
#define HEAD_VERSION    1

struct head {
	char     magic[8];
	uint32_t version;
	uint32_t slot;
	uint64_t generation;            /* the newest good slot is the one with the highest */
	uint64_t bytes;                 /* the archive, without the padding to a whole block */
	uint64_t entries;
	uint64_t seconds;               /* when it was written */
	uint32_t crc;                   /* of those bytes */
	uint32_t head_crc;              /* of this structure with head_crc zero */
};

struct entry {
	uint32_t kind;
	uint32_t mode;                  /* permission bits */
	uint32_t uid, gid;
	uint32_t flags;                 /* st_flags */
	uint32_t pathlen;
	uint32_t nxattr;
	uint32_t mtime_nsec;
	int64_t  mtime_sec;
	uint64_t size;                  /* a file's contents, a link's target, a hard link's first name */
};

/* ---- the kernel's side of it: the boot-arg, the handshake, the claim ---- */

#define VAR_SAVE_NONE   0
#define VAR_SAVE_IDLE   1
#define VAR_SAVE_WANTED 2
#define VAR_SAVE_DONE   3

/* Is NAME=VALUE among the kernel's arguments? (as init.c reads them) */
static int
boot_arg_is(const char *name, const char *value)
{
	static char args[1024];
	size_t len = sizeof(args) - 1, n = strlen(name), v = strlen(value);

	if (sysctlbyname("kern.bootargs", args, &len, NULL, 0) != 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	args[len < sizeof(args) ? len : sizeof(args) - 1] = 0;
	for (char *p = args; *p;) {
		while (*p == ' ') {
			p++;
		}
		if (strncmp(p, name, n) == 0 && p[n] == '=' && strncmp(p + n + 1, value, v) == 0 &&
		    (p[n + 1 + v] == 0 || p[n + 1 + v] == ' ')) {
			return 1;
		}
		while (*p && *p != ' ') {
			p++;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

static long
parse_number(const char *text)
{
	long value = 0;

	for (; *text >= '0' && *text <= '9'; text++) {
		value = value * 10 + (*text - '0');
	}
	return value;
}

static int
sysctl_int(const char *name, int *value)
{
	size_t len = sizeof(*value);

	return sysctlbyname(name, value, &len, NULL, 0);
}

static int
sysctl_set_int(const char *name, int value)
{
	return sysctlbyname(name, NULL, NULL, &value, sizeof(value));
}

/* The claim on the store: nothing may be written without it, and only one program may hold it. */
static int
claim(void)
{
	if (sysctl_set_int("kern.hakios.var_busy", 1) != 0) {
		printf("var_store: the store is claimed by another saver (%s)\n", strerror(errno));
		return 0;
	}
	return 1;
}

static void
release(void)
{
	(void)sysctl_set_int("kern.hakios.var_busy", 0);
}

/* ---- checksum (the same one the loader reads a write back with) ---- */

static uint32_t crc_table[256];

static void
crc_init(void)
{
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 256; i++) {
		uint32_t c = i;

		for (int k = 0; k < 8; k++) {
			c = (c >> 1) ^ (0xedb88320u & (0u - (c & 1)));
		}
		crc_table[i] = c;
	}
}

static uint32_t
crc_add(uint32_t c, const void *p, uint64_t n)
{
	const uint8_t *b = p;

	for (uint64_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		c = crc_table[(c ^ b[i]) & 0xff] ^ (c >> 8);
	}
	return c;
}

static uint32_t
head_checksum(const struct head *h)
{
	struct head copy = *h;

	copy.head_crc = 0;
	return crc_add(0xffffffffu, &copy, sizeof(copy)) ^ 0xffffffffu;
}

/* ---- the store, as a stream of bytes in one slot ---- */

static int fd = -1;
static uint8_t *buffer;
static uint8_t *already;                /* what the slot holds there now, to not write it again */
static uint64_t skipped_blocks, written_blocks;
static uint64_t buffered;               /* bytes in the buffer: to be written, or still to be read */
static uint64_t taken;                  /* of those, already read out (load) */
static off_t at;                        /* where in the device the buffer begins */
static uint64_t stream_bytes;           /* the archive's own bytes so far */
static uint64_t stream_left;            /* bytes of the archive still to come (load) */
static off_t stream_limit;              /* the end of the slot: nothing is read or written past it */
static uint32_t stream_crc;
static uint64_t entries;

static off_t
slot_at(int slot)
{
	return STORE_AT + (off_t)slot * SLOT_BYTES;
}

static int
device_write(off_t where, const void *data, uint64_t n)
{
	const uint8_t *p = data;

	while (n > 0) {
		ssize_t wrote = pwrite(fd, p, (size_t)n, where);

		if (wrote <= 0) {
			printf("var_store: writing %llu bytes at %lld: %s\n", (unsigned long long)n,
			    (long long)where, strerror(errno));
			return 0;
		}
		p += wrote;
		where += wrote;
		n -= (uint64_t)wrote;
	}
	return 1;
}

static int
device_read(off_t where, void *data, uint64_t n)
{
	uint8_t *p = data;

	while (n > 0) {
		ssize_t got = pread(fd, p, (size_t)n, where);

		if (got <= 0) {
			printf("var_store: reading %llu bytes at %lld: %s\n", (unsigned long long)n,
			    (long long)where, strerror(errno));
			return 0;
		}
		p += got;
		where += got;
		n -= (uint64_t)got;
	}
	return 1;
}

/* ---- writing the archive out ---- */

static int
out_flush(int last)
{
	uint64_t n = buffered;

	if (n == 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	if (last) {
		/* whole blocks only: the tail is padded, and the header says where the archive ends */
		while (n % BLOCK != 0) {
			buffer[n++] = 0;
		}
	}
	if (at + (off_t)n > stream_limit) {
		printf("var_store: the archive does not fit in its slot: nothing more is written\n");
		return 0;
	}
	/*
	 * What is already there is read first, and if it is what we were about to write, it is not
	 * written. A volume that Darwin has stopped touching packs to the very same bytes -- measured:
	 * two saves a minute apart came out with the same checksum -- and the slots hold alternate
	 * copies of it, so a save that changes nothing then costs reads and no writes at all. Reads
	 * of this storage are several times cheaper than writes, and flash wears by writing.
	 */
	if (already != NULL && device_read(at, already, n) && memcmp(already, buffer, (size_t)n) == 0) {
		skipped_blocks += n / BLOCK;
	} else if (!device_write(at, buffer, n)) {
		return 0;
	} else {
		written_blocks += n / BLOCK;
	}
	at += (off_t)n;
	buffered = 0;
	return 1;
}

static int
out(const void *data, uint64_t n)
{
	const uint8_t *p = data;

	stream_crc = crc_add(stream_crc, data, n);
	stream_bytes += n;
	while (n > 0) {
		uint64_t room = BUFFER - buffered;

		if (room == 0) {
			if (!out_flush(0)) {
				return 0;
			}
			continue;
		}
		if (room > n) {
			room = n;
		}
		memcpy(buffer + buffered, p, (size_t)room);
		buffered += room;
		p += room;
		n -= room;
	}
	return 1;
}

static int
out_pad(void)
{
	static const uint8_t zero[8] = { 0 };
	uint64_t over = stream_bytes % 8;

	return over == 0 ? 1 : out(zero, 8 - over);
}

/* ---- reading the archive in ---- */

static int
in(void *data, uint64_t n)
{
	uint8_t *p = data;

	if (n > stream_left) {
		printf("var_store: the archive ends in the middle of an entry\n");
		return 0;
	}
	stream_left -= n;
	stream_bytes += n;
	while (n > 0) {
		uint64_t have = buffered - taken;

		if (have == 0) {
			uint64_t want = BUFFER;

			if (at + (off_t)want > stream_limit) {
				want = (uint64_t)(stream_limit - at);
			}
			if (want == 0 || !device_read(at, buffer, want)) {
				return 0;
			}
			at += (off_t)want;
			buffered = want;
			taken = 0;
			continue;
		}
		if (have > n) {
			have = n;
		}
		if (p != NULL) {
			memcpy(p, buffer + taken, (size_t)have);
			p += have;
		}
		stream_crc = crc_add(stream_crc, buffer + taken, have);
		taken += have;
		n -= have;
	}
	return 1;
}

/* n bytes of the archive passed over, their checksum counted in */
static int
in_skip(uint64_t n)
{
	uint8_t waste[512];

	while (n > 0) {
		uint64_t piece = n > sizeof(waste) ? sizeof(waste) : n;

		if (!in(waste, piece)) {
			return 0;
		}
		n -= piece;
	}
	return 1;
}

static int
in_pad(void)
{
	uint64_t over = stream_bytes % 8;

	return over == 0 ? 1 : in_skip(8 - over);
}

static void
stream_start(int slot, uint64_t bytes)
{
	at = slot_at(slot) + BLOCK;
	stream_limit = slot_at(slot) + SLOT_BYTES;
	buffered = taken = 0;
	stream_bytes = 0;
	stream_left = bytes;
	stream_crc = 0xffffffffu;
}

/* ---- the slots ---- */

/* The slot's header, if it is one of ours and says of itself what it should. */
static int
read_head(int slot, struct head *into)
{
	static uint8_t block[BLOCK];
	struct head *h = (struct head *)block;

	if (!device_read(slot_at(slot), block, BLOCK)) {
		return 0;
	}
	if (memcmp(h->magic, HEAD_MAGIC, sizeof(h->magic)) != 0 || h->version != HEAD_VERSION ||
	    h->slot != (uint32_t)slot || h->bytes > (uint64_t)SLOT_BYTES - BLOCK ||
	    h->head_crc != head_checksum(h)) {
		return 0;
	}
	*into = *h;
	return 1;
}

/* The newest slot whose header checks out, or -1. */
static int
newest(struct head *out_head)
{
	int best = -1;

	for (int slot = 0; slot < SLOTS; slot++) {
		struct head h;

		if (!read_head(slot, &h)) {
			continue;
		}
		if (best < 0 || h.generation > out_head->generation) {
			best = slot;
			*out_head = h;
		}
	}
	return best;
}

/* ---- packing ---- */

/*
 * How much of this save is new since the last one: an entry whose time of writing is later than
 * the second the previous generation was saved at. It costs nothing to count -- the walk has every
 * entry's time in hand anyway -- and it is what says whether saving only the difference would be
 * worth building, or whether Darwin rewrites the volume faster than any such thing could help.
 */
static uint64_t last_saved_at, changed_entries, changed_bytes;

static char path[MAX_PATH];               /* the whole path, under ROOT */
static struct { uint64_t ino; char path[LINK_PATH]; } *links;
static uint64_t skipped_kinds, skipped_big;

static int
is_skipped(const char *relative)
{
	for (int i = 0; SKIP[i] != NULL; i++) {
		if (strcmp(relative, SKIP[i]) == 0) {
			return 1;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

/* The name this inode was first met under, if it has one; otherwise this one is remembered. */
static const char *
link_name(uint64_t ino, const char *relative)
{
	uint64_t slot = (ino * 2654435761u) % LINKS;

	for (uint64_t tries = 0; tries < LINKS; tries++, slot = (slot + 1) % LINKS) {
		if (links[slot].ino == ino) {
			return links[slot].path;
		}
		if (links[slot].ino == 0) {
			if (strlen(relative) < LINK_PATH) {
				links[slot].ino = ino;
				strcpy(links[slot].path, relative);
			}
			return NULL;
		}
	}
	return NULL;                    /* the table is full: this one is written out whole */
}

/*
 * The extended attributes of path -- Darwin keeps container metadata and much else in them -- packed
 * into a buffer of their own, because the entry's head says how many there are and has to go out
 * before them. One that does not fit is left out and counted.
 */
static uint8_t xpack[XPACK];

static uint64_t
pack_xattrs(uint32_t *count)
{
	static char names[16384];
	static uint8_t value[MAX_XATTR];
	ssize_t n = listxattr(path, names, sizeof(names), XATTR_NOFOLLOW);
	uint64_t used = 0;

	*count = 0;
	if (n <= 0) {
		return 0;
	}
	for (ssize_t i = 0; i < n && i < (ssize_t)sizeof(names); i += (ssize_t)strlen(names + i) + 1) {
		uint32_t namelen = (uint32_t)strlen(names + i), vlen;
		ssize_t size = getxattr(path, names + i, value, sizeof(value), 0, XATTR_NOFOLLOW);

		if (size < 0) {
			continue;
		}
		vlen = (uint32_t)size;
		if (used + 8 + namelen + vlen > XPACK) {
			skipped_big++;
			continue;
		}
		memcpy(xpack + used, &namelen, sizeof(namelen));
		memcpy(xpack + used + 4, &vlen, sizeof(vlen));
		memcpy(xpack + used + 8, names + i, namelen);
		memcpy(xpack + used + 8 + namelen, value, vlen);
		used += 8 + namelen + vlen;
		(*count)++;
	}
	return used;
}

/* One entry: its head, its name, its extended attributes, its contents. */
static int
pack_one(const char *relative, const struct stat *st)
{
	struct entry e;
	static char target[MAX_PATH];
	const char *first;
	uint32_t kind = 0;
	uint64_t size = 0;
	const void *tail = NULL;
	int in_fd = -1;

	switch (st->st_mode & S_IFMT) {
	case S_IFDIR:
		kind = ENT_DIR;
		break;
	case S_IFLNK: {
		ssize_t n = readlink(path, target, sizeof(target));

		if (n <= 0) {
			return 1;
		}
		kind = ENT_SYMLINK;
		size = (uint64_t)n;
		tail = target;
		break;
	}
	case S_IFREG:
		kind = ENT_FILE;
		size = (uint64_t)st->st_size;
		if (st->st_nlink > 1) {
			first = link_name(st->st_ino, relative);
			if (first != NULL) {
				kind = ENT_HARDLINK;
				size = strlen(first);
				tail = first;
				break;
			}
		}
		in_fd = open(path, O_RDONLY, 0);
		if (in_fd < 0) {
			return 1;       /* gone, or not ours to read: it is not in the archive */
		}
		break;
	default:
		skipped_kinds++;        /* a socket, a fifo, a device: a new boot makes its own */
		return 1;
	}

	memset(&e, 0, sizeof(e));
	e.kind = kind;
	e.mode = st->st_mode & 07777;
	e.uid = st->st_uid;
	e.gid = st->st_gid;
	e.flags = st->st_flags & FLAGS_KEPT;
	e.pathlen = (uint32_t)strlen(relative);
	e.mtime_sec = st->st_mtimespec.tv_sec;
	e.mtime_nsec = (uint32_t)st->st_mtimespec.tv_nsec;
	e.size = size;
	if (last_saved_at != 0 && (uint64_t)st->st_mtimespec.tv_sec > last_saved_at) {
		changed_entries++;
		changed_bytes += size;
	}
	{
		uint64_t xlen = pack_xattrs(&e.nxattr);

		if (!out(&e, sizeof(e)) || !out(relative, e.pathlen) || !out(xpack, xlen)) {
			if (in_fd >= 0) {
				close(in_fd);
			}
			return 0;
		}
	}
	if (tail != NULL && !out(tail, size)) {
		if (in_fd >= 0) {
			close(in_fd);
		}
		return 0;
	}
	if (in_fd >= 0) {
		static uint8_t piece[256 * 1024];
		uint64_t left = size;

		while (left > 0) {
			uint64_t want = left > sizeof(piece) ? sizeof(piece) : left;
			ssize_t got = read(in_fd, piece, (size_t)want);

			if (got <= 0) {
				/* the file shrank under us: the rest is zeros, so the archive stays whole */
				memset(piece, 0, (size_t)want);
				got = (ssize_t)want;
			}
			if (!out(piece, (uint64_t)got)) {
				close(in_fd);
				return 0;
			}
			left -= (uint64_t)got;
		}
		close(in_fd);
	}
	if (!out_pad()) {
		return 0;
	}
	entries++;
	return 1;
}

/* The directory's own times once more, after its contents: making them moved them. */
static int
pack_dirtime(const char *relative, const struct stat *st)
{
	struct entry e;

	memset(&e, 0, sizeof(e));
	e.kind = ENT_DIRTIME;
	e.flags = st->st_flags & FLAGS_KEPT;
	e.pathlen = (uint32_t)strlen(relative);
	e.mtime_sec = st->st_mtimespec.tv_sec;
	e.mtime_nsec = (uint32_t)st->st_mtimespec.tv_nsec;
	if (!out(&e, sizeof(e)) || !out(relative, e.pathlen) || !out_pad()) {
		return 0;
	}
	entries++;
	return 1;
}

/*
 * The names of one directory, gathered and sorted. The archive is meant to come out the same
 * bytes for the same tree: the order getdirentries gives shifts as a directory is written to, and
 * then every byte after it in the archive moves, which is the difference between a save that
 * writes nothing into the flash and one that writes all of itself. Both arenas are used as stacks
 * -- a level marks them on the way in and gives them back on the way out.
 */
#define NAME_ARENA      (2u << 20)
#define NAME_MAX_NAMES  65536

static char name_arena[NAME_ARENA];
static uint32_t name_at[NAME_MAX_NAMES];
static uint64_t arena_used, names_used, unsorted_dirs;

static void
sort_names(uint32_t *at, uint64_t n)
{
	/* insertion sort: a directory holds tens of names, and this keeps the program small */
	for (uint64_t i = 1; i < n; i++) {
		uint32_t v = at[i];
		uint64_t j = i;

		while (j > 0 && strcmp(name_arena + at[j - 1], name_arena + v) > 0) {
			at[j] = at[j - 1];
			j--;
		}
		at[j] = v;
	}
}

/* Every name in the open directory into the arena, sorted. Returns the count, or -1 if it did not fit. */
static long
gather_names(int dir_fd, char *buf, size_t bufsize, uint64_t mark_a, uint64_t mark_n)
{
	off_t position = 0;
	ssize_t n;

	while ((n = getdirentries(dir_fd, buf, bufsize, &position)) > 0) {
		for (ssize_t i = 0; i < n;) {
			struct dirent *d = (struct dirent *)(buf + i);
			const char *name = d->d_name;
			size_t len = strlen(name);

			i += d->d_reclen;
			if (strcmp(name, ".") == 0 || strcmp(name, "..") == 0) {
				continue;
			}
			if (arena_used + len + 1 > NAME_ARENA || names_used >= NAME_MAX_NAMES) {
				arena_used = mark_a;
				names_used = mark_n;
				return -1;
			}
			name_at[names_used++] = (uint32_t)arena_used;
			strcpy(name_arena + arena_used, name);
			arena_used += len + 1;
		}
	}
	sort_names(name_at + mark_n, names_used - mark_n);
	return (long)(names_used - mark_n);
}

/* relative: the path under ROOT, "" for ROOT itself. path holds the whole of it. */
static int
pack_tree(const char *relative)
{
	static char dirbuf[MAX_DEPTH][4096];    /* one read buffer a level */
	static int depth;
	struct stat st;
	size_t base = strlen(path), rbase = strlen(relative);
	int dir_fd, ok = 1;

	if (lstat(path, &st) != 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	if (relative[0] != 0 && !pack_one(relative, &st)) {
		return 0;
	}
	if ((st.st_mode & S_IFMT) != S_IFDIR || (relative[0] != 0 && is_skipped(relative))) {
		return 1;
	}
	if (depth >= MAX_DEPTH) {
		printf("var_store: %s: deeper than this program walks\n", path);
		return 1;
	}
	if ((dir_fd = open(path, O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY, 0)) < 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	depth++;
	{
		uint64_t mark_a = arena_used, mark_n = names_used;
		long count = gather_names(dir_fd, dirbuf[depth - 1], sizeof(dirbuf[0]), mark_a, mark_n);

		if (count < 0) {
			/* more names than the arena holds: this one goes in whatever order it is given */
			unsorted_dirs++;
		}
		for (long k = 0; ok && k < count; k++) {
			const char *name = name_arena + name_at[mark_n + k];
			char child[MAX_PATH];           /* the caller's while this one recurses: not static */

			if (base + 1 + strlen(name) >= MAX_PATH || rbase + 1 + strlen(name) >= MAX_PATH) {
				printf("var_store: %s/%s: the path is too long\n", path, name);
				continue;
			}
			path[base] = '/';
			strcpy(path + base + 1, name);
			if (rbase > 0) {
				memcpy(child, relative, rbase);
				child[rbase] = '/';
				strcpy(child + rbase + 1, name);
			} else {
				strcpy(child, name);
			}
			ok = pack_tree(child);
			path[base] = 0;
		}
		arena_used = mark_a;
		names_used = mark_n;
	}
	depth--;
	close(dir_fd);
	if (ok && relative[0] != 0 && lstat(path, &st) == 0) {
		ok = pack_dirtime(relative, &st);
	}
	return ok;
}

static int
save(void)
{
	struct head old, h;
	int slot, best;
	static uint8_t block[BLOCK];

	memset(&old, 0, sizeof(old));
	best = newest(&old);
	slot = best < 0 ? 0 : (best + 1) % SLOTS;
	printf("var_store: saving into slot %d (slot %d holds generation %llu)\n", slot, best,
	    best < 0 ? 0ULL : (unsigned long long)old.generation);

	/* the slot's header first, so that a save cut short cannot leave an old header over a new archive */
	memset(block, 0, sizeof(block));
	if (!device_write(slot_at(slot), block, BLOCK)) {
		return 0;
	}
	stream_start(slot, 0);
	entries = 0;
	last_saved_at = best < 0 ? 0 : old.seconds;
	changed_entries = changed_bytes = 0;
	skipped_blocks = written_blocks = 0;
	arena_used = names_used = unsorted_dirs = 0;
	/* a watcher saves more than once: nothing of the save before is carried into this one */
	memset(links, 0, LINKS * sizeof(*links));
	skipped_kinds = skipped_big = 0;
	strcpy(path, ROOT);
	if (!pack_tree("") || !out_flush(1)) {
		return 0;
	}
	memset(&h, 0, sizeof(h));
	memcpy(h.magic, HEAD_MAGIC, sizeof(h.magic));
	h.version = HEAD_VERSION;
	h.slot = (uint32_t)slot;
	h.generation = (best < 0 ? 0 : old.generation) + 1;
	h.bytes = stream_bytes;
	h.entries = entries;
	{
		struct timeval tv = { 0, 0 };

		gettimeofday(&tv, NULL);
		h.seconds = (uint64_t)tv.tv_sec;
	}
	h.crc = stream_crc ^ 0xffffffffu;
	h.head_crc = head_checksum(&h);
	if (h.bytes > (uint64_t)SLOT_BYTES - BLOCK) {
		printf("var_store: the archive is %llu bytes, more than a slot holds (%llu): nothing saved\n",
		    (unsigned long long)h.bytes, (unsigned long long)(SLOT_BYTES - BLOCK));
		return 0;
	}
	memset(block, 0, sizeof(block));
	memcpy(block, &h, sizeof(h));
	if (!device_write(slot_at(slot), block, BLOCK)) {
		return 0;
	}
	printf("var_store: slot %d: generation %llu, %llu entries, %llu bytes, crc %08x%s%s\n", slot,
	    (unsigned long long)h.generation, (unsigned long long)h.entries, (unsigned long long)h.bytes,
	    h.crc, skipped_kinds ? " (sockets and the like left out)" : "",
	    skipped_big ? " (something too big left out)" : "");
	if (last_saved_at != 0) {
		printf("var_store: %llu entries and %llu bytes of it were written since the last save "
		    "(%llu seconds ago)\n", (unsigned long long)changed_entries,
		    (unsigned long long)changed_bytes, (unsigned long long)(h.seconds - last_saved_at));
	}
	printf("var_store: %llu blocks into the flash, %llu left alone (they held this already)%s\n",
	    (unsigned long long)written_blocks, (unsigned long long)skipped_blocks,
	    unsorted_dirs ? " (a directory was too big to put in order)" : "");
	return 1;
}

/* ---- unpacking ---- */

static uint64_t made_dirs, made_files, made_links, made_bytes, short_files, lost_bytes;
/*
 * A belt, after the braces: the memory filesystem no longer answers ENOSPC for want of a page
 * (bsd/miscfs/ramfs, ramfs_grow_slots now takes an array found without the mount lock), so a short
 * write here means the volume really is full. Waiting a little and trying again still earns its
 * place -- the pageout path cannot wait for an array either, and it may be what answered -- but
 * the whole restore spends at most RETRY_MS on it, so a volume that is truly full does not turn
 * the boot into a crawl.
 */
#define RETRY_MS        2000
static uint64_t retry_ms_left = RETRY_MS;

static int
whole_path(const char *relative, uint32_t len)
{
	if (len == 0 || len >= MAX_PATH - sizeof(ROOT) - 1 || relative[0] == '/') {
		return 0;
	}
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i + 1 < len; i++) {
		if (relative[i] == '.' && relative[i + 1] == '.' &&
		    (i == 0 || relative[i - 1] == '/') && (i + 2 == len || relative[i + 2] == '/')) {
			return 0;       /* nothing of this archive is unpacked outside ROOT */
		}
	}
	strcpy(path, ROOT);
	path[sizeof(ROOT) - 1] = '/';
	memcpy(path + sizeof(ROOT), relative, len);
	path[sizeof(ROOT) + len] = 0;
	return 1;
}

static void
set_times(const struct entry *e)
{
	struct timeval times[2];

	times[0].tv_sec = (long)e->mtime_sec;
	times[0].tv_usec = (int)(e->mtime_nsec / 1000);
	times[1] = times[0];
	utimes(path, times);
}

/*
 * One entry out of the archive and into /private/var. make: with 0, the entry is only read past
 * (the first pass, which proves the archive's checksum before anything is made).
 */
static int
unpack_one(int make)
{
	struct entry e;
	static char relative[MAX_PATH];
	static uint8_t value[MAX_XATTR];
	static char name[1024];
	int out_fd = -1, ok = 1;

	if (!in(&e, sizeof(e))) {
		return 0;
	}
	if (e.pathlen >= MAX_PATH || e.nxattr > 4096) {
		printf("var_store: an entry this program cannot read (kind %u, path %u bytes)\n", e.kind,
		    e.pathlen);
		return 0;
	}
	if (!in(relative, e.pathlen)) {
		return 0;
	}
	relative[e.pathlen] = 0;
	if (make && !whole_path(relative, e.pathlen)) {
		make = 0;               /* read past it: an archive is not to make names of its own choosing */
	}
	if (make) {
		switch (e.kind) {
		case ENT_DIR:
			if (mkdir(path, (int)e.mode) == 0) {
				made_dirs++;
			}
			break;
		case ENT_FILE:
			out_fd = open(path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, (int)e.mode);
			if (out_fd < 0) {
				printf("var_store: %s cannot be made: %s\n", path, strerror(errno));
			} else {
				made_files++;
			}
			break;
		default:
			break;
		}
	}
	/* the attributes, before the contents, as they were packed */
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < e.nxattr; i++) {
		uint32_t namelen, vlen;

		if (!in(&namelen, sizeof(namelen)) || !in(&vlen, sizeof(vlen))) {
			ok = 0;
			break;
		}
		if (namelen >= sizeof(name) || vlen > sizeof(value)) {
			ok = in_skip(namelen) && in_skip(vlen);
			skipped_big++;
			continue;
		}
		if (!in(name, namelen) || !in(value, vlen)) {
			ok = 0;
			break;
		}
		name[namelen] = 0;
		if (make && e.kind != ENT_HARDLINK) {
			setxattr(path, name, value, vlen, 0, XATTR_NOFOLLOW);
		}
	}
	if (!ok) {
		if (out_fd >= 0) {
			close(out_fd);
		}
		return 0;
	}
	/* the contents */
	if (e.kind == ENT_FILE) {
		static uint8_t piece[256 * 1024];
		uint64_t left = e.size, in_file = 0;

		while (left > 0) {
			uint64_t want = left > sizeof(piece) ? sizeof(piece) : left, done = 0;

			if (!in(piece, want)) {
				ok = 0;
				break;
			}
			/*
			 * A whole data volume goes in at once, faster than the memory filesystem can find
			 * pages for it, and it then says ENOSPC for want of one page rather than for want
			 * of room (bsd/miscfs/ramfs, ramfs_grow_slots and the page limit). So a short write
			 * is waited out and tried again, and only a file that will not go in at all after a
			 * second of trying is given up on -- with its name, so it is known which.
			 */
			while (out_fd >= 0 && done < want) {
				ssize_t wrote = write(out_fd, piece + done, (size_t)(want - done));

				if (wrote > 0) {
					done += (uint64_t)wrote;
					continue;
				}
				if (retry_ms_left < 5) {
					printf("var_store: %s: %llu of %llu bytes, no more would go in: %s\n",
					    path, (unsigned long long)(in_file + done),
					    (unsigned long long)e.size, strerror(errno));
					short_files++;
					lost_bytes += e.size - in_file - done;
					close(out_fd);
					out_fd = -1;
					break;
				}
				usleep(5000);
				retry_ms_left -= 5;
			}
			in_file += done;
			left -= want;
		}
		if (make) {
			made_bytes += in_file;
		}
	} else if (e.kind == ENT_SYMLINK || e.kind == ENT_HARDLINK) {
		static char target[MAX_PATH];

		if (e.size >= MAX_PATH) {
			ok = in_skip(e.size);
		} else if (!in(target, e.size)) {
			ok = 0;
		} else {
			target[e.size] = 0;
			if (make && e.kind == ENT_SYMLINK) {
				/* a name the skeleton made too comes out as the store has it */
				unlink(path);
				if (symlink(target, path) == 0) {
					made_links++;
				}
			} else if (make) {
				static char from[MAX_PATH];
				char keep[MAX_PATH];

				strcpy(keep, path);
				if (whole_path(target, (uint32_t)e.size)) {
					strcpy(from, path);
					strcpy(path, keep);
					unlink(path);
					if (link(from, path) == 0) {
						made_links++;
					}
				} else {
					strcpy(path, keep);
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if (out_fd >= 0) {
		close(out_fd);
	}
	if (!ok || !in_pad()) {
		return 0;
	}
	if (!make) {
		return 1;
	}
	/*
	 * Owner, then permissions, then the times (writing moved them), and the flags last of all:
	 * one of them may be what keeps the file from being changed again.
	 */
	switch (e.kind) {
	case ENT_DIR:
		/* its flags wait for ENT_DIRTIME: one of them may be what stops anything being made in it */
		chown(path, (int)e.uid, (int)e.gid);
		chmod(path, (int)e.mode);
		break;
	case ENT_DIRTIME:
		set_times(&e);
		if (e.flags != 0) {
			chflags(path, (int)e.flags);
		}
		break;
	case ENT_SYMLINK:
		lchown(path, (int)e.uid, (int)e.gid);
		break;
	case ENT_HARDLINK:
		break;                  /* the same inode: it has them already */
	default:
		chown(path, (int)e.uid, (int)e.gid);
		chmod(path, (int)e.mode);
		set_times(&e);
		if (e.flags != 0) {
			chflags(path, (int)e.flags);
		}
		break;
	}
	return 1;
}

static int
pass(const struct head *h, int make)
{
	stream_start((int)h->slot, h->bytes);
	for (uint64_t i = 0; i < h->entries; i++) {
		if (!unpack_one(make)) {
			return 0;
		}
	}
	if (stream_left != 0) {
		printf("var_store: %llu bytes left over after %llu entries\n",
		    (unsigned long long)stream_left, (unsigned long long)h->entries);
		return 0;
	}
	if ((stream_crc ^ 0xffffffffu) != h->crc) {
		printf("var_store: slot %u: the contents are not the %08x the header says (%08x)\n", h->slot,
		    h->crc, stream_crc ^ 0xffffffffu);
		return 0;
	}
	return 1;
}

static int
load(void)
{
	struct head h;
	int best;

	memset(&h, 0, sizeof(h));
	best = newest(&h);
	if (best < 0) {
		printf("var_store: no store yet: /private/var stays as init made it\n");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("var_store: slot %d: generation %llu of %llu seconds, %llu entries, %llu bytes\n", best,
	    (unsigned long long)h.generation, (unsigned long long)h.seconds,
	    (unsigned long long)h.entries, (unsigned long long)h.bytes);
	/* read once to prove the checksum, and only then make anything */
	if (!pass(&h, 0)) {
		struct head other;
		int left = -1;

		/* the newest is torn: the one before it, which a save never touches, may still be whole */
		for (int slot = 0; slot < SLOTS; slot++) {
			if (slot != best && read_head(slot, &other) && pass(&other, 0)) {
				left = slot;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (left < 0) {
			printf("var_store: nothing good in the store: /private/var stays as init made it\n");
			return 1;
		}
		h = other;
		printf("var_store: slot %d is good after all: generation %llu\n", left,
		    (unsigned long long)h.generation);
	}
	if (!pass(&h, 1)) {
		printf("var_store: the archive read differently the second time: what was made stays\n");
		return 0;
	}
	printf("var_store: %llu directories, %llu files (%llu bytes), %llu links back in /private/var\n",
	    (unsigned long long)made_dirs, (unsigned long long)made_files, (unsigned long long)made_bytes,
	    (unsigned long long)made_links);
	if (short_files != 0) {
		printf("var_store: %llu files did not fit: %llu bytes of them are not there\n",
		    (unsigned long long)short_files, (unsigned long long)lost_bytes);
	}
	return 1;
}

static void
show(void)
{
	for (int slot = 0; slot < SLOTS; slot++) {
		static uint8_t block[BLOCK];
		struct head *h = (struct head *)block;

		if (!device_read(slot_at(slot), block, BLOCK)) {
			continue;
		}
		if (memcmp(h->magic, HEAD_MAGIC, sizeof(h->magic)) != 0) {
			printf("var_store: slot %d: empty\n", slot);
			continue;
		}
		printf("var_store: slot %d: version %u, generation %llu, %llu entries, %llu bytes, crc %08x, "
		    "written at %llu, header %s\n", slot, h->version, (unsigned long long)h->generation,
		    (unsigned long long)h->entries, (unsigned long long)h->bytes, h->crc,
		    (unsigned long long)h->seconds, h->head_crc == head_checksum(h) ? "right" : "WRONG");
	}
}

static int
erase(void)
{
	static uint8_t block[BLOCK];

	memset(block, 0, sizeof(block));
	for (int slot = 0; slot < SLOTS; slot++) {
		if (!device_write(slot_at(slot), block, BLOCK)) {
			return 0;
		}
	}
	printf("var_store: both slots forgotten\n");
	return 1;
}

/*
 * Stay and save by itself. The kernel is told there is a saver, and then this waits: for the
 * kernel to ask (the run is ending, and it waits for the answer before it goes), and, if seconds
 * is given, for that long to pass between saves of its own accord. A save that fails is said so
 * and the waiting goes on -- the one at the end of the run still gets its chance.
 */
static int
save_once(void)
{
	int ok;

	/*
	 * The device is opened for the save and closed again, not held: while a write is in flight
	 * this kernel's own transfer list is out of the controller, and it goes back in when the
	 * device is closed (drivers/storage/hakios.ufs.c, ufs_cclose). A watcher that kept the device open
	 * would leave Darwin reading the flash through the loader for the rest of the run.
	 */
	fd = open(DEVICE, O_RDWR, 0);
	if (fd < 0) {
		printf("var_store: %s: %s\n", DEVICE, strerror(errno));
		return 0;
	}
	ok = claim() && save();
	release();
	close(fd);
	fd = -1;
	return ok;
}

static int
watch(int seconds)
{
	uint64_t last = 0;
	int asked = 0;

	fd = open(DEVICE, O_RDWR, 0);
	if (fd < 0) {
		printf("var_store: %s cannot be written (%s): nothing would be saved\n", DEVICE,
		    strerror(errno));
		return 0;
	}
	close(fd);
	fd = -1;
	if (sysctl_set_int("kern.hakios.var_save", VAR_SAVE_IDLE) != 0) {
		printf("var_store: this kernel does not keep the data volume (%s)\n", strerror(errno));
		return 0;
	}
	printf("var_store: watching: the volume is saved when the run ends%s\n",
	    seconds > 0 ? ", and in between" : "");
	{
		struct timeval tv = { 0, 0 };

		gettimeofday(&tv, NULL);
		last = (uint64_t)tv.tv_sec;
	}
	for (;;) {
		struct timeval tv = { 0, 0 };
		int state = VAR_SAVE_NONE;

		if (sysctl_int("kern.hakios.var_save", &state) == 0 && state == VAR_SAVE_WANTED) {
			asked = 1;
		}
		gettimeofday(&tv, NULL);
		if (asked || (seconds > 0 && (uint64_t)tv.tv_sec - last >= (uint64_t)seconds)) {
			int ok = save_once();

			if (!ok) {
				printf("var_store: this save came to nothing; the store keeps what it had\n");
			}
			last = (uint64_t)tv.tv_sec;
			if (asked) {
				/* answered either way: the kernel is waiting on this to go back to the loader */
				(void)sysctl_set_int("kern.hakios.var_save", VAR_SAVE_DONE);
				return ok;
			}
		}
		usleep(100000);
	}
}

/* A line saying when, for a run to leave behind and the next one to find. */
static int
stamp(const char *where)
{
	struct timeval tv = { 0, 0 };
	char line[256];
	int out_fd = open(where, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND, 0644);
	int n;

	if (out_fd < 0) {
		printf("var_store: %s: %s\n", where, strerror(errno));
		return 0;
	}
	gettimeofday(&tv, NULL);
	n = 0;
	{
		static const char head[] = "written by run of ";
		unsigned long long seconds = (unsigned long long)tv.tv_sec;
		char digits[24];
		int k = 0;

		memcpy(line, head, sizeof(head) - 1);
		n = (int)sizeof(head) - 1;
		do {
			digits[k++] = (char)('0' + seconds % 10);
			seconds /= 10;
		} while (seconds > 0);
		while (k-- > 0) {
			line[n++] = digits[k];
		}
		line[n++] = '\n';
	}
	if (write(out_fd, line, (size_t)n) != n) {
		printf("var_store: %s: %s\n", where, strerror(errno));
		close(out_fd);
		return 0;
	}
	close(out_fd);
	printf("var_store: %s: %d bytes added\n", where, n);
	return 1;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv, char **envp)
{
	const char *what = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "show";
	int ok;

	(void)envp;
	crc_init();
	if (strcmp(what, "stamp") == 0) {
		return stamp(argc > 2 ? argv[2] : "/private/var/hakios-stamp") ? 0 : 1;
	}
	buffer = mmap(NULL, BUFFER, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANON, -1, 0);
	links = mmap(NULL, LINKS * sizeof(*links), PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANON, -1, 0);
	if (buffer == MAP_FAILED || links == MAP_FAILED) {
		printf("var_store: no memory for the buffers\n");
		return 1;
	}
	/* for comparing with what the slot holds before writing over it; doing without is only slower */
	already = mmap(NULL, BUFFER, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANON, -1, 0);
	if (already == MAP_FAILED) {
		already = NULL;
	}
	if (strcmp(what, "watch") == 0) {
		if (!boot_arg_is("var_store", "1")) {
			printf("var_store: not asked to keep the data volume (var_store=1): nothing to watch\n");
			return 0;
		}
		return watch(argc > 2 ? (int)parse_number(argv[2]) : 0) ? 0 : 1;
	}
	fd = open(DEVICE, strcmp(what, "load") == 0 || strcmp(what, "show") == 0 ? O_RDONLY : O_RDWR, 0);
	if (fd < 0) {
		printf("var_store: %s: %s (the kernel takes writes with ufs_write=1)\n", DEVICE,
		    strerror(errno));
		return 1;
	}
	if (strcmp(what, "save") == 0) {
		ok = claim() && save();
		release();
	} else if (strcmp(what, "load") == 0) {
		ok = load();
	} else if (strcmp(what, "erase") == 0) {
		ok = claim() && erase();        /* a write like any other: the claim first */
		release();
	} else {
		show();
		ok = 1;
	}
	close(fd);
	return ok ? 0 : 1;
}

```

`userland/src/vk_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * Turnip on the phone, the smallest whole round: Mesa's Vulkan driver for the Adreno (tools/mk-turnip.sh) loaded as a
 * Vulkan loader would load it (vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr), an instance, the GPU as a physical device, a device and its
 * queue, a buffer in host-visible memory filled by the GPU (vkCmdFillBuffer), the submission waited for by a fence
 * (a syncobj of tools/mesa/hakios-drm), and every word of the buffer checked. Then the same fill a hundred times, timed:
 * what one submission and its wait cost. RC_JOBS=rc.jobs.vktest runs it (an image built with TURNIP=1).
 */
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <sys/ucontext.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

#define VK_NO_PROTOTYPES
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>

/* (vk_icd.h's: the loader-to-driver handshake) */
typedef VkResult (VKAPI_PTR *PFN_vkNegotiateLoaderICDInterfaceVersion)(uint32_t *pVersion);

#define DRIVER "/redwood/lib/libvulkan_freedreno.dylib"
#define WORDS (1u << 20)        /* a 4 MB buffer */

static PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr gipa;
static VkInstance instance;
static VkDevice device;

#define I(name) PFN_##name name = (PFN_##name)gipa(instance, #name)
#define CHECK(what, call) do { VkResult r_ = (call); if (r_ != VK_SUCCESS) { \
	printf("vk_test: %s failed: VkResult %d\n", what, r_); return 1; } } while (0)

/* a crash says where: the pc and lr, as offsets into the image each falls in */
static void
where(const char *what, uintptr_t a)
{
	Dl_info info;

	if (dladdr((void *)a, &info) && info.dli_fname != NULL)
		printf("vk_test:   %s %#lx = %s+%#lx (%s+%#lx)\n", what, (unsigned long)a, info.dli_fname,
		    (unsigned long)(a - (uintptr_t)info.dli_fbase), info.dli_sname ? info.dli_sname : "?",
		    (unsigned long)(a - (uintptr_t)info.dli_saddr));
	else
		printf("vk_test:   %s %#lx\n", what, (unsigned long)a);
}

static void
crashed(int sig, siginfo_t *si, void *context)
{
	ucontext_t *uc = context;

	printf("vk_test: signal %d at address %p\n", sig, si->si_addr);
	where("pc", (uintptr_t)uc->uc_mcontext->__ss.__pc);
	where("lr", (uintptr_t)uc->uc_mcontext->__ss.__lr);
	uintptr_t fp = (uintptr_t)uc->uc_mcontext->__ss.__fp;
	for (int i = 0; i < 16 && fp != 0 && (fp & 7) == 0; i++) {
		where("frame", ((uintptr_t *)fp)[1]);
		fp = ((uintptr_t *)fp)[0];
	}
	fflush(stdout);
	_exit(128 + sig);
}

static double
now_ms(void)
{
	struct timespec t;

	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &t);
	return t.tv_sec * 1e3 + t.tv_nsec / 1e6;
}

int
main(void)
{
	struct sigaction sa = { .sa_sigaction = crashed, .sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO };
	sigaction(SIGSEGV, &sa, NULL);
	sigaction(SIGBUS, &sa, NULL);
	sigaction(SIGILL, &sa, NULL);
	sigaction(SIGABRT, &sa, NULL);
	sigaction(SIGTRAP, &sa, NULL);
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
	dup2(1, 2);                     /* Mesa's own messages (stderr) beside ours */
	setenv("TU_DEBUG", "startup", 0);
	void *driver = dlopen(DRIVER, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);

	if (driver == NULL) {
		printf("vk_test: %s does not load: %s\n", DRIVER, dlerror());
		return 1;
	}
	gipa = (PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr)dlsym(driver, "vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr");
	PFN_vkNegotiateLoaderICDInterfaceVersion negotiate =
	    (PFN_vkNegotiateLoaderICDInterfaceVersion)dlsym(driver, "vk_icdNegotiateLoaderICDInterfaceVersion");
	if (gipa == NULL) {
		printf("vk_test: no vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr in the driver\n");
		return 1;
	}
	if (negotiate != NULL) {
		uint32_t version = 5;
		negotiate(&version);
		printf("vk_test: loader interface version %u\n", version);
	}

	I(vkCreateInstance);
	VkApplicationInfo app = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_APPLICATION_INFO, .pApplicationName = "vk_test",
	    .apiVersion = VK_API_VERSION_1_1 };
	VkInstanceCreateInfo ici = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_INSTANCE_CREATE_INFO, .pApplicationInfo = &app };
	CHECK("vkCreateInstance", vkCreateInstance(&ici, NULL, &instance));
	printf("vk_test: instance made\n");

	I(vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices);
	I(vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties);
	I(vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties);
	I(vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties);
	uint32_t count = 1;
	VkPhysicalDevice gpu = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
	VkResult er = vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices(instance, &count, &gpu);
	if ((er != VK_SUCCESS && er != VK_INCOMPLETE) || count == 0) {
		printf("vk_test: no physical device (VkResult %d, %u devices)\n", er, count);
		return 1;
	}
	VkPhysicalDeviceProperties props;
	vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(gpu, &props);
	printf("vk_test: device \"%s\", Vulkan %u.%u.%u, driver %#x, vendor %#x device %#x\n", props.deviceName,
	    VK_API_VERSION_MAJOR(props.apiVersion), VK_API_VERSION_MINOR(props.apiVersion), VK_API_VERSION_PATCH(props.apiVersion),
	    props.driverVersion, props.vendorID, props.deviceID);
	uint32_t families = 0;
	vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties(gpu, &families, NULL);
	printf("vk_test: %u queue families\n", families);

	float priority = 1.0f;
	VkDeviceQueueCreateInfo qci = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_QUEUE_CREATE_INFO, .queueFamilyIndex = 0,
	    .queueCount = 1, .pQueuePriorities = &priority };
	VkDeviceCreateInfo dci = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_CREATE_INFO, .queueCreateInfoCount = 1,
	    .pQueueCreateInfos = &qci };
	I(vkCreateDevice);
	CHECK("vkCreateDevice", vkCreateDevice(gpu, &dci, NULL, &device));
	printf("vk_test: device made\n");

	I(vkGetDeviceQueue);
	I(vkCreateBuffer);
	I(vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements);
	I(vkAllocateMemory);
	I(vkBindBufferMemory);
	I(vkMapMemory);
	I(vkCreateCommandPool);
	I(vkAllocateCommandBuffers);
	I(vkBeginCommandBuffer);
	I(vkCmdFillBuffer);
	I(vkEndCommandBuffer);
	I(vkCreateFence);
	I(vkQueueSubmit);
	I(vkWaitForFences);
	I(vkResetFences);
	VkQueue queue;
	vkGetDeviceQueue(device, 0, 0, &queue);

	VkBufferCreateInfo bci = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO, .size = WORDS * 4,
	    .usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT };
	VkBuffer buffer;
	CHECK("vkCreateBuffer", vkCreateBuffer(device, &bci, NULL, &buffer));
	VkMemoryRequirements req;
	vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements(device, buffer, &req);
	VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties mp;
	vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties(gpu, &mp);
	uint32_t type = UINT32_MAX;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < mp.memoryTypeCount; i++) {
		const VkMemoryPropertyFlags want = VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT | VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT;
		if ((req.memoryTypeBits & (1u << i)) && (mp.memoryTypes[i].propertyFlags & want) == want) {
			type = i;
			break;
		}
	}
	if (type == UINT32_MAX) {
		printf("vk_test: no host-visible coherent memory type\n");
		return 1;
	}
	VkMemoryAllocateInfo mai = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MEMORY_ALLOCATE_INFO, .allocationSize = req.size,
	    .memoryTypeIndex = type };
	VkDeviceMemory memory;
	CHECK("vkAllocateMemory", vkAllocateMemory(device, &mai, NULL, &memory));
	CHECK("vkBindBufferMemory", vkBindBufferMemory(device, buffer, memory, 0));
	uint32_t *words;
	CHECK("vkMapMemory", vkMapMemory(device, memory, 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE, 0, (void **)&words));
	memset(words, 0, WORDS * 4);

	VkCommandPoolCreateInfo pci = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_INFO, .queueFamilyIndex = 0 };
	VkCommandPool pool;
	CHECK("vkCreateCommandPool", vkCreateCommandPool(device, &pci, NULL, &pool));
	VkCommandBufferAllocateInfo cai = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_ALLOCATE_INFO, .commandPool = pool,
	    .level = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_LEVEL_PRIMARY, .commandBufferCount = 1 };
	VkCommandBuffer cb;
	CHECK("vkAllocateCommandBuffers", vkAllocateCommandBuffers(device, &cai, &cb));
	VkCommandBufferBeginInfo begin = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_BEGIN_INFO };
	CHECK("vkBeginCommandBuffer", vkBeginCommandBuffer(cb, &begin));
	vkCmdFillBuffer(cb, buffer, 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE, 0x600dc0de);
	CHECK("vkEndCommandBuffer", vkEndCommandBuffer(cb));
	VkFenceCreateInfo fci = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FENCE_CREATE_INFO };
	VkFence fence;
	CHECK("vkCreateFence", vkCreateFence(device, &fci, NULL, &fence));
	VkSubmitInfo si = { .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SUBMIT_INFO, .commandBufferCount = 1, .pCommandBuffers = &cb };
	double t0 = now_ms();
	CHECK("vkQueueSubmit", vkQueueSubmit(queue, 1, &si, fence));
	CHECK("vkWaitForFences", vkWaitForFences(device, 1, &fence, VK_TRUE, 2000000000ull));
	double t1 = now_ms();
	uint32_t right = 0, first_wrong = UINT32_MAX;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < WORDS; i++) {
		if (words[i] == 0x600dc0de) right++;
		else if (first_wrong == UINT32_MAX) first_wrong = i;
	}
	printf("vk_test: the GPU filled %u of %u words with 0x600dc0de in %.2f ms%s\n", right, WORDS, t1 - t0,
	    right == WORDS ? "" : " -- WRONG");
	if (first_wrong != UINT32_MAX) printf("vk_test: word %u is %#x\n", first_wrong, words[first_wrong]);

	/* a hundred more submissions of the same, each waited for */
	double best = 1e9, sum = 0;
	for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
		CHECK("vkResetFences", vkResetFences(device, 1, &fence));
		double a = now_ms();
		CHECK("vkQueueSubmit", vkQueueSubmit(queue, 1, &si, fence));
		CHECK("vkWaitForFences", vkWaitForFences(device, 1, &fence, VK_TRUE, 2000000000ull));
		double d = now_ms() - a;
		sum += d;
		if (d < best) best = d;
	}
	printf("vk_test: 100 fills of 4 MB, each submitted and waited for: %.3f ms on average, %.3f at best\n", sum / 100, best);
	printf("vk_test: %s\n", right == WORDS ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
	return right == WORDS ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`userland/src/vol_ls.c`:

```c
/*
 * A look at a mounted volume from user space, on a system that has no ls of its own (the
 * Darwin root has df and ps in /bin and nothing else): what ls -l and cat would show, how
 * the volume is mounted, and a hash of a file read both ways.
 *
 * usage: vol_ls fs PATH              the file system PATH is on: type, device, mount point, flags
 *        vol_ls ls DIR...            one line an entry, sorted: kind and mode, links, owner,
 *                                    group, size, name (and where a symbolic link points)
 *        vol_ls cat FILE [BYTES]     the file's first BYTES (default 4096), as they are
 *        vol_ls hash FILE...         FNV-1a of the whole file through read(2) and through a
 *                                    mapping, and its size: the hash tools/apfs prints on the
 *                                    build machine for the same file
 *        vol_ls sysctl NAME...       a string the kernel keeps (kern.apfs_stats: where the APFS
 *                                    driver's time went -- reads, page-ins, the lock)
 *        vol_ls zero NAME...         write to it (kern.apfs_stats: its counters zeroed)
 *        vol_ls cpuload SECONDS      how busy each processor is over the next SECONDS
 */
#include <dirent.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/mount.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <mach/processor_info.h>

#define FNV_INIT  0xcbf29ce484222325ULL
#define FNV_PRIME 0x100000001b3ULL

static int
by_name(const void *a, const void *b)
{
	return strcmp(*(char *const *)a, *(char *const *)b);
}

static void
mode_string(mode_t m, char *out)
{
	const char *rwx = "rwxrwxrwx";
	int i;

	out[0] = S_ISDIR(m) ? 'd' : S_ISLNK(m) ? 'l' : S_ISREG(m) ? '-' : S_ISCHR(m) ? 'c' :
	    S_ISBLK(m) ? 'b' : S_ISFIFO(m) ? 'p' : S_ISSOCK(m) ? 's' : '?';
	for (i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
		out[1 + i] = (m & (0400 >> i)) ? rwx[i] : '-';
	}
	if (m & S_ISUID) {
		out[3] = (m & 0100) ? 's' : 'S';
	}
	if (m & S_ISGID) {
		out[6] = (m & 0010) ? 's' : 'S';
	}
	if (m & S_ISVTX) {
		out[9] = (m & 0001) ? 't' : 'T';
	}
	out[10] = '\0';
}

static int
do_fs(const char *path)
{
	struct statfs sf;

	if (statfs(path, &sf) != 0) {
		printf("vol_ls: %s: statfs: %s\n", path, strerror(errno));
		return 1;
	}
	printf("vol_ls: %s is on %s, a %s file system mounted on %s%s%s%s; %llu blocks of %u, "
	    "%llu files\n", path, sf.f_mntfromname, sf.f_fstypename, sf.f_mntonname,
	    (sf.f_flags & MNT_RDONLY) ? ", read only" : ", writable",
	    (sf.f_flags & MNT_NOSUID) ? ", nosuid" : "", (sf.f_flags & MNT_NODEV) ? ", nodev" : "",
	    (unsigned long long)sf.f_blocks, (unsigned)sf.f_bsize, (unsigned long long)sf.f_files);
	return 0;
}

static int
do_ls(const char *dir)
{
	DIR *d = opendir(dir);
	struct dirent *de;
	char **names = NULL;
	size_t n = 0, cap = 0, i;
	int bad = 0;

	if (d == NULL) {
		printf("vol_ls: %s: %s\n", dir, strerror(errno));
		return 1;
	}
	while ((de = readdir(d)) != NULL) {
		if (strcmp(de->d_name, ".") == 0 || strcmp(de->d_name, "..") == 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (n == cap) {
			cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 64;
			names = realloc(names, cap * sizeof(*names));
			if (names == NULL) {
				closedir(d);
				return 1;
			}
		}
		names[n++] = strdup(de->d_name);
	}
	closedir(d);
	qsort(names, n, sizeof(*names), by_name);
	printf("vol_ls: %s: %zu entries\n", dir, n);
	for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		char path[PATH_MAX], mode[11], target[PATH_MAX];
		struct stat st;

		snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/%s", dir, names[i]);
		if (lstat(path, &st) != 0) {
			printf("  %s: %s\n", names[i], strerror(errno));
			bad++;
			free(names[i]);
			continue;
		}
		mode_string(st.st_mode, mode);
		if (S_ISLNK(st.st_mode)) {
			ssize_t len = readlink(path, target, sizeof(target) - 1);

			target[len > 0 ? len : 0] = '\0';
			/* the time of writing as the seconds of the epoch: whether a name is this boot's */
			printf("  %s %3u %4u %4u %12lld %11lld %s -> %s\n", mode, (unsigned)st.st_nlink,
			    (unsigned)st.st_uid, (unsigned)st.st_gid, (long long)st.st_size,
			    (long long)st.st_mtimespec.tv_sec, names[i], target);
		} else {
			printf("  %s %3u %4u %4u %12lld %11lld %s\n", mode, (unsigned)st.st_nlink,
			    (unsigned)st.st_uid, (unsigned)st.st_gid, (long long)st.st_size,
			    (long long)st.st_mtimespec.tv_sec, names[i]);
		}
		free(names[i]);
	}
	free(names);
	return bad;
}

static int
do_cat(const char *file, long want)
{
	char *buf;
	ssize_t got;
	int fd = open(file, O_RDONLY);

	if (fd < 0) {
		printf("vol_ls: %s: %s\n", file, strerror(errno));
		return 1;
	}
	buf = malloc((size_t)want);
	got = buf != NULL ? read(fd, buf, (size_t)want) : -1;
	close(fd);
	if (got < 0) {
		printf("vol_ls: %s: read: %s\n", file, strerror(errno));
		free(buf);
		return 1;
	}
	printf("vol_ls: %s, the first %zd bytes:\n", file, got);
	fwrite(buf, 1, (size_t)got, stdout);
	if (got > 0 && buf[got - 1] != '\n') {
		putchar('\n');
	}
	free(buf);
	return 0;
}

static int
do_hash(const char *file)
{
	static unsigned char buf[65536];
	unsigned long long h_read = FNV_INIT, h_map = FNV_INIT;
	struct stat st;
	ssize_t got;
	off_t i;
	int fd = open(file, O_RDONLY);

	if (fd < 0 || fstat(fd, &st) != 0) {
		printf("vol_ls: %s: %s\n", file, strerror(errno));
		if (fd >= 0) {
			close(fd);
		}
		return 1;
	}
	while ((got = read(fd, buf, sizeof(buf))) > 0) {
		for (i = 0; i < got; i++) {
			h_read = (h_read ^ buf[i]) * FNV_PRIME;
		}
	}
	if (st.st_size > 0) {
		const unsigned char *m = mmap(NULL, (size_t)st.st_size, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0);

		if (m == MAP_FAILED) {
			printf("vol_ls: %s: mmap: %s\n", file, strerror(errno));
			close(fd);
			return 1;
		}
		for (i = 0; i < st.st_size; i++) {
			h_map = (h_map ^ m[i]) * FNV_PRIME;
		}
		munmap((void *)m, (size_t)st.st_size);
	}
	close(fd);
	printf("vol_ls: %s: %lld bytes, read %016llx, mapped %016llx%s\n", file,
	    (long long)st.st_size, h_read, h_map, h_read == h_map ? "" : " -- they differ");
	return h_read == h_map ? 0 : 1;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int i, bad = 0;

	if (argc < 3) {
		printf("usage: vol_ls fs PATH | ls DIR... | cat FILE [BYTES] | hash FILE... | sysctl NAME...\n");
		return 2;
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "fs") == 0) {
		return do_fs(argv[2]);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "cat") == 0) {
		return do_cat(argv[2], argc > 3 ? atol(argv[3]) : 4096);
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "cpuload") == 0) {
		/*
		 * How busy every processor was over the next SECONDS: user, system, idle, and its
		 * interrupts (IPIs among them).  On the phone the slower cores' (4-6) idle count runs
		 * ~56 times too fast -- the "all" line comes out at 1% user while each fast core shows
		 * ~43% -- so their "99% idle" says nothing; their IPIs and the threads that run there
		 * (kern.apfs_stats: where long waits ended) show they work.
		 */
		processor_info_array_t a = NULL, b = NULL, sa = NULL, sb = NULL;
		mach_msg_type_number_t na = 0, nb = 0, nsa = 0, nsb = 0;
		natural_t ncpu = 0, n2 = 0, n3 = 0, n4 = 0;
		unsigned seconds = (unsigned)atoi(argv[2]);
		unsigned long long tu = 0, ts = 0, ti = 0;

		if (host_processor_info(mach_host_self(), PROCESSOR_CPU_LOAD_INFO, &ncpu, &a, &na) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
			printf("cpuload: host_processor_info failed\n");
			return 1;
		}
		(void)host_processor_info(mach_host_self(), PROCESSOR_CPU_STAT64, &n3, &sa, &nsa);
		sleep(seconds);
		(void)host_processor_info(mach_host_self(), PROCESSOR_CPU_STAT64, &n4, &sb, &nsb);
		if (host_processor_info(mach_host_self(), PROCESSOR_CPU_LOAD_INFO, &n2, &b, &nb) != KERN_SUCCESS || n2 != ncpu) {
			printf("cpuload: host_processor_info failed\n");
			return 1;
		}
		for (natural_t c = 0; c < ncpu; c++) {
			const unsigned *x = (const unsigned *)a + c * CPU_STATE_MAX, *y = (const unsigned *)b + c * CPU_STATE_MAX;
			unsigned u = y[CPU_STATE_USER] - x[CPU_STATE_USER] + y[CPU_STATE_NICE] - x[CPU_STATE_NICE];
			unsigned sy = y[CPU_STATE_SYSTEM] - x[CPU_STATE_SYSTEM], id = y[CPU_STATE_IDLE] - x[CPU_STATE_IDLE];
			unsigned all = u + sy + id;

			printf("cpuload: cpu %u over %u s: user %u%%, system %u%%, idle %u%%", c, seconds,
			    all ? u * 100 / all : 0, all ? sy * 100 / all : 0, all ? id * 100 / all : 0);
			if (sa != NULL && sb != NULL && n3 == ncpu && n4 == ncpu) {
				/* (the 64-bit form: packed, 4-byte aligned, so read field by field) */
				const struct processor_cpu_stat64 *p = (const struct processor_cpu_stat64 *)sa + c;
				const struct processor_cpu_stat64 *q = (const struct processor_cpu_stat64 *)sb + c;

				printf("; interrupts %llu, of them IPIs %llu, timer %llu",
				    (unsigned long long)(q->irq_ex_cnt - p->irq_ex_cnt), (unsigned long long)(q->ipi_cnt - p->ipi_cnt),
				    (unsigned long long)(q->timer_cnt - p->timer_cnt));
			}
			printf("\n");
			tu += u;
			ts += sy;
			ti += id;
		}
		printf("cpuload: all %u processors over %u s: user %llu%%, system %llu%%, idle %llu%%\n", ncpu, seconds,
		    (tu + ts + ti) ? tu * 100 / (tu + ts + ti) : 0, (tu + ts + ti) ? ts * 100 / (tu + ts + ti) : 0,
		    (tu + ts + ti) ? ti * 100 / (tu + ts + ti) : 0);
		return 0;
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "zero") == 0) {
		/* (kern.apfs_stats: writing anything zeroes the counters) */
		for (i = 2; i < argc; i++) {
			char zero = 0;

			if (sysctlbyname(argv[i], NULL, NULL, &zero, 1) != 0) {
				printf("%s: %s\n", argv[i], strerror(errno));
				bad++;
			}
		}
		return bad ? 1 : 0;
	}
	if (strcmp(argv[1], "sysctl") == 0) {
		for (i = 2; i < argc; i++) {
			static char text[16384];
			size_t len = sizeof(text) - 1;

			if (sysctlbyname(argv[i], text, &len, NULL, 0) != 0) {
				printf("%s: %s\n", argv[i], strerror(errno));
				bad++;
				continue;
			}
			text[len] = 0;
			printf("%s:\n%s\n", argv[i], text);
		}
		return bad ? 1 : 0;
	}
	for (i = 2; i < argc; i++) {
		if (strcmp(argv[1], "ls") == 0) {
			bad += do_ls(argv[i]);
		} else if (strcmp(argv[1], "hash") == 0) {
			bad += do_hash(argv[i]);
		} else {
			printf("vol_ls: no such thing as %s\n", argv[1]);
			return 2;
		}
	}
	return bad ? 1 : 0;
}
```

`userland/src/wifipw_test.c`:

```c
/*
 * wifipw_test: what wifid does with a network's password when Settings joins it, done here the same
 * way: MobileWiFi's WiFiSecuritySetPassword() into the keychain, WiFiSecurityCopyPassword() back
 * (what Auto-Join asks before it joins a known network on its own), WiFiSecurityRemovePassword()
 * (what "Forget This Network" does). The network is a made-up one ("hakios-wifipw-test") with a
 * made-up password, neither printed in full. Signed with wifipw_test.entitlements: wifid's name
 * and its right to the system keychain, as the keychain answers a program by those.
 * MobileWiFi's own os_log lines ("__WiFiSecuritySetPassword:[...] Error result -25291") say the
 * keychain's answer; they are printed on the console as well (OS_ACTIVITY_DT_MODE).
 */
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <Security/Security.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define SSID	CFSTR("hakios-wifipw-test")
#define SECRET	CFSTR("not-a-real-password")

static CFStringRef (*copy_password)(CFStringRef ssid);

static void
read_back(const char *when)
{
	CFStringRef pw = copy_password(SSID);

	printf("wifipw_test: %s: WiFiSecurityCopyPassword: %s\n", when,
	    pw == NULL ? "nothing" : CFEqual(pw, SECRET) ? "THE SAME PASSWORD" : "another password");
	if (pw != NULL)
		CFRelease(pw);
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	void *mw;
	Boolean (*set_password)(CFStringRef ssid, CFStringRef password);
	Boolean (*remove_password)(CFStringRef ssid);
	CFMutableDictionaryRef q;
	CFTypeRef attrs = NULL;
	OSStatus status;

	(void)argc;
	if (getenv("OS_ACTIVITY_DT_MODE") == NULL) {
		/* os_log decides where it prints when the process starts */
		setenv("OS_ACTIVITY_DT_MODE", "YES", 1);
		execv(argv[0], argv);
	}
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
	mw = dlopen("/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/MobileWiFi.framework/MobileWiFi", RTLD_NOW);
	set_password = mw ? dlsym(mw, "WiFiSecuritySetPassword") : NULL;
	copy_password = mw ? dlsym(mw, "WiFiSecurityCopyPassword") : NULL;
	remove_password = mw ? dlsym(mw, "WiFiSecurityRemovePassword") : NULL;
	if (set_password == NULL || copy_password == NULL || remove_password == NULL) {
		printf("wifipw_test: MobileWiFi or its functions not found: %s\n", dlerror());
		return 1;
	}
	read_back("before");
	printf("wifipw_test: WiFiSecuritySetPassword: %s\n", set_password(SSID, SECRET) ? "yes" : "NO");
	read_back("after");

	/* the item itself, as the keychain has it: wifid's service name, the network's name for account */
	q = CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	CFDictionarySetValue(q, kSecClass, kSecClassGenericPassword);
	CFDictionarySetValue(q, kSecAttrService, CFSTR("AirPort"));
	CFDictionarySetValue(q, kSecAttrAccount, SSID);
	CFDictionarySetValue(q, kSecAttrSynchronizable, kSecAttrSynchronizableAny);
	CFDictionarySetValue(q, kSecReturnAttributes, kCFBooleanTrue);
	status = SecItemCopyMatching(q, &attrs);
	printf("wifipw_test: the item (service AirPort): %d\n", (int)status);
	if (attrs != NULL && CFGetTypeID(attrs) == CFDictionaryGetTypeID()) {
		CFTypeRef group = CFDictionaryGetValue(attrs, kSecAttrAccessGroup);
		CFTypeRef cls = CFDictionaryGetValue(attrs, kSecAttrAccessible);
		CFTypeRef sync = CFDictionaryGetValue(attrs, kSecAttrSynchronizable);
		char g[64] = "?", c[16] = "?";

		if (group != NULL && CFGetTypeID(group) == CFStringGetTypeID())
			CFStringGetCString(group, g, sizeof(g), kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
		if (cls != NULL && CFGetTypeID(cls) == CFStringGetTypeID())
			CFStringGetCString(cls, c, sizeof(c), kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
		printf("wifipw_test: its access group %s, protection class %s, synchronizable %s\n", g, c,
		    sync == NULL ? "?" : CFEqual(sync, kCFBooleanTrue) ? "yes" : "no");
	}
	if (attrs != NULL)
		CFRelease(attrs);
	CFRelease(q);

	printf("wifipw_test: WiFiSecurityRemovePassword: %s\n", remove_password(SSID) ? "yes" : "NO");
	read_back("after removing");
	return 0;
}
```

`userland/var/mobile/Library/Preferences/com.apple.springboard.plist`:

```plist
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
	<!-- one processor core and a software renderer: applications need more time to come up than the
	     watchdog gives them on Apple's hardware (20 s for the first frame) -->
	<key>FBLaunchWatchdogScale</key>
	<real>20</real>
	<!-- ... and the other watchdogs have no scale: 10 s to answer any change to a scene (going to the
	     background, the scene of the widgets coming up while the system starts) is not always enough
	     under QEMU, where the window server takes most of the one processor during an animation. This
	     switches all of FrontBoard's watchdogs off; an application that really hangs is closed from
	     the application switcher. -->
```

`wifi/lx/include/linux/of.h`:

```h
/*
 * The device tree as Linux drivers read it. There is no flattened tree under XNU, and so far no
 * node either: the files of the driver that are built ask two questions of it, which
 * src/lx_bus.c answers with "no". The rest is declared for the driver's bus file, which reads
 * its own node's properties; those will be made from what the kernel says about the radio.
 * Cells are kept in the processor's byte order.
 */
#ifndef _LX_LINUX_OF_H
#define _LX_LINUX_OF_H

#include <linux/types.h>
#include <linux/errno.h>
#include <linux/kobject.h>
#include <linux/mod_devicetable.h>
#include <linux/fwnode.h>

typedef u32 phandle;

struct property {
	const char *name;
	int length;			/* bytes */
	const void *value;
};

struct device_node {
	const char *name;
	const char *full_name;
	phandle phandle;
	const struct property *properties;
	int nproperties;
	struct device_node *parent;
	struct device_node *child;
	struct device_node *sibling;
	struct fwnode_handle fwnode;
};

struct of_device_id {
	char name[32];
	char type[32];
	char compatible[128];
	const void *data;
};

const struct property *of_find_property(const struct device_node *np, const char *name, int *lenp);
const void *of_get_property(const struct device_node *np, const char *name, int *lenp);
int of_property_read_string(const struct device_node *np, const char *name, const char **out);
int of_property_read_u32_index(const struct device_node *np, const char *name, u32 index, u32 *out);
bool of_device_is_compatible(const struct device_node *np, const char *compatible);
bool of_machine_is_compatible(const char *compatible);
struct device_node *of_get_child_by_name(const struct device_node *np, const char *name);
struct device_node *of_find_node_by_phandle(phandle handle);
struct device_node *of_parse_phandle(const struct device_node *np, const char *name, int index);
const struct of_device_id *of_match_node(const struct of_device_id *matches, const struct device_node *np);

static inline int
of_property_read_u32(const struct device_node *np, const char *name, u32 *out)
{
	return (of_property_read_u32_index(np, name, 0, out));
}

static inline bool
of_property_present(const struct device_node *np, const char *name)
{
	return (of_find_property(np, name, NULL) != NULL);
}

static inline bool
of_property_read_bool(const struct device_node *np, const char *name)
{
	return (of_find_property(np, name, NULL) != NULL);
}

/* the nodes live as long as the layer does */
static inline struct device_node *of_node_get(struct device_node *np) { return (np); }
static inline void of_node_put(struct device_node *np) { }

#endif

```

`wifi/lx/include/linux/rhashtable.h`:

```h
/*
 * Linux's hash table that resizes itself, as far as the driver uses it: things found by a key
 * that lies inside them (peer.c: a peer by its address, and by its number). LinuxKPI's header
 * has the names and nothing behind them -- its rhashtable_init() fails --, so this one stands
 * in its place: a fixed number of chains, which never resize. The functions are in
 * src/lx_base.c.
 */
#ifndef _LX_LINUX_RHASHTABLE_H
#define _LX_LINUX_RHASHTABLE_H

#include <linux/types.h>

struct rhash_head {
	struct rhash_head *next;
};

struct rhashtable_params {
	uint16_t	head_offset;		/* of the thing's rhash_head, in the thing */
	uint16_t	key_len;
	uint16_t	key_offset;		/* of the key, in the thing */
	uint16_t	nelem_hint;
	bool		automatic_shrinking;
};

struct rhashtable {
	struct rhash_head *chains[64];
};

int	 rhashtable_init(struct rhashtable *table, const struct rhashtable_params *params);
void	 rhashtable_destroy(struct rhashtable *table);
/* the thing with that key, or NULL */
void	*rhashtable_lookup_fast(struct rhashtable *table, const void *key, const struct rhashtable_params params);
/* the thing already there under the new thing's key; or NULL, and the new thing is in */
void	*rhashtable_lookup_get_insert_fast(struct rhashtable *table, struct rhash_head *head,
	    const struct rhashtable_params params);
int	 rhashtable_remove_fast(struct rhashtable *table, struct rhash_head *head, const struct rhashtable_params params);

#endif

```

```h
 * request: the mode the firmware is asked for. The radio's registers answer in mission mode only.
```

```h
/*
 * FreeBSD's <sys/cdefs.h>, for objects that are linked into a Mach-O kernel: a section there is named
 * "segment,section" with at most sixteen characters each, so the ELF section names of FreeBSD's
 * headers cannot be used. The placement attributes (__read_mostly and the like) are dropped; linker
```

`wifi/lx/include/sys/linker_set.h`:

```h
/*
 * FreeBSD's linker sets, for a Mach-O kernel. A set is a section of pointers that the linker
 * gathers from every object; FreeBSD's kernel walks many of them, the layer has a use for one:
 * the startup functions (sysinit_set, where a Linux module's module_init() ends up). That one is
 * kept, in a section of ours, for the layer to walk when a file that has one is built: none of
 * those built so far does. The entries of the others (the sysctl tree, module metadata, shutdown
 * functions) are dropped, since nothing here reads them. A set that this file does not know
 * stops the compilation.
 */
#ifndef _SYS_LINKER_SET_H_
#define _SYS_LINKER_SET_H_

#define __LX_SET_KEEP(sect, set, sym, qv)					\
	static void const * qv __set_##set##_sym_##sym				\
	    __attribute__((__section__("__DATA," sect), __used__)) = &(sym)
#define __LX_SET_DROP(set, sym, qv)						\
	static void const * qv __set_##set##_sym_##sym __attribute__((__unused__)) = &(sym)

#define __LX_SET_sysinit_set(set, sym, qv)	__LX_SET_KEEP("lx_sysinit", set, sym, qv)
#define __LX_SET_sysuninit_set(set, sym, qv)	__LX_SET_DROP(set, sym, qv)
#define __LX_SET_sysctl_set(set, sym, qv)	__LX_SET_DROP(set, sym, qv)
#define __LX_SET_modmetadata_set(set, sym, qv)	__LX_SET_DROP(set, sym, qv)

#define __MAKE_SET_QV(set, sym, qv)	__LX_SET_##set(set, sym, qv)
#define __MAKE_SET(set, sym)		__MAKE_SET_QV(set, sym, const)
#define TEXT_SET(set, sym)		__MAKE_SET(set, sym)
#define DATA_SET(set, sym)		__MAKE_SET(set, sym)
#define DATA_WSET(set, sym)		__MAKE_SET_QV(set, sym, )
#define BSS_SET(set, sym)		__MAKE_SET(set, sym)
#define ABS_SET(set, sym)		__MAKE_SET(set, sym)
#define SET_ENTRY(set, sym)		__MAKE_SET(set, sym)

/*
 * Walking a set: FreeBSD's names for its ends are declared, and for the sets that are dropped
 * nothing defines them, so code that walks one shows up when the object is linked.
 */
#define SET_DECLARE(set, ptype)							\
	extern ptype *__CONCAT(__start_set_,set);				\
	extern ptype *__CONCAT(__stop_set_,set)
#define SET_BEGIN(set)		(&__CONCAT(__start_set_,set))
#define SET_LIMIT(set)		(&__CONCAT(__stop_set_,set))
#define SET_FOREACH(pvar, set)	for (pvar = SET_BEGIN(set); pvar < SET_LIMIT(set); pvar++)
#define SET_ITEM(set, i)	((SET_BEGIN(set))[i])
#define SET_COUNT(set)		(SET_LIMIT(set) - SET_BEGIN(set))

#endif

```
