`xl`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# xl — drive the XNU loader on the phone over USB (fastboot protocol).
#
#   xl enter            get the phone into the resident loader (from Android or stock fastboot)
#   xl run [N]          upload the current kernel, run it (optionally stop at checkpoint N), fetch the log
#   xl ramdisk [FILE]   upload the big system image (default userland/system.apfs) once; it stays in
#                       the phone's RAM across kernel runs and is the root filesystem (/dev/md0)
#                       ("xl ramdisk none" forgets it; the image sent with the kernel is then the root)
#   xl screenshot [F]   save what is in the phone's framebuffer as a PNG (default logs/screen.png);
#                       works during a run too (from another terminal)
#   xl recording [F]    fetch the screen recording the last run made (rec_secs=N among XL_CMDLINE) and
#                       make a video of it (default logs/recording.mp4)
#   xl sound [F]        fetch the sound the last run recorded (rec_sound=N among XL_CMDLINE: the first N
#                       seconds of what Darwin played) and make a WAV file of it (default logs/sound.wav)
#   xl camera [P]       fetch the frames the last run's camera left (cam=3 and up among XL_CMDLINE) and make
#                       pictures of them (P-0.png, ...; default prefix logs/camera)
#   xl selftest         exercise only the kernel->loader return path
#   xl log              fetch the loader's current log; during a run, the kernel's log so far as well
#   xl stop             end the run in progress now (the kernel returns as when its time is up)
#   xl hang             watchdog test: make the loader hang on purpose
#   xl reboot           cold-reset the phone (back to Android)
#   xl reload           restart the phone into a freshly built loader (after changing xnuloader/)
#   xl memmap           the phone's memory map as its firmware reports it
#   xl state            where is the phone right now
#
# Logs land in logs/. Environment for `run`:
#   XL_CMDLINE  extra kernel boot-args; default "-v": the boot is shown as text on the phone's screen
#               (XL_CMDLINE="" for a blank screen, XL_CMDLINE="-v systrace=1" to trace failing syscalls)
#   XL_SECS     seconds after which the kernel returns to the loader on its own (default 8)
#   XL_FOLLOW=N fetch the kernel's log every N seconds during a run (default 10; XL_FOLLOW= for never), so that a kernel
#               that hangs leaves what it said in logs/<time>-run.log.live; after a hang `run` brings the phone back to
#               Android itself, or says what to press if it is stuck on the logo
#   XL_HOME=fastboot   after a hang, keep the phone in its bootloader instead of sending it to Android (and send it
#               there from Android): a long session of runs never waits for Android to start
#   XL_REBOOT_AFTER=1  when the run is over, send the phone back to Android (it charges there; in the loader it does not,
#               and its screen stays on: a phone left in the loader overnight is a flat one by morning)
#   XL_FIRMWARE=u-boot|silicium   what the phone's bootloader starts the loader with (default: Silicium's UEFI when its
#               image is built, else HakiOS's U-Boot: docs/u-boot.md); either way from RAM, nothing is flashed
#   XL_SB_DELAY seconds SpringBoard waits before it starts (default 8; see userland/src/inject_sb.c)
#               Among XL_CMDLINE, for the phone: bootcpu=7 runs the kernel on the biggest core instead of
#               the small one the firmware starts on (the loader then watches from the first core, and a
#               kernel that hangs still gets its log out); cpufreq=1 sets that core to its top speed;
#               touchscreen=1 turns the touch screen on.
#   XL_RAMDISK  the image sent with the kernel: the small one that is mounted on /redwood
#               (default userland/root.apfs; "none" sends none). Without a system image in the
#               phone's RAM it is the root itself (e.g. XL_RAMDISK=userland/hello).
# One phone, several working copies: a run holds a lock, and `stop` and `reboot` from another working
# copy than the one it was started from are refused (XL_FORCE=1 to end it all the same). While a run
# is in progress every other command is refused too, `ramdisk` among them.
# The lock says whether a run is live; it says nothing about the image resident in the phone's memory,
# which outlives both the lock and any note beside it and belongs to whoever uploaded it last. So
# `ramdisk` records who uploaded what, and how big it was, in $PHONE.ramdisk, and `run` prints that
# when the last upload was not from this copy. The record starts empty -- an upload by a copy without
# this change leaves none -- and `run` says so rather than assuming.
cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" || exit 1
# On a Mac: flock, GNU timeout and stat, and Android's platform-tools, from tools/macos-bin (see its README)
[ "$(uname)" = Darwin ] && PATH=$PWD/tools/macos-bin:$PWD/tools/macos-bin/platform-tools:$PATH
# the kernel and the loader built here, or else the ones that come with the repository
K=hakios-kernel                 # make kernel makes it
[ -f $K ] || K=prebuilt/hakios-kernel
L=xnuloader/loader.efi
if [ ! -f $L ]; then
	L=prebuilt/loader.efi
	echo "xl: no xnuloader/loader.efi: using prebuilt/loader.efi, which has no iPhone identity in it (Darwin will not start; make loader builds one from your own IPSW)" >&2
fi
mkdir -p logs
# There is one phone, whichever working copy (tools/new-workspace.sh) talks to it: the locks are
# outside all of them.
PHONE=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/darwin-hakios-phone
# adb starts a server of its own the first time, and the server inherits every open descriptor: started during a run it
# kept the run's lock (descriptor 8, below) for as long as it lived, and every later command said a run was in progress
# (27 October). So adb never gets that descriptor.
adb() { command adb "$@" 8>&-; }

# one fastboot at a time (a run in one terminal, "xl screenshot" in another): each takes the lock for itself
fb() { flock -w 90 $PHONE.lock timeout "${FB_TIMEOUT:-10}" fastboot "$@" 2>&1; }
# does the loader answer while its kernel runs (0.5 and later)? an older one answers only when the run is over
live_loader() { fb getvar version | grep -Eq 'version: 0\.([5-9]|[1-9][0-9])'; }
in_fastboot() { fastboot devices 2>/dev/null | grep -q fastboot; }
is_loader() { in_fastboot && fb getvar product | grep -q 'product: xnuloader'; }
state() {
	if is_loader; then echo loader
	elif in_fastboot; then echo fastboot
	elif [ "$(adb get-state 2>/dev/null)" = device ]; then echo android
	else echo absent; fi
}
wait_for() { # wait_for <state> <seconds>
	local i
	for ((i = 0; i < $2; i += 2)); do [ "$(state)" = "$1" ] && return 0; sleep 2; done
	return 1
}

# After a hang the watchdog resets the phone, and what comes up is not always Android: it can stop in its bootloader (it
# charges badly there and a person has to notice), or on the logo, where it does not show on USB at all. Wait for Android;
# a phone that appears in the bootloader or in this loader is sent on to Android at once; if nothing has come back after
# two and a half minutes, say what a person has to do, because nothing here can reach a phone that is not on USB.
# XL_HOME=fastboot: the other way round, for a session of many runs: the phone is kept in its bootloader, where the next
# run starts at once, and one that comes up in Android is sent there (the logo is the one place nothing here can help).
recover_phone() {
	local i s
	for ((i = 0; i < 150; i += 3)); do
		s=$(state)
		if [ "${XL_HOME:-android}" = fastboot ]; then
			case "$s" in
			fastboot) echo "xl: phone is back in its bootloader (XL_HOME=fastboot)"; return 0 ;;
			android) echo "xl: the phone came up in Android: sending it to its bootloader (XL_HOME=fastboot)"; adb reboot bootloader ;;
			loader) echo "xl: the phone is in this loader: restarting it (it comes up in Android, and goes on from there)"; fb reboot >/dev/null ;;
			esac
		else
			case "$s" in
			android) echo "xl: phone is back in Android"; return 0 ;;
			fastboot) echo "xl: the phone stopped in its bootloader: sending it on to Android"; timeout 10 fastboot reboot >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
			loader) echo "xl: the phone is in this loader: sending it on to Android"; fb reboot >/dev/null ;;
			esac
		fi
		sleep 3
	done
	echo "xl: the phone has not come back (state: $(state)): it is on the logo, off, or not on this cable."
	echo "xl:   hold the power button for about 15 seconds; it restarts into Android."
	echo "xl:   for the bootloader (fastboot) hold power and volume-down while it restarts."
	return 1
}

# What the phone's bootloader starts the loader with: Project Silicium's UEFI (mkxnuimg.py) or HakiOS's U-Boot
# (tools/mkubootimg.py, docs/u-boot.md). XL_FIRMWARE says which; without it, Silicium's when its image has been built
# (it is made from the phone's own vendor drivers and is not in the repository), else U-Boot's.
firmware() {
	case "${XL_FIRMWARE:-}" in
	u-boot|silicium) echo "$XL_FIRMWARE"; return ;;
	esac
	if [ -f Mu-Silicium/Build/redwoodPkg/RELEASE_CLANGPDB/FV/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd ] || [ -f devices/redwood/prebuilt/SILICIUM_UEFI.fd ]; then
		echo silicium
	else
		echo u-boot
	fi
}

enter() {
	case "$(state)" in
	loader) return 0 ;;
	android) adb reboot bootloader; wait_for fastboot 60 || { echo "xl: phone did not reach fastboot"; return 1; } ;;
	fastboot) ;;
	absent) echo "xl: waiting for the phone (Android or fastboot)..."
		local i; for ((i = 0; i < 180; i += 3)); do [ "$(state)" != absent ] && break; sleep 3; done
		[ "$(state)" = absent ] && { echo "xl: phone not reachable"; return 1; }
		enter; return ;;
	esac
	xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o usb-payload.bin loader.efi=$L --usb >/dev/null || { echo "xl: payload build failed"; return 1; }
	case "$(firmware)" in
	u-boot) tools/mkubootimg.py -d "${DEVICE:-redwood}" -l $L -p usb-payload.bin -o xnu-usb.img >/dev/null ;;
	*) ./mkxnuimg.py -p usb-payload.bin -o xnu-usb.img >/dev/null ;;
	esac || { echo "xl: image build failed ($(firmware))"; return 1; }
	# Right after the phone enters fastboot the first "boot" is sometimes not taken: try twice.
	local try
	for try in 1 2; do
		FB_TIMEOUT=40 fb boot xnu-usb.img | grep -q OKAY || { sleep 3; continue; }
		sleep 6
		wait_for loader 30 && { rm -f $PHONE.ran; return 0; }
		[ "$(state)" = fastboot ] || break
	done
	echo "xl: loader did not come up on USB (state: $(state))"; return 1
}

fetch_log() { # fetch_log <file>
	rm -f "$1"
	FB_TIMEOUT=20 fb get_staged "$1" >/dev/null
	[ -s "$1" ] && tr -d '\0' < "$1" > "$1.tmp" && mv "$1.tmp" "$1"
}

# A second kernel in one session of the loader dies at once (27 October, four runs: every run after one that returned,
# whatever its arguments, gave no answer within 5 s; every first run of a session lived). Restart the phone into its own
# bootloader between runs ("xl run" warns when this session has run a kernel already).
run() { # run <oem command> <label>
	if [ "$(state)" = loader ] && [ -f $PHONE.ran ]; then
		echo "xl: warning: a kernel has already run in this session of the loader, and a second one has died at once every time it was tried"
	fi
	enter || return 1
	exec 8> $PHONE.run
	flock -n 8 || { echo "xl: a run is in progress, started from $(cat $PHONE.who 2>/dev/null) (xl stop ends it)"; return 1; }
	pwd > $PHONE.who
	local stamp log result
	stamp=$(date +%H%M%S); log="logs/$stamp-$2.log"
	if [ "$1" != "oem selftest" ]; then
		# The kernel hands control back after XL_SECS seconds even if it is just waiting.
		local rd=${XL_RAMDISK:-userland/root.apfs}
		case "$rd" in
		none|resident) rd= ;;
		*) [ -f "$rd" ] || { echo "xl: ramdisk $rd not found"; return 1; } ;;
		esac
		case $K in prebuilt/*) echo "xl: no kernel built here, running $K" >&2 ;; esac
		# The resident image: whose it is and how big, when the last upload was not from here.
		# Both values and not just "not from here", because a foreign image of the same kind
		# changes nothing, while a foreign one of another kind makes the boot fail in a way that
		# names neither it nor its owner -- /sbin/launchd.darwin: No such file or directory, with a
		# perfectly good image on this side. The warning is not a refusal: relying on another
		# copy's upload is legitimate when you know what it is, and this says what it is.
		if [ -s $PHONE.ramdisk ]; then
			local rwho rwhat rsize
			IFS=$'\t' read -r rwho rwhat rsize < $PHONE.ramdisk
			if [ "$rwho" != "$(pwd)" ]; then
				echo "xl: the resident image was uploaded from $rwho:" \
				     "$rwhat, $(( rsize / 1048576 )) MB. Upload your own" \
				     "(./xl ramdisk FILE) unless that is the one you want" >&2
			fi
		else
			echo "xl: nothing here recorded who uploaded the resident image;" \
			     "if this run needs a particular one, upload it" >&2
		fi
		# A run about Wi-Fi is given the radio's own address, which is this phone's and so is kept in a
		# file that is not in the repository: fw-wifi/mac, one line, six bytes in hexadecimal with colons.
		local args=${XL_CMDLINE--v}
		case " $args " in
		*" wifi="*|*" wifi_step="*) [ -s fw-wifi/mac ] && args="$args wifi_mac=$(tr -d ' \n\r' < fw-wifi/mac)" ;;
		esac
		xnuloader/mkpayload.py -o run-payload.bin kernel=$K ${rd:+ramdisk=$rd} --cmdline "loader_return_after=${XL_SECS:-8} epoch=$(date +%s) sb_delay=${XL_SB_DELAY:-8} $args" >/dev/null || return 1
		FB_TIMEOUT=30 fb stage run-payload.bin | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: upload failed"; return 1; }
	fi
	local live=; live_loader && live=1
	fb $1 >/dev/null
	if [ -n "$live" ] && [ "$1" != "oem selftest" ]; then
		# the loader goes on answering: ask every two seconds until the result is no longer "running".
		# XL_FOLLOW=N: fetch the log as it stands every N seconds as well, so that a phone that
		# resets without a word leaves all it said up to then ($log.live)
		local XL_FOLLOW=${XL_FOLLOW-10}      # (a run that hangs leaves $log.live: what the kernel said up to a few seconds before)
		local deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + ${XL_SECS:-8} + 100 )) followed=$(date +%s)
		while :; do
			result=$(FB_TIMEOUT=15 fb getvar result | grep '^result:')
			case "$result" in ""|*running*) ;; *) break ;; esac
			[ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ] && { result=; break; }
			if [ -n "$XL_FOLLOW" ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - followed )) -ge "$XL_FOLLOW" ]; then
				followed=$(date +%s)
				# (XL_FOLLOW_KEEP=1: every one kept, $log.live.1, .2, ...: a long run's middle, which the log
				# itself loses once more than a megabyte follows it, is then all there)
				followed_n=$(( ${followed_n:-0} + 1 ))
				fb oem log | grep -q OKAY && fetch_log "$log.live" && { [ -z "$XL_FOLLOW_KEEP" ] || cp "$log.live" "$log.live.$followed_n"; }
			fi
			sleep 2
		done
	else
		result=$(FB_TIMEOUT=$(( ${XL_SECS:-8} + 100 )) fb getvar result | grep '^result:')
	fi
	if [ -z "$result" ]; then
		echo "xl: no answer — the kernel hung; waiting for the watchdog to reset the phone"
		[ -f "$log.live" ] && echo "xl: what the kernel said before it stopped answering: $log.live"
		recover_phone
		return 2
	fi
	fetch_log "$log"
	touch $PHONE.ran                # (this session of the loader has run its kernel: see fresh_session)
	ln -sf "$(basename "$log")" logs/last.log
	echo "$result  [$log]"
	case "$result" in
	*hung*|*no-such-core*)
		# (bootcpu=N) the kernel is stuck on the core it was given and nothing can take the core back
		echo "xl: the kernel did not come back from its core; restarting the phone"
		fb reboot >/dev/null
		return 2 ;;
	esac
	# XL_REBOOT_AFTER=1: the run is over and the phone goes back to Android, which charges it. A phone left in the loader
	# keeps its screen on and charges nothing, so a battery is flat by morning; for a run nobody waits for.
	if [ -n "$XL_REBOOT_AFTER" ]; then
		echo "xl: XL_REBOOT_AFTER: the phone goes back to Android (it charges there)"
		fb reboot >/dev/null
	fi
}

recording() { # recording [file.mp4]
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/recording.mp4}
	fb oem recording | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the last run left no recording (boot-arg rec_secs=N)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=120 fb get_staged logs/recording.raw >/dev/null
	# (XL_REC_KEEP=1: the recording itself stays in logs/recording.raw, for tools/recording.py --frames)
	tools/recording.py logs/recording.raw "$out" && { [ -n "$XL_REC_KEEP" ] || rm -f logs/recording.raw; }
}

sound() { # sound [file.wav]
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/sound.wav}
	fb oem sound | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the last run left no sound recording (boot-arg rec_sound=N)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=120 fb get_staged logs/sound.raw >/dev/null
	tools/sound.py logs/sound.raw "$out" && rm -f logs/sound.raw
}

camera() { # camera [prefix]: the frames the last run's camera left (boot-arg cam=3 and up), as pictures
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/camera}
	fb oem recording | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the last run left no frames (boot-arg cam=3)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=120 fb get_staged logs/camera.raw >/dev/null
	tools/camraw.py logs/camera.raw "$out"
}

ramdisk() { # ramdisk [<file>|none]
	enter || return 1
	if [ "$1" = none ]; then
		fb oem ramdisk none >/dev/null; rm -f $PHONE.ramdisk
		echo "xl: resident ramdisk dropped"; return
	fi
	set -- "${1:-userland/system.apfs}"
	[ -f "$1" ] || { echo "xl: $1 not found"; return 1; }
	local t0=$(date +%s) size=$(stat -c %s "$1")
	fb oem ramdisk | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the loader refused (no memory window?)"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=1800 fb stage "$1" | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: upload failed"; return 1; }
	local dt=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 )); [ $dt -lt 1 ] && dt=1
	echo "xl: $(( size / 1048576 )) MB uploaded in $dt s ($(( size / 1048576 / dt )) MB/s)"
	# Who put what there, for `run` to warn about below. The resident image is a third state of
	# the phone that neither the lock nor the note describes: it stays in memory across runs and
	# across working copies, so a run that uploads nothing boots against whatever the last upload
	# left -- which may be another copy's, of another kind. That cost two runs on 20 October, and
	# the only thing that distinguished them on sight was the loader's own "resident image at pa
	# ... size 400000" against "size 97308000". The size is recorded for exactly that reason: a
	# foreign image of the same kind is harmless, a foreign one of another kind kills the run and
	# says nothing.
	printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(pwd)" "$1" "$size" > $PHONE.ramdisk 2>/dev/null
}

screenshot() { # screenshot [file.png]
	enter || return 1
	local out=${1:-logs/screen.png} geom
	geom=$(fb getvar screen | sed -n 's/^screen: //p')
	[ -n "$geom" ] && fb oem screenshot | grep -q OKAY || { echo "xl: the loader has no display"; return 1; }
	FB_TIMEOUT=60 fb get_staged logs/screen.raw >/dev/null
	python3 - logs/screen.raw "$out" $geom <<'PY' && rm -f logs/screen.raw && echo "xl: $out ($geom)"
import struct, sys, zlib
raw, out, width, height, stride = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], *map(int, sys.argv[3:6])
data = open(raw, 'rb').read()
rows = bytearray()
for y in range(height):
    line = data[y * stride:y * stride + width * 4]
    rows.append(0)                                    # PNG filter type: none
    rgb = bytearray(width * 3)
    rgb[0::3], rgb[1::3], rgb[2::3] = line[2::4], line[1::4], line[0::4]   # the panel is BGRX
    rows += rgb
def chunk(kind, body):
    return struct.pack('>I', len(body)) + kind + body + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(kind + body))
with open(out, 'wb') as f:
    f.write(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) +
            chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(bytes(rows), 6)) + chunk(b'IEND', b''))
PY
}

# stop and reboot end a run. One that was started from another working copy is somebody else's work
# (an agent's measurement, a long session): not ended from here unless XL_FORCE=1 says so.
not_anothers_run() { # not_anothers_run <command>
	flock -n $PHONE.run true 2>/dev/null && return 0
	[ "$(cat $PHONE.who 2>/dev/null)" = "$(pwd)" ] || [ -n "$XL_FORCE" ] && return 0
	echo "xl: a run started from $(cat $PHONE.who 2>/dev/null) is in progress; XL_FORCE=1 ./xl $1 ends it all the same" >&2
	return 1
}

# While a run is in progress the loader takes only what does not disturb the kernel: state, screenshot,
# log, stop, reboot. Anything else would wait for nothing.
case "$1" in
""|run|selftest|state|screenshot|log|stop|reboot) ;;
*)	if ! flock -n $PHONE.run true 2>/dev/null; then
		echo "xl: a run is in progress: only state, screenshot, log, stop and reboot now" >&2; exit 1
	fi ;;
esac

case "$1" in
enter) enter && echo "xl: loader is up" ;;
screenshot) screenshot "$2" ;;
recording) recording "$2" ;;
camera) camera "$2" ;;
sound) sound "$2" ;;
ramdisk) ramdisk "$2" ;;
run) run "oem run $2" "run${2:+-cp$2}" ;;
selftest) run "oem selftest" selftest ;;
log) enter && fb oem log >/dev/null && fetch_log logs/loader.log && cat logs/loader.log ;;
stop) not_anothers_run stop && fb oem stop | grep -q OKAY && echo "xl: asked the kernel to come back" ;;
memmap) enter && fb oem memmap >/dev/null && fb oem log >/dev/null && fetch_log logs/loader.log && sed -n '/^memory map/,$p' logs/loader.log ;;
hang) enter && fb oem hang; echo "xl: waiting for the watchdog..."; t0=$(date +%s); wait_for android 150 && echo "xl: back in Android after $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) s" || echo "xl: not back (state: $(state))" ;;
reboot) not_anothers_run reboot && fb reboot ;;
reload) [ "$(state)" = loader ] && { fb reboot >/dev/null; wait_for android 120; }; enter && echo "xl: loader is up" ;;
state) state ;;
*) awk 'NR > 1 && /^#/ { print; next } NR > 1 { exit }' "$0" ;;
esac

```

`xnu-build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build XNU for redwood on Linux. Extra make args are passed through.
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/xnu-env.sh"
cd "$XNU_SRC" || exit 1
# The Wi-Fi driver's object (tools/mk-ath11k.sh) is linked into the kernel when it is there; make
# does not see it change, so the linked kernel is thrown away when it has.
LX=$XNUDEPS/build/ath11k/out/ath11k.o
# ... only into a kernel that has the Wi-Fi driver (CONFIG_HAKIOS_WIFI): the object's calls are answered by hakios.lx.c
if [ -f config/MASTER.hakios ] && ! grep -q '^#  HAKIOS_DRIVERS = \[.* hakios_wifi ' config/MASTER.hakios; then LX=/nonexistent; fi
STAMP=BUILD/obj/hakios-objects
mtime() { if [ "$XNU_HOST_OS" = Darwin ]; then stat -f %m "$1"; else stat -c %Y "$1"; fi; }
if [ -f "$LX" ]; then now="$LX $(mtime "$LX")"; else LX= now=; fi
# the build tools of SETUP/ are Apple's: on macOS they build as they are, on Linux with a compatibility header
if [ "$XNU_HOST_OS" = Darwin ]; then HOSTCC=clang; else
HOSTCC="clang -include $XNUDEPS/hostinc/hostcompat.h -I$XNUDEPS/hostinc -Wno-unused-command-line-argument -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration"; fi
if [ -d BUILD/obj ] && [ "$(cat $STAMP 2>/dev/null)" != "$now" ]; then
	rm -f BUILD/obj/*/mach.*.unstripped
	echo "$now" > $STAMP
fi
exec make HAKIOS_OBJECTS="$LX" SDKROOT=iphoneos ARCH_CONFIGS=ARM64 MACHINE_CONFIGS=${MACHINE:-BCM2837} KERNEL_CONFIGS=DEVELOPMENT \
  ARCH_STRING_FOR_CURRENT_MACHINE_CONFIG=arm64 BUILD_WERROR=0 BUILD_LTO=0 DO_CTFMERGE=0 \
  HOST_CC="$HOSTCC" HOST_FLEX=flex HOST_BISON=bison HOST_GM4=m4 CC=xnu-clang CXX=xnu-clang++ LOGCOLORS=n "$@"

```

`xnu-deps/build/lzbitmap/libzbitmap.c`:

```c
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0+ OR MIT
/*
 * Copyright (C) 2022 Corellium LLC
 *
 * Author: Ernesto A. Fernández <ernesto@corellium.com>
 *
 * Ported from libzbitmap (https://github.com/eafer/libzbitmap). Only the
 * decompression code is included.
 */

#include <errno.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "libzbitmap.h"

#define ZBM_MAGIC       "ZBM\x09"
#define ZBM_MAGIC_SZ    4

#define ZBM_MAX_DECMP_CHUNK_SIZE        0x8000
#define ZBM_MAX_DECMP_CHUNK_SIZE_BITS   15

struct uint24 {
    uint8_t     low;
    uint8_t     mid;
    uint8_t     hig;
};

/* This header is shared by both compressed and decompressed chunks */
struct zbm_chunk_hdr {
    struct uint24   len;        /* Length of the chunk */
    struct uint24   decmp_len;  /* Length of the chunk after decompression */
};

/* The full header for compressed chunks */
struct zbm_cmp_chunk_hdr {
    /* Shared with decompressed chunks */
    struct zbm_chunk_hdr hdr;

    /* Offset for each of the three metadata areas */
    struct uint24   meta_off_1;
    struct uint24   meta_off_2;
    struct uint24   meta_off_3;
};

/* Pointer to a half-byte */
struct nybl_ptr {
    uint8_t         *addr;  /* Address of the byte */
    int             nibble; /* Which of the two nibbles? */
};

/* 0-2 and 0xf are not real bitmap indexes */
#define ZBM_BITMAP_COUNT        (16 - 1 - 3)
#define ZBM_BITMAP_BASE         3
#define ZBM_BITMAP_BYTECNT      17
#define ZBM_MAX_PERIOD_BYTECNT  2

struct zbm_bmap {
    uint8_t     bitmap;         /* The bitmap */
    uint8_t     period_bytecnt; /* Read this many bytes to get the new period */
};

struct zbm_state {
    /* Updated during a chunk read */
    uint8_t         *dest;      /* Write the next byte here */
    size_t          dest_left;  /* Room left in destination buffer */
    uint32_t        written;    /* Bytes written so far for current chunk */
    uint16_t        period;     /* Repetition period for decompression, in bytes */

    /* Updated right before a chunk read */
    const uint8_t   *src_end;   /* End of current chunk */
    uint32_t        len;        /* Length of the chunk */
    uint32_t        decmp_len;  /* Expected chunk length after decompression */

    /* Updated after a chunk read */
    const uint8_t   *src;       /* Start of buffer, or current chunk if any */
    size_t          src_left;   /* Room left in the source buffer */
    size_t          prewritten; /* Bytes written for previous chunks */

    /* Current position in data and metadata areas for this chunk */
    const uint8_t   *data;
    const uint8_t   *meta_1;
    const uint8_t   *meta_2;
    struct nybl_ptr meta_3;

    /* Array of bitmaps for the current chunk */
    struct zbm_bmap bitmaps[ZBM_BITMAP_COUNT];
};

static int zbm_check_magic(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    if(state->src_left < ZBM_MAGIC_SZ)
        return -EINVAL;

    if(memcmp(state->src, ZBM_MAGIC, ZBM_MAGIC_SZ))
        return -EINVAL;

    state->src += ZBM_MAGIC_SZ;
    state->src_left -= ZBM_MAGIC_SZ;
    return 0;
}

static uint32_t zbm_u24_to_u32(struct uint24 n)
{
    uint32_t res;

    res = n.hig;
    res <<= 8;
    res += n.mid;
    res <<= 8;
    res += n.low;
    return res;
}

/* Some chunks just have regular uncompressed data, but with a header */
static int zbm_chunk_is_uncompressed(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    return state->len == state->decmp_len + sizeof(struct zbm_chunk_hdr);
}

static int zbm_handle_uncompressed_chunk(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    state->meta_1 = state->meta_2 = NULL;
    state->meta_3.addr = NULL;
    state->meta_3.nibble = 0;
    state->data = state->src + sizeof(struct zbm_chunk_hdr);
    memcpy(state->dest, state->data, state->decmp_len);

    state->dest += state->decmp_len;
    state->dest_left -= state->decmp_len;
    state->written = state->decmp_len;
    return 0;
}

static int zbm_read_nibble(struct nybl_ptr *nybl, const uint8_t *limit, uint8_t *result)
{
    if(nybl->addr >= limit)
        return -EINVAL;

    if(nybl->nibble == 0) {
        *result = *nybl->addr & 0xf;
        nybl->nibble = 1;
    } else {
        *result = (*nybl->addr >> 4) & 0xf;
        nybl->nibble = 0;
        ++nybl->addr;
    }
    return 0;
}

static void zbm_rewind_nibble(struct nybl_ptr *nybl)
{
    if(nybl->nibble == 0) {
        nybl->nibble = 1;
        --nybl->addr;
    } else {
        nybl->nibble = 0;
    }
}

static int zbm_apply_bitmap(struct zbm_state *state, struct zbm_bmap *bitmap)
{
    int i;

    /* The periods are stored in the first metadata area */
    if(bitmap->period_bytecnt) {
        state->period = 0;
        for(i = 0; i < bitmap->period_bytecnt; ++i) {
            if(state->meta_1 >= state->src_end)
                return -EINVAL;
            state->period |= *state->meta_1 << i * 8;
            ++state->meta_1;
        }
    }
    if(state->period == 0)
        return -EINVAL;

    for(i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
        if(state->written == state->decmp_len)
            break;
        if(bitmap->bitmap & 1 << i) {
            if(state->data >= state->src_end)
                return -EINVAL;
            *state->dest = *state->data;
            ++state->data;
        } else {
            if(state->prewritten + state->written < state->period)
                return -EINVAL;
            *state->dest = *(state->dest - state->period);
        }
        ++state->dest;
        --state->dest_left;
        ++state->written;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int zbm_apply_bitmap_number(struct zbm_state *state, uint8_t bmp_num)
{
    struct zbm_bmap next = {0};

    /* Not a valid bitmap number (it signals a repetition) */
    if(bmp_num == 0xf)
        return -EINVAL;

    /* An actual index in the bitmap array */
    if(bmp_num > ZBM_MAX_PERIOD_BYTECNT)
        return zbm_apply_bitmap(state, &state->bitmaps[bmp_num - ZBM_BITMAP_BASE]);

    /* For < 2, use the next bitmap in the second metadata area */
    if(state->meta_2 >= state->src_end)
        return -EINVAL;
    next.bitmap = *state->meta_2;
    next.period_bytecnt = bmp_num;
    ++state->meta_2;
    return zbm_apply_bitmap(state, &next);
}

/* Find out how many times we need to repeat the current bitmap operation */
static int zbm_read_repetition_count(struct zbm_state *state, uint16_t *repeat)
{
    uint8_t nibble;
    uint16_t total;
    int err;

    /* Don't confuse the trailing bitmaps with a repetition count */
    if(state->decmp_len - state->written <= 8) {
        *repeat = 1;
        return 0;
    }

    err = zbm_read_nibble(&state->meta_3, state->src_end, &nibble);
    if(err)
        return err;

    if(nibble != 0xf) {
        /* No repetition count: the previous bitmap number gets applied once */
        zbm_rewind_nibble(&state->meta_3);
        *repeat = 1;
        return 0;
    }

    /*
     * Under this scheme, repeating a bitmap number 3 times wouldn't save any
     * space, so the repetition count starts from 4.
     */
    total = 4;
    while(nibble == 0xf) {
        err = zbm_read_nibble(&state->meta_3, state->src_end, &nibble);
        if(err)
            return err;
        total += nibble;
        if(total < nibble)
            return -EINVAL;
    }

    *repeat = total;
    return 0;
}

static int zbm_decompress_single_bitmap(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    uint8_t bmp_num;
    uint16_t repeat;
    int i;
    int err;

    /* The current nibble is the offset of the next bitmap to apply */
    err = zbm_read_nibble(&state->meta_3, state->src_end, &bmp_num);
    if(err)
        return err;

    err = zbm_read_repetition_count(state, &repeat);
    if(err)
        return err;

    for(i = 0; i < repeat; ++i) {
        err = zbm_apply_bitmap_number(state, bmp_num);
        if(err)
            return err;
    }
    return 0;
}

/* Pointer to a bit */
struct bit_ptr {
    uint8_t         *addr;  /* Address of the byte */
    int             offset; /* Bit number */
};

/* This function does not perform boundary checks, the caller must do it */
static int zbm_read_single_bit(struct bit_ptr *bit)
{
    int res = *bit->addr >> bit->offset & 1;

    ++bit->offset;
    if(bit->offset != 8)
        return res;
    bit->offset = 0;
    ++bit->addr;
    return res;
}

static int zbm_read_single_bitmap(struct bit_ptr *bit, const uint8_t *limit, struct zbm_bmap *result)
{
    int i;

    result->bitmap = 0;
    result->period_bytecnt = 0;

    /* The bitmap itself */
    for(i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
        if(bit->addr >= limit)
            return -EINVAL;
        result->bitmap |= zbm_read_single_bit(bit) << i;
    }

    /*
     * The two trailing bits tell us how many bytes to read for the next
     * repetition period
     */
    for(i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
        if(bit->addr >= limit)
            return -EINVAL;
        result->period_bytecnt |= zbm_read_single_bit(bit) << i;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int zbm_read_bitmaps(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    struct bit_ptr bmap = {0};
    int err, i;

    if(state->len < ZBM_BITMAP_BYTECNT)
        return -EINVAL;

    bmap.addr = (uint8_t *)state->src_end - ZBM_BITMAP_BYTECNT;
    bmap.offset = 0;

    for(i = 0; i < ZBM_BITMAP_COUNT; ++i) {
        err = zbm_read_single_bitmap(&bmap, state->src_end, &state->bitmaps[i]);
        if(err)
            return err;
        if(state->bitmaps[i].period_bytecnt > ZBM_MAX_PERIOD_BYTECNT)
            return -EINVAL;
    }
    return 0;
}

static int zbm_handle_compressed_chunk(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    const struct zbm_cmp_chunk_hdr *hdr = NULL;
    uint32_t meta_off_1, meta_off_2, meta_off_3;
    int err;

    state->written = 0;
    state->period = 8;

    if(state->len < sizeof(*hdr))
        return -EINVAL;
    hdr = (struct zbm_cmp_chunk_hdr *)state->src;
    state->data = state->src + sizeof(*hdr);

    meta_off_1 = zbm_u24_to_u32(hdr->meta_off_1);
    meta_off_2 = zbm_u24_to_u32(hdr->meta_off_2);
    meta_off_3 = zbm_u24_to_u32(hdr->meta_off_3);
    if(meta_off_1 >= state->len || meta_off_2 >= state->len || meta_off_3 >= state->len)
        return -EINVAL;
    state->meta_1 = state->src + meta_off_1;
    state->meta_2 = state->src + meta_off_2;
    state->meta_3.addr = (uint8_t *)state->src + meta_off_3;
    state->meta_3.nibble = 0;

    err = zbm_read_bitmaps(state);
    if(err)
        return err;

    while(state->written < state->decmp_len) {
        err = zbm_decompress_single_bitmap(state);
        if(err)
            return err;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int zbm_handle_chunk(struct zbm_state *state)
{
    const struct zbm_chunk_hdr *decmp_hdr = NULL;

    if(state->src_left < sizeof(*decmp_hdr))
        return -EINVAL;
    decmp_hdr = (struct zbm_chunk_hdr *)state->src;

    state->len = zbm_u24_to_u32(decmp_hdr->len);
    if(state->len > state->src_left)
        return -EINVAL;
    state->src_end = state->src + state->len;

    state->decmp_len = zbm_u24_to_u32(decmp_hdr->decmp_len);
    if(state->decmp_len > ZBM_MAX_DECMP_CHUNK_SIZE)
        return -EINVAL;
    if(!state->dest) /* We just wanted the length, so we are done */
        return 0;
    if(state->decmp_len > state->dest_left)
        return -ERANGE;

    if(zbm_chunk_is_uncompressed(state))
        return zbm_handle_uncompressed_chunk(state);

    return zbm_handle_compressed_chunk(state);
}

int zbm_decompress(void *dest, size_t dest_size, const void *src, size_t src_size, size_t *out_len)
{
    struct zbm_state state = {0};
    int err;

    state.src = src;
    state.src_left = src_size;
    state.dest = dest;
    state.dest_left = dest_size;
    state.prewritten = 0;

    err = zbm_check_magic(&state);
    if(err)
        return err;

    /* The final chunk has zero decompressed length */
    do {
        err = zbm_handle_chunk(&state);
        if(err)
            return err;
        state.src += state.len;
        state.src_left -= state.len;
        state.prewritten += state.decmp_len;
    } while(state.decmp_len != 0);

    *out_len = state.prewritten;
    return 0;
}

```

`xnu-deps/build/lzbitmap/unzbm.c`:

```c
/*
 * unzbm: finish what 7z leaves undone for files compressed with LZBITMAP.
 *
 * 7z extracts such a file from an APFS image as an empty file plus its two
 * attributes, "NAME:com.apple.decmpfs" (the compression header) and
 * "NAME:com.apple.ResourceFork" (the compressed data, in 64K blocks behind a
 * table of offsets). For every NAME given, this writes the real contents and
 * removes the two attribute files.
 *
 * The decompressor is libzbitmap (Ernesto A. Fernandez, GPL-2.0+ OR MIT),
 * as shipped with the linux-apfs-rw driver.
 */
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "libzbitmap.h"

#define BLOCK 0x10000u
#define LZBITMAP_RSRC 14

static uint8_t *
slurp(const char *path, size_t *size)
{
	FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
	uint8_t *data;

	if (!f) {
		return NULL;
	}
	fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
	*size = (size_t)ftell(f);
	rewind(f);
	data = malloc(*size + 1);
	if (fread(data, 1, *size, f) != *size) {
		free(data);
		data = NULL;
	}
	fclose(f);
	return data;
}

static uint32_t
le32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return p[0] | p[1] << 8 | p[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[3] << 24;
}

static int
expand(const char *name)
{
	char header_path[4096], fork_path[4096];
	size_t header_size, fork_size;
	uint8_t *header, *fork, *out;
	uint64_t size, blocks;
	FILE *f;

	snprintf(header_path, sizeof(header_path), "%s:com.apple.decmpfs", name);
	snprintf(fork_path, sizeof(fork_path), "%s:com.apple.ResourceFork", name);
	header = slurp(header_path, &header_size);
	fork = slurp(fork_path, &fork_size);
	if (!header || !fork || header_size < 16 || memcmp(header, "fpmc", 4) != 0 || le32(header + 4) != LZBITMAP_RSRC) {
		fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: not an LZBITMAP resource-fork file\n", name);
		return 1;
	}
	size = le32(header + 8) | (uint64_t)le32(header + 12) << 32;
	blocks = (size + BLOCK - 1) / BLOCK;
	if ((blocks + 1) * 4 > fork_size) {
		fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: block table does not fit\n", name);
		return 1;
	}
	out = malloc(size ? size : 1);
	for (uint64_t b = 0; b < blocks; b++) {
		uint32_t from = le32(fork + 4 * b), to = le32(fork + 4 * (b + 1));
		size_t want = size - b * BLOCK > BLOCK ? BLOCK : (size_t)(size - b * BLOCK), got = 0;

		/* a block that did not shrink is stored as it is behind one byte, 0xff */
		if (from < to && to <= fork_size && to - from == want + 1 && fork[from] == 0xff) {
			memcpy(out + b * BLOCK, fork + from + 1, want);
			continue;
		}
		if (from > to || to > fork_size || zbm_decompress(out + b * BLOCK, want, fork + from, to - from, &got) != 0 ||
		    got != want) {
			fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: block %llu does not decompress\n", name, (unsigned long long)b);
			return 1;
		}
	}
	f = fopen(name, "wb");
	if (!f || fwrite(out, 1, size, f) != size || fclose(f) != 0) {
		fprintf(stderr, "unzbm: %s: %s\n", name, strerror(errno));
		return 1;
	}
	unlink(header_path);
	unlink(fork_path);
	free(out);
	free(fork);
	free(header);
	return 0;
}

int
main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int failed = 0;

	for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
		failed += expand(argv[i]);
	}
	return failed != 0;
}

```

`xnu-deps/build/pthread/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the open-source pthread kernel extension (libpthread/kern) as a static
# library that gets linked into the XNU kernel image (there is no kext loader
# in this setup). Requires an XNU build tree for the exported kernel headers.
set -e
# The two -D renames below avoid clashes with kernel symbols of the same name:
# as a real kext these live in a separate link unit.
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
source ../../../xnu-env.sh
X=$XNU_SRC; E=$X/BUILD/obj/EXPORT_HDRS; P=$XNUDEPS/libpthread
[ -d $E/osfmk ] || { echo "pthread kext: no exported kernel headers in $E (run: xnu-build.sh exporthdrs)" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel
for f in kern_init kern_support kern_synch; do
  xnu-clang -arch arm64 -c -Os -mkernel -nostdinc -fno-builtin -fno-common -Wno-int-conversion \
    -DKERNEL=1 -DKERNEL_PRIVATE=1 -DPRIVATE=1 -D__PTHREAD_EXPOSE_INTERNALS__=1 -Dpthread_kern=pthread_kext_kern -Dcurrent_uthread=pthread_kext_current_uthread -D__DARWIN_64_BIT_INO_T=1 -DARM64_BOARD_CONFIG_BCM2837 \
    -Iinc -I$P -I$E/osfmk -I$E/bsd -I$E/libkern -I$E/pexpert -I$E/iokit -I$E/security -I$X/EXTERNAL_HEADERS \
    -I$P/include -I$P/private -o pthread_$f.o $P/kern/$f.c
done
libtool -static -o $XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel/libpthread_kext.a pthread_kern_init.o pthread_kern_support.o pthread_kern_synch.o
ls -la $XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel/libpthread_kext.a

`xnu-deps/gen-iig-stubs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate stand-in DriverKit implementation files for the XNU build.

Apple's `iig` tool (closed source) normally generates <Class>.iig.cpp: the RPC
marshalling for DriverKit (user-space driver) interfaces. Without it the kernel
fails to link. This script reads the linker's undefined-symbol list and emits:
  * metaclass definitions for classes that only exist as DriverKit interfaces
  * a stub returning kIOReturnUnsupported for every remaining generated method
The kernel then links and runs; user-space DriverKit drivers are non-functional.

usage: gen-iig-stubs.py <undefined.txt> <outdir> [kernel-symbols (nm -n output)]
"""
import re, sys, os

undefined = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if l.strip()]
outdir = sys.argv[2]

# class -> superclass, for classes whose OSMetaClass the generated code owns
META = {
    'IODispatchSource': ('OSObject', True),
    'IOEventLink': ('OSObject', False),
    'IOWorkGroup': ('OSObject', False),
    'IODispatchQueue': ('OSObject', False),
    'OSAction': ('OSObject', False),
    'IODataQueueDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
    'IOInterruptDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
    'IOServiceNotificationDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
    'IOServiceStateNotificationDispatchSource': ('IODispatchSource', False),
}

meta_needed, funcs = [], []
for sym in undefined:
    m = re.match(r'__ZN(\d+)', sym)
    if not m:
        continue
    n = int(m.group(1)); cls = sym[len(m.group(0)):len(m.group(0)) + n]
    if sym.endswith('9metaClassE') and sym == '__ZN%d%s9metaClassE' % (n, cls):
        meta_needed.append(cls)
    else:
        funcs.append(sym)
vt = [s for s in undefined if s.startswith('__ZTV')]

out = ['/* Generated by gen-iig-stubs.py: stand-in for iig output. Do not edit. */',
       '#include <IOKit/IOLib.h>', '#include <IOKit/IOReturn.h>', '#include <IOKit/IOService.h>',
       '#include <IOKit/IOUserClient.h>', '#include <IOKit/IOUserServer.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IODispatchSource.h>', '#include <DriverKit/IODispatchQueue.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IOEventLink.h>', '#include <DriverKit/IOWorkGroup.h>', '#include <DriverKit/OSAction.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IODataQueueDispatchSource.h>', '#include <DriverKit/IOInterruptDispatchSource.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IOServiceNotificationDispatchSource.h>',
       '#include <DriverKit/IOServiceStateNotificationDispatchSource.h>', '']
want = set(meta_needed)
if any(META.get(c, ('', 0))[0] == 'IODispatchSource' for c in want) or vt:
    want.add('IODispatchSource')
for cls, (sup, abstract) in META.items():
    if cls in want:
        macro = 'OSDefineMetaClassAndAbstractStructors' if abstract else 'OSDefineMetaClassAndStructors'
        out.append('%s(%s, %s);' % (macro, cls, sup))
out.append('')
# Kernel-implemented methods: the real generated wrapper marshals the call into
# an RPC and dispatches it back to Class::Method_Impl(). For objects that live
# in the kernel that round trip is equivalent to calling _Impl directly, and
# the kernel itself relies on it (e.g. IOService::StateNotificationItemCreate).
# The wrapper only has one extra trailing argument (the "supermethod"), so a
# tail branch is argument-compatible on arm64.
SUPER = 'PFiP15OSMetaClassBase5IORPCE'
defined = set()
if len(sys.argv) > 3:
    for line in open(sys.argv[3]):
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1] in 'tTsS':  # kernel text lives in __TEXT_EXEC, which nm reports as 'S'
            defined.add(parts[2])

def impl_name(sym):
    m = re.match(r'__ZN(\d+)', sym)
    if not m or not sym.endswith(SUPER):
        return None
    pos = len(m.group(0)) + int(m.group(1))
    m2 = re.match(r'(\d+)', sym[pos:])
    if not m2:
        return None
    mlen = int(m2.group(1)); mstart = pos + len(m2.group(1))
    method = sym[mstart:mstart + mlen]
    rest = sym[mstart + mlen:]
    if not rest.startswith('E'):
        return None
    params = rest[1:-len(SUPER)] or 'v'
    return '%s%d%s_ImplE%s' % (sym[:pos], mlen + 5, method, params)

direct, unsupported = [], []
for sym in sorted(set(funcs)):
    impl = impl_name(sym)
    if impl and impl in defined:
        direct.append((sym, impl))
    else:
        unsupported.append(sym)

out.append('/* wrappers forwarded straight to their kernel implementation */')
for sym, impl in direct:
    out.append('__asm__(".text\\n.globl %s\\n.p2align 2\\n%s:\\n\\tb %s\\n");' % (sym, sym, impl))
out.append('')
out.append('/* everything else (RPC dispatch, user-space-only methods) is not available */')
out.append('extern "C" {')
for i, sym in enumerate(unsupported):
    # sym carries the Mach-O leading underscore already
    out.append('kern_return_t __iig_stub_%d(void) __asm__("%s");' % (i, sym))
    out.append('kern_return_t __iig_stub_%d(void) { return kIOReturnUnsupported; }' % i)
out.append('}')
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
open(os.path.join(outdir, 'OSObject.iig.cpp'), 'w').write('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
print('metaclasses:', len(want), 'forwarded to _Impl:', len(direct), 'unsupported stubs:', len(unsupported))

```

`xnu-deps/host/bin/iig`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# Stand-in for Apple's closed-source iig (DriverKit interface generator).
# Headers: taken pre-generated from the macOS 13.3 SDK (same xnu-8796 family).
# Implementation: taken from $XNUDEPS/iig-impl/<name>.iig.cpp if present, else an empty TU.
XNUDEPS=${XNUDEPS:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)}
SDKH="$XNUDEPS/MacOSX13.3.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/Kernel.framework/Headers"
def=""; hdr=""; impl=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
  --def) def="$2"; shift 2;; --header) hdr="$2"; shift 2;; --impl) impl="$2"; shift 2;;
  --) break;; *) shift;; esac; done
name="$(basename "$def" .iig)"
src="$(find "$SDKH" -name "$name.h" -path '*DriverKit*' | head -1)"
[ -z "$src" ] && src="$(find "$SDKH" -name "$name.h" | xargs grep -l 'iig(DriverKit' 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -z "$src" ]; then echo "iig shim: no pre-generated header for $name" >&2; exit 1; fi
cp "$src" "$hdr"
if [ -f "$XNUDEPS/iig-impl/$name.iig.cpp" ]; then cp "$XNUDEPS/iig-impl/$name.iig.cpp" "$impl"
else echo "/* $name: no DriverKit implementation generated (iig shim) */" > "$impl"; fi

```

`xnu-deps/host/bin/xcrun`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# Minimal xcrun replacement for building XNU on Linux
HB="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# On macOS the host side (the SDK and tools the build tools of SETUP/ are made with) is the real
# xcrun's business; only the kernel's own SDK is ours.
case " $* " in *" -sdk macosx"*) [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ] && exec /usr/bin/xcrun "$@" ;; esac
sdk=""; find=""; show=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
  -sdk) sdk="$2"; shift 2;; -verbose) shift;;
  -find|--find|-f) find="$2"; shift 2;;
  -show-sdk-path|--show-sdk-path) show=path; shift;;
  -show-sdk-version|--show-sdk-version) show=version; shift;;
  -show-sdk-platform-path|--show-sdk-platform-path) show=platform; shift;;
  -show-sdk-platform-version) show=version; shift;;
  *) break;; esac; done
SDKP="${XNU_SDK_PATH:?XNU_SDK_PATH not set}"
case "$show" in
  path) case "$sdk" in /*) echo "$sdk";; *) echo "$SDKP";; esac; exit 0;;
  version) echo "${XNU_SDK_VERSION:-16.5}"; exit 0;;
  platform) echo "${XNU_PLATFORM_PATH:-/Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform}"; exit 0;;
esac
if [ -n "$find" ]; then
  for d in "$HB" /usr/bin; do [ -x "$d/$find" ] && { echo "$d/$find"; exit 0; }; done
  [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ] && exec /usr/bin/xcrun -find "$find"
  exit 1
fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] && exec "$@"

```

`xnu-deps/host/bin/xnu-clang`:

```
#!/bin/bash
# clang wrapper for cross-building XNU on Linux:
#  - forces an Apple Mach-O target (stock Linux clang defaults to ELF)
#  - drops flags only Apple's clang understands
#  - links with the cctools ld64
HB="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
case "$(basename "$0")" in *++) drv=clang++; extra=(-fno-use-cxa-atexit);; *) drv=clang; extra=();; esac
args=()
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -enable-trivial-auto-var-init-zero-knowing-it-will-be-removed-from-clang) ;;
    -fapple-kext-vtable-verify|-Wno-vla-cxx-extension) ;;
    -Werror|-Werror=*|-Weverything|-pedantic-errors) ;;
    *) args+=("$a");;
  esac
done
exec /usr/bin/$drv -include "$HB/../../hostinc/xnu_clang_compat.h" -target arm64-apple-ios${XNU_SDK_VERSION:-16.5} --ld-path="$HB/ld64" \
  -w "${extra[@]}" "${args[@]}"

`xnu-deps/hostinc/copyfile.h`:

```h
#ifndef HOST_COPYFILE_H
#define HOST_COPYFILE_H
#include <unistd.h>
#define COPYFILE_DATA 8
typedef void *copyfile_state_t;
static inline int fcopyfile(int from, int to, copyfile_state_t s, unsigned flags) {
	char buf[65536]; ssize_t n;
	(void)s; (void)flags;
	while ((n = read(from, buf, sizeof buf)) > 0) {
		char *p = buf; while (n > 0) { ssize_t w = write(to, p, n); if (w < 0) return -1; p += w; n -= w; }
	}
	return n < 0 ? -1 : 0;
}
#endif

`xnu-deps/hostinc/xnu_clang_compat.h`:

```h
/*
 * Force-included into every XNU translation unit when building with stock
 * (non-Apple) clang. Apple's clang has builtins that describe the pointer/data
 * layout of a type for kalloc_type; upstream clang lacks them, so every type
 * is conservatively described as "mixed pointers and data".
 */
#ifndef XNU_CLANG_COMPAT_H
#define XNU_CLANG_COMPAT_H
#if !defined(ASSEMBLER) && !defined(__ASSEMBLER__)
#if !__has_builtin(__builtin_xnu_type_signature)
#define XNU_NO_TYPE_BUILTINS                     1
#define __builtin_xnu_type_signature(type)       "12"
#define __builtin_xnu_type_summary(type)         ((1U << 1) | (1U << 2))
#ifdef __cplusplus
#define __builtin_xnu_types_compatible(a, b)     __is_same(a, b)
#else
#define __builtin_xnu_types_compatible(a, b)     __builtin_types_compatible_p(a, b)
#endif
#else
#define XNU_NO_TYPE_BUILTINS                     0       /* Apple's clang: the real ones */
#endif
#endif
#endif

```

`xnu-deps/setup.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Everything the kernel build needs that this repository does not carry: open sources of
# Apple's and others' that are fetched and built here, and the SDK the kernel is compiled
# against. What is already there is left alone, so this can be run again at any time.
#
#   xnu-deps/setup.sh             both stages (the second only once the kernel tree exists)
#   xnu-deps/setup.sh --stage1    sources, host tools, the SDK
#   xnu-deps/setup.sh --stage2    the two static libraries that are compiled against the
#                                 kernel's own exported headers (needs xnu/apply.sh first)
#   xnu-deps/setup.sh --rebuild-libs   stage 2 again from scratch (after the kernel headers changed)
#
# Needs on the machine: git curl tar xz make cc clang flex bison m4 perl python3 autoconf
# automake, and theos ($THEOS, default ~/theos) with its Linux toolchain
# (toolchain/linux/iphone: the cctools linker) and sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk.
#
# What ends up where (all under xnu-deps/, none of it committed):
#   AvailabilityVersions libdispatch libpthread     Apple open source, at the releases of Darwin userland 16.5
#   mm_bootstrap_cmds tcsh unifdef                  sources of mig, csh and unifdef
#   MacOSX13.3.sdk                                  only Kernel.framework: the DriverKit headers
#                                                   that Apple's closed "iig" would generate
#   host/bin                                        mig, migcom, unifdef, tcsh, csh, unzbm, and links
#                                                   to the cctools (next to our own wrappers)
#   sdk/iPhoneOS16.5.xnu.sdk                        the theos SDK (as links) plus usr/local: what
#                                                   Apple's internal SDK has and the public one lacks
set -e -o pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
source "$HERE/../xnu-env.sh"
cd "$XNUDEPS"
JOBS=${JOBS:-$(nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu)}
CCTOOLS=$THEOS/toolchain/linux/iphone/bin
DARWIN_SDK=$THEOS/sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk
MACOS_SDK_URL=https://github.com/joseluisq/macosx-sdks/releases/download/13.3/MacOSX13.3.sdk.tar.xz

log() { echo "setup: $*"; }
die() { echo "setup: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# fetch DIR URL COMMIT: one commit of a repository, without its history
fetch() {
	# there already? (its own repository, not the one this directory is part of)
	[ -d "$1" ] && git -C "$1" rev-parse -q --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
		[ "$(git -C "$1" rev-parse --show-toplevel)" = "$(cd "$1" && pwd -P)" ] && return 0
	log "fetching $1"
	rm -rf "$1"
	git init -q "$1"
	git -C "$1" remote add origin "$2"
	git -C "$1" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$3" || die "cannot fetch $3 from $2"
	git -C "$1" -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
}

# link TARGET NAME: a symbolic link, made only when it is not there already
link() {
	[ "$(readlink "$2" 2>/dev/null)" = "$1" ] || ln -sfn "$1" "$2"
}

# replace FILE with what is on standard input, unless it is the same already (make looks at time stamps)
update() {
	cat > "$1.new"
	if cmp -s "$1.new" "$1"; then rm "$1.new"; else mv "$1.new" "$1"; fi
}

# macOS: no theos, but Xcode has the same cctools and the SDK can be had from github.com/theos/sdks.
# theos-mac/ is laid out like theos so that the rest of this script does not care.
theos_mac() {
	local tool
	mkdir -p "$THEOS/toolchain/linux/iphone/bin" "$THEOS/sdks"
	for tool in ld nm otool strip lipo libtool nmedit ctf_insert codesign_allocate install_name_tool; do
		link "$(/usr/bin/xcrun -f $tool)" "$THEOS/toolchain/linux/iphone/bin/$tool"
	done
	if [ ! -d "$THEOS/sdks-git/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk/usr/include" ]; then
		log "fetching iPhoneOS16.5.sdk from github.com/theos/sdks (about 220 MB)"
		rm -rf "$THEOS/sdks-git"
		git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/theos/sdks.git "$THEOS/sdks-git" &&
			git -C "$THEOS/sdks-git" sparse-checkout set iPhoneOS16.5.sdk || die "cannot fetch the SDK"
	fi
	link ../sdks-git/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk "$THEOS/sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk"
}

# linktree FROM TO: TO becomes a tree of links to the files of FROM (cp -rs, which BSD cp lacks)
linktree() {
	if [ "$XNU_HOST_OS" = Darwin ]; then
		python3 - "$1" "$2" <<-'PY'
		import os, sys
		src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
		for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src):
		    rel = os.path.relpath(root, src)
		    out = dst if rel == '.' else os.path.join(dst, rel)
		    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
		    for name in files:
		        os.symlink(os.path.join(root, name), os.path.join(out, name))
		PY
	else
		cp -rs "$1" "$2"
	fi
}

stage1() {
	local missing= tool
	local tools="git curl tar xz make cc clang clang++ flex bison m4 perl python3 autoreconf automake"
	[ "$XNU_HOST_OS" = Darwin ] && { theos_mac; tools="git curl tar make cc clang clang++ flex bison m4 perl python3"; }
	for tool in $tools; do
		command -v $tool >/dev/null || missing="$missing $tool"
	done
	[ -z "$missing" ] || die "not installed:$missing"
	[ -x "$CCTOOLS/ld" ] || die "no cctools in $CCTOOLS: install theos with its Linux toolchain (or set THEOS)"
	[ -d "$DARWIN_SDK/usr/include" ] || die "no $DARWIN_SDK (the SDKs of github.com/theos/sdks go to \$THEOS/sdks)"

	# --- sources -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	fetch AvailabilityVersions https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/AvailabilityVersions.git \
		5d9baee345b3bc72b26c71adc65f94f2d5e9ced2        # AvailabilityVersions-115.4
	fetch libdispatch https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/libdispatch.git \
		a641558f447659d90ad002ef0ee6f0212273fbfc        # libdispatch-1415.100.11
	fetch libpthread https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/libpthread.git \
		a6c70ca0e544347a0377babf748f831577ec24f9        # libpthread-514.100.2
	fetch mm_bootstrap_cmds https://github.com/markmentovai/bootstrap_cmds \
		f337e600741638896fb6056ce87c6479f74b89a3        # cross_platform/bootstrap_cmds-138
	fetch tcsh https://github.com/tcsh-org/tcsh.git b7db07931546178c4cb2542b5fc850c483628ed5
	fetch unifdef https://github.com/fanf2/unifdef.git 08d12cd3059fe072929ea001ad9833f5487fd355

	# Apple's iig (the DriverKit interface generator) is closed. host/bin/iig hands out the headers it
	# would generate, which the macOS SDK of the same XNU release ships ready-made.
	if [ ! -d MacOSX13.3.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/Kernel.framework/Headers/DriverKit ]; then
		log "downloading the macOS 13.3 SDK for its DriverKit headers"
		curl -L --fail --retry 3 -s -o macos-sdk.tar.xz "$MACOS_SDK_URL" || die "download failed: $MACOS_SDK_URL"
		local wild=--wildcards; [ "$XNU_HOST_OS" = Darwin ] && wild=        # bsdtar: patterns as they are
		tar -xJf macos-sdk.tar.xz $wild '*MacOSX13.3.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/Kernel.framework*' ||
			die "cannot unpack the macOS SDK"
		rm -f macos-sdk.tar.xz
	fi

	# --- host tools ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
	mkdir -p host/bin
	if [ "$XNU_HOST_OS" = Darwin ]; then
		# macOS has it all: mig (Xcode's; it takes $MIGCC and $MIGCOM from the kernel build), unifdef, csh
		link "$(/usr/bin/xcrun -f mig)" host/bin/mig
		# with the command-line tools alone, migcom is in usr/libexec, where xcrun does not look (and xcrun must not find
		# host/bin's own link on the PATH)
		migcom=$(xcode-select -p)/usr/libexec/migcom
		[ -x "$migcom" ] || migcom=$(PATH=/usr/bin:/bin /usr/bin/xcrun -f migcom)
		link "$migcom" host/bin/migcom
		link /usr/bin/unifdef host/bin/unifdef
		link /bin/tcsh host/bin/tcsh
		# what XNU's makefiles call by Linux's names: GNU's nproc (MakeInc.cmd's job count) and python
		printf '#!/bin/sh\n# nproc as GNU coreutils has it, on macOS\nexec sysctl -n hw.ncpu\n' | update host/bin/nproc
		chmod +x host/bin/nproc
		# (a script, not a link: /usr/bin/python3 is a shim that looks for the tool its own name says, and "python" there is none)
		rm -f host/bin/python
		printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec python3 "$@"\n' | update host/bin/python
		chmod +x host/bin/python
	fi
	# mig: Apple's own does not build on glibc; this is a port that does
	if [ ! -x host/bin/migcom ] || [ ! -x host/bin/mig ]; then
		log "building mig"
		(cd mm_bootstrap_cmds && autoreconf --install && sh configure --prefix="$XNUDEPS/host" &&
			make -j$JOBS && make install) > mig-build.log 2>&1 || die "mig did not build, see xnu-deps/mig-build.log"
	fi
	if [ ! -x host/bin/unifdef ]; then
		log "building unifdef"
		# its makefile takes the version from the git history; any text will do
		[ -f unifdef/version.h ] || printf '"@(#) $Version: unifdef-2.12 $\\n"\n"@(#) $Date: 2020-11-06 11:22:51 +0000 $\\n"\n' > unifdef/version.h
		# gnu11: "constexpr", a variable name in unifdef.c, is a keyword in C23
		cc -std=gnu11 -O2 -w -o host/bin/unifdef unifdef/unifdef.c
	fi
	# csh: XNU's SETUP/config/doconf is a csh script
	if [ ! -x host/bin/tcsh ]; then
		log "building tcsh"
		(cd tcsh && ./configure --prefix="$XNUDEPS/host" && make -j$JOBS) > tcsh-build.log 2>&1 ||
			die "tcsh did not build, see xnu-deps/tcsh-build.log"
		cp tcsh/tcsh host/bin/tcsh
	fi
	link tcsh host/bin/csh
	# what 7z leaves undone when it extracts files of the Darwin images (see build/lzbitmap/unzbm.c)
	if [ ! -x host/bin/unzbm ]; then
		cc -O2 -w -o host/bin/unzbm build/lzbitmap/unzbm.c build/lzbitmap/libzbitmap.c
	fi
	# the Mach-O linker and its companions come with theos
	for tool in nm otool strip lipo libtool nmedit ctf_insert codesign_allocate install_name_tool; do
		link "$CCTOOLS/$tool" host/bin/$tool
	done
	if [ "$XNU_HOST_OS" = Darwin ]; then
		# (not a link: Xcode's ld looks itself up by the name it was called by, and knows no "ld64")
		printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec "%s" "$@"\n' "$(/usr/bin/xcrun -f ld)" > host/bin/ld64.new && chmod +x host/bin/ld64.new && mv host/bin/ld64.new host/bin/ld64
	else
		link "$CCTOOLS/ld" host/bin/ld64
	fi
	link xnu-clang host/bin/xnu-clang++

	# --- the SDK -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	# The makefiles ask xcrun (ours: host/bin/xcrun) for an SDK and a platform directory.
	mkdir -p sdk/Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform
	if [ ! -d "$XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/include" ]; then
		log "making the SDK: links to $DARWIN_SDK"
		rm -rf "$XNU_SDK_PATH"
		linktree "$(cd "$DARWIN_SDK" && pwd -P)" "$XNU_SDK_PATH"
	fi
	local sdk_local=$XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local
	mkdir -p $sdk_local/include/kernel/os $sdk_local/include/os $sdk_local/lib/kernel $sdk_local/libexec
	update $sdk_local/libexec/availability.pl < AvailabilityVersions/availability.pl
	[ -x $sdk_local/libexec/availability.pl ] || chmod +x $sdk_local/libexec/availability.pl
	# the kernel's half of a private libdispatch header (unifdef exits with 1 when it removed something)
	{ host/bin/unifdef -DOS_FIREHOSE_SPI=1 -DKERNEL=1 libdispatch/os/firehose_buffer_private.h || [ $? -eq 1 ]; } |
		update $sdk_local/include/kernel/os/firehose_buffer_private.h
	update $sdk_local/include/kernel/os/firehose_types.defs < libdispatch/src/firehose/firehose_types.defs
	log "stage 1 done"
}

# The firehose (os_log) buffer code of libdispatch and the pthread kernel extension are open
# source but not part of XNU: Apple links the first from its internal SDK and loads the second
# as a kext. Here both become static libraries in the SDK (makedefs/MakeInc.def links them into
# the kernel). They are compiled against the headers the kernel build exports, so that step
# of the kernel build comes first.
stage2() {
	[ -f "$XNU_SRC/makedefs/MakeInc.def" ] || die "no kernel tree in $XNU_SRC (xnu/apply.sh makes it)"
	[ -x host/bin/migcom ] && [ -d "$XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel" ] || die "stage 1 has not been done"
	local lib=$XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/lib/kernel hdrs=$XNU_SRC/BUILD/obj/EXPORT_HDRS file
	# three Mach-O headers for the build tools the kernel build compiles for this machine (SETUP/)
	mkdir -p hostinc/mach-o
	for file in loader.h nlist.h fat.h; do
		[ -f hostinc/mach-o/$file ] || cp "$XNU_SRC/EXTERNAL_HEADERS/mach-o/$file" hostinc/mach-o/
	done
	if [ -n "$REBUILD_LIBS" ]; then rm -f $lib/libfirehose_kernel.a $lib/libpthread_kext.a; fi
	if [ -f $lib/libfirehose_kernel.a ] && [ -f $lib/libpthread_kext.a ]; then
		log "stage 2: nothing to do"
		return 0
	fi
	log "exporting the kernel's headers (xnu-build.sh exporthdrs)"
	"$DARWIN_REDWOOD/xnu-build.sh" -j$JOBS exporthdrs > exporthdrs.log 2>&1 && [ -d "$hdrs/osfmk" ] ||
		die "the kernel headers were not exported, see xnu-deps/exporthdrs.log"
	if [ ! -f $lib/libfirehose_kernel.a ]; then
		log "building libfirehose_kernel.a"
		mkdir -p build/firehose
		xnu-clang -arch arm64 -c -Os -mkernel -nostdinc -fno-builtin \
			-DKERNEL=1 -DKERNEL_PRIVATE=1 -DXNU_KERNEL_PRIVATE=0 -DPRIVATE=1 -D__DARWIN_64_BIT_INO_T=1 \
			-DDISPATCH_USE_DTRACE=0 -DOS_ATOMIC_CONFIG_MEMORY_ORDER_DEPENDENCY=1 \
			-DOS_ATOMIC_CONFIG_STARVATION_FREE_ONLY=0 -DOS_FIREHOSE_SPI=1 -DARM64_BOARD_CONFIG_BCM2837 \
			-Ilibdispatch -Ilibdispatch/src -Ilibdispatch/src/firehose \
			-I$hdrs/osfmk -I$hdrs/bsd -I$hdrs/libkern -I$hdrs/pexpert -I$hdrs/iokit -I$hdrs/security \
			-I$XNU_SRC/libkern/firehose -I$hdrs/libkern/os -I$XNU_SRC/EXTERNAL_HEADERS \
			-I$XNU_SDK_PATH/usr/local/include/kernel \
			-o build/firehose/firehose_buffer.o libdispatch/src/firehose/firehose_buffer.c
		libtool -static -o $lib/libfirehose_kernel.a build/firehose/firehose_buffer.o
	fi
	if [ ! -f $lib/libpthread_kext.a ]; then
		log "building libpthread_kext.a"
		build/pthread/build.sh
	fi
	log "stage 2 done; now: ./xnu-build.sh -j$JOBS -k"
}

case "$1" in
--stage1) stage1 ;;
--stage2) stage2 ;;
--rebuild-libs) REBUILD_LIBS=1 stage2 ;;
"")
	stage1
	if [ -f "$XNU_SRC/makedefs/MakeInc.def" ]; then
		stage2
	else
		log "no kernel tree yet: run xnu/apply.sh, then this script again"
	fi ;;
*) sed -n '2,12p' "$HERE/setup.sh"; exit 1 ;;
esac

```

`xnu-env.sh`:

# source this (from bash) before building XNU on Linux
# Everything is found relative to this file. THEOS (default ~/theos) provides the cctools and the
# Darwin SDK; XNU_SRC is the kernel tree (xnu/apply.sh creates it).

# On macOS there is no theos: xnu-deps/setup.sh lays out xnu-deps/theos-mac like one (links to the

	export THEOS=${THEOS:-$HOME/theos}
fi

export XNU_SDK_VERSION=16.5
export XNU_PLATFORM_PATH=$XNUDEPS/sdk/Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform

`xnu/README.md`:

```md
# The kernel

Our changes to XNU `xnu-8796.121.2` (the kernel of Darwin userland 16.5, Darwin 22.5.0):

- `hakios.patch`: changes to Apple's files;
- `files/`: new files at their paths in the XNU tree;
- `../drivers/`: the drivers, by subsystem (`drivers/README.md`); `apply.sh` puts them at their paths in the tree;
- `apply.sh`: fetches the sources from Apple's GitHub and lays all of this over them;
  `export.sh`: the reverse, run before committing.

It builds on Linux with stock clang (no macOS, no Xcode) and on macOS with Xcode.

## Build

Linux (Arch): `sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel git curl clang lld python perl xz`, and
[theos](https://theos.dev/docs/installation-linux) in `~/theos` (or `$THEOS`) for its cctools
(`ld64`, `nm`, `otool`, `strip`) and `sdks/iPhoneOS16.5.sdk`. macOS: Xcode and MacPorts coreutils;
`xnu-deps/setup.sh` lays out `xnu-deps/theos-mac` itself.

```sh
xnu/apply.sh             # the xnu-8796.121.2 tag from apple-oss-distributions/xnu + our changes -> xnu-src/
xnu-deps/setup.sh        # dependencies, mig/unifdef/tcsh, the SDK overlay, two libraries
./xnu-build.sh -j8 -k    # about a minute on 12 threads
```

The kernel: `hakios-kernel` at the top of the repository (`make kernel` copies it there from XNU's `xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2/BUILD/obj/DEVELOPMENT_ARM64_BCM2837/mach.development.bcm2837`).
`./xl run` and `qemu/run-darwin.sh` take it from there (`prebuilt/` only when it is missing).

Things to know:

- `-k` is required: the build always ends with an error in `check_all_exports` (export lists), after
  the kernel has been linked. Look at the file's date, not at make's exit code.
- No spaces in the repository's path.
- After changing kernel headers that the two external libraries see: `xnu-deps/setup.sh --rebuild-libs`.
- Apple's DriverKit generator (`iig`) is closed; `xnu-deps/iig-impl/` holds stubs generated from
  the linker's undefined symbols (`xnu-deps/gen-iig-stubs.py`).
- A driver can be edited in `drivers/<subsystem>/`: `make kernel` runs `xnu/sync-drivers.sh`, which copies it into
  the tree when it is newer than the tree's copy (never the other way round). Everything else, and drivers edited
  in the tree, go back with `xnu/export.sh`.
- Edit `xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2` directly (a git tree on branch `redwood`); `xnu/export.sh`
  regenerates the patch and `files/` from the whole tree, so bring the tree up to the current patch
  first if somebody else changed the kernel meanwhile.

## What is added

| Files | What |
|---|---|
| `osfmk/arm64/gic_v3_irq.c`, `generic_arm64_support.c`, `psci_smp.c`, `loader_return.c` | the platform: GICv3, the timer, several CPUs through PSCI, the return to the loader with the log, the hypervisor watchdog |
| `osfmk/minicrypto/` | a replacement for corecrypto (MD5, SHA, HMAC, DRBG, AES) |
| `iokit/Kernel/GenericARMPE.cpp`, `MiniIOSurface.*`, `MiniIOMobileFramebuffer.cpp`, `MiniAppleKeyStore.cpp` | the platform expert and replacements for closed drivers: surfaces, the display, the key store |
| `bsd/miscfs/apfs/`, `bsd/miscfs/ramfs/` | read-only APFS and a writable RAM file system |
| `bsd/kern/kern_minimac.c`, `libkern/amfi/` | AMFI and Sandbox stubs |
| `drivers/input/hakios.input.c`, `hakios.goodix.c` | input: `/dev/hakios-touch`, the Goodix GT9916 touch controller |
| `drivers/power/hakios.cpufreq.c` | CPU clocks (Qualcomm EPSS) |
| `drivers/net/hakios.net.c`, `hakios.virtio_net.c` | the `en0` network interface |
| `drivers/gpu/hakios.adreno.c`, `drivers/gpu/hakios.gpu.cpp` | the Adreno 642L GPU |
| `drivers/wifi/hakios.wifi.c`, `hakios.wlfw.c` | Wi-Fi (WCN6750): shared memory, the radio's DSP, the driver |
| `drivers/modem/hakios.qmi.c`, `hakios.nas.c` | QMI and the NAS client |
| `drivers/modem/hakios.mpss.c` | the modem: firmware, file systems, IPA, SIM, registration |
| `drivers/audio/hakios.audio.c`, `hakios.adsp.c`, `hakios.speaker.c`, `hakios.mic.c` | sound through the audio DSP; the battery comes through it too |
| `drivers/haptic/hakios.haptic.c`, `hakios.camera.c`, `hakios.ufs.c` | the vibration motor, the cameras, the UFS storage |
| `bsd/pthread/pthread_kext_static.c` | the pthread kext linked into the kernel |

The patch also fixes what keeps open XNU from building and running outside Apple: the makefiles
on Linux, the `BCM2837` configuration it is based on, bugs in abandoned code.

License: a derivative work of XNU, Apple Public Source License 2.0 (`LICENSE.APSL` at the top).

`xnu/apply.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Get Apple's XNU sources (the release that Darwin userland 16.5 was built from) and put the HakiOS
# work on top of them: hakios.patch changes Apple's files, files/ holds the new ones.
# usage: xnu/apply.sh [DIR]              (default: $XNU_SRC, else xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2 next to this directory)
# env:   XNU_URL   where to fetch from (default: Apple's repository on GitHub; an existing clone
#                  that has the tag will do: XNU_URL=file:///path/to/xnu)
# The result is a git tree on the branch "hakios" with the work uncommitted, which is how
# xnu/export.sh expects to find it. A directory that already exists is left alone.
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
DIR=${1:-${XNU_SRC:-$HERE/../xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2}}
URL=${XNU_URL:-https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu.git}
TAG=xnu-8796.121.2
BASE=c54f35ca767986246321eb901baf8f5ff7923f6a

[ -e "$DIR" ] && { echo "apply.sh: $DIR already exists; not touching it" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -s "$HERE/hakios.patch" ] && [ -d "$HERE/files" ] || { echo "apply.sh: no hakios.patch and files/ in $HERE" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$HERE/../drivers/map" ] || { echo "apply.sh: no drivers/map next to xnu/ (the drivers are in drivers/)" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DIR")"
DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$DIR")" && pwd)/$(basename "$DIR")
git init -q "$DIR"
trap 'echo "apply.sh: failed; removing the incomplete $DIR" >&2; rm -rf "$DIR"' ERR
cd "$DIR"
git remote add origin "$URL"
git fetch -q --depth 1 origin "refs/tags/$TAG:refs/tags/$TAG"      # that one release, without the history
git checkout -q -b hakios "$TAG"
[ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$BASE" ] || { echo "apply.sh: $TAG is $(git rev-parse HEAD), expected $BASE" >&2; false; }
echo 'BUILD/' >> .git/info/exclude
git apply --whitespace=nowarn "$HERE/hakios.patch"
cp -a "$HERE/files/." .
# HFS Plus (the data volume): Apple's release, fetched like XNU, and this port's changes over it
"$HERE/hfs/hfs.sh" put "$DIR"
# the drivers are kept by subsystem (drivers/<subsystem>/), not at their place in Apple's tree: drivers/map says where
# each one goes, one line per file: "<subsystem> <path in the tree>"
NDRIVERS=0
while read -r sub tree _; do
	case "$sub" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
	[ -f "$HERE/../drivers/$sub/$(basename "$tree")" ] || { echo "apply.sh: drivers/$sub/$(basename "$tree") is in drivers/map but missing" >&2; false; }
	mkdir -p "$(dirname "$tree")"
	cp -p "$HERE/../drivers/$sub/$(basename "$tree")" "$tree"
	NDRIVERS=$((NDRIVERS + 1))
done < "$HERE/../drivers/map"
# the drivers of the SoC and device repositories checked out (socs/*/drivers/, devices/*/drivers/)
python3 "$HERE/../tools/hakios-config.py" external-files | while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r src tree; do
	mkdir -p "$(dirname "$tree")"
	cp -p "$src" "$tree"
done
# which of them are built is the configuration's (drivers/*/conf, CONFIG_HAKIOS_*): put into the tree as XNU reads it.
# What that writes is made again for every build, so it is kept out of the work that xnu/export.sh saves.
printf '%s\n' config/MASTER.hakios bsd/dev/hakios.drivers.h >> .git/info/exclude
python3 "$HERE/../tools/hakios-config.py" kernel --tree "$DIR"
echo "apply.sh: $DIR: $TAG + $(grep -c '^diff --git' "$HERE/hakios.patch") changed and $(find "$HERE/files" -type f | wc -l) new files + $NDRIVERS drivers"

```

`xnu/export.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Save the kernel work as it is in the working tree, in the two forms apply.sh puts back:
#   hakios.patch   the changes to Apple's files (against the tag the work sits on)
#   files/          the files that are not in Apple's tree, at their paths
# usage: xnu/export.sh [KERNEL-TREE]     (default: $XNU_SRC, else xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2)
# Run it before committing whenever the kernel tree has changed. Committed or not makes no
# difference there: everything is compared with the base commit.
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
SRC=${1:-${XNU_SRC:-$HERE/../xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2}}
BASE=c54f35ca767986246321eb901baf8f5ff7923f6a           # tag xnu-8796.121.2
# never part of the work: build output and what editors, patch and python leave behind
# nor what tools/hakios-config.py kernel writes for one configuration (the drivers' choice)
JUNK='^BUILD/|^config/MASTER\.hakios$|^bsd/dev/hakios\.drivers\.h$|(^|/)__pycache__/|\.(orig|rej|pyc|o|swp)$|\.bak[0-9]*$|~$|(^|/)\.DS_Store$'

cd "$SRC"
git cat-file -e "$BASE^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || { echo "export.sh: $SRC is not a clone of xnu at $BASE" >&2; exit 1; }

# no renames: a moved file is a deletion in the patch and a new file in files/
git -c core.abbrev=12 diff --binary --no-renames --no-color --no-ext-diff --diff-filter=MDT "$BASE" -- . > "$HERE/hakios.patch.new"
mv "$HERE/hakios.patch.new" "$HERE/hakios.patch"

rm -rf "$HERE/files.new"
mkdir "$HERE/files.new"
{ git diff --no-renames --name-only --diff-filter=A "$BASE" -- .; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } |
	sort -u | grep -Ev "$JUNK" > "$HERE/files.list"
while IFS= read -r f; do
	[ -f "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ] || continue      # added in a commit, deleted since
	mkdir -p "$HERE/files.new/$(dirname "$f")"
	if [ "$(uname)" = Darwin ]; then cp -pP "$f" "$HERE/files.new/$f"; else cp -P --preserve=mode "$f" "$HERE/files.new/$f"; fi
done < "$HERE/files.list"

# The drivers of SoC and device repositories (tools/hakios-config.py external-files) are theirs, not this repository's: they are
# left out of files/ and are not refused as unlisted. Edit them in their repository; xnu/sync-drivers.sh copies them in.
EXTERNAL=$(python3 "$HERE/../tools/hakios-config.py" external-files | cut -f2)
if [ -n "$EXTERNAL" ]; then
	printf '%s\n' "$EXTERNAL" | while IFS= read -r tree; do rm -f "$HERE/files.new/$tree"; done
fi

# Apple's HFS Plus is not kept here: what this port changes in it goes into xnu/hfs/hfs.patch, and Apple's files are
# fetched again by xnu/apply.sh (xnu/hfs/hfs.sh). Its own files (bsd/hfs/hfs_builtin.c) stay in files/.
while read -r f; do rm -f "$HERE/files.new/bsd/hfs/$f"; done < "$HERE/hfs/core.list"
while read -r f; do rm -f "$HERE/files.new/bsd/hfs_encodings/$f"; done < "$HERE/hfs/encodings.list"
"$HERE/hfs/hfs.sh" export "$SRC"

# The drivers (drivers/map) are kept by subsystem in drivers/<subsystem>/, not under files/: take them out of
# files.new and put each one where the map says. A hakios.* file the map does not list is refused, not guessed at.
MAP="$HERE/../drivers/map"
[ -f "$MAP" ] || { echo "export.sh: no $MAP" >&2; exit 1; }
LISTED=$(awk '{ sub(/#.*/, "") } NF == 2 { print $2 }' "$MAP")
UNLISTED=$(cd "$HERE/files.new" && find bsd/dev iokit/Kernel -type f -name 'hakios.*' 2>/dev/null | sort |
	grep -vxF -f <(printf '%s\n' "$LISTED") || true)
if [ -n "$UNLISTED" ]; then
	echo "export.sh: these new drivers are not in drivers/map (add '<subsystem> <path>' for each, then run this again):" >&2
	echo "$UNLISTED" | sed 's/^/    /' >&2
	rm -rf "$HERE/files.new"; exit 1
fi
NDRIVERS=0
while read -r sub tree _; do
	case "$sub" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
	if [ ! -f "$HERE/files.new/$tree" ]; then
		echo "export.sh: drivers/map lists $tree but the kernel tree has no such new file (deleted? take its line out of drivers/map)" >&2
		rm -rf "$HERE/files.new"; exit 1
	fi
	mkdir -p "$HERE/../drivers/$sub"
	mv "$HERE/files.new/$tree" "$HERE/../drivers/$sub/$(basename "$tree")"
	NDRIVERS=$((NDRIVERS + 1))
done < "$MAP"
find "$HERE/files.new" -type d -empty -delete 2>/dev/null || true
mkdir -p "$HERE/files.new"
rm -rf "$HERE/files" "$HERE/files.list"
mv "$HERE/files.new" "$HERE/files"

echo "xnu/hakios.patch: $(grep -c '^diff --git' "$HERE/hakios.patch") files changed, $(wc -c < "$HERE/hakios.patch") bytes"
echo "xnu/files: $(find "$HERE/files" -type f | wc -l) new files, $(du -sk "$HERE/files" | cut -f1) KB"
echo "drivers/: $NDRIVERS drivers"

```

`xnu/files/bsd/hfs/hfs_builtin.c`:

```c
/*
 * HakiOS: what HFS's kext had in its C++ part (hfs_iokit.cpp), for HFS built into the kernel.
 *
 * The kext registered the filesystem from its IOService's start(); built in, it is an entry of the static table
 * (bsd/vfs/vfs_conf.c) and hfs_init() does the rest.  The IOKit questions -- is the medium ejectable, which media
 * carry a given content UUID, the platform's serial number -- have no use for a data volume on the phone's own
 * flash, and the keys of content protection are AppleKeyStore's, which this kernel does not have: a volume made
 * without content protection never asks for them.
 */
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <mach/kern_return.h>
#include "hfs.h"
#include "hfs_iokit.h"

#ifndef panic_on_assert
bool panic_on_assert = false;
#endif

int
hfs_is_ejectable(__unused const char *cdev_name)
{
	return 0;
}

void
hfs_iterate_media_with_content(__unused const char *content_uuid_cstring,
    __unused int (*func)(const char *bsd_name, const char *uuid_str, void *arg), __unused void *arg)
{
}

kern_return_t
hfs_get_platform_serial_number(__unused char *serial_number_str, __unused uint32_t len)
{
	return KERN_FAILURE;
}

#if CONFIG_PROTECT
int
hfs_unwrap_key(__unused aks_cred_t access, __unused const aks_wrapped_key_t wrapped_key_in,
    __unused aks_raw_key_t key_out)
{
	return ENOTSUP;
}

int
hfs_rewrap_key(__unused aks_cred_t access, __unused cp_key_class_t dp_class,
    __unused const aks_wrapped_key_t wrapped_key_in, __unused aks_wrapped_key_t wrapped_key_out)
{
	return ENOTSUP;
}

int
hfs_new_key(__unused aks_cred_t access, __unused cp_key_class_t dp_class, __unused aks_raw_key_t key_out,
    __unused aks_wrapped_key_t wrapped_key_out)
{
	return ENOTSUP;
}

int
hfs_backup_key(__unused aks_cred_t access, __unused const aks_wrapped_key_t wrapped_key_in,
    __unused aks_wrapped_key_t wrapped_key_out)
{
	return ENOTSUP;
}
#endif /* CONFIG_PROTECT */
