`xnu/files/bsd/kern/kern_minimac.c`:

```c
/*
 * Stand-ins for the two closed security policies user space cannot do
 * without: AMFI and the Sandbox. On a device they are kexts that register
 * MAC policies of those names; system software talks to them through
 * __mac_syscall() and relies on what they decide.
 *
 * Neither stand-in is a security mechanism. This kernel runs whatever it is
 * given (see libkern/amfi/miniamfi.c); these only give the answers the Darwin
 * user space needs in order to run at all:
 *
 *   AMFI     The binaries of the operating system carry ad hoc signatures
 *            (no certificate chain); on a device AMFI finds their hashes
 *            in the trust cache and flags them as platform binaries.
 *            launchd panics if a system daemon is not one. There is no
 *            trust cache here, so every ad hoc signed binary is taken for
 *            a platform binary. Unsigned programs (our own) are not.
 *
 *   Sandbox  Every query (may this process look up that service?) is
 *            answered "allowed", and every request to apply a profile
 *            succeeds without applying anything. The one question with
 *            an answer of its own is which container a process is in.
 */

#include <sys/param.h>
#include <sys/systm.h>
#include <sys/kernel.h>
#include <sys/codesign.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/kpi_socket.h>
#include <sys/priv.h>
#include <sys/proc_internal.h>
#include <sys/ubc_internal.h>
#include <sys/vnode_internal.h>
#include <libkern/libkern.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/task.h>
#include <mach/vm_param.h>
#include <vm/vm_kern.h>
#include <vm/vm_map.h>
#include <security/mac_framework.h>
#include <security/mac_policy.h>

void minimac_policy_init(void);

static int
miniamfi_vnode_check_signature(__unused struct vnode *vp, __unused struct label *label, __unused cpu_type_t cpu_type,
    struct cs_blob *cs_blob, unsigned int *cs_flags, __unused unsigned int *signer_type, __unused int flags,
    __unused unsigned int platform, __unused char **fatal_failure_desc, __unused size_t *fatal_failure_desc_len)
{
	if (cs_blob == NULL) {
		return 0;
	}
	/*
	 * Accepting a signature is what marks the process as signed; the
	 * kernel consults the signature of a process only when that is set.
	 */
	*cs_flags |= CS_SIGNED;
	if (*cs_flags & CS_ADHOC) {
		*cs_flags |= CS_PLATFORM_BINARY;
	}
	return 0;
}

/*
 * dyld asks AMFI what it may do for the process it is starting (request 0x5a, "check dyld
 * policy"): the argument is { flags in, pointer to flags out }. Everything is allowed --
 * @paths, the DYLD_* variables, inserted libraries and interposing -- which is what lets
 * our own library be loaded into stock daemons (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES).
 */
#define AMFI_SYSCALL_CHECK_DYLD_POLICY  0x5a
#define AMFI_DYLD_OUTPUT_ALLOW_ALL      0xffULL

/*
 * Request 0x60, "query boot-arg state" (amfi_interface_query_bootarg_state() in libamfi): the
 * argument points to 64 bits of flags, one for each boot-arg that switches a part of AMFI off
 * (amfi_get_out_of_my_way and its kin). ExtensionKit asks, and unless one of the bits 0x86 is set
 * it wants the signature of the system's table of extension points
 * (/System/Library/xpc/extensions.plist.sig) verified by AMFI's IOKit service. There is no such
 * service here ("Unable to find AMFI"); the table is then not read and LaunchServices knows no
 * extension point: every application extension is refused when the applications are registered
 * ("does not correspond to a known extension point"), pkd cannot make a record for any extension
 * point, and Shortcuts dies on a nil one. Nothing is enforced by this kernel, so that is what it
 * says. (Which of the three bits stands for which boot-arg is not known; ExtensionKit takes any
 * of them.)
 */
#define AMFI_SYSCALL_QUERY_BOOTARG_STATE 0x60
#define AMFI_BOOTARG_STATE_NOT_ENFORCING 0x86ULL

static int
miniamfi_policy_syscall(__unused struct proc *p, int call, user_addr_t arg)
{
	struct {
		uint64_t input_flags;
		user_addr_t output_flags;
	} args;
	uint64_t flags = AMFI_DYLD_OUTPUT_ALLOW_ALL;
	uint64_t state = AMFI_BOOTARG_STATE_NOT_ENFORCING;
	int error;

	if (call == AMFI_SYSCALL_QUERY_BOOTARG_STATE) {
		return copyout(&state, arg, sizeof(state));
	}
	if (call != AMFI_SYSCALL_CHECK_DYLD_POLICY) {
		return ENOPOLICY;               /* what user space got before there was a handler */
	}
	error = copyin(arg, &args, sizeof(args));
	if (error == 0) {
		error = copyout(&flags, args.output_flags, sizeof(flags));
	}
	return error;
}

static const struct mac_policy_ops miniamfi_ops = {
	.mpo_vnode_check_signature = miniamfi_vnode_check_signature,
	.mpo_policy_syscall = miniamfi_policy_syscall,
};

SECURITY_READ_ONLY_LATE(static struct mac_policy_conf) miniamfi_conf = {
	.mpc_name = "AMFI",
	.mpc_fullname = "Apple Mobile File Integrity (stand-in)",
	.mpc_ops = &miniamfi_ops,
};
SECURITY_READ_ONLY_LATE(static mac_policy_handle_t) miniamfi_handle;

/*
 * Request 4, "container path of a process": sandbox_container_path_for_pid() and
 * sandbox_container_path_for_audit_token() of libsystem_sandbox. The argument is
 * { pid, version of the pid, buffer, its size, whether the version is to be compared }.
 *
 * On a device the Sandbox learns the container when the program is executed (it asks
 * containermanagerd) and confines the process to it. Nothing is confined here, but the question
 * is still asked and the answer matters: an application extension hosted by PlugInKit does not
 * run without a container. It gives the buffer a "?" to start with and wants a longer string
 * back, else "plugin has invalid sandbox or container" (-[PKService checkEnvironment:]) -- the
 * end of every Intents extension while this request "succeeded" without writing anything.
 *
 * Whoever starts a program that lives in a container -- RunningBoard an application, pkd an
 * extension -- has had the path from containermanagerd and passes it in the environment as
 * CFFIXED_USER_HOME, which is where Foundation takes the home directory from. So that is the
 * answer: it is looked up among the strings exec left at the top of the stack of the process.
 * A process without the variable has no container, and gets what every process got before:
 * success and an untouched buffer.
 */
#define SANDBOX_SYSCALL_CONTAINER_PATH  4
#define SANDBOX_CONTAINER_VARIABLE      "CFFIXED_USER_HOME="

static int
minisandbox_container_path(user_addr_t arg)
{
	struct {
		int64_t     pid;
		uint64_t    pidversion;
		user_addr_t buffer;
		user_size_t size;
		uint64_t    check_pidversion;
	} args;
	const size_t prefix_len = sizeof(SANDBOX_CONTAINER_VARIABLE) - 1;
	proc_t p;
	task_t task;
	vm_map_t map;
	vm_map_copy_t copy = NULL;
	vm_offset_t strings = 0;
	vm_size_t strings_size;
	user_addr_t user_stack;
	size_t argslen, len;
	const char *s, *end;
	int error;

	error = copyin(arg, &args, sizeof(args));
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	p = proc_find((int)args.pid);
	if (p == PROC_NULL) {
		return ESRCH;
	}
	if (args.check_pidversion && (uint64_t)proc_pidversion(p) != args.pidversion) {
		proc_rele(p);
		return ESRCH;
	}
	user_stack = p->user_stack;
	argslen = p->p_argslen;
	task = proc_task(p);
	if (user_stack == 0 || argslen == 0 || task == TASK_NULL) {
		proc_rele(p);
		return 0;
	}
	/* the same way as sysctl_procargsx(): the task keeps the map alive once the process is let go */
	task_reference(task);
	proc_rele(p);
	map = get_task_map_reference(task);
	task_deallocate(task);
	if (map == VM_MAP_NULL) {
		return 0;
	}
	strings_size = vm_map_round_page(argslen, vm_map_page_mask(map));
	if (kmem_alloc(kernel_map, &strings, strings_size, KMA_DATA | KMA_ZERO, VM_KERN_MEMORY_BSD) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		vm_map_deallocate(map);
		return ENOMEM;
	}
	if (vm_map_copyin(map, (vm_map_address_t)(user_stack - strings_size), strings_size, FALSE, &copy) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		copy = NULL;
	}
	vm_map_deallocate(map);
	if (copy == NULL || vm_map_copy_overwrite(kernel_map, strings, copy, strings_size, FALSE) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
		if (copy != NULL) {
			vm_map_copy_discard(copy);
		}
		kmem_free(kernel_map, strings, strings_size);
		return 0;                       /* the process is on its way out, or has unmapped its own stack */
	}

	end = (const char *)(strings + strings_size);
	for (s = end - argslen; s < end; s += len + 1) {
		len = strnlen(s, end - s);
		if (len > prefix_len && s + len < end && strncmp(s, SANDBOX_CONTAINER_VARIABLE, prefix_len) == 0) {
			s += prefix_len;
			len -= prefix_len;
			error = len < args.size ? copyout(s, args.buffer, len + 1) : ENAMETOOLONG;
			break;
		}
	}
	kmem_free(kernel_map, strings, strings_size);
	return error;
}

/* Which request numbers have been seen: one log line each, to learn what user space asks for. */
static uint64_t minisandbox_seen;

static int
minisandbox_policy_syscall(struct proc *p, int call, user_addr_t arg)
{
	if (call >= 0 && call < 64 && (minisandbox_seen & (1ULL << call)) == 0) {
		minisandbox_seen |= 1ULL << call;
		printf("minisandbox: request %d (first seen from %s[%d]): %s\n", call, p->p_comm, proc_getpid(p),
		    call == SANDBOX_SYSCALL_CONTAINER_PATH ? "answered" : "allowed");
	}
	if (call == SANDBOX_SYSCALL_CONTAINER_PATH) {
		return minisandbox_container_path(arg);
	}
	return 0;
}

/*
 * Privileges for processes that are not root. On a device the sandbox hands them out by
 * entitlement: a privilege is granted to a process whose code signature has the entitlement
 * that goes with it. The table is the same pairing: the names are the entitlements Darwin's own
 * programs carry for them (dasd "vm-pressure-level", symptomsd and aggregated
 * com.apple.private.network.statistics, mediaserverd and mDNSResponder
 * com.apple.private.network.socket-delegate -- without which NECP said "does not hold the
 * necessary entitlement to delegate network traffic" -- and so on).
 *
 * That NECP line is worth knowing for what it is NOT: it costs nothing. The macro that prints it
 * (bsd/net/necp.c, NECP_VERIFY_DELEGATION_ENTITLEMENT) only breaks out of the parameter it was
 * reading, so the delegation is dropped and the policy is matched against the caller itself; no
 * error is returned and no connection is refused. A session where trustd prints it four hundred
 * times is a session where trustd's own connections all go through. A stock iPhone prints it too.
 * It is noise, not a wall -- do not go looking for a daemon's missing network behind it.
 *
 *   PRIV_WORK_INTERVAL    is granted to every process, entitlement or not: telling the scheduler
 *                         about the work of drawing a frame. UIKit does it as soon as anything
 *                         scrolls, and takes a refusal for a programming error ("Failed to create
 *                         work interval"): SpringBoard died of it on the first swipe between
 *                         pages of the home screen.
 *
 * Whatever is refused is said once, to learn what there is. Boot-arg privs=0: only
 * PRIV_WORK_INTERVAL, as before.
 */
extern kern_return_t miniamfi_entitlement_boolean(struct proc *proc, const char *name);

static const struct {
	int priv;
	const char *entitlement;
} minisandbox_privileges[] = {
	{ PRIV_PROC_UUID_POLICY, "com.apple.private.kernel.uuid-policy" },
	{ PRIV_GLOBAL_PROC_INFO, "com.apple.private.kernel.global-proc-info" },
	{ PRIV_SYSTEM_OVERRIDE, "com.apple.private.kernel.system-override" },
	{ PRIV_HW_DEBUG_DATA, "com.apple.private.kernel.hw-debug-data" },
	{ PRIV_SELECTIVE_FORCED_IDLE, "com.apple.private.kernel.selective-forced-idle" },
	{ PRIV_DARKBOOT, "com.apple.private.kernel.darkboot" },
	{ PRIV_AUDIO_LATENCY, "com.apple.private.kernel.audio_latency" },
	{ PRIV_KTRACE_BACKGROUND, "com.apple.private.kernel.ktrace-background" },
	{ PRIV_SETPRIORITY_DARWIN_ROLE, "com.apple.private.kernel.setpriority-darwin-role" },
	{ PRIV_PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS, "com.apple.private.kernel.set-package-extensions" },
	{ PRIV_TRIM_ACTIVE_FILE, "com.apple.private.apfs.trim-active-file" },
	{ PRIV_PROC_CPUMON_OVERRIDE, "com.apple.private.kernel.override-cpumon" },
	{ PRIV_VM_PRESSURE, "vm-pressure-level" },
	{ PRIV_VM_JETSAM, "com.apple.private.kernel.jetsam" },
	{ PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_TRAFFIC_CLASS, "com.apple.private.network.privileged-traffic-class" },
	{ PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_SOCKET_DELEGATE, "com.apple.private.network.socket-delegate" },
	{ PRIV_NET_INTERFACE_CONTROL, "com.apple.private.network.interface-control" },
	{ PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_NETWORK_STATISTICS, "com.apple.private.network.statistics" },
	{ PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_NECP_POLICIES, "com.apple.private.necp.policies" },
	{ PRIV_NET_RESTRICTED_AWDL, "com.apple.private.network.awdl.restricted" },
	{ PRIV_NET_QOSMARKING_POLICY_OVERRIDE, "com.apple.private.network.qos-marking-policy-override" },
	{ PRIV_NET_RESTRICTED_MULTIPATH_EXTENDED, "com.apple.developer.networking.multipath_extended" },
	{ PRIV_NET_RESTRICTED_ROUTE_NC_READ, "com.apple.developer.networking.route_nc_read" },
	{ PRIV_NET_VALIDATED_RESOLVER, "com.apple.private.validated-resolver" },
	{ PRIV_NET_CUSTOM_PROTOCOL, "com.apple.developer.networking.custom-protocol" },
	{ PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_NECP_DROP_ALL_BYPASS, "com.apple.private.necp.drop_all_bypass" },
	{ PRIV_NET_PRIVILEGED_IPSEC_WAKE_PACKET, "com.apple.private.network.ipsec-wake-packet" },
	{ PRIV_NETINET_RESERVEDPORT, "com.apple.private.network.reserved-port" },
	{ PRIV_NETINET_TCP_KA_OFFLOAD, "com.apple.developer.networking.tcp_ka_offload" },
	{ PRIV_SKYWALK_REGISTER_USER_PIPE, "com.apple.private.skywalk.register-user-pipe" },
	{ PRIV_SKYWALK_REGISTER_KERNEL_PIPE, "com.apple.private.skywalk.register-kernel-pipe" },
	{ PRIV_SKYWALK_REGISTER_NET_IF, "com.apple.private.skywalk.register-net-if" },
	{ PRIV_SKYWALK_REGISTER_FLOW_SWITCH, "com.apple.private.skywalk.register-flow-switch" },
	{ PRIV_SKYWALK_OBSERVE_ALL, "com.apple.private.skywalk.observe-all" },
	{ PRIV_SKYWALK_OBSERVE_STATS, "com.apple.private.skywalk.observe-stats" },
	{ PRIV_VFS_OPEN_BY_ID, "com.apple.private.vfs.open-by-id" },
	{ PRIV_VFS_MOVE_DATA_EXTENTS, "com.apple.private.vfs.move-data-extents" },
	{ PRIV_VFS_SNAPSHOT, "com.apple.private.vfs.snapshot" },
	{ PRIV_VFS_DATALESS_RESOLVER, "com.apple.private.vfs.dataless-resolver" },
	{ PRIV_VFS_SETSIZE, "com.apple.private.vfs.setsize" },
};
static TUNABLE(uint32_t, minisandbox_by_entitlement, "privs", 1);

static int
minisandbox_priv_grant(kauth_cred_t cred, int priv)
{
	static int seen[32];
	static unsigned seen_count;
	proc_t proc = current_proc();

	if (priv == PRIV_WORK_INTERVAL) {
		return 0;
	}
	/* (the entitlements are the current process's: only for a question about its own credential) */
	for (unsigned i = 0; minisandbox_by_entitlement && cred == kauth_cred_get() &&
	    i < sizeof(minisandbox_privileges) / sizeof(minisandbox_privileges[0]); i++) {
		if (minisandbox_privileges[i].priv == priv) {
			if (miniamfi_entitlement_boolean(proc, minisandbox_privileges[i].entitlement) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
				return 0;
			}
			break;
		}
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < seen_count; i++) {
		if (seen[i] == priv) {
			return EPERM;
		}
	}
	if (seen_count < sizeof(seen) / sizeof(seen[0])) {
		seen[seen_count++] = priv;
		printf("minisandbox: privilege %d refused to %s[%d] (first time)\n", priv, proc->p_comm,
		    proc_getpid(proc));
	}
	return EPERM;
}

static const struct mac_policy_ops minisandbox_ops = {
	.mpo_policy_syscall = minisandbox_policy_syscall,
	.mpo_priv_grant = minisandbox_priv_grant,
};

SECURITY_READ_ONLY_LATE(static struct mac_policy_conf) minisandbox_conf = {
	.mpc_name = "Sandbox",
	.mpc_fullname = "Seatbelt sandbox policy (stand-in)",
	.mpc_ops = &minisandbox_ops,
};
SECURITY_READ_ONLY_LATE(static mac_policy_handle_t) minisandbox_handle;

/* Called from kernel_bootstrap_thread() once the MAC framework is up. */
void
minimac_policy_init(void)
{
	mac_policy_register(&miniamfi_conf, &miniamfi_handle, NULL);
	mac_policy_register(&minisandbox_conf, &minisandbox_handle, NULL);
}
```

`xnu/files/bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs.h`:

```h
/*
 * apfs: reading an Apple File System volume from the kernel.
 *
 * The format itself is in apfs_lib.{h,c}, which knows nothing of vnodes and is checked
 * against real images on the build machine (tools/apfs/run-tests.sh).  This is the layer
 * between that and VFS: a mount, a vnode per object, and the vnode operations.
 *
 * Read only.  Nothing here writes to the device.
 *
 * apfs_lib keeps a cache of metadata blocks and hands out pointers into it, and its
 * cursors are plain structures with no locking of their own, so every call into it is
 * made with am_lock held.  That makes the whole volume one lock wide, which is enough for
 * a read-only root: the work under the lock is a few block reads, usually from the cache.
 */

#ifndef _MISCFS_APFS_APFS_H_
#define _MISCFS_APFS_APFS_H_

#include <sys/param.h>
#include <sys/mount.h>
#include <sys/vnode.h>
#include <kern/locks.h>

#include "apfs_lib.h"

/* Buckets in the table that finds an existing vnode by object identifier. */
#define APFS_HASH_BUCKETS 1024

struct apfs_node;

/*
 * What one round of vnop_read reads.  Alone on the volume, am_iobuf_size (boot-arg
 * apfs_round): a read(2) of that much is one request to apfs_lib, whose whole compressed
 * pieces are decompressed on several processors -- the bigger the round, the more there is
 * to share out.  With other reads in flight, APFS_ROUND_SHARED: the processors are busy
 * anyway, and a round that stays in the cache until uiomove copies it out is worth more.
 * One reader with 1 MB reads over the restore ramdisk, rounds of 128 KB / 256 KB / 512 KB /
 * 1 MB: 867 / 663 / 612 / 561 ms; four readers: 1429 / 1534 / 1747 / 2009 ms, and 1327
 * with rounds of 64 or 128 KB and no helpers.
 */
#define APFS_IOBUF_DEFAULT (1024 * 1024)
#define APFS_IOBUF_MAX     (2 * 1024 * 1024)
#define APFS_ROUND_SHARED  (128 * 1024)
#define APFS_IOBUF_KEEP    8

#define APFS_SYNTH_MAX     64
#define APFS_SYNTH_NAMELEN 96
/*
 * Object ids from here up are synthetic: the last few of the 60 bits an id has.  (Not
 * 0x0FFFFFFF00000000: the Darwin root volume numbers its own objects from there.)
 */
#define APFS_SYNTH_BASE    0x0FFFFFFFFFFFF000ULL

struct apfs_synth {
	uint64_t parent;                /* the directory it is in (a real one, or synthetic) */
	uint64_t id;                    /* its own, or the directory it is another name for */
	bool     alias;                 /* another name for a directory of the volume */
	char     name[APFS_SYNTH_NAMELEN];
};

struct apfs_mount {
	mount_t            am_mp;
	vnode_t            am_devvp;
	lck_mtx_t          am_lock;
	struct apfs_nx     am_nx;
	struct apfs_vol    am_vol;
	uint32_t           am_devblock;
	bool               am_owns_devvp;  /* we opened it, so we close it */
	bool               am_shares_devvp; /* another container of a device one of ours has open: not opened again */
	dev_t              am_rdev;         /* the device, for those other containers to find (apfs_mounts) */
	struct apfs_mount *am_next;         /* in apfs_mounts */
	struct apfs_node  *am_hash[APFS_HASH_BUCKETS];
	uint64_t           am_root_id;
	/*
	 * Where the time goes at the vnode operations, to set beside the container's own
	 * counters (waiting for the device, decompressing).  Ticks; see apfs_ticks().
	 */
	uint64_t           am_pagein_calls, am_pagein_ticks, am_pagein_bytes;
	/* read(2) through the page cache: bytes copied from pages already there, bytes read into it (atomic) */
	uint64_t           am_read_cached, am_read_filled;
	uint64_t           am_read_calls, am_read_ticks, am_read_bytes;
	/*
	 * What the one lock round apfs_lib costs: how long callers stood waiting for it, and
	 * how long it was held.  Held time is the part of the work that cannot happen on two
	 * processors at once, so with several readers it is the ceiling.
	 */
	uint64_t           am_lock_waits;
	uint64_t           am_lock_wait_ticks;
	uint64_t           am_lock_held_ticks;
	uint64_t           am_lock_t0;      /* when the holder took it; only the holder writes */
	/* how long takes waited: up to 2 us, 10 us, 100 us, 1 ms, more; and the longest (the holder writes) */
	uint64_t           am_lock_wait_hist[5];
	uint64_t           am_lock_wait_max;
	/*
	 * The operations going on (taken apfs_lock, not yet apfs_unlock; apfs_lib may let go of
	 * the lock in between), and the container's epoch each began at: retired cache memory
	 * older than the oldest of them is freed (apfs_nx_reclaim). Under am_lock.
	 */
#define APFS_OPS_MAX 128
	struct {
		thread_t           th;
		uint64_t           epoch;
		const char        *site;        /* the function that began it */
	}                  am_ops[APFS_OPS_MAX];
	/*
	 * The lock by who takes it (the function that called apfs_lock; apfs_lib's taking it back in
	 * the middle of an operation counts for the operation's): takes, waiting (in all, the longest,
	 * how many over 1 ms), holding (the same). Under am_lock.
	 */
#define APFS_LOCK_SITES 32
	struct apfs_lock_site {
		const char        *name;
		uint64_t           takes, relocks;
		uint64_t           wait, wait_max, wait_long;
		uint64_t           hold, hold_max, hold_long;
	}                  am_sites[APFS_LOCK_SITES];
	const char        *am_lock_site;    /* the holder's */
	uint32_t           am_lock_waiting; /* threads waiting for it now (atomic) */
	uint64_t           am_waiters_hist[5];  /* others waiting when it was taken: 0, 1, 2-3, 4-7, 8 or more */
	uint64_t           am_lookup_negative;  /* names not there, now known to the name cache */
	uint64_t           am_lookup_negative_hits;     /* lookups the name cache answered with "not there" */
	uint64_t           am_inactive_free;    /* vnop_inactive with nothing to give back: no lock taken */
	uint64_t           am_lookup_positive_hits;     /* lookups the name cache answered with the vnode */
	uint64_t           am_node_found, am_node_made; /* apfs_node_vnode: a vnode there already, a new one */
	uint64_t           am_node_named;       /* of those there already, entered in the name cache by a lookup */
	/* waiting by the waiter's base priority: up to 4, 20, 31, 46, higher (all waits; those over 1 ms) */
	uint64_t           am_prio_wait[5], am_prio_long[5], am_prio_long_wait[5];
	/*
	 * The waits over 1 ms, by the same priorities, taken apart: blocked (the lock not given),
	 * queued (runnable, no processor to run on), on a processor (spinning, the lock's own work).
	 */
	uint64_t           am_long_blocked[5], am_long_queued[5], am_long_oncpu[5];
	uint64_t           am_long_cpu[8];      /* the processor each one ended on */
	/*
	 * Who waits (waits over 10 us) and who reads (read(2), pagein), by process name; the
	 * first APFS_LOCK_PROCS-1 names, the last entry takes the rest.  Changed under am_lock,
	 * entries only ever added; read without it.  Allocated with the mount (the mount itself
	 * has to stay within kalloc_type's 16 KB); NULL if that failed: then not kept.
	 */
#define APFS_LOCK_PROCS 64
	struct apfs_lock_proc {
		char       name[MAXCOMLEN + 1];
		uint64_t   waits, wait, wait_max, wait_long;
		uint64_t   read_calls, read_bytes, pagein_calls, pagein_bytes;
		uint64_t   read_ticks, pagein_ticks;     /* time in them, added without the lock (atomic) */
	}                 *am_procs;
	uint32_t           am_nprocs;
	lck_spin_t         am_procs_spin;   /* finding or adding an entry (a read from the page cache has no am_lock) */
	bool               am_ubc_read;     /* read(2) through the page cache (boot-arg apfs_ubc_read, default 1) */
	uint32_t           am_nops;
	uint32_t           am_untracked;    /* operations the table had no room for: nothing is freed meanwhile */
	/* how long it was held: up to 10 us, 100 us, 1 ms, 10 ms, more; and the longest */
	uint64_t           am_lock_hold_hist[5];
	uint64_t           am_lock_hold_max;
	/*
	 * vnop_read's buffers, kept for the next read rather than allocated and freed for
	 * every one (at that size the kernel goes to the VM).  Under am_lock.
	 */
	void              *am_iobuf[APFS_IOBUF_KEEP];
	uint32_t           am_iobuf_kept;
	lck_spin_t         am_iobuf_spin;   /* the two above: their own lock, not am_lock */
	uint32_t           am_iobuf_size;
	/*
	 * Synthetic directories: empty directories that are not on the volume, for mount
	 * points on a volume nobody can add a directory to -- what macOS's synthetic.conf is
	 * for its sealed system volume.  Added through sysctl kern.apfs_synthetic; seen by
	 * lookup and readdir of their parent, empty, owned by root.  Or another name for a
	 * directory of the same volume ("PATH=TARGET"): the directory itself, with PATH's
	 * parent for its "..".  Under am_lock.
	 */
	struct apfs_synth *am_synth;        /* APFS_SYNTH_MAX of them, made at the first */
	uint32_t           am_nsynth;
};

/* The private part of a vnode: which object it is. */
struct apfs_node {
	struct apfs_node  *an_next;     /* the hash chain */
	struct apfs_mount *an_mount;
	vnode_t            an_vp;
	uint64_t           an_id;       /* the object identifier */
	uint64_t           an_parent;
	uint16_t           an_mode;
	uint64_t           an_size;     /* the logical size, as a reader of the file sees it */
	bool               an_attached; /* an_vp is set and the node is in the hash */
	/*
	 * What has been worked out about how this file's contents are stored, kept for as
	 * long as the vnode lives: the table of compressed pieces and the piece last
	 * decompressed.  Without it every read and every page fault would find them again.
	 * Guarded by am_lock, like everything else that reaches apfs_lib.
	 */
	struct apfs_cfile  an_cf;
	/*
	 * The inode record as it was when the vnode was made.  Nothing on this volume can
	 * change -- the mount is read only and there is no writer anywhere -- so there is
	 * nothing to invalidate, and a read no longer walks the tree for the record and the
	 * decmpfs header on every call.
	 */
	struct apfs_inode  an_ino;
	/*
	 * A symbolic link's target, read once: every path through the link asks for it again
	 * (/var, /tmp, /etc -- thousands of times a second after a boot), and it cannot change.
	 * Put in once (atomically), read without the lock, freed with the vnode.
	 */
	struct apfs_link  *an_link;
	/* read(2) through the page cache: where a reader in order would read next, and how much it was given ahead (hints, atomic) */
	uint64_t           an_read_next;
	uint32_t           an_read_window;
};

struct apfs_link {
	size_t             len;
	char               text[];
};

#define APFS_MP(mp)       ((struct apfs_mount *)vfs_fsprivate(mp))
const struct apfs_synth *apfs_synth_find(struct apfs_mount *am, uint64_t parent,
    const char *name, size_t len);      /* with am_lock held */

#define APFS_VP(vp)       ((struct apfs_node *)vnode_fsnode(vp))
#define APFS_VP_MOUNT(vp) (APFS_VP(vp)->an_mount)

/* apfs_vfsops.c */
extern struct vfsops apfs_vfsops;
int apfs_mountroot(mount_t mp, vnode_t devvp, vfs_context_t ctx);
int apfs_node_vnode(struct apfs_mount *am, uint64_t obj_id, vnode_t dvp,
    struct componentname *cnp, vnode_t *vpp);
void apfs_node_detach(struct apfs_node *an);

/* the breakdown of where the time went, straight to the log (apfs_vfsops.c) */
void apfs_stats_print(void);

void apfs_lock_at(struct apfs_mount *am, const char *site);  /* an operation begins */
#define apfs_lock(am) apfs_lock_at((am), __func__)
void apfs_unlock(struct apfs_mount *am);         /* and ends */
void apfs_lock_inner(struct apfs_mount *am);     /* the lock taken back in the middle of one (apfs_lib) */
void apfs_unlock_inner(struct apfs_mount *am);   /* let go of in the middle of one */

/* apfs_vnops.c */
extern const struct vnodeopv_desc apfs_vnodeop_opv_desc;
extern int (**apfs_vnodeop_p)(void *);

#endif /* _MISCFS_APFS_APFS_H_ */

```

`xnu/files/bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_deflate.c`:

```c
/*
 * libdeflate's decompressor, for the zlib pieces of compressed files.  The same file is
 * built into the kernel and into tools/apfs/apfs-tool, so the two run one decoder.
 *
 * The sources are bsd/miscfs/apfs/libdeflate as tools/mk-libdeflate.sh takes them from the
 * release, unchanged.  libdeflate is Copyright 2016 Eric Biggers and 2024 Google LLC, under
 * the MIT licence (libdeflate/COPYING).
 *
 * Built FREESTANDING: no C library, memcpy and friends become compiler built-ins, and the
 * CPU's features are only what the compiler is told -- here, NEON and nothing past it, so
 * the Adler-32 over each piece's output is libdeflate's NEON one (the decompressor itself
 * has no arm code of its own).  The kernel saves the vector registers on every exception
 * and its own lz4 decoder uses them, so that is safe here.  <arm_neon.h> comes from the
 * compiler (bsd/conf/Makefile.arm64).  What lib/utils.c would add is two pointers, the
 * allocator, given here instead; its fallback memset/memcpy are not wanted next to the
 * kernel's own.
 */
#define FREESTANDING 1

#include "libdeflate/lib/deflate_decompress.c"
#include "libdeflate/lib/zlib_decompress.c"
#include "libdeflate/lib/adler32.c"

/* in apfs_lib.c, which knows how this side allocates */
extern void *apfs_deflate_malloc(size_t size);
extern void apfs_deflate_free(void *ptr);

malloc_func_t libdeflate_default_malloc_func = apfs_deflate_malloc;
free_func_t libdeflate_default_free_func = apfs_deflate_free;
```

`xnu/files/bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_format.h`:

```h
/*
 * APFS on-disk layout, read side.
 *
 * Written from Apple's "Apple File System Reference" (2020-06-22), which is the only
 * description of the format there is.  Names and field order follow that document, so
 * that a reader can hold the two side by side; what the document calls out but we never
 * read on the way to a file's bytes (the space manager, the reaper, fusion, encryption
 * rolling, snapshots) is left out rather than copied in unused.
 *
 * Everything here is little-endian on disk and is read straight out of a block, so the
 * structures must match the disk byte for byte.  tools/apfs/fmt_check.c prints every
 * size and field offset in this file and tools/apfs/apfs.py checks its own idea of the
 * layout against that output -- run tools/apfs/run-tests.sh after touching this file.
 *
 * Decompression of file contents (the com.apple.decmpfs attribute) is not part of APFS
 * and is not in the reference; it is at the end of this file, from bsd/sys/decmpfs.h and
 * from what the Darwin userland 16.5 root file system actually contains.
 */

#ifndef _MISCFS_APFS_APFS_FORMAT_H_
#define _MISCFS_APFS_APFS_FORMAT_H_

#include <stdint.h>

typedef int64_t  apfs_paddr_t;   /* a block address within the container */
typedef uint64_t apfs_oid_t;     /* an object identifier */
typedef uint64_t apfs_xid_t;     /* a transaction identifier */

/* A run of blocks: pr_block_count blocks starting at pr_start_paddr. */
struct apfs_prange {
	apfs_paddr_t pr_start_paddr;
	uint64_t     pr_block_count;
};

/*
 * Objects
 *
 * Every object that occupies whole blocks starts with this header.  o_cksum is
 * Fletcher-64 over the rest of the block and is the only integrity check we have, so we
 * verify it on every block we read.
 */
#define APFS_MAX_CKSUM_SIZE 8

struct apfs_obj_phys {
	uint8_t    o_cksum[APFS_MAX_CKSUM_SIZE];
	apfs_oid_t o_oid;
	apfs_xid_t o_xid;
	uint32_t   o_type;      /* storage class and flags in the high half, type in the low */
	uint32_t   o_subtype;
};

/* o_type: the low half is the type, the high half says how the object is stored */
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_MASK           0x0000ffff
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_FLAGS_MASK     0xffff0000
#define APFS_OBJ_STORAGETYPE_MASK       0xc0000000
#define APFS_OBJ_VIRTUAL                0x00000000  /* found through an object map */
#define APFS_OBJ_EPHEMERAL              0x80000000  /* found through a checkpoint map */
#define APFS_OBJ_PHYSICAL               0x40000000  /* the identifier is the block address */
#define APFS_OBJ_NOHEADER               0x20000000  /* no apfs_obj_phys at the front */
#define APFS_OBJ_ENCRYPTED              0x10000000
#define APFS_OBJ_NONPERSISTENT          0x08000000

#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_NX_SUPERBLOCK  0x00000001
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_BTREE          0x00000002  /* a tree's root node */
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_BTREE_NODE     0x00000003  /* any other node */
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_SPACEMAN       0x00000005
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_SPACEMAN_BITMAP 0x00000008
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_OMAP           0x0000000b
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_CHECKPOINT_MAP 0x0000000c
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_FS             0x0000000d  /* a volume superblock */
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_FSTREE         0x0000000e  /* subtype: the file-system tree */
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_BLOCKREFTREE   0x0000000f  /* subtype: the extent reference tree */
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_SNAPMETATREE   0x00000010
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_NX_REAPER      0x00000011
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_EFI_JUMPSTART  0x00000014
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_INTEGRITY_META 0x0000001e
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_FEXT_TREE      0x0000001f
#define APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_INVALID        0x00000000

#define APFS_OID_INVALID        0ULL
#define APFS_OID_NX_SUPERBLOCK  1ULL
#define APFS_OID_RESERVED_COUNT 1024

/*
 * Container
 *
 * Block zero holds a copy of the container superblock, but it can be stale.  The live one
 * is the superblock with the largest transaction identifier in the checkpoint descriptor
 * area (nx_xp_desc_base, nx_xp_desc_blocks blocks long); that copy also names the
 * checkpoint's extent of descriptor blocks, nx_xp_desc_index..+nx_xp_desc_len.
 */
#define APFS_NX_MAGIC            0x4253584e  /* 'NXSB', little-endian on disk */
#define APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS 100
#define APFS_NX_EPH_INFO_COUNT   4
#define APFS_NX_NUM_COUNTERS     32
#define APFS_NX_DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE 4096
#define APFS_NX_MINIMUM_BLOCK_SIZE 4096
#define APFS_NX_MAXIMUM_BLOCK_SIZE 65536

struct apfs_nx_superblock {
	struct apfs_obj_phys nx_o;
	uint32_t     nx_magic;
	uint32_t     nx_block_size;
	uint64_t     nx_block_count;

	uint64_t     nx_features;
	uint64_t     nx_readonly_compatible_features;
	uint64_t     nx_incompatible_features;

	uint8_t      nx_uuid[16];

	apfs_oid_t   nx_next_oid;
	apfs_xid_t   nx_next_xid;

	/* the checkpoint areas: a ring of descriptor blocks and a ring of data blocks */
	uint32_t     nx_xp_desc_blocks;
	uint32_t     nx_xp_data_blocks;
	apfs_paddr_t nx_xp_desc_base;
	apfs_paddr_t nx_xp_data_base;
	uint32_t     nx_xp_desc_next;
	uint32_t     nx_xp_data_next;
	uint32_t     nx_xp_desc_index;
	uint32_t     nx_xp_desc_len;
	uint32_t     nx_xp_data_index;
	uint32_t     nx_xp_data_len;

	apfs_oid_t   nx_spaceman_oid;
	apfs_oid_t   nx_omap_oid;      /* the container's object map, a physical object */
	apfs_oid_t   nx_reaper_oid;

	uint32_t     nx_test_type;

	uint32_t     nx_max_file_systems;
	apfs_oid_t   nx_fs_oid[APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS];  /* volume superblocks, virtual */
	uint64_t     nx_counters[APFS_NX_NUM_COUNTERS];
	struct apfs_prange nx_blocked_out_prange;
	apfs_oid_t   nx_evict_mapping_tree_oid;
	uint64_t     nx_flags;
	apfs_paddr_t nx_efi_jumpstart;
	uint8_t      nx_fusion_uuid[16];
	struct apfs_prange nx_keylocker;
	uint64_t     nx_ephemeral_info[APFS_NX_EPH_INFO_COUNT];

	apfs_oid_t   nx_test_oid;

	apfs_oid_t   nx_fusion_mt_oid;
	apfs_oid_t   nx_fusion_wbc_oid;
	struct apfs_prange nx_fusion_wbc;

	uint64_t     nx_newest_mounted_version;

	struct apfs_prange nx_mkb_locker;
};

/* nx_incompatible_features: a container we would misread if we ignored these */
#define APFS_NX_INCOMPAT_VERSION1 0x0000000000000001ULL
#define APFS_NX_INCOMPAT_VERSION2 0x0000000000000002ULL
#define APFS_NX_INCOMPAT_FUSION   0x0000000000000100ULL

/*
 * Checkpoint maps
 *
 * Ephemeral objects live in the checkpoint data area rather than at a fixed place, so a
 * checkpoint's descriptor blocks carry a map from object identifier to block address.
 * We need this only for the space manager, so the read path mostly skips it.
 */
#define APFS_CHECKPOINT_MAP_LAST 0x00000001

struct apfs_checkpoint_mapping {
	uint32_t   cpm_type;
	uint32_t   cpm_subtype;
	uint32_t   cpm_size;
	uint32_t   cpm_pad;
	apfs_oid_t cpm_fs_oid;
	apfs_oid_t cpm_oid;
	apfs_oid_t cpm_paddr;
};

struct apfs_checkpoint_map_phys {
	struct apfs_obj_phys cpm_o;
	uint32_t             cpm_flags;
	uint32_t             cpm_count;
	struct apfs_checkpoint_mapping cpm_map[];
};

/*
 * Object maps
 *
 * A virtual object identifier means nothing by itself: it has to be looked up in an
 * object map, which is a B-tree keyed by (identifier, transaction) and whose values give
 * the block address.  The container's map resolves volume superblocks; each volume's map
 * resolves the nodes of that volume's file-system tree.
 */
struct apfs_omap_phys {
	struct apfs_obj_phys om_o;
	uint32_t   om_flags;
	uint32_t   om_snap_count;
	uint32_t   om_tree_type;
	uint32_t   om_snapshot_tree_type;
	apfs_oid_t om_tree_oid;            /* the map itself, a physical B-tree */
	apfs_oid_t om_snapshot_tree_oid;
	apfs_xid_t om_most_recent_snap;
	apfs_xid_t om_pending_revert_min;
	apfs_xid_t om_pending_revert_max;
};

struct apfs_omap_key {
	apfs_oid_t ok_oid;
	apfs_xid_t ok_xid;
};

struct apfs_omap_val {
	uint32_t     ov_flags;
	uint32_t     ov_size;
	apfs_paddr_t ov_paddr;
};

#define APFS_OMAP_VAL_DELETED           0x00000001
#define APFS_OMAP_VAL_SAVED             0x00000002
#define APFS_OMAP_VAL_ENCRYPTED         0x00000004
#define APFS_OMAP_VAL_NOHEADER          0x00000008
#define APFS_OMAP_VAL_CRYPTO_GENERATION 0x00000010

/*
 * Volumes
 */
#define APFS_MAGIC_VOL        0x42535041  /* 'APSB', little-endian on disk */
#define APFS_MAX_HIST         8
#define APFS_MODIFIED_NAMELEN 32
#define APFS_VOLNAME_LEN      256

struct apfs_modified_by {
	uint8_t    id[APFS_MODIFIED_NAMELEN];
	uint64_t   timestamp;
	apfs_xid_t last_xid;
};

/* The metadata encryption state; we only read it to check the volume is not encrypted. */
struct apfs_wrapped_meta_crypto_state {
	uint16_t major_version;
	uint16_t minor_version;
	uint32_t cpflags;
	uint32_t persistent_class;
	uint32_t key_os_version;
	uint16_t key_revision;
	uint16_t unused;
} __attribute__((aligned(2), packed));

struct apfs_superblock {
	struct apfs_obj_phys apfs_o;

	uint32_t   apfs_magic;
	uint32_t   apfs_fs_index;

	uint64_t   apfs_features;
	uint64_t   apfs_readonly_compatible_features;
	uint64_t   apfs_incompatible_features;

	uint64_t   apfs_unmount_time;

	uint64_t   apfs_fs_reserve_block_count;
	uint64_t   apfs_fs_quota_block_count;
	uint64_t   apfs_fs_alloc_count;

	struct apfs_wrapped_meta_crypto_state apfs_meta_crypto;

	uint32_t   apfs_root_tree_type;
	uint32_t   apfs_extentref_tree_type;
	uint32_t   apfs_snap_meta_tree_type;

	apfs_oid_t apfs_omap_oid;            /* this volume's object map, physical */
	apfs_oid_t apfs_root_tree_oid;       /* the file-system tree, virtual */
	apfs_oid_t apfs_extentref_tree_oid;
	apfs_oid_t apfs_snap_meta_tree_oid;

	apfs_xid_t apfs_revert_to_xid;
	apfs_oid_t apfs_revert_to_sblock_oid;

	uint64_t   apfs_next_obj_id;

	uint64_t   apfs_num_files;
	uint64_t   apfs_num_directories;
	uint64_t   apfs_num_symlinks;
	uint64_t   apfs_num_other_fsobjects;
	uint64_t   apfs_num_snapshots;

	uint64_t   apfs_total_blocks_alloced;
	uint64_t   apfs_total_blocks_freed;

	uint8_t    apfs_vol_uuid[16];
	uint64_t   apfs_last_mod_time;

	uint64_t   apfs_fs_flags;

	struct apfs_modified_by apfs_formatted_by;
	struct apfs_modified_by apfs_modified_by[APFS_MAX_HIST];

	uint8_t    apfs_volname[APFS_VOLNAME_LEN];
	uint32_t   apfs_next_doc_id;

	uint16_t   apfs_role;
	uint16_t   reserved;

	apfs_xid_t apfs_root_to_xid;
	apfs_oid_t apfs_er_state_oid;

	uint64_t   apfs_cloneinfo_id_epoch;
	uint64_t   apfs_cloneinfo_xid;

	apfs_oid_t apfs_snap_meta_ext_oid;

	uint8_t    apfs_volume_group_id[16];

	apfs_oid_t apfs_integrity_meta_oid;

	apfs_oid_t apfs_fext_tree_oid;
	uint32_t   apfs_fext_tree_type;

	uint32_t   reserved_type;
	apfs_oid_t reserved_oid;
};

/* apfs_incompatible_features: these change how we read names and extents */
#define APFS_INCOMPAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE          0x00000001ULL
#define APFS_INCOMPAT_DATALESS_SNAPS            0x00000002ULL
#define APFS_INCOMPAT_ENC_ROLLED                0x00000004ULL
#define APFS_INCOMPAT_NORMALIZATION_INSENSITIVE 0x00000008ULL
#define APFS_INCOMPAT_INCOMPLETE_RESTORE        0x00000010ULL
#define APFS_INCOMPAT_SEALED_VOLUME             0x00000020ULL

/* apfs_fs_flags */
#define APFS_FS_UNENCRYPTED 0x00000001ULL
#define APFS_FS_ONEKEY      0x00000008ULL
#define APFS_FS_SPILLEDOVER 0x00000010ULL

/* apfs_role */
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_NONE      0x0000
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_SYSTEM    0x0001
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_USER      0x0002
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_RECOVERY  0x0004
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_VM        0x0008
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_PREBOOT   0x0010
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_INSTALLER 0x0020
#define APFS_VOLUME_ENUM_SHIFT  6
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_DATA      (1 << APFS_VOLUME_ENUM_SHIFT)
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_BASEBAND  (2 << APFS_VOLUME_ENUM_SHIFT)
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_UPDATE    (3 << APFS_VOLUME_ENUM_SHIFT)
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_XART      (4 << APFS_VOLUME_ENUM_SHIFT)
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_HARDWARE  (5 << APFS_VOLUME_ENUM_SHIFT)
#define APFS_VOL_ROLE_BACKUP    (6 << APFS_VOLUME_ENUM_SHIFT)

/*
 * B-trees
 *
 * Every tree is one of these node blocks.  A node is laid out as: the header, then a
 * table of contents, then keys growing from the start of the key area forward, then free
 * space, then values growing from the end of the block backwards.  A root node keeps a
 * struct apfs_btree_info in the last bytes of the block, so the value area of a root node
 * stops short of it.
 *
 * Two layouts of the table of contents: with BTNODE_FIXED_KV_SIZE every key and value is
 * the same size and an entry is a struct apfs_kvoff (offsets only); otherwise an entry is
 * a struct apfs_kvloc (offset and length for each).
 *
 * Offsets in the table of contents are relative to the start of the key area for keys,
 * and backwards from the end of the value area for values.
 */
#define APFS_BTNODE_ROOT             0x0001
#define APFS_BTNODE_LEAF             0x0002
#define APFS_BTNODE_FIXED_KV_SIZE    0x0004
#define APFS_BTNODE_HASHED           0x0008
#define APFS_BTNODE_NOHEADER         0x0010
#define APFS_BTNODE_CHECK_KOFF_INVAL 0x8000

#define APFS_BTOFF_INVALID 0xffff

struct apfs_nloc {         /* a location inside a node: offset and length */
	uint16_t off;
	uint16_t len;
};

struct apfs_kvloc {        /* a table-of-contents entry, variable sizes */
	struct apfs_nloc k;
	struct apfs_nloc v;
};

struct apfs_kvoff {        /* a table-of-contents entry, fixed sizes */
	uint16_t k;
	uint16_t v;
};

struct apfs_btree_node_phys {
	struct apfs_obj_phys btn_o;
	uint16_t btn_flags;
	uint16_t btn_level;        /* 0 at the leaves */
	uint32_t btn_nkeys;
	struct apfs_nloc btn_table_space;   /* the table of contents, within btn_data */
	struct apfs_nloc btn_free_space;    /* the gap between keys and values */
	struct apfs_nloc btn_key_free_list;
	struct apfs_nloc btn_val_free_list;
	uint64_t btn_data[];
};

#define APFS_BTREE_UINT64_KEYS       0x00000001
#define APFS_BTREE_SEQUENTIAL_INSERT 0x00000002
#define APFS_BTREE_ALLOW_GHOSTS      0x00000004
#define APFS_BTREE_EPHEMERAL         0x00000008
#define APFS_BTREE_PHYSICAL          0x00000010  /* child identifiers are block addresses */
#define APFS_BTREE_NONPERSISTENT     0x00000020
#define APFS_BTREE_KV_NONALIGNED     0x00000040
#define APFS_BTREE_HASHED            0x00000080
#define APFS_BTREE_NOHEADER          0x00000100

#define APFS_BTREE_NODE_HASH_SIZE_MAX 64
#define APFS_BTREE_NODE_SIZE_DEFAULT  4096

struct apfs_btree_info_fixed {
	uint32_t bt_flags;
	uint32_t bt_node_size;

/*

/*
 * Compressed file contents
 *
 * Not part of APFS and not in Apple's reference.  A compressed file carries the attribute
 * com.apple.decmpfs, whose value starts with this header; where the compressed bytes
 * themselves are depends on the type.  The header is little-endian.
 *
 * XNU (bsd/sys/decmpfs.h) names only type 1; the rest live in Apple's closed
 * AppleFSCompression.  The types below are the ones the Darwin userland 16.5 root file system
 * actually uses -- see tools/apfs/apfs.py, which counts them over the whole volume.
 *
 * In the attribute (types 3 and 4 the common pair): the bytes after the header are a
 * single zlib stream, except that a first byte of 0xff means the rest is the uncompressed
 * contents as they are.  In the resource fork (the com.apple.ResourceFork attribute): the
 * contents are cut into 64 KB pieces, each its own zlib stream, with a table of their
 * offsets at the front.
 */
#define APFS_DECMPFS_XATTR_NAME  "com.apple.decmpfs"
#define APFS_DECMPFS_MAGIC       0x636d7066   /* 'cmpf' */
#define APFS_RSRC_FORK_XATTR_NAME "com.apple.ResourceFork"

struct apfs_decmpfs_disk_header {
	uint32_t compression_magic;
	uint32_t compression_type;
	uint64_t uncompressed_size;
	uint8_t  attr_bytes[0];
} __attribute__((packed));

#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_ZLIB_ATTR  3   /* zlib, bytes in the attribute */
#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_ZLIB_RSRC  4   /* zlib, bytes in the resource fork */
#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_RAW_ATTR   9   /* uncompressed, bytes in the attribute */
#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_RAW_RSRC   10  /* uncompressed, bytes in the resource fork */
#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_LZFSE_ATTR 11
#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_LZFSE_RSRC 12
#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_LZBITMAP_ATTR 13  /* LZBITMAP, bytes in the attribute */
#define APFS_DECMPFS_TYPE_LZBITMAP_RSRC 14  /* LZBITMAP, 64 KB pieces in the resource fork behind
                                               a table of n+1 little-endian offsets */

/* the pieces a resource-fork-compressed file is cut into */
#define APFS_DECMPFS_BLOCK_SIZE 65536

#endif /* _MISCFS_APFS_APFS_FORMAT_H_ */

```

`xnu/files/bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_lib.c`:

```c
/*
 * Reading the Apple File System.  See apfs_lib.h for what this does and does not do, and
 * apfs_format.h for the layout.  Nothing here writes to the device.
 *
 * Everything on disk is little-endian and is read with memcpy through the le* helpers, so
 * none of this depends on the alignment of a field inside a block.
 *
 * Validation is the point of most of the code that is not a struct field being copied: a
 * block that fails its Fletcher-64, an offset that leaves its node, a length that does not
 * fit the record it came from, a tree deeper than APFS_MAX_LEVELS -- each ends the call
 * with EIO rather than being followed.
 */

#include "apfs_lib.h"

#if defined(KERNEL) || defined(APFS_HOST_UNICODE)
#define APFS_HAVE_UNICODE 1
#include <sys/unicode.h>                /* utf8_normalizeOptCaseFoldAndHash, ...AndCompare (bsd/vfs/vfs_unicode.c) */
#else
#define APFS_HAVE_UNICODE 0
#endif

#ifdef KERNEL
#include <libkern/zlib.h>
#else
#include <zlib.h>
#endif
#include "libdeflate/libdeflate.h"
#include "libzbitmap/libzbitmap.h"
#ifdef KERNEL
#include <libkern/crypto/sha2.h>
#else
#include <openssl/sha.h>
#endif

/* The pieces a resource-fork-compressed file is cut into. */
#define APFS_RSRC_PIECE APFS_DECMPFS_BLOCK_SIZE

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ bytes */

static inline uint16_t
le16(const uint8_t *p)
{
	uint16_t v;
	memcpy(&v, p, sizeof(v));
	return v;
}

static inline uint32_t
le32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	uint32_t v;
	memcpy(&v, p, sizeof(v));
	return v;
}

static inline uint64_t
le64(const uint8_t *p)
{
	uint64_t v;
	memcpy(&v, p, sizeof(v));
	return v;
}

static inline uint32_t
be32(const uint8_t *p)
{
	return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) |
	       ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | (uint32_t)p[3];
}

/*
 * Fletcher-64 as APFS uses it: over the block with its own checksum field included, the
 * result is zero; over the block after the field, the result is what the field holds.
 */
uint64_t
apfs_fletcher64(const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
{
	const uint64_t mod = 0xFFFFFFFFULL;
	uint64_t sum1 = 0, sum2 = 0;
	size_t i;

	for (i = 0; i + 4 <= len; i += 4) {
		sum1 = (sum1 + le32(data + i)) % mod;
		sum2 = (sum2 + sum1) % mod;
	}
	{
		uint64_t c1 = mod - ((sum1 + sum2) % mod);
		uint64_t c2 = mod - ((sum1 + c1) % mod);
		return (c2 << 32) | c1;
	}
}

bool
apfs_checksum_ok(const uint8_t *block, uint32_t block_size)
{
	if (block_size < 8 || (block_size % 4) != 0) {
		return false;
	}
	return apfs_fletcher64(block + 8, block_size - 8) == le64(block);
}

uint16_t
apfs_mode_to_dtype(uint16_t mode)
{
	switch (mode & APFS_S_IFMT) {
	case APFS_S_IFIFO:  return APFS_DT_FIFO;
	case APFS_S_IFCHR:  return APFS_DT_CHR;
	case APFS_S_IFDIR:  return APFS_DT_DIR;
	case APFS_S_IFBLK:  return APFS_DT_BLK;
	case APFS_S_IFREG:  return APFS_DT_REG;
	case APFS_S_IFLNK:  return APFS_DT_LNK;
	case APFS_S_IFSOCK: return APFS_DT_SOCK;
	default:            return APFS_DT_UNKNOWN;
	}
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ blocks */

/*
 * A block of metadata, from the cache or from the device.  The returned pointer stays
 * good while fewer than APFS_CACHE_RECENT further blocks have been fetched -- the clock
 * hand passes over a block used that recently -- which is why a B-tree descent holds
 * block addresses and not pointers.
 */
static inline uint32_t
cache_bucket(uint64_t addr)
{
	return (uint32_t)((addr * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL) >> 40) & (APFS_CACHE_HASH - 1);
}

/* A cached block's memory leaves the cache; it is freed by apfs_nx_reclaim once nobody can be reading it. */
static void
cache_retire(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint8_t *data)
{
	struct apfs_retired *r = apfs_alloc(sizeof(*r));

	if (r == NULL) {
		return;                 /* never freed then: that is safe, merely a block lost */
	}
	r->data = data;
	r->epoch = nx->epoch++;
	r->next = nx->retired;
	nx->retired = r;
	if (++nx->retired_now > nx->retired_most) {
		nx->retired_most = nx->retired_now;
	}
}

void
apfs_nx_reclaim(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint64_t oldest)
{
	struct apfs_retired **pp = &nx->retired, *r;

	/* newest first: past the first one old enough, all are */
	while (*pp != NULL && (*pp)->epoch >= oldest) {
		pp = &(*pp)->next;
	}
	while ((r = *pp) != NULL) {
		*pp = r->next;
		apfs_free(r->data, nx->block_size);
		apfs_free(r, sizeof(*r));
		nx->retired_now--;
	}
}

#ifndef KERNEL
void
apfs_nx_cache_flush(struct apfs_nx *nx)
{
	uint32_t i;

	for (i = 0; i < APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS; i++) {
		struct apfs_buf *b = &nx->cache[i];

		if (b->data != NULL && nx->unlock != NULL) {
			cache_retire(nx, b->data);
			b->data = NULL;
		}
		b->addr = APFS_BUF_EMPTY;
		b->next = -1;
		b->ref = false;
	}
	for (i = 0; i < APFS_CACHE_HASH; i++) {
		nx->cache_hash[i] = -1;
	}
	if (nx->omap_cache != NULL) {
		memset(nx->omap_cache, 0, APFS_OMAP_CACHE * sizeof(*nx->omap_cache));
	}
}
#endif

/* A free slot, or the first the clock hand finds neither used since it last passed nor recent. */
static struct apfs_buf *
cache_victim(struct apfs_nx *nx)
{
	struct apfs_buf *victim;
	uint32_t steps = 0;
	int32_t *pp;

	for (;;) {
		victim = &nx->cache[nx->hand];
		nx->hand = (nx->hand + 1) % APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS;
		if (victim->data == NULL) {
			victim->data = apfs_alloc(nx->block_size);
			if (victim->data == NULL) {
				return NULL;
			}
			break;
		}
		if (!victim->ref && nx->fetches - victim->used >= APFS_CACHE_RECENT) {
			break;
		}
		victim->ref = false;
		if (++steps >= 2 * APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS) {
			/* every block used that recently: the one used longest ago, then */
			uint32_t k, best = 0;

			for (k = 1; k < APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS; k++) {
				if (nx->fetches - nx->cache[k].used > nx->fetches - nx->cache[best].used) {
					best = k;
				}
			}
			victim = &nx->cache[best];
			break;
		}
	}
	if (nx->unlock != NULL && victim->data != NULL && victim->addr != APFS_BUF_EMPTY) {
		/* somebody may still be reading the block that had it: new memory for the new one */
		uint8_t *fresh = apfs_alloc(nx->block_size);

		if (fresh == NULL) {
			return NULL;
		}
		cache_retire(nx, victim->data);
		victim->data = fresh;
	}
	if (victim->addr != APFS_BUF_EMPTY) {
		/* out of its old chain */
		for (pp = &nx->cache_hash[cache_bucket(victim->addr)]; *pp >= 0;
		    pp = &nx->cache[*pp].next) {
			if (&nx->cache[*pp] == victim) {
				*pp = victim->next;
				break;
			}
		}
		victim->addr = APFS_BUF_EMPTY;
	}
	victim->next = -1;
	return victim;
}

static void
cache_link(struct apfs_nx *nx, struct apfs_buf *b, uint64_t addr)
{
	uint32_t bucket = cache_bucket(addr);

	b->addr = addr;
	b->next = nx->cache_hash[bucket];
	nx->cache_hash[bucket] = (int32_t)(b - nx->cache);
}

static struct apfs_buf *
cache_find(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint64_t addr)
{
	int32_t i;

	for (i = nx->cache_hash[cache_bucket(addr)]; i >= 0; i = nx->cache[i].next) {
		if (nx->cache[i].addr == addr) {
			return &nx->cache[i];
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}

static inline void nx_unlock(struct apfs_nx *nx);
static inline void nx_relock(struct apfs_nx *nx);

/*
 * A block of metadata not in the cache, read without the lock: the block and its aligned
 * neighbours into memory of this call's own, the lock taken back, and put in -- unless
 * somebody put the block in meanwhile, whose copy is used then (and only the neighbours not
 * there yet go in). Cache slots that get a block get new memory (cache_victim), so nothing
 * anyone still reads is overwritten.
 */
static int
nx_block_unlocked(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint64_t addr, const uint8_t **out, bool verify)
{
	uint32_t bs = nx->block_size;
	uint32_t k = nx->meta_cluster != 0 ?
	    (nx->meta_cluster > APFS_META_CLUSTER ? APFS_META_CLUSTER : nx->meta_cluster) : APFS_META_CLUSTER_DEFAULT;
	uint64_t first = addr - addr % k, count = nx->block_count - first < k ? nx->block_count - first : k, i, t0, dt;
	struct apfs_buf *b;
	uint8_t *mine = apfs_alloc((size_t)count * bs);
	int error;

	if (mine == NULL) {
		return ENOMEM;
	}
	nx->unlocked_fills++;
	nx_unlock(nx);
	t0 = apfs_ticks();
	error = nx->dev.read_data(nx->dev.ctx, first * (uint64_t)bs, mine, (size_t)count * bs);
	dt = apfs_ticks() - t0;
	nx_relock(nx);
	nx->dev_ticks += dt;
	nx->dev_calls++;
	nx->dev_bytes += count * bs;
	if (error) {
		apfs_free(mine, (size_t)count * bs);
		return error;
	}
	nx->fetches++;
	b = cache_find(nx, addr);
	if (b != NULL) {
		nx->fill_races++;               /* in already, by somebody else's read */
		if (verify && !b->checked) {
			if (!apfs_checksum_ok(b->data, bs)) {
				apfs_log("block %llu: bad checksum\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
				apfs_free(mine, (size_t)count * bs);
				return EIO;
			}
			b->checked = true;
		}
	} else {
		b = cache_victim(nx);
		if (b == NULL) {
			apfs_free(mine, (size_t)count * bs);
			return ENOMEM;
		}
		memcpy(b->data, mine + (addr - first) * bs, bs);
		nx->reads++;
		if (verify && !apfs_checksum_ok(b->data, bs)) {
			apfs_log("block %llu: bad checksum\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
			apfs_free(mine, (size_t)count * bs);
			return EIO;             /* (the slot stays empty: cache_victim took it out of its chain) */
		}
		b->checked = verify;
		cache_link(nx, b, addr);
	}
	b->ref = true;
	b->used = nx->fetches;
	/* the neighbours not there yet: kept as if long unused, checked when asked for */
	for (i = first; i < first + count; i++) {
		struct apfs_buf *nb;

		if (i == addr || i == 0 || cache_find(nx, i) != NULL) {
			continue;
		}
		nb = cache_victim(nx);
		if (nb == NULL) {
			break;
		}
		memcpy(nb->data, mine + (i - first) * bs, bs);
		nb->checked = false;
		nb->ref = false;
		nb->used = nx->fetches - APFS_CACHE_RECENT;
		cache_link(nx, nb, i);
		nx->prefetched++;
	}
	apfs_free(mine, (size_t)count * bs);
	*out = b->data;
	return 0;
}

static int
nx_block(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint64_t addr, const uint8_t **out, bool verify)
{
	struct apfs_buf *victim, *b;
	uint64_t first = 0, count = 0, i;
	int error;

	if (addr == 0 || addr >= nx->block_count) {
		return EIO;
	}
	if (addr > nx->max_addr) {
		nx->max_addr = addr;
	}
	b = cache_find(nx, addr);
	if (b != NULL) {
		if (verify && !b->checked) {
			/* brought in as a neighbour, asked for now */
			if (!apfs_checksum_ok(b->data, nx->block_size)) {
				apfs_log("block %llu: bad checksum\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
				return EIO;
			}
			b->checked = true;
		}
		if (!b->ref && nx->fetches - b->used >= APFS_CACHE_RECENT) {
			nx->prefetch_used++;    /* (or one used long ago; near enough) */
		}
		b->ref = true;
		b->used = nx->fetches;
		nx->hits++;
		*out = b->data;
		return 0;
	}
	if (nx->unlock != NULL && nx->dev.read_data != NULL && !nx->cheap_requests) {
		return nx_block_unlocked(nx, addr, out, verify);
	}
	victim = cache_victim(nx);
	if (victim == NULL) {
		return ENOMEM;
	}
	nx->fetches++;
	if (nx->cluster == NULL && nx->dev.read_data != NULL) {
		nx->cluster = apfs_alloc((size_t)APFS_META_CLUSTER * nx->block_size);
	}
	{
		uint64_t t0 = apfs_ticks();

		uint32_t k = nx->meta_cluster != 0 ?
		    (nx->meta_cluster > APFS_META_CLUSTER ? APFS_META_CLUSTER : nx->meta_cluster) :
		    nx->cheap_requests ? 1 : APFS_META_CLUSTER_DEFAULT;

		if (nx->cluster != NULL && k > 1) {
			/* the block and its aligned neighbours, in one request */
			first = addr - addr % k;
			count = nx->block_count - first < k ? nx->block_count - first : k;
			error = nx->dev.read_data(nx->dev.ctx, first * (uint64_t)nx->block_size,
			    nx->cluster, (size_t)count * nx->block_size);
			if (error == 0) {
				memcpy(victim->data, nx->cluster + (addr - first) * nx->block_size,
				    nx->block_size);
			}
			nx->dev_bytes += count * nx->block_size;
		} else {
			error = nx->dev.read(nx->dev.ctx, addr * (uint64_t)nx->block_size,
			    victim->data, nx->block_size);
			nx->dev_bytes += nx->block_size;
		}
		nx->dev_ticks += apfs_ticks() - t0;
		nx->dev_calls++;
	}
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	nx->reads++;
	if (verify && !apfs_checksum_ok(victim->data, nx->block_size)) {
		apfs_log("block %llu: bad checksum\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
		return EIO;
	}
	victim->checked = verify;
	victim->ref = true;
	victim->used = nx->fetches;
	cache_link(nx, victim, addr);
	/*
	 * The neighbours: kept as if long unused, so that they are the first to go if nobody
	 * asks for them, and checked when somebody does.
	 */
	for (i = first; i < first + count; i++) {
		struct apfs_buf *nb;

		if (i == addr || i == 0 || cache_find(nx, i) != NULL) {
			continue;
		}
		nb = cache_victim(nx);
		if (nb == NULL) {
			break;
		}
		memcpy(nb->data, nx->cluster + (i - first) * nx->block_size, nx->block_size);
		nb->checked = false;
		nb->ref = false;
		nb->used = nx->fetches - APFS_CACHE_RECENT;
		cache_link(nx, nb, i);
		nx->prefetched++;
	}
	*out = victim->data;
	return 0;
}

static inline void
nx_unlock(struct apfs_nx *nx)
{
	if (nx->unlock != NULL) {
		nx->unlock(nx->lock_ctx);
	}
}

static inline void
nx_relock(struct apfs_nx *nx)
{
	if (nx->relock != NULL) {
		nx->relock(nx->lock_ctx);
	}
}

static uint32_t
obj_type(const uint8_t *blk)
{
	return le32(blk + 24) & APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_MASK;
}

static apfs_xid_t
obj_xid(const uint8_t *blk)
{
	return le64(blk + 16);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ b-tree nodes */

struct node {
	const uint8_t *blk;
	uint16_t       flags;
	uint16_t       level;
	uint32_t       nkeys;
	uint32_t       toc_off;
	uint32_t       toc_len;
	uint32_t       key_base;
	uint32_t       val_end;
	bool           fixed;
	bool           leaf;
};

/*
 * Pick a node block apart and check that every area it describes is inside the block.
 * A node is: the object header, the table of contents, then keys growing forward from the
 * end of the table and values growing backwards from the end of the block -- short of the
 * btree_info that a root node keeps in its last bytes.
 */
static int
node_parse(struct apfs_btree *tree, const uint8_t *blk, struct node *n)
{
	uint32_t bs = tree->nx->block_size;
	uint32_t ts_off, ts_len, ent, need;

	n->blk = blk;
	n->flags = le16(blk + 32);
	n->level = le16(blk + 34);
	n->nkeys = le32(blk + 36);
	ts_off = le16(blk + 40);
	ts_len = le16(blk + 42);
	n->fixed = (n->flags & APFS_BTNODE_FIXED_KV_SIZE) != 0;
	n->leaf = (n->flags & APFS_BTNODE_LEAF) != 0;

	if (n->level >= APFS_MAX_LEVELS) {
		return EIO;
	}
	n->toc_off = 56 + ts_off;
	n->toc_len = ts_len;
	if (n->toc_off < 56 || n->toc_off > bs || n->toc_len > bs - n->toc_off) {
		return EIO;
	}
	n->key_base = n->toc_off + n->toc_len;
	n->val_end = bs;
	if (n->flags & APFS_BTNODE_ROOT) {
		if (bs < 56 + sizeof(struct apfs_btree_info)) {
			return EIO;
		}
		n->val_end = bs - (uint32_t)sizeof(struct apfs_btree_info);
	}
	if (n->key_base > n->val_end) {
		return EIO;
	}
	/* the table of contents must hold the entries the header claims */
	ent = n->fixed ? 4u : 8u;
	if (n->nkeys > (bs / ent)) {
		return EIO;
	}
	need = n->nkeys * ent;
	if (need > n->toc_len) {
		return EIO;
	}
	if (n->fixed && n->leaf && tree->key_size == 0) {
		return EIO;         /* fixed layout with no size to use */
	}
	return 0;
}

/*
 * Entry i of a node.  A value offset of 0xffff marks a key with no value ("a ghost"),
 * which comes back as a zero length rather than an error.
 */
static int
node_entry(struct apfs_btree *tree, const struct node *n, uint32_t i,
    const uint8_t **kp, uint16_t *klen, const uint8_t **vp, uint16_t *vlen)
{
	uint32_t koff, voff, kl, vl;

	if (i >= n->nkeys) {
		return EIO;
	}
	if (n->fixed) {
		koff = le16(n->blk + n->toc_off + 4 * i);
		voff = le16(n->blk + n->toc_off + 4 * i + 2);
		kl = tree->key_size;
		vl = n->leaf ? tree->val_size : 8;
	} else {
		koff = le16(n->blk + n->toc_off + 8 * i);
		kl = le16(n->blk + n->toc_off + 8 * i + 2);
		voff = le16(n->blk + n->toc_off + 8 * i + 4);
		vl = le16(n->blk + n->toc_off + 8 * i + 6);
	}
	/* a key lives at key_base + offset and must end before the value area */
	if (koff > n->val_end - n->key_base || kl > n->val_end - n->key_base - koff) {
		return EIO;
	}
	*kp = n->blk + n->key_base + koff;
	*klen = (uint16_t)kl;

	if (voff == APFS_BTOFF_INVALID && !n->fixed) {
		*vp = NULL;
		*vlen = 0;
		return 0;
	}
	/* a value is measured backwards from the end of the value area */
	if (voff > n->val_end || vl > voff || n->val_end - voff < n->key_base) {
		return EIO;
	}
	*vp = n->blk + n->val_end - voff;
	*vlen = (uint16_t)vl;
	return 0;
}

/* The identifier of child i of a non-leaf node. */
static int
node_child(struct apfs_btree *tree, const struct node *n, uint32_t i, uint64_t *oid)
{
	const uint8_t *k, *v;
	uint16_t kl, vl;
	int error = node_entry(tree, n, i, &k, &kl, &v, &vl);

	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	if (v == NULL || vl < 8) {
		return EIO;
	}
	*oid = le64(v);
	return 0;
}

static int cfile_header(struct apfs_vol *vol, const struct apfs_inode *ino,
    bool *compressed, uint32_t *type, uint64_t *size, bool *in_rsrc);

/* Where a node identifier actually is: a block address, directly or through a map. */
static int
tree_node_addr(struct apfs_btree *tree, uint64_t oid, uint64_t *addr);

/*
 * Read a node that is already known by block address.
 *
 * Everything that walks a tree keeps block addresses, never object identifiers: the root
 * is only ever an address, so a cursor that mixed the two would resolve the root's
 * address through the object map as though it were an identifier.  That lookup fails with
 * ENOENT, which a caller scanning for records reads as "there are no more" -- the records
 * of the object quietly go missing instead of the read failing.
 */
/*
 * A sealed volume (the Darwin cryptexes) keeps its file-system tree in nodes without an object
 * header -- no Fletcher checksum -- and each parent keeps the SHA-256 of each child's whole
 * block instead.  Checked once per block the cache brings in (b->checked, which for such a
 * block means "its hash was right"); `len` is 32 on the way down, 8 when a cursor comes back
 * to a node it had left (apfs_cursor.hash8).  The root has no parent: Apple checks it against
 * the volume's root hash, which is kept outside the image (the IPSW's .root_hash), and
 * nothing here has that.
 */
static void
apfs_sha256(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, uint8_t out[32])
{
#ifdef KERNEL
	SHA256_CTX c;

	SHA256_Init(&c);
	SHA256_Update(&c, data, len);
	SHA256_Final(out, &c);
#else
	SHA256(data, len, out);
#endif
}

static int
node_hash_check(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint64_t addr, const uint8_t *blk, const uint8_t *hash, size_t len)
{
	struct apfs_buf *b = cache_find(nx, addr);
	uint8_t d[32];

	if (b != NULL && b->checked) {
		return 0;
	}
	apfs_sha256(blk, nx->block_size, d);
	if (memcmp(d, hash, len) != 0) {
		apfs_log("block %llu: not the node its parent names (SHA-256)\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
		return EIO;
	}
	if (b != NULL) {
		b->checked = true;
	}
	return 0;
}

/* hash8: for a sealed tree's node, the first 8 bytes of its SHA-256 (0 for the root: none) */
static int
node_at_h(struct apfs_btree *tree, uint64_t addr, uint64_t hash8, const uint8_t **blk, struct node *n)
{
	bool noheader = (tree->flags & APFS_BTREE_NOHEADER) != 0;
	int error = nx_block(tree->nx, addr, blk, !noheader);

	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	if (noheader) {
		uint8_t h[8];

		if ((le16(*blk + 32) & APFS_BTNODE_NOHEADER) == 0) {
			return EIO;
		}
		if (addr != tree->root) {
			if (hash8 == 0) {
				return EIO;     /* (a node below the root always comes with its parent's hash) */
			}
			memcpy(h, &hash8, 8);
			error = node_hash_check(tree->nx, addr, *blk, h, 8);
			if (error) {
				return error;
			}
		}
	} else if (obj_type(*blk) != APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_BTREE &&
	    obj_type(*blk) != APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_BTREE_NODE) {
		return EIO;
	}
	return node_parse(tree, *blk, n);
}

static int
node_at(struct apfs_btree *tree, uint64_t addr, const uint8_t **blk, struct node *n)
{
	return node_at_h(tree, addr, 0, blk, n);
}

/*
 * The block address of child i of a non-leaf node.  In a sealed (hashed) tree the value also
 * holds the child's SHA-256, and the id in it is an offset from the root's id -- apfsck says
 * so as well; Apple's reference does not.  The child's block is checked against the hash
 * here, and the first 8 bytes of it given back for a cursor to keep (hash8, may be NULL).
 */
static int
node_child_addr(struct apfs_btree *tree, const struct node *n, uint32_t i, uint64_t *addr,
    uint64_t *hash8)
{
	const uint8_t *k, *v, *blk;
	uint16_t kl, vl;
	uint8_t hash[32];
	uint64_t oid;
	int error;

	if ((tree->flags & APFS_BTREE_HASHED) == 0) {
		error = node_child(tree, n, i, &oid);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
		if (hash8 != NULL) {
			*hash8 = 0;
		}
		return tree_node_addr(tree, oid, addr);
	}
	error = node_entry(tree, n, i, &k, &kl, &v, &vl);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	if (v == NULL || vl != 8 + sizeof(hash)) {
		apfs_log("a sealed tree's node with a %u-byte child entry (only SHA-256 is known here)\n", vl);
		return ENOTSUP;
	}
	oid = le64(v) + tree->root_oid;
	memcpy(hash, v + 8, sizeof(hash));
	error = tree_node_addr(tree, oid, addr);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	error = nx_block(tree->nx, *addr, &blk, (tree->flags & APFS_BTREE_NOHEADER) == 0);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	if (tree->flags & APFS_BTREE_NOHEADER) {
		error = node_hash_check(tree->nx, *addr, blk, hash, sizeof(hash));
	}
	if (error == 0 && hash8 != NULL) {
		memcpy(hash8, hash, 8);
	}
	return error;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ object maps */

static int omap_find(struct apfs_omap *omap, uint64_t oid, apfs_xid_t want_xid,
    uint64_t *addr);

static int
tree_node_addr(struct apfs_btree *tree, uint64_t oid, uint64_t *addr)
{
	if (tree->omap == NULL || (tree->flags & APFS_BTREE_PHYSICAL)) {
		*addr = oid;
		return 0;
	}
	return omap_find(tree->omap, oid, tree->nx->xid, addr);
}

/* Read a tree's root and remember what its btree_info says about the whole tree. */
static int
btree_open(struct apfs_nx *nx, struct apfs_omap *omap, uint64_t root_oid,
    struct apfs_btree *tree)
{
	const uint8_t *blk;
	uint64_t addr;
	uint32_t bs = nx->block_size;
	const uint8_t *info;
	int error;

	memset(tree, 0, sizeof(*tree));
	tree->nx = nx;
	tree->omap = omap;
	/* the root is found the same way as any node, but its flags are not known yet */
	if (omap == NULL) {
		addr = root_oid;
	} else {
		error = omap_find(omap, root_oid, nx->xid, &addr);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
	}
	if (bs < 56 + sizeof(struct apfs_btree_info)) {
		return EIO;
	}
	error = nx_block(nx, addr, &blk, false);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	info = blk + bs - sizeof(struct apfs_btree_info);
	if (le64(blk) == 0 && le64(blk + 8) == 0 && le32(blk + 24) == 0 &&
	    (le16(blk + 32) & APFS_BTNODE_NOHEADER) && (le32(info) & APFS_BTREE_NOHEADER)) {
		/* a sealed tree's root: no header, no checksum (see node_hash_check) */
	} else {
		error = nx_block(nx, addr, &blk, true);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
		if (obj_type(blk) != APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_BTREE) {
			apfs_log("block %llu is not a b-tree root\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
			return EIO;
		}
	}
	tree->root = addr;
	tree->root_oid = root_oid;
	tree->flags = le32(info);
	tree->key_size = le32(info + 8);
	tree->val_size = le32(info + 12);
	tree->key_count = le64(info + 24);
	tree->node_count = le64(info + 32);
	return 0;
}

static int
omap_open(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint64_t omap_addr, struct apfs_omap *omap)
{
	const uint8_t *blk;
	uint64_t tree_oid;
	int error;

	memset(omap, 0, sizeof(*omap));
	error = nx_block(nx, omap_addr, &blk, true);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	if (obj_type(blk) != APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_OMAP) {
		apfs_log("block %llu is not an object map\n", (unsigned long long)omap_addr);
		return EIO;
	}
	tree_oid = le64(blk + 48);          /* om_tree_oid, a physical tree */
	error = btree_open(nx, NULL, tree_oid, &omap->tree);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	omap->ready = true;
	return 0;
}

/*
 * Where an object lives.  The map is keyed by (identifier, transaction) in that order, so
 * the versions of one object are a run; we want the newest that is not past want_xid.
 */
static int
omap_find(struct apfs_omap *omap, uint64_t oid, apfs_xid_t want_xid, uint64_t *addr)
{
	struct apfs_btree *tree = &omap->tree;
	uint64_t node_oid = tree->root;
	struct node n;
	const uint8_t *blk;
	int level, error;

	struct apfs_omap_hit *hit = NULL;

	if (!omap->ready) {
		return EIO;
	}
	if (tree->nx->omap_cache != NULL) {
		uint64_t h = (oid ^ (tree->root * 0xff51afd7ed558ccdULL)) * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ULL;

		hit = &tree->nx->omap_cache[h >> 53 & (APFS_OMAP_CACHE - 1)];
		if (hit->oid == oid && oid != 0 && hit->xid == want_xid &&
		    hit->map == tree->root) {
			tree->nx->omap_hits++;
			*addr = hit->addr;
			return 0;
		}
		tree->nx->omap_misses++;
	}
	error = nx_block(tree->nx, node_oid, &blk, true);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	error = node_parse(tree, blk, &n);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	for (level = 0; level < APFS_MAX_LEVELS; level++) {
		uint32_t lo = 0, hi, best;

		if (n.nkeys == 0) {
			return ENOENT;
		}
		/* the last entry whose key is at or before what we are looking for: halving */
		hi = n.nkeys;
		while (lo < hi) {
			uint32_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
			const uint8_t *k, *v;
			uint16_t kl, vl;
			uint64_t o, x;

			error = node_entry(tree, &n, mid, &k, &kl, &v, &vl);
			if (error) {
				return error;
			}
			if (kl < 16) {
				return EIO;
			}
			o = le64(k);
			x = le64(k + 8);
			if (o < oid || (o == oid && x <= want_xid)) {
				lo = mid + 1;
			} else {
				hi = mid;
			}
		}
		if (lo == 0) {
			return ENOENT;
		}
		best = lo - 1;
		if (n.leaf) {
			const uint8_t *k, *v;
			uint16_t kl, vl;

			error = node_entry(tree, &n, best, &k, &kl, &v, &vl);
			if (error) {
				return error;
			}
			if (kl < 16 || le64(k) != oid) {
				return ENOENT;
			}
			if (v == NULL || vl < 16) {
				return EIO;
			}
			/* omap_val: flags, size, then the block address */
			*addr = le64(v + 8);
			if (*addr == 0 || *addr >= tree->nx->block_count) {
				return EIO;
			}
			if (hit != NULL) {
				hit->map = tree->root;
				hit->oid = oid;
				hit->xid = want_xid;
				hit->addr = *addr;
			}
			return 0;
		}
		error = node_child(tree, &n, best, &node_oid);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
		error = nx_block(tree->nx, node_oid, &blk, true);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
		error = node_parse(tree, blk, &n);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
	}
	return EIO;             /* deeper than any real tree: treat as damage */
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ container */

/* The key of a file-system record: the object id and the kind, packed into eight bytes. */
static inline uint64_t
jkey_id(const uint8_t *k)
{
	return le64(k) & APFS_OBJ_ID_MASK;
}

static inline uint8_t
jkey_type(const uint8_t *k)
{
	return (uint8_t)(le64(k) >> APFS_OBJ_TYPE_SHIFT);
}

int
apfs_nx_open(struct apfs_nx *nx, const struct apfs_dev *dev)
{
	uint8_t *block0;
	const uint8_t *blk;
	uint32_t bs, i, desc_blocks;
	uint64_t desc_base;
	apfs_xid_t best_xid = 0;
	uint64_t best_addr = 0;
	int error;

	memset(nx, 0, sizeof(*nx));
	nx->dev = *dev;
	nx->cache = apfs_alloc(APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS * sizeof(*nx->cache));
	nx->cache_hash = apfs_alloc(APFS_CACHE_HASH * sizeof(*nx->cache_hash));
	if (nx->cache == NULL || nx->cache_hash == NULL) {
		return ENOMEM;                  /* apfs_nx_close() frees what there is */
	}
	for (i = 0; i < APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS; i++) {
		nx->cache[i].addr = APFS_BUF_EMPTY;
		nx->cache[i].next = -1;
	}
	for (i = 0; i < APFS_CACHE_HASH; i++) {
		nx->cache_hash[i] = -1;
	}
	/* zeroed, so every slot is empty; without it the object maps are simply walked */
	nx->omap_cache = apfs_alloc(APFS_OMAP_CACHE * sizeof(*nx->omap_cache));

	/*
	 * Block zero holds a container superblock, but it can be behind: the live one is
	 * whichever copy in the checkpoint descriptor area has the largest transaction
	 * identifier.  Block zero is read only to find that area.
	 */
	block0 = apfs_alloc(APFS_NX_MINIMUM_BLOCK_SIZE);
	if (block0 == NULL) {
		return ENOMEM;
	}
	error = nx->dev.read(nx->dev.ctx, 0, block0, APFS_NX_MINIMUM_BLOCK_SIZE);
	if (error) {
		goto out;
	}
	error = EINVAL;
	if (le32(block0 + 32) != APFS_NX_MAGIC) {
		goto out;           /* not an APFS container; let the caller try something else */
	}
	bs = le32(block0 + 36);
	if (bs < APFS_NX_MINIMUM_BLOCK_SIZE || bs > APFS_NX_MAXIMUM_BLOCK_SIZE ||
	    (bs & (bs - 1)) != 0) {
		apfs_log("block size %u makes no sense\n", bs);
		goto out;
	}
	nx->block_size = bs;
	nx->block_count = le64(block0 + 40);
	if (nx->block_count < 16) {
		goto out;
	}
	if (nx->dev.size != 0 && nx->block_count * (uint64_t)bs > nx->dev.size) {
		apfs_log("container claims %llu blocks, the device holds %llu bytes\n",
		    (unsigned long long)nx->block_count, (unsigned long long)nx->dev.size);
		goto out;
	}
	desc_blocks = le32(block0 + 104);
	desc_base = le64(block0 + 112);
	error = EIO;
	if (desc_base == 0 || desc_blocks == 0 || desc_blocks > nx->block_count ||
	    desc_base >= nx->block_count ||
	    desc_base + desc_blocks > nx->block_count) {
		apfs_log("the checkpoint descriptor area is not inside the container\n");
		goto out;
	}

	for (i = 0; i < desc_blocks; i++) {
		/*
		 * Most of the descriptor area is free or holds older checkpoints, so a block
		 * that fails its checksum here is ordinary and is passed over without a word.
		 */
		if (nx_block(nx, desc_base + i, &blk, false) != 0) {
			continue;
		}
		if (!apfs_checksum_ok(blk, nx->block_size)) {
			continue;
		}
		if (obj_type(blk) != APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_NX_SUPERBLOCK ||
		    le32(blk + 32) != APFS_NX_MAGIC || le64(blk + 8) != APFS_OID_NX_SUPERBLOCK) {
			continue;
		}
		if (obj_xid(blk) > best_xid) {
			best_xid = obj_xid(blk);
			best_addr = desc_base + i;
		}
	}
	if (best_addr == 0) {
		apfs_log("no usable container superblock in the checkpoint area\n");
		goto out;
	}
	error = nx_block(nx, best_addr, &blk, true);
	if (error) {
		goto out;
	}
	nx->xid = obj_xid(blk);
	nx->block_count = le64(blk + 40);
	memcpy(nx->uuid, blk + 72, sizeof(nx->uuid));
	nx->xp_desc_blocks = le32(blk + 104);
	nx->xp_data_blocks = le32(blk + 108);
	nx->xp_desc_base = le64(blk + 112);
	nx->xp_data_base = le64(blk + 120);
	nx->omap_addr = le64(blk + 160);
	{
		uint32_t maxfs = le32(blk + 180);

		if (maxfs > APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS) {
			maxfs = APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS;
		}
		nx->fs_count = 0;
		for (i = 0; i < maxfs; i++) {
			uint64_t oid = le64(blk + 184 + 8 * i);

			nx->fs_oid[i] = oid;
			if (oid != 0) {
				nx->fs_count = i + 1;
			}
		}
	}
	error = omap_open(nx, nx->omap_addr, &nx->omap);
	if (error) {
		goto out;
	}
	error = 0;
out:
	apfs_free(block0, APFS_NX_MINIMUM_BLOCK_SIZE);
	if (error) {
		apfs_nx_close(nx);
	}
	return error;
}

static void scratch_drain(struct apfs_nx *nx);

void
apfs_nx_close(struct apfs_nx *nx)
{
	uint32_t i;

	scratch_drain(nx);
	if (nx->omap_cache != NULL) {
		apfs_free(nx->omap_cache, APFS_OMAP_CACHE * sizeof(*nx->omap_cache));
		nx->omap_cache = NULL;
	}

	if (nx->cache != NULL) {
		for (i = 0; i < APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS; i++) {
			if (nx->cache[i].data != NULL) {
				apfs_free(nx->cache[i].data, nx->block_size);
			}
		}
		apfs_free(nx->cache, APFS_CACHE_BLOCKS * sizeof(*nx->cache));
		nx->cache = NULL;
	}
	if (nx->cache_hash != NULL) {
		apfs_free(nx->cache_hash, APFS_CACHE_HASH * sizeof(*nx->cache_hash));
		nx->cache_hash = NULL;
	}
	if (nx->cluster != NULL) {
		apfs_free(nx->cluster, (size_t)APFS_META_CLUSTER * nx->block_size);
		nx->cluster = NULL;
	}
	apfs_nx_reclaim(nx, ~0ULL);
}

int
apfs_vol_open(struct apfs_nx *nx, uint32_t index, struct apfs_vol *vol)
{
	const uint8_t *blk;
	uint64_t addr, omap_oid, root_oid, fext_oid, er_oid;
	uint32_t fext_type, er_type;
	int error;

	if (index >= APFS_NX_MAX_FILE_SYSTEMS || nx->fs_oid[index] == 0) {
		return ENOENT;
	}
	memset(vol, 0, sizeof(*vol));
	vol->nx = nx;
	vol->index = index;
	vol->oid = nx->fs_oid[index];
	error = omap_find(&nx->omap, vol->oid, nx->xid, &addr);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	error = nx_block(nx, addr, &blk, true);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	if (obj_type(blk) != APFS_OBJECT_TYPE_FS || le32(blk + 32) != APFS_MAGIC_VOL) {
		apfs_log("volume %u: block %llu is not a volume superblock\n", index,
		    (unsigned long long)addr);
		return EIO;
	}
	vol->incompat = le64(blk + 56);
	vol->alloc_count = le64(blk + 88);
	er_type = le32(blk + 120);
	omap_oid = le64(blk + 128);
	root_oid = le64(blk + 136);
	er_oid = le64(blk + 144);
	vol->num_files = le64(blk + 184);
	vol->num_dirs = le64(blk + 192);
	vol->num_symlinks = le64(blk + 200);
	vol->num_snapshots = le64(blk + 216);
	vol->integrity_meta_oid = le64(blk + 1024);
	vol->fs_flags = le64(blk + 264);
	memcpy(vol->name, blk + 704, APFS_VOLNAME_LEN);
	vol->name[APFS_VOLNAME_LEN - 1] = '\0';
	vol->role = le16(blk + 964);
	fext_oid = le64(blk + 0x408);           /* apfs_fext_tree_oid, apfs_fext_tree_type */
	fext_type = le32(blk + 0x410);
	vol->hashed_names = (vol->incompat & (APFS_INCOMPAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE |
	    APFS_INCOMPAT_NORMALIZATION_INSENSITIVE)) != 0;

	if (vol->incompat & ~(uint64_t)(APFS_INCOMPAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE |
	    APFS_INCOMPAT_NORMALIZATION_INSENSITIVE | APFS_INCOMPAT_SEALED_VOLUME |
	    APFS_INCOMPAT_DATALESS_SNAPS)) {
		apfs_log("volume %u: incompatible features 0x%llx are not understood\n",
		    index, (unsigned long long)vol->incompat);
		return ENOTSUP;
	}
	if ((vol->fs_flags & APFS_FS_UNENCRYPTED) == 0) {
		apfs_log("volume %u (%s) is encrypted\n", index, vol->name);
		return ENOTSUP;
	}
	/* the volume's own map resolves the nodes of its file-system tree */
	error = omap_open(nx, omap_oid, &vol->omap);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	error = btree_open(nx, &vol->omap, root_oid, &vol->tree);
	if (error) {
		return error;
	}
	if (fext_oid != 0) {
		if ((fext_type & APFS_OBJ_STORAGETYPE_MASK) != APFS_OBJ_PHYSICAL) {
			apfs_log("volume %u (%s): an extent tree that is not physical (0x%x)\n", index, vol->name,
			    fext_type);
			return ENOTSUP;
		}
		error = btree_open(nx, NULL, fext_oid, &vol->fext);
		if (error) {
			return error;
		}
		vol->has_fext = true;
	}
	/*
	 * The extent-reference tree is of no use to a reader, so it is not opened here: only
```
