`xnu/files/osfmk/arm64/gic_v3_irq.c`:

```c
/*
 * Minimal GICv3 support for generic (non-Apple) ARMv8 boards.
 *
 * Open-source XNU has no interrupt controller driver: on Apple hardware that
 * is a kext (AppleInterruptController), and the timer arrives as FIQ. Here
 * everything is a Group 1 IRQ, which is what an EL1 guest gets from a stock
 * hypervisor or from QEMU's virt machine:
 *
 *   - the CPU interface is driven through the ICC_*_EL1 system registers
 *   - the EL1 virtual timer PPI is routed to the kernel's rtclock
 *   - with more than one processor (psci_smp.c), two software-generated
 *     interrupts carry the kernel's signals between them: cpu_signal() and
 *     the order to stop when the system goes back to the boot loader
 *   - a shared peripheral interrupt (SPI, numbers 32 to 1019) is a driver's once it
 *     is attached (gic_v3_spi_attach()): configured, routed to the processor that
 *     attaches it, enabled, and its handler called in interrupt context for each
 *     one that arrives, before it is ended
 *   - any other interrupt that fires is masked and counted, until a real
 *     driver registers a handler for it
 *
 * Every processor has its own CPU interface, redistributor frame and timer,
 * and sets them up for itself (gic_v3_irq_cpu_init(), from PE_init_cpu()).
 *
 * Registers come from the device tree node /arm-io/gic:
 *   reg = <distributor offset, size, redistributor offset, size>
 */
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <kern/debug.h>
#include <kern/simple_lock.h>
#include <os/atomic_private.h>
#include <arm/cpu_data_internal.h>
#include <arm/cpu_internal.h>
#include <arm/machine_cpu.h>
#include <arm/machine_routines.h>
#include <arm/rtclock.h>
#include <arm64/psci_smp.h>
#include <arm64/proc_reg.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <pexpert/device_tree.h>
#include <pexpert/arm64/board_config.h>

#if defined(GENERIC_GIC_V3_IRQ)

#define GICD_CTLR               0x0000
#define GICD_CTLR_ENABLE_G1NS   (1u << 1)
#define GICD_CTLR_ARE_NS        (1u << 4)
#define GICD_CTLR_RWP           (1u << 31)
#define GICD_IGROUPR(n)         (0x0080 + 4 * (n))
#define GICD_ISENABLER(n)       (0x0100 + 4 * (n))
#define GICD_ICENABLER(n)       (0x0180 + 4 * (n))
#define GICD_ICPENDR(n)         (0x0280 + 4 * (n))
#define GICD_ICACTIVER(n)       (0x0380 + 4 * (n))
#define GICD_IPRIORITYR(n)      (0x0400 + (n))
#define GICD_ICFGR(n)           (0x0c00 + 4 * (n))
#define GICD_IGRPMODR(n)        (0x0d00 + 4 * (n))
#define GICD_IROUTER(n)         (0x6000 + 8 * (n))

#define GICR_FRAME_SIZE         0x20000     /* RD_base + SGI_base per CPU */
#define GICR_TYPER              0x0008
#define GICR_TYPER_LAST         (1u << 4)
#define GICR_WAKER              0x0014
#define GICR_WAKER_PROCSLEEP    (1u << 1)
#define GICR_WAKER_CHILDASLEEP  (1u << 2)
#define GICR_SGI_BASE           0x10000
#define GICR_IGROUPR0           (GICR_SGI_BASE + 0x0080)
#define GICR_ISENABLER0         (GICR_SGI_BASE + 0x0100)
#define GICR_ICENABLER0         (GICR_SGI_BASE + 0x0180)
#define GICR_ICPENDR0           (GICR_SGI_BASE + 0x0280)
#define GICR_ICACTIVER0         (GICR_SGI_BASE + 0x0380)
#define GICR_IPRIORITYR(n)      (GICR_SGI_BASE + 0x0400 + (n))
#define GICR_IGRPMODR0          (GICR_SGI_BASE + 0x0d00)

#define GIC_SGI_SIGNAL          0           /* cpu_signal(): another processor wants this one's attention */
#define GIC_SGI_STOP            1           /* psci_smp_stop_here(): the system is going back to the boot loader */
#define GIC_INTID_VTIMER        27          /* EL1 virtual timer PPI */
#define GIC_INTID_SPI_MIN       32
#define GIC_INTID_SPURIOUS_MIN  1020
#define GIC_SPI_MOST            48          /* attached at a time */
#define GIC_PRIORITY_DEFAULT    0xa0

static vm_offset_t gicd_base, gicr_base;
static vm_size_t   gicr_size;
static vm_offset_t gicr_cpu_base[MAX_CPUS]; /* each processor's redistributor frame */

/*
 * Acknowledged, not yet EOI'd; 0: none. The signal between processors is interrupt 0 and reads
 * as 0 from ICC_IAR1_EL1, hence the mark: without it a core switched off in the middle of that
 * signal (which is where every core but one is during a panic) kept it active, and with the
 * active priority still set in its CPU interface the next kernel on that core saw no interrupt
 * at all.
 */
#define GIC_IAR_TAKEN           (1ULL << 63)
static uint64_t gic_active_iar[MAX_CPUS];
uint64_t        gic_unhandled_count;
uint32_t        gic_last_unhandled;

/*
 * The attached SPIs. A slot is filled before its interrupt is enabled and emptied after it has
 * been disabled and no handler of it runs any more (busy), so the handler path reads the table
 * without a lock.
 */
struct gic_spi {
	uint32_t intid;                     /* 0: a free slot */
	void   (*handler)(void *context, uint32_t intid);
	void    *context;
	uint32_t busy;                      /* handlers of it running now */
	uint64_t count;
};
static struct gic_spi gic_spi[GIC_SPI_MOST];
static decl_simple_lock_data(, gic_spi_lock);

void gic_v3_irq_cpu_init(void);
void gic_v3_irq_quiesce(void);
kern_return_t gic_v3_spi_attach(uint32_t intid, bool edge, void (*handler)(void *context, uint32_t intid), void *context);
void gic_v3_spi_mask(uint32_t intid);
void gic_v3_spi_unmask(uint32_t intid);
void gic_v3_spi_detach(uint32_t intid);
uint64_t gic_v3_spi_count(uint32_t intid);
void gic_v3_irq_cpu_shutdown(void);
void gic_v3_irq_signal(uint32_t phys_id);
void gic_v3_irq_signal_stop(uint32_t phys_id);

static inline uint32_t
gic_read32(vm_offset_t addr)
{
	return *(volatile uint32_t *)addr;
}

static inline void
gic_write32(vm_offset_t addr, uint32_t value)
{
	*(volatile uint32_t *)addr = value;
}

static void
gic_mask(uint32_t intid)
{
	if (intid < 32) {
		gic_write32(gicr_cpu_base[cpu_number()] + GICR_ICENABLER0, 1u << intid);
	} else {
		gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ICENABLER(intid / 32), 1u << (intid % 32));
	}
}

/*
 * A software-generated interrupt for the processor with that MPIDR (its two
 * low affinity fields, as in the device tree's "reg").
 * ICC_SGI1R_EL1: Aff1 in [23:16], the interrupt in [27:24], and in [15:0] a
 * bit for every Aff0 addressed -- which is why Aff0 has to be below 16.
 */
static void
gic_send_sgi(uint32_t phys_id, uint32_t sgi)
{
	uint64_t aff0 = phys_id & 0xff, aff1 = (phys_id >> 8) & 0xff;

	__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_SGI1R_EL1", ((uint64_t)sgi << 24) | (aff1 << 16) | (1ULL << (aff0 & 15)));
	__builtin_arm_isb(ISB_SY);
}

/* The platform's half of cpu_signal(): interrupt that processor (GenericARMCPU::signalCPU()). */
void
gic_v3_irq_signal(uint32_t phys_id)
{
	gic_send_sgi(phys_id, GIC_SGI_SIGNAL);
}

void
gic_v3_irq_signal_stop(uint32_t phys_id)
{
	gic_send_sgi(phys_id, GIC_SGI_STOP);
}

/* An SPI that a driver has attached: its handler called. false: nobody has it. */
static bool
gic_spi_handle(uint32_t intid)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < GIC_SPI_MOST; i++) {
		struct gic_spi *spi = &gic_spi[i];

		if (os_atomic_load(&spi->intid, acquire) == intid) {
			os_atomic_inc(&spi->busy, acquire);
			if (os_atomic_load(&spi->intid, relaxed) == intid) {
				spi->count++;
				spi->handler(spi->context, intid);
			}
			os_atomic_dec(&spi->busy, release);
			return true;
		}
	}
	return false;
}

static void
gic_distributor_settle(void)
{
	while (gic_read32(gicd_base + GICD_CTLR) & GICD_CTLR_RWP) {
		/* wait for the change to take effect */
	}
}

void
gic_v3_spi_mask(uint32_t intid)
{
	if (gicd_base != 0 && intid >= GIC_INTID_SPI_MIN && intid < GIC_INTID_SPURIOUS_MIN) {
		gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ICENABLER(intid / 32), 1u << (intid % 32));
		gic_distributor_settle();
	}
}

void
gic_v3_spi_unmask(uint32_t intid)
{
	if (gicd_base != 0 && intid >= GIC_INTID_SPI_MIN && intid < GIC_INTID_SPURIOUS_MIN) {
		gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ISENABLER(intid / 32), 1u << (intid % 32));
	}
}

/*
 * A driver takes an SPI: edge- or level-triggered, Group 1, the default priority, routed to the
 * processor this runs on, and enabled. The handler runs in interrupt context, with interrupts off,
 * before the interrupt is ended; for a level-triggered one it has to quiet the source or mask the
 * interrupt (gic_v3_spi_mask()). Thread context.
 */
kern_return_t
gic_v3_spi_attach(uint32_t intid, bool edge, void (*handler)(void *context, uint32_t intid), void *context)
{
	uint64_t mpidr = __builtin_arm_rsr64("MPIDR_EL1");
	struct gic_spi *slot = NULL;
	uint32_t config;

	if (gicd_base == 0 || intid < GIC_INTID_SPI_MIN || intid >= GIC_INTID_SPURIOUS_MIN || handler == NULL) {
		return KERN_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
	}
	simple_lock(&gic_spi_lock, LCK_GRP_NULL);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < GIC_SPI_MOST; i++) {
		if (gic_spi[i].intid == intid) {
			simple_unlock(&gic_spi_lock);
			return KERN_NAME_EXISTS;
		}
		if (slot == NULL && gic_spi[i].intid == 0 && gic_spi[i].busy == 0) {
			slot = &gic_spi[i];
		}
	}
	if (slot == NULL) {
		simple_unlock(&gic_spi_lock);
		return KERN_RESOURCE_SHORTAGE;
	}
	slot->handler = handler;
	slot->context = context;
	slot->count = 0;
	os_atomic_store(&slot->intid, intid, release);
	simple_unlock(&gic_spi_lock);

	gic_v3_spi_mask(intid);
	gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ICPENDR(intid / 32), 1u << (intid % 32));
	gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ICACTIVER(intid / 32), 1u << (intid % 32));
	gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_IGROUPR(intid / 32), gic_read32(gicd_base + GICD_IGROUPR(intid / 32)) | 1u << (intid % 32));
	gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_IGRPMODR(intid / 32), gic_read32(gicd_base + GICD_IGRPMODR(intid / 32)) & ~(1u << (intid % 32)));
	*(volatile uint8_t *)(gicd_base + GICD_IPRIORITYR(intid)) = GIC_PRIORITY_DEFAULT;
	config = gic_read32(gicd_base + GICD_ICFGR(intid / 16)) & ~(3u << (intid % 16 * 2));
	gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ICFGR(intid / 16), config | (edge ? 2u : 0u) << (intid % 16 * 2));
	/* GICD_IROUTER: Aff3 in [39:32], Aff2.Aff1.Aff0 in [23:0]; bit 31 (any processor) clear */
	*(volatile uint64_t *)(gicd_base + GICD_IROUTER(intid)) = (mpidr & 0xff00000000ull) | (mpidr & 0xffffff);
	gic_distributor_settle();
	gic_v3_spi_unmask(intid);
	return KERN_SUCCESS;
}

/* ... and gives it back: disabled, nothing pending, and no handler of it running when this returns. */
void
gic_v3_spi_detach(uint32_t intid)
{
	gic_v3_spi_mask(intid);
	if (gicd_base != 0 && intid >= GIC_INTID_SPI_MIN && intid < GIC_INTID_SPURIOUS_MIN) {
		gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ICPENDR(intid / 32), 1u << (intid % 32));
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < GIC_SPI_MOST; i++) {
		if (gic_spi[i].intid == intid) {
			os_atomic_store(&gic_spi[i].intid, 0, release);
			while (os_atomic_load(&gic_spi[i].busy, acquire) != 0) {
				/* a handler of it on another processor is finishing */
			}
		}
	}
}

/* How many have arrived since it was attached. */
uint64_t
gic_v3_spi_count(uint32_t intid)
{
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < GIC_SPI_MOST; i++) {
		if (gic_spi[i].intid == intid) {
			return gic_spi[i].count;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

static void
gic_irq_handler(__unused void *target, __unused void *refCon, __unused void *nub, __unused int source)
{
	int cpu = cpu_number();

	for (;;) {
		uint64_t iar = __builtin_arm_rsr64("ICC_IAR1_EL1");
		uint32_t intid = (uint32_t)(iar & 0xffffff);

		if (intid >= GIC_INTID_SPURIOUS_MIN) {
			break;
		}
		gic_active_iar[cpu] = iar | GIC_IAR_TAKEN;

		if (intid == GIC_INTID_VTIMER) {
			/* same sequence as the FIQ path in sleh_fiq() */
			getCpuDatap()->cpu_decrementer = -1; /* Large */
			rtclock_intr(TRUE);
		} else if (intid == GIC_SGI_SIGNAL) {
			cpu_signal_handler();
		} else if (intid == GIC_SGI_STOP) {
			/* comes back only if nobody has in fact asked for that */
			psci_smp_stop_here();
		} else if (intid >= GIC_INTID_SPI_MIN && gic_spi_handle(intid)) {
			/* a driver's */
		} else {
			/* nobody owns this interrupt yet: keep it from storming */
			gic_mask(intid);
			gic_unhandled_count++;
			gic_last_unhandled = intid;
		}

		__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_EOIR1_EL1", iar);
		__builtin_arm_isb(ISB_SY);
		gic_active_iar[cpu] = 0;
	}
}

/*
 * Leave the controller in a state another environment can take over from:
 * finish any interrupt that this processor acknowledged but did not complete.
 * Used when control goes back to the boot loader (see loader_return.c), and
 * by a processor that is about to be switched off for that (psci_smp.c).
 */
void
gic_v3_irq_quiesce(void)
{
	int cpu;

	if (gicd_base == 0) {
		return;         /* as early as this there is no interrupt, nor a cpu number to ask for */
	}
	cpu = cpu_number();
	/* (what drivers had of the shared interrupts goes with this kernel: none of them may fire under the loader) */
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < GIC_SPI_MOST; i++) {
		uint32_t intid = gic_spi[i].intid;

		if (intid != 0) {
			gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_ICENABLER(intid / 32), 1u << (intid % 32));
		}
	}
	if (gic_active_iar[cpu] != 0) {
		__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_EOIR1_EL1", gic_active_iar[cpu] & ~GIC_IAR_TAKEN);
		__builtin_arm_isb(ISB_SY);
		gic_active_iar[cpu] = 0;
	}
}

/*
 * This processor is leaving for good: the firmware is about to be asked to switch it off
 * (psci_smp_cpu_off(), and the boot processor in the loader's stub when the kernel has a core of
 * its own). Nothing may be left that could interrupt it. The redistributor outlives the core, and
 * so does what is pending in it: the "stop" signal that reached a core whose interrupts were off
 * (every core is in that state while another one panics), or its timer. A core asked to go with
 * an interrupt pending and the CPU interface still passing it on does not go cleanly, and the
 * next kernel that is started on it hangs.
 */
void
gic_v3_irq_cpu_shutdown(void)
{
	vm_offset_t gicr;

	if (gicd_base == 0) {
		return;
	}
	gic_v3_irq_quiesce();
	gicr = gicr_cpu_base[cpu_number()];
	if (gicr != 0) {
		gic_write32(gicr + GICR_ICENABLER0, 0xffffffffu);
		gic_write32(gicr + GICR_ICPENDR0, 0xffffffffu);
		gic_write32(gicr + GICR_ICACTIVER0, 0xffffffffu);
	}
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_IGRPEN1_EL1", 0);
	__builtin_arm_isb(ISB_SY);
}

static vm_offset_t
gic_find_redistributor(void)
{
	uint64_t mpidr = __builtin_arm_rsr64("MPIDR_EL1");
	/* GICR_TYPER[63:32] packs Aff3.Aff2.Aff1.Aff0 */
	uint32_t affinity = (uint32_t)(((mpidr >> 32) & 0xff) << 24 | (mpidr & 0xffffff));

	for (vm_offset_t frame = gicr_base; frame + GICR_FRAME_SIZE <= gicr_base + gicr_size; frame += GICR_FRAME_SIZE) {
		uint64_t typer = *(volatile uint64_t *)(frame + GICR_TYPER);

		if ((uint32_t)(typer >> 32) == affinity) {
			return frame;
		}
		if (typer & GICR_TYPER_LAST) {
			break;
		}
	}
	panic("gic: no redistributor for MPIDR 0x%llx", mpidr);
}

/* Per-CPU bring-up: every processor calls this for itself, the boot processor first. */
void
gic_v3_irq_cpu_init(void)
{
	int cpu = cpu_number();
	vm_offset_t gicr;
	uint32_t mine = 1u << GIC_INTID_VTIMER;

	if (gicd_base == 0) {
		DTEntry entry;
		void const *prop;
		unsigned int prop_size;

		if (SecureDTLookupEntry(NULL, "/arm-io/gic", &entry) != kSuccess ||
		    SecureDTGetProperty(entry, "reg", &prop, &prop_size) != kSuccess ||
		    prop_size < 4 * sizeof(uint64_t)) {
			panic("gic: no usable /arm-io/gic node in the device tree");
		}
		uint64_t const *reg = prop;
		vm_offset_t soc_base = pe_arm_get_soc_base_phys();

		simple_lock_init(&gic_spi_lock, 0);
		gicd_base = ml_io_map(soc_base + reg[0], reg[1]);
		gicr_base = ml_io_map(soc_base + reg[2], reg[3]);
		gicr_size = reg[3];
		if (gicd_base == 0 || gicr_base == 0) {
			panic("gic: cannot map the distributor/redistributor");
		}
	} else if (gicr_cpu_base[cpu] != 0) {
		return;
	}

	/* System-register CPU interface */
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_SRE_EL1", __builtin_arm_rsr64("ICC_SRE_EL1") | 1);
	__builtin_arm_isb(ISB_SY);

	gicr = gicr_cpu_base[cpu] = gic_find_redistributor();

	uint32_t waker = gic_read32(gicr + GICR_WAKER);
	if (waker & (GICR_WAKER_PROCSLEEP | GICR_WAKER_CHILDASLEEP)) {
		gic_write32(gicr + GICR_WAKER, waker & ~GICR_WAKER_PROCSLEEP);
		while (gic_read32(gicr + GICR_WAKER) & GICR_WAKER_CHILDASLEEP) {
			/* spin until the redistributor is awake */
		}
	}

	/*
	 * The interrupts between processors, where there is more than one. A core that an earlier
	 * kernel switched off in the middle of one (a return to the boot loader, started again
	 * since) may still have it marked active, and would then never see another.
	 */
	if (ml_get_cpu_count() > 1) {
		uint32_t sgis = (1u << GIC_SGI_SIGNAL) | (1u << GIC_SGI_STOP);

		gic_write32(gicr + GICR_ICACTIVER0, sgis);
		gic_write32(gicr + GICR_ICPENDR0, sgis);        /* ... or one that it never took */
		*(volatile uint8_t *)(gicr + GICR_IPRIORITYR(GIC_SGI_SIGNAL)) = GIC_PRIORITY_DEFAULT;
		*(volatile uint8_t *)(gicr + GICR_IPRIORITYR(GIC_SGI_STOP)) = GIC_PRIORITY_DEFAULT;
		mine |= sgis;
	}

	/* Virtual timer PPI (and those): Group 1 (IRQ), default priority, enabled */
	gic_write32(gicr + GICR_IGROUPR0, gic_read32(gicr + GICR_IGROUPR0) | mine);
	gic_write32(gicr + GICR_IGRPMODR0, gic_read32(gicr + GICR_IGRPMODR0) & ~mine);
	*(volatile uint8_t *)(gicr + GICR_IPRIORITYR(GIC_INTID_VTIMER)) = GIC_PRIORITY_DEFAULT;
	gic_write32(gicr + GICR_ISENABLER0, mine);

	/* Distributor: affinity routing, Group 1 enabled (normally already so) */
	uint32_t ctlr = gic_read32(gicd_base + GICD_CTLR);
	if ((ctlr & (GICD_CTLR_ENABLE_G1NS | GICD_CTLR_ARE_NS)) != (GICD_CTLR_ENABLE_G1NS | GICD_CTLR_ARE_NS)) {
		gic_write32(gicd_base + GICD_CTLR, ctlr | GICD_CTLR_ENABLE_G1NS | GICD_CTLR_ARE_NS);
		while (gic_read32(gicd_base + GICD_CTLR) & GICD_CTLR_RWP) {
			/* wait for the write to take effect */
		}
	}

	/*
	 * CPU interface: accept all priorities, no preemption grouping, Group 1 on. And no priority
	 * active: a core that the firmware switches off and on again need not lose that, and a
	 * kernel that left in the middle of an interrupt without ending it would leave this one
	 * waiting for an end that never comes.
	 */
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_AP1R0_EL1", 0);
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_PMR_EL1", 0xff);
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_BPR1_EL1", 0);
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("ICC_IGRPEN1_EL1", 1);
	__builtin_arm_isb(ISB_SY);

	ml_install_interrupt_handler(NULL, 0, NULL, gic_irq_handler, NULL);
	kprintf("gic: v3, distributor %p, cpu %d's redistributor %p, virtual timer on PPI %d\n",
	    (void *)gicd_base, cpu, (void *)gicr, GIC_INTID_VTIMER);
}

#endif /* GENERIC_GIC_V3_IRQ */

```

`xnu/files/osfmk/arm64/loader_return.c`:

```c
/*
 * Return-to-loader debug channel.
 *
 * On hardware without a serial port there is no way to get the kernel log
 * out. The XNU loader therefore leaves UEFI intact (no ExitBootServices) and
 * publishes the physical address of a return stub in /chosen/loader-return.
 * When the kernel has nothing more to do (panic, halt, timer) it collects its
 * message buffer, the panic buffer and any kprintf output, maps the stub 1:1
 * through TTBR0 and jumps to it with that log. The loader then restores the UEFI environment and writes
 * the log to storage.
 *
 * Only valid while the kernel does not drive hardware that UEFI also uses.
 */
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <machine/atomic.h>
#include <kern/cpu_number.h>
#include <kern/debug.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <arm/cpu_internal.h>
#include <arm/machine_routines.h>
#include <arm64/psci_smp.h>
#include <arm64/proc_reg.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <pexpert/arm64/board_config.h>
#include <vm/vm_page.h>
#include <vm/vm_compressor.h>

/*
 * The console log handed back to the loader. A long session writes more than fits, and both
 * ends matter: the start of the boot is kept as it is, and of everything after it the most
 * recent part (a ring); room is left for what is appended on the way out (the kernel message
 * buffer, a panic's text). loader_log_linearize() puts the pieces in order before returning.
 */
#define LOADER_LOG_SIZE (1536 * 1024)
#define LOADER_LOG_HEAD (256 * 1024)
#define LOADER_LOG_RING (1024 * 1024)

#if defined(GENERIC_GIC_V3_IRQ)
extern void gic_v3_irq_quiesce(void);
extern void gic_v3_irq_cpu_shutdown(void);
#endif

void loader_log_putc(char c);
void loader_return(void);
extern void hakios_adreno_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_adreno_stop(void);
extern void hakios_adreno_minute(void);
extern void hakios_wifi_stop(void);
extern void hakios_wifi_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_adsp_stop(void);
extern void hakios_adsp_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_mpss_stop(void);
extern void hakios_mpss_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_ddr_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_haptic_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_torch_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_camera_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_mic_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_ufs_quiesce(void);
extern void hakios_var_save_on_return(void);   /* drivers/storage/hakios.ufs.c: the data volume into the flash */
void loader_checkpoint(uint64_t n);

/* Also referenced from the early exception vector in start.s. */
char     loader_log[LOADER_LOG_SIZE];
uint32_t loader_log_len;
static bool     loader_return_entered;

/* One L1 table and one L2 table are enough to map a single 2 MB block. */
static uint64_t loader_l1[512] __attribute__((aligned(4096)));
static uint64_t loader_l2[512] __attribute__((aligned(4096)));

static uint32_t loader_log_ring_at;      /* where the next character goes in the ring */
static bool     loader_log_wrapped;
static bool     loader_log_linear;       /* the pieces have been put in order: only appending from now on */
static char     loader_log_scratch[LOADER_LOG_RING];

/*
 * Characters come from every processor, and from interrupt handlers on top of whatever was
 * writing one. The lock is of the simplest kind, good from the first line of C code to the
 * last of a panic; whoever cannot have it for a long while (its holder is gone: a panic
 * inside this very function) goes ahead without it.
 */
static uint32_t loader_log_lock;

static void loader_log_put_locked(char c);

void
loader_log_putc(char c)
{
	uint64_t daif;
	bool locked = false;

	if (c == '\r') {
		return;
	}
	daif = __builtin_arm_rsr64("DAIF");
	__builtin_arm_wsr("DAIFSet", DAIFSC_IRQF | DAIFSC_FIQF);
	for (uint32_t tries = 0; !locked && tries < 10000000; tries++) {
		locked = os_atomic_cmpxchg(&loader_log_lock, 0, 1, acquire);
	}
	loader_log_put_locked(c);
	if (locked) {
		os_atomic_store(&loader_log_lock, 0, release);
	}
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("DAIF", daif);
}

/*
 * A whole line at once, under the lock: lines written from several processors at the same time
 * (tools/latency.py's "tl:" lines, a frame's on one and a touch's on another) are not mixed up.
 */
void loader_log_line(const char *line);

void
loader_log_line(const char *line)
{
	uint64_t daif;
	bool locked = false;

	daif = __builtin_arm_rsr64("DAIF");
	__builtin_arm_wsr("DAIFSet", DAIFSC_IRQF | DAIFSC_FIQF);
	for (uint32_t tries = 0; !locked && tries < 10000000; tries++) {
		locked = os_atomic_cmpxchg(&loader_log_lock, 0, 1, acquire);
	}
	for (; *line != 0; line++) {
		if (*line != '\r') {
			loader_log_put_locked(*line);
		}
	}
	if (locked) {
		os_atomic_store(&loader_log_lock, 0, release);
	}
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("DAIF", daif);
}

static void
loader_log_put_locked(char c)
{
	if (loader_log_linear || loader_log_len < LOADER_LOG_HEAD) {
		if (loader_log_len < LOADER_LOG_SIZE) {
			loader_log[loader_log_len++] = c;
		}
	} else {
		loader_log[LOADER_LOG_HEAD + loader_log_ring_at] = c;
		if (++loader_log_ring_at == LOADER_LOG_RING) {
			loader_log_ring_at = 0;
			loader_log_wrapped = true;
		}
		if (!loader_log_wrapped) {
			loader_log_len = LOADER_LOG_HEAD + loader_log_ring_at;
		}
	}
}

/* Oldest first: the head, a note about what was dropped, then the ring from its oldest character. */
static void
loader_log_linearize(void)
{
	static const char note[] = "\n\n[... the log between the first 256 KB and the last 1 MB was dropped ...]\n\n";
	uint32_t older = LOADER_LOG_RING - loader_log_ring_at, n = LOADER_LOG_HEAD;

	if (loader_log_linear) {
		return;
	}
	loader_log_linear = true;
	if (!loader_log_wrapped) {
		return;
	}
	__builtin_memcpy(loader_log_scratch, loader_log + LOADER_LOG_HEAD + loader_log_ring_at, older);
	__builtin_memcpy(loader_log_scratch + older, loader_log + LOADER_LOG_HEAD, loader_log_ring_at);
	/* the note takes the place of the oldest characters of the ring */
	__builtin_memcpy(loader_log + n, note, sizeof(note) - 1);
	n += sizeof(note) - 1;
	__builtin_memcpy(loader_log + n, loader_log_scratch + sizeof(note) - 1, LOADER_LOG_RING - (sizeof(note) - 1));
	loader_log_len = LOADER_LOG_HEAD + LOADER_LOG_RING;
}

/* Patched by the loader: { magic, PA of its return stub, checkpoint to stop at, PA - VA }. See start.s. */
extern uint64_t loader_stub_slot[4];

/*
 * For a loader that watches from another processor core while the kernel runs (it starts the
 * kernel on a core of its choice and stays on the first one): a sign of life, and where the log
 * is, so that the log of a kernel that hangs -- or dies before it has said a word through any
 * other channel -- is not lost with it. The loader finds this by its first word in the kernel
 * it has loaded. The addresses are the kernel's virtual ones, filled in by the linker and so
 * valid from the first instruction; the loader knows the distance to the physical ones.
 */
struct loader_live {
	uint64_t magic;                 /* "XNULIVE!" */
	uint64_t heartbeat;             /* goes up every HV_WDT_PET_SECONDS while the kernel is alive */
	const char *log;                /* loader_log */
	const uint32_t *log_len;        /* how much of it is in use */
	const uint32_t *log_ring_at;    /* where the ring part is being written */
	const bool *log_wrapped;        /* the ring has gone round */
	uint64_t log_head, log_ring;    /* sizes of the two parts */
	const uint64_t *recording;      /* loader_recording: { physical address, length } of a screen recording */
	volatile uint64_t stop;         /* the loader's to write: the host has asked for the run to end */
	uint64_t magic2;                /* "XNULIVE2": what follows is there (a loader may meet an older kernel) */
	const uint64_t *sound;          /* loader_sound: the same for a recording of the sound */
};

/*
 * A screen recording (the display driver makes one with boot-arg rec_secs): where it is, for the
 * loader to hand to the host once the kernel is back. { physical address, bytes, kernel address }.
 */
uint64_t loader_recording[3];
/* ... and of the sound (/dev/hakios-audio makes one with boot-arg rec_sound). */
uint64_t loader_sound[3];

struct loader_live loader_live = {
	.magic = 0x214556494c554e58ULL, .log = loader_log, .log_len = &loader_log_len, .log_ring_at = &loader_log_ring_at,
	.log_wrapped = &loader_log_wrapped, .log_head = LOADER_LOG_HEAD, .log_ring = LOADER_LOG_RING,
	.recording = loader_recording,
	.magic2 = 0x324556494c554e58ULL, .sound = loader_sound,
};

/* Valid from the first instruction of C code: does not depend on gVirtBase/gPhysBase being set up. */
static inline uint64_t
static_kvtophys(const void *va)
{
	return (uint64_t)va + loader_stub_slot[3];
}

/*
 * Jump to the loader's return stub. reason: 0 = orderly end, 2 = checkpoint.
 * Returns only if no loader is listening.
 */
static void
loader_jump(uint64_t reason, uint64_t code)
{
#if ARM_PGSHIFT == 12
	uint64_t stub = loader_stub_slot[1];
	uint64_t tcr, t0sz;
	uint32_t own_core = 0;

	if (stub == 0 || loader_return_entered) {
		return;
	}

	tcr = __builtin_arm_rsr64("TCR_EL1");
	t0sz = tcr & 0x3f;
	/* The TTBR0 walk must start at L1 (1 GB per entry) and reach the stub. */
	if (t0sz < 25 || t0sz > 33 || (stub >> (64 - t0sz)) != 0) {
		return;
	}
	loader_return_entered = true;
#if defined(GENERIC_GIC_V3_IRQ)
	gic_v3_irq_quiesce();
	/*
	 * With a core of its own (bootcpu=) the kernel does not go back into the loader's code on
	 * this processor: the stub leaves the log where the loader's core finds it and has the
	 * firmware switch this one off. It must go as the other cores do (psci_smp_cpu_off()), with
	 * nothing pending: after a panic the "stop" signal and the timer are.
	 */
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("bootcpu", &own_core, sizeof(own_core))) {
		__builtin_arm_wsr64("CNTV_CTL_EL0", CNTV_CTL_EL0_IMASKED);
		gic_v3_irq_cpu_shutdown();
	}
#endif

	loader_l1[stub >> 30] = static_kvtophys(loader_l2) | ARM_TTE_TYPE_TABLE | ARM_TTE_VALID;
	loader_l2[(stub >> 21) & 0x1ff] = (stub & ~0x1fffffULL) | ARM_TTE_VALID | ARM_TTE_TYPE_BLOCK |
	    ARM_TTE_BLOCK_AF | ARM_TTE_BLOCK_SH(SH_OUTER_MEMORY) | ARM_TTE_BLOCK_AP(AP_RWNA) |
	    ARM_TTE_BLOCK_ATTRINDX(CACHE_ATTRINDX_WRITEBACK);

	/*
	 * The stub turns the MMU off, and on real hardware dirty cache lines do
	 * not survive that: write the log back to RAM first.
	 */
	for (uintptr_t p = (uintptr_t)loader_log & ~63UL; p < (uintptr_t)loader_log + loader_log_len; p += 64) {
		__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" (p));
	}
	/* ... and a screen recording, and the note of where it is */
	for (uintptr_t p = loader_recording[2] & ~63UL; p < loader_recording[2] + loader_recording[1]; p += 64) {
		__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" (p));
	}
	__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" ((uintptr_t)loader_recording));
	__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" ((uintptr_t)loader_recording + 16));
	for (uintptr_t p = loader_sound[2] & ~63UL; p < loader_sound[2] + loader_sound[1]; p += 64) {
		__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" (p));
	}
	__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" ((uintptr_t)loader_sound));
	__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" ((uintptr_t)loader_sound + 16));
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy");

	register uint64_t r_ttbr0 __asm__("x0") = static_kvtophys(loader_l1);
	register uint64_t r_log __asm__("x2") = static_kvtophys(loader_log);
	register uint64_t r_len __asm__("x3") = loader_log_len;
	register uint64_t r_tcr __asm__("x4") = tcr;
	register uint64_t r_stub __asm__("x5") = stub;
	register uint64_t r_reason __asm__("x6") = reason;
	register uint64_t r_code __asm__("x7") = code;

	__asm__ volatile (
                "msr DAIFSet, #0xf\n"
                "bic x4, x4, #0x80\n"           /* TCR_EL1.EPD0: allow TTBR0 walks */
                "msr TCR_EL1, x4\n"
                "msr TTBR0_EL1, x0\n"
                "isb\n"
                "tlbi vmalle1\n"
                "dsb sy\n"
                "isb\n"
                "mov x0, x2\n"
                "mov x1, x3\n"
                "mov x2, x6\n"
                "mov x3, x7\n"
                "br x5\n"
                : : "r" (r_ttbr0), "r" (r_log), "r" (r_len), "r" (r_tcr), "r" (r_stub), "r" (r_reason), "r" (r_code));
	__builtin_unreachable();
#else
	(void)reason; (void)code;
#endif /* ARM_PGSHIFT == 12 */
}

extern char *debug_buf_base, *debug_buf_ptr;

/* bsd/sys/msgbuf.h (not includable from osfmk) */
struct msgbuf {
	int   msg_magic;
	int   msg_size;
	int   msg_bufx;         /* write pointer */
	int   msg_bufr;         /* read pointer */
	char *msg_bufc;         /* buffer */
};
extern struct msgbuf *msgbufp;

static void
loader_log_puts(const char *s)
{
	for (; *s; s++) {
		loader_log_putc(*s);
	}
}

/*
 * Everything printf()/IOLog()/os_log wrote ends up in the kernel message
 * buffer (what dmesg shows), whether or not a console displayed it.
 */
static void
loader_log_append_msgbuf(void)
{
	struct msgbuf *mb = msgbufp;

	if (mb == NULL || mb->msg_bufc == NULL || mb->msg_size <= 0 || mb->msg_bufx < 0 || mb->msg_bufx > mb->msg_size) {
		return;
	}
	loader_log_puts("\n--- kernel message buffer ---\n");
	/* oldest data first: [bufx, size) is only meaningful once the buffer has wrapped */
	for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++) {
		int from = pass == 0 ? mb->msg_bufx : 0;
		int to = pass == 0 ? mb->msg_size : mb->msg_bufx;
		for (int i = from; i < to; i++) {
			if (mb->msg_bufc[i] != 0) {
				loader_log_putc(mb->msg_bufc[i]);
			}
		}
	}
}

void
loader_return(void)
{
#if defined(GENERIC_PSCI_SMP)
	/*
	 * With more than one processor: the others switch themselves off first, and the rest of
	 * this is done by the boot processor, the one the loader gave us. This call comes back
	 * on that processor only (on another one it has it call loader_return() in its turn).
	 */
	psci_smp_stop_others();
#endif
	hakios_ufs_quiesce();          /* this kernel's requests to the storage done, UEFI's list as it was, for the log */
	hakios_adreno_quiesce();       /* the GPU block, if it was started, has tables in memory that is about to be reused */
	hakios_wifi_quiesce();         /* the Wi-Fi DSP, if it still runs (a panic), is not left to itself */
	hakios_adsp_quiesce();         /* nor the audio DSP */
	hakios_mpss_quiesce();         /* nor the modem */
	hakios_ddr_quiesce();          /* and the vote for the memory's bandwidth taken away */
	hakios_haptic_quiesce();       /* the vibration motor's chip back into reset, if it was let out */
	hakios_torch_quiesce();        /* the flashlight off, if it was lit */
	hakios_camera_quiesce();       /* the camera powered down, if it was powered up */
	hakios_mic_quiesce();          /* (what the microphones' path did, said again: it happens in the log's middle) */
	/*
	 * A panic's text is first collected in the panic buffer and only later
	 * flushed to the console; if the console itself is what failed, that
	 * never happens. Append the buffer so the loader gets it either way.
	 */
	loader_log_linearize();
	if (!loader_return_entered) {
		loader_log_append_msgbuf();
	}
	if (!loader_return_entered && debug_buf_base != NULL && debug_buf_ptr > debug_buf_base &&
	    (size_t)(debug_buf_ptr - debug_buf_base) < 256 * 1024) {
		loader_log_puts("\n--- panic buffer ---\n");
		for (const char *c = debug_buf_base; c < debug_buf_ptr; c++) {
			loader_log_putc(*c);
		}
	}
	loader_jump(0, 0);
}

/* Bring-up aid: stop here if the loader asked for checkpoint n. */
void
loader_checkpoint(uint64_t n)
{
	if (loader_stub_slot[2] == n) {
		loader_jump(2, n);
	}
}

/*
 * boot-arg loader_return_after=<seconds>: hand control back to the loader
 * after that long, whatever the kernel is doing. This is how the log gets out
 * when the kernel does not panic but simply waits (e.g. for a root device).
 */
/*
 * For trying the ways out when there is more than one processor: boot-arg return_cpu=<n> has
 * that processor make the timed return, from an interrupt handler -- any but the boot processor
 * has to hand it over (psci_smp_stop_others()) --, and return_panic=1 makes a panic of it.
 */
static void
loader_return_test(void *as_panic)
{
	if (as_panic != (void *)1) {
		panic("return_panic: the panic that was asked for, on cpu %d", cpu_number());
	}
	loader_return();
}

static void
loader_return_timer(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	static const char banner[] = "\n--- loader_return_after expired ---\n";
	uint32_t cpu = 0, as_panic = 0;

	for (const char *c = banner; *c; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	PE_parse_boot_argn("return_panic", &as_panic, sizeof(as_panic));
	if (!as_panic) {
		hakios_var_save_on_return();   /* the data volume kept, while the system is still whole */
		hakios_adreno_stop();          /* a GPU kept for the system is given back while there is a thread to wait in */
		hakios_wifi_stop();            /* and the Wi-Fi DSP, if it runs, shut down */
		hakios_adsp_stop();            /* and the audio DSP */
		hakios_mpss_stop();            /* and the modem */
	}
	if (PE_parse_boot_argn("return_cpu", &cpu, sizeof(cpu)) && cpu <= (uint32_t)ml_get_max_cpu_number() &&
	    cpu_xcall((int)cpu, loader_return_test, (void *)(uintptr_t)(as_panic ? 2 : 1)) == KERN_SUCCESS) {
		for (;;) {
			delay_for_interval(1000, NSEC_PER_MSEC);        /* that processor ends it */
		}
	}
	loader_return_test((void *)(uintptr_t)(as_panic ? 2 : 1));
}

__startup_func
static void
loader_return_timer_init(void)
{
	uint32_t seconds = 0;
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("loader_return_after", &seconds, sizeof(seconds)) || seconds == 0) {
		return;
	}
	thread_call_t call = thread_call_allocate(loader_return_timer, NULL);
	clock_interval_to_deadline(seconds, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(call, deadline);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, loader_return_timer_init);

/*
 * A loader that watches from another core also listens to the host, and passes on a request to
 * end the run ("xl stop") by setting loader_live.stop. Look once a second.
 */
static thread_call_t loader_stop_call;

static void
loader_stop_poll(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (loader_live.stop) {
		static const char banner[] = "\n--- the host asked for the end of the run: back to the loader ---\n";
		for (const char *c = banner; *c; c++) {
			loader_log_putc(*c);
		}
		hakios_var_save_on_return();
		hakios_adreno_stop();
		hakios_wifi_stop();
		hakios_adsp_stop();
		loader_return();
	}
	clock_interval_to_deadline(1, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(loader_stop_call, deadline);
}

__startup_func
static void
loader_stop_poll_init(void)
{
	loader_stop_call = thread_call_allocate(loader_stop_poll, NULL);
	loader_stop_poll(NULL, NULL);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, loader_stop_poll_init);

/*
 * boot-arg hv_wdt_pet=1: the loader has armed the Qualcomm hypervisor's
 * virtual watchdog (it resets the phone when a kernel hangs, so that test
 * runs need nobody at the device). Its timeout is at most 65 seconds; feed
 * it from a timer so that a healthy kernel can run for as long as it likes.
 */
#define VIRT_WDT_PET            0x86000007u
#define HV_WDT_PET_SECONDS      10

static thread_call_t hv_wdt_call;
static uint32_t hv_wdt_enabled;

#define MEMORY_REPORT_BEATS     6               /* a line about memory every so many heartbeats */

extern unsigned int memorystatus_available_pages, memorystatus_available_pages_critical,
    memorystatus_available_pages_critical_base;
extern uint32_t c_segment_pages_compressed;
extern _Atomic uint64_t ramfs_pages_in_use;
extern void MiniIOSurfaceUsage(uint32_t *count, uint64_t *bytes);

/*
 * Where the memory is, in megabytes: for reading a session's log afterwards. "available" is what
 * the kernel's own count says (free and file-backed): below the first threshold it kills idle
 * daemons, and once none is left and it is below the second, whatever is next in line -- the
 * window server included.
 */
void hakios_memory_line(char *buf, size_t len);

/* The line itself (also kern.hakios_memory, for a job list to keep: bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_vfsops.c) */
void
hakios_memory_line(char *buf, size_t len)
{
#define MB(pages)       ((unsigned int)(((uint64_t)(pages) * PAGE_SIZE) >> 20))
	uint32_t surfaces = 0;
	uint64_t surface_bytes = 0;

	MiniIOSurfaceUsage(&surfaces, &surface_bytes);
	snprintf(buf, len, "memory: free %u, files %u, programs %u, wired %u (%u surfaces %u, ramfs %u), compressor %u "
	    "(holding %u) MB; available %u, kills below %u (the idle) and %u (anybody)\n",
	    MB(vm_page_free_count), MB(vm_page_pageable_external_count), MB(vm_page_pageable_internal_count),
	    MB(vm_page_wire_count), surfaces, (unsigned int)(surface_bytes >> 20),
	    MB(os_atomic_load(&ramfs_pages_in_use, relaxed)),
	    MB(VM_PAGE_COMPRESSOR_COUNT), MB(c_segment_pages_compressed),
	    MB(memorystatus_available_pages),
	    MB(memorystatus_available_pages_critical), MB(memorystatus_available_pages_critical_base));
#undef MB
}

static void
memory_report(void)
{
	char line[256];

	hakios_memory_line(line, sizeof(line));
	printf("%s", line);
	hakios_adreno_minute();                /* (and how warm the GPU is, if it is in use) */
}

/* Every HV_WDT_PET_SECONDS: feed the watchdog if there is one, and show any watching loader a sign of life. */
static void
hv_wdt_pet(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (hv_wdt_enabled) {
		register uint64_t x0 __asm__("x0") = VIRT_WDT_PET;
		register uint64_t x1 __asm__("x1") = 0;
		register uint64_t x2 __asm__("x2") = 0;
		register uint64_t x3 __asm__("x3") = 0;

		__asm__ volatile ("smc #0" : "+r" (x0), "+r" (x1), "+r" (x2), "+r" (x3) : :
		    "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x9", "x10", "x11", "x12", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "x17");
	}
	if (++loader_live.heartbeat % MEMORY_REPORT_BEATS == 0) {
		memory_report();
	}

	clock_interval_to_deadline(HV_WDT_PET_SECONDS, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(hv_wdt_call, deadline);
}

__startup_func
static void
hv_wdt_pet_init(void)
{
	PE_parse_boot_argn("hv_wdt_pet", &hv_wdt_enabled, sizeof(hv_wdt_enabled));
	hv_wdt_call = thread_call_allocate(hv_wdt_pet, NULL);
	hv_wdt_pet(NULL, NULL);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, hv_wdt_pet_init);
```

`xnu/files/osfmk/arm64/psci_smp.c`:

```c
/*
 * More than one processor on generic (non-Apple) ARMv8 boards.
 *
 * On Apple hardware the other cores are powered up by closed drivers. Here
 * the firmware does it, through the standard power interface of ARM systems
 * (PSCI): CPU_ON starts a core at an address of the caller's choice, CPU_OFF
 * stops the calling core for good. The address we give is the kernel's own
 * reset vector (LowResetVectorBase in start.s), so that a new core takes the
 * path Apple's cores take: it finds its cpu data by its MPIDR, turns the MMU
 * on and comes out in arm_init_cpu(). The calls are made with SMC or, under
 * a hypervisor that implements them itself, with HVC; the boot loader says
 * which (/chosen/psci-method).
 *
 * The platform expert (iokit/Kernel/GenericARMPE.cpp) registers the cores of
 * the device tree and starts them here, one after the other. Signals between
 * processors are interrupts of the GIC (gic_v3_irq.c).
 *
 * A new core begins with its MMU and caches off, and what it reads then it
 * reads from memory. On real hardware that is not the same as what the
 * running processors see: under Qualcomm's hypervisor (the phone this was
 * written for) a line that is dirty in another core's cache is simply not
 * there yet. QEMU has no cache and shows none of this. So before CPU_ON
 * everything that core will read before its MMU is on is written back to
 * memory (psci_smp_start_cpu()), and what it writes in that state is read
 * only after throwing away the reader's cached copy.
 *
 * The other half is the way out. The kernel ends by returning to the boot
 * loader (loader_return.c), and the loader gets back only what it started:
 * one core, the boot processor's. psci_smp_stop_others() makes every other
 * core switch itself off first, wherever it is.
 */
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/cpu_number.h>
#include <kern/debug.h>
#include <kern/kalloc.h>
#include <kern/misc_protos.h>
#include <libkern/kernel_mach_header.h>
#include <machine/atomic.h>
#include <arm/caches_internal.h>
#include <arm/cpu_data_internal.h>
#include <arm/cpu_internal.h>
#include <arm/machine_routines.h>
#include <arm64/proc_reg.h>
#include <arm64/psci_smp.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>
#include <pexpert/device_tree.h>
#include <pexpert/arm64/board_config.h>
#include <vm/pmap.h>

#if defined(GENERIC_PSCI_SMP)

#define PSCI_CPU_OFF            0x84000002u
#define PSCI_CPU_ON             0xC4000003u
#define PSCI_AFFINITY_INFO      0xC4000004u
#define PSCI_AFFINITY_OFF       1

#define PSCI_SMP_START_SECONDS  5       /* how long a started core is waited for */
#define PSCI_SMP_STOP_SECONDS   3       /* ... and the cores that were told to stop */

extern void loader_return(void);
extern void loader_log_putc(char c);
extern unsigned long gVirtBase, gPhysBase;

/* The firmware is called with HVC, not SMC. (start.s reads this too, at its physical address.) */
uint32_t psci_smp_hvc;

/*
 * Left by a core that took an exception between its first instruction and the kernel's vectors
 * (Lsecondary_early_exception in start.s). That core writes it with its cache off; it has a
 * cache line to itself so that looking at memory does not disturb anything else.
 */
struct psci_smp_start_fault {
	uint64_t valid, mpidr, esr, elr, far, lr, sp, unused;
} psci_smp_start_fault __attribute__((aligned(64)));
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct psci_smp_start_fault) == 64, "one cache line");

static uint32_t psci_smp_cpu_stage[MAX_CPUS];   /* PSCI_SMP_CPU_*, by cpu number */
static uint32_t psci_smp_started;               /* a bit per core that CPU_ON was granted for */

static int      psci_smp_stop_owner = -1;       /* the processor that began the return to the boot loader */
static bool     psci_smp_boot_wanted;           /* it was not the boot processor: that one is to finish */
static bool     psci_smp_boot_busy;             /* ... and has begun to */
static bool     psci_smp_stopping;              /* every other core switches itself off */

static int64_t
psci_call(uint64_t function, uint64_t arg1, uint64_t arg2, uint64_t arg3)
{
	register uint64_t x0 __asm__("x0") = function;
	register uint64_t x1 __asm__("x1") = arg1;
	register uint64_t x2 __asm__("x2") = arg2;
	register uint64_t x3 __asm__("x3") = arg3;

	if (psci_smp_hvc) {
		__asm__ volatile ("hvc #0" : "+r" (x0), "+r" (x1), "+r" (x2), "+r" (x3) : :
                    "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x9", "x10", "x11", "x12", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "x17");
	} else {
		__asm__ volatile ("smc #0" : "+r" (x0), "+r" (x1), "+r" (x2), "+r" (x3) : :
                    "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x9", "x10", "x11", "x12", "x13", "x14", "x15", "x16", "x17");
	}
	return (int64_t)x0;
}

static const char *
psci_error(int64_t status)
{
	static const char *const names[] = {
		"success", "not supported", "invalid parameters", "denied", "already on", "on pending",
		"internal failure", "not present", "disabled", "invalid address",
	};

	return (status <= 0 && status > -(int64_t)(sizeof(names) / sizeof(names[0]))) ? names[-status] : "?";
}

void
psci_smp_init(void)
{
	DTEntry chosen;
	void const *prop;
	unsigned int size;

	if (SecureDTLookupEntry(NULL, "/chosen", &chosen) == kSuccess &&
	    SecureDTGetProperty(chosen, "psci-method", &prop, &size) == kSuccess &&
	    size >= 3 && strncmp((const char *)prop, "hvc", 3) == 0) {
		psci_smp_hvc = 1;
	}
}

/* A processor other than the boot processor says how far it has come. */
void
psci_smp_cpu_reached(uint32_t stage)
{
	os_atomic_store(&psci_smp_cpu_stage[cpu_number()], stage, release);
}

/* ... all the way: from GenericARMCPU::initCPU(), where the scheduler takes it. */
void
psci_smp_cpu_running(void)
{
	psci_smp_cpu_reached(PSCI_SMP_CPU_RUNNING);
}

static void
psci_smp_clean_segment(const char *name)
{
	unsigned long size = 0;
	vm_offset_t start = (vm_offset_t)getsegdatafromheader(&_mh_execute_header, name, &size);

	if (start != 0 && size != 0) {
		CleanPoC_DcacheRegion(start, size);
	}
}

/*
 * Start a registered processor: the platform's half of cpu_start(). Waits until the core has
 * joined the scheduler, and says what became of it if it has not: on a phone the log is all
 * there is to go by.
 */
kern_return_t
psci_smp_start_cpu(int cpu)
{
	cpu_data_t *cdp = cpu_datap(cpu);
	uint32_t phys_id = cdp->cpu_phys_id, stage;
	uint64_t entry = ml_static_vtop((vm_offset_t)&LowResetVectorBase);
	uint64_t now, deadline;
	int64_t status;

	/*
	 * What that core reads with its MMU off: the code and the page tables of start.s, and what
	 * the reset vector finds its way by (ResetHandlerData, CpuDataEntries, the boot arguments,
	 * cpu_ttep, psci_smp_hvc ...), all of it in the kernel's own segments; and the cpu data of
	 * every processor, which the reset vector goes through looking for its own.
	 * Clean, not flush: the processors that are running keep using all of it.
	 */
	psci_smp_start_fault.valid = 0;
	psci_smp_clean_segment("__TEXT");
	psci_smp_clean_segment("__DATA_CONST");
	psci_smp_clean_segment("__TEXT_EXEC");
	psci_smp_clean_segment("__DATA");
	psci_smp_clean_segment("__BOOTDATA");
	for (int other = 0; other <= ml_get_max_cpu_number(); other++) {
		if (cpu_datap(other) != NULL) {
			CleanPoC_DcacheRegion((vm_offset_t)cpu_datap(other), sizeof(cpu_data_t));
		}
	}
	__builtin_arm_dsb(DSB_SY);

	os_atomic_store(&psci_smp_cpu_stage[cpu], PSCI_SMP_CPU_ASKED, release);
	status = psci_call(PSCI_CPU_ON, phys_id, entry, 0);
	if (status != 0) {
		os_atomic_store(&psci_smp_cpu_stage[cpu], 0, release);
		printf("psci: cpu %d (MPIDR 0x%x) was not started: the firmware answers %lld (%s)\n",
		    cpu, phys_id, status, psci_error(status));
		return KERN_FAILURE;
	}
	os_atomic_or(&psci_smp_started, 1u << cpu, relaxed);

	clock_interval_to_deadline(PSCI_SMP_START_SECONDS, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	do {
		stage = os_atomic_load(&psci_smp_cpu_stage[cpu], acquire);
		if (stage >= PSCI_SMP_CPU_RUNNING) {
			return KERN_SUCCESS;
		}
		/* memory, not this processor's copy of it */
		FlushPoC_DcacheRegion((vm_offset_t)&psci_smp_start_fault, sizeof(psci_smp_start_fault));
		if (psci_smp_start_fault.valid != 0) {
			break;
		}
		delay_for_interval(1, NSEC_PER_MSEC);
		now = mach_absolute_time();
	} while (now < deadline);

	if (psci_smp_start_fault.valid != 0) {
		struct psci_smp_start_fault *f = &psci_smp_start_fault;
		uint64_t to_virtual = gVirtBase - gPhysBase;

		printf("psci: cpu %d (MPIDR 0x%llx) took an exception on its way in and has switched itself off: "
		    "ESR 0x%llx ELR 0x%llx FAR 0x%llx LR 0x%llx SP 0x%llx (ELR and LR as kernel addresses: 0x%llx 0x%llx)\n",
		    cpu, f->mpidr, f->esr, f->elr, f->far, f->lr, f->sp, f->elr + to_virtual, f->lr + to_virtual);
		os_atomic_andnot(&psci_smp_started, 1u << cpu, relaxed);        /* nothing of it is left to stop */
	} else {
		printf("psci: cpu %d (MPIDR 0x%x) was started %d seconds ago and has not joined: %s\n",
		    cpu, phys_id, PSCI_SMP_START_SECONDS,
		    stage >= PSCI_SMP_CPU_IN_KERNEL ? "it got as far as arm_init_cpu()" : "no sign of it since the firmware took the request");
	}
	return KERN_FAILURE;
}

/*
 * The calling processor switches itself off. Its interrupted work, if any, is abandoned where
 * it was: only for the end of the system.
 */
void
psci_smp_cpu_off(void)
{
	__builtin_arm_wsr("DAIFSet", DAIFSC_ALL);
	/* leave nothing behind that would interrupt a core that is no longer there */
	__builtin_arm_wsr64("CNTV_CTL_EL0", CNTV_CTL_EL0_IMASKED);
	gic_v3_irq_cpu_shutdown();
	os_atomic_store(&psci_smp_cpu_stage[cpu_number()], PSCI_SMP_CPU_OFF, release);
	__builtin_arm_dsb(DSB_SY);

	(void) psci_call(PSCI_CPU_OFF, 0, 0, 0);
	for (;;) {
		__builtin_arm_wfi();    /* the firmware refused: stay out of the way all the same */
	}
}

static void
psci_smp_note(const char *what, int cpu)
{
	static const char prefix[] = "\npsci: cpu ";

	for (const char *c = prefix; *c; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
	loader_log_putc((char)('0' + cpu));
	for (const char *c = what; *c; c++) {
		loader_log_putc(*c);
	}
}

/* Tell every core but this one to switch itself off (psci_smp_stop_here() is where they hear it). */
static void
psci_smp_stop_rest(void)
{
	int me = cpu_number(), max_cpu = ml_get_max_cpu_number();

	os_atomic_store(&psci_smp_stopping, true, release);
	__builtin_arm_dsb(DSB_SY);
	for (int cpu = 0; cpu <= max_cpu; cpu++) {
		cpu_data_t *cdp = cpu_datap(cpu);

		if (cpu != me && cdp != NULL && (cpu == master_cpu || (psci_smp_started & (1u << cpu)))) {
			gic_v3_irq_signal_stop(cdp->cpu_phys_id);
		}
	}
	/* for those that wait with their interrupts off (wait_while_mp_kdp_trap(), after a panic) */
	__builtin_arm_sev();
}

/*
 * The system is going back to the boot loader (loader_return()). Returns on the boot processor
 * only, once the other cores are off -- or have been given up on. On any other processor it
 * does not return: that one hands the job to the boot processor, which the loader's side of
 * the return belongs to, and switches itself off like the rest.
 */
void
psci_smp_stop_others(void)
{
	int me, max_cpu;
	uint64_t now, deadline;

	if (psci_smp_started == 0) {
		return;                 /* there is only this one */
	}
	__builtin_arm_wsr("DAIFSet", DAIFSC_ALL);
	me = cpu_number();
	max_cpu = ml_get_max_cpu_number();
	if (!os_atomic_cmpxchg(&psci_smp_stop_owner, -1, me, acq_rel) && psci_smp_stop_owner != me && me != master_cpu) {
		psci_smp_cpu_off();     /* another processor is at it already */
	}

	if (me != master_cpu) {
		/*
		 * Nobody is stopped before the boot processor has answered: a core that is switched
		 * off while it holds a lock the boot processor is waiting for would take the return
		 * with it.
		 */
		psci_smp_note(" ends the system: the return to the boot loader is the boot processor's to make\n", me);
		os_atomic_store(&psci_smp_boot_wanted, true, release);
		__builtin_arm_dsb(DSB_SY);
		gic_v3_irq_signal_stop(cpu_datap(master_cpu)->cpu_phys_id);
		__builtin_arm_sev();
		now = mach_absolute_time();
		nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(PSCI_SMP_STOP_SECONDS * NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
		deadline += now;
		while (!os_atomic_load(&psci_smp_stopping, acquire) && now < deadline) {
			now = mach_absolute_time();
		}
		if (!os_atomic_load(&psci_smp_stopping, acquire)) {
			/*
			 * It does not hear (stuck with its interrupts off). There is no return without
			 * it; a loader that watches from its own core will find the kernel silent and
			 * take the log as it is, and so this goes into the log.
			 */
			psci_smp_note(" cannot return to the boot loader and the boot processor does not answer: all cores stop here\n", me);
			psci_smp_stop_rest();
		}
		psci_smp_cpu_off();
	}

	psci_smp_stop_rest();
	now = mach_absolute_time();
	nanoseconds_to_absolutetime(PSCI_SMP_STOP_SECONDS * NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	deadline += now;
	for (int cpu = 0; cpu <= max_cpu; cpu++) {
		cpu_data_t *cdp = cpu_datap(cpu);

		if (cpu == me || cdp == NULL || !(psci_smp_started & (1u << cpu))) {
			continue;
		}
		while (now < deadline) {
			if (os_atomic_load(&psci_smp_cpu_stage[cpu], acquire) == PSCI_SMP_CPU_OFF) {
				/* it has said it is going; the firmware knows when it has gone (if it can tell at all) */
				int64_t state = psci_call(PSCI_AFFINITY_INFO, cdp->cpu_phys_id, 0, 0);

				if (state == PSCI_AFFINITY_OFF || state < 0) {
					break;
				}
			}
			now = mach_absolute_time();
		}
		if (os_atomic_load(&psci_smp_cpu_stage[cpu], acquire) != PSCI_SMP_CPU_OFF &&
		    psci_call(PSCI_AFFINITY_INFO, cdp->cpu_phys_id, 0, 0) != PSCI_AFFINITY_OFF) {
			psci_smp_note(" did not stop: it is left running\n", cpu);
		}
	}
}

/*
 * Where a processor learns that the system is ending: the interrupt psci_smp_stop_rest() sends,
 * and the loop in which the processors wait while another one panics (they have their
 * interrupts off there). Comes back if there is nothing of the kind going on.
 */
void
psci_smp_stop_here(void)
{
	if (psci_smp_started == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (cpu_number() != master_cpu) {
		if (os_atomic_load(&psci_smp_stopping, acquire)) {
			psci_smp_cpu_off();
		}
		return;
	}
	if (os_atomic_load(&psci_smp_boot_wanted, acquire) && !psci_smp_boot_busy) {
		psci_smp_boot_busy = true;
		loader_return();        /* stops the rest (psci_smp_stop_others()); back only if no loader listens */
		for (;;) {
			__builtin_arm_wfi();
		}
	}
}

#endif /* defined(GENERIC_PSCI_SMP) */
```

```h
/*
 * More than one processor on generic (non-Apple) ARMv8 boards: see psci_smp.c.
 */
#ifndef _ARM64_PSCI_SMP_H_
#define _ARM64_PSCI_SMP_H_

#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <sys/cdefs.h>

__BEGIN_DECLS

/* How far a processor other than the boot processor has come (psci_smp_cpu_reached()). */
#define PSCI_SMP_CPU_ASKED      1       /* the firmware has agreed to start it */
#define PSCI_SMP_CPU_IN_KERNEL  2       /* it runs C code on the kernel's page tables (arm_init_cpu()) */
#define PSCI_SMP_CPU_RUNNING    3       /* it has joined the scheduler (psci_smp_cpu_running()) */
#define PSCI_SMP_CPU_OFF        4       /* it has switched itself off, or is about to */

extern void             psci_smp_init(void);
extern kern_return_t    psci_smp_start_cpu(int cpu);
extern void             psci_smp_cpu_reached(uint32_t stage);
extern void             psci_smp_cpu_running(void);
extern void             psci_smp_cpu_off(void) __dead2;

extern void             psci_smp_stop_others(void);
extern void             psci_smp_stop_here(void);

/* osfmk/arm64/gic_v3_irq.c */
extern void             gic_v3_irq_signal(uint32_t phys_id);
extern void             gic_v3_irq_signal_stop(uint32_t phys_id);
extern void             gic_v3_irq_quiesce(void);
extern void             gic_v3_irq_cpu_shutdown(void);

__END_DECLS

#endif /* _ARM64_PSCI_SMP_H_ */
```

`xnu/files/osfmk/arm64/user_exception_trace.c`:

```c
/*
 * Bring-up aid: with boot-arg systrace set, describe every fatal-looking
 * exception a user thread takes, before it is delivered. There is no crash
 * reporter in this system, so this is the only place a crash is recorded.
 *
 * Besides the registers it prints the shared cache slide (most crashes are
 * inside system libraries: subtract the slide and look the address up in
 * the cache with "ipsw dyld a2s"), any text a register points at (the
 * library crash helpers leave their message in one) and the return
 * addresses found by walking the frame pointers.
 */

#include <arm/thread.h>
#include <kern/debug.h>
#include <kern/misc_protos.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/task.h>
#include <kern/thread.h>
#include <mach/exception_types.h>
#include <mach/machine/thread_status.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <vm/vm_map.h>
#include <vm/vm_shared_region.h>

extern char *proc_name_address(struct proc *p);

void user_exception_trace(exception_type_t exception, mach_exception_data_t code, mach_msg_type_number_t count, thread_t thread);

static TUNABLE(uint32_t, user_exception_trace_enabled, "systrace", 0);

static bool
plausible_user_address(uint64_t address)
{
	return address >= 0x100000000ULL && address < MACH_VM_MAX_ADDRESS;
}

void
user_exception_trace(exception_type_t exception, mach_exception_data_t code, mach_msg_type_number_t count, thread_t thread)
{
	static const unsigned message_registers[] = { 0, 1, 2, 3, 8, 16 };
	const arm_saved_state_t *state;
	vm_shared_region_t region;
	uint64_t frame[2], fp;
	uint32_t slide = 0;
	task_t task;
	struct proc *proc;

	if (!user_exception_trace_enabled || thread != current_thread()) {
		return;
	}
	if (exception != EXC_BAD_ACCESS && exception != EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION && exception != EXC_ARITHMETIC &&
	    exception != EXC_BREAKPOINT) {
		return;
	}
	task = get_threadtask(thread);
	state = get_user_regs(thread);
	if (task == kernel_task || state == NULL || !is_saved_state64(state)) {
		return;
	}
	region = vm_shared_region_get(task);
	if (region != NULL) {
		slide = region->sr_slide;
		vm_shared_region_deallocate(region);
	}
	proc = get_bsdtask_info(task);

	printf("usertrap: %s[%d] exception %d code 0x%llx 0x%llx: pc 0x%llx lr 0x%llx sp 0x%llx, shared cache slide 0x%x\n",
	    proc ? proc_name_address(proc) : "?", proc ? proc_pid(proc) : -1, exception,
	    count > 0 ? (unsigned long long)code[0] : 0, count > 1 ? (unsigned long long)code[1] : 0,
	    (unsigned long long)get_saved_state_pc(state), (unsigned long long)get_saved_state_lr(state),
	    (unsigned long long)get_saved_state_sp(state), slide);

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(message_registers) / sizeof(message_registers[0]); i++) {
		uint64_t value = (uint64_t)get_saved_state_reg(state, message_registers[i]);
		char text[128];
		vm_size_t length = 0;
		bool printable = true;

		if (!plausible_user_address(value)) {
			continue;
		}
		bzero(text, sizeof(text));
		(void)copyinstr((user_addr_t)value, text, sizeof(text) - 1, &length);
		for (unsigned c = 0; c < 6; c++) {
			printable = printable && text[c] >= 0x20 && text[c] < 0x7f;
		}
		if (printable) {
			printf("usertrap:   x%u -> \"%s\"\n", message_registers[i], text);
		}
	}

	fp = (uint64_t)get_saved_state_fp(state);
	for (int depth = 0; depth < 10 && plausible_user_address(fp) && (fp & 7) == 0; depth++) {
		if (copyin((user_addr_t)fp, frame, sizeof(frame)) != 0) {
			break;
		}
		printf("usertrap:   called from 0x%llx\n", (unsigned long long)frame[1]);
		if (frame[0] <= fp) {
			break;
		}
		fp = frame[0];
	}
}

/*
 * A program calls abort(): say which, and from where. The reason is usually an exception nobody
 * caught, or an assertion; the text of it goes to the program's standard error (boot-arg applog=1
 * puts that on the console), the stack is here.
 */
void user_abort_trace(void);

void
user_abort_trace(void)
{
	thread_t thread = current_thread();
	task_t task = get_threadtask(thread);
	const arm_saved_state_t *state = get_user_regs(thread);
	struct proc *proc = get_bsdtask_info(task);
	vm_shared_region_t region;
	uint64_t frame[2], fp;
	uint32_t slide = 0;

	if (task == kernel_task || state == NULL || !is_saved_state64(state)) {
		return;
	}
	region = vm_shared_region_get(task);
	if (region != NULL) {
		slide = region->sr_slide;
		vm_shared_region_deallocate(region);
	}
	printf("userabort: %s[%d] aborts, shared cache slide 0x%x; called from:", proc ? proc_name_address(proc) : "?",
	    proc ? proc_pid(proc) : -1, slide);
	fp = (uint64_t)get_saved_state_fp(state);
	for (int depth = 0; depth < 24 && plausible_user_address(fp) && (fp & 7) == 0; depth++) {
		if (copyin((user_addr_t)fp, frame, sizeof(frame)) != 0) {
			break;
		}
		printf(" 0x%llx", (unsigned long long)frame[1]);
		if (frame[0] <= fp) {
			break;
		}
		fp = frame[0];
	}
	printf("\n");
}

/*
 * Boot-args ustacks=NAME ustacks_at=SECONDS [ustacks_ms=MILLISECONDS]: that long after boot
 * (and then periodically) print where every thread of every process called NAME is -- pc, lr
 * and the return addresses up the stack. Shows what a daemon that "does nothing" waits for.
 * ustacks_now(NAME) does it at once: under QEMU, "qemu/touch.py stacks NAME" on the host.
 * The addresses are symbolized on the host (qemu/symstack.py).
 * The name "top" asks for something else: who has had the processor (see ustacks_top()).
 */
#include <kern/recount.h>
#include <kern/thread_call.h>
#include <kern/clock.h>
#include <kern/queue.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>

extern queue_head_t tasks;
extern lck_mtx_t tasks_threads_lock;

#define USTACKS_MAX_THREADS 96
#define USTACKS_MAX_FRAMES  14

static char ustacks_name[32];
static uint32_t ustacks_every;
static uint32_t ustacks_threads = USTACKS_MAX_THREADS;  /* boot-arg ustacks_threads=N: only the first N (1: the main thread) */
/*
 * Boot-arg ustacks_tname=TEXT: only the threads whose name has TEXT in it (ustacks_tname=coreanimation:
 * the window server's render-server and its other threads), each line with the thread's name and, in
 * the first, the time in microseconds of mach_absolute_time (as the "tl:" lines of tools/latency.py);
 * the lines are few enough then to go to the loader's log as well, where all of a long run is kept.
 * ustacks_tname=* takes every thread, named or not, and sends them to the loader's log too.
 */
static char ustacks_tname[32];
static uint32_t ustacks_count;          /* boot-arg ustacks_count=N: so many times, then no more (0: for ever) */
static thread_call_t ustacks_call;

extern void bsd_getthreadname(void *uth, char *buffer);
extern void loader_log_line(const char *line);

static void
ustacks_say(const char *line)
{
	printf("%s", line);
	if (ustacks_tname[0] != 0) {
		loader_log_line(line);
	}
}

static void
ustacks_task(task_t task, struct proc *proc)
{
	static struct {
		uint64_t tid, pc, lr, fp;
		int state;
		char name[64];          /* (bsd_getthreadname() copies MAXTHREADNAMESIZE, 64) */
	} snap[USTACKS_MAX_THREADS];
	char line[512];
	int at;
	vm_shared_region_t region;
	vm_map_t map, old_map;
	thread_t thread;
	uint32_t slide = 0;
	unsigned count = 0;

	task_lock(task);
	queue_iterate(&task->threads, thread, thread_t, task_threads) {
		const arm_saved_state_t *state = get_user_regs(thread);

		if (count == USTACKS_MAX_THREADS || count >= ustacks_threads || state == NULL || !is_saved_state64(state)) {
			continue;
		}
		snap[count].name[0] = 0;
		if (get_bsdthread_info(thread) != NULL) {
			bsd_getthreadname(get_bsdthread_info(thread), snap[count].name);
			snap[count].name[63] = 0;
		}
		if (ustacks_tname[0] != 0 && strcmp(ustacks_tname, "*") != 0 &&
		    strnstr(snap[count].name, ustacks_tname, sizeof(snap[count].name)) == NULL) {
			continue;
		}
		snap[count].tid = thread_tid(thread);
		snap[count].state = thread->state;
		snap[count].pc = get_saved_state_pc(state);
		snap[count].lr = get_saved_state_lr(state);
		snap[count].fp = get_saved_state_fp(state);
		count++;
	}
	map = task->map;
	if (map != VM_MAP_NULL) {
		vm_map_reference(map);
	}
	task_unlock(task);
	if (map == VM_MAP_NULL) {
		return;
	}
	region = vm_shared_region_get(task);
	if (region != NULL) {
		slide = region->sr_slide;
		vm_shared_region_deallocate(region);
	}
	clock_sec_t secs;
	clock_usec_t usecs;

	uint64_t nanos;

	clock_get_system_microtime(&secs, &usecs);
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(mach_absolute_time(), &nanos);
	snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "ustacks: %s[%d] %u threads, shared cache slide 0x%x, uptime %lu.%03u, at %llu\n",
	    proc_name_address(proc), proc_pid(proc), count, slide, (unsigned long)secs, (unsigned)usecs / 1000, nanos / 1000);
	ustacks_say(line);

	old_map = vm_map_switch(map);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		uint64_t frame[2], fp = snap[i].fp;

		/* (a thread that runs shows where it last came into the kernel, not where it is) */
		at = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "ustacks:  thread 0x%llx%s%s%s%s: 0x%llx 0x%llx", (unsigned long long)snap[i].tid,
		    snap[i].name[0] ? " \"" : "", snap[i].name, snap[i].name[0] ? "\"" : "",
		    (snap[i].state & TH_RUN) ? " (running)" : "", (unsigned long long)snap[i].pc, (unsigned long long)snap[i].lr);
		for (int depth = 0; depth < USTACKS_MAX_FRAMES && plausible_user_address(fp) && (fp & 7) == 0; depth++) {
			if (copyin((user_addr_t)fp, frame, sizeof(frame)) != 0) {
				break;
			}
			if (at < (int)sizeof(line) - 24) {
				at += snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - at, " 0x%llx", (unsigned long long)frame[1]);
			}
			if (frame[0] <= fp) {
				break;
			}
			fp = frame[0];
		}
		snprintf(line + at, sizeof(line) - at, "\n");
		ustacks_say(line);
	}
	vm_map_switch(old_map);
	vm_map_deallocate(map);
}

/*
 * ustacks_now("top"): the processes that have had the processor since this was last asked (the
 * first time: since boot), each with its share of that time. A system that feels slow is either
 * busy -- this says with what -- or waiting for something, and the two look the same on the screen.
 */
#define USTACKS_TOP_TASKS 512
#define USTACKS_TOP_LINES 12

static void
ustacks_top(void)
{
	static struct {
		int pid;
		uint64_t total;                 /* user + system time so far, in Mach time units */
		uint64_t used;                  /* ... of it since the last time */
		char name[33];                  /* as long as a process name gets (2 * MAXCOMLEN + 1) */
	} now[USTACKS_TOP_TASKS];
	static struct {
		int pid;
		uint64_t total;
	} before[USTACKS_TOP_TASKS];
	static unsigned before_count;
	static uint64_t before_when;
	uint64_t when = mach_absolute_time(), elapsed = when - before_when, elapsed_ns, busy = 0;
	unsigned count = 0;
	task_t task;

	lck_mtx_lock(&tasks_threads_lock);
	queue_iterate(&tasks, task, task_t, tasks) {
		struct proc *proc = get_bsdtask_info(task);
		struct recount_times_mach times;

		if (count == USTACKS_TOP_TASKS || proc == NULL) {
			continue;
		}
		times = recount_task_times(task);
		now[count].pid = proc_pid(proc);
		now[count].total = times.rtm_user + times.rtm_system;
		strlcpy(now[count].name, proc_name_address(proc), sizeof(now[count].name));
		count++;
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&tasks_threads_lock);

	/* a process that was not there the last time has used all it has since */
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		uint64_t earlier = 0;

		for (unsigned j = 0; j < before_count; j++) {
			if (before[j].pid == now[i].pid) {
				earlier = before[j].total;
				break;
			}
		}
		now[i].used = now[i].total - MIN(earlier, now[i].total);
		busy += now[i].used;
	}
	absolutetime_to_nanoseconds(elapsed, &elapsed_ns);
	printf("top: in the last %llu ms the processor was busy %llu%% of the time\n", elapsed_ns / NSEC_PER_MSEC,
	    elapsed ? busy * 100 / elapsed : 0);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		before[i].pid = now[i].pid;
		before[i].total = now[i].total;
	}
	before_count = count;
	before_when = when;
	for (unsigned line = 0; line < USTACKS_TOP_LINES && count != 0 && elapsed != 0; line++) {
		unsigned most = 0;

		for (unsigned i = 1; i < count; i++) {
			if (now[i].used > now[most].used) {
				most = i;
			}
		}
		if (now[most].used * 1000 / elapsed == 0) {
			break;
		}
		printf("top:  %3llu.%llu%%  %s[%d]\n", now[most].used * 100 / elapsed, now[most].used * 1000 / elapsed % 10,
		    now[most].name, now[most].pid);
		now[most].used = 0;
	}
}

static void
ustacks_fire(__unused thread_call_param_t p0, __unused thread_call_param_t p1)
{
	static task_t found[8];
	unsigned count = 0;
	task_t task;

	if (strcmp(ustacks_name, "top") == 0) {
		ustacks_top();
		goto again;
	}
	lck_mtx_lock(&tasks_threads_lock);
	queue_iterate(&tasks, task, task_t, tasks) {
		struct proc *proc = get_bsdtask_info(task);

		if (count < 8 && proc != NULL && strncmp(proc_name_address(proc), ustacks_name, sizeof(ustacks_name)) == 0) {
			task_reference(task);
			found[count++] = task;
		}
	}
	lck_mtx_unlock(&tasks_threads_lock);
	if (count == 0) {
		printf("ustacks: no process called %s\n", ustacks_name);
	}
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		struct proc *proc = get_bsdtask_info(found[i]);

		if (proc != NULL) {
			ustacks_task(found[i], proc);
		}
		task_deallocate(found[i]);
	}
again:
	if (ustacks_count != 0 && --ustacks_count == 0) {
		return;
	}
	if (ustacks_every != 0) {
		uint64_t deadline;

		clock_interval_to_deadline(ustacks_every, NSEC_PER_MSEC, &deadline);
		thread_call_enter_delayed(ustacks_call, deadline);
	}
}

/* The same at once, for whoever asks (a debugging key sequence, see drivers/input/hakios.virtio_input.c). */
void ustacks_now(const char *name);

void
ustacks_now(const char *name)
{
	strlcpy(ustacks_name, name, sizeof(ustacks_name));
	if (ustacks_call == NULL) {
		ustacks_call = thread_call_allocate(ustacks_fire, NULL);
	}
	thread_call_enter(ustacks_call);
}

static void
ustacks_init(void)
{
	uint32_t at = 0;
	uint64_t deadline;

	if (!PE_parse_boot_argn("ustacks", ustacks_name, sizeof(ustacks_name)) ||
	    !PE_parse_boot_argn("ustacks_at", &at, sizeof(at)) || at == 0) {
		return;
	}
	PE_parse_boot_argn("ustacks_ms", &ustacks_every, sizeof(ustacks_every));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("ustacks_threads", &ustacks_threads, sizeof(ustacks_threads));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("ustacks_tname", ustacks_tname, sizeof(ustacks_tname));
	PE_parse_boot_argn("ustacks_count", &ustacks_count, sizeof(ustacks_count));
	ustacks_call = thread_call_allocate(ustacks_fire, NULL);
	clock_interval_to_deadline(at, NSEC_PER_SEC, &deadline);
	thread_call_enter_delayed(ustacks_call, deadline);
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_LAST, ustacks_init);

```

```c
 * A compact byte-oriented implementation written from the specification; the
 * S-boxes were generated from their definition. It is not constant-time and
 * not fast: it exists so that kernel code which merely needs a block cipher
```
