```c
struct mc_aes_key {
	uint32_t rounds;
	uint8_t  rk[240];           /* (rounds + 1) round keys of 16 bytes */
};

static inline uint8_t
xtime(uint8_t x)
{
	return (uint8_t)((x << 1) ^ ((x >> 7) * 0x1b));
}

static inline uint8_t
gmul(uint8_t a, uint8_t b)
{
	uint8_t p = 0;
	while (b) {
		if (b & 1) {
			p ^= a;
		}
		a = xtime(a);
		b >>= 1;
	}
	return p;
}

static int
mc_aes_setkey(struct mc_aes_key *k, size_t key_len, const uint8_t *key)
{
	uint32_t nk = (uint32_t)key_len / 4;
	uint8_t rcon = 1;

	if (key_len != 16 && key_len != 24 && key_len != 32) {
		return -1;
	}
	k->rounds = nk + 6;
	memcpy(k->rk, key, key_len);
	for (uint32_t i = nk; i < 4 * (k->rounds + 1); i++) {
		uint8_t t[4];
		memcpy(t, k->rk + 4 * (i - 1), 4);
		if (i % nk == 0) {
			uint8_t first = t[0];
			t[0] = aes_sbox[t[1]] ^ rcon;
			t[1] = aes_sbox[t[2]];
			t[2] = aes_sbox[t[3]];
			t[3] = aes_sbox[first];
			rcon = xtime(rcon);
		} else if (nk > 6 && i % nk == 4) {
			for (int j = 0; j < 4; j++) {
				t[j] = aes_sbox[t[j]];
			}
		}
		for (int j = 0; j < 4; j++) {
			k->rk[4 * i + j] = k->rk[4 * (i - nk) + j] ^ t[j];
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

static void
mc_aes_encrypt_block(const struct mc_aes_key *k, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out)
{
	uint8_t s[16], t[16];

	for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
		s[i] = in[i] ^ k->rk[i];
	}
	for (uint32_t r = 1; r <= k->rounds; r++) {
		/* SubBytes + ShiftRows (state is column-major: s[4*col + row]) */
		for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
			for (int row = 0; row < 4; row++) {
				t[4 * c + row] = aes_sbox[s[4 * ((c + row) & 3) + row]];
			}
		}
		if (r != k->rounds) {
			for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
				uint8_t *p = t + 4 * c;
				uint8_t a0 = p[0], a1 = p[1], a2 = p[2], a3 = p[3];
				p[0] = (uint8_t)(xtime(a0) ^ xtime(a1) ^ a1 ^ a2 ^ a3);
				p[1] = (uint8_t)(a0 ^ xtime(a1) ^ xtime(a2) ^ a2 ^ a3);
				p[2] = (uint8_t)(a0 ^ a1 ^ xtime(a2) ^ xtime(a3) ^ a3);
				p[3] = (uint8_t)(xtime(a0) ^ a0 ^ a1 ^ a2 ^ xtime(a3));
			}
		}
		for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
			s[i] = t[i] ^ k->rk[16 * r + i];
		}
	}
	memcpy(out, s, 16);
}

static void
mc_aes_decrypt_block(const struct mc_aes_key *k, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out)
{
	uint8_t s[16], t[16];

	for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
		s[i] = in[i] ^ k->rk[16 * k->rounds + i];
	}
	for (uint32_t r = k->rounds; r-- > 0;) {
		/* InvShiftRows + InvSubBytes */
		for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
			for (int row = 0; row < 4; row++) {
				t[4 * ((c + row) & 3) + row] = aes_inv_sbox[s[4 * c + row]];
			}
		}
		for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
			t[i] ^= k->rk[16 * r + i];
		}
		if (r != 0) {
			for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
				uint8_t *p = t + 4 * c;
				uint8_t a0 = p[0], a1 = p[1], a2 = p[2], a3 = p[3];
				p[0] = (uint8_t)(gmul(a0, 14) ^ gmul(a1, 11) ^ gmul(a2, 13) ^ gmul(a3, 9));
				p[1] = (uint8_t)(gmul(a0, 9) ^ gmul(a1, 14) ^ gmul(a2, 11) ^ gmul(a3, 13));
				p[2] = (uint8_t)(gmul(a0, 13) ^ gmul(a1, 9) ^ gmul(a2, 14) ^ gmul(a3, 11));
				p[3] = (uint8_t)(gmul(a0, 11) ^ gmul(a1, 13) ^ gmul(a2, 9) ^ gmul(a3, 14));
			}
		}
		memcpy(s, t, 16);
	}
	memcpy(out, s, 16);
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- ECB --- */

static int
mc_ecb_init(const struct ccmode_ecb *ecb __unused, ccecb_ctx *ctx, size_t key_nbytes, const void *key)
{
	return mc_aes_setkey((struct mc_aes_key *)ctx, key_nbytes, key);
}

static int
mc_ecb_encrypt(const ccecb_ctx *ctx, size_t nblocks, const void *in, void *out)
{
	const uint8_t *i = in;
	uint8_t *o = out;
	for (; nblocks > 0; nblocks--, i += 16, o += 16) {
		mc_aes_encrypt_block((const struct mc_aes_key *)ctx, i, o);
	}
	return 0;
}

static int
mc_ecb_decrypt(const ccecb_ctx *ctx, size_t nblocks, const void *in, void *out)
{
	const uint8_t *i = in;
	uint8_t *o = out;
	for (; nblocks > 0; nblocks--, i += 16, o += 16) {
		mc_aes_decrypt_block((const struct mc_aes_key *)ctx, i, o);
	}
	return 0;
}

const struct ccmode_ecb mc_aes_ecb_encrypt = {
	.size = sizeof(struct mc_aes_key),
	.block_size = 16,
	.init = mc_ecb_init,
	.ecb = mc_ecb_encrypt,
};

const struct ccmode_ecb mc_aes_ecb_decrypt = {
	.size = sizeof(struct mc_aes_key),
	.block_size = 16,
	.init = mc_ecb_init,
	.ecb = mc_ecb_decrypt,
};

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- CBC --- */

static int
mc_cbc_init(const struct ccmode_cbc *cbc __unused, cccbc_ctx *ctx, size_t key_len, const void *key)
{
	return mc_aes_setkey((struct mc_aes_key *)ctx, key_len, key);
}

static int
mc_cbc_encrypt(const cccbc_ctx *ctx, cccbc_iv *iv, size_t nblocks, const void *in, void *out)
{
	const uint8_t *i = in;
	uint8_t *o = out, *chain = (uint8_t *)iv;

	for (; nblocks > 0; nblocks--, i += 16, o += 16) {
		for (int b = 0; b < 16; b++) {
			chain[b] ^= i[b];
		}
		mc_aes_encrypt_block((const struct mc_aes_key *)ctx, chain, chain);
		memcpy(o, chain, 16);
	}
	return 0;
}

static int
mc_cbc_decrypt(const cccbc_ctx *ctx, cccbc_iv *iv, size_t nblocks, const void *in, void *out)
{
	const uint8_t *i = in;
	uint8_t *o = out, *chain = (uint8_t *)iv;

	for (; nblocks > 0; nblocks--, i += 16, o += 16) {
		uint8_t cipher[16], plain[16];
		memcpy(cipher, i, 16); /* in and out may be the same buffer */
		mc_aes_decrypt_block((const struct mc_aes_key *)ctx, cipher, plain);
		for (int b = 0; b < 16; b++) {
			o[b] = plain[b] ^ chain[b];
		}
		memcpy(chain, cipher, 16);
	}
	return 0;
}

const struct ccmode_cbc mc_aes_cbc_encrypt = {
	.size = sizeof(struct mc_aes_key),
	.block_size = 16,
	.init = mc_cbc_init,
	.cbc = mc_cbc_encrypt,
};

const struct ccmode_cbc mc_aes_cbc_decrypt = {
	.size = sizeof(struct mc_aes_key),
	.block_size = 16,
	.init = mc_cbc_init,
	.cbc = mc_cbc_decrypt,
};

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- CTR --- */

struct mc_aes_ctr {
	struct mc_aes_key key;
	uint8_t  counter[16];       /* 128-bit big-endian counter */
	uint8_t  stream[16];
	uint32_t used;              /* bytes of stream[] already consumed */
};

static int
mc_ctr_setctr(const struct ccmode_ctr *mode __unused, ccctr_ctx *ctx, const void *ctr)
{
	struct mc_aes_ctr *c = (struct mc_aes_ctr *)ctx;
	memcpy(c->counter, ctr, 16);
	c->used = 16;
	return 0;
}

static int
mc_ctr_init(const struct ccmode_ctr *mode, ccctr_ctx *ctx, size_t key_len, const void *key, const void *iv)
{
	struct mc_aes_ctr *c = (struct mc_aes_ctr *)ctx;
	int rc = mc_aes_setkey(&c->key, key_len, key);
	if (rc == 0) {
		rc = mc_ctr_setctr(mode, ctx, iv);
	}
	return rc;
}

static int
mc_ctr_crypt(ccctr_ctx *ctx, size_t nbytes, const void *in, void *out)
{
	struct mc_aes_ctr *c = (struct mc_aes_ctr *)ctx;
	const uint8_t *i = in;
	uint8_t *o = out;

	for (; nbytes > 0; nbytes--) {
		if (c->used == 16) {
			mc_aes_encrypt_block(&c->key, c->counter, c->stream);
			for (int b = 15; b >= 0 && ++c->counter[b] == 0; b--) {
			}
			c->used = 0;
		}
		*o++ = *i++ ^ c->stream[c->used++];
	}
	return 0;
}

const struct ccmode_ctr mc_aes_ctr_crypt = {
	.size = sizeof(struct mc_aes_ctr),
	.block_size = 1,
	.ecb_block_size = 16,
	.init = mc_ctr_init,
	.setctr = mc_ctr_setctr,
	.ctr = mc_ctr_crypt,
};

/* ---------------------------------------------------------- self test --- */

/* Returns a description of the first failing check, or NULL if all pass. */
const char *
mc_aes_selftest(void)
{
	static const uint8_t key[32] = { 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0d, 0x0e, 0x0f, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x18, 0x19, 0x1a, 0x1b, 0x1c, 0x1d, 0x1e, 0x1f };
	static const uint8_t iv[16] = { 0xf0, 0xf1, 0xf2, 0xf3, 0xf4, 0xf5, 0xf6, 0xf7, 0xf8, 0xf9, 0xfa, 0xfb, 0xfc, 0xfd, 0xfe, 0xff };
	static const uint8_t plain[48] = { 0x00, 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44, 0x55, 0x66, 0x77, 0x88, 0x99, 0xaa, 0xbb, 0xcc, 0xdd, 0xee, 0xff, 0x6b, 0xc1, 0xbe, 0xe2, 0x2e, 0x40, 0x9f, 0x96, 0xe9, 0x3d, 0x7e, 0x11, 0x73, 0x93, 0x17, 0x2a, 0xae, 0x2d, 0x8a, 0x57, 0x1e, 0x03, 0xac, 0x9c, 0x9e, 0xb7, 0x6f, 0xac, 0x45, 0xaf, 0x8e, 0x51 };
	static const uint8_t ecb128[16] = { 0x69, 0xc4, 0xe0, 0xd8, 0x6a, 0x7b, 0x04, 0x30, 0xd8, 0xcd, 0xb7, 0x80, 0x70, 0xb4, 0xc5, 0x5a };   /* FIPS 197 C.1 */
	static const uint8_t ecb256[16] = { 0x8e, 0xa2, 0xb7, 0xca, 0x51, 0x67, 0x45, 0xbf, 0xea, 0xfc, 0x49, 0x90, 0x4b, 0x49, 0x60, 0x89 };   /* FIPS 197 C.3 */
	static const uint8_t cbc128[48] = { 0x77, 0x02, 0xfc, 0x9b, 0x71, 0xc6, 0x3d, 0x26, 0xa2, 0xf0, 0x9d, 0xf5, 0xc4, 0x45, 0x10, 0x2a, 0x12, 0x4e, 0x7d, 0x18, 0xd9, 0x0f, 0xb7, 0x68, 0x47, 0x71, 0xd3, 0xb9, 0x5b, 0x9b, 0x45, 0xcd, 0x56, 0x95, 0x95, 0xd6, 0xeb, 0x0c, 0x39, 0x43, 0x74, 0xf8, 0x70, 0x7e, 0xa5, 0x3e, 0xe7, 0x03 };      /* OpenSSL */
	static const uint8_t ctr256[40] = { 0x92, 0x11, 0xef, 0xbe, 0x67, 0xc3, 0xe6, 0xbc, 0xd2, 0xf0, 0x4c, 0xef, 0x8c, 0xef, 0x8d, 0xeb, 0xa1, 0x9e, 0xc5, 0xa2, 0xdf, 0x6a, 0xab, 0x57, 0x87, 0x9a, 0x2b, 0x30, 0x39, 0xe4, 0x91, 0xa4, 0x37, 0x41, 0xab, 0x0c, 0x0a, 0x1b, 0x59, 0x04 };      /* OpenSSL */
	struct mc_aes_key k;
	struct mc_aes_ctr c;
	uint8_t chain[16], out[48];

	mc_aes_setkey(&k, 16, key);
	mc_aes_encrypt_block(&k, plain, out);
	if (memcmp(out, ecb128, 16) != 0) {
		return "aes-128 encrypt";
	}
	mc_aes_decrypt_block(&k, ecb128, out);
	if (memcmp(out, plain, 16) != 0) {
		return "aes-128 decrypt";
	}
	mc_aes_setkey(&k, 32, key);
	mc_aes_encrypt_block(&k, plain, out);
	if (memcmp(out, ecb256, 16) != 0) {
		return "aes-256 encrypt";
	}
	mc_aes_decrypt_block(&k, ecb256, out);
	if (memcmp(out, plain, 16) != 0) {
		return "aes-256 decrypt";
	}

	mc_aes_setkey(&k, 16, key);
	memcpy(chain, iv, 16);
	mc_cbc_encrypt((const cccbc_ctx *)&k, (cccbc_iv *)chain, 3, plain, out);
	if (memcmp(out, cbc128, 48) != 0) {
		return "aes-128-cbc encrypt";
	}
	memcpy(chain, iv, 16);
	mc_cbc_decrypt((const cccbc_ctx *)&k, (cccbc_iv *)chain, 3, out, out); /* in place */
	if (memcmp(out, plain, 48) != 0) {
		return "aes-128-cbc decrypt";
	}

	mc_ctr_init(&mc_aes_ctr_crypt, (ccctr_ctx *)&c, 32, key, iv);
	mc_ctr_crypt((ccctr_ctx *)&c, 7, plain, out);          /* uneven pieces */
	mc_ctr_crypt((ccctr_ctx *)&c, 33, plain + 7, out + 7);
	if (memcmp(out, ctr256, 40) != 0) {
		return "aes-256-ctr";
	}
	return NULL;
}

```

`xnu/files/osfmk/minicrypto/mc_digests.c`:

```c
/*
 * minicrypto: message digests that the kernel's crypto interface needs but
 * that are not part of the SHA-256-only "built-in corecrypto" shipped in the
 * XNU sources: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-384 and SHA-512.
 *
 * Written from the public algorithm specifications (RFC 1321, FIPS 180-4).
 * The constant tables were generated from their mathematical definitions.
 * Plain portable C, no assembly; correctness is checked at boot against
 * reference vectors (see mc_digest_selftest).
 */
#include <corecrypto/ccdigest.h>
#include <corecrypto/ccdigest_priv.h>
#include <corecrypto/cc_priv.h>
#include <corecrypto/ccsha1.h>
#include <corecrypto/ccsha2.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "minicrypto.h"

/* from the kernel's built-in corecrypto subset (osfmk/corecrypto) */
extern void ccdigest_final_64be(const struct ccdigest_info *di, ccdigest_ctx_t ctx, unsigned char *digest);

#define ROL32(x, n) (((x) << (n)) | ((x) >> (32 - (n))))
#define ROR64(x, n) (((x) >> (n)) | ((x) << (64 - (n))))

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- MD5 --- */

#define MD5_STATE_SIZE  16
#define MD5_BLOCK_SIZE  64
#define MD5_OUTPUT_SIZE 16

static const uint32_t md5_initial_state[4] = { 0x67452301, 0xefcdab89, 0x98badcfe, 0x10325476 };

static const uint32_t md5_k[64] = {
	0xd76aa478, 0xe8c7b756, 0x242070db, 0xc1bdceee,
	0xf57c0faf, 0x4787c62a, 0xa8304613, 0xfd469501,
	0x698098d8, 0x8b44f7af, 0xffff5bb1, 0x895cd7be,
	0x6b901122, 0xfd987193, 0xa679438e, 0x49b40821,
	0xf61e2562, 0xc040b340, 0x265e5a51, 0xe9b6c7aa,
	0xd62f105d, 0x02441453, 0xd8a1e681, 0xe7d3fbc8,
	0x21e1cde6, 0xc33707d6, 0xf4d50d87, 0x455a14ed,
	0xa9e3e905, 0xfcefa3f8, 0x676f02d9, 0x8d2a4c8a,
	0xfffa3942, 0x8771f681, 0x6d9d6122, 0xfde5380c,
	0xa4beea44, 0x4bdecfa9, 0xf6bb4b60, 0xbebfbc70,
	0x289b7ec6, 0xeaa127fa, 0xd4ef3085, 0x04881d05,
	0xd9d4d039, 0xe6db99e5, 0x1fa27cf8, 0xc4ac5665,
	0xf4292244, 0x432aff97, 0xab9423a7, 0xfc93a039,
	0x655b59c3, 0x8f0ccc92, 0xffeff47d, 0x85845dd1,
	0x6fa87e4f, 0xfe2ce6e0, 0xa3014314, 0x4e0811a1,
	0xf7537e82, 0xbd3af235, 0x2ad7d2bb, 0xeb86d391,
};

static const uint8_t md5_s[64] = {
	7, 12, 17, 22, 7, 12, 17, 22, 7, 12, 17, 22, 7, 12, 17, 22,
	5, 9, 14, 20, 5, 9, 14, 20, 5, 9, 14, 20, 5, 9, 14, 20,
	4, 11, 16, 23, 4, 11, 16, 23, 4, 11, 16, 23, 4, 11, 16, 23,
	6, 10, 15, 21, 6, 10, 15, 21, 6, 10, 15, 21, 6, 10, 15, 21,
};

static void
md5_compress(ccdigest_state_t state, size_t nblocks, const void *in)
{
	uint32_t *s = ccdigest_u32(state);
	const uint8_t *buf = in;

	for (; nblocks > 0; nblocks--, buf += MD5_BLOCK_SIZE) {
		uint32_t m[16], a = s[0], b = s[1], c = s[2], d = s[3];

		for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
			m[i] = cc_load32_le(buf + 4 * i);
		}
		for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
			uint32_t f;
			int g;
			if (i < 16) {
				f = (b & c) | (~b & d);
				g = i;
			} else if (i < 32) {
				f = (d & b) | (~d & c);
				g = (5 * i + 1) & 15;
			} else if (i < 48) {
				f = b ^ c ^ d;
				g = (3 * i + 5) & 15;
			} else {
				f = c ^ (b | ~d);
				g = (7 * i) & 15;
			}
			f += a + md5_k[i] + m[g];
			a = d;
			d = c;
			c = b;
			b += ROL32(f, md5_s[i]);
		}
		s[0] += a;
		s[1] += b;
		s[2] += c;
		s[3] += d;
	}
}

/* Finalisation for digests with a 64-byte block and a little-endian bit count. */
static void
mc_final_64le(const struct ccdigest_info *di, ccdigest_ctx_t ctx, unsigned char *digest)
{
	if (ccdigest_num(di, ctx) >= di->block_size) {
		ccdigest_num(di, ctx) = 0;
	}
	ccdigest_di_decl(di, tmp);
	memcpy(tmp, ctx, ccdigest_di_size(di));

	ccdigest_nbits(di, tmp) += ccdigest_num(di, tmp) * 8;
	ccdigest_data(di, tmp)[ccdigest_num(di, tmp)++] = 0x80;
	if (ccdigest_num(di, tmp) > 64 - 8) {
		while (ccdigest_num(di, tmp) < 64) {
			ccdigest_data(di, tmp)[ccdigest_num(di, tmp)++] = 0;
		}
		di->compress(ccdigest_state(di, tmp), 1, ccdigest_data(di, tmp));
		ccdigest_num(di, tmp) = 0;
	}
	while (ccdigest_num(di, tmp) < 64 - 8) {
		ccdigest_data(di, tmp)[ccdigest_num(di, tmp)++] = 0;
	}
	uint64_t nbits = ccdigest_nbits(di, tmp);
	cc_store32_le((uint32_t)nbits, ccdigest_data(di, tmp) + 56);
	cc_store32_le((uint32_t)(nbits >> 32), ccdigest_data(di, tmp) + 60);
	di->compress(ccdigest_state(di, tmp), 1, ccdigest_data(di, tmp));

	for (unsigned int i = 0; i < di->output_size / 4; i++) {
		cc_store32_le(ccdigest_state_u32(di, tmp)[i], digest + 4 * i);
	}
	ccdigest_di_clear(di, tmp);
}

const struct ccdigest_info mc_md5_di = {
	.output_size = MD5_OUTPUT_SIZE,
	.state_size = MD5_STATE_SIZE,
	.block_size = MD5_BLOCK_SIZE,
	.oid_size = 10,
	.oid = CC_DIGEST_OID_MD5,
	.initial_state = md5_initial_state,
	.compress = md5_compress,
	.final = mc_final_64le,
};

/* -------------------------------------------------------------- SHA-1 --- */

static const uint32_t sha1_initial_state[5] = { 0x67452301, 0xefcdab89, 0x98badcfe, 0x10325476, 0xc3d2e1f0 };

static void
sha1_compress(ccdigest_state_t state, size_t nblocks, const void *in)
{
	uint32_t *s = ccdigest_u32(state);
	const uint8_t *buf = in;

	for (; nblocks > 0; nblocks--, buf += CCSHA1_BLOCK_SIZE) {
		uint32_t w[80], a = s[0], b = s[1], c = s[2], d = s[3], e = s[4];

		for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
			w[i] = cc_load32_be(buf + 4 * i);
		}
		for (int i = 16; i < 80; i++) {
			w[i] = ROL32(w[i - 3] ^ w[i - 8] ^ w[i - 14] ^ w[i - 16], 1);
		}
		for (int i = 0; i < 80; i++) {
			uint32_t f, k;
			if (i < 20) {
				f = (b & c) | (~b & d);
				k = 0x5a827999;
			} else if (i < 40) {
				f = b ^ c ^ d;
				k = 0x6ed9eba1;
			} else if (i < 60) {
				f = (b & c) | (b & d) | (c & d);
				k = 0x8f1bbcdc;
			} else {
				f = b ^ c ^ d;
				k = 0xca62c1d6;
			}
			uint32_t t = ROL32(a, 5) + f + e + k + w[i];
			e = d;
			d = c;
			c = ROL32(b, 30);
			b = a;
			a = t;
		}
		s[0] += a;
		s[1] += b;
		s[2] += c;
		s[3] += d;
		s[4] += e;
	}
}

const struct ccdigest_info mc_sha1_di = {
	.output_size = CCSHA1_OUTPUT_SIZE,
	.state_size = CCSHA1_STATE_SIZE,
	.block_size = CCSHA1_BLOCK_SIZE,
	.oid_size = ccoid_sha1_len,
	.oid = CC_DIGEST_OID_SHA1,
	.initial_state = sha1_initial_state,
	.compress = sha1_compress,
	.final = ccdigest_final_64be,
};

/* ------------------------------------------------- SHA-512 / SHA-384 --- */

static const uint64_t sha512_initial_state[8] = {
	0x6a09e667f3bcc908ULL, 0xbb67ae8584caa73bULL,

static void
sha512_compress(ccdigest_state_t state, size_t nblocks, const void *in)
{
	uint64_t *s = ccdigest_u64(state);
	const uint8_t *buf = in;

	for (; nblocks > 0; nblocks--, buf += CCSHA512_BLOCK_SIZE) {
		uint64_t w[80], v[8];

		for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
			w[i] = cc_load64_be(buf + 8 * i);
		}
		for (int i = 16; i < 80; i++) {
			uint64_t s0 = ROR64(w[i - 15], 1) ^ ROR64(w[i - 15], 8) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 7);
			uint64_t s1 = ROR64(w[i - 2], 19) ^ ROR64(w[i - 2], 61) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 6);
			w[i] = w[i - 16] + s0 + w[i - 7] + s1;
		}
		memcpy(v, s, sizeof(v));
		for (int i = 0; i < 80; i++) {
			uint64_t S1 = ROR64(v[4], 14) ^ ROR64(v[4], 18) ^ ROR64(v[4], 41);
			uint64_t ch = (v[4] & v[5]) ^ (~v[4] & v[6]);
			uint64_t t1 = v[7] + S1 + ch + sha512_k[i] + w[i];
			uint64_t S0 = ROR64(v[0], 28) ^ ROR64(v[0], 34) ^ ROR64(v[0], 39);
			uint64_t maj = (v[0] & v[1]) ^ (v[0] & v[2]) ^ (v[1] & v[2]);
			uint64_t t2 = S0 + maj;
			v[7] = v[6];
			v[6] = v[5];
			v[5] = v[4];
			v[4] = v[3] + t1;
			v[3] = v[2];
			v[2] = v[1];
			v[1] = v[0];
			v[0] = t1 + t2;
		}
		for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
			s[i] += v[i];
		}
	}
}

/* Finalisation for 128-byte-block digests with a 128-bit big-endian bit count. */
static void
mc_final_128be(const struct ccdigest_info *di, ccdigest_ctx_t ctx, unsigned char *digest)
{
	if (ccdigest_num(di, ctx) >= di->block_size) {
		ccdigest_num(di, ctx) = 0;
	}
	ccdigest_di_decl(di, tmp);
	memcpy(tmp, ctx, ccdigest_di_size(di));

	ccdigest_nbits(di, tmp) += ccdigest_num(di, tmp) * 8;
	ccdigest_data(di, tmp)[ccdigest_num(di, tmp)++] = 0x80;
	if (ccdigest_num(di, tmp) > 128 - 16) {
		while (ccdigest_num(di, tmp) < 128) {
			ccdigest_data(di, tmp)[ccdigest_num(di, tmp)++] = 0;
		}
		di->compress(ccdigest_state(di, tmp), 1, ccdigest_data(di, tmp));
		ccdigest_num(di, tmp) = 0;
	}
	while (ccdigest_num(di, tmp) < 128 - 8) {
		ccdigest_data(di, tmp)[ccdigest_num(di, tmp)++] = 0;
	}
	cc_store64_be(ccdigest_nbits(di, tmp), ccdigest_data(di, tmp) + 128 - 8);
	di->compress(ccdigest_state(di, tmp), 1, ccdigest_data(di, tmp));

	for (unsigned int i = 0; i < di->output_size / 8; i++) {
		cc_store64_be(ccdigest_state_u64(di, tmp)[i], digest + 8 * i);
	}
	ccdigest_di_clear(di, tmp);
}

const struct ccdigest_info mc_sha512_di = {
	.output_size = CCSHA512_OUTPUT_SIZE,
	.state_size = CCSHA512_STATE_SIZE,
	.block_size = CCSHA512_BLOCK_SIZE,
	.oid_size = ccoid_sha512_len,
	.oid = CC_DIGEST_OID_SHA512,
	.initial_state = sha512_initial_state,
	.compress = sha512_compress,
	.final = mc_final_128be,
};

const struct ccdigest_info mc_sha384_di = {
	.output_size = CCSHA384_OUTPUT_SIZE,
	.state_size = CCSHA512_STATE_SIZE,
	.block_size = CCSHA512_BLOCK_SIZE,
	.oid_size = ccoid_sha384_len,
	.oid = CC_DIGEST_OID_SHA384,
	.initial_state = sha384_initial_state,
	.compress = sha512_compress,
	.final = mc_final_128be,
};

/* ---------------------------------------------------------- self test --- */

void
mc_digest(const struct ccdigest_info *di, size_t len, const void *data, void *digest)
{
	ccdigest_di_decl(di, ctx);
	ccdigest_init(di, ctx);
	ccdigest_update(di, ctx, len, data);
	di->final(di, ctx, digest);
	ccdigest_di_clear(di, ctx);
}

/* Reference digests of "abc" and of the 300-byte pattern msg[i] = 7*i + 3 (computed with OpenSSL). */

/* Returns the name of the first digest that fails, or NULL if all pass. */
const char *
mc_digest_selftest(void)
{
	uint8_t pattern[300], out[64];

	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(pattern); i++) {
		pattern[i] = (uint8_t)(i * 7 + 3);
	}
	for (unsigned v = 0; v < sizeof(mc_vectors) / sizeof(mc_vectors[0]); v++) {
		const struct mc_vector *vec = &mc_vectors[v];

		mc_digest(vec->di, 3, "abc", out);
		if (memcmp(out, vec->abc, vec->di->output_size) != 0) {
			return vec->name;
		}
		/* feed the pattern in uneven pieces to exercise the buffering */
		ccdigest_di_decl(vec->di, ctx);
		ccdigest_init(vec->di, ctx);
		ccdigest_update(vec->di, ctx, 1, pattern);
		ccdigest_update(vec->di, ctx, 130, pattern + 1);
		ccdigest_update(vec->di, ctx, 169, pattern + 131);
		vec->di->final(vec->di, ctx, out);
		if (memcmp(out, vec->pattern, vec->di->output_size) != 0) {
			return vec->name;
		}
	}
	return NULL;
}
```

`xnu/files/osfmk/minicrypto/mc_provider.c`:

```c
/*
 * minicrypto provider: registers a crypto backend with the kernel in place
 * of Apple's corecrypto kext (com.apple.kec.corecrypto), which is not part
 * of the open-source release and cannot be loaded into this static kernel.
 *
 * Provided:
 *   - digests: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 (the kernel's built-in), SHA-384, SHA-512
 *   - HMAC over those digests
 *   - the kernel PRNG, an HMAC-DRBG (SHA-256) seeded from the boot seed and
 *     reseeded from the kernel entropy collector
 *   - the small non-cryptographic generator the VM layer asks for
 *
 *   - AES in ECB, CBC and CTR modes (mc_aes.c; the TCP stack needs it at boot)
 *
 * NOT provided (function pointers left NULL; using them will fault): AES-XTS,
 * AES-GCM, DES/3DES, ChaCha20-Poly1305, RSA. Encrypted volumes, IPsec and
 * signature checks need those; the boot path to a ramdisk shell does not.
 */
#include <mach/mach_types.h>
#include <kern/debug.h>
#include <kern/startup.h>
#include <kern/simple_lock.h>
#include <machine/machine_routines.h>
#include <libkern/crypto/register_crypto.h>
#include <libkern/crypto/rand.h>
#include <corecrypto/cc_priv.h>
#include <corecrypto/ccdigest.h>
#include <corecrypto/ccdrbg.h>
#include <corecrypto/cchmac.h>
#include <corecrypto/cckprng.h>
#include <corecrypto/ccrng.h>
#include <corecrypto/ccsha2.h>
#include <prng/random.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "minicrypto.h"

#ifndef MIN
#define MIN(a, b) ((a) < (b) ? (a) : (b))
#endif

extern void read_random(void *buffer, u_int numBytes);
extern int printf(const char *format, ...) __printflike(1, 2);

/* ------------------------------------------------------- kernel PRNG --- */

static struct {
	struct ccdrbg_info info;
	struct ccdrbg_nisthmac_custom custom;
	uint8_t state[512];
	cckprng_getentropy getentropy;
	void *getentropy_arg;
	bool ready;
	simple_lock_data_t lock;
} mc_prng;

static boolean_t
mc_prng_lock(void)
{
	boolean_t intr = ml_set_interrupts_enabled(FALSE);
	simple_lock(&mc_prng.lock, LCK_GRP_NULL);
	return intr;
}

static void
mc_prng_unlock(boolean_t intr)
{
	simple_unlock(&mc_prng.lock);
	ml_set_interrupts_enabled(intr);
}

static void
mc_prng_init_with_getentropy(struct cckprng_ctx *ctx __unused, unsigned max_ngens __unused, size_t seed_nbytes,
    const void *seed, size_t nonce_nbytes, const void *nonce, cckprng_getentropy getentropy, void *getentropy_arg)
{
	static const char ps[] = "xnu minicrypto kernel prng";

	simple_lock_init(&mc_prng.lock, 0);
	mc_prng.custom.di = &ccsha256_ltc_di;
	mc_prng.custom.strictFIPS = 0;
	ccdrbg_factory_nisthmac(&mc_prng.info, &mc_prng.custom);
	if (mc_prng.info.size > sizeof(mc_prng.state)) {
		panic("minicrypto: DRBG state does not fit (%zu)", mc_prng.info.size);
	}
	int rc = ccdrbg_init(&mc_prng.info, (struct ccdrbg_state *)mc_prng.state, seed_nbytes, seed, nonce_nbytes, nonce,
	    sizeof(ps) - 1, ps);
	if (rc != CCDRBG_STATUS_OK) {
		panic("minicrypto: ccdrbg_init failed (%d)", rc);
	}
	mc_prng.getentropy = getentropy;
	mc_prng.getentropy_arg = getentropy_arg;
	mc_prng.ready = true;
}

static void
mc_prng_init(struct cckprng_ctx *ctx, size_t seed_nbytes, const void *seed, size_t nonce_nbytes, const void *nonce,
    cckprng_getentropy getentropy, void *getentropy_arg)
{
	mc_prng_init_with_getentropy(ctx, 1, seed_nbytes, seed, nonce_nbytes, nonce, getentropy, getentropy_arg);
}

static void
mc_prng_initgen(struct cckprng_ctx *ctx __unused, unsigned gen_idx __unused)
{
	/* one generator shared by all CPUs */
}

/* Mix caller-supplied bytes into the generator (HMAC-DRBG "additional input"). */
static void
mc_prng_reseed(struct cckprng_ctx *ctx __unused, size_t nbytes, const void *seed)
{
	uint8_t discard[32];

	if (!mc_prng.ready || nbytes == 0) {
		return;
	}
	boolean_t intr = mc_prng_lock();
	(void)ccdrbg_generate(&mc_prng.info, (struct ccdrbg_state *)mc_prng.state, sizeof(discard), discard, nbytes, seed);
	mc_prng_unlock(intr);
	cc_clear(sizeof(discard), discard);
}

/* Pull whatever the kernel entropy collector has accumulated and mix it in. */
static void
mc_prng_refresh(struct cckprng_ctx *ctx)
{
	uint8_t entropy[CCKPRNG_ENTROPY_SIZE];
	size_t nbytes = sizeof(entropy);

	if (!mc_prng.ready || mc_prng.getentropy == NULL) {
		return;
	}
	if (mc_prng.getentropy(&nbytes, entropy, mc_prng.getentropy_arg) > 0 && nbytes > 0) {
		mc_prng_reseed(ctx, nbytes, entropy);
	}
	cc_clear(sizeof(entropy), entropy);
}

static void
mc_prng_generate(struct cckprng_ctx *ctx __unused, unsigned gen_idx __unused, size_t nbytes, void *out)
{
	uint8_t *p = out;

	while (nbytes > 0) {
		size_t n = MIN(nbytes, (size_t)1024);
		boolean_t intr = mc_prng_lock();
		int rc = ccdrbg_generate(&mc_prng.info, (struct ccdrbg_state *)mc_prng.state, n, p, 0, NULL);
		mc_prng_unlock(intr);
		if (rc != CCDRBG_STATUS_OK) {
			panic("minicrypto: ccdrbg_generate failed (%d)", rc);
		}
		p += n;
		nbytes -= n;
	}
}

static const struct cckprng_funcs mc_prng_funcs = {
	.init = mc_prng_init,
	.initgen = mc_prng_initgen,
	.reseed = mc_prng_reseed,
	.refresh = mc_prng_refresh,
	.generate = mc_prng_generate,
	.init_with_getentropy = mc_prng_init_with_getentropy,
};

/* ccrng handle: random bytes straight from the kernel PRNG. */
static int
mc_rng_generate(struct ccrng_state *rng __unused, size_t outlen, void *out)
{
	read_random(out, (u_int)outlen);
	return 0;
}

static struct ccrng_state mc_rng_state = { .generate = mc_rng_generate };

static struct ccrng_state *
mc_ccrng(int *error)
{
	if (error != NULL) {
		*error = 0;
	}
	return &mc_rng_state;
}

/* ------------------------------------- lock-free generator for kmem --- */
/* xoshiro256**: fast, no locks, explicitly not cryptographic (see rand.h). */

struct mc_random_ctx {
	uint64_t s[4];
};

static inline uint64_t
mc_rotl(uint64_t x, int k)
{
	return (x << k) | (x >> (64 - k));
}

static uint64_t
mc_random_next(struct mc_random_ctx *r)
{
	uint64_t result = mc_rotl(r->s[1] * 5, 7) * 9;
	uint64_t t = r->s[1] << 17;

	r->s[2] ^= r->s[0];
	r->s[3] ^= r->s[1];
	r->s[1] ^= r->s[2];
	r->s[0] ^= r->s[3];
	r->s[2] ^= t;
	r->s[3] = mc_rotl(r->s[3], 45);
	return result;
}

static size_t
mc_random_kmem_ctx_size(void)
{
	return sizeof(struct mc_random_ctx);
}

static void
mc_random_kmem_init(crypto_random_ctx_t ctx)
{
	struct mc_random_ctx *r = ctx;

	read_random(r->s, sizeof(r->s));
	r->s[0] |= 1; /* the all-zero state is invalid */
}

static void
mc_random_generate(crypto_random_ctx_t ctx, void *random, size_t random_size)
{
	uint8_t *p = random;

	while (random_size > 0) {
		uint64_t v = mc_random_next(ctx);
		size_t n = MIN(random_size, sizeof(v));
		memcpy(p, &v, n);
		p += n;
		random_size -= n;
	}
}

static void
mc_random_uniform(crypto_random_ctx_t ctx, uint64_t bound, uint64_t *random)
{
	if (bound < 2) {
		*random = 0;
		return;
	}
	/* rejection sampling keeps the distribution flat */
	uint64_t limit = UINT64_MAX - (UINT64_MAX % bound);
	uint64_t v;
	do {
		v = mc_random_next(ctx);
	} while (v >= limit);
	*random = v % bound;
}

/* ---------------------------------------- generic digest / HMAC API --- */

static const struct ccdigest_info *
mc_di(crypto_digest_alg_t alg)
{
	switch (alg) {
	case CRYPTO_DIGEST_ALG_MD5:
		return &mc_md5_di;
	case CRYPTO_DIGEST_ALG_SHA1:
		return &mc_sha1_di;
	case CRYPTO_DIGEST_ALG_SHA256:
		return ccsha256_di();
	case CRYPTO_DIGEST_ALG_SHA384:
		return &mc_sha384_di;
	case CRYPTO_DIGEST_ALG_SHA512:
		return &mc_sha512_di;
	default:
		panic("minicrypto: unsupported digest algorithm %d", (int)alg);
	}
}

static void
mc_ccdigest_final(const struct ccdigest_info *di, ccdigest_ctx_t ctx, void *digest)
{
	di->final(di, ctx, digest);
}

static void
mc_ccdigest(const struct ccdigest_info *di, unsigned long len, const void *data, void *digest)
{
	mc_digest(di, len, data, digest);
}

static size_t
mc_digest_ctx_size(crypto_digest_alg_t alg)
{
	return ccdigest_di_size(mc_di(alg));
}

static void
mc_digest_init(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, void *ctx, size_t ctx_size __unused)
{
	ccdigest_init(mc_di(alg), ctx);
}

static void
mc_digest_update(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, void *ctx, size_t ctx_size __unused, const void *data, size_t data_size)
{
	ccdigest_update(mc_di(alg), ctx, data_size, data);
}

static void
mc_digest_final(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, void *ctx, size_t ctx_size __unused, void *digest, size_t digest_size)
{
	const struct ccdigest_info *di = mc_di(alg);
	uint8_t out[64];

	di->final(di, ctx, out);
	memcpy(digest, out, MIN(digest_size, di->output_size));
}

static void
mc_digest_oneshot(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, const void *data, size_t data_size, void *digest, size_t digest_size)
{
	const struct ccdigest_info *di = mc_di(alg);
	uint8_t out[64];

	mc_digest(di, data_size, data, out);
	memcpy(digest, out, MIN(digest_size, di->output_size));
}

static size_t
mc_hmac_ctx_size(crypto_digest_alg_t alg)
{
	return cchmac_di_size(mc_di(alg));
}

static void
mc_hmac_init(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, void *ctx, size_t ctx_size __unused, const void *key, size_t key_size)
{
	cchmac_init(mc_di(alg), ctx, key_size, key);
}

static void
mc_hmac_update(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, void *ctx, size_t ctx_size __unused, const void *data, size_t data_size)
{
	cchmac_update(mc_di(alg), ctx, data_size, data);
}

static void
mc_hmac_final_generate(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, void *ctx, size_t ctx_size __unused, void *tag, size_t tag_size)
{
	const struct ccdigest_info *di = mc_di(alg);
	uint8_t out[64];

	cchmac_final(di, ctx, out);
	memcpy(tag, out, MIN(tag_size, di->output_size));
	cc_clear(sizeof(out), out);
}

static bool
mc_hmac_final_verify(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, void *ctx, size_t ctx_size __unused, const void *tag, size_t tag_size)
{
	const struct ccdigest_info *di = mc_di(alg);
	uint8_t out[64];

	if (tag_size == 0 || tag_size > di->output_size) {
		return false;
	}
	cchmac_final(di, ctx, out);
	bool ok = (cc_cmp_safe(tag_size, out, tag) == 0);
	cc_clear(sizeof(out), out);
	return ok;
}

static void
mc_hmac_generate(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, const void *key, size_t key_size, const void *data, size_t data_size,
    void *tag, size_t tag_size)
{
	const struct ccdigest_info *di = mc_di(alg);
	uint8_t out[64];

	cchmac(di, key_size, key, data_size, data, out);
	memcpy(tag, out, MIN(tag_size, di->output_size));
	cc_clear(sizeof(out), out);
}

static bool
mc_hmac_verify(crypto_digest_alg_t alg, const void *key, size_t key_size, const void *data, size_t data_size,
    const void *tag, size_t tag_size)
{
	const struct ccdigest_info *di = mc_di(alg);
	uint8_t out[64];

	if (tag_size == 0 || tag_size > di->output_size) {
		return false;
	}
	cchmac(di, key_size, key, data_size, data, out);
	bool ok = (cc_cmp_safe(tag_size, out, tag) == 0);
	cc_clear(sizeof(out), out);
	return ok;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------ registration --- */

static struct crypto_functions mc_funcs = {
	.ccdigest_init_fn = ccdigest_init,
	.ccdigest_update_fn = ccdigest_update,
	.ccdigest_final_fn = mc_ccdigest_final,
	.ccdigest_fn = mc_ccdigest,
	.ccmd5_di = &mc_md5_di,
	.ccsha1_di = &mc_sha1_di,
	.ccsha384_di = &mc_sha384_di,
	.ccsha512_di = &mc_sha512_di,

	.cchmac_init_fn = cchmac_init,
	.cchmac_update_fn = cchmac_update,
	.cchmac_final_fn = cchmac_final,
	.cchmac_fn = cchmac,

	.ccaes_ecb_encrypt = &mc_aes_ecb_encrypt,
	.ccaes_ecb_decrypt = &mc_aes_ecb_decrypt,
	.ccaes_cbc_encrypt = &mc_aes_cbc_encrypt,
	.ccaes_cbc_decrypt = &mc_aes_cbc_decrypt,
	.ccaes_ctr_crypt = &mc_aes_ctr_crypt,

	.ccrng_fn = mc_ccrng,

	.random_generate_fn = mc_random_generate,
	.random_uniform_fn = mc_random_uniform,
	.random_kmem_ctx_size_fn = mc_random_kmem_ctx_size,
	.random_kmem_init_fn = mc_random_kmem_init,

	.digest_ctx_size_fn = mc_digest_ctx_size,
	.digest_init_fn = mc_digest_init,
	.digest_update_fn = mc_digest_update,
	.digest_final_fn = mc_digest_final,
	.digest_fn = mc_digest_oneshot,

	.hmac_ctx_size_fn = mc_hmac_ctx_size,
	.hmac_init_fn = mc_hmac_init,
	.hmac_update_fn = mc_hmac_update,
	.hmac_final_generate_fn = mc_hmac_final_generate,
	.hmac_final_verify_fn = mc_hmac_final_verify,
	.hmac_generate_fn = mc_hmac_generate,
	.hmac_verify_fn = mc_hmac_verify,
};

/*
 * Runs where the corecrypto kext would normally have been started: before
 * the first consumer in the EARLY_BOOT stage (kmem's random generator).
 */
__startup_func
static void
minicrypto_init(void)
{
	const char *failed = mc_digest_selftest();
	if (failed == NULL) {
		failed = mc_aes_selftest();
	}
	if (failed != NULL) {
		panic("minicrypto: %s self-test failed", failed);
	}

	mc_funcs.ccsha256_di = ccsha256_di();
	if (register_crypto_functions(&mc_funcs) != 0) {
		return; /* a real provider got there first */
	}
	/* The PRNG context is ours; the kernel only hands the pointer back to us. */
	register_and_init_prng((struct cckprng_ctx *)(void *)&mc_prng, &mc_prng_funcs);
	printf("minicrypto: registered (md5, sha1, sha2, hmac, aes-ecb/cbc/ctr, hmac-drbg prng); no xts/gcm, no RSA\n");
}
STARTUP(EARLY_BOOT, STARTUP_RANK_FIRST, minicrypto_init);
```

```h
 * open-source kernel to boot without it. See mc_provider.c.

extern const struct ccmode_ctr mc_aes_ctr_crypt;

#endif /* _MINICRYPTO_H_ */
```

```patch
+ * systrace=2 logs all of them (to the kernel message buffer). For calls that
+ * take a path, the path is shown. systrace_name=NAME keeps it to the processes
+ * of that name: with a whole system running, everybody's failed calls are
+ * megabytes a minute.
+ */
+static TUNABLE(uint32_t, systrace_level, "systrace", 0);
+static TUNABLE_STR(systrace_name, MAXCOMLEN + 1, "systrace_name", "");
+extern const char *syscallnames[];
+
+static void
+systrace_report(struct proc *proc, unsigned short syscode, struct uthread *uthread, int error)
+{
+	/* system calls whose first (or, for the second list, second) argument is a path */
+	static const unsigned short path_arg0[] = {
+		SYS_open, SYS_link, SYS_unlink, SYS_chdir, SYS_mknod, SYS_chmod, SYS_chown, SYS_access, SYS_readlink,
+		SYS_execve, SYS_chroot, SYS_rename, SYS_mkdir, SYS_rmdir, SYS_pathconf, SYS_getattrlist, SYS_setattrlist,
+		SYS_getxattr, SYS_listxattr, SYS_fsctl, SYS_stat64, SYS_lstat64, SYS_statfs64, SYS_open_nocancel,
+		SYS_open_dprotected_np, SYS_symlink, SYS_unmount, SYS_stat64_extended, SYS_lstat64_extended,
+	};
+	static const unsigned short path_arg1[] = {
+		SYS_mount, SYS_posix_spawn, SYS_openat, SYS_openat_nocancel, SYS_fstatat64, SYS_faccessat, SYS_readlinkat,
+		SYS_getattrlistat, SYS_mkdirat, SYS_unlinkat,
+	};
+	char path[160] = "";
+	/*
+	 * Two calls are worth more than their arguments' addresses, because what they ASK is the whole
+	 * of what they do. __mac_syscall carries the policy's name and the request number: this
+	 * kernel's AMFI stand-in answers only 0x5a and 0x60 and returns ENOPOLICY to anything else
+	 * (bsd/kern/kern_minimac.c), so a daemon refused there is refused in a way nothing in user
+	 * space can see -- and a library of ours cannot watch it either, since the call is made inside
+	 * libsystem and dyld interposing only stands between images. The name matters as much as the
+	 * number: the same call goes to Sandbox as well. And sysctl carries its MIB, which is the only
+	 * thing that says what was asked about.
+	 */
+	char detail[112] = "";
+	size_t done;
+
+	if (systrace_level < 2 && (error == 0 || error == EJUSTRETURN || error == ERESTART)) {
+		return;
+	}
+	if (systrace_name[0] != 0 && strncmp(proc->p_comm, systrace_name, MAXCOMLEN) != 0) {
+		return;
+	}
+	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(path_arg0) / sizeof(path_arg0[0]); i++) {
+		if (path_arg0[i] == syscode) {
+			(void)copyinstr((user_addr_t)uthread->uu_arg[0], path, sizeof(path), &done);
+		}
+	}
+	for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(path_arg1) / sizeof(path_arg1[0]); i++) {
+		if (path_arg1[i] == syscode) {
+			(void)copyinstr((user_addr_t)uthread->uu_arg[1], path, sizeof(path), &done);
+		}
+	}
+	path[sizeof(path) - 1] = 0;
+	if (syscode == SYS___mac_syscall) {
+		char policy[32] = "";
+
+		(void)copyinstr((user_addr_t)uthread->uu_arg[0], policy, sizeof(policy), &done);
+		policy[sizeof(policy) - 1] = 0;
+		snprintf(detail, sizeof(detail), " policy \"%s\" request %lld", policy,
+		    (long long)uthread->uu_arg[1]);
+	} else if (syscode == SYS_sysctl) {
+		int mib[6];
+		unsigned count = (unsigned)uthread->uu_arg[1];
+
+		if (count > 6) {
+			count = 6;
+		}
+		if (count > 0 && copyin((user_addr_t)uthread->uu_arg[0], mib, count * sizeof(mib[0])) == 0) {
+			size_t used = (size_t)snprintf(detail, sizeof(detail), " mib");
+
+			for (unsigned i = 0; i < count && used + 12 < sizeof(detail); i++) {
+				used += (size_t)snprintf(detail + used, sizeof(detail) - used, " %d", mib[i]);
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	detail[sizeof(detail) - 1] = 0;
+	printf("systrace: %s[%d] %s(0x%llx, 0x%llx, 0x%llx, 0x%llx)%s%s%s%s = %d\n",
+	    proc->p_comm, proc_getpid(proc), syscallnames[syscode],
+	    (unsigned long long)uthread->uu_arg[0], (unsigned long long)uthread->uu_arg[1],
+	    (unsigned long long)uthread->uu_arg[2], (unsigned long long)uthread->uu_arg[3],
+	    path[0] ? " \"" : "", path, path[0] ? "\"" : "", detail, error);
+}
+
 #if CONFIG_DTRACE

 extern void dtrace_systrace_syscall_return(unsigned short, int, int *);

+		systrace_report(proc, syscode, uthread, error);
+	}

 #endif /* CONFIG_MACF */

+/*
+ * For a filesystem that reads a memory disk in place: where the disk is in the kernel's
+ * address space. Not for disks given by physical address (those are not mapped).
+ */
+int
+mdevgetkernelrange(dev_t dev, vm_offset_t *base, uint64_t *size)
+{
+	for (int i = 0; i < NB_MAX_MDEVICES; i++) {
+		if ((mdev[i].mdFlags & mdInited) && mdev[i].mdBDev == dev) {
+			if (mdev[i].mdFlags & mdPhys) {
+				return ENOTSUP;
+			}
+			*base = (vm_offset_t)(mdev[i].mdBase << 12);
+			*size = mdev[i].mdSize << 12;
+			return 0;
+		}
+	}
+	return ENXIO;
+}

+/*
+ * Bring-up aid, boot-arg applog=1: what applications and other programs started without a
+ * terminal say is worth reading here. Their standard output and error, which launchd opens on
+ * /dev/null, go to the console instead (that shows NSLog and the "Terminating app due to
+ * uncaught exception" kind of message). With applog=2 every program also gets
+ * OS_ACTIVITY_DT_MODE in its environment, which makes os_log write to standard error as well:
+ * everything any program logs, and a much slower system. applog_name=NAME[,NAME...] with
+ * applog=1 does that for the programs whose file names begin with one of the NAMEs only,
+ * which is how to read what one application extension has to say (launchd starts those for
+ * whoever asks, so there is no job description of ours to put the variable in).
+ */
+static TUNABLE(uint32_t, exec_applog, "applog", 0);
+static TUNABLE_STR(exec_applog_name, 128, "applog_name", "");
+
+static bool
+exec_applog_oslog(struct image_params *imgp)
+{
+	const char *name, *p = exec_applog_name;
+
+	if (exec_applog >= 2) {
+		return true;
+	}
+	if (exec_applog == 0 || *p == 0 || imgp->ip_ndp == NULL) {
+		return false;
+	}
+	name = imgp->ip_ndp->ni_cnd.cn_nameptr;
+	while (*p != 0) {
+		const char *word = p;
+
+		while (*p != 0 && *p != ',') {
+			p++;
+		}
+		if (p != word && (size_t)(p - word) <= imgp->ip_ndp->ni_cnd.cn_namelen && strncmp(word, name, (size_t)(p - word)) == 0) {
+			return true;
+		}
+		if (*p == ',') {
+			p++;
+		}
+	}
+	return false;
+}
+
+static const char *
+exec_applog_path(int fd, const char *path)
+{
+	if (exec_applog && (fd == 1 || fd == 2) && strcmp(path, "/dev/null") == 0) {
+		return "/dev/console";
+	}
+	return path;
+}

+/*
+ * Bring-up aid: the sysctl kern.exec_inject holds "LIBRARY NAME NAME ..."; every program
+ * whose file name is one of the NAMEs is started with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=LIBRARY in its
+ * environment, so that dyld loads our library into it. Several such groups may follow each
+ * other, separated by ";". A program named in more than one group gets every one of those
+ * libraries, joined with ":" in the one DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, so SpringBoard can carry both
+ * our window-server library and the tweak loader. launchd refuses to pass DYLD_ variables
+ * from a job description, which is why the kernel adds this one. Set once by our init (from
+ * etc/inject.conf) before it hands over to launchd.
+ */
+static char exec_inject_conf[512];
+SYSCTL_STRING(_kern, OID_AUTO, exec_inject, CTLFLAG_RW | CTLFLAG_LOCKED, exec_inject_conf, sizeof(exec_inject_conf),
+    "LIBRARY NAME... [; LIBRARY NAME...]: programs started with the library inserted");
+
+static bool
+exec_inject_env(struct image_params *imgp, char *env, size_t size)
+{
+	const char *name, *p = exec_inject_conf;
+	size_t namelen, used;
+	bool any = false;
+
+	if (*p == 0 || imgp->ip_ndp == NULL) {
+		return false;
+	}
+	name = imgp->ip_ndp->ni_cnd.cn_nameptr;
+	namelen = imgp->ip_ndp->ni_cnd.cn_namelen;
+	used = strlcpy(env, "DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=", size);
+	while (*p != 0) {
+		const char *library;
+		size_t liblen;
+		bool matched = false;
+
+		while (*p == ' ' || *p == ';') {
+			p++;
+		}
+		library = p;
+		while (*p != 0 && *p != ' ' && *p != ';') {
+			p++;
+		}
+		liblen = (size_t)(p - library);
+		while (*p == ' ') {
+			const char *word = ++p;
+
+			while (*p != 0 && *p != ' ' && *p != ';') {
+				p++;
+			}
+			if (!matched && (size_t)(p - word) == namelen && namelen != 0 && liblen != 0 &&
+			    strncmp(word, name, namelen) == 0) {
+				matched = true;         /* this group names this program; its library is added once */
+			}
+		}
+		if (matched && liblen != 0 && used + 1 + liblen < size) {
+			if (any) {
+				env[used++] = ':';      /* dyld takes several libraries separated by ":" */
+			}
+			memcpy(env + used, library, liblen);
+			used += liblen;
+			env[used] = 0;
+			any = true;
+		}
+	}
+	return any;
+}

+/*
+ * hakios: the system does not sleep. There is nothing here to sleep into and nothing that would
+ * wake it: with the screen locked, powerd asks for system sleep within seconds, and that request
+ * ended in IOCPUSleepKernel() -- with one processor it came straight back out, again and again
+ * (every time a round of sleep and wake notifications to all the system); with more than one it
+ * stopped there for good, waiting for a processor to go that never goes. Refused instead, the
+ * system stays awake with its display off, and the side button or a tap wakes the screen.
+ * Boot-arg syssleep=1 gives the old behaviour back.
+ */

+/*
+ * Boot-arg regtrace=1: report the registry properties user space asks for and does not
+ * find (regtrace=2: every property asked for). Shows what a daemon expects of a driver.
+ */
+static TUNABLE(uint32_t, regtrace_level, "regtrace", 0);
+
+static void
+regtrace_report(IORegistryEntry * entry, const char * property, bool found)
+{
+	char procname[32] = "?";
+
+	if (regtrace_level == 0 || (found && regtrace_level < 2)) {
+		return;
+	}
+	proc_selfname(procname, sizeof(procname));
+	IOLog("regtrace: %s[%d] %s(%s).%s %s\n", procname, proc_selfpid(), entry->getName(),
+	    entry->getMetaClass()->getClassName(), property, found ? "found" : "MISSING");
+}

+/*
+ * The slower cores (an L2 access penalty, or the loader's "small-core"): each is made the SMT
+ * sibling ("secondary") of a faster core of its own, and the scheduler then treats it as XNU
+ * treats the second thread of a hyperthreaded core: a thread is put on it only when no faster
+ * core is idle or running something of lower priority; it looks for work only when none of
+ * them is idle; and what runs on it goes back to the run queue at every rescheduling, to be
+ * put on a faster core that has come free meanwhile. (XNU itself pairs such a core with the
+ * boot processor, which allows one of them; the phone has three: with cpus=8, cores 3, 2 and
+ * 1 go with 4, 5 and 6, so that 7, the boot core and the fastest, where real-time threads go
+ * first, stays alone: the scheduler idles a secondary while its primary runs a real-time
+ * thread.)
+ */
+static uint32_t small_cores_apart = 2;          /* boot-arg small_cores, read in ml_parse_cpu_topology() (before tunables are) */
+static int ml_slow_core_partner[MAX_CPUS];      /* by cpu_id: the faster core it is paired with, -1 if none */
+
+static void
+ml_choose_slow_core_partners(void)
+{
+	bool taken[MAX_CPUS] = { false };
+
+	for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CPUS; i++) {
+		ml_slow_core_partner[i] = -1;
+	}
+	for (int i = 0; i < (int)topology_info.num_cpus; i++) {
+		int partner = -1;
+
+		if (topology_info.cpus[i].l2_access_penalty == 0) {
+			continue;
+		}
+		/* the last fast core not yet taken; the boot core only if there is no other */
+		for (int j = (int)topology_info.num_cpus - 1; j >= 0; j--) {
+			if (topology_info.cpus[j].l2_access_penalty != 0 || taken[j]) {
+				continue;
+			}
+			if (&topology_info.cpus[j] == topology_info.boot_cpu) {
+				if (partner < 0) {
+					partner = j;
+				}
+				continue;
+			}
+			partner = j;
+			break;
+		}
+		if (partner >= 0) {
+			taken[partner] = true;
+			ml_slow_core_partner[i] = partner;
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+extern void loader_log_line(const char *line);
+
+/* At the registration of each processor: pairs it with its partner, if that one is registered too. */
+static void
+ml_pair_slow_processors(int cpu_id)
+{
+	for (int i = 0; i < (int)topology_info.num_cpus; i++) {
+		int partner = ml_slow_core_partner[i];
+		processor_t slow, fast;
+		char line[128];
+
+		if (partner < 0 || (i != cpu_id && partner != cpu_id)) {
+			continue;
+		}
+		slow = processor_array[i];
+		fast = processor_array[partner];
+		if (slow == PROCESSOR_NULL || fast == PROCESSOR_NULL || slow->processor_primary == fast) {
+			continue;
+		}
+		sched_slow_secondaries = small_cores_apart >= 2;
+		processor_set_primary(slow, fast);
+		snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "cpu %d (phys id 0x%x) is a slower core: the scheduler uses it after cpu %d (phys id 0x%x)\n",
+		    i, topology_info.cpus[i].phys_id, partner, topology_info.cpus[partner].phys_id);
+		printf("%s", line);
+		loader_log_line(line);          /* (the kernel's own log of a run keeps only its end) */
+	}
+}
+
+/* How long processor cpu_id has been idle since it started, in mach_absolute_time() units (hakios.cpufreq.c's cpuload). */
+bool ml_cpu_idle_time(int cpu_id, uint64_t *idle);
+
+bool
+ml_cpu_idle_time(int cpu_id, uint64_t *idle)
+{
+	struct recount_usage usage = { 0 };
+
+	if (cpu_id < 0 || cpu_id >= MAX_SCHED_CPUS || processor_array[cpu_id] == PROCESSOR_NULL) {
+		return false;
+	}
+	recount_processor_usage(&processor_array[cpu_id]->pr_recount, &usage, idle);
+	return true;
+}

+/*
+ * For apfs's lock statistics (bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_vnops.c): how long the current thread has
+ * been runnable (running included) and how long it has run, in mach_absolute_time() units.
+ * Taken before and after a wait for a lock, the two tell the wait apart: blocked, queued for

+
+void
+thread_runnable_and_run_self(uint64_t *runnable, uint64_t *run)
+{
+	thread_t thread = current_thread();
+	boolean_t istate = ml_set_interrupts_enabled(FALSE);
+	uint64_t now = mach_absolute_time();
+
+	*runnable = thread->runnable_timer.all_bits + (now - thread->runnable_timer.tstamp);
+	*run = recount_current_thread_time_mach();
+	ml_set_interrupts_enabled(istate);
+}
```

`xnu/hfs/hfs.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# HFS Plus for the kernel (the data volume, bsd/hfs): Apple's sources are not kept here, as XNU's are not. They are
# fetched from Apple's own release, hfs-627.100.6, and what this port changes in them is xnu/hfs/hfs.patch; the
# files of its own (bsd/hfs/hfs_builtin.c) are in xnu/files like every other new file.
#
#   xnu/hfs/hfs.sh put TREE      Apple's files that core.list and encodings.list name into TREE's bsd/hfs and
#                                bsd/hfs_encodings, and hfs.patch over them (xnu/apply.sh does this)
#   xnu/hfs/hfs.sh export TREE   hfs.patch again from TREE (xnu/export.sh does this)
#
# env: HFS_URL  where to fetch from (default Apple's repository on GitHub; a clone that has the tag will do)
#      HFS_SRC  where the release is kept once fetched (default xnu-src/hfs-627.100.6 beside the kernel tree)
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TAG=hfs-627.100.6
BASE=31d5ec238dfab485e78a9a30b8b92d13e8914f03
URL=${HFS_URL:-https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/hfs.git}
SRC=${HFS_SRC:-$HERE/../../xnu-src/$TAG}
CMD=$1 TREE=$2
[ -n "$CMD" ] && [ -d "$TREE" ] || { echo "usage: xnu/hfs/hfs.sh put|export TREE" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ ! -d "$SRC/core" ]; then
	rm -rf "$SRC"
	git init -q "$SRC"
	git -C "$SRC" remote add origin "$URL"
	git -C "$SRC" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "refs/tags/$TAG:refs/tags/$TAG"
	git -C "$SRC" checkout -q "$TAG"
fi
[ "$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$BASE" ] || { echo "hfs.sh: $SRC is not $TAG ($BASE)" >&2; exit 1; }

case "$CMD" in
put)
	mkdir -p "$TREE/bsd/hfs" "$TREE/bsd/hfs_encodings"
	while read -r f; do cp "$SRC/core/$f" "$TREE/bsd/hfs/$f"; done < "$HERE/core.list"
	while read -r f; do cp "$SRC/hfs_encodings/$f" "$TREE/bsd/hfs_encodings/$f"; done < "$HERE/encodings.list"
	git -C "$TREE" apply --whitespace=nowarn "$HERE/hfs.patch"
	echo "hfs.sh: $TAG: $(wc -l < "$HERE/core.list") + $(wc -l < "$HERE/encodings.list") files, $(grep -c '^+++ ' "$HERE/hfs.patch") changed"
	;;
export)
	: > "$HERE/hfs.patch.new"
	while read -r f; do
		diff -u --label "a/bsd/hfs/$f" --label "b/bsd/hfs/$f" "$SRC/core/$f" "$TREE/bsd/hfs/$f" >> "$HERE/hfs.patch.new" || true
	done < "$HERE/core.list"
	while read -r f; do
		diff -u --label "a/bsd/hfs_encodings/$f" --label "b/bsd/hfs_encodings/$f" "$SRC/hfs_encodings/$f" \
		    "$TREE/bsd/hfs_encodings/$f" >> "$HERE/hfs.patch.new" || true
	done < "$HERE/encodings.list"
	mv "$HERE/hfs.patch.new" "$HERE/hfs.patch"
	;;
*)
	echo "usage: xnu/hfs/hfs.sh put|export TREE" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

```

`xnu/sync-drivers.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Copy the drivers that were edited in drivers/ into the kernel tree, so that `make kernel` builds what is in
# the repository. A driver is copied only when the file in drivers/ is NEWER than the one in the tree: a driver
# that was edited in the tree (and not yet exported with xnu/export.sh) is never overwritten by an old copy.
# usage: xnu/sync-drivers.sh [KERNEL-TREE]       (default: $XNU_SRC, else xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2)
# prints one line per file it copied, and "drivers: in step" when there was nothing to do.
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TREE=${1:-${XNU_SRC:-$HERE/../xnu-src/xnu-8796.121.2}}
[ -d "$TREE" ] || { echo "sync-drivers: no kernel tree at $TREE (xnu/apply.sh makes it)" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$HERE/../drivers/map" ] || { echo "sync-drivers: no drivers/map" >&2; exit 1; }
copied=0
while read -r sub tree _; do
	case "$sub" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
	src="$HERE/../drivers/$sub/$(basename "$tree")"
	[ -f "$src" ] || { echo "sync-drivers: drivers/$sub/$(basename "$tree") is in drivers/map but missing" >&2; exit 1; }
	if [ ! -e "$TREE/$tree" ] || { [ "$src" -nt "$TREE/$tree" ] && ! cmp -s "$src" "$TREE/$tree"; }; then
		mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TREE/$tree")"
		cp -p "$src" "$TREE/$tree"
		echo "sync-drivers: drivers/$sub/$(basename "$tree") -> $tree"
		copied=$((copied + 1))
	fi
done < "$HERE/../drivers/map"
# ... and the drivers of the SoC and device repositories checked out (socs/*/drivers/, devices/*/drivers/: docs/porting/repositories.md)
while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r src tree; do
	[ -n "$src" ] || continue
	[ -f "$src" ] || { echo "sync-drivers: $src is named by its repository's conf but missing" >&2; exit 1; }
	if [ ! -e "$TREE/$tree" ] || { [ "$src" -nt "$TREE/$tree" ] && ! cmp -s "$src" "$TREE/$tree"; }; then
		mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TREE/$tree")"
		cp -p "$src" "$TREE/$tree"
		echo "sync-drivers: ${src#$HERE/../} -> $tree"
		copied=$((copied + 1))
	fi
done <<EOF2
$(python3 "$HERE/../tools/hakios-config.py" external-files)
EOF2
[ "$copied" -gt 0 ] || echo "sync-drivers: drivers in step with the kernel tree"

```

`xnuloader/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the XNU loader as a freestanding AArch64 UEFI application.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
# the iPhone's identity for XNU, from the device tree of the builder's own IPSW (not in the repository)
[ -f identity.h ] || ./mkidentity.sh

clang --target=aarch64-unknown-windows -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -fno-stack-protector -fshort-wchar \
  -mgeneral-regs-only -O1 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter -c loader.c -o loader.obj
# /base: UEFI loads an image at its preferred address when that is free. The PE default (0x140000000)
# is in the middle of the phone's largest block of RAM, which XNU needs in one piece.
lld-link /subsystem:efi_application /entry:efi_main /nodefaultlib /base:0xA1000000 /out:loader.efi loader.obj
ls -la loader.efi

```

```h
/*
 * Minimal UEFI definitions for the XNU loader (freestanding, no EDK2).
 * Only what the loader touches is declared; unused slots are void pointers
 * so that structure layouts still match the UEFI specification.
 */
#ifndef XNULOADER_EFI_H
#define XNULOADER_EFI_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>

#define EFIAPI
typedef uint64_t efi_status;
typedef void *efi_handle;
typedef uint16_t char16;

#define EFI_ERROR_BIT        0x8000000000000000ULL
#define EFI_ERROR(s)         (((s) & EFI_ERROR_BIT) != 0)
#define EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL (EFI_ERROR_BIT | 5)

typedef struct {
	uint32_t a; uint16_t b; uint16_t c; uint8_t d[8];
} efi_guid;

typedef struct {
	uint64_t signature; uint32_t revision; uint32_t header_size; uint32_t crc32; uint32_t reserved;
} efi_table_header;

struct efi_text_output;

	void *reset;
	efi_status (EFIAPI *output_string)(struct efi_text_output *self, const char16 *str);
} efi_text_output;

enum { EfiLoaderData = 2, EfiConventionalMemory = 7 };
enum { AllocateAnyPages = 0, AllocateMaxAddress = 1, AllocateAddress = 2 };

typedef struct {

	void *connect_controller, *disconnect_controller, *open_protocol, *close_protocol, *open_protocol_information;

	    const void *ctx, const efi_guid *group, void **event);
} efi_boot_services;

struct efi_time {
	uint16_t year;
	uint8_t  month, day, hour, minute, second, pad1;
	uint32_t nanosecond;
	int16_t  timezone;              /* minutes; 0x7FF = not specified */
	uint8_t  daylight, pad2;
};

typedef struct {
	efi_table_header hdr;
	efi_status (EFIAPI *get_time)(struct efi_time *time, void *capabilities);
	void *set_time, *get_wakeup_time, *set_wakeup_time;

	void *get_next_high_mono_count;

} efi_runtime_services;

typedef struct {
	efi_table_header hdr;

	efi_handle con_in_handle; void *con_in;
	efi_handle con_out_handle; efi_text_output *con_out;
	efi_handle stderr_handle; efi_text_output *std_err;
	efi_runtime_services *rt;
	efi_boot_services *bs;
	uint64_t nr_tables;                     /* the configuration tables: ACPI, a device tree, ... */
	struct { efi_guid guid; void *table; } *tables;
} efi_system_table;

/* a device path is a list of these, each followed by its data, ending with type 0x7f subtype 0xff */
typedef struct {
	uint8_t type, subtype;
	uint8_t length[2];                      /* of the whole node, header included, little endian */
} efi_device_path;

/* Graphics Output */
typedef struct {
	uint32_t version, width, height, pixel_format;

	efi_status (EFIAPI *set_mode)(struct efi_gop *self, uint32_t mode);
	void *blt;

/*
 * Qualcomm's open ChargerEx protocol.  The protocol is implemented by the
 * stock ChargerExDxe in the redwood UEFI image and is safe to use for
 * read-only charger/battery queries while boot services remain resident.
 */
typedef struct {
	uint64_t revision;
	efi_status (EFIAPI *get_charger_presence)(uint8_t *present);
	efi_status (EFIAPI *get_battery_presence)(uint8_t *present);

	efi_status (EFIAPI *is_offmode_charging)(uint8_t *offmode);
	efi_status (EFIAPI *is_power_ok)(uint32_t type, void *info);
} efi_charger_ex;

/*
 * The first public entries of Xiaomi's Qualcomm charger protocol.  Its GUID,
 * revision and function layout are taken from the QcomChargerDxeLA.efi and
 * QcomChargerApp.efi shipped in this repository.  get_charging_action is used
 * only as a status read: the loader never calls take_action and therefore does
 * not change current/voltage limits or bypass the firmware's JEITA checks.

typedef struct {

	void *reserved_18;

	efi_status (EFIAPI *take_action)(uint32_t action, const void *battery_status);
} efi_qcom_charger;

/* Block I/O + Partition Info (used to persist the log on the phone) */

	uint32_t media_id; uint8_t removable, present, logical, read_only, write_caching; uint8_t pad[3];
	uint32_t block_size; uint32_t io_align; uint64_t last_block;

	efi_status (EFIAPI *write_blocks)(struct efi_block_io *self, uint32_t media_id, uint64_t lba, uint64_t size, void *buf);

/*
```

`xnuloader/im4p.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The payload of an IM4P container (an Image4 payload: what the files of Firmware/ in an IPSW are).
usage: im4p.py IN.im4p OUT
IM4P is DER: SEQUENCE { IA5String "IM4P", IA5String type, IA5String description, OCTET STRING payload, ... }.
The payload comes out as it is in the container -- for a device tree that is an LZFSE stream ("bvx2"),
to be decoded by lzfse(1), compression_tool(1) of macOS, or the lzfse Python module (see mkidentity.sh).
"""
import sys


def tlv(data, pos):
    """One DER element: (tag, value start, value end)."""
    tag = data[pos]
    length = data[pos + 1]
    pos += 2
    if length & 0x80:
        n = length & 0x7f
        length = int.from_bytes(data[pos:pos + n], 'big')
        pos += n
    return tag, pos, pos + length


def main():
    data = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
    tag, pos, end = tlv(data, 0)
    if tag != 0x30:
        sys.exit('im4p.py: not a DER sequence')
    strings = []
    while pos < end:
        tag, start, stop = tlv(data, pos)
        if tag == 0x16:
            strings.append(data[start:stop].decode('ascii', 'replace'))
        elif tag == 0x04:
            if len(strings) < 2 or strings[0] != 'IM4P':
                sys.exit('im4p.py: not an IM4P (%r)' % strings)
            with open(sys.argv[2], 'wb') as out:
                out.write(data[start:stop])
            print('im4p.py: %s (%s): payload of %d bytes%s' % (strings[1], strings[2] if len(strings) > 2 else '',
                  stop - start, ', LZFSE' if data[start:start + 3] == b'bvx' else ''))
            return
        pos = stop
    sys.exit('im4p.py: no payload')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`xnuloader/loader.c`:

```c
/*
 * XNU loader: a UEFI application that plays the role of iBoot for an
 * open-source arm64 XNU kernel on non-Apple hardware.
 *
 *   - finds the "XNUP" payload in RAM (placed there by the boot shim on the
 *     phone, by `-device loader` under QEMU) and the Mach-O kernel inside it
 *   - picks a block of free RAM to be XNU's [physBase, physBase + memSize)
 *   - copies the Mach-O segments there, builds an Apple-format device tree
 *     and a boot_args structure behind the kernel
 *   - exits boot services, turns the MMU off and jumps to the kernel entry
 */
#include "efi.h"
#include "identity.h"         /* who Darwin shall think we are: from the iPhone's own device tree (mkidentity.py) */

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Fixed conventions shared with the boot shim, the packer and the kernel   */

#define PAYLOAD_BASE        0xF0000000ULL
#define PAYLOAD_MAGIC       0x50554E58u /* "XNUP" */

struct payload_header { uint32_t magic; uint32_t size; };
struct payload_entry { char name[16]; uint32_t size; uint32_t reserved; };

#define KERNEL_VIRT_BASE    0xFFFFFFF004000000ULL /* boot_args.virtBase */
#define KERNEL_LINK_OFFSET  0x03000000ULL         /* kernel text sits 48 MB above the base */
#define BASE_ALIGN          0x02000000ULL         /* 32 MB: L2 block size with 16K pages */
#define MAX_MEM_SIZE        0x180000000ULL        /* 6 GB; the kernel's bootstrap page tables cover 8 */
/*
 * A root image too big for the payload area is placed here, at a fixed
 * offset inside the kernel's memory window, once; it then survives any
 * number of kernel runs (nothing writes to it: the root is read-only).
 */
#define RESIDENT_RD_OFFSET  0x08000000ULL
#define RESIDENT_RD_RESERVE 0x30000000ULL         /* RAM that must remain for the kernel itself */
#define PAGE_SIZE_MAX       0x4000ULL

#define LOG_PARTITION       u"logdump"
#define CHECKPOINT_SELFTEST 999
#define PANIC_LOG_SIZE      0x80000u
#define NVRAM_BANK_SIZE     0x2000u
#define PANIC_LOG_BASE      (PAYLOAD_BASE + PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE - 0x100000ULL)
#define PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE    0x04000000ULL         /* RAM reserved for the payload in the UEFI memory map */

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* XNU structures (pexpert/pexpert/arm64/boot.h, mach-o/loader.h)           */

struct boot_video {
	uint64_t v_baseAddr, v_display, v_rowBytes, v_width, v_height, v_depth;
};

#define BOOT_LINE_LENGTH 608

struct boot_args {
	uint16_t revision;
	uint16_t version;
	uint64_t virtBase;
	uint64_t physBase;
	uint64_t memSize;
	uint64_t topOfKernelData;
	struct boot_video video;
	uint32_t machineType;
	uint64_t deviceTreeP;
	uint32_t deviceTreeLength;
	char commandLine[BOOT_LINE_LENGTH];
	uint64_t bootFlags;
	uint64_t memSizeActual;
};

#define MH_MAGIC_64      0xFEEDFACFu
#define LC_SEGMENT_64    0x19
#define LC_UNIXTHREAD    0x5

struct mach_header_64 { uint32_t magic, cputype, cpusubtype, filetype, ncmds, sizeofcmds, flags, reserved; };
struct load_command { uint32_t cmd, cmdsize; };
struct segment_command_64 {
	uint32_t cmd, cmdsize; char segname[16];
	uint64_t vmaddr, vmsize, fileoff, filesize;
	uint32_t maxprot, initprot, nsects, flags;
};

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Globals and small helpers                                                */

static efi_system_table *ST;
static efi_boot_services *BS;
static efi_handle IMAGE;

static char log_buf[32768];
static uint32_t log_len;

void *
memset(void *dst, int c, size_t n)
{
	uint8_t *d = dst;
	while (n--) {
		*d++ = (uint8_t)c;
	}
	return dst;
}

int
memcmp(const void *a, const void *b, size_t n)
{
	const uint8_t *x = a, *y = b;

	for (; n > 0; n--, x++, y++) {
		if (*x != *y) {
			return *x < *y ? -1 : 1;
		}
	}
	return 0;
}

void *
memcpy(void *dst, const void *src, size_t n)
{
	uint8_t *d = dst;
	const uint8_t *s = src;

	/*
	 * Word at a time when possible: USB transfer buffers are uncached, where
	 * a byte loop costs one bus access per byte (6 MB/s instead of 30+).
	 */
	if ((((uintptr_t)d | (uintptr_t)s) & 7) == 0) {
		uint64_t *dw = (uint64_t *)d;
		const uint64_t *sw = (const uint64_t *)s;

		for (; n >= 32; n -= 32, dw += 4, sw += 4) {
			uint64_t a = sw[0], b = sw[1], c = sw[2], e = sw[3];
			dw[0] = a;
			dw[1] = b;
			dw[2] = c;
			dw[3] = e;
		}
		for (; n >= 8; n -= 8) {
			*dw++ = *sw++;
		}
		d = (uint8_t *)dw;
		s = (const uint8_t *)sw;
	}
	while (n--) {
		*d++ = *s++;
	}
	return dst;
}

static size_t
str_len(const char *s)
{
	size_t n = 0;
	while (s[n]) {
		n++;
	}
	return n;
}

static int
str_eq(const char *a, const char *b)
{
	while (*a && *a == *b) {
		a++, b++;
	}
	return *a == *b;
}

/*
 * Set once the loader takes commands over USB: its log travels that way, and
 * the screen is left to the kernel (and to "oem screenshot").
 */
static int screen_quiet;
/*
 * And while the kernel runs, whatever started the loader: under HakiOS's U-Boot (the menu of an installed HakiOS) there
 * is no USB command loop, the text console is U-Boot's, drawn into the framebuffer the kernel shows Darwin in, and every
 * line core 0 printed during a run (the storage's, the battery's, the watchdog's) ran over the system's screen.
 * What it was before the run, to go back to.
 */
static int screen_quiet_before_run;

static void
put_char(char c)
{
	char16 w[3] = { 0, 0, 0 };

	if (log_len < sizeof(log_buf) - 1) {
		log_buf[log_len++] = c;
	}
	if (ST->con_out != NULL && !screen_quiet) {
		if (c == '\n') {
			w[0] = '\r', w[1] = '\n';
		} else {
			w[0] = (char16)c;
		}
		ST->con_out->output_string(ST->con_out, w);
	}
}

/* printf subset: %s %x %d (64-bit values), %% */
static void
print(const char *fmt, ...)
{
	__builtin_va_list ap;
	__builtin_va_start(ap, fmt);
	for (; *fmt; fmt++) {
		if (*fmt != '%') {
			put_char(*fmt);
			continue;
		}
		fmt++;
		if (*fmt == 's') {
			const char *s = __builtin_va_arg(ap, const char *);
			while (*s) {
				put_char(*s++);
			}
		} else if (*fmt == 'x' || *fmt == 'd') {
			uint64_t v = __builtin_va_arg(ap, uint64_t);
			unsigned base = (*fmt == 'x') ? 16 : 10;
			char tmp[24];
			int i = 0;
			do {
				tmp[i++] = "0123456789abcdef"[v % base];
				v /= base;
			} while (v);
			while (i) {
				put_char(tmp[--i]);
			}
		} else {
			put_char(*fmt);
		}
	}
	__builtin_va_end(ap);
}

#define READ_SYSREG(name) ({ uint64_t _v; __asm__ volatile ("mrs %0, " #name : "=r" (_v)); _v; })

/*
 * Write back and drop cached copies of a range. Required for memory the
 * kernel will touch with the MMU (and so the data cache) off: its early code
 * builds page tables that way, and a stale cached copy of those pages would
 * be what the table walker sees once caches are turned on again.
 */
static void
flush_dcache(uint64_t start, uint64_t end)
{
	uint64_t line = 4ULL << ((READ_SYSREG(CTR_EL0) >> 16) & 0xF);
	for (uint64_t p = start & ~(line - 1); p < end; p += line) {
		__asm__ volatile ("dc civac, %0" : : "r" (p));
	}
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy");
}

static void
clean_dcache(uint64_t start, uint64_t end)
{
	uint64_t line = 4ULL << ((READ_SYSREG(CTR_EL0) >> 16) & 0xF);
	for (uint64_t p = start & ~(line - 1); p < end; p += line) {
		__asm__ volatile ("dc cvac, %0" : : "r" (p));
	}
	__asm__ volatile ("dsb sy");
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Log persistence: raw write to a GPT partition (phone only)               */

static efi_block_io *
find_log_partition(void)
{
	static const efi_guid part_guid = EFI_PARTITION_INFO_GUID;
	static const efi_guid blk_guid = EFI_BLOCK_IO_GUID;
	static const char16 want[] = LOG_PARTITION;
	efi_handle *handles;
	uint64_t count;

	if (EFI_ERROR(BS->locate_handle_buffer(ByProtocol, &part_guid, NULL, &count, &handles))) {
		return NULL;
	}
	for (uint64_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		efi_partition_info *info;
		efi_block_io *bio;
		int match = 1;

		if (EFI_ERROR(BS->handle_protocol(handles[i], &part_guid, (void **)&info)) || info->type != 2) {
			continue;
		}
		for (unsigned k = 0; k < sizeof(want) / sizeof(want[0]); k++) {
			if (info->name[k] != want[k]) {
				match = 0;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (match && !EFI_ERROR(BS->handle_protocol(handles[i], &blk_guid, (void **)&bio))) {
			/* (the handle array is pool memory the caller owns; this runs on every log write) */
			BS->free_pool(handles);
			return bio;
		}
	}
	BS->free_pool(handles);
	return NULL;
}

/*
 * The "staged" buffer holds the loader log followed by the kernel log of the
 * last run. It is what gets written to the log partition and what the host
 * fetches over USB (fastboot get_staged).
 */
/* aligned for any firmware's block I/O: U-Boot's wants a buffer aligned to the block size (media->io_align) */
static char out_buf[2 * 1024 * 1024] __attribute__((aligned(0x2000)));
/* the storage's reads for the kernel land here (block_poll), and nothing else may be put in it */
#define BLOCK_BUFFER_SIZE  (4u << 20)
static uint8_t block_buffer[BLOCK_BUFFER_SIZE] __attribute__((aligned(0x2000)));
/*
 * Where the log is read back to compare it (write_logs). Not block_buffer: that is the kernel's
 * mailbox buffer, and a read-back landing in it while the kernel runs on the other core would
 * overwrite data the kernel is still copying out of it.
 */
static uint8_t log_verify[sizeof(out_buf) + 8192] __attribute__((aligned(0x2000)));
static const char *staged_data = out_buf;   /* what "upload" sends: normally the log in out_buf */
static uint64_t staged_len;

static void
compose_logs(const char *klog, uint64_t klog_len)
{
	static const char sep[] = "\n== KERNEL LOG ==\n", end[] = "\n== END OF LOG ==\n";
	uint64_t n = log_len;

	staged_data = out_buf;
	memset(out_buf, 0, sizeof(out_buf));
	memcpy(out_buf, log_buf, log_len);
	if (klog != NULL) {
		if (klog_len > sizeof(out_buf) - n - 8192) {
			klog_len = sizeof(out_buf) - n - 8192;
		}
		memcpy(out_buf + n, sep, sizeof(sep) - 1);
		n += sizeof(sep) - 1;
		memcpy(out_buf + n, klog, klog_len);
		n += klog_len;
		memcpy(out_buf + n, end, sizeof(end) - 1);
		n += sizeof(end) - 1;
	}
	staged_len = n;
}

static int hc_list_is_uefis(void);
static int hc_log_skips;                /* logs not written this run (said twice at most) */
static void hc_print_state(const char *when);
static void hc_take_back(const char *when);

static void
write_logs(const char *klog, uint64_t klog_len)
{
	efi_block_io *bio = find_log_partition();

	compose_logs(klog, klog_len);
	if (bio == NULL) {
		/* No log partition (QEMU): echo the returned kernel log on the console instead. */
		if (klog != NULL) {
			print("\n== KERNEL LOG ==\n");
			for (uint64_t i = 0; i < klog_len; i++) {
				put_char(klog[i]);
			}
			print("\n== END OF LOG ==\n");
		}
		return;
	}
	uint64_t bs = bio->media->block_size;
	uint64_t len = (staged_len + 1 + bs - 1) / bs * bs;
	efi_status ws, rs = 0;
	int same = 0;

	/* only through UEFI's own transfer list (see hc_take_back) */
	if (!hc_list_is_uefis()) {
		if (hc_log_skips++ < 2) {
			hc_print_state("log not written");
			print("log: NOT WRITTEN to logdump: UEFI's transfer list is not the one in the controller\n");
		}
		compose_logs(klog, klog_len);
		return;
	}
	ws = bio->write_blocks(bio, bio->media->media_id, 0, len, out_buf);

	if (!EFI_ERROR(ws)) {
		bio->flush_blocks(bio);
		/*
		 * And read back: that the log is in the partition is what a run of the kernel's own UFS
		 * driver must leave possible (the controller is shared with this one). The line goes into
		 * the copy the host fetches over USB, not into the partition, which already has the rest.
		 */
		if (len <= sizeof(log_verify)) {
			rs = bio->read_blocks(bio, bio->media->media_id, 0, len, log_verify);
			flush_dcache((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)log_verify, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)log_verify + len);
			same = !EFI_ERROR(rs) && memcmp(log_verify, out_buf, len) == 0;
		}
	}
	print("log: %d bytes written to logdump (%x), read back %s (%x)\n", len, ws,
	    EFI_ERROR(ws) ? "not tried" : same ? "the same" : "DIFFERENT", rs);
	compose_logs(klog, klog_len);
}

static void
flush_log(void)
{
	write_logs(NULL, 0);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Apple device tree writer                                                 */
/*                                                                          */
/* node := u32 nProperties, u32 nChildren, props[], children[]              */
/* prop := char name[32], u32 length, value padded to 4 bytes               */

struct dt_writer {
	uint8_t *base, *cur;
	uint8_t *end;         /* the first byte after the room reserved for the tree */
	int overflow;         /* something did not fit: nothing more is written, run_kernel refuses the tree */
	uint32_t scratch[2];  /* the counts of a node that was not written (after an overflow) */
	uint32_t *counts[16]; /* [depth] -> {nProperties, nChildren} of the open node */
	int depth;
};

static void
dt_prop(struct dt_writer *w, const char *name, const void *data, uint32_t len)
{
	uint64_t padded = ((uint64_t)len + 3) & ~3ULL;

	/*
	 * Not past the room reserved for the tree (boot_args follows it), and not a name longer than the
	 * 32-byte field: either would overwrite what is next to it with no message.
	 */
	if (w->overflow || str_len(name) > 32 ||(uint64_t)(w->end - w->cur) < 36 + padded) {
		w->overflow = 1;
		return;
	}
	memset(w->cur, 0, 32);
	memcpy(w->cur, name, str_len(name));
	*(uint32_t *)(w->cur + 32) = len;
	memset(w->cur + 36, 0, (size_t)padded);
	memcpy(w->cur + 36, data, len);
	w->cur += 36 + padded;
	w->counts[w->depth - 1][0]++;
}

static void
dt_prop_str(struct dt_writer *w, const char *name, const char *value)
{
	dt_prop(w, name, value, (uint32_t)str_len(value) + 1);
}

static void
dt_prop_u32(struct dt_writer *w, const char *name, uint32_t value)
{
	dt_prop(w, name, &value, sizeof(value));
}

static void
dt_prop_u64(struct dt_writer *w, const char *name, uint64_t value)
{
	dt_prop(w, name, &value, sizeof(value));
}

/* Seconds since 1970 by the firmware's real-time clock, or 0 when it has none or it is not set. */
static uint64_t
firmware_epoch(void)
{
	static const uint16_t before_month[12] = { 0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334 };
	struct efi_time t;
	uint64_t days;

	if (ST->rt == NULL || ST->rt->get_time == NULL || EFI_ERROR(ST->rt->get_time(&t, NULL)) ||
	    t.year < 2024 || t.year > 2099 || t.month < 1 || t.month > 12) {
		return 0;
	}
	days = (uint64_t)(t.year - 1970) * 365 + (t.year - 1969) / 4 + before_month[t.month - 1] + (t.day - 1);
	if (t.month > 2 && t.year % 4 == 0) {
		days++;
	}
	uint64_t secs = days * 86400 + (uint64_t)t.hour * 3600 + (uint64_t)t.minute * 60 + t.second;
	if (t.timezone != 0x7FF) {
		secs += (int64_t)t.timezone * 60;       /* local time = UTC - timezone */
	}
	return secs;
}

/* A string in a field of fixed size, the rest zeros. */
static void
dt_prop_padded(struct dt_writer *w, const char *name, const char *value, uint32_t size)
{
	uint8_t field[64];

	memset(field, 0, sizeof(field));
	memcpy(field, value, str_len(value));
	dt_prop(w, name, field, size);
}

/*
 * Properties copied from the iPhone's device tree (identity.h), but one: the iPhone X's display is a
 * wide-gamut one ("artwork-display-gamut" P3), and with it Darwin takes the screen for one that shows
 * extended colour (MobileGestalt's HasExtendedColorDisplay): WebKit then draws a page's tiles into
 * surfaces of ten bits a colour ('w30r', 'b3a8'), which neither the kernel's surfaces nor the window
 * server's renderer here do (eight bits, BGRA), and every page comes out black. Here the screen is
 * what the framebuffer is: sRGB.
 */
static int gamut_p3;    /* boot-arg gamut=p3 (a test): the iPhone's own "P3" left in place */

static void
dt_identity(struct dt_writer *w, const struct identity_prop *props, uint32_t count, const unsigned char *data)
{
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		if (str_eq(props[i].name, "artwork-display-gamut") && !gamut_p3) {
			dt_prop(w, props[i].name, "sRGB", 5);
			continue;
		}
		dt_prop(w, props[i].name, data + props[i].offset, props[i].length);
	}
}

/* One property of those copied from the iPhone's device tree, by name. */
static void
dt_identity_one(struct dt_writer *w, const struct identity_prop *props, uint32_t count, const unsigned char *data, const char *name)
{
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
		if (str_eq(props[i].name, name)) {
			dt_prop(w, props[i].name, data + props[i].offset, props[i].length);
		}
	}
}

static void
dt_begin(struct dt_writer *w, const char *name)
{
	if (w->depth > 0) {
		w->counts[w->depth - 1][1]++;
	}
	if (w->overflow || (uint64_t)(w->end - w->cur) < 8) {
		/* no room: the node is not written, the depth is kept so that dt_end still pairs with it */
		w->overflow = 1;
		w->counts[w->depth++] = w->scratch;
		return;
	}
	w->counts[w->depth++] = (uint32_t *)w->cur;
	memset(w->cur, 0, 8);
	w->cur += 8;
	dt_prop_str(w, "name", name);
}

static void
dt_end(struct dt_writer *w)
{
	w->depth--;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Platform description                                                     */

struct platform {
	const char *name;
	uint64_t io_base, io_size;       /* one window covering the SoC peripherals */
	uint64_t gic_dist, gic_redist;   /* GICv3 */
	uint64_t uart;                   /* PL011, 0 if none */
	int psci_hvc;                    /* the firmware's power interface is called with HVC, not SMC */
	int log_other_cpu;               /* keep notes in the log partition while a kernel starts on another core */
	int cores;                       /* at most this many processor cores, numbered from 0 ... */
	int core_shift;                  /* ... in this bit of MPIDR: the phone numbers them in the second affinity field */
	uint32_t timeout_scale;          /* a kernel on several cores gets this much longer to wait for a lock, 0: as it is */
	uint32_t small_cores;            /* a bit for each of the slower cores, by number: "small-core" in the device tree */
};

static const struct platform platform_qemu_virt = {
	.name = "qemu-virt", .io_base = 0x08000000, .io_size = 0x08000000,
	.gic_dist = 0x08000000, .gic_redist = 0x080A0000, .uart = 0x09000000, .psci_hvc = 1,
	.cores = 8, .core_shift = 0,
	/*
	 * QEMU's emulated cores stop each other all the time (every flush of a page from all the
	 * TLBs is a rendezvous of all its CPU threads), and the kernel's patience with a spin lock
	 * is that of real hardware: an eighth of a second by a 24 MHz clock, a twentieth here.
	 */
	.timeout_scale = 20,
};

static const struct platform platform_redwood = {
	/* io_base must be non-zero: XNU treats a zero SoC base as "no SoC" and skips clock setup. */
	.name = "redwood", .io_base = 0x00400000, .io_size = 0x3FC00000,
	.gic_dist = 0x17A00000, .gic_redist = 0x17A60000, .uart = 0, .log_other_cpu = 1,
	.cores = 8, .core_shift = 8,
	/*
	 * Cores 0-3 are Cortex-A55s (1.8 GHz at most), 4-7 Cortex-A78s (2.4 GHz): a big one is about
	 * 2.5 times as fast. The kernel uses the small ones only when the big ones are all busy
	 * (XNU's machine_routines.c, ml_choose_slow_core_partners()).
	 */
	.small_cores = 0x0f,
};

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */

static void
reboot(void)
{
	hc_take_back("before the reset");
	flush_log();
	ST->rt->reset_system(0 /* EfiResetCold */, 0, 0, NULL);
	for (;;) {
	}
}

/*
 * Return-from-kernel support.
 *
 * Boot services are never exited: UEFI stays resident outside XNU's memory
 * window. loader_save_ctx() records the UEFI execution environment and
 * returns 0. When the kernel is done it jumps to loader_return_stub (mapped
 * 1:1 or with the MMU off) with x0 = PA of its log, x1 = length, x2 = reason
 * (0 = orderly, 1 = early exception, then x3..x7 = ESR, ELR, FAR, LR, SP).
 * The stub switches the MMU off, reinstates the saved environment and makes
 * loader_save_ctx() return a second time, with 1.
 *
 * The EL1 physical timer (CNTP_*) is deliberately left alone: the Qualcomm
 * hypervisor traps it. The CTX_CNTP_* slots are unused.
 */
enum {
	CTX_TTBR0, CTX_TCR, CTX_MAIR, CTX_SCTLR, CTX_VBAR, CTX_CPACR, CTX_SP, CTX_SPSEL, CTX_DAIF,
	CTX_CNTV_CTL, CTX_CNTV_CVAL, CTX_CNTP_CTL, CTX_CNTP_CVAL, CTX_CNTKCTL,
	CTX_X18, CTX_X19, /* ... x30 */
	CTX_LOG_PA = CTX_X19 + 12, CTX_LOG_LEN, CTX_REASON, CTX_ESR, CTX_ELR, CTX_FAR, CTX_LR, CTX_KSP,
	CTX_TPIDR_EL1, CTX_TPIDR_EL0, CTX_TPIDRRO_EL0, CTX_SP_EL0, CTX_CONTEXTIDR, CTX_MDSCR, CTX_FPCR, CTX_FPSR,
	CTX_ICC_PMR, CTX_ICC_IGRPEN1, CTX_ICC_BPR1, CTX_COUNT
};
uint64_t loader_ctx[CTX_COUNT];
int loader_save_ctx(void);
void loader_return_stub(void);

__asm__ (
        ".text\n"
        ".balign 64\n"
        ".globl loader_save_ctx\n"
        "loader_save_ctx:\n"
        "  adrp x10, loader_ctx\n"
        "  add  x10, x10, :lo12:loader_ctx\n"
        "  mrs x9, ttbr0_el1\n   str x9, [x10, #0]\n"
        "  mrs x9, tcr_el1\n     str x9, [x10, #8]\n"
        "  mrs x9, mair_el1\n    str x9, [x10, #16]\n"
        "  mrs x9, sctlr_el1\n   str x9, [x10, #24]\n"
```
